senses.definition: That place, near the listener or already mentioned.

examples.text: 거기에 무엇이 있습니까?
examples.translation: What is there?

examples.text: 거기 잠깐만 기다려 주세요.
examples.translation: Please wait there for a moment.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning; 'early' is one sense.

faults.quote: 일찍 often functions like 'early' in English.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition and gloss.

notes: Opposite of 늦게 (late).

senses.definition: Before the usual or expected time.

examples.text: 오늘 아침에는 평소보다 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.translation: I woke up earlier than usual this morning.

examples.text: 일찍 도착해서 친구를 기다렸어요.
examples.translation: I arrived early and waited for my friend.

faults.quote: 지름 is a common misspelling of 지금, but 지름 does not mean
faults.why: Unhelpful and fabricated note about a random typo.

notes: Also used as a noun. 지금 simply refers to the present moment, whereas 이제 ('now') emphasizes a change or new state starting from this moment.

senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: 지금 뭐 해요?
examples.translation: What are you doing now?

examples.text: 저는 지금 바쁩니다.
examples.translation: I am busy right now.

faults.quote: Used for liquids extracted from fruits or vegetables.
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler (restating the definition and listing unrelated drinks); broken plural missing.

notes: Plural: عَصَائِر (ʕaṣāʔir).

senses.definition: The liquid obtained from pressing or squeezing fruit or vegetables.

examples.text: أَشْرَبُ عَصِيرَ بُرْتُقَالٍ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: I drink orange juice every morning.

notes: The standard MSA term; in everyday speech, the loanword بِيرَة (bīra) is much more common.

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grain.

examples.text: تُصْنَعُ الجِعَةُ مِنَ الحُبُوبِ المُتَخَمِّرَةِ.
examples.translation: Beer is made from fermented grains.

faults.quote: Borrowed from English.
faults.why: Both notes state the obvious while omitting that this loanword does not inflect for case.

notes: Invariable loanword: does not take case endings.

senses.definition: A large self-service shop that sells food, drinks, and household goods.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ الخُضَارَ مِنَ السُّوبَرْمَارْكِت.
examples.translation: I bought the vegetables from the supermarket.

faults.quote: /baʕda z.zuð.huɾ/

examples.translation: I will visit you in the afternoon.

faults.why: Lacks the irregular long-vowel inflection in construct/pronoun forms (أبو / أبا / أبي) and the broken plural (آباء).

senses.definition: A male parent.

examples.text: هَذَا أَبِي.
examples.translation: This is my father.

faults.why: Wrong tone in romanization: สั้น has a falling tone (sân), not rising (sǎn).

examples.text: เรามีการประชุมสั้นๆ ก่อนเริ่มงาน
examples.translation: We had a short meeting before starting work.

faults.quote: While หิว on its own means hungry, adding น้ำ makes it specifically

examples.text: ฉันหิวน้ำมากหลังออกกำลังกาย
examples.translation: I am very thirsty after exercising.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with โชคดี (chōk diː), which means 'lucky'.
faults.why: Filler note; learners do not confuse ใจดี with โชคดี.

senses.definition: Friendly, caring, and generous toward other people.

examples.text: คุณครูใจดีมากและช่วยเหลือนักเรียนเสมอ
examples.translation: The teacher is very kind and always helps the students.

faults.quote: When talking about younger siblings or people in general, use 'เด็ก' (dèk)

notes: Used for physical size, opposite of ใหญ่ (big). For a small amount or quantity ('little', 'few'), use น้อย instead.

senses.definition: Not large in physical size.

examples.text: บ้านหลังนี้เล็กมาก
examples.translation: This house is very small.

faults.quote: or the stability of an object

senses.definition: Lacking physical or emotional strength; not strong or resilient.

examples.text: สุขภาพของเขาอ่อนแอลงเรื่อยๆ
examples.translation: His health is getting weaker and weaker.

examples.text: อย่าทำตัวอ่อนแอต่อหน้าคู่แข่ง
examples.translation: Do not act weak in front of your competitor.

faults.quote: Use 'jardin' for the outdoor space with grass and flowers
faults.why: Restates the definition; also mentions 'public park' which is missing from senses.

examples.translation: The children are playing in the garden.

faults.quote: [0] (time) ... or the daylight part ... [1] (light) Light from the sun or daylight

senses.definition: A period of twenty-four hours, used as a unit of time or a date on the calendar.

examples.text: Je reste à Paris pendant trois jours.
examples.translation: I am staying in Paris for three days.

senses.definition: The time between sunrise and sunset, or the natural light of that time.

examples.text: Le jour commence à se lever sur la ville.
examples.translation: Daylight is starting to break over the city.

faults.why: Should mention the silent final '-s' to help A2 learners with pronunciation.

notes: The final '-s' is always silent, even in the plural.

senses.definition: Liquid obtained from pressing fruit or vegetables.

examples.text: Je bois un verre de jus d'orange le matin.
examples.translation: I drink a glass of orange juice in the morning.

senses.definition: The liquid that comes out of meat while it cooks.

examples.text: La viande est cuite dans son jus.
examples.translation: The meat is cooked in its own juices.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'la laid', which is an adjective meaning ugly.

senses.definition: A white liquid produced by cows, goats, or other mammals, used as a drink and in cooking.

examples.text: Je bois un grand verre de lait tous les matins.
examples.translation: I drink a big glass of milk every morning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with kamar mandi, which is the bathroom.

senses.definition: A room in a house or hotel used for sleeping.

examples.translation: She cleans the bedroom every morning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'pekerjaan' (job/work); 'kantor' is the place

examples.translation: He goes to the office every morning.

faults.quote: the two are almost always used together to refer to the specific
faults.why: Wordy filler explaining the obvious meaning of 'post office'.

notes: From kantor (office) + pos (mail, post).

senses.definition: A public building where you can send letters and parcels or buy stamps.

examples.text: Saya harus pergi ke kantor pos untuk mengirim paket ini.
examples.translation: I have to go to the post office to send this package.

faults.quote: /kaˈra.na/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: the second syllable has schwa /ə/, /ka.rə.na/ (often pronounced /kar.na/).

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: Single-word conjunction/preposition, not a multi-word expression.
Missing common prepositional use 'because of' before a noun (e.g. karena hujan).

faults.quote: Saya tinggal di rumah karena hari hujan.
faults.why: 'Tinggal di rumah' means 'live in a house'; 'stayed home' is 'tetap di rumah'.

notes: Often pronounced as two syllables, 'karna', in everyday speech.
Do not confuse with oleh karena itu, which means 'therefore'.

senses.definition: Used before a clause to give the reason for something.

examples.text: Saya tetap di rumah karena sedang hujan.
examples.translation: I stayed at home because it was raining.

senses.definition: Used before a noun or pronoun to state who or what caused something.

examples.text: Dia terlambat karena macet.
examples.translation: He was late because of the traffic jam.

faults.quote: tomatoes are almost always treated as a vegetable in Korean cooking.
faults.why: False; in Korea, tomatoes are widely eaten as fruit/dessert, often with sugar.

notes: In Korea, tomatoes are commonly treated as a fruit and eaten fresh as a snack or dessert.

senses.definition: A soft red fruit eaten raw in salads or as a snack, and used in sauces and cooking.

examples.text: 아침에 신선한 토마토를 먹었어요.
examples.translation: I ate a fresh tomato in the morning.

faults.quote: 정문으로 들어오세요.
faults.why: Uses the compound word 정문 (main gate) instead of the headword 문.

faults.quote: 문 can also refer to a gateway or a doorway itself
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding useful usage information.

notes: Commonly used with the verbs 열다 (to open), 닫다 (to close), and 잠그다 (to lock).

senses.definition: A movable barrier used to open and close the entrance to a room, building, or vehicle.

examples.text: 문을 열어 주세요.
examples.translation: Please open the door.

senses.definition: A gate or outer entrance to a large building, palace, or city wall, or the opening of a doorway.

examples.text: 이 문으로 들어가면 고궁이 나와요.
examples.translation: If you go in through this gate, you will see the old palace.

faults.quote: Often associated with playfulness, intelligence, or sometimes someone who is very active.
faults.why: Vague encyclopedic filler that does not help with Korean language usage.

notes: Used as the general everyday term for both monkeys and apes.

senses.definition: A mammal with hands that can grasp things and usually a long tail, known for climbing trees.

examples.text: 원숭이가 나무를 잘 타요.
examples.translation: The monkey is good at climbing trees.

notes: The final consonant 'ㅊ' is pronounced as an unreleased 't' sound at the end of a word or before a consonant, but moves to the next syllable as a 'ch' sound before a vowel particle (e.g., 꽃이 sounds like 꼬치).

senses.definition: The coloured part of a plant that grows from a bud and is often fragrant.

examples.text: 정원에 아름다운 꽃이 많이 피었습니다.
examples.translation: Many beautiful flowers have bloomed in the garden.

faults.quote: The younger, unmarried brother of one's father.
faults.why: Too restrictive; technically any brother of one's father (especially unmarried), and broadly any uncle.

notes: Traditionally refers to one's father's unmarried brother (while a married elder brother is 큰아버지 and a married younger brother is 작은아버지, and a mother's brother is 외삼촌), but in everyday speech it is widely used for any uncle or close male family friend.

senses.definition: A brother of one's parent, especially one's father's unmarried brother.

examples.text: 우리 삼촌은 아직 결혼하지 않았어요.
examples.translation: My uncle is not married yet.

senses.definition: A friendly term of address or reference for a younger or unmarried adult male who is a family friend or acquaintance.

examples.text: 옆집 사는 삼촌이 선물을 주셨어요.
examples.translation: The man next door gave me a gift.

faults.quote: A thick cover that keeps you warm in bed.
faults.why: Contradicts the note: 담요 is a thin throw or blanket, unlike thick 이불.

notes: Refers to a thinner wool or fleece blanket or throw, whereas 이불 is a thicker quilt or comforter used as main bedding.

senses.definition: A warm cloth cover, usually made of wool or fleece, used on a bed or around the shoulders.

examples.text: 날씨가 추워서 담요를 덮었어요.
examples.translation: It was cold, so I covered myself with a blanket.

faults.quote: 동물 is a general word for any living creature that is not
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.
Should mention the counter 마리 used for counting animals.

notes: Counted using the counter 마리 (e.g., 동물 세 마리, 'three animals').
Often appears in compounds such as 동물원 (zoo) and 반려동물 / 애완동물 (pet).

senses.definition: A living creature that can move around and is not a plant.

examples.text: 나는 모든 동물을 좋아해요.
examples.translation: I like all animals.

faults.quote: This word is a homonym. Depending on context, it refers either to
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: In the 'apology' sense, it combines with 하다 to form the verb 사과하다 (to apologize).

senses.definition: The round, crisp, red or green fruit of an apple tree.

examples.text: 아침에 사과를 한 개 먹었어요.
examples.translation: I ate an apple in the morning.

senses.definition: An expression of regret for a mistake or offense.

examples.text: 진심으로 사과를 받아 주세요.
examples.translation: Please accept my sincere apology.

notes: Unlike the general word 벌 (which includes wasps and hornets), 꿀벌 refers specifically to the honeybee.

senses.definition: A winged insect that collects nectar from flowers and makes honey.

examples.text: 꿀벌이 꽃에서 꿀을 모으고 있어요.
examples.translation: The honeybee is collecting nectar from the flower.

faults.quote: This is a common way to refer to someone you have never
faults.why: Restates the definition and makes an odd comparison with 'foreigner'.

notes: Literally 'a person one does not know' (from 모르다, 'not to know', and 사람, 'person').
Compare with 남, a broader word meaning 'others' or people outside one's family or close circle.

senses.definition: A person you do not know or have never met before.

examples.text: 모르는 사람을 따라가면 안 돼요.
examples.translation: You should not follow a stranger.

faults.quote: /nɯt̚.ɡe/
faults.why: After an unreleased stop [t̚], ㄱ is tensified to [k͈]: /nɯt̚.k͈e/.

notes: Formed from the adjective 늦다 (to be late) + -게. The opposite is 일찍 (early).

senses.definition: After the expected, usual, or arranged time, or far into the day or night.

examples.text: 오늘 버스가 늦게 왔습니다.
examples.translation: The bus came late today.

faults.quote: adding the adverbial suffix -이 to the noun root 없-
faults.why: 없- is an adjective stem, not a noun root.

faults.quote: commonly paired with particles like -없이
faults.why: Nonsensical statement claiming 없이 is paired with a particle '-없이'.
Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning ('without'); example 1 even translates as 'without'.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 없이 is an adverb, not an expression.

notes: Formed from the adjective 없다 (to not exist, to not have) + adverbial suffix -이.
Placed directly after a noun (often dropping object/subject particles) to mean 'without [noun]'.

senses.definition: In the absence of someone or something; not having or doing something.

examples.text: 고민 없이 결정을 내렸다.
examples.translation: I made a decision without hesitation.

examples.text: 너 없이 어떻게 살겠니?
examples.translation: How could I live without you?

faults.quote: For a softer or slightly more casual tone, Koreans often use... 죄송합니다
faults.why: Confusing wording implies 죄송합니다 has a casual tone, when it is actually more deferential/formal.

notes: Polite formal form of 미안하다 (to be sorry). In everyday polite speech, 미안해요 is common; towards superiors, strangers, or for more serious apologies, 죄송합니다 is preferred.

senses.definition: Said to apologize when one has done something wrong or caused trouble.

examples.text: 늦어서 미안합니다.
examples.translation: I am sorry for being late.

senses.definition: Said to politely get someone's attention or excuse oneself when asking a question or interrupting.

examples.text: 미안합니다만, 길 좀 묻겠습니다.
examples.translation: Excuse me, but I would like to ask for directions.

faults.quote: When following a verb stem (e.g., '먹어 주세요')
faults.why: It follows the -아/어 conjugated form of a verb, not the bare verb stem.

notes: Polite request form of 주다 (to give).
Used after a noun (물 주세요, 'water, please') or after a verb in the -아/어 form (먹어 주세요, 'please eat it').

senses.definition: Used after a noun to politely ask for that item, or after a verb (-아/어 주세요) to ask someone to do that action.

examples.text: 물 주세요.
examples.translation: Please give me water.

examples.text: 도와주세요.
examples.translation: Please help me.

faults.why: Missing the everyday classifier ตู้ (tûu) or เครื่อง (khrʉ̂ang) needed by A2 learners.

notes: Compound of ตู้ ('cabinet') and เย็น ('cold'). Counted with the classifier ตู้ (tûu) or เครื่อง (khrʉ̂ang).

senses.definition: An electrical appliance used for keeping food and drinks cold and fresh.

examples.text: ฉันเก็บนมไว้ในตู้เย็น
examples.translation: I keep milk in the refrigerator.

faults.quote: /ʔɛːp.pɤ̄n/
faults.why: Wrong tones and vowel length; standard pronunciation is /ʔɛ́p.pɤ̂n/ or /ʔɛ̂p.pɤ̂n/.

faults.quote: Used as a loanword from English, referring both to the fresh fruit
faults.why: Filler note; should instead mention common alternate spelling แอปเปิ้ล and classifier ลูก/ผล.

notes: Often spelled แอปเปิ้ล with a tone mark to reflect how it is pronounced; the final -l is pronounced as an -n sound in Thai.
Counted with the classifier ลูก (lûuk) or, more formally, ผล (phǒn).

senses.definition: A round fruit with firm white flesh and red, green, or yellow skin.

examples.text: ฉันชอบกินแอปเปิลสีแดงมากกว่าสีเขียว
examples.translation: I like eating red apples more than green ones.

faults.why: Does not explain the irregular reading of รร as -an- plus linking r-.

notes: The letters รร here are pronounced as -an- followed by a linking r- (phan-ra-yaa), or less commonly without the r- (phan-yaa).
ภรรยา is the polite, standard word for 'wife'. In casual speech among friends and family, เมีย (mia) is very common, though it can sound coarse in polite company.

senses.definition: The woman a person is married to.

examples.text: เขาไปเที่ยวกับภรรยา
examples.translation: He went traveling with his wife.

faults.quote: Do not confuse สามี with ภรรยา (phan ra yaa), which means 'wife'.
faults.why: Trivial antonym filler; misses the actual informal counterpart ผัว (phǔa).

notes: สามี is the polite, standard term for 'husband'. In casual speech, people often refer to their spouse simply as แฟน (faen, 'partner'); the informal word ผัว (phǔa) is common among close friends but sounds coarse in polite company.

senses.definition: The man a person is married to.

examples.text: เธอไปทานข้าวเย็นกับสามี
examples.translation: She went to have dinner with her husband.

faults.quote: it most specifically denotes a picture created using paint
faults.why: วาด means both 'to draw' and 'to paint'; ภาพวาด covers drawings and paintings equally.

notes: Compound of ภาพ ('picture, image') and วาด ('to draw, to paint'), covering both drawings and paintings. In everyday speech, รูปวาด (rûup-wâat) is an equally common synonym.
Counted with the classifier ภาพ (phâap), รูป (rûup), or แผ่น (phàen).

senses.definition: A picture drawn or painted by hand.

examples.text: เธอแขวนภาพวาดสวยๆ ไว้บนผนังห้องนอน
examples.translation: She hung a beautiful painting on the bedroom wall.

faults.quote: Involving risk or uncertainty of failure.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning; 'risqué' means risky for decisions, not 'dangereux'.

notes: The feminine form is 'dangereuse' (/dɑ̃.ʒʁøz/).

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or damage.

examples.text: Ce pont est dangereux pour les piétons.
examples.translation: This bridge is dangerous for pedestrians.

faults.quote: Unlike English, which often uses the progressive 'to be dancing'
faults.why: Generic grammar rule about the French present tense, not specific to 'danser'.

notes: Takes 'sur' for the music you dance to ('danser sur une chanson') and 'avec' for a partner.

senses.definition: To move your body in time with music.

examples.text: Elle aime danser sur sa chanson préférée.
examples.translation: She likes to dance to her favorite song.

faults.why: Missing the very common A1/A2 sense 'ever / before' in past-tense questions and statements.

faults.quote: Used to express that something has happened sooner than expected
faults.why: Simply restates the definition of sense 0.

notes: In the passé composé, 'déjà' normally goes between the auxiliary verb and the past participle ('J'ai déjà mangé').
In questions in the passé composé ('Tu es déjà allé à Paris ?'), it translates to English 'ever' ('Have you ever been to Paris?').

senses.definition: Before now, or sooner than expected.

examples.text: Tu es déjà là ?
examples.translation: Are you already here?

examples.text: J'ai déjà fini mon travail.
examples.translation: I have already finished my work.

senses.definition: At any time in the past, especially in questions about past experiences.

examples.text: Tu as déjà visité Paris ?
examples.translation: Have you ever visited Paris?

faults.quote: While primarily used for food that tastes exceptionally good, 'délicieux' can also
faults.why: Restates the two senses instead of giving grammatical or form help.

notes: The feminine form is 'délicieuse' (/de.li.sjøz/).

senses.definition: Having a very pleasant taste or smell.

examples.text: Ce gâteau au chocolat est absolument délicieux.
examples.translation: This chocolate cake is absolutely delicious.

senses.definition: Giving great pleasure or delight.

examples.text: Nous avons passé une journée délicieuse à la campagne.
examples.translation: We spent a delightful day in the countryside.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'demain' with 'matin' (morning).
faults.why: English learners do not confuse 'demain' and 'matin'; misses key usage without prepositions.

notes: Combine directly with parts of the day without a preposition: 'demain matin' (tomorrow morning), 'demain soir' (tomorrow evening).
'À demain !' means 'See you tomorrow!'

senses.definition: On the day after today.

examples.text: Je pars en vacances demain.
examples.translation: I am leaving on vacation tomorrow.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with '공원' (worker)
faults.why: The homophone meaning 'factory worker' is outdated and rare; useless for A2 learners.

notes: Combine with '에 가다' (to go to) or '에서 산책하다' (to take a walk in): '공원에 가다', '공원에서 산책하다'.

senses.definition: A public area of land with grass and trees where people go to walk, exercise, or relax.

examples.text: 주말에 공원에서 산책했어요.
examples.translation: I took a walk in the park on the weekend.

faults.quote: 선물 is the standard word for any gift or present
faults.why: Merely restates the gloss without adding usage information.

notes: Common collocations: '선물을 주다' (to give a gift), '선물을 받다' (to receive a gift), and the verb '선물하다' (to give as a gift).

senses.definition: Something that you give to someone as a sign of affection or for a special occasion.

examples.text: 친구에게 줄 생일 선물을 샀어요.
examples.translation: I bought a birthday gift for my friend.

notes: While '가족' refers to the family unit, '식구' is often used in conversation for family members who live together and share meals.

senses.definition: A group consisting of parents, children, and other relatives.

examples.text: 주말에는 가족과 시간을 보냅니다.
examples.translation: I spend time with my family on the weekends.

faults.why: Must contrast '밥' (cooked rice) with '쌀' (uncooked rice) and mention honorific '진지'.

faults.quote: 오늘 점심은 밥을 먹었어요.
faults.why: Ambiguous in Korean; natively understood as 'had lunch/a meal' rather than specifically 'cooked rice'.

notes: Refers to cooked rice; uncooked rice is '쌀'. When speaking to elders, use the honorific word '진지' instead of '밥'.
'밥 먹었어?' (Did you eat?) is a common everyday greeting in Korea, similar to asking how someone is doing.

senses.definition: Rice that has been boiled or steamed, eaten as a staple food.

examples.text: 빵보다 밥이 더 좋아요.
examples.translation: I like rice better than bread.

senses.definition: An occasion when food is eaten, or the food eaten at that time.

examples.text: 밥 먹었어?
examples.translation: Have you eaten?

faults.why: Should mention the silent ㄹ in pronunciation [닥꼬기] and contrast with '치킨' (fried chicken).

notes: The 'ㄹ' in '닭' is silent here, and the following 'ㄱ' is tensed: pronounced [닥꼬기].
'닭' refers to the live bird, '닭고기' to chicken meat as an ingredient, and '치킨' specifically to fried chicken.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.text: 닭고기를 구워서 먹어요.
examples.translation: I grill the chicken and eat it.

faults.quote: Use 'sera' for the evening hours, typically from sunset until bedtime.
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to explain the contrast with 'serata'.

notes: Italians use 'sera' until bedtime (e.g., 'stasera' = tonight); 'notte' refers mainly to the hours of sleep.
Contrast with 'la serata', which emphasizes the duration or how the evening is spent (e.g., 'una bella serata').

senses.definition: The part of the day between the end of the afternoon and going to bed.

examples.text: La sera leggo sempre un libro prima di dormire.
examples.translation: In the evening I always read a book before going to sleep.

faults.quote: The working days of the week, excluding the weekend.
faults.why: Contextual shade of 'week' (as in English), not a separate lexical sense.

faults.quote: preceded by the masculine article 'il' when talking about a specific day
faults.why: In Italian, 'il lunedì' means 'on Mondays' (habitual); a specific Monday takes no article.

notes: Common expressions: 'la settimana prossima' (next week), 'la settimana scorsa' (last week), 'il fine settimana' (the weekend).

senses.definition: A period of seven consecutive days, in Italy starting on Monday.

examples.text: Questa settimana ho molto lavoro da fare.
examples.translation: This week I have a lot of work to do.

faults.quote: Use 'sorella' when talking about a female sibling.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful grammar or usage information.
Should note that singular family members drop the definite article after possessive adjectives.

notes: Like other singular family nouns, 'sorella' drops the definite article with possessive adjectives: 'mia sorella' (my sister), not 'la mia sorella' (except in the plural: 'le mie sorelle').

senses.definition: A girl or woman who has the same parents as another person.

examples.text: Ho una sorella che vive a Roma.
examples.translation: I have a sister who lives in Rome.

faults.quote: Use spiaggia when talking about a sandy or pebbly shore
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition; a note on the plural 'le spiagge' is much more useful.

faults.quote: beach, seashore, sand
faults.why: 'Sand' is 'la sabbia', not 'la spiaggia'.

notes: The plural drops the 'i': 'le spiagge'.
Often used with the preposition 'in' without an article ('andare in spiaggia' = to go to the beach).

senses.definition: An area of sand or pebbles beside the sea or a lake.

examples.text: Domani andiamo in spiaggia a prendere il sole.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we are going to the beach to sunbathe.

faults.quote: room; chamber
faults.why: 'Chamber' is not in the sense glosses and is archaic/unnatural for A2.

notes: 'Stanza' is the general word for any room in a building. Use 'camera' specifically for a bedroom ('camera da letto') or a hotel room ('camera d'albergo').

senses.definition: A separate space inside a house or building, enclosed by walls, a floor, and a ceiling.

examples.text: La stanza è molto luminosa.
examples.translation: The room is very bright.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'शहर' (shahar), which is used for a
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; 'शहर' and 'गाँव' are basic opposites, not lookalikes or near-synonyms.

notes: Does not change form in the direct plural ('दो गाँव'). In the oblique plural, it becomes 'गाँवों'.
In India, people often use 'मेरा गाँव' to mean their ancestral home or native place, even if it is now a town.

senses.definition: A small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a town.

examples.text: मेरा गाँव बहुत छोटा और सुंदर है।
examples.translation: My village is very small and beautiful.

faults.quote: While 'जैकेट' is a loanword from English, it is the most common
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Usually feminine in standard Hindi ('मेरी जैकेट'), though some speakers treat it as masculine.
Unlike 'कोट' (coat), which refers to a suit jacket, blazer, or long overcoat, 'जैकेट' refers to casual waist-length outerwear or a sleeveless vest.

senses.definition: A short coat worn as an outer layer of clothing for warmth.

faults.quote: Used as a noun, 'डर' refers to the internal state of being
faults.why: Pure filler restating the part of speech and definition.
Missing the essential dative construction 'को ... से डर लगना' used to express feeling fear.

notes: To say you are afraid of something, use the construction '[person] को [thing] से डर लगना' (e.g., 'मुझे कुत्तों से डर लगता है' — I am afraid of dogs).
The related verb is 'डरना' (to be afraid).

senses.definition: The unpleasant feeling caused by the belief that someone or something is dangerous.

examples.text: अंधेरे का डर सबको होता है।
examples.translation: Everyone has a fear of the dark.

examples.text: उसका डर धीरे-धीरे कम हो गया।
examples.translation: His fear gradually faded away.

faults.quote: Use 'लड़का' for a male child or a boy. When speaking about
faults.why: Mostly restates the two senses; misses the standard inflection pattern of '-आ' masculine nouns.

notes: Changes to 'लड़के' in the direct plural and oblique singular, and 'लड़कों' in the oblique plural.
For 'son', 'बेटा' is more common and affectionate, while 'लड़का' is more matter-of-fact.

senses.definition: A male child or a young male person.

examples.text: वह लड़का मेरा दोस्त है।
examples.translation: That boy is my friend.

senses.definition: Someone's male child.

examples.text: उनका बड़ा लड़का विदेश में रहता है।
examples.translation: Their elder son lives abroad.

notes: Specifically means your father's younger brother (his wife is 'चाची'). Compare 'ताऊ' (father's older brother) and 'मामा' (mother's brother).
Does not change to '-ए' in the plural or oblique singular ('मेरे चाचा', not '*मेरे चाचे').

senses.definition: The younger brother of one's father.

examples.text: मेरे चाचा कल दिल्ली से आएँगे।
examples.translation: My uncle will come from Delhi tomorrow.

faults.quote: covered with sand or small pebbles.
faults.why: Contradicts the word (砂 means sand) and note[0]; 砂浜 is specifically sandy, not pebbled.

notes: Specifically refers to a beach covered in sand (砂). For the coast or shore in general, whether sandy or rocky, use 海岸 (かいがん).

senses.definition: A stretch of land along the edge of the sea or a lake covered with sand.

notes: Refers to modern, desk-oriented workplaces. For smaller, administrative, or more traditional offices, 事務所 (じむしょ) is also common.

senses.definition: A room or building where people work at desks.

examples.text: オフィスで働いています。

examples.translation: I like to drink coffee every morning.

faults.quote: Used to talk about the time between noon and evening.

examples.text: Он режет хлеб острым ножом.
examples.translation: He is cutting bread with a sharp knife.

faults.quote: /ˈpalʲɪtS/

Missing note on the fleeting vowel 'е' in declined forms (пальца, пальцы).

senses.definition: At all times; on every occasion without exception.

examples.text: वह हमेशा समय पर आता है।
examples.translation: He always comes on time.

faults.quote: It is a Persian loanword widely used in everyday Hindi conversation.
faults.why: Etymology filler; better to note the emphatic phrase शायद ही ('hardly/scarcely').

notes: Usually placed at the beginning of the sentence or just before the verb. Followed by ही (शायद ही), the meaning shifts to 'hardly' or 'almost certainly not'.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible, though not certain.

examples.text: शायद कल बारिश होगी।
examples.translation: Perhaps it will rain tomorrow.

faults.quote: Used to show that something happened a long time in the past.
faults.why: Both senses mean 'already'; 'long ago' is just a contextual shade of 'already finished'.

notes: It is often interchangeable with 이미, but 이미 simply states that something is already done, whereas 벌써 expresses surprise that it happened sooner than expected.

senses.definition: Before now, or sooner than expected.

examples.text: 벌써 겨울이 왔다.
examples.translation: Winter has already arrived.

examples.text: 그 일은 벌써 끝났다.
examples.translation: That matter is already finished.

faults.quote: than formal writing, where 어쩌면 is sometimes preferred.
faults.why: 어쩌면 differs in nuance ('perhaps/by some chance'), not formality; 아마(도) is fine in writing.

notes: Often paired with endings like -(으)ㄹ 거예요 ('will probably') or -(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 ('might') to express a guess.
Can be followed by the particle 도 (아마도) with little change in meaning.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is likely, though not certain.

examples.text: 아마 비가 올 거예요.
examples.translation: It will probably rain.

faults.quote: adv
faults.why: 여기 is a place pronoun (대명사), taking case particles like 에, 에서, 가, 를.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 여기 with 이 곳 ('this place').
faults.why: 이곳 (spelled as one word) and 여기 are near-synonyms; learners do not confuse them negatively.

notes: Refers to a place close to the speaker, contrast with 거기 (near the listener) and 저기 (far from both).
Although translated as 'here', it is a pronoun and takes particles such as 에, 에서, or 은/는 (often contracted to 여긴 in speech).

senses.definition: This place, near the speaker.

examples.text: 여기에 앉으세요.
examples.translation: Please sit here.

senses.definition: Used when handing something to someone or calling someone's attention (e.g., a waiter).

examples.text: 여기 거스름돈입니다.
examples.translation: Here is your change.

faults.quote: In casual speech, it is sometimes shortened to '어저께'.
faults.why: 어저께 is three syllables and longer than 어제 (two syllables); अ제 is shortened from 어저께.

faults.quote: The day before today.
faults.why: Defined as a noun while pos is adv and example[1] uses it as a noun.

notes: Used both as an adverb without a particle (어제 만났어요) and as a noun taking particles (어제는, 어제부터).
Remember that in Korean, the verb must still take the past tense ending (-았/었-) even when 어제 is in the sentence.

senses.definition: On the day before today; the day before today.

examples.text: 어제 친구를 만났어요.
examples.translation: I met a friend yesterday.

examples.text: 어제는 날씨가 정말 좋았어요.
examples.translation: The weather was really nice yesterday.

faults.quote: The day after today.
faults.why: Defined only as a noun while pos is adv.

notes: Used both as an adverb without a particle (내일 만나요) and as a noun taking particles (내일은, 내일까지).

senses.definition: On the day after today; the day after today.

examples.text: 내일 만나요.
examples.translation: Let's meet tomorrow.

faults.quote: with رِيَح (riyaḥ) being very common in everyday speech.
faults.why: رِيَح is not a word; the standard plural is رِيَاح (riyāḥ).

notes: The common plural is رِيَاح (riyāḥ); أَرْيَاح (ʾaryāḥ) also exists.
Do not confuse with رَائِحَة (rāʾiḥa), which means 'smell' or 'scent'.

senses.definition: Air moving naturally outside.

examples.text: الرِّيحُ قَوِيَّةٌ اليَوْمَ.
examples.translation: The wind is strong today.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who works the land, whether as a modern
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and glosses while omitting feminine and plural forms.

notes: Regular plural: فَلَّاحُونَ (fallāḥūna); feminine: فَلَّاحَة (fallāḥa).

senses.definition: A person who works the land and grows crops.

examples.text: يَعْمَلُ الفَلَّاحُ فِي الحَقْلِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: The farmer works in the field every morning.

faults.quote: /dʒaˈwaːzi ˈsafari/
faults.why: Wrong case vowel /i/ on the first word of the construct; cite in pausal form.

faults.quote: أرني جَوَاز سَفَر من فضلك.
faults.why: Uses indefinite 'a passport' where Arabic requires 'your passport' (جَوَازَ سَفَرِكَ) or 'the passport'.

notes: Plural: جَوَازَات سَفَر (jawāzāt safar). Often shortened to جَوَاز (jawāz) when the context is clear.

senses.definition: An official document that identifies you as a citizen of a country when travelling abroad.

examples.text: أَرِنِي جَوَازَ سَفَرِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: Show me your passport, please.

notes: The plural is أَخَوَات (ʾakhawāt).
The masculine counterpart is أَخ (ʾakh, 'brother').

senses.definition: A girl or woman who has the same parents as another person.

examples.text: هٰذِهِ أُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَةُ.
examples.translation: This is my little sister.

notes: Usually used as an uncountable noun for strawberries in general; for a single one, say حَبَّة فَرَاوِلَة (ḥabbat farāwila).

senses.definition: A small, soft red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: أُحِبُّ أَكْلَ الفَرَاوِلَةِ الطَّازَجَةِ فِي الصَّيْفِ.
examples.translation: I like eating fresh strawberries in the summer.

faults.quote: /ˈfɛrmʲɪr/
faults.why: The initial 'ф' before 'е' in 'фермер' is soft: /ˈfʲer.mʲɪr/.

faults.quote: Used to refer to someone who owns or manages a farm,
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Refers to a modern owner or manager of a private farm; contrast with 'крестьянин' (peasant, traditional country dweller).

senses.definition: A person who owns or runs a farm, grows crops, or keeps animals.

examples.text: Местный фермер продаёт свежие овощи на рынке.
examples.translation: The local farmer sells fresh vegetables at the market.

faults.quote: Used mainly for heavy weather at sea or large bodies of
faults.why: Restates the definition and duplicates the second note.

notes: Used mainly for storms at sea or on large lakes; contrast with 'буря' (any violent storm on land or sea) and 'гроза' (thunderstorm).

senses.definition: Very bad weather with strong winds and high waves, especially at sea.

examples.text: Корабль попал в сильный шторм.
examples.translation: The ship got caught in a severe storm.

faults.quote: Used when you catch a mild viral infection with a runny
faults.why: Restates the definition of the word.

notes: Contrast with 'грипп' (the flu), which is more severe and involves a high fever.

senses.definition: A common mild illness with a runny nose, sneezing, and a sore throat.

examples.text: У меня сильная простуда, поэтому я остаюсь дома.
examples.translation: I have a bad cold, so I am staying home.

faults.quote: or 'page' of a document.
faults.why: 'Лицо' does not mean 'page' of a document.

faults.quote: This is an official person.
faults.why: Calqued translation; 'официальное лицо' means 'an official' in English.

notes: In the plural ('лица', genitive 'лиц'), stress shifts to the first syllable: /ˈlʲi.tsə/.
Also used in grammar for grammatical person (e.g., 'первое лицо' — first person).

senses.definition: The front part of the human head containing the eyes, nose, and mouth.

examples.text: У него было доброе лицо.
examples.translation: He had a kind face.

senses.definition: An individual human being, especially in formal or legal contexts.

examples.text: Вход посторонним лицам запрещён.
examples.translation: Entry for unauthorized persons is prohibited.

faults.quote: На улице шла женщина с зонтом.
faults.why: With 'идти' (walking along), Russian requires 'По улице', not 'На улице'.

notes: Contrast with 'девушка' (young woman), which is also the polite way to address a female stranger or server; addressing someone as 'женщина' can sound blunt.

senses.definition: An adult female person.

examples.text: По улице шла женщина с зонтом.
examples.translation: A woman with an umbrella was walking down the street.

faults.quote: The physical feeling of wanting to eat.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('the feeling'); should be 'wanting or needing food'.

faults.quote: Used to describe the physical sensation of needing food.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage info.

notes: In Indonesian, 'lapar' is used directly after the subject without a verb like 'to be' (e.g., 'Saya lapar' = 'I am hungry'). The noun 'hunger' is 'kelaparan'.

senses.definition: Wanting or needing to eat food.

examples.text: Saya merasa sangat lapar setelah bekerja.
examples.translation: I feel very hungry after working.

faults.quote: sea, ocean
faults.why: 'Laut' is 'sea'; 'ocean' is 'samudra' or 'lautan'.

notes: Refers to the sea in general. For 'ocean', Indonesian uses 'samudra' or 'lautan'. Placed after another noun, it means 'sea-' or 'marine' (e.g., 'air laut' = seawater, 'ikan laut' = saltwater fish).

senses.definition: The large body of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface.

examples.text: Kami melihat lumba-lumba di tengah laut.
examples.translation: We saw dolphins in the middle of the sea.

faults.quote: /ˈlɛ.bah/
faults.why: The first vowel is schwa /ə/, not /ɛ/: /ləˈbah/.

notes: The 'e' is pronounced as a weak schwa /ə/, like the 'a' in 'about'. In everyday speech, people often call bees 'tawon', though strictly 'tawon' means 'wasp' or 'hornet'.

senses.definition: A flying insect with a yellow and black body that makes honey.

examples.text: Seekor lebah sedang mengisap nektar dari bunga di taman.
examples.translation: A bee is sipping nectar from a flower in the garden.

faults.quote: Use 'lebih awal' to describe doing something before the scheduled, expected, or
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Literally 'more early' ('lebih' + 'awal'). Often followed by 'dari' or 'daripada' to mean 'earlier than'.

senses.definition: Before the usual, expected, or scheduled time.

examples.text: Dia datang lebih awal agar mendapat tempat duduk yang bagus.
examples.translation: He arrived early so he could get a good seat.

examples.text: Kami menyelesaikan pekerjaan itu lebih awal dari perkiraan.
examples.translation: We finished the work earlier than expected.

faults.quote: /ˈlɛ.lah/
faults.why: The first vowel is schwa /ə/, not /ɛ/: /ləˈlah/.

faults.quote: Lelah means tired or fatigued and is used in both everyday conversation
faults.why: Restates the glosses and neutral register.

notes: In casual conversation, 'capek' (or 'cape') is much more common than 'lelah'.

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep because of physical or mental effort.

examples.text: Saya merasa lelah setelah bekerja seharian.
examples.translation: I feel tired after working all day.

senses.definition: Having lost patience or interest because something has gone on too long.

examples.text: Dia sudah lelah dengan janji-janji palsu itu.
examples.translation: She is already tired of those false promises.

notes: The vowel 'е' drops in declined forms (e.g. genitive singular 'кашля').

senses.definition: An act or condition of forcing air out of the throat with a sharp sound.

examples.text: У него сильный кашель.
examples.translation: He has a bad cough.

faults.quote: The word can mean both the prepared dish (salad) and the
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses without adding grammatical or usage info.

notes: Russian salads are often dressed with mayonnaise or sour cream (e.g., Olivier salad), not just raw leafy greens.

senses.definition: A cold dish of mixed vegetables or other chopped ingredients, usually with a dressing.

examples.text: На обед я ел свежий салат.
examples.translation: I ate a fresh salad for lunch.

senses.definition: A leafy green plant eaten raw as a vegetable.

examples.text: Добавь в этот бутерброд немного салата.
examples.translation: Add a little lettuce to this sandwich.

faults.quote: In Russian, the genitive plural form 'сыновей' is used after numbers
faults.why: Explains a general Russian grammar rule about numbers; only the irregular form 'сыновей' is word-specific.

notes: Has an irregular plural: nominative 'сыновья', genitive 'сыновей'.

senses.definition: A person's male child.

faults.quote: masculine
faults.why: Plural-only nouns (pluralia tantum) in Russian do not have grammatical gender.

faults.quote: The numerical score earned during a game or competition.
faults.why: In the 'points' sense, 'очки' is the regular plural of 'очко' (neuter), not this lemma.

notes: A plural-only noun in Russian (genitive 'очков'). Use plural adjectives, pronouns, and verb forms even for one pair.
Do not confuse with 'очки' meaning 'points' in a game, which is the plural of 'очко' (point).

senses.definition: A pair of lenses in a frame worn on the face to help you see or to protect the eyes.

examples.text: Я ничего не вижу без своих очков.
examples.translation: I cannot see anything without my glasses.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (そぼ) for a kanji headword.

notes: Use 祖母 (sobo) when talking about your own grandmother to people outside your family.
When addressing your own grandmother directly or referring to someone else's, use the polite おばあさん (obāsan).

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother (used when referring to one's own grandmother to others).

examples.text: 私の祖母は料理がとても上手です。
examples.translation: My grandmother is very good at cooking.

faults.quote: Note the difference between 'kami' (paper) and 'kami' (god/hair).
faults.why: Unhelpful filler unless pitch accent is explained (紙 is かみ [2], vs 髪 [2] / 神 [1]).

notes: Counted in sheets with 枚 (mai), e.g., 紙を一枚ください (Please give me one sheet of paper).
Pronounced with a rising pitch on み (ka-MI), distinguishing it from 神 (KA-mi, god), though identical in Tokyo pitch to 髪 (ka-MI, hair).

senses.definition: The thin, flat material used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

examples.text: 紙に名前を書いてください。
examples.translation: Please write your name on the paper.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (ばんごはん) for a kanji headword.

notes: 晩ご飯 is the most common everyday word for dinner; 夕食 (yūshoku) is slightly more formal, while 晩飯 (banmeshi) is rough and casual.

senses.definition: The main meal eaten in the evening.

examples.text: 今、晩ご飯を食べています。
examples.translation: I am eating dinner right now.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (にわとり) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: The kanji 鶏 is also used in compounds related to poultry.
faults.why: Vague filler that gives no actionable information to an A2 learner.

notes: 鶏 (niwatori) refers to the live bird; for chicken meat as food, use 鶏肉 (toriniku) or simply とり (tori).

senses.definition: A common farm bird kept for its eggs and meat.

examples.text: 庭で鶏を飼っています。
examples.translation: I keep chickens in the yard.

faults.quote: (child) A young person... / (baby) A very young child...
faults.why: Arabic طِفْل covers both child and baby as one sense; الرَّضِيعُ specifies 'baby' in example[1].

notes: The plural is أَطْفَال (ʾaṭfāl); the feminine is طِفْلَة (ṭifla).

senses.definition: A young human being, from birth to puberty; a child or baby.

examples.text: يَلْعَبُ الطِّفْلُ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ.
examples.translation: The child is playing in the park.

faults.quote: /ˈʃa.ɡa.ra/
faults.why: Uses Egyptian dialect /ɡ/ instead of Modern Standard Arabic /d͡ʒ/ for ج.

notes: Countable unit noun (nomen unitatis) from the collective شَجَر (šajar, 'trees'); the broken plural is أَشْجَار (ʾašjār).

senses.definition: A tall plant with a wooden trunk and branches.

examples.text: جَلَسْنَا تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ.
examples.translation: We sat under the tree.

faults.quote: Note the plural is سِنِين (sinīn)
faults.why: Gives the oblique case form سِنِين instead of the nominative citation form سِنُون (sinūn).

notes: Has two plurals: سَنَوَات (sanawāt, more common in MSA) and سِنُون (sinūn, oblique سِنِين sinīn). Synonym: عَام (ʿām, masculine).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months.

examples.text: سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مِصْرَ السَّنَةَ المَاضِيَةَ.
examples.translation: I traveled to Egypt last year.

faults.quote: Used to mean a female child or daughter. It often connects
faults.why: Restates the gloss, states regular ة grammar, and omits the plural and initial hamzat waṣl.

notes: Starts with hamzat waṣl (silent in connected speech). The plural is بَنَات (banāt), shared with بِنْت (bint, 'girl; daughter').

senses.definition: A person's female child.

examples.text: هٰذِهِ ابْنَتِي الصُّغْرَى.
examples.translation: This is my youngest daughter.

faults.quote: This word is the plural form of 'مُثَلَّج' (frozen), but as
faults.why: Restates the gloss and misses the grammatical note that this plural noun takes feminine singular agreement.

notes: Always plural in form (literally 'frozen things'). As a non-human plural, it takes feminine singular agreement.

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk or cream.

examples.text: أُحِبُّ أَكْلَ المُثَلَّجَاتِ فِي الصَّيْفِ.
examples.translation: I like eating ice cream in the summer.

faults.quote: While '卧室' is the standard term for a bedroom
faults.why: Wordy regional note; omits the essential measure word 间 (jiān).

notes: Takes the measure word 间 (jiān): 一间卧室 (a bedroom).

senses.definition: A room in a home used for sleeping.

examples.text: 我的卧室很大。
examples.translation: My bedroom is very big.

faults.quote: As a noun, 雨 is used for the weather phenomenon itself.
faults.why: Restates the part of speech and definition without adding useful grammar.

notes: To say 'to rain', combine it with the verb 下 (xià): 下雨 (xià yǔ).
Takes the measure words 场 (chǎng) for a spell of rain and 阵 (zhèn) for a brief shower.

senses.definition: Water falling in drops from clouds in the sky.

examples.text: 今天有雨，记得带伞。
examples.translation: There is rain in the forecast today; remember to bring an umbrella.

faults.why: Omits the common measure word 张 (zhāng) and verb collocation 拍 (pāi).

notes: Takes the measure word 张 (zhāng). To take a photo is 拍照片 (pāi zhàopiàn) or 照相 (zhào xiàng).

senses.definition: A picture taken with a camera.

examples.text: 我在旅行时拍了很多照片。
examples.translation: I took many photos while traveling.

faults.quote: Used in both formal writing and daily speech to refer to clouds.
faults.why: Filler note; misses the everyday spoken form 云彩 (yúncai) and measure word 朵 (duǒ).

notes: Often takes the measure word 朵 (duǒ) or 片 (piàn). In casual speech, 'cloud' is often called 云彩 (yúncai).

senses.definition: A white or grey mass floating in the sky.

examples.text: 天上有白云。
examples.translation: There are white clouds in the sky.

faults.quote: 他受伤了胳膊。
faults.why: Ungrammatical: 受伤 is an intransitive verb and cannot take a direct object like 胳膊.

faults.quote: While '胳膊' refers to the entire limb from shoulder to hand
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses that 胳膊 is colloquial compared to 手臂 (shǒubì).

notes: The second syllable is pronounced with a neutral tone (gēbo). It is the everyday spoken word for 'arm'; 手臂 (shǒubì) is slightly more formal. Takes the measure word 只 (zhī) or 条 (tiáo).

senses.definition: The part of the body between the shoulder and the hand.

examples.text: 他的胳膊受伤了。
examples.translation: His arm was injured.

notes: The classifier for pillows and cushions is ใบ (bai), e.g., หมอนหนึ่งใบ (one pillow).

senses.definition: A soft bag filled with feathers, foam, or fiber, used to support the head in bed or for sitting on.

examples.text: ฉันชอบนอนหมอนนิ่มๆ
examples.translation: I like sleeping on a soft pillow.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages that distinguish between the animal and the meat
faults.why: English also uses 'fish' for both animal and food; add the classifier ตัว instead.

notes: The classifier for live or whole fish is ตัว (tua), e.g., ปลาสองตัว (two fish).

senses.definition: A cold-blooded animal with fins and gills that lives in water, or its flesh eaten as food.

examples.text: แม่ชอบกินปลาทอด
examples.translation: Mom likes to eat fried fish.

notes: Also used as a classifier for boxes and boxed items, e.g., นมหนึ่งกล่อง (one carton of milk); empty boxes can also be counted with ใบ (bai).

senses.definition: A rigid container with flat sides, typically square or rectangular, made of cardboard, wood, or plastic.

examples.text: ฉันเก็บของใส่กล่อง
examples.translation: I put the things in a box.

faults.quote: (furniture) A small seat, usually without a back or arms
faults.why: Standalone ม้า for bench/stool is archaic or dialectal; standard Thai uses ม้านั่ง.

faults.quote: it is also common to call a small, backless bench or footstool a 'mâ'
faults.why: Wrong tone diacritic ('mâ' instead of 'máa') and misleading claim about standalone usage.

notes: The classifier for horses is ตัว (tua).
Appears in common compounds such as ม้านั่ง (máa-nâng, 'bench/stool') and ทางม้าลาย (thaang-máa-laai, 'zebra crossing').

senses.definition: A large animal with four legs and a mane, used for riding and pulling loads.

examples.text: เขาชอบขี่ม้า
examples.translation: He likes to ride horses.

notes: Used for deep dishes holding soup or noodles, whereas จาน (jaan) is a flat plate. The classifier is ใบ (bai), or ชาม itself for servings of food.

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for holding food, especially soup or noodles.

examples.text: แม่ตักซุปใส่ชามให้ฉัน
examples.translation: Mother ladled soup into the bowl for me.

faults.quote: Used for the glass opening in a wall that lets in
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'la balconata' (balcony) or 'la porta' (door).
faults.why: Unlikely confusion with completely different words; better to contrast with 'finestrino' or 'vetrina'.

notes: For the window of a car, train, or plane, use 'il finestrino'; for a shop window, use 'la vetrina'.

senses.definition: An opening in the wall of a building that lets in light and air, usually fitted with glass; also a window on a computer screen.

examples.text: Apro la finestra per fare entrare un po' d'aria fresca.
examples.translation: I open the window to let in a little fresh air.

faults.quote: Plural is le foglie.
faults.why: The plural is completely regular (-a to -e) and needs no note.

notes: Do not confuse with 'il foglio' (sheet of paper). Notice that 'gl' before 'i' is pronounced /ʎ/ (like 'lli' in 'million').

senses.definition: A flat, usually green part of a plant or tree that grows from a stem or branch.

examples.text: La foglia è caduta dall'albero.
examples.translation: The leaf fell from the tree.

faults.quote: Used with the preposition 'con' (con la forchetta) when talking about
faults.why: Standard instrumental 'con' ('with') applies to any tool and is not specific to 'forchetta'.

notes: Spelled with 'ch' to keep the hard /k/ sound before 'e' (plural: 'le forchette').

senses.definition: A small tool with three or four points used for picking up and eating food.

examples.text: Ho bisogno di una forchetta per mangiare la pasta.
examples.translation: I need a fork to eat the pasta.

faults.quote: Gli alberi alti coprono la foresta.
faults.why: Tautological: a forest is made of trees, so trees do not 'cover' a forest.

notes: Refers to a large, dense, wild expanse of trees (e.g., 'la foresta tropicale'). For smaller local woods, 'il bosco' is much more common.

senses.definition: A very large, dense area of land covered with trees and wild plants.

examples.text: Molti animali selvatici vivono nella foresta.
examples.translation: Many wild animals live in the forest.

faults.quote: While it can mean 'wealth' or 'a fortune' in some contexts,
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already shown in the entry.

faults.quote: I had the luck to find a seat on the train.
faults.why: Calqued translation; natural English is 'I was lucky enough to find...'.

notes: Common expressions: 'buona fortuna!' (good luck!) and 'per fortuna' (fortunately / luckily).

senses.definition: Good things that happen by chance, or the force that causes things to happen by chance.

examples.text: Ho avuto la fortuna di trovare un posto a sedere sul treno.
examples.translation: I was lucky enough to find a seat on the train.

senses.definition: A very large amount of money.

examples.text: Quell'orologio è costato una fortuna.
examples.translation: That watch cost a fortune.

faults.quote: /ˈðon.ti/
faults.why: In standard Modern Greek, ντ is voiced to /nd/ (or /d/), not /nt/.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with το στόμα, which means the mouth itself.
faults.why: δόντι and στόμα do not look or sound alike; nobody confuses them.

notes: Commonly used in the phrase πλένω τα δόντια μου (to brush one's teeth, literally 'wash my teeth').

senses.definition: One of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.

examples.text: Με πονάει το δόντι μου.
examples.translation: My tooth hurts.

faults.quote: /ˈdatus/
faults.why: Completely wrong transcription; ντους is pronounced /dus/.
Missing essential grammar note that ντους is an indeclinable loanword and collocation κάνω ντους.

notes: Indeclinable loanword (from French douche): it keeps the same form ντους in all cases, singular and plural.
'To take a shower' is expressed with the verb κάνω: κάνω ντους.

senses.definition: An act of washing the body under sprayed water.

examples.text: Κάνω ένα γρήγορο ντους πριν φύγω.
examples.translation: I am taking a quick shower before I leave.

senses.definition: The fixture or stall in a bathroom that sprays water for washing.

examples.text: Το μπάνιο έχει ωραίο ντους.
examples.translation: The bathroom has a nice shower.

faults.quote: as well as diagrams or plans of a city or building
faults.why: A building plan is σχέδιο or κάτοψη, not χάρτης; also misses false friend χαρτί (paper).

notes: Do not confuse with το χαρτί (paper) or η κάρτα (card).

senses.definition: A drawing or plan of an area that shows countries, cities, roads, or natural features.

examples.text: Κοιτάζω τον χάρτη για να βρω τον δρόμο.
examples.translation: I am looking at the map to find the way.

faults.quote: Used for the thick cover on a bed, but also for a
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning of 'blanket' without adding useful linguistic information.

senses.definition: A thick warm cover used on a bed or for wrapping around oneself.

examples.text: Έβαλα άλλη μια κουβέρτα στο κρεβάτι γιατί κάνει κρύο.
examples.translation: I put another blanket on the bed because it is cold.

faults.quote: /kataˈʝiða/
faults.why: The second vowel is spelled αι and pronounced /e/, so /kateˈʝiða/, not /kataˈʝiða/.

faults.quote: Used for a sudden, violent storm involving wind, rain, and often thunder
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definition and contrast unrelated words (καιρός, βροχή).

senses.definition: A severe storm with strong wind, heavy rain, and usually thunder and lightning.

examples.text: Μια δυνατή καταιγίδα χτύπησε ξαφνικά το νησί.
examples.translation: A strong thunderstorm suddenly hit the island.

faults.quote: /sənˈdɔk/
faults.why: The first vowel is /ɛ/ or /e/, not schwa /ə/, with penultimate stress: /ˈsɛndɔk/.

notes: Commonly used with a fork ('garpu') for everyday meals, or in cooking measures like 'sendok makan' (tablespoon) and 'sendok teh' (teaspoon).

senses.definition: A utensil with a small shallow bowl at the end of a handle, used for eating, stirring, or serving food.

examples.text: Tolong ambilkan sendok untuk makan sup ini.
examples.translation: Please get a spoon to eat this soup.

senses.definition: The amount that a spoon can hold, used as a measure in cooking.

examples.text: Tambahkan satu sendok gula ke dalam teh.
examples.translation: Add one spoonful of sugar to the tea.

faults.quote: Do not confuse sepatu with kaos kaki, which means socks.
faults.why: 'Sepatu' and 'kaos kaki' look and sound nothing alike; this is pure filler.

notes: Counted in pairs using the classifier 'pasang': 'sepasang sepatu' (a pair of shoes).

senses.definition: An outer covering for the foot with a sturdy sole, not reaching above the ankle.

examples.text: Dia memakai sepatu baru ke kantor.
examples.translation: He is wearing new shoes to the office.

faults.quote: In casual conversation, people often just say 'sepeda' even when referring to
faults.why: Calling a mountain bike or road bike a 'bike' is obvious in any language.

notes: Used with the verb 'naik' or 'bersepeda' for riding a bike. Do not confuse with 'sepeda motor' (or simply 'motor'), which means 'motorcycle'.

senses.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle that you ride by pushing pedals with your feet.

examples.text: Saya pergi ke kantor naik sepeda.
examples.translation: I go to the office by bicycle.

faults.quote: Use 'sering' to describe actions that happen with high frequency.
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'sering' with 'banyak'. 'Banyak' means 'many'
faults.why: Artificial confusion; English speakers do not confuse 'often' and 'many'.

faults.quote: Happening many times at short intervals.
faults.why: Defined as an adjective ('Happening...') rather than an adverb ('Many times...').

notes: Placed directly before the verb it modifies. Its opposite is 'jarang' (rarely, seldom).

senses.definition: Many times; on many occasions.

examples.text: Dia sering pergi ke pasar pada pagi hari.
examples.translation: He often goes to the market in the morning.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (ちゃわん) for a word containing kanji.

notes: While the word literally includes 'tea' (茶), in everyday Japanese it most commonly refers to a rice bowl (often called ご飯茶碗, gohanjawan).
For an everyday teacup, 湯呑み (yunomi) is more commonly used.

senses.definition: A small, round bowl used for serving and eating rice.

examples.text: 茶わんにご飯を盛る。
examples.translation: I serve rice into the rice bowl.

senses.definition: A cup or bowl without a handle used for drinking tea, especially in a tea ceremony.

faults.quote: 森 (mori) refers to a large, dense forest.
faults.why: Note [0] merely restates the definition; notes should be consolidated into a single contrast note.

notes: Refers to a dense, natural forest, whereas 林 (hayashi) refers to a smaller, thinner wood or a planted grove.

senses.definition: A large area of land thickly covered with trees.

examples.text: 森の中を歩く。
examples.translation: I walk through the forest.

faults.quote: Unlike English where we distinguish between fruit and vegetables, in Japanese
faults.why: Japanese clearly distinguishes between vegetables (野菜) and fruit (果物).

senses.definition: A plant or part of a plant used as food in savory dishes.

examples.text: 毎日、新鮮な野菜を食べています。
examples.translation: I eat fresh vegetables every day.

faults.quote: While 'heya' (room) can refer to any room, 'shinshitsu' is specific
faults.why: Explaining that 'bedroom' is more specific than 'room' is unhelpful filler.

notes: A somewhat formal word often used in floor plans or for hotel rooms; in casual speech, people often just say 寝る部屋 (sleeping room) or 自分の部屋 (my room).

senses.definition: A room in a house or hotel used for sleeping.

examples.text: 寝室は二階にあります。
examples.translation: The bedroom is on the second floor.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (ごご) for a kanji word.

faults.quote: you say the time then the word, e.g., '午後三時' for 3:00 PM.
faults.why: Says the time comes before the word, which is false and contradicts its own example.

notes: When telling time, 午後 is placed before the hour (e.g., 午後三時 for 3:00 p.m.), unlike English 'p.m.'
Contrasts with 午前 (gozen, morning / a.m.).

senses.definition: The period of time from 12:00 noon until evening, or after noon when telling time.

examples.text: 午後から雨が降ります。
examples.translation: It will rain in the afternoon.

examples.text: 会議は午後二時からです。
examples.translation: The meeting starts at 2:00 p.m.

faults.quote: Used as a singular noun, but because it is a collective staple
faults.why: Wordy filler instead of explaining invariant plural declension (आलू/आलुओं).

faults.quote: A very versatile vegetable in Indian cuisine, often paired with almost anything
faults.why: Culinary trivia, not useful grammatical or lexical information.

notes: As a masculine noun ending in -ऊ (-ū), its direct plural is identical to the singular (आलू), while the oblique plural is आलुओं (āluõ).

senses.definition: A round, starchy vegetable that grows underground.

examples.text: मैंने आज आलू की सब्ज़ी बनाई है।
examples.translation: I made a potato dish today.

faults.quote: In Hindi, दीवार (dīvār) is the general term for a wall
faults.why: Merely restates the gloss without adding usage or grammar help.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with कमरा (kamrā), which means 'room'.
faults.why: Artificial warning; दीवार and कमरा neither look nor sound alike.

notes: Its plural form is दीवारें (dīvārẽ) in the direct case and दीवारों (dīvārõ) before postpositions.

senses.definition: A vertical structure of brick, stone, or wood that encloses or divides a space.

examples.text: दीवार पर एक तस्वीर है।
examples.translation: There is a picture on the wall.

faults.quote: /vɪʃvəˈviːd̪əlaj/
faults.why: Wrong transcription of विद्यालय; misses /d̪j/ cluster and puts wrong vowel lengths.

notes: A compound of विश्व (world) and विद्यालय (school). In everyday speech, the English word यूनिवर्सिटी (yūnivarsiṭī) is much more common, while वि.वि. is used as a written abbreviation.

senses.definition: An institution of higher education that grants academic degrees.

examples.text: वह विश्वविद्यालय में पढ़ता है।
examples.translation: He studies at the university.

faults.why: Splits 'child' and 'baby' while leaving 'young of an animal' only in the notes.

notes: Inflects regularly: बच्चे (bacce) in the oblique singular and direct plural, and बच्चों (baccõ) in the oblique plural. The feminine counterpart is बच्ची (baccī, 'little girl').

senses.definition: A young human being, from an infant to a school-age child.

examples.text: वह बच्चा स्कूल जा रहा है।
examples.translation: That child is going to school.

examples.text: छोटा बच्चा अभी सो रहा है।
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping right now.

senses.definition: The young offspring of an animal, usually following the animal's name with का (kā).

examples.text: बिल्ली का बच्चा दूध पी रहा है।
examples.translation: The kitten is drinking milk.

faults.quote: 'भोजन-सूची' (bhojan-soochni)
faults.why: False romanization: सूची is transcribed 'sūcī' (or 'soochee'), not 'soochni' (which would be सूचनी).

notes: Borrowed from English and also spelled मेनू (menū). It does not change form in the plural.

senses.definition: A list of food and drink options available at a restaurant.

examples.text: वेटर, कृपया मेन्यू दीजिए।
examples.translation: Waiter, please give me the menu.

faults.quote: Use фрукт for sweet plant parts containing seeds. Do not confuse
faults.why: Explains English 'fruit' vs 'vegetable'; misses that фрукт is countable (plural фрукты) and excludes berries.

faults.quote: Я ем свежий фрукт каждый день.
faults.why: Singular 'свежий фрукт' is unnatural here; Russians use plural 'свежие фрукты'. English 'a fruit' is ungrammatical.

notes: Countable in Russian, so the plural фрукты is used for fruit in general. Small soft fruits like strawberries or grapes are usually called ягоды (berries) rather than фрукты.

senses.definition: The sweet and fleshy product of a tree or other plant that contains seeds and is eaten as food.

examples.text: Я ем свежие фрукты каждый день.
examples.translation: I eat fresh fruit every day.

faults.why: Misses the irregular end-stress across all forms (зонта́, зонты́).

notes: In everyday speech, the diminutive form зонтик is very common for a standard handheld umbrella.
The stress moves to the ending in all other forms: зонта́ (genitive singular), зонты́ (nominative plural).

senses.definition: A folding fabric canopy on a handle, carried for protection against rain or sun.

examples.text: Я забыл свой зонт дома, а на улице начался сильный дождь.
examples.translation: I left my umbrella at home, and it started raining heavily outside.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a married woman in relation to her husband.
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the irregular plural stem change with ё (жёны).

notes: In the plural, the stress shifts to the first syllable and е changes to ё: жёны (wives).

senses.definition: The woman that someone is married to.

examples.text: Моя жена работает врачом.
examples.translation: My wife works as a doctor.

faults.quote: Use 'вечер' for the part of the day between late afternoon and
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions; misses 'вечером' (in the evening) and plural 'вечера́'.

notes: The instrumental form вечером is used as an adverb meaning 'in the evening' (e.g., сегодня вечером — tonight).
The nominative plural is irregular with end stress: вечера́.

senses.definition: The part of the day between the end of the afternoon and night.

examples.text: Добрый вечер!
examples.translation: Good evening!

examples.text: Мы гуляем каждый вечер.
examples.translation: We go for a walk every evening.

senses.definition: An organized social or cultural event held in the evening.

examples.text: Мы идём на поэтический вечер.
examples.translation: We are going to a poetry evening.

faults.quote: A single page of a calendar showing the days, weeks, and months
faults.why: календарь does not mean 'calendar page' (that is листок календаря); the example is unnatural.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with калорийность (calorie content) or коридор (hallway).
faults.why: Bizarre warning about unrelated words; notes[1] fails to mention end-stress shifts to endings in declension.

notes: Although it ends in a soft sign (-ь), it is a masculine noun. The stress moves to the ending in all other forms: календаря́ (genitive singular), календари́ (nominative plural).

senses.definition: A chart, series of pages, or digital app showing the days, weeks, and months of a year, or a system for organizing dates.

examples.text: Я повесил новый календарь на стену в офисе.
examples.translation: I hung a new calendar on the wall in the office.

faults.why: Fails to mention that 'dentiste' is the same form for both masculine and feminine.

notes: The form is the same for men and women: un dentiste, une dentiste.
Use 'chez' (not 'à') to say 'to/at the dentist's': aller chez le dentiste.

senses.definition: A medical professional who treats people's teeth.

examples.text: Je dois aller chez le dentiste demain pour une carie.
examples.translation: I have to go to the dentist tomorrow for a cavity.

faults.quote: (isolation) An empty, lonely, or uninhabited place.
faults.why: Figurative sense is not needed as a separate sense for an A2 learner.

notes: Do not confuse with 'le dessert' /de.sɛʁ/ (dessert), which has a double 's' and a voiceless /s/ sound.

senses.definition: A large, hot, dry area of land with very little rain or plant life.

examples.text: Le Sahara est un grand désert chaud.
examples.translation: The Sahara is a large hot desert.

faults.quote: In France, 'le dîner' is traditionally the main evening meal
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of noting regional usage (Belgium/Switzerland/Canada) where it means lunch.

notes: In France, 'le dîner' is the evening meal. In Belgium, Switzerland, and Quebec, it refers to lunch (and the evening meal is 'le souper').

senses.definition: The main meal of the day, eaten in the evening.

examples.text: Nous préparons le dîner pour toute la famille.
examples.translation: We are preparing dinner for the whole family.

faults.quote: Do not forget that 'doigt' is masculine: un doigt.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender while failing to note the silent 'g' and 't'.

notes: Both the 'g' and the 't' at the end are silent: pronounced /dwa/.
For a toe, French uses the phrase 'un doigt de pied' (or the word 'un orteil').

senses.definition: One of the five parts at the end of the hand.

examples.text: Il s'est coupé le doigt avec un couteau.
examples.translation: He cut his finger with a knife.

senses.definition: Specifically in 'doigt de pied': one of the five parts at the end of the foot.

examples.text: J'ai mal au gros doigt de pied.
examples.translation: My big toe hurts.

faults.quote: /ˈteːləfoːn/
faults.why: Primary stress in Dutch 'telefoon' is on the final syllable: /ˌteːləˈfoːn/.

faults.quote: Ik heb een telefoon van mijn moeder.
faults.why: In nl-NL, a countable call is 'telefoontje'; 'telefoon' as a call is uncountable.

notes: For an individual phone call, the diminutive 'het telefoontje' is usually used in the Netherlands, though uncountable 'telefoon' is used in phrases like 'telefoon krijgen' (to get a call).

senses.definition: An electronic device used for calling people and talking to them, or a smartphone.

examples.text: De telefoon ligt op de tafel.
examples.translation: The phone is on the table.

senses.definition: A phone call, especially in fixed expressions when receiving or answering a call.

examples.text: Er is telefoon voor je.
examples.translation: There is a phone call for you.

faults.quote: /ˈteːləˌvizi.ə/
faults.why: In Dutch, final '-ie' is pronounced /i/, and primary stress is on '-vi-': /ˌteːləˈvizi/.

faults.quote: 'op de tv kijken' (to watch TV)
faults.why: Ungrammatical Dutch; 'to watch TV' is 'tv-kijken' or 'naar de tv kijken'.

faults.quote: (screen) A flat screen used specifically for watching programmes
faults.why: 'Televisie' does not mean 'screen' or 'display'; it means the device or the broadcast medium.

notes: Often shortened to 'de tv' (/teːˈveː/) in everyday speech: 'tv-kijken' (to watch TV).
Without an article after 'op', it refers to the medium: 'op televisie komen' (to be on TV).

senses.definition: An electronic device with a screen used for watching broadcast programmes and films.

examples.text: De nieuwe televisie hangt strak tegen de muur.
examples.translation: The new television hangs flat against the wall.

senses.definition: The system or medium of broadcasting programmes for people to watch.

examples.text: Er is vanavond een goede film op televisie.
examples.translation: There is a good movie on television tonight.

faults.quote: Use the common article 'de' for thee: 'de thee'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and headword already shown in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'het thee', which does not exist
faults.why: Pure filler repeating the article information.

notes: The 'h' is silent; 'thee' is pronounced just like the letter 't' (/teː/).

senses.definition: A hot drink made by pouring boiling water over dried leaves, or the leaves themselves.

examples.text: Wil je een kopje thee?
examples.translation: Do you want a cup of tea?

faults.quote: unlike English where ages like 11 and 12 are not teens
faults.why: Confusing and misleading; in Dutch 'tiener' routinely includes 10- to 12-year-olds (ages 10–19).

notes: Formed from 'tien' (ten); in Dutch, 'tiener' is often used broadly for anyone from 10 to 19 years old, not only 13 to 19.

senses.definition: A young person between roughly ten and nineteen years old.

examples.text: De tiener luistert de hele dag naar muziek op zijn telefoon.
examples.translation: The teenager listens to music on his phone all day.

faults.why: Should mention the female equivalent 'de toeriste' and the pronunciation of 'oe' as /u/.

notes: Can refer to any tourist, though the specific female form 'de toeriste' also exists.
The Dutch vowel 'oe' is pronounced like 'oo' in English 'boot' (/u/).

senses.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure and interest, usually while on holiday.

examples.text: De toerist maakt foto's van de oude kerk.
examples.translation: The tourist takes photos of the old church.

faults.quote: Use 'buổi chiều' when talking about the late part of the day
faults.why: First sentence restates the definition; note should focus on dropping 'buổi' with 'hôm nay/mai'.

notes: Often shortened to 'chiều', especially before words like 'nay' (this afternoon) or 'mai' (tomorrow afternoon).

senses.definition: The part of the day from around 1 p.m. until sunset.

examples.text: Tôi thường đi dạo vào buổi chiều.
examples.translation: I usually go for a walk in the afternoon.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the early part of the day
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: Often shortened to 'sáng' before words like 'nay' (this morning) or 'mai' (tomorrow morning), but kept as 'Chào buổi sáng' for 'Good morning'.

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: Buổi sáng tôi thường uống cà phê.
examples.translation: In the morning I usually drink coffee.

faults.quote: Use buổi tối for the time between late afternoon and bedtime
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to contrast with 'đêm' (late night) and mention dropping 'buổi'.

notes: Often shortened to 'tối' in phrases like 'tối nay' (tonight). Refers to the evening before bedtime, whereas 'đêm' is late night.

senses.definition: The part of the day from sunset until bedtime.

examples.text: Tôi thường đọc sách vào buổi tối.
examples.translation: I usually read books in the evening.

faults.quote: /bɨ̌m/
faults.why: Wrong vowel and tone notation; Hanoi IPA for 'bướm' is /ɓɨəm˧˦/.

faults.quote: In compound words, 'con bướm' is the full word
faults.why: 'Con' is the animate classifier used before the noun, not a compound-only form.

notes: Takes the classifier 'con' (con bướm). In everyday speech, the reduplicated form 'bươm bướm' is also very common.

senses.definition: An insect with large, often brightly coloured wings.

examples.text: Con bướm đậu trên bông hoa.
examples.translation: The butterfly landed on the flower.

faults.quote: Feeling weary because one has nothing to do
faults.why: Example describes a situation ('boring'), and 'bored' is usually 'buồn chán' or 'chán'.

notes: Also used before verbs of bodily urges to mean 'to feel like doing': 'buồn ngủ' (sleepy), 'buồn cười' (funny / feel like laughing).

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy or showing sorrow; causing a gloomy feeling.

examples.text: Tôi cảm thấy buồn vì phải chia tay bạn.
examples.translation: I feel sad because I have to say goodbye to you.

senses.definition: Feeling or causing boredom because there is nothing interesting to do.

examples.text: Ở nhà một mình cả ngày rất buồn.
examples.translation: Staying at home alone all day is very boring.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with полуостров (peninsula), which is connected to the mainland.
faults.why: Unnecessary contrast; misses the essential grammar note on taking the preposition на (and plural острова́).

notes: Takes the preposition на (not в) for 'on/to an island': на острове, на остров.
Stress shifts to the ending in the plural: острова́.

senses.definition: A piece of land completely surrounded by water.

examples.text: Мы отдыхали на тропическом острове.
examples.translation: We vacationed on a tropical island.

faults.quote: After the long road, a hot meal was very timely.
faults.why: Calqued translation ('the long road' instead of 'the long journey') and 'горячая еда' means 'hot food'.

notes: Uncountable (singular only), like English 'food'. In formal style, пища is used instead.

senses.definition: What people or animals eat.

examples.text: Домашняя еда всегда самая вкусная.
examples.translation: Home-cooked food is always the tastiest.

examples.text: После долгой дороги горячая еда была очень кстати.
examples.translation: After the long journey, hot food was very welcome.

senses.definition: An occasion when food is eaten; mealtime.
