notes: In its second sense, 'sạch' often follows a verb (like 'ăn sạch' – eat everything, or 'hết sạch' – completely run out) to show that nothing is left.

senses.definition: Free from dirt, dust, or unwanted marks.

examples.text: Căn phòng này rất sạch.
examples.translation: This room is very clean.

senses.definition: With nothing remaining; completely used up or gone.

examples.text: Tôi ăn sạch bát cơm rồi.
examples.translation: I ate the whole bowl of rice.

faults.quote: Sách is the general term for a book. While it refers to
faults.why: Filler note stating the obvious; should instead mention common classifiers 'cuốn' and 'quyển'.

notes: Takes the classifier 'quyển' or 'cuốn' (e.g., 'một quyển sách' – a book).
Do not confuse with 'vở', which refers to a blank notebook for writing in rather than a printed book for reading.

senses.definition: A set of printed pages bound together inside a cover for reading.

examples.text: Tôi đang đọc một cuốn sách hay.
examples.translation: I am reading a good book.

examples.text: Cô ấy có rất nhiều sách trên kệ.
examples.translation: She has a lot of books on the shelf.

faults.quote: Jendela refers to the physical opening in a wall, usually fitted with
faults.why: Note merely repeats the definition of the word.

senses.definition: An opening in the wall of a building or vehicle fitted with glass to let in light and air.

examples.text: Dia membuka jendela kamar setiap pagi.
examples.translation: She opens the bedroom window every morning.

faults.quote: A round, juicy citrus fruit with a thick, bright orange skin.
faults.why: Indonesian oranges are often green-skinned, and jeruk covers any citrus fruit, as the note states.

notes: Used alone for an orange or tangerine, and as a general term for citrus fruits in compounds like 'jeruk nipis' (lime), 'jeruk lemon' (lemon), and 'jeruk bali' (pomelo).

senses.definition: An orange or tangerine, or any other citrus fruit.

examples.text: Saya suka makan jeruk di pagi hari.
examples.translation: I like to eat an orange in the morning.

faults.quote: Used specifically for the liquid extracted from fruits or vegetables.
faults.why: Note merely repeats the definition of the word.

notes: In Indonesia, 'jus' often refers to a thick blended fruit drink (like a smoothie), such as 'jus alpukat' (avocado shake), as well as pressed fruit juice.

senses.definition: A drink made from squeezed or blended fruits or vegetables.

examples.text: Saya suka minum jus jeruk di pagi hari.
examples.translation: I like to drink orange juice in the morning.

examples.text: Apakah ada jus apel di kulkas?
examples.translation: Is there apple juice in the fridge?

notes: Used for both prescription glasses and sunglasses. To specify sunglasses, use 'kacamata hitam'.

senses.definition: A pair of lenses set in a frame worn on the nose and ears to correct vision or protect the eyes.

examples.text: Dia memakai kacamata untuk membaca.
examples.translation: He wears glasses for reading.

faults.quote: Happening or appearing on some occasions, but not all the time.
faults.why: Adverb is defined as a participial phrase/adjective ('Happening or appearing...') rather than an adverb.

notes: Often shortened to 'kadang' in everyday speech, or replaced by 'terkadang', which is slightly more formal.

senses.definition: On some occasions, rather than all the time.

examples.text: Saya kadang-kadang pergi ke perpustakaan untuk membaca buku.
examples.translation: I sometimes go to the library to read books.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with حَسُوب (hasub), which means calculating or judicious.
faults.why: حَسُوب is an obscure word a beginner will never encounter; missing the broken plural حَوَاسِيب.

notes: The broken plural is حَوَاسِيب (ḥawāsīb).
Used in formal and written Arabic, while the loanword كُمْبْيُوتَر (kumbyūtar) is common in daily speech.

senses.definition: An electronic machine used for storing and processing data, work, and the internet.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ حَاسُوبًا جَدِيدًا لِلْعَمَلِ.
examples.translation: I bought a new computer for work.

faults.quote: /ˈkursij/
faults.why: Missing the geminated final consonant of the shadda: should be /kurˈsijj/.

faults.quote: Used for any standard single seat with a back, whether at a
faults.why: Restates the definition of a chair while omitting the irregular broken plural كَرَاسِيّ.

notes: The broken plural is كَرَاسِيّ (karāsiyy).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for one person to sit on, typically having a back and four legs.

examples.text: جَلَسَ عَلَى الكُرْسِيِّ بِجَانِبِ الطَّاوِلَةِ.
examples.translation: He sat on the chair next to the table.

faults.quote: Used when traveling or staying away from home.
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning of 'hotel' already given in the definition.

notes: The broken plural is فَنَادِق (fanādiq), which is diptote (does not take nunation).

senses.definition: A building where you pay to have a room to sleep in when traveling.

examples.text: حَجَزْنَا فُنْدُقًا قَرِيبًا مِنَ البَحْرِ.
examples.translation: We booked a hotel near the sea.

notes: The broken plural is مُدُن (mudun).

senses.definition: A large town or urban area.

examples.text: هَذِهِ المَدِينَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ.
examples.translation: This city is big and beautiful.

faults.quote: Used for both ice and frost on surfaces during cold weather.
faults.why: Restates the glosses and fails to distinguish جَلِيد (natural ice) from ثَلْج (snow/drink ice).
Ice and frost on cold surfaces are shades of one meaning in Arabic; صَقِيع is specifically frost.

notes: Refers to natural ice in the environment (on roads, lakes, or windows). For ice cubes in a drink or snow, ثَلْج (ṯalj) is commonly used.

senses.definition: Frozen water forming a solid layer on the ground, water surfaces, or windows in cold weather.

examples.text: تَكَوَّنَ الجَلِيدُ عَلَى النَّافِذَةِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
examples.translation: Ice formed on the window in the morning.

faults.quote: kǒng jù
faults.why: Standard Pinyin writes disyllabic words without a space between syllables.

faults.quote: neutral
faults.why: The note rightly says it is formal, yet the register field says neutral.

notes: More formal and intense than 害怕 (hàipà), which is the everyday word for being afraid; 恐惧 is also used as a verb (to fear, to dread).

senses.definition: A strong feeling of fear or dread in the face of danger or the unknown.

examples.text: 黑暗中未知的危险让他感到极大的恐惧。
examples.translation: The unknown danger in the dark filled him with great fear.

faults.quote: In China, beer is almost always served chilled
faults.why: False cultural claim (room-temperature beer is very common in China) and irrelevant filler.

faults.quote: Note that '啤酒' refers specifically to the fermented, carbonated alcoholic beverage
faults.why: Restates the definition without giving useful grammar like measure words.

faults.quote: pí jiǔ
faults.why: Standard Pinyin writes disyllabic words without a space between syllables.

notes: Common measure words: 杯 (bēi, glass/cup), 瓶 (píng, bottle), 罐 (guàn, can). Notice how 酒 (jiǔ, alcohol) forms the names of many drinks, such as 红酒 (hóngjiǔ, red wine).

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grains.

examples.text: 服务员，请给我来两瓶冰啤酒。
examples.translation: Waiter, please bring me two bottles of cold beer.

faults.quote: 邻居 refers generally to anyone living nearby, as well as specifically
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition instead of giving useful grammar like the measure word.

faults.quote: lín jū
faults.why: Standard Pinyin writes disyllabic words without a space between syllables.

notes: Takes the measure word 个 (gè) or, politely, 位 (wèi).

senses.definition: A person who lives near you, especially next door.

examples.text: 我的邻居非常热情。
examples.translation: My neighbor is very warm and friendly.

faults.quote: To establish or set up something abstract, such as an image
faults.why: Wrong POS (verb in a noun entry) and bound usage; example uses 树立, not 树.

faults.quote: 我们要树立好榜样。
faults.why: Uses the two-syllable compound verb 树立 rather than the headword 树.

faults.quote: tree; to plant; to establish
faults.why: Includes bound verb meanings inappropriate for a noun entry.

faults.quote: As a noun, 树 means tree.
faults.why: Restates the gloss and POS while omitting the essential measure word 棵 (kē).

notes: Takes the measure word 棵 (kē): 一棵树 (yì kē shù, a tree).

senses.definition: A tall plant with a wooden trunk and branches.

examples.text: 公园里有很多大树。
examples.translation: There are many big trees in the park.

faults.quote: mā ma
faults.why: Standard Pinyin writes disyllabic words without a space between syllables.

notes: The second syllable is pronounced in the neutral tone (māma). In casual conversation it is often shortened to 妈 (mā); in formal contexts, 母亲 (mǔqīn, mother) is used instead.

senses.definition: A female parent.

examples.text: 我妈妈做的菜最好吃。
examples.translation: The food my mom makes is the most delicious.

faults.quote: Used to store small items like keys, phone, or money.
faults.why: Explains what a pocket is instead of giving linguistic information (like its broken plural).

faults.quote: Commonly found in trousers, shirts, and coats.
faults.why: World knowledge filler; does not help with Arabic usage.

notes: The plural is جُيُوب (juyūb).

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: مِفْتَاحِي فِي جَيْبِي.
examples.translation: My key is in my pocket.

notes: Plural: ثَلَّاجَات (thallājāt). From the root ث-ل-ج relating to ice and snow.

senses.definition: An appliance that keeps food and drinks cold.

examples.text: الْحَلِيبُ فِي الثَّلَّاجَةِ.
examples.translation: The milk is in the refrigerator.

faults.quote: /sa.jaː.raᲦ ʔuɡ.ra/
faults.why: Contains a corrupt character (Ღ), missing gemination on /j/, and Egyptian /ɡ/ instead of MSA /dʒ/.

notes: Literally 'car of fare'. In everyday speech, تَاكْسِي (tāksī) is also very common.

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: رَكِبْتُ سَيَّارَةَ أُجْرَةٍ لِأَصِلَ إِلَى الْمَطَارِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْمُنَاسِبِ.
examples.translation: I took a taxi to get to the airport on time.

faults.quote: Used for both physical letters sent through the post and electronic messages
faults.why: Restates the two senses; missing the essential broken plural رَسَائِل.

notes: The plural is رَسَائِل (rasāʾil).

senses.definition: A written or printed communication sent to someone, typically by post.

examples.text: وَصَلَتْنِي رِسَالَةٌ فِي البَرِيدِ.
examples.translation: I received a letter in the post.

senses.definition: A written communication sent electronically, such as a text or email.

examples.text: أَرْسَلْتُ لَكَ رِسَالَةً قَبْلَ قَلِيلٍ.
examples.translation: I sent you a message a short while ago.

faults.quote: /ˈɣroːtˌmoː.dər/
faults.why: The second vowel is /u/, not /oː/: /ˈɣroːtˌmu.dər/.

notes: In daily conversation, Dutch speakers much more frequently use the informal word 'oma' instead of 'grootmoeder'.

senses.definition: The mother of someone's father or mother.

examples.text: Mijn grootmoeder bakt altijd lekkere koekjes.
examples.translation: My grandmother always bakes delicious cookies.

faults.quote: A person's style of handwriting.
faults.why: Archaic sense; modern Dutch uses 'handschrift' for handwriting.

faults.quote: Ik kan zijn hand niet lezen.
faults.why: Unnatural; 'de hand lezen' means palm reading, while handwriting is 'handschrift'.

faults.quote: Use 'hand' primarily for the physical body part at the end of
faults.why: Restates the definitions without giving useful grammatical or usage advice.

notes: The final 'd' is pronounced as /t/ in the singular ('hand'), but as /d/ in the plural ('handen').
Very common in everyday expressions, such as 'een hand geven' (to shake hands) and 'een handje helpen' (to lend a hand).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers.

examples.text: Geef me je hand als we oversteken.
examples.translation: Give me your hand when we cross the street.

faults.quote: /ˈɦɑnt.duːk/
faults.why: Assimilated 'dd' is pronounced as single /d/, and 'oe' is short /u/: /ˈɦɑn.duk/.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'wasmand' (laundry basket) or 'badjas' (bathrobe).
faults.why: Unrelated words in form and meaning that no learner would confuse.

notes: A compound of 'hand' (hand) and 'doek' (cloth); the double 'dd' in the middle is pronounced as a single /d/.
Used for any cloth towel for drying the body (including bath towels), whereas a kitchen towel for dishes is 'de theedoek'.

senses.definition: A piece of absorbent cloth used for drying your body or hands after washing.

examples.text: Pak een schone handdoek uit de kast om je af te drogen.
examples.translation: Take a clean towel from the cupboard to dry yourself.

faults.quote: /ɦɛrft/
faults.why: Missing the /s/ sound in the consonant cluster: /ɦɛrfst/.

faults.quote: In the Netherlands, de herfst officially runs from September to November
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia and an unmotivated comparison instead of useful language guidance.

notes: To say 'in (the) autumn', Dutch uses the preposition 'in' with the definite article: 'in de herfst'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between summer and winter, when leaves fall from the trees.

examples.text: In de herfst vallen de bladeren van de bomen.
examples.translation: In autumn, the leaves fall from the trees.

faults.quote: [0] (retail) ... [1] (restaurant) ...
faults.why: 店員 is one concept in Japanese (staff at a shop or restaurant); splitting is English-driven.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, you do not use 'ten-in' to address the person
faults.why: English speakers do not address staff as 'shop assistant' either; 店員さん can be used.

notes: Covers staff in both retail shops and restaurants or cafes.
To call a staff member over, say すみません (sumimasen, 'excuse me'). When referring to them politely, add さん: 店員さん (ten'in-san).

senses.definition: A person who works serving customers in a shop, store, restaurant, or cafe.

examples.text: 店員に服のサイズを聞きました。
examples.translation: I asked the shop assistant about the clothing size.

examples.text: 店員が注文した料理を持ってきました。
examples.translation: The server brought the food I ordered.

faults.quote: secret; privacy
faults.why: 'privacy' is not in the sense glosses and is a misleading translation for 秘密.

faults.quote: Used for both personal secrets and classified or restricted information.
faults.why: Same as English 'secret'; adds no useful usage information for a learner.

notes: Can modify another noun using の, as in 秘密の部屋 (himitsu no heya, 'secret room').
Often used in the phrase 秘密にする (himitsu ni suru, 'to keep something a secret').

senses.definition: Information that is kept hidden from other people.

examples.text: この話は誰にも秘密にしてください。
examples.translation: Please keep this story a secret from everyone.

faults.quote: In casual speech, it is often shortened to 'パソコン' (pasokon)
faults.why: パソコン is not an abbreviation of コンピューター, and is the standard everyday word for a PC.

notes: For a personal computer (desktop or laptop), パソコン (pasokon) is much more common in everyday conversation. コンピューター often refers to computer systems more broadly.
Also written and pronounced コンピュータ without the final long vowel.

senses.definition: An electronic machine that stores and processes data.

examples.text: 仕事で新しいコンピューターを使っています。
examples.translation: I am using a new computer for work.

faults.quote: While it most commonly refers to a flower on a plant...
faults.why: Discusses advanced idiomatic senses not included in the entry instead of A2 usage.

notes: Often takes the polite prefix お to become お花 (o-hana), which can also mean生け花 (ikebana, traditional flower arrangement).
shares the same pronunciation (はな, hana) as 鼻 ('nose'), though their pitch accents differ in Tokyo Japanese.

senses.definition: The colourful part of a plant that produces seeds and often has a pleasant smell.

examples.text: 庭にきれいな花が咲いています。
examples.translation: There are beautiful flowers blooming in the garden.

faults.why: Kanji headword 写真 is missing its hiragana reading (しゃしん).

faults.quote: Used for both physical prints and digital images captured with a camera.
faults.why: True of English 'photo' as well; states the obvious.

notes: Used with the verb 撮る (toru) in the phrase 写真を撮る (shashin o toru, 'to take a photo'); note the kanji 撮る rather than 取る.

senses.definition: An image taken with a camera.

examples.text: 旅の思い出に写真をたくさん撮りました。
examples.translation: I took many photographs as travel memories.

faults.quote: Often used to mean both the physical room and the style
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the needed preposition note (на кухне vs. в кухне).

notes: Usually takes the preposition на rather than в: на кухне (in the kitchen), пойти на кухню (to go to the kitchen).
Genitive plural: кухонь.

senses.definition: The room in a house or apartment where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: Мы готовим ужин на кухне.
examples.translation: We are cooking dinner in the kitchen.

senses.definition: The style of cooking or culinary tradition of a particular region or culture.

examples.text: Мне очень нравится итальянская кухня.
examples.translation: I really like Italian cuisine.

faults.quote: Добавьте немного растительное масло на сковороду.
faults.why: Ungrammatical: 'немного' requires the genitive case (растительного масла), not accusative.

notes: Usually uncountable. Distinguish from сливочное масло (butter); масло alone can mean either depending on context.
In Russia, default растительное масло is almost always sunflower oil (подсолнечное масло).

senses.definition: Liquid fat of plant origin used for cooking and dressing food.

examples.text: Налейте немного растительного масла на сковороду.
examples.translation: Pour a little vegetable oil into the frying pan.

faults.quote: In Russian, 'юбка' specifically refers to the garment worn from the waist
faults.why: Restates the definition; English speakers do not confuse 'skirt' and 'dress'.

notes: Genitive plural: юбок.

senses.definition: A garment that hangs from the waist and covers all or part of the legs.

examples.text: Она надела новую синюю юбку.
examples.translation: She put on a new blue skirt.

faults.quote: /ɛɡˈzamʲɪn/
faults.why: Unstressed initial 'э' reduces to [ɪ] in standard Russian (/ɪɡˈzamʲɪn/).
Misses the essential verb collocations (сдавать/сдать экзамен) and preposition (по + dative) for learners.

notes: Note the aspect difference with сдавать/сдать: сдавать экзамен (imperfective) means 'to take/sit an exam', while сдать экзамен (perfective) means 'to pass an exam'.
The subject of an exam is expressed with по + dative: экзамен по русскому языку (Russian exam).

senses.definition: A formal test to evaluate a person's knowledge or proficiency in a subject.

examples.text: Я готовлюсь к завтрашнему экзамену.
examples.translation: I am preparing for tomorrow's exam.

examples.text: Он успешно сдал экзамен по истории.
examples.translation: He passed the history exam.

faults.quote: 내 생일은 삼월 삼일입니다.
faults.why: Mixing non-humble '내' with formal polite '입니다' is unnatural; use '제' with '입니다'.

notes: When speaking about an elder's birthday or in formal situations, use the honorific word 생신 instead.

senses.definition: The anniversary of the day on which a person was born.

examples.text: 제 생일은 삼월 삼일입니다.
examples.translation: My birthday is March third.

faults.quote: 저사자 (grim reaper) or 사자성어 (four-character idiom).
faults.why: Misspells 저승사자 as 저사자, and falsely claims 사자 in 사자성어 means messenger (it means four-character).

faults.quote: A person sent to deliver a message or represent someone; an envoy.
faults.why: Literary/historical homonym not needed as a main sense for an A2 beginner.

senses.definition: A large wild cat native to Africa and India, known for the male's heavy mane.

examples.text: 사자가 초원에서 쉬고 있어요.
examples.translation: The lion is resting in the grassland.

faults.quote: Unlike some Korean food items that have native Korean equivalents, '버터' is
faults.why: Stating that '버터' is an English loanword is obvious and unhelpful filler.

senses.definition: A yellow fat made from cream or milk, used in cooking or spread on bread.

examples.text: 따뜻한 빵에 버터를 발라 먹었어요.
examples.translation: I spread butter on the warm bread and ate it.

faults.quote: The word 의사 is a homonym. As a professional title, it means
faults.why: merely restates the definitions and glosses of the two senses.

faults.quote: The state of wanting or intending to do something.
faults.why: '의사' meaning 'intention' is a formal/advanced homonym, not an everyday A2 sense.

notes: When addressing or referring to a doctor politely, attach 선생님: 의사 선생님.

senses.definition: A person who is trained and licensed to treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: 몸이 아파서 의사를 만나러 병원에 갔습니다.
examples.translation: I went to the hospital to see a doctor because I was sick.

faults.quote: Even though it refers to a pet, the word is grammatically feminine
faults.why: Restates the gender field; missing everyday sense of '@' in email addresses.

notes: Refers to any dog regardless of its sex; a male dog specifically is 'пёс' or 'кобель'.
In informal speech, 'собака' (or the diminutive 'собачка') is also the name of the '@' symbol in email addresses.

senses.definition: A common four-legged animal kept as a pet or used to guard or hunt.

examples.text: У меня есть маленькая собака.
examples.translation: I have a small dog.

notes: Always plural (plurale tantum); use 'пара брюк' (a pair of trousers) to count them.
More formal than 'штаны', which is everyday colloquial and covers jeans, sweatpants, etc.

senses.definition: An outer garment covering each leg separately, from the waist to the ankles.

examples.text: Он купил новые чёрные брюки.
examples.translation: He bought new black trousers.

faults.quote: Бумага refers both to the material you write on and to official
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to note countability and how to say 'a sheet'.

notes: Uncountable in the 'material' sense; for a single sheet, say 'лист бумаги' (or colloquially 'бумажка').
In the 'document' sense, it is countable and most often used in the plural ('бумаги').

senses.definition: The thin material made from wood that you write, draw, or print on.

examples.text: Мне нужна чистая бумага для принтера.
examples.translation: I need blank paper for the printer.

senses.definition: An official document, certificate, or piece of paperwork.

examples.text: Нужно подписать эти бумаги.
examples.translation: These papers need to be signed.

faults.quote: Used for both writing and drawing on paper.
faults.why: World-knowledge filler about what a pencil is; misses the stress shift in oblique cases.

faults.quote: He is writing a letter with a simple pencil.
faults.why: Calque: 'простой карандаш' means an ordinary lead/graphite pencil (as opposed to a coloured one).

notes: Stress is always on the ending in all inflected forms: карандаша́, карандашо́м, карандаши́.
An ordinary graphite pencil (as opposed to a coloured one, 'цветной карандаш') is called 'простой карандаш'.

senses.definition: A thin wooden tool with a stick of graphite inside, used for writing or drawing.

examples.text: Он пишет письмо простым карандашом.
examples.translation: He is writing a letter with a lead pencil.

faults.quote: Used both for the green grass on a lawn and for wild
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses; misses countability and the stress shift in the plural.

faults.quote: herb, weed
faults.why: 'Weed' does not match the definition of a plant used in medicine or cooking ('сорняк').

notes: Uncountable in the 'grass' sense; countable and usually plural ('тра́вы', with stress shifting to the stem) when referring to herbs.

senses.definition: The short green plants that cover the ground in a lawn, park, or field.

examples.text: Во дворе растёт зелёная трава.
examples.translation: Green grass grows in the yard.

senses.definition: A wild or garden plant used in medicine, tea, or cooking.

examples.text: Бабушка собирает целебные травы.
examples.translation: Grandmother gathers medicinal herbs.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the current day or to the present
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Can also be used as an indeclinable noun with the neuter article: το σήμερα (the present day).

senses.definition: On this present day.

examples.text: Σήμερα έχω πολλή δουλειά.
examples.translation: Today I have a lot of work.

senses.definition: At the present time; in the modern era.

examples.text: Σήμερα τα πράγματα είναι διαφορετικά.
examples.translation: Nowadays things are different.

faults.quote: Used very frequently in everyday conversation to express uncertainty or possibility.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving the grammatical construction (optional να).

notes: Often followed directly by the verb, or by να + verb with no change in meaning (e.g., ίσως πάω or ίσως να πάω).

senses.definition: Possibly, but not certainly.

examples.text: Ίσως πάω αύριο στη θάλασσα.
examples.translation: Maybe I will go to the sea tomorrow.

faults.quote: Use εκεί for a place away from both the speaker and
faults.why: In Greek, εκεί covers any place away from the speaker, including near the listener.

notes: Contrasts with εδώ (here). Used for both static location ('in that place') and movement ('to that place').

senses.definition: In or to that place, away from the speaker.

examples.text: Το βιβλίο είναι εκεί.
examples.translation: The book is there.

faults.quote: /ekseleˈtoriko/
faults.why: Completely garbled IPA; neither matches the headword nor even the noun εξωτερικό.

faults.quote: combining the preposition 'στος' (in/to) with the neuter noun
faults.why: There is no preposition 'στος'; στο is the contraction of σε + το.

notes: Literally 'in/to the exterior', from στο (σε + το) and the neuter noun το εξωτερικό.
Used both for being in a foreign country (ζω στο εξωτερικό) and for going to one (ταξιδεύω στο εξωτερικό).

senses.definition: In or to a foreign country.

examples.text: Θέλω να ταξιδέψω στο εξωτερικό το καλοκαίρι.
examples.translation: I want to travel abroad this summer.

examples.text: Ο αδερφός μου ζει στο εξωτερικό.
examples.translation: My brother lives abroad.

faults.quote: already; now
faults.why: Includes 'now', which is not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: ἤδη primarily means 'already' when used with past or present actions
faults.why: Restates the meaning and uses archaic polytonic spelling (ἤδη) instead of standard monotonic (ήδη).

notes: In everyday spoken Greek, κιόλας is often used instead of ήδη.

senses.definition: Before now, or earlier than expected.

examples.text: Είναι ήδη αργά.
examples.translation: It is already late.

faults.quote: Kan is a fundamental body-related noun, essential for talking about health
faults.why: Pure filler stating the obvious instead of useful usage information.

faults.quote: Blood is flowing from my hand.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English one naturally says 'My hand is bleeding'.

notes: Often used in medical expressions like 'kan vermek' (to give/donate blood) and 'kan tahlili' (blood test).

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows inside the body through veins and arteries.

examples.text: Elimden kan akıyor.
examples.translation: My hand is bleeding. (lit. Blood is flowing from my hand.)

faults.quote: Kapı primarily refers to a physical door you open to enter
faults.why: Restates the definitions and glosses without adding grammatical or usage help.

notes: Because the word ends in a vowel, it takes the buffer consonant 'y' before case endings: 'kapıyı' (accusative), 'kapıya' (dative). Do not confuse with 'kap' (container).

senses.definition: The movable barrier that you open and close to enter a room, building, or vehicle.

examples.text: Lütfen kapıyı kapat.
examples.translation: Please close the door.

senses.definition: An opening or movable barrier in a wall or fence for entering an outdoor area, or an airport boarding point.

examples.text: Bahçenin kapısı açık kaldı.
examples.translation: The garden gate was left open.

faults.quote: Use 'kapatmak' for closing physical objects like doors or windows
faults.why: Restates the senses without giving new grammar or usage details.

corrected.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to turn off
notes: Transitive verb taking a direct object in the accusative case (e.g., 'kapıyı kapatmak'). Its opposite for both physical openings and electronics is 'açmak' (to open / turn on).
Also used for ending a phone call ('telefonu kapatmak' — to hang up) or closing an account or shop.

senses.definition: To move something so that it covers an opening, or to shut an object like a book or container.

examples.text: Lütfen kapıyı kapat.
examples.translation: Please close the door.

senses.definition: To stop a device, light, or machine from operating, or to end a phone call.

examples.text: Televizyonu kapatır mısın?
examples.translation: Could you turn off the television?

faults.quote: Although they are spelled similarly without the circumflex in modern spelling
faults.why: Standard Turkish orthography (TDK) explicitly retains the circumflex on 'kâr' to distinguish it from 'kar'.

notes: Used with the verb 'yağmak' (to fall/precipitate): 'kar yağıyor' (it is snowing).
Do not confuse with 'kâr' (profit), which is pronounced with afronted/palatalized 'k' (/cɑːɾ/) and keeps its circumflex in standard spelling.

senses.definition: Soft white pieces of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather.

examples.text: Yarın çok kar yağacak.
examples.translation: It will snow a lot tomorrow.

faults.quote: Sokaklar çok karanlık, lütfen dikkatli yürüsün.
faults.why: Grammatical mismatch: 'lütfen' addresses 'you', so imperative must be 2nd person ('yürü'/'yürüyün'), not 3rd ('yürüsün').

faults.quote: dark, darkness
faults.why: 'Darkness' is a noun gloss, but the entry POS and definition are strictly adjective.

faults.quote: Karanlık can describe both physical spaces lacking light and abstract concepts
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses instead of explaining that 'karanlık' also functions as a noun.

notes: Also commonly used as a noun meaning 'darkness' or 'the dark' (e.g., 'karanlıkta' — in the dark). Its opposite is 'aydınlık' (bright / light).

senses.definition: With little or no light.

examples.text: Sokaklar çok karanlık, lütfen dikkatli yürü.
examples.translation: The streets are very dark, please walk carefully.

senses.definition: Kept secret, mysterious, or suspicious.

examples.text: Bu olay hakkında hâlâ karanlık noktalar var.
examples.translation: There are still obscure points about this incident.

faults.quote: without a brim, like baseball caps or beanies, Dutch uses 'muts' or 'pet'.
faults.why: A baseball cap ('pet') has a visor/brim; only 'muts' (beanie) has none.

notes: Use 'hoed' for hats with an all-around brim (like a sun hat or fedora). Use 'pet' for a peaked cap (like a baseball cap) and 'muts' for a knit beanie.

senses.definition: A covering for the head, typically with an all-around brim and a shaped crown.

examples.text: Zij draagt een mooie hoed tegen de zon.
examples.translation: She is wearing a nice hat to keep the sun off.

faults.quote: Use 'hoek' both for geometric angles and for street corners
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'kanteel' or other words;
faults.why: 'Kanteel' (battlement/merlon) is a rare architectural term no A2 learner will confuse with 'hoek'.

notes: Takes the preposition 'in' for an inside corner ('in de hoek van de kamer', in the corner of the room) and 'op' or 'om' for an outside street corner ('op/om de hoek', on/around the corner).

senses.definition: The place where two streets, walls, or edges meet, or the area around a bend.

examples.text: Hij wacht op de hoek van de straat.
examples.translation: He is waiting on the corner of the street.

senses.definition: The space between two intersecting lines or surfaces, measured in degrees.

examples.text: Teken een rechte hoek op het papier.
examples.translation: Draw a right angle on the paper.

faults.quote: Pushing air out of the throat with a noise.
faults.why: Defined as a verb phrase (gerund) rather than a noun.

faults.quote: Use 'de hoest' for the condition or the act of coughing itself
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

faults.quote: Ik heb veel last van de hoest.
faults.why: 'Last van de hoest' is unnatural; Dutch uses 'last van hoest' or 'een nare hoest'.

notes: In everyday speech, Dutch often uses the verb 'hoesten' (to cough) or the diminutive 'een hoestje' where English uses the noun: 'Ik moet veel hoesten' (I have a bad cough).

senses.definition: An act or sound of forcing air out of the lungs through the throat, or an illness that causes this.

examples.text: Hij heeft al een week een nare hoest.
examples.translation: He has had a nasty cough for a week already.

faults.quote: Takes the common gender article 'de'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already shown in the headword.

senses.definition: A common four-legged animal that barks and is often kept as a pet or working animal.

examples.text: De hond blaft naar de postbode.
examples.translation: The dog is barking at the mail carrier.

faults.quote: /ˈɦoːfd.pɛi̯n/
faults.why: In 'hoofdpijn', the 'd' undergoes final devoicing (/t/) or is elided: /ˈɦoːft.pɛi̯n/.
Missing essential grammar note: 'hoofdpijn' is uncountable and used without 'een' ('Ik heb hoofdpijn').

notes: Unlike English 'a headache', 'hoofdpijn' is uncountable and used without an article: 'Ik heb hoofdpijn' (I have a headache).

senses.definition: A continuous pain in the head.

examples.text: Ik heb vandaag erge hoofdpijn.
examples.translation: I have a bad headache today.

faults.why: Should mention that 'foto' is invariable in the plural ('le foto').

notes: Short for 'fotografia', which is why it is feminine even though it ends in -o. It is invariable in the plural ('le foto').

senses.definition: A picture taken with a camera.

examples.text: Ho fatto una bella foto davanti al Colosseo.
examples.translation: I took a nice photo in front of the Colosseum.

faults.quote: /ˈfru.ta/
faults.why: Wrong IPA: misses geminate /t/ in 'frutta' (/ˈfrut.ta/).

notes: Used as an uncountable collective noun for fruit as food ('mangio la frutta'). For a single piece of fruit or the botanical/figurative sense, use 'il frutto'.

senses.definition: Sweet plant parts with seeds, eaten collectively as food.

examples.text: Mangia più frutta fresca ogni giorno.
examples.translation: Eat more fresh fruit every day.

faults.quote: (person) A timid person who is afraid of everything.
faults.why: English calque; Italian uses 'coniglio' or 'fifone' for coward, not 'gallina'.

notes: Refers to the live adult female bird. For the male, use 'il gallo'; for chicken in general or chicken meat, use 'il pollo'.

senses.definition: An adult female chicken, kept on farms for its eggs.

examples.text: La gallina fa le uova fresche ogni mattina.
examples.translation: The hen lays fresh eggs every morning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'piede' (foot) or 'ginocchio' (knee).
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; learners do not confuse unrelated words like 'gamba' and 'piede'.

notes: Common in the idiom 'In bocca al lupo!' — 'Crepi!' or 'In gamba!' (to wish someone good luck or say someone is capable: 'è molto in gamba').

senses.definition: One of the limbs of a person or animal used for standing and walking.

examples.text: Mi sono rotto una gamba sciando.
examples.translation: I broke a leg skiing.

senses.definition: A vertical support for a piece of furniture such as a table or chair.

examples.text: La gamba del tavolo è traballante.
examples.translation: The table leg is wobbly.

faults.quote: Used to address or refer to one's grandmother.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding grammar or usage information.
Missing note on singular family members omitting the article after possessive adjectives.

notes: Like other singular family words, 'nonna' usually drops the definite article with possessive adjectives (e.g., 'mia nonna', not 'la mia nonna'), unless it is plural ('le mie nonne') or affectionate ('la mia nonnina').

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: La nonna prepara sempre una torta deliziosa.
examples.translation: Grandma always makes a delicious cake.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'nuvola' with 'nebbia', which means fog.
faults.why: Unlikely point of confusion for learners.

senses.definition: A white or grey mass in the sky made of small drops of water.

examples.text: Il cielo è pieno di nuvole nere oggi.
examples.translation: The sky is full of dark clouds today.

faults.quote: In Italian, 'pasta' primarily refers to the staple food made from
faults.why: Restates the senses and falsely claims 'pasta' alone means pastry cream.

faults.quote: dough, batter
faults.why: Contradicts note[1]; liquid batter is 'pastella', whereas 'pasta' is firmer dough.

faults.quote: Stasera cucino la pasta con il pomodoro.
faults.why: 'Pasta al pomodoro' is the natural Italian collocation, not 'con il pomodoro'.

notes: As food (sense 1) and dough (sense 2), 'pasta' is uncountable in the singular ('mangio la pasta'). As a sweet pastry (sense 3), it is countable ('una pasta', 'due paste').

senses.definition: A staple Italian food made from flour and water, such as spaghetti or penne, cooked by boiling.

examples.text: Stasera cucino la pasta al pomodoro.
examples.translation: Tonight I am cooking pasta with tomato sauce.

senses.definition: A firm mixture of flour and liquid used to make bread, pizza, or pastries.

examples.text: Devo lasciare lievitare la pasta per la pizza.
examples.translation: I need to let the pizza dough rise.

senses.definition: A small individual cake or sweet pastry, often eaten for breakfast at a café.

examples.text: Prendo un caffè e una pasta al bar.
examples.translation: I'll have a coffee and a pastry at the café.

faults.quote: Used commonly in everyday cooking, especially for side dishes
faults.why: Encyclopedic filler about potatoes rather than linguistic usage.

faults.quote: Tuber grow underground, used widely as a vegetable in cooking.
faults.why: Ungrammatical English ('Tuber grow underground').

notes: Common culinary terms include 'patate al forno' (roasted potatoes), 'patate lesse' (boiled potatoes), and 'patatine fritte' (French fries).

senses.definition: A round vegetable with brown or red skin and white or yellow flesh that grows underground.

examples.text: Le patate al forno sono croccanti fuori e morbide dentro.
examples.translation: The roasted potatoes are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.

faults.quote: neutral
faults.why: The notes correctly explain that व्यक्ति is formal, so register should be 'formal'.

notes: व्यक्ति is the standard formal word for 'person' (used in writing and official contexts); in casual speech, लोग use इंसान (human being) or आदमी (person/man).
Although grammatically masculine, it can refer to a person of any gender; the plural in the oblique case is व्यक्तियों (vyaktiyon).

senses.definition: A single human being.

examples.text: वह एक बहुत दयालु व्यक्ति है।
examples.translation: He is a very kind person.

examples.text: हर व्यक्ति को अपनी बात कहने का अधिकार है।
examples.translation: Every individual has the right to express their opinion.

faults.quote: होमवर्क is a direct borrowing from English 'homework' and is widely used
faults.why: Two notes repeat the same point; collocation with करना is more useful for learners.

notes: Used with करना (karna, to do) for 'to do homework' and मिलना (milna) for 'to get homework'. The formal Sanskritized term गृहकार्य (gṛhkārya) is only seen in textbooks or official notices.

senses.definition: Schoolwork that a student is given to do at home.

examples.text: मैंने अपना सारा होमवर्क पूरा कर लिया है।
examples.translation: I have finished all my homework.

faults.quote: It is feminine, so adjectives and verbs agreeing with it
faults.why: Restates the gender field without adding useful usage or pronunciation information.

faults.quote: /t̪ən.kʰʋɑːɦ/
faults.why: Spelled तनख्वाह or तनख़्वाह, the standard pronunciation is /t̪ən.xʋɑːɦ/ or /t̪ən.kʰɑː/ (the व is often silent).

notes: Often spelled तनख़्वाह with a nuqta. In everyday speech, the 'व' (v) is frequently dropped, making it sound like 'tankhā' (/t̪ən.kʰɑː/).
The formal Hindi equivalent is वेतन (vetan, masculine).

senses.definition: Regular money paid for work, usually received every month.

examples.text: महीने के आखिर में तनख्वाह मिलती है।
examples.translation: Salary is paid at the end of the month.

faults.quote: A derogatory term used to insult someone by calling them a dog.
faults.why: Vulgar/insult usage is already covered in the note and should not be a main A2 sense.

faults.quote: dog; cur
faults.why: 'cur' is archaic in English and unsuitable as a short gloss for A2 learners.

notes: Inflects like a regular -आ (-ā) masculine noun: कुत्ते (kutte) in the plural and oblique singular. The feminine form (female dog) is कुतिया (kutiyā).

senses.definition: A common four-legged animal kept as a pet or for guarding.

examples.text: मेरा कुत्ता बहुत वफ़ादार है।
examples.translation: My dog is very loyal.

faults.quote: In India, this word is used for many styles of headwear
faults.why: Repeats what the gloss 'hat, cap' already conveys without adding linguistic value.

notes: Covers both brimmed hats and brimless caps (unlike पगड़ी, pagṛī, which is a wrapped turban). With पहनना (pahannā, to wear) or लगाना (lagānā, to put on).

senses.definition: A soft covering for the head, worn for protection from the sun or cold, or as part of an outfit.

examples.text: धूप से बचने के लिए मैंने टोपी पहनी है।
examples.translation: I am wearing a cap to protect myself from the sun.

faults.quote: Use 'बाँह' when emphasizing the arm as a part of the body
faults.why: Wordy filler; can be merged briefly into the first note or dropped.

notes: In everyday speech, 'हाथ' (hand) is often used for the whole arm; 'बाँह' refers specifically to the arm, especially in expressions of holding or embracing (e.g., बाँहों में लेना, to take in one's arms).

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body, from the shoulder to the hand.

examples.text: उसने बच्चे को अपनी बाँहों में उठा लिया।
examples.translation: She picked the child up in her arms.

senses.definition: The part of a garment that covers the arm.

examples.text: इस कमीज़ की बाँहें बहुत लंबी हैं।
examples.translation: The sleeves of this shirt are very long.

faults.quote: उसने बहुत से देशों की यात्रा की। — He traveled to many regions.
faults.why: Here देशों means 'countries', not 'regions'; mistranslated to fit a marginal sense.

faults.quote: (region) A geographical area or a region.
faults.why: Poetic or compound-only sense; 'हमार देश' (native village/homeland) is more everyday than 'region'.

faults.quote: For 'my country' (India), speakers often use 'भारत' (Bharat) for the name
faults.why: Trivial observation about proper nouns vs. common nouns.

notes: In colloquial speech, many speakers also use 'देश' (or 'देस') to mean their native village or hometown when living away from it.

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and territory.

examples.text: भारत एक बड़ा देश है।
examples.translation: India is a big country.

examples.text: उसने बहुत से देशों की यात्रा की।
examples.translation: He traveled to many countries.

senses.definition: One's native land, home region, or ancestral village.

examples.text: वह छुट्टियों में अपने देश जा रहा है।
examples.translation: He is going to his native place for the holidays.

faults.quote: This loanword from English is frequently used in daily life
faults.why: Repeats note 0 and the definition without adding learner value.

notes: An English loanword used daily alongside 'कमीज़' (kamīz). Both words are feminine in standard Hindi.

senses.definition: A garment for the upper body, typically with a collar and buttons down the front.

examples.text: उसने नीली शर्ट पहनी है।
examples.translation: He is wearing a blue shirt.

faults.quote: It is almost always masculine.
faults.why: Restates the gender field (and hedges inaccurately: it is always masculine).

notes: An uncountable (mass) noun used in the singular.

senses.definition: The white liquid produced by cows, buffaloes, and other mammals, used as a drink or in cooking.

examples.text: बच्चा रोज़ सुबह दूध पीता है।
examples.translation: The child drinks milk every morning.

faults.quote: neutral
faults.why: 'त्वचा' is formal/Sanskritized; everyday spoken Hindi uses 'चमड़ी' or 'स्किन'.

senses.definition: The thin outer layer covering the body of a person or animal.

examples.text: धूप से मेरी त्वचा जल गई है।
examples.translation: My skin got sunburned.

faults.quote: Use the masculine article 'il' (plural 'i libri').
faults.why: Restates the headword's article and regular plural formation.

senses.definition: A set of written, printed, or blank pages bound together between two covers.

examples.text: Ho comprato un libro nuovo.

faults.quote: though the noun itself strictly refers to the fruit or the tree.

faults.quote: In Italian slang, 'limonare' (derived from this noun) means to make out

senses.definition: A yellow, oval citrus fruit with a thick skin and sour juice.

senses.definition: The tree that produces lemons.

examples.text: C'è un grande limone nel cortile della casa.
examples.translation: There is a large lemon tree in the courtyard of the house.

senses.definition: A warm knitted garment for the upper body with long sleeves.

examples.text: Ho messo un maglione pesante perché fa molto freddo.
examples.translation: I put on a heavy sweater because it is very cold.

faults.quote: While 'maiale' refers to the live animal, 'maiale' or 'carne di maiale'

senses.definition: A pink or dark-skinned farm animal with short legs, raised for its meat.

examples.text: Il maiale mangia nel fango.
examples.translation: The pig is eating in the mud.

senses.definition: The meat of a pig, eaten as food.

examples.text: Stasera cucino il maiale con le patate.
examples.translation: Tonight I am cooking pork with potatoes.

faults.quote: Used with the verb avere (to have), as in avere il mal di testa.

faults.quote: /le.te/

examples.text: 가격이 너무 비싸요.
examples.translation: The price is too high.

faults.quote: (phobia) A strong, often irrational, fear of a specific thing or situation.
faults.why: Medical/specific phobias are '공포증' (e.g., 거미 공포증), not '공포' alone.

faults.quote: 많은 사람들이 거미 공포를 겪는다.
faults.why: Unnatural Korean; native speakers say '거미 공포증이 있다' for spider phobia.

faults.quote: 그는 어둠에 대한 강한 공포를 가지고 있다.
faults.why: Reads like a direct English translation ('has a strong fear of'); '공포를 느끼다' is natural.

notes: Describes intense fear or terror, and is also used for the 'horror' genre (e.g., 공포 영화, 'horror movie'). For everyday 'being scared', Koreans usually use the adjective '무섭다'.

senses.definition: An intense feeling of fear, shock, or dread, or a genre of fiction meant to scare people.

examples.text: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 공포를 느꼈어요.
examples.translation: I felt terror when there was a sudden loud noise.

examples.text: 저는 공포 영화를 잘 못 봐요.
examples.translation: I can't watch horror movies very well.

faults.quote: It is a popular ingredient in desserts like cakes and parfaits
faults.why: Trivial encyclopedic filler that adds no linguistic value for the learner.

senses.definition: A small, sweet, red fruit with tiny seeds on the outside.

examples.text: 딸기를 깨끗이 씻어서 먹어요.
examples.translation: Wash the strawberries well and eat them.

faults.quote: As a noun, '아침' refers to the time of day, but it
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to note the compound '아침밥' and similar meal words.

notes: When meaning 'breakfast', it is a shortening of '아침밥' (morning meal). The same pattern applies to '점심' (lunchtime / lunch) and '저녁' (evening / dinner).

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: 오늘 아침에는 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.translation: I woke up early this morning.

senses.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.

examples.text: 아침을 먹고 학교에 가요.
examples.translation: I eat breakfast and go to school.

notes: Refers specifically to Western-style (often thick or creamy) soups. Traditional Korean broth dishes are called '국' (guk) or '탕' (tang). Often pronounced and colloquially spelled '스프'.

senses.definition: A Western-style liquid dish, typically thick or creamy, made from vegetables, meat, or stock.

examples.text: 점심으로 따뜻한 수프를 먹었어요.
examples.translation: I had warm soup for lunch.

faults.quote: /ˈka.me.ra da ˈlet.to/
faults.why: Missing syntactic gemination after 'da' (/ˈka.me.ra da lˈlɛt.to/).
Missing plural formation for compound noun ('le camere da letto').

notes: In the plural, only 'camera' changes: 'le camere da letto'.
Often shortened to 'la camera' when the context is clear. Do not confuse this with 'la stanza', which means any room in a house.

senses.definition: A room in a home used for sleeping.

examples.text: La nostra camera da letto è al primo piano.
examples.translation: Our bedroom is on the first floor.

faults.why: Should mention the plural spelling rule ('le camicie' keeps the 'i').

notes: Use 'camicia' for a button-down shirt with a collar. For a T-shirt or soft knitted top, use 'maglietta'.
The plural keeps the 'i': 'le camicie'.

senses.definition: A cloth garment for the upper body with a collar and buttons down the front.

examples.text: Ho comprato una camicia bianca nuova per il colloquio di lavoro.
examples.translation: I bought a new white shirt for the job interview.

faults.quote: meat, flesh
faults.why: 'Flesh' is not used in English for animal meat eaten as food.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with 'la pelle', which is the outer skin
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'meat' with 'skin'; misses the useful 'in carne e ossa' idiom.

notes: Usually singular and uncountable when referring to food in general (e.g., 'non mangio carne' — I don't eat meat).
In the sense of 'flesh', it is very common in the expression 'in carne e ossa' (in the flesh / in person).

senses.definition: Animal tissue eaten as food.

examples.text: A me piace molto la carne ai ferri.
examples.translation: I really like grilled meat.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of a human or animal body, between the skin and the bones.

examples.text: Finalmente ho conosciuto il mio attore preferito in carne e ossa.
examples.translation: I finally met my favorite actor in the flesh.

faults.quote: Add a sliced carrot into the soup.
faults.why: Unnatural preposition in English ('add ... to the soup', not 'into').

senses.definition: A long, orange root vegetable eaten cooked or raw.

examples.text: Aggiungi una carota tagliata a rondelle nella zuppa.
examples.translation: Add a sliced carrot to the soup.

notes: In Vietnamese, 'bánh' covers many baked or steamed foods (both sweet and savory); 'ngọt' (sweet) specifies cakes and pastries, in contrast to 'bánh mì' (bread, baguette).
Takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc' for whole items, and 'miếng' for a slice.

senses.definition: A sweet baked food made from flour and sugar, such as a cake or pastry.

examples.text: Tôi thích ăn bánh ngọt vào buổi chiều.
examples.translation: I like eating pastries in the afternoon.

faults.quote: /baʊ˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong tone and consonant: 'ngã' tone is creaky rising (˦ˀ˥), and initial is /ɓ/.

notes: Takes the classifier 'cơn' (e.g., 'một cơn bão' — a storm).
Refers to severe storms with strong winds, especially tropical storms and typhoons.

senses.definition: Very bad weather with strong winds and heavy rain, especially a tropical cyclone.

examples.text: Cơn bão lớn đang tiến vào đất liền.
examples.translation: The big storm is moving toward the mainland.

faults.quote: /1baːw3 taːŋ2/
faults.why: Corrupted IPA with ASCII digits instead of standard tone letters and implosive /ɓ/.

notes: Also called 'viện bảo tàng'; in everyday speech, the shorter 'bảo tàng' is very common, especially before the museum's type or name (e.g., 'bảo tàng lịch sử').

senses.definition: A building where objects of historical, artistic, or scientific interest are kept and shown to the public.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đi thăm bảo tàng lịch sử vào cuối tuần.
examples.translation: We visit the history museum on the weekend.

faults.quote: Can also be used as a noun meaning 'the beginning' in certain
faults.why: Vague and unhelpful; 'bắt đầu' is also used before 'từ' ('starting from').

notes: Can be used on its own ('Trận đấu bắt đầu'), or followed directly by another verb ('bắt đầu học' — start studying) or by 'từ' ('bắt đầu từ hôm nay' — starting from today).

senses.definition: To start doing something, or to start happening.

examples.text: Trận đấu sắp bắt đầu.
examples.translation: The match is about to begin.

examples.text: Chúng tôi bắt đầu học tiếng Việt.
examples.translation: We are starting to learn Vietnamese.

faults.quote: Often used to describe behavior that violates social norms or common courtesy.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: Formed from the Sino-Vietnamese prefix 'bất' (not, un-) and 'lịch sự' (polite). Takes the preposition 'với' to mark the person one is rude to ('bất lịch sự với ai').

senses.definition: Not polite; showing a lack of good manners or respect for others.

examples.text: Hành động chen hàng của anh ấy rất bất lịch sự.
examples.translation: His act of cutting in line is very impolite.

examples.text: Đừng nói chuyện với người lớn bằng thái độ bất lịch sự như vậy.
examples.translation: Don't talk to adults with such a rude attitude.

faults.quote: This word has two completely unrelated meanings that share the same spelling
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two senses and gender while missing the irregular plural 'le risa'.

faults.quote: La sua battuta ha scatenato un grande riso tra i presenti.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation; 'riso' as laughter is usually used in the plural 'risa' or fixed phrases.

notes: For the 'rice' sense, the plural 'i risi' refers to varieties of rice. For 'laughter', the plural is irregular and feminine: 'le risa' (bursts of laughter).
In everyday speech, 'la risata' is much more common than 'il riso' for 'a laugh'.

senses.definition: The small white or brown grains from a plant that are cooked and eaten.

examples.text: Oggi cucino il risotto con il riso avanzato.
examples.translation: Today I am cooking risotto with the leftover rice.

senses.definition: The action or sound of laughing.

examples.text: Non riusciva a trattenere il riso durante la lezione.
examples.translation: He couldn't hold back his laughter during the lesson.

faults.quote: Used with the definite article il (il sale).
faults.why: Merely restates the headword and gender.

notes: Uncountable in everyday cooking contexts, though the plural 'i sali' is used in chemistry or for bath salts ('i sali da bagno').

senses.definition: A white substance used to season and preserve food.

examples.text: Aggiungi un po' di sale alla pasta.
examples.translation: Add a little salt to the pasta.

faults.quote: Ho visto un po' di sangue dopo il piccolo taglio.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing in Italian; native speakers talk about blood coming out of a cut.

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows through the bodies of humans and animals.

examples.text: Mi esce un po' di sangue dal dito.
examples.translation: A little blood is coming out of my finger.

faults.why: Shades of one meaning; 'segreto' does not mean 'mystery' in general, only a hidden key/method.

faults.quote: Used as a noun, it describes information kept hidden.
faults.why: Restates the definition and POS without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

faults.quote: /seˈɡɾe.to/
faults.why: Uses narrow phonetic tap [ɾ] instead of broad phonemic /r/ and lacks syllable dot.

notes: Commonly used in the phrases 'mantenere un segreto' (to keep a secret) and 'in segreto' (secretly / in secret).

senses.definition: Information kept hidden from others, or a special way of achieving something.

examples.text: Puoi mantenere un segreto?
examples.translation: Can you keep a secret?

faults.quote: /kukˈka.jo/
faults.why: Missing the palatal glide /j/ after /k/; should be /kukˈkja.jo/.
Missing the everyday cooking measurement sense ('tablespoon' / 'spoonful').

notes: Refers to a soup spoon or tablespoon. For a small spoon (teaspoon), use the diminutive 'cucchiaino'.

senses.definition: A utensil with a small shallow bowl at the end, used for eating or serving food.

examples.text: Ho bisogno di un cucchiaio per la zuppa.
examples.translation: I need a spoon for the soup.

senses.definition: The amount a spoon holds, especially as a cooking measure.

examples.text: Aggiungi due cucchiai di olio d'oliva.
examples.translation: Add two tablespoons of olive oil.

faults.why: Should note that the definite article is dropped with singular possessive adjectives ('mio cugino').

notes: Use 'cugino' for a male cousin, 'cugina' for a female cousin, and the plural 'cugini' for a mixed group.
Like other singular family nouns, it does not take the definite article after a possessive adjective ('mio cugino', not 'il mio cugino'), EXCEPT in the plural ('i miei cugini').

senses.definition: A son of one's uncle or aunt (or any cousin in the plural).

examples.text: Mio cugino viene a trovarci questo fine settimana.
examples.translation: My cousin is coming to visit us this weekend.

faults.why: Should note the feminine form 'cuoca' and irregular velar plural 'cuochi'.

notes: The feminine form is 'la cuoca'. The masculine plural is 'i cuochi' (spelled with 'ch' to keep the hard /k/ sound).
Use 'cuoco' for a cook in general; for a head or executive chef, Italians also use 'lo chef'. Do not confuse with 'la cucina' (the kitchen or cuisine).

senses.definition: A person who prepares and cooks food, especially as a job.

examples.text: Il cuoco prepara la cena per tutti gli ospiti.
examples.translation: The cook prepares dinner for all the guests.

faults.why: The emotional sense and the heart shape are mentioned in notes or omitted, not given as senses.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical organ and as the seat of emotions
faults.why: Restates meanings that belong in the senses.

notes: Note: 'by heart' (from memory) is 'a memoria' in Italian, not 'a cuore'.

senses.definition: The organ in the chest that pumps blood through the body.

examples.text: Il medico ha ascoltato il battito del mio cuore.
examples.translation: The doctor listened to the beating of my heart.

senses.definition: A person's feelings, love, or kindness, thought of as a place inside them; also the shape representing it.

examples.text: È una persona di buon cuore.
examples.translation: She is a kind-hearted person.

senses.definition: The central or most important part of something.

examples.text: Vivono nel cuore della città vecchia.
examples.translation: They live in the heart of the old city.

faults.quote: (bed) A soft bag for your head in bed.
faults.why: Italian 'cuscino' is a single concept covering both English 'pillow' and 'cushion'.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with divano, which is a sofa.
faults.why: 'Cuscino' and 'divano' neither look nor sound alike; unhelpful warning.

faults.quote: /kuˈʃiːno/
faults.why: Intervocalic /ʃ/ is always geminate in standard Italian (/kuʃˈʃi.no/).

notes: Covers both a bed 'pillow' and a decorative or seat 'cushion'.

senses.definition: A soft bag filled with feathers, foam, or other soft material, used to rest your head in bed or to sit or lean on.

examples.text: Appoggio la testa sul cuscino.
examples.translation: I rest my head on the pillow.

examples.text: Ci sono molti cuscini colorati sul divano.
examples.translation: There are many colorful cushions on the sofa.

faults.quote: A कंबल is specifically a thick, warm cover for a bed
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: To say 'to cover oneself with a blanket', use the verb ओढ़ना (oṛhnā): कंबल ओढ़ना.
Do not confuse it with चादर (chādar, feminine), which refers to a thin bed sheet or light cover.

senses.definition: A thick cover made of wool or other warm material used to keep warm in bed.

examples.text: सर्दियों में कंबल ओढ़कर सोना अच्छा लगता है।
examples.translation: It feels good to sleep wrapped in a blanket during winter.

faults.quote: A journey to a place and back again.
faults.why: यात्रा simply means journey or travel, not specifically a round trip.

notes: To say 'to travel', use यात्रा करना (yātrā karnā). In casual conversation, सफ़र (safar, masculine) is also very common.
Also used specifically for a religious pilgrimage (तीर्थयात्रा).

senses.definition: An act of traveling from one place to another, or a trip.

examples.text: हमारी यात्रा बहुत सुखद थी।
examples.translation: Our journey was very pleasant.

examples.text: लंबी यात्रा के बाद मैं थक गया हूँ।
examples.translation: I am tired after the long journey.

faults.quote: In more formal Hindi, you might hear 'शीतगृह' (sheetgrih)
faults.why: शीतगृह means industrial cold storage, not a household refrigerator.

notes: Often spelled and pronounced फ्रिज (/pʰɾɪdʒ/) without the dot (nuqta).

senses.definition: A household appliance used for keeping food and drinks cold and fresh.

examples.text: दूध फ़्रिज में रख दो।
examples.translation: Put the milk in the fridge.

faults.quote: alongside the traditional term 'धाय'
faults.why: धाय means wet nurse or midwife, not a hospital nurse.

notes: The formal Hindi word परिचारिका (paricārikā) exists on official signs and forms, but नर्स is used by everyone in daily speech.

senses.definition: A person trained to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital.

examples.text: अस्पताल में नर्स मरीज़ों की देखभाल करती है।
examples.translation: The nurse takes care of patients in the hospital.

faults.quote: Used as a feminine noun; pay attention to verb agreements.
faults.why: Merely restates the grammatical gender already shown in the gender field.

notes: In everyday conversation, speakers very often say ट्रेन (ṭren, feminine) or simply गाड़ी (gāṛī) instead of रेलगाड़ी.

senses.definition: A series of connected railway carriages that transport people or goods along a track.

examples.text: रेलगाड़ी समय पर स्टेशन पहुँची।
examples.translation: The train arrived at the station on time.

examples.text: मुझे रेलगाड़ी से सफ़र करना पसंद है।
examples.translation: I like traveling by train.

faults.quote: A side, direction, or party in a contest or negotiation.
faults.why: มือ does not mean direction or party; left/right hand is ขวามือ/ซ้ายมือ, not มือขวา.

faults.quote: รถวิ่งมาทางมือขวา
faults.why: Unnatural; 'on the right-hand side' in Thai is ทางขวามือ (or ด้านขวา), whereas มือขวา means right hand.

faults.quote: Used figuratively to mean someone skilled or expert in a certain area
faults.why: Restates sense 2 instead of giving useful learner information such as the classifier ข้าง.

notes: The classifier for hands is ข้าง (for one hand) or คู่ (for a pair).
In compounds, มือ often begins words for a player, specialist, or role (e.g. มือใหม่ 'beginner', มืออาชีพ 'professional', มือกลอง 'drummer').

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the palm and fingers.

examples.text: เขาล้างมือ
examples.translation: He washes his hands.

senses.definition: A person with a particular skill, level of experience, or role, especially in a sport, band, or profession (used in compounds).

examples.text: เขาเป็นมืออาชีพ
examples.translation: He is a professional.

faults.quote: This is the standard term for a financial institution.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition; classifier แห่ง or colloquial แบงก์ would be useful.

notes: In everyday spoken Thai, people also often use the English loanword แบงก์ (bɛ́ŋ). The classifier for banks or branches is แห่ง or สาขา.

senses.definition: An institution or building where people deposit, withdraw, and borrow money.

examples.text: ฉันไปธนาคารเพื่อถอนเงิน
examples.translation: I went to the bank to withdraw money.

faults.quote: /rɯ̀.duː.nǎːw/
faults.why: Wrong tone on the first syllable: ฤดู starts with a high tone (/rɯ́.duː.nǎːw/).

notes: In everyday conversation, หน้าหนาว (nâː nǎːw) is more common and less formal than ฤดูหนาว.
In Thailand, this refers to the cool, dry season from around November to February.

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year.

examples.text: ฉันชอบไปเที่ยวภาคเหนือในฤดูหนาว
examples.translation: I like to travel to the north in winter.

faults.quote: It is also used figuratively in some contexts to refer to
faults.why: Hallucinated figurative meaning; กระเป๋าเสื้อ simply means a shirt or jacket pocket.

corrected.headword: กระเป๋าเสื้อ
notes: Composed of กระเป๋า ('bag; pocket') and เสื้อ ('shirt; upper garment'). Compare กระเป๋ากางเกง ('trouser pocket').

senses.definition: A pocket on a shirt, coat, or jacket.

examples.text: เขาใส่ปากกาไว้ในกระเป๋าเสื้อ
examples.translation: He put the pen in his shirt pocket.
examples.matchedForm: กระเป๋าเสื้อ

faults.quote: Used specifically to refer to a person's female child.
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: Composed of ลูก ('child, offspring') and สาว ('young woman'). Compare ลูกชาย ('son').

senses.definition: A person's female child.

examples.text: ฉันมีลูกสาวสองคน
examples.translation: I have two daughters.

faults.quote: /byˈɟyc/
faults.why: Wrong consonant: the middle sound is /j/, not /ɟ/ (/byˈjyc/).
Missing the common everyday sense 'great, important, major'.

faults.quote: Use büyük for physical size, scale, and also to describe someone
faults.why: Restates the senses; a note on consonant softening (büyüklere vs. büyüğüm) or placement is better.

notes: Before an indefinite article ('bir'), it precedes 'bir': 'büyük bir ev' (a big house).

senses.definition: Of considerable physical size, extent, or capacity.

examples.text: Bu büyük bir ev.
examples.translation: This is a large house.

senses.definition: Older in age, or fully grown.

examples.text: Büyük kardeşim üniversitede okuyor.
examples.translation: My older sibling is studying at university.

senses.definition: Important, serious, or significant in scale or degree.

examples.text: Bu bizim için büyük bir fırsat.
examples.translation: This is a great opportunity for us.

faults.quote: In everyday speech, the affectionate diminutive 'büyükanne' or the more casual
faults.why: 'Büyükanne' is neither a diminutive nor casual; it is formal compared to 'anneanne' and 'babaanne'.

faults.quote: Büyükanne bize her hafta sonu lezzetli kurabiyeler pişirir.
faults.why: Without a possessive suffix ('büyükannem'), 'büyükanne' as a bare subject sounds unnatural.

notes: A compound of 'büyük' (big/great) and 'anne' (mother). In everyday speech, speakers usually specify the side of the family: 'anneanne' (mother's mother) or 'babaanne' (father's mother), or use the affectionate 'nine'.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Büyükannem bize her hafta sonu lezzetli kurabiyeler yapar.
examples.translation: My grandmother makes us delicious cookies every weekend.

faults.quote: Dedede is a much more common, everyday alternative for grandfather
faults.why: Misspelled Turkish word: should be 'dede', not 'dedede'.

faults.quote: Büyükbaba her yaz köyden bize gelir.
faults.why: Needs a possessive suffix ('büyükbabam') to sound natural as a subject.

notes: A compound of 'büyük' (big/great) and 'baba' (father). In everyday speech, 'dede' is much more common, while 'büyükbaba' sounds somewhat more formal.

senses.definition: The father of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Büyükbabam her yaz köyden bize gelir.
examples.translation: My grandfather comes to visit us from the village every summer.

faults.quote: Unlike 'kar' (snow), which refers to frozen precipitation, 'buz' refers specifically
faults.why: Explaining the difference between ice and snow is unnecessary filler.

notes: Often used in the expression 'buz gibi' (ice-cold) to describe very cold drinks, weather, or hands.

senses.definition: Water that has frozen solid.

examples.text: Bardaktaki buz eridi.
examples.translation: The ice in the glass melted.

notes: A compound of 'buz' (ice) and 'dolap' (cupboard). Because it ends in the compound suffix '-ı', an 'n' is added before case suffixes: 'buzdolabında' (in the fridge), 'buzdolabına' (into the fridge).

senses.definition: An appliance used for keeping food and drinks cold.

examples.text: Sütü buzdolabına koydum.
examples.translation: I put the milk in the refrigerator.

faults.quote: unlike English, which treats cheese as an uncountable mass noun
faults.why: English also uses plural 'cheeses' for varieties; the contrast is false and filler.

notes: The plural formaggi has a single -i (not -ii): un formaggio, i formaggi.

senses.definition: A food made from milk, produced in many textures and flavors.

examples.text: Amo mangiare il formaggio con un buon bicchiere di vino.
examples.translation: I love eating cheese with a good glass of wine.

faults.quote: Il frate aiuta i poveri nel convento.
faults.why: Uses the noun 'frate' instead of the headword 'fratello'.

faults.quote: A member of a male religious order.
faults.why: Marginal religious sense for A2; the everyday word for friar is 'frate'.
Missing essential A1/A2 grammar note: singular family members drop the article with possessives.

notes: Like other singular family members, it takes no article with possessive adjectives (mio fratello, not il mio fratello), except in the plural (i miei fratelli) or with loro (il loro fratello).
