examples.text: Ho freddo, ho bisogno di un'altra coperta.
examples.translation: I'm cold, I need another blanket.

faults.quote: When referring to yourself or a colleague as a teacher, use
faults.why: Contains the honorific suffix -님, so it is never used to refer to oneself.

faults.quote: While it means 'teacher', it is also used as a universal
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Because it contains the honorific suffix -님 (-nim), never use it to refer to yourself; for your own occupation, say 교사 (gyosa) or 선생 (seonsaeng).
Often used to address doctors (의사 선생님) or other respected professionals, as well as strangers of high status or older age.

senses.definition: A person who teaches at a school or gives instruction in a subject.

examples.text: 선생님께서 우리에게 한국어를 가르쳐 주십니다.
examples.translation: The teacher teaches us Korean.

senses.definition: A respectful title used after someone's name or alone to address a professional or an older person politely.

examples.text: 김 선생님, 질문이 하나 있습니다.
examples.translation: Mr. Kim, I have a question.

faults.quote: 휴가 (hyu-ga) is the most common word for a vacation
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss.

faults.quote: A period of time off from work or school
faults.why: 휴가 is leave from work or military service; school breaks are 방학, as note[1] says.

notes: Used for time off from work or military service; for school or university breaks, use 방학 (banghak).
Commonly used in the phrases 휴가를 가다 (to go on vacation) and 휴가를 내다 (to take leave from work).

senses.definition: A period of time off from work or duty, often used for traveling or resting.

examples.text: 다음 달에 휴가를 가요.
examples.translation: I am going on vacation next month.

faults.quote: Used both for the time of day after the afternoon and
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given.

notes: In sense 2, it is short for 저녁 식사 (evening meal) or 저녁밥; like 아침 (morning/breakfast) and 점심 (noon/lunch), the time word alone commonly names the meal.
Contrast with 밤 (bam), which refers to night when it is dark.

senses.definition: The part of the day between the end of the afternoon and night.

examples.text: 오늘 저녁에 시간이 있어요?
examples.translation: Do you have time this evening?

senses.definition: The main meal eaten in the evening.

examples.text: 우리 같이 저녁 먹을까요?
examples.translation: Shall we eat dinner together?

faults.quote: 설탕 is the most common word for table sugar. In Korean
faults.why: Restates the gloss and adds culinary trivia unhelpful for an A2 learner.

senses.definition: A sweet crystalline substance added to food and drinks to make them sweet.

examples.text: 커피에 설탕을 넣어 드릴까요?
examples.translation: Would you like me to put sugar in your coffee?

faults.quote: 할머니 is used both for one's own grandmother and as a
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: In traditional usage, 할머니 alone refers to one's paternal grandmother, while 외할머니 (oehalmeoni) specifies one's maternal grandmother, though both are addressed as 할머니.
A more formal honorific form, 할머님 (halmeonim), is often used when speaking to or about someone else's grandmother.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: 주말에 할머니 댁에 갔어요.
examples.translation: I went to my grandmother's house on the weekend.

senses.definition: A polite way to refer to or address an elderly woman who is not a relative.

examples.text: 지하철에서 할머니께 자리를 양보했어요.
examples.translation: I gave up my seat to an elderly woman on the subway.

faults.quote: Used for both a private garden next to a house and
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; broken plural حَدَائِق is more useful.

notes: Plural: حَدَائِق (ḥadāʾiq).

senses.definition: A piece of land next to a house with flowers, grass, or trees.

examples.text: فِي حَدِيقَةِ بَيْتِنَا أَزْهَارٌ جَمِيلَةٌ.
examples.translation: There are beautiful flowers in the garden of our house.

senses.definition: A public area with trees and grass where people go to walk and relax.

examples.text: نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ.
examples.translation: We go to the park on Friday.

faults.quote: Used for eating liquid or semi-liquid foods like soup or yogurt.
faults.why: Explains what a spoon is in the real world; broken plural مَلَاعِق is needed.

notes: Plural: مَلَاعِق (malāʿiq).

senses.definition: A small utensil with a shallow bowl at the end, used for eating or stirring food.

examples.text: اِسْتَخْدِمِ المِلْعَقَةَ لِتَنَاوُلِ الشُّورْبَةِ.
examples.translation: Use the spoon to eat the soup.

notes: Plural: مَرَاحِيض (marāḥīḍ). In everyday speech, people more politely ask for الحَمَّام (al-ḥammām, the bathroom) or دَوْرَة المِيَاه (dawrat al-miyāh, the restroom).

senses.definition: A toilet bowl, or a small room containing a toilet.

examples.text: أَيْنَ المِرْحَاضُ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
examples.translation: Where is the toilet, please?

faults.quote: /baˈlad/
faults.why: Wrong stress; two light syllables stress the first: /ˈba.lad/.

faults.quote: Plural is أَبْلَاد (ablād) or بِلَاد (bilād)
faults.why: Standard plurals are بُلْدَان and بِلَاد, not أَبْلَاد; also בَلَد is both masculine and feminine.

notes: Can be treated as masculine or feminine. Common plurals are بِلَاد (bilād) and بُلْدَان (buldān).

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and territory.

examples.text: هَذَا الْبَلَدُ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This country is very beautiful.

senses.definition: A town, city, or local area, especially the place where one comes from.

examples.text: رَجَعْتُ إِلَى بَلَدِي بَعْدَ غِيَابٍ طَوِيلٍ.
examples.translation: I returned to my hometown after a long absence.

faults.quote: Used mainly for the piece of furniture you sleep on in
faults.why: Restates the definition; broken plural أَسِرَّة is what a learner needs.

faults.quote: السرير مريح جدا في غرفة النوم.
faults.why: Awkward word order and phrasing in both Arabic and English.

notes: Plural: أَسِرَّة (ʾasirra).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for sleeping on.

examples.text: هَذَا السَّرِيرُ مُرِيحٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This bed is very comfortable.

faults.quote: Note that while technically a fruit, tomatoes are exclusively treated as vegetables
faults.why: Botanical trivia identical to English; misses useful grammar like the -a accusative/genitive singular ending.

notes: Like many fruits and vegetables, it takes the ending -a in both the genitive and accusative singular (e.g., jem pomidora — I'm eating a tomato).

senses.definition: A soft, red, round fruit eaten raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable.

examples.text: Pokrój pomidora do sałatki.
examples.translation: Slice a tomato for the salad.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: Single-word subordinating conjunction, not a multi-word expression.

faults.quote: Ponieważ is a standard conjunction used to introduce a reason or cause
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage information.

notes: Slightly more formal than bo, which is preferred in everyday conversation. Always preceded by a comma when introducing a clause inside a sentence.

senses.definition: Used to introduce a reason or cause.

examples.text: Zostaję w domu, ponieważ pada deszcz.
examples.translation: I am staying home because it is raining.

faults.quote: Used with the preposition 'po' in phrases like 'po południu'
faults.why: 'po południu' uses the noun 'południe' (noon), not 'popołudnie' (afternoon).

notes: To say 'in the afternoon', Polish normally uses the two-word phrase po południu (literally 'after noon'), or the instrumental plural popołudniami for 'in the afternoons'.

senses.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening.

examples.text: Mam dzisiaj wolne popołudnie.
examples.translation: I have a free afternoon today.

faults.quote: A flat case or folder for carrying documents, drawings, or loose papers.
faults.why: In modern Polish, 'portfel' does not mean briefcase or physical folder (that is 'teczka').

faults.quote: wallet; briefcase
faults.why: Includes the false gloss 'briefcase'.

notes: Takes the ending -a in the genitive singular (szukam portfela), like many inanimate masculine nouns for small everyday objects.

senses.definition: A small, flat folding case for carrying paper money, bank cards, and documents.

examples.text: Zapomniałem portfela w domu i nie mogę zapłacić za zakupy.
examples.translation: I left my wallet at home and cannot pay for the shopping.

faults.quote: stress shifts in the plural to го́ры (nominative) and горы́ (genitive)
faults.why: гор́ы is genitive singular, not plural (genitive plural is гор); misses accusative singular го́ру.

notes: The stress shifts to the first syllable in the accusative singular (го́ру) and nominative/accusative plural (го́ры). The genitive plural is гор.

senses.definition: A very high natural elevation of earth and rock.

examples.text: Мы поднялись на высокую гору.
examples.translation: We climbed a high mountain.

senses.definition: A large pile or amount of something (followed by the genitive).

examples.text: На столе лежала гора писем.
examples.translation: A mountain of letters lay on the table.

faults.quote: Её почерк — это красивое письмо.
faults.why: Unnatural Russian; 'письмо' is not used to describe someone's handwriting like this.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'книга' (book)
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'письмо' with 'книга'; misses irregular plural 'пи́сьма' (genitive 'пи́сем').

notes: In the plural, the stress shifts to the first syllable: пи́сьма (nominative), пи́сем (genitive).
Sense 2 ('writing') is uncountable and used only in the singular, often for language skills (чтение и письмо — reading and writing).

senses.definition: A written message sent by post or email.

examples.text: Я получил письмо от друга.
examples.translation: I received a letter from a friend.

senses.definition: The activity or skill of writing, or a system of writing.

examples.text: На уроке мы тренируем чтение и письмо.
examples.translation: In class we practice reading and writing.

faults.why: Missing the essential locative form 'в снегу́ / на снегу́' and common collocation 'идёт снег'.

notes: To say 'it is snowing', Russian uses the verb идти (to go): идёт снег.
After the prepositions в and на to indicate location, it takes the stressed ending -у́: в снегу́ (in the snow), на снегу́ (on the snow).

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky and cover the ground.

examples.text: На улице идёт сильный снег.
examples.translation: It is snowing heavily outside.

faults.quote: female cat, cat
faults.why: 'cat' is the primary translation in everyday use; 'female cat' as primary gloss is over-specific.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a female cat, though often used generally
faults.why: Fails to name the male counterpart 'кот' or the fleeting vowel in genitive plural 'ко́шек'.

notes: Ко́шка is both the general word for a cat of unknown sex and the word for a female cat; a male cat is кот.
The genitive and accusative plural form has a fleeting vowel: ко́шек.

senses.definition: A small furry domestic animal often kept as a pet, or specifically a female one.

examples.text: Маленькая кошка спит на диване.
examples.translation: The small cat is sleeping on the sofa.

faults.quote: 모자 refers to any type of headgear, whether it has a
faults.why: Restates the glosses; misses the essential verb collocation 쓰다/벗다.

notes: Takes the verb 쓰다 (to put on/wear on the head), not 입다, and 벗다 (to take off).

senses.definition: A covering worn on the head for warmth, protection from the sun, or style.

examples.text: 햇빛이 너무 강해서 모자를 썼어요.
examples.translation: The sun was so strong that I wore a hat.

faults.quote: The meat of a pig, used as food.
faults.why: 돼지 alone does not mean 'pork'; pork is the compound 돼지고기.

faults.quote: 오늘 저녁은 돼지 고기를 먹을 거예요.
faults.why: Uses the compound 돼지고기 (misspelled with a space) rather than 돼지.

faults.quote: pig; pork
faults.why: 돼지 does not mean 'pork'.

notes: For the meat (pork), use 돼지고기.
Also used informally to call someone who eats a lot or is greedy a 'pig'.

senses.definition: A pink or bristly farm animal with a flat snout, kept for its meat.

examples.text: 농장에 귀여운 돼지가 있어요.
examples.translation: There is a cute pig on the farm.

faults.quote: While '칼' is the general word for knife, it is also
faults.why: Vague filler; better to note that 칼 covers knives, swords, and cutters.

notes: Covers any bladed tool or weapon, including kitchen knives (식칼), utility knives (커터칼), and swords.

senses.definition: A sharp metal blade with a handle, used for cutting or as a weapon.

examples.text: 칼을 조심해서 사용하세요.
examples.translation: Please use the knife carefully.

faults.quote: 바닥 most commonly refers to the floor of a room or
faults.why: Restates the two senses in the entry without adding useful learner guidance.

notes: Refers to the surface you walk or sit on (indoors or outdoors), not a building storey (which is 층).

senses.definition: The lower surface of a room, or the ground outside, that people walk or sit on.

examples.text: 바닥에 앉아서 이야기를 나눴어요.
examples.translation: We sat on the floor and talked.

senses.definition: The lowest inside or underside surface of a container, body of water, or object.

examples.text: 상자 바닥에 구멍이 뚫려 있어요.
examples.translation: There is a hole in the bottom of the box.

faults.quote: village; countryside
faults.why: Includes 'countryside', which is absent from the sense glosses (and actually means εξοχή).

notes: Often used to refer to one's family hometown or ancestral village (e.g., πάμε στο χωριό — we're going to our family village).

senses.definition: A very small town in the countryside.

examples.text: Το καλοκαίρι πάμε στο χωριό.
examples.translation: In the summer we go to the village.

faults.quote: The child of one's uncle or aunt.
faults.why: Defines any cousin, but the masculine noun ο ξάδερφος refers specifically to a male cousin.

notes: For a female cousin, use η ξαδέρφη. The plural οι ξάδερφοι (or the neuter τα ξαδέρφια) is used for a mixed group.
Also spelled and pronounced ξάδελφος, or more formally εξάδελφος.

senses.definition: A son of one's uncle or aunt.

examples.text: Ο ξάδερφός μου μένει στην Αθήνα.
examples.translation: My cousin lives in Athens.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense of 'can / tin' (for drinks or canned food) and 'carton/pack'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'κάλυμμα', which refers specifically to a cover
faults.why: Learners have no reason to confuse κουτί with κάλυμμα.

notes: The diminutive το κουτάκι is the most common word for a drink can (ένα κουτάκι μπίρα — a can of beer).

senses.definition: A rigid container with flat sides, used for storing or moving things.

examples.text: Το δώρο ήταν μέσα σε ένα μεγάλο κουτί.
examples.translation: The gift was inside a big box.

senses.definition: A small sealed cardboard or metal container in which food, drink, or other items are sold.

examples.text: Αγόρασα ένα κουτί γάλα.
examples.translation: I bought a carton of milk.

faults.quote: Θέλω λίγο χυμό από το λεμόνι στη σαλάτα.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing; in Greek one simply says «Θέλω λίγο λεμόνι στη σαλάτα».

notes: Do not confuse the fruit (το λεμόνι, neuter) with the lemon tree (η λεμονιά, feminine).

senses.definition: A sour, yellow citrus fruit used in cooking and drinks.

examples.text: Θέλω λίγο λεμόνι στη σαλάτα.
examples.translation: I want a little lemon on the salad.

faults.quote: Note that it is always used in the singular form (το παντελόνι)
faults.why: False claim: it has a normal plural (τα παντελόνια) used for more than one pair.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'το σορτς' (shorts)
faults.why: No learner would confuse παντελόνι with σορτς.

notes: Unlike English 'trousers' or 'pants', one pair is singular in Greek: ένα παντελόνι (a pair of trousers). The plural τα παντελόνια means several pairs.

senses.definition: An piece of clothing covering the body from the waist to the ankles, with a separate part for each leg.

examples.text: Αγόρασα ένα μπλε παντελόνι για τη δουλειά.
examples.translation: I bought a pair of blue trousers for work.

faults.quote: A foolish person who lacks initiative and acts silly.
faults.why: Colloquial 'banana' means a weak, passive person (pushover/wimp), not someone who acts silly.

faults.quote: idiot, wimp, fool
faults.why: 'Idiot' and 'fool' are inaccurate; 'wimp' or 'pushover' is the right meaning.

faults.quote: banana; silly person
faults.why: Should say 'wimp' or 'pushover' instead of 'silly person'.

faults.quote: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'banana' is not only the yellow fruit
faults.why: merely restates the two senses; better to note gender usage for sense 2.

notes: When referring to a passive person (sense 2), 'banana' is informal and changes article according to the person's gender (e.g., 'um banana').

senses.definition: A long curved fruit with yellow or green skin and sweet soft flesh inside.

examples.text: Comi uma banana no café da manhã.
examples.translation: I ate a banana for breakfast.

senses.definition: An informal term for a weak, timid person who lacks initiative and lets others take advantage of them.

examples.text: Não seja banana e vá falar com ela.
examples.translation: Don't be a wimp and go talk to her.

faults.quote: /bi.si.klɛ.tɐ/
faults.why: Missing the primary stress mark before the stressed syllable: /bi.siˈklɛ.tɐ/.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'moto' (motorcycle), which has an engine.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'bicicleta' with 'moto'; replace with useful preposition usage.

notes: Use 'andar de bicicleta' for 'to ride a bike'. In casual Brazilian speech, the English word 'bike' (pronounced /ˈbaj.ki/) is also very common.

senses.definition: A vehicle with two wheels that you move by pushing pedals with your feet.

examples.text: Eu vou trabalhar de bicicleta todos os dias.
examples.translation: I go to work by bicycle every day.

faults.quote: Küvet specifically refers to the bathtub you sit or lie in
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and contrasts two unrelated English words (bathtub vs. shower).

faults.quote: Sıcak bir küvet keyfi bütün yorgunluğumu aldı.
faults.why: Banyo keyfi is natural for a bath; küvet refers to the physical fixture itself.

notes: Refers only to the physical tub; for the room use 'banyo', and for the act of taking a bath use 'banyo yapmak'.

senses.definition: A large container that you fill with water and sit or lie in to wash your body.

examples.text: Küveti sıcak suyla doldurdum.
examples.translation: I filled the bathtub with hot water.

notes: Traditional terms specify the exact relation (such as 'amca oğlu' for a paternal uncle's son, or 'teyze kızı' for a maternal aunt's daughter), whereas 'kuzen' is used for any cousin regardless of gender or side of the family.

senses.definition: A child of one's uncle or aunt.

examples.text: Yaz tatilinde kuzenimle sahilde vakit geçirdik.
examples.translation: During the summer holiday, I spent time at the beach with my cousin.

faults.quote: Parkta oynayan tatlı bir kız çocuk gördüm.
faults.why: In indefinite singular, Turkish speakers almost always say 'bir kız çocuğu', with the compound suffix.

faults.quote: In Turkish, nouns modifying other nouns often appear in their bare stem
faults.why: Vague grammar lecture that misses the actual usage rule ('kız çocuğu' vs 'kız çocuk').

notes: In everyday speech, this is most often used with the compound suffix as 'kız çocuğu' (singular) or 'kız çocukları' (plural). Simply 'kız' is much more common for 'girl' or 'daughter'.

senses.definition: A female child; a girl or daughter.

examples.text: Onların iki kız çocuğu var.
examples.translation: They have two daughters.

faults.quote: /kɯz caɾˈceʃ/
faults.why: Wrong transcription for 'kardeş': has /c/ instead of /k/ and /d/.

notes: Composed of 'kız' (girl/female) and 'kardeş' (sibling), as 'kardeş' alone is gender-neutral.
Can refer to any sister, though 'abla' specifically means 'older sister', so 'kız kardeş' often implies a younger sister.

senses.definition: A female sibling.

examples.text: Kız kardeşimin adresi bu.
examples.translation: This is my sister's address.

faults.quote: Used both to mean a female child or young person (girl) and
faults.why: Simply restates the two senses and glosses already given in the entry.

notes: When used with a possessive suffix (such as 'kızım' or 'kızı'), it almost always means 'daughter' rather than 'girl'.
Also used before another noun to indicate gender, as in 'kız kardeş' (sister) or 'kız arkadaş' (girlfriend).

senses.definition: A female child or young woman.

examples.text: O küçük kız parkta oynuyor.
examples.translation: That little girl is playing in the park.

senses.definition: A person's female child.

examples.text: Yarın kızımla markete gideceğiz.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will go to the grocery store with my daughter.

faults.quote: Terkejut means surprised or shocked, often happening in an instant
faults.why: Restates the glosses and definition without adding useful usage information.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with terkejut used as a sudden involuntary physical
faults.why: Compares the word to itself and falsely denies that it means 'startled'.

faults.quote: /tərˈkə.dʒʊt/
faults.why: Schwa cannot carry primary stress in Indonesian; stress falls on the final syllable /tər.kəˈdʒʊt/.

notes: More formal than its everyday synonym 'kaget'.
Often followed by a verb (e.g., 'terkejut mendengar' – surprised to hear) or prepositions like 'dengan' or 'akan'.

senses.definition: Feeling sudden surprise or shock because of something unexpected.

examples.text: Dia terkejut saat mendengar berita itu.
examples.translation: He was surprised when he heard the news.

faults.quote: Used when someone or something misses a deadline or arrives after
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0.

faults.quote: To become aware of something too late to take action
faults.why: Not a separate meaning; 'realizing' comes from 'sadar' in the example, and the definition is a verb.

faults.quote: late; delayed
faults.why: Includes 'delayed', which does not appear in any sense's glosses.

notes: Do not confuse with the root word 'lambat' (slow in speed). 'Terlambat' means behind schedule or past the proper time.
In everyday speech, the colloquial synonym 'telat' is very common.

senses.definition: Arriving, happening, or done after the expected, planned, or proper time.

examples.text: Maaf, saya terlambat karena macet.
examples.translation: Sorry, I am late because of traffic.

examples.text: Saya sadar saya sudah terlambat untuk mendaftar.
examples.translation: I realized I was already too late to register.

faults.quote: /tərˈsə.ɲum/
faults.why: Schwa does not take primary stress in Indonesian; stress is on the final syllable /tər.səˈɲum/.

faults.quote: the ter- prefix here often indicates an involuntary or natural action
faults.why: Misleading; 'tersenyum' is the standard verb for smiling, whether deliberate or spontaneous.

notes: Formed from the noun 'senyum' (a smile). In informal speech, the root 'senyum' is often used directly as a verb.
Takes the preposition 'kepada' or 'pada' for the person smiled at (e.g., 'tersenyum kepada saya' – smile at me).

senses.definition: To make a happy or friendly expression by curving the corners of your mouth upwards.

examples.text: Dia tersenyum ketika melihat anak itu bermain.
examples.translation: She smiled when she saw the child playing.

faults.quote: Tertawa is the standard word for laughing out loud.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding grammar or usage help for a beginner.

notes: Intransitive. To say 'laugh at someone/something', use the transitive form 'menertawakan'.
In casual speech, the shortened form 'ketawa' is very common.

senses.definition: To make the sounds and movements of the face and body that show you think something is funny.

examples.text: Dia tertawa mendengar lelucon itu.
examples.translation: He laughed when he heard that joke.

faults.quote: /təˈtang.ga/
faults.why: Uses spelling 'ng' instead of IPA velar nasal /ŋ/ (/təˈtaŋ.ɡa/).

faults.quote: Used to refer generally to people living nearby, or specifically to

faults.quote: (afternoon) The time of day from noon until evening. | glosses en: afternoon, P.M.

notes: Placed before the hour to mean 'p.m.' (e.g., 오후 3시 = 3:00 p.m.). Its opposite is '오전' (morning; a.m.).

senses.definition: The time of day from noon until evening, or from noon until midnight when telling time.

examples.text: 오후 세 시에 만나요.
examples.translation: Let's meet at 3 p.m.

faults.quote: (distance) A traditional Korean unit of distance equal to about two kilometers.
faults.why: '오 리' (five li) is two separate words, not a lexicalized sense of '오리', and archaic for A2.

faults.quote: duck; five li (distance)
faults.why: Includes the spurious 'five li' sense.

faults.quote: 오리 has two completely unrelated meanings that share the exact same spelling
faults.why: Explains the spurious '오 리' (five li) sense, which is written with a space.

senses.definition: A water bird with a flat beak, webbed feet, and short legs.

examples.text: 호수에 오리들이 헤엄치고 있어요.
examples.translation: Ducks are swimming in the lake.

faults.quote: use 'disponibile' when asking if someone is free to meet up.
faults.why: False: 'Sei libero stasera?' is the standard Italian way to ask if someone is free.
Should warn learners to use 'gratuito' or 'gratis' for 'free of charge'.

notes: For 'free of charge' (costing no money), Italian usually uses 'gratuito' or the adverb 'gratis' rather than 'libero' (though 'ingresso libero' is used for 'free admission').

senses.definition: Of a place or thing: available to be used or occupied; of a person or time: without work or plans.

examples.text: Il posto accanto a me è libero.
examples.translation: The seat next to me is free.

examples.text: Sei libero stasera?
examples.translation: Are you free tonight?

senses.definition: Not under the control of another; able to act or choose as one wants.

examples.text: Siamo liberi di scegliere cosa fare.
examples.translation: We are free to choose what to do.

notes: Use 'specchio' with the reflexive verb 'guardarsi' ('guardarsi allo specchio' or 'nello specchio') to say 'to look at oneself in the mirror'.

senses.definition: A surface of glass that reflects the image of whatever is in front of it.

examples.text: Mi guardo allo specchio prima di uscire.
examples.translation: I look at myself in the mirror before going out.

faults.why: Missing irregular plural 'gli stomachi' (and common contrast with 'pancia' for outer belly).

notes: The plural is 'gli stomachi', spelled with 'ch' to keep the hard /k/ sound.
Usually refers to the internal digestive organ; for the outside belly or tummy, 'la pancia' is more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: The organ inside the body where food goes to be digested.

examples.text: Ho mal di stomaco dopo aver mangiato troppo.
examples.translation: I have a stomachache after eating too much.

faults.quote: Use 'lo studente' with masculine singular nouns starting s+consonant or z.
faults.why: Garbled wording ('use lo studente with nouns'); should explain the article 'lo' and plural 'gli'.

notes: The feminine form is 'la studentessa' (plural 'le studentesse').
Because it starts with 's' + consonant, the masculine forms take the articles 'lo' / 'uno' in the singular and 'gli' in the plural ('gli studenti').

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a secondary school, college, or university.

examples.text: Lo studente legge un libro interessante in biblioteca.
examples.translation: The student is reading an interesting book in the library.

notes: In the Netherlands, 'student' is used for someone in higher or vocational education (universiteit, hbo, mbo). For a pupil in primary or secondary school, use 'leerling' or 'scholier'.
The feminine form is 'studente'.

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a university or college.

examples.text: De student studeert rechten aan de universiteit.
examples.translation: The student studies law at the university.

faults.quote: /ˈsʏpərˌmɑrkt/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: the first vowel in 'supermarkt' is long /y/, not short /ʏ/.

faults.quote: Takes the article 'de', like most compound nouns ending in '-markt'.
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword 'de supermarkt'.

senses.definition: A large self-service shop that sells food, drinks, and household goods.

examples.text: Ik ga even naar de supermarkt om brood te halen.
examples.translation: I'm just going to the supermarket to get some bread.

faults.why: Dutch 'taart' is one concept covering large cakes, pies, and tarts; splitting mirrors English.

faults.quote: De bakker maakt heerlijke appeltaart met kaneel.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'appeltaart' rather than the word 'taart' itself.

notes: 'Taart' covers both layered celebration cakes and sweet baked pies or tarts (such as 'appeltaart'). For a loaf cake such as pound cake, Dutch uses 'cake'; for a biscuit or cookie, 'koek' or 'koekje'.

senses.definition: A large sweet baked food, often with cream, fruit, or icing, cut into slices and eaten at celebrations or with coffee.

examples.text: We eten morgen taart omdat opa jarig is.
examples.translation: We're having cake tomorrow because it's grandpa's birthday.

examples.text: De bakker bakt een heerlijke taart met appels en kaneel.
examples.translation: The baker is baking a delicious pie with apples and cinnamon.

faults.quote: table; multiplication table; board
faults.why: 'board' is not in any sense.

faults.quote: Used for both furniture and mathematical multiplication tables.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

notes: Often used without an article in fixed phrases about meals: 'aan tafel zitten' (to sit at the table), 'Aan tafel!' (Dinner's ready!), 'de tafel dekken / afruimen' (to set / clear the table).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs, used for eating, writing, or working.

examples.text: De borden staan op de tafel.
examples.translation: The plates are on the table.

senses.definition: A list of multiplication facts for a given number, learned at school.

examples.text: Op school leren de kinderen vandaag de tafel van zeven.
examples.translation: At school today the children are learning the seven times table.

faults.quote: Note that although 'água' starts with a, it is a feminine noun
faults.why: Nouns starting with -a and ending in -a are regularly feminine in Portuguese; restates gender.

faults.quote: (nature) A large body of liquid, such as that found in oceans
faults.why: Drinking water and seawater are the same core meaning of H2O for an A2 learner.

notes: Usually uncountable, like English 'water', though the plural 'águas' is used for bodies of water or bottles of water (e.g., 'duas águas').

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain, fills rivers and seas, and is drunk by people and animals.

examples.text: Eu bebo muita água durante o dia.
examples.translation: I drink a lot of water during the day.

examples.text: A água do mar está gelada hoje.
examples.translation: The sea water is cold today.

faults.quote: /a.aˈɾɐ̃.ɲɐ/
faults.why: Includes the definite article 'a' in the transcription; must be the lemma only (/aˈɾɐ̃.ɲɐ/).

faults.quote: Even though it is feminine, remember to use 'a' before it
faults.why: Nonsensical wording ('even though it is feminine, use the feminine article') and restates gender.

faults.quote: usually with the adjective 'teia'
faults.why: 'Teia' is a noun meaning 'web' (teia de aranha), not an adjective.

notes: A spider's web is called 'teia de aranha'.

senses.definition: A small creature with eight legs that spins webs to catch insects.

examples.text: A aranha subiu pela parede.
examples.translation: The spider climbed up the wall.

faults.quote: /ˈaʁ.vi.ɾi/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in the middle syllable; 'árvore' has /o/ or /u/, not /i/ (/ˈaʁ.vo.ɾi/).

notes: Feminine ('a árvore'), even though many nouns ending in -e are masculine in Portuguese.

senses.definition: A tall plant with a wooden trunk, branches, and leaves.

faults.quote: 네 is the standard polite way to say 'yes' in Korean.
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the senses; missing comparison with 예 and 응, or negative-question agreement.

notes: Interchangeable with 예, which sounds slightly more formal; in casual speech with friends, use 응 or 어.
Answers whether the speaker agrees with the statement: to 'You didn't eat?', 네 means 'Yes (that's right, I didn't eat)'.

senses.definition: Used to express polite agreement or to answer 'yes'.

examples.text: 네, 알겠습니다.
examples.translation: Yes, I understand.

senses.definition: Used to show that you are listening, answer when called, or ask someone to repeat themselves.

examples.text: 네? 뭐라고 하셨어요?
examples.translation: Pardon? What did you say?

faults.why: Should mention pronunciation assimilation [고맙씀니다] and the common polite form 고마워요.

notes: Pronounced [고맙씀니다], as ㅂ before ㄴ nasalizes to ㅁ.
Formal polite form of 고맙다; in everyday polite conversation, 고마워요 is also common, and 고마워 is used with close friends.
Very similar to 감사합니다, which is Sino-Korean and slightly more formal in business or public settings.

senses.definition: Polite expression used to thank someone.

examples.text: 도와주셔서 고맙습니다.
examples.translation: Thank you for helping me.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 함께 is an adverb, not a multi-word or conversational expression.

notes: Often used after a noun with the particle 과/와, (으)랑, or 하고 ('together with ...').
Very similar to 같이, which is more common in everyday speech, whereas 함께 sounds slightly more formal or written.

senses.definition: In company with another person or thing; doing something jointly.

examples.text: 친구와 함께 영화를 보러 갔어요.
examples.translation: I went to see a movie with my friend.

notes: Literally 'go in peace'. Said when you are staying and the other person is leaving, or when both of you are leaving.
If you are leaving and the other person is staying, say 안녕히 계세요 ('stay in peace') instead.

senses.definition: Polite farewell said to someone who is leaving.

examples.text: 내일 봐요. 안녕히 가세요!
examples.translation: See you tomorrow. Goodbye!

faults.quote: (refusal) A polite word ... / (disagreement) A polite word ...
faults.why: Both senses are the same meaning ('no') in slightly different contexts.
Learners need to know how 아니요 works with negative questions in Korean.

notes: In casual speech with close friends or children, use 아니 instead.
Disagrees with the statement inside the question: to 'You didn't eat?', 아니요 means 'No (that's not true — I did eat)'.

senses.definition: Polite word used to give a negative answer, disagree, or decline an offer or compliment.

examples.text: 아니요, 아직 안 갔어요.
examples.translation: No, I haven't gone yet.

examples.text: 아니요, 괜찮습니다.
examples.translation: No, that's fine.

faults.quote: Note that '袜子' is a collective noun for both individual socks
faults.why: Wordy and calls a normal Chinese noun a 'collective noun'; just give the classifiers.

notes: Takes the measure word 双 (shuāng) for a pair and 只 (zhī) for a single sock.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the foot, usually inside a shoe.

examples.text: 今天天气很冷，我要穿厚袜子。
examples.translation: It is very cold today, so I need to wear thick socks.

faults.quote: 我想吃一碗牛肉面条。
faults.why: Unnatural; dish names use 面 (牛肉面), while 面条 refers to the food or uncooked noodles.

faults.quote: Unlike the English word 'noodles' which can be plural, 'miàntiáo' can
faults.why: Explains general Chinese grammar (lack of plural inflection) rather than this word.

notes: Often shortened to 面 (miàn), especially in the names of dishes like 牛肉面 (niúròumiàn, beef noodles).

senses.definition: A food made from flour and water, shaped into long, thin strips and boiled.

examples.text: 今天晚上我们吃面条吧。
examples.translation: Let's eat noodles tonight.

faults.quote: A place where children learn.
faults.why: Too narrow; 学校 includes high schools, colleges, and universities, not only schools for children.
Missing the common measure word 所 (suǒ) or 家 (jiā).

notes: Takes the measure word 所 (suǒ), as in 一所学校 (a school).
Use 上学 (shàng xué) for going to school as a student, and 放学 (fàng xué) for finishing school for the day.

senses.definition: A place where students go to be educated, from primary school to university.

examples.text: 孩子们每天早上都去学校上课。
examples.translation: The children go to school every morning for class.

faults.quote: T xù shān
faults.why: Should give full pinyin pronunciation (tī xù shān) for the Latin letter T.

notes: Often shortened to T恤 (tī xù) in everyday speech. Takes the measure word 件 (jiàn).
Do not confuse with 衬衫 (chèn shān), which is a button-up shirt with a collar.

senses.definition: A casual short-sleeved top without a collar.

examples.text: 今天天气很热，我只想穿一件T恤衫。
examples.translation: It is very hot today; I just want to wear a T-shirt.

faults.quote: you can insert other words between 付 and 钱, such as 付现金
faults.why: 付现金 replaces 钱 rather than inserting words between 付 and 钱.

faults.quote: 我在买咖啡以后付钱。
faults.why: Unnatural Chinese grammar (在...以后 without aspect or modal) and illogical ('pay after buying').

notes: A separable verb (离合词): words like 了 (le) or an indirect object go between 付 and 钱, as in 付了钱 (paid) or 付给他钱 (pay him).

senses.definition: To give money for goods or services.

examples.text: 请先付钱，再拿咖啡。
examples.translation: Please pay first, then take your coffee.

faults.quote: La jupe is a piece of clothing worn hanging from the waist.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Do not confuse with 'une robe' (dress), which covers both the top and bottom of the body.

senses.definition: A garment hanging from the waist, covering all or part of the legs.

examples.text: Elle porte une jolie jupe bleue pour aller au travail.
examples.translation: She is wearing a pretty blue skirt to go to work.

faults.quote: While 'lettre' most commonly means a written message sent by post
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Ce mot commence par une grande lettre.
faults.why: 'Une grande lettre' is unnatural for 'a capital letter' ('une majuscule' or 'une lettre majuscule').

notes: In the plural, 'les lettres' can also refer to literature or the humanities.

senses.definition: A written message sent by mail to someone.

examples.text: J'attends une lettre importante.
examples.translation: I am waiting for an important letter.

senses.definition: Each of the graphic signs that make up an alphabet.

examples.text: Ce mot commence par la lettre A.
examples.translation: This word starts with the letter A.

faults.quote: light, lamp, bulb
faults.why: Contradicts note[1]; 'lamp' is 'lampe' and 'bulb' is 'ampoule'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'une lampe' (a physical lamp) or 'une ampoule' (a light bulb), though 'la lumière' is used in everyday speech for electric room lighting ('allumer/éteindre la lumière').
Do not confuse with 'un feu' when referring to a traffic light.

senses.definition: The brightness that lets you see, coming from the sun, a lamp, or fire.

examples.text: Ouvre les volets pour laisser entrer la lumière.
examples.translation: Open the shutters to let the light in.

senses.definition: Electric lighting in a room or building.

examples.text: Éteins la lumière avant de partir.
examples.translation: Turn off the light before you leave.

faults.quote: Used with the feminine article 'la' or 'une'.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender, which is already shown in the entry fields.

notes: Commonly used in the expression 'être dans la lune' (to be daydreaming / to have one's head in the clouds).

senses.definition: The celestial body that travels around the Earth and shines in the night sky.

examples.text: La lune brille dans le ciel ce soir.
examples.translation: The moon is shining in the sky tonight.

faults.quote: The second syllable 'xie' is usually spoken in a neutral tone
faults.why: Restates what is already shown in the reading and IPA.

notes: Common replies are 不客气 (bù kè qi) or 不用谢 (bù yòng xiè), both meaning 'you're welcome'.

senses.definition: Words said to show you are grateful.

examples.text: 谢谢你的帮助。
examples.translation: Thank you for your help.

faults.quote: it is very common to hear it as 'hú luó bǒ'
faults.why: 卜 is never pronounced bǒ here; it takes a neutral tone (bo).

faults.quote: It is a versatile vegetable used in everything from stir-fries to soups.
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia about cooking, not a usage note; common classifier needed instead.

notes: Counted with the measure word 根 (gēn): 一根胡萝卜 (one carrot).

senses.definition: A long, crunchy, orange root vegetable.

examples.text: 胡萝卜对眼睛很好。
examples.translation: Carrots are good for your eyes.

faults.quote: 耗子 (hàozi) for a rat
faults.why: 耗子 is northern colloquial for mouse/rat alike, not specifically 'rat'; classifier只 is missing.

notes: Covers both mice and rats. Counted with 只 (zhī): 一只老鼠 (a mouse/rat). Notice the tone sandhi: two third tones together make 老 sound like láo.

senses.definition: A small rodent with a long tail.

examples.text: 厨房里有一只老鼠。
examples.translation: There is a mouse in the kitchen.

faults.quote: Use 'สกปรก' for anything physically covered in dirt or grime.
faults.why: Restates the definition; furthermore, it can also be used figuratively (e.g. dirty jokes/money).
Missing note on irregular pronunciation: unwritten vowel /o/ between ก and ป.

notes: Pronounced with three syllables (sòk-kà-pròk), with an unwritten 'a' sound after the first 'ก'.
Do not confuse with 'เลอะ', which describes something stained, smeared, or superficially messy rather than thoroughly dirty.

senses.definition: Covered in dirt or filth; not clean (also used figuratively of language or behaviour).

examples.text: เสื้อตัวนี้สกปรกมาก
examples.translation: This shirt is very dirty.

faults.quote: The colour of grass or leaves.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun rather than a quality.

notes: In Thai, 'สี' (colour) is usually kept before the hue name when describing nouns (e.g., รถสีเขียว 'green car'), though 'เขียว' can stand alone for natural things like leaves.

senses.definition: Having the colour of grass or leaves.

examples.text: หญ้าในสวนสีเขียวสวยมาก
examples.translation: The grass in the garden is a very pretty green.

faults.quote: เต็ม is used both for physical containers holding as much as possible
faults.why: Simply restates the two sense definitions.

notes: Often followed by ไปด้วย (bpai dûai) to mean 'full of': ห้องเต็มไปด้วยคน (The room is full of people).
Do not confuse with ทั้ง (táng), which means 'all' or 'the whole' of something rather than being filled to capacity.

senses.definition: Containing as much or as many as is possible or normal.

examples.text: แก้วนี้เต็มแล้ว
examples.translation: This glass is full.

senses.definition: Complete, maximum, or lacking nothing.

examples.text: เขาทำงานเต็มเวลา
examples.translation: He works full time.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear, cloudless sky during the day.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun rather than a quality.

notes: Thai treats 'สีฟ้า' (light/sky blue) and 'สีน้ำเงิน' (dark/navy blue) as two separate basic colours.
The word 'ฟ้า' (fáa) literally means 'sky', as this colour comes from a clear daytime sky.

senses.definition: Having the colour of a clear daytime sky.

examples.text: วันนี้ท้องฟ้าเป็นสีฟ้าสดใส
examples.translation: Today the sky is a bright light blue.

faults.quote: Used both as the general noun for the animal and affectionately
faults.why: Filler note; misses the essential classifier 'con' for animals.

faults.quote: A small domesticated carnivorous mammal with soft fur, a short snout, and
faults.why: Overly technical encyclopedic definition instead of plain learner's dictionary style.

notes: Takes the classifier 'con' when referring to an individual cat (con mèo).

senses.definition: A small furry animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet.

examples.text: Con mèo đang ngủ trên ghế.
examples.translation: The cat is sleeping on the chair.

faults.quote: /mə̰t˨/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in IPA; 'ê' in 'mệt' is /e/, not /ə/.

faults.quote: tired; exhausted
faults.why: 'exhausted' is not in any sense's glosses, while sense 1 ('weary, fed up') is omitted.

faults.quote: Use 'mệt' when you feel physically drained or mentally worn out.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: Often intensified as 'mệt quá' (so tired) or used in the compound 'mệt mỏi' (exhausted, weary).
In colloquial speech, can also mean slightly unwell or sick.

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep because of physical or mental effort.

examples.text: Tôi cảm thấy mệt sau một ngày làm việc dài.
examples.translation: I feel tired after a long day of work.

senses.definition: Feeling weary or annoyed because of a situation or someone's behavior.

examples.text: Tôi mệt vì phải đợi anh ấy quá lâu.
examples.translation: I am tired of waiting for him for so long.

faults.quote: /miw˧🏻 ʔɔwŋ͡m˧˥/
faults.why: Corrupt emoji in tone mark and wrong pronunciation (/miw/ instead of /mi˨˩/ for 'mì').

faults.quote: particularly tubular pasta like macaroni or spaghetti
faults.why: Spaghetti is not tubular; 'mì ống' literally means tube noodles (macaroni/penne), while spaghetti is 'mì Ý'.

notes: Literally 'tube noodles' (such as macaroni or penne), though often used broadly for Western pasta. Long pasta like spaghetti is usually called 'mì Ý' (Italian noodles).

senses.definition: Pasta shaped into short hollow tubes, or Western pasta in general.

examples.text: Tôi thích ăn mì ống với sốt cà chua.
examples.translation: I like to eat pasta with tomato sauce.

faults.quote: Giao hàng này hoàn toàn miễn phí cho đơn hàng lớn.
faults.why: 'Giao hàng này' is an unnatural calque of 'This delivery' ('giao hàng' is a verb phrase).

faults.quote: miễn phí is commonly seen on signs and advertisements to indicate
faults.why: Restates the meaning without useful grammatical guidance.

notes: Can also be used as an adverb after a verb (e.g., 'giao hàng miễn phí' — to deliver for free).
Refers only to cost. Do not confuse with 'tự do' (free, not restricted) or 'rảnh' (free, having spare time).

senses.definition: Costing no money; provided without charge.

examples.text: Cửa hàng giao hàng hoàn toàn miễn phí cho đơn hàng lớn.
examples.translation: The shop delivers completely free of charge for large orders.

faults.quote: /miəŋw˧˨ˀ/
faults.why: Invalid IPA: 'miệng' has no /-w/ offglide (/miəŋ˧˨ˀ/).

faults.quote: Used both for the human mouth and for openings of inanimate objects
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the northern synonym 'mồm'.

notes: In casual northern speech, 'mồm' is very commonly used for a person's or animal's mouth, while 'miệng' sounds more polite or standard.

senses.definition: The part of the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Hãy há miệng ra để bác sĩ kiểm tra họng.
examples.translation: Open your mouth so the doctor can check your throat.

senses.definition: The top opening or entrance of a container, cave, hole, or river.

examples.text: Miệng hang tối và có gió thổi ra.
examples.translation: The mouth of the cave is dark and has wind blowing out of it.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the winter season, often associated with rain
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss; broken plural أَشْتِيَة is more useful.

notes: Plural: أَشْتِيَة (ʾaštiya), though usually used in the singular.

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year, coming after autumn and before spring.

examples.text: يأتي الشتاء بعد الخريف.
examples.translation: Winter comes after autumn.

faults.quote: اللوحة تعلَق على الجِدَار.
faults.why: Wrong vocalization and verb form for 'hangs' (state); should be مُعَلَّقَة.

faults.quote: Used mainly for the walls of a room, house, or building.
faults.why: Restates the definition; should give the broken plural جُدْرَان instead.

notes: Plural: جُدْرَان (judrān).
Often interchangeable with حَائِط (ḥāʾiṭ), whereas سُور (sūr) refers to a surrounding outdoor wall or fence.

senses.definition: A vertical structure that divides or encloses a room or building.

examples.text: اللَّوْحَةُ مُعَلَّقَةٌ عَلَى الجِدَارِ.
examples.translation: The painting is hanging on the wall.

faults.quote: It refers both to the physical sky above us and, in religious
faults.why: Restates the two senses; note[0] also partly restates the gender field.

notes: Feminine by usage without a feminine ending (ـة). Plural: سَمَاوَات (samāwāt).

senses.definition: The space above the earth where clouds, the sun, and the stars are seen.

examples.text: السَّمَاءُ صَافِيَةٌ اليَوْمَ.
examples.translation: The sky is clear today.
