faults.quote: أُحِبُّ أَنْ آكُلَ الشُوكُولَاتَةَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
faults.why: Missing shadda on the sun letter ش in الشُّوكُولَاتَةَ.

notes: Uncountable; to refer to a single piece or bar, use قِطْعَةُ شُوكُولَاتَة (a piece of chocolate) or لَوْحُ شُوكُولَاتَة (a bar of chocolate).

senses.definition: A sweet brown food made from roasted and ground cacao seeds.

examples.text: أُحِبُّ أَنْ آكُلَ الشُّوكُولَاتَةَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
examples.translation: I like to eat chocolate in the evening.

faults.quote: غابة refers to a large forest, while حريشة or غُيَيْبَة can
faults.why: Teaches obscure words (حريشة, غييبة) useless to an A2 learner; misses plural and 'jungle' meaning.

notes: The plural is غَابَات.
Covers both temperate forests/woods and tropical jungles.

senses.definition: A large area of land covered thickly with trees and plants.

examples.text: نَمْشِي فِي الغَابَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
examples.translation: We walk in the forest every day.

faults.quote: (tradition) A group of artists, thinkers, or scientists
faults.why: Artistic/intellectual movement sense is not everyday A2 vocabulary.
Missing two vital A2 facts: takes prepositions в/из, and differs from English 'school' (university).

notes: Takes the prepositions в and из (в школе 'at school', в школу 'to school', из школы 'from school').
Refers to primary and secondary school (or music/art school), never to university (университет, вуз).

senses.definition: A place or institution where children go to learn, or the lessons there.

examples.text: Дети идут в школу каждое утро.
examples.translation: The children go to school every morning.

faults.quote: Use билет for travel tickets, event entries, and lottery slips.
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses; fails to give the required preposition (билет на + accusative).

faults.quote: A card with questions used by students during an exam.
faults.why: Exam question card is a specific academic sense, not everyday A2.

notes: Use the preposition на + accusative for the transport or event: билет на поезд (train ticket), билет на концерт (concert ticket), or в + accusative for a venue: билет в кино (cinema ticket).

senses.definition: A printed or digital document that gives you the right to travel on public transport or enter an event.

examples.text: Я купил билет на поезд заранее.
examples.translation: I bought a train ticket in advance.

faults.quote: Мой брат работает повар в новом ресторане.
faults.why: Ungrammatical: работать requires the instrumental case (работает поваром), not nominative.

notes: Used for anyone who cooks professionally, and for both men and women. For a head chef running a kitchen, шеф-повар is used.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to prepare and cook food.

examples.text: Мой брат работает поваром в новом ресторане.
examples.translation: My brother works as a cook in a new restaurant.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'авиация' (aviation)
faults.why: No beginner confuses 'airplane' with 'aviation'; misses useful grammar like на самолёте / самолётом.

notes: To say 'by plane', use на самолёте (or the instrumental самолётом): лететь на самолёте.

senses.definition: A vehicle with wings and one or more engines that flies through the air.

examples.text: Мой самолёт вылетает завтра утром.
examples.translation: My plane leaves tomorrow morning.

faults.quote: Used to describe anyone currently enrolled in an educational institution
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage help.

notes: Pronounced [학쌩] (with a tense 's').
Often shortened to -생 after a school level, as in 대학생 (university student) or 고등학생 (high school student).

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a school, college, or university.

examples.text: 그 학생은 매일 도서관에 갑니다.
examples.translation: That student goes to the library every day.

faults.quote: (food) The meat obtained from a cow.
faults.why: Beef is normally 소고기; 소 alone as 'beef' is elliptical and misleads beginners.

notes: Counted with the counter 마리 (e.g., 소 두 마리, 'two cows').
refers to cows, bulls, and oxen alike. For beef, use 소고기 (though 소 is sometimes used on restaurant menus as short for 소고기).

senses.definition: A large farm animal kept for milk or meat.

examples.text: 농장에 소가 많아요.
examples.translation: There are many cows on the farm.

faults.quote: you will frequently hear people shorten it to 자전거
faults.why: Nonsensical claim that 자전거 is shortened to 자전거; 바이크 usually means motorcycle.

notes: Takes the verb 타다 ('to ride'): 자전거를 타다 ('to ride a bicycle').
Counted with the counter 대 (e.g., 자전거 한 대, 'one bicycle').

senses.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle that you ride by pushing its pedals with your feet.

examples.text: 주말에 공원에서 자전거를 타요.
examples.translation: I ride a bike in the park on weekends.

notes: Contrasts with 시골 (countryside) and 마을 (village or neighborhood).
Often used in compounds like 대도시 (major city) and 신도시 (new town).

senses.definition: A large, densely populated area with many buildings, roads, and services.

examples.text: 나는 큰 도시에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.translation: I want to live in a big city.

faults.quote: you can also use the native Korean word '주황색'
faults.why: 주황색 (橘黃色) is a Sino-Korean word, not native Korean.

faults.quote: 그 셔츠는 오렌지색이에요.
faults.why: Uses the compound word 오렌지색 instead of the headword 오렌지.

faults.quote: (color) The color between red and yellow
faults.why: The color is normally 주황색 or 오렌지색; bare 오렌지 is mainly the fruit.

notes: Refers to the fruit. For the color orange, use 주황색 or 오렌지색.

senses.definition: A round citrus fruit with a thick, bright orange skin and juicy segments inside.

examples.text: 오렌지를 먹고 싶어요.
examples.translation: I want to eat an orange.

faults.quote: هَذَا الشَّارِعُ كَبِيرٌ وَمَزْدَحِمٌ.
faults.why: مَزْدَحِمٌ is ungrammatical; the active participle of ازْدَحَمَ is مُزْدَحِمٌ.

faults.quote: شَارِع refers specifically to a street or road within a town
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the broken plural شَوَارِع.

notes: Takes the broken plural شَوَارِع (šawāriʕ).
Do not confuse with طَرِيق (ṭarīq), which is a broader term for any road or path, including highways between cities.

senses.definition: A paved public road in a city or town, typically with buildings on one or both sides.

examples.text: هَذَا الشَّارِعُ كَبِيرٌ وَمُزْدَحِمٌ.
examples.translation: This street is big and crowded.

examples.text: بَيْتِي فِي هَذَا الشَّارِعِ.
examples.translation: My house is on this street.

faults.quote: Used for resting your head while sleeping in bed.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving the irregular broken plural وَسَائِد.

notes: Takes the broken plural وَسَائِد (wasāʔid).

senses.definition: A soft bag filled with comfortable material used to support your head in bed or to sit on.

examples.text: وَضَعْتُ رَأْسِي عَلَى الْوِسَادَةِ لِأَنَّنِي كُنْتُ مُتْعَبًا.
examples.translation: I put my head on the pillow because I was tired.

faults.quote: /maˈħatˤ.ta/
faults.why: Second geminate consonant must also be pharyngealized: /maˈħatˤ.tˤa/.

faults.quote: Used for trains, buses, and metro stops.
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 0.

notes: Do not confuse with مَوْقِف (mawqif), which is a parking lot or a simple roadside bus stop.

senses.definition: A place where trains or buses stop to let passengers on and off.

examples.text: أَنْتَظِرُ الْقِطَارَ فِي الْمَحَطَّةِ.
examples.translation: I am waiting for the train at the station.

senses.definition: A facility or channel for broadcasting television or radio programs.

examples.text: هَذِهِ مَحَطَّةُ إِذَاعَةٍ مَحَلِّيَّةٌ.
examples.translation: This is a local radio station.

faults.quote: hand; arm
faults.why: Includes 'arm', which is not in the senses or glosses.

faults.quote: اغسل يدك قبل الأكل.
faults.why: Unnatural in the singular; one washes both hands (يَدَيْكَ).

notes: Feminine despite lacking the ة (-a) ending, as with most paired body parts.
Takes the dual يَدَان (yadān, 'two hands') and the irregular plural أَيْدٍ (ʔaydin; definite الْأَيْدِي al-ʔaydī).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the palm and fingers.

examples.text: اِغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ قَبْلَ الْأَكْلِ.
examples.translation: Wash your hands before eating.

faults.quote: Used to describe the medical condition of coughing or the act
faults.why: Merely restates the meaning of 'cough'.

faults.quote: Pushing air out of the throat with a noise, often because
faults.why: Defined as a participle phrase instead of a noun phrase.

notes: Uncountable verbal noun from the verb سَعَلَ (saʕala, 'to cough').

senses.definition: An act or condition of forcing air out of the throat with a sudden sharp sound, often due to illness.

examples.text: عِنْدَهُ سُعَالٌ شَدِيدٌ فِي اللَّيْلِ.
examples.translation: He has a severe cough at night.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'ο χειμώνας' (winter), which comes right after it.
faults.why: The words do not look or sound alike; no learner will confuse them.

notes: The accusative with the definite article ('το φθινόπωρο') is used without a preposition to mean 'in autumn'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between summer and winter, when leaves fall from the trees.

examples.text: Το φθινόπωρο τα φύλλα πέφτουν από τα δέντρα.
examples.translation: In autumn the leaves fall from the trees.

faults.quote: Note that 'σύννεφο' is the standard term for a weather cloud.
faults.why: Restates the definition and notes an obvious figurative use shared with English.

senses.definition: A white or grey mass of water drops or ice crystals in the sky.

examples.text: Στον ουρανό εμφανίστηκε ένα μεγάλο σύννεφο.
examples.translation: A large cloud appeared in the sky.

faults.quote: In Greek, the word κουνέλι is used for both the animal
faults.why: Restates the two senses; English 'rabbit' also covers both animal and meat.

notes: The diminutive 'το κουνελάκι' is often used for a small or cute rabbit ('bunny').

senses.definition: A small mammal with long ears and a short fluffy tail, kept as a pet or living in the wild.
The meat of this animal eaten as food.

faults.quote: the shortened word 'αμάξι' in daily, casual conversation
faults.why: 'αμάξι' is not a shortened form of 'αυτοκίνητο'; it comes from 'άμαξα' (carriage).

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'όχημα', which is a broader, more formal
faults.why: Unrelated word in form and sound; no reason a beginner would confuse them.

notes: In everyday conversation, the synonym 'το αμάξι' is also very common.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: Πήγαμε στη δουλειά με το αυτοκίνητο.
examples.translation: We went to work by car.

faults.quote: Used for standard public buses operating within cities or between them.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of a bus.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'το τρόλεϊ' (trolleybus) or 'το τρένο' (train).
faults.why: Completely different words that no learner would confuse with 'λεωφορείο'.

senses.definition: A large motor vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route.

examples.text: Περιμένω το λεωφορείο στη στάση.
examples.translation: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.

faults.quote: monkey; ape
faults.why: 'ape' is in shortGloss and notes, but missing from sense[0] glosses and excluded by definition.

notes: In everyday French, 'singe' covers both monkeys and apes (sometimes called 'grands singes').

senses.definition: A furry primate that climbs trees and has hands and feet that can grasp things; a monkey or ape.

examples.text: Le singe grimpe vite dans l'arbre.
examples.translation: The monkey climbs quickly up the tree.

faults.quote: evening; night
faults.why: 'night' appears in shortGloss, where French often uses 'soir' ('hier soir'), but is missing from glosses.

notes: 'Le soir' is used for the evening up until bedtime, so English 'last night' or 'tonight' (before sleeping) is 'hier soir' or 'ce soir', whereas 'la nuit' is for the hours when people sleep.

senses.definition: The final part of the day, between the end of the afternoon and going to bed.

examples.text: Je rentre à la maison le soir.
examples.translation: I go home in the evening.

faults.quote: Use 'le soleil' for the star itself or for direct sunshine
faults.why: Note [0] merely restates the two senses; note [1] is an unlikely confusion.

notes: To say it is sunny, French uses the expression 'il fait soleil' or 'il y a du soleil'.

senses.definition: The star that gives the earth light and heat by day.

examples.text: Le soleil brille dans le ciel bleu.
examples.translation: The sun is shining in the blue sky.

senses.definition: The light and heat that come from the sun.

examples.text: Nous aimons profiter du soleil sur la terrasse.
examples.translation: We like to enjoy the sunshine on the terrace.

faults.quote: J'ai perdu mon stylo sur le bureau.
faults.why: Saying you lost something 'on the desk' is odd in both French and English.

senses.definition: A small tool used for writing or drawing with ink.

examples.text: Tu peux me prêter un stylo pour signer ?
examples.translation: Can you lend me a pen to sign?

faults.quote: Used with the feminine article 'la'
faults.why: Restates the gender and headword article; keep only the preposition usage.

notes: To say 'in spring', use the preposition 'in' without an article: 'in primavera'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between winter and summer.

examples.text: In primavera i fiori sbocciano nei campi.
examples.translation: In spring the flowers bloom in the fields.

faults.quote: Used both for a young female child or teenager
faults.why: False: 'ragazza' is for a teenager or young woman; a female child is 'bambina'.

faults.quote: from childhood up to young adulthood.
faults.why: 'Ragazza' does not include childhood (which is 'bambina').

notes: Used for teenagers and young women; for a young female child, use 'bambina'.
With a possessive (e.g., 'la mia ragazza'), it means 'girlfriend'.

senses.definition: A female teenager or young woman.

examples.text: La ragazza sta leggendo un libro sul treno.
examples.translation: The girl is reading a book on the train.

senses.definition: A female romantic partner.

examples.text: Lui va al cinema con la sua ragazza.
examples.translation: He is going to the cinema with his girlfriend.

faults.quote: /ri.uˈni.o.ne/
faults.why: Wrong syllabification and vowel instead of glide: should be /rjuˈnjo.ne/ or /ri.uˈnjo.ne/.
Both senses describe an organized meeting or gathering of people; merge into one.

notes: Used for planned work meetings, committee sessions, or organized family gatherings. For a casual meet-up with friends, use 'incontro' or 'uscita'.

senses.definition: An organized gathering of people to discuss business, work, or shared matters.

examples.text: Ho una riunione importante con il direttore alle dieci.
examples.translation: I have an important meeting with the director at ten.

faults.quote: Ho comprato una nuova scarpa da ginnastica per correre.
faults.why: Unnatural: nobody buys a single running shoe, and 'per correre' is redundant.

notes: Usually used in the plural, 'le scarpe' (shoes), when talking about a pair.

senses.definition: An outer covering worn on the foot.

examples.text: Ho comprato un paio di scarpe da ginnastica nuove.
examples.translation: I bought a new pair of sneakers.

faults.quote: Ho aperto una scatola di tonno.
faults.why: For a small can of tuna, Italians normally use the diminutive 'scatoletta', or 'in scatola'.

notes: For canned food, the phrase 'in scatola' (canned/tinned) and the diminutive 'la scatoletta' (small can/tin, e.g., of tuna) are very common.

senses.definition: A rigid container with flat sides, usually made of cardboard, wood, or plastic, used for storing or packing things.

examples.text: Ho messo le scarpe nella scatola.
examples.translation: I put the shoes in the box.

senses.definition: A sealed metal container for preserving food.

examples.text: Compriamo spesso i fagioli in scatola.
examples.translation: We often buy canned beans.

faults.quote: 蛋糕 is a general term for all kinds of cakes
faults.why: Restates the gloss; misses useful measure words (块 for a slice, 个 for a whole).

notes: Counted with 块 (kuài) for a slice or piece, and 个 (gè) for a whole cake.

senses.definition: A sweet baked food made from flour, sugar, and eggs.

examples.text: 今天是我生日，我吃了很多蛋糕。
examples.translation: Today is my birthday, and I ate a lot of cake.

faults.quote: (home) A domestic environment or the private sphere of home life.
faults.why: Attributive uses like 家庭生活 ('family life') are shades of sense 0, not a separate meaning.
An everyday abstract noun with usage distinctions needs an example sentence.

notes: Refers to the family as a household or social unit. For 'home' or 'my family' in a personal sense, use 家 (jiā) or 家人 (jiārén).

senses.definition: A social unit consisting of parents and children living together as a household.

examples.text: 她来自一个幸福的家庭。
examples.translation: She comes from a happy family.

notes: Refers to an adult male. In everyday speech, 男生 (nánshēng) is often used for boys or young men, and 男士 (nánshì) is a polite term for 'gentleman'.

senses.definition: An adult male person.

examples.text: 那个男人是谁？
examples.translation: Who is that man?

faults.quote: 世界 is a noun meaning 'world'. It can refer to
faults.why: Merely restates the part of speech, gloss, and definitions.

faults.quote: world; society
faults.why: 'Society' is not in the senses and belongs to 社会, not 世界.

senses.definition: The earth, together with all its countries and peoples.

examples.text: 我想去世界各地旅行。
examples.translation: I want to travel to all parts of the world.

senses.definition: A particular sphere of life, activity, or experience.

examples.text: 欢迎来到音乐的世界。
examples.translation: Welcome to the world of music.

faults.why: Should mention the common compound 'ngửi thấy' (to smell/detect a scent), used in the example.

notes: Often combined with 'thấy' as 'ngửi thấy' to mean detecting a scent (literally 'smell and perceive'), whereas 'ngửi' alone can just mean sniffing at something.
Only used as an active verb (using one's nose). To say something smells good or has a scent, use 'thơm' (fragrant) or 'có mùi' (has a smell).

senses.definition: To detect a scent or breathe in through the nose to smell something.

examples.text: Tôi ngửi thấy mùi cà phê buổi sáng.
examples.translation: I smell the morning coffee.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone you have never met or whose identity is
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Literally 'strange/unfamiliar person' ('người' = person, 'lạ' = strange, unfamiliar).
Do not confuse with 'người nước ngoài', which specifically means a foreigner.

senses.definition: A person whom one does not know.

examples.text: Đừng nói chuyện với người lạ.
examples.translation: Do not talk to strangers.

faults.quote: /ŋɨəj˨˩ lən˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length in 'lớn': 'ơ' is /əː/ (/ləːn˧˥/), whereas /ə/ is short 'â' ('lân').

faults.quote: (behavior) Behaving in a mature, responsible way appropriate for an adult.
faults.why: Entry POS is noun, not adjective, and the example uses 'một người lớn' (a noun).

faults.quote: Trẻ em cần được bảo vệ bởi người lớn.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of English passive ('được ... bởi'); Vietnamese prefers active voice here.

notes: Literally 'big person' ('người' = person, 'lớn' = big/grown). Compare with 'trẻ em' or 'trẻ con' (children).

senses.definition: A fully grown person, as opposed to a child.

examples.text: Người lớn cần phải bảo vệ trẻ em.
examples.translation: Adults need to protect children.

faults.quote: (people) Humanity or people in general.
faults.why: Vietnamese nouns do not inflect for number; 'person/people' is one sense, and example uses 'con người'.
Missing the essential everyday sense of physical body ('đau người', 'mệt người').

faults.quote: When referring to people in general, it translates to humans or people.
faults.why: Restates the glosses without explaining that Vietnamese nouns lack singular/plural inflection.

notes: Also used as the main classifier for people (e.g., 'ba người bạn' = three friends) and as a prefix for nationalities or professions ('người Việt' = Vietnamese person).
Vietnamese nouns do not change form for singular or plural, so 'người' means both 'person' and 'people'.

senses.definition: A human being, or people in general.

examples.text: Đó là một người tốt.
examples.translation: That is a good person.

senses.definition: One's physical body, especially when talking about health or how one feels.

examples.text: Hôm nay tôi thấy mệt trong người.
examples.translation: Today I feel tired in my body.

faults.quote: dangerous; perilous
faults.why: 'Perilous' is absent from the sense glosses; 'hazardous' should be used instead.

notes: Can also be used as a noun meaning 'danger' (e.g., 'gặp nguy hiểm' = to be in danger).

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or damage.

examples.text: Đừng đi vào khu vực nguy hiểm này.
examples.translation: Do not enter this dangerous area.

faults.quote: It is a fundamental word; you will use it every day
faults.why: Pure filler; fails to mention the crucial irregular buffer consonant 'y' in inflection.
'su' takes an irregular buffer 'y' (not 'n' or 's') in genitive and possessive forms.

notes: Takes the irregular buffer consonant 'y' instead of 's' or 'n' before vowel-initial suffixes: suyu (its water / the water), suyun (of the water), suyunu.
Combined with fruit or vegetable names in possessive compounds to mean 'juice', e.g., elma suyu (apple juice).

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain and is used for drinking and washing.

examples.text: Bir bardak soğuk su lütfen.
examples.translation: A glass of cold water, please.

senses.definition: The liquid obtained from a fruit, vegetable, or cooked dish.

examples.text: Taze portakal suyu içiyorum.
examples.translation: I am drinking fresh orange juice.

faults.quote: Used for large self-service grocery stores, very similar to the English word.
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful usage information.

notes: In everyday speech, Turkish speakers more commonly use the shorter word market for grocery stores of any size.

senses.definition: A large shop that sells food, drinks, and goods for the home.

examples.text: Yarın sabah süpermarketten biraz meyve alacağım.
examples.translation: Tomorrow morning I will buy some fruit from the supermarket.

faults.quote: Sıcak havada yürüyünce çok susamış hissettim.
faults.why: 'susamış hissettim' is an unnatural English calque ('felt thirsty'); 'susamış' is mainly attributive.
Learners must know that 'I am thirsty' is expressed verbally as 'Susadım', not with 'susamış'.

notes: Derived from the verb susamak (to get thirsty). To say 'I am thirsty', Turkish uses the past tense of the verb: Susadım (literally 'I have become thirsty'), whereas susamış is mainly used before a noun or mean 'looking thirsty'.

senses.definition: Feeling a need to drink water.

examples.text: Susamış kediye bir kap su verdik.
examples.translation: We gave a bowl of water to the thirsty cat.

notes: Unlike solid fats like butter (tereyağı) or margarine (margarin), sıvı yağ refers strictly to liquid cooking oils such as sunflower or corn oil.

senses.definition: Plant-based oil that remains liquid at room temperature and is used for cooking and frying.

examples.text: Tavaya biraz sıvı yağ döküp ısıttı.
examples.translation: He poured a little cooking oil into the pan and heated it.

faults.quote: /ˈu.ðun/
faults.why: Missing initial glottal stop /ʔ/.

faults.quote: It can also refer to the handle or lug of a pot
faults.why: Restates sense 1; notes[0] also just restates gender without explaining why it's unmarked feminine.
Missing irregular broken plural آذَان (ʔāḏān) and alternative pronunciation أُذْن.

faults.quote: (object) A projecting part of an object used as a handle.
faults.why: Cup handle (أذن الفنجان) is minor for A2 compared to the body part.

notes: Feminine by convention (as a paired body part) despite having no feminine ending (-a). Dual: أُذُنَانِ; broken plural: آذَان.
Also pronounced and vocalized as أُذْن (/ʔuðn/).

senses.definition: The organ on the side of the head that people and animals use to hear.

examples.text: وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى أُذُنِهِ لِيَسْمَعَ جَيِّدًا.
examples.translation: He put his hand to his ear to hear well.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a women's one-piece garment that includes a skirt.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

notes: Broken plural: فَسَاتِين (/fasaːˈtiːn/).

senses.definition: A women's one-piece garment consisting of a bodice and a skirt.

examples.text: اشْتَرَتْ فُسْتَانًا جَمِيلًا لِلْحَفْلِ.
examples.translation: She bought a beautiful dress for the party.

faults.quote: /ˈsaːndawitʃ/
faults.why: Has an extra /a/ vowel not matching the vowelled headword سَانْدْوِيتْش.

faults.quote: local names like 'shater' or 'kaak' may also be used
faults.why: Misleading: 'kaak' is a bread/pastry, and 'shater' is only half of 'shater wa mashtour'.

notes: A loanword with several common spellings, including ساندوتش and سندويش. Plural: سَانْدْوِيتْشَات.
The formal Arabic equivalent شَطِيرَة is mainly seen in menus and formal writing.

senses.definition: Two or more pieces of bread or a roll with a filling between them.

examples.text: أَكَلْتُ سَانْدْوِيتْشَ جُبْنَةٍ عَلَى الْغَدَاءِ.
examples.translation: I ate a cheese sandwich for lunch.

faults.quote: /darˈraː.dʒa ha.waːˈij.ja/
faults.why: Missing glottal stop /ʔ/ in هَوَائِيَّة (/ha.waː.ˈʔij.ja/).

notes: Often shortened to دَرَّاجَة when the context is clear, though دَرَّاجَة نَارِيَّة means 'motorcycle'. Plural: دَرَّاجَات هَوَائِيَّة.

senses.definition: A vehicle with two wheels and pedals, moved by the rider's feet.

examples.text: أَرْكَبُ دَرَّاجَتِي الْهَوَائِيَّةَ إِلَى الْعَمَلِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
examples.translation: I ride my bicycle to work every day.

faults.quote: /saːlaˈta/
faults.why: Wrong stress and false vowel length; stressed on the second syllable (/saˈlata/).

faults.quote: (plant) A leafy green vegetable used to make salads, such as lettuce.
faults.why: 'Salata' alone does not mean lettuce in standard Turkish ('göbek salata' or 'marul' does).

faults.quote: Manuptan iki baş salata aldım.
faults.why: 'Manuptan' is a non-existent word, likely a garbled typo for 'manavdan' (from the greengrocer).

faults.quote: 'salata' can mean both the prepared dish (salad) and the plant itself (lettuce)
faults.why: Confuses Turkish with other languages; bare 'salata' is not used for lettuce.

notes: Do not confuse with 'salatalık' (cucumber), though in some regions 'salata' is used colloquially for cucumber.

senses.definition: A cold dish of raw or cooked vegetables, usually seasoned with oil, lemon juice, or vinegar.

examples.text: Yemeğin yanında taze bir salata sipariş ettik.
examples.translation: We ordered a fresh salad with the meal.

faults.quote: /sandaɫˈje/
faults.why: Wrong stress; 'sandalye' is stressed on the second syllable (/sanˈdalje/).

notes: Do not confuse with 'koltuk', which refers to an armchair, sofa seat, or upholstered seat.

senses.definition: A seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.

examples.text: Mutfak masasının etrafında dört tane sandalye var.
examples.translation: There are four chairs around the kitchen table.

faults.quote: /ˈsan.di.tʃ/
faults.why: Missing the /v/ consonant and has wrong syllable division and stress (/sandˈvitʃ/).

faults.quote: Sandviç is a loanword from English, pronounced very similarly
faults.why: Etymology and basic 'ç' pronunciation are filler; better to contrast with 'tost'.

notes: Refers to a cold sandwich; a grilled or pressed hot sandwich is called 'tost'.

senses.definition: Two pieces of bread or a roll with cheese, meat, or vegetables between them.

examples.text: Öğle yemeğinde peynirli sandviç yedim.
examples.translation: I ate a cheese sandwich for lunch.

faults.quote: "Şans" is a common borrowing from French used in everyday speech.
faults.why: Etymology does not help an A2 learner use the word.

notes: Often used in the expression 'İyi şanslar!' (Good luck!).

senses.definition: Good things that happen by chance; favorable fortune.

examples.text: Bugün şans benden yana.
examples.translation: Today luck is on my side.

senses.definition: An occasion or opportunity that makes it possible to do something.

examples.text: Bana bir şans daha ver.
examples.translation: Give me one more chance.

faults.quote: /ʃapˈka/
faults.why: Wrong stress; 'şapka' has initial stress (/ˈʃapka/).

faults.quote: Used for any head covering with a brim or a structured shape
faults.why: Restates the definition; a note on the verb it takes ('takmak') is much more useful.

notes: Used with the verb 'takmak' (to put on / wear): 'şapka takmak' (to wear a hat). A knitted winter beanie is usually called 'bere'.

senses.definition: A covering worn on the head, typically with a brim or visor, for warmth or protection from the sun.

examples.text: Yaz aylarında güneşten korunmak için mutlaka şapka takarım.
examples.translation: I always wear a hat in the summer months to protect myself from the sun.

faults.quote: Used specifically to talk about a park in a town or
faults.why: Restates the definition; should note how the noun-adjective phrase takes the definite article.

notes: Distinguishes a public park from a private yard or garden (حَدِيقَة). When definite, both words take الـ: الحَدِيقَة العَامَّة.

senses.definition: A public garden or park in a town where people can walk and relax.

examples.text: نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ العَامَّةِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ.
examples.translation: We go to the public park on Friday.

faults.why: Learners confuse its masculine gender because it ends in alif maqṣūra (ـى) and broken plural.

notes: Masculine despite ending in ـى (alif maqṣūra): مُسْتَشْفًى كَبِير (a big hospital). Plural: مُسْتَشْفَيَات.

senses.definition: A place where sick and injured people are treated by doctors and nurses.

examples.text: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْمُسْتَشْفَى.
examples.translation: I went to the hospital.

faults.quote: Used commonly for public squares in cities, as well as open
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses without adding helpful usage or plural information.

notes: Plural: سَاحَات.

senses.definition: An open public area or square in a town or city.

examples.text: اجْتَمَعَ النَّاسُ فِي سَاحَةِ المَدِينَةِ.
examples.translation: The people gathered in the town square.

senses.definition: An open courtyard or yard attached to a building.

examples.text: يَلْعَبُ الأَطْفَالُ فِي سَاحَةِ المَدْرَسَةِ.
examples.translation: The children are playing in the schoolyard.

faults.quote: We rode a boat in the river.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English one 'takes' or 'goes in' a boat 'on' a river.

notes: Used for smaller boats on rivers, lakes, or the sea, unlike a large ship (سَفِينَة). Broken plural: قَوَارِب.

senses.definition: A small vessel for travelling on water.

examples.text: رَكِبْنَا قَارِبًا فِي النَّهْرِ.
examples.translation: We took a boat on the river.

faults.quote: Used for holding liquids like water, juice, or oil.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of a bottle.

notes: Formed from زُجَاج (glass, uncountable). Plural: زُجَاجَات.

senses.definition: A container for liquid with a narrow neck, typically made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: اِشْتَرِ زُجَاجَةَ مَاءٍ بَارِدٍ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: Buy a bottle of cold water, please.

notes: Plural: die Schweine. For the meat (pork), German uses 'das Schweinefleisch'.
The common informal idiom 'Schwein haben' means to be lucky (e.g., 'Da hast du aber Schwein gehabt!').

senses.definition: A pink or spotted farm animal with short legs that is kept for its meat.

examples.text: Das Schwein suhlt sich im Schlamm.
examples.translation: The pig is wallowing in the mud.

faults.quote: The words 'Sofa', 'Couch', and 'Cautsch' are all common
faults.why: 'Cautsch' is a non-standard misspelling, not a common German word.

notes: Plural: die Sofas. 'Die Couch' (feminine) is an equally common synonym.

senses.definition: A long, soft seat for several people, usually with a backrest and armrests.

examples.text: Wir sitzen abends gemütlich auf dem Sofa.
examples.translation: We sit comfortably on the sofa in the evening.

faults.quote: Note the neuter gender ('das'). In German, many loanwords
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword and fields.

faults.quote: Unlike in some English contexts, this specifically refers to a garment
faults.why: Meaningless filler; 'T-Shirt' means the exact same thing in German and English.

notes: Plural: die T-Shirts.

senses.definition: A simple casual top with short sleeves and no collar.

examples.text: Ich trage heute ein blaues T-Shirt.
examples.translation: I am wearing a blue T-shirt today.

faults.quote: Taxi is neuter (das Taxi) in German.
faults.why: Restates the gender already given in the headword and gender field.

faults.quote: In Germany, you can often find them at designated stands
faults.why: Generic trivia about how taxis work rather than useful linguistic guidance.

notes: Plural: die Taxis (or less commonly: die Taxen).

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you to a specific place.

examples.text: Ich nehme ein Taxi zum Bahnhof.
examples.translation: I am taking a taxi to the train station.

examples.text: Kannst du mir ein Taxi rufen?
examples.translation: Can you call me a taxi?

faults.quote: telephone; phone call
faults.why: 'Das Telefon' does not mean 'phone call', contradicting both the sense and the note.

notes: Plural: die Telefone. Usually refers to a landline or the device in general; a mobile phone is 'das Handy'.
For a phone call, use 'der Anruf' or 'das Telefongespräch', or the verb 'telefonieren'.

senses.definition: A device used for talking to someone who is in another place.

examples.text: Das Telefon klingelt im Flur.
examples.translation: The telephone is ringing in the hallway.

faults.quote: Used to talk about a period of seven days
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Notice the common time expressions 'bu hafta' (this week), 'geçen hafta' (last week), and 'gelecek hafta' (next week), which are used without a case suffix.

senses.definition: A period of seven consecutive days.

examples.text: Gelecek hafta İstanbul'a gideceğim.
examples.translation: I will go to Istanbul next week.

faults.quote: /ˈhafta ˈsonu/
faults.why: Word stress in Turkish is word-final here: /hafˈta soˈnu/.
Should mention the irregular plural 'hafta sonları' where the possessive drops before '-lar'.

notes: Literally 'end of the week'. In the plural ('hafta sonları', 'on weekends'), the plural suffix '-lar' comes before the possessive '-ı'.

senses.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the days of the week when people usually do not work.

examples.text: Bu hafta sonu ne yapacaksın?
examples.translation: What are you going to do this weekend?

faults.quote: /haːˈla/
faults.why: The noun 'hala' (aunt) has two short vowels: /haˈla/. Long /haːˈlaː/ is the adverb 'hâlâ'.

faults.quote: with the adverb hâla (still, yet), which has a circumflex over the first 'a'
faults.why: The adverb is spelled 'hâlâ' with two circumflexes in current standard Turkish, not just one.

faults.quote: (time) Up to this time or continuing until now.
faults.why: Conflates distinct adverb 'hâlâ' into the noun entry 'hala', contradicting its own note.

notes: Specifically refers to your father's sister; your mother's sister is 'teyze'.
Do not confuse with the adverb 'hâlâ' ('still, yet'), which is pronounced with two long vowels (/haːˈlaː/) and often written without circumflexes in casual text.

senses.definition: The sister of one's father.

examples.text: Yarın halama gideceğiz.
examples.translation: We are going to my aunt's tomorrow.

faults.quote: /haɾiˈta/
faults.why: Place and map words like 'harita' have penultimate stress in Turkish: /haˈɾita/.

faults.quote: Harita takes the dative case (e.g., haritaya bakmak) when looking at a map.
faults.why: The dative case is governed by the verb 'bakmak', not by the noun 'harita'.

notes: Pronounced with stress on the middle syllable (/haˈɾita/), not at the end.

senses.definition: A drawing of an area that shows where roads, cities, rivers, etc. are.

examples.text: Şehirde kaybolmamak için haritaya bakıyorum.
examples.translation: I am looking at the map so as not to get lost in the city.

faults.quote: /hɑs.tɑ/
faults.why: Missing stress mark and uses non-standard /ɑ/ instead of /a/: should be /hasˈta/.

faults.quote: It is a very common word, so pay attention to whether the speaker
faults.why: Pure filler advice; it would be much more useful to mention 'hasta olmak' (to get sick).

notes: Used both as an adjective ('ill, sick') and as a noun ('patient').
Often combined with 'olmak' as 'hasta olmak' ('to get sick, to fall ill').

senses.definition: Not in good health; suffering from an illness.

examples.text: Bugün kendimi biraz hasta hissediyorum.
examples.translation: I feel a little ill today.

senses.definition: A person receiving medical treatment.

examples.text: Doktor hastayı muayene ediyor.
examples.translation: The doctor is examining the patient.

faults.quote: /maˈcaiɾi/
faults.why: Wrong transcription: 'χ' before 'αι' (/e/) is [ç], and 'αι' is /e/, not /ai/.

faults.quote: While 'μαχαίρι' is the standard term for a kitchen or pocket knife
faults.why: Advanced idiom unnecessary at A2; plural/diminutive info or empty note is better.

senses.definition: A tool with a sharp blade and a handle, used for cutting.

examples.text: Χρειάζομαι ένα κοφτερό μαχαίρι για να κόψω το ψωμί.
examples.translation: I need a sharp knife to cut the bread.

faults.quote: (phobia) An extreme or irrational fear of a specific thing or situation.
faults.why: Shades of one meaning; 'phobia' in Greek is 'φοβία', while 'φόβος' is just 'fear'.

faults.quote: Often used with the verb 'έχω' (to have) to express being afraid: 'έχω φόβο'
faults.why: Unnatural; 'I am afraid' is normally expressed with the verb 'φοβάμαι', not 'έχω φόβο'.

faults.quote: Ο φόβος για το σκοτάδι είναι κοινός στα παιδιά.
faults.why: 'Κοινός' is a calque of English 'common'; 'συνηθισμένος' is natural for 'frequent/common'.

notes: To say 'I am afraid', Greek normally uses the related verb 'φοβάμαι' rather than a phrase with the noun 'φόβος'.

senses.definition: The unpleasant feeling you get when you think something dangerous or bad might happen.

examples.text: Έχει μεγάλο φόβο για τα ύψη.
examples.translation: He has a great fear of heights.

faults.quote: The standard word for a cow, commonly seen on farms
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss and definition.

notes: For the meat ('beef'), Greek uses 'μοσχάρι' (veal/beef) or 'βοδινό', not 'αγελάδα'.

senses.definition: A large female farm animal kept for milk and meat.

examples.text: Η αγελάδα βόσκει στο λιβάδι.
examples.translation: The cow is grazing in the meadow.

faults.quote: Note that 'κουζίνα' functions similarly to 'kitchen' in English, referring to both the room and the appliance
faults.why: False claim about English ('kitchen' does not mean 'stove'), and otherwise restates the senses.

senses.definition: The room in a home where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: Τρώμε πάντα το πρωινό μας στην κουζίνα.
examples.translation: We always eat our breakfast in the kitchen.

senses.definition: A large kitchen appliance used for cooking food, combining an oven and burners.

examples.text: Μην ξεχάσεις να κλείσεις την κουζίνα.
examples.translation: Don't forget to turn off the stove.

senses.definition: The style of cooking of a particular country or region.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει πολύ η ελληνική κουζίνα.
examples.translation: I like Greek cuisine very much.

faults.quote: Used for eating liquid foods like soup or porridge
faults.why: Explains what a spoon is in the real world instead of Russian usage.

notes: The genitive plural has a fleeting vowel: ложек (e.g., пять ложек — five spoons).

senses.definition: A small utensil with a round bowl at the end, used for eating or stirring.

examples.text: Мне нужна ложка для супа.
examples.translation: I need a spoon for the soup.

senses.definition: The amount that one spoon can hold.

examples.text: Положи две ложки сахара в чай.
examples.translation: Put two spoonfuls of sugar in the tea.

faults.quote: Used specifically for large public vehicles that follow fixed routes
faults.why: Restates the definition; also false because it includes tour and charter buses.

notes: To say 'by bus', use на автобусе (prepositional case). Do not confuse with маршрутка, a smaller minibus.

senses.definition: A large road vehicle that carries many passengers.

examples.text: Я еду на работу на автобусе.
examples.translation: I am going to work by bus.

examples.text: Автобус приехал вовремя.
examples.translation: The bus arrived on time.

faults.quote: A fact or quality that makes something hard to understand
faults.why: 'Secret of success' is a standard shade of 'secret', not 'mystery' (which is тайна/загадка).

faults.quote: mystery, secret
faults.why: Секрет does not mean 'mystery' in Russian; that is тайна or загадка.

notes: Commonly used in храни́ть секре́т (to keep a secret) and по секре́ту (in secret / confidentially).

senses.definition: Something kept hidden from others, or the key to achieving something.

examples.text: Это наш маленький секрет.
examples.translation: This is our little secret.

examples.text: В чём секрет твоего успеха?
examples.translation: What is the secret to your success?

faults.quote: /ˈsvʲitɨr/
faults.why: In 'свитер', the consonant 'т' is pronounced hard (/ˈsvʲitɨr/ has soft vʲ; standard is /ˈsvʲitɨr/ or /ˈsvʲitɛr/, actually wait: 'в' is soft, 'т' is hard, so /ˈsvʲitɨr/ is actually right! Let's check note instead).

notes: Although spelled with 'е', the 'т' is pronounced hard: [сви́тэр]. Distinct from кофта (usually buttons or zips up).

senses.definition: A warm knitted piece of clothing with long sleeves, worn on the upper body.

examples.text: На улице холодно, надень тёплый свитер.
examples.translation: It is cold outside, put on a warm sweater.

notes: Ends in -а, so it declines like a feminine noun, but can refer to a man or a woman: мой коллега (male) or моя коллега (female).

senses.definition: A person that you work with.

examples.text: Мой коллега помогает мне с новым проектом.
examples.translation: My colleague is helping me with the new project.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who has a lot of work
faults.why: Restates the definition; should note the common pattern 'bận + verb' instead.

faults.quote: /bə̰n/
faults.why: Missing tone letters (should be /ɓən˧˨ʔ/) for Vietnamese.

notes: Followed directly by a verb or noun to say what someone is busy with (e.g. 'bận làm việc', busy working).

senses.definition: Having a lot of work or things to do; not free.

examples.text: Hôm nay tôi rất bận.
examples.translation: I am very busy today.

faults.quote: /1baːn2 t͡ɕəŋ/
faults.why: Corrupt digits instead of tone marks, and southern final /-ŋ/ instead of northern /-n/.

notes: Refers specifically to the foot below the ankle, unlike 'chân' on its own, which can mean either the foot or the whole leg.

senses.definition: The part of the body at the bottom of the leg on which a person stands.

examples.text: Cô ấy bị đau bàn chân sau khi chạy bộ.
examples.translation: Her foot hurts after jogging.

faults.quote: Tôi cần dọn dẹp bàn làm việc của mình.
faults.why: Adding 'của mình' is a calque of English 'my'; Vietnamese omits it here.

notes: Literally 'work table' ('bàn' = table, 'làm việc' = to work); takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc'.

senses.definition: A table used for working, reading, or studying.

examples.text: Tôi cần dọn dẹp bàn làm việc.
examples.translation: I need to tidy up my desk.

faults.why: Missing the essential A1/A2 pronoun sense 'you' used among peers or in general address.

faults.quote: /ʔɓan˧ˀ/
faults.why: Wrong vowel (/a/ instead of long /aː/) and non-standard tone notation.

notes: Used as 'you' with people of roughly the same age, with strangers of similar age, or in writing addressed to the general reader.

senses.definition: A person you know well and like, who is not a member of your family.

examples.text: Đây là bạn của tôi.
examples.translation: This is my friend.

senses.definition: Used to address a friend, someone of a similar age, or a reader.

examples.text: Bạn tên là gì?
examples.translation: What is your name?

faults.quote: (discussion) To discuss or talk over a plan, problem, or topic
faults.why: Entry POS is noun; verb 'to discuss' is a different part of speech.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'bàn' means table or desk. As a verb
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses of the senses.

faults.quote: Tôi ngồi ở bàn làm việc cả ngày.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'bàn làm việc' or verb phrase 'làm việc', obscuring standalone noun 'bàn'.

notes: Takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc' for a piece of furniture.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs, used for eating, working, or putting things on.

examples.text: Chúng tôi ngồi quanh cái bàn trong bếp.
examples.translation: We sat around the table in the kitchen.

senses.definition: A point scored in a game such as football (often 'bàn thắng').

examples.text: Đội nhà đã ghi được hai bàn.
examples.translation: The home team scored two goals.

faults.quote: do not use a preposition like 'in' before a month name
faults.why: Both 'a' and 'in' are correct before month names ('a marzo' or 'in marzo'); also 'a' is a preposition.

notes: In Italian, the names of months are not capitalized unless they start a sentence.
To say 'in [month]', use the preposition 'a' or 'in' with no article: 'a marzo' or 'in marzo' (in March).

senses.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.

examples.text: Febbraio è il mese più corto dell'anno.
examples.translation: February is the shortest month of the year.

examples.text: Ci vediamo il mese prossimo.
examples.translation: See you next month.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with the adjective 'minuto' (tiny/minute)
faults.why: Literary/advanced adjective not relevant or confusing for an A2 learner.

notes: In everyday speech, 'un minuto' often means a short moment rather than exactly sixty seconds.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds, or a very short moment.

examples.text: Aspetta un minuto, per favore.
examples.translation: Wait a minute, please.

faults.quote: Tutto il mondo era presente alla festa.
faults.why: Calque of French 'tout le monde'; Italian uses 'tutti' for 'everybody at the party'.

faults.quote: world, everybody, society
faults.why: 'Il mondo' does not translate to 'everybody' in standard Italian.

faults.quote: world; people; realm
faults.why: 'Realm' is not covered in the senses; 'people' is misleading.

faults.quote: Il mondo is used both for the physical planet and for society
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the senses.

faults.why: Missing vowel length on the first syllable: should be /ˈtˤaː.wi.la/.

faults.quote: Used for furniture with a flat surface supported by legs
faults.why: Merely restates the definition instead of giving useful grammar or usage.

faults.quote: الطَّاوِلَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ فِي الغُرْفَةِ.
faults.why: Unnatural syntax and English translation ('The table is big in the room').

notes: The plural is طَاوِلَات (ṭāwilāt).
Used for any table; مَائِدَة (māʾida) refers specifically to a dining table set with food.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs, used for eating, writing, or putting things on.

examples.text: وَضَعْتُ الكِتَابَ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ.
examples.translation: I put the book on the table.

faults.why: Notes state it is collective, while gender says masculine and the example uses feminine agreement.

notes: Collective noun that usually takes feminine singular agreement (e.g., خُضَار طَازَجَة), though masculine is also possible.
Also used in the plural form خَضْرَاوَات (ḵaḍrāwāt).

senses.definition: Plants or parts of plants eaten as food.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ خُضَارًا طَازَجَةً مِنَ السُّوقِ.
examples.translation: I bought fresh vegetables from the market.

faults.quote: Meat from a sheep, eaten as food.
faults.why: خروف alone is the animal; the meat requires لحم ('meat of') as in the example.

notes: The broken plural is خِرَاف (ḵirāf) or خِرْفَان (ḵirfān).
Refers to a male or young sheep; for the meat, say لَحْم خَرُوف (laḥm ḵarūf, 'lamb/mutton').

senses.definition: A woolly farm animal raised for its meat and wool, especially a young one or a male.

examples.text: رَأَيْتُ خَرُوفًا أَبْيَضَ فِي الحَقْلِ.
examples.translation: I saw a white sheep in the field.

faults.quote: مكتب can mean both the physical room or office where people work
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: office, desk
faults.why: Sense 0 is the room/workplace, so 'desk' belongs only in Sense 1.

notes: The broken plural is مَكَاتِب (makātib).

senses.definition: A room or building where people work at desks.

examples.text: أَعْمَلُ فِي مَكْتَبٍ كَبِيرٍ.
examples.translation: I work in a large office.

senses.definition: A table with drawers that you sit at to read, write, or work.

examples.text: جَلَسَ الطَّالِبُ إِلَى المَكْتَبِ لِيَدْرُسَ.
examples.translation: The student sat at the desk to study.

faults.quote: A social occasion where tea is served
faults.why: Having tea is a normal use of the drink sense; tip ('на чай') is missing.

notes: often takes the partitive ending -ю in the genitive ('чашка чаю' — 'a cup of tea') and the locative ending -ю after 'в'/'на'
the set phrase 'на чай' means 'a tip' (e.g., 'оставить на чай' — 'to leave a tip')

senses.definition: A hot drink made by pouring boiling water over dried tea leaves, or the leaves themselves.

examples.text: Я пью горячий чай с лимоном.
examples.translation: I am drinking hot tea with lemon.

examples.text: Приходи ко мне на чай в субботу.
examples.translation: Come over to my place for tea on Saturday.

faults.quote: A place with fruit trees, such as apple or cherry trees.
faults.why: Russian 'сад' is one concept covering both garden and orchard; kindergarten sense is missing.

faults.quote: the word for a indoor houseplant is 'комнатное растение'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'сад' with houseplants; the locative 'в саду' is needed instead.

notes: takes the stressed locative ending -у after 'в' and 'на': 'в саду' (in the garden)
denotes land with trees, shrubs, or flowers; a vegetable patch is 'огород'

senses.definition: A piece of land planted with fruit trees, shrubs, or flowers.

examples.text: В нашем саду растут яблони и цветы.
examples.translation: Apple trees and flowers grow in our garden.

senses.definition: Short for 'детский сад': a school or care centre for young children before primary school.

examples.text: Утром я отвожу сына в сад.
examples.translation: In the morning I take my son to kindergarten.

faults.quote: use the preposition 'ночью' (in the night)
faults.why: 'ночью' is the instrumental case (or an adverb), not a preposition.

notes: feminine 3rd-declension noun (genitive/dative/prepositional 'ночи')
to say 'at night', use the instrumental form 'ночью' without a preposition

senses.definition: The dark part of the 24-hour day, between evening and morning.

examples.text: На улице уже ночь, и все спят.
examples.translation: It is already night outside, and everyone is sleeping.

faults.quote: To have very little money or few possessions to live comfortably.
faults.why: Adjective defined as an infinitive verb ('To have...') instead of a quality.

notes: Unlike the English word 'poor', which can also mean 'of low quality' or 'pitiful', 가난하다 only describes having little money.

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions.

examples.text: 그는 가난하지만 행복하게 살고 있어요.
examples.translation: He is poor, but he lives happily.

faults.why: Missing essential A1/A2 grammar note: 춥다 is a ㅂ-irregular adjective (추워요, 추운).

notes: Used for the weather, a room, or how a person feels. For things that feel cold to the touch (like water, food, or hands), use 차갑다.
ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (추워요, 추워서, 추운).

senses.definition: Of the weather, air, or a person's body: having or feeling a low temperature.

examples.text: 날씨가 너무 추워서 밖에 나가기 싫어요.
examples.translation: The weather is so cold that I don't want to go outside.

faults.quote: (emphasis) Absolutely; completely; without any doubt.
faults.why: Adverbial 절대 takes negative predicates; positive '그건 절대 사실이야' is unidiomatic calque of 'absolutely'.

notes: As an adverb, 절대 is normally followed by a negative verb or adjective (안, 못, 없다, 아니다, or imperatives with -지 마세요) to mean 'never' or 'under no circumstances'.
Often used with -로 as 절대로 with no change in meaning.

senses.definition: In no circumstances; at no time (used with negative expressions).

examples.text: 나는 절대 거짓말을 안 해요.
examples.translation: I never tell lies.

examples.text: 이건 비밀이니까 절대 말하지 마세요.
examples.translation: This is a secret, so don't ever tell anyone.

faults.quote: 가끔 is used when something happens on some occasions, but not regularly
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss without adding usage value.

notes: Compare frequency adverbs: 항상/늘 (always) — 자주 (often) — 가끔 (sometimes) — 거의 안 (hardly ever) — 절대 안 (never).

senses.definition: On some occasions, rather than all the time or often.

examples.text: 나는 가끔 영화를 보러 간다.
examples.translation: I sometimes go to see a movie.

notes: Do not confuse with 아주 (very), which sounds similar but modifies adjectives or adverbs.

senses.definition: Many times at short intervals.

examples.text: 저는 도서관에 자주 갑니다.
examples.translation: I go to the library often.

examples.text: 그 친구를 자주 만나요.
examples.translation: I meet that friend often.

faults.quote: Remember that in Dutch, 'appel' is a common gender word
faults.why: Restates gender and article already shown in the headword and gender field.
Missing note that both plural forms 'appels' and 'appelen' exist in Dutch.

notes: The plural is usually 'appels', though 'appelen' is also used in some fixed expressions and recipes.
Often used in the expression 'voor een appel en een ei', meaning 'very cheaply'.

senses.definition: The round, firm fruit of an apple tree, with red, green, or yellow skin.

examples.text: Ik eet elke dag een appel.
examples.translation: I eat an apple every day.

faults.why: Should mention the common homonym 'arm' (adjective meaning 'poor').

notes: The plural is 'armen'.
Also exists as an adjective ('arm') meaning 'poor'.

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body from the shoulder to the hand.

examples.text: Hij tilt de zware doos op met zijn armen.
examples.translation: He lifts the heavy box with his arms.

faults.quote: Use 'de' because it is a de-word.
faults.why: Restates the article and gender already shown in the headword.

notes: The plural takes an apostrophe: 'auto's' (to keep the long 'o' sound).
To say 'by car', use 'met de auto'.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: Ik parkeer de auto om de hoek.
examples.translation: I am parking the car around the corner.

faults.quote: In de avond lees ik graag een boek.
faults.why: Native Dutch strongly prefers ''s avonds' over 'in de avond' for habitual actions.

notes: Use ''s avonds' for 'in the evening(s)' and 'vanavond' for 'this evening' or 'tonight'.
Do not confuse 'avond' (evening) with 'nacht' (night), which refers to the late hours when people sleep.

senses.definition: The part of the day between the end of the afternoon and the time you go to bed.

examples.text: Wij eten meestal om zes uur 's avonds.
examples.translation: We usually eat at six o'clock in the evening.

faults.quote: When talking about employment or the work you are paid for, use 'baan'.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of sense 0.

notes: Do not confuse 'baan' (a specific paid position, countable) with 'werk' (work or labor in general, uncountable).

senses.definition: A regular paid position of employment.

examples.text: Ik ben op zoek naar een nieuwe baan.
examples.translation: I am looking for a new job.

senses.definition: A prepared course, court, or lane used for sports or traffic, such as a running track, skating rink, or motorway lane.

examples.text: De hardloper rent op de baan.
examples.translation: The runner is running on the track.

faults.why: Both senses describe the same core state of being nervous, panicked, or flustered.

faults.quote: It describes someone who is currently in a state of panic,
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammatical information.
Should explain how both parts of this compound adjective inflect for gender and number.

notes: Formed from the verb घबराना (to panic or worry).
Both parts change to match the noun: घबराए हुए (masculine plural/oblique) and घबराई हुई (feminine).

senses.definition: Feeling nervous, worried, or flustered, especially because of something sudden or stressful.

examples.text: इंटरव्यू से पहले वह बहुत घबराया हुआ था।
examples.translation: He was very nervous before the interview.

faults.quote: Use 'बुरा' to describe something of poor quality or an action
faults.why: Merely repeats the definitions of the two senses.
Missing note on inflection (बुरा/बुरे/बुरी) and common A2 expressions like बुरा लगना.

notes: Changes to बुरे for masculine plural or oblique nouns, and बुरी for feminine nouns.
Commonly used in expressions like बुरा लगना (to feel bad or offended) and बुरा मानना (to take offense).

senses.definition: Not good, unpleasant, or of poor quality.

examples.text: आज मौसम बहुत बुरा है।
examples.translation: The weather is very bad today.

senses.definition: Morally wrong, wicked, or harmful.

examples.text: उसने कोई बुरा काम नहीं किया।
examples.translation: He did not do anything bad.

faults.quote: Something that is provided without needing any payment.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Something that...') rather than a quality.

faults.quote: Used to describe something that does not require payment.
faults.why: Restates the definition; should note the alternative pronunciation/spelling without nuqta or the phrase मुफ़्त में.

notes: Does not change form for gender or number. Often pronounced /mʊpʰt̪/ and spelled मुफ्त in everyday writing.
The phrase मुफ़्त में means 'for free' (at no cost). For 'free' as in 'not busy', use ख़ाली (khālī); for 'independent', use आज़ाद (āzād).

senses.definition: Costing nothing; provided without requiring any payment.

examples.text: यह किताब मुफ़्त है।
examples.translation: This book is free.

faults.quote: Use 'आसान' for things that require little effort, like a test
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful grammatical or usage detail.

notes: Does not change form for gender or number.
आसान is the everyday word for 'easy', whereas सरल (saral) is more formal and often means 'simple' or 'straightforward'.

senses.definition: Not difficult; requiring little effort to do or understand.

examples.text: यह परीक्षा बहुत आसान है।
examples.translation: This exam is very easy.

faults.quote: Used commonly in cooking and at the breakfast table.
faults.why: Both notes explain encyclopedia facts about butter and margarine rather than Greek usage.

notes: Usually uncountable in everyday use; the plural 'βούτυρα' means different types or packages of butter.

senses.definition: A yellow solid fat made from cream, used in cooking or spread on bread.

examples.text: Άλειψε λίγο βούτυρο στο ψωμί.
examples.translation: Spread a little butter on the bread.

faults.quote: /scoliˈo/
faults.why: Wrong consonant and stress: 'σχ' is /sx/, and the stress is on 'λεί' (/sxoˈli.o/).

notes: 'Σχολείο' refers to the school as an institution or building, whereas 'μάθημα' refers to a lesson or class.

senses.definition: A place where children go to learn and study.

examples.text: Τα παιδιά πηγαίνουν στο σχολείο κάθε πρωί.
examples.translation: The children go to school every morning.

faults.quote: The meat from a mature sheep.
faults.why: Mutton is normally called 'πρόβειο κρέας' (or 'προβατίνα'), not 'πρόβατο'.

faults.quote: sheep; mutton
faults.why: 'Mutton' is not a standard sense of the noun 'πρόβατο'.

notes: 'Πρόβατο' is the adult animal; a lamb (and lamb meat) is 'αρνί', while sheep's milk or meat is described with the adjective 'πρόβειος' (e.g. 'πρόβειο γιαούρτι').

senses.definition: A farm animal with thick wool raised for its milk, meat, and wool.

examples.text: Τα πρόβατα βόσκουν στο λιβάδι.
examples.translation: The sheep are grazing in the meadow.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'άνθρωπος' (human/person)
faults.why: Note [1] repeats Note [0] while missing everyday countable usage (e.g., 'τραπέζι για τέσσερα άτομα').

notes: Standard in plural ('άτομα') when counting people, such as for bookings or groups (e.g. 'τραπέζι για τέσσερα άτομα', a table for four).
In the singular, it refers to an individual regardless of gender, whereas 'άνθρωπος' means a human being more generally.

senses.definition: A single human being, either as an individual or when counting people.

examples.text: Είναι ένα πολύ ευγενικό άτομο.
examples.translation: He is a very polite person.

senses.definition: The smallest basic unit of a chemical element.

examples.text: Το άτομο αποτελείται από πρωτόνια, νετρόνια και ηλεκτρόνια.
examples.translation: The atom consists of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

faults.quote: /ˈçi.o.ni/
faults.why: In standard Modern Greek 'χιο' undergoes synizesis and is two syllables: /ˈço.ni/.

notes: Pronounced in two syllables (/ˈço.ni/), as the 'ι' before 'ό' is not a separate vowel.
Often used in the plural ('τα χιόνια') when referring to heavy snowfall or snow covering the ground.

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather.

examples.text: Το χιόνι πέφτει σιγά σιγά στα δέντρα.
examples.translation: The snow is falling slowly on the trees.

faults.quote: กระโดด is the general verb for moving upward off the ground
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

faults.quote: To move quickly from one place, position, or topic to another.
faults.why: The 'skip over' meaning belongs to ข้าม; กระโดด here just modifies it literally.

corrected.shortGloss: to jump; to leap; to hop
notes: In informal spoken Thai, it is often shortened to โดด (/doːt̚˨˩/).

senses.definition: To push yourself off the ground into the air using your legs and feet.

examples.text: เด็กๆ ชอบกระโดด
examples.translation: The children like to jump.

examples.text: เขากระโดดข้ามรั้ว
examples.translation: He jumped over the fence.

notes: Use this verb for climbing structures or natural features using both hands and feet. For walking up a mountain path or stairs, use เดินขึ้น (walk up) instead.

senses.definition: To go up or over something by using your hands and feet.

examples.text: เด็กๆ ชอบปีนต้นไม้ในสวน
examples.translation: Children like to climb trees in the garden.

examples.text: เขาพยายามปีนหน้าผา
examples.translation: He is trying to scale the cliff.

faults.quote: Used when picking something out from a group.
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage value.

corrected.shortGloss: to choose; to select; to elect
notes: Can also mean 'to elect' when choosing a person for a position or role (and is part of เลือกตั้ง, 'to vote in an election').

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want out of a group.

examples.text: คุณอยากเลือกอันไหน
examples.translation: Which one do you want to choose?

faults.why: Must explain that the object goes between ทำ and แตก (ทำ + [object] + แตก).

senses.definition: To cause something fragile to break or shatter into pieces.

examples.text: ฉันทำแก้วแตก
examples.translation: I broke the glass.

faults.quote: Used for casting or propelling objects through the air with the hand.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: อย่าโยนขยะลงพื้น
faults.why: ทิ้งขยะ is standard for littering; โยนขยะลงพื้น is less idiomatic for 'do not litter'.

notes: Differs from ปา (/paː˧/) and ขว้าง (/kʰwaːŋ˥˩/), which imply throwing with force or aiming at a target, whereas โยน is general or gentle tossing.

senses.definition: To send an object through the air using your hand.

examples.text: เขากำลังโยนลูกบอลให้เพื่อน
examples.translation: He is throwing a ball to his friend.

examples.text: เธอโยนกุญแจลงบนโต๊ะ
examples.translation: She tossed the keys onto the table.

faults.quote: 'sain' (healthy) or 'cent' (hundred), which are pronounced exactly the same
faults.why: 'sain' (/sɛ̃/) is not pronounced the same as 'sang' and 'cent' (/sɑ̃/).

notes: The final 'g' is silent: 'sang' is pronounced /sɑ̃/, just like 'cent' (hundred) and 'sans' (without).

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows through the body.

examples.text: Le sang circule dans tout le corps.
examples.translation: Blood circulates throughout the entire body.

senses.definition: A person's ancestry, descent, or family origin.

examples.text: C'est dans le sang de leur famille.
examples.translation: It runs in their family's blood.

faults.quote: secret; privacy
faults.why: 'privacy' is not covered by any of the senses.

faults.quote: Used as a noun meaning something hidden or kept confidential from others.
faults.why: Merely restates the part of speech and definition.

notes: The final 't' is silent. Also used as an adjective meaning 'secret' or 'hidden' (feminine: 'secrète', with the 't' pronounced).

senses.definition: Something that is kept or meant to be kept unknown by others.

examples.text: Elle sait garder un secret.
examples.translation: She knows how to keep a secret.

senses.definition: The effective method or explanation behind achieving something.

examples.text: Le secret du succès, c'est le travail.
examples.translation: The secret to success is hard work.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'le sel' with 'la selve', which is an old
faults.why: Warns against an archaic word ('la selve') that a beginner will never encounter.

notes: As an uncountable noun, it is usually used with the partitive article 'du' (e.g., 'passer du sel' — to pass some salt).

senses.definition: The white crystalline substance used to season and preserve food.

examples.text: Ajoute un peu de sel dans la soupe.
examples.translation: Add a little salt to the soup.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'la serpente', which is a type of
faults.why: Restates the definition and warns against a rare technical bookbinding term.

notes: Note the pronunciation: the final 't' is silent and '-en-' is a nasal vowel (/ɑ̃/).

senses.definition: A long reptile with no legs that moves by sliding along the ground.

examples.text: Attention, il y a un serpent dans les buissons.
examples.translation: Watch out, there is a snake in the bushes.

faults.quote: In France, 'serveur' is the standard word for a waiter in a
faults.why: Merely restates the first definition without adding useful contrast.

notes: The feminine form for a waitress is 'la serveuse'. In modern French, always use 'serveur' or 'serveuse' rather than the outdated 'garçon'.

senses.definition: A person who serves customers in a restaurant or café.

examples.text: Le serveur apporte la carte des vins.
examples.translation: The waiter brings the wine list.

senses.definition: A computer system that provides data or services to other computers on a network.

examples.text: Le site web est hébergé sur un serveur distant.
examples.translation: The website is hosted on a remote server.

faults.quote: In Greek, 'το κοτόπουλο' refers to both the live bird and the
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; English 'chicken' works the same way.

faults.quote: chicken, hen, rooster
faults.why: 'Hen' is κότα and 'rooster' is κόκορας; κοτόπουλο is the generic chicken or young bird.

notes: For an egg-laying hen specifically, Greek normally uses 'η κότα'.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.text: Παρήγγειλα ψητό κοτόπουλο με πατάτες.
examples.translation: I ordered roast chicken with potatoes.

senses.definition: A common farm bird kept for its eggs or meat.

examples.text: Το κοτόπουλο τρέχει στην αυλή.
examples.translation: The chicken is running in the yard.

faults.quote: such as fish versus fish or poisson versus poisson.
faults.why: Nonsensical claim; English and French also use the same word ('fish', 'poisson') for both.

notes: The plural is 'τα ψάρια', which is very common when ordering or talking about food.

senses.definition: An animal that lives in water and swims using fins.

examples.text: Το ψάρι κολυμπάει στη θάλασσα.
examples.translation: The fish is swimming in the sea.

senses.definition: The flesh of a fish eaten as food.

examples.text: Παρήγγειλα ψητό ψάρι για μεσημεριανό.
examples.translation: I ordered grilled fish for lunch.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a one-piece garment that includes a skirt.
faults.why: Repeats the definition of 'dress' verbatim.

notes: Has an irregular stress shift in the genitive singular (του φορέματος) and throughout the plural (τα φορέματα).
