senses.definition: A one-piece garment for women or girls that covers the body and extends down over the legs.

examples.text: Αυτό το κόκκινο φόρεμα είναι πολύ όμορφο.
examples.translation: This red dress is very beautiful.

faults.quote: Used extensively in Greece to mean both a traditional coffee shop and
faults.why: Contradicts note 1 and is false: a traditional Greek coffee house is 'το καφενείο', not 'η καφετέρια'.

notes: False friend: despite looking like English 'cafeteria', it means a modern café or coffee bar, not a self-service canteen.
Contrast with 'το καφενείο', a traditional Greek coffee house.

senses.definition: A modern café where people meet to drink coffee and other beverages.

examples.text: Πάμε σε μια καφετέρια για έναν καφέ.
examples.translation: Let's go to a café for a coffee.

faults.quote: /astu-nomiˈkos/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'υ' in Modern Greek is pronounced /i/, not /u/ (/astinomiˈkos/).

faults.quote: though the grammatical gender is masculine with the article ο.
faults.why: It is a common-gender noun: for a female officer, it takes the feminine article 'η αστυνομικός'.

notes: Used for both male and female officers with the same endings; for a woman, use the feminine article: 'η αστυνομικός'.

senses.definition: A member of the police force.

examples.text: Ο αστυνομικός ζήτησε από τον οδηγό τα στοιχεία του.
examples.translation: The police officer asked the driver for his ID.

faults.quote: /kʰɔːŋ˩.kʰwan˩/
faults.why: Both syllables have a rising tone (/kʰɔ̌ːŋ.kʰwǎn/), not a low tone.

faults.quote: ของขวัญ is used for any physical gift given on a special occasion
faults.why: Restates the definition; should give the classifier (ชิ้น or กล่อง) instead.

notes: Counted with the classifier ชิ้น (piece) or กล่อง (box).

senses.definition: Something you give to someone on a special occasion such as a birthday or New Year.

examples.text: ฉันซื้อของขวัญวันเกิดให้เพื่อน
examples.translation: I bought a birthday gift for my friend.

faults.quote: ขอ น้ำ เปล่า หนึ่ง แก้ว ครับ
faults.why: Thai script does not put spaces between words.

faults.quote: The liquid extract or juice of fruits or vegetables.
faults.why: น้ำ alone means any liquid or fluid; 'juice' is only in compounds like น้ำส้ม.

notes: Used as the first word in compounds for drinks, juices, and sauces, such as น้ำส้ม (orange juice) and น้ำปลา (fish sauce).

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain, fills rivers, and is drunk by people and animals.

examples.text: ขอน้ำเปล่าหนึ่งแก้วครับ
examples.translation: One glass of plain water, please.

senses.definition: Any liquid, fluid, or drink, especially in compounds naming a kind of drink or sauce.

examples.text: ฉันชอบดื่มน้ำส้มทุกเช้า
examples.translation: I like to drink orange juice every morning.

faults.quote: Used specifically for political or international boundaries between countries.
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: Used for the border area between countries; for the edge of an object (like a table or page), use ขอบ.

senses.definition: The official boundary line or area separating two countries.

examples.text: เราไปเที่ยวที่ชายแดนไทย-ลาว
examples.translation: We went to visit the Thai-Lao border.

faults.quote: Often shortened to just สุดสัปดาห์ in casual conversation.
faults.why: In casual Thai people say เสาร์อาทิตย์ (Saturday-Sunday); สุดสัปดาห์ and วันหยุดสุดสัปดาห์ are both formal.

corrected.headword: วันหยุดสุดสัปดาห์
notes: Formed from วันหยุด (day off) + สุดสัปดาห์ (end of the week). Rather formal; in everyday speech, people usually say เสาร์อาทิตย์ (literally 'Saturday-Sunday').

senses.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the two days at the end of the week when most people do not work.

examples.text: ฉันอยากไปเที่ยวทะเลในวันหยุดสุดสัปดาห์นี้
examples.translation: I want to go to the beach this weekend.
examples.matchedForm: วันหยุดสุดสัปดาห์

faults.why: Physical and emotional pain are one abstract noun sense in Thai; examples are also missing.

corrected.headword: ความเจ็บปวด
notes: An abstract noun formed with ความ + เจ็บปวด (to feel pain). In everyday speech, to say a body part hurts, use the verbs เจ็บ or ปวด directly rather than this noun.

senses.definition: The feeling of physical pain or deep emotional suffering.

examples.text: ยาตัวนี้ช่วยลดความเจ็บปวดได้
examples.translation: This medicine helps reduce the pain.
examples.matchedForm: ความเจ็บปวด

faults.quote: The police officer guided me on the road.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of '길을 안내해 주다' (to give directions / show the way).

notes: 경찰관 is the specific word for an individual officer, though 경찰 (police) is often used for both the force and an officer in everyday speech.

senses.definition: A member of the police force.

examples.text: 경찰관이 길을 안내해 주었습니다.
examples.translation: The police officer showed me the way.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with '반쪽' (half), which sounds somewhat similar.
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; learners need the verb for wearing a ring ('끼다') instead.

notes: Takes the verb 끼다 for 'to wear/put on' (반지를 끼다), not 입다.
Matching rings worn by romantic partners are commonly called 커플링 (couple ring).

senses.definition: A small circular band, usually made of metal, worn on a finger.

examples.text: 그녀는 아름다운 다이아몬드 반지를 끼고 있다.
examples.translation: She is wearing a beautiful diamond ring.

faults.quote: Something that is difficult to understand or explain.
faults.why: Oversplit; in sense 1's example, 비밀 still means 'secret', not 'mystery' (미스터리/수수께끼).

faults.quote: 비밀 is used for both things kept hidden from others and
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions.

notes: Common collocations: 비밀을 지키다 (to keep a secret), 비밀로 하다 (to keep something a secret).

senses.definition: Information kept hidden from others, or not yet known.

examples.text: 그는 나에게 비밀을 지켜 달라고 부탁했다.
examples.translation: He asked me to keep the secret.

faults.quote: /tɕʰo.kʰo.lit̚/
faults.why: Wrong IPA; intervocalic ㄹ after ㄹ in 초콜릿 is geminate [ɭ.ɭ], not [l].

notes: The final ㅅ is pronounced [t̚] before a pause or consonant, and [s] before a vowel particle (e.g. 초콜릿을 [초콜리슬]).

senses.definition: A sweet brown food or candy made from cocoa.

examples.text: 초콜릿을 너무 많이 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.translation: You shouldn't eat too much chocolate.

faults.quote: This word is a homonym in Korean. The meaning is usually clear
faults.why: Pure filler; fails to mention the vowel-length distinction or useful collocations.

faults.quote: Soft white water that falls from the sky when it is cold.
faults.why: 'Soft white water' is an awkward and inaccurate way to define snow.

notes: When meaning 'snow', it takes the verbs 오다 or 내리다 (눈이 오다/내리다, 'to snow').

senses.definition: The part of the body used for seeing.

examples.text: 아기 눈이 정말 커요.
examples.translation: The baby's eyes are really big.

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of ice that fall from the sky in cold weather.

examples.text: 밖에는 눈이 많이 와요.
examples.translation: It is snowing a lot outside.

faults.quote: 'Eu nunca não fui' (I have never not gone).
faults.why: Misexplains Portuguese negative concord; 'não' is required only when 'nunca' follows the verb.

notes: Before the verb, 'nunca' is used alone ('Eu nunca fui'); after the verb, 'não' is required before the verb ('Eu não fui nunca', I never went).
Opposite of 'sempre' (always).

senses.definition: At no time; on no occasion.

examples.text: Eu nunca comi sushi.
examples.translation: I have never eaten sushi.

examples.text: Nós nunca chegamos atrasados.
examples.translation: We never arrive late.

faults.quote: lamp, lampshade
faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'abajur' is the whole table lamp; the shade is 'cúpula'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'lâmpada', which in Brazil means the light bulb itself; 'abajur' is the whole table or bedside lamp.

senses.definition: A small lamp with a shade, placed on a table or beside a bed.

examples.text: Eu liguei o abajur para ler um livro antes de dormir.
examples.translation: I turned on the lamp to read a book before going to sleep.

faults.quote: Note that the masculine article 'o' is used before 'açúcar'
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'sal' (salt), which looks somewhat similar
faults.why: Trivial real-world observation, not a linguistic confusion for learners.

notes: Usually uncountable; plural 'açúcares' is used only for types of sugar.

senses.definition: A sweet crystalline substance used to sweeten food and drinks.

examples.text: Eu coloco açúcar no café todas as manhãs.
examples.translation: I put sugar in my coffee every morning.

faults.quote: /ɐ.du.le.sẽ.tʃi/
faults.why: Uses European Portuguese vowel reduction (/ɐ.du/) and lacks primary stress mark.

notes: Has the same form in the masculine ('o adolescente') and the feminine ('a adolescente'); also used as an adjective.
By Brazilian law, 'adolescente' refers to a person aged twelve to eighteen.

senses.definition: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult.

examples.text: O adolescente passa muito tempo no celular.
examples.translation: The teenager spends a lot of time on his cell phone.

notes: Feminine form: 'a adulta'. Also used as an adjective ('uma pessoa adulta').

senses.definition: A grown-up person who is fully developed and legally responsible.

examples.text: O ingresso para adulto custa mais caro.
examples.translation: The adult ticket costs more.

faults.quote: Both are generally interchangeable in everyday conversation.
faults.why: सागर is not used in everyday conversation; समंदर (samandar) is the common colloquial word.

notes: समुद्र (samudra) is the standard formal word. In everyday speech, songs, and films, the colloquial variant समंदर (samandar) is very common; सागर (sāgar) is mainly literary.

senses.definition: A vast body of salt water covering much of the earth.

examples.text: समुद्र का पानी खारा होता है।
examples.translation: Sea water is salty.

examples.text: हम कल समुद्र के किनारे जाएँगे।
examples.translation: We will go to the seaside tomorrow.

faults.why: Lacks the feminine counterpart किशोरी (adolescent girl) and the formal register.

notes: Used mainly in news and formal writing; the feminine form for a teenage girl is किशोरी (kiśorī). In everyday speech, people usually say टीनेजर (teenager) or लड़का/लड़की (boy/girl).

senses.definition: A young person between childhood and adulthood; a teenage boy or teenager.

examples.text: आजकल के किशोर इंटरनेट पर बहुत समय बिताते हैं।
examples.translation: Teenagers these days spend a lot of time on the internet.

faults.why: Overcoat and suit jacket are a single sense in Hindi for the English loanword कोट.

notes: In Hindi, कोट most often refers to a suit jacket or blazer, as well as a winter overcoat. For a casual or zip-up jacket, जैकेट (jacket) is used.

senses.definition: An outer garment with sleeves worn over a shirt for warmth or formal wear, such as a suit jacket, blazer, or overcoat.

examples.text: बाहर ठंड है, अपना कोट पहन लो।
examples.translation: It is cold outside, put on your coat.

examples.text: शादी के लिए उसने नया कोट सिलवाया।
examples.translation: He had a new suit jacket tailored for the wedding.

faults.quote: /zuŋ͡m ˈkaːm/
faults.why: Lacks tone marks and uses English-style primary stress.

faults.quote: Dũng cảm describes someone who faces danger, difficulty, or pain without backing down.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition.

notes: The letter 'd' is pronounced /z/ in northern (Hanoi) Vietnamese and /j/ in southern Vietnamese.

senses.definition: Of a person or action: not afraid of danger; showing courage in the face of difficulty or fear.

examples.text: Anh ấy rất dũng cảm khi cứu đứa trẻ khỏi đám cháy.
examples.translation: He was very brave when saving the child from the fire.

faults.quote: Use 'dừng' to indicate that a movement or process has come to
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the very common collocation 'dừng lại'.

notes: Very often paired with 'lại' as 'dừng lại' (to come to a stop).
Unlike 'ngừng' or 'dứt' (to cease permanently), 'dừng' usually implies a temporary stop or pause in movement or action.

senses.definition: To cease moving, or to bring an ongoing movement or action to a halt.

examples.text: Xe buýt sẽ dừng lại ở trạm tiếp theo.
examples.translation: The bus will stop at the next stop.

examples.text: Xin hãy dừng nói chuyện.
examples.translation: Please stop talking.

faults.quote: /ɛm ʔbeː/
faults.why: Lacks tone marks and gives wrong vowel quality (/eː/ instead of /ɛ/).

notes: Literally 'little younger sibling' ('em' + 'bé'). It can be used with or without the classifier 'đứa'.

senses.definition: A baby or very young child.

examples.text: Em bé đang ngủ ngon trong nôi.
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping soundly in the crib.

faults.quote: It is also commonly used as a friendly or polite pronoun to
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1 without explaining what pronouns pair with it.

notes: Composed of 'em' (younger sibling/person) and 'gái' (female). Compare 'chị gái' (older sister) and 'em trai' (younger brother).
When addressing a young woman as 'em gái', the speaker refers to themselves as 'anh' (if male) or 'chị' (if female).

senses.definition: A female sibling who is younger than you.

examples.text: Em gái tôi đang học đại học ở Hà Nội.
examples.translation: My younger sister is studying at university in Hanoi.

senses.definition: A friendly term of address for a girl or young woman who is younger than the speaker.

examples.text: Em gái ơi, cho chị một cốc nước mía.
examples.translation: Miss, please give me a glass of sugarcane juice.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the dark hours between sunset and sunrise.
faults.why: Repeats the definition word for word and omits the distinction from 'tối'.

notes: Compare with 'tối' (evening/early night, roughly 6–10 p.m.): 'đêm' refers to late night (after about 10 p.m.) or the whole night until dawn.
Commonly used in 'ban đêm' (at night / nighttime) and 'đêm qua' (last night).

senses.definition: The dark part of the twenty-four-hour day, especially late at night until sunrise.

examples.text: Đêm qua tôi không ngủ được.
examples.translation: I couldn't sleep last night.

faults.quote: /ˈmoːsəm/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: औ represents /ɔː/, not /oː/.

faults.quote: Use 'मौसम' for the daily weather report and 'ऋतु' for the cycles
faults.why: Overstates 'ऋतु' (very formal); 'मौसम' is the normal everyday word for seasons too.
Polysemous entry has no examples showing how the two senses are used.

notes: Used in everyday Hindi for both the daily weather and the seasons of the year (e.g., सर्दी का मौसम, the winter season). The synonym ऋतु (ritu, 'season') is much more formal and literary.

senses.definition: The condition of the air outside at a particular time and place, such as whether it is hot, rainy, or windy.

examples.text: आज मौसम बहुत अच्छा है।
examples.translation: The weather is very nice today.

senses.definition: One of the main periods of the year with its own typical weather, such as summer, winter, or the rainy season.

examples.text: मुझे सर्दियों का मौसम बहुत पसंद है।
examples.translation: I really like the winter season.

faults.quote: It is a feminine noun, so you will typically use it with
faults.why: Restates the gender field without giving useful collocations like 'बारिश होना'.

notes: To say 'to rain', Hindi uses the noun बारिश with the verb होना (to happen): बारिश हो रही है (it is raining).
More common in everyday speech than the formal Sanskrit-derived word वर्षा (varṣā).

senses.definition: Water that falls from the clouds in drops.

examples.text: आज बहुत तेज़ बारिश हो रही है।
examples.translation: It is raining very heavily today.

faults.quote: It is a central place in Indian cities and towns for mailing
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition of a post office.

notes: A compound of डाक (post, mail) and घर (house). In everyday speech, the English word 'post office' (पोस्ट ऑफ़िस) is also very widely used.

senses.definition: A building where you go to send letters and parcels or buy stamps.

examples.text: मुझे डाकघर जाना है।
examples.translation: I have to go to the post office.

faults.quote: A very high hill that stands prominently in the landscape.
faults.why: Artificial split: 'mountain' and 'very high hill' are the same sense of पहाड़.

faults.quote: हिमालय एक बहुत ऊँचा पहाड़ है। — The Himalayas is a very
faults.why: Ungrammatical English ('The Himalayas is...'), and Himalayas are a range, not one mountain.

notes: Do not confuse with the feminine noun पहाड़ी (pahāṛī), which means a smaller hill, or as an adjective/noun, 'from the mountains'.

senses.definition: A very high area of land with steep sides, much higher than a hill.

examples.text: यह एक बहुत ऊँचा पहाड़ है।
examples.translation: This is a very high mountain.

faults.quote: This word is feminine in Hindi, so any adjectives or verbs describing
faults.why: Both notes are filler: one restates the gender, the other is trivia.

notes: Like other feminine nouns ending in -ई (-ī), its plural is formed with -इयाँ (-iyā̃): तितलियाँ (titliyā̃, 'butterflies').

senses.definition: An insect with large, often brightly coloured wings.

examples.text: फूल पर एक सुंदर तितली बैठी है।
examples.translation: A beautiful butterfly is sitting on the flower.

faults.quote: where it often changes to बहुते or takes an oblique form
faults.why: False grammar: बहुत is an invariable adjective/adverb in standard Hindi; बहुते is dialectal.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with थोड़ा (thoṛā), which means 'a little'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse unrelated antonyms that neither sound nor look alike.

faults.quote: A large quantity or number of something.
faults.why: Defined as a noun rather than a determiner/adverb.

notes: Used both as an adverb before adjectives ('very') and as an invariable determiner before nouns ('much', 'many'). It never changes form for gender or number.

senses.definition: To a high degree; used before adjectives or adverbs, or with verbs.

examples.text: यह खाना बहुत स्वादिष्ट है।
examples.translation: This food is very delicious.

senses.definition: In a large quantity or number; used before countable or uncountable nouns.

examples.text: मेरे पास बहुत काम है।
examples.translation: I have a lot of work.

faults.quote: अब से मैं रोज़ पढ़ाई करूँगा।
faults.why: 'From now on' is the phrase अब से (with postposition से), not a separate sense of अब.

notes: Do not confuse with अभी (abhī), which is more immediate ('right now', 'just now').

senses.definition: At the present time or moment, as opposed to the past or future.

examples.text: अब बारिश रुक गई है।
examples.translation: Now the rain has stopped.

examples.text: अब वह यहाँ नहीं रहता।
examples.translation: He doesn't live here anymore.

faults.quote: It is used to indicate that an action happens occasionally
faults.why: Second sentence just restates the definition.

notes: Formed by reduplicating कभी ('ever').

senses.definition: At times or on some occasions, but not regularly.

examples.text: मैं कभी-कभी चाय पीता हूँ।
examples.translation: I sometimes drink tea.

faults.quote: For a natural geological wall or cliff, use tebing.
faults.why: Compares with 'tebing' (cliff) instead of the common near-synonym 'tembok' (masonry/outer wall).

notes: Often contrasted with 'tembok': 'dinding' is the general word for any interior wall or room divider, while 'tembok' specifically refers to a thick brick or concrete wall (especially outdoors).

senses.definition: A vertical structure that divides or encloses a room or building.

examples.text: Dia menggantung lukisan di dinding.
examples.translation: She hung a painting on the wall.

faults.why: Cold weather and cold objects are the same literal temperature sense.

notes: Do not confuse with 'sejuk', which describes a pleasant, refreshing coolness rather than an uncomfortably low temperature.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm.

examples.text: Udara di puncak gunung sangat dingin pada malam hari.
examples.translation: The air at the mountain peak is very cold at night.

examples.text: Tolong ambilkan air dingin dari kulkas.
examples.translation: Please get me some cold water from the fridge.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: unfriendly or showing no emotion.

examples.text: Sikapnya sangat dingin kepada saya hari ini.
examples.translation: His attitude toward me is very cold today.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'perawat', which means nurse.
faults.why: Explains the universal difference between a doctor and a nurse; misses the title/address 'Dok'.

notes: Used as a title before a name (written 'dr.' in lowercase, e.g., 'dr. Budi'), and shortened to 'Dok' when addressing a doctor directly.

senses.definition: A person who is qualified to treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: Saya harus pergi ke dokter karena sakit kepala.
examples.translation: I have to go to the doctor because of a headache.

examples.text: Dokter itu memberikan resep obat kepada pasien.
examples.translation: The doctor gave a prescription to the patient.

faults.quote: and to the material produced by them (wool).
faults.why: 'Domba' does not mean wool; wool is 'wol' or 'bulu domba'.

notes: Also called 'biri-biri' in everyday speech. Do not confuse with 'kambing' (goat), though in Indonesian cuisine lamb and mutton dishes are often grouped under 'kambing'.

senses.definition: A farm animal with a thick woolly coat, kept for its wool or meat.

examples.text: Banyak domba makan rumput di bukit.
examples.translation: Many sheep are eating grass on the hill.

faults.quote: Used to describe feeling surprise or astonishment when something unexpected happens.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

faults.quote: Can be intensified with rất (very) or quá (too/so).
faults.why: True of almost all Vietnamese adjectives; not specific to this word.

notes: Followed by 'về' (about) or 'trước' (at/by) to name what causes the surprise, or 'khi' (when) before a clause.

senses.definition: Feeling surprise because something unexpected has happened.

examples.text: Tôi rất ngạc nhiên khi thấy anh ấy ở đây.
examples.translation: I was very surprised to see him here.

notes: Unlike English 'short', 'ngắn' only describes length or duration (and opposite 'dài'). For a person's or object's height, use 'thấp'.

senses.definition: Measuring a small distance from one end to the other; not long.

examples.text: Cái bút này quá ngắn.
examples.translation: This pen is too short.

senses.definition: Lasting for a small amount of time.

examples.text: Chúng tôi có một chuyến đi ngắn.
examples.translation: We had a short trip.

faults.quote: /ŋən˧ t͡ɕaːŋ˨˩/
faults.why: Wrong consonant /t͡ɕ/ for 'hàng'; in Hanoi Vietnamese it is /haːŋ˨˩/.

faults.quote: A place or a storehouse where things like data, blood, or organs
faults.why: Secondary compound usage ('blood bank'); unnecessary separate sense for A2.

faults.quote: bank; depository

faults.quote: Used to mean both the financial institution and the physical building
faults.why: Works the same way as English 'bank'; no special learner note needed.

notes: Takes the classifier 'nhà' or 'cái' only rarely; usually used without a classifier.

senses.definition: An organization or building where people keep, borrow, and exchange money.

examples.text: Tôi cần đến ngân hàng để rút tiền mặt.
examples.translation: I need to go to the bank to withdraw cash.

faults.quote: /ŋàj 1 maːj 1/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA containing raw digits '1' and wrong vowel length for 'ngày'.

faults.quote: adv
faults.why: Time expressions like 'ngày mai' are nouns in Vietnamese, though used adverbially.

faults.quote: Use ngày mai when talking about the day immediately following today.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with hôm qua, which means yesterday.
faults.why: Unmotivated filler; 'ngày mai' and 'hôm qua' do not look or sound alike.

faults.why: «Человек» means person/human; adult male is «мужчина». Confusing for beginners.

notes: The plural of «челове́к» is «лю́ди». However, after numbers and «ско́лько» / «не́сколько», the form «челове́к» is used for the genitive plural (e.g., «пять челове́к» — five people).
To refer specifically to an adult male ('a man'), use «мужчи́на».

senses.definition: A human being; an individual person.

examples.text: На улице стоял высокий человек.
examples.translation: A tall person was standing on the street.

examples.text: Этот человек помог мне донести сумку.
examples.translation: This person helped me carry my bag.

faults.quote: Literally means 'honey-eater' (мед + ведать).
faults.why: «Ведать» means 'to know', not 'to eat' (the root is *ěd- 'eat', not ведать).

faults.quote: Often used metaphorically in Russian culture to represent Russia
faults.why: Cultural trivia and restatement of sense 1; not useful usage guidance.

notes: This is an animate noun, so its accusative form matches the genitive («встре́тить медве́дя»).

senses.definition: A large, heavy wild animal with thick fur, sharp claws, and a short tail.

examples.text: В лесу можно встретить медведя.
examples.translation: You can meet a bear in the forest.

senses.definition: A large, clumsy, or awkward person.

examples.text: Ну ты и медведь, опять чашку разбил!
examples.translation: You are such a clumsy bear, you broke a cup again!

faults.quote: A tool that rotates rapidly to cut or drill into hard materials.
faults.why: Technical sense (milling cutter/dental burr) is not everyday A2 vocabulary.

faults.quote: Me gusta comer una fresa dulce con yogur por la mañana.
faults.why: Eating 'one sweet strawberry' is unnatural; plurals are standard here.

notes: In Mexico and some other Latin American countries, 'fresa' is also common slang for a snobbish or preppy person.

senses.definition: A small, red, sweet fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: Me gusta desayunar yogur con fresas.
examples.translation: I like to have yogurt with strawberries for breakfast.

faults.quote: Used for both physical dividing lines between countries and metaphoric limits
faults.why: Generic statement that adds nothing beyond the standard meaning of 'border/frontier'.

senses.definition: The dividing line that separates two countries or regions.

examples.text: Tuvimos que enseñar el pasaporte al cruzar la frontera.
examples.translation: We had to show our passports when crossing the border.

faults.quote: Used for the edible sweet part of a plant containing seeds
faults.why: Merely restates the definition while missing usage notes on countability and 'fruto'.

notes: Often used in the singular as an uncountable noun for fruit in general ('comer fruta'), or in the plural for a single piece ('una pieza de fruta').
Do not confuse with 'el fruto', which refers to the botanical fruit, nuts ('frutos secos'), or a figurative result.

senses.definition: The sweet, edible part of a plant that contains seeds.

examples.text: Compro fruta fresca en el mercado todos los martes.
examples.translation: I buy fresh fruit at the market every Tuesday.

faults.quote: It is also used informally to call someone a coward.
faults.why: Restates sense 1 without adding grammar (e.g., that it stays 'un gallina' for men).

notes: Refers to the living female bird (as opposed to 'el gallo', rooster); for chicken meat as food, use 'el pollo'.
In the 'coward' sense, the word does not change ending for a man: 'es un gallina'.

senses.definition: A female bird kept on farms for its eggs and meat.

examples.text: Las gallinas del abuelo ponen huevos todos los días.
examples.translation: Grandpa's hens lay eggs every day.

senses.definition: (informal) A person who lacks courage or is easily frightened.

examples.text: No seas gallina y sube a la montaña rusa.
examples.translation: Don't be a coward and get on the roller coaster.

faults.quote: Use frontière for the official political border between countries, as well as
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses without adding useful information.

faults.quote: Il y a une frontière mince entre la réalité et l'illusion.
faults.why: Calque from English 'thin line'; French says 'la frontière est mince entre...' or 'une fine frontière'.

notes: The adjective 'sans frontières' means 'without borders' (e.g. Médecins Sans Frontières).

senses.definition: The dividing line between two countries.

examples.text: Nous avons traversé la frontière en voiture.
examples.translation: We crossed the border by car.

senses.definition: A limit between two areas, subjects, or ideas.

examples.text: La frontière entre le travail et la vie privée est parfois floue.
examples.translation: The boundary between work and private life is sometimes blurry.

notes: Alone, 'la gare' always means a train station. A bus or coach station is 'la gare routière', and a metro or bus stop is 'une station'.

senses.definition: A place where trains stop for passengers to get on and off.

examples.text: Nous allons à la gare pour prendre le train.
examples.translation: We are going to the station to catch the train.

faults.quote: La glace covers both ice cream and frozen water, which often confuses
faults.why: Merely restates the senses; should explain countability ('une glace' vs 'de la glace') or 'glaçon'.

notes: Countable 'une glace' means an ice cream or a mirror; uncountable 'de la glace' means ice or ice cream in bulk. Ice cubes in a drink are 'des glaçons'.

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk or cream.

examples.text: Je voudrais une glace à la vanille.
examples.translation: I would like a vanilla ice cream.

senses.definition: Water that has frozen solid.

examples.text: Il y a de la glace sur le trottoir ce matin.
examples.translation: There is ice on the sidewalk this morning.

senses.definition: A piece of glass that reflects images.

examples.text: Elle se regarde dans la glace avant de sortir.
examples.translation: She looks at herself in the mirror before going out.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'la grand-maman', which is also used
faults.why: Unhelpful filler; 'grand-maman' is old-fashioned or regional in France and not a confusion trap.

notes: In everyday speech, French speakers usually call their grandmother 'mamie'.
Plural: 'les grands-mères' or 'les grand-mères' (the 'd' is always silent).

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Ma grand-mère prépare toujours des gâteaux pour le goûter.
examples.translation: My grandmother always makes cakes for the afternoon snack.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with pied, which is specifically the foot
faults.why: Filler note; English speakers do not confuse 'leg' and 'foot', whereas French grammar with body parts is needed.

notes: As with other body parts, French often uses the definite article ('la jambe') rather than a possessive ('ma jambe') when the owner is clear: 'J'ai mal à la jambe' (My leg hurts).

senses.definition: One of the long limbs of the body used for standing and walking.

examples.text: Elle s'est cassé la jambe en faisant du ski.
examples.translation: She broke her leg while skiing.

faults.quote: Used for both large mountains and very high hills.
faults.why: Restates the glosses without giving useful grammatical information like broken plurals.

faults.quote: النَّظَرُ مِنْ قِمَّةِ الجَبَلِ
faults.why: الْمَنْظَرُ (the view/scenery) is required here, not النَّظَرُ (the act of looking/sight).

notes: The broken plural is جِبَال (jibāl), or أَجْبَال (ʔajbāl).

senses.definition: A very high natural elevation of the earth's surface.

examples.text: الْمَنْظَرُ مِنْ قِمَّةِ الْجَبَلِ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: The view from the top of the mountain is very beautiful.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a job interview, but can also mean a general
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

faults.quote: A formal meeting where someone is asked questions to see if they
faults.why: Too narrow; مقابلة means any interview (job, media, official); مقابلة عمل is job interview.

notes: For a job interview specifically, the phrase مُقَابَلَةُ عَمَل (muqābalatu ʕamal) is commonly used.

senses.definition: A formal meeting in which someone is asked questions, such as for a job or in the media.

examples.text: عِنْدِي مُقَابَلَةُ عَمَلٍ غَدًا فِي الشَّرِكَةِ.
examples.translation: I have a job interview tomorrow at the company.

senses.definition: An occasion when people meet face to face, or a sports match between two teams.

examples.text: كَانَتْ مُقَابَلَةً قَصِيرَةً وَلَكِنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ.
examples.translation: It was a short but useful meeting.

faults.quote: Used both for the hot drink itself and for the place where
faults.why: Restates the two senses; should instead note that the café sense is informal/colloquial.

notes: In formal Modern Standard Arabic, a café is usually called مَقْهًى (maqhan), while قَهْوَة is very common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: A hot dark drink made from roasted coffee beans.

examples.text: أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: I drink coffee every morning.

senses.definition: A casual place where people meet to drink coffee or tea and socialize.

examples.text: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْقَهْوَةِ مَعَ صَدِيقِي.
examples.translation: I went to the café with my friend.

faults.quote: Used to refer to any living creature that is not a plant
faults.why: Repeats the definition instead of giving useful grammar like its sound feminine plural.

notes: Although masculine, it takes the sound feminine plural ending: حَيَوَانَات (ḥayawānāt).

senses.definition: A living creature such as a mammal, bird, reptile, or insect, as opposed to a human or plant.

examples.text: الْحَيَوَانَاتُ تَعِيشُ فِي الْغَابَةِ.
examples.translation: Animals live in the forest.

faults.quote: 달 has two very common meanings: the moon in the sky
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of explaining how 달 (with native numerals) differs from 월/개월.

notes: For counting months, 달 is used after native Korean numbers (한 달, 두 달 'one month, two months'), whereas 개월 is used after Sino-Korean numbers (일 개월, 이 개월).
For naming the months of the year, use 월 instead (일월 'January', 이월 'February').

senses.definition: The bright round object that shines in the night sky.

examples.text: 오늘 밤에는 달이 참 밝아요.
examples.translation: The moon is very bright tonight.

senses.definition: A period of about four weeks, especially when counting months or referring to a whole month.

examples.text: 다음 달에 한국으로 여행을 가요.
examples.translation: I am going on a trip to Korea next month.

faults.why: 'Trip' and 'travel' in English translate the same single Korean sense of 여행.

faults.quote: For the act of taking a walk, use 산책 instead.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'travel' with 'taking a walk'; note on 여행하다/여행을 가다 is needed.

notes: Commonly used in the expressions 여행을 가다 (to go on a trip) and 여행(을) 하다 (to travel).
여행 usually refers to leisure travel or vacation. For a business trip, use 출장.

senses.definition: The act of going to another place, especially far away, for pleasure or sightseeing.

examples.text: 여름에 일본으로 여행을 갈 거예요.
examples.translation: I am going on a trip to Japan in the summer.

examples.text: 여행은 새로운 문화를 배우는 좋은 방법입니다.
examples.translation: Travel is a good way to learn about new cultures.

notes: While 포도주 is the traditional Korean word for grape wine, 와인 is much more commonly used in everyday conversation, menus, and shops.

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

examples.text: 저녁 식사 때 와인을 마셨어요.
examples.translation: I drank wine at dinner.

faults.quote: Often shortened simply to 비행 in some compound words
faults.why: 비행 is the base word 'flight', not a shortening of 비행기.

faults.quote: /bi.ɦɛŋ.ɡi/
faults.why: Initial ㅂ in Korean is voiceless [p], not voiced /b/.

notes: Used with the verb 타다 for boarding or riding: 비행기를 타다 (to take/ride a plane), and the counter 대.

senses.definition: A vehicle with wings and engines that flies in the sky.

examples.text: 비행기를 타고 제주도에 갔어요.
examples.translation: I went to Jeju Island by plane.

faults.quote: /oˈfiθina/
faults.why: Stress is on the penultimate syllable: /ofiˈθina/.

notes: In Spain, 'oficina' usually refers to a shared or corporate workplace; for a private office or a home study, 'despacho' is more common.
Do not confuse with 'oficio', which means a trade, craft, or occupation.

senses.definition: A room, building, or area where people do administrative or clerical work.

examples.text: Ella trabaja en una oficina en el centro.
examples.translation: She works in an office in the city center.

examples.text: Tengo que ir a la oficina para terminar el informe.
examples.translation: I have to go to the office to finish the report.

faults.quote: /oˈvexa/
faults.why: Spanish 'v' represents the phoneme /b/, not /v/: /oˈbexa/.

senses.definition: A farm animal with a thick woolly coat, kept for its wool or meat.

examples.text: Las ovejas comen hierba fresca en el campo.
examples.translation: The sheep eat fresh grass in the countryside.

faults.quote: Necesito otra pareja de calcetines.
faults.why: A pair of socks is 'un par de calcetines', never 'una pareja'.

faults.quote: While 'pareja' can mean any pair of objects, when applied to people
faults.why: False: 'par' is used for objects like shoes/socks; 'pareja' also means non-romantic human pairs.

faults.quote: Two people who are in a romantic relationship.
faults.why: Definition only covers 'couple', missing the very common sense 'romantic partner' (one person).

notes: Even when referring to a man as someone's romantic partner, 'la pareja' remains grammatically feminine (e.g., 'Juan es mi pareja').
For pairs of everyday objects like shoes or socks, use 'el par' ('un par de calcetines'), not 'pareja'.

senses.definition: Two people who are in a romantic relationship.

examples.text: Ellos son una pareja muy feliz.
examples.translation: They are a very happy couple.

senses.definition: The person someone is in a romantic relationship with.

examples.text: Te presento a mi pareja, Carlos.
examples.translation: Let me introduce you to my partner, Carlos.

senses.definition: Two people or animals that do something together or form a set.

examples.text: En clase trabajamos en parejas.
examples.translation: In class we work in pairs.

faults.quote: Use 'маленький' for physical size.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two senses and their definitions.

faults.quote: small; little
faults.why: Omits 'young' from the second sense.

notes: The comparative form is irregular: 'меньше' (smaller). Its short forms come from the related adjective 'малый' ('мал', 'мала', 'мало', 'малы') and often mean 'too small' when used for clothes or shoes.

senses.definition: Of a small physical size; not big.

examples.text: У меня маленькая собака.
examples.translation: I have a small dog.

senses.definition: Of a child: young in age.

examples.text: Когда я был маленький, я любил играть.
examples.translation: When I was young, I loved to play.

faults.quote: Use 'тихий' for things that produce little sound
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0.

faults.quote: rather than volume
faults.why: Implies 'тихий' is only for volume, whereas it also commonly describes calm weather or places.

faults.quote: В библиотеке очень тихо.
faults.why: Uses the adverb/predicative 'тихо' instead of a form of the adjective 'тихий'.

notes: The comparative form is irregular: 'тише' (quieter). For people's character or emotional state, 'спокойный' (calm) is more common than 'тихий'.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise.

examples.text: Он говорил тихим голосом.
examples.translation: He spoke in a quiet voice.

senses.definition: Of a place, time, or weather: free from disturbance or strong movement.

examples.text: Мы живём на тихой улице.
examples.translation: We live on a quiet street.

faults.quote: /nʲɪˈpravʲɪlnɨj/
faults.why: Missing palatalization on /lʲ/ for 'ль': should be /nʲɪˈpravʲɪlʲnɨj/.

faults.quote: Use неправильный when something contains an error
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

faults.quote: У этого глагола неправильный тип спряжения.
faults.why: Stiff phrasing; 'неправильный глагол' (irregular verb) is the natural everyday collocation.

notes: Formed from 'правильный' (correct, regular) with the negative prefix 'не-'. For 'the wrong one' (a mistaken choice rather than an error), Russian usually uses 'не тот': 'не тот автобус' (the wrong bus).

senses.definition: Not true or accurate; containing an error or mistake.

examples.text: Ты дал неправильный ответ на этот вопрос.
examples.translation: You gave an incorrect answer to this question.

senses.definition: Not following the normal rules, pattern, or standard shape.

examples.text: Это неправильный глагол, его нужно запомнить.
examples.translation: This is an irregular verb; you need to memorize it.

faults.quote: Use this to describe anything that is not clean
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning without adding useful grammatical or usage information.

faults.quote: dirty; soiled; muddy
faults.why: Includes 'muddy', which is absent from the sense glosses.

notes: Related to the noun 'грязь' (dirt, mud), so it covers both 'dirty' (unclean) and 'muddy' (covered in mud, e.g. of shoes or roads).

senses.definition: Not clean; covered in dirt, dust, or mud.

examples.text: У меня грязные руки после работы в саду.
examples.translation: My hands are dirty after working in the garden.

examples.text: Не надевай эту грязную рубашку.
examples.translation: Do not wear that dirty shirt.

faults.quote: Used to describe food or drink that has a very pleasant flavor.
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim.

notes: Pronounced with initial /fk-/ due to assimilation before the voiceless 'к'. To say 'It is delicious!' as a standalone comment, use the adverbial form 'Вкусно!'.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a pleasant flavor.

examples.text: Это очень вкусный суп.
examples.translation: This is a very tasty soup.

faults.quote: Used as a general adjective for things that are not good
faults.why: Restates the definition and glosses without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: The feminine form is سَيِّئَة (sayyiʾa), with the hamza written on a kursi (ئ) before the feminine ending.

senses.definition: Not good, of poor quality, or unpleasant.

examples.text: كان الطقس سيئاً اليوم.
examples.translation: The weather was bad today.

notes: Takes the preposition مِنْ (min) to introduce what someone is afraid of (خَائِف مِنْ).
Grammatically an active participle from خَافَ (to fear); feminine خَائِفَة, masculine plural خَائِفُونَ.

senses.definition: Feeling fear or worry about something.

examples.text: الطفل خائف من الكلب.
examples.translation: The child is afraid of the dog.

examples.text: أنا لست خائفاً من الظلام.
examples.translation: I am not afraid of the dark.

faults.quote: This word can describe physical speed, like a person walking
faults.why: Restates the definition; works just like English 'slow'.

notes: In the feminine form بَطِيئَة (baṭīʾa), the final hamza sits on a kursi (ئ) because it follows a long ī.

senses.definition: Not fast; taking a long time to move or happen.

examples.text: الإنترنت بَطِيء جداً اليوم.
examples.translation: The internet is very slow today.

faults.quote: يَبْدُو الصَّدِيقُ هَادِئًا جِدًّا.
faults.why: Using definite 'الصديق' ('the friend') without a possessive pronoun is unnatural in Arabic.

notes: Contrasts with مُزْعِج (noisy, annoying) for places and مُتَوَتِّر (stressed, tense) for people.

senses.definition: With little or no noise or disturbance; silent and peaceful.

examples.text: الْمَكَانُ هَادِئٌ هُنَا فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
examples.translation: The place is quiet here in the evening.

senses.definition: Of a person or manner: not worried, excited, or angry; relaxed.

examples.text: يَبْدُو صَدِيقِي هَادِئًا جِدًّا اليَوْمَ.
examples.translation: My friend seems very calm today.

notes: Like other basic colour adjectives, it has the feminine form خَضْرَاء (ḵaḍrāʾ) and plural خُضْر (ḵuḍr), and does not take nunation (tanwīn).

senses.definition: Having the colour of grass or leaves.

examples.text: هَذَا العُشْبُ أَخْضَرُ جِدّاً.
examples.translation: This grass is very green.

faults.quote: While 'anel' refers specifically to a ring worn on a finger, it
faults.why: Filler note about technical senses; missing key contrast with 'aliança' (wedding ring).

notes: The plural is 'anéis'.
For a plain wedding or engagement band, use 'a aliança' instead.

senses.definition: A small circular band, typically of precious metal, worn on a finger as jewelry.

examples.text: Ela usa um anel de ouro na mão esquerda.
examples.translation: She wears a gold ring on her left hand.

faults.quote: /aniˈmaw dʒi istimiˈsɐ̃w̃/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in 'estimação': the third syllable has /a/ (/is.tʃi.maˈsɐ̃w̃/), not /i/, and missing palatalization /tʃ/.

notes: Plural: 'os animais de estimação'.
In informal Brazilian Portuguese, people very often say 'o bicho de estimação' or simply the English loanword 'o pet' (/ˈpɛtʃi/).

senses.definition: A domestic animal kept in the home for company.

examples.text: Eu quero adotar um animal de estimação.
examples.translation: I want to adopt a pet.

faults.quote: The cat is a very popular house animal.
faults.why: Calqued translation; 'animal doméstico' is 'domestic animal' or 'pet', not 'house animal'.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who behaves in a wild, cruel, or aggressive
faults.why: Meta-language ('Used to describe...') instead of a direct noun definition.
Missing irregular plural 'animais' (-al -> -ais), essential for A2 learners.

notes: The plural is 'animais'.

senses.definition: A living creature that can move and feel, and is not a plant or a human.

examples.text: O gato é um animal doméstico muito popular.
examples.translation: The cat is a very popular domestic animal.

senses.definition: A cruel, wild, or brutal person.

examples.text: Ele se comportou como um animal durante a briga.
examples.translation: He behaved like an animal during the fight.

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'aniversário' is used for both a person's birthday and a
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses without adding usage information.

notes: Used alone, 'aniversário' almost always means 'birthday'; for a wedding anniversary, specify 'aniversário de casamento'.
To say 'happy birthday', Brazilians commonly say 'parabéns!' or 'feliz aniversário!'.

senses.definition: The day of the year on which someone was born.

examples.text: O meu aniversário é em outubro.
examples.translation: My birthday is in October.

senses.definition: The date on which a past event, such as a wedding, happened in a previous year.

examples.text: Eles vão comemorar o aniversário de casamento hoje.
examples.translation: They are going to celebrate their wedding anniversary today.

faults.quote: Note that 'meisje' is a neuter noun, so you use 'het'
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already shown in the headword.

faults.quote: A young woman or a romantic partner.
faults.why: Lumps 'young woman' with 'romantic partner', and the example does not show 'girlfriend'.

notes: Historically the diminutive of 'de meid'; like all Dutch diminutives ending in '-je', it is a 'het'-word (plural: 'de meisjes').
For a romantic partner, 'vriendin' is much more common in modern Dutch.

senses.definition: A female child or young woman.

examples.text: Het kleine meisje speelt in de tuin.
examples.translation: The little girl is playing in the garden.

senses.definition: A man's or boy's female romantic partner.

examples.text: Hij neemt zijn meisje mee naar het feest.
examples.translation: He is bringing his girlfriend to the party.

notes: For the physical card or booklet listing dishes in a restaurant, 'de menukaart' is often used to avoid confusion with a set meal.
The plural takes an apostrophe: 'de menu's'.

senses.definition: A list of dishes available in a restaurant, or a list of options on a screen.

examples.text: Mag ik alstublieft het menu zien?
examples.translation: May I please see the menu?

senses.definition: A meal consisting of several courses served at a fixed price.

examples.text: We kiezen vandaag voor het menu van de chef.
examples.translation: Today we are choosing the chef's set menu.

faults.quote: Takes the neuter article 'het' in the singular (het mes)
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already in the headword.

notes: The plural doubles the 's': 'de messen'.
Do not confuse with 'met', a common preposition meaning 'with'.

senses.definition: A tool with a sharp blade used for cutting food or other materials.

examples.text: Ik snijd de tomaat met een scherp mes.
examples.translation: I am cutting the tomato with a sharp knife.

notes: Has two correct plural forms: 'de musea' (more common) and 'de museums'.

senses.definition: A building where objects of artistic, cultural, historical, or scientific importance are displayed.

examples.text: We bezoeken morgen het museum in de stad.
examples.translation: We are visiting the museum in the city tomorrow.

faults.quote: Used for both a single step and a full flight of stairs.
faults.why: 楼梯 refers to the stairs/staircase as a whole; a single step is 台阶 (táijiē).

faults.quote: Use the measure word '条' (tiáo) for a flight of stairs
faults.why: 条 is unnatural for 楼梯; 段 (duàn) or 个 (gè) is used.

faults.quote: 我在楼梯上走。
faults.why: Unnatural sentence; native speakers say 走楼梯 (take the stairs) or 上/下楼梯.

notes: Refers to the staircase as a whole; a single step is 台阶 (táijiē), counted with 级 (jí).
Commonly used in phrases like 上楼梯 (go upstairs), 下楼梯 (go downstairs), and 走楼梯 (take the stairs).

senses.definition: A set of steps for going from one level to another inside or outside a building.

examples.text: 电梯坏了，我们走楼梯吧。
examples.translation: The elevator is broken, let's take the stairs.

faults.why: Should mention the standard measure word 台 (tái) for appliances.

notes: Counted with the measure word 台 (tái) or 个 (gè): 一台冰箱 (a refrigerator).
Literally 'ice box', from 冰 (bīng, ice) + 箱 (xiāng, box).

senses.definition: A large kitchen appliance that keeps food and drinks cold.

examples.text: 冰箱里有苹果。
examples.translation: There are apples in the refrigerator.

faults.quote: When used as a verb, it often takes an object
faults.why: 咳嗽 is an intransitive verb and cannot take a direct object.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 咳嗽 (ké sou) with 吐 (tù)
faults.why: 咳嗽 and 吐 look and sound completely different; learners do not confuse them.

faults.quote: 他因为感冒而咳嗽。
faults.why: Entry POS is noun, but the example uses 咳嗽 as a verb after 而.

notes: Used equally often as a noun and as an intransitive verb ('to cough').
Note that the second syllable 嗽 (sou) is pronounced in the neutral tone.

senses.definition: The act or sound of forcing air out of the throat, or an illness that causes this.

examples.text: 他的咳嗽还没好。
examples.translation: His cough hasn't gotten better yet.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'car trunk / boot'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with '手提包' (shǒutí bāo)
faults.why: No learner confuses 行李箱 with 手提包; measure word 个 (gè) is more useful.

notes: 行李 (xíngli) is luggage in general; adding 箱 (xiāng, box/case) specifies a suitcase, counted with 个 (gè).

senses.definition: A large case, often with a handle and wheels, used for carrying clothes when traveling.

examples.text: 我的行李箱太重了。
examples.translation: My suitcase is too heavy.

senses.definition: The storage space at the back of a car for bags and other items.

examples.text: 请把包放在汽车的行李箱里。
examples.translation: Please put the bag in the trunk of the car.

faults.quote: /ʈʂʰu˧˥ ʂɻ̩˥/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in 厨: chú is /ʈʂʰu˧˥/, not retroflex /ʈʂʰɻ̩˧˥/, and 师 is /ʂʅ˥/ or /ʂɻ̩˥/.

faults.quote: cooking at home as a hobby or a family member... use 厨子
faults.why: 厨子 also means a professional cook (old-fashioned/informal), not a family member cooking at home.

notes: Refers only to someone who cooks as a profession, counted with 个 (gè) or 位 (wèi, polite). For someone who cooks at home, say 做饭的人 (person who cooks).

senses.definition: A person whose job is to prepare and cook food in a restaurant or hotel.

examples.text: 这家餐厅的厨师很有名。
examples.translation: The chef at this restaurant is very famous.

faults.quote: for on the sandwich.
faults.why: Calqued from Dutch 'voor op de boterham'; unnatural in English.

senses.definition: A soft red fruit with juicy pulp and seeds, eaten as a vegetable in salads and cooked dishes.

examples.text: Ik snijd een rode tomaat in dunne plakjes voor op de boterham.
examples.translation: I cut a red tomato into thin slices to put on the sandwich.

faults.quote: De trap is used for both indoor stairs and outdoor steps
faults.why: Restates the senses and definitions without adding useful grammar or usage details.

notes: Do not confuse 'trap' (the whole staircase) with 'trede', which means a single step or stair.
To say 'up/down the stairs', Dutch uses postpositions: 'de trap op' (upstairs) and 'de trap af' (downstairs).

senses.definition: A set of steps inside or outside for going from one level to another.

examples.text: Hij loopt de trap op naar zijn slaapkamer.
examples.translation: He is walking up the stairs to his bedroom.

senses.definition: A movable piece of equipment with steps used for climbing up high.

examples.text: Zij gebruikt een trap om de lamp te vervangen.
examples.translation: She uses a stepladder to replace the lamp.

senses.definition: A sudden blow given with the foot.

examples.text: De speler gaf de bal een harde trap.
examples.translation: The player gave the ball a hard kick.

faults.quote: In Flemish regions, people sometimes use 'vest' for a cardigan or
faults.why: Confusingly worded and partly repeats the glosses; contrast with 'vest' can be much simpler.

notes: In the Netherlands, 'trui' is a pullover without buttons or a zipper down the front; a cardigan or zip-up hoodie is called 'het vest'.

senses.definition: A warm knitted top without buttons down the front, worn on the upper body.

examples.text: Het is koud buiten, dus ik trek een warme trui aan.
examples.translation: It is cold outside, so I am putting on a warm sweater.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'tuin' (garden) with 'park' (park), which is a
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'garden' and 'park', and 'park' is an obvious cognate.

senses.definition: A piece of ground next to a house, used for growing flowers, grass, or vegetables.

examples.text: De kinderen spelen in de tuin.
examples.translation: The children are playing in the garden.

faults.quote: While 'kalām' is the standard word
faults.why: Wrong romanization: 'kalām' (कलाम) means speech/discourse; कलम is 'kalam' (or 'qalam').

notes: Often spelled क़लम with a nuqta (dot). In everyday speech, the English loanword पेन (pen, masculine) is even more common for a ballpoint pen.

senses.definition: A tool used for writing or drawing on paper with ink.

examples.text: क्या मुझे आपकी कलम मिल सकती है?
examples.translation: Can I have your pen?

faults.quote: In the context of a restaurant, this word refers specifically
faults.why: Merely restates sense 0; also misleading in note 1 since only sense 0 is English.

notes: Two unrelated words with the same spelling: 'bill' is borrowed from English, while 'burrow/hole' is a native Hindi word.

senses.definition: A written or printed statement of money owed for goods or services, such as a meal or utility.

examples.text: कृपया बिल लाइए।
examples.translation: Please bring the bill.

senses.definition: A hole or tunnel in the ground made by a small animal such as a snake, mouse, or rabbit.

examples.text: खरगोश अपने बिल में चला गया।
examples.translation: The rabbit went into its burrow.

faults.quote: Used for both a professional 'leave of absence' and a personal 'vacation'.
faults.why: Restates the two senses directly below without adding usage information.

notes: Common expressions: छुट्टी लेना (to take time off), छुट्टी मनाना (to celebrate/spend a holiday), and छुट्टी होना (for school/work to let out or be closed).

senses.definition: A day or period of time away from work or school for rest, travel, or a festival.

examples.text: अगले महीने मैं छुट्टियों पर जा रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am going on holiday next month.

senses.definition: Permission to be absent from work or school.

examples.text: क्या मुझे कल की छुट्टी मिल सकती है?
examples.translation: Can I get leave for tomorrow?

faults.quote: मैंने अपना बटुआ दुकान पर भूल दिया।
faults.why: Ungrammatical: भूलना is intransitive (takes में, not ने) and builds compounds with जाना, not देना.

faults.quote: /baʈuːɑː/
faults.why: Incorrect vowels: first vowel is /ə/ and second is short /ʊ/ (/bəʈʊɑː/).

faults.quote: बटुआ (batua) usually refers to a small purse, pouch, or traditional wallet
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition and glosses.

notes: Inflects as a regular masculine -आ noun: बटुए (oblique singular and direct plural). In everyday urban speech, the English loanword पर्स (pars) is also very common for both a man's wallet and a woman's handbag.

senses.definition: A small folding case or pouch used for carrying paper money, coins, and cards.

examples.text: मैं अपना बटुआ दुकान पर भूल गया।
examples.translation: I forgot my wallet at the shop.

faults.why: Food egg and biological egg are one sense for a beginner.

notes: Often written as 玉子 when referring to eggs as food, especially cooked egg dishes.

senses.definition: The oval object laid by a bird, fish, or reptile, especially a hen's egg eaten as food.

examples.text: 毎朝、卵を一つ食べます。
examples.translation: I eat one egg every morning.

faults.quote: It is commonly used when discussing travel, immigration, or geopolitical issues.
faults.why: Obvious from the meaning 'national border'; adds no linguistic value.

notes: Specifically refers to borders between countries; for a general boundary or border between regions, use 境 (sakai).

senses.definition: The official dividing line between two countries.

examples.text: 私たちは車で国境を越えた。
examples.translation: We crossed the border by car.

faults.quote: A colloquial or slang term referring to a cramped space
faults.why: Slang sense 'music venue' (often written ハコ) is marginal for A2; 'cramped space' is inaccurate.

faults.quote: Not used for flexible containers like bags (袋) or open bowls (器).
faults.why: Merely explains the English concept of a box.

notes: When used as a counter for boxes of something, 1, 2, and 3 are read いっぱこ (ippako), ふたはこ (futahako), and みはこ (mihako) or さんぱこ (sanpako).

senses.definition: A container with flat sides, usually made of cardboard, wood, or plastic, used for storing or carrying things.

examples.text: この箱の中に本が入っています。
examples.translation: There are books inside this box.

faults.quote: This is a common loanword used throughout India.
faults.why: Pure filler; adds no useful linguistic information.

faults.quote: While it functions as a noun, it is almost always used in
faults.why: Pointless statement about real-world context rather than grammar or usage.

notes: Forms the plural टैक्सीयाँ (taxis) in the direct case and टैक्सियों in the oblique case.

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: मैंने स्टेशन जाने के लिए टैक्सी ली।
examples.translation: I took a taxi to go to the station.

examples.text: क्या यहाँ कोई टैक्सी मिल सकती है?
examples.translation: Can I get a taxi here?

faults.quote: This is a common loanword from English used throughout India to refer
faults.why: Restates the definition and states the obvious.

faults.quote: Unlike traditional Hindi words for bags, 'सूटकेस' specifically implies a rigid, rectangular
faults.why: Merely restates the meaning of 'suitcase'.

senses.definition: A case with a handle and flat sides, used for carrying clothes when travelling.

examples.text: मैंने अपना सूटकेस पैक कर लिया है।
examples.translation: I have packed my suitcase.

faults.quote: The device used to control a cursor on a computer screen.
faults.why: Hindi speakers use the English loanword माउस (māus) for a computer mouse, not चूहा.

notes: Covers both 'mouse' and 'rat'. The feminine form चूहिया (chūhiyā) refers either to a female mouse/rat or specifically to a small mouse.
Do not use this word for a computer mouse; the English loanword माउस (māus) is used instead.

senses.definition: A small grey or brown rodent with a long thin tail.

examples.text: बिल्ली ने चूहे को पकड़ लिया।
examples.translation: The cat caught the mouse.

faults.quote: Used both for the literal images seen during sleep and for a
faults.why: Just repeats the two senses listed directly below.

faults.quote: My dream is that I see the whole world.
faults.why: Calqued translation; natural English is 'My dream is to see the whole world.'

notes: To say 'to have a dream' or 'to dream', Hindi uses सपना आना ('a dream comes', with को) or सपना देखना ('to see a dream').

senses.definition: A series of images or events that happen in your mind while you are sleeping.

examples.text: कल रात मुझे एक अजीब सपना आया।
examples.translation: I had a strange dream last night.

senses.definition: Something that you strongly wish to happen or achieve in the future.

examples.text: मेरा सपना है कि मैं पूरी दुनिया देखूँ।
examples.translation: My dream is to see the whole world.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'y tá', which means 'nurse'.
faults.why: No reason a learner would confuse 'bác sĩ' with 'y tá'.

notes: Can be used both as a noun (usually with the classifier 'người' or 'vị') and as a respectful title or form of address.

senses.definition: A person trained and qualified to treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: Bác sĩ đang khám bệnh cho bệnh nhân.
examples.translation: The doctor is examining the patient.

faults.quote: /1baːj˧ˀ˥ 1biən˧ˀ˥/
faults.why: Contains stray digits '1' and gives wrong tone (ngã instead of hỏi) for 'biển'.

notes: Combines 'bãi' (flat expanse) and 'biển' (sea). Often shortened to 'biển' in phrases like 'đi biển' (go to the beach).

senses.definition: A sandy or stony shore next to the sea where people go to relax and swim.

examples.text: Cuối tuần này chúng ta sẽ đi ra bãi biển.
examples.translation: This weekend we will go to the beach.

faults.quote: /1baːj˨˩ 1hɔwk͡p̚˧˥/
faults.why: Contains stray digits '1' and gives wrong tone (sắc instead of nặng) for 'học'.

faults.quote: Used both for a structured period of instruction in school and for
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses defined below.

faults.quote: That is an expensive lesson for everyone.
faults.why: Calque of 'bài học đắt giá'; natural English is 'a costly/hard lesson'.

notes: Refers to the content or unit in a textbook or syllabus, whereas 'tiết học' or 'buổi học' refers to the scheduled class period.

senses.definition: A unit of teaching or study in a course or textbook.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đang chuẩn bị cho bài học ngày mai.
examples.translation: We are preparing for tomorrow's lesson.

senses.definition: An experience that teaches you how to behave better in the future.

examples.text: Đó là một bài học đắt giá cho tất cả mọi người.
examples.translation: That was a costly lesson for everyone.

faults.quote: /bàːj tȁp vè nāː/
faults.why: Non-standard diacritics and wrong consonant and tone on 'nhà' (/nāː/ instead of /ɲaː˨˩/).

notes: Often shortened to 'bài tập' (exercise/assignment) in everyday conversation when the school context is clear.

senses.definition: School work that a teacher gives students to do at home.

examples.text: Tôi phải làm bài tập về nhà tối nay.
examples.translation: I have to do my homework tonight.

faults.quote: Use 'bẩn' to describe something covered in dirt or grime.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss.

notes: Standard in Northern Vietnam and understood everywhere; in Southern Vietnam, 'dơ' is more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: Covered in dirt, dust, or other unwanted substances.

examples.text: Tay con bẩn quá, đi rửa tay đi.
examples.translation: Your hands are so dirty, go wash them.

examples.text: Đừng để quần áo bẩn trên giường.
examples.translation: Do not leave dirty clothes on the bed.

faults.quote: /ɪnɡɐˈda/
faults.why: Wrong IPA: misses the reduced vowel /ɐ/ between /n/ and /ɡ/; should be /ɪnɐˈɡda/.

faults.quote: Use иногда when something happens on some occasions, but not regularly
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammar guidance.

notes: Usually takes the imperfective aspect of the verb because it describes repeated actions.

senses.definition: From time to time; on some occasions, but not always.

examples.text: Иногда я пью чай по вечерам.
examples.translation: Sometimes I drink tea in the evenings.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the day following today.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful learner guidance.

notes: Also used as an indeclinable noun in phrases like 'до завтра' (until tomorrow / see you tomorrow).
With parts of the day, place 'завтра' first without a preposition: 'завтра утром' (tomorrow morning), 'завтра вечером' (tomorrow evening).

senses.definition: On the day after today.

examples.text: Завтра будет хорошая погода.
examples.translation: Tomorrow the weather will be good.

faults.why: Missing essential pronunciation note: spelled with 'г' but pronounced with /v/, while notes are filler.

notes: The letter 'г' in this word is pronounced like 'в' (/v/), not /ɡ/.
With parts of the day, place 'сегодня' first without a preposition: 'сегодня утром' (this morning), 'сегодня вечером' (this evening / tonight).

senses.definition: On this present day.

examples.text: Сегодня хорошая погода.
examples.translation: Today the weather is good.

senses.definition: At the present time or in the modern period.

examples.text: Сегодня многие люди работают из дома.
examples.translation: Nowadays many people work from home.

faults.quote: This summer we are going to the sea.
faults.why: Calqued translation; 'andare al mare' means going to the beach/seaside, as note[0] says.

notes: Use 'al mare' when talking about going to the beach or spending time on the coast.

senses.definition: The large area of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface, or the coast beside it as a place for holidays.

examples.text: Il mare è molto calmo oggi.
examples.translation: The sea is very calm today.

examples.text: Quest'estate andiamo al mare.
examples.translation: This summer we are going to the beach.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a married man in relation to his wife.
faults.why: Restates the definition; also misses the rule on dropping the article with 'mio marito'.

notes: Like other singular family nouns, 'marito' drops the definite article after possessive adjectives: 'mio marito' (not 'il mio marito'), unless it is plural ('i nostri mariti') or modified.

senses.definition: The man a person is married to.

examples.text: Mio marito cucina la cena ogni sera.
examples.translation: My husband cooks dinner every evening.

faults.quote: Il matrimonio can mean either the wedding ceremony itself or the state
faults.why: Note[0] restates the two senses; note[1] warns about an archaic word A2 learners won't meet.

notes: The plural is 'i matrimoni' (with a single '-i').

senses.definition: The ceremony in which two people get married.

examples.text: Siamo invitati a un matrimonio sabato prossimo.
examples.translation: We are invited to a wedding next Saturday.

senses.definition: The legal or religious union between two people.

examples.text: Il loro matrimonio dura da trent'anni.
examples.translation: Their marriage has lasted for thirty years.

faults.quote: In Italian, menù can also refer to a fixed-price meal
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 instead of noting the invariable plural and unaccented spelling 'menu'.

notes: Invariable in the plural ('i menù'). Also commonly spelled 'menu' without the accent, with the same pronunciation.

senses.definition: The list of dishes and drinks available at a restaurant.

examples.text: Possiamo avere il menù, per favore?
examples.translation: Can we have the menu, please?

senses.definition: A complete meal of several courses offered at a fixed price.

examples.text: Oggi prendo il menù del giorno.
examples.translation: Today I'll have the daily set menu.

faults.quote: Use 'il mercato' for both open-air street markets and indoor food markets.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Use 'a buon mercato' (literally 'at a good market') to mean 'cheap' or 'inexpensive'.

senses.definition: An outdoor or indoor place where food and other goods are sold at stalls.

examples.text: Compro la frutta fresca al mercato.
examples.translation: I buy fresh fruit at the market.

senses.definition: The system of trade and buying and selling of goods or services.

examples.text: I prezzi cambiano secondo il mercato.
examples.translation: Prices change according to the market.

faults.quote: (job) A formal meeting ... (media) A meeting where a reporter
faults.why: Job and media interviews are one sense in Vietnamese; do not split by context.

faults.quote: The famous singer is answering the journalist's interview.
faults.why: Calqued translation; natural English is 'giving an interview to the journalist' or 'answering questions'.

notes: Also very commonly used as a verb ('to interview').
As a noun, it often takes the classifier 'cuộc' or 'buổi' (e.g., một buổi phỏng vấn — an interview session).

senses.definition: A formal meeting in which someone is asked questions, especially for a job or by a journalist.

examples.text: Tôi có một buổi phỏng vấn vào sáng mai.
examples.translation: I have an interview tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Ca sĩ nổi tiếng đang trả lời phỏng vấn của nhà báo.
examples.translation: The famous singer is giving an interview to the journalist.

faults.quote: /fʊ̀ nɨ̌/
faults.why: Wrong vowel and tones for Hanoi Vietnamese; 'phụ nữ' is /fu˧˨ʔ nɨ˦ˀ˥/.

faults.quote: Used to refer generally to adult females.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

notes: More formal and collective than 'người đàn bà' (woman); for one specific woman, takes the classifier 'người' (một người phụ nữ).
Do not confuse with 'con gái', which means 'girl', 'young unmarried woman', or 'daughter'.

senses.definition: An adult female person, or women in general.

examples.text: Phụ nữ Việt Nam rất chăm chỉ.
examples.translation: Vietnamese women are very hardworking.

faults.why: That is Southern pronunciation; Northern (Hanoi) IPA for 'phút' has final /-t̚/: /fut̚˧˦/.

faults.quote: (time) A unit of time ... (moment) A very short duration
faults.why: Oversplit; Sense 1's example even translates 'vài phút' literally as 'a few minutes'.

faults.quote: Used to measure both sixty seconds of time and as a brief
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving a grammatical note (e.g., no classifier needed).

notes: Used directly after numbers without a classifier (e.g., năm phút — five minutes).

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds, or a very short period of time.

examples.text: Xin vui lòng đợi một phút.
examples.translation: Please wait a minute.

examples.text: Tôi sẽ xong trong vài phút nữa.
examples.translation: I will be done in a few minutes.

faults.quote: When used alone, 'quà' most commonly refers to a gift or present
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two senses without adding grammar or classifier usage.

notes: In the 'gift' sense, it takes the classifier 'món' (một món quà).
In the 'snack' sense, it is mainly Northern and usually appears in expressions like 'ăn quà' or 'quà vặt'.

senses.definition: Something given to someone, especially on a special occasion or when returning from a trip.

examples.text: Tôi mua món quà này cho bạn.
examples.translation: I bought this gift for you.

senses.definition: A small snack or treat eaten between meals (often in 'ăn quà' or 'quà vặt').

examples.text: Buổi chiều chúng tôi hay ăn quà vặt.
examples.translation: In the afternoon we often eat snacks.

faults.quote: /kwən˧˥ ʔaːw˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong tone on 'quần'; 'quần' has the falling (huyền) tone /kwən˨˩/, not rising.

notes: Literally 'trousers and shirts', used as a collective noun for clothing in general; use 'bộ quần áo' for a single outfit or set of clothes.

senses.definition: Things worn to cover the body, such as shirts, trousers, and dresses.

examples.text: Tôi cần giặt quần áo vào cuối tuần.
examples.translation: I need to wash my clothes on the weekend.

faults.quote: Used for physical structures like houses, walls, or bridges.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value; also misses common compound 'xây dựng'.

notes: Often used in the compound 'xây dựng' (to build, to construct), which can also be used figuratively (e.g., building a relationship or plan).

senses.definition: To make a building, wall, or other structure by putting bricks or other materials together.

examples.translation: Many cars are driving on the road.

examples.text: Bác sĩ đang xem vết thương cho bệnh nhân.
examples.translation: The doctor is examining the patient's wound.

examples.translation: There is a lot of pollution in the air.

senses.definition: Moving air, especially a natural current felt outdoors.

examples.text: बाहर ठंडी हवा चल रही है।
examples.translation: A cool breeze is blowing outside.

senses.definition: A soft, round red fruit eaten raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable.

examples.translation: Cut two tomatoes to make the curry.

faults.quote: Used commonly to refer to various species of monkeys found in India.

senses.definition: A mammal with a long tail that lives in trees and climbs well.

examples.text: पेड़ पर एक बंदर बैठा है।
examples.translation: A monkey is sitting in the tree.

examples.translation: He pours cool water into a glass.

senses.definition: A hard, clear, and fragile material that lets light pass through.

senses.definition: A very small town in the country.

examples.text: Il habite dans un petit village pittoresque.
examples.translation: He lives in a small picturesque village.

faults.quote: The general appearance or expression of a person's face.

senses.definition: The front part of the human head, including the eyes, nose, and mouth.

examples.text: Elle avait un grand sourire sur le visage.
examples.translation: She had a big smile on her face.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with 'le quartier', which refers to

senses.definition: A person who lives next door or nearby.

faults.quote: Todos los seres vivos necesitan agua.
faults.why: Uses the noun/adjective 'vivos', not the verb 'vivir'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'convivir'

examples.translation: The weekend flies by when you are having fun.

examples.text: В воскресенье у нас большой семейный обед.
examples.translation: On Sunday we have a big family lunch.

examples.translation: The shop is closed for lunch.
