examples.text: أَرْسَلْتُ لَهُ بَرِيدًا إِلِكْتْرُونِيًّا أَمْسِ.
examples.translation: I sent him an email yesterday.

faults.quote: It is the standard, formal way to refer to a
faults.why: Filler note; omits how to form the feminine, plural, and definite forms.

notes: Literally 'doctor of teeth' (an iḍāfa construction). To make it definite, add الـ only to the second word: طَبِيبُ الأَسْنَانِ ('the dentist').
Feminine: طَبِيبَة أَسْنَان (ṭabībat ʾasnān); masculine/mixed plural: أَطِبَّاء أَسْنَان (ʾaṭibbāʾ ʾasnān).

senses.definition: A doctor who treats people's teeth and gums.

examples.text: يَجِبُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى طَبِيبِ الْأَسْنَانِ غَدًا.
examples.translation: I must go to the dentist tomorrow.

faults.quote: The darkest colour, absorbing all light and having no hue.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun rather than a quality.

faults.quote: Siyah is of Arabic origin... kara is often used... for hair
faults.why: Siyah is of Persian origin, and hair is usually described as siyah, not kara.

notes: 'Siyah' is the standard everyday word for black (including hair and clothes). The synonym 'kara' is mostly used in idioms, place names, or poetic expressions.

senses.definition: Of the darkest colour, like coal or the night sky.

examples.text: Gece gökyüzü siyah ve yıldızsızdı.
examples.translation: The night sky was black and starless.

faults.why: Missing note on final consonant softening (ışık -> ışığı/ışığa) before vowel suffixes.

notes: When a suffix starting with a vowel is added, the final 'k' softens to 'ğ' (e.g., ışığı, ışığa).
Use 'ışık' for general illumination or room lights (e.g., ışığı aç/kapat), and 'lamba' for a physical lamp or bulb.

senses.definition: The natural or artificial brightness that allows you to see.

examples.text: Odanın ışığı çok parlak.
examples.translation: The light in the room is very bright.

senses.definition: An electric lamp or fixture that gives off light, or a traffic light.

examples.text: Lütfen çıkarken ışığı kapat.
examples.translation: Please turn off the light when you leave.

faults.quote: Bu kafe sık sık gidiyorum.
faults.why: Ungrammatical: 'gitmek' requires the dative case ('kafeye', not bare 'kafe').

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'birdenbire' (suddenly) or 'bazen'
faults.why: Unlikely confusion with unrelated words.

notes: Formed by repeating the adjective 'sık' (frequent, dense). Usually placed before the verb.

senses.definition: Many times or at short intervals.

examples.text: Bu kafeye sık sık gidiyorum.
examples.translation: I go to this cafe often.

faults.quote: bored; squeezed; tired of waiting
faults.why: 'tired of waiting' is overly specific and not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: Tüm gün evde oturmaktan çok sıkılmış.
faults.why: Uses 'sıkılmış' as an inferential finite verb rather than an adjective.

notes: Participle of 'sıkılmak' (to be bored / to be squeezed). Do not confuse with 'sıkıcı' (boring).

senses.definition: Feeling weary and impatient because there is nothing interesting to do.

examples.text: Bana sıkılmış bir ifadeyle baktı.
examples.translation: He looked at me with a bored expression.

senses.definition: Pressed or crushed to extract juice or liquid.

examples.text: Kahvaltıda taze sıkılmış portakal suyu içtik.
examples.translation: We drank freshly squeezed orange juice at breakfast.

faults.quote: Unlike English, where 'wedding' refers specifically to the ceremony
faults.why: False contrast: 'свадьба' and 'брак' divide the meaning just like English 'wedding' and 'marriage'.

notes: Refers to the wedding ceremony and celebration; for the state of marriage, use «брак».

senses.definition: A marriage ceremony and the celebrations that follow.

examples.text: На их свадьбе было много гостей.
examples.translation: There were many guests at their wedding.

faults.quote: В окнах домов уже горели огоньки.
faults.why: Uses the separate diminutive lemma «огонёк» (plural «огоньки») instead of «огонь» (plural «огни»).

notes: Has a fleeting vowel: genitive «огня́», plural «огни́», with stress on the ending.
Often used in the plural («огни») for lights in a city or distant windows.

senses.definition: Flames and heat produced by burning something.

examples.text: Мы сидели у костра и смотрели на огонь.
examples.translation: We sat by the campfire and watched the fire.

senses.definition: A bright point of light, such as from a lamp, streetlamp, or window.

examples.text: В окнах домов уже горели огни.
examples.translation: Lights were already shining in the windows of the houses.

faults.quote: Used for deep, round tableware typically used for soups
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; furthermore, «тарелка» (глубокая тарелка) is more standard for soup.

notes: Genitive plural is «мисок».
Often used for mixing bowls, salad bowls, or pet bowls; a soup bowl at the table is commonly called «глубокая тарелка».

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for serving or preparing food.

examples.text: Он налил суп в миску.
examples.translation: He poured soup into a bowl.

faults.quote: Used literally to mean physical pain, but very commonly used figuratively
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses the useful note that Russian prefers the verb phrase «болит голова».

notes: In everyday speech, «У меня болит голова» ('My head hurts') is more common than «У меня головная боль».

senses.definition: A continuous pain in the head.

examples.text: У меня сильная головная боль.
examples.translation: I have a bad headache.

senses.definition: A person, task, or situation that causes a lot of worry or difficulty.

examples.text: Этот проект стал для нас настоящей головной болью.
examples.translation: This project has become a real headache for us.

faults.quote: (seriousness) Earnestness or seriousness in behavior and speech.
faults.why: جَدّ (jadd) is grandfather; 'seriousness' is mostly جِدّ (jidd), a different vocalized lemma.

faults.quote: Talk to me with seriousness.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of 'talk to me seriously' (and uses جِدّ, not جَدّ).

notes: Plural: أَجْدَاد (ʾajdād) or جُدُود (judūd); feminine: جَدَّة (jadda, grandmother).
Do not confuse with جِدّ (jidd, 'seriousness'), as in بِجِدّ (bi-jidd, 'seriously').

senses.definition: The father of your father or your mother; also, in the plural, a forefather or ancestor.

examples.text: جَدِّي يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَحْكِيَ لَنَا قِصَصًا قَدِيمَةً.
examples.translation: My grandfather loves to tell us old stories.

faults.quote: أريكة refers to a comfortable upholstered seat for sitting or lounging
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the irregular broken plural أَرَائِك (ʾarāʾik).

notes: Plural: أَرَائِك (ʾarāʾik).
More formal than the everyday word كَنَبَة (kanaba).

senses.definition: A long soft seat with a back and arms for several people to sit on.

examples.text: جَلَسَ عَلَى الأَرِيكَةِ لِيُشَاهِدَ التِّلْفَازَ.
examples.translation: He sat on the sofa to watch television.

faults.quote: تَاوَلْتُ غَدَاءً لَذِيذًا فِي الْمَطْعَمِ.
faults.why: Typo in the verb: تَاوَلْتُ is missing ن and should be تَنَاوَلْتُ (tanāwaltu).

faults.quote: Used for the main meal eaten in the middle of the day.
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim instead of noting the lookalike غِذَاء (nutrition/food).

notes: Do not confuse with غِذَاء (ḡiḏāʾ, 'food, nutrition'), spelled with ذ instead of د.

senses.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

examples.text: تَنَاوَلْتُ غَدَاءً لَذِيذًا فِي الْمَطْعَمِ.
examples.translation: I had a delicious lunch at the restaurant.

faults.quote: In Arabic culture, a 'neighbor' (جَار) is considered to have very close
faults.why: Cultural filler note while the irregular plural جِيرَان (jīrān) is missing.

notes: Feminine: جَارَة (jāra); plural: جِيرَان (jīrān).

senses.definition: A person who lives in the house or apartment next to or near yours.

examples.text: جَارِي رَجُلٌ طَيِّبٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: My neighbor is a very kind man.

faults.quote: Use 'le miroir' for any glass or polished surface
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'la vitre', which is
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'miroir' and 'vitre'; replace with 'glace' (mirror).

notes: In everyday speech, a bathroom or wall mirror is also commonly called 'une glace'.

senses.definition: A piece of specially coated glass that reflects images.

examples.text: Elle se regarde dans le miroir avant de sortir.
examples.translation: She looks at herself in the mirror before going out.

notes: Spelled the same in the singular and the plural ('un mois', 'deux mois'), and the final 's' is silent unless linked to a following vowel sound.

senses.definition: One of the twelve parts into which a year is divided.

examples.text: Le mois de janvier est souvent très froid.
examples.translation: The month of January is often very cold.

faults.quote: world; people; society
faults.why: 'Society' is not covered in the senses or glosses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'la terre', which is more specifically
faults.why: Misleading: 'la Terre' also means planet Earth; should highlight 'tout le monde' instead.

notes: Used as an uncountable noun ('du monde', 'beaucoup de monde') to mean 'people' or 'a crowd'. The very common phrase 'tout le monde' means 'everyone' and takes a third-person singular verb.

senses.definition: The earth, together with all of its countries and peoples.

examples.text: Il rêve de voyager partout dans le monde.
examples.translation: He dreams of traveling all over the world.

senses.definition: People in general, or a large number of people in one place.

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup de monde dans le magasin aujourd'hui.
examples.translation: There are a lot of people in the store today.

faults.quote: Refers to both the live animal (sheep) and its meat
faults.why: Restates the two senses; only the contrast with 'agneau' is useful.

notes: For the meat, 'l'agneau' (lamb, a young sheep) is much more commonly eaten in France than 'le mouton' (mutton, an adult sheep).

senses.definition: A farm animal raised for its thick wool and its meat.

examples.text: Les moutons mangent de l'herbe dans le pré.
examples.translation: The sheep are eating grass in the meadow.

senses.definition: The meat of an adult sheep eaten as food.

examples.text: Nous mangeons du mouton ce soir.
examples.translation: We are eating mutton tonight.

faults.quote: Use 'mur' for the vertical surfaces of a room or building.
faults.why: Restates the definition and contrasts with advanced words an A2 learner will not confuse.

notes: Usually takes 'au' or 'sur le' for things hanging on a wall (e.g., 'accrocher un cadre au mur' / 'sur le mur').

senses.definition: A vertical structure of stone, brick, or other material that encloses a room or area, or supports a building.

examples.text: Il y a un tableau accroché au mur.
examples.translation: There is a painting hanging on the wall.

faults.quote: which can sound similar to other neuter plural nouns in Greek
faults.why: Nonsensical filler remark; it is simply a regular neuter noun in -ί.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'η χερσόνησος' (peninsula)
faults.why: Unnecessary encyclopedia-style contrast with an advanced word for A2 learners.

notes: Plural: τα νησιά (pronounced as two syllables: /niˈsça/).

senses.definition: A piece of land that is surrounded by water on all sides.

examples.text: Η Κρήτη είναι το μεγαλύτερο νησί της Ελλάδας.
examples.translation: Crete is the largest island in Greece.

faults.quote: While 'ώρα' can mean the exact time on a clock, it is
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Use the plural 'ώρες' when talking about duration, such as
faults.why: Obvious plural usage that works identically to English.

faults.quote: Είναι η ώρα να φύγουμε.
faults.why: 'Είναι ώρα να...' (without the definite article) is the natural phrasing for 'it's time to'.

notes: For clock time and moments of the day, use 'ώρα', whereas for general or abstract time (or weather), use 'ο χρόνος' or 'ο καιρός'.

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: Το μάθημα διαρκεί μία ώρα.
examples.translation: The lesson lasts one hour.

senses.definition: The point in the day as shown on a clock.

examples.text: Τι ώρα είναι;
examples.translation: What time is it?

senses.definition: A suitable or specific time to do something.

examples.text: Είναι ώρα να φύγουμε.
examples.translation: It is time to leave.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse 'μέλισσα' with 'μέλισμα'
faults.why: 'Μέλισμα' is a rare, literary word that an A2 learner will not encounter.

faults.quote: honeybee, bee
faults.why: Most common everyday translation 'bee' should come first, also in shortGloss and primaryGloss.

notes: Related to 'το μέλι' (honey).

senses.definition: A winged insect that collects nectar from flowers and makes honey.

examples.text: Η μέλισσα πετάει από λουλούδι σε λουλούδι.
examples.translation: The bee flies from flower to flower.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with mutande, which means underwear.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'pantaloni' with 'mutande'; mention British English 'pants' instead.

notes: Almost always used in the plural (i pantaloni), even for a single pair.
Means 'trousers' (or American English 'pants'), not underwear ('le mutande').

senses.definition: A piece of clothing that covers the lower body and each leg separately.

examples.text: Ho comprato un paio di pantaloni nuovi.
examples.translation: I bought a new pair of trousers.

faults.quote: A piece of clothing that covers the body from the shoulders down, worn especially by women.
faults.why: Definition only describes a woman's dress, omitting 'suit', which is in the glosses.

notes: In the plural (i vestiti), it usually means clothes in general; in the singular (il vestito), it means a dress or a suit.

senses.definition: The things you wear on your body, such as shirts, trousers, and jackets.

examples.text: Metto via i vestiti puliti nell'armadio.
examples.translation: I put the clean clothes away in the wardrobe.

senses.definition: A one-piece garment for a woman, or a matching jacket and trousers or skirt.

examples.text: Ha comprato un bel vestito rosso per la festa.
examples.translation: She bought a nice red dress for the party.

faults.quote: The room in a house that contains a shower, a bathtub, and a toilet.
faults.why: Too narrow; 'il bagno' also refers to a public restroom without a bath or shower.

notes: Notice the expressions 'andare in bagno' (to go to the bathroom/toilet) and 'fare il bagno' (to take a bath or go for a swim).

senses.definition: A room with a toilet and sink, and in a home usually a shower or bathtub.

examples.text: Scusa, dov'è il bagno?
examples.translation: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

senses.definition: An act of washing yourself in a bathtub, or of going into the sea or a pool for pleasure.

examples.text: Dopo la corsa faccio un bagno caldo.
examples.translation: After the run I take a hot bath.

examples.text: Andiamo a fare il bagno al mare!
examples.translation: Let's go for a swim in the sea!

faults.why: Needs to state that it declines like a neuter adjective, not give etymology.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'мороженица', which means an ice cream maker
faults.why: Rare word that A2 learners will not encounter or confuse with 'мороженое'.

notes: Declines like a neuter adjective (genitive моро́женого, dative моро́женому, etc.) and is usually uncountable.

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk or cream.

examples.text: Я хочу купить шоколадное мороженое.
examples.translation: I want to buy chocolate ice cream.

faults.why: Missing two vital grammar facts: fleeting 'о' in declension and irregular genitive plural 'носков'.

notes: Has a fleeting 'о' in all declined forms: singular genitive носка́, plural носки́.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the foot inside a shoe.

examples.text: Я надел тёплые носки перед выходом на улицу.
examples.translation: I put on warm socks before going outside.

senses.definition: The front part of a shoe, boot, or sock that covers the toes.

examples.text: У этих туфель острый носок.
examples.translation: These shoes have a pointed toe.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'ручей', which is a smaller stream or creek.
faults.why: No learner confuses 'река' and 'ручей'; they neither look nor sound alike.

notes: Stress is on the ending in the singular (река́, реки́, реке́, В реку́ / ре́ку, реко́й) and shifts to the stem in the plural (ре́ки, рек, ре́кам).

senses.definition: A large natural flow of water that goes across land into the sea, a lake, or another river.

examples.text: Мы отдыхали у реки.
examples.translation: We were relaxing by the river.

examples.text: Эта река очень длинная.
examples.translation: This river is very long.

faults.quote: Note that this word also functions as an adjective meaning 'police'
faults.why: Should explicitly tell the learner that the noun declines like a masculine adjective.

notes: Declines like a masculine adjective (genitive полице́йского, plural полице́йские); also used as the adjective 'police' (e.g. полице́йская маши́на 'police car').

senses.definition: A person whose job is to enforce the law and maintain public order.

examples.text: Полицейский помог мне найти дорогу.
examples.translation: The police officer helped me find my way.

faults.quote: Used both for a kitchen tool and a general cutting implement.
faults.why: Contradicts note 1; ナイフ is a table/pocket knife, not a kitchen cooking knife (包丁).

notes: Refers to a table knife, pocketknife, or utility knife. A kitchen knife for cooking is 包丁 (hōchō).

senses.definition: A small blade with a handle used at the table or as a pocket tool, not a kitchen cooking knife.

examples.text: ナイフとフォークを使って食べます。
examples.translation: I eat using a knife and fork.

faults.quote: Unlike English, where 'sock' is usually singular, the Japanese word 靴下
faults.why: All Japanese nouns lack singular/plural; what learners actually need is the verb (履く) and counter (足).

notes: Uses the verb 履く (haku, to put on / wear on the lower body) and the counter 足 (soku) for pairs.

senses.definition: A soft garment worn on the foot inside a shoe.

examples.text: 寒いので厚い靴下を履きました。
examples.translation: It was cold, so I put on thick socks.

faults.quote: In Japanese culture, bears are often associated with the mountains
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia; learners need to know the common katakana spelling クマ and dark-circles idiom.

notes: Often written in katakana as クマ.

senses.definition: A large, heavy wild mammal with thick fur.

examples.text: 山で熊を見かけました。
examples.translation: I saw a bear in the mountains.

faults.why: Kanji headword 鍵 is missing its hiragana reading かぎ.

notes: Used for both the key and the lock itself: 鍵をかける (kagi o kakeru, to lock) and 鍵を開ける (kagi o akeru, to unlock).

senses.definition: A small metal tool used to open or lock a door, gate, or container.

examples.text: 鍵を忘れないようにしてください。
examples.translation: Please make sure not to forget your key.

senses.definition: A fastening mechanism that keeps a door or container shut.

examples.text: 出かける前に鍵をかけました。
examples.translation: I locked the door before I left.

notes: Used when speaking about your own aunt to others. For someone else's aunt or when addressing an aunt directly, use おばさん.
Written in kanji as 伯母 (an aunt older than your parent) or 叔母 (an aunt younger than your parent).

senses.definition: The sister of one's father or mother, or the wife of one's uncle.

examples.text: 私のおばは大阪に住んでいます。
examples.translation: My aunt lives in Osaka.

faults.quote: Derived from Dutch 'ijs' (ice) combined with 'krim' (cream), reflecting historical ties.
faults.why: Etymology trivia is not useful usage guidance for an A2 learner.

notes: Counted with 'rasa' for flavours (e.g. 'es krim rasa cokelat') or 'sendok' / 'scop' for scoops.

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk or cream.

examples.text: Dia membeli es krim cokelat di toko.
examples.translation: She bought chocolate ice cream at the shop.

faults.quote: In Indonesian, 'es' not only refers to frozen water, but is also
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: For 'ice cube', use 'es batu'. Placed before a drink name, 'es' makes it iced (e.g. 'es teh' = iced tea, 'es kopi' = iced coffee).

senses.definition: Frozen water.

examples.text: Tolong masukkan es ke dalam gelas ini.
examples.translation: Please put ice into this glass.

senses.definition: A cold or iced drink, or a sweet dessert made with shaved ice.

examples.text: Saya mau pesan es teh manis satu.
examples.translation: I would like to order one sweet iced tea.

faults.quote: Used as a common noun for a photograph, often shortened from 'fotografi'.
faults.why: 'Foto' is a direct Dutch loan ('foto'), not a shortening of 'fotografi' (photography).

notes: To say 'take a photo', use 'mengambil foto' or the verb 'memfoto' / 'memotret'; in everyday speech, 'foto' is also used as a verb ('Ayo kita foto!').

senses.definition: A picture taken with a camera.

examples.text: Bolehkah saya mengambil foto di sini?
examples.translation: May I take a photo here?

faults.quote: /ˈɡajah/
faults.why: Indonesian 'j' is the voiced palatal affricate /dʒ/, not the approximant /j/.

faults.quote: (chess) The bishop piece in the game of chess.
faults.why: Chess terminology is marginal for an A2 beginner and clutters a simple animal word.

faults.why: Restates the marginal chess sense with historical trivia.

senses.definition: A very large grey mammal with a long trunk and tusks.

examples.text: Gajah itu minum air menggunakan belalainya yang panjang.
examples.translation: That elephant drinks water using its long trunk.

faults.quote: salary; wages
faults.why: Includes 'wages', which is absent from the sense glosses and contrasted against in note[1].

faults.quote: Use 'gaji' for a fixed salary paid periodically, typically monthly.
faults.why: Repeats the definition almost word for word.

notes: Contrast with 'upah' (wages), which usually refers to daily, hourly, or piecework pay for manual labour rather than a fixed monthly salary.

senses.definition: A fixed amount of money paid regularly, usually monthly, to an employee for their work.

examples.text: Dia menggunakan gaji bulanannya untuk menabung.
examples.translation: He uses his monthly salary to save money.

examples.text: Perusahaan itu memberikan gaji yang adil kepada semua staf.
examples.translation: The company pays a fair salary to all staff.

faults.quote: áo khoác dài specifically refers to a long coat that reaches below
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammatical information.

notes: Counted with the classifier 'chiếc' or 'cái' (e.g., một chiếc áo khoác dài).

examples.translation: She wore a long coat to keep warm in the winter.

faults.quote: /ʔaːu˧˦ kwaːk̚˧˥/

examples.translation: It is cold now, please put on a coat.

examples.translation: It is cold, so I am wearing a thick sweater.

faults.quote: To move food around in a pan or pot while cooking.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'đảo' means an island. As a verb, it means
faults.why: Explains the verb homonym and restates the gloss instead of giving noun usage.

senses.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đi tham quan hòn đảo xanh mát vào mùa hè.
examples.translation: We went to visit the lush green island in the summer.

faults.quote: Used for natural flowing bodies of water larger than a stream.
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the broken plural (أَنْهَار).

notes: The most common plural is أَنْهَار (anhār).
Do not confuse with بَحْر (baḥr, 'sea').

senses.definition: A large natural flow of water that runs across the land into a sea or lake.

examples.text: يَجْرِي النَّهْرُ بَيْنَ الجِبَالِ.
examples.translation: The river flows between the mountains.

faults.why: Arabic كُوب covers both a mug/cup and a drinking glass in one concept.

faults.why: فِنْجَان is used for any teacup or coffee cup, not only for Arabic coffee; transliteration is MSA finjān.

faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the broken plural (أَكْوَاب).

notes: The plural is أَكْوَاب (akwāb).
كُوب is used for a glass, tumbler, or mug; a smaller cup with a saucer for tea or coffee is usually called فِنْجَان (finjān).

senses.definition: A cup, mug, or glass used for drinking.

examples.text: أَشْرَبُ كُوبًا مِنَ المَاءِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: I drink a glass of water every morning.

faults.quote: /aˈruzz/

Should mention the very common variant رُزّ (ruzz) and the related word أَرْز (cedar).

notes: Also commonly written and pronounced رُزّ (ruzz). Used as an uncountable mass noun for both raw grains and cooked rice.
Do not confuse with أَرْز (arz, 'cedar').

senses.definition: Small white or brown grains that are cooked and eaten as food.

examples.text: آكُلُ الأَرُزَّ مَعَ الدَّجَاجِ.
examples.translation: I eat rice with chicken.

faults.quote: with 'سَرّ' (joy), which has a different vowel sound

notes: The plural is أَسْرَار (asrār).
Do not confuse with the verb سَرَّ (sarra, 'to please, make happy').

senses.definition: Something kept hidden from others and known only to a few people.

examples.text: لَا تُخْبِرْ أَحَدًا، هٰذَا سِرٌّ.
examples.translation: Do not tell anyone, this is a secret.

faults.quote: Used for any standard hat worn on the head
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful grammar or usage info.

faults.quote: something worn on the head
faults.why: Too broad; covers helmets, scarves, crowns, and glasses.

notes: Takes the sound feminine plural قُبَّعَات (qubbaʿāt).

senses.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the head, often with a brim, to protect from the sun or weather.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ قُبَّعَةً جَدِيدَةً لِلشَّمْسِ.
examples.translation: I bought a new sun hat.

faults.quote: Use the masculine article 'il' in the singular
faults.why: Restates the article and gender already shown in the headword.

notes: The plural is 'i laghi', written with 'gh' to keep the hard /ɡ/ sound.

senses.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

examples.text: Il lago è molto calmo oggi.
examples.translation: The lake is very calm today.

faults.quote: Use 'lavoro' both for the general activity of working and
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Often used with 'andare al lavoro' (to go to work) and 'essere al lavoro' (to be at work).
Do not confuse with 'il mestiere', which specifically means a trade or craft.

senses.definition: A paid position of regular employment.

examples.text: Cerco un nuovo lavoro con orari flessibili.
examples.translation: I am looking for a new job with flexible hours.

senses.definition: Physical or mental effort done to achieve a result, or a specific piece of work to be done.

examples.text: Questo lavoro di ristrutturazione richiede molta pazienza.
examples.translation: This renovation work requires a lot of patience.

faults.quote: Il leone rugbisce nella savana.
faults.why: Misspelled verb: 'rugbisce' is not a word; it must be 'ruggisce'.

faults.quote: A person who shows great courage, strength, or fierceness.
faults.why: Transparent simile ('come un leone'), not a separate everyday sense for A2.

faults.quote: Used for the large wild cat with a mane, but
faults.why: Merely repeats the definitions of the senses.

notes: The feminine form is 'la leonessa' (lioness).

senses.definition: A large wild cat native to Africa and India, known for the male's thick mane.

examples.text: Il leone ruggisce nella savana.
examples.translation: The lion roars in the savanna.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with 'la lettera' (letter)
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; misses the real homograph 'letto' (past participle of 'leggere') and article usage.

notes: Used without an article in common expressions like 'andare a letto' (to go to bed) and 'stare a letto' (to stay in bed).
Spelled and pronounced the same as 'letto', the past participle of 'leggere' (to read).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for sleeping on.

examples.text: Vado a letto presto stasera.
examples.translation: I am going to bed early tonight.

senses.definition: The ground at the bottom of a river.

examples.text: Il fiume è secco e si vede il letto di sassi.
examples.translation: The river is dry and you can see the stony riverbed.

faults.quote: (call) A conversation held by using this device.
faults.why: 'Téléphone' alone does not mean 'phone call' in standard French (that is 'coup de téléphone').

faults.quote: Use 'téléphone' to mean both the physical device and the call itself
faults.why: It is 'coup de téléphone' that means a call, not 'téléphone' by itself.

notes: Notice common expressions: 'être au téléphone' (to be on the phone), 'un coup de téléphone' (a phone call), and 'un numéro de téléphone' (a phone number).

senses.definition: A device or system used for talking to people who are far away.

examples.text: J'ai perdu mon téléphone dans le train.
examples.translation: I lost my phone on the train.

examples.text: Il est au téléphone avec sa mère.
examples.translation: He is on the phone with his mother.

faults.quote: In French, 'le temps' covers both abstract time and meteorological weather
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the silent final '-ps' and contrast with 'fois'.

notes: The final '-ps' is silent, and the singular and plural forms are identical ('le temps', 'les temps').
For 'time' as a countable occasion (one time, three times), use 'la fois', not 'le temps'.

senses.definition: Duration measured in seconds, minutes, hours, days, or years; available time.

examples.text: Le temps passe vite quand on s'amuse.
examples.translation: Time flies when you are having fun.

senses.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a given place and time, such as rain, sun, or wind.

examples.text: Quel temps fait-il aujourd'hui ?
examples.translation: What is the weather like today?

faults.why: Should mention that the 'h' in 'thé' is silent, pronounced /te/, not like English 'th'.

notes: The 'h' is silent: 'thé' is pronounced /te/, with a simple 't' sound.
Use the partitive 'du thé' for tea in general, and 'un thé' when ordering a cup of tea in a café.

senses.definition: A hot drink made by pouring boiling water over dried leaves of the tea plant.

examples.text: Je bois une tasse de thé chaud tous les matins.
examples.translation: I drink a cup of hot tea every morning.

faults.quote: roof; ceiling
faults.why: 'Toit' does not mean 'ceiling' (as the entry's own note points out), and no sense has it.

notes: The final '-t' is silent.
Do not confuse 'le toit' (roof, on the outside of a building) with 'le plafond' (ceiling, on the inside of a room).

senses.definition: The top covering of a building or vehicle, which protects the inside from rain, snow, and sun.

examples.text: La neige recouvre le toit de la maison.
examples.translation: The snow covers the roof of the house.

senses.definition: A home or place to live, especially in expressions about having shelter.

examples.text: Tout le monde a besoin d'un toit pour dormir.
examples.translation: Everyone needs a roof over their head to sleep.

faults.quote: Though grammatically masculine as 'le touriste', it can refer to a person
faults.why: 'Touriste' has the same spelling for both genders: 'un/le touriste' (masculine) and 'une/la touriste' (feminine).

notes: The form is the same in the masculine and the feminine: 'un touriste' / 'une touriste'.

senses.definition: A person who travels to and visits a place for pleasure.

examples.text: Les touristes prennent des photos devant la tour Eiffel.
examples.translation: The tourists are taking photos in front of the Eiffel Tower.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'рост' (height or growth)
faults.why: Unlikely confusion for beginners; should instead contrast with 'завод' (factory/plant).

faults.quote: The houseplant is standing on the windowsill.
faults.why: Calque of Russian 'стоит'; in natural English a plant 'is' or 'sits' on a windowsill.

notes: Used only for living plants; a 'plant' in the sense of a factory is 'завод' or 'фабрика'.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in soil or water and usually has leaves, stems, and roots.

examples.text: Комнатное растение стоит на подоконнике.
examples.translation: The houseplant is on the windowsill.

faults.quote: A sad sight opened up before us.
faults.why: Calque of 'открылась картина'; unnatural in English.

notes: Refers to a painted or drawn picture; for a photograph, use 'фотография' or 'фото', and for a small drawing or illustration in a book, 'картинка'.

senses.definition: A work of art made with paint on a canvas or other surface.

examples.text: На стене висит красивая картина.
examples.translation: A beautiful painting is hanging on the wall.

senses.definition: A view, sight, or general situation that one sees or imagines.

examples.text: Перед нами открылась грустная картина.
examples.translation: A sad scene unfolded before us.

faults.quote: The noun час has an irregular plural form: часа
faults.why: 'часа' (genitive singular) and 'часов' (genitive plural) are regular case forms after numbers, except stress.

notes: After the numbers 2, 3, and 4, the stress shifts to the ending in the genitive singular: два часа́ ('two hours' or 'two o'clock').
The plural form часы́ also means 'clock' or 'watch'.

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: Мы ждём уже целый час.
examples.translation: We have been waiting for a whole hour.

senses.definition: A point in time or hour of the day, used when telling the time.

examples.text: Который час? — Сейчас два часа.
examples.translation: What time is it? — It's two o'clock.

faults.quote: Used both for fruit and vegetable juices to drink, and for
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the special partitive/locative form 'в соку'.

notes: Takes the stressed ending -у in the prepositional case after в or на: в соку́ (e.g., в собственном соку́ — 'in its own juice').

senses.definition: A drink made from the liquid of fruits or vegetables.

examples.text: Я пью апельсиновый сок по утрам.
examples.translation: I drink orange juice in the morning.

senses.definition: The natural liquid inside a plant, tree, or fruit.

examples.text: Весной берёзы дают сладкий сок.
examples.translation: In spring, birch trees produce sweet sap.

faults.why: A visitor at a home and a guest at a hotel are the same basic meaning.

faults.quote: Used both for someone invited to your home or an event
faults.why: Restates the definitions instead of teaching the essential everyday phrases 'в гости' and 'в гостях'.

notes: Very common in the plural phrases идти́/ходи́ть в го́сти ('to go visiting someone') and быть в гостя́х ('to be visiting at someone's place').
The feminine form for a female guest is го́стья.

senses.definition: A person invited to visit someone's home or an event, or staying at a hotel.

examples.text: Мы ждём гостей на ужин.
examples.translation: We are expecting guests for dinner.

faults.quote: Used to indicate that something happens after the expected or usual time.
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim.

notes: Common in 'più tardi' (later, e.g. 'a più tardi', see you later) and 'fare tardi' (to be running late / to stay out late).
Do not confuse with the noun 'ritardo' (delay), used in 'essere in ritardo' (to be late for an appointment or schedule).

senses.definition: After the expected or usual time, or towards the end of the day.

examples.text: Arrivo sempre tardi quando c'è traffico.
examples.translation: I always arrive late when there is traffic.

examples.text: È troppo tardi per chiamare gli amici.
examples.translation: It is too late to call friends.

notes: Takes the preposition 'a' before the person called (telefonare a qualcuno), using indirect object pronouns (gli telefono, le telefono).
Specifically refers to making a phone call; 'chiamare' (with a direct object) is also very common for phone calls as well as calling out to someone.

senses.definition: To contact someone by telephone.

examples.text: Devo telefonare a mia madre stasera.
examples.translation: I have to call my mother tonight.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who feels nervous or uncomfortable around other people
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.

examples.text: Da bambino ero molto timido e non riuscivo a parlare con gli sconosciuti.
examples.translation: As a child I was very shy and couldn't talk to strangers.

faults.quote: It is also widely used for throwing objects (like a ball)
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 without adding usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to pull; to throw; to shoot
notes: On doors, 'tirare' (pull) contrasts with 'spingere' (push).
Also used in everyday expressions about wind: 'tira vento' (it's windy / the wind is blowing).

senses.definition: To move something towards oneself or in a given direction using force.

examples.text: Devi tirare la corda con forza per aprire la porta.
examples.translation: You have to pull the rope hard to open the door.

senses.definition: To throw, hurl, or kick an object such as a ball in a particular direction.

examples.text: Il bambino vuole tirare la palla al cane.
examples.translation: The boy wants to throw the ball to the dog.

faults.quote: triste is invariable in the plural for masculine and feminine nouns
faults.why: Standard grammar for all Italian '-e' adjectives; calling it 'invariable' is confusing.

senses.definition: Feeling, showing, or causing sadness and unhappiness.

examples.text: Ho visto un film molto triste ieri sera.
examples.translation: I saw a very sad movie last night.

faults.quote: It is a versatile fruit used in everything from school lunches
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia about apples, not linguistic information.

notes: Usually written in hiragana (りんご) or katakana (リンゴ); the kanji 林檎 is rare in everyday writing.

senses.definition: The round, crisp fruit of the apple tree, usually red, yellow, or green.

faults.quote: The word is often used metaphorically to mean 'skill' or 'ability,'
faults.why: merely restates sense 1 and its example.

notes: Refers to the whole arm from shoulder to wrist; in idioms, it often means practical skill (e.g., 腕がいい 'skilled', 腕を上げる 'to improve one's skill').

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body from the shoulder to the wrist.

examples.text: 彼は腕を組んで考えている。
examples.translation: He is thinking with his arms crossed.

senses.definition: Practical skill or ability in a craft or activity.

examples.text: 毎日練習して料理の腕を上げた。
examples.translation: I practiced every day and improved my cooking skills.

faults.why: Missing required hiragana reading (がっこう) for a kanji headword.

notes: Note the small っ (double consonant) and long vowel in the reading がっこう (gakkō), where 学 (がく) combines with 校 (こう).

senses.definition: An institution for educating children or students.

examples.text: 毎日バスで学校に行きます。
examples.translation: I go to school by bus every day.

faults.quote: While '女の子' is the standard word for 'girl,' it is also frequently
faults.why: merely restates the two senses already given.

faults.quote: '女性' (josei), which is the formal, gender-neutral term for an adult woman
faults.why: 女性 means 'woman/female'; calling it 'gender-neutral' is contradictory and false.

notes: Compare 女性 (じょせい), the standard polite term for an adult woman, and 女子 (じょし), used for girls or young women in school, sports, or casual speech.

senses.definition: A female child.

examples.text: 公園で小さな女の子が遊んでいる。
examples.translation: A little girl is playing in the park.

senses.definition: A young unmarried woman, in casual speech.

faults.why: Missing required hiragana reading (おなかがすく) for a headword containing kanji.

faults.quote: I get hungry as soon as past lunchtime.
faults.why: Ungrammatical English translation.

notes: Literally 'one's stomach becomes empty'. To say 'I am hungry' right now, use the past tense お腹がすいた (casual) or お腹がすきました (polite).
