senses.definition: To come to feel a need for food; to become hungry.

examples.text: たくさん運動したので、お腹がすきました。
examples.translation: I exercised a lot, so I'm hungry.

examples.text: お昼の時間を過ぎると、すぐにお腹がすく。
examples.translation: I get hungry right after lunchtime passes.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (まくら) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: 枕を高くして寝る。
faults.why: An idiom is unhelpful as the sole example of a basic noun for beginners.

faults.quote: Used specifically for the soft cushion you place your head on
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: For a decorative cushion on a sofa or chair, use クッション (kusshon); for a floor cushion to sit on, use 座布団 (zabuton).

senses.definition: A soft cushion used to support the head while sleeping.

examples.text: この枕は柔らかくて気持ちいい。
examples.translation: This pillow is soft and comfortable.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (こうえん) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: always a public, communal space managed by the local government.
faults.why: Overstated: national parks (国立公園) and private theme parks (遊園地/テーマパーク) also use 公園.

notes: Refers to a public park; a traditional landscaped garden is 庭園 (teien), and a home yard or garden is 庭 (niwa).

senses.definition: A public area with trees, grass, and paths, used for rest and recreation.

examples.text: 週末は公園で散歩します。
examples.translation: I go for a walk in the park on weekends.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (ゆき) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: 雪 (yuki) is used for both the falling flakes and the layer
faults.why: Restates the definition and adds poetic filler instead of grammatical guidance.

notes: Use 雪が降る (yuki ga furu) for 'to snow' and 雪が積もる (yuki ga tsumoru) when snow piles up on the ground.

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky and cover the ground.

examples.text: 外は雪が降っています。
examples.translation: It is snowing outside.

examples.text: 昨日の雪はとても綺麗でした。
examples.translation: Yesterday's snow was very beautiful.

faults.quote: I fell and blood came out of my knee.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of 血が出た; natural English is 'my knee bled' or 'started bleeding'.

notes: 'To bleed' is expressed with the phrase 血が出る (chi ga deru, literally 'blood comes out').
Also used figuratively for family lineage, as in 血のつながり (blood ties).

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows inside the body of humans and animals.

examples.text: 転んで膝から血が出た。
examples.translation: I fell and my knee started bleeding.

faults.quote: Note that '農家' can refer to either the person (the farmer) or
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: Literally 'farming household' (家 means house or family), so it often refers to a farming family or business rather than a single individual.
Do not confuse with 農業 (nōgyō), which refers to the industry of agriculture itself.

senses.definition: A family or person whose job is growing crops or raising animals on a farm.

examples.text: 彼は代々続く農家です。
examples.translation: He comes from a long line of farmers.

senses.definition: A traditional house on a farm where a farming family lives.

examples.text: その古い農家を改装してレストランにした。
examples.translation: They renovated the old farmhouse into a restaurant.

faults.quote: /paˈtaːtes/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and stress: standard Turkish is /pataˈtes/, with no long vowel.

notes: Like other Turkish nouns, singular 'patates' is often used generically for potatoes in general or in dishes (e.g., 'patates kızartması' — French fries).

senses.definition: A round or oval starchy vegetable that grows underground.

examples.text: Akşam yemeği için fırında patates yaptım.
examples.translation: I made baked potatoes for dinner.

faults.quote: (craft) A pattern or template used in sewing or design.
faults.why: Sewing 'patron' is technical/dated (modern Turkish uses 'kalıp'), not an A2 everyday sense.

faults.quote: Yarın izin almak için patron ile konuşacağım.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing: native speakers say 'patronla' (or 'patronumla'), not separate 'patron ile'.

notes: Refers to the owner of a business or the top boss. Do not confuse with 'müdür', which means a salaried manager, director, or school principal.

senses.definition: The person in charge of you at work or the owner of a business.

examples.text: Yarın izin almak için patronla konuşacağım.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will talk to the boss to ask for time off.

faults.quote: Pazar has two common meanings that seem unrelated. Use the context
faults.why: Filler note that merely restates the two senses without useful linguistic advice.

notes: As a place, 'pazar' usually refers to a weekly neighborhood street market (or figuratively to an economic market), not a grocery store ('market' or 'süpermarket').
When used for the day of the week, it is often followed by 'günü' (e.g., 'pazar günü' — on Sunday).

senses.definition: An open-air street market where vendors set up stalls to sell fresh fruit, vegetables, and household goods.

examples.text: Annem taze sebze almak için pazara gitti.
examples.translation: My mother went to the market to buy fresh vegetables.

senses.definition: The day of the week between Saturday and Monday.

examples.text: Pazar günü evde dinlenmeyi seviyorum.
examples.translation: I like to rest at home on Sunday.

faults.quote: /ˈpændʒeɾe/
faults.why: Wrong stress and first vowel: standard Turkish 'pencere' is stressed on the final syllable /pendʒeˈɾe/.

faults.quote: Used mainly for glass windows in houses and buildings, as well as
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning, which works just like English 'window'.

notes: Since 'pencere' ends in a vowel, it takes the buffer consonant 'y' before vowel-initial suffixes: 'pencereyi' (the window, accusative), 'pencereden' (from/out of the window).

senses.definition: An opening in a wall or vehicle fitted with glass to let in light and air.

examples.text: Temiz hava almak için pencereyi açtı.
examples.translation: He opened the window to get some fresh air.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'ekmek' (bread), which you will almost always eat
faults.why: Nonsensical confusion warning: 'peynir' and 'ekmek' look and sound nothing alike.

notes: Often used in compounds for common varieties, such as 'beyaz peynir' (white brined cheese, similar to feta) and 'kaşar peyniri' (yellow melting cheese).

senses.definition: A solid food made from milk.

examples.text: Kahvaltıda ekmek ve peynir yiyorum.
examples.translation: I eat bread and cheese for breakfast.

faults.quote: ดินสอ is used for writing or drawing and can be erased
faults.why: Explains what a pencil is in the real world rather than giving Thai usage information.
Missing the essential classifier for pencils in Thai (แท่ง / ด้าม).

notes: The classifier for ดินสอ is แท่ง (thâeng) or ด้าม (dâam).

senses.definition: A tool for writing or drawing, usually made of wood with a graphite core.

examples.text: ฉันใช้ดินสอเขียนลงในสมุด
examples.translation: I use a pencil to write in the notebook.

faults.quote: /dɛ̀k pùː jǐŋ/
faults.why: Wrong vowel, aspiration, and tone on ผู้ (/pʰûː/, falling tone, not /pùː/) and เด็ก (/dèk/).

corrected.headword: เด็กผู้หญิง
notes: Literally 'female child', from เด็ก (child) + ผู้หญิง (woman, female). Its counterpart is เด็กผู้ชาย (boy). The classifier is คน (khon).

senses.definition: A female child.

examples.text: เด็กผู้หญิงคนนั้นกำลังเล่นของเล่น
examples.translation: That girl is playing with a toy.
examples.matchedForm: เด็กผู้หญิง

faults.quote: While this word is used for 'coin' (physical money), it is also
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.
Fails to mention that เหรียญ is its own classifier and is used colloquially for 'dollar'.

notes: เหรียญ is also used as its own classifier (e.g. เหรียญสองเหรียญ, 'two coins'), and colloquially as a classifier for foreign dollar currencies (e.g. สิบเหรียญ, 'ten dollars').
Contrast with แบงก์ (báeng, spoken) or ธนบัตร (thá-ná-bàt, formal), which refer to paper banknotes.

senses.definition: A small, flat, round piece of metal used as money.

examples.text: ฉันมีเหรียญอยู่ในกระเป๋า
examples.translation: I have some coins in my bag.

senses.definition: A flat piece of metal given as a prize or award in a competition.

examples.text: เขาได้รับเหรียญทองจากการแข่งขัน
examples.translation: He received a gold medal from the competition.

faults.why: Missing the essential classifier วง (wong) used for rings in Thai.

notes: The classifier for แหวน is วง (wong).
Refers to a finger ring (or a washer in hardware); other circular loops like key rings or hoops are called ห่วง (hùang).

senses.definition: A small circular band, typically of precious metal, worn on a finger as jewelry.

examples.text: เธอใส่แหวนทองที่นิ้วนาง
examples.translation: She is wearing a gold ring on her ring finger.

faults.quote: While this word means both 'milk' and 'breast', the context makes
faults.why: Restates the glosses without providing useful usage or register guidance for the body sense.

notes: Also used for plant-based milks, such as นมถั่วเหลือง (soy milk).
For the body part, นม is casual or blunt; หน้าอก (nâa-òk, 'chest') or เต้านม (tâo-nom, medical/formal) is more polite.

senses.definition: The white liquid produced by female mammals, or a similar plant-based drink.

examples.text: ฉันชอบดื่มนมสดในตอนเช้า
examples.translation: I like to drink fresh milk in the morning.

senses.definition: Either of the two milk-producing parts on a woman's chest.

examples.text: แม่กำลังให้นมลูก
examples.translation: The mother is breastfeeding her baby.

faults.quote: Remember that main is feminine: la main, une main.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the entry fields.

faults.quote: The style of a person's handwriting.
faults.why: Archaic/literary sense; everyday French uses 'écriture' for handwriting.

faults.quote: Elle écrit avec une belle main.
faults.why: Unnatural in modern French; native speakers say 'Elle a une belle écriture'.

notes: Take care not to confuse 'main' (/mɛ̃/) with 'moins' (/mwɛ̃/, less).
Common expressions: 'donner un coup de main' (to give a hand / to help), 'serrer la main' (to shake hands).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers.

examples.text: Il a levé la main pour poser une question.
examples.translation: He raised his hand to ask a question.

faults.quote: Use 'maison' for a physical house or building, but also when
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without adding usage guidance.

faults.quote: A building where a family lives.
faults.why: Conflates the physical building ('house') with one's place of residence ('home', as in 'à la maison').

notes: To say 'at home' or 'home' (with verbs of motion), use 'à la maison' or 'chez' + pronoun (e.g. 'chez moi'): 'Je rentre à la maison' (I'm going home).
Placed directly after another noun without a preposition, 'maison' means 'homemade': 'un gâteau maison' (a homemade cake).

senses.definition: A building where people, especially a family, live.

examples.text: J'habite dans une grande maison avec un jardin.
examples.translation: I live in a big house with a garden.

senses.definition: The place where one lives, whether a house or an apartment, especially in 'à la maison'.

examples.text: Ce soir, je reste à la maison.
examples.translation: Tonight, I am staying at home.

senses.definition: A traditional commercial firm, such as a fashion label or publishing company.

examples.text: Cette maison de couture est très célèbre à Paris.
examples.translation: This fashion house is very famous in Paris.

faults.quote: Use 'la mer' when talking about the sea in general
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning without giving useful grammatical or collocation help.

notes: Often used in 'aller à la mer' (to go to the seaside) and 'au bord de la mer' (by the sea).
Sounds identical to 'la mère' (the mother) and 'le maire' (the mayor): /mɛʁ/.

senses.definition: The large body of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface.

examples.text: Nous passons nos vacances au bord de la mer.
examples.translation: We are spending our holidays by the sea.

notes: When speaking to or about their own mother in everyday conversation, French speakers usually say 'maman' (mum/mom).
Sounds identical to 'la mer' (the sea) and 'le maire' (the mayor): /mɛʁ/.

senses.definition: A female parent; a woman in relation to her child or children.

examples.text: Ma mère prépare un bon gâteau pour mon anniversaire.
examples.translation: My mother is baking a good cake for my birthday.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'la minute' (sixty seconds) with 'le moment'
faults.why: Invented confusion; English speakers already share both cognates and contradicts sense 1.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.

examples.text: Le train arrive dans cinq minutes.
examples.translation: The train arrives in five minutes.

senses.definition: A very short period of time.

examples.text: Attends une minute, s'il te plaît.
examples.translation: Wait a minute, please.

faults.quote: नदी (nadī) is feminine. Remember that most Hindi nouns ending in
faults.why: Restates the gender field; plural declension (-इयाँ) is more useful.

notes: In the plural, the final long ई (-ī) shortens to इ (-i): नदियाँ (nadiyā̃, rivers), नदियों (nadiyõ, oblique plural).

senses.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

examples.text: नदी का पानी बहुत साफ़ है।
examples.translation: The river water is very clean.

faults.quote: /səmuːd̪ɾə təʈ/
faults.why: समुद्र has a short u (/u/), not a long ū (/uː/).
Seaside/coast and beach are shades of one meaning in Hindi for समुद्र तट.

faults.quote: If you want to specifically refer to the sandy part of
faults.why: किनारा means 'edge/bank/shore', not specifically the sandy part.

notes: A somewhat formal compound (from समुद्र 'sea' + तट 'shore/bank'). In everyday speech, people often say समंदर का किनारा (samandar kā kinārā) or use the English word बीच (bīc) for a recreational beach.

senses.definition: The land or sandy area along the edge of the sea.

examples.text: बच्चे समुद्र तट पर खेल रहे हैं।
examples.translation: The children are playing on the beach.

examples.text: समुद्र तट का मौसम बहुत सुहावना होता है।
examples.translation: The weather at the coast is very pleasant.

faults.quote: 'चावल' is the general term for the grain itself.
faults.why: Contradicts note 0; in standard Hindi चावल is the normal word for cooked rice too.

notes: Used for both uncooked rice grains and cooked rice. Can be treated as singular or plural in agreement (e.g., चावल पका है or चावल पके हैं).
Regional speakers may use भात (bhāt) specifically for cooked boiled rice, but चावल is standard everywhere.

senses.definition: Small white or brown grains grown in wet fields and eaten cooked as a staple food.

examples.text: मैंने आज चावल बनाए हैं।
examples.translation: I have made rice today.

examples.text: दाल-चावल मेरा पसंदीदा खाना है।
examples.translation: Lentils and rice is my favorite food.

faults.quote: Use 'फ़र्श' when talking about indoor surfaces in a home or
faults.why: Repeats note 0 and the definition without adding new grammatical or usage information.

notes: Refers to the built floor of a room (takes the postposition पर 'on': फ़र्श पर 'on the floor'). Do not confuse with ज़मीन (zamīn), which means the ground, earth, or land (though ज़मीन is also loosely used for floor).
For a storey or level of a building ('first floor'), use मंज़िल (manzil), not फ़र्श.

senses.definition: The lower surface of a room that you walk on.

examples.text: मैंने फ़र्श साफ़ किया।
examples.translation: I cleaned the floor.

faults.quote: Used commonly to refer to commercial passenger planes.
faults.why: Obvious from the gloss 'airplane' and repeats the definition.

notes: Literally 'air ship' (from हवाई 'aerial' + जहाज़ 'ship'). In everyday conversation, it is often shortened to जहाज़ (jahāz) or replaced by the English word प्लेन (plen).
Many speakers pronounce ज़ (z) as ज (j): जहाज (jahāj).

senses.definition: A vehicle with wings and engines that flies through the air and carries passengers or cargo.

examples.text: हवाई जहाज़ आसमान में उड़ रहा है।
examples.translation: The airplane is flying in the sky.

faults.quote: [0] (live) ... [1] (occupy) To occupy a living space
faults.why: Living in a place and inhabiting it are the same meaning (intransitive vs. transitive).
Learners need to know it can be used with or without a preposition ('habiter Paris' / 'habiter à Paris').

notes: Use 'habiter' for where you live; use 'vivre' for being alive or living with someone.
Can be used with a preposition ('J'habite à Paris', 'J'habite dans une maison') or directly before a place or home ('J'habite Paris', 'J'habite un petit appartement').

senses.definition: To have your home in a place; to reside.

examples.text: J'habite dans un petit appartement à Lyon.
examples.translation: I live in a small apartment in Lyon.

faults.quote: Heureux is the standard word for happy, but it can also mean
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without adding grammatical or usage information.
Needs the irregular feminine form 'heureuse' and the preposition 'de' (+ infinitive).

faults.quote: Having good luck, favored by destiny.
faults.why: Fails to cover things/outcomes ('un choix heureux'), which its own example uses.

faults.quote: Nous avons eu un concours de circonstances heureux.
faults.why: Too complex for A2 and contradicts note[1] about pre-nominal placement.

notes: Feminine form: 'heureuse' (/œ.ʁøz/). The final 'x' of 'heureux' is silent except in liaison.
Followed by 'de' before an infinitive ('Je suis heureux de vous connaître').

senses.definition: Feeling joy, pleasure, or satisfaction.

examples.text: Elle est très heureuse de voir ses amis ce soir.
examples.translation: She is very happy to see her friends tonight.

senses.definition: Of a person: having good luck; of an event or choice: turning out well, favorable.

examples.text: Ce voyage a été une heureuse surprise.
examples.translation: This trip was a fortunate surprise.

faults.quote: Hier refers specifically to the day immediately preceding today.
faults.why: Restates the definition; notes should instead cover 'hier matin/soir' vs. 'la veille'.

faults.quote: The day before today.
faults.why: Defined as a noun rather than an adverb ('on the day before today').

notes: The 'h' is mute (pronounced /jɛʁ/), and the 'r' is always pronounced.
Combine directly with parts of the day: 'hier matin' (yesterday morning), 'hier soir' (last night).
For 'the day before' a past event in a story, use 'la veille', not 'hier'.

senses.definition: On the day before today.

examples.text: J'ai visité un musée hier.
examples.translation: I visited a museum yesterday.

faults.quote: Used to indicate the place where the speaker is located.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'là', which points to a place further away.
faults.why: Misleading: in everyday spoken French, 'là' very commonly means 'here' as well.

notes: In everyday spoken French, 'là' is very often used instead of 'ici' to mean 'here' (e.g., 'Je suis là' = I'm here). To clearly mean 'over there', use 'là-bas'.

senses.definition: In, at, or to this place, where the speaker is.

examples.text: Venez ici, s'il vous plaît.
examples.translation: Come here, please.

faults.quote: /ɡaˈʎĩɲɐ/
faults.why: Wrong consonant: 'l' in 'galinha' is /l/, not palatal /ʎ/.

notes: Refers to the live bird (especially the female; the rooster is 'o galo'). For chicken as food or meat, use 'o frango' (though dishes like 'galinha caipira' or 'canja de galinha' keep 'galinha').

senses.definition: A female farm bird raised for its eggs and meat.

examples.text: A galinha botou um ovo hoje de manhã.
examples.translation: The hen laid an egg this morning.

senses.definition: A container for liquids with a narrow neck, usually made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: Ela abriu uma garrafa de vinho.
examples.translation: She opened a bottle of wine.

examples.text: Preciso comprar uma garrafa de água.
examples.translation: I need to buy a bottle of water.

faults.quote: This word is essential for any kitchen-related conversation.
faults.why: Pure filler note with no linguistic information.

notes: Standard in Brazil; in Portugal, the word is 'o frigorífico'.

senses.definition: A large kitchen appliance that keeps food and drinks cold.

examples.text: Vou colocar o leite na geladeira.
examples.translation: I am going to put the milk in the fridge.

faults.quote: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'a grama' refers to the grass in a garden
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss.

notes: Feminine 'a grama' means grass (in Portugal, 'a relva'). Do not confuse it with masculine 'o grama', the unit of weight (gram), though in informal Brazilian speech people often make the weight feminine too ('duzentas gramas').

senses.definition: Short green plants that cover the ground in a garden, lawn, or park.

examples.text: Nós fizemos um piquenique sentados na grama.
examples.translation: We had a picnic sitting on the grass.

faults.quote: /ˈo.ɾɐ/
faults.why: Wrong vowel quality: 'hora' has an open-mid /ɔ/ (/ˈɔ.ɾɐ/), not close-mid /o/.

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'a hora' can mean both the specific time on the
faults.why: Restates the two senses; meanwhile a note on plural 'Que horas são?' is missing.

notes: To ask or tell the time of day, use the plural 'horas' (except for one o'clock): 'Que horas são?' (What time is it?), 'São três horas' (It's three o'clock).
Do not confuse with 'o tempo', which means time in general or weather ('Não tenho tempo' = I don't have time).

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: A reunião vai durar uma hora.
examples.translation: The meeting will last an hour.

senses.definition: The time of day as shown on a clock, or a particular moment for something to happen.

examples.text: Você sabe que horas são?
examples.translation: Do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Está na hora de ir embora.
examples.translation: It is time to leave.

faults.quote: गर्मी (garmi) can mean both the physical sensation of heat
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

faults.quote: Today there is a lot of heat.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English one says 'It is very hot today'.

notes: To say someone feels hot, use the dative subject with लगना: मुझे गर्मी लग रही है (I am feeling hot).
In the sense 'summer', it is often used in the plural (गर्मियाँ, oblique गर्मियों में 'in the summer').

senses.definition: High temperature, warmth, or the uncomfortable feeling of being hot.

examples.text: आज बहुत गर्मी है।
examples.translation: It is very hot today.

senses.definition: The warmest season of the year, between spring and monsoon or autumn.

examples.text: गर्मी की छुट्टी में हम नानी के घर जाएंगे।
examples.translation: In the summer holidays we will go to grandma's house.

faults.quote: In Hindi, name is often used in the context of asking
faults.why: Filler note; does not explain the grammar or usage of the word नाम itself.

notes: An unmarked masculine noun: its plural and singular oblique forms stay नाम (plural oblique नामों).

senses.definition: The word or words that a person, place, or thing is known by.

examples.text: आपका नाम क्या है?
examples.translation: What is your name?

faults.quote: While 'bed' is the most common translation, 'बिस्तर' (bistar) can also
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses useful collocations and区分 with पलंग.

notes: Refers to a made bed or the bedding itself; for the wooden or metal bedframe, पलंग is used.
Commonly used with लगाना (बिस्तर लगाना, 'to make the bed').

senses.definition: A place or piece of furniture arranged for sleeping.

examples.text: वह बिस्तर पर लेटा है।
examples.translation: He is lying on the bed.

senses.definition: The mattress, sheets, pillows, and covers laid out for sleeping.

examples.text: सोने से पहले अपना बिस्तर लगा लो।
examples.translation: Make your bed before sleeping.

faults.quote: Used as a primary source of protein in many Indian households.
faults.why: Encyclopedic filler and restates the gender field.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with simple round objects
faults.why: Pointless warning; no learner confuses 'egg' with 'round object'.
Splitting culinary egg and bird's biological egg is unnecessary for an A2 learner.

notes: A regular -आ masculine noun: plural and oblique singular अंडे, oblique plural अंडों.

senses.definition: The oval object with a thin shell laid by a female bird, especially a hen, often eaten as food.

examples.text: नाश्ते के लिए मैंने एक अंडा उबाला।
examples.translation: I boiled an egg for breakfast.

faults.quote: कीमत is commonly used to ask for or state the price
faults.why: Restates sense 0.

faults.quote: It can also be used figuratively to mean the worth
faults.why: Restates sense 1.

notes: Also spelled क़ीमत (pronounced /qiː.mət̪/) in more formal registers.

senses.definition: The amount of money asked or paid for something.

examples.text: इस किताब की कीमत क्या है?
examples.translation: What is the price of this book?

senses.definition: The importance or worth of something.

examples.text: हमें समय की कीमत समझनी चाहिए।
examples.translation: We should understand the value of time.

faults.quote: Note the liaison after the article: 'l'île' is pronounced 'lil'
faults.why: This is elision (enchaînement), not liaison, and is unnecessary filler.

notes: The preposition for being on an island is usually 'sur' ('sur une île').

senses.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water on all sides.

examples.text: Nous avons passé nos vacances sur une île déserte.
examples.translation: We spent our holidays on a deserted island.

faults.quote: Used as a noun for a person you do not know
faults.why: Restates the definitions instead of giving useful grammar or usage notes.

notes: For a female stranger, the feminine form is 'l'inconnue' (pronounced the same). Also used as an adjective meaning 'unknown'.

senses.definition: A person you do not know.

examples.text: Ne parle jamais à un inconnu dans la rue.
examples.translation: Never talk to a stranger in the street.

senses.definition: What is not known or familiar, especially the future or unfamiliar situations.

examples.text: Il a peur de l'inconnu.
examples.translation: He is afraid of the unknown.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'le docteur', which means doctor.
faults.why: Unhelpful filler; learners do not confuse 'infirmier' with 'docteur'.

faults.quote: The male nurse takes my blood pressure every morning.
faults.why: Unnatural translation; English simply uses 'nurse' unless gender is specifically contrasted.

notes: The feminine form, for a female nurse, is 'l'infirmière' (/ɛ̃.fiʁ.mjɛʁ/).

senses.definition: A man trained to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital.

examples.text: L'infirmier prend ma tension tous les matins.
examples.translation: The nurse takes my blood pressure every morning.

faults.quote: guest; caller
faults.why: 'Caller' is not in the senses and is not a standard meaning of 'invité'.
A guest on a show is the same core meaning as a guest at an event.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with client, which is a customer
faults.why: Filler note; there is no reason a learner would confuse 'invité' with 'client'.

notes: The feminine form is 'l'invitée' (pronounced the same). Do not confuse with the false friend 'l'hôte', which can mean either 'host' or 'guest'.

senses.definition: A person invited to a home, an event, or a television or radio show.

examples.text: Nous préparons le dîner pour nos invités.
examples.translation: We are preparing dinner for our guests.

faults.quote: /l‿wɔ.ɲɔ̃/
faults.why: IPA includes the article 'l'' and gives a non-standard vowel (/wɔ/ instead of /ɔ/).

faults.quote: Note the traditional spelling 'oignon', though the reformed spelling 'ognon'
faults.why: Fails to explicitly state the misleading pronunciation: the 'i' is silent (/ɔ.ɲɔ̃/).

notes: The 'i' is silent: 'oi' is pronounced /ɔ/ here, not /wa/. Because of this, the spelling 'ognon' is also accepted.

senses.definition: A round vegetable with a strong smell and flavour, made up of many layers.

examples.text: Je coupe un oignon pour la soupe.
examples.translation: I am cutting an onion for the soup.

faults.quote: Jus is a loanword from English, commonly used in everyday Hindi.
faults.why: Both notes are filler; the Hindi equivalent 'रस' is worth mentioning instead.

notes: An English loanword, often preferred in everyday speech over the native Hindi word रस (ras) for packaged or glass-served fruit juice.

senses.definition: The liquid extracted from fruit or vegetables.

examples.text: मुझे सुबह ताज़ा जूस पीना पसंद है।
examples.translation: I like to drink fresh juice in the morning.

faults.quote: used as an affectionate term of endearment for any younger male
faults.why: As a term of address, 'बेटा' is used by elders for both boys and girls.

faults.quote: An affectionate term for a young boy or a young man.
faults.why: Elders commonly address both young males and females as 'बेटा'.

notes: The feminine equivalent is बेटी (beṭī, 'daughter'), though as an affectionate form of address, elders commonly call both boys and girls बेटा.
In the vocative case (when calling someone directly), the singular stays बेटा rather than changing to बेटे.

senses.definition: A person's male child.

examples.text: मेरे दो बेटे हैं।
examples.translation: I have two sons.

senses.definition: An affectionate form of address used by an older person for a child or younger person of either gender.

examples.text: क्या हुआ, बेटा?
examples.translation: What happened, dear?

faults.quote: box; carton; container
faults.why: Omits the second sense (train coach/carriage).

notes: Used for cans, tins, cartons, and boxes of any material. The feminine diminutive डिब्बी (ḍibbī) refers to a very small box or case.

senses.definition: A container made of cardboard, plastic, or metal, often with a lid.

examples.text: मैंने सारा सामान एक बड़े डिब्बे में रख दिया।
examples.translation: I put all the things in a large box.

senses.definition: A separate passenger car or compartment of a train.

examples.text: हमारी सीट ट्रेन के तीसरे डिब्बे में है।
examples.translation: Our seat is in the third coach of the train.

faults.quote: /bət̪.t̪ʰəkʰ/
faults.why: The geminate is unaspirated /t̪.t̪/, not aspirated /t̪.t̪ʰ/.

notes: Also spelled बत्तख़ (battax) with a nuqta, pronounced /bət̪.t̪əx/.

senses.definition: A water bird with a flat beak, webbed feet, and a waddling walk.

examples.text: तालाब में बत्तख तैर रही है।
examples.translation: The duck is swimming in the pond.

faults.why: Hindi 'पत्थर' covers both 'stone' and 'rock' as a single concept; note[0] already explains this.

notes: Covers both small stones you can pick up and large rocks or stone as a material.
Used in the common compound पत्थर-दिल (patthar-dil, 'stone-hearted') to describe an unfeeling person.

senses.definition: Hard, solid mineral matter found in the ground, or a piece of it of any size.

examples.text: नदी के किनारे बहुत पत्थर हैं।
examples.translation: There are many stones on the river bank.

examples.text: यह पहाड़ बड़े-बड़े पत्थरों से बना है।
examples.translation: This mountain is made of large rocks.

faults.quote: В комнате было очень тёмно.
faults.why: 'Тёмно' is incorrect; the short form/predicative is 'темно' (stressed on last syllable). Use adjective form.

faults.quote: Used for physical lack of light, dark colors, or metaphorical situations
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage information.

notes: In the short form and the adverb/predicative 'темно́' ('it is dark'), the stress shifts to the end and 'ё' becomes 'е'.

senses.definition: Having little or no light.

examples.text: Мы вошли в тёмную комнату.
examples.translation: We entered a dark room.

senses.definition: Not light in color; deep in shade.

examples.text: У него тёмные волосы.
examples.translation: He has dark hair.

senses.definition: Not clear or easily understood; mysterious or suspicious.

examples.text: Это тёмное дело.
examples.translation: This is a shady affair.

faults.why: Missing the common A1/A2 sense 'grown-up / old enough' (of children).

notes: For tall people or buildings, use 'высокий' instead. The comparative form is irregular: 'бо́льше' (bigger/more).

senses.definition: Of a physical size that is above average.

examples.text: У них очень большой дом.
examples.translation: They have a very large house.

senses.definition: Great in degree, amount, or importance.

examples.text: Это большой успех для нашей команды.
examples.translation: This is a great success for our team.

senses.definition: Of a child: grown-up or no longer little.

examples.text: Твой сын уже такой большой!
examples.translation: Your son is so big already!

faults.quote: In or to a foreign country.
faults.why: 'За границей' only means 'in a foreign country' (location), never 'to' (direction, 'за границу').

faults.quote: Used when someone is living, traveling, or working outside their home country.
faults.why: Restates the definition of 'abroad'.

notes: Describes location (where: 'жить за границей'). For movement to a foreign country (where to), use 'за границу' ('поехать за границу').

senses.definition: In a foreign country.

examples.text: Они любят отдыхать за границей каждое лето.
examples.translation: They like to vacation abroad every summer.

faults.quote: Do not confuse с здесь with тут;
faults.why: Contains stray Russian preposition 'с' inside an English sentence.

faults.quote: Положи книгу здесь.
faults.why: 'Положить' usually takes directional 'сюда' ('Положи книгу сюда'), not locational 'здесь'.

faults.quote: Use здесь when pointing out a place where you are right now.
faults.why: Restates the meaning of 'here'; missing the crucial contrast with directional 'сюда'.

notes: Describes static location (where: 'я здесь'). For movement toward this place (where to), use 'сюда' ('иди сюда').
Synonym 'тут' is slightly more informal in conversation.

senses.definition: In, at, or to this place or position.

examples.text: Мы здесь живём.
examples.translation: We live here.

examples.text: Здесь очень красиво.
examples.translation: It is very beautiful here.

faults.quote: starting from January 1st and ending on December 31st.
faults.why: Too narrow; excludes the duration sense shown in the second example and non-Gregorian years.

notes: The most common everyday word for 'year' (including when stating someone's age); 'वर्ष' (varṣ) is more formal.
To state someone's age, use the postposition 'का/की/के': वह दस साल का है (He is ten years old).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months, or a calendar year.

examples.text: अगला साल बहुत अच्छा होगा।
examples.translation: Next year will be very good.

examples.text: मैं यहाँ दो साल से रह रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I have been living here for two years.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'धुआँ' (smoke)
faults.why: Smoke and fire are unrelated in form and meaning; notes repeat the senses.

notes: Commonly used in compound verbs: आग लगना (for a fire to break out), आग लगाना (to set fire to; to provoke), and आग जलाना (to light a fire).

senses.definition: Burning material that produces light, heat, and flames.

examples.text: ठंड के मौसम में आग बहुत काम आती है।
examples.translation: Fire is very useful in cold weather.

examples.text: उसने सूखी लकड़ियों से आग जलाई।
examples.translation: He lit a fire with dry sticks.

senses.definition: A feeling of intense anger or passion.

examples.text: उसकी बातों ने मेरे अंदर आग लगा दी।
examples.translation: His words sparked rage inside me.

faults.quote: Used as a common noun for the animal. In Hindi, it is masculine.
faults.why: Note [0] restates POS and gender; replace with the irregular feminine form 'हथिनी'.

notes: The feminine form (female elephant) is 'हथिनी' (hathinī).

senses.definition: A very large grey mammal with a long trunk, big ears, and tusks.

examples.text: हाथी बहुत बड़ा और समझदार जानवर है।
examples.translation: The elephant is a very big and intelligent animal.

faults.quote: Commonly confused with shoes (जूते), but remember that मोज़ा is the soft
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; replace with a note on the nuqta spelling and pronunciation.

notes: Usually used in the plural (मोज़े) when referring to a pair of socks.
Often written without the dot (नुक़्ता) as 'मोजा' and pronounced /moːdʒaː/ in everyday speech.

senses.definition: A piece of soft clothing worn on the foot, usually inside a shoe.

examples.text: मेरे मोज़े गीले हो गए।
examples.translation: My socks got wet.

examples.text: मैंने नए मोज़े पहने हैं।
examples.translation: I am wearing new socks.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical plate you eat from and for
faults.why: merely restates the two senses; better to note restaurant course names (primo/secondo piatto)

notes: In restaurants, courses are called 'primo piatto' (first course, usually pasta or soup) and 'secondo piatto' (main course, meat or fish).

senses.definition: A flat round object used for eating or serving food.

examples.text: Metti il piatto sulla tavola.
examples.translation: Put the plate on the table.

senses.definition: Food prepared in a particular way as part of a meal.

examples.text: Questo è il mio piatto preferito.
examples.translation: This is my favorite dish.

faults.quote: Used for both human feet and the base or bottom of
faults.why: restates the senses; misses the essential A1/A2 expressions 'a piedi' and 'in piedi'

notes: Very common in the plural phrases 'a piedi' (on foot, walking) and 'in piedi' (standing up).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the bottom of the leg, used for standing and walking.

examples.text: Mi fa male il piede sinistro.
examples.translation: My left foot hurts.

examples.text: Vado a scuola a piedi.
examples.translation: I go to school on foot.

senses.definition: The lowest part of something, such as a mountain, stairs, or a page.

examples.text: La casa si trova ai piedi della montagna.
examples.translation: The house is at the foot of the mountain.

faults.quote: /ˈpɔllo/
faults.why: standard Italian has a close-mid /o/ in 'pollo' (/ˈpol.lo/), not /ɔ/

faults.quote: chicken, rooster, hen
faults.why: 'pollo' is a young chicken; 'rooster' is 'gallo' and 'hen' is 'gallina'

faults.quote: In the farmyard there are many hens and a rooster.
faults.why: translates 'pollo' as 'rooster', which is false ('gallo')

faults.quote: chicken; naive person
faults.why: names a meaning ('naive person') that is not in the senses

faults.quote: In Italian, 'pollo' refers to both the live animal and the
faults.why: merely restates the two senses

notes: Refers to the young bird raised for meat; an adult egg-laying hen is 'la gallina' and a rooster is 'il gallo'.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.text: Stasera cucino il pollo al forno con le patate.
examples.translation: Tonight I am cooking roast chicken with potatoes.

senses.definition: A young domestic bird raised on farms, especially for its meat.

examples.text: Nella fattoria allevano polli e conigli.
examples.translation: On the farm they raise chickens and rabbits.

notes: To say 'in the afternoon', use 'di pomeriggio' (habitually) or 'nel pomeriggio' (on a specific day), or simply 'il pomeriggio'.

senses.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening.

examples.text: Studio italiano tutto il pomeriggio.
examples.translation: I study Italian all afternoon.

faults.quote: Handuk is used for drying both the body and the hair
faults.why: Restates what a towel is and adds no linguistic value.

notes: A Dutch loanword (from 'handdoek'); do not confuse with 'saputangan' (handkerchief).

senses.definition: A piece of thick cloth used for drying the body or hair after washing or swimming.

examples.text: Dia melilitkan handuk di pinggangnya setelah mandi.
examples.translation: He wrapped a towel around his waist after taking a bath.

faults.quote: Having a temperature that is not too hot or too cold
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are both physical warmth ('warm'); lukewarm is 'suam-suam kuku'.
Missing the common figurative sense 'warm, friendly, cordial' (e.g., sambutan hangat).

faults.quote: Unlike 'panas' which can sometimes feel aggressive or excessive
faults.why: Repeats note 0 with vague filler.

notes: Use 'hangat' for pleasant warmth (like tea or mild weather), and 'panas' for things that are hot.

senses.definition: Having a comfortable, moderate level of heat; not too hot and not cold.

examples.text: Minumlah air hangat setiap pagi.
examples.translation: Drink warm water every morning.

senses.definition: Of a person, welcome, or atmosphere: friendly and affectionate.

examples.text: Mereka memberikan sambutan yang hangat kepada kami.
examples.translation: They gave us a warm welcome.

senses.definition: Of news or topics: very recent and still being talked about.

examples.text: Berita ini masih hangat.
examples.translation: This news is still fresh.

faults.quote: Harga is the standard word for the cost or price
faults.why: Simply restates the gloss and definition.

faults.quote: Kita harus menjaga harga diri kita.
faults.why: Uses the fixed compound 'harga diri' (self-esteem) instead of showing 'harga' meaning value/worth.

notes: Use 'harga' mainly for monetary price (and in 'harga diri', self-respect); for abstract value, worth, or a grade/score, use 'nilai'.

senses.definition: The amount of money required or given in payment for something.

examples.text: Berapa harga baju ini?
examples.translation: What is the price of this shirt?

senses.definition: The importance, worth, or respect that something or someone has, especially in set phrases like 'harga diri' (self-respect).

examples.text: Kita harus menjaga harga diri kita.
examples.translation: We must maintain our self-respect.

faults.quote: Hari is the general word for day, used for both
faults.why: Note 0 repeats the definition; note 1 contrasts words no learner would confuse.

notes: To name a day of the week, place 'hari' before the day's name: 'hari Senin' (Monday). Common compounds include 'hari ini' (today) and 'hari ulang tahun' (birthday).

senses.definition: A period of twenty-four hours, or the daylight part of it.

examples.text: Seminggu ada tujuh hari.
examples.translation: There are seven days in a week.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'ra' (ระ), which is a common prefix
faults.why: Bizarre confusion target; learners do not confuse เรือ with the prefix ระ.
Missing the essential classifier ลำ (lam) for boats and vehicles.

notes: Covers all watercraft from small boats to large ships. Its classifier is ลำ (lam).

senses.definition: A vehicle used for traveling on water.

examples.text: เรือลำนี้ใหญ่มาก
examples.translation: This boat is very big.

faults.quote: Thai uses the loanword 'ka-fae' which is universally understood.
faults.why: Uses ad-hoc romanization without Thai script for ร้อน and เย็น; misses common classifiers.

notes: When ordering, add ร้อน (hot) or เย็น (iced), e.g. กาแฟเย็น (iced coffee). Common classifiers are แก้ว (glass/cup) and ถ้วย (cup).

senses.definition: A hot or cold drink made from roasted coffee beans.

examples.text: ฉันอยากดื่มกาแฟร้อน
examples.translation: I want to drink hot coffee.

notes: Usually used with the verb เป็น (to be/have) as เป็นหวัด (to have a cold), or ติดหวัด (to catch a cold).

senses.definition: A common viral illness that causes a runny nose, sneezing, and sometimes a cough or sore throat.

examples.text: ฉันเป็นหวัดเลยจามทั้งวัน
examples.translation: I have a cold, so I have been sneezing all day.

faults.quote: star, asterisk
faults.why: ดาว means a star shape or rating star; 'asterisk' is ดอกจัน, not ดาว.

faults.quote: star; famous person; asterisk
faults.why: Includes 'asterisk', which is an inaccurate translation of ดาว.

faults.quote: Used metaphorically for a celebrity or a person with great talent
faults.why: Both notes merely restate senses 1 and 2 while omitting the classifier ดวง.

notes: The classifier for stars in the sky and star shapes is ดวง (duang). For movie or music stars, ดารา is even more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: A bright point of light in the night sky.

examples.text: คืนนี้มีดาวเต็มฟ้า
examples.translation: Tonight the sky is full of stars.

senses.definition: A five-pointed figure or symbol, often used for ratings or rank.

examples.text: โรงแรมนี้ได้ห้าดาว
examples.translation: This hotel got five stars.

senses.definition: A famous or talented person in entertainment, sports, or a group.

faults.quote: Used to identify people, objects, or places. In Thai, it is common
faults.why: Restates the definition and example using ad-hoc romanization instead of Thai script.

faults.quote: คุณชื่ออะไร
faults.why: Uses ชื่อ as a verb ('to be named') inside a noun-only entry without explanation.

notes: Also used directly as a verb meaning 'to be named', as in คุณชื่ออะไร (What is your name?).
In daily life, Thai people usually go by their ชื่อเล่น (nickname) rather than their formal given name (ชื่อจริง).

senses.definition: A word or set of words by which a person, place, or thing is known.

examples.text: ผมจำชื่อเขาไม่ได้
examples.translation: I cannot remember his name.

examples.text: คุณชื่ออะไรครับ
examples.translation: What is your name?

faults.quote: /kəːw/
faults.why: Wrong vowel and missing tone; Hanoi IPA for 'kéo' is /kɛw˧˦/.

faults.quote: Đừng kéo dài cuộc họp quá lâu.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'kéo dài' instead of the bare verb 'kéo'.

faults.quote: In some contexts, 'kéo' can also mean to lengthen or stretch
faults.why: Restates sense 1 without adding grammar or usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to pull; to drag; to stretch
notes: The opposite of 'kéo' (to pull) is 'đẩy' (to push). It is also a homonym of the noun 'kéo' (scissors).
Often combines with 'dài' (long) to form 'kéo dài' (to last, to prolong, to extend in time).

senses.definition: To apply force to something to move it towards you or along with you.

examples.text: Anh ấy kéo cái bàn lại gần.
examples.translation: He pulled the table closer.

senses.definition: To pull something out to its full length or make it taut.

examples.text: Họ đang kéo dây điện qua đường.
examples.translation: They are stretching an electric wire across the street.

faults.why: Southern pronunciation; northern (Hanoi) IPA for 'khách' is /xajk̟̚˧˦/.

faults.quote: In Vietnamese, the word 'khách' is versatile; it can refer to
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions and glosses of the two senses.

notes: Often used without a classifier when referring to guests or customers collectively (e.g., 'có khách' = to have guests, 'đông khách' = busy with customers). For an individual, use 'vị khách' (polite) or 'người khách'.

senses.definition: A person invited to a home or event, or visiting a place.

examples.text: Hôm nay nhà tôi có khách.
examples.translation: Today we have guests at home.

senses.definition: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or business.

examples.text: Cửa hàng đang rất đông khách.
examples.translation: The shop is very busy with customers right now.

faults.quote: /xajx ʂan/
faults.why: Invalid final consonant /x/, retroflex /ʂ/ is not Hanoi Vietnamese, and tones are missing.

notes: Do not confuse with 'nhà nghỉ', which refers to a simpler, cheaper motel or guesthouse.

senses.definition: A building where people pay for a room to sleep in when traveling.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đã đặt một phòng ở khách sạn gần biển.
examples.translation: We booked a room at a hotel near the beach.

faults.quote: here it is treated as a noun meaning the sensation of pain
faults.why: Restates the POS and glosses already shown in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'sehat', which means healthy.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion between dissimilar antonyms; not a helpful usage note.

notes: Most often used as an adjective ('sick', 'painful'). As a noun, it combines with body parts to name specific aches (e.g., 'sakit kepala' = headache, 'sakit gigi' = toothache).

senses.definition: An unpleasant physical feeling when a part of the body hurts.

examples.text: Dia merasakan sakit di punggungnya setelah mengangkat kotak itu.
examples.translation: He felt pain in his back after lifting the box.

senses.definition: A condition of poor health or disease.

examples.text: Sakitnya sudah sembuh setelah beristirahat beberapa hari.
examples.translation: His illness was cured after resting for a few days.

faults.quote: A small bag or container used for carrying items.
faults.why: Archaic or rare in modern Indonesian; 'saku' today means a clothing pocket.

faults.quote: Ibu membawa saku kecil untuk uang receh.
faults.why: Unnatural; a native speaker would say 'dompet kecil' or 'kantong kecil', not 'saku kecil'.

faults.quote: it is also used for a small bag or pouch.
faults.why: In modern usage 'saku' is a pocket; 'kantong' is the everyday synonym for pocket/bag.

notes: In everyday speech, 'kantong' is very often used instead of 'saku' for a pocket (as well as for bags and pouches). Placed after another noun, 'saku' means 'pocket-sized' (e.g., 'kamus saku' = pocket dictionary, 'uang saku' = pocket money).

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into or onto clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: Dia menyimpan kunci di dalam saku celananya.
examples.translation: He keeps his keys inside his pants pocket.

faults.quote: Saya suka makan salad segar untuk siang hari.
faults.why: 'Untuk siang hari' is a calque for 'for lunch'; natural Indonesian is 'untuk makan siang'.

faults.quote: Used mainly for vegetable or fruit dishes tossed in a dressing.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of salad.

notes: Refers to Western-style salads; traditional Indonesian vegetable dishes with dressing have their own names, such as 'gado-gado' or 'karedok'.

senses.definition: A dish of raw or cooked vegetables or fruit, usually served cold with a dressing.

examples.text: Saya suka makan salad segar untuk makan siang.
examples.translation: I like to eat a fresh salad for lunch.

faults.quote: Bukan salah saya.
faults.why: In 'Bukan salah saya', 'salah' is used as a noun ('my fault'), not an adjective.

notes: Also very common before a verb to mean 'do something by mistake' (e.g., 'salah beli' = buy the wrong thing, 'salah paham' = misunderstand), and in 'salah satu' ('one of').

senses.definition: Not correct or not true.

examples.text: Jawaban kamu salah.
examples.translation: Your answer is wrong.

senses.definition: Mistaken in judgment or responsible for an error or offense.

examples.text: Maaf, saya salah karena tidak memberi tahu kamu lebih awal.
examples.translation: Sorry, I was wrong not to tell you earlier.

faults.quote: Salju is an uncountable noun in Indonesian, representing the substance.
faults.why: Indonesian does not grammatically distinguish countable and uncountable nouns like English does.

notes: To say 'it is snowing', Indonesian uses 'turun salju' or 'salju turun' (literally 'snow falls').

senses.definition: Soft white bits of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather.

examples.text: Salju turun dengan sangat lebat di gunung pagi ini.
examples.translation: Snow is falling very heavily on the mountain this morning.

faults.quote: /jeˈtiʃcin/
faults.why: Word-final stress in standard Turkish: /jetiʃˈcin/.

faults.quote: While 'büyük' can mean 'adult' in the sense of 'the grown-ups
faults.why: Repeats the exact point made in note 0.

notes: Also used as an adjective ('adult'). More neutral or formal than 'büyük' (literally 'big'), which is used colloquially for 'grown-up' (especially in the plural, 'büyükler').

senses.definition: A person who is fully grown and no longer a child.

examples.text: Bu film sadece yetişkinler içindir.
examples.translation: This movie is for adults only.

faults.quote: To wash one's hair or body during a bath or shower.
faults.why: Washing hands/hair and washing objects are a single sense of 'yıkamak'.
Should mention the reflexive 'yıkanmak' (to wash oneself / take a shower), which learners need.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case (e.g., 'arabayı yıkamak' – to wash the car, 'ellerini yıkamak' – to wash one's hands).
To say 'to wash oneself', 'to bathe', or 'to take a shower', use the reflexive form 'yıkanmak'.

senses.definition: To clean something, or a part of the body, with water and usually soap.

examples.text: Yemekten önce ellerini yıkamalısın.
examples.translation: You should wash your hands before eating.

examples.text: Babam hafta sonu arabayı yıkadı.
examples.translation: My father washed the car on the weekend.

faults.quote: In Turkish culture, the yılan is often a symbol of both danger
faults.why: Generic cultural trivia, not useful linguistic advice for a beginner.

notes: Do not confuse with 'yalan' (lie); 'yılan' begins with the undotted 'ı' (/ɯ/).

senses.definition: A long, legless reptile that slides along the ground.

examples.text: Yılan çimlerin arasında hızla gözden kayboldu.
examples.translation: The snake quickly disappeared into the grass.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a large building or institution for medical care.
faults.why: Restates the definition and adds filler.

notes: Do not confuse with 'ιατρείο' (doctor's office or small clinic).

senses.definition: A large building where doctors and nurses treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: Πρέπει να πάμε στο νοσοκομείο αμέσως.
examples.translation: We must go to the hospital immediately.

faults.quote: is a neuter noun, so it is always preceded by 'το'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and falsely claims it is always preceded by 'το'.

notes: In Greek, both a countable serving ('ένα παγωτό') and the food in general ('τρώω παγωτό') use the same word; a scoop is 'μια μπάλα παγωτό'.

senses.definition: A frozen sweet food made from milk, cream, and sugar.

examples.text: Θέλω ένα παγωτό σοκολάτα.
examples.translation: I want a chocolate ice cream.

examples.text: Το καλοκαίρι τρώμε συχνά παγωτό.
examples.translation: In the summer we often eat ice cream.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, where you might say 'it is winter', in Greek
faults.why: Claims contrast with English where the structure ('είναι χειμώνας' = 'it is winter') is identical.

notes: To say 'in (the) winter', Greek uses the accusative with the definite article and no preposition: 'τον χειμώνα'.

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.

examples.text: Ο χειμώνας στην Ελλάδα είναι συνήθως ήπιος.
examples.translation: Winter in Greece is usually mild.

notes: Most often used in the plural, 'τα λαχανικά', to refer to vegetables in general.

senses.definition: A plant or part of a plant used as food, such as a potato, carrot, or cabbage.

examples.text: Πρέπει να τρώμε φρέσκα λαχανικά κάθε μέρα.
examples.translation: We must eat fresh vegetables every day.

faults.quote: Used for both the floor of a room and a floor or storey
faults.why: Simply restates the two senses; should instead contrast with 'όροφος' for storey.

senses.definition: The lower surface of a room that you walk on.

examples.text: Τα παιδιά παίζουν στο πάτωμα.
examples.translation: The children are playing on the floor.

senses.definition: A level of a building.

examples.text: Μένουμε στο ίδιο πάτωμα.
examples.translation: We live on the same floor.

faults.quote: Used with Asian dishes such as noodles and rice meals.
faults.why: World knowledge filler; misses the classifiers คู่ (for a pair) and ข้าง (for one).

notes: Counted with คู่ (pair) for a pair of chopsticks, or ข้าง for a single stick.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used for eating.

examples.text: ฉันใช้ตะเกียบกินก๋วยเตี๋ยว
examples.translation: I use chopsticks to eat noodles.

examples.text: Preciso limpar o vaso sanitário hoje.

examples.translation: She bought a blue dress for the party.

examples.translation: He was hired immediately because his record is clean.

examples.translation: My parents are going to their hometown this weekend.

faults.why: Trivial contrast with 'rain' and 'wind'; comparing with 태풍 (typhoon) or 폭풍우 is useful.

examples.translation: I put a coin into the vending machine and bought a drink.

faults.quote: To no longer want to do or be around something

senses.definition: Weary or impatient with something that has become repetitive or annoying.

examples.text: เขาเบื่อการทำงานหนักทุกวัน

examples.text: ส้มตำจานนี้เผ็ดมาก
examples.translation: This papaya salad is very spicy.

faults.quote: Use 'ยาว' for physical length (like a ruler or a snake)

examples.text: งูตัวนี้ยาวมาก
examples.translation: This snake is very long.

senses.definition: Lasting or continuing for a great amount of time.

examples.text: เราคุยกันยาวเลย
examples.translation: We talked for a long time.

senses.definition: A large, heavy wild mammal with thick fur.

examples.text: Los osos hibernan durante el invierno.
examples.translation: Bears hibernate during the winter.

senses.definition: The season between summer and winter, when temperatures cool and leaves fall.

examples.translation: In autumn, the leaves on the trees change color and fall.

senses.definition: (usually in the plural) A person's mother and father.

examples.text: Los padres deben cuidar a sus hijos.
examples.translation: Parents must take care of their children.

examples.text: Essa nova dança virou uma febre no país inteiro.
examples.translation: This new dance became a craze all over the country.

senses.definition: A line of people or vehicles waiting for their turn.

examples.translation: The line for the register is very long.

senses.definition: The colored part of a plant that produces seeds or fruit.

examples.text: Comprei flores para colocar na sala.
examples.translation: I bought flowers to put in the living room.

faults.quote: Do not confuse vino with vine (the plant is called la vid

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

examples.text: Pedimos una botella de vino tinto para la cena.
examples.translation: We ordered a bottle of red wine for dinner.

faults.quote: Use 'zapato' for ordinary shoes, sneakers, and dress shoes.

senses.definition: A covering for the foot, usually made of leather or a firm material, that does not go above the ankle.

examples.text: Me compré unos zapatos nuevos para la boda.
examples.translation: I bought some new shoes for the wedding.

faults.quote: Think of 'elegir' as the act of picking the best option
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful linguistic information.

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want out of several options.

examples.text: Es difícil elegir solo un postre de este menú.
examples.translation: It is hard to choose only one dessert from this menu.

senses.definition: To choose someone for an official position by voting.

examples.text: Los ciudadanos deben elegir a su representante.
examples.translation: The citizens must elect their representative.

faults.quote: เขาวางแผนการเดินทาง — He is laying down a travel plan.
faults.why: Example means 'to draw up a plan', contradicting the sense 'to abandon or put aside'.

faults.quote: วาง (waang) is the most common way to say 'put' or 'place'
faults.why: Restates the glosses and definition of sense 0.

corrected.shortGloss: to place; to put down; to set
notes: Do not confuse with ใส่ (sài), which is used for putting things into a container or putting on clothes and accessories.
Often used in everyday compounds like วางแผน (waang-phǎen, 'to plan') and วางสาย (waang-sǎai, 'to hang up the phone').

senses.definition: To put or set something down on a surface.

examples.text: เขาวางหนังสือบนโต๊ะ
examples.translation: He placed the book on the table.

senses.definition: To set up, arrange, or lay out something, such as a plan or a system.

examples.text: เขากำลังวางแผนการเดินทาง
examples.translation: He is laying out a travel plan.

faults.quote: Thai distinguishes between 'sleeping' and 'lying down' using the same word, นอน.

notes: นอน covers both lying down and sleeping. To specify actually being asleep rather than just lying in bed, use นอนหลับ (nɔɔn-làp).

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed, especially at night.

examples.text: ฉันอยากนอนแล้ว
examples.translation: I want to go to sleep now.

senses.definition: To be in or move into a flat, horizontal position on a surface.

examples.text: เขานอนอ่านหนังสืออยู่บนโซฟา
examples.translation: He is lying on the sofa reading a book.

faults.quote: ซ่อม is used for repairing physical objects like cars, electronics, or shoes
faults.why: Restates the definition; can be merged into the contrast note with แก้ไข.

corrected.shortGloss: to repair; to fix; to mend
notes: Used for physical objects like cars, machines, or buildings. To 'fix' abstract things like problems, mistakes, or documents, use แก้ (gâe) or แก้ไข (gâe-khǎi).

senses.definition: To put something damaged, broken, or not working back into good condition.

examples.text: ช่างกำลังซ่อมรถยนต์ของฉันอยู่
examples.translation: The mechanic is repairing my car.

faults.quote: Thai speakers often repeat this word to show an extended period

faults.quote: stay for

notes: Takes a direct object without a preposition: รอฉัน (rɔɔ chǎn, 'wait for me').

senses.definition: To stay in a place or delay doing something until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: ฉันรอคุณอยู่ที่ร้านอาหาร

examples.text: เราต้องรอจนกว่าฝนจะหยุด
examples.translation: We have to wait until the rain stops.

faults.quote: This word has two completely unrelated meanings
faults.why: Restates the senses; should give useful classifier info ('con' for road) instead.

examples.text: Con đường này dẫn ra trung tâm thành phố.
examples.translation: This road leads to the city center.

senses.definition: A sweet substance made from plants, used to flavor food and drinks.

examples.text: Cho tôi thêm một ít đường vào cà phê.

examples.text: Bạn phải uống thuốc này sau khi ăn.

faults.quote: (damp) Slightly wet or damp, often referring to weather, hair
faults.why: 'ướt' simply means wet; slightly damp is 'ẩm', not a separate sense of 'ướt'.

notes: Opposite of 'khô' (dry). For something slightly damp or humid, use 'ẩm'.

examples.text: Áo của tôi đã ướt hết vì trời mưa.
examples.translation: My shirt is completely wet because of the rain.

examples.text: Tóc cô ấy còn ướt sau khi gội đầu.

examples.text: เขาสวมแหวนที่นิ้วมือ
examples.translation: He wears a ring on his finger.

examples.translation: My dog likes to run around in the garden.

faults.quote: /t͡ɕat̚˨˩.tu˨˩.rat̚˦˥/

senses.definition: An open public area in a town or city, usually surrounded by buildings.

examples.text: ผู้คนมารวมตัวกันที่จัตุรัสกลางเมือง
examples.translation: People gather at the town square.

examples.text: วาดรูปสี่เหลี่ยมจัตุรัสลงในกระดาษ

senses.definition: A person whom one does not know.

examples.text: किसी अजनबी से बात मत करो।

faults.why: Restates the two senses; missing the irregular feminine form 'jalouse' and preposition 'de'.

examples.translation: She is a little jealous when he talks with his colleagues.

examples.text: Ik draag vandaag een blauw T-shirt.
examples.translation: I am wearing a blue T-shirt today.

faults.quote: toilet; restroom; dressing

senses.definition: A small room with a toilet bowl, or a public restroom.

examples.text: Waar is het toilet?
examples.translation: Where is the toilet?

senses.definition: The bowl and seat used for getting rid of bodily waste.

examples.text: Maak het toilet goed schoon na gebruik.
