examples.text: Les enfants vont à l'école tous les matins.
examples.translation: The children go to school every morning.

faults.quote: Do not use 'de' or just the direct object.
faults.why: False for Mexican Spanish, where 'jugar fútbol' (without 'a') is the most common form.
Missing two vital A1/A2 points: stem change (u > ue) and 'tocar' for musical instruments.

faults.quote: to play (game/sport); to participate
faults.why: Sense 2 is 'to gamble/bet', not 'to participate'.

notes: Stem-changing verb (u → ue) in the present tense: juego, juegas, juega, juegan.
In Mexico, sports are played with or without 'a' (jugar fútbol / jugar al fútbol). For musical instruments, use 'tocar', not 'jugar'.

senses.definition: To take part in a game or sport.

examples.text: Ellos juegan fútbol los sábados por la tarde.
examples.translation: They play soccer on Saturday afternoons.

senses.definition: To spend time doing something for fun, especially with toys.

examples.text: Los niños juegan con bloques en el suelo.
examples.translation: The children play with blocks on the floor.

senses.definition: To bet money on a game of chance or a lottery.

examples.text: Mucha gente juega a la lotería en diciembre.
examples.translation: Many people play the lottery in December.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the mother of one's father or mother.
faults.why: Restates the definition verbatim.

faults.quote: Often shortened to the affectionate form 'abuelita'.
faults.why: 'Abuelita' is a longer diminutive suffix form, not a shortened form ('abue' is shortened).

notes: In Mexico, the affectionate diminutive 'abuelita' or the shortened form 'abue' are very common.

senses.definition: The mother of your father or mother.

examples.text: Mi abuela prepara la mejor sopa de pollo.
examples.translation: My grandmother makes the best chicken soup.

faults.quote: /alˈmo.a.ða/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'almohada' is stressed on the penult (/almoˈaða/), not on '-mo-'.

notes: An 'almohada' is for sleeping in bed, whereas a 'cojín' is a cushion for a sofa or chair. The 'h' is silent.

senses.definition: A soft cushion you rest your head on while sleeping in bed.

examples.text: Puse la cabeza sobre la almohada y me quedé dormido de inmediato.
examples.translation: I put my head on the pillow and fell asleep immediately.

faults.quote: In many Spanish-speaking countries, especially in Mexico and the Caribbean, this word
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1; in Mexico 'candil' or 'candelabro' is actually more common for chandelier.

notes: For 'chandelier', 'el candil' or 'el candelabro' is more common in Mexico.

senses.definition: A small creature with eight legs that spins webs to catch insects.

examples.text: Vi una araña grande en la esquina del cuarto.
examples.translation: I saw a big spider in the corner of the room.

senses.definition: A decorative light fixture hanging from the ceiling with several branches.

examples.text: La araña de cristal ilumina todo el comedor.
examples.translation: The crystal chandelier lights up the whole dining room.

faults.quote: nickname for someone who is sneaky or quiet, similar to how 'catty'
faults.why: 'แมว' is a common pet name without sneaky connotations, and English 'catty' means spiteful.
For a Thai noun at A1/A2, the classifier (ตัว) is essential.

notes: The classifier for cats and other animals is ตัว (tua), e.g., แมวสองตัว (two cats).

senses.definition: A small furry animal often kept as a pet.

examples.text: ฉันชอบเล่นกับแมวที่บ้าน
examples.translation: I like playing with the cat at home.

faults.why: Wrong tone on second syllable: องุ่น has low tone on both syllables (/ʔa˨˩.ŋun˨˩/).

faults.quote: องุ่น is used for both the fresh fruit eaten as a snack
faults.why: Restates what English 'grape' already means; better to give the Thai classifiers.

notes: Counted using ลูก (lûuk) or เม็ด (mét) for individual grapes, and พวง (phuang) for a bunch of grapes.

senses.definition: A small, round purple or green fruit that grows in bunches on a vine.

examples.text: ฉันชอบกินองุ่นสีม่วงมากกว่าสีเขียว
examples.translation: I like eating purple grapes more than green ones.

faults.quote: /kìat/
faults.why: Missing the consonant cluster /kl/ and vowel length: เกลียด is pronounced /klìːat/ (/kliːat̚˨˩/).

notes: Stronger than ไม่ชอบ (mâi chôop, 'to dislike'), though also used casually for things like foods or weather.

senses.definition: To dislike someone or something very much.

examples.text: ฉันเกลียดคนโกหก
examples.translation: I hate liars.

examples.text: เขาเกลียดอากาศร้อน
examples.translation: He hates hot weather.

faults.quote: It is similar to 'to want' but carries more of an emotional
faults.why: Explains the English concept of 'hope' rather than Thai usage.

notes: Usually followed by ว่า (wâa, 'that') before a clause: หวังว่า... (to hope that...).

senses.definition: To want something to happen and think that it is possible.

examples.text: ฉันหวังว่าฝนจะไม่ตกวันนี้
examples.translation: I hope it won't rain today.

examples.text: เขาหวังว่าจะได้งานทำเร็วๆ นี้
examples.translation: He hopes to get a job soon.

faults.quote: /chuaj˥˩/
faults.why: Invalid IPA symbol 'ch' (should be /t͡ɕʰ/) and missing vowel length (/t͡ɕʰuːaj˥˩/).

faults.quote: ฉันช่วยเธอยกของหน่อย
faults.why: Adding request particle หน่อย to 'I help you' is unidiomatic; needs ให้ (let me) or drop หน่อย.
Senses 0 and 1 are both 'to help'; meanwhile the everyday request sense ('please') is missing.

faults.quote: before another action to mean 'please do' (e.g., ช่วยด้วย - help!)
faults.why: 'ช่วยด้วย' has no second verb and means 'Help!', not 'please do'.

notes: The exclamation ช่วยด้วย! (chûai dûai!) means 'Help!' in an emergency.
ช่วยเหลือ (chûai-lǔea) is a more formal word for providing aid or assistance.

senses.definition: To make it easier for someone to do something, or to make something easier.

examples.text: เดี๋ยวฉันช่วยยกของนะ
examples.translation: Let me help you carry your things.

examples.text: วิธีนี้ช่วยให้ทำงานเร็วขึ้น
examples.translation: This method helps make the work faster.

senses.definition: Used before a verb (often with หน่อย at the end) to politely ask someone to do something.

examples.text: ช่วยเปิดประตูให้หน่อย
examples.translation: Please open the door for me.

faults.why: Headword is kana せき; missing the very common everyday sense 'seat' (席).

faults.quote: When used as a verb, it becomes 咳をする
faults.why: Standard usage is 咳が出る; 咳をする is mainly for deliberate coughing.

notes: Written 席 for 'seat' (pitch: se↓ki) and 咳 for 'cough' (pitch: seki↑).
For coughing, use せきが出る (a cough comes out); せきをする means to cough deliberately.

senses.definition: A place to sit, such as a chair in a room, train, or theater.

examples.text: どうぞ、せきにおつきください。
examples.translation: Please take your seat.

senses.definition: The act or sound of pushing air out of the throat, often from illness.

examples.text: きのうからせきが止まりません。
examples.translation: My cough hasn't stopped since yesterday.

faults.quote: A large farm tool with long metal prongs
faults.why: 'Pitchfork' is a rare meaning for A2 learners; utensil is the everyday sense.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'hōku' (hook)
faults.why: 'Hook' in Japanese is フック (fukku), not hōku.

faults.quote: Used as a loanword from English, referring to both
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and obvious katakana origin.

senses.definition: A small tool with several thin points used for picking up and eating food.

examples.text: フォークでパスタを食べる。
examples.translation: I eat pasta with a fork.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading あかちゃん for headword containing kanji.

faults.quote: Avoid using '子' (ko) for a baby
faults.why: Unnecessary advice; この子 or 赤ん坊 are more relevant.

notes: Can be used for both human babies and newborn animals. A slightly more casual synonym for a human baby is 赤ん坊 (あかんぼう).

senses.definition: A very young child or newborn animal.

examples.text: 赤ちゃんが眠っています。
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping.

faults.quote: A person who is shy, cowardly, or likes to hide away; or a common computing input device.
faults.why: Hallucinated English senses; computer mouse is マウス, and ネズミ does not mean coward.

faults.quote: パソコンのネズミを動かす。
faults.why: Completely unnatural; a computer mouse is always called マウス in Japanese.

faults.quote: in biology or formal contexts, it is written with the kanji 鼠
faults.why: In biology, animal names are standardly written in katakana (ネズミ), not kanji.

notes: Covers both 'mouse' and 'rat'. To specify, use ハツカネズミ for a small mouse or ドブネズミ for a large rat.
Often written in katakana (ネズミ) or hiragana (ねずみ); the kanji is 鼠.

senses.definition: A small rodent with a pointed snout, round ears, and a long thin tail.

examples.text: 家の中にネズミがいる。
examples.translation: There is a mouse in the house.

faults.quote: costoso sounds slightly more formal or literary.
faults.why: 'Costoso' is completely normal in everyday speech, not literary; 'caro' also means 'dear'.

notes: The everyday synonym 'caro' is also very common, though 'caro' can also mean 'dear' or 'beloved'.

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: Questo ristorante è troppo costoso per noi.
examples.translation: This restaurant is too expensive for us.

faults.quote: [0] (build) To build... [1] (create) To make something by joining...
faults.why: Both senses and examples mean 'to build/construct' by putting parts together.

notes: Takes '-isc-' in most present forms: 'costruisco, costruisci, costruisce, costruiamo, costruite, costruiscono'. Past participle: 'costruito'.

senses.definition: To make a building, structure, or object by putting parts or materials together.

examples.text: Vogliono costruire una nuova scuola nel quartiere.
examples.translation: They want to build a new school in the neighborhood.

examples.text: Il bambino costruisce un castello con le scatole.
examples.translation: The child is building a castle with the boxes.

faults.quote: Use cucinare when talking about preparing food in general
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; should contrast with 'cuocere' or note stress in 'cucino'.

notes: Used for preparing meals (both transitive and intransitive). For the physical process of food cooking or baking, 'cuocere' is also common.

senses.definition: To prepare food or a meal by heating it.

examples.text: Mi piace cucinare per la mia famiglia.
examples.translation: I like cooking for my family.

examples.text: Stasera cucino la pasta.
examples.translation: Tonight I'm cooking pasta.

faults.quote: to give; to hit; to turn
faults.why: 'To turn' is not in the senses; sense 2 is 'to face / look out onto'.

faults.quote: Dare is one of the most common irregular verbs in Italian.
faults.why: Calls the verb irregular without giving the learner any of its irregular forms.

faults.quote: Attento a non dare la testa contro la porta.
faults.why: 'Sbattere la testa' is normal for bumping one's head; 'dare una festa/un esame' is much more useful.

corrected.shortGloss: to give; to hold; to look out onto
notes: Irregular present tense: 'do, dai, dà, diamo, date, danno' (note the accent on 'dà'). Past participle: 'dato'.

senses.definition: To hand or transfer something to someone.

examples.text: Mi puoi dare il sale, per favore?
examples.translation: Can you pass me the salt, please?

senses.definition: To host an event, or to sit an exam (especially at university).

examples.text: Sabato prossimo diamo una festa.
examples.translation: Next Saturday we are throwing a party.

senses.definition: Of a room, window, or building: to face or overlook a place (with 'su').

examples.text: La mia camera dà sul giardino.
examples.translation: My bedroom looks out onto the garden.

faults.quote: Tetapi is the standard conjunction used to connect two contrasting clauses
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful information.

notes: In everyday conversation and informal writing, 'tetapi' is very often shortened to 'tapi'.

senses.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what was just said.

examples.text: Saya ingin pergi, tetapi hari sedang hujan.
examples.translation: I want to go, but it is raining.

faults.quote: (suddenly) Happening without warning or expectation.
faults.why: Single 'tiba' does not mean 'suddenly'; only the reduplicated form 'tiba-tiba' does.

faults.quote: Hujan turun tiba tanpa disangka.
faults.why: Ungrammatical in Indonesian; requires 'tiba-tiba' to mean 'suddenly'.

faults.quote: to arrive; suddenly
faults.why: Includes the false meaning 'suddenly'.

notes: Often followed by the preposition 'di' to indicate the destination (e.g., 'tiba di rumah').
Slightly more formal than 'datang' or 'sampai', which are more common in casual speech.

senses.definition: To reach a place at the end of a journey.

examples.text: Kami tiba di stasiun tepat waktu.
examples.translation: We arrived at the station on time.

faults.why: Missing note on common spoken forms like 'nggak' or 'tak' and contrast with 'belum'.

notes: Used to negate verbs and adjectives; to negate nouns, use 'bukan' instead.
If an action has not happened yet but might in the future, use 'belum' rather than 'tidak'.
In casual speech, it is very often replaced by 'nggak', 'enggak', or 'gak'.

senses.definition: Used before verbs, adjectives, and adverbs to make them negative.

examples.text: Rumah itu tidak besar.
examples.translation: That house is not big.

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer or reply.

examples.text: Tidak, saya mau minum air saja.
examples.translation: No, I just want to drink water.

faults.quote: Used to express that an action has not occurred at any time in the past.
faults.why: False restriction to the past; 'tidak pernah' is also used for present habits (as shown in the examples) and the future.

notes: Do not confuse with 'belum pernah', which is used when you have not done something yet (e.g., 'Have you ever...? — Not yet.').

senses.definition: At no time in the past, present, or future; not on any occasion.

examples.text: Saya tidak pernah makan makanan pedas.
examples.translation: I never eat spicy food.

examples.text: Dia tidak pernah datang terlambat ke sekolah.
examples.translation: He never comes late to school.

faults.quote: (rest) To rest with your eyes closed without necessarily falling into deep sleep.
faults.why: Artificial split; 'tidur sebentar' simply means to take a short nap, which is still sleeping.

faults.quote: Use 'tidur' for ordinary nighttime sleep as well as resting with your eyes closed.
faults.why: merely repeats the definitions.

notes: Can mean both 'to be asleep' and 'to go to sleep' depending on context.
Do not confuse with 'istirahat', which means to rest or take a break without sleeping.

senses.definition: To rest your body and mind with your eyes closed in a natural state of unconsciousness.

examples.text: Anak itu sudah tidur di kamarnya.
examples.translation: That child is already asleep in their room.

examples.text: Dia duduk di kursi dan tidur sebentar.
examples.translation: She sat in the chair and slept for a moment.

faults.quote: (clothing) The part of a piece of clothing that covers the arm.
faults.why: 'Brazo' does not mean 'sleeve' (which is 'manga', as the example itself shows).

faults.quote: Se manchó la manga de la camisa en el brazo.
faults.why: Uses 'manga' for sleeve and 'brazo' for the body part.

faults.quote: Refers specifically to the upper limb from the shoulder to the hand.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of sense 0.

notes: For the whole limb (arm and hand together), anatomy and formal contexts use 'miembro superior', while everyday speech distinguishes 'brazo' (shoulder to wrist) from 'mano' (hand).

senses.definition: The limb of the human body that extends from the shoulder to the hand.

examples.text: Levantó el brazo para saludar a sus amigos.
examples.translation: He raised his arm to greet his friends.

senses.definition: The side part of a chair or sofa on which you rest your arm.

examples.text: Se sentó en el brazo del sillón.
examples.translation: He sat on the arm of the armchair.

faults.quote: In Mexico, the word 'caballo' is used for the animal in
faults.why: Pure filler; 'caballo' means horse everywhere and learners won't confuse it with 'caballete'.

notes: The female is 'la yegua' (mare). Note the common phrase 'a caballo' (on horseback, without an article).

senses.definition: A large four-legged animal that people ride and use for pulling or carrying things.

examples.text: Montar a caballo es muy relajante.
examples.translation: Riding a horse is very relaxing.

faults.why: In Mexico, 'café' is the standard everyday word for the color brown.

faults.quote: In Spanish, 'café' refers both to the drink itself and to
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: In Mexico, 'café' is also the standard adjective and noun for the color brown (instead of 'marrón'): 'ojos cafés' (brown eyes).

senses.definition: A hot, dark drink made from the roasted seeds of a tropical plant, or the seeds and powder themselves.

examples.text: Me gusta tomar un café por la mañana.
examples.translation: I like to have a coffee in the morning.

senses.definition: A small restaurant where coffee, drinks, and light meals are served.

examples.text: Nos vemos en el café de la esquina.
examples.translation: Let's meet at the café on the corner.

senses.definition: The dark color of coffee or wood.

examples.text: El café es un color muy fácil de combinar.
examples.translation: Brown is a very easy color to match.

faults.quote: In Spain and many other Spanish-speaking countries, the plural is 'calcetines'.
faults.why: Misleadingly implies Mexico doesn't use 'calcetines'; it is the plural everywhere.

notes: Plural: 'los calcetines' (loses the written accent). In Mexico, 'calcetas' is also used, especially for thicker or knee-high athletic socks, while 'medias' usually means stockings or tights.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing that covers the foot and ankle, worn inside a shoe.

examples.text: No encuentro el otro calcetín negro.
examples.translation: I can't find the other black sock.

faults.why: Chart of dates and system of dividing the year are one everyday sense ('calendar').

faults.quote: Use 'el calendario' for the system of measuring time or the
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions without adding useful learner information.

senses.definition: A chart, app, or system that shows the days, weeks, and months of the year.

examples.text: Marqué en el calendario el día en que empieza el viaje.
examples.translation: I marked the day the trip starts on the calendar.

senses.definition: A planned list of dates for events, classes, or payments over a period of time.

examples.text: Ya publicaron el calendario escolar del próximo año.
examples.translation: They already published next year's school calendar.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with kahvaltı, which is breakfast.
faults.why: No learner confuses 'öğle yemeği' with 'kahvaltı'; they look and sound completely different.
Needs a note on the buffer letter -n- before case suffixes (e.g. öğle yemeğinde).

notes: Formed from 'öğle' (noon) and 'yemek' (meal, food).
Because it ends in the possessive suffix '-i', add the buffer letter '-n-' before case endings (e.g., 'öğle yemeğinde' – at lunch).

senses.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

examples.text: Öğle yemeği için ne yiyeceğiz?
examples.translation: What are we going to eat for lunch?

faults.quote: /œːleˈden soɾˈna/
faults.why: 'sonra' is spelled and standardly pronounced with /nɾ/, not metathesized /ɾn/, and stressed initially.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, you do not use 'saat' before the time
faults.why: English does not use 'o'clock' before 'in the afternoon' either; confusing explanation.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'sabah', which means morning.
faults.why: Unrelated word forms that learners will not confuse.

notes: Literally 'after noon' ('öğle' = noon, '-den' = from, 'sonra' = after).
Used both as a noun ('afternoon') and directly as an adverb ('in the afternoon') without adding a case suffix.

senses.definition: The part of the day from noon until evening, or during this time.

examples.text: Öğleden sonra kahve içmek istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to drink coffee in the afternoon.

faults.quote: with the suffix '-ci', which denotes a profession or habitual doer.
faults.why: False morphology: '-ci' attaches to nouns, not verbs; 'öğrenci' uses the deverbal suffix '-(y)ici'.

faults.quote: Üniversitede her yıl binlerce yeni öğrenci kayıt yaptırıyor.
faults.why: 'kayıt yaptırmak' takes the dative ('üniversiteye'), not the locative ('üniversitede').

notes: Formed from the verb 'öğrenmek' (to learn).

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a school, university, or other place of education.

examples.text: Üniversiteye her yıl binlerce yeni öğrenci kayıt yaptırıyor.
examples.translation: Thousands of new students register at the university every year.

faults.quote: Use 'öğrenmek' when you acquire new knowledge or a skill.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of the first sense.

notes: Do not confuse with 'öğretmek' (to teach) or 'okumak' (to read, to study at a school/university).

senses.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill through study, practice, or being taught.

examples.text: Yeni bir dil öğrenmek zaman alır.
examples.translation: Learning a new language takes time.

senses.definition: To find out or come to know information by hearing or asking.

examples.text: Bu haberi bugün öğrendim.
examples.translation: I found out about this news today.

faults.quote: To show someone how something is done or how to behave.
faults.why: Showing someone how something works via 'öğretmek' is just teaching them; 'show' is 'göstermek'.

notes: Takes the dative case (-e/-a) for the person being taught, and the accusative case (-i/-ı) for the definite thing or skill taught.
Do not confuse with 'öğrenmek' (to learn).

senses.definition: To give someone knowledge or train them in a skill so that they learn how to do something.

examples.text: Annem bana yemek yapmayı öğretmek istiyor.
examples.translation: My mother wants to teach me how to cook.

faults.quote: Derived from the passive past participle of the verb удивлять (to surprise).
faults.why: Derived from perfective удивить, not imperfective удивлять.
Should note that short form удивлён (-ена, -ены) is standard when used as a predicate.

notes: In sentences like 'I am surprised', use the short form: удивлён (m), удивлена (f), удивлены (pl), followed by the instrumental case (Он удивлён новостью — He is surprised by the news).

senses.definition: Feeling or showing surprise because something unexpected has happened.

examples.text: Он посмотрел на меня удивлёнными глазами.
examples.translation: He looked at me with surprised eyes.

faults.quote: [0] (age) Having lived or existed... [1] (condition) Not new; used...
faults.why: 'Existed for a long time' and 'not new' are one core sense; 'former/previous' is missing.
Missing the everyday sense 'former, previous' or 'long-standing' (старый друг, старый адрес).

faults.quote: old; aged; antique
faults.why: 'Antique' is not in the senses and usually translates as старинный or антикварный.

notes: When speaking about people, пожилой (elderly) is more polite and respectful than старый.
Comparative form: старше (older, for age) or старее (older, for things).

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time; not new or young.

examples.text: Мы живём в старом доме.
examples.translation: We live in an old house.

examples.text: Она надела свой старый свитер.
examples.translation: She put on her old sweater.

senses.definition: Known for a long time, or dating from an earlier period; former.

examples.text: Вчера я встретил старого друга.
examples.translation: Yesterday I met an old friend.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the deep sea.
faults.why: Defined as a noun ('The colour of...'); Also, clear daytime sky is голубой, not синий.

notes: Russian divides English 'blue' into two distinct basic colours: синий (medium to dark blue) and голубой (light blue, sky blue).

senses.definition: Having the colour of the deep sea or the evening sky; medium to dark blue.

examples.text: На ней было красивое синее платье.
examples.translation: She was wearing a beautiful blue dress.

faults.quote: Used for physical objects that yield to pressure, as well as...
faults.why: Merely restates the senses while omitting the irregular pronunciation of 'гк' as [xʲkʲ].
Needs a pronunciation note: the cluster 'гк' is pronounced [xʲkʲ], like 'хк'.

notes: The letter combination гк is pronounced like хк (/xʲkʲ/).
Also used in grammar for 'soft' (palatalized) consonants and the soft sign (мягкий знак: ь).

senses.definition: Not hard or firm; easy to press and pleasant to touch.

examples.text: Этот диван очень мягкий и удобный.
examples.translation: This sofa is very soft and comfortable.

senses.definition: Not harsh, severe, or extreme; gentle in character, climate, or effect.

examples.text: У него очень мягкий характер.
examples.translation: He has a very gentle character.

examples.text: Зима в этом году была мягкой.
examples.translation: The winter was mild this year.

faults.quote: Takes short forms: жёлт, жёлта, жёлто, жёлты.
faults.why: The feminine short form is желта́ (stressed ending, with е), and short forms are rare.

faults.quote: Often used to describe autumn leaves, lemons, and the sun.
faults.why: Pure filler; obvious from the meaning 'yellow' and the definition.

notes: Spelled with ё (after ж) eventhough it is pronounced like a hard о.

senses.definition: Having the colour of gold, butter, or a ripe lemon.

examples.text: У неё жёлтый зонт.
examples.translation: She has a yellow umbrella.

examples.text: Осенью листья становятся жёлтыми.
examples.translation: In autumn, the leaves turn yellow.

faults.quote: Thai distinguishes between clouds (เมฆ) and fog or mist (หมอก).
faults.why: English also distinguishes cloud and fog; missing classifier note (ก้อน) and silent final consonant warning.

notes: The final consonant ฆ is pronounced as an unreleased /k/ sound. The classifier for individual clouds is ก้อน (kɔ̂ːn).

senses.definition: A white or grey mass of water droplets floating in the sky.

examples.text: ท้องฟ้าวันนี้มีเมฆมาก
examples.translation: There are many clouds in the sky today.

faults.quote: /nɔ́ŋ saːw/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and wrong tone on second syllable: should be /nɔ́ːŋ sǎːw/.

faults.quote: น้องสาว refers specifically to a younger sister.
faults.why: Restates the gloss instead of giving the classifier (คน) or broader usage.

notes: Composed of น้อง (younger sibling) + สาว (young woman). Contrast with พี่สาว (older sister). The classifier is คน.

senses.definition: A female sibling who is younger than the speaker.

examples.text: ฉันมีน้องสาวหนึ่งคน
examples.translation: I have one younger sister.

notes: Composed of น้อง (younger sibling) + ชาย (male). Contrast with พี่ชาย (older brother). The classifier is คน.

senses.definition: A male sibling who is younger than the speaker.

examples.text: น้องชายของฉันกำลังเรียนมหาวิทยาลัย
examples.translation: My younger brother is attending university.

faults.quote: (care) To look after, nurse, or tend to someone
faults.why: Entry POS is noun, but sense 1 is a verb (and rare in everyday A2 Thai).

faults.quote: As a noun, พยาบาล means a nurse who looks after patients.
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definition without adding useful learner information.

notes: Often called นางพยาบาล for a female nurse or บุรุษพยาบาล for a male nurse. Note the related word โรงพยาบาล (hospital). The classifier is คน.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital.

examples.text: พยาบาลช่วยดูแลผู้ป่วยที่โรงพยาบาล
examples.translation: The nurse helps take care of the patients at the hospital.

faults.quote: It is the standard, neutral word for an airplane
faults.why: Pure filler; misses the essential classifier ลำ (lam).

corrected.headword: เครื่องบิน
notes: Literally 'flying machine', from เครื่อง (machine, device) + บิน (to fly). The classifier is ลำ (lam).

senses.definition: A vehicle with wings and one or more engines that flies through the air.

examples.text: เครื่องบินจะออกเดินทางในอีกหนึ่งชั่วโมง
examples.translation: The airplane will depart in one hour.
examples.matchedForm: เครื่องบิน

faults.quote: किस्मत (kismat) is an Arabic loanword... It is grammatically feminine
faults.why: Restates the gloss and gender already given in the fields.

faults.quote: windfall
faults.why: 'Windfall' means an unexpected financial gain, which किस्मत does not mean.

notes: Often written with a nuqta as क़िस्मत (qismat). A more formal Sanskrit synonym is भाग्य (bhāgya).
Often contrasted with कर्म (karma): कर्म refers to one's own actions and their consequences, while किस्मत refers to chance or pre-ordained fate.

senses.definition: Chance or fortune that brings good or bad results.

examples.text: लॉटरी जीतना सिर्फ किस्मत की बात है।
examples.translation: Winning the lottery is just a matter of luck.

senses.definition: The predetermined course of someone's life.

examples.text: हर इंसान अपनी किस्मत खुद लिखता है।
examples.translation: Every person writes their own destiny.

faults.quote: This is a direct loanword from English and is commonly used
faults.why: Obvious filler note stating that an English loanword means the same as in English.

notes: In India, smaller neighborhood grocery shops are called किराने की दुकान (kirāne kī dukān), while सुपरमार्केट refers to larger self-service stores.

senses.definition: A large self-service store that sells food, drinks, and household goods.

examples.text: मैं आज सुपरमार्केट से फल और सब्ज़ियाँ लाऊँगा।
examples.translation: I will bring fruits and vegetables from the supermarket today.

notes: Although आदमी can mean 'person' or 'human' in general statements, in everyday speech it usually means an adult man. For a gender-neutral word for 'person', use इंसान (insān) or व्यक्ति (vyakti).
It keeps the same form in the direct plural (दो आदमी, 'two men'), taking endings only in the oblique plural (आदमियों को, 'to the men').

senses.definition: An adult male human.

examples.text: वह आदमी बहुत लंबा है।
examples.translation: That man is very tall.

senses.definition: A human being in general.

examples.text: आदमी अपनी गलतियों से सीखता है।
examples.translation: A person learns from their mistakes.

faults.quote: 'अतिथि' is more formal and often implies a guest who arrives without
faults.why: In modern Hindi, अतिथि is simply a formal synonym, not specifically an uninvited guest.

notes: मेहमान is the standard everyday word; अतिथि (atithi) is a more formal synonym.
It stays unchanged in the direct plural: घर में मेहमान आए हैं (Guests have come home).

senses.definition: A person visiting someone's home or attending an event.

examples.text: आज घर पर मेहमान आने वाले हैं।
examples.translation: Guests are coming to the house today.

faults.quote: Unlike many animals, this word is considered masculine in grammatical gender
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender and makes a vague claim ('unlike many animals').

notes: The chandrabindu (ँ) nasalizes the vowel (/sãːp/). Without nasalization, साप is not a standard word (compare शाप, 'curse').
It stays unchanged in the direct plural (दो साँप, 'two snakes'). To say a snake bit someone, Hindi uses the verb काटना (kāṭnā): साँप ने काटा।

senses.definition: A long, legless reptile.

examples.text: घास में एक बड़ा साँप है।
examples.translation: There is a big snake in the grass.

faults.quote: Remember that 'het' is the article for this word.
faults.why: Restates the gender/article already shown in the headword.

notes: The plural is 'potloden', where the final 'd' is voiced (/d/) instead of devoiced (/t/).

senses.definition: A thin wooden tool with a graphite core, used for writing or drawing.

examples.text: Ik schrijf mijn aantekeningen met een potlood.
examples.translation: I write my notes with a pencil.

faults.quote: De foto zit in een mooi houten raam.
faults.why: A picture frame in Dutch is 'lijst' (fotolijst), not 'raam'.

faults.quote: A rigid structure that holds something, such as a picture
faults.why: 'Raam' as a physical frame is technical/specialized; picture frame is false.

faults.quote: which is also the word for the Japanese noodle dish
faults.why: Trivial English/loanword homograph joke, unhelpful for A2 Dutch learners.

notes: Use 'het raam' for the whole window (frame and glass), and 'de ruit' for just the pane of glass.
Note the vowel change in the diminutive: 'het raampje' (plural: 'ramen').

senses.definition: An opening in a wall or vehicle with glass in it to let in light and air.

examples.text: Ik kijk uit het raam naar de regen.
examples.translation: I am looking out the window at the rain.

examples.text: Zou je het raam open willen doen?
examples.translation: Would you mind opening the window?

faults.quote: We gaan tonight naar een Italiaans restaurant in het centrum.
faults.why: Contains the English word 'tonight' instead of Dutch 'vanavond'.

faults.quote: Note that 'het restaurant' takes the neuter article 'het'
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword.

notes: To say 'at a restaurant', Dutch usually uses the preposition 'in' ('in een restaurant') or the phrase 'uit eten gaan' (to go out to eat).

senses.definition: A place where you can buy and eat a meal.

examples.text: We gaan vanavond naar een Italiaans restaurant in het centrum.
examples.translation: Tonight we are going to an Italian restaurant in the city center.

faults.quote: Used for the fixed payment you receive regularly from your employer.
faults.why: Simply repeats the definition of the word.

notes: Often used interchangeably with 'het loon', though 'salaris' usually refers to a fixed monthly pay, while 'loon' can also refer to hourly wages.

senses.definition: A fixed amount of money that an employee receives from their employer, usually every month.

examples.text: Hij is erg tevreden met zijn salaris.
examples.translation: He is very satisfied with his salary.

examples.text: Wanneer wordt het salaris gestort?
examples.translation: When does the salary get paid into the account?

faults.quote: Ik drink elke ochtend een glas vers sinaasappelsap.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'sinaasappelsap' instead of the standalone word 'sap'.

faults.quote: Use 'sap' for fruit juice, but note that the plural 'sappen'
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Frequently used in compounds with the name of a fruit, such as 'het sinaasappelsap' (orange juice) or 'het appelsap' (apple juice), and often in the diminutive 'het sapje' for a single serving.

senses.definition: The liquid that comes from pressing fruit or vegetables, often drunk as a beverage.

examples.text: Wil je een glas vers sap bij het ontbijt?
examples.translation: Would you like a glass of fresh juice with breakfast?

senses.definition: The liquid that carries food and water through a plant or tree.

examples.text: In de lente stroomt het sap weer door de bomen.
examples.translation: In spring, the sap flows through the trees again.

faults.quote: يَعْمَلُ الطَّبَّاخُ فِي مِطْعَمٍ كَبِيرٍ.
faults.why: Wrong vowel in مِطْعَمٍ; the word for 'restaurant' is مَطْعَم (maṭʿam).

faults.quote: طَبَّاخ usually refers to a cook or a chef who prepares food
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss; feminine and plural forms are more useful.

notes: Feminine: طَبَّاخَة (ṭabbāḵa). Plural: طَبَّاخُون (ṭabbāḵūn).

senses.definition: A person whose job is to prepare and cook food.

examples.text: يَعْمَلُ الطَّبَّاخُ فِي مَطْعَمٍ كَبِيرٍ.
examples.translation: The cook works in a large restaurant.

faults.quote: /qitˤ/
faults.why: Missing gemination on the final consonant; should be /qitˤtˤ/ or /qitˤː/.

faults.quote: A small domesticated carnivorous mammal with soft fur, a short snout, and
faults.why: Encyclopedic definition; too complex for A2 learners.

notes: Refers to a male cat or a cat in general; the feminine form is قِطَّة (qiṭṭa), and the plural is قِطَط (qiṭaṭ).

senses.definition: A small furry animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet.

examples.text: الْقِطُّ يَجْلِسُ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ.
examples.translation: The cat is sitting under the tree.

faults.quote: /taˈbiːb/
faults.why: Initial consonant is emphatic /tˤ/ (ط), not plain /t/ (ت).

faults.quote: Used to refer to a medical doctor, especially a male physician.
faults.why: Restates the gloss and gender without giving the feminine or plural forms.

notes: Feminine: طَبِيبَة (ṭabība). Broken plural: أَطِبَّاء (ʾaṭibbāʾ).
Often interchangeable with دُكْتُور (duktūr) in everyday speech, though طَبِيب is standard and specifically means a medical doctor.

senses.definition: A person who is qualified to treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الطَّبِيبِ لِأَنَّنِي مَرِيضٌ.
examples.translation: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

faults.why: General trip and organized excursion/school trip are shades of one meaning in Arabic.
Missing the everyday travel sense 'flight' (e.g., رِحْلَة طَيَرَان or airport flight number).

notes: Plural: رِحْلَات (riḥlāt).
Do not confuse with سَفَر (safar, travel in general); رِحْلَة refers to a specific trip, outing, or scheduled flight.

senses.definition: An act of traveling from one place to another, or an outing for pleasure or education.

examples.text: ذَهَبْنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ مَدْرَسِيَّةٍ إِلَى الْمُتْحَفِ.
examples.translation: We went on a school trip to the museum.

senses.definition: A scheduled journey on an airplane.

examples.text: تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ بِسَبَبِ الطَّقْسِ.
examples.translation: The flight was delayed because of the weather.

notes: Often shortened to das Bad in everyday conversation.

senses.definition: A room in a house or apartment that contains a bath or shower, a washbasin, and often a toilet.

examples.text: Das Badezimmer wird gerade renoviert.
examples.translation: The bathroom is being renovated right now.

faults.quote: Bargeld is a neuter noun and is generally used without
faults.why: Restates gender; misses that it is uncountable and the common phrase 'bar bezahlen'.

notes: Uncountable (no plural). To say 'pay in cash', both mit Bargeld bezahlen and simply bar bezahlen are common.

senses.definition: Money in the form of coins and banknotes, rather than cards or digital payment.

examples.text: Ich habe heute kein Bargeld dabei.
examples.translation: I don't have any cash with me today.

faults.quote: Der Hund kaut auf einem Knochen.
faults.why: Example does not contain the headword 'Bein' at all.

faults.quote: (bone) A hard structure that forms part of the skeleton.
faults.why: Archaic or restricted to compounds and idioms; standard German for bone is 'Knochen'.

faults.quote: leg; bone
faults.why: Includes archaic/compound-only meaning 'bone' as a main gloss for beginners.

notes: Plural: die Beine.

Also used for the legs of furniture (e.g., das Tischbein) or trouser legs (das Hosenbein). In older idioms and anatomical compounds (such as das Schlüsselbein, collarbone), it retains an older meaning of 'bone', though the normal word for bone is der Knochen.

senses.definition: One of the lower limbs of a person or animal, used for standing and walking, or a vertical support of a piece of furniture.

examples.text: Sie hat sich beim Sport das Bein gebrochen.
examples.translation: She broke her leg while playing sports.

faults.quote: Note that while 'Bett' is used for the piece of furniture
faults.why: Trivial observation; misses irregular plural 'die Betten' and preposition distinction ('ins' vs 'im').

notes: Plural: die Betten.
Common expressions: ins Bett gehen (to go to bed) and im Bett liegen/bleiben (to lie/stay in bed).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a mattress for sleeping or resting on.

examples.text: Ich bin müde und gehe jetzt ins Bett.
examples.translation: I am tired and am going to bed now.

notes: When ordering in a bar or restaurant, the singular form is stays unchanged after numbers: Zwei Bier, bitte! (Two beers, please!).

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from malted grain and hops, or a glass or bottle of this drink.

examples.text: Ich trinke gerne ein kühles Bier nach der Arbeit.
examples.translation: I like to drink a cold beer after work.

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'sonho' covers both the mental images experienced while sleeping
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses given below instead of offering usage info.
Missing the common Brazilian bakery meaning: a filled doughnut/pastry.

notes: Just as in English, you say 'ter um sonho' (to have a dream).
In Brazilian bakeries ('padarias'), a 'sonho' is also a very popular sweet fried pastry filled with cream.

senses.definition: A series of images, thoughts, or feelings that happen in your mind while you sleep.

examples.text: Eu tive um sonho estranho ontem à noite.
examples.translation: I had a strange dream last night.

senses.definition: Something that you want very much to happen or do in the future.

examples.text: O meu maior sonho é viajar pelo mundo.
examples.translation: My biggest dream is to travel the world.

senses.definition: A round, fried sweet pastry filled with cream or dulce de leche.

examples.text: Comprei um sonho de creme na padaria.
examples.translation: I bought a cream-filled doughnut at the bakery.

faults.why: Should mention the standard collocation 'tomar sorvete' (to have/eat ice cream) instead of 'sobremesa'.

notes: Brazilians usually say 'tomar sorvete' (literally, to drink/take ice cream) rather than 'comer sorvete' (to eat ice cream).
In Portugal, ice cream is called 'gelado'.

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk, cream, or fruit.

examples.text: Eu gosto muito de tomar sorvete de chocolate no verão.
examples.translation: I really like having chocolate ice cream in the summer.

faults.quote: In Brazil, 'suéter' is commonly used for a knitted pullover
faults.why: Restates the definition; also 'suéter' normally has sleeves (sleeveless is 'colete').

notes: In everyday Brazilian speech, people very often say 'blusa de frio' or 'casaco' for any warm top or sweater.

senses.definition: A warm knitted piece of clothing with long sleeves, worn on the upper body.

examples.text: Comprei um suéter de lã para o inverno.
examples.translation: I bought a wool sweater for the winter.

faults.quote: While 'mercado' often refers to a traditional open-air market
faults.why: In Brazil, 'mercado' is routinely used as short for 'supermercado'; open-air market is 'feira'.

notes: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, people very often shorten 'supermercado' to just 'mercado' (e.g., 'Vou ao mercado'). An open-air street market is called a 'feira'.

senses.definition: A large self-service shop that sells food, drinks, and household goods.

examples.text: Eu vou ao supermercado comprar leite e pão.
examples.translation: I am going to the supermarket to buy milk and bread.

faults.quote: In Spain and many Latin American countries, 'la comida' refers
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and fails to mention 'almuerzo', which learners confuse in Mexican Spanish.

faults.quote: Vamos a preparar la comida para la familia.
faults.why: Ambiguous between 'food' and 'lunch', and the English translation 'midday meal' is stiff.

notes: In Mexico, 'la comida' is the main afternoon meal (lunch, usually eaten between 2 and 4 p.m.), while 'el almuerzo' refers to a hearty late-morning meal or brunch.

senses.definition: Something that people or animals eat.

examples.text: Hay mucha comida en la mesa.
examples.translation: There is a lot of food on the table.

senses.definition: The main meal of the day, eaten in the afternoon.

examples.text: Nos vemos mañana a la hora de la comida.
examples.translation: See you tomorrow at lunchtime.

faults.quote: A record of money held in a bank.
faults.why: Too narrow; 'cuenta' is equally common for email and online user accounts at A2.

notes: In restaurants in Mexico, you can ask for the bill by saying 'La cuenta, por favor'. It is also used in common phrases like 'darse cuenta' (to realize).

senses.definition: A statement of the money owed for food, drinks, or a service.

examples.text: Disculpe, ¿nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
examples.translation: Excuse me, can you bring us the check, please?

senses.definition: An arrangement to keep money in a bank, or to use a website or service.

examples.text: Abrí una cuenta nueva en el banco.
examples.translation: I opened a new account at the bank.

faults.quote: A difficult or important task or project that requires effort
faults.why: Literary sense ('undertaking/endeavor') is not suitable for an A2 beginner entry.

notes: Use 'empresa' or 'compañía' for a company or firm; 'negocio' usually refers to a smaller business, a shop, or business in general.

senses.definition: A commercial organization that sells goods or provides services.

examples.text: Mi hermano trabaja en una empresa de tecnología.
examples.translation: My brother works at a technology company.

faults.why: Lacks the essential note that the plural 'los tés' keeps the written accent.

notes: Written with an accent mark (té) to distinguish it from the pronoun 'te'; the plural 'los tés' also keeps the accent.

senses.definition: A drink made by pouring hot water over dried tea leaves, or the leaves themselves.

examples.text: Prefiero tomar un té caliente por la mañana.
examples.translation: I prefer to drink a hot cup of tea in the morning.

faults.quote: In Spanish, 'techo' is used for both the 'ceiling'
faults.why: Restates the senses and duplicates note 1.

faults.quote: Hay muchos pájaros sobre el techo de la casa.
faults.why: In Peninsular Spanish, the exterior roof of a house is 'tejado', whereas 'techo' for 'roof' is mainly figurative (a home/shelter) or used for vehicles.

notes: In Spain, 'el techo' is the indoor ceiling (or the roof of a car, or figuratively a home/shelter), while the outer roof of a building is usually called 'el tejado'.

senses.definition: The upper interior surface of a room or vehicle.

examples.text: He pintado el techo del salón de blanco.
examples.translation: I have painted the living room ceiling white.

senses.definition: The top covering of a building or vehicle, or a place that provides shelter.

examples.text: Por suerte tenemos un techo donde dormir.
examples.translation: Luckily we have a roof over our heads to sleep under.

faults.why: Missing the everyday A1/A2 sense 'telephone number' (e.g., '¿Cuál es tu teléfono?').

faults.quote: The telephone rings in the living room.
faults.why: Spanish simple present 'suena' here translates naturally as English present continuous 'is ringing'.

notes: In Spain, a mobile phone is usually called 'el móvil', while 'el teléfono' (or 'el fijo') refers to a landline or to phones in general.

senses.definition: A device used to talk to other people over a distance.

examples.text: El teléfono está sonando en el salón.
examples.translation: The phone is ringing in the living room.

senses.definition: The sequence of digits dialled to call someone's phone.

examples.text: ¿Me das tu teléfono para llamarte mañana?
examples.translation: Can you give me your phone number so I can call you tomorrow?

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'teneduría' (bookkeeping)
faults.why: Pure filler; no A2 learner will ever encounter or confuse it with 'teneduría'.

senses.definition: A small tool with three or four points used for picking up food and eating.

examples.text: Se me ha caído el tenedor al suelo.
examples.translation: I dropped my fork on the floor.

faults.quote: Use 'tiempo' for both clock time and weather conditions.

senses.definition: Time as something that passes or as a period available for doing something.

examples.text: No tengo tiempo para terminar este ejercicio hoy.
examples.translation: I don't have time to finish this exercise today.

senses.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a place and time, such as sun, rain, or wind.

examples.text: Hoy hace muy buen tiempo para dar un paseo por el parque.
examples.translation: The weather is very nice today for taking a walk in the park.

faults.quote: to run; to jog; to rush
faults.why: Includes 'to rush', which is not covered by the senses or glosses.

faults.quote: วิ่ง is the standard verb for running on foot...
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss without adding learner-specific usage info.

notes: Also used for vehicles operating or moving along a route (e.g., รถวิ่ง 'the car is moving / the bus is running').

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: เขาชอบวิ่งตอนเช้า
examples.translation: He likes to run in the morning.

faults.why: Definition restricts the meaning to dry tools, missing painting (e.g. with a brush).

senses.definition: To make a picture by drawing or painting.

examples.text: ฉันชอบวาดรูปในเวลาว่าง
examples.translation: I like to draw in my free time.
