examples.text: 昨日、友達と映画を見ました。
examples.translation: Yesterday, I watched a movie with a friend.

faults.quote: In the genitive case, it becomes 'e-mailu'
faults.why: The genitive (and accusative) singular is 'e-maila' (for a message), taking the animate-type ending.

notes: Takes the -a ending in the genitive and accusative singular: 'wysłać e-maila' or 'wysłać e-mail' (to send an email).
In everyday conversation and at work, the shorter form 'mail' (/mɛjl/) is much more common.

senses.definition: A message sent and received through the internet, or the system for sending such messages.

examples.text: Muszę wysłać ważny e-mail do szefa.
examples.translation: I have to send an important email to my boss.

faults.quote: The plural form is 'egzaminy', which is often used collectively
faults.why: Regular plural; misses essential collocations like 'zdać/oblać egzamin z + genitive'.

notes: Used for formal school, university, or professional exams (e.g., 'egzamin na prawo jazdy' – driving test). For a smaller school test or quiz, use 'sprawdzian' or 'kartkówka'.
Common collocations: 'zdawać egzamin' (to take an exam), 'zdać egzamin' (to pass an exam), 'oblać egzamin' (to fail an exam). The subject takes 'z' + genitive: 'egzamin z polskiego'.

senses.definition: A formal test of knowledge or ability in a subject.

examples.text: Muszę się uczyć, bo jutro mam ważny egzamin.
examples.translation: I have to study because I have an important exam tomorrow.

senses.definition: A difficult situation that shows how good, strong, or capable someone or something is.

examples.text: To będzie prawdziwy egzamin dla naszej drużyny.
examples.translation: This will be a real test for our team.

faults.quote: Firma is the most common way to refer to a business
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: To say you work for a company, use 'pracować w firmie' (literally 'in a company').

senses.definition: A business organization that sells goods or provides services.

examples.text: Moja firma zatrudnia sto osób.
examples.translation: My company employs one hundred people.

examples.text: Pracuję w dużej firmie budowlanej.
examples.translation: I work at a large construction firm.

faults.quote: In Polish, you do not 'have' hunger. You 'are' hungry
faults.why: English speakers already say 'to be hungry'; they need to know the feminine form 'głodna'.

notes: Agrees in gender and number with the person who is hungry: a man says 'jestem głodny', a woman says 'jestem głodna', and for a group of people it is 'jesteśmy głodni'.

senses.definition: Feeling a need or desire to eat food.

examples.text: Jestem bardzo głodny po pracy.
examples.translation: I am very hungry after work.

faults.quote: 약 is the general term for any kind of medicine
faults.why: Restates the definition; omits that taking medicine uses 먹다 ('to eat').
Should mention the common determiner homograph 약 ('approximately') used before numbers.

notes: To say 'take medicine' in Korean, use the verb 먹다 (literally 'to eat'): 약을 먹다. For liquid medicine, 마시다 ('to drink') is also used, and for ointment, 바르다 ('to apply').
Count individual pills with the counter 알: 약 한 알 (one pill).
Don't confuse this noun with the common word 약 placed before numbers, which means 'approximately' (e.g., 약 한 시간, 'about an hour').

senses.definition: A substance, such as a pill, liquid, or ointment, that you take or use to treat an illness.

examples.text: 아플 때 약을 먹어야 해요.
examples.translation: You should take medicine when you are sick.

faults.quote: /jo̞k̚ɕil/
faults.why: Missing tensification after obstruent coda: 욕실 is pronounced [jo̞k̚ɕ͈il] with tense /ɕ͈/.

notes: 욕실 specifically refers to a room with a bathtub or shower. In everyday speech, Koreans much more commonly use 화장실 for any bathroom at home or in public, even when referring to showering.

senses.definition: A room in a house or hotel equipped with a bathtub or shower.

examples.text: 욕실에 따뜻한 물이 잘 나와요.
examples.translation: Warm water runs well in the bathroom.

faults.quote: Two things that go together or are perceived as a pair.
faults.why: 커플 does not mean a pair of objects; it contradicts note[0].

notes: Unlike English 'couple', 커플 only refers to two people in a romantic relationship (usually unmarried), never to 'a few' or a pair of objects. Married couples are usually called 부부.
Often used before other nouns to describe matching items for romantic partners, such as 커플티 (matching T-shirts) or 커플링 (couple rings).

senses.definition: Two people who are in a romantic relationship.

examples.text: 공원에 커플들이 많아요.
examples.translation: There are many couples in the park.

faults.quote: Since it is a loanword from English, it is easy to remember
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler; they omit the common short form 메일 and collocations.

notes: In everyday speech, it is very often shortened to 메일 (e.g., 메일을 보내다, 'to send an email').

senses.definition: A message sent or received electronically over the internet, or the system for sending such messages.

examples.text: 이메일을 확인했어요.
examples.translation: I checked my email.

faults.quote: Used to describe living organisms like trees, flowers, and grasses
faults.why: Restates the definition in different words without adding usage information.

notes: Pronounced [싱물] because ㄱ nasalizes to ㅇ before ㅁ.
To talk about growing or caring for houseplants, use the verb 키우다 (식물을 키우다).

senses.definition: A living thing such as a tree, flower, or herb that grows in soil or water.

examples.text: 집에 식물을 많이 키워요.
examples.translation: I grow a lot of plants at home.

faults.quote: Note that 'beurre' is masculine (le beurre).
faults.why: Restates grammatical gender already shown in the entry header.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'la beurrée'
faults.why: 'Beurrée' is a rare regional/dated word an A2 learner will not encounter.

notes: Usually used as an uncountable noun with the partitive article 'du' (e.g., 'manger du beurre').

senses.definition: A soft yellow dairy food made by churning cream, spread on bread or used in cooking.

examples.text: J'ajoute un morceau de beurre dans la poêle.
examples.translation: I'm adding a piece of butter to the pan.

faults.quote: While 'billet' can mean a banknote, a small note, or a ticket
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without adding useful distinction (like 'billet' vs 'ticket').

faults.quote: (message) A short written message or memo left for someone.
faults.why: Dated/literary in modern everyday French; 'un petit mot' is used instead.

notes: For travel and events, 'billet' is used for long-distance trains, planes, concerts, and museums, whereas 'ticket' is commonly used for the metro, buses, and receipts.
In the sense of paper money, it is short for 'billet de banque'.

senses.definition: A printed or electronic document that gives the right to travel on a train or plane, or to enter a show or museum.

examples.text: J'ai acheté mon billet de train pour Paris.
examples.translation: I bought my train ticket to Paris.

senses.definition: A piece of paper money.

examples.text: Il m'a donné un billet de vingt euros.
examples.translation: He gave me a twenty-euro bill.

faults.quote: Unlike an 'assiette' (plate), a 'bol' is round and deep.
faults.why: Explaining the difference between a bowl and a plate is unnecessary filler.

notes: In France, hot drinks like coffee or hot chocolate are traditionally drunk from a 'bol' at breakfast.

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for eating soup or cereal, or for drinking hot beverages at breakfast.

examples.text: Elle verse le lait chaud dans le bol.
examples.translation: She pours the hot milk into the bowl.

faults.quote: Korkmuş comes from the verb korkmak (to fear) and describes someone
faults.why: Restates the gloss instead of explaining the -miş past participle formation.

notes: Formed as the past participle (-miş) of the verb korkmak (to be afraid), literally meaning 'having become frightened'.
Do not confuse with korkunç (scary, terrifying), which describes the thing causing fear rather than the person feeling it.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing fear; having been frightened.

examples.text: Karanlık odada kalan çocuk çok korkmuş görünüyordu.
examples.translation: The child left in the dark room looked very frightened.

faults.why: Fear of danger and fear of a bad outcome are shades of one meaning.

notes: Derived from the verb korkmak (to be afraid). Often used as a modifier before another noun, as in korku filmi (horror movie).

senses.definition: An unpleasant emotion caused by danger, threat, or the expectation of something bad happening.

examples.text: Karanlık, çocuklarda korku yaratabilir.
examples.translation: Darkness can create fear in children.

examples.text: Sınavı geçememe korkusuyla çok çalıştı.
examples.translation: He studied hard out of fear of not passing the exam.

faults.why: Indoor, object, and street corners are all one concept in both Turkish and English.

faults.quote: Used for both indoor corners of a room and outdoor street corners.
faults.why: Simply restates the two senses; English 'corner' works the exact same way.

notes: Because the word ends in a vowel, it takes the buffer consonant -y- before vowel-initial suffixes: köşeye (to the corner), köşeyi (the corner).

senses.definition: A place or angle where two edges, walls, or streets meet.

examples.text: Koltuğu odanın köşesine koyduk.
examples.translation: We put the armchair in the corner of the room.

examples.text: Marketin köşesinde buluşalım.
examples.translation: Let's meet at the corner by the market.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'yürümek', which means 'to walk'.
faults.why: The words look and sound nothing alike; learners will not confuse them.

notes: Takes the dative case (-e/-a) for the destination or goal: yardıma koşmak (to run to help), işe koşmak (to rush to work).

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking, or to compete in a footrace.

examples.text: Çocuklar parkta neşeyle koşuyor.
examples.translation: The children are running happily in the park.

faults.quote: Kötü is the most common word for 'bad' or 'poor' in quality
faults.why: Merely repeats the glosses of the two senses without adding usage information.

notes: Like most Turkish adjectives, it can also be used directly as an adverb meaning 'badly': Kötü oynadık (We played badly).

senses.definition: Unpleasant, harmful, or of low quality; not good.

examples.text: Bugün hava çok kötü.
examples.translation: The weather is very bad today.

senses.definition: Morally wrong, wicked, or cruel.

examples.text: O kötü bir insan değil.
examples.translation: He is not a bad person.

faults.quote: The day before today.
faults.why: Adverb defined as a noun phrase instead of an adverbial time expression.

notes: अَمْسِ is an indeclinable adverb that always ends with a kasrah (-i); when used with the definite article (الأَمْس), it becomes a regular declinable noun.

senses.definition: On the day before today.

examples.text: وَصَلْتُ أَمْسِ.
examples.translation: I arrived yesterday.

faults.quote: It functions as an adverbial phrase meaning 'abroad' or 'outside the country'
faults.why: Restates the glosses and part of speech without adding grammar or usage help.

notes: Literally 'outside the country'; خَارِجَ is in the adverbial accusative (-a) followed by البِلَادِ in the genitive (-i).

senses.definition: In or to a foreign country.

examples.text: سَافَرَ خَارِجَ البِلَادِ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ.
examples.translation: He traveled abroad to study.

faults.quote: اليَوْمَ can mean either specifically 'today' (on this day) or more broadly
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: اليَوْمَ يَتَصَفَّحُ الجَمِيعُ الهَوَاتِفَ الذَّكِيَّةَ.
faults.why: One browses the internet or websites, not 'smartphones'; unnatural collocation.

notes: Formed from the noun يَوْم (day) in the accusative case (-a), which marks adverbs of time in Arabic.

senses.definition: On this current day.

examples.text: اليَوْمَ سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
examples.translation: Today I will go to the market.

senses.definition: At the present time; in the modern era.

examples.text: اليَوْمَ يَسْتَخْدِمُ الجَمِيعُ الهَوَاتِفَ الذَّكِيَّةَ.
examples.translation: Nowadays everyone uses smartphones.

faults.quote: words ending in a fatḥa (the dash above the letter) like 'الآنَ' are often fixed
faults.why: Misleading generalization: most words ending in fatḥa are simply in the accusative case, not indeclinable.

faults.quote: This word is used to signal that an action is happening in the immediate present
faults.why: Pure filler that just explains the English meaning of 'now'.

notes: الآنَ has a fixed fatḥah (-a) ending, even after prepositions: حَتَّى الآنَ (until now), مِنَ الآنَ (from now on).

senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: أَنَا مَشْغُولٌ الآنَ.
examples.translation: I am busy now.

faults.quote: رُبَّمَا نَسَافِرُ غَدًا.
faults.why: Incorrect vowelization on the verb: Form III يُسَافِرُ takes a ḍammah (نُسَافِرُ), not نَسَافِرُ.

faults.quote: It is often followed by a verb in the past tense, even when referring to the future
faults.why: In MSA, رُبَّمَا + past tense refers to past or present, whereas future takes the imperfect (مُضَارِع).

notes: Can be followed directly by a verb (present for future/present possibility, past for past possibility) or by a noun/pronoun.

senses.definition: Used to say that something may happen or may be true.

examples.text: رُبَّمَا نُسَافِرُ غَدًا.
examples.translation: Perhaps we will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رُبَّمَا كَانَ عَلَى حَقٍّ.
examples.translation: Perhaps he was right.

faults.quote: While 'adolescent' sounds formal or medical,
faults.why: 'Adolescent' is standard and neutral in French, not restricted to formal or medical registers.

notes: The feminine form is 'une adolescente' (/a.dɔ.lɛ.sɑ̃t/).
In everyday spoken French, it is very often shortened to 'un ado' (or 'une ado').

senses.definition: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult.

examples.text: Cet adolescent passe beaucoup de temps dans sa chambre.
examples.translation: This teenager spends a lot of time in his room.

faults.quote: (nature) An animal or plant that is fully grown.
faults.why: Shades of one meaning; moreover, the example uses 'adulte' as an adjective, not a noun.

faults.quote: Cet arbre adulte produit des fruits chaque année.
faults.why: 'Adulte' is used here as an adjective modifying 'arbre', whereas the entry is a noun.

faults.quote: adult, fully grown
faults.why: 'Fully grown' is an adjective, not a noun gloss.

notes: Has the same form in the masculine and feminine ('un adulte', 'une adulte'), and is also used as an adjective ('un chat adulte').

senses.definition: A person or animal that is fully grown.

examples.text: Il faut être un adulte pour signer ce document.
examples.translation: You need to be an adult to sign this document.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'la gare', which is for trains, not planes.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'aéroport' (a transparent cognate of 'airport') with 'gare'.

notes: Takes the preposition 'à': 'aller à l'aéroport' (to go to the airport), 'être à l'aéroport' (to be at the airport).

senses.definition: A place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers to wait in.

examples.text: Nous devons arriver à l'aéroport deux heures avant le vol.
examples.translation: We need to arrive at the airport two hours before the flight.

notes: The feminine form is 'l'agricultrice' (/a.ɡʁi.kyl.tʁis/).
'Agriculteur' is the neutral modern term for a professional farmer, whereas 'paysan' refers more to traditional country life and can sometimes sound dated or pejorative.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to grow crops or raise animals for food.

examples.text: L'agriculteur travaille dans les champs toute la journée.
examples.translation: The farmer works in the fields all day long.

faults.quote: /la.mi/
faults.why: IPA includes the definite article 'l''; it must transcribe the lemma 'ami' only (/a.mi/).

notes: The feminine form is 'l'amie' (pronounced the same, /a.mi/).
To clearly mean 'boyfriend', 'petit ami' or 'copain' is more common; 'mon ami' with a possessive can mean 'my boyfriend' or 'my partner', especially among adults.

senses.definition: A person you know well and like, who is not a member of your family.

examples.text: C'est un bon ami qui m'aide toujours.
examples.translation: He is a good friend who always helps me.

senses.definition: A man or boy with whom someone is in a romantic relationship (usually with a possessive or 'petit').

examples.text: Elle nous a présenté son petit ami hier soir.
examples.translation: She introduced us to her boyfriend last night.

faults.quote: /ʔaːu˧˥ fawk͡m˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong tone for 'phông' (level ˧, not rising ˧˥) and non-standard vowel transcription.

notes: Takes the classifier 'chiếc' or 'cái'.
Common in northern Vietnam; in the south, 'áo thun' is used instead.

senses.definition: A simple shirt with short sleeves and no collar, usually made of cotton.

examples.text: Tôi mặc một chiếc áo phông trắng khi đi chơi với bạn bè.
examples.translation: I wore a white T-shirt when going out with friends.

faults.quote: /ʔaːw ʂə mi/
faults.why: Missing tone marks, and 's' in Hanoi Vietnamese is /s/, not retroflex /ʂ/.

notes: Takes the classifier 'chiếc' or 'cái'.
Borrowed from French 'chemise'. Unlike a T-shirt ('áo phông' or 'áo thun'), an 'áo sơ mi' has a collar and buttons down the front.

senses.definition: A shirt with a collar and buttons down the front.

examples.text: Anh ấy mặc một chiếc áo sơ mi trắng đến buổi phỏng vấn.
examples.translation: He wore a white dress shirt to the interview.

faults.quote: Use 'đắt' to describe something that costs a high price.
faults.why: Restates the definition; fails to mention the common Southern equivalent 'mắc'.

notes: The opposite is 'rẻ' (cheap). In southern Vietnam, 'mắc' is commonly used instead of 'đắt'.

senses.definition: Of an item or service: costing a lot of money.

examples.text: Cái áo này đẹp quá nhưng hơi đắt.
examples.translation: This shirt is so nice, but a bit expensive.

faults.quote: /dət̚˧˥ nɨək̚˧˥/
faults.why: Letter 'đ' is implosive /ɗ/ in Vietnamese, not /d/ (which represents 'd/gi/r').

notes: Literally combines 'đất' (land) and 'nước' (water/country). It carries a warmer, more emotional tone than the formal term 'quốc gia' (nation/state).

senses.definition: An area of land with its own government, people, and culture.

examples.text: Tôi rất yêu đất nước và con người Việt Nam.
examples.translation: I really love the country and people of Vietnam.

faults.why: Wrong tone: 'đặt' has the nặng (low glottalized) tone /˧˨ʔ/, not sắc /˧˥/.

faults.quote: Used when physically placing or setting an object down on a surface.
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the two sense definitions without adding usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to put; to book; to order
notes: Also used in common expressions like 'đặt tên' (to name) and 'đặt câu hỏi' (to ask a question).

senses.definition: To put or set something down in a particular place.

examples.text: Tôi đặt cuốn sách lên bàn.
examples.translation: I put the book on the table.

senses.definition: To arrange for a table, room, ticket, or goods in advance.

examples.text: Chúng tôi muốn đặt một bàn cho tối nay.
examples.translation: We want to book a table for tonight.

faults.quote: Used for people, animals, and things that have existed for a long
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions of the two senses instead of giving usage tips.

notes: For old things or places, 'lama' is often used instead (e.g., 'rumah lama' = old house, 'teman lama' = old friend).

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time.

examples.text: Kakek saya sudah tua.
examples.translation: My grandfather is already old.

senses.definition: Of a color: dark or deep in shade (as opposed to 'muda', light).

examples.text: Dia memakai baju biru tua.
examples.translation: He is wearing a dark blue shirt.

faults.quote: The complete and immediate fulfillment of a payment or an obligation.
faults.why: Oversplit: 'tunai' is one concept (cash / paid upfront rather than on credit).

faults.quote: Dia membayar pembelian itu secara tunai. — He paid for that purchase
faults.why: 'Secara tunai' means 'in cash' (or upfront, not on credit), whereas 'in full' is 'lunas'.

notes: Often used as a modifier after nouns or verbs, as in 'uang tunai' (physical cash) or 'bayar tunai' (to pay in cash / upfront, as opposed to 'kredit', on credit).

senses.definition: Money in the form of coins and banknotes, or immediate payment rather than credit.

examples.text: Apakah toko ini menerima pembayaran tunai?
examples.translation: Does this shop accept cash payments?

examples.text: Dia membayar secara tunai.
examples.translation: He paid in cash.

faults.quote: Used for someone who is traveling for pleasure rather than for business
faults.why: Both notes just restate the definition of a tourist; mention the formal synonym 'wisatawan' instead.

notes: In formal or official contexts (such as news and signs), the synonym 'wisatawan' is commonly used instead.

senses.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure, especially while on holiday.

examples.text: Banyak turis mengunjungi pulau itu pada musim panas.
examples.translation: Many tourists visit that island in the summer.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'uang' (money) with 'pulang' (to go home)
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; learners do not confuse 'uang' with 'pulang'.

faults.quote: money; funds
faults.why: 'funds' is not in the sense glosses.

notes: In casual speech, Indonesians very often use 'duit' instead of 'uang'.

senses.definition: Coins, banknotes, or funds used to buy things.

examples.text: Saya tidak punya cukup uang untuk membeli sepatu itu.
examples.translation: I do not have enough money to buy those shoes.

faults.quote: /ˈudʒan/
faults.why: Wrong IPA: /ˈudʒan/ is 'ujan' (hujan, rain); 'ujian' is three syllables /uˈdʒi.an/.

faults.quote: Ujian refers to formal exams or tests, such as those taken
faults.why: Restates sense 0's definition without adding usage or morphological information.

notes: Formed from the root 'uji' (to test) + '-an'. Do not confuse with 'tes', which is used for shorter quizzes, medical tests, or equipment checks.

senses.definition: A formal test of knowledge or ability, especially in school or university.

examples.text: Besok ada ujian matematika yang sulit.
examples.translation: Tomorrow there is a difficult mathematics exam.

senses.definition: A difficult experience that tests someone's patience or character.

examples.text: Ini adalah ujian besar bagi kesabaran mereka.
examples.translation: This is a great trial for their patience.

faults.quote: A formal meeting where a person is asked questions
faults.why: Job and media interviews are one meaning; 'job interview' specifically adds งาน.

faults.quote: ฉันเพิ่งผ่านการสัมภาษณ์งานมาเมื่อเช้านี้
faults.why: ผ่านการสัมภาษณ์งาน means 'passed the job interview', not 'finished'.

corrected.headword: การสัมภาษณ์
notes: Formed from the prefix การ and the verb สัมภาษณ์ (to interview). The characters ษณ are silent.
For a job interview specifically, Thai usually adds งาน (work): การสัมภาษณ์งาน.

senses.definition: A formal meeting or conversation in which someone is asked questions, such as for a job or a news report.

examples.text: ฉันตื่นเต้นกับการสัมภาษณ์พรุ่งนี้มาก
examples.translation: I am very nervous about the interview tomorrow.
examples.matchedForm: การสัมภาษณ์

examples.text: นักข่าวเตรียมตัวสำหรับการสัมภาษณ์ดาราชื่อดัง
examples.translation: The reporter is preparing for an interview with the famous celebrity.
examples.matchedForm: การสัมภาษณ์

faults.quote: It is a loanword from Chinese, specifically from the Hokkien
faults.why: False etymology; สิงห์ is from Sanskrit siṃha and โต means 'big/large'.
Missing essential classifier (ตัว) for a concrete animal noun.

notes: The classifier for lions and other animals is ตัว (e.g. สิงโตสองตัว — two lions).

senses.definition: A large wild cat found in Africa and India, known for the male's thick mane.

examples.text: สิงโตเป็นเจ้าป่า
examples.translation: The lion is the king of the jungle.

faults.quote: Unlike some other languages that use specific loanwords for dining
faults.why: Vague filler note; a note on the common synonym ข้าวเย็น is much more useful.

faults.quote: คืนนี้เราจะทานอาหารเย็นที่ไหนดี
faults.why: คืนนี้ (tonight) is late night; เย็นนี้ (this evening) is natural with อาหารเย็น.

notes: Compound of อาหาร (food) and เย็น (evening).
In everyday conversation, people very often say ข้าวเย็น (evening rice) instead, and มื้อเย็น when referring to the meal time.

senses.definition: The main meal eaten in the evening.

examples.text: เย็นนี้เราจะทานอาหารเย็นที่ไหนดี
examples.translation: Where should we have dinner this evening?

faults.quote: /sàt liang/
faults.why: Missing the high tone mark on the second syllable (/sàt líaŋ/).

faults.quote: ชาวนาเลี้ยงโคเป็นสัตว์เลี้ยงในไร่
faults.why: Unnatural mix of words: ชาวนา (rice farmer), โค (formal cattle), and ไร่ (crop field).

corrected.headword: สัตว์เลี้ยง
notes: Combines สัตว์ (animal, with a silent ว) and เลี้ยง (to raise or feed). The classifier for individual animals is ตัว.
Contrast with สัตว์ป่า (wild animal).

senses.definition: An animal kept at home for companionship.

examples.text: ฉันชอบสุนัขเพราะมันเป็นสัตว์เลี้ยงที่น่ารัก
examples.translation: I like dogs because they are cute pets.
examples.matchedForm: สัตว์เลี้ยง

senses.definition: An animal raised on a farm for food, products, or work.

examples.text: วัวและไก่เป็นสัตว์เลี้ยงในฟาร์มที่มีประโยชน์
examples.translation: Cows and chickens are useful farm animals.
examples.matchedForm: สัตว์เลี้ยง

faults.quote: In Thai, people often specify the sauce
faults.why: Trivial filler notes that offer no useful linguistic guidance.

notes: Counted by จาน (plate/dish) when served.

senses.definition: Italian-style noodles made from flour, water, and sometimes eggs, usually served with a sauce.

faults.quote: A printed collection of pages showing the days of the year
faults.why: Shades of one meaning: a wall calendar is just a calendar.

faults.quote: मैंने कैलेंडर पर अपनी छुट्टी की तारीख निशान लगा दी है।
faults.why: Ungrammatical: missing postposition 'पर' after 'तारीख', and wrong verb agreement ('लगा दिया है').

senses.definition: A chart, set of pages, or app showing the days, weeks, and months of a year.

examples.text: मैंने कैलेंडर में अपनी छुट्टी की तारीख पर निशान लगा दिया है।
examples.translation: I have marked the date of my vacation on the calendar.

faults.quote: Unlike a pen, mistakes made with a pencil can be easily erased.
faults.why: Explains what a real-world pencil is, not how the Hindi word works.

notes: Although borrowed from English, it is grammatically feminine in Hindi (plural: पेंसिलें).

senses.definition: A thin wooden tool with a graphite or colored core, used for writing or drawing.

examples.text: मैंने नई पेंसिल से अपना नाम लिखा।
examples.translation: I wrote my name with a new pencil.

faults.quote: While 'jaanvar' is the general word for animal, it is sometimes used
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: वह आदमी बिल्कुल जानवर की तरह बर्ताव करता है।
faults.why: Simile ('like an animal') uses the literal sense, not the figurative sense.

notes: The most common everyday word for an animal; 'पशु' (pashu) is more formal.

senses.definition: A living creature that is not a human or a plant.

examples.text: चिड़ियाघर में कई तरह के जानवर हैं।
examples.translation: There are many kinds of animals in the zoo.

senses.definition: A cruel, violent, or uncivilized person.

examples.text: वह इंसान नहीं, पूरा जानवर है।
examples.translation: He is not a human, he is a total beast.

notes: Spelled with a nuqta (dot) under ज for the /z/ sound, though often pronounced /dʒ/ in casual speech. For a building's floor, 'मंज़िल' is common in everyday speech, while 'तल' (tal) is more formal.

senses.definition: A level of a building.

examples.text: मेरा घर तीसरी मंज़िल पर है।
examples.translation: My house is on the third floor.

senses.definition: The place someone is going to, or a goal one is trying to reach.

examples.text: हम अपनी मंज़िल के बहुत करीब हैं।
examples.translation: We are very close to our destination.

faults.quote: Used specifically for drying the body or hands after washing.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding linguistic or usage information.

notes: Unlike 'रुमाल' (rumaal, handkerchief or small face cloth), 'तौलिया' refers to a hand or bath towel. It inflects like a regular '-आ' masculine noun (oblique/plural: तौलिए).

senses.definition: A piece of cloth used for drying the body or hands after washing.

examples.text: नहाने के बाद साफ तौलिया इस्तेमाल करें।
examples.translation: Use a clean towel after bathing.

faults.quote: Mavi is a direct borrowing from Arabic, but it is the standard
faults.why: Etymology is unhelpful filler for an A2 learner.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages that have different native words for light and dark
faults.why: Misleading: Turkish commonly uses a separate word, 'lacivert', for dark/navy blue.

faults.quote: Deniz burada berrak ve masmavi.
faults.why: Uses the derived word 'masmavi' instead of the headword 'mavi'.

notes: Combine with açık (açık mavi, light blue) or koyu (koyu mavi, dark blue) for shades, though very dark or navy blue is usually called lacivert.
The intensive form is masmavi (bright or deep blue).

senses.definition: Having the color of a clear sky or the sea.

examples.text: Bugün gökyüzü çok mavi ve temiz.
examples.translation: Today the sky is very blue and clear.

faults.quote: (person) A person who acts silly or cannot stay still.
faults.why: Transparent figurative use; the example is even a literal simile ('bir maymun gibi').

faults.quote: Used metaphorically to describe someone who is restless, easily distracted, or acting
faults.why: Unnecessary note explaining a universal figurative comparison.

notes: Covers both monkeys and apes; Turkish does not distinguish between them in everyday speech.

senses.definition: An intelligent animal that lives in trees in warm countries, often with a long tail, or a larger tailless primate.

examples.text: Hayvanat bahçesinde maymunlar muz yiyordu.
examples.translation: The monkeys were eating bananas at the zoo.

faults.quote: Used specifically for a written or printed message sent to someone, typically
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the essential consonant mutation (mektubu) and contrast with 'harf'.

notes: Final -p softens to -b- before a vowel suffix: mektubu (the letter), mektuba (to the letter).
Means only a written message sent by mail; a letter of the alphabet is harf.

senses.definition: A written or printed message sent to someone, usually in an envelope by post.

examples.text: Postacı bugün bana bir mektup getirdi.
examples.translation: The postman brought me a letter today.

faults.quote: Used both for the printed list of dishes in a restaurant and
faults.why: Merely repeats the two sense definitions without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Because it ends in a vowel, it takes the buffer consonant -y- before case suffixes (menüyü, menüye) and -s- for the third-person possessive (günün menüsü).

senses.definition: A list of food and drink choices available in a restaurant.

examples.text: Lütfen menüyü getirebilir misiniz?
examples.translation: Could you please bring the menu?

senses.definition: A complete meal or combo offered together at a fixed price.

examples.text: Günün menüsünü alacağım.
examples.translation: I will take the set meal of the day.

faults.quote: Merdiven is used for both permanent architectural stairs in a building and
faults.why: Restates the two senses; a note on how to say go up/down stairs is much more helpful.

notes: Often used in the singular in Turkish where English uses plural 'stairs': merdivenden çıkmak (to go up the stairs), merdivenden inmek (to go down the stairs).

senses.definition: A set of steps for going from one level to another in a building.

examples.text: Merdivenden çıkarken dikkat et.
examples.translation: Be careful while going up the stairs.

senses.definition: A movable piece of equipment with rungs for climbing up or down.

examples.text: Kediyi kurtarmak için merdiven kullandık.
examples.translation: We used a ladder to rescue the cat.

faults.why: Missing the essential everyday sense of duration (a long time, lengthy).

faults.quote: tall, long
faults.why: English does not use 'long' for a person's height.

notes: Used for a person's height ('tall') as well as length and duration; 'groot' is also used for tall people, while 'hoog' is for things like buildings.

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from one end to the other.

examples.text: De straat is erg lang.
examples.translation: The street is very long.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a great amount of time.

examples.text: Het was een lange reis.
examples.translation: It was a long journey.

senses.definition: Of a person: of greater than average height.

examples.text: Mijn broer is erg lang.
examples.translation: Mijn broer is erg lang.

faults.quote: The old train runs very slow.
faults.why: Should use the standard adverb 'slowly' in a learner example.

notes: Like most Dutch adjectives, it can also be used as an adverb ('slowly') without changing form.
When inflected before a noun, the 'aa' becomes a single 'a': 'een langzame trein'.

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or done at a low speed.

examples.text: De oude trein rijdt erg langzaam.
examples.translation: The old train runs very slowly.

faults.quote: (empty) Containing nothing inside. / (vacant) Without people or activity.
faults.why: An empty bottle and an empty street are the same core meaning for A2.

faults.quote: Use 'leeg' to describe something that lacks contents, like a bottle
faults.why: Merely restates the definition while missing the spelling change 'lege' and battery usage.

notes: When inflected before a noun, the 'ee' becomes a single 'e': 'een lege fles'.
Also used for batteries that have run out of power ('mijn batterij is leeg').

senses.definition: Containing nothing or having no people inside; for a battery, out of power.

examples.text: De fles is helemaal leeg.
examples.translation: The bottle is completely empty.

examples.text: Mijn telefoon is bijna leeg.
examples.translation: My phone is almost dead.

faults.quote: ugly; nasty; badly
faults.why: 'badly' is not in any sense's glosses.

faults.quote: Use 'lelijk' to describe things or people that are unpleasant to
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0 without adding useful grammar or usage info.

notes: Notice the pronunciation: the first syllable has a long /eː/, while the ending '-lijk' is unstressed and pronounced /lək/.

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; lacking beauty.

examples.text: Die jas is echt heel lelijk.
examples.translation: That coat is really very ugly.

senses.definition: Unpleasant, unkind, or bad in nature, such as a fall, injury, or remark.

examples.text: Hij heeft een lelijke wond op zijn arm.
examples.translation: He has a nasty wound on his arm.

faults.quote: Mijn vader gaat mij autorijden leren.
faults.why: Unnatural Dutch; with an infinitive it is 'mijn vader leert mij autorijden'.

notes: Means both 'to learn' and 'to teach' (e.g., 'hij leert mij zwemmen' = he teaches me how to swim).
Do not confuse with 'studeren', which means studying at a university or college.

senses.definition: To acquire knowledge or a new skill, or to study for a test.

examples.text: Ik wil graag Nederlands leren.
examples.translation: I would like to learn Dutch.

senses.definition: To give someone knowledge or show them how to do something.

examples.text: Mijn vader leert mij autorijden.
examples.translation: My father is teaching me how to drive.

faults.quote: Used to refer to or address an older sister.
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions of the two senses without adding grammar or usage.
Missing common classifiers (个, 位) and contrast with 妹妹 (younger sister).

notes: The second syllable is pronounced in the neutral tone (jiějie). Unlike English 'sister', Chinese distinguishes between 姐姐 (older sister) and 妹妹 (mèimei, younger sister).
Common classifiers: 个 (gè) or 位 (wèi, polite).

senses.definition: A female sibling who is older than oneself.

examples.text: 我有两个姐姐。
examples.translation: I have two older sisters.

senses.definition: A polite or friendly form of address for a young woman slightly older than the speaker.

examples.text: 姐姐，请问去车站怎么走？
examples.translation: Excuse me, miss, how do I get to the station?

faults.quote: unlike many other Chinese nouns, you do not need a measure word
faults.why: Misleading: no Chinese noun takes a classifier without a determiner or number.

notes: Counted with 杯 (bēi, cup), as in 一杯咖啡 (a cup of coffee).

senses.definition: A drink made from roasted coffee beans, served hot or iced.

examples.text: 我想喝一杯咖啡。
examples.translation: I want to drink a cup of coffee.

examples.text: 你喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？
examples.translation: Do you like to drink coffee or tea?

faults.quote: 车站 explicitly combines 'vehicle' and 'station' to clarify
faults.why: Wordy filler; omits the practical distinction that 站 is used after a transit type.

notes: Covers both bus stops and train stations. To be specific, name the transport followed by 站 (zhàn) or 车站: 公共汽车站 (bus stop), 火车站 (train station), 地铁站 (subway station).

senses.definition: A place where buses or trains stop for passengers to get on and off.

examples.text: 我在车站等公共汽车。
examples.translation: I am waiting for the bus at the bus stop.

examples.text: 请问，去火车站怎么走？
examples.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?

faults.quote: 衬衫 refers generally to shirts and blouses, especially those with buttons
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition and glosses while omitting the required classifier 件 (jiàn).

notes: Takes the classifier 件 (jiàn) for upper-body garments, and is used with the verb 穿 (chuān, to wear). For a T-shirt, use T恤 (T-xù).

senses.definition: A garment for the upper body, typically with a collar, sleeves, and buttons down the front.

examples.text: 他今天穿了一件白衬衫。
examples.translation: He is wearing a white shirt today.

faults.why: Lacks the essential usage note that 考试 is also a separable verb (考完试) and takes 次/场.

notes: Commonly used with 准备 (zhǔnbèi, to prepare for) and 参加 (cānjiā, to take), and counted with 次 (cì) or 场 (chǎng).

senses.definition: A formal test of a person's knowledge or skill in a subject.

examples.text: 明天的考试非常重要，我必须好好准备。
examples.translation: Tomorrow's exam is very important, so I must prepare well.

faults.quote: A chaotic, unorganized, or messy situation.
faults.why: Primarily Belgian Dutch or fixed in idioms ('in de soep lopen'); marginal as standalone noun.

faults.quote: soup; mess
faults.why: 'mess' should be dropped along with the marginal second sense.

faults.quote: Unlike in some languages, 'soep' is not used to describe physical liquids
faults.why: Bizarre and unhelpful comparison that no learner needs.

notes: Dutch speakers generally say 'soep eten' (to eat soup) rather than 'drinken' (to drink).
In the idiom 'in de soep lopen', it means to go wrong or fall through (e.g., 'Onze plannen zijn in de soep gelopen').

senses.definition: A liquid dish, typically served warm, made by cooking vegetables, meat, or fish in water or stock.

examples.text: Ik eet vanavond een kom verse tomatensoep.
examples.translation: I am eating a bowl of fresh tomato soup tonight.

faults.quote: /ˈspɛi.ɣəl/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'ie' in Dutch is pronounced /i/, not /ɛi/ ('ij'/'ei').

faults.quote: Takes the definite article 'de' because it is a common gender noun
faults.why: Restates the headword and gender field.

notes: The plural is 'spiegels'. Note that 'ie' is pronounced like 'ee' in 'see' (/i/).

senses.definition: A piece of glass that reflects an image of whatever is in front of it.

examples.text: Zij kijkt in de spiegel om haar haar te kammen.
examples.translation: She looks in the mirror to comb her hair.

faults.quote: The act or process of spinning yarn or thread.

senses.definition: A small eight-legged creature that spins webs to catch insects.

examples.text: Er zit een grote spin in de hoek van de kamer.
examples.translation: There is a big spider in the corner of the room.

faults.why: Missing the irregular plural with vowel change: 'steden'.

senses.definition: A large urban area where many people live and work, larger than a village.

examples.text: Amsterdam is de grootste stad van Nederland.
examples.translation: Amsterdam is the largest city in the Netherlands.

senses.definition: The commercial center of a town or city, where shops and restaurants are located.

examples.text: We gaan vanmiddag even de stad in om te winkelen.
examples.translation: We are going into town this afternoon to do some shopping.

faults.quote: it is also frequently used as a short form for 'sayuran'

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'buah', which means fruit.
faults.why: Unrelated basic vocabulary; no real risk of confusion.

notes: The derived form 'sayuran' or 'sayur-sayuran' is also very common when referring to vegetables collectively or in general.

senses.definition: A plant or part of a plant eaten as food.

examples.text: Setiap hari ibu membeli sayur segar di pasar tradisional.
examples.translation: Every day mother buys fresh vegetables at the traditional market.

senses.definition: A traditional Indonesian soupy dish made with vegetables, often served with rice.

examples.text: Makan siang hari ini sangat nikmat dengan nasi dan sayur bayam.
examples.translation: Today's lunch is very delicious with rice and spinach soup.

faults.quote: Sedih is the most common word for feeling sad.
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definition without adding useful usage information.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with kecewa, which specifically means 'disappointed'.
faults.why: No reason a learner would confuse 'sedih' and 'kecewa'.

notes: Can refer to a person's feeling ('merasa sedih') or something that causes sadness, such as a sad story ('cerita sedih').

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy or showing sorrow; causing sorrow.

examples.text: Dia merasa sedih karena kehilangan kucingnya.
examples.translation: She feels sad because she lost her cat.

faults.quote: /səhat/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: the first syllable in 'sehat' is /se/ or /sɛ/, not schwa /ə/.

faults.quote: Use 'sehat' when talking about physical health, eating well, or lifestyle habits
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning of 'healthy'.

notes: Can describe both people in good health ('badan sehat') and things that are good for your health ('makanan sehat').

senses.definition: In good physical or mental condition; promoting good health.

examples.text: Makan buah dan sayur setiap hari membuat badan kita sehat.
examples.translation: Eating fruit and vegetables every day keeps our bodies healthy.

faults.quote: Use 'sekarang' to talk about what is happening at this very moment
faults.why: Simply repeats the definitions of the two senses.

faults.quote: now; currently

examples.text: Saya sedang sibuk sekarang.

examples.text: Sekarang banyak orang menggunakan telepon pintar.
examples.translation: Nowadays many people use smartphones.

faults.quote: 'sekolah' can refer to both the building (school) and the act
faults.why: Just repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: school
faults.why: Leaves out the second sense ('schooling').

senses.definition: A place or institution where children and students go to learn.

examples.text: Anak-anak pergi ke sekolah setiap pagi.
examples.translation: Children go to school every morning.

senses.definition: The process of receiving an education at an institution.

examples.text: Dia ingin melanjutkan sekolah ke tingkat universitas.
examples.translation: He wants to continue his schooling to the university level.

faults.quote: The whole family gathers around the cozy dinner meal.

notes: Use 'bữa ăn' when referring to a specific meal (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) rather than food in general ('thức ăn' or 'đồ ăn').

senses.definition: An occasion when people sit down to eat food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

examples.text: Cả nhà quây quần bên bữa ăn ấm cúng.
examples.translation: The whole family gathers around a cozy meal.

faults.quote: Tôi thường ăn phở cho bữa sáng.

senses.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.

examples.text: Bữa sáng là bữa ăn quan trọng nhất trong ngày.
examples.translation: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.

faults.quote: /bɨaw˧˥ toj˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong vowel (/ɨaw/ instead of /ɨə/) and wrong tone on 'bữa' (ngã tone).

faults.quote: Used to refer to the evening meal, which is typically eaten
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful usage information.

senses.definition: The main meal of the day, eaten in the evening.

examples.text: Gia đình tôi thường ăn bữa tối lúc bảy giờ.
examples.translation: My family usually has dinner at seven o'clock.

faults.quote: /bɨə˧ˀ˥ t͡ɕuə˧/
faults.why: Northern Vietnamese 'tr' is pronounced /t͡ɕ/ or /c/, and the vowel in 'trưa' is /ɨə/, not /uə/.

faults.quote: Often shortened to just 'trưa' in casual conversation among friends
faults.why: False claim; people say the verb phrase 'ăn trưa' (eat lunch), not 'trưa' alone for the meal.

senses.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

examples.text: Bữa trưa hôm nay có món gì?
examples.translation: What do we have for lunch today?

faults.quote: /bʊŋm2/
faults.why: Corrupted tone notation ('2' instead of IPA tone marks).

faults.quote: While 'bụng' primarily refers to the physical stomach or belly, it is
