notes: In Vietnamese, the belly ('bụng' or 'lòng') is traditionally seen as the seat of thoughts and feelings, much like 'heart' or 'mind' in English (e.g., 'tốt bụng' means 'kind-hearted', literally 'good-bellied').

senses.definition: The front part of the body below the chest, or the organ inside where food goes.

examples.text: Tôi ăn nhiều quá nên bây giờ đau bụng.
examples.translation: I ate too much, so now my stomach hurts.

senses.definition: A person's inner thoughts, feelings, or intentions.

examples.text: Nghĩ sao nói vậy, đừng để trong bụng.
examples.translation: Say what you think, don't keep it inside your mind.

faults.quote: Use смотреть when you want to describe the general act of looking
faults.why: Restates the glosses; should instead mention aspect pair (посмотреть) and prepositions (на + accusative).

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is посмотреть. Use на + accusative for 'to look at' (смотреть на картину), or a direct object in the accusative for 'to watch' (смотреть фильм).
Do not confuse with видеть ('to see'), which describes the ability or result of seeing rather than the intentional action.

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward something or someone.

examples.text: Не смотри туда!
examples.translation: Don't look over there!

senses.definition: To view something attentively over a period of time, such as a film, show, or match.

examples.text: Мы будем смотреть фильм вечером.
examples.translation: We will watch a movie in the evening.

faults.quote: Деревянные доски могут плавать на воде.
faults.why: Плавать takes в воде, not на воде; Дерево не тонет / плавает в воде is natural.

corrected.shortGloss: to swim; to float; to sail
notes: Multidirectional verb of motion: used for the ability to swim, swimming as an activity, or moving in water without a single direction.
Do not confuse with плыть, which describes swimming, floating, or sailing in one specific direction at a given moment.

senses.definition: To move through water by using body movements.

examples.text: Я люблю плавать в озере летом.
examples.translation: I love swimming in the lake in summer.

senses.definition: To stay on the surface of a liquid without sinking, or (of a boat or sailor) to travel on water.

examples.text: Сухое дерево хорошо плавает в воде.
examples.translation: Dry wood floats well in water.

corrected.shortGloss: to tell; to narrate; to recount
notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is рассказать. Takes the dative for the listener (рассказывать другу) and the accusative or о + prepositional for the topic.
Unlike говорить or сказать ('to say/speak'), рассказывать means telling a story or giving a detailed account.

senses.definition: To give someone an account of an event or share a story in words.

examples.text: Он любит рассказывать интересные истории.
examples.translation: He loves telling interesting stories.

faults.quote: Официант принес меню.
faults.why: Uses the perfective verb принёс (принести) instead of a form of the lemma приносить.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is принести. Note the consonant change in the 1st person singular: я приношу.
Used for bringing something on foot or by hand. For bringing something by vehicle, use привозить; for leading a person or animal here, use приводить.

senses.definition: To carry something here on foot or by hand.

examples.text: Почтальон приносит газеты каждое утро.
examples.translation: The postman brings the newspapers every morning.

senses.definition: To produce or result in a feeling, benefit, or outcome.

examples.text: Эта работа приносит хорошие деньги.
examples.translation: This job brings in good money.

faults.quote: Used when someone moves their body rhythmically to music
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving grammar information like the -овать → -ую conjugation.

notes: Imperfective (perfective: станцевать or потанцевать). Like most -овать/-евать verbs, the suffix changes to -у- in the present tense: я танцую, ты танцуешь.

senses.definition: To move your body rhythmically to music.

examples.text: Мы любим танцевать под живую музыку.
examples.translation: We love dancing to live music.

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'relógio' is used for both a clock
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses and glosses; better to show how to specify each.

notes: To specify which kind, say 'relógio de parede' (wall clock) or 'relógio de pulso' (wristwatch).

senses.definition: A device on a wall or surface that shows what time it is.

examples.text: O relógio da sala está marcando três horas.
examples.translation: The living room clock shows three o'clock.

senses.definition: A small timepiece worn on a strap around the wrist.

examples.text: Ele ganhou um relógio de pulso no aniversário.
examples.translation: He got a wristwatch for his birthday.

notes: In Brazil, 'remédio' is the everyday word for any medicine, pill, or syrup, and is much more common in conversation than 'medicamento'.

senses.definition: A substance or product used to cure or relieve an illness.

examples.text: Preciso tomar um remédio para dor de cabeça.
examples.translation: I need to take some headache medicine.

senses.definition: A way of dealing with a difficult problem or situation.

examples.text: Não vejo outro remédio para esta situação.
examples.translation: I see no other solution for this situation.

faults.quote: cold; sniffles
faults.why: 'sniffles' is not in the sense glosses and is too informal as a main gloss.

notes: Use 'resfriado' for a mild common cold (runny nose, sneezing), and 'gripe' for the flu (with fever and body aches).

senses.definition: A mild, common illness that causes a blocked or runny nose and sneezing.

examples.text: Peguei um resfriado forte e estou espirrando o dia todo.
examples.translation: I caught a bad cold and I've been sneezing all day.

faults.quote: This word is used for any place where you pay
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding learner-specific usage information.

notes: Unlike a 'restaurante', a 'lanchonete' is a casual Brazilian snack bar serving mostly sandwiches, savory snacks ('salgados'), and juices.

senses.definition: A place where you buy and eat prepared meals.

examples.text: Nós vamos jantar em um restaurante italiano hoje à noite.
examples.translation: We are going to have dinner at an Italian restaurant tonight.

faults.quote: It is used primarily for people traveling for pleasure or sightseeing
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the irregular declension (a masculine noun ending in -a).

notes: The feminine form is 'turystka'.
Although masculine, it ends in -a and declines like a feminine noun in the singular (e.g., genitive 'turysty'), with masculine plural forms (nominative plural 'turyści').

senses.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure and interest, especially when on holiday.

examples.text: W lecie miasto jest pełne turystów.
examples.translation: In the summer, the city is full of tourists.

faults.quote: Use 'tutaj' when pointing out or specifying the exact location
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning; fails to note that 'tutaj' covers both location and direction.

notes: Used for both location ('jestem tutaj' — I am here) and direction ('chodź tutaj' — come here).
Interchangeable with 'tu', which is shorter and slightly more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: In or to this place or location.

examples.text: Spotkajmy się tutaj o osiemnastej.
examples.translation: Let's meet here at six o'clock.

notes: Used for physical objects that resist pressure, as well as food that is hard to chew (such as stale bread or tough meat).

senses.definition: Firm and resistant to pressure; not soft to the touch or to chew.

examples.text: Ten materac jest za twardy dla moich pleców.
examples.translation: This mattress is too hard for my back.

senses.definition: Difficult to endure or deal with; harsh or strict.

examples.text: Życie na wsi bywa twarde.
examples.translation: Life in the countryside can be tough.

faults.quote: It is not used for the 'side' of an object or a person's personality
faults.why: False claim: 'twarz' is commonly used figuratively for someone's character/nature ('prawdziwa twarz') or reputation ('stracić twarz').

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'oblicze', which is a literary
faults.why: An A2 learner will not confuse 'twarz' with the literary word 'oblicze'.

notes: Despite ending in a consonant, 'twarz' is a feminine noun (e.g., genitive singular 'twarzy').
It refers to a person's face; for the face of a clock or watch, use 'tarcza'.

senses.definition: The front part of a person's head, from the forehead to the chin.

examples.text: Ona ma bardzo miłą twarz.
examples.translation: She has a very kind face.

faults.quote: When you decline it, the 'e' drops in many forms (e.g., tygodnia).
faults.why: Misleading explanation: 'tydzień' has an irregular stem change to 'tygodni-', not a simple dropped 'e'.

notes: Has an irregular stem in almost all declined forms: 'tygodni-' (e.g., genitive singular 'tygodnia', nominative plural 'tygodnie').
Common time expressions include 'w tym tygodniu' (this week), 'w przyszłym tygodniu' (next week), and 'raz w tygodniu' (once a week).

senses.definition: A period of seven consecutive days, in Poland counted from Monday to Sunday.

examples.text: Mam dużo pracy w przyszłym tygodniu.
examples.translation: I have a lot of work next week.

faults.quote: Used for settlements smaller than a city (مَدِينَة).
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition; the broken plural (قُرًى) is needed instead.

faults.quote: A very small town in the country, typically smaller than a town.
faults.why: Circular wording ('a very small town... smaller than a town').

notes: The plural is قُرًى (quran).

senses.definition: A small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a town.

examples.text: أَعِيشُ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ هَادِئَةٍ.
examples.translation: I live in a small, quiet village.

faults.quote: /matbax/
faults.why: Missing pharyngealization on /tˤ/ (ط is emphatic).

faults.quote: الْطَّبْخُ يَحْدُثُ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing ('Cooking happens in the kitchen') and wrong sukūn on sun-letter article.
Missing the common everyday sense 'cuisine, style of cooking'.

notes: The plural is مَطَابِخ (maṭābiḵ).

senses.definition: The room in a home or restaurant where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: أُمِّي تُعِدُّ الْعَشَاءَ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ.
examples.translation: My mother is preparing dinner in the kitchen.

senses.definition: A style or tradition of cooking, especially of a particular country or region.

examples.text: أُحِبُّ الْمَطْبَخَ الشَّامِيَّ كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: I love Levantine cuisine very much.

faults.quote: Used as a foundational ingredient in many savory dishes across the Arab world.
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia; learners need to know بَصَل is a collective noun (singulative بَصَلَة).

notes: Collective noun referring to onions in general; a single onion is بَصَلَة (baṣala).

senses.definition: A round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste.

examples.text: أُقَطِّعُ الْبَصَلَ بِحَذَرٍ.
examples.translation: I am cutting the onions carefully.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with خَيْمَة (khaymah), which means tent.
faults.why: खَيْمَة does not closely resemble خَاتَم; the broken plural خَوَاتِم is what learners need.

faults.quote: A stamp, seal, or signet used for marking documents
faults.why: In modern Arabic a stamp/seal is خَتْم (ḵatm); خَاتَم is specifically a finger ring.

notes: The plural is خَوَاتِم (ḵawātim).

senses.definition: A small circular band of metal worn on a finger as jewelry or a symbol of marriage.

examples.text: اشْتَرَى خَاتَمًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ لِزَوْجَتِهِ.
examples.translation: He bought a gold ring for his wife.

faults.quote: /waˈra.qa/
faults.why: Wrong stress: three light syllables take initial stress /ˈwa.ra.qa/.

faults.quote: سَقَطَتِ الْوَرَقَةُ السَّوْدَاءُ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ فِي الخَرِيفِ.
faults.why: Example has السَّوْدَاءُ ('black'), which is unnatural for autumn leaves and omitted from translation.
Missing the common everyday sense 'banknote, bill' and/or playing card/ticket.

notes: Singulative noun from the collective وَرَق (waraq, 'paper; foliage'); the plural is أَوْرَاق (ʔawrāq), which also means 'documents' or 'papers'.

senses.definition: A single flat piece of paper used for writing, drawing, or printing.

examples.text: أَعْطِنِي وَرَقَةً وَقَلَمًا لِأَكْتُبَ الرِّسَالَةَ.
examples.translation: Give me a piece of paper and a pen to write the letter.

senses.definition: A single flat, usually green part of a plant growing from a stem or branch.

examples.text: سَقَطَتِ الْوَرَقَةُ الصَّفْرَاءُ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ فِي الْخَرِيفِ.
examples.translation: The yellow leaf fell from the tree in autumn.

senses.definition: A piece of paper money.

examples.text: دَفَعْتُ بِوَرَقَةٍ مِنْ فِئَةِ خَمْسِينَ جُنَيْهًا.
examples.translation: I paid with a fifty-pound note.

faults.quote: It is often used both for physical fitness and for mental
faults.why: Restates the senses already covered in the entry; should mention feminine form instead.

notes: Declines in -ής (masc./fem.), -ές (neuter); plural υγιείς (masc./fem.), υγιή (neuter).

senses.definition: Of a person or body: well and strong, free from illness.

examples.text: Πρέπει να τρώμε φρούτα για να είμαστε υγιείς.
examples.translation: We must eat fruit to stay healthy.

senses.definition: Of a mind, attitude, or system: sensible, balanced, or functioning well.

examples.text: Έχει μια υγιή στάση απέναντι στη ζωή.
examples.translation: He has a healthy attitude toward life.

faults.quote: /enθusiAzˈmenos/
faults.why: Contains uppercase letter 'A' instead of standard IPA '/a/'.

faults.quote: I am very excited with my new car.
faults.why: Calque of Greek 'με'; natural English is 'excited about my new car'.

notes: Commonly followed by με (with/about) or για (about/for) to indicate the cause of excitement.

senses.definition: Feeling very happy, eager, and enthusiastic about something.

examples.text: Είμαι πολύ ενθουσιασμένος με το νέο μου αυτοκίνητο.
examples.translation: I am very excited about my new car.

faults.why: Splitting literal low temperature into 'weather' and 'object' is artificial oversplitting.

faults.quote: Note that 'κρύος' is masculine. The feminine form is 'κρύα'
faults.why: Explaining regular -ος, -α, -ο adjective endings is unnecessary filler.

notes: The neuter form is also used as a noun, το κρύο (the cold), especially in Κάνει κρύο (It is cold).

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm or hot.

examples.text: Το νερό στο ποτήρι είναι κρύο.
examples.translation: The water in the glass is cold.

examples.text: Σήμερα ο καιρός είναι πολύ κρύος.
examples.translation: Today the weather is very cold.

faults.quote: Someone who is frequently jealous in a relationship
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Someone who...').

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who frequently feels jealousy
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage info; missing irregular endings.

notes: Takes the endings -ης (masculine), -α (feminine: ζηλιάρα), and -ικο (neuter: ζηλιάρικο). Also used as a noun.

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling or showing jealousy in relationships or envy of others.

examples.text: Είναι πολύ ζηλιάρης με τη σύντροφό του.
examples.translation: He is very jealous when it comes to his partner.

faults.quote: Τα ρούχα είναι ακόμα στεγνά.
faults.why: Saying laundry is 'still dry' is pragmatically odd compared to 'already dry' or 'dry now'.

notes: Used for things free of water or moisture (e.g., clothes, surfaces), whereas ξηρός is used for naturally dry things (climate, skin, wine, nuts).

senses.definition: Not wet or damp; free from water or moisture.

examples.text: Τα ρούχα είναι επιτέλους στεγνά.
examples.translation: The clothes are finally dry.

faults.quote: An outer garment covering the body from the waist to the ankles
faults.why: Contradicts the note; 'celana' covers shorts and underwear too, not only ankle-length outer garments.

notes: Covers all kinds of lower-body garments with leg openings: 'celana panjang' (long trousers), 'celana pendek' (shorts), and 'celana dalam' (underwear).

senses.definition: A garment covering the lower body from the waist, with a separate part for each leg.

examples.text: Dia memakai celana biru dan baju putih.
examples.translation: He is wearing blue pants and a white shirt.

faults.quote: jealous, envious
faults.why: Romantic jealousy is not 'envious' in English; directly blurs the distinction between the two senses.

notes: Often used with 'pada', 'kepada', or 'terhadap' to indicate the person one is jealous of.
Mainly used for romantic or personal jealousy; for envy of someone's possessions or success, 'iri' is more common.

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy or angry because someone you love might be giving attention to someone else.

examples.text: Dia merasa cemburu ketika pacarnya berbicara dengan perempuan lain.
examples.translation: He felt jealous when his girlfriend talked to another woman.

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy because someone else has something that you want.

examples.text: Jangan cemburu dengan kesuksesan orang lain.
examples.translation: Do not be envious of other people's success.

faults.quote: /tʃepat/
faults.why: The first vowel in 'cepat' is a schwa /ə/, not /e/ (/tʃəˈpat/).
Moving fast and happening in a short time are shades of one meaning.
Missing the common everyday sense 'early; ahead of time' (e.g. datang cepat, jam cepat).

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'awal', which means 'early'
faults.why: 'Cepat' very commonly means 'early' or 'soon' in everyday Indonesian (e.g., tidur cepat, datang cepat).

notes: Frequently used directly as an adverb meaning 'quickly', 'soon', or 'early' (e.g., 'cepat datang' = come quickly/early).

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or done at high speed or in a short time.

examples.text: Dia adalah pelari yang sangat cepat.
examples.translation: He is a very fast runner.

examples.text: Kita butuh solusi cepat untuk masalah ini.
examples.translation: We need a quick solution for this problem.

senses.definition: Happening or arriving before the usual or expected time; ahead of time (of a clock).

examples.text: Hari ini dia pulang lebih cepat dari biasanya.
examples.translation: Today he went home earlier than usual.

faults.quote: Cermin is used for any standard looking glass
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; could instead note that 'kaca' is often used colloquially for mirror.

notes: In everyday conversation, 'kaca' (glass) is also commonly used to mean 'mirror'.

senses.definition: A piece of glass with a shiny metallic backing that reflects images.

examples.text: Dia berdiri di depan cermin sambil merapikan bajunya.
examples.translation: She stood in front of the mirror while tidying her clothes.

senses.definition: Something that clearly shows the nature of a situation, person, or society.

examples.text: Karya seni ini adalah cermin dari budaya masyarakat setempat.
examples.translation: This artwork is a reflection of the local community's culture.

faults.quote: /tʃiŋ.tʃin/
faults.why: Wrong nasal consonant: 'n' before 'c' is alveolar /n/ (or palatal [ɲ]), not velar /ŋ/.

faults.quote: Anything shaped like a circle or a loop.
faults.why: Overbroad and marginal for A2; 'cincin' is specifically a finger ring (or ring-shaped fitting).

senses.definition: A small circular band, typically of precious metal, worn on a finger as jewelry or a token of marriage.

examples.text: Dia memakai cincin emas di jari manisnya.
examples.translation: She is wearing a gold ring on her ring finger.

faults.quote: Unlike 'staircase' in English, which might feel more formal, 계단 is used
faults.why: Repeats note [0] and the glosses without adding useful information.

notes: 계단 refers to a whole staircase or steps in general. Individual steps are counted with 칸 (e.g., 계단 한 칸, 'one step').

senses.definition: A series of steps for going from one level to another.

examples.text: 계단으로 올라가세요.
examples.translation: Please go up the stairs.

examples.text: 이 건물은 계단이 너무 많아요.
examples.translation: This building has too many stairs.

faults.quote: In Korean culture, the word '이모' is also commonly used
faults.why: Merely restates sense [1] while omitting the contrast with 고모 (paternal aunt).

notes: Refers only to your mother's sister; your father's sister is 고모. In family contexts, the honorific form 이모님 is often used.

senses.definition: The sister of one's mother.

examples.text: 주말에 이모 집에 갈 거예요.
examples.translation: I am going to my aunt's house on the weekend.

senses.definition: A friendly term of address for a middle-aged woman, especially one working at a casual restaurant.

examples.text: 이모, 여기 물 좀 주세요!
examples.translation: Excuse me, could we have some water here please!

faults.quote: specific terms based on which side of the family they are from (e.g., 고모사촌, 이모사촌)
faults.why: 고모사촌 and 이모사촌 are non-standard; Korean uses 외사촌, 고종사촌, and 이종사촌.

notes: Often paired with sibling terms to specify age and gender (e.g., 사촌 동생 for a younger cousin, 사촌 형/오빠/누나/언니 for an older one). Maternal cousins are also specifically called 외사촌.

senses.definition: A first cousin; the child of one's uncle or aunt.

examples.text: 사촌 동생이랑 같이 놀았어요.
examples.translation: I played with my younger cousin.

faults.quote: 열을 내리기 위해 물을 마셨어요.
faults.why: 열을 내리다 means bringing down a fever/body heat (sense 0), not physical heat (sense 1).
Missing the everyday homonym meaning 'row; line' (e.g. seating, columns).

notes: To say you have a fever, use the verb 나다: 열이 나요 ('I have a fever'). To take someone's temperature, say 열을 재다.
Do not confuse this with the native Korean number 열 ('ten').

senses.definition: A body temperature that is higher than normal due to illness.

examples.text: 감기에 걸려서 열이 많이 나요.
examples.translation: I caught a cold and have a high fever.

senses.definition: The quality of being hot, or energy in the form of warmth.

examples.text: 이 유리는 열에 강해요.
examples.translation: This glass is resistant to heat.

senses.definition: A straight line of people or things, especially seats or columns.

examples.text: 학생들이 열을 맞춰 서 있어요.
examples.translation: The students are standing in line.

faults.quote: (school) A period during the year when schools are closed.
faults.why: School break and time away from work or school are the same sense.

notes: Often used in the plural ('le vacanze') for a holiday period ('le vacanze estive', 'le vacanze di Natale') and in the phrase 'andare in vacanza' (to go on holiday).
Do not confuse with 'la festa' or 'il giorno festivo', which is a single public holiday on the calendar.

senses.definition: A period of time away from work or school for rest or travel.

examples.text: Quest'estate faremo una lunga vacanza al mare.
examples.translation: This summer we will take a long holiday by the sea.

examples.text: Non vedo l'ora che arrivino le vacanze di Natale.
examples.translation: I can't wait for the Christmas holidays to arrive.

faults.quote: Use 'valigia' for a standard suitcase you take on trips.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful grammar or usage information.
Missing irregular plural 'le valigie' (often misspelled) and common phrase 'fare la valigia'.

notes: The plural is 'le valigie' (retaining the 'i' in standard spelling). Common phrase: 'fare la valigia / le valigie' (to pack one's bags).
Do not confuse with 'il bagaglio' (luggage in general) or 'la borsa' (handbag, shoulder bag, or soft bag).

senses.definition: A case with a handle, used for carrying clothes and personal belongings when travelling.

examples.text: Ho messo tutti i vestiti nella valigia.
examples.translation: I put all the clothes in the suitcase.

faults.quote: It can also refer to a pool or a large tank.
faults.why: Second sentence merely repeats the glosses of sense 1.

notes: In everyday Italian, 'vasca' alone usually means a bathtub (short for 'vasca da bagno'). In swimming, 'fare una vasca' means to swim one length of the pool.

senses.definition: A large container in a bathroom that you fill with water to sit in and wash your body.

examples.text: Ho riempito la vasca di acqua calda.
examples.translation: I filled the bathtub with hot water.

senses.definition: A large open container or basin used to hold liquids or keep fish.

examples.text: I pesci rossi nuotano nella vasca.
examples.translation: The goldfish are swimming in the tank.

faults.quote: Used both for the sister of a parent and for the wife of an uncle.
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim and behaves just like English 'aunt'.
Missing the Italian article rule with singular family members ('mia zia', not 'la mia zia').

notes: Like other singular family members, 'zia' does not take the definite article after a possessive adjective: 'mia zia' (my aunt), not 'la mia zia'. The article is kept in the plural ('le mie zie').

senses.definition: The sister of your father or mother, or the wife of your uncle.

examples.text: Domani vado a trovare mia zia.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to visit my aunt.

faults.quote: In German, 'Küche' has a double meaning: it refers to both
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses already shown in the entry.

notes: Do not confuse 'die Küche' (plural 'die Küchen') with 'der Kuchen' (cake).

senses.definition: The room in a house or apartment where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: Ich verbringe viel Zeit in der Küche.
examples.translation: I spend a lot of time in the kitchen.

senses.definition: A particular style of cooking or regional way of preparing food.

examples.text: Ich mag die italienische Küche sehr.
examples.translation: I really like Italian cuisine.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with 'Kalb', which refers specifically
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'Kuh' and 'Kalb'; this is unhelpful filler.

notes: The plural of 'Kuh' takes an umlaut: 'die Kühe'.

senses.definition: An adult female farm animal kept for milk and meat.

examples.text: Auf der Weide steht eine Kuh.
examples.translation: There is a cow standing in the pasture.

faults.quote: Use 'Landkarte' for printed or physical maps of regions, countries, or cities.
faults.why: 'Landkarte' is for countries or regions; a city map is 'Stadtplan', not 'Landkarte'.

notes: 'Landkarte' refers to a map of a region, country, or the world. A street map of a city or town is called 'der Stadtplan'.
In everyday speech, people often just say 'die Karte'.

senses.definition: A drawing of a country or region showing features like roads, rivers, and cities.

examples.text: Ich habe die Landkarte vergessen.
examples.translation: I forgot the map.

examples.text: Wir haben die Stadt auf der Landkarte gesucht.
examples.translation: We looked for the city on the map.

faults.quote: stairs; ladder; scale
faults.why: Includes 'scale', which is not covered by the senses.

notes: Usually plural ('le scale') for stairs inside a building, and singular ('la scala') for a ladder or a single flight of stairs.

senses.definition: A series of steps for going from one level to another in a building.

examples.text: Salgo le scale con le borse della spesa.
examples.translation: I go up the stairs with the grocery bags.

senses.definition: A movable structure with rungs used for climbing up or down.

examples.text: Ho messo la scala contro il muro per dipingere.
examples.translation: I put the ladder against the wall to paint.

faults.why: Reading handwriting is a shade of reading, not a distinct everyday sense.
Should note that root-stressed 'e' is open /ɛ/ (distinguishing it from 'legge' with /e/).

notes: Irregular past participle: 'letto' (auxiliary 'avere').
Stressed on the first syllable with an open 'e' (/ˈlɛd.dʒe.re/).

senses.definition: To look at written words or symbols and understand their meaning.

examples.text: Mi piace leggere un libro prima di dormire.
examples.translation: I like to read a book before going to sleep.

examples.text: Non riesco a leggere la sua scrittura.
examples.translation: I can't read his handwriting.

faults.quote: light; slight; easy
faults.why: Includes 'easy', which is not covered by the senses.

faults.quote: Used both for physical weight (weighing little) and abstract lightness
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already listed in the entry.

senses.definition: Weighing very little; easy to lift or carry.

examples.text: Questa valigia è molto leggera.
examples.translation: This suitcase is very light.

senses.definition: Of food, drink, or clothing: not heavy, rich, or thick.

examples.text: A pranzo preferisco mangiare qualcosa di leggero.
examples.translation: For lunch I prefer to eat something light.

senses.definition: Not strong or intense; small in degree.

examples.text: C'è un leggero vento oggi.
examples.translation: There is a light wind today.

faults.quote: Used to describe both physical movement and the speed of things
faults.why: Obvious from the definition and works the same way as English 'slow'.

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or working at a low speed.

examples.text: Il traffico è molto lento oggi.
examples.translation: The traffic is very slow today.

faults.why: 'Right there' is just an emphatic use of 'there', not a separate sense.
Should mention the written accent and the interchangeable synonym 'là'.

notes: Always written with an accent mark to distinguish it from the pronoun 'li' (them).
Interchangeable with 'là'; both contrast with 'qui' and 'qua' (here).

senses.definition: In, at, or to that place, away from the speaker.

examples.text: Le chiavi sono lì sul tavolo.
examples.translation: The keys are there on the table.

faults.quote: Eu trabalho com o computador o dia todo.
faults.why: In Portuguese, 'no computador' is much more natural than 'com o computador'.

senses.definition: An electronic machine used for working, studying, and browsing the internet.

examples.text: Eu trabalho no computador o dia todo.
examples.translation: I work on the computer all day long.

faults.why: Party guest and media guest are shades of the same 'invited person' meaning.

notes: Use 'convidado' for someone invited to an event, party, or show. For a guest staying overnight at a home or hotel, use 'hóspede'. The feminine form is 'a convidada'.

senses.definition: A person invited to an event, party, someone's home, or a show.

examples.text: Todos os convidados já chegaram para a festa.
examples.translation: All the guests have already arrived for the party.

faults.quote: /ˈko.pu/
faults.why: Wrong vowel height: 'copo' has an open /ɔ/, pronounced /ˈkɔ.pu/.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'vidrio' (the material glass)
faults.why: 'Vidrio' is Spanish; the Portuguese word for the material glass is 'vidro'.

notes: Use 'copo' for drinking glasses and plastic or paper cups (for mugs or teacups with a handle, use 'xícara' or 'caneca'). Do not confuse it with 'vidro' (the material glass) or 'óculos' (eyeglasses).

senses.definition: A small container without a handle, usually made of glass or plastic, used for drinking liquids.

examples.text: Encha o copo com água gelada.
examples.translation: Fill the glass with cold water.

faults.quote: Use 'coração' both for the physical organ in your chest and as
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses irregular plural 'corações' and shape meaning.

notes: The plural is irregular: 'os corações'. In Brazil, 'coração' is also widely used as an affectionate term like 'sweetheart'.

senses.definition: The organ in the chest that pumps blood through the body, or a symbol representing its shape.

examples.text: O coração bombeia sangue para todo o corpo.
examples.translation: The heart pumps blood to the whole body.

senses.definition: The center of a person's feelings, love, and kindness.

examples.text: Ela tem um bom coração e ajuda todo mundo.
examples.translation: She has a good heart and helps everyone.

faults.quote: The person responsible for delivering letters and packages
faults.why: Metonymic colloquial use; the standard everyday word for mail carrier is 'carteiro'.
Polysemous word with no examples to show how the senses are used.

notes: In Brazil, the post office is often referred to in the plural ('os Correios') after the national postal company. The person who delivers the mail is 'o carteiro' (though people colloquially say 'o correio chegou' when mail is delivered).

senses.definition: The building or official system where letters and parcels are sent and received.

examples.text: Preciso ir ao correio enviar este pacote.
examples.translation: I need to go to the post office to send this package.

senses.definition: Letters and packages sent or delivered through the postal system.

examples.text: Você já olhou se chegou correio hoje?
examples.translation: Have you checked if any mail arrived today?

faults.quote: Dispositivo luminoso que regula el tráfico de vehículos y peatones
faults.why: Definition is written in Spanish instead of English.

senses.definition: A set of red, yellow, and green lights that controls traffic on a road.

examples.text: Mi fermo sempre al semaforo rosso.
examples.translation: I always stop at the red traffic light.

faults.quote: Used for both harmless and venomous snakes, as well as the symbolic
faults.why: Pure filler; instead, note that 'serpente' is masculine despite ending in '-e'.

notes: Masculine despite ending in -e (plural: i serpenti).

senses.definition: A long, legless reptile with a scaly body.

examples.text: Ho visto un serpente nell'erba alta.
examples.translation: I saw a snake in the tall grass.

faults.quote: Soggiorno has two common meanings: the room in a house where you
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with stanza, which is a general bedroom or
faults.why: 'Stanza' means any room, whereas 'camera' is a bedroom; a useful distinction is 'salotto'.

notes: For the room, 'il soggiorno' and 'il salotto' are often used interchangeably, though 'soggiorno' is the everyday living and dining area.

senses.definition: The main room in a house used for sitting, relaxing, and spending time together.

examples.text: La famiglia si riunisce la sera in soggiorno per guardare la televisione.
examples.translation: The family gathers in the living room in the evening to watch television.

senses.definition: A period of time spent staying in a place as a visitor or guest.

examples.text: Il nostro soggiorno a Roma è stato davvero indimenticabile.
examples.translation: Our stay in Rome was truly unforgettable.

faults.quote: Used both for the mental images during sleep and for a strong
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Takes the verb 'fare': 'fare un sogno' (to have a dream).
Do not confuse with 'il sonno' (sleep, sleepiness).

senses.definition: Images and stories that happen in your mind while you sleep.

examples.text: Ho fatto uno strano sogno stanotte.
examples.translation: I had a strange dream last night.

senses.definition: A strong hope, wish, or ambition for the future.

examples.text: Il mio sogno è viaggiare per il mondo.
examples.translation: My dream is to travel around the world.

faults.quote: Used with the masculine article 'il'. In the plural ('soli'), it is
faults.why: Restates gender and gives obvious facts instead of useful collocations like 'c'è il sole'.

notes: Common expressions: 'c'è il sole' (it's sunny), 'prendere il sole' (to sunbathe).

senses.definition: The star that the earth moves around and that gives us light and heat.

examples.text: Il sole scalda la terra.
examples.translation: The sun warms the earth.

senses.definition: The light and warmth that come from the sun.

examples.text: Oggi c'è molto sole in spiaggia.
examples.translation: Today there is a lot of sun at the beach.

notes: A compound word made from 'Σάββατο' (Saturday) and 'Κυριακή' (Sunday); also written in lowercase ('σαββατοκύριακο').

senses.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the two days of the week when most people do not work.

examples.text: Τι σχέδια έχεις για το Σαββατοκύριακο;
examples.translation: What are your plans for the weekend?

faults.quote: This noun can mean both 'foreigner' and 'stranger'
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses already given in the senses.

faults.quote: the adjective form which simply means 'foreign' or 'strange'
faults.why: As an adjective, 'ξένος' means 'foreign' or 'belonging to someone else', not 'strange' ('παράξενος').

notes: The feminine form is 'η ξένη'. It is also used as an adjective meaning 'foreign' or 'someone else's'.

senses.definition: A person from another country.

examples.text: Ο ξένος δυσκολεύεται λίγο με τη γλώσσα.
examples.translation: The foreigner is struggling a bit with the language.

senses.definition: A person you do not know.

examples.text: Δεν πρέπει να μιλάς σε ξένους στον δρόμο.
examples.translation: You must not talk to strangers in the street.

senses.definition: A person who is visiting or being hosted at your home.

examples.text: Έχουμε ξένους στο σπίτι απόψε.
examples.translation: We have guests at home tonight.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'το σακίδιο', which specifically refers to a backpack.
faults.why: Contradicts note 0 ('school backpack') and warns against a word learners won't confuse dynamically.

notes: Used for almost any bag you carry, such as a handbag, schoolbag, or shopping bag.

senses.definition: A container of cloth, leather, or plastic with handles or a strap, used to carry personal items or shopping.

examples.text: Ξέχασα την τσάντα μου στο αυτοκίνητο.
examples.translation: I forgot my bag in the car.

faults.quote: /ta ksiˈlakca/
faults.why: Includes the article 'τα', which must be omitted, and uses non-standard '/kc/' for '/ca/'.

notes: Plural of 'το ξυλάκι' (little stick, diminutive of 'το ξύλο', wood). In the plural, it commonly refers to chopsticks.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used as eating utensils, especially in East Asian cuisine.

examples.text: Τρώω το σούσι με ξυλάκια.
examples.translation: I eat sushi with chopsticks.

senses.definition: Small thin pieces of wood, such as toothpicks, skewers, or ice-cream sticks.

examples.text: Μάζεψα μερικά ξυλάκια από το πάτωμα.
examples.translation: I picked up a few little sticks from the floor.

faults.quote: /pə.la.ˈja.ran/
faults.why: Indonesian 'j' is pronounced /d͡ʒ/, not /j/.

faults.quote: with the prefix 'pe-' and suffix '-an'
faults.why: It uses the circumfix 'per-...-an' (which becomes 'pel-...-an' on 'ajar'), not 'pe-...-an'.

notes: Derived from the root 'ajar' (teach); do not confuse with 'belajar' (to study) or 'mengajar' (to teach).
For a school subject, the fuller term 'mata pelajaran' is also very common.

senses.definition: A period of time when someone is taught something.

examples.text: Pelajaran bahasa Indonesia mulai jam delapan pagi.
examples.translation: The Indonesian language lesson starts at eight in the morning.

senses.definition: An area of knowledge studied in school.

examples.text: Matematika adalah pelajaran yang paling sulit bagi saya.
examples.translation: Mathematics is the most difficult subject for me.

senses.definition: An experience that teaches someone how to behave better in the future.

examples.text: Pengalaman itu menjadi pelajaran berharga untuk masa depan.
examples.translation: That experience became a valuable lesson for the future.

faults.quote: While it originally meant anyone who serves, in modern usage it most
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses instead of giving useful usage or register advice.

notes: Derived from the root 'layan' (to serve, as in 'melayani').

In restaurants, 'pelayan' is used to talk about staff, not to call them; address them as 'Mas' (young man) or 'Mbak' (young woman) instead. For a household worker, 'pembantu' or 'ART' (asisten rumah tangga) is more common.

senses.definition: A person who serves food and drinks in a restaurant or cafe.

examples.text: Pelayan itu membawa menu kepada kami.
examples.translation: The waiter brought the menu to us.

senses.definition: A person employed to perform domestic duties in someone's home or to attend to someone.

examples.text: Dia bekerja sebagai pelayan di rumah besar itu.
examples.translation: She works as a servant in that large house.

faults.quote: Describes someone who feels nervous or uncomfortable around other people.
faults.why: Meta-definition starting with 'Describes someone who' instead of a direct adjective definition.

notes: Can also be used as a noun ('a shy person'). Do not confuse with 'malu' (embarrassed, ashamed, or feeling shy in a specific moment): 'pemalu' describes a lasting personality trait.

senses.definition: Of a person: nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.

examples.text: Dia anak yang pemalu dan jarang berbicara di kelas.
examples.translation: He is a shy child and rarely speaks in class.

faults.quote: short; brief
faults.why: 'brief' is in shortGloss, but there is no sense for duration or briefness, and note[1] contrasts it.

notes: Used for both physical length (opposite of 'panjang', long) and height of people or objects (opposite of 'tinggi', tall/high).
For a short duration or brief message, 'singkat' is more natural (e.g., 'waktu singkat', a short time), though 'pendek' is used in 'cerita pendek' (short story).

senses.definition: Measuring a small distance from end to end.

examples.text: Jalan ini sangat pendek.
examples.translation: This road is very short.

senses.definition: Of a person or thing: of small height.

examples.text: Adik saya masih pendek, belum sampai ke meja itu.
examples.translation: My younger sibling is still short and cannot reach that table yet.

faults.quote: Unlike 'pulpen' (pen), which uses ink, a 'pensil' uses graphite and can
faults.why: Explains the real-world difference between a pen and a pencil rather than linguistic usage.

senses.definition: A thin wooden tool with a graphite core, used for writing or drawing.

faults.quote: When used for people's hair, 'sarı' means blonde.
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'siyah' (black) or 'beyaz' (white).
faults.why: Absurd filler; these words neither sound nor look alike.

faults.quote: The bright colour of a lemon or the sun.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality.

faults.quote: Güneş sarı bir renge sahip.
faults.why: Awkward translationese; 'renge sahip' is unnatural in everyday Turkish.

faults.quote: Having light-coloured or blonde hair.
faults.why: 'Sarı' does not mean blonde-haired of a person (that is 'sarışın'); it modifies 'saç'.

notes: Used of hair ('sarı saç'), it means blond; to describe a blond person, use 'sarışın' instead.
The final 'ı' is an unrounded vowel (/ɯ/), not pronounced like English 'ee'.

senses.definition: Of the colour of a lemon or ripe wheat; (of hair) blond or fair.

examples.text: Ablam sarı bir elbise giydi.
examples.translation: My older sister wore a yellow dress.

examples.text: Onun uzun sarı saçları var.
examples.translation: She has long blond hair.

senses.definition: Of a person's face or complexion: pale and unhealthy-looking.

examples.text: Hasta mısın? Yüzün çok sarı görünüyor.
examples.translation: Are you ill? Your face looks very pale.

faults.quote: Used to refer generally to wine made from fermented grapes.
faults.why: First sentence repeats the definition; misses the crucial consonant voicing rule (şarap -> şarabı).

faults.quote: Akşam yemekte bir kadeh kırmızı şarap içtik.
faults.why: Should be 'akşam yemeğinde' (at dinner), not 'akşam yemekte'.

notes: The final 'p' softens to 'b' before a vowel suffix: 'şarabı' (the wine), 'şarabım' (my wine).
Red wine is 'kırmızı şarap' and white wine is 'beyaz şarap'; a wineglass is 'şarap kadehi'.

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grape juice.

examples.text: Akşam yemeğinde bir kadeh kırmızı şarap içtik.
examples.translation: We drank a glass of red wine at dinner.

faults.quote: and the auxiliary verb söylemek (to say/tell).
faults.why: 'Söylemek' is a lexical verb here, not an auxiliary verb, and note[1] is redundant.

notes: Literally 'to say a song'. When naming a specific song, 'şarkı' is dropped and the song takes the accusative case: 'Bu şarkıyı çok güzel söylüyorsun' (You sing this song very well).

senses.definition: To make musical sounds with the voice.

examples.text: Duşta şarkı söylemek çok keyiflidir.
examples.translation: Singing in the shower is very enjoyable.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with şaşkın, which describes a more permanent state
faults.why: 'Şaşkın' also very commonly describes temporary surprise or bewilderment, not just permanent scatterbrainedness.

notes: Past participle of 'şaşırmak' (to be surprised; to get confused), often used with verbs like 'görünmek' (to look) or 'bakmak' (to look at). 'Şaşkın' is a very common near-synonym.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing surprise because something unexpected happened.

examples.text: Sürprizi görünce çok şaşırmış görünüyordu.
examples.translation: Seeing the surprise, he looked very surprised.

senses.definition: Uncertain about what to do or think; puzzled.

examples.text: Karmaşık talimatları okurken biraz şaşırmış duruyordu.
examples.translation: He looked a bit confused while reading the complicated instructions.

faults.quote: (layer) A layer of something spread over a surface
faults.why: Confuses 'tabak' (plate) with 'tabaka' (layer/sheet).

faults.quote: Yemek masaya sıcak bir tabak çorba koydu.
faults.why: Ungrammatical noun compound; 'dining table' is 'yemek masasına', not 'yemek masaya'.
Needs a note on consonant softening (tabak -> tabağı) before vowels.

notes: The final -k softens to -ğ- when a suffix starting with a vowel is added (e.g., tabağı, tabağa).
Often used as a measure word for a serving of food: bir tabak çorba (a bowl/plate of soup).

senses.definition: A flat, usually round dish that you eat food from or serve food on, or the amount of food it holds.

examples.text: Masaya sıcak bir tabak çorba koydu.
examples.translation: She put a warm bowl of soup on the table.

faults.quote: /taːˈblo/
faults.why: First vowel is not long in Turkish; stress is initial (/ˈtablo/) or final (/tabˈlo/).

faults.quote: in everyday speech it almost always refers to a painting
faults.why: Overstated; 'tablo' for a table/chart in school, work, or apps is completely everyday.

notes: For a piece of furniture ('table'), use masa; tablo is only a painting or a chart/table of information.

senses.definition: A picture made with paint on canvas or another surface and hung on a wall.

examples.text: Duvarlardaki eski tablolar çok güzeldi.
examples.translation: The old paintings on the walls were very beautiful.

senses.definition: An arrangement of information or numbers in rows and columns.

examples.text: Verileri anlaşılır bir tablo halinde hazırladı.
examples.translation: He prepared the data in a clear table.

faults.quote: Taksi is used universally in Turkish for a licensed cab.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages that use distinct native roots for cab and taxi
faults.why: Pure filler offering no practical usage help.

notes: Commonly used in expressions like taksiye binmek (to take/get in a taxi) and taksi çağırmak (to call a taxi).

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: Yağmur başladığı için bir taksi çağırıyorum.
examples.translation: I am calling a taxi because it started raining.

faults.quote: A single page of days, weeks, and months
faults.why: 'Takvim' means calendar; 'calendar page' is 'takvim yaprağı' (as the example itself shows).

faults.quote: calendar; a page of days, weeks and months
faults.why: Includes the false 'calendar page' sense.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical object hanging on the wall and
faults.why: Trivial filler; true of the English word 'calendar' too.

senses.definition: A chart, book, or app showing the days, weeks, and months of a year.

examples.text: Duvara yeni bir takvim astık.
examples.translation: We hung a new calendar on the wall.

faults.quote: Ustalar kırılan sandalyeyi tamir etmek için workshopa götürdü.
faults.why: Uses untranslated English word 'workshopa' instead of Turkish 'atölyeye' or 'tamirhaneye'.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case (-i). The auxiliary verb etmek softens to ed- before suffixes starting with a vowel (e.g., tamir ediyor).
Used for broken objects, machines, and vehicles; for fixing mistakes or tidying things up, use düzeltmek.

senses.definition: To make something broken or damaged work again.

examples.text: Usta kırılan sandalyeyi tamir etti.
examples.translation: The craftsman repaired the broken chair.

faults.quote: Il professore ha scritto la regola sul quadro.
faults.why: False friend with French/Portuguese: a classroom board in Italian is 'la lavagna', never 'il quadro'.

faults.quote: painting; picture; frame; board
faults.why: 'Frame' (cornice) is not a meaning of 'quadro' and is not in the senses.
Lacks the common everyday sense 'overall situation, overview, or description' (e.g. quadro della situazione).

notes: Use 'quadro' for a painting or framed picture on a wall; a classroom blackboard or whiteboard is 'la lavagna', and a picture frame is 'la cornice'.

senses.definition: A picture made with paint on canvas, or a framed picture hung on a wall.

examples.text: Ho comprato un quadro bellissimo per il soggiorno.
examples.translation: I bought a very nice painting for the living room.

senses.definition: A general description or view of a situation.

examples.text: Il medico mi ha fatto un quadro chiaro della situazione.
examples.translation: The doctor gave me a clear picture of the situation.

senses.definition: A panel containing switches, dials, or controls, such as an electrical panel or dashboard.

examples.text: C'è un guasto al quadro elettrico.
examples.translation: There is a fault in the electrical panel.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'la febbre', which means fever.
faults.why: Learners have no reason to confuse 'raffreddore' with 'febbre'; replace with useful collocation 'prendere il raffreddore'.

notes: Common expressions are 'avere il raffreddore' (to have a cold) and 'prendere il raffreddore' (to catch a cold).

senses.definition: A common illness with a runny nose and sneezing.

examples.text: Ho un brutto raffreddore e continuo a starnutire.
examples.translation: I have a bad cold and I keep sneezing.

faults.quote: Often used colloquially to mean 'boyfriend' (il mio ragazzo)
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and wrongly labels the standard word for boyfriend as colloquial.

notes: With a possessive ('il mio ragazzo'), it normally means 'boyfriend'. The plural 'i ragazzi' is used for a mixed group of boys and girls, or to address friends ('Ciao ragazzi!').

senses.definition: A male child, teenager, or young man.

examples.text: Il ragazzo gioca a calcio nel parco.
examples.translation: The boy is playing soccer in the park.

senses.definition: A person's male romantic partner.

examples.text: Questo è il mio ragazzo, Marco.
examples.translation: This is my boyfriend, Marco.

faults.quote: so it takes the article il (or l' before a vowel)
faults.why: A word starting with 'r-' never starts with a vowel and never takes the article 'l''.

faults.quote: Not to be confused with ragna, which means a spiderweb
faults.why: 'Ragna' is rare/archaic; the everyday word to mention is 'la ragnatela' (spiderweb/cobweb).

notes: The letters 'gn' are pronounced like the 'ny' in 'canyon'. A spiderweb is 'la ragnatela'.

senses.definition: A small creature with eight legs that spins webs to catch insects.

examples.text: C'è un ragno grosso sul muro della cucina.
examples.translation: There is a big spider on the kitchen wall.

faults.quote: small town
faults.why: A village is smaller than a town; 'small town' is 小镇.

faults.quote: While '城市' (chéngshì) refers to a city, '村子' is used for
faults.why: Both notes explain what a village is rather than how the Chinese word is used.

notes: The second syllable is spoken in the neutral tone (cūnzi). Counted with 个 (gè) or 座 (zuò).

senses.definition: A small group of houses and other buildings in the countryside, smaller than a town.

examples.text: 这个村子很安静。

faults.quote: or informally to describe someone who behaves very crudely.
faults.why: Restates sense 1.

notes: For a household pet, Italian uses 'l'animale domestico'.

senses.definition: A living creature that can move and feel, not a plant.

examples.text: Il cane è un animale molto fedele.
examples.translation: The dog is a very loyal animal.

senses.definition: A person who behaves in a brutal, cruel, or uncivilized way.

examples.text: Si è comportato come un animale.
examples.translation: He behaved like an animal.

faults.quote: Use 'l'anno' with the preposition 'a' for specific years (nel 2024)
faults.why: 'Nel' is 'in + il', not 'a', and does not use the word 'anno'.

notes: Used with 'avere' to state age: 'Ho vent'anni' (I am twenty years old).
Pronounce the double 'nn' clearly to distinguish 'l'anno' (the year) from 'l'ano' (the anus).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months, or a unit used to measure age.

examples.text: L'anno scorso sono andato in vacanza in Spagna.
examples.translation: Last year I went on vacation to Spain.

faults.quote: /ˈlaːpe/

faults.quote: A small utility vehicle with three wheels.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'capra' (goat) or 'pera' (pear).
faults.why: Arbitrary, unrelated words that learners do not confuse with 'ape'.

notes: Plural: 'le api'. Do not confuse with 'la vespa' (wasp).

senses.definition: A flying insect that makes honey and lives in a hive.

examples.text: Un'ape si è posata sul fiore.
examples.translation: A bee landed on the flower.

faults.quote: जीवन में पैसा ही सब کچھ نہیں होता।
faults.why: Example switches from Devanagari to Perso-Arabic (Urdu) script mid-sentence.

faults.quote: Wealth, riches, or financial resources owned by a person.

faults.why: shortGloss lists 'coin', which is absent from the senses.
Missing note on the very common plural use पैसे (paise) for money/cash.

senses.definition: Coins or notes used to buy things, or financial wealth in general.

examples.text: मेरे पास ज़्यादा पैसे नहीं हैं।
examples.translation: I do not have much money.

examples.text: जीवन में पैसा ही सब कुछ नहीं होता।
examples.translation: Money is not everything in life.

senses.definition: A unit of currency in India and several other countries, equal to one hundredth of a rupee.

examples.text: एक रुपये में सौ पैसे होते हैं।
examples.translation: There are one hundred paise in one rupee.

senses.definition: An official government document that proves your identity and nationality when you travel to other countries.

examples.text: सीमा पार करने के लिए अपना पासपोर्ट दिखाएँ।
examples.translation: Show your passport to cross the border.

faults.quote: Relating to China, its people, or its language.
faults.why: Entry is a feminine noun, but sense 1 defines and exemplifies an adjective.

faults.quote: In the context of food, it is strictly the uncountable noun
faults.why: Notes 0 and 2 mostly restate the definitions and glosses.

notes: चीनी is also used as an invariable adjective meaning 'Chinese' (e.g., चीनी खाना, 'Chinese food').
When referring to a person from China, the noun is masculine (एक चीनी) or used as an adjective before a noun (चीनी व्यक्ति).

senses.definition: A sweet white or brown substance added to food and drinks.

examples.text: चाय में थोड़ी चीनी डालो।
examples.translation: Put a little sugar in the tea.

senses.definition: The language spoken in China, or a person from China.

examples.text: वह थोड़ी चीनी बोल लेता है।
examples.translation: He can speak a little Chinese.

faults.quote: While it falls under the category of accessories or clothes
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler stating obvious facts about rings vs. jewelry.

notes: Plural: अंगूठियाँ (aṅgūṭhiyā̃).

senses.definition: A small round piece of metal, often with a stone, that you wear on your finger.

examples.text: उसने अपनी उंगली में सोने की अंगूठी पहनी है।
examples.translation: She is wearing a gold ring on her finger.

faults.quote: While 'रसोई' (rasoi) refers to the act of cooking
faults.why: False claim: रसोई (f.) is actually the most common everyday word for 'kitchen'.

notes: In everyday speech, the shorter feminine noun रसोई (rasoī) and the English loanword किचन (kican) are very common.

senses.definition: The room in a home where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: मेरी माँ रसोईघर में खाना बना रही हैं।
examples.translation: My mother is cooking food in the kitchen.

faults.quote: /ɐ.paʁ.taˈmẽ.tu/
faults.why: Pretonic 'a' is /a/ in Brazilian Portuguese, not European /ɐ/.

notes: Often shortened informally to 'apê'.

senses.definition: A home on one floor of a larger building.

examples.text: Eu moro em um apartamento no centro da cidade.
examples.translation: I live in an apartment in the city center.

faults.quote: /aˈʁɔs/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'arroz' has a close-mid /o/ (/aˈʁos/ or /aˈʁojs/), not open /ɔ/.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, where rice can be countable or uncountable
faults.why: False claim about English ('rice' is uncountable in both languages) and filler.

notes: Uncountable; use 'um grão de arroz' for a single grain. Commonly paired with beans ('arroz com feijão') at everyday meals.

senses.definition: Small white or brown grains from a cereal plant, cooked and eaten as food.

examples.text: O arroz está quase pronto.
examples.translation: The rice is almost ready.

faults.quote: Used generally for any powered flying vehicle with fixed wings.
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the irregular plural 'aviões' and preposition 'de'.

notes: Plural: 'os aviões'. Use 'de avião' (without an article) to mean 'by plane' (e.g., 'viajar de avião').

senses.definition: A large vehicle with wings that flies through the air and carries passengers or cargo.

examples.text: O avião decolou no horário previsto.
examples.translation: The airplane took off on schedule.

faults.quote: 'avô' (grandfather) is written with a circumflex and has an open, nasal-ish ending
faults.why: False phonetics: the circumflex marks a close-mid oral vowel /o/, neither open nor nasal.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'avô' with 'avo', which means great-grandmother
faults.why: False meaning ('avo' does not mean great-grandmother) and misses the plural 'avós' (grandparents).

notes: Do not confuse with 'a avó' (grandmother, with an open /ɔ/). The masculine plural 'os avôs' refers only to grandfathers, while 'os avós' means 'grandparents'.
Informally shortened to 'vô' or 'vovô'.

senses.definition: The father of someone's father or mother.

examples.text: O meu avô conta histórias antigas todas as noites.
examples.translation: My grandfather tells old stories every night.

faults.quote: While 'banco' is used for both a financial institution and a seat, context
faults.why: Pure filler restating the senses.
Missing the everyday sense of 'stool' or 'car/bicycle seat'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'a banca' (newsstand or market stall).

senses.definition: A financial institution where money is kept, deposited, or borrowed.

examples.text: Preciso ir ao banco sacar dinheiro.
examples.translation: I need to go to the bank to withdraw money.

senses.definition: A long seat for two or more people, or a seat in a vehicle or on a stool.

examples.text: Sentamos no banco da praça para conversar.
examples.translation: We sat on the bench in the square to talk.

faults.quote: (fortune) To show favour or bring good luck to someone.
faults.why: Figurative idiom ('la chance sourit à'), not a separate everyday sense for A2.
Missing irregular conjugation note (conjugated like 'rire', and also used as a noun).

notes: Conjugated like 'rire' (je souris, nous sourions, j'ai souri). Also a masculine noun: 'un sourire' (a smile).
Takes the preposition 'à' before the person you smile at: 'sourire à quelqu'un' (to smile at someone).

senses.definition: To curve the corners of your mouth upwards to show happiness, pleasure or friendliness.

examples.text: Elle commence à sourire quand elle voit ses amis.
examples.translation: She starts to smile when she sees her friends.

faults.quote: (quantity) A large number of times.
faults.why: Artificial split; 'souvent' has one core meaning ('often').

faults.quote: Do not confuse "souvent" (often) with "toujours" (always).
faults.why: No obvious reason for learners to confuse 'souvent' and 'toujours'.

notes: Placed after the conjugated verb in simple tenses ('je vais souvent') and between the auxiliary and past participle in compound tenses ('j'ai souvent pensé').
The final 't' is silent, except in rare formal liaisons.

senses.definition: Many times; on many occasions.

examples.text: Je vais souvent au cinéma le week-end.
examples.translation: I often go to the cinema at the weekend.

faults.quote: Use sucré for foods and drinks that taste of sugar or have added sugar.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding new grammatical or usage information.

notes: Used for sweet food and drink (as opposed to 'salé', savoury/salty). For a 'sweet' person, gentleness or a mild taste, use 'doux'.

senses.definition: Containing sugar or having the taste of sugar.

examples.text: Ce gâteau est très sucré.
examples.translation: This cake is very sweet.

notes: Takes 'de' before a noun or infinitive ('être sûr de quelque chose'), or 'que' before a clause. Common in the phrase 'bien sûr' (of course).
Do not confuse with the preposition 'sur' (on), which is pronounced the same (/syʁ/) but written without the circumflex accent.

senses.definition: Having no doubt about something; confident that something is true.

examples.text: Je suis sûr qu'il va venir.
examples.translation: I am sure he is going to come.

senses.definition: Protected from danger or harm; reliable.

examples.text: Ce quartier est très sûr la nuit.
examples.translation: This neighbourhood is very safe at night.

faults.quote: (caught) Caught in the act of doing something, often secret or forbidden.
faults.why: 'Il a été surpris' is a passive verb form of 'surprendre', not the adjective 'surpris'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with étonné, which is very close in meaning
faults.why: 'Surpris' and 'étonné' are interchangeable in everyday French; telling learners not to confuse them is unhelpful.

notes: The final 's' is silent in the masculine ('surpris' /syʁ.pʁi/) and pronounced /z/ in the feminine ('surprise' /syʁ.pʁiz/).
Followed by 'de' + noun/infinitive, 'par' + noun, or 'que' + subjunctive.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing surprise because something unexpected has happened.

examples.text: Je suis très surpris de te voir ici.
examples.translation: I am very surprised to see you here.

faults.quote: box; chest; cash register; checkout
faults.why: 'chest' is not in any of the entry's senses or glosses.

faults.quote: In a supermarket, 'caja' refers to both the checkout counter
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and is tautological ('checkout counter and the place where you pay').

notes: 'Caja' refers to a rigid container (cardboard, wood, plastic). For a bag, use 'bolsa'.

senses.definition: A rigid container with flat sides, often made of cardboard, wood, or metal, used for storing or carrying things.

examples.text: He guardado los libros en una caja de cartón.
examples.translation: I have stored the books in a cardboard box.

senses.definition: The counter or machine in a shop where a customer pays for their items.

examples.text: Hay mucha cola en la caja del supermercado.
examples.translation: There is a long line at the supermarket checkout.

notes: 'Calle' is used for a street in a town or city with buildings on the sides. For a highway or country road between towns, use 'carretera'.
In addresses, it is often abbreviated as 'C/' (e.g., C/ Mayor, 5).

senses.definition: A public road in a town or city that has buildings on one or both sides.

examples.text: Vivimos en una calle muy tranquila.
examples.translation: We live on a very quiet street.

examples.text: La tienda está al final de la calle.
examples.translation: The shop is at the end of the street.

faults.quote: use 'estoy en la cama' ... just as you would say 'I am in bed'
faults.why: Misses the key grammar point: Spanish requires the definite article ('en la cama'), unlike English ('in bed').

notes: Unlike English ('in bed', 'to bed'), Spanish keeps the definite article in expressions like 'estar en la cama' (to be in bed) and 'irse a la cama' (to go to bed).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a mattress, used for sleeping or resting.

examples.text: He comprado una cama nueva muy cómoda.
examples.translation: I have bought a very comfortable new bed.

notes: In Spain, 'camiseta' is the standard word for a casual T-shirt, a sports jersey, or an undershirt ('camiseta interior'). For a shirt with a collar and buttons, use 'camisa'.

senses.definition: A casual top, usually with short sleeves and no collar, or a sports jersey.

examples.text: Me he puesto una camiseta blanca porque hace calor.
examples.translation: I have put on a white T-shirt because it's hot.

senses.definition: A lightweight piece of underwear worn beneath a shirt.

examples.text: Lleva una camiseta interior debajo de la camisa.
examples.translation: He is wearing an undershirt beneath his shirt.

faults.quote: /1baːt̚35/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA with a stray '1' and numeric tone instead of standardIPA.

faults.quote: In southern Vietnam, this item is commonly called 'tô'

notes: Standard in northern Vietnam; in southern Vietnam, a small eating bowl is called 'chén' (while 'tô' is a larger soup bowl).
Takes the classifier 'cái' when referring to the object itself (e.g., 'một cái bát'), or functions as a measure word for food (e.g., 'một bát cơm' — a bowl of rice).

senses.definition: A small, deep round dish used for holding food such as rice or soup.

examples.text: Mẹ múc cơm đầy một bát.
examples.translation: Mother scooped a full bowl of rice.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'to force / make someone do something'.

faults.quote: to catch; to arrest; to begin

faults.quote: Bắt is a highly versatile verb. While its primary sense is
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already listed in the entry and calls taking a bus 'starting a process'.

corrected.shortGloss: to catch; to arrest; to force
notes: In the sense 'to force', it is followed directly by the person and the action: 'bắt ai làm gì' (to make someone do something).

senses.definition: To capture or grab something that is moving or trying to escape.

examples.text: Anh ấy bắt quả bóng rất nhanh.
examples.translation: He catches the ball very quickly.

senses.definition: To hails or board a public transport vehicle such as a bus or taxi.

examples.text: Tôi cần bắt xe buýt để đến trường.
examples.translation: I need to catch a bus to get to school.

senses.definition: To compel or make someone do something against their wishes.

examples.text: Mẹ bắt tôi đi ngủ sớm.
examples.translation: My mother made me go to bed early.

senses.definition: To take someone into custody, especially by the police.

examples.text: Cảnh sát đã bắt tên trộm đêm qua.
examples.translation: The police arrested the thief last night.

faults.quote: /bəw˨ ʈəj˨/
faults.why: Wrong Hanoi IPA: 'tr' is /tɕ/ (not retroflex /ʈ/), 'ời' has long /əːj/, and 'b' is /ɓ/.

faults.quote: Use 'bầu trời' when talking about the sky as a whole
faults.why: Filler restating the definition without contrasting it with the common synonym 'trời'.

notes: Refers specifically to the physical expanse of the sky; in everyday speech, 'trời' alone is also used for weather, heaven, or impersonal expressions (e.g., 'trời mưa' — it is raining).

senses.definition: The space above the earth where the sun, moon, stars, and clouds appear.

examples.text: Bầu trời hôm nay rất xanh và không có mây.
examples.translation: The sky today is very blue and there are no clouds.

faults.quote: /bəi zəːw/
faults.why: Wrong IPA: 'giờ' has no final /w/, 'b' is /ɓ/, and tone marks are missing.

faults.quote: Used to indicate the present time, equivalent to 'now' in English.
faults.why: Simply repeats the definition and gloss.

notes: Often shortened to 'giờ' in casual speech.
