senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: Bây giờ tôi rất bận.
examples.translation: I am very busy right now.

faults.quote: to fly; to cost (money); to evaporate
faults.why: 'to cost (money)' is not a meaning of 'bay' and is not in the senses.

faults.quote: (money) To disappear or vanish quickly, like vapor or money spent fast.
faults.why: Conflates physical evaporation with colloquial slang for losing money; marginal for A2 compared to core senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to fly; to fade or vanish
notes: Used both for things that fly with wings (birds, planes) and for passengers traveling by air.
Colloquially, 'bay' can also mean that money or possessions have quickly disappeared (e.g., 'bay hết tiền' — all the money is gone).

senses.definition: To move through the air using wings or in an aircraft.

examples.text: Chim đang bay trên trời.
examples.translation: The birds are flying in the sky.

examples.text: Ngày mai tôi bay vào Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am flying to Ho Chi Minh City.

senses.definition: To be carried away in the air, or of a scent, color, or vapor: to fade or evaporate.

examples.text: Gió thổi làm lá khô bay khắp sân.
examples.translation: The wind blew the dry leaves flying all over the yard.

faults.quote: /kăn ˈhộ/
faults.why: Contains Vietnamese orthographic characters and English stress mark instead of valid IPA.

faults.quote: Used to describe a self-contained housing unit in a larger residential building
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

faults.quote: Tôi mới chuyển vào căn hộ mới ở tầng mười.
faults.why: Awkward repetition of 'mới' (just ... new) in a five-word span.

notes: Refers to an individual apartment unit, whereas 'chung cư' refers to the whole apartment building or complex ('căn hộ chung cư').

senses.definition: A set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a larger building.

examples.text: Gia đình tôi vừa chuyển vào một căn hộ ở tầng mười.
examples.translation: My family just moved into an apartment on the tenth floor.

faults.why: 'Need (a noun)' and 'need (to do)' are syntactic patterns of one meaning.

faults.quote: Tôi cần mua một ít đồ ăn ở chợ.
faults.why: Uses 'cần + verb' in the sense meant for 'need (something)' as opposed to sense 1.

notes: Followed directly by a noun ('cần tiền' – to need money) or another verb ('cần đi' – to need to go). Negated as 'không cần' (don't need to).

senses.definition: To require something, or to have to do something, because it is necessary or important.

examples.text: Tôi cần một chút thời gian để suy nghĩ.
examples.translation: I need a little time to think.

examples.text: Bạn cần hoàn thành bài tập này trước ngày mai.
examples.translation: You need to finish this homework before tomorrow.

faults.quote: Căng thẳng can describe both a mental state of stress or anxiety
faults.why: Merely summarizes the two senses already given below.

notes: Can describe both a person feeling stress ('tôi thấy căng thẳng' – I feel stressed) and a thing causing stress ('công việc căng thẳng' – stressful work).

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling worried and under pressure; of a situation: causing worry and pressure.

examples.text: Trước kỳ thi quan trọng, tôi cảm thấy rất căng thẳng.
examples.translation: Before the important exam, I feel very stressed.

senses.definition: Of a situation or relationship: not relaxed or friendly; strained and likely to cause conflict.

examples.text: Mối quan hệ giữa hai nước đang trở nên căng thẳng.
examples.translation: The relationship between the two countries is becoming tense.

faults.quote: Used both to refer to the police force as a whole and
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses the key contrast with 'công an'.

notes: For an individual officer, use the classifier 'người' or a pronoun/title like 'anh', 'chú' ('anh cảnh sát'). In Vietnam, 'công an' (public security) is more commonly used in everyday speech for the local police.

senses.definition: The official organization responsible for maintaining public order and enforcing the law.

examples.text: Cảnh sát đã có mặt tại hiện trường vụ tai nạn.
examples.translation: The police were present at the scene of the accident.

senses.definition: A member of the police force.

examples.text: Anh ấy là một cảnh sát giao thông.
examples.translation: He is a traffic police officer.

faults.quote: /kaːjŋ͡m taːj/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and final consonant for 'cánh', and missing tone marks.

notes: In everyday Vietnamese, 'tay' alone can refer to either the hand or the arm; 'cánh tay' specifically means the arm (as opposed to 'bàn tay', the hand).

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body, from the shoulder to the wrist.

examples.text: Anh ấy bị đau ở cánh tay phải sau khi tập thể thao.
examples.translation: He has pain in his right arm after exercising.

faults.quote: often interchangeable with pullover or jersey.
faults.why: Restates English glosses instead of giving useful Arabic usage or plural form.

notes: Plural: كَنْزَات (kanzāt). Especially common in Levantine usage.

senses.definition: A warm knitted top worn in cold weather.

examples.text: لَبِسَتْ كَنْزَةً صُوفِيَّةً حَمْرَاءَ.
examples.translation: She wore a red woolen sweater.

faults.why: Missing the common modern sense 'computer mouse' (usually in the feminine form فَأْرَة).

notes: Broken plural: فِئْرَان (fiʾrān). The feminine form فَأْرَة (faʾra) is used for a female mouse, a single mouse, or a computer mouse.

senses.definition: A small rodent with a pointed snout, rounded ears, and a long thin tail.

examples.text: رَأَيْتُ فَأْرًا صَغِيرًا تَحْتَ الطَّاوِلَةِ.
examples.translation: I saw a small mouse under the table.

senses.definition: A small hand-held device moved across a surface to control the cursor on a computer screen (usually in the feminine form فَأْرَة).

examples.text: تَوَقَّفَتْ فَأْرَةُ الحَاسُوبِ عَنِ العَمَلِ.
examples.translation: The computer mouse stopped working.

faults.quote: Used to refer to stairs or steps in a building,
faults.why: Restates the definition without explaining the singulative دَرَجَة or plural أَدْرَاج.

notes: Collective noun referring to a whole flight of stairs (plural: أَدْرَاج, ʾadrāj). A single step is دَرَجَة (daraja).

senses.definition: A set of steps for going from one level to another in a building.

examples.text: اصْعَدِ الدَّرَجَ بِهُدُوءٍ.
examples.translation: Go up the stairs quietly.

faults.quote: Refers primarily to vegetable oil or olive oil used in cooking,
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses instead of giving grammar information like the plural.

notes: Uncountable; the plural زُيُوت (zuyūt) is used for different types of oil. Specifically for crude petroleum, نِفْط (nifṭ) is preferred.

senses.definition: A smooth, thick liquid made from plants, used in cooking.

examples.text: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى زَيْتٍ لِقَلْيِ البَطَاطِسِ.
examples.translation: I need oil to fry the potatoes.

senses.definition: A thick liquid derived from petroleum, used to lubricate engines or as fuel.

examples.text: يَجِبُ تَغْيِيرُ زَيْتِ السَّيَّارَةِ.
examples.translation: The car's oil needs to be changed.

faults.quote: /saˈjaːra/
faults.why: Missing consonant gemination (/jj/) required by the shadda on ي.

faults.quote: Used commonly for any standard passenger vehicle.
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler; learners do not confuse 'car' with 'bus'.

notes: Sound feminine plural: سَيَّارَات (sayyārāt).

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: اشْتَرَى أَبِي سَيَّارَةً جَدِيدَةً لَوْنُهَا أَحْمَرُ.
examples.translation: My father bought a new red car.

faults.quote: In Spain and many other countries, bread is an essential daily item
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia that offers no linguistic or grammatical help.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'pan' with 'panadero', which is the person
faults.why: Unnecessary warning; beginners do not confuse root words with agent derivatives.
Should note that 'pan' is uncountable for bread in general (unlike loaves).

notes: Usually uncountable; to ask for a single loaf in Spain, use 'una barra de pan'.

senses.definition: A basic food made by baking a mixture of flour, water, and yeast.

examples.text: Voy a la panadería a comprar pan recién hecho.
examples.translation: I am going to the bakery to buy freshly baked bread.

faults.quote: Used both for the thin material you write on and for
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the first two senses.

notes: In the sense of official documents or ID, it is almost always used in the plural ('los papeles').

senses.definition: A thin material made from plant pulp, used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

examples.text: Necesito una hoja de papel para apuntar tu número.
examples.translation: I need a sheet of paper to write down your number.

senses.definition: A character played by an actor in a play or film, or the part someone plays in a situation.

examples.text: Ella consiguió el papel principal en la película.
examples.translation: She got the main role in the film.

senses.definition: An official document containing legal, personal, or administrative information, usually in the plural.

examples.text: Tienes que firmar estos papeles antes de salir.
examples.translation: You have to sign these papers before leaving.

notes: Does not change form in the plural: 'un paraguas' (one umbrella), 'dos paraguas' (two umbrellas).

senses.definition: A folding object with a cloth cover that you hold over your head to stay dry in the rain.

examples.text: Lleva el paraguas porque va a llover.
examples.translation: Take the umbrella because it is going to rain.

faults.quote: Use 'parque' for both a public green space and a children's
faults.why: Restates the two senses directly.

faults.quote: Los niños juegan al fútbol en el parque.
faults.why: Playing football fits a general park, not a playground with play structures.

notes: False friend: do not confuse with English 'to park' or 'car park' ('el aparcamiento' or 'el parking' in Spain).

senses.definition: A public area with grass and trees in a town or city for walking and relaxing.

examples.text: Vamos a dar un paseo por el parque esta tarde.
examples.translation: Let's go for a walk in the park this afternoon.

senses.definition: An outdoor area equipped with swings, slides, and other structures for children to play on.

examples.text: Llevé a los niños a los columpios del parque.
examples.translation: I took the children to the swings at the playground.

faults.quote: /pasapoɾte/
faults.why: Missing primary stress mark in the IPA transcription.

faults.quote: Don't confuse this with 'el pasaje', which means 'ticket'
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; 'pasaporte' is a transparent cognate of English 'passport'.

senses.definition: An official document issued by a government that identifies a citizen for international travel.

examples.text: Tengo que renovar mi pasaporte para el viaje del próximo mes.
examples.translation: I have to renew my passport for next month's trip.

faults.quote: While 'moeilijk' can mean both 'difficult' (a hard task) and 'hard' (a solid object)
faults.why: False claim: 'moeilijk' never means physically solid ('hard').

faults.quote: Requiring a lot of effort or skill; complicated.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are identical shades of the same meaning.

notes: For the English word 'hard', use 'moeilijk' when it means 'difficult' (a hard task) and 'hard' when it means 'solid' or 'loud' (a hard stone, a hard sound).
Often used in the phrase 'moeilijk doen' (to make a fuss / be difficult).

senses.definition: Not easy to do, understand, or deal with; requiring a lot of effort or skill.

examples.text: Dit is een erg moeilijke vraag.
examples.translation: This is a very difficult question.

examples.text: Hij heeft een moeilijke opdracht gekregen.
examples.translation: He has been given a difficult task.

faults.quote: /mɔi̯/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: Dutch 'ooi' has a long tense /oː/, so /moːi̯/.

faults.quote: Moọi is the standard word
faults.why: Contains a corrupt Vietnamese character 'ọ' with an underdot.

faults.quote: Moọi is the standard word for both 'beautiful' and 'nice'
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and senses without adding grammar or usage help.

notes: For weather, experiences, or food, Dutch speakers also very often use 'lekker' (nice, pleasant, tasty) where English uses 'nice'.

senses.definition: Very pleasant to look at or listen to.

examples.text: Wat een mooie jurk heb je aan.
examples.translation: What a beautiful dress you are wearing.

senses.definition: Pleasant, enjoyable, or favourable.

examples.text: We hebben morgen mooi weer.
examples.translation: We are having nice weather tomorrow.

faults.quote: The early part of the day, from sunrise to noon.
faults.why: Part-of-speech mismatch: 'de morgen' (morning) is a noun, not an adverb.

notes: As a noun ('de morgen'), it also means 'morning', especially in fixed expressions like ''s morgens' (in the morning) and 'Goedemorgen!' (Good morning!), though 'de ochtend' is more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: On the day after today.

examples.text: Morgen heb ik een belangrijk tentamen.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I have an important exam.

faults.quote: Liquid used as food, especially a broth or gravy.
faults.why: Part-of-speech mismatch and marginal sense: 'het nat' is a noun, not an adjective.

faults.quote: wet; liquid
faults.why: As an adjective, 'nat' means 'wet' or 'rainy', not 'liquid'.

faults.quote: Used to describe objects, clothing, or weather covered in liquid
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the spelling rule that inflected form doubles the 't' ('natte').

notes: The inflected form doubles the 't' to keep the vowel short: 'natte' (e.g. 'natte kleren').
Do not confuse with 'vochtig', which means slightly wet ('damp' or 'humid') rather than thoroughly wet.

senses.definition: Covered or soaked in water or another liquid; rainy.

examples.text: Mijn jas is helemaal nat door de regen.
examples.translation: My coat is completely wet from the rain.

faults.quote: Use 'nee' to give a negative answer, refuse an offer
faults.why: Repeats the definition word for word.

faults.quote: no; refusal or disagreement
faults.why: 'refusal or disagreement' is a meta-description, not a translation of 'nee'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'niet' (not, used to negate verbs or adjectives) or 'geen' (no / not any, used before nouns: 'Ik heb geen tijd').

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer or to express refusal or disagreement.

examples.text: Wil je nog koffie? — Nee, dank je.
examples.translation: Do you want more coffee? — No, thank you.

faults.quote: /donduɾˈma/
faults.why: The noun meaning 'ice cream' has stress on the penult (/donˈduɾma/), while the verbal noun has final stress.

faults.quote: Etin dondurma işlemi birkaç saat sürer.
faults.why: Unnatural Turkish phrasing; native speakers say 'Eti dondurma işlemi' (accusative) or 'Et dondurma işlemi'.

faults.quote: Traditional Maraş dondurması has a famously chewy and elastic texture
faults.why: Cultural trivia rather than a linguistic note; a note on stress distinction is needed instead.

notes: Comes from 'dondurmak' (to freeze). When meaning 'ice cream', stress is on the middle syllable (don-DUR-ma); when meaning the act of freezing or 'don't freeze!', stress is on the last syllable (don-dur-MA).

senses.definition: A sweet frozen food made from milk or cream, sugar, and flavorings.

examples.text: Sıcak yaz gününde vanilyalı dondurma yedik.
examples.translation: We ate vanilla ice cream on a hot summer day.

senses.definition: The act of freezing something or making it solid with cold.

examples.text: Sebzeleri dondurma işlemi oldukça kolaydır.
examples.translation: The process of freezing vegetables is quite easy.

faults.quote: /dyːˈɟyn/
faults.why: 'ğ' between two front rounded vowels is pronounced [j] or elided (/dyˈjyn/ or /dyˈyn/), never [ɟ].

notes: 'Düğün' refers to the celebratory party or reception, whereas 'nikâh' refers to the official legal marriage ceremony. A couple often has a 'nikâh' at a municipal office and a separate 'düğün' for guests.
Do not confuse with 'evlilik', which refers to the state of being married or marriage as an institution.

senses.definition: A ceremony and celebratory party marking the marriage of two people.

examples.text: Yazın yapılan düğünler çok eğlenceli olur.
examples.translation: Weddings held in the summer are a lot of fun.

faults.quote: /dycˈkan/
faults.why: Because of the circumflex on 'â', the second 'k' is also palatalized: /dycˈcan/.

faults.quote: sometimes written simply as 'dukkan' in informal contexts.
faults.why: Even without the circumflex, it is written 'dükkan' (with 'ü'), not 'dukkan', unless typing on an ASCII keyboard.

notes: Used for smaller, independent shops and workshops, whereas 'mağaza' refers to a larger retail store or department store.
The circumflex on 'â' shows that the preceding 'k' is pronounced soft (palatalized); in informal writing it is often omitted ('dükkan').

senses.definition: A small building or room where goods or services are sold to the public.

examples.text: Mahallemizdeki küçük dükkândan taze ekmek aldık.
examples.translation: We bought fresh bread from the small shop in our neighborhood.

faults.quote: /døn/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'ü' is /y/ (/dyn/), whereas /døn/ is 'dön' (turn).

faults.quote: Do not confuse dün (yesterday) with yarın (tomorrow).
faults.why: 'Dün' and 'yarın' do not look or sound alike; a note on 'dün gece' vs 'bu gece' is much more useful.

notes: Combines directly with parts of the day: 'dün sabah' (yesterday morning), 'dün akşam' (yesterday evening), 'dün gece' (last night).

senses.definition: On the day before today.

examples.text: Dün hava çok güzeldi.
examples.translation: The weather was very nice yesterday.

faults.quote: /dynˈja/
faults.why: In this Arabic loanword, the final 'a' is long: /dynˈjaː/.

faults.quote: (planet) The earth and all its countries, peoples... / (society) Human society
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 both define 'world' as human society/people, and their examples do not distinguish planet Earth from society.

faults.quote: Used both for the planet as a physical body and for the human world
faults.why: Merely restates the senses.

notes: Capitalized as 'Dünya' when referring to planet Earth as an astronomical body, and takes an apostrophe before suffixes (e.g., Dünya'nın).
Because it ends in a vowel, it takes the buffer consonant 'y' before vowel-initial suffixes (e.g., dünyayı, dünyaya).

senses.definition: The earth together with all its countries, peoples, and human society.

examples.text: Dünyayı gezip görmek istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to travel and see the world.

senses.definition: The planet on which we live; the third planet from the sun.

examples.text: Dünya, Güneş'in etrafında döner.
examples.translation: The Earth revolves around the Sun.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the sea.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality.
Missing helpful note that 'azul' does not change for gender (azul/azules).

notes: The form 'azul' is the same for masculine and feminine nouns; the plural is 'azules'.

senses.definition: Of the colour of a clear sky or the sea.

examples.text: Hoy el cielo está muy azul.
examples.translation: Today the sky is very blue.

faults.quote: note the accent mark on the 'i' in forms like bailía
faults.why: Confusing and unnecessary filler; 'bailía' is an archaic noun, not a verb form.

faults.quote: Do not confuse bailar (to dance) with volar (to fly)
faults.why: Filler note; 'bailar' and 'volar' are not commonly confused.

senses.definition: To move one's body rhythmically to music.

examples.text: Me gusta bailar salsa con mis amigos los fines de semana.
examples.translation: I like to dance salsa with my friends at the weekend.

faults.why: Missing everyday sense 'low in amount, level, price, or volume' (e.g. precios bajos, voz baja).

faults.quote: Remember that 'bajo' changes to 'baja' when referring to a feminine noun.
faults.why: Explains standard regular adjective agreement without adding word-specific value.

notes: When describing people, 'bajo' means short in height. Do not confuse it with 'corto', which means short in length or duration (una película corta, el pelo corto).

senses.definition: Of a person: of small height.

examples.text: Mi hermano es muy bajo.
examples.translation: My brother is very short.

senses.definition: Not high or tall; close to the ground.

examples.text: El techo es bastante bajo en esta habitación.
examples.translation: The ceiling is quite low in this room.

senses.definition: Small in amount, level, intensity, or volume.

examples.text: Habla en voz baja, por favor.
examples.translation: Speak in a low voice, please.

examples.text: En invierno las temperaturas son muy bajas.
examples.translation: In winter the temperatures are very low.

faults.quote: Use 'barato' to describe things that cost little money
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: It changes to 'barata' with feminine nouns.
faults.why: States basic regular adjective inflection.

notes: Also commonly used as an adverb with verbs like 'salir' or 'costar' (e.g. 'Me salió barato' — It worked out cheap for me).

senses.definition: Costing little money; low in price.

examples.text: Compré unos zapatos muy baratos en el mercado.
examples.translation: I bought some very cheap shoes at the market.

faults.quote: (swallow) To swallow a liquid intentionally or physically.
faults.why: Duplicates sense 0; 'beber' does not mean 'to swallow' (tragar) as a distinct sense.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'beber' with 'comer', which is the verb for eating solids.
faults.why: Trivial distinction that just restates the basic vocabulary meanings.

notes: In Spain, 'beber' is the normal everyday word for drinking any liquid, whereas in Latin America 'tomar' is much more common.

senses.definition: To take liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.text: Es importante beber mucha agua durante el día.
examples.translation: It is important to drink plenty of water during the day.

senses.definition: To drink alcohol, especially regularly.

examples.text: Hoy no bebo porque tengo que conducir.
examples.translation: I'm not drinking today because I have to drive.

faults.quote: Used both as a polite or affectionate term for an older woman
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; further, addressing a stranger as бабушка is not always polite.

notes: Addressing an elderly woman you do not know as «бабушка» can sound overly familiar or rude; it is safer to avoid it in direct address.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Моя бабушка живёт в деревне.
examples.translation: My grandmother lives in the countryside.

senses.definition: An elderly woman (colloquial).

examples.text: Добрая бабушка угостила детей конфетами.
examples.translation: The kind old woman treated the children to candy.

faults.quote: (media) A periodical publication containing articles and stories.
faults.why: False friend: магазин never means a periodical; that is журнал, as the example's note admits.

faults.quote: Он купил новый музыкальный журнал.
faults.why: Example uses журнал instead of the headword магазин.

faults.quote: shop; magazine
faults.why: Includes false friend 'magazine' (gun magazine is technical, print magazine is wrong).
Should warn learners about the false friend 'magazine' (which is журнал in Russian).

notes: False friend: «магазин» means a shop or store, not a printed magazine (which is «журнал»).Takes «в» + accusative for going to a shop («в магазин») and «в» + prepositional for being at a shop («в магазине»).

senses.definition: A place where goods are sold to the public.

examples.text: Я иду в магазин за хлебом.
examples.translation: I am going to the shop for bread.

faults.quote: In Russian culture, the uzhin is typically the main meal
faults.why: Traditionally обед (midday meal) is considered the main meal, though ужин is the evening meal.

notes: «Ужин» is always the evening meal; do not confuse it with «обед», which is the midday meal (lunch/dinner), even when «обед» is the largest meal of the day.
With meal names, Russian uses the preposition «на»: «на ужин» (for dinner), «после ужина» (after dinner).

senses.definition: The meal eaten in the evening.

examples.text: Мы готовим ужин дома.
examples.translation: We are cooking dinner at home.

faults.quote: Used for any room in a house or apartment. It is very
faults.why: Pure filler explaining what the English word 'room' already means; misses hotel room distinction.

notes: For a hotel room, Russian normally uses «номер» rather than «комната».

senses.definition: A separate part of the inside of a building, enclosed by walls, a floor, and a ceiling.

examples.text: Моя комната очень светлая.
examples.translation: My room is very bright.

faults.quote: Я иду домой.
faults.why: Uses the adverb домой instead of the noun дом (or adverb дома).

notes: Irregular plural: «дома́» (stress on the last syllable). Do not confuse this with the adverb «до́ма» (at home, stress on the first syllable) or «домо́й» (homeward, going home).

senses.definition: A building in which people live, whether a single-family house or an apartment block.

examples.text: Мы купили новый дом.
examples.translation: We bought a new house.

senses.definition: The place where one lives and feels one belongs.

examples.text: Здесь мой дом и моя семья.
examples.translation: My home and my family are here.

faults.why: Missing the standard measure word 件 (jiàn) for clothing, essential for A2 learners.

notes: The measure word is 件 (jiàn): 一件大衣.
Refers to a long, heavy winter coat, whereas 外套 (wàitào) is a general term for any jacket or coat.

senses.definition: A long, warm coat worn over other clothes in cold weather.

examples.text: 外面很冷，记得穿上大衣。
examples.translation: It's very cold outside; remember to put on your overcoat.

notes: 秋天 is the standard everyday word for autumn; 秋季 (qiūjì) is used in more formal contexts.

senses.definition: The season between summer and winter when the weather turns cool.

examples.text: 秋天的树叶变黄了。
examples.translation: The leaves have turned yellow in autumn.

faults.quote: An establishment that sells alcoholic drinks, often with food.
faults.why: Archaic/historical sense ('tavern/wine shop'); modern Mandarin uses 酒吧 for pub/bar.

notes: The measure word is 家 (jiā): 一家酒店.
Despite containing 酒 ('alcohol'), in modern Chinese 酒店 means 'hotel' (especially a larger or more upscale one, similar to 宾馆), not a bar (酒吧). For a small, budget guesthouse, 旅馆 is used.

senses.definition: A building where travellers pay to stay in rooms, often with a restaurant and other services.

examples.text: 这家酒店的服务非常好。
examples.translation: The service at this hotel is very good.

faults.why: Lacks examples for a core A1/A2 word with two distinct senses, and omits neutral tone note.

notes: The second syllable 子 is pronounced in the neutral tone (zi). The measure word is 个 (gè).
To specify gender, use 男孩 (nánhái, 'boy') or 女孩 (nǚhái, 'girl').

senses.definition: A young person who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: 公园里有很多孩子在玩。
examples.translation: There are many children playing in the park.

senses.definition: A person's son or daughter of any age.

examples.text: 他们有两个孩子，一个儿子和一个女儿。
examples.translation: They have two children, a son and a daughter.

faults.quote: 我们赶上了红绿灯。
faults.why: Ambiguous and unnatural phrasing; unclear whether it means catching a green light or hitting a red.

notes: Literally 'red-green light'. To talk about a specific signal, use 红灯 (hóngdēng, 'red light') or 绿灯 (lǜdēng, 'green light').

senses.definition: A set of red, yellow, and green lights at road intersections that control traffic.

examples.text: 请在前面的红绿灯往左拐。
examples.translation: Please turn left at the traffic light ahead.

faults.quote: 'Machigai o okonaimashita' (I made a mistake).
faults.why: Ungrammatical and unnatural Japanese; 間違いをする or 間違える is used, never 間違いを行う.

faults.quote: It differs from 'misuteru' (to fail)
faults.why: 見捨てる (misuteru) means 'to abandon', not 'to fail' (which is 失敗する or ミスをする).

faults.quote: (accident) Something done wrong by accident, without intending to cause an error.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning; 'blunder' is just a shade.

faults.quote: mistake; error; accident
faults.why: Contains 'accident', which is a distinct sense not covered properly in the entry.

notes: To say 'make a mistake', use the verb 間違える (machigaeru) or the phrase 間違いをする (machigai o suru).
Often used in the pattern 間違いありません (machigai arimasen) to mean 'there is no doubt' or 'that is correct'.

senses.definition: Something done or thought incorrectly; an error or fault.

examples.text: 計算に間違いがありました。
examples.translation: There was a mistake in the calculation.

examples.text: それは間違いです。
examples.translation: That is a mistake.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading ゆうびんきょく for a kanji headword.

notes: In Japan, post offices are easily identified by the red '〒' symbol on signs and mailboxes, and most also offer banking and ATM services.

senses.definition: A public building where you can send letters and packages and buy stamps.

examples.text: 郵便局で手紙を出します。
examples.translation: I will send a letter at the post office.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading こううん for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: (state) The state of being fortunate or having good things happen
faults.why: Oversplit of a single meaning; sense 1 just shows its na-adjective usage and glosses.

faults.quote: 幸運 (kōun) refers to the state or quality of having good luck
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage info like its na-adjective function.

notes: Also used as a na-adjective (幸運な, kōun na) meaning 'lucky' or 'fortunate'.
Distinguish from 幸せ (shiawase), which focuses on personal happiness and emotional well-being rather than luck.

senses.definition: Good luck or favorable circumstances that bring a good result.

examples.text: 宝くじに当たったのはすごい幸運だ。
examples.translation: Winning the lottery is incredible good luck.

examples.text: 良い友人に恵まれるのは幸運なことです。
examples.translation: It is fortunate to be blessed with good friends.

faults.quote: Used for all kinds of plants, from tiny garden flowers to
faults.why: Purely restates the definition.

notes: Unlike 植木 (ueki) or 観葉植物 (kan'yō shokubutsu, 'houseplant'), 植物 is the general and scientific term for any plant.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in soil or water and has leaves or roots, such as a tree, flower, or grass.

examples.text: 部屋に植物を置くと癒されます。
examples.translation: Putting plants in my room is soothing.

examples.text: この植物は水をたくさん必要とします。
examples.translation: This plant needs a lot of water.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading ちず for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: 地図 is used for both physical paper maps and digital maps
faults.why: Trivial filler note; English 'map' works the exact same way.

senses.definition: A drawing or image of an area that shows streets, buildings, or landmarks to help you find your way.

examples.text: 駅の地図を見ています。
examples.translation: I am looking at a map of the station.

faults.quote: Used for someone who lives nearby, usually in the same building
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; missing useful note on the feminine counterpart पड़ोसिन.

notes: The plural stays पड़ोसी, becoming पड़ोसियों before a postposition.
Can refer to a neighbor of any gender, though पड़ोसिन exists specifically for a female neighbor.

senses.definition: A person who lives next door or very close to your home.

examples.text: मेरे पड़ोसी बहुत अच्छे हैं।
examples.translation: My neighbors are very nice.

faults.quote: you might also hear 'aasn' for a seat on the floor
faults.why: Unhelpful and badly romanized ('aasn'); better to note plural formation (कुर्सियाँ).

faults.quote: chair
faults.why: Does not cover the second sense (political seat/office).

notes: The final long -ई shortens in the plural: कुर्सियाँ (chairs), कुर्सियों (before a postposition).
Also spelled कुरसी.

senses.definition: A seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.

examples.text: वह कुर्सी पर बैठा है।
examples.translation: He is sitting on the chair.

senses.definition: A position of political power or authority.

examples.text: उसने अपनी कुर्सी बचाने के लिए समझौता किया।
examples.translation: He made a compromise to save his seat.

faults.quote: the internal organ is sometimes referred to as 'आमाशय'
faults.why: Medical jargon (आमाशय) is not useful at A2; common everyday expressions with पेट are better.

notes: Used in common expressions like पेट भरना (to get full) and पेट खराब होना (to have an upset stomach).

senses.definition: The front part of the body between the chest and the hips, or the organ where food is digested.

examples.text: मेरे पेट में दर्द है।
examples.translation: I have a stomachache.

examples.text: खाना खाकर मेरा पेट भर गया।
examples.translation: I am full after eating.

faults.quote: you can say 'पंजों' (panjō - toes/front of foot)
faults.why: पंजों is the oblique plural, not the lemma (पंजा), and rather than পंजा/तलवा, learners need टाँग (leg).

examples.text: Мы остановились на светофоре.
examples.translation: We stopped at the traffic light.

faults.quote: Са́хар is used for both the white granulated sweetener and sugar
faults.why: Filler note; misses that it is uncountable and can take partitive genitive -у.

notes: Uncountable (singular only). In spoken Russian, the partitive genitive form са́хару is often used alongside са́хара for 'some sugar'.

senses.definition: A sweet white or brown substance added to food and drinks to make them sweet.

examples.text: Ты пьёшь чай с сахаром или без?
examples.translation: Do you drink tea with or without sugar?

faults.why: Missing note on irregular stress shift in accusative singular (ру́ку) and nominative plural (ру́ки).

notes: Russian uses рука́ for both the hand and the arm; Кисть specifically means 'hand' (from the wrist down) when precision is needed.
Stress shifts to the stem in the accusative singular (ру́ку) and nominative/accusative plural (ру́ки), but returns to the ending in other plural cases (рука́ми, в рука́х).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers, used for holding things.

examples.text: Мы вымыли руки перед обедом.
examples.translation: We washed our hands before lunch.

senses.definition: The entire upper limb of the human body from the shoulder to the wrist.

examples.text: Он несёт спящего ребёнка на руках.
examples.translation: He is carrying the sleeping child in his arms.

faults.why: Missing essential preposition note: takes на (на рабо́те / на рабо́ту).

notes: Takes the preposition на for location and direction: на рабо́те ('at work'), идти́ на рабо́ту ('to go to work'), с рабо́ты ('from work').

senses.definition: Mental or physical effort done to achieve something or make something.

examples.text: У меня сегодня очень много работы.
examples.translation: I have a lot of work today.

senses.definition: Regular paid employment, or the place where one works.

examples.text: Я ищу новую работу в центре города.
examples.translation: I am looking for a new job in the city center.

senses.definition: A specific task, assignment, or piece of work created by someone.

examples.text: Учитель проверил наши контрольные работы.
examples.translation: The teacher checked our test papers.

faults.quote: /bɐ̃ˈjɐi.ru/
faults.why: Wrong IPA for Brazilian Portuguese; should be /bɐ̃ˈɲej.ɾu/.

faults.quote: The room in a house that contains a shower, sink, and toilet.
faults.why: Too narrow; excludes public restrooms despite the gloss and note.

notes: In Brazil, 'banheiro' is the standard word for both a bathroom at home and a public restroom.
Do not confuse with 'banheira' (bathtub).

senses.definition: A room with a toilet and sink, and in a home usually a shower or bath.

examples.text: O banheiro fica no final do corredor.
examples.translation: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.

faults.why: Missing note that 'o bebê' stays masculine even when referring to a baby girl.

notes: Grammatically masculine ('o bebê') even when referring to a baby girl.
Written with a circumflex accent in Brazil (plural: 'bebês'), unlike European 'bebé'.

senses.definition: A very young child, especially one that cannot yet walk or talk.

examples.text: O bebê está dormindo no berço.
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping in the crib.

faults.quote: cake; bun; mass
faults.why: 'Bun' is not in the senses and 'bolo' does not mean 'bun'.

faults.quote: A shapeless mass or cluster of things pressed together.
faults.why: Informal sense not essential for A2, while common idioms like 'dar um bolo' exist.

faults.quote: When referring to a small bread roll or a sweet bun, regional
faults.why: Confusing note contrasting 'bolo' with bread rolls and biscuits.

notes: In informal Brazilian Portuguese, 'dar um bolo em alguém' means to stand someone up (miss a planned meeting).

senses.definition: A sweet food made from flour, sugar, eggs, and other ingredients, baked in an oven.

examples.text: Ela preparou um bolo de chocolate para a festa.
examples.translation: She made a chocolate cake for the party.

faults.quote: /ˈbow.zu/
faults.why: Wrong consonant in IPA; the 's' in 'bolso' is voiceless /s/, not /z/.

faults.quote: A small bag or pouch, often with a strap, used for carrying
faults.why: False sense (Spanish interference); 'bolso' does not mean handbag in Portuguese, contradicting note[0].

notes: Do not confuse with 'a bolsa', which means 'bag', 'handbag', or 'purse'.

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into or onto clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: Coloquei as chaves no bolso da calça.
examples.translation: I put the keys in my pants pocket.

faults.quote: Ho lasciato il telefono sulla cucina.
faults.why: 'Sulla cucina' means on the stove; 'in the kitchen' is 'in cucina'.

notes: Used for both landline and mobile phones, though 'cellulare' is also common for a mobile phone.

senses.definition: A device used for talking to people who are in another place.

examples.text: Ho lasciato il telefono in cucina.
examples.translation: I left the phone in the kitchen.

faults.quote: In Italian, 'il tempo' does double duty for both 'time'
faults.why: Restates the two senses; better to distinguish 'tempo' from 'volta' and 'ora'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'la volta' (time as an occasion, e.g., 'tre volte' = 'three times') or 'l'ora' (clock time, e.g., 'Che ora è?' = 'What time is it?').

senses.definition: Measured or available time, or the passage of days, hours, and minutes.

examples.text: Non ho tempo oggi.
examples.translation: I don't have time today.

senses.definition: The conditions outside at a particular time, such as sun, rain, wind, or cold.

examples.text: Che tempo fa oggi?
examples.translation: What is the weather like today?

faults.quote: roof; ceiling; limit
faults.why: 'Ceiling' in shortGloss misleads learners into thinking it means a room's ceiling ('soffitto').

notes: Use 'tetto' for the outside top covering of a building. For the inside upper surface of a room (ceiling), use 'soffitto'.

senses.definition: The top covering of a building that protects it from rain and sun.

examples.text: I gatti camminano sul tetto della casa.
examples.translation: The cats are walking on the roof of the house.

senses.definition: A maximum limit placed on prices, expenses, or quantities.

examples.text: Il governo ha deciso di mettere un tetto ai prezzi dell'energia.
examples.translation: The government has decided to put a cap on energy prices.

faults.quote: A small hand-held device used to control a computer screen.
faults.why: In Italian of Italy, a computer mouse is called 'il mouse', not 'il topo'.

faults.quote: For a rat, Italians use 'ratto'.
faults.why: In everyday Italian, 'topo' (or 'topo di fogna') is commonly used for rats too.

notes: In everyday speech, 'topo' is used for both mice and rats (though 'ratto' also exists for a rat). A computer mouse is called 'il mouse', never 'il topo'.

senses.definition: A small rodent with pointed snout and a long thin tail.

examples.text: Ho visto un topo correre sotto il divano.
examples.translation: I saw a mouse run under the sofa.

faults.quote: (vehicles) A line of carriages on rails.
faults.why: Sense 1 is identical to sense 0 ('a railway train').

notes: Use 'prendere il treno' for catching or taking a train, and 'in treno' for travelling by train.

senses.definition: A railway vehicle made of connected carriages that carries passengers or goods along a track.

examples.text: Il treno parte dal binario tre.
examples.translation: The train leaves from platform three.

faults.quote: arm; handle
faults.why: 'handle' is not covered in the senses; senses only cover 'arm' and 'armrest'.

faults.quote: The side part of a piece of furniture
faults.why: Usually 'accoudoir' in everyday French; 'bras' for an armchair is marginal at A2.

faults.quote: For the hand alone, use 'la main'.
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'arm' and 'hand'; omits silent final -s and identical plural.

notes: The final '-s' is silent, and the singular and plural forms are identical ('un bras', 'des bras').

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body extending from the shoulder to the hand.

examples.text: Il porte son sac sous le bras.
examples.translation: He is carrying his bag under his arm.

faults.quote: In French, 'bureau' means both the piece of furniture (desk)
faults.why: Restates the senses and glosses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'magasin' or 'boutique'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'bureau' with shops; misses the irregular plural 'bureaux'.

notes: The plural is formed by adding '-x': 'des bureaux' (pronounced the same as the singular).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat surface used for writing, reading, or working.

examples.text: Mon ordinateur portable est posé sur mon bureau.
examples.translation: My laptop is on my desk.

senses.definition: A room or building where business or professional work is done.

examples.text: Je commence à travailler au bureau à neuf heures.
examples.translation: I start working at the office at nine o'clock.

faults.why: Needs to note that the final '-s' is pronounced and contrasting 'bus' with 'car'.

notes: Unlike in many French words, the final '-s' is pronounced (/bys/).
Used for city transport; for long-distance coaches between towns, 'le car' is usually used.

senses.definition: A large motor vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route, especially in a city.

examples.text: Je prends le bus pour aller au travail tous les matins.
examples.translation: I take the bus to go to work every morning.

faults.quote: Use 'cadeau' for any physical item given as a present
faults.why: Restates the definition and is overly restrictive; omits the '-x' plural.

notes: The plural is formed by adding '-x': 'des cadeaux' (pronounced the same as the singular).

senses.definition: Something given to someone willingly, without payment, to make them happy or celebrate an occasion.

examples.text: Elle a ouvert son cadeau avec enthousiasme.
examples.translation: She opened her gift with enthusiasm.

faults.quote: In French, 'le café' refers both to the drink itself
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

notes: In France, ordering just 'un café' gets you a small espresso; for coffee with milk, ask for 'un café au lait' or 'un café crème'.

senses.definition: A hot, dark drink made from roasted coffee beans.

examples.text: Je bois un café tous les matins.
examples.translation: I drink a coffee every morning.

senses.definition: A small restaurant or bar where drinks and light meals are served.

examples.text: Nous nous retrouvons au café du coin pour discuter.
examples.translation: We are meeting at the corner cafe to chat.

faults.why: Both senses mean 'to begin/start'; sense 0's first example is intransitive like sense 1.

faults.quote: It is often contrasted with 'bitirmek' (to finish)
faults.why: The direct intransitive counterpart of 'başlamak' is 'bitmek'; 'bitirmek' is the transitive counterpart of 'başlatmak'.

notes: Takes the dative case (-a/-e) for the thing or activity started: 'okula başlamak' (to start school), 'çalışmaya başlamak' (to start working).
Intransitive in grammar; to say 'to start something (up)', use the causative 'başlatmak'. Its opposite is 'bitmek' (to end/finish).

senses.definition: To begin to happen, or to start doing something.

examples.text: Ders saat dokuzda başlayacak.
examples.translation: The lesson will begin at nine o'clock.

examples.text: Yeni bir işe başladım.
examples.translation: I started a new job.

faults.quote: Used for any thick bed cover that keeps you warm.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful linguistic or cultural distinction (e.g. vs. 'yorgan').

notes: Refers to a woven or fleece blanket; a thick quilted duvet or comforter is called 'yorgan'.

senses.definition: A warm woven cover used on a bed or around the body.

examples.text: Soğuk gecelerde battaniye altında kitap okumayı severim.
examples.translation: I like reading books under a blanket on cold nights.

faults.quote: /baˈzen/
faults.why: Stress is on the first syllable with a long vowel: /ˈbaːzen/.

faults.quote: Use bazen when something happens on some occasions, but not all
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the non-final stress and long first vowel.

notes: Pronounced with stress and a long vowel on the first syllable (/ˈbaːzen/), not the last.

senses.definition: On some occasions, rather than all the time.

examples.text: Bazen kahve yerine çay içiyorum.
examples.translation: Sometimes I drink tea instead of coffee.

examples.text: Akşamları bazen yürüyüşe çıkarız.
examples.translation: In the evenings we sometimes go for a walk.

faults.quote: Used for cutting food or other materials, typically with a sharp
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the consonant alternation (bıçak -> bıçağı) before vowels.

notes: Final 'k' softens to 'ğ' before a vowel suffix: 'bıçağı' (the knife, accusative / his knife).

senses.definition: A tool with a sharp blade and a handle, used for cutting.

examples.text: Ekmek kesmek için keskin bir bıçak gerekiyor.
examples.translation: A sharp knife is needed to cut bread.

faults.quote: The dark circular opening in the center of the eye
faults.why: Means 'pupil' only in the compound 'göz bebeği', not as standalone 'bebek'.

faults.quote: In addition to meaning a human baby, 'bebek' is also used
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of noting the 'k' to 'ğ' consonant softening.

notes: Final 'k' softens to 'ğ' before a vowel suffix: 'bebeği' (the baby / her doll).
For an older child (roughly toddler to teenager), use 'çocuk'.

senses.definition: A very young child, especially one not yet able to walk or talk.

examples.text: Bebek bütün gece uyumadı.
examples.translation: The baby didn't sleep all night.

senses.definition: A child's toy made to look like a small person or baby.

examples.text: Çocuk yeni bebeğiyle oynuyor.
examples.translation: The child is playing with her new doll.

faults.quote: In Hindi, 'चॉकलेट' is almost always treated as a feminine noun.
faults.why: Restates the gender field without adding useful grammar information.

faults.quote: Be aware that this is a loanword from English
faults.why: Obvious filler; does not explain the special vowel symbol 'ॉ'.

faults.quote: मुझे दूध वाली चॉकलेट बहुत पसंद है।
faults.why: Calque of 'milk chocolate'; Hindi speakers say 'मिल्क चॉकलेट' or simply 'चॉकलेट'.

notes: The symbol 'ॉ' represents the English open 'o' sound /ɔ/, used mainly in English loanwords.
Unmarked in the singular and direct plural (दो चॉकलेट); takes -ओं in the oblique plural (चॉकलेटों में).

senses.definition: A sweet brown food or candy made from cocoa.

examples.text: मुझे चॉकलेट बहुत पसंद है।
examples.translation: I really like chocolate.

faults.quote: Used for both physical boundaries (like between countries) and abstract limits
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Plural: सीमाएँ (direct), सीमाओं (oblique).
Common collocations: सीमा पार करना (to cross a border/limit), सीमा तय करना (to set a limit).

senses.definition: The official dividing line between two countries or regions.

examples.text: भारत और पाकिस्तान की सीमा पर सुरक्षा बहुत सख्त है।
examples.translation: Security is very strict at the border between India and Pakistan.

senses.definition: The furthest point or degree to which something can go or is allowed.

examples.text: मेरी सहनशीलता की भी एक सीमा होती है।
examples.translation: There is a limit even to my patience.

faults.quote: use the word 'सीढ़ी' (singular) or 'लद्दा' instead.
faults.why: 'लद्दा' does not mean ladder in standard Hindi; this teaches a false word.
Senses 0 and 1 are the same meaning ('stairs/steps') split unnecessarily.

notes: Plural of सीढ़ी. Used in the plural for a flight of stairs or steps, whereas singular सीढ़ी means a single step or a portable ladder.
Oblique plural: सीढ़ियों (as in सीढ़ियों पर, 'on the stairs').

senses.definition: A set of steps leading from one level of a building or place to another.

examples.text: वह सीढ़ियाँ चढ़कर ऊपर गया।
examples.translation: He went upstairs by climbing the stairs.

examples.text: सीढ़ियों पर ध्यान से चलो।
examples.translation: Walk carefully on the steps.

faults.quote: This word is borrowed from Arabic and is very widely used
faults.why: Etymology and frequency filler instead of useful plural morphology.

notes: Plural: किताबें (direct), किताबों (oblique).
The synonym पुस्तक (also feminine) is used in more formal or literary contexts.

senses.definition: A set of written or printed pages bound together inside a cover.

examples.text: मैं एक नई किताब पढ़ रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am reading a new book.

faults.why: In textbooks and school, 'lesson' and 'chapter' are the same sense of पाठ; 'class' is कक्षा.

faults.quote: lesson; chapter; reading
faults.why: 'reading' is in shortGloss, but there is no sense for reading/recitation.

faults.quote: In Hindi, the word 'पाठ' is used both for a chapter
faults.why: Just repeats the senses.

notes: For a school lesson or textbook unit, पाठ and सबक़ are synonyms; for a class period or classroom session, use क्लास or कक्षा.
Common collocations: पाठ पढ़ाना (to teach a lesson, also figuratively), पाठ करना (to recite a religious text).

senses.definition: A unit of instruction or a numbered chapter in a textbook; something to be learned.

examples.text: आज का पाठ बहुत रोचक था।
examples.translation: Today's lesson was very interesting.

examples.text: अगला पाठ घर से पढ़कर आना।
examples.translation: Read the next chapter at home before coming.

senses.definition: The reading aloud or recitation of a text, especially a religious scripture.

examples.text: दादी रोज़ सुबह रामायण का पाठ करती हैं।
examples.translation: Grandmother recites the Ramayana every morning.

faults.quote: For a smaller administrative division, use 'daerah'.
faults.why: Learners actually confuse 'negara' (sovereign state) with 'negeri' (homeland/country) and 'bangsa' (nation/people).

notes: Refers to a sovereign political state. Compare 'negeri' (country as a homeland, or state in Malaysia) and 'bangsa' (nation as a people).
In compounds, it often translates as 'state' or 'national', as in 'kepala negara' (head of state).

senses.definition: A territory with its own government and borders.

examples.text: Indonesia adalah negara kepulauan.
examples.translation: Indonesia is an archipelagic country.

senses.definition: The government and public institutions of a country.

examples.text: Dia bekerja untuk negara.
examples.translation: He works for the state.

faults.quote: /ˈnənɛk/
faults.why: First vowel is /e/ (or [ɛ]), not schwa /ə/: /ˈnenɛk/ or /ˈnɛnɛʔ/.

faults.quote: Used as both a kinship term for a grandmother and
faults.why: Notes restate the two senses and lack the common shortened vocative form 'Nek'.

notes: Often shortened to 'Nek' when addressing someone directly, and also used in place of 'you' when speaking politely to an elderly woman.
Some families use 'oma' (from Dutch) for grandmother instead.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Nenek saya tinggal di desa.
examples.translation: My grandmother lives in the village.

senses.definition: A polite term of address or reference for an elderly woman.

examples.text: Mari saya bantu, Nek.
examples.translation: Let me help you, ma'am.

faults.quote: A chemical substance used for a specific purpose, such as photography
faults.why: Archaic or restricted to fixed compounds (e.g. 'obat nyamuk', 'obat bedil'), not a general beginner sense.

faults.quote: Obat is the general word for any medicine, pill, or
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of noting the collocation 'minum obat' (literally 'drink medicine').

notes: To say 'take medicine', Indonesian uses the verb 'minum' (to drink), even for solid pills: 'minum obat'.
Also appears in everyday compounds for household chemicals or treatments, such as 'obat nyamuk' (mosquito repellent) and 'obat gigi' (toothpaste, informal).

senses.definition: A pill, liquid, or other substance taken to treat an illness or injury.

examples.text: Saya harus minum obat tiga kali sehari.
examples.translation: I have to take medicine three times a day.

faults.quote: In Indonesian, 'orang asing' is a compound noun used for both
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses without explaining the literal components or the informal alternative 'bule'.

notes: Literally 'foreign/unfamiliar person', from 'orang' (person) + 'asing' (foreign, strange).
In everyday speech, Western foreigners are very often called 'bule' (informal) rather than 'orang asing'.

senses.definition: A person from another country.

examples.text: Banyak orang asing mengunjungi pulau itu setiap tahun.
examples.translation: Many foreigners visit that island every year.

senses.definition: A person whom one does not know.

examples.text: Jangan bicara dengan orang asing di jalan.
examples.translation: Do not talk to strangers on the street.

faults.quote: Use 'minuut' when talking about time on the clock or duration.
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning; English speakers do not confuse 'minuut' and 'moment'.

notes: Plural: 'minuten' (spelled with one 'u' because the syllable is open).

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.

examples.text: Wacht even, ik ben over één minuut klaar.
examples.translation: Wait a moment, I will be ready in one minute.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a female parent.
faults.why: First sentence repeats the definition; note[1] introduces a less common derivative.

notes: In casual speech and when addressing one's own mother, 'mama' or 'mam' is usually used.

senses.definition: A female parent of a child or children.

examples.text: Mijn moeder werkt in een ziekenhuis.
examples.translation: My mother works in a hospital.

faults.quote: frequently used metaphorically for openings of containers or rivers.
faults.why: False: 'monding' is used for rivers, 'opening'/'hals' for containers; 'bek' is the needed contrast.

faults.quote: The wide opening of a river where it flows into the sea.
faults.why: In everyday Dutch a river mouth is 'de monding'; 'mond' here is formal or in place names.

notes: Used for people; for animals, use 'de bek' (using 'bek' for a person is rude).
The final '-d' is pronounced /t/, but becomes /d/ in the plural 'monden'.

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Doe je mond open en zeg 'aa'.
examples.translation: Open your mouth and say 'ah'.

faults.quote: In Dutch, just like in English, 'muis' is used for both
faults.why: Restates the two senses without adding grammar or usage information.

faults.quote: Klik met de muis op het scherm om te openen.
faults.why: Missing an object for 'openen' and 'op het scherm' sounds unnatural with a mouse.

notes: Plural: 'muizen' (the 's' changes to 'z').

senses.definition: A small furry rodent with a pointed nose and a long tail.

examples.text: De kat vangt een kleine muis in de tuin.
examples.translation: The cat catches a small mouse in the garden.

senses.definition: A small handheld device used to move the cursor on a computer screen.

examples.text: Klik met de muis op het pictogram om het bestand te openen.
examples.translation: Click the icon with the mouse to open the file.

faults.quote: A factory where coins are made.
faults.why: Coin factory is a rare, specialized sense not needed at A2.

faults.quote: Munt is a homonym in Dutch. It means both physical money
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving useful grammar or usage advice.

faults.quote: Ik heb geen enkele munt bij me voor de winkelmand.
faults.why: Shopping baskets do not take coins; shopping carts ('winkelwagentjes') do, usually taking 'een muntje'.

notes: In everyday speech, the diminutive 'het muntje' is very often used for a single coin.

senses.definition: A small, flat, round piece of metal used as money.

examples.text: Heb je een munt van één euro voor het winkelwagentje?
examples.translation: Do you have a one-euro coin for the shopping cart?

senses.definition: An aromatic herb with green leaves, used in cooking and tea.

examples.text: Verse munt in de thee smaakt erg lekker.
examples.translation: Fresh mint in the tea tastes very good.

faults.quote: It is a versatile word, so if you are at a cafe
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions; umlaut plural 'die Gäste' is missing.

faults.quote: in a restaurant, hotel, or shop.
faults.why: Shop customers are 'Kunden', not 'Gäste'; 'Gast' applies to hospitality.

notes: Plural: 'die Gäste'.
In a restaurant, bar, or hotel, paying customers are called 'Gäste', whereas in a shop they are 'Kunden'.

senses.definition: A person invited to visit someone's home or attend a social event.

examples.text: Wir erwarten heute Abend einen Gast zum Essen.
examples.translation: We are expecting a guest for dinner this evening.

senses.definition: A paying customer in a restaurant, café, bar, or hotel.

examples.text: Der Kellner bringt dem Gast die Speisekarte.
examples.translation: The waiter brings the customer the menu.

faults.why: Needs a note on the fixed expression 'Geburtstag haben' (without article) vs English 'it is my birthday'.

notes: To say when someone's birthday is, German uses 'Geburtstag haben' without an article: 'Ich habe heute Geburtstag' (It's my birthday today).
Common birthday wishes are 'Alles Gute zum Geburtstag!' and 'Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!'.

senses.definition: The anniversary of the day on which a person was born.

examples.text: Ich habe heute Geburtstag.
examples.translation: It is my birthday today.

examples.text: Wann hast du Geburtstag?
examples.translation: When is your birthday?

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'Großvater' used in compound words;
faults.why: Nonsensical filler note; meanwhile the umlaut plural 'Großväter' is not mentioned.

notes: Plural: 'die Großväter'.
In everyday family life, people almost always use the affectionate 'der Opa' (grandpa).

senses.definition: The father of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Mein Großvater erzählt mir oft Geschichten aus seiner Kindheit.
examples.translation: My grandfather often tells me stories from his childhood.

faults.why: 'Hase' is a weak masculine noun (n-declension: 'den Hasen'), as seen in the second example.
