Strictly means 'hare', while 'das Kaninchen' is 'rabbit', but in everyday speech 'Hase' is widely used for pet rabbits and the Easter Bunny ('der Osterhase').

senses.definition: A fast-running wild animal with long ears and strong hind legs, larger than a rabbit.

examples.text: Der Hase sprang schnell über das Feld.
examples.translation: The hare jumped quickly across the field.

senses.definition: In everyday speech, a rabbit, especially kept as a pet.

examples.text: Die Kinder füttern den kleinen Hasen mit Gras.
examples.translation: The children feed the little rabbit grass.

faults.quote: In the US, this season is called 'fall', while in the UK
faults.why: Note 0 explains English dialects and Note 1 repeats the definition; neither teaches German usage (e.g. 'im Herbst').

notes: Like all seasons in German, it is masculine and used with 'im' (= in dem) to mean 'in autumn': 'im Herbst'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between summer and winter.

examples.text: Im Herbst werden die Blätter bunt und fallen von den Bäumen.
examples.translation: In autumn, the leaves turn colorful and fall from the trees.

faults.quote: (knowledge) To know or understand something thoroughly and clearly.
faults.why: Entry is a noun; this sense is a literary verb/adjective and confuses POS.

faults.quote: Anh ấy hiểu tường tận mọi chuyện.
faults.why: Uses the compound word 'tường tận' instead of standalone 'tường'.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'tường' refers to a vertical structure like a wall.
faults.why: Restates the definitions; should instead give the common classifier 'bức'.

notes: Takes the classifier 'bức' (bức tường).

senses.definition: A vertical structure that divides or encloses a room, building, or area.

examples.text: Bức tường phòng khách được sơn màu trắng.
examples.translation: The living room wall is painted white.

faults.why: Corrupt IPA string; should be /ɗuə˦ˀ˥/.

faults.quote: Always used as a pair for eating Asian cuisine
faults.why: Encyclopedic filler; should explain classifiers 'đôi' (pair) and 'chiếc' (single).

notes: Takes the classifier 'đôi' for a pair (một đôi đũa) and 'chiếc' for a single chopstick (một chiếc đũa).

senses.definition: Thin sticks used in pairs as eating utensils.

examples.text: Tôi dùng đũa để ăn cơm.
examples.translation: I use chopsticks to eat rice.

faults.quote: /ɗʊŋ35/
faults.why: Uses digits instead of standard IPA tone letters and lacks labial-velar coarticulation.

faults.quote: Used both as an adjective meaning correct or accurate
faults.why: Restates the senses.

notes: Commonly used in 'đúng giờ' (on time) and 'đúng rồi!' (that's right!).

senses.definition: Free from error; in accordance with fact or truth.

examples.text: Câu trả lời của bạn rất đúng.
examples.translation: Your answer is completely right.

senses.definition: Precisely matching a time, amount, or person.

examples.text: Hãy đến đúng giờ nhé.
examples.translation: Please arrive right on time.

faults.quote: Used to describe the physical posture of being on one's feet
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage info.

notes: Often combines with directional particles: 'đứng lên' or 'đứng dậy' (to stand up), 'đứng lại' (to stop moving).

senses.definition: To be in an upright position on your feet.

examples.text: Tôi đang đứng chờ xe buýt ở góc đường.
examples.translation: I am standing waiting for the bus at the street corner.

senses.definition: To stop moving or working.

examples.text: Chiếc đồng hồ đã đứng rồi.
examples.translation: The clock has stopped.

faults.quote: you will often hear 'culebra' in daily conversation in Mexico
faults.why: In Mexico, 'víbora' is the most common everyday word for snake, alongside 'culebra'.

notes: In everyday Mexican Spanish, people often say 'víbora' (strictly a viper, but used for any snake) or 'culebra' (especially for non-venomous ones) instead of 'serpiente'.

senses.definition: A long, limbless reptile that moves by slithering.

examples.text: La serpiente se escondió entre las rocas al vernos llegar.
examples.translation: The snake hid among the rocks when it saw us arriving.

faults.quote: Used for any standard seat with a back designed for one person
faults.why: merely restates the definition; contrast with 'sillón' or 'banco' is much more useful

notes: Distinguish from 'el sillón' (a soft armchair) and 'el banco' (a stool or bench without a back).

senses.definition: A seat with a back for one person.

examples.text: Me senté en la silla de madera.
examples.translation: I sat on the wooden chair.

faults.quote: Bread soaked in liquid, or a dish made with pieces of bread
faults.why: 'bread soaked in liquid' is archaic; 'sopa de ajo' is just sense 0

faults.quote: bread soup, sopas
faults.why: 'sopas' is Spanish, not an English gloss
in Mexico, 'sopa' very commonly refers to cooked pasta or rice dishes ('sopa seca')

notes: In Mexico, 'sopa' refers both to broth-based soups ('sopa aguada') and to cooked pasta or rice dishes where the broth has been absorbed ('sopa seca', such as 'sopa de arroz' or 'sopa de coditos').

senses.definition: A hot liquid food made by boiling meat, vegetables, or pasta in broth or water.

examples.text: Mamá preparó una sopa de verduras para la comida.
examples.translation: Mom made vegetable soup for lunch.

senses.definition: (Mexico) A savory dish of pasta or rice cooked in broth or sauce until the liquid is absorbed, served before the main course.

examples.text: De entrada hay sopa de arroz o sopa de coditos con crema.
examples.translation: For a starter there is Mexican rice or elbow macaroni with cream.

faults.quote: Es cuestión de suerte si el tren llega a tiempo.
faults.why: 'cuestión de suerte' means 'a matter of luck' (sense 0), not 'a matter of fate'

faults.quote: The way in which things happen, seemingly outside of a person's control.
faults.why: for A2, 'suerte' is simply 'luck' (good or bad); 'destino' is standard for 'fate'

faults.quote: Used to describe both the random nature of events
faults.why: restates the definition instead of teaching useful collocations like 'tener suerte' or '¡buena suerte!'

notes: Commonly used in 'tener suerte' (to be lucky), 'por suerte' (luckily), and '¡Buena suerte!' or simply '¡Suerte!' (Good luck!).
Without an adjective, 'tener suerte' means to have good luck.

senses.definition: Chance as a force that brings good or bad things; specifically, good fortune.

examples.text: Tuve mucha suerte en el examen.
examples.translation: I was very lucky on the exam.

examples.text: ¡Te deseo mucha suerte en tu nuevo trabajo!
examples.translation: I wish you the best of luck in your new job!

faults.quote: The owner or head of a company, business, or shop.
faults.why: Manager and business owner are shades of one meaning ('boss') in Indonesian.

notes: Used in informal and semi-formal contexts for a manager, employer, or business owner; the formal term is 'atasan'.
Often used in spoken Indonesian as a friendly or respectful form of address for a customer or acquaintance.

senses.definition: A person in charge of employees or a business, such as a manager, employer, or owner.

examples.text: Saya harus berbicara dengan bos saya tentang jadwal cuti.
examples.translation: I need to talk to my boss about the leave schedule.

examples.text: Bos toko itu sangat ramah kepada semua pelanggan.
examples.translation: The owner of that shop is very friendly to all customers.

notes: Cannot be used to describe something that causes boredom ('boring'); use 'membosankan' for that (e.g., 'film yang membosankan').
Often followed by a verb, or by 'dengan' or (informally) 'sama' before a noun, to mean 'tired of' or 'fed up with'.

senses.definition: Feeling weary and restless through lack of interest.

examples.text: Saya merasa bosan karena tidak ada yang menarik untuk dilakukan.
examples.translation: I feel bored because there is nothing interesting to do.

senses.definition: Feeling annoyed or impatient from having had too much of something repetitive.

examples.text: Dia bosan menunggu bus yang tidak kunjung datang.
examples.translation: She is fed up with waiting for the bus that never seems to arrive.

faults.quote: This is the standard term for a container used for liquids.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition; omits its common use as a measure word ('sebotol').

faults.quote: Dia minum air dari satu botol plastik.
faults.why: 'Satu botol plastik' is a calque of English 'a plastic bottle'; omit 'satu'.

notes: Also used as a classifier for bottled liquids, often with the prefix 'se-' for 'one' (e.g., 'sebotol air', 'dua botol bir').

senses.definition: A glass or plastic container with a narrow neck, used for holding liquids.

examples.text: Dia minum air dari botol plastik.
examples.translation: He is drinking water from a plastic bottle.

faults.quote: Use 'dag' both for the full twenty-four hour period
faults.why: Restates the definition; fails to note irregular vowel lengthening in plural 'dagen' /ˈdaːɣə(n)/.

notes: The plural is 'dagen' (/ˈdaːɣə(n)/), with a long 'a' sound.
'Dag!' is also very commonly used as an informal greeting ('hello') or farewell ('bye').

senses.definition: A period of twenty-four hours, or the hours of daylight.

examples.text: Elke dag begin ik vroeg met werken.
examples.translation: Every day I start working early.

examples.text: De zon schijnt de hele dag.
examples.translation: The sun is shining all day.

faults.quote: comforter
faults.why: A comforter/duvet in Dutch is 'dekbed', not 'deken' (which is a woven/fleece blanket).

faults.quote: Don't confuse this with the word 'deken' meaning a dean
faults.why: Warns about a rare homonym instead of contrasting with the everyday word 'dekbed' (duvet/comforter).

notes: Refers to a woven or fleece blanket; a quilted duvet or comforter is 'het dekbed'.

senses.definition: A large piece of thick cloth used on a bed or around the body for warmth.

examples.text: Het is koud buiten, dus ik pak nog een extra deken.
examples.translation: It is cold outside, so I am grabbing an extra blanket.

faults.quote: Use 'de deur' when talking about the physical barrier
faults.why: Pure filler that just repeats the definition.

faults.quote: Remember that 'deur' is a de-word, so it takes 'de'
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword.

senses.definition: A movable barrier used to open and close the entrance to a building, room, or vehicle.

examples.text: Doe alstublieft de deur dicht.
examples.translation: Please close the door.

faults.quote: Use 'dochter' when describing someone's female child.
faults.why: Restates the definition and matches English 'daughter' usage.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'meisje', which simply means 'girl'.
faults.why: Unnecessary note; English speakers already distinguish between 'daughter' and 'girl'.

notes: The plural is 'dochters'.

senses.definition: A person's female child.

examples.text: Zij is de dochter van mijn buurman.
examples.translation: She is my neighbor's daughter.

faults.why: Should warn about false friend / spelling confusion with 'doctor' (academic title, PhD).

notes: 'Dokter' is the everyday word for a medical doctor; 'arts' is the more formal term (as in 'huisarts', general practitioner).
Spelled with 'k' for a medical physician; 'doctor' with 'c' is an academic title (PhD).

senses.definition: A person who is qualified to treat sick or injured people.

examples.text: Ik moet een afspraak maken bij de dokter omdat ik griep heb.
examples.translation: I need to make an appointment with the doctor because I have the flu.

faults.quote: minggu has two very common meanings: a period of seven days
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses capitalization (Minggu for Sunday) and 'hari Minggu' usage.

notes: Capitalized as 'Minggu' when meaning 'Sunday', and often preceded by 'hari' (day): 'hari Minggu'.

senses.definition: A period of seven days.

examples.text: Saya akan pergi ke Bali minggu depan.
examples.translation: I will go to Bali next week.

senses.definition: The day of the week between Saturday and Monday.

examples.text: Kami biasanya beristirahat di rumah pada hari Minggu.
examples.translation: We usually rest at home on Sunday.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'to take (medicine)', which uses 'minum' in Indonesian.

faults.quote: Minum refers to the act of consuming any liquid
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition; should note 'minum obat' (take medicine) and 'meminum'.

notes: Used in its base form in everyday speech; the prefixed form 'meminum' is more formal.
Also used for taking medicine ('minum obat'), even for solid pills or tablets.

senses.definition: To swallow a liquid such as water, juice, or tea.

examples.text: Saya ingin minum air putih.
examples.translation: I want to drink plain water.

senses.definition: To swallow medicine, including pills or tablets.

examples.text: Jangan lupa minum obat setelah makan.
examples.translation: Don't forget to take your medicine after eating.

notes: Literally 'frying oil', from 'minyak' (oil) + 'goreng' (to fry).

senses.definition: Liquid fat derived from plants, used for frying and cooking food.

examples.text: Ibu menuangkan minyak goreng ke dalam wajan panas.
examples.translation: Mother poured cooking oil into the hot pan.

notes: Calling a person 'miskin' directly can sound blunt; 'kurang mampu' (less well-off) is a more polite alternative.

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions.

examples.text: Banyak keluarga miskin membutuhkan bantuan pemerintah.
examples.translation: Many poor families need government assistance.

senses.definition: Having very little of a needed substance or quality.

examples.text: Tanah di daerah ini miskin nutrisi.
examples.translation: The soil in this area is poor in nutrients.

faults.quote: Used for any standard four-wheeled motor vehicle.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding learner value.

notes: Do not confuse with 'motor', which in everyday Indonesian means 'motorcycle'.

senses.definition: A four-wheeled road vehicle with an engine for carrying a small number of people.

examples.text: Dia membeli mobil baru tahun ini.
examples.translation: He bought a new car this year.

faults.quote: One of the digits at the end of the foot.
faults.why: Indonesian 'jari' is a single concept (digit); toes usually require 'jari kaki'.

faults.quote: finger; digit
faults.why: Sense 1 is 'toe', which is missing from shortGloss.

notes: By itself, 'jari' usually means a finger, though it covers both fingers and toes. To be specific, use 'jari tangan' (finger) or 'jari kaki' (toe).

senses.definition: One of the five digits at the end of the hand or foot.

examples.text: Dia menunjuk ke arah pintu dengan jari telunjuknya.
examples.translation: She pointed toward the door with her index finger.

examples.text: Saya tersandung dan jari kaki saya sakit sekali.
examples.translation: I tripped and my toe hurts a lot.

faults.quote: An outer garment worn over other clothing for warmth or protection
faults.why: 'Jas' alone means suit jacket; it only means raincoat or lab coat in fixed compounds.

faults.quote: Jas specifically refers to a tailored, formal jacket
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1, which claims 'jas' means raincoat or coat in general.

notes: Alone, 'jas' refers to a formal suit jacket (for a casual jacket, use 'jaket'). It also appears in common compounds like 'jas hujan' (raincoat) and 'jas lab' (lab coat).

senses.definition: A formal tailored jacket, or a protective outer coat in compounds such as 'jas hujan' (raincoat).

examples.text: Dia memakai jas hitam ke pesta pernikahan itu.
examples.translation: He wore a black suit jacket to the wedding party.

examples.text: Jangan lupa membawa jas hujan karena langit mulai mendung.
examples.translation: Don't forget to bring a raincoat because the sky is starting to get cloudy.

faults.quote: To fail an exam or a test.
faults.why: Using 'jatuh' for failing an exam is unidiomatic ('gagal' or 'tidak lulus' is standard).
Should mention common everyday expressions like 'jatuh cinta' (fall in love) or 'jatuh sakit' (fall ill).

notes: Often used in everyday expressions just like English 'fall', such as 'jatuh cinta' (to fall in love) and 'jatuh sakit' (to fall ill).

senses.definition: To move down suddenly from a higher place, or to drop from a standing position.

examples.text: Buah mangga itu jatuh dari pohon.
examples.translation: The mango fell from the tree.

senses.definition: To decrease sharply in price, value, or level.

examples.text: Harga beras jatuh bulan ini.
examples.translation: The price of rice fell this month.

faults.quote: /dʒələk/
faults.why: Second vowel in 'jelek' is /e/ (or /ɛ/), not schwa /ə/: /dʒəˈlek/.

notes: Used for both physical appearance and poor quality (like weather, grades, or signal). Calling a person 'jelek' is blunt and offensive.

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; not attractive.

examples.text: Lukisan itu jelek sekali.
examples.translation: That painting is very ugly.

senses.definition: Of poor quality, low standard, or not working well.

examples.text: Koneksi internet di sini sangat jelek.
examples.translation: The internet connection here is very bad.

faults.quote: Used physically for structures, but also commonly used metaphorically
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses without adding useful learner information.

notes: A pedestrian overpass across a busy road is called 'jembatan penyeberangan'.

senses.definition: A structure built to cross over a river, road, or railway.

examples.text: Kami menyeberangi jembatan untuk sampai ke seberang sungai.
examples.translation: We crossed the bridge to get to the other side of the river.

senses.definition: Something that connects or builds understanding between different people or groups.

examples.text: Bahasa sering menjadi jembatan antara dua budaya yang berbeda.
examples.translation: Language often becomes a bridge between two different cultures.

faults.quote: Use 'bruyant' to describe places, people, or things that produce a lot
faults.why: Restates the definition and states completely regular feminine agreement.

notes: The 'y' splits into two sounds: 'brui-yant' (/bʁɥi.jɑ̃/).

senses.definition: Making a lot of noise, or full of noise.

examples.text: Les enfants sont très bruyants dans la cour de récréation.
examples.translation: The children are very noisy in the playground.

faults.quote: As an adjective, 'calme' agrees in gender (calme / calme) but has
faults.why: Explains a basic A1 grammar rule true for all adjectives ending in -e.

senses.definition: Free from agitation, excitement, or worry; peaceful and relaxed.

examples.text: Après l'examen, elle est restée très calme.
examples.translation: After the exam, she stayed very calm.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise; quiet.

examples.text: La rue est calme ce soir.
examples.translation: The street is quiet tonight.

faults.quote: To damage or injure a part of one's body.
faults.why: Breaking a bone is the same meaning; uses reflexive 'se casser' which needs a note.

faults.quote: Use casser when something hard or solid breaks into pieces, like a
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: For breaking a body part, use the reflexive 'se casser' with the definite article (e.g., 'se casser le bras' = to break one's arm).
Do not confuse 'casser' with 'briser', which is more literary and often used for abstract things like hearts or silence.

senses.definition: To damage something so that it separates into pieces or stops working; to fracture a bone.

examples.text: Attention à ne pas casser ce verre.
examples.translation: Be careful not to break this glass.

examples.text: Il est tombé de vélo et s'est cassé le bras.
examples.translation: He fell off his bike and broke his arm.

faults.quote: it is also the standard way to say 'I am sorry' when apologizing
faults.why: Everyday apologies use ขอโทษ; เสียใจ expresses deeper regret or condolence.

faults.quote: It is important not to confuse this with 'sad' in the sense
faults.why: Explains English slang 'sad' rather than Thai usage.

notes: Literally 'to lose heart' (เสีย 'lose' + ใจ 'heart/mind').
For everyday apologies ('Excuse me', 'I'm sorry'), use ขอโทษ (khǎaw-thôot). เสียใจ expresses genuine sadness, deeper regret, or condolences (เสียใจด้วยนะ 'I'm sorry for your loss').

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy or sorrowful about something unfortunate.

examples.text: ฉันรู้สึกเสียใจมากที่ได้ยินข่าวนี้
examples.translation: I feel very sad to hear this news.

senses.definition: Feeling regret or remorse for something one has done.

examples.text: ฉันเสียใจที่มาสาย
examples.translation: I am sorry that I came late.

faults.quote: In Thai, 'มีความสุข' is used to describe a state of being happy
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value; misses literal breakdown and ดีใจ contrast.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages where 'happy' might be used for 'lucky'
faults.why: Irrelevant comparison to English 'happy coincidence'.

notes: Literally 'to have happiness' (มี 'have' + ความสุข 'happiness').
Describes general contentment or well-being, whereas ดีใจ (dii-jai) refers to being glad or pleased about a specific piece of news or event.

senses.definition: Feeling pleasure and contentment with one's life or situation.

examples.text: ฉันมีความสุขมากที่ได้เจอคุณ
examples.translation: I am very happy to meet you.

faults.quote: Used when someone feels nervous or tense, especially right before facing
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim; misses useful contrast with ตื่นเต้น.

notes: Specifically refers to stage fright, shyness, or uneasiness in front of people. In everyday speech, Thais also frequently use ตื่นเต้น (tùuen-tên, 'excited') to mean 'nervous' before an exam or event.

senses.definition: Feeling nervous, uneasy, or self-conscious, especially when performing or in front of others.

examples.text: ฉันรู้สึกประหม่ามากตอนที่ต้องพูดต่อหน้าคนเยอะๆ
examples.translation: I felt very nervous when I had to speak in front of a lot of people.

faults.quote: /pʰaːŋ˧/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: แพง has vowel /ɛː/ (/pʰɛːŋ/), not /aː/ (which is พาง).

faults.quote: รอยยิ้มของเธอดູแพงมาก
faults.why: Contains Lao vowel character U+0EB9 (ູ) instead of Thai U+0E39 (ู) in ดู.

faults.quote: Valuable, precious, or high in worth. | glosses en: precious, valuable
faults.why: แพง does not mean 'precious/valuable' (มีค่า); ดูแพง is modern slang for 'classy/elegant'.

faults.quote: แพง is used for things that cost a lot of money.
faults.why: Simply restates the definition.

notes: The opposite is ถูก (thùuk, 'cheap').
In modern slang, ดูแพง (duu phaeng, literally 'to look expensive') describes someone or something that looks classy, elegant, or sophisticated.

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: เสื้อตัวนี้แพงเกินไป
examples.translation: This shirt is too expensive.

senses.definition: Looking sophisticated, elegant, or high-class (usually in the phrase ดูแพง).

examples.text: ชุดนี้ดูแพงมาก
examples.translation: This outfit looks very classy.

faults.why: Lacks the grammar/derivation note on 'membenci' vs 'benci pada/sama'.

notes: Much stronger than 'tidak suka' (to dislike).

In formal contexts or before a direct noun object, the derived transitive form 'membenci' is often used (e.g., 'Dia membenci kebohongan'). In everyday speech, 'benci' is used directly or followed by 'pada' / 'sama'.

senses.definition: To dislike someone or something very much.

examples.text: Saya benci sekali harus bangun pagi-pagi.
examples.translation: I really hate having to wake up early.

examples.text: Dia benci makan sayuran.
examples.translation: He hates eating vegetables.

faults.quote: Use 'berangkat' when talking about leaving a place to go
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value such as common collocations or prepositions.

corrected.shortGloss: to depart; to leave; to set off
notes: Used both for vehicles departing on a trip and for everyday departures like leaving for work or school ('berangkat kerja', 'berangkat ke sekolah').
Often paired with 'ke' (to) or 'dari' (from). Unlike 'pergi' (to go), 'berangkat' focuses on the moment of setting off.

senses.definition: To leave a place to start a journey or go somewhere.

examples.text: Kereta api akan berangkat dalam lima menit.
examples.translation: The train will depart in five minutes.

examples.text: Saya berangkat ke kantor jam tujuh pagi.
examples.translation: I leave for the office at seven in the morning.

faults.quote: Ready and willing to do something challenging or to speak
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning ('brave' / 'dare to' before a verb); 'ready, willing' are misleading glosses.

faults.quote: Use 'berani' to describe someone who faces danger or fear
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Before a verb, 'berani' translates naturally as 'to dare to' or 'to be brave enough to' (e.g., 'tidak berani bertanya' = not dare to ask).
Do not confuse it with 'benar' (correct, true).

senses.definition: Not afraid of danger, pain, or difficulty; having the courage to do something.

examples.text: Pemadam kebakaran itu sangat berani.
examples.translation: That firefighter is very brave.

examples.text: Dia berani mengatakan yang sebenarnya kepada gurunya.
examples.translation: She dared to tell her teacher the truth.

faults.quote: Serious or severe in nature.

senses.definition: The sweet and fleshy part of a tree or plant that contains seeds and is eaten as food.

examples.text: Compro frutas frescas na feira toda terça-feira.
examples.translation: I buy fresh fruit at the market every Tuesday.

faults.quote: Used as a standalone greeting (صباح الخير) or to refer to

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ يَا صَدِيقِي.
examples.translation: Good morning, my friend.

notes: The plural is نَبَاتَات (nabātāt). نَبَات can also be used collectively to mean 'vegetation'.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in soil, has leaves and roots, and cannot move around.

examples.text: هَذَا النَّبَاتُ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الكَثِيرِ مِنَ المَاءِ.
examples.translation: This plant needs a lot of water.

faults.quote: /qalv/

faults.quote: Used both for the physical organ and metaphorically for emotions, feelings,
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving the broken plural قُلُوب (qulūb).

senses.definition: The organ in the chest that pumps blood through the body, or the seat of emotions and feelings.

examples.text: يَنْبِضُ الْقَلْبُ بِسُرْعَةٍ عِنْدَمَا تَخَافُ.
examples.translation: The heart beats fast when you are afraid.

senses.definition: The middle or most important part of a place or thing.

examples.text: يَقَعُ الْمَسْجِدُ فِي قَلْبِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
examples.translation: The mosque is located in the heart of the city.

faults.quote: It is commonly used with numbers to count weeks, e.g., أسبوعان
faults.why: Unhelpful filler; أُسْبُوعَانِ is the dual form without a number, and any time unit is counted.

faults.quote: I will travel after a week.
faults.why: Calque of بَعْدَ أُسْبُوعٍ; natural English is 'in a week'.

notes: The plural is أَسَابِيع (asābīʿ), which is diptote (does not take nunation).

senses.definition: A period of seven days.

examples.text: سَأُسَافِرُ بَعْدَ أُسْبُوعٍ.
examples.translation: I will travel in a week.

faults.quote: uncle; guy; buddy
faults.why: 'buddy' is in shortGloss (and note) but missing from the senses and glosses.

notes: The feminine form is 'la tía' (aunt; girl, mate).
In Spain, 'tío' and 'tía' are very common in informal speech to refer to a guy or girl, or to address a friend ('¡Hola, tío!').

senses.definition: The brother of one's father or mother, or the husband of one's aunt.

examples.text: Mi tío vive en Madrid.
examples.translation: My uncle lives in Madrid.

senses.definition: (informal, Spain) A man or guy, or a friendly way to address a friend.

examples.text: Aquel tío me ayudó con el coche.
examples.translation: That guy helped me with the car.

faults.quote: work; job; task
faults.why: 'task' is in shortGloss, but the senses lack the countable 'assignment/piece of work' meaning.

faults.quote: Use 'trabajo' when talking about your job or the effort you put
faults.why: merely restates the two sense definitions without adding usage information.

notes: Also refers to one's workplace: 'Estoy en el trabajo' (I'm at work).

senses.definition: A regular occupation or employment done to earn money.

examples.text: Busco un trabajo nuevo con mejor horario.
examples.translation: I am looking for a new job with better hours.

senses.definition: Physical or mental effort used to do or make something.

examples.text: Este proyecto requiere mucho trabajo.

senses.definition: A specific piece of work, task, or school assignment.

examples.text: Tengo que entregar un trabajo de historia mañana.
examples.translation: I have to hand in a history assignment tomorrow.

faults.quote: Used for both passenger trains and freight trains running on tracks.
faults.why: restates the definition and is identical to English 'train'.

notes: Use 'en tren' (without an article) to say 'by train': 'Viajamos en tren' (We travel by train).

senses.definition: A line of railway carriages pulled by an engine along a track to transport people or goods.

examples.text: El tren llega a la estación a las tres.
examples.translation: The train arrives at the station at three.

faults.quote: It is a common mistake to think 'turista' is only masculine;
faults.why: repeats the exact point already explained in notes[0].

notes: Even though it ends in -a, the form does not change for gender; use the article and adjectives to show gender: 'el turista alemán' (masculine) vs. 'la turista alemana' (feminine).

senses.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure, especially while on holiday.

examples.text: El turista busca el museo en el centro de la ciudad.
examples.translation: The tourist is looking for the museum in the city center.

faults.why: Lacks the crucial grammar note that both parts inflect for gender and number.

notes: Formed from the verb डरना (to fear). Both parts change for gender and number: डरी हुई (feminine), डरे हुए (masculine plural or oblique).

senses.definition: Feeling fear or anxiety about something dangerous, painful, or threatening.

examples.text: अंधेरे कमरे में बच्चा बहुत डरा हुआ था।
examples.translation: The child was very scared in the dark room.

faults.quote: Use 'शांत' when describing a calm environment, a quiet person, or a
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions and senses without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Invariable adjective: its form does not change for gender or number.
Do not confuse with चुप (chup), which specifically means silent or not speaking, whereas शांत describes a wider state of peace, calm, or stillness.

senses.definition: Of a place or atmosphere: free from noise, commotion, or disturbance.

examples.text: रात में यह कमरा बहुत शांत रहता है।
examples.translation: This room stays very quiet at night.

senses.definition: Of a person or mind: free from worry, anxiety, or strong emotion.

examples.text: परीक्षा के बाद मेरा मन एकदम शांत था।
examples.translation: After the exam, my mind was completely calm.

faults.quote: It changes its ending to -ी (bhūkī) when describing a feminine noun.
faults.why: Wrong romanization: 'bhūkī' drops the aspiration of ख (kh); it is भूखी (bhūkhī).

faults.quote: not to the long-term condition of poverty or famine, which is typically
faults.why: भूखा is commonly used for starving/famine-stricken too, and 'grast'/'pīḍit' mean 'afflicted', not 'famine'.

notes: Inflects for gender and number: भूखी (feminine), भूखे (masculine plural or oblique).
In everyday conversation, 'I am hungry' is just as often expressed with the noun भूख (hunger): मुझे भूख लगी है (literally 'hunger has struck me').

senses.definition: Feeling a need or desire to eat.

examples.text: मैं बहुत भूखा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am very hungry.

faults.quote: Halka is a versatile word. It can mean light in weight, but
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: light; mild; slight
faults.why: Includes 'slight', which is absent from the senses and glosses.

notes: Inflects for gender and number: हल्की (feminine), हल्के (masculine plural or oblique).
Do not confuse with कम (kam), which refers to a smaller quantity (less, fewer) rather than weight or intensity.

senses.definition: Having little weight; not heavy.

examples.text: यह बक्सा बहुत हल्का है।
examples.translation: This box is very light.

senses.definition: Low in intensity, strength, or degree; gentle, pale, or easy to digest.

examples.text: मुझे हल्का खाना पसंद है।
examples.translation: I like light food.

examples.text: मुझे हल्का बुखार है।
examples.translation: I have a slight fever.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with सुंदर (sundar), which means beautiful.
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; learners do not randomly confuse unrelated-sounding antonyms.

notes: Invariable adjective: its form does not change for gender or number. Formed from बद- (bad) + सूरत (face, appearance).

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; lacking beauty.

examples.text: उस पुरानी इमारत का डिज़ाइन बहुत बदसूरत है।
examples.translation: The design of that old building is very ugly.

faults.quote: Είναι ωραία μέρα σήμερα, ναι;
faults.why: Unnatural calque of English 'right?'; Greek uses 'έτσι δεν είναι;' or 'ε;' here.

faults.quote: Used as a question tag or to solicit agreement from the listener.
faults.why: 'Ναι' is not a general question tag in Greek; merge into one sense.

faults.quote: yes; indeed; right
faults.why: Includes 'indeed' which is missing from senses, and false tag 'right'.

notes: False friend: although it sounds like English 'nay' or 'no', it means 'yes'.

senses.definition: Used to give an affirmative answer or express agreement.

examples.text: — Θέλεις καφέ; — Ναι, ευχαριστώ.
examples.translation: — Do you want coffee? — Yes, thank you.

faults.quote: expression

senses.definition: In the absence of something or someone; not having or doing something.

examples.text: Πίνω τον καφέ μου χωρίς ζάχαρη.
examples.translation: I drink my coffee without sugar.

examples.text: Έφυγε χωρίς να μου πει τίποτα.
examples.translation: He left without saying anything to me.

faults.quote: The continuous sequence of existence and events that occurs in an apparently

faults.quote: While 'χρόνος' is the primary word for the concept of time
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses without adding grammatical or usage help.

notes: Do not confuse with η ώρα, which is used for clock time ('what time is it?') or hours.

senses.definition: The ongoing passage of seconds, minutes, days, and years, or the amount of it available.

examples.text: Ο χρόνος περνάει πολύ γρήγορα.
examples.translation: Time passes very quickly.

examples.text: Δεν έχω χρόνο σήμερα.
examples.translation: I don't have time today.

senses.definition: A period of twelve months.

examples.text: Θα πάω διακοπές σε έναν χρόνο.
examples.translation: I will go on vacation in a year.

faults.quote: Use 원하다 when you have a specific desire for an object

senses.definition: To have a desire to possess, obtain, or do something.

examples.text: 나는 평화로운 삶을 원한다.
examples.translation: I want a peaceful life.

examples.text: 그는 무엇을 원해?
examples.translation: What does he want?

faults.quote: 청소하다 refers to the act of cleaning a space
faults.why: Mostly restates the definition instead of contrasting with 씻다 or 닦다.

notes: Used for cleaning a room, building, or area (like 방을 청소하다). Do not use it for washing dishes (설거지하다), doing laundry (빨래하다), or washing your body or hands (씻다).

senses.definition: To remove dirt, dust, or mess from a room or place to make it tidy.

examples.text: 주말에 방을 청소해요.
examples.translation: I clean my room on the weekend.

faults.quote: To have shoes or socks on one's feet.

senses.definition: To put or have shoes, socks, or other footwear on one's feet.

examples.text: 외출하기 전에 운동화를 신어요.
examples.translation: I put on my sneakers before going out.

examples.text: 양말을 신고 자면 안 돼요.
examples.translation: You shouldn't sleep with your socks on.

faults.quote: 내일 친구를 집으로 가져와.
faults.why: 가져오다 is only for inanimate objects; bringing a person requires 데려오다.

faults.why: False claim that 가져오다 can be used for bringing a person ('someone').

senses.definition: To carry or take a thing with you to the place where the speaker is.

examples.text: 내일 우산을 꼭 가져와.
examples.translation: Make sure to bring your umbrella tomorrow.

examples.text: 책 좀 가져와 줄래요?
examples.translation: Could you bring me the book?

senses.definition: To hold someone or something closely in one's arms, especially to show affection.

examples.text: 엄마가 아기를 안아요.

examples.text: 친구를 따뜻하게 안아 주었어요.
examples.translation: I gave my friend a warm hug.

faults.why: Missing note on the irregular dental-stem declension (δέρματος, δέρματα).

senses.definition: The natural outer covering of a human or animal body.

examples.text: Το δέρμα μου είναι πολύ ευαίσθητο στον ήλιο.
examples.translation: My skin is very sensitive to the sun.

senses.definition: Animal hide treated and used to make clothes, shoes, bags, or furniture.

examples.text: Αυτό το μπουφάν είναι φτιαγμένο από γνήσιο δέρμα.
examples.translation: This jacket is made of genuine leather.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the institution of higher education itself or the

examples.translation: I study at the University of Athens.

faults.quote: Used for both rooms in a home and rooms in a hotel
faults.why: Merely restates the meaning of 'room', which works identically in English.

examples.text: Το δωμάτιο είναι μεγάλο και φωτεινό.

senses.definition: A flat or slightly deep container from which food is eaten or served.

examples.text: Βάλε το φαγητό στο πιάτο.
examples.translation: Put the food on the plate.

senses.definition: A particular type of prepared food served as part of a meal.

examples.text: Αυτό είναι το αγαπημένο μου πιάτο.
examples.translation: This is my favorite dish.

faults.quote: The appearance or quality of the skin on a person's face.
faults.why: Skin and complexion/skincare are one continuous sense for 피부 in Korean.

senses.definition: The outer layer covering a person's or animal's body.

examples.text: 피부가 정말 부드러워요.
examples.translation: Your skin is very soft.

examples.text: 요즘 피부 관리에 관심이 많아요.
examples.translation: I am very interested in skincare these days.

examples.text: 현금으로 계산할게요.
examples.translation: I will pay in cash.

faults.quote: While '지도' can mean 'guidance' or 'coaching' (like a teacher guiding

examples.translation: I found the way by looking at the map.

senses.definition: The act of teaching, training, or directing someone.

examples.text: 선생님의 지도를 받아서 실력이 늘었어요.
examples.translation: My skills improved under the teacher's guidance.

senses.definition: Showing or feeling strong interest, excitement, and eagerness about something.

examples.text: هو مُتَحَمِّسٌ جِدًّا لِلسَّفَرِ إلى مِصْر.
examples.translation: He is very excited about traveling to Egypt.

examples.text: كُنتُ مُتَحَمِّسًا لِبَدْءِ العَمَلِ اليَوْم.
examples.translation: I was eager to start work today.

faults.quote: Used to describe both physical beauty and general pleasantness

senses.definition: Enjoyable, pleasant, or fine.

examples.text: قَضَيْنَا يَوْمًا جَمِيلًا مَعًا.
examples.translation: We spent a lovely day together.

faults.quote: Khajool is used to describe someone who naturally tends to be quiet

examples.translation: The child is very shy in front of strangers.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk; the lightest colour.

faults.quote: It is a very common adjective used for almost anything that has

senses.definition: Having the colour of snow or milk; of the lightest colour.

examples.text: الثَّلْجُ أَبْيَضُ.
examples.translation: Snow is white.

faults.quote: /naˈdˤiːf/
faults.why: In Modern Standard Arabic, ظ is pronounced /ðˤ/, not colloquial /dˤ/.

examples.text: ताला लगाना मत भूलना।
examples.translation: Do not forget to lock the door.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'sleepiness/drowsiness' (used in 'tener sueño') and figurative 'dream/goal'.

faults.quote: sleep; dream; sleepiness
faults.why: 'sleepiness' is in shortGloss, but missing from the senses.

notes: Use 'tener sueño' (literally 'to have sleepiness') to say 'to be sleepy'.
Note that 'sueño' is also the 'yo' present form of the verb 'soñar' (to dream): 'Sueño contigo' (I dream of you).

senses.definition: The natural state of rest of the body and mind.

examples.text: El sueño es muy importante para la salud.
examples.translation: Sleep is very important for health.

senses.definition: The images, ideas, or sounds in your mind while sleeping, or a strong hope for the future.

examples.text: Tuve un sueño muy extraño anoche.
examples.translation: I had a very strange dream last night.

senses.definition: The feeling of needing to sleep.

examples.text: Tengo mucho sueño; me voy a la cama.
examples.translation: I am very sleepy; I am going to bed.

faults.quote: In Mexico and many other Spanish-speaking regions, "suéter" is the standard everyday
faults.why: Two wordy notes where one brief note about plural formation and regional difference suffices.

notes: Plural: 'los suéteres'. In Spain, 'el jersey' is used instead.

senses.definition: A warm knitted top with long sleeves, worn on the upper body.

examples.text: Traigo puesto un suéter grueso porque hace mucho frío hoy.
examples.translation: I am wearing a thick sweater because it is very cold today.

faults.quote: /taˈθon/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican seseo /s/ (/taˈson/).

faults.quote: A large cup, often without a handle or with a sturdy one
faults.why: In Mexico, a mug with a handle is 'una taza', not 'un tazón'.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse 'tazón' with 'taza'.
faults.why: Notes [0] and [1] repeat the exact same comparison between 'tazón' and 'taza'.

notes: Plural: 'los tazones'. Do not confuse with 'la taza' (cup or mug with a handle).

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for serving food like soup, cereal, or fruit.

examples.text: Ella sirvió la sopa caliente en un tazón.
examples.translation: She served the hot soup in a bowl.

faults.quote: While 'kamra' is a common word for any room, specific rooms
faults.why: Trivial filler; replaceable by the useful irregular plural/oblique rule (कमरा -> कमरे).

notes: The final -आ (-ā) changes to -ए (-e) in the plural and before postpositions: कमरे (kamre, 'rooms'), कमरे में (kamre mẽ, 'in the room').
Do not confuse with कमर (kamar, feminine), which means 'waist'.

senses.definition: A space in a building separated by walls, used for living, working, or sleeping.

examples.text: उसका कमरा बहुत बड़ा और साफ़ है।
examples.translation: His room is very big and clean.

faults.quote: cow
faults.why: Does not cover sense 1 (gentle person).

faults.quote: Because of this, the word is sometimes used metaphorically to describe
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1 instead of giving grammar (such as plural गायें).

notes: The plural is गायें (gāyẽ).

senses.definition: A large female farm animal kept for its milk.

examples.text: खेत में गाय घास चर रही है।
examples.translation: The cow is grazing in the field.

senses.definition: A person who is very calm, quiet, and harmless.

examples.text: वह तो बिल्कुल गाय है, किसी का बुरा नहीं सोचती।
examples.translation: She is such a gentle soul; she never thinks ill of anyone.

faults.quote: /kəmˈpjuːṭər/
faults.why: Uses Indological 'ṭ' instead of IPA /ʈ/.

faults.quote: This is a loanword from English and is used universally across

faults.quote: The word is treated as masculine, so you will often see
faults.why: Restates the gender field.

notes: Also commonly spelled कंप्यूटर.

senses.definition: An electronic machine used for storing and processing information, working, and browsing the internet.

examples.text: मेरा कम्प्यूटर ख़राब हो गया है।
examples.translation: My computer has broken down.

faults.quote: गायें एक उपयोगी पालतू जानवर हैं।
faults.why: Number mismatch between plural subject 'गायें' (cows) and singular 'एक ... जानवर'.

faults.quote: While it literally means 'domesticated animal', it is the standard way

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'āwārā jānvar', which refers to a
