senses.definition: Not afraid of danger; showing courage.

examples.text: वह बहुत बहादुर लड़की है।
examples.translation: She is a very brave girl.

faults.quote: correct; right; true
faults.why: Misses the second sense ('fine, okay').

notes: Invariable adjective; does not change for gender or number. Also commonly used on its own as a response meaning 'right' or 'got it'.

senses.definition: Free from error; conforming to fact or truth.

examples.text: आपका उत्तर सही है।
examples.translation: Your answer is correct.

senses.definition: Satisfactory, acceptable, or in good condition.

examples.text: यहाँ सब कुछ सही है।
examples.translation: Everything is fine here.

faults.quote: The colour of a lemon, or the colour of a ripe banana.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality ('having the colour...').

faults.quote: هذه الليمونة لونها أَصْفَر.
faults.why: Using 'لونها' avoids showing feminine agreement (صَفْرَاء) with 'الليمونة'.

notes: Irregular feminine form: صَفْرَاء (ṣafrāʾ); plural: صُفْر (ṣufr).
Both أَصْفَر and صَفْرَاء are diptotes and do not take nunation (tanwīn).

senses.definition: Having the colour of a lemon or a ripe banana.

examples.text: اِشْتَرَيْتُ قَمِيصًا أَصْفَرَ.
examples.translation: I bought a yellow shirt.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'safe, unharmed, intact' (already listed in shortGloss).

faults.quote: الجسم السليم في العقل السليم.
faults.why: Inverts the famous Arabic proverb 'العقل السليم في الجسم السليم'.

faults.quote: Used to describe a body or mind that is free from illness
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: Takes the preposition مِنْ (min) when meaning 'free from' a flaw or illness.

senses.definition: In good physical or mental health, free from illness.

examples.text: العَقْلُ السَّلِيمُ فِي الجِسْمِ السَّلِيمِ.
examples.translation: A sound mind is in a healthy body.

senses.definition: Unharmed, undamaged, or out of danger.

examples.text: خَرَجَ السَّائِقُ مِنَ الحَادِثِ سَلِيمًا.
examples.translation: The driver came out of the accident unharmed.

senses.definition: Correct, well-founded, and free from errors or flaws.

examples.text: هٰذَا قَرَارٌ سَلِيمٌ.
examples.translation: This is a sound decision.

faults.quote: The feminine form of this adjective is عَطْشَانَة (ʿaṭšāna).
faults.why: In MSA, the standard feminine of فَعْلَان adjectives is فَعْلَى (عَطْشَى); عَطْشَانَة is colloquial/secondary.

faults.quote: It is used specifically to express the bodily sensation of needing liquid
faults.why: Pure filler restating the meaning of 'thirsty'.

notes: In formal Arabic, the feminine is عَطْشَى (ʿaṭšā) and the plural is عِطَاش (ʿiṭāš), though عَطْشَانَة (ʿaṭšāna) is very common in everyday speech.
As a diptote, عَطْشَان does not take nunation (tanwīn).

senses.definition: Feeling a need to drink water or another liquid.

examples.text: أَنَا عَطْشَانُ جِدًّا بَعْدَ الرِّيَاضَةِ.
examples.translation: I am very thirsty after exercise.

faults.why: 'Bored' and 'weary/fed up' are shades of the same state for ضَجِر.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who feels restless or uninspired
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the required preposition مِنْ (min).

notes: Takes the preposition مِنْ (min) to indicate the cause of boredom or annoyance.

senses.definition: Feeling bored, impatient, or fed up because something is dull or annoying.

examples.text: هُوَ ضَجِرٌ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ العَمَلِ الروتِينِيِّ.
examples.translation: He is fed up with too much routine work.

faults.quote: Wadud is often used to describe someone who is naturally kind
faults.why: Restates the definition and misses that فَعُول adjectives do not take ة for feminine.

notes: Takes the preposition مَعَ (maʿa, 'with').
In formal Arabic, adjectives of the pattern فَعُول (faʿūl) use the same form for both masculine and feminine (إِمْرَأَةٌ وَدُودٌ), though وَدُودَة is also seen in modern usage.

senses.definition: Warm, pleasant, and friendly towards other people.

examples.text: هُوَ شَخْصٌ وَدُودٌ جِدًّا مَعَ الجَمِيعِ.
examples.translation: He is a very friendly person with everyone.

faults.why: Missing essential grammar note about the stem vowel dropping before vowel-initial suffixes (karnı).

faults.quote: Use 'karın' when talking about the general stomach area, the belly,
faults.why: Restates the definition and glosses without adding usage information.

notes: The second vowel drops when a suffix starting with a vowel is added: karın → karnım (my stomach), karnı (his/her stomach).
Do not confuse with 'mide', which specifically refers to the internal digestive organ. Note also the common idiom 'karnım aç' (I am hungry, lit. 'my belly is hungry').

senses.definition: The front part of the body below the chest; the belly or abdomen.

examples.text: Çok yemek yedikten sonra karnım ağrıyor.
examples.translation: My stomach hurts after eating too much.

faults.quote: /kaːˈse/
faults.why: Initial /k/ before front/palatalized /aː/ in 'kâse' is palatalized [c] in standard Turkish.

faults.quote: Note the circumflex on the 'a' (â), which softens the preceding
faults.why: Refers to a circumflex in the headword, which is spelled 'kase' without one here.

notes: Officially spelled 'kâse' with a circumflex, though commonly written 'kase'. The 'k' is pronounced soft (like in 'kâr') and the 'a' is long.

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for holding soup, cereal, or fruit.

examples.text: Sabah kahvaltısında bir kase çorba içti.
examples.translation: He had a bowl of soup for breakfast.

faults.quote: Used for eating liquid or semi-liquid foods like soup, yogurt, or
faults.why: Explains what a spoon is rather than giving linguistic information; missing consonant mutation note.

notes: The final 'k' softens to 'ğ' when a suffix starting with a vowel is added: kaşık → kaşığı (the spoon).

senses.definition: A utensil with a small shallow bowl on a handle, used for eating, stirring, or serving food.

examples.text: Çorba içmek için bir kaşık aldım.
examples.translation: I took a spoon to eat soup.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'times / -fold' (e.g., iki kat = twice as much).

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'kat' as in a layer or fold of material.
faults.why: Tells the learner not to confuse the word with its own second sense.

notes: In Turkish buildings, the ground floor is called 'zemin kat' or 'giriş katı', and 'birinci kat' (first floor) is the level above it.

senses.definition: One level or storey of a building.

examples.text: Dairemiz üçüncü katta.
examples.translation: Our apartment is on the third floor.

senses.definition: A single thickness, sheet, or coating of a material.

examples.text: Pastayı iki kat kremayla yaptım.
examples.translation: I made the cake with two layers of cream.

senses.definition: A multiple of an amount or degree (used with numbers).

examples.text: Bu ev diğerinden iki kat daha büyük.
examples.translation: This house is twice as big as the other one.

faults.quote: /kajbetaec/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA: missing the 'm' of '-mek' and has 'ae' instead of 'e'.

faults.quote: to lose, to pass away
faults.why: 'Kaybetmek' means to lose someone to death (transitive), not 'to pass away' (intransitive).

faults.quote: Do not confuse kaybetmek (to lose) with kazanmak (to win) or
faults.why: Pointless note warning against confusing the word with unrelated antonyms.

notes: Formed from 'kayıp' (loss) + 'etmek'. The 't' softens to 'd' before suffixes starting with a vowel: kaybederim (I lose), kaybediyor (he/she is losing).

senses.definition: To no longer have something because you do not know where it is.

examples.text: Anahtarımı evde kaybettim.
examples.translation: I lost my key at home.

senses.definition: To fail to win a game, competition, or match.

examples.text: Maçı son dakikada kaybettik.
examples.translation: We lost the match in the last minute.

senses.definition: To suffer the death of a relative or friend.

examples.text: Geçen yıl büyükbabasını kaybetti.
examples.translation: He lost his grandfather last year.

faults.quote: smile, beam
faults.why: 'Mỉm cười' is a faint, closed-mouth smile, not 'beam' (which is 'cười rạng rỡ').

faults.quote: It is often used when someone feels happy, satisfied, or is being
faults.why: Generic statement about smiling in general; adds no specific linguistic value.

notes: Describes a quiet, gentle smile with the lips closed, unlike 'cười' which can mean either to smile or to laugh aloud.

senses.definition: To make a gentle, quiet smile without opening your mouth or making a sound.

examples.text: Cô ấy mỉm cười khi nhìn thấy bạn.
examples.translation: She smiled when she saw you.

faults.quote: /məːŋ˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong vowel, wrong tone (sắc instead of hỏi), and spurious final velar nasal /ŋ/.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'bật', which specifically means to switch on lights
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1 and its example 'mở đèn'; 'mở' and 'bật' overlap in meaning.

corrected.shortGloss: to open; to turn on; to start
notes: For lights and electrical appliances, both 'mở' and 'bật' mean 'to turn on' ('bật' is more common in the North, 'mở' in the South).
The opposite is 'đóng' (to close) for physical objects, and 'tắt' (to turn off) for devices and lights.

senses.definition: To move something such as a door, window, or container so that it is no longer shut.

examples.text: Xin vui lòng mở cửa.
examples.translation: Please open the door.

senses.definition: To start or turn on a machine, light, or electronic device.

examples.text: Bạn có thể mở đèn giúp tôi không?
examples.translation: Can you turn on the light for me?

senses.definition: To start or establish a new business, bank account, or class.

examples.text: Họ chuẩn bị mở một nhà hàng mới.
examples.translation: They are preparing to open a new restaurant.

faults.quote: Tôi mới mua một cái áo mới.
faults.why: Uses both the adverbial and adjectival senses of 'mới' in one sentence, confusing beginners.

notes: Placed after a noun, 'mới' is an adjective meaning 'new' (áo mới = new shirt). Placed before a verb, it is an adverb meaning 'just' or 'recently' (mới mua = just bought).

senses.definition: Not old; recently made, bought, or started.

examples.text: Hôm nay tôi mặc một cái áo mới.
examples.translation: Today I am wearing a new shirt.

senses.definition: Happening or done a very short time ago (used before a verb).

examples.text: Anh ấy mới đi làm về.
examples.translation: He just came home from work.

faults.quote: /mǔ/
faults.why: Uses Pinyin caron instead of IPA tone notation; missing glottalization of northern ngã tone.

faults.quote: while "nón" specifically refers to the traditional conical palm hat.
faults.why: In southern Vietnam, 'nón' is the normal everyday word for all hats and caps.

notes: 'Mũ' is the standard northern word for hats, caps, and helmets (e.g. 'mũ bảo hiểm' = safety helmet). In southern Vietnam, 'nón' is used instead (whereas in the North, 'nón' usually refers to the traditional conical hat).
Takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc', and the verb 'đội' (to wear on the head).

senses.definition: A covering worn on the head for protection against the sun, weather, or injury, or as a fashion item.

examples.text: Trời nắng quá, bạn nên đội mũ vào.
examples.translation: It is so sunny, you should put on a hat.

faults.quote: /mùa hɛ̀/
faults.why: Not valid IPA; uses Vietnamese orthography and grave accents instead of IPA symbols.

faults.quote: In southern Vietnam, this season is often referred to as mùa khô
faults.why: False: 'mùa hè' (summer, June–August) is during the southern rainy season, not dry season.

notes: Also called 'mùa hạ' in formal or poetic contexts. In everyday speech, 'hè' is often used alone, as in 'nghỉ hè' (summer vacation).

senses.definition: The warmest season of the year, between spring and autumn.

examples.text: Trời rất nóng vào mùa hè.
examples.translation: It is very hot in the summer.

faults.quote: /mənˈtəga/
faults.why: The second vowel in 'mentega' is /e/, not schwa /ə/: /mənˈteɡa/.

faults.quote: While they are often used interchangeably in recipes, they are distinct
faults.why: In everyday Indonesian, speakers often call margarine 'mentega'; note misses the actual usage point.

notes: In everyday speech, Indonesians often call margarine ('margarin') 'mentega' as well.

senses.definition: A soft yellow fat made from cream or milk, spread on bread or used in cooking.

examples.text: Oleskan sedikit mentega pada roti panggang Anda.
examples.translation: Spread a little butter on your toast.

faults.quote: Boleh saya lihat menu, tolong?
faults.why: Appending ', tolong?' is a calque of English ', please?'; Indonesian uses 'menunya' without 'tolong'.

senses.definition: A list of dishes available in a restaurant.

examples.text: Boleh saya lihat menunya?
examples.translation: May I see the menu, please?

senses.definition: A list of options or commands on a computer or phone screen.

examples.text: Pilih pengaturan dari menu utama.
examples.translation: Select settings from the main menu.

faults.why: Writing words on paper and writing a story are one everyday sense of 'to write'.

faults.quote: to write, to type
faults.why: 'To type' is 'mengetik', not 'menulis'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'membaca', which means to read.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'menulis' with 'membaca'; explain the nasal drop of 't' in 'meN- + tulis' instead.

notes: Formed from the root 'tulis' with the active prefix 'meN-' (the initial 't' drops and becomes 'n').

senses.definition: To put words, letters, or numbers on paper or a screen, or to compose a text such as a letter, book, or story.

examples.text: Dia menulis surat untuk temannya di Bali.
examples.translation: He is writing a letter to his friend in Bali.

examples.text: Penulis itu suka menulis cerita misteri.
examples.translation: That author likes to write mystery stories.

faults.quote: /mə.nu.ŋu/
faults.why: Missing the velar nasal coda before /ɡ/: should be /məˈnuŋɡu/.

faults.quote: If you are waiting for an event or for something to happen
faults.why: Wordy filler; a single concise note on the direct object vs English 'wait for' suffices.

notes: Formed from 'meN-' + 'tunggu' (the 't' drops). Unlike English 'wait for', 'menunggu' takes a direct object without a preposition: 'menunggu bus' (wait for the bus).

senses.definition: To stay in a place until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: Saya sedang menunggu teman di depan stasiun.
examples.translation: I am waiting for a friend in front of the station.

examples.text: Kami harus menunggu sampai hujan berhenti.
examples.translation: We have to wait until the rain stops.

faults.quote: Tolong menutup pintu itu.
faults.why: Imperatives with 'tolong' drop the 'meN-' prefix ('Tolong tutup pintu itu'), so 'menutup' is unnatural here.

corrected.shortGloss: to close, to shut; to cover
notes: Active form of the root 'tutup' ('meN-' + 'tutup'; the initial 't' drops). In polite requests with 'tolong', use the root 'tutup' instead: 'Tolong tutup pintu.'

senses.definition: To move something such as a door, window, or lid so that it is no longer open.

examples.text: Dia menutup pintu kamar dengan pelan.
examples.translation: She closed the bedroom door quietly.

senses.definition: To place something over something else in order to hide or protect it.

examples.text: Ibu menutup makanan itu dengan kain.
examples.translation: Mother covered the food with a cloth.

faults.quote: (study) The act of studying a subject to gain knowledge.
faults.why: 'ders' means lesson/subject; 'studying' is the idiom 'ders çalışmak', not 'ders' alone.
Missing the everyday sense 'school subject / course' (e.g., Matematik dersi).

notes: To say 'to study' or 'to do homework', use the collocation 'ders çalışmak' (e.g., Bu akşam ders çalışmam lazım — I need to study tonight).

senses.definition: A period of time in which a teacher instructs students.

examples.text: Ders saat on birde başlıyor.
examples.translation: The class starts at eleven o'clock.

senses.definition: An area of knowledge studied in school or university.

examples.text: En sevdiğim ders matematik.
examples.translation: My favorite subject is math.

faults.why: Should note that 'dinlemek' takes a direct object (accusative), unlike English 'listen to'.

notes: Unlike English 'listen to', 'dinlemek' is transitive and takes a direct object (accusative case when specific), not the dative '-e'.
Contrast with 'duymak' (to hear), which is passive, and 'dinlenmek' (to rest), which looks similar.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a sound or to someone speaking.

examples.text: Müzik dinlemeyi seviyorum.
examples.translation: I like listening to music.

examples.text: Lütfen beni dikkatlice dinle.
examples.translation: Please listen to me carefully.

faults.quote: Yarın diş hekimine randevum var.
faults.why: Ungrammatical case; 'randevum var' takes '-de' or '-den' (diş hekiminde randevum var), not '-e'.

notes: Literally 'tooth physician'. In everyday speech, 'dişçi' is also very common, while 'diş hekimi' is the standard, polite term.

senses.definition: A doctor who treats teeth and gums.

examples.text: Yarın diş hekiminde randevum var.
examples.translation: I have an appointment at the dentist's tomorrow.

faults.quote: (mechanics) A projecting part on a wheel, gear, comb, or saw.
faults.why: Gear/saw tooth is marginal at A2, while everyday 'clove (of garlic)' is missing.
Missing everyday cooking sense 'clove (of garlic)' (bir diş sarımsak).

faults.quote: The word 'diş' refers primarily to anatomical teeth, but it is also
faults.why: merely restates the senses.

notes: In recipes and everyday cooking, 'diş' is used as a measure word with numbers for cloves of garlic: iki diş sarımsak (two cloves of garlic).

senses.definition: One of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.

examples.text: Her sabah dişlerini fırçalar.
examples.translation: He brushes his teeth every morning.

senses.definition: A single section of a garlic bulb.

examples.text: Yemeğe iki diş sarımsak ekledim.
examples.translation: I added two cloves of garlic to the dish.

faults.quote: correct; straight; towards
faults.why: Includes 'towards' (a postposition), which is not covered in the adjective senses.

faults.quote: Bu yolu takip et, sonra doğru git.
faults.why: 'doğru git' uses 'doğru' as an adverb ('go straight'), not an adjective.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with sol (left) or yanlış (wrong).
faults.why: Unhelpful filler; 'sol' means left and 'yanlış' is simply the antonym.

notes: Also used as an adverb meaning 'straight' (Doğru git — Go straight) and, after the dative case (-e/-a), as a postposition meaning 'towards' in space or time (eve doğru — towards home; akşama doğru — towards evening).

senses.definition: Free from error; matching the facts.

examples.text: Bu bilgi tamamen doğru.
examples.translation: This information is completely correct.

senses.definition: Going in one direction without bending or curving.

examples.text: Kağıda doğru bir çizgi çizdi.
examples.translation: She drew a straight line on the paper.

faults.quote: The time of day after sunset and before going to sleep.
faults.why: Entry POS is adj, but sense 1 is a noun ('evening').

notes: It differs from 'đen' (black, the color).
As a noun (often 'buổi tối'), it means 'evening' or 'night'.

senses.definition: Having little or no light.

examples.text: Trời đã tối rồi.
examples.translation: It is already dark outside.

faults.quote: /tnot̚˧˥/
faults.why: Corrupted IPA with an extra 'n'; should be /tot̚˧˦/.

faults.quote: Cô ấy là một người rất tốt bụng.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'tốt bụng' instead of 'tốt' on its own.

faults.quote: "Tốt" is the standard, everyday word for good
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definitions instead of contrasting with 'ngon' or 'giỏi'.

notes: Used for quality, health, or moral character. For tasty food use 'ngon'; for skill or ability use 'giỏi'; for good looks use 'đẹp'.

senses.definition: Of high quality, or having positive and favourable qualities.

examples.text: Thời tiết hôm nay rất tốt.
examples.translation: The weather is very good today.

senses.definition: Kind, helpful, or morally upright in character.

examples.text: Anh ấy là một người bạn rất tốt.
examples.translation: He is a very good friend.

faults.quote: Use this to describe someone who is genuinely helpful, caring, and warm-hearted
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

notes: Literally 'good belly' ('tốt' = good, 'bụng' = belly/stomach, traditionally seen as the seat of one's feelings and intentions).

senses.definition: Kind, warm-hearted, and willing to help others.

examples.text: Cô ấy là một người rất tốt bụng.
examples.translation: She is a very kind person.

faults.quote: Use trả lời when someone asks you a question
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition.

notes: Takes a direct object without a preposition: 'trả lời câu hỏi' (to answer a question), 'trả lời tin nhắn' (to reply to a message), 'trả lời tôi' (to answer me).

senses.definition: To speak or write back to someone in response to a question, message, or letter.

examples.text: Xin hãy trả lời câu hỏi của tôi.
examples.translation: Please answer my question.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 枝子 (zhī zi), which refers to branches
faults.why: 枝子 is not a lookalike or soundalike; learners need the classifier 片 (piàn) instead.

notes: Counted with the measure word 片 (piàn): 一片叶子 (a leaf).
The suffix 子 (zi) is pronounced in the neutral tone.

senses.definition: The flat, usually green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch.

examples.text: 秋天到了，树上的叶子变黄了。
examples.translation: Autumn has arrived, and the leaves on the tree have turned yellow.

faults.quote: The character '博' (bó) relates to being extensive or broad
faults.why: Etymology filler; learners need the common measure words 家 (jiā) or 座 (zuò).

notes: Counted with the measure words 家 (jiā) or 座 (zuò): 一家博物馆 (a museum).

senses.definition: A building where objects of historical, scientific, artistic, or cultural interest are kept and shown to the public.

examples.text: 这个城市的博物馆很大。
examples.translation: The museum in this city is very big.

faults.why: Drinking water and water on the ground are the same everyday sense; standalone 水 does not mean any liquid.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'fruit juice' (shuǐguǒ zhī)
faults.why: Nobody confuses a one-syllable noun with a three-syllable compound; give common classifiers instead.

notes: Commonly counted with container or portion measure words such as 杯 (bēi, cup/glass), 瓶 (píng, bottle), or 滴 (dī, drop): 一杯水 (a glass of water).

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain, forms rivers and seas, and is drunk by people and animals.

examples.text: 我想喝一杯水。
examples.translation: I want to drink a glass of water.

examples.text: 地上有很多水。
examples.translation: There is a lot of water on the ground.

faults.quote: always pronounced as the third tone.
faults.why: False: third-tone sandhi changes 鸟 to second tone before another third tone; also tautological filler.

notes: Counted with the measure word 只 (zhī), or 群 (qún) for a flock: 一只鸟 (a bird).
In spoken Mandarin, it often takes the兒化 (érhuà) suffix: 鸟儿 (niǎor), or is used in the two-syllable form 小鸟 (xiǎo niǎo).

senses.definition: An animal with feathers, wings, and a beak that can usually fly.

examples.text: 树上有一只小鸟。
examples.translation: There is a little bird in the tree.

faults.quote: A hard, brittle, transparent substance used to make windows and bottles.
faults.why: As the note admits, the material 'glass' is 'kaca' in everyday Indonesian.

faults.quote: Meja itu mempunyai permukaan yang terbuat dari gelas.
faults.why: A glass tabletop is 'terbuat dari kaca', never 'terbuat dari gelas'.

notes: Refers to a drinking vessel (usually without a handle, unlike 'cangkir', a cup or mug). For the material glass (as in windows or bottles), use 'kaca'.
Often used as a classifier for drinks: 'segelas air' (a glass of water).

senses.definition: A container made of glass or plastic used for drinking liquids, or the amount it holds.

examples.text: Tolong ambilkan segelas air putih untuk saya.
examples.translation: Please get me a glass of water.

faults.quote: In addition to teeth in the mouth, 'gigi' is also used
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: A projecting part on a wheel or bar
faults.why: Defines only the cog tooth, missing vehicle transmission gears ('masuk gigi satu').

notes: The common verb for brushing one's teeth is 'sikat gigi' or 'menggosok gigi'.

senses.definition: One of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.

examples.text: Sikat gigi dua kali sehari.
examples.translation: Brush your teeth twice a day.

senses.definition: A toothed wheel in a machine or the gear setting of a vehicle or bicycle.

examples.text: Sepeda ini memiliki gigi yang bisa diatur.
examples.translation: This bicycle has adjustable gears.

faults.quote: It is synonymous with 'cuma-cuma' or 'percuma'
faults.why: In standard Indonesian, 'percuma' means 'in vain / useless', not 'free of charge'.

notes: Means 'free of charge' (synonymous with 'cuma-cuma'). For 'free' in the sense of freedom or having no obligations, use 'bebas'.

senses.definition: Costing nothing; not requiring payment.

examples.text: Minuman ini gratis untuk semua pelanggan.
examples.translation: This drink is free for all customers.

examples.text: Dia mendapatkan tiket konser itu secara gratis.
examples.translation: He got the concert ticket for free.

faults.why: Being nervous before a presentation and flustered talking to strangers are one meaning.

notes: Describes an immediate, often visible reaction (such as stage fright or stammering), whereas 'cemas' refers to general worry or anxiety.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing nervousness, agitation, or lack of calm in a stressful situation.

examples.text: Dia merasa gugup sebelum presentasi di depan kelas.
examples.translation: He felt nervous before the presentation in front of the class.

examples.text: Saya menjadi gugup saat harus berbicara dengan orang asing.
examples.translation: I get flustered when I have to talk to strangers.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'sans' is a single-word preposition, not an expression.

faults.quote: or plural with a determiner, you may see 'sans les' or 'sans des'
faults.why: 'sans des' is normally ungrammatical; 'sans' drops indefinite and partitive articles.

notes: Usually followed directly by a noun with no article where English uses 'a' or 'any' (sans sucre, sans veste). A definite article or possessive is kept when the noun is specific (sans le livre, sans mes clés).
Followed by the infinitive when it means 'without doing something' (sans dire un mot).

senses.definition: Not having, using, or accompanied by someone or something; not doing something.

examples.text: Je prends mon café sans sucre.
examples.translation: I take my coffee without sugar.

examples.text: Il est parti sans dire au revoir.
examples.translation: He left without saying goodbye.

faults.quote: to jump; to skip; to blow up
faults.why: 'to blow up' is in shortGloss, but there is no sense for it.

faults.quote: Use sauter when talking about jumping into the air or over
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions; more useful to note that 'skip' is neutral, not colloquial.

notes: Conjugated with avoir in compound tenses (j'ai sauté).

senses.definition: To push yourself off the ground into the air, or over something, using your legs.

examples.text: Il aime sauter par-dessus les flaques d'eau.
examples.translation: He likes to jump over the puddles.

senses.definition: To leave out a meal, a class, or a step instead of doing or having it.

examples.text: On peut sauter cette question si elle est trop difficile.
examples.translation: We can skip this question if it is too difficult.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to know how to
notes: Use savoir for facts, information, and (+ infinitive) knowing how to do something. Do not confuse it with connaître, which is followed by a noun and means being familiar with a person, place, or thing.
Highly irregular in the present: je sais, tu sais, il sait, nous savons, vous savez, ils savent; past participle: su.

senses.definition: To have a fact or piece of information in your mind, or be sure of it.

examples.text: Je sais où elle habite.
examples.translation: I know where she lives.

senses.definition: Followed by an infinitive: to have learned the skill to do something.

examples.text: Il sait jouer du piano.
examples.translation: He knows how to play the piano.

faults.quote: To become conscious or active after a period of rest or inactivity.
faults.why: Figurative shade of sense 0 ('a city waking up'), not a distinct A2 sense.

faults.quote: /ʁe.vɛ.je/
faults.why: Missing the reflexive pronoun /sə/ in the transcription of 'se réveiller'.

notes: Use se réveiller for stopping sleep, and se lever for getting out of bed. Without 'se', réveiller means to wake someone else up.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping and become awake.

examples.text: Je me réveille tous les jours à sept heures.
examples.translation: I wake up every day at seven o'clock.

faults.why: Should contrast with 'se rappeler', which beginners constantly confuse in construction.

notes: Takes the preposition de before a noun (se souvenir de quelque chose / de quelqu'un), unlike its synonym se rappeler, which takes a direct object.
Conjugated like venir (je me souviens, nous nous souvenons).

senses.definition: To have or bring a past event, person, or fact back into your mind.

examples.text: Je me souviens de notre premier voyage à Paris.
examples.translation: I remember our first trip to Paris.

faults.quote: /res.fɾjaˈðo/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'resfriado' is paroxytone (/resˈfɾja.ðo/), not oxytone.

notes: In Mexico, 'gripa' (or 'gripe') is also very commonly used in everyday speech for a common cold, alongside 'resfriado' and 'catarro'.

senses.definition: A common illness with a runny nose, sneezing, and sometimes a slight cough.

examples.text: Tengo un resfriado fuerte y no puedo salir de casa.
examples.translation: I have a bad cold and I cannot leave the house.

faults.quote: While the word comes from the French 'restaurer' (to restore)...
faults.why: Useless etymology warning against a false friend no English speaker would imagine.

faults.quote: Commonly shortened to 'el resto' in informal conversation in some regions...
faults.why: Irrelevant regionalism ('restó' is Rioplatense/Peninsular, not Mexican) for an A2 learner.

senses.definition: A place where you pay to eat a meal prepared and served by staff.

examples.text: Vamos a cenar a un restaurante muy bueno en el centro.
examples.translation: We are going to have dinner at a very good restaurant downtown.

faults.quote: A river (río) is a large, flowing body of water...
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage information.

notes: The written accent on the 'í' marks a hiatus, so the word is pronounced as two syllables (rí-o).

senses.definition: A large natural flow of water that runs along a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

examples.text: El río corre hacia el mar.
examples.translation: The river runs toward the sea.

notes: In Mexico, 'el sándwich' refers specifically to a sandwich made with sliced bread ('pan de caja'), whereas one made on a crusty roll is called 'la torta'.
Plural: 'los sándwiches'.

senses.definition: Food consisting of two slices of bread with fillings such as ham, cheese, or vegetables between them.

examples.text: Me preparé un sándwich de jamón y queso para cenar.
examples.translation: I made myself a ham and cheese sandwich for dinner.

faults.quote: A fact or piece of information that is not known to the
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same everyday meaning ('a secret').

faults.quote: secret, mystery
faults.why: Glosses 'secreto' as 'mystery' while note[1] explicitly warns not to confuse them.

notes: Commonly used in the phrase 'en secreto' (in secret / secretly).
Also used as an adjective ('secreto / secreta', secret).

senses.definition: A piece of information that is kept hidden from others or known only to a few people.

examples.text: Guarda este secreto y no se lo digas a nadie.
examples.translation: Keep this secret and don't tell anyone.

examples.text: El chef compartió el secreto de su receta.
examples.translation: The chef shared the secret of his recipe.

faults.quote: (memory) A short note or message written to help someone remember something.
faults.why: Literary/archaic sense not needed at A2; in modern Arabic مُلَاحَظَة or تَذْكِير is used.
Should give the broken plural تَذَاكِر (tadhākir) instead of discussing the literary sense.

notes: The plural is تَذَاكِر (tadhākir).
A return (round-trip) ticket is تَذْكِرَة ذَهَاب وَإِيَاب (tadhkirat dhahāb wa-ʾiyāb).

senses.definition: A paper or electronic document that allows you to travel on a vehicle or enter an event.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ تَذْكِرَةَ طَائِرَةٍ إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ.
examples.translation: I bought a plane ticket to Cairo.

faults.quote: Used both to mean a female child (girl) and a female offspring
faults.why: Restates the senses and misses the irregular plural بَنَات (banāt).

notes: The plural is بَنَات (banāt).
In the meaning 'daughter', it is interchangeable with اِبْنَة (ibna), which is slightly more formal.

senses.definition: A female child or young woman.

examples.text: هٰذِهِ بِنْتٌ لَطِيفَةٌ.
examples.translation: This is a nice girl.

senses.definition: A female child in relation to her parents.

examples.text: عِنْدِي بِنْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
examples.translation: I have one daughter.

faults.quote: The plural is أَحْذِيَة (aḥdiyyah), which you will often see
faults.why: Wrong transliteration: أَحْذِيَة is aḥdhiya (with dh and single y), not aḥdiyyah.

faults.quote: I bought a new shoe for work.
faults.why: In Arabic, singular حِذَاء regularly refers to a pair of shoes, not a single shoe.

notes: The singular حِذَاء usually refers to a pair of shoes, not just one shoe. The plural is أَحْذِيَة (ʾaḥdhiya).
حِذَاء رِيَاضِيّ (ḥidhāʾ riyāḍiyy) means 'trainers' or 'sneakers'.

senses.definition: An outer covering for the foot, usually worn in pairs.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ حِذَاءً جَدِيدًا لِلْعَمَلِ.
examples.translation: I bought a new pair of shoes for work.

faults.quote: Used specifically for the thick, warm covering on a bed.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Also spelled and pronounced بَطَّانِيَّة (baṭṭāniyya). The plural is بِطَانِيَّات (biṭāniyyāt).
Do not confuse with لِحَاف (liḥāf), which refers to a quilt or duvet.

senses.definition: A thick piece of cloth used as a cover to keep you warm in bed.

examples.text: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ جِدًّا، أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى بِطَانِيَّةٍ إِضَافِيَّةٍ.
examples.translation: The weather is very cold; I need an extra blanket.

faults.quote: عِنْدِي اجْتِمَاعٌ مُهِمٌّ مَعَ الْمُدِيرِ الصَّبَاحَ.
faults.why: Bare الصَّبَاحَ for 'in the morning' is unnatural; use فِي الصَّبَاحِ or هٰذَا الصَّبَاحَ.

faults.quote: Used frequently in both professional and formal contexts to refer to scheduled
faults.why: Restates the definition and misses the plural اجْتِمَاعَات.

notes: Takes the sound feminine plural اجْتِمَاعَات (ijtimāʿāt).

senses.definition: An occasion when people come together to discuss work, business, or official matters.

examples.text: عِنْدِي اجْتِمَاعٌ مُهِمٌّ مَعَ الْمُدِيرِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
examples.translation: I have an important meeting with the manager in the morning.

faults.why: 'Company/workplace' is an everyday informal meaning in France, mentioned in the note instead of senses.

notes: Since the 1990 spelling reform, 'boite' without the circumflex accent is also accepted.
For 'nightclub' (short for 'boîte de nuit'), the phrase 'aller en boîte' (without an article) is standard.

senses.definition: A container with flat sides, usually made of cardboard, wood, or plastic, used for storing or carrying things.

examples.text: J'ai rangé mes vieux livres dans une grande boîte en carton.
examples.translation: I put my old books away in a large cardboard box.

senses.definition: A sealed metal container for preserving food; a tin or can (short for 'boîte de conserve').

examples.text: Où est la boîte de thon pour la salade ?
examples.translation: Where is the tin of tuna for the salad?

senses.definition: (informal) A place where people go at night to dance and listen to music (short for 'boîte de nuit').

examples.text: On va en boîte ce samedi avec les copains.
examples.translation: We're going to a club this Saturday with friends.

senses.definition: (informal) A business or organization where one works.

examples.text: Il travaille dans une petite boîte d'informatique.
examples.translation: He works at a small IT company.

faults.quote: Use 'bouche' for the physical mouth on the face
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Used for the human mouth; for most animals, use 'la gueule' (which is very informal or vulgar when used for people).

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating and speaking.

examples.text: Elle a ouvert la bouche pour parler.
examples.translation: She opened her mouth to speak.

faults.quote: Use 'bouteille' for any container with a narrow neck
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition instead of giving useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Takes 'de' (or 'd'') without an article to name the contents: 'une bouteille d'eau' (a bottle of water), 'une bouteille de vin' (a bottle of wine).

senses.definition: A container for liquids with a narrow neck, typically made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: Elle a posé la bouteille d'eau sur la table.
examples.translation: She put the bottle of water on the table.

faults.quote: as in 'vivir à la campagne'.
faults.why: 'vivir' is Spanish; the French verb is 'vivre'.

notes: Use 'à la campagne' for being in or going to the countryside (e.g., 'vivre à la campagne'). Do not confuse with 'le pays' (a country/nation).

senses.definition: Land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, and villages.

examples.text: Nous aimons passer le week-end à la campagne.
examples.translation: We like to spend the weekend in the countryside.

senses.definition: An organized series of actions to achieve a political, commercial, or social goal.

examples.text: La campagne électorale commence la semaine prochaine.
examples.translation: The election campaign starts next week.

faults.quote: the expression 'tirer une carotte' means to swindle or trick someone
faults.why: 'Tirer une carotte' is dated/obscure slang and unhelpful for an A2 beginner.

notes: Notice the spelling difference from English: one 'r' and two 't's.

senses.definition: A long, pointed orange root eaten as a vegetable.

examples.text: Elle coupe une carotte pour la soupe.
examples.translation: She is cutting a carrot for the soup.

faults.quote: Bolehkah saya beli buah ini, paman?
faults.why: Addressing a seller as 'paman' is unnatural in modern daily Indonesian; 'Pak' is used.

notes: Used for both maternal and paternal uncles, as well as the husband of one's aunt.
In casual daily conversation, Indonesians often use 'om' (from Dutch) instead of 'paman'.

senses.definition: The brother of one's father or mother, or the husband of one's aunt.

examples.text: Paman saya datang berkunjung kemarin.
examples.translation: My uncle came to visit yesterday.

faults.why: Weather temperature and touch temperature are shades of one meaning ('hot').

faults.quote: hot, warm
faults.why: 'Warm' is 'hangat' in Indonesian, not 'panas'.
Missing the very common everyday sense of having a fever.

notes: Do not confuse with 'hangat' (warm) or 'pedas' (spicy hot, as in chili).

senses.definition: Having a high temperature; producing or feeling a lot of heat.

examples.text: Cuaca hari ini sangat panas.
examples.translation: The weather is very hot today.

examples.text: Hati-hati, kopinya masih panas.
examples.translation: Be careful, the coffee is still hot.

senses.definition: Of a person or body: having a fever.

examples.text: Badan anak itu panas sejak semalam.
examples.translation: That child has had a fever since last night.

faults.quote: fountain, spout
faults.why: A decorative park fountain is 'air mancur'; 'pancuran' is a water spout or pipe.

notes: For a modern bathroom shower, the English loanword 'shower' is very commonly used in conversation. For a decorative fountain, use 'air mancur'.

senses.definition: A bathroom fixture that sprays water from above for washing oneself.

examples.text: Dia sedang mandi di bawah pancuran.
examples.translation: She is bathing under the shower.

senses.definition: A pipe or bamboo tube from which a stream of water flows, used for washing or collecting water.

examples.text: Warga desa mencuci tangan di pancuran air.
examples.translation: The villagers wash their hands at the water spout.

faults.quote: /ˈpaɲaŋ/
faults.why: Missing the affricate /dʒ/: should be /ˈpandʒaŋ/.

faults.quote: Having a height that is greater than average, used for people.
faults.why: 'Panjang' never means 'tall' for people; the entry's own note contradicts this sense.

faults.quote: Anak itu memiliki rambut yang panjang.
faults.why: Example shows 'long hair' (sense 0), not a tall person.

notes: Used for objects, distances, hair, and time. For a person's or building's height, use 'tinggi' (tall). For a long duration of time, 'lama' is also very common.

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from one end to the other.

examples.text: Sungai itu sangat panjang.
examples.translation: That river is very long.

examples.text: Anak itu memiliki rambut yang panjang.
examples.translation: That child has long hair.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a great amount of time.

examples.text: Kami punya waktu libur yang panjang.
examples.translation: We have a long holiday.

faults.quote: Use 'pantai' for the area where land meets the sea.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful usage information.

senses.definition: The sandy or stony area of land along the edge of the sea.

examples.text: Anak-anak sedang bermain pasir di pantai.
examples.translation: The children are playing with sand on the beach.

examples.text: Kami ingin berlibur ke pantai minggu depan.
examples.translation: We want to go on vacation to the beach next week.

faults.quote: Used for any form of admission or passage: buses, trains, movies,
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammar help.

notes: The classifier is ใบ (bai).
Do not confuse with บัตร (bàt), which usually refers to a card (credit card, ID card), though บัตร is also often used for event or concert tickets.

senses.definition: A piece of paper or digital record that allows you to enter a place or travel on a vehicle.

examples.text: ฉันต้องซื้อตั๋วรถไฟไปเชียงใหม่
examples.translation: I need to buy a train ticket to Chiang Mai.

faults.quote: (trip) A journey to a place and back again. | glosses en: round trip
faults.why: การเดินทาง does not specifically mean a round trip; this is an invented sense.

corrected.headword: การเดินทาง
notes: Formed from การ (kaːn, nominalizer) + เดินทาง (dɤːn-tʰaːŋ, 'to travel').
For a casual vacation trip, the English loanword ทริป (tríp) is often used instead.

senses.definition: The act of traveling from one place to another, or a particular journey.

examples.text: การเดินทางไปเชียงใหม่ใช้เวลาเจ็ดชั่วโมง
examples.translation: The journey to Chiang Mai takes seven hours.
examples.matchedForm: การเดินทาง

faults.quote: /nǎŋ.sือ̌ː/
faults.why: Contains Thai vowel characters instead of IPA symbols (/nǎŋ.sɯ̌ː/).

notes: The classifier for books is เล่ม (lêm); for official documents or letters it is ฉบับ (cʰa.bàp).
อ่านหนังสือ (literally 'to read a book') is also the standard everyday phrase for 'to study'.

senses.definition: Pages with writing, bound together.

examples.text: ฉันกำลังอ่านหนังสืออยู่ที่บ้าน
examples.translation: I am reading a book at home.

senses.definition: An official written document or formal letter.

examples.text: เขาได้รับหนังสือจากบริษัท
examples.translation: He received an official letter from the company.

faults.quote: เราจะเจอกันที่เท้าภูเขา — We will meet at the base of the mountain.
faults.why: Thai uses เชิงเขา or ตีนเขา for the foot of a mountain, never เท้าภูเขา.

senses.definition: The part of the body at the bottom of the leg that you stand and walk on.

examples.text: เท้าของฉันเจ็บเพราะเดินนานเกินไป
examples.translation: My foot hurts because I walked too long.

faults.quote: fire; flames
faults.why: Does not cover the second sense (cooking heat/burner).

faults.quote: A hearth, stove, or burner used for cooking food.
faults.why: In cooking, 'fuego' usually means the cooking heat or flame, as in the example.

notes: In Mexican Spanish, an uncontrolled fire (as in a house or forest) is 'un incendio', while a campfire or bonfire is 'una fogata'.

senses.definition: The flames, heat, and light produced when something burns.

examples.text: Los niños se acercaron para calentarse con el fuego.
examples.translation: The children moved closer to warm themselves by the fire.

senses.definition: The flame, heat, or burner on a stove used for cooking.

examples.text: Pon la sopa a fuego lento para que no se queme.
examples.translation: Put the soup on low heat so it doesn't burn.

faults.quote: Like in English, it can also refer to the mechanical tool

notes: For a female cat specifically, use 'la gata'.
In Mexico, the game tic-tac-toe is also called 'el juego del gato' or simply 'el gato'.

senses.definition: A small furry mammal often kept as a pet.

examples.text: Mi gato duerme mucho durante el día.
examples.translation: My cat sleeps a lot during the day.

senses.definition: A tool used to lift a car off the ground to change a tire.

examples.text: Necesito el gato para cambiar esta llanta.
examples.translation: I need the jack to change this tire.

notes: In Mexico, 'helado' usually refers to cream-based ice cream, while water-based sorbet or sherbet is called 'nieve', and a popsicle is a 'paleta'.

senses.definition: A sweet, frozen food made from cream or milk.

examples.text: Quiero un helado de chocolate.
examples.translation: I want a chocolate ice cream.

faults.quote: A member of a religious brotherhood or community.
faults.why: Marginal sense for an A2 learner; informal 'bro/friend' or 'siblings' is much more useful.

notes: For a sister, use 'la hermana'. The masculine plural 'los hermanos' can mean either 'brothers' or 'siblings' (brothers and sisters together).

senses.definition: A boy or man who has the same parents as another person; in the plural ('hermanos'), brothers and sisters.

examples.text: Mi hermano menor vive en Guadalajara.
examples.translation: My younger brother lives in Guadalajara.

examples.text: ¿Tienes hermanos?
examples.translation: Do you have any siblings?

faults.quote: Jadwalnya masih ada yang luang.
faults.why: Example talks about a schedule (time, sense 0), not physical space (sense 1).

faults.quote: (space) Having space or a gap; not completely filled.
faults.why: Using 'luang' for physical space is rare in everyday Indonesian; 'lega' or 'kosong' is used.

faults.quote: While 'kosong' describes a container with nothing inside
faults.why: 'Kosong' is very commonly used for free time and schedules ('waktu kosong', 'jadwal kosong').

notes: Most commonly used in the phrase 'waktu luang' (free/spare time) and the derived verb 'meluangkan waktu' (to make time).

senses.definition: Of time or a schedule: free and unoccupied; available for other activities.

examples.text: Saya punya waktu luang sore ini untuk membaca.
examples.translation: I have spare time this afternoon to read.

examples.text: Jadwalnya masih ada yang luang.
examples.translation: There are still some free slots in the schedule.

faults.quote: funny, amusing, hilarous
faults.why: Typo in gloss: 'hilarous' instead of 'hilarious'.

faults.quote: That movie was so funny until I laughed out loud.
faults.why: Calqued 'sampai' as 'until'; in English result clauses it translates to 'that'.

faults.quote: Lihat kucing kecil itu, sangat lucu sekali.
faults.why: 'Sangat ... sekali' is a redundant double intensifier.

faults.quote: While 'lucu' primarily means funny, it is also frequently used
faults.why: merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Often used for small children, pets, or objects to mean 'cute' rather than 'humorous'; context makes the meaning clear.

senses.definition: Causing laughter or amusement.

examples.text: Film itu sangat lucu sampai saya tertawa terbahak-bahak.
