Should warn learners not to use قديم for a person's age (كبير في السن is used) and give the broken plural قُدَمَاء / قَدَامَى.

notes: Used for things, places, or how long a relationship has lasted, never for a person's age in years (use كَبِير فِي السِّنّ for an elderly person).
Opposite of جَدِيد (jadīd, 'new'). For human plurals, it takes the broken plural قُدَمَاء (qudamā').

senses.definition: Having existed or been used for a long time; not new.

examples.text: هٰذَا الكِتَابُ قَدِيمٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This book is very old.

senses.definition: Dating from the past, or having been in a role or relationship for a long time.

examples.text: هُوَ صَدِيقٌ قَدِيمٌ لِي.
examples.translation: He is an old friend of mine.

faults.quote: Feeling unhappy or angry because you want what someone else has.
faults.why: Oversplit senses, and puts envy first; غَيُور primarily means romantically/protectively jealous (حَسُود is envious).

faults.quote: Do not be too jealous of your life partner.
faults.why: غَيُور عَلَى means 'jealous/possessive over' a partner, whereas English 'jealous of' means envying them.
Needs to explain the prepositions (عَلَى for protective/romantic jealousy, مِن for jealousy toward a rival) and invariant gender.

notes: Takes عَلَى ('alā) for the person or thing one is possessive over, and مِن (min) for the person one envies or sees as a rival.
As an adjective on the فَعُول (fa'ūl) pattern, it stays غَيُور for both masculine and feminine singular in formal Arabic (though غَيُورَة is common in everyday speech).

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy, protective, or possessive because someone you love might be interested in others, or because someone else has what you want.

examples.text: لَا تَكُنْ غَيُورًا جِدًّا عَلَى شَرِيكِ حَيَاتِكَ.
examples.translation: Do not be overly jealous and possessive of your life partner.

examples.text: هُوَ غَيُورٌ مِنْ نَجَاحِ صَدِيقِهِ.
examples.translation: He is jealous of his friend's success.

faults.quote: One of the four periods that the year is divided into.
faults.why: 'Stazione' does not mean season; that is 'stagione' (which note[1] itself says).

faults.quote: /staˈtjo.ne/
faults.why: Standard Italian has geminate affricate /ts/: /statˈtsjo.ne/.

faults.quote: station; season
faults.why: Includes 'season', which is false for 'stazione'.

notes: By itself, 'la stazione' usually means the train station. It is also used in combinations like 'stazione degli autobus' (bus station), 'stazione di polizia' (police station), and 'stazione radio' (radio station).
Do not confuse with 'la stagione', which means 'season'.

senses.definition: A building and place where trains or buses regularly stop for passengers.

examples.text: Ci vediamo davanti alla stazione centrale.
examples.translation: Let's meet in front of the central station.

faults.quote: Used both for the celestial body and metaphorically for famous people
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Also used for star-shaped ratings, such as hotel categories ('un albergo a quattro stelle' — a four-star hotel).

senses.definition: A bright point of light seen in the night sky.

examples.text: C'è una stella molto luminosa stasera.
examples.translation: There is a very bright star tonight.

senses.definition: A very famous performer in cinema, music, or sports.

examples.text: Quell'attore è diventato una grande stella del cinema.
examples.translation: That actor has become a big movie star.

faults.why: Italian 'strada' covers both 'road' and 'street' as a single everyday concept.
Missing the very common everyday sense of 'way, route, direction' (e.g. 'sbagliare strada').

faults.quote: La strada è lunga per arrivare al mare.
faults.why: Awkward word order in Italian and calqued English translation.

notes: Covers both English 'road' (between towns) and 'street' (in a town). Compare with 'la via', which is used in street names and addresses (e.g. 'Via Roma').

senses.definition: A paved way for vehicles and people, either in a town or between places.

examples.text: Questa strada è piena di negozi.
examples.translation: This street is full of shops.

senses.definition: The route or direction taken to get somewhere.

examples.text: Scusi, mi può indicare la strada per la stazione?
examples.translation: Excuse me, can you tell me the way to the station?

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'borsa', which is a full-sized bag
faults.why: Restates the definition and warns against a word ('borsa') that neither looks nor sounds similar.

notes: The plural has a hard 'c', spelled 'ch': 'le tasche' (/ˈtas.ke/). Often used without an article after 'in': 'avere le mani in tasca' (to have one's hands in one's pockets).

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into clothing or a bag for carrying small items.

examples.text: Ho messo le chiavi nella tasca del cappotto.
examples.translation: I put the keys in my coat pocket.

notes: Used for cups with a handle for hot drinks like tea, milk, or American coffee; a small espresso cup is usually called 'la tazzina'. Compare with 'il bicchiere' (a drinking glass).

senses.definition: A small container with a handle, usually ceramic, used for drinking hot liquids such as tea or coffee.

examples.text: Ho bevuto una tazza di tè caldo.
examples.translation: I drank a cup of hot tea.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with the actual plant; context
faults.why: Obvious filler note; replaces useful grammar information such as classifiers.

faults.quote: น้ำไหลอ่อนจากฝักบัว
faults.why: Unnatural Thai phrasing; native speakers say น้ำฝักบัวไหลเบา.

notes: Literally 'lotus pod' (ฝัก 'pod' + บัว 'lotus'), named because the spray holes resemble the seeds in a lotus pod.
Takes the classifier อัน or หัว for a shower head, and ฝัก for a lotus pod.

senses.definition: A device in a bathroom or on a watering can that sprays water through small holes.

examples.text: น้ำฝักบัวไหลเบามาก
examples.translation: The water from the shower head has very low pressure.

senses.definition: The cone-shaped seed pod of a lotus plant, containing edible seeds.

examples.text: แม่ซื้อฝักบัวมาจากตลาด
examples.translation: Mom bought lotus pods from the market.

faults.why: Splits the English distinction between 'street' and 'road', which is one sense in Thai.

notes: Covers both city streets and intercity highways. A smaller side street or lane branching off a main road is called ซอย.
Its classifier is สาย.

senses.definition: A paved way for vehicles and people to travel on, either in a town or between places.

examples.text: ถนนสายนี้มีร้านอาหารอร่อยเยอะมาก
examples.translation: This street has many delicious restaurants.

examples.text: กรุณามองซ้ายมองขวาก่อนข้ามถนน
examples.translation: Please look left and right before crossing the road.

faults.quote: /dɔ̀ːk.máːj/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length in second syllable; ไม้ has a short vowel (/dɔ̀ːk.máj/).

notes: ดอกไม้ is the general word for a flower. When naming a specific flower or counting flowers, use ดอก alone (e.g. ดอกกุหลาบ 'rose', ดอกไม้สามดอก 'three flowers').

senses.definition: The coloured part of a plant that produces seeds and often has a pleasant smell.

examples.text: เธอชอบดอกไม้สีแดง
examples.translation: She likes red flowers.

faults.quote: While botanically a fruit, Thai speakers categorize this strictly as a vegetable
faults.why: Botanical trivia that does not help a learner use the Thai word.

notes: Literally 'foreign eggplant' (มะเขือ 'eggplant' + เทศ 'foreign'). Its classifier is ลูก or ผล.

senses.definition: A soft, round, red fruit eaten raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable.

examples.text: ฉันชอบใส่มะเขือเทศในสลัด
examples.translation: I like to put tomatoes in my salad.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical organ/area and the state of being pregnant.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions and glosses without adding usage guidance.

faults.quote: The state of being pregnant.
faults.why: Defined as a noun, but the gloss 'pregnant' and example 'เธอท้อง' are verbal/adjectival.

notes: Very common in everyday compounds: ปวดท้อง (stomachache), ท้องเสีย (diarrhea), and ท้องผูก (constipation).
For the internal organ specifically (such as in medical contexts), กระเพาะอาหาร is more precise.

senses.definition: The front part of the body below the chest, or the organ inside it where food goes.

examples.text: วันนี้ฉันปวดท้องมาก
examples.translation: I have a bad stomachache today.

senses.definition: (used as a verb) To be pregnant; (as a noun) pregnancy or the womb.

examples.text: ตอนนี้เธอท้องได้สามเดือนแล้ว
examples.translation: She is three months pregnant now.

faults.quote: Use 'Mutter' (mother) or 'Vater' (father) if you need to
faults.why: Misses the actual German word for a single parent ('das Elternteil').

notes: Always plural ('Meine Eltern sind...'). To refer to a single parent, use 'das Elternteil' (literally 'parent-part').

senses.definition: A person's mother and father.

examples.text: Meine Eltern kommen am Wochenende zu Besuch.
examples.translation: My parents are coming to visit on the weekend.

examples.text: Ich wohne noch bei meinen Eltern.
examples.translation: I still live with my parents.

faults.quote: hoax, fake news, scoop
faults.why: 'Scoop' means an exclusive true story, not a false report ('Ente' / canard).

faults.quote: (journalism) A false or misleading story published in the media.
faults.why: The journalistic idiom 'Zeitungsente' is not an everyday A2 sense.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'die Antenne' (antenna), which sounds
faults.why: Invented confusion; 'Ente' and 'Antenne' do not sound similar.

notes: Plural: 'die Enten'.

senses.definition: A common water bird with a flat beak, short legs, and webbed feet.

examples.text: Die Ente schwimmt auf dem See.
examples.translation: The duck is swimming on the lake.

faults.quote: Ich esse gerne eine Erdbeere zum Frühstück.
faults.why: Unnatural to eat a single strawberry for breakfast; plural 'Erdbeeren' is natural.

notes: Usually used in the plural when talking about food: 'die Erdbeeren'.

senses.definition: A small, soft, red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: Ich esse gerne Erdbeeren zum Frühstück.
examples.translation: I like eating strawberries for breakfast.

faults.quote: /ˈɛsˌʃtɛpçən/
faults.why: The vowel 'ä' in 'Stäbchen' is long (/ˈɛsˌʃtɛːpçən/), not short.

faults.quote: Always used in the plural in German, just as in
faults.why: False: the singular 'das Essstäbchen' exists, though plural is much more common.

faults.quote: Kannst du mit den Essstäbchen essen?
faults.why: Definite article 'den' is unnatural for general ability; 'mit Stäbchen / Essstäbchen' is used.

notes: Spelled with three 's's ('Ess' + 'Stäbchen'). Usually used in the plural (singular: 'das Essstäbchen'). In everyday speech, people often just say 'Stäbchen'.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used as utensils for eating, especially in East Asian cuisine.

examples.text: Kannst du mit Essstäbchen essen?
examples.translation: Can you eat with chopsticks?

faults.quote: the colloquial term 'die Klinik' used to refer to a hospital
faults.why: 'Die Klinik' is standard German (often for a specialized or university hospital), not colloquial.

notes: The plural is 'die Krankenhäuser'.
To say you are going to the hospital as a patient, use 'ins Krankenhaus' (into the hospital).

senses.definition: A large building where sick or injured people are treated by doctors and nurses.

examples.text: Mein Bruder muss heute ins Krankenhaus.
examples.translation: My brother has to go to the hospital today.

examples.text: Sie arbeitet als Ärztin in diesem Krankenhaus.
examples.translation: She works as a doctor in this hospital.

faults.why: In Germany, 'Land' (or 'Bundesland') very commonly means a federal state (e.g., Bavaria).

faults.quote: while 'die Lande' is a poetic or archaic way to say 'lands'
faults.why: An A2 learner does not need archaic/poetic plural forms; better to note uncountable 'countryside'.

notes: The plural is 'die Länder'. When meaning 'countryside', 'Land' is only used in the singular.
Use 'auf dem Land' (in the countryside) and 'aufs Land' (to the countryside), but 'im Land' for inside a country or state.

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and borders.

examples.text: Welches Land möchtest du als Nächstes besuchen?
examples.translation: Which country would you like to visit next?

senses.definition: Areas outside of towns and cities, with fields, forests, and farms.

examples.text: Wir fahren am Wochenende aufs Land.
examples.translation: We are going to the countryside this weekend.

senses.definition: One of the federal states that make up Germany or Austria (short for 'Bundesland').

examples.text: Deutschland besteht aus sechzehn Ländern.
examples.translation: Germany consists of sixteen federal states.

faults.quote: Note that 'Licht' is neuter. Confusingly, the German word 'Lichtblick'
faults.why: Restates gender and gives a bizarre, unhelpful tangent about an unrelated compound noun.

notes: The plural is 'die Lichter' (used for individual lights or lamps). To say 'turn on/off the light', use 'das Licht anmachen / ausmachen'.

senses.definition: The brightness from the sun, a lamp, or fire that allows you to see, or an electric lamp.

examples.text: Mach bitte das Licht an.
examples.translation: Please turn on the light.

examples.text: Das Licht der Sonne ist hell.
examples.translation: The light of the sun is bright.

faults.quote: A young unmarried woman. | glosses en: young woman, maiden
faults.why: Archaic/dated sense ('maiden') or indistinct from sense 0; A2 learners only need 'girl'.

notes: Grammatically neuter ('das') because of the diminutive ending '-chen' (all '-chen' nouns are neuter). The plural is 'die Mädchen' (unchanged).

senses.definition: A female child or teenager.

examples.text: Das Mädchen spielt im Garten.
examples.translation: The girl is playing in the garden.

faults.quote: Use 'Meer' when talking about the large, salt-water body
faults.why: Purely repeats the definition of the word.

notes: The plural is 'die Meere'.
Do not confuse with 'der See' (lake). The feminine 'die See' also means 'the sea', especially in northern Germany and in names like 'die Nordsee' (the North Sea).

senses.definition: The large body of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface.

examples.text: Wir fahren diesen Sommer ans Meer.
examples.translation: We are going to the sea this summer.

examples.text: Das Meer ist heute sehr ruhig.
examples.translation: The sea is very calm today.

faults.quote: Use mulut for the human or animal mouth.
faults.why: Restates the two senses; and 'mulut gua/botol' is standard Indonesian, not merely colloquial.

notes: The mouth or estuary of a river is usually called 'muara', while 'mulut' is used for caves, alleys, and containers ('mulut gua', 'mulut botol').

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Dia membuka mulutnya untuk berbicara.
examples.translation: He opened his mouth to speak.

senses.definition: The narrow opening or entrance of a cave, alley, or container.

examples.text: Kami berdiri di mulut gua yang gelap itu.
examples.translation: We stood at the mouth of that dark cave.

faults.quote: Used to express uncertainty or a possibility.
faults.why: All three notes are filler or misleading; 'mungkin' does not need to be sentence-initial.

faults.quote: maybe; possibly; perhaps
faults.why: Does not cover sense 1 ('possible').

notes: Can stand at the start of a sentence ('Mungkin dia lelah') or right before the predicate ('Dia mungkin lelah').
Also used as an adjective meaning 'possible', and in 'semungkin' or 'se-... mungkin' ('secepat mungkin' = as fast as possible).

senses.definition: Used to say that something may be true or may happen, without being sure.

examples.text: Mungkin dia akan datang nanti.
examples.translation: Maybe he will come later.

examples.text: Dia mungkin lelah hari ini.
examples.translation: Perhaps he is tired today.

senses.definition: Able to happen, exist, or be done.

examples.text: Apakah itu mungkin?
examples.translation: Is that possible?

faults.quote: Giving or sharing something generously, often used in the phrase 'murah hati'.
faults.why: 'Murah' alone does not mean generous; it only means this in compounds like 'murah hati'.

notes: Unlike English 'cheap', 'murah' is neutral and does not imply poor quality. To mean 'cheap-looking, tacky, trashy', use 'murahan'.
Appears in common compounds: 'murah hati' (generous) and 'murah senyum' (quick to smile).

senses.definition: Costing little money or lower in price than expected.

examples.text: Sayuran di pasar ini sangat murah.
examples.translation: The vegetables at this market are very cheap.

faults.quote: In Indonesian, the word is a loanword from European languages
faults.why: Stating that 'museum' looks like English 'museum' is obvious filler.

notes: Pronounced in three syllables: mu-se-um (/muˈse.ʊm/), not like English.

senses.definition: A building where historical, scientific, or artistic objects are kept and shown to the public.

examples.text: Kami mengunjungi museum seni di pusat kota.
examples.translation: We visited the art museum in the city center.

faults.quote: Di negara-negara Eropa, musim dingin sangatlah dingin dan sering turun salju.
faults.why: Repetitive ('musim dingin sangatlah dingin') and stiff for an A2 example.

notes: Literally 'cold season'. Indonesia itself has only two seasons: 'musim hujan' (rainy season) and 'musim kemarau' (dry season).

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.

examples.text: Di Jepang, salju turun pada musim dingin.
examples.translation: In Japan, it snows in the winter.

faults.quote: /pos.taˈne/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length in second syllable; should be /pos.taːˈne/.

faults.quote: Postane is the standard word for post office, often shortened from posta
faults.why: Restates the gloss and gives unhelpful historical trivia instead of pronunciation guidance.

notes: The first 'a' is pronounced long (/pos.taːˈne/). In Turkey, post offices are run by the national postal service and marked with yellow 'PTT' signs.

senses.definition: A building where you send letters and parcels and buy stamps.

examples.text: Yarın mektubu göndermek için postaneye gideceğim.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will go to the post office to send the letter.

faults.quote: /ɾyˈja/
faults.why: Missing vowel length; the first syllable has a long vowel (/ɾyːˈjaː/).

faults.quote: While 'rüya' refers specifically to the mental images you experience during sleep,
faults.why: Restates the two sense definitions without adding usage information like 'rüya görmek'.

notes: To say 'to have a dream' (while sleeping), Turkish uses the verb 'görmek' (to see): 'rüya görmek'.
For a life goal or daydream while awake, 'hayal' is much more common than 'rüya'.

senses.definition: A series of images, events, and feelings in your mind while you are sleeping.

examples.text: Dün gece çok ilginç bir rüya gördüm.
examples.translation: I had a very interesting dream last night.

senses.definition: Something that you strongly hope for or want to achieve.

examples.text: Üniversiteyi bitirmek onun en büyük rüyası.
examples.translation: Finishing university is his biggest dream.

faults.quote: /ɾyçˈɡaːɾ/
faults.why: Wrong consonant and vowel length; should be /ɾyzˈɟaɾ/ with palatalized /ɟ/ and short vowel.

faults.quote: it shows that the preceding consonant /ɡ/ is pronounced long or palatalized,
faults.why: Consonants are not pronounced 'long' due to â, nor is it dropped in speech.

notes: The circumflex over 'â' shows that the preceding 'g' is pronounced soft (palatalized, /ɟ/). In everyday writing, the circumflex is often omitted ('rüzgar').
commonly used with the verb 'esmek' (to blow): 'rüzgâr esiyor' (the wind is blowing).

senses.definition: Air moving naturally outside.

examples.text: Dışarıda çok sert bir rüzgâr esiyor.
examples.translation: A very strong wind is blowing outside.

faults.quote: /saːt/
faults.why: Wrong transcription; in standard Turkish it is disyllabic /saˈat/.
Missing the essential A1/A2 sense 'time of day / o'clock' (e.g., Saat kaç?).

faults.quote: (clock) A mechanical or electronic device... / (watch) A small portable clock...
faults.why: Clock and watch are a single sense in Turkish ('kol saati'/'duvar saati' specify).
Missing crucial irregular vowel harmony note: 'saat' takes front-vowel suffixes (saati, saatler).

faults.quote: The word 'saat' is used for a wall clock, a wrist watch,
faults.why: Merely repeats the senses; note[1] about 'sakat' is also unhelpful filler.

notes: Irregular vowel harmony: although its last vowel is 'a', 'saat' takes front-vowel suffixes: 'saati' (the clock/his watch), 'saatler' (clocks/hours), 'saatte' (at ... o'clock).

senses.definition: A device that measures and shows the time, worn on the wrist or placed in a room.

examples.text: Duvardaki saat yavaş çalışıyor.
examples.translation: The clock on the wall is running slow.

examples.text: Yeni aldığım saat suya dayanıklı.
examples.translation: The watch I just bought is water-resistant.

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: Toplantı bir saat sürecek.
examples.translation: The meeting will last one hour.

senses.definition: A particular point in the day, as shown by a clock.

examples.text: Affedersiniz, saat kaç?
examples.translation: Excuse me, what time is it?

examples.text: Ders saat dokuzda başlıyor.
examples.translation: The lesson starts at nine o'clock.

faults.quote: 已经 indicates that an action or state has already taken place
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage guidance.

notes: Placed before the verb or adjective, and commonly paired with 了 (le) at the end of the clause.

senses.definition: Before now or a specified time; by this time.

examples.text: 他已经走了。
examples.translation: He has already left.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 因为 is a conjunction/preposition, not a multi-word expression.

notes: Often paired with 所以 (suǒyǐ, 'so') in the second clause: 因为……，所以…… (Because..., therefore...); English never uses both 'because' and 'so' together, whereas Chinese normally does.

senses.definition: Used to introduce the cause or reason for something.

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以我没去。
examples.translation: Because it was raining, I didn't go.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 没有 is a verb/adverb, not a fixed expression.

faults.quote: Use 没有 to say something does not exist or you do not
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 0's definition; omits that 没 is a common short form.

corrected.shortGloss: not have; there is no; did not
notes: Often shortened to 没 (méi) in speech, especially before verbs.
To negate past or completed actions, use 没有 (or 没) instead of 不 (bù), which negates habitual, present, or future actions.

senses.definition: To not possess something, or for something not to exist (the negative of 有).

examples.text: 我没有钱。
examples.translation: I have no money.

senses.definition: Used before a verb to show that an action did not happen or has not been completed.

examples.text: 我没有去过北京。
examples.translation: I have never been to Beijing.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 和 is a conjunction and preposition, not an expression.

faults.quote: and, with
faults.why: 'with' belongs to sense 1 (preposition), not sense 0 ('and').

notes: As 'and', 和 connects nouns or pronouns, never whole clauses or sentences.
When meaning 'with', 和 is interchangeable with 跟 (gēn), which is slightly more colloquial.

senses.definition: Used to connect two or more nouns or noun phrases.

examples.text: 我喜欢苹果和香蕉。
examples.translation: I like apples and bananas.

senses.definition: Used before a person or noun to indicate doing something together or in relation to them.

examples.text: 我想和你看电影。
examples.translation: I want to watch a movie with you.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 但是 is a conjunction, not an expression.

faults.quote: Used to connect two contrasting clauses, much like "but" or "however"
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding new grammar insight.

notes: Often paired with 虽然 (suīrán, 'although') in the first clause: 虽然……，但是…… Unlike English, Chinese regularly uses both 'although' and 'but' in the same sentence.

senses.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what has just been said.

examples.text: 我想去，但是我没有时间。
examples.translation: I want to go, but I don't have time.

faults.quote: It is more formal and specific than ตรงนี้ (trong níi)
faults.why: ที่นี่ is broader ('this place/venue'), whereas ตรงนี้ is more specific ('this exact spot'), not less formal.

notes: Refers to a general place or venue (such as a building, city, or country), whereas ตรงนี้ refers to an exact physical spot ('right here').

senses.definition: In or at this place where the speaker is.

examples.text: ฉันชอบอยู่ที่นี่
examples.translation: I like living here.

faults.quote: Used to talk about the current moment.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

notes: Usually placed at the beginning or end of a clause. Do not confuse with เดี๋ยวนี้, which means 'right now' or 'immediately' (often in commands).

senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: ตอนนี้ฉันอยู่ที่บ้าน
examples.translation: I am at home now.

examples.text: ตอนนี้กี่โมงแล้ว
examples.translation: What time is it right now?

faults.quote: adv
faults.why: ต่างประเทศ is a noun ('foreign country') that modifies nouns or follows prepositions/verbs, not an adverb.

faults.quote: เขาสั่งซื้อสินค้ามาจากต่างประเทศ
faults.why: มาจากต่างประเทศ uses ต่างประเทศ as a noun ('a foreign country'), not as an attributive modifier ('foreign').

corrected.headword: ต่างประเทศ
notes: Used directly after verbs like ไป (go) or อยู่ (be at) to mean 'abroad' without needing a preposition, or placed after another noun to mean 'foreign' (e.g. นักท่องเที่ยวต่างประเทศ, 'foreign tourist').

senses.definition: A country other than one's own; abroad.

examples.text: ฉันอยากไปเที่ยวต่างประเทศปีหน้า
examples.translation: I want to travel abroad next year.
examples.matchedForm: ต่างประเทศ

examples.text: เขาสั่งซื้อสินค้ามาจากต่างประเทศ
examples.translation: He ordered products from abroad.
examples.matchedForm: ต่างประเทศ

senses.definition: Placed after a noun: from or relating to another country.

examples.text: บริษัทนี้มีลูกค้าต่างประเทศเยอะ
examples.translation: This company has many foreign customers.
examples.matchedForm: ต่างประเทศ

faults.quote: (past) Indicates a time before the current moment.
faults.why: แล้ว does not mean 'previously'; in the example, เคย means 'ever/before' while แล้ว marks completion ('already').

notes: As 'already', it goes at the end of the clause. As 'then' (often แล้วก็), it connects two clauses and comes at the start of the second.
Do not confuse with เพิ่ง ('just'), which comes before the verb for something that happened a moment ago.

senses.definition: At the end of a sentence: indicates that an action is completed or a new state has begun.

examples.text: ฉันกินข้าวแล้ว
examples.translation: I have already eaten.

senses.definition: Between clauses: after that; next in a sequence of events.

examples.text: ไปตลาดแล้วค่อยไปบ้านเพื่อน
examples.translation: Go to the market, and then go to a friend's house.

faults.quote: Used to express possibility or uncertainty. Note that in some contexts,
faults.why: Merely repeats the two sense definitions without adding grammar or usage guidance.

notes: Usually placed at the beginning of a sentence. When it means 'perhaps', the verb is often preceded by อาจจะ ('might').
In the sense 'sometimes', it is interchangeable with บางครั้ง.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible, though not certain.

examples.text: บางทีเขาอาจจะมาสาย
examples.translation: Perhaps he will be late.

senses.definition: On some occasions, rather than all the time.

examples.text: บางทีผมก็ไปเดินเล่นที่สวน
examples.translation: Sometimes I go for a walk in the park.

faults.quote: Used to describe the time between the middle of the afternoon
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

faults.quote: late afternoon, dusk
faults.why: 'Dusk' is twilight after sunset ('crepúsculo' or 'anoitecer'), not 'fim da tarde'.

notes: Usually used with the preposition 'em' ('no fim da tarde' = in the late afternoon); 'fim de tarde' without the article is also common.

senses.definition: The last part of the afternoon, before sunset.

examples.text: Eu gosto de caminhar no parque no fim da tarde.
examples.translation: I like to walk in the park in the late afternoon.

faults.quote: This term is used across all Portuguese-speaking countries to refer to
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the common colloquial synonym 'final de semana'.

faults.quote: In Portugal, you might occasionally hear the term 'fim-de-semana' with hyphens
faults.why: Hyphens are not heard in speech, and the 1990 Orthographic Agreement removed them everywhere.

notes: The plural is 'os fins de semana'. In Brazil, 'o final de semana' is equally common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: The period of Saturday and Sunday, usually a time for rest or leisure.

examples.text: Eu gosto de viajar no fim de semana.
examples.translation: I like to travel on the weekend.

examples.text: O fim de semana foi muito tranquilo.
examples.translation: The weekend was very peaceful.

faults.quote: 'fogo' is used both for the controlled fire we cook with and for destructive wildfires.
faults.why: In Brazil, a destructive wildfire or building fire is normally called 'incêndio', not 'fogo'.

notes: For a large, destructive fire (such as a building fire or wildfire), Portuguese normally uses 'o incêndio'. In the kitchen, 'fogo' also refers to a stove burner ('em fogo baixo' = on low heat).

senses.definition: Flames, heat, and light produced when something burns.

examples.text: Cuidado, não chegue perto do fogo!
examples.translation: Careful, don't get close to the fire!

examples.text: Deixe a sopa cozinhar em fogo baixo.
examples.translation: Let the soup cook on low heat.

faults.quote: The meat of a bird that is eaten as food.
faults.why: Too broad: defines poultry in general, not specifically chicken meat.

faults.quote: chicken, rooster
faults.why: 'Frango' is a young chicken or cockerel; an adult rooster that crows is 'galo'.

faults.quote: O frango canta cedo no terreiro da fazenda.
faults.why: In Portuguese, 'o galo canta' (the rooster crows), not 'o frango'; 'franga' lays eggs.

notes: In Brazil, 'frango' is the standard word for chicken as food. For the live bird on a farm, 'galinha' (hen) and 'galo' (rooster) are much more common.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken eaten as food.

examples.text: No almoço de domingo, comemos frango assado com batatas.
examples.translation: For Sunday lunch, we eat roast chicken with potatoes.

senses.definition: A young chicken, especially one raised for its meat.

examples.text: Eles criam frangos no sítio.
examples.translation: They raise chickens on the farm.

faults.why: Should give the feminine counterpart 'a garçonete' (waitress), which A1–A2 learners need together with 'garçom'.

notes: The feminine form is 'a garçonete' (waitress), and the plural of 'garçom' is 'os garçons'. In Portugal, 'empregado de mesa' is used instead.

senses.definition: A man who works in a restaurant or bar serving food and drinks to customers.

examples.text: O garçom trouxe o cardápio.
examples.translation: The waiter brought the menu.

faults.quote: eye; view; attention
faults.why: 'view' is not covered by the senses.

faults.quote: Note the irregular plural: l'occhio becomes gli occhi.
faults.why: The plural 'occhi' is regular for nouns in '-io' with an unstressed 'i'.

faults.quote: Ha chiuso un occhio per stanchezza.
faults.why: 'Chiudere un occhio' is the idiom 'to turn a blind eye'; people close both eyes.

notes: The plural is gli occhi (only one -i). Used as an informal exclamation, 'Occhio!' means 'Watch out!'.

senses.definition: The organ of sight in humans and animals.

examples.text: Ha gli occhi verdi come sua madre.
examples.translation: He has green eyes like his mother.

senses.definition: Watchful care or attention given to someone or something, especially in phrases like 'tenere d'occhio' (to keep an eye on).

examples.text: Tieni d'occhio la borsa mentre vado a comprare i biglietti.
examples.translation: Keep an eye on the bag while I go buy the tickets.

faults.quote: Most commonly refers to olive oil (olio d'oliva) in everyday Italian cooking,
faults.why: Mostly restates the two senses; plural spelling 'gli oli' is worth noting.

notes: In food contexts, 'olio' alone defaults to olive oil ('olio d'oliva'). The plural is 'gli oli' (with a single -i).

senses.definition: Liquid fat used for cooking or seasoning food, especially olive oil.

examples.text: Aggiungi un filo d'olio nella padella.
examples.translation: Add a drizzle of oil to the pan.

senses.definition: A thick liquid used to lubricate engines or machinery.

examples.text: Devo controllare l'olio della macchina.
examples.translation: I need to check the car's oil.

faults.quote: Even though an umbrella is carried rather than worn, it is often
faults.why: Pure filler about vocabulary categorization with no linguistic value for the learner.

notes: For a large beach or patio parasol, Italian uses 'l'ombrellone'.

senses.definition: A folding canopy on a stick carried to protect a person from rain.

examples.text: Prendi l'ombrello prima di uscire perché piove.
examples.translation: Take your umbrella before going out because it's raining.

faults.quote: /ˈɔ.ra/
faults.why: 'ora' has a close-mid vowel /ˈo.ra/, not open-mid /ˈɔ.ra/.

faults.quote: Used to mean both a sixty-minute period of time and the specific
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; should explain clock-telling or the adverb 'ora' (now).

notes: Used in telling the time: 'Che ora è?' or 'Che ore sono?' (What time is it?). As an adverb, 'ora' also means 'now'.

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: La lezione dura un'ora.
examples.translation: The lesson lasts an hour.

senses.definition: The time of day as shown by a clock, or the moment for something to happen.

examples.text: Ci vediamo a che ora?
examples.translation: What time are we meeting?

faults.quote: Ho sentito un rumore strano e ho teso l'orecchio.
faults.why: Uses a figurative idiom ('tendere l'orecchio') for the literal anatomical sense.

notes: In the plural, both the feminine 'le orecchie' (more common in everyday speech) and the masculine 'gli orecchi' are used.

senses.definition: The organ on the side of the head that humans and animals use to hear.

examples.text: Mi fa male l'orecchio destro.
examples.translation: My right ear hurts.

senses.definition: The ability to recognize and reproduce musical sounds accurately, especially in 'a orecchio' (by ear).

examples.text: Marco suona il pianoforte a orecchio senza leggere gli spartiti.
examples.translation: Marco plays the piano by ear without reading sheet music.

faults.quote: /deːr/
faults.why: Wrong initial consonant; 'beer' is pronounced /beːr/, not /deːr/.

faults.quote: An adult uncastrated male pig.
faults.why: Agricultural term 'breeding boar' is not an everyday A2 meaning.

faults.quote: The word 'beer' primarily means the wild animal, but it can also
faults.why: Restates the senses and contains a nonsensical typo ('berm/boar').

notes: Do not confuse with English 'beer', which is 'het bier' (/biːr/) in Dutch.

senses.definition: A large, heavy wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

examples.text: In het bos zagen we een grote beer lopen.
examples.translation: In the woods we saw a big bear walking.

faults.quote: While 'berg' primarily means mountain, it is also frequently used metaphorically
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: The plural 'de bergen' is often used to mean 'the mountains' as a holiday region (e.g., 'op vakantie naar de bergen').

senses.definition: A very high hill that rises high above the surrounding land.

examples.text: De top van de berg is bedekt met sneeuw.
examples.translation: The top of the mountain is covered with snow.

senses.definition: A large pile or amount of things.

examples.text: Er ligt een hele berg wasgoed op de stoel.
examples.translation: There is a whole pile of laundry on the chair.

faults.quote: bee; near
faults.why: Includes 'near' (preposition), which is not a sense of this noun entry.

notes: Do not confuse the noun 'de bij' (bee) with the very common preposition 'bij' (at, near, with).

senses.definition: A black and yellow flying insect that makes honey.

examples.text: De bij vliegt van bloem naar bloem.
examples.translation: The bee flies from flower to flower.

faults.quote: The noun 'bloem' is common gender, so it takes 'de'.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the header and headword.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse 'bloem' (flower or flour) with 'bloempot' (flowerpot).
faults.why: Trivial compound warning; learners do not confuse 'bloem' with 'bloempot'.
Should mention countability difference between the two senses, and contrast with 'meel'.

notes: In the sense of 'flour', 'bloem' is uncountable and refers to finely sifted white flour (as opposed to 'het meel', which includes wholemeal flour).

senses.definition: The coloured part of a plant that grows from the stem.

examples.text: Zij plukte een mooie bloem in de tuin.
examples.translation: She picked a pretty flower in the garden.

senses.definition: A fine white powder made from grain, used for baking bread or cake.

examples.text: Je hebt bloem en suiker nodig om deze taart te bakken.
examples.translation: You need flour and sugar to bake this cake.

faults.quote: farmer; peasant
faults.why: 'Peasant' is not in the senses and contradicts note [1].

faults.quote: the Dutch 'boer' is purely a professional title and does not carry
faults.why: False: 'boer' is also commonly used figuratively for someone rude or uncultured (boor).

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'boer' is the standard word for someone who runs a
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: A female farmer is 'de boerin'.
In informal speech, calling someone 'een boer' can also mean they are rude or unmannered.

senses.definition: A person who owns or runs a farm, grows crops, or keeps animals.

examples.text: De boer werkt elke dag hard op het land.
examples.translation: The farmer works hard on the land every day.

senses.definition: Air from the stomach that comes out noisily through the mouth (often in the diminutive 'boertje').

examples.text: De baby liet een boertje na het drinken.
examples.translation: The baby let out a little burp after drinking.

faults.quote: Often used in the plural 'la montagne' or 'les montagnes'
faults.why: 'la montagne' is singular, not plural; French uses singular 'à la montagne' where English uses plural.

faults.quote: (geography) A very high hill.
faults.why: Redundant duplicate of sense 0.

notes: French uses the singular 'à la montagne' to mean 'in the mountains' as a holiday destination or region.
Do not confuse with 'la colline' (hill), which is smaller and rounder.

senses.definition: A very high natural elevation of the earth's surface, or a mountainous region.

examples.text: La montagne est couverte de neige en hiver.
examples.translation: The mountain is covered in snow in winter.

examples.text: Nous aimons passer nos vacances à la montagne.
examples.translation: We like to spend our holidays in the mountains.

faults.quote: (display) A glass window at the front of a shop
faults.why: Dated/literary sense; everyday French uses 'la vitrine' for a shop window.

faults.quote: Often confused with 'l'heure' (time)... Be careful not to mix it up
faults.why: Unlikely confusions; misses the actually helpful contrast with 'l'horloge' / ' la pendule' (clock).

notes: Refers specifically to a small timepiece worn on the wrist or carried in a pocket; a wall or standing clock is 'une horloge' or 'une pendule'.

senses.definition: A small timepiece worn on the wrist.

examples.text: Elle regarde sa montre pour voir l'heure.
examples.translation: She looks at her watch to see the time.

faults.quote: Used with the partitive article 'de la' when talking about snow in general
faults.why: Inaccurate ('snow in general' takes 'la') and misses the common verb 'neiger' (to snow).

notes: To say 'it is snowing', French usually uses the impersonal verb 'il neige' rather than the noun.

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky and cover the ground.

examples.text: La neige recouvre les toits des maisons.
examples.translation: The snow covers the roofs of the houses.

faults.quote: Used for human and animal skin alike.
faults.why: Restates sense 0's definition.

notes: Do not confuse with 'le cuir' (leather), which is tanned animal skin used as a material.

senses.definition: The outer covering of a human or animal body.

examples.text: Elle a la peau douce.
examples.translation: She has soft skin.

senses.definition: The thin outer layer of certain fruits and vegetables.

examples.text: On peut manger la pomme avec la peau.
examples.translation: You can eat the apple with the skin on.

faults.quote: Used both for the literal colour of grass and leaves
faults.why: Restates the senses; should instead explain that it is a variable adjective (हरा/हरी/हरे).

faults.quote: बाज़ार में ताज़ा हरी सब्जियाँ मिलती हैं।
faults.why: हरी सब्जियाँ means 'green vegetables', and ताज़ा already means 'fresh'; fails to show 'unripe/raw'.

notes: Changes ending to match the noun: हरा (masculine singular), हरे (masculine plural/oblique), हरी (feminine).

senses.definition: Of the colour of growing grass or leaves.

examples.text: उसका हरा कोट बहुत सुंदर है।
examples.translation: His green coat is very nice.

senses.definition: Of fruit, plants, or wood: not yet ripe or dry; fresh.

examples.text: पेड़ पर अभी हरे आम लगे हैं।
examples.translation: There are still unripe mangoes on the tree.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning ('safe, secure').

faults.quote: It is commonly used both for physical safety from danger
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding usage or grammar help.

notes: Invariable adjective: its form does not change for gender or number.

senses.definition: Protected from danger, harm, loss, or theft.

examples.text: हम इस घर में सुरक्षित हैं।
examples.translation: We are safe in this house.

examples.text: आपकी फ़ाइलें कंप्यूटर में सुरक्षित हैं।
examples.translation: Your files are safe on the computer.

faults.quote: Used for general happiness or satisfaction.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Invariable adjective: its form does not change for gender or number.
To say what someone is happy with, use से (e.g. काम से खुश, 'happy with the work').
Also spelled ख़ुश (/xʊʃ/).

senses.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure and satisfaction.

examples.text: वह आज बहुत खुश है।
examples.translation: He is very happy today.

examples.text: मैं अपनी नौकरी से खुश हूँ।
examples.translation: I am pleased with my job.

faults.quote: suffering from an illness or injury.
faults.why: बीमार means ill/sick from disease, not injured.

faults.quote: बीमार is used for both temporary illnesses (like a cold)
faults.why: Obvious; works just like English 'ill/sick'.

notes: Invariable adjective: its form does not change for gender or number. With पड़ना (बीमार पड़ना) it means 'to fall ill'.

senses.definition: Not in good health; suffering from an illness.

examples.text: वह आज बहुत बीमार है।
examples.translation: He is very ill today.

faults.quote: compare it with 'vevla' (useless/idle)
faults.why: 'vevla' is not a standard Hindi word (corrupted Punjabi 'vehla', written only in Latin script).

faults.quote: Use 'khali' for physical objects, schedules, or seats.
faults.why: Just restates the senses using Latin transliteration.

notes: Invariable adjective: despite ending in -ई, its form never changes for gender or number.
Also spelled ख़ाली (/xɑː.liː/).

senses.definition: Having nothing inside; containing nothing.

examples.text: यह डिब्बा खाली है।
examples.translation: This box is empty.

senses.definition: Of a seat, room, or place: not being used or occupied.

examples.text: क्या यह सीट खाली है?
examples.translation: Is this seat free?

senses.definition: Of a person or time: not busy; having no work to do.

examples.text: मैं आज शाम को खाली हूँ।
examples.translation: I am free this evening.

faults.quote: sea; large area of salt water
faults.why: Includes a definition rather than just translation terms.

faults.quote: while the feminine form is often used in poetic contexts
faults.why: Misses the very common everyday Spanish idiom 'la mar de' (lots of / super).

notes: Usually masculine ('el mar'), though the feminine ('la mar') appears in weather forecasts, among sailors, and in the everyday idiom 'la mar de' (meaning 'lots of' or 'very', e.g. 'la mar de bien').

senses.definition: The large area of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface, or a particular part of it.

examples.text: Me encanta caminar por la orilla del mar.
examples.translation: I love walking along the edge of the sea.

faults.quote: Used for a male doctor; use 'la médica' for a female doctor.
faults.why: In Spain, 'la médico' is also widely used alongside 'la médica'.

notes: For a female doctor, both 'la médica' and 'la médico' are used in Spain.
'El doctor' / 'la doctora' is also used, especially as a title when addressing a doctor directly ('Buenos días, doctora').

senses.definition: A person who is qualified to treat people who are ill or injured.

examples.text: El médico me recetó un jarabe para la tos.
examples.translation: The doctor prescribed me cough syrup.

examples.text: Voy a ir al médico porque me duele mucho la espalda.
examples.translation: I am going to the doctor because my back hurts a lot.

faults.quote: Podría ver el menú, por favor?
faults.why: Missing required Spanish opening question mark '¿'.

notes: In Spain, 'el menú' (or 'el menú del día') usually means a fixed-price lunch of two courses, drink, and dessert or coffee. For the full list of dishes, ask for 'la carta'.

senses.definition: A fixed-price meal at a restaurant consisting of several courses.

examples.text: Hoy hemos comido el menú del día en la plaza.
examples.translation: Today we had the set lunch menu in the square.

senses.definition: The list of dishes and drinks available in a restaurant, or a list of options on a screen.

examples.text: ¿Podría ver el menú, por favor?
examples.translation: Could I see the menu, please?

faults.quote: While 'el mercado' can refer to the abstract concept of the economy
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions and obvious English meanings.

notes: In Spain, 'el mercado' usually refers to a permanent indoor food market with stalls, whereas an open-air street market held once a week is called 'el mercadillo'.

senses.definition: A building or open place with stalls selling food and other goods.

examples.text: Voy al mercado cada sábado para comprar fruta fresca.
examples.translation: I go to the market every Saturday to buy fresh fruit.

senses.definition: The system of buying and selling goods or services; trade.

examples.text: El mercado laboral es difícil para los jóvenes.
examples.translation: The job market is difficult for young people.

faults.quote: /sʏs/
faults.why: Standard Dutch pronunciation begins with a voiced /z/, i.e. /zʏs/.

notes: The diminutive 'zusje' is commonly used for a younger sister.
The longer form 'zuster' sounds formal or old-fashioned for a sibling, and usually means 'nurse' or 'nun' in modern Dutch.

senses.definition: A female person who shares at least one parent with another person.

examples.text: Mijn zus woont in Amsterdam.
examples.translation: My sister lives in Amsterdam.

faults.quote: use 'Ik denk dat...' followed by a standard word order clause.
faults.why: In Dutch, 'dat' introduces a subordinate clause, which sends the conjugated verb to the end.

faults.quote: Use 'denken' when you are considering an idea or forming an opinion.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition without adding usage or grammar information.

faults.quote: Laat me er even over denken.
faults.why: In this phrasing, native speakers normally use 'nadenken' ('er even over nadenken').

notes: Irregular verb: past tense 'dacht' / 'dachten', past participle 'gedacht' (hebben).
Takes the preposition 'aan' for thinking of someone or something ('Ik denk aan jou'). For pondering or reflecting on something, use the separable verb 'nadenken (over)'.
For a personal opinion or taste ('I think it's nice'), Dutch uses 'vinden' rather than 'denken' ('Ik vind het leuk'). Use 'denken' for a supposition or guess ('Ik denk dat hij komt').

senses.definition: To use the mind to consider something, or to believe that something is likely to be true.

examples.text: Ik denk dat het morgen gaat regenen.
examples.translation: I think it is going to rain tomorrow.

examples.text: Waar denk je aan?
examples.translation: What are you thinking about?

faults.quote: Ze draagt een donker blauwe jas.
faults.why: Spelling error: compound color adjectives in Dutch are written as one word ('donkerblauwe').

faults.quote: Use donker for places with little or no light, or for colors
faults.why: Restates the two sense definitions without adding new usage details.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with zwart (black); donker describes a lack of light
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'dark' and 'black' any more than in English.

notes: When combined with a color, it is written as a single compound word, e.g., 'donkerblauw' (dark blue) or 'donkergroen' (dark green).
Also used as a neuter noun, 'het donker' (the dark), as in 'in het donker' (in the dark).

senses.definition: Of a place or time: having little or no light.

examples.text: Het wordt al donker buiten.
examples.translation: It is already getting dark outside.

senses.definition: Of a color or object: deep in shade, not pale or light.

examples.text: Ze heeft donker haar en bruine ogen.
examples.translation: She has dark hair and brown eyes.

faults.quote: Ik heb na het sporten erg dorst.
faults.why: Before the noun 'dorst', the adjective 'erge' (or 'ontzettende' / 'veel') is more natural than 'erg'.

notes: Unlike English, where you 'are' thirsty, in Dutch you literally 'have' thirst ('Ik heb dorst'). To say 'very thirsty', use 'erge dorst hebben' or 'veel dorst hebben'.

senses.definition: To feel a need to drink something.

examples.text: Ik heb altijd dorst na het sporten.
examples.translation: I am always thirsty after exercising.

faults.quote: Use 'dragen' both when you are wearing clothes ('een jas dragen') and
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already shown in the entry.
Missing irregular past tense and participle forms ('droeg'/'droegen', 'gedragen') for strong verb.

notes: Irregular verb: past tense 'droeg' / 'droegen', past participle 'gedragen' (hebben).

senses.definition: To have clothes, shoes, glasses, or jewelry on your body.

examples.text: Wie draagt er vandaag een blauwe trui?
examples.translation: Who is wearing a blue sweater today?

senses.definition: To hold and support something or someone while moving.

examples.text: Kun je deze zware tas voor mij dragen?
examples.translation: Can you carry this heavy bag for me?

faults.why: Missing the essential everyday sense 'ir a + infinitive' (going to do), only mentioned in notes.

faults.quote: To leave a place.
faults.why: Does not mention that the departure sense requires the reflexive form 'irse'.

notes: Highly irregular: present 'voy, vas, va...', preterite 'fui, fuiste, fue...' (identical to 'ser').
Takes the preposition 'a' for destinations ('ir a Madrid') and 'en' for means of transport ('ir en tren').

senses.definition: To move or travel to a place.

examples.text: Voy a la tienda a comprar pan.
examples.translation: I am going to the shop to buy bread.

senses.definition: (ir a + infinitive) To intend or be about to do something in the near future.

examples.text: Mañana vamos a visitar a mis abuelos.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we are going to visit my grandparents.

senses.definition: (irse) To leave a place.

examples.text: Ya es tarde, me tengo que ir.
examples.translation: It is late, I have to go.

faults.quote: /xoˈβen/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'joven' is stressed on the first syllable (/ˈxoβen/).

faults.quote: It applies to people who have been alive for only a short time.
faults.why: Purely repeats the definition; should note the plural spelling 'jóvenes' and 'ser vs. estar'.

notes: Same form for masculine and feminine ('un chico joven', 'una chica joven'). The plural takes an accent mark: 'jóvenes'.
Also used as a noun ('un joven', 'una joven') meaning 'a young person'.

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for only a short time; not old.

examples.text: Mi profesora de español es muy joven.
examples.translation: My Spanish teacher is very young.

faults.why: Missing two crucial learner points: stem change (u -> ue) and contrast with 'tocar' for musical instruments.

faults.quote: No es bueno jugar con el dinero de los ahorros.
faults.why: 'Jugar con el dinero' means to be reckless with money; gambling is 'jugar dinero' or 'jugarse el dinero'.

notes: Stem-changing verb (u → ue): 'juego, juegas, juega...'
Followed by 'a' + definite article before a sport or game ('jugar al fútbol', 'jugar a las cartas'). For musical instruments, use 'tocar', not 'jugar'.

senses.definition: To take part in a game or sport for enjoyment.

examples.text: Ellos quieren jugar al baloncesto esta tarde.
examples.translation: They want to play basketball this afternoon.

senses.definition: To risk money on a game of chance or a bet.

examples.text: Perdió mucho dinero por jugar en el casino.
examples.translation: He lost a lot of money gambling at the casino.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the mother of one's mother or father.
faults.why: Restates the definition verbatim.

notes: Often used affectionately as 'abuelita' or shortened to 'abu'. The masculine plural 'los abuelos' means 'grandparents'.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace galletas para toda la familia.
examples.translation: My grandmother makes biscuits for the whole family.

faults.quote: /uˈtaŋatʃ/
faults.why: Wrong stress and missing /g/ phoneme; standard Turkish is /utanˈɡatʃ/.

faults.quote: Use this when describing someone who is naturally quiet or uncomfortable
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: Describes a lasting personality trait; compare with 'utanmış' (feeling ashamed or embarrassed in the moment).

senses.definition: Nervous or uncomfortable in social situations, especially around people one does not know well.

examples.text: Çok utangaç bir çocuk olduğu için kimseyle konuşmadı.
examples.translation: Because he is a very shy child, he did not speak with anyone.

faults.quote: /u.taˈnɯʃ/
faults.why: Missing the /m/ sound; 'utanmış' is pronounced /utanˈmɯʃ/, not 'utanış'.

faults.quote: Feeling shy and uncomfortable in front of others.
faults.why: Oversplit and confuses 'utanmış' (embarrassed/ashamed) with 'utangaç' (shy), contradicting note[1].

faults.quote: Topluluk önünde konuşurken biraz utanmış hissediyordu.
faults.why: 'Utanmış hissetmek' is an English calque ('feel embarrassed/shy'); Turkish uses the verb 'utanmak'.

notes: Past participle of 'utanmak' (to be ashamed/embarrassed).
Do not confuse with 'utangaç', which describes a habitually shy person; 'utanmış' describes someone feeling shame or embarrassment in a specific situation.

senses.definition: Feeling shame, guilt, or embarrassment, especially after doing something wrong or awkward.

examples.text: Yaptığı hatadan sonra çok utanmış görünüyordu.
examples.translation: He looked very ashamed after the mistake he made.

faults.quote: /yjaɯnˈmak/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA with wrong vowels; standard pronunciation is /ujanˈmak/.

faults.quote: To become aware of something or realize a situation.
faults.why: Slang/colloquial figurative sense ('wise up') is marginal for A2 and poorly exemplified.

notes: Intransitive (to wake up on one's own). Do not confuse with 'uyandırmak' (to wake someone else up).

senses.definition: To stop sleeping and become awake.

examples.text: Her sabah erken uyanırım.
examples.translation: I wake up early every morning.

faults.quote: To remain inactive, dormant, or unresponsive.
faults.why: Marginal figurative sense for A2; note[0] also makes an unnatural claim about 'mechanisms'.

faults.quote: to sleep; to be inactive
faults.why: Includes a marginal figurative sense unnecessary for A2 learners.

notes: Do not confuse with 'uyanmak' (to wake up) or 'uyutmak' (to put to sleep).

senses.definition: To rest your body and mind with your eyes closed, especially at night.

examples.text: Çok yorgunum, hemen uyumak istiyorum.
examples.translation: I am very tired, I want to sleep right away.

faults.quote: When apologizing, it often takes a dative suffix (üzgünüm).
faults.why: False grammar: '-üm' in 'üzgünüm' is the first-person singular copula ('I am'), not a dative suffix.

notes: Used both to describe feeling sad and to apologize. With the first-person ending, 'üzgünüm' means 'I am sorry'.

senses.definition: Feeling sorrow or unhappiness.

examples.text: Sınavı kazanamadığı için çok üzgün.
examples.translation: He is very sad because he didn't pass the exam.

senses.definition: Feeling regret for something that has happened or that one has done.

examples.text: Yaptığım hata için gerçekten üzgünüm.
examples.translation: I am truly sorry for the mistake I made.

faults.quote: /βakaˈθjon.es/
faults.why: Uses peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican /s/, and initial /b/ instead of /β/.

faults.quote: It covers both 'vacation' (the act of taking time off) and 'holidays'
faults.why: Filler note explaining US vs. UK English rather than Spanish usage (e.g. 'de vacaciones').

notes: Almost always used in the plural in Spanish ('mis vacaciones', not 'mi vacación').
Often used in the phrase 'estar de vacaciones' (to be on vacation) or 'ir de vacaciones' (to go on vacation).

senses.definition: A period of time when you do not work or go to school, often used for traveling or resting.

examples.text: Voy a pasar mis vacaciones en la playa.
examples.translation: I am going to spend my vacation at the beach.

faults.why: Needs to explain the reflexive form 'lavarse' used with body parts and definite articles.

faults.quote: Use 'lavar' for cleaning things with water, like dishes, clothes, or your hands.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: When washing a part of your own body, use the reflexive 'lavarse' with the definite article instead of a possessive: 'Me lavo las manos' (I wash my hands).
Do not confuse with 'limpiar' (to clean), which does not necessarily involve water.

senses.definition: To clean something using water and usually soap.

examples.text: Tengo que lavar los platos después de comer.
examples.translation: I have to wash the dishes after eating.

faults.quote: the stem changes slightly in some past and present forms (leí, leyó, leyendo)
faults.why: Not a stem or present-tense change; unstressed 'i' becomes 'y' between vowels in endings.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'leer' with 'ver' (to see).
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'to read' with 'to see'.

faults.quote: To interpret or understand someone's mood, intention, or a situation based on signs.
faults.why: Marginal figurative sense not needed at A2.

notes: Between vowels, the 'i' in endings changes to 'y' (for example: 'leyó', 'leyeron', 'leyendo'), and some endings take a written accent ('leí', 'leído').

senses.definition: To look at written words or symbols and understand their meaning.

examples.text: Me gusta leer novelas antes de dormir.
examples.translation: I like to read novels before going to sleep.

examples.text: Ella está leyendo un artículo muy interesante.
examples.translation: She is reading a very interesting article.

faults.quote: Used to describe both physical speed (a slow person) and the pace
faults.why: Both notes are filler; misses the useful 'ser lento' vs. 'estar lento' distinction.

notes: Used with 'ser' for something slow by nature ('un animal lento') and with 'estar' for something running slower than usual ('el internet está lento').

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or working at a low speed; not fast.

examples.text: El tráfico está muy lento hoy.
examples.translation: The traffic is very slow today.

faults.quote: Use libre to mean both physically free or unbound, and free from obligations
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses that 'libre' does not mean 'free of charge' ('gratis') and is invariable for gender.

notes: Does not change form for masculine and feminine ('un día libre', 'una mesa libre').
Do not use 'libre' to mean 'free of charge' (costing no money); use 'gratis' instead.

senses.definition: Of a person or time: not busy or restricted by work or obligations; of a seat, room, or taxi: not being used.

examples.text: ¿Estás libre mañana por la tarde?
examples.translation: Are you free tomorrow afternoon?

examples.text: ¿Está libre este asiento?
examples.translation: Is this seat taken?

senses.definition: Not in prison, in a cage, or under the control of another.

examples.text: Los pájaros vuelan libres por el cielo.
examples.translation: The birds fly free through the sky.

faults.quote: often shortened to 'papà' in everyday speech
faults.why: 'papà' is an informal synonym ('dad'), not a shortened form of 'padre'.
Missing vital A1/A2 grammar rule: singular family members drop the article with possessives ('mio padre').

notes: With singular possessive adjectives, drop the definite article (e.g., 'mio padre', not 'il mio padre'), except in the plural ('i miei padri') or with 'loro' ('il loro padre').
In everyday family speech, the informal words 'papà' or (especially in Tuscany) 'babbo' are used for 'dad'.

senses.definition: A male parent.

examples.text: Mio padre lavora in un ufficio.
examples.translation: My father works in an office.

faults.quote: Il paese has a useful double meaning: it can mean an entire
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: When referring to a state or nation, it is sometimes capitalized ('il Paese') to distinguish it from a village or small town.

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and borders.

examples.text: L'Italia è un paese bellissimo.
examples.translation: Italy is a very beautiful country.

senses.definition: A small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a city.

examples.text: Ieri sono andato a trovare i miei nonni in un piccolo paese in montagna.
examples.translation: Yesterday I went to visit my grandparents in a small mountain village.

faults.quote: In Italy, buying fresh bread daily at the local 'forno' (bakery) is
faults.why: Cultural trivia filler instead of useful linguistic guidance on countability.

notes: Usually uncountable in the singular; to ask for a single loaf or roll, use 'una pagnotta' (loaf) or 'un panino' (bread roll).

senses.definition: A baked food made from flour, water, and yeast.

examples.text: Compro sempre il pane fresco al mattino.
examples.translation: I always buy fresh bread in the morning.

faults.quote: consisting of two slices of bread or a split roll
faults.why: Contradicts the note; a sandwich made with sliced loaf bread is a 'tramezzino' or 'toast'.

notes: Refers specifically to a bread roll (plain or filled); sandwiches made with soft sliced bread are called 'tramezzini' (cold) or 'toast' (toasted).

senses.definition: A small bread roll split open and filled with ingredients such as cured meat, cheese, or vegetables.

examples.text: Mangio un panino al prosciutto per pranzo.
examples.translation: I am eating a ham sandwich for lunch.

senses.definition: A small, individual loaf of bread, eaten plain with a meal or used to make a sandwich.

examples.text: Compro due panini freschi dal fornaio.
examples.translation: I am buying two fresh bread rolls from the baker.

faults.quote: park; grounds
faults.why: 'grounds' is not in any of the senses.

faults.quote: In Italian, 'parco' is used for both large, protected areas of nature
faults.why: Simply repeats the two sense definitions.

notes: Forms the plural 'i parchi' (pronounced /ˈpar.ki/) to keep the hard /k/ sound.
Unlike 'parco' (usually a large public green space), 'giardino' typically refers to a smaller, often private garden with flowers or plants.

senses.definition: A large public green area in a town or city, used for walking and recreation.

examples.text: Oggi andiamo a fare una passeggiata al parco.
examples.translation: Today we are going for a walk in the park.

senses.definition: A large, protected area of natural land.

examples.text: Il parco nazionale è molto grande e pieno di animali.
examples.translation: The national park is very large and full of animals.

faults.quote: (anxiety) ... (tension)
faults.why: Nervousness and physical tension are one meaning in Korean (긴장하다).

faults.quote: 발표하기 전에 너무 긴장돼요.
faults.why: Uses the passive/inchoative verb 긴장되다 instead of the headword 긴장하다.

faults.quote: Use this when you feel nervous or anxious before an important event
faults.why: Restates the definition; should instead explain the common alternative 긴장되다.

corrected.shortGloss: to be nervous; to tense up
notes: In Korean, 긴장하다 is an action verb, so it uses present-tense forms like 긴장해요 or past-tense 긴장했어요 ('got nervous') to describe a current state.
The passive form 긴장되다 ('to feel nervous involuntarily') is also very common in spoken Korean.

senses.definition: To feel nervous, anxious, or physically tense before or during a stressful event.

examples.text: 발표하기 전에 너무 긴장했어요.
examples.translation: I was very nervous before giving the presentation.

examples.text: 어깨에 힘을 빼세요. 너무 긴장하지 말고요.
examples.translation: Relax your shoulders. Try not to tense up so much.

faults.quote: 내일 친구의 집을 방문할 거예요.
faults.why: Contradicts note[1]; 방문하다 is unnaturally stiff for visiting a friend's house.

notes: 방문하다 is a somewhat formal Sino-Korean verb used for visiting places, institutions, websites, or people in polite contexts (takes the object particle 을/를).
For casual visits to a friend's house, speakers normally say (집에) 놀러 가다 ('to go hang out').

senses.definition: To go to see a place or a person, especially officially or formally.

examples.text: 주말에 할머니 댁을 방문할 거예요.
examples.translation: I will visit my grandmother's house on the weekend.

examples.text: 어제 국립 박물관을 방문했습니다.
examples.translation: I visited the national museum yesterday.

faults.quote: (comprehension) ... (meaning)
faults.why: Both senses describe grasping meaning; they are the same sense.

faults.quote: 이 단어가 무슨 뜻인지 이해해요.
faults.why: For knowing a word's meaning, Koreans say 무슨 뜻인지 알아요, not 이해해요.
Missing the common sympathetic sense: understanding someone's feelings or situation.

notes: Do not confuse with 알다 ('to know'), which is used for knowing facts, word meanings, or people. To say 'I understand' in response to an instruction, Koreans usually say 알겠습니다.

senses.definition: To grasp the meaning, logic, or explanation of something.

examples.text: 선생님의 설명을 잘 이해했어요.
examples.translation: I understood the teacher's explanation well.

senses.definition: To sympathize with or accept someone's feelings, actions, or situation.

examples.text: 그 친구의 마음을 충분히 이해해요.
examples.translation: I fully understand how that friend feels.

faults.quote: /mʌmt͡ɕuda/
faults.why: 치읓 (ㅊ) is aspirated /t͡ɕʰ/, not unaspirated /t͡ɕ/.

faults.quote: (stop) ... (weather)
faults.why: Weather stopping is just an intransitive use of stopping; better split by intransitive vs. transitive.

notes: 멈추다 is used both intransitively (차가 멈추다, 'the car stops') and transitively (차를 멈추다, 'to stop the car').
For rain, snow, or crying coming to an end, 그치다 is also very common.

senses.definition: To cease moving, working, or happening.

examples.text: 갑자기 차가 멈추었다.
examples.translation: The car suddenly stopped.

examples.text: 비가 멈추면 나가자.
examples.translation: Let's go out when the rain stops.

senses.definition: To cause something moving or ongoing to stop.

examples.text: 그는 걸음을 멈추고 뒤를 돌아보았다.
examples.translation: He stopped walking and looked back.

faults.quote: (affection) ... (pleasure)
faults.why: Both senses mean 'to like' (taking 을/를); they are the same everyday meaning.
Note should explain the grammatical difference: 좋아하다 takes 을/를, while 좋다 takes 이/가.

notes: 좋아하다 is a transitive action verb taking the object particle 을/를 (영화를 좋아해요). Compare with the descriptive verb 좋다 ('to be good/liked'), which takes 이/가 (영화가 좋아요) and is most often used for the speaker's own preferences.

senses.definition: To find a person, thing, or activity pleasant or enjoyable; to be fond of.

examples.text: 나는 영화 보는 것을 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: I like watching movies.

examples.text: 동생은 강아지를 아주 좋아해요.
examples.translation: My younger sibling likes puppies very much.

faults.quote: I bought a new shoe for the party.
faults.why: Calque: singular 'um sapato' often refers to a pair in Portuguese, not one shoe.
Should note that singular 'sapato' is commonly used to mean a pair of shoes.

notes: Use 'tênis' for sneakers or athletic footwear; 'sapato' usually refers to dress or leather shoes.
In Brazilian Portuguese, the singular ('um sapato novo') is often used to refer to a pair of shoes.

senses.definition: An item of footwear that covers the foot, firmer than a slipper or sandal and shorter than a boot.

examples.text: Comprei sapatos novos para a festa.
examples.translation: I bought new shoes for the party.

faults.quote: /suˈɡɾe.du/
faults.why: Wrong first vowel for Brazilian Portuguese; it is /seˈɡɾe.du/.

faults.quote: secret; mystery; key
faults.why: 'mystery' is not in any sense's glosses and contradicts the note.

notes: Note the difference between 'segredo' (information deliberately kept hidden) and 'mistério' (something unknown or unexplained).

senses.definition: Information that is kept hidden from other people.

examples.text: Eu contei um segredo para a minha melhor amiga.
examples.translation: I told my best friend a secret.

senses.definition: The essential method or trick to achieve a good result.

examples.text: O segredo de um bom bolo é o tempo de forno.
examples.translation: The secret to a good cake is the baking time.

faults.quote: In São Paulo and other areas, 'semáforo' is more common in formal speech
faults.why: In São Paulo, 'farol' is the everyday word; 'semáforo' is the formal/standard term.

notes: 'Semáforo' is understood everywhere in Brazil, though everyday regional terms are very common, such as 'sinal' (Rio de Janeiro) and 'farol' (São Paulo).

senses.definition: A set of red, yellow, and green lights on the road that controls traffic.

examples.text: O carro parou no semáforo vermelho.
examples.translation: The car stopped at the red traffic light.

faults.quote: /soˈfa/
faults.why: The stressed vowel 'á' has an open sound in Portuguese: /soˈfa/ works, wait—actually in pt-BR 'canapé' in the note is an appetizer, not a common word for couch.

faults.quote: both 'sofá' and 'canapé' can refer to a couch
faults.why: Misleading for A2: in Brazil 'canapé' means a party appetizer; the furniture sense is obsolete.

notes: The stress is on the last syllable (so-FÁ), unlike English 'SO-fa'.

senses.definition: A long, soft seat with a back and arms for two or more people.

examples.text: Ele comprou um sofá novo para a sala de estar.
examples.translation: He bought a new sofa for the living room.

faults.quote: Used with the masculine article 'o'.
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

faults.quote: It is different from 'luz' (light) because 'sol' refers specifically
faults.why: Unnecessary filler; learners do not confuse 'sun' and 'light'.

notes: Notice the common expression 'tomar sol' (literally 'to take sun'), which means 'to sunbathe' or 'to get some sun'.

senses.definition: The star that gives the Earth light and heat during the day.

examples.text: O sol está brilhando muito hoje.
examples.translation: The sun is shining brightly today.

senses.definition: The light and heat coming from the sun.

examples.text: Não gosto de ficar muito tempo no sol.
examples.translation: I don't like staying in the sun for a long time.

faults.quote: Use 'vlees' when talking about animal tissue eaten as food, or simply
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

faults.quote: De wond deed pijn aan het vlees.
faults.why: Unidiomatic Dutch phrasing; 'tot op het vlees' or 'diep in het vlees' is natural.

notes: Uncountable; it does not have a plural form. For cold cuts or sliced meat for bread, use 'vleeswaren'.

senses.definition: Animal flesh eaten as food.

examples.text: Ik eet graag vlees bij het avondeten.
examples.translation: I like to eat meat with dinner.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of the body of a human or animal, consisting of muscle and fat.

examples.text: Het mes sneed diep in het vlees.
examples.translation: The knife cut deep into the flesh.

faults.quote: Use the neuter article 'het' with 'vliegtuig'.
faults.why: Merely restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword.

notes: To say 'by plane', use the preposition 'met': 'met het vliegtuig'.

senses.definition: A powered flying vehicle with wings used for carrying passengers or cargo.

examples.text: Het vliegtuig landt op de luchthaven.
examples.translation: The airplane lands at the airport.

faults.quote: /ˈvliɣ.vɛlt/
faults.why: After voiceless /x/ in 'vlieg-', the /v/ of '-veld' typically devoicest to /f/: /ˈvlix.fɛlt/.

notes: In everyday speech, 'het vliegveld' is the standard word for any airport. 'De luchthaven' is more formal and used in official names.

senses.definition: A place where aircraft arrive and depart, with runways and buildings for passengers.

examples.text: Ik moet op tijd op het vliegveld zijn voor mijn vlucht.
examples.translation: I have to be at the airport on time for my flight.

faults.quote: /ˈvʏy̯r/
faults.why: Wrong vowel transcription; 'uu' before 'r' in Dutch is /yːr/, not a diphthong.

faults.quote: Note that 'vuur' is a neuter noun, so it takes 'het vuur'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already given in the headword.

faults.quote: It can refer to both literal flames and the abstract feeling
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

notes: Use 'het vuur' for flames in general or a controlled fire (like a campfire). For a destructive, uncontrolled fire (like a house fire), use 'de brand'.

senses.definition: Flames that burn and give off heat and light.

examples.text: We warmen ons aan het vuur.
examples.translation: We are warming ourselves by the fire.

senses.definition: Strong enthusiasm, passion, or drive in a person.

examples.text: Ze spreekt met veel vuur over haar plannen.
examples.translation: She talks about her plans with a lot of passion.

faults.quote: This word is often used to describe the colour of things
faults.why: Trivial filler note that applies to the color yellow in any language.

faults.quote: The colour of a lemon, or of a ripe banana.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun phrase.

notes: Formed from สี ('color') + เหลือง ('yellow'). When describing a noun, สี is often dropped in casual speech (e.g. เสื้อเหลือง 'yellow shirt').

senses.definition: Having the color of a lemon or a ripe banana.

examples.text: ฉันชอบเสื้อสีเหลืองตัวนี้
examples.translation: I like this yellow shirt.

faults.quote: Behavior that is morally offensive or shameful.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Behavior that...').

notes: Literally 'worthy of dislike' (น่า + เกลียด). It is quite strong when used for someone's appearance, and very common for criticizing bad manners or inappropriate behavior.

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; unattractive.

examples.text: เสื้อตัวนี้สีน่าเกลียดมาก
examples.translation: This shirt is a very ugly color.

senses.definition: Of behavior: socially inappropriate, rude, or shameful.

examples.text: เขาทำตัวน่าเกลียดมากในงานปาร์ตี้
examples.translation: He behaved shamefully at the party.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are both 'dark' (without light); 'dusk' is a noun.

faults.quote: dark, dusk
faults.why: 'Dusk' is a noun, not an adjective.
Missing the everyday color modifier sense ('dark', as in สีน้ำเงินมืด / สีมืด).
