notes: False friend: 'un crayon' is a lead pencil ('un crayon à papier' or 'un crayon de couleur'), not an English wax crayon; a pen is 'un stylo'.

senses.definition: A thin wooden tool with a graphite or colored core, used for writing or drawing.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un crayon pour écrire.
examples.translation: I need a pencil to write.

faults.quote: A person who enjoys cooking meals at home for family or friends.
faults.why: Professional vs. amateur cook is one meaning ('un bon cuisinier'); no need for two senses.

faults.quote: Mon père est un bon cuisinier le dimanche.
faults.why: 'Être un bon cuisinier le dimanche' is unnatural; being a good cook isn't limited to Sundays.

faults.quote: and cuisinière when referring to a female cook or chef.
faults.why: Should warn that 'une cuisinière' also commonly means a kitchen stove/cooker.

notes: The feminine is 'la cuisinière' (/kɥi.zi.njɛʁ/), which also means a kitchen stove (cooker).
'Un chef' (or 'chef cuisinier') is the head of a restaurant kitchen; 'un cuisinier' is anyone who cooks professionally or well.

senses.definition: A person who prepares and cooks food, especially as a job.

examples.text: Le cuisinier prépare les plats pour les clients.
examples.translation: The cook prepares the dishes for the customers.

examples.text: Mon père est un très bon cuisinier.
examples.translation: My father is a very good cook.

faults.quote: Note the silent final 'r' in pronunciation.
faults.why: Completely false: the final 'r' in 'cœur' (/kœʁ/) is always pronounced.
Missing the everyday sense of 'heart' as the seat of emotions/feelings (noted in notes[1]).

notes: Spelled with the ligature 'œ' (o and e joined) and pronounced with a clear final 'r' (/kœʁ/).
Very common in the expression 'apprendre par cœur' (to learn by heart).

senses.definition: The organ in the chest that pumps blood through the body.

examples.text: Le médecin écoute son cœur avec un stéthoscope.
examples.translation: The doctor listens to his heart with a stethoscope.

senses.definition: The part of a person believed to feel love, kindness, or sadness, or the shape that represents it.

examples.text: Elle a bon cœur et aide toujours ses amis.
examples.translation: She has a kind heart and always helps her friends.

senses.definition: The central or most important part of a place or thing.

examples.text: Ils habitent au cœur de la ville.
examples.translation: They live in the heart of the city.

faults.quote: Do not confuse vinho (wine) with vinagre (vinegar).
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; filler note.

notes: Commonly specified as 'vinho tinto' (red wine), 'vinho branco' (white wine), or 'vinho seco / suave' (dry / sweet wine).

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grape juice.

examples.text: Nós gostamos de beber um bom vinho no jantar.
examples.translation: We like to drink good wine at dinner.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with 'próximo', which means 'near'
faults.why: Restates the definition and warns against an unlikely confusion.

notes: For a female neighbor, use 'a vizinha'. Also used as an adjective meaning 'neighboring' or 'next door' (e.g., 'a casa vizinha').

senses.definition: A person who lives next door or very close to you.

examples.text: O meu vizinho é muito simpático.
examples.translation: My neighbor is very friendly.

faults.quote: It is important to remember this distinction, as it is a fundamental
faults.why: Pure filler adding no information to the first note.

notes: Agrees with the gender of the speaker: men say 'obrigado' and women say 'obrigada'.
Followed by the preposition 'por' when thanking someone for something (e.g., 'obrigado pela ajuda').

senses.definition: Used to politely express gratitude to someone.

examples.text: Muito obrigado pela sua ajuda!
examples.translation: Thank you very much for your help!

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'ocupado' is used both for a person who has
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses and their glosses.

notes: Usually used with the verb 'estar' for temporary states (e.g., 'estou ocupado' — I am busy right now).

senses.definition: Of a person or time: having a lot of work or tasks to do.

examples.text: Desculpe, estou muito ocupado hoje.
examples.translation: Sorry, I am very busy today.

senses.definition: Of a place, seat, or phone line: currently in use or not available.

examples.text: Este assento está ocupado?
examples.translation: Is this seat taken?

faults.quote: (dislike) To dislike something very much; to find something extremely unpleasant.

Missing irregular present-tense stem change (odeio, odeia), essential for A2 learners.

faults.quote: It is less 'evil' than the English word 'hate'.
faults.why: Misleading: English 'hate' is used casually in the exact same way.

notes: Irregular in the present tense: the '-i-' changes to '-ei-' in the singular and third-person plural forms (eu odeio, você odeia, eles odeiam, but nós odiamos).

senses.definition: To feel a strong dislike for someone or something.

examples.text: Odeio acordar muito cedo na segunda-feira.
examples.translation: I hate waking up very early on Monday.

faults.quote: Used figuratively to describe a treacherous or deceitful person.
faults.why: merely repeats sense 1 instead of giving useful grammar or usage notes

senses.definition: A long, limbless reptile that crawls along the ground.

examples.text: Το φίδι γλίστρησε μέσα στα χόρτα.
examples.translation: The snake slithered into the grass.

senses.definition: A person who is not trustworthy or who acts in a deceitful way.

examples.text: Μην τον εμπιστεύεσαι, είναι φίδι.
examples.translation: Do not trust him, he is a snake.

faults.quote: Note the stress: the accent is on the final syllable 'o'.

faults.quote: Use this when you need to mail a letter or pick up
faults.why: merely restates the definition of a post office

senses.definition: A place where you go to send letters, postcards, and parcels.

examples.text: Πρέπει να πάω στο ταχυδρομείο να στείλω ένα δέμα.
examples.translation: I have to go to the post office to send a parcel.

senses.definition: The system of collecting and delivering letters and packages, or the items delivered.

examples.text: Θα σου στείλω το βιβλίο με το ταχυδρομείο.
examples.translation: I will send you the book by mail.

faults.quote: The word originates from 'κράσις' (mixture), reflecting the ancient Greek tradition
faults.why: etymological trivia is not needed by an A2 learner

notes: On wine lists and bottle labels, you will often see the formal word 'οίνος' (e.g. 'λευκός οίνος' for white wine), while 'κρασί' is the everyday word.

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grape juice.

examples.text: Θέλετε κόκκινο ή λευκό κρασί;
examples.translation: Do you want red or white wine?

faults.quote: Note that 'μάθημα' can refer to the lesson itself, the physical time
faults.why: merely restates the senses already listed in the entry

notes: Notice the irregular neuter plural in -τα: τα μαθήματα (genitive: του μαθήματος).
Often used in the phrase 'κάνω μάθημα' (to have a class / to teach a class).

senses.definition: A period of time during which someone is taught or learns something.

examples.text: Το μάθημα ξεκινά στις εννέα.
examples.translation: The lesson starts at nine.

senses.definition: A field of study or a specific subject in a school or university.

examples.text: Τα μαθηματικά είναι το αγαπημένο μου μάθημα.
examples.translation: Mathematics is my favorite subject.

senses.definition: An experience that teaches you how to behave better in the future.

examples.text: Αυτό ήταν ένα σκληρό μάθημα για όλους.
examples.translation: That was a hard lesson for everyone.

faults.quote: Τα δέντρα καθρεφτίζονται στα ήσυχη νερά στη λίμνη.
faults.why: ungrammatical gender/number agreement: 'στα ήσυχη νερά' instead of 'στα ήσυχα νερά της λίμνης'

faults.quote: A small pool of water, often left after rain.
faults.why: a rain puddle in everyday Greek is 'λακκούβα'; 'λίμνη' for puddle is marginal

senses.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

examples.text: Τα δέντρα καθρεφτίζονται στα ήσυχα νερά της λίμνης.
examples.translation: The trees are reflected in the calm waters of the lake.

faults.quote: Smutny describes a state of sadness or unhappiness.
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage info.

faults.quote: That was a very unhappy movie.
faults.why: Unnatural English translation; a movie is 'sad', not 'unhappy'.

notes: Unlike 'nieszczęśliwy' (unhappy, miserable), which describes a deeper or more permanent state, 'smutny' is used for a passing mood or something that causes sadness (like a film or song).

senses.definition: Feeling, showing, or causing sadness.

examples.text: Dzisiaj czuję się bardzo smutny.
examples.translation: I feel very sad today.

examples.text: To był bardzo smutny film.
examples.translation: That was a very sad movie.

faults.quote: Used as the standard term for the first meal of the day
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.
Should mention the common preposition 'na' ('na śniadanie' = for breakfast).

notes: Use 'jeść śniadanie' for 'to eat breakfast', and the preposition 'na' for 'for breakfast' (e.g., 'Co jest na śniadanie?').

senses.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.

examples.text: Jem śniadanie o ósmej rano.
examples.translation: I eat breakfast at eight in the morning.

faults.why: Should highlight that Polish says 'pada śnieg' (snow falls) for 'it is snowing'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'śnieżny' (adjective: snowy) or 'śnieżyć'
faults.why: Listing related words as 'do not confuse' is unhelpful filler.

notes: To say 'it is snowing', Polish uses the phrase 'pada śnieg' (literally 'snow is falling').
The final 'g' is pronounced as 'k' at the end of the word, but returns to a 'g' sound when endings are added (e.g., 'śniegu', 'na śniegu').

senses.definition: Soft, white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky when it is cold.

examples.text: Dzisiaj pada śnieg.
examples.translation: It is snowing today.

examples.text: Wszędzie leży biały śnieg.
examples.translation: White snow lies everywhere.

faults.quote: While 'słodki' directly translates to 'sweet' in terms of taste, it is
faults.why: Purely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

senses.definition: Having the taste of sugar or honey.

examples.text: Ten tort jest bardzo słodki.
examples.translation: This cake is very sweet.

senses.definition: Charming, cute, or endearing.

examples.text: Masz słodkiego psa.
examples.translation: You have a cute dog.

faults.quote: The liquid substance that circulates within a plant.
faults.why: Botanical 'sap' is not an everyday A2 sense; takes up room unnecessarily.

faults.quote: Sok usually refers to fruit or vegetable juice. It is a masculine
faults.why: Restates the gloss and gender field.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'sokół', which means 'falcon'.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; unhelpful filler note.

notes: Type of juice is usually expressed with an adjective after the noun (e.g., 'sok pomarańczowy' – orange juice, 'sok jabłkowy' – apple juice) or with 'z' + genitive ('sok z cytryny' – lemon juice).

senses.definition: A drink made from the liquid of fruit or vegetables.

examples.text: Piję świeży sok pomarańczowy.
examples.translation: I am drinking fresh orange juice.

faults.quote: Use 'casa' for the building itself or for saying 'at home'
faults.why: Wordy note; misses the crucial grammar point that 'en/a casa' drops the article.

notes: Notice that the article is dropped in expressions like 'en casa' (at home) and 'ir a casa' (to go home). Use 'hogar' when emphasizing the emotional feeling of a home.

senses.definition: A building where a person or family lives, or the place where one lives.

examples.text: Mi familia vive en una casa pequeña pero muy acogedora.
examples.translation: My family lives in a small but very cozy house.

senses.definition: A business, company, or institution.

examples.text: Esa casa editorial publica libros excelentes.
examples.translation: That publishing house publishes excellent books.

faults.quote: /seˈβoʎa/
faults.why: Gives seseo /s/ instead of Castilian /θ/ for initial 'ce-'.

faults.quote: onion; head (slang)
faults.why: Names a slang meaning that is not in the senses.

faults.quote: A bulbous plant grown for its edible bulb.
faults.why: Oversplits the vegetable and the plant into two separate senses for beginners.

faults.quote: La cebolla is the everyday bulb vegetable
faults.why: Note [0] restates the definition; note [1] teaches obscure slang not needed at A2.

senses.definition: A round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste.

examples.text: Cortar la cebolla siempre me hace llorar.
examples.translation: Cutting onions always makes me cry.

faults.quote: A social gathering or party where a meal is eaten
faults.why: Having dinner with others is a shade of the same meaning, not a separate sense.

notes: In Spain, 'la cena' is lighter than lunch and is typically eaten late in the evening, often from 9:00 p.m. onwards.

senses.definition: The main meal eaten in the evening, or a social gathering for this meal.

examples.text: Preparo la cena para toda la familia.
examples.translation: I prepare dinner for the whole family.

examples.text: Tenemos una cena de empresa el viernes.
examples.translation: We have a company dinner on Friday.

faults.quote: A piece of formal clothing worn over a shirt
faults.why: Shades of meaning (outer jacket vs. suit jacket/cardigan) are one sense in Spanish.

notes: In Spain, 'chaqueta' covers light outer jackets, suit jackets (also called 'americana'), and knitted cardigans. For a heavy winter coat, use 'abrigo'; for a sporty or leather jacket, 'cazadora' is very common.

senses.definition: A short piece of clothing with sleeves worn on the upper body over a shirt or top.

examples.text: Se puso la chaqueta porque hace frío fuera.
examples.translation: He put on his jacket because it is cold outside.

faults.quote: /krasʲɪvɨj/
faults.why: Missing primary stress mark and unstressed vowel reduction (/krɐˈsʲivɨj/).

faults.quote: Use 'красивый' as a general term for anything visually pleasing,
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Covers English 'beautiful', 'handsome' (for men), and 'pretty'.
Do not confuse with 'прекрасный', which is stronger and often means 'wonderful' or 'excellent'.

senses.definition: Very pleasant to look at; attractive.

examples.text: Это очень красивый город.
examples.translation: This is a very beautiful city.

examples.text: У неё красивое платье.
examples.translation: She has a pretty dress.

faults.quote: Used when someone has a lot of work or things to do.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two definitions.
Needs a note on the essential short forms (занят, занята, занято) and variant занятой.

notes: In everyday speech, the short forms 'за́нят' (m), 'занята́' (f), 'за́нято' (n), 'за́няты' (pl) are much more common than the long form: 'Я сейчас занят' (I'm busy right now).
Before a noun meaning 'a busy person', the stress often shifts to the end: 'занято́й человек'.

senses.definition: Having a lot of work or tasks to do; not free.

examples.text: Он сейчас очень занят.
examples.translation: He is very busy right now.

examples.text: Извините, это место занято.
examples.translation: Excuse me, this seat is taken.

faults.quote: Use мокрый when something is covered in liquid or soaked through
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Do not confuse with 'сырой', which means 'damp', 'humid' (of weather), or 'raw' (of food), nor with 'влажный' ('moist', 'slightly damp').

senses.definition: Covered or soaked in water or another liquid.

examples.text: После дождя моя куртка была совсем мокрая.
examples.translation: After the rain, my jacket was completely wet.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who has good manners and respects others.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Do not confuse with 'любезный' (kind, obliging), which refers to helpful behaviour rather than good manners.

senses.definition: Having or showing good manners and respect for others.

examples.text: Он очень вежливый мальчик и всегда здоровается.
examples.translation: He is a very polite boy and always says hello.

faults.quote: This word is a homonym: it can mean 'expensive' (related to cost)
faults.why: Restates the two senses and falsely calls a polysemous word a homonym.

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: Этот телефон слишком дорогой для меня.
examples.translation: This phone is too expensive for me.

senses.definition: Loved or valued very much; used to address someone with affection or politeness.

examples.text: Мой дорогой друг, я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.translation: My dear friend, I am very happy to see you.

notes: Do not confuse with 'oficina', which is a workshop or garage where machines or cars are repaired.

senses.definition: A room or building where administrative or professional work is done, typically with desks and computers.

examples.text: Ele passa o dia inteiro no escritório.
examples.translation: He spends the entire day at the office.

senses.definition: A room in a house used for reading, writing, or working.

examples.text: Vou terminar de ler este livro no meu escritório.
examples.translation: I will finish reading this book in my study.

faults.quote: Use 'espelho' for both the glass reflecting an image and for rearview
faults.why: Filler note; English 'mirror' works the exact same way.

notes: Note the closed 'ê' vowel sound /e/ (unlike the verb form 'eu espelho', which has an open 'é' sound /ɛ/).

senses.definition: A smooth glass surface that reflects the image of whatever is in front of it.

examples.text: Ela se olha no espelho antes de sair de casa.
examples.translation: She looks at herself in the mirror before leaving the house.

notes: 'Estudante' is a common-gender noun: the word itself does not change, only the article ('o estudante' for a male, 'a estudante' for a female).

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a school, college, or university.

examples.text: Ela é estudante de medicina.
examples.translation: She is a medical student.

faults.why: Missing crucial A1/A2 note that plural 'os filhos' means 'children' (sons and daughters).

senses.definition: A male child in relation to his parents; in the plural ('filhos'), offspring of either sex.

examples.text: O meu filho gosta de brincar no parque.
examples.translation: My son likes to play in the park.

examples.text: Eles têm três filhos: um menino e duas meninas.
examples.translation: They have three children: one boy and two girls.

faults.quote: péng yǒu

notes: The second syllable is pronounced in the neutral tone (péngyou). Common measure words are 个 (gè) and 位 (wèi, polite).

examples.translation: He is my best friend.

examples.text: 我们在聚会上认识了几个新朋友。
examples.translation: We made some new friends at the party.

faults.quote: 地图 is used for any kind of geographical map
faults.why: States the obvious instead of giving the measure word (张).

notes: Counted with 张 (zhāng) for flat or sheet maps: 一张地图 (a map).

senses.definition: A drawing or plan of an area that shows where roads, places, and rivers are.

examples.text: 请问附近有卖地图的吗？
examples.translation: Excuse me, is there anywhere nearby that sells maps?

notes: 奶酪 is the standard term for cheese in China. You will also often see and hear 芝士 (zhīshì), a loanword from English 'cheese' that is very common on menus and in bakeries.

examples.text: 我在披萨上加了很多奶酪。
examples.translation: I added a lot of cheese to the pizza.

faults.quote: Tea is essential to Chinese social and daily life.

senses.definition: A drink made by pouring hot water over dried leaves.

examples.text: 请喝一杯茶。
examples.translation: Please have a cup of tea.

senses.definition: The dried leaves used to make this drink, or the plant they grow on.

faults.quote: 同事 can refer to one colleague or several colleagues

notes: Counted with 个 (gè) or the polite 位 (wèi). Do not confuse with 同学 (tóngxué, classmate), which shares the prefix 同 ('same').

senses.definition: A person you work with at the same job or company.

examples.text: 今天中午我和同事一起去吃午饭。
examples.translation: I am going to have lunch with my colleagues at noon today.

faults.quote: While 'der Teller' is a flat plate, 'die Schüssel' is always

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for holding, mixing, or serving food.

examples.text: Ich habe den Salat in eine große Schüssel gegeben.
examples.translation: I put the salad into a large bowl.

faults.quote: Note that the word 'Schwester' has two common meanings: a female sibling
faults.why: First sentence merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

examples.translation: My sister is studying in Berlin.

senses.definition: A woman whose job is to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital.

examples.text: Die Schwester kommt gleich, um deinen Verband zu wechseln.
examples.translation: The nurse will be here soon to change your bandage.

faults.quote: A common struggle is that socks often go missing in the laundry

senses.definition: A short piece of soft clothing that covers the foot and ankle, worn inside a shoe.

examples.translation: I am putting on warm socks today.

faults.quote: Used with the definite article 'die' when talking about our star.

faults.quote: Similar to English, it can also refer to a sunlamp or

examples.translation: The sun is shining very brightly today.

examples.translation: Let's sit in the sun for a bit.

examples.translation: I hope you have good luck on this exam.

faults.quote: It is a fundamental ingredient in Japanese cooking, used in everything

notes: Often written in hiragana as たまねぎ, or with the kanji 玉葱.

senses.definition: A round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and flavor.

examples.text: 玉ねぎを切ると涙が出ます。
examples.translation: When I cut an onion, tears come out.

faults.quote: In Japanese, 'pasta' is a broad term that covers all types
faults.why: Notes [0] and [1] are redundant filler explaining what 'pasta' means in English.

senses.definition: Italian-style noodles made from flour, water, or eggs, typically served with a sauce.

examples.text: ランチにパスタを食べました。
examples.translation: I ate pasta for lunch.

faults.quote: Use 'sueldo' for a regular, fixed payment received monthly or yearly
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage guidance.

notes: Often interchangeable with 'el salario', though 'sueldo' is more common in everyday speech for a monthly paycheque.

senses.definition: Regular money paid to someone for their work, usually every month.

examples.text: Con mi nuevo sueldo puedo ahorrar un poco cada mes.
examples.translation: With my new salary I can save a little each month.

faults.quote: floor; ground; soil
faults.why: 'soil' is in shortGloss and notes, or missing from sense 1 glosses.

notes: Do not confuse with 'la planta' or 'el piso', which refer to a floor or storey of a building (e.g. 'la segunda planta').

senses.definition: The surface inside a room or building that you walk on.

examples.text: He tenido que limpiar el suelo porque se cayó el café.
examples.translation: I had to clean the floor because the coffee spilled.

senses.definition: The solid surface of the earth outside, or the soil in which plants grow.

examples.text: Las hojas secas cubren todo el suelo del parque.
examples.translation: The dry leaves cover all the ground in the park.

faults.quote: A state of rest in which conscious functions are suspended.
faults.why: Overly technical definition for A2; fails to include 'sleepiness' shown in the example.

notes: 'Tener sueño' means to be sleepy (literally 'to have sleepiness'), not to have a dream ('tener un sueño').

senses.definition: The natural state of resting with your eyes closed, or the feeling of needing to sleep.

examples.text: Tengo mucho sueño después de trabajar todo el día.
examples.translation: I am very sleepy after working all day.

examples.text: Tiene el sueño muy ligero.
examples.translation: He is a very light sleeper.

senses.definition: Events or images that you see in your mind while you are sleeping.

examples.text: Anoche tuve un sueño muy raro con gatos voladores.
examples.translation: Last night I had a very strange dream about flying cats.

senses.definition: Something that you want very much to happen in the future.

examples.text: Su gran sueño es viajar por todo el mundo.
examples.translation: Her big dream is to travel all over the world.

faults.quote: Used for large self-service food stores.
faults.why: Repeats the definition instead of giving useful usage notes (like the shortening 'el súper').

notes: In everyday speech, it is very often shortened to 'el súper' (e.g. 'Voy al súper').

senses.definition: A large shop selling food and household goods where customers serve themselves.

examples.text: Voy al supermercado a comprar fruta.
examples.translation: I am going to the supermarket to buy fruit.

faults.quote: some regions use 'cab' or 'remis'
faults.why: 'Cab' is an English word, not a regional Spanish word for taxi.

notes: In Spain, common expressions are 'pedir un taxi' (to order a taxi) and 'coger un taxi' (to take a taxi).

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: Voy a pedir un taxi para ir a la estación.
examples.translation: I am going to order a taxi to go to the station.

faults.why: Missing note on irregular -ής/-ής/-ές declension and everyday antonym ευγενικός.

notes: Declines in -ής (masculine), -ής (feminine), -ές (neuter): ο/η αγενής, το αγενές. The everyday opposite is 'ευγενικός' (polite).

senses.definition: Lacking manners or showing a lack of respect toward others.

examples.text: Είναι πολύ αγενής συμπεριφορά να μιλάς στο τηλέφωνο στο σινεμά.
examples.translation: It is very rude behavior to talk on the phone in the cinema.

faults.quote: Use 'αδύναμος' to describe someone lacking physical strength, but also to describe
faults.why: merely restates the two senses; better to distinguish from false friend αδύνατος.

notes: Do not confuse with 'αδύνατος', which usually means 'thin, slim' or 'impossible' rather than lacking strength.

senses.definition: Not strong; lacking physical power or energy.

examples.text: Μετά την αρρώστια ένιωθε πολύ αδύναμος.
examples.translation: After the illness he felt very weak.

senses.definition: Lacking force, effectiveness, or intensity; not convincing.

examples.text: Το επιχείρημά του ήταν αδύναμο και δεν έπεισε κανέναν.
examples.translation: His argument was weak and convinced no one.

faults.quote: /ðipzasˈmenos/
faults.why: Greek ψ is voiceless /ps/, never /pz/.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who physically needs water, but can also be
faults.why: Restates the senses; should instead note the common verb διψάω and preposition για.

notes: To say 'I am thirsty' in everyday conversation, Greek speakers more commonly use the verb 'διψάω' rather than 'είμαι διψασμένος'.
In the figurative sense ('thirsty for'), it takes the preposition 'για' (+ accusative).

senses.definition: Feeling a need for something to drink.

examples.text: Είμαι πολύ διψασμένος μετά τη γυμναστική.
examples.translation: I am very thirsty after the workout.

senses.definition: Having a strong desire for something, such as knowledge or success.

examples.text: Είναι διψασμένος για μάθηση και καινούργιες εμπειρίες.
examples.translation: He is thirsty for learning and new experiences.

faults.quote: /ðωreˈan/
faults.why: Contains Greek letter ω instead of IPA symbol /o/.

notes: Unlike English 'free', 'δωρεάν' only means 'costing nothing' (for 'not busy' or 'at liberty', use 'ελεύθερος').
It is indeclinable (never changes its ending) and is also used as an adverb ('μπήκαμε δωρεάν' — we got in for free).

senses.definition: Costing nothing; provided without payment.

examples.text: Το μουσείο είναι δωρεάν για όλους τους φοιτητές.
examples.translation: The museum is free for all students.

faults.quote: Like most Greek adjectives, πράσινος changes its ending to match the gender
faults.why: Generic grammar rule applicable to almost all Greek adjectives; filler.

senses.definition: Having the colour of grass or fresh leaves.

examples.text: Το γρασίδι στον κήπο είναι πράσινο.
examples.translation: The grass in the garden is green.

faults.why: In Mexico, 'huevos' is vulgar slang for testicles; learners should know 'blanquillos' as a polite alternative.

faults.quote: When a word starts with 'ue-', Spanish spelling adds a silent 'h'
faults.why: Redundant after note 0 and not useful for an A2 vocabulary card.

notes: The initial 'h' is silent.
In Mexico, the plural 'huevos' is also vulgar slang for testicles. It is completely normal for food, though some speakers say 'blanquillos' in markets to avoid double meanings.

senses.definition: The oval food with a shell that a hen or other bird lays.

examples.text: Me gusta comer un huevo frito en el desayuno.
examples.translation: I like to eat a fried egg for breakfast.

faults.quote: It is the coldest season of the year, following autumn and preceding
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: In Spanish, seasons are usually used with the definite article ('el invierno', 'la primavera') except often after 'en' or 'de' ('en invierno'), and are not capitalized.

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.

examples.text: El invierno es la estación más fría del año.
examples.translation: Winter is the coldest season of the year.

faults.quote: A person who takes part in a television, radio show, or public
faults.why: Shades of one meaning ('guest'); a media guest is just a guest at a show.

faults.quote: Use 'invitado' for anyone who is invited to your home, a party,
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition instead of giving grammatical or usage help.
Should mention 'la invitada' for a female guest and contrast with 'huésped' (hotel guest).

notes: Use 'el invitado' for a man and 'la invitada' for a woman.
For a paying guest at a hotel, use 'el/la huésped' rather than 'invitado'.

senses.definition: A person who is invited to a home, party, event, or show.

examples.text: Cada invitado trajo un regalo pequeño para la fiesta.
examples.translation: Each guest brought a small gift for the party.

faults.quote: Use 'jardín' for the plot of land around a house with grass
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: The children are playing in the house garden.
faults.why: 'In the house garden' is unnatural English; 'in the garden' or 'in the yard' is natural.

notes: Plural: 'los jardines' (no written accent).
Do not confuse with 'el patio', which usually refers to a paved courtyard or open space rather than a grassy or planted area.

senses.definition: An area of land next to a house or in a public space with grass, flowers, or trees.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín de la casa.
examples.translation: The children are playing in the yard.

faults.quote: A person who is the leader of an organization or a group.
faults.why: Both senses mean the person in charge of a group or workplace; merge them.

notes: Use 'el jefe' for a man and 'la jefa' for a woman.
In informal Mexican Spanish, 'mi jefe' and 'mi jefa' are also very commonly used to mean 'my dad' and 'my mom'.

senses.definition: The person in charge of a workplace, department, or group.

examples.text: Tengo una reunión importante con mi jefe mañana por la mañana.
examples.translation: I have an important meeting with my boss tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Ella es la jefa de todo el proyecto.
examples.translation: She is the head of the whole project.

faults.quote: Klimmen is used for both using hands and feet...
faults.why: Restates the senses; omits strong conjugation and auxiliary verbs (zijn/hebben).

notes: Strong verb: klom, geklommen. Takes 'zijn' when a direction or destination is given (Ik ben naar boven geklommen), and 'hebben' for the activity itself.

senses.definition: To go up using hands and feet, or using equipment, on a steep surface.

examples.text: De kinderen klimmen graag in de oude eik in het park.
examples.translation: The children love to climb the old oak tree in the park.

senses.definition: To rise or go up to a higher level, often used for prices, numbers, or the sun.

examples.text: De temperaturen klimmen deze week naar recordhoogten.
examples.translation: Temperatures are climbing to record highs this week.

faults.quote: Use knuffelen when you want to express warmth, comfort, or affection
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage info.

notes: Can be used transitively (iemand knuffelen) or with 'met' (knuffelen met iemand).
Do not confuse with 'omhelzen', which is slightly more formal and means to embrace briefly, whereas 'knuffelen' implies a softer, longer cuddle.

senses.definition: To hold someone close in your arms to show affection or comfort.

examples.text: De moeder wil haar kind knuffelen na een lange dag.
examples.translation: The mother wants to cuddle her child after a long day.

faults.quote: To heat a liquid until it bubbles and turns to steam.
faults.why: Defines only the transitive use, while the example is intransitive ('Het water begint te koken').

faults.quote: Use koken for preparing food in general, but also specifically...
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses listed below.

notes: Unlike English 'to cook', 'koken' is also the standard word for 'to boil' (een ei koken = to boil an egg; het water kookt = the water is boiling).

senses.definition: To prepare food or a meal by heating it.

examples.text: Ik ga vandaag lekker voor ons koken.
examples.translation: I am going to cook a nice meal for us today.

senses.definition: Of a liquid: to reach the temperature at which it bubbles; or to heat a liquid or food in this way.

examples.text: Het water begint te koken.
examples.translation: The water is starting to boil.

faults.quote: Note that 'komen' is also used as an auxiliary verb in phrases like 'ik kom eraan'
faults.why: 'Komen' is a main verb here (from 'eraankomen'), not an auxiliary verb.

faults.quote: De trein komt om vijf uur aan op het station.
faults.why: Uses the separable verb 'aankomen' ('komt ... aan'), not 'komen'.
Senses 0 and 1 are both 'to come/get somewhere'; misses the common sense 'to happen/be caused by'.
Missing irregular conjugation (komt, kwam/kwamen, is gekomen).

notes: Irregular verb: hij komt, kwam/kwamen, is gekomen (always takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense).
Used for movement towards the speaker or the place being talked about, or for accompanying the speaker (Kom je mee?).

senses.definition: To move towards or reach the speaker or a specified place.

examples.text: Kom je morgen naar mijn feestje?
examples.translation: Are you coming to my party tomorrow?

senses.definition: To happen, arise, or be caused by something (especially with 'door').

examples.text: Hoe komt het dat je zo laat bent?
examples.translation: How come you are so late?

faults.quote: Use 'kopen' for everyday purchases like groceries, clothes, or household items.
faults.why: Omits irregular past forms 'kocht, gekocht', which an A2 learner needs.

notes: Irregular verb: kocht, heeft gekocht.
Standard everyday word for buying; 'aanschaffen' is more formal.

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.

examples.text: Ik wil graag een nieuwe jas kopen.
examples.translation: I would like to buy a new jacket.

faults.quote: Use the preposition 'na' with the accusative when you are calling
faults.why: 'Dzwonić/zamawiać' do not take 'na', and the given examples lack 'na' entirely.

faults.quote: żeby nie spóższyć się na pociąg.
faults.why: Non-existent spelling 'spóższyć'; the correct verb is 'spóźnić'.

notes: For travelling by taxi, use the instrumental case without a preposition: 'jechać taksówką' (to go by taxi).
Common collocations: 'brać/łapać taksówkę' (to take/catch a taxi), 'zamawiać taksówkę' (to order a taxi), 'czekać na taksówkę' (to wait for a taxi).

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: Musimy złapać taksówkę, żeby nie spóźnić się na pociąg.
examples.translation: We need to catch a taxi so we don't miss the train.

faults.quote: Can also refer to a 'cymbal' in a musical drum kit
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding grammar or usage help.

faults.quote: A metal percussion instrument used in a drum set.
faults.why: Cymbal is rarely singular and marginal for A2 compared to 'plate/bowl of food'.

notes: Covers both flat dinner plates ('talerz płytki') and soup bowls with a rim ('talerz głęboki'). Contrast with 'miska' (a deeper, rimless bowl).

senses.definition: A flat or slightly hollow dish from which food is eaten, or the amount of food on it.

examples.text: Połóż jedzenie na talerzu.
examples.translation: Put the food on the plate.

examples.text: Zjadłem cały talerz gorącej zupy.
examples.translation: I ate a whole bowl of hot soup.

faults.quote: /ˈtaɲ.t͡ɕit͡ɕ/
faults.why: 'cz' is retroflex /t͡ʂ/ and 'y' is /ɨ/: correct IPA is /ˈtaɲ.t͡ʂɨt͡ɕ/.

faults.quote: Note the consonant cluster 'ńc'. ... before the soft 'ć'
faults.why: The word contains 'ńcz' (hard /t͡ʂ/), not 'ńc' or soft 'ć'.

notes: Imperfective aspect. Use the perfective 'zatańczyć' for a single, completed dance.

senses.definition: To move your body rhythmically, usually to music.

examples.text: Lubię tańczyć do muzyki jazzowej.
examples.translation: I like to dance to jazz music.

examples.text: Na weselu wszyscy zaczęli tańczyć.
examples.translation: At the wedding, everyone started to dance.

faults.quote: Das Opernhaus ist sehr alt.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'Opernhaus' instead of the headword 'Haus'.
Missing the essential A1/A2 sense 'home' in 'zu Hause' and 'nach Hause'.

notes: Plural: die Häuser.
Notice the difference between 'nach Hause' (going home, direction) and 'zu Hause' (at home, location).

senses.definition: A building where a person or family lives.

examples.text: Das Haus hat einen großen Garten.
examples.translation: The house has a big garden.

senses.definition: The place where one lives, especially in fixed phrases like 'zu Hause' (at home) and 'nach Hause' (homeward).

examples.text: Ich gehe jetzt nach Hause.
examples.translation: I am going home now.

senses.definition: A building used for a specific public or commercial purpose.

examples.text: Dieses Haus wurde vor hundert Jahren gebaut.
examples.translation: This building was built a hundred years ago.

faults.quote: Haustier covers both household pets like dogs and cats, and farm animals
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with Wildtier, which means a wild animal.
faults.why: Learners are unlikely to confuse 'Haustier' with 'Wildtier'.

notes: Plural: die Haustiere. For farm animals specifically, 'das Nutztier' is more common today.

senses.definition: An animal kept in the home as a companion.

examples.text: Unser Haustier ist ein sehr verspielter Hund.
examples.translation: Our pet is a very playful dog.

senses.definition: A tamed animal raised by humans, such as on a farm.

examples.text: Rinder und Schweine sind typische Haustiere auf dem Bauernhof.
examples.translation: Cattle and pigs are typical domestic animals on the farm.

faults.quote: Das Hemd refers specifically to a button-down shirt with a collar
faults.why: Repeats the definition; misses the irregular plural 'die Hemden' and counterpart 'die Bluse'.

notes: Plural: die Hemden.
Unlike English 'shirt', 'das Hemd' usually means a collared button-up shirt (mainly for men). A casual knit shirt is 'das T-Shirt', and a woman's button-up shirt is 'die Bluse'.

senses.definition: A garment for the upper body, typically with a collar, sleeves, and buttons down the front.

examples.text: Er trägt heute ein weißes Hemd.
examples.translation: He is wearing a white shirt today.

faults.quote: Just like in English, 'Herz' is used for both the biological organ
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of noting the irregular singular forms 'des Herzens / dem Herzen'.

faults.quote: She has a heart in the right place.
faults.why: Unnatural English calque; the idiom is 'Her heart is in the right place.'

notes: Irregular forms: dative singular 'dem Herzen', genitive singular 'des Herzens', plural 'die Herzen'.

senses.definition: The organ in the chest that pumps blood through the body.

examples.text: Das Herz pumpt Blut durch den ganzen Körper.
examples.translation: The heart pumps blood through the whole body.

senses.definition: The center of a person's feelings, love, and kindness.

examples.text: Er hat ein gutes Herz und hilft jedem.
examples.translation: He has a kind heart and helps everyone.

faults.quote: Note the neuter gender ('das Hotel').
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

notes: Plural: die Hotels. Stress is on the second syllable (/hoˈteːl/).
Use 'im Hotel' for staying at a hotel (Wir übernachten im Hotel) and 'ins Hotel' for going back to it.

senses.definition: A building where travellers pay for a room to sleep and stay in.

examples.text: Wir übernachten in einem kleinen Hotel.
examples.translation: We are staying the night at a small hotel.

faults.quote: Used for physical length, duration of time, and to describe hair.
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding grammar or usage guidance; contrast with 'klein' for height needed.

notes: For a person's height, Dutch usually uses 'klein' (small) rather than 'kort'.

senses.definition: Having a small distance from one end to the other, or less long than usual.

examples.text: Hij heeft heel kort haar.
examples.translation: He has very short hair.

senses.definition: Lasting for a small amount of time, or using few words.

examples.text: We namen een korte pauze.
examples.translation: We took a short break.

faults.why: Cold weather and cold objects are the same basic meaning of low temperature.

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'koud' is used for both the temperature of the weather
faults.why: Restates the senses and behaves exactly like English 'cold'.

faults.quote: It is the opposite of 'warm'.
faults.why: Trivial filler note.

notes: To say a person feels cold, use 'het koud hebben' (e.g., 'ik heb het koud'), not 'ik ben koud'.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm.

examples.text: Het is vandaag erg koud buiten.
examples.translation: It is very cold outside today.

examples.text: Ik drink mijn water graag koud.
examples.translation: I like to drink my water cold.

faults.quote: Ze gingen elkaar bij het afscheid kussen.
faults.why: 'Gingen ... kussen' is unnatural in Dutch; simple past 'kusten elkaar' is natural.

notes: Do not confuse with the neuter noun 'het kussen', which means 'pillow' or 'cushion'.

senses.definition: To touch someone with your lips to show love, affection, or as a greeting.

examples.text: Ze kusten elkaar bij het afscheid.
examples.translation: They kissed each other when saying goodbye.

faults.quote: Compare with 'ten minste' (at least) which sounds similar to English speakers
faults.why: 'Ten minste' sounds nothing like 'laat'; nonsensical false-friend note.

faults.quote: We hebben gisteren heel laat gepraat.
faults.why: Requires 'tot' ('tot heel laat') to mean 'until very late'.
Should mention the essential A1 idiom 'Hoe laat is het?' (What time is it?).

notes: Also used as an adjective ('een late trein').
Used in the common question 'Hoe laat is het?' (What time is it?, literally 'How late is it?').

senses.definition: After the expected, arranged, or usual time.

examples.text: De trein komt vandaag erg laat aan.
examples.translation: The train is arriving very late today.

senses.definition: Near the end of the day, evening, or night.

examples.text: We hebben gisteren tot heel laat gepraat.
examples.translation: We talked until very late yesterday.

faults.quote: Ze keek naar de foto en begon zachtjes te lachen.
faults.why: 'Zachtjes lachen' refers to an audible laugh/chuckle, contradicting 'without making sound'.
Missing irregular verb forms (lachte, heeft gelachen) and preposition 'om' (laugh at).

notes: Has a regular past tense ('lachte', 'lachten') but an irregular past participle ('heeft gelachen').
Use 'lachen om' for 'to laugh at' something funny, and 'lachen naar' for 'to smile at' someone.
Often used for smiling too, especially in photos; 'glimlachen' specifically means a silent smile.

senses.definition: To make sounds and movements of the face because something is funny.

examples.text: De grap was zo goed dat we moesten lachen.
examples.translation: The joke was so good that we had to laugh.

senses.definition: To curve the corners of your mouth upwards to show friendliness or happiness, or for a photo.

examples.text: De baby lachte vriendelijk naar haar moeder.
examples.translation: The baby smiled kindly at her mother.

faults.quote: Use this word to describe someone who is warm-hearted
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; could instead contrast with 친절하다.

notes: Compared to 친절하다 (kind, polite to anyone), 다정하다 implies warmth, tenderness, and close affection.

senses.definition: Warm, affectionate, and gentle in how one treats others.

examples.text: 그는 누구에게나 다정하다.
examples.translation: He is warm and kind to everyone.

examples.text: 그녀는 다정한 목소리로 말을 건넸다.
examples.translation: She spoke to me in an affectionate voice.

faults.quote: Compare with 추우다 (chuu-da, weather is cold)
faults.why: The dictionary form for cold weather is 춥다, not the non-existent 추우다.
Missing note on ㅂ-irregular conjugation (차갑다 -> 차가워요, 차가운).

faults.quote: 차갑다 is used for things that feel cold to the touch
faults.why: Simply restates the two sense definitions.

notes: ㅂ-irregular adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (차가워요, 차가운).
Compare with 춥다 (cold weather or feeling cold in one's body): 차갑다 describes objects that feel cold to the touch, or a cold attitude.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature, especially to the touch.

examples.text: 냉장고에서 꺼낸 물이 아주 차갑다.
examples.translation: The water from the fridge is very cold.

senses.definition: Unkind, unfeeling, or distant in attitude or manner.

examples.text: 그는 사람들에게 언제나 차갑게 대한다.
examples.translation: He always treats people coldly.

notes: Literally 'height (키) is small (작다)'. The subject marker 가 is often dropped in speech (키 작다), or replaced by 은/는 for contrast.
Do not confuse with 작다 alone (small in size); 키가 작다 specifically refers to a person's height.

senses.definition: Of a person: having a height below average; not tall.

examples.text: 그 친구는 키가 작아서 항상 맨 앞줄에 앉아요.
examples.translation: That friend is short, so they always sit in the front row.

faults.why: Missing critical note for A2 learners: 쉽다 is a ㅂ-irregular adjective (쉬워요, 쉬운).

faults.quote: Unlike English 'easy', '쉽다' is an adjective, so it is used
faults.why: English 'easy' is also an adjective used with a subject; the comparison makes no sense.

faults.quote: 그는 감기에 쉽게 걸려요.
faults.why: Uses the adverbial form 쉽게, rather than showing the -기 쉽다 ('likely to') construction.

notes: ㅂ-irregular adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (쉬워요, 쉬운).
In the pattern 동사 + -기(가) 쉽다, it means 'easy to do' or 'likely/prone to happen'.

senses.definition: Not difficult; requiring little effort or skill.

examples.text: 이 문제는 아주 쉬워요.
examples.translation: This problem is very easy.

senses.definition: Used after -기: likely or prone to happen.

examples.text: 환절기에는 감기에 걸리기 쉬워요.
examples.translation: It is easy to catch a cold when the seasons change.

faults.quote: to be needed, to be necessary, to require
faults.why: 필요하다 is an intransitive adjective ('to be necessary/needed'), not a transitive verb ('to require').

notes: Because 필요하다 is an adjective in Korean, the thing needed takes the subject particle 이/가, not the object particle 을/를 (돈이 필요해요 = I need money).
For the person who needs something, use 에게/한테 (저에게 시간이 필요해요).

senses.definition: Needed in order to do something or for a purpose.

examples.text: 공부하기 위해서 시간이 필요하다.
examples.translation: Time is needed in order to study.

examples.text: 더 많은 도움이 필요해요.
examples.translation: I need more help.

faults.quote: Plural is 'i pomodori'.
faults.why: The plural is completely regular and does not need a note.

faults.quote: Tagliare un pomodoro fresco per l'insalata.
faults.why: Bare infinitive fragment is unnatural as a dictionary example; use a full sentence.

senses.definition: A soft red fruit eaten raw in salads or cooked in sauces.

examples.text: Taglio un pomodoro fresco per l'insalata.
examples.translation: I'm cutting a fresh tomato for the salad.

faults.quote: A flat case for carrying loose documents, drawings, or business papers.
faults.why: A physical case for drawings is 'cartella'; 'portafoglio' in business means an investment/client portfolio.

faults.quote: Derived from portare (to carry) and foglio (sheet of paper)
faults.why: Etymology and unrelated 'borsetta' are filler; should note the alternative form 'portafogli' instead.

notes: Also spelled 'il portafogli' in the singular; the plural is always 'i portafogli'.

senses.definition: A small flat case used to carry paper money, bank cards, and identification.

examples.text: Ho lasciato il portafoglio a casa.
examples.translation: I left my wallet at home.

faults.quote: A large or formal meal shared by a group on a special occasion.
faults.why: 'Pranzo di Natale' is still the midday meal; English just translates a festive lunch as 'dinner'.

notes: 'Il pranzo' is the midday meal, while 'la cena' is the evening meal. To have lunch is 'pranzare' or 'fare pranzo'.

senses.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

examples.text: Prepariamo qualcosa di buono per pranzo?
examples.translation: Shall we make something nice for lunch?

examples.text: Ci siamo riuniti tutti per il pranzo di Natale.
examples.translation: We all got together for Christmas lunch.

faults.quote: Use 'prezzo' when asking how much something costs
faults.why: Restates the definition and gives no useful grammar or usage information.

senses.definition: The amount of money you must pay to buy something.

examples.text: Il prezzo di questa giacca è troppo alto.
examples.translation: The price of this jacket is too high.

faults.quote: Use the article 'het' for 'huiswerk'.
faults.why: Restates the gender/article already shown in the headword; misses uncountability and 'huiswerk maken'.

notes: Uncountable (no plural). In Dutch you 'make' homework: 'huiswerk maken' (to do homework).

senses.definition: School work that a student is given to do at home.

examples.text: Ik moet vandaag al mijn huiswerk maken.
examples.translation: I have to do all my homework today.

notes: Uncountable. For an individual portion of ice cream (a cone, scoop, or ice lolly), use the countable diminutive 'het ijsje'.

senses.definition: Frozen water that has become solid at or below zero degrees.

examples.text: In de winter schaatsen we op het ijs.
examples.translation: In the winter we skate on the ice.

senses.definition: A sweet, frozen dessert made from milk, cream, or fruit juice.

examples.text: Wil je nog wat ijs als toetje?
examples.translation: Would you like some more ice cream for dessert?

faults.why: Using 'jaar' to state someone's age is the same meaning of 'year', not a distinct sense.

faults.quote: Takes the neuter article 'het' (het jaar)
faults.why: Restates the article already shown in the headword.

notes: The plural is 'jaren', but after a number or 'hoeveel' / 'een paar', the singular form 'jaar' is used: 'twee jaar' (two years), 'twintig jaar oud' (twenty years old).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months, or the unit used to state age or duration.

examples.text: Dit jaar ga ik op vakantie naar Spanje.
examples.translation: This year I am going on holiday to Spain.

examples.text: Mijn broer is vijfentwintig jaar oud.
examples.translation: My brother is twenty-five years old.

faults.quote: Bayi refers specifically to a human infant from birth
faults.why: Can also refer to animal offspring (e.g., bayi kucing); contrast with 'balita' (toddler) is better.

notes: For a toddler (under five years old), the word 'balita' is commonly used.

senses.definition: A very young child who has been recently born.

examples.text: Bayi itu tidur dengan nyenyak di tempat tidurnya.
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping soundly in its crib.

faults.quote: Used both for the live animal and as food
faults.why: Restates the senses; better to note its synonym 'itik' or 'motor bebek' (underbone motorcycle).

notes: In more formal contexts, the synonym 'itik' is also used. In everyday speech, 'motor bebek' refers to a common step-through motorcycle.

senses.definition: A water bird with a short neck, webbed feet, and a broad flat bill, or its meat eaten as food.

examples.text: Bebek itu berenang di kolam.
examples.translation: The duck is swimming in the pond.

examples.text: Kami makan bebek goreng malam ini.
examples.translation: We are eating fried duck tonight.

faults.quote: /bəˈkər.ja/
faults.why: Indonesian 'j' is [dʒ], not [j]; final syllable has [dʒa].

notes: Derived from 'kerja' with the prefix 'ber-' (which drops the 'r' here). In casual speech, people often just say 'kerja'.
It is intransitive; use 'di' for a workplace or 'sebagai' for a role (e.g., bekerja sebagai guru).

senses.definition: To do a job or carry out duties, especially to earn a living.

examples.text: Ayah saya bekerja di kantor setiap hari.
examples.translation: My father works at the office every day.

senses.definition: To operate or function properly, as a machine, system, or medicine does.

examples.text: Mesin ini tidak bisa bekerja dengan baik.
examples.translation: This machine cannot work properly.

faults.why: Indonesian 'belajar' covers both 'study' and 'learn' as a single undivided concept.

notes: Irregularly formed from the root 'ajar' and prefix 'ber-'. Can be followed directly by a noun or verb without a preposition (e.g., belajar bahasa Indonesia, belajar berenang).
Do not confuse with 'mengajar' (to teach) or 'mempelajari' (to study something in depth).

senses.definition: To spend time studying a subject or gaining knowledge and skills.

examples.text: Dia belajar di kamar setiap malam.
examples.translation: He studies in his room every night.

examples.text: Saya ingin belajar bahasa Indonesia.
examples.translation: I want to learn Indonesian.

faults.quote: Cuaca hari ini benar panas.
faults.why: As an intensifier ('very'), 'benar' must follow the adjective (e.g., 'panas benar'), never precede it.

faults.quote: Benar is versatile and can mean 'correct' (a fact), 'true'
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without explaining grammar or usage.

notes: Often interchangeable with 'betul', though 'benar' is slightly more formal. Reduplicated as 'benar-benar', it means 'really' or 'truly' and goes before the word it modifies.
When used to mean 'very', a single 'benar' must be placed after the adjective (e.g., 'mahal benar').

senses.definition: In accordance with fact or truth; not mistaken.

examples.text: Jawaban kamu benar.
examples.translation: Your answer is correct.

senses.definition: Placed after an adjective to emphasize its degree.

examples.text: Cuaca hari ini panas benar.
examples.translation: The weather today is so hot.

faults.quote: Used for floors in a building, but also for layers of things
faults.why: Restates the definitions; better to note Northern vs. Southern 'lầu' and floor numbering.

notes: In Northern Vietnam, 'tầng một' is the ground floor; in the South, 'tầng trệt' is the ground floor and 'lầu' is often used for upper floors.

senses.definition: One level or story of a building.

examples.text: Căn hộ của tôi ở tầng ba.
examples.translation: My apartment is on the third floor.

senses.definition: A single layer in a stack or series of things placed one on top of another.

examples.text: Chiếc bánh kem này có ba tầng.
examples.translation: This cake has three tiers.

notes: Takes the classifier 'quả' (Northern) or 'trái' (Southern). Can refer to both the Western apple ('táo tây') and the local green jujube ('táo ta') or red Chinese date ('táo tàu').

senses.definition: A round, crisp fruit with red, green, or yellow skin.

examples.text: Tôi ăn một quả táo mỗi ngày để giữ sức khỏe.
examples.translation: I eat an apple every day to stay healthy.

senses.definition: A small sweet fruit with a single stone, eaten fresh as a crunchy green fruit or dried in sweet soups and medicine.

examples.text: Mẹ nấu chè với táo tàu và hạt sen.
examples.translation: Mother cooks sweet soup with jujubes and lotus seeds.

faults.quote: (quantity) Everything or all of something without exception.
faults.why: Etymologically unrelated homonym and not a noun (note[1] itself warns not to confuse them).

faults.quote: sock; all
faults.why: Includes 'all', which belongs to a different word and part of speech.

faults.quote: Tôi mang tất trắng trước khi xỏ giày.
faults.why: In Northern Vietnamese, 'đi tất' is the natural collocation for wearing socks ('mang' is Southern).

notes: Takes the classifier 'chiếc' for one sock or 'đôi' for a pair, and the verb 'đi' in the North (e.g. 'đi tất'). In Southern Vietnam, 'vớ' (with 'mang') is more common.
Do not confuse with the homonym 'tất' meaning 'all' (most often seen in 'tất cả').

senses.definition: A piece of soft clothing worn on the foot inside a shoe.

examples.text: Tôi đi tất trắng trước khi xỏ giày.
examples.translation: I put on white socks before putting on my shoes.

faults.quote: Tàu hỏa refers specifically to a train that runs on railway tracks
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of a train.

notes: Standard in Northern Vietnam and often shortened to 'tàu' in context. In Southern Vietnam, 'xe lửa' is more commonly used.

senses.definition: A connected line of railway carriages that carries passengers or goods along a track.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đi du lịch bằng tàu hỏa.
examples.translation: We traveled by train.

faults.quote: /ˈtaksi/
faults.why: Gives English/French stress-based IPA instead of Northern Vietnamese tonal IPA.

faults.quote: In Vietnamese, 'taxi' is a common loanword used widely
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler; should mention alternative spelling 'tắc xi' and collocation 'bắt/gọi taxi'.

notes: Also spelled 'tắc xi' or 'tắc-xi'. Common collocations include 'bắt taxi' (to hail/catch a taxi), 'gọi taxi' (to call a taxi), and 'đi taxi' (to go by taxi).

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: Tôi bắt một chiếc taxi ra sân bay.
examples.translation: I caught a taxi to the airport.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the countryside or rural regions as opposed to
faults.why: Restates the definition; should give the broken plural أَرْيَاف instead.

notes: Usually used in the singular with the definite article: الرِّيف (the countryside). Its plural is أَرْيَاف (ʾaryāf).

senses.definition: Land outside towns and cities, with fields, farms, and natural scenery.

examples.text: أُفَضِّلُ الْحَيَاةَ فِي الرِّيفِ عَلَى صَخَبِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
examples.translation: I prefer life in the countryside over the noise of the city.

faults.quote: room; compartment
faults.why: 'compartment' is not in the sense glosses or definition.

faults.quote: Used mainly for indoor spaces enclosed by walls, like a bedroom or
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving the irregular plural غُرَف.

notes: The plural is غُرَف (ḡuraf). Often used in compounds for specific rooms, such as غُرْفَة نَوْم (bedroom) and غُرْفَة جُلُوس (living room).

senses.definition: A space inside a building with its own walls, floor, and ceiling.

examples.text: هَذِهِ غُرْفَةُ نَوْمٍ نَظِيفَةٌ.
examples.translation: This is a clean bedroom.

faults.quote: Used mainly for the sandy or stony edge of the sea, ocean,
faults.why: Restates the definition; should give the broken plural شَوَاطِئ instead.

notes: The plural is شَوَاطِئ (šawāṭiʾ).

senses.definition: The sandy or stony land next to the sea, an ocean, or a lake.

examples.text: نَمْشِي عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: We walk on the beach every morning.

faults.quote: A major port city on the Red Sea in Saudi Arabia.
faults.why: Proper noun (usually vocalized جُدَّة); should not be mixed with the common noun 'grandmother'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with جَدِيد (jadīd), which means new.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; better to contrast with the masculine form جَدّ (grandfather).

notes: The plural is جَدَّات (jaddāt). The masculine form is جَدّ (jadd, 'grandfather').

senses.definition: The mother of your father or mother.

examples.text: جَدَّتِي تَطْبُخُ طَعَاماً لَذِيذاً.
examples.translation: My grandmother cooks delicious food.

faults.why: Missing the common irregular broken plural طُلَّاب (ṭullāb).

faults.quote: الطَّالِبُ يَجْلِسُ فِي القَاعَةِ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ.
faults.why: Stilted and unnatural phrasing for a simple learner example.

notes: The feminine form is طَالِبَة (ṭāliba), and the masculine plural is طُلَّاب (ṭullāb).
Often used specifically for a university or high school student, as opposed to تِلْمِيذ (tilmīdh, younger pupil).

senses.definition: A person who is studying at a school, college, or university.

examples.text: هُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي الجَامِعَةِ.
examples.translation: He is a student at the university.

senses.definition: Someone who is looking for or requesting something.

examples.text: هُوَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
examples.translation: He is a seeker of knowledge.

faults.quote: /amˈra.at/
faults.why: Wrong vowel and ending; standard pronunciation is /im.ra.ʔa/.

faults.quote: هَذِهِ امْرَأَتُهِ.
faults.why: Ungrammatical vowel harmony: nominative -u takes -hu (امْرَأَتُهُ), not -hi.

notes: The plural is نِسَاء (nisāʾ), which comes from a different root.
Starts with a hamzat waṣl (ا), which drops when the definite article is added: المَرْأَة (al-marʾa).

senses.definition: An adult female human being.

examples.text: رَأَيْتُ امْرَأَةً تَمْشِي فِي الشَّارِعِ.
examples.translation: I saw a woman walking in the street.

senses.definition: A female partner in a marriage.

examples.text: هَذِهِ امْرَأَتُهُ.
examples.translation: This is his wife.

faults.quote: /qaː.i.ma.t͡sˤ tˤa.ʕaːm/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA (/t͡sˤ/ does not exist in Arabic and glottal stop /ʔ/ is missing).

faults.quote: مُمكِن قَائِمَة طَعَام مِن فَضْلِك؟
faults.why: Colloquial phrasing without full MSA vocalization, and missing the definite article on الطَّعَام.

notes: A construct phrase (iḍāfa) literally meaning 'list of food'. To make it definite ('the menu'), add الـ only to the second word: قَائِمَة الطَّعَام.

senses.definition: A list of food and drinks available in a restaurant.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي رُؤْيَةُ قَائِمَةِ الطَّعَامِ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
examples.translation: Could I see the menu, please?

faults.quote: /ʃaxˤsˤ/
faults.why: /x/ is not pharyngealized in Arabic; should be /ʃaxsˤ/.

notes: The plural is أَشْخَاص (ʾashkhāṣ), used for a countable number of individuals. For 'people' in general, نَاس (nās) is used.

senses.definition: A human being, considered as an individual.

examples.text: هَذَا الشَّخْصُ لَطِيفٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This person is very kind.

faults.quote: تلفاز is the standard Modern Standard Arabic word for television, often shortened to تلفيزيون
faults.why: تلفيزيون (tilifizyūn) is longer than تلفاز (tilfāz), not a shortened form of it.

faults.quote: television, tv, screen
faults.why: 'Screen' is شَاشَة (shāsha), not تِلْفَاز.

notes: The plural is تِلْفَازَات (tilfāzāt). In everyday speech and media, the loanword تِلِفِزْيُون (tilifizyūn) is also very common.

senses.definition: An electronic device with a screen used for watching broadcast programmes and shows.

examples.text: اشْتَرَى أَبِي تِلْفَازًا جَدِيدًا لِلْغُرْفَةِ.
examples.translation: My father bought a new television for the room.

faults.quote: In Greek, this word covers both a physical calendar for dates
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'ημερολόγιο εργασιών'
faults.why: Transparent compound phrase that a beginner will not confuse with the base noun.

notes: The word is stressed on the third syllable from the end, so it takes a second accent mark when followed by a possessive pronoun: το ημερολόγιό μου.

senses.definition: A printed or digital chart showing the days, weeks, and months of a year.

examples.text: Κοίταξα το ημερολόγιο για να βρω μια ελεύθερη μέρα.
examples.translation: I checked the calendar to find a free day.

senses.definition: A book used to record personal daily experiences and thoughts.

examples.text: Γράφω κάθε βράδυ στο ημερολόγιό μου.
examples.translation: I write in my diary every night.

faults.quote: duck; scoop
faults.why: 'Scoop' is not a meaning of this word or in the senses.

faults.quote: (medical) A curved container used in hospitals for patients
faults.why: Hospital urinal is not an everyday A1-A2 beginner sense.

faults.quote: Pay attention to the accent on the first syllable: πά-πι-α.
faults.why: Pronounced as two syllables (/ˈpa.pça/), not three; 'ια' undergoes synizesis.

notes: Pronounced as two syllables (/ˈpa.pça/), because the ending -ια is pronounced together as /ça/.

senses.definition: A water bird with webbed feet and a flat beak.

examples.text: Η πάπια κολυμπάει στη λίμνη με τα παπάκια της.
examples.translation: The duck is swimming in the lake with its ducklings.

faults.quote: A small bird is sitting on the tree.
faults.why: Unnatural English preposition; birds sit 'in' a tree.

notes: The diminutive form 'το πουλάκι' (little bird) is very common in everyday speech, and is also used as a term of endearment ('πουλάκι μου').

senses.definition: An animal with feathers, wings, and a beak, usually able to fly.

examples.text: Ένα μικρό πουλί κάθεται στο δέντρο.
examples.translation: A small bird is sitting in the tree.

faults.quote: A small hard piece of rock.
faults.why: Both senses and examples refer to small stones/pebbles; they are one sense.

faults.quote: Used for both small stones you might pick up and large rock formations.
faults.why: Large rock formations are 'βράχος', not 'πέτρα', contradicting note 1.

notes: Refers to the hard mineral material or to loose stones you can pick up; for a large rock formation, boulder, or cliff, use 'ο βράχος'.

senses.definition: The hard, solid mineral material that forms part of the earth's surface, or a loose piece of it.

examples.text: Τα παιδιά πετούν πέτρες στη θάλασσα.
examples.translation: The children are throwing stones into the sea.

examples.text: Μια μικρή πέτρα μπήκε στο παπούτσι μου.
examples.translation: A small stone got into my shoe.

faults.quote: A period of twelve months. ... A numbered year in the calendar
faults.why: Duration vs. calendar date are shades of one meaning ('year'); combine them.

notes: Placed directly before a number to name a calendar year: 'tahun 2000' (in 2000).
Do not confuse with 'tahu' (to know, or tofu).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months, or a particular calendar year.

examples.text: Saya tinggal di sini selama dua tahun.
examples.translation: I have lived here for two years.

examples.text: Dia lahir pada tahun dua ribu.
examples.translation: She was born in the year 2000.

faults.quote: Often shortened in casual speech to just 'taks'
faults.why: 'Taksi' is never shortened to 'taks' in Indonesian.

faults.quote: Used for standard metered or hired cars that transport passengers for a
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Take a taxi is 'naik taksi'. App-based ride-hailing cars are often called 'taksi online'.

senses.definition: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

examples.text: Saya naik taksi ke stasiun.
examples.translation: I took a taxi to the station.

faults.quote: Takut can mean feeling afraid in the moment, but it is also
faults.why: Restates the two senses; a note on prepositions ('akan', 'pada', 'sama') is needed instead.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with malu, which means shy or embarrassed
faults.why: Unlikely confusion visually or semantically; filler note.

faults.quote: afraid; scared; fearful
faults.why: Does not cover the second sense ('worried').

notes: Can be followed directly by a noun ('takut anjing' = afraid of dogs) or by 'pada', 'akan', or in casual speech 'sama' / 'dengan'.

senses.definition: Feeling fear about something dangerous, painful, or frightening.

examples.text: Anak kecil itu takut pada anjing besar di jalan.
examples.translation: The small child is afraid of the big dog on the street.

senses.definition: Anxious or worried that something bad might happen.

examples.text: Saya takut hujan turun deras sebelum sampai di rumah.
examples.translation: I am worried that heavy rain will fall before I get home.

faults.quote: An area of land used for growing flowers, ornamental plants, and vegetables
faults.why: A vegetable garden is a 'kebun', whereas 'taman' is an ornamental or flower garden.

notes: 'Taman' is a public park or an ornamental flower garden; a vegetable garden, orchard, or plantation is 'kebun'.

senses.definition: An open public area with grass and trees in a town or city, used for recreation.

examples.text: Anak-anak bermain bola di taman kota.
examples.translation: The children are playing ball in the city park.

senses.definition: An area of land by a house or building planted with flowers and ornamental plants.

examples.text: Ibu menyirami bunga di taman depan rumah.
examples.translation: Mother is watering the flowers in the front garden.

faults.quote: A person invited to your home or event. ... Someone who is staying
faults.why: Home visitor and hotel guest are shades of one meaning ('guest/visitor') in Indonesian.

faults.quote: Using the word 'tamu' can also imply a sense of social obligation
faults.why: Generic cultural commentary about hospitality rather than useful linguistic guidance.

notes: Used for a visitor to a home, an invited guest at an event, or a hotel guest. A visitor to a public place (like a museum or park) is 'pengunjung'.

senses.definition: A person visiting someone's home or attending an event, or a paying customer at a hotel.

examples.text: Kami sedang menyiapkan makanan untuk tamu yang akan datang nanti malam.
examples.translation: We are preparing food for the guests who are coming tonight.

examples.text: Tamu hotel itu bisa menggunakan kolam renang secara gratis.
examples.translation: The hotel guests can use the swimming pool for free.

faults.quote: سَأَلَ الشُّرْطِيُّ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ.
faults.why: Usually someone asks the police officer for directions, not the other way around.
Missing the common collective/plural forms (شُرْطَة / شُرْطِيُّون).

notes: Feminine: شُرْطِيَّة. Plural: شُرْطِيُّون, or collective شُرْطَة (the police).

senses.definition: A member of the police force.

examples.text: سَأَلْتُ الشُّرْطِيَّ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ.
examples.translation: I asked the police officer for directions.

faults.why: Should state that بَطَاطِس is an uncountable collective noun treated as feminine singular.

notes: Collective noun treated as feminine singular and declined as a diptote (no nunation). In the Levant and Iraq, بَطَاطَا is the standard word for potatoes.

senses.definition: A round, starchy root vegetable that grows underground and is a common food.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ بَطَاطِسَ طَازَجَةً مِنَ السُّوقِ.
examples.translation: I bought fresh potatoes from the market.

faults.quote: /ba.tˤn/
faults.why: بَطْن is one syllable /batˤn/, not two.

senses.definition: The front part of the body between the chest and the legs, or the stomach area inside it.

examples.text: يُؤْلِمُهُ بَطْنُهُ بَعْدَ تَنَاوُلِ الكَثِيرِ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ.

senses.definition: A list showing how much you have to pay for food or services.

examples.text: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، الحِسَابَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: Excuse me, the bill, please.

senses.definition: An arrangement with a bank or online service to keep money or personal information.

examples.text: فَتَحْتُ حِسَابًا جَدِيدًا فِي البَنْكِ.

senses.definition: The act of working out an amount or number using math.

examples.text: أَخْطَأْتُ فِي حِسَابِ المَبْلَغِ.

faults.quote: In modern Standard Arabic, نَبِيذ specifically refers to wine made from grapes.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

examples.text: شَرِبْنَا نَبِيذًا أَحْمَرَ فِي العَشَاءِ.
examples.translation: We drank red wine at dinner.

faults.quote: While 'машина' is the standard word for a car, it also functions
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses given in the entry.

notes: The more formal word 'автомобиль' (automobile) is used mainly in official or technical contexts; in everyday speech, 'машина' is standard.
Take care with prepositions: 'в машине' means inside the car, while 'на машине' means by car (e.g., ехать на машине).

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: Моя машина стоит во дворе.
examples.translation: My car is parked in the yard.

senses.definition: A piece of equipment with moving parts that uses power to do a particular type of work.

examples.text: Стиральная машина работает очень тихо.
examples.translation: The washing machine runs very quietly.

faults.quote: chair; stool
faults.why: 'Stool' as furniture is 'табурет' (false friend); medical sense is missing from senses.

notes: False friend: 'стул' is a chair with a back; a stool without a back is 'табурет' or 'табуретка', while a soft armchair is 'кресло'.
Has an irregular plural: 'стулья' (genitive plural 'стульев').

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a back and four legs.

examples.text: Он сел на стул у окна.
examples.translation: He sat down on the chair by the window.

faults.quote: /ˈvʲilka/
