senses.definition: A small tool with three or four points and a handle, used for picking up food and eating.

examples.text: Положи вилку на стол.
examples.translation: Put the fork on the table.

senses.definition: A small plastic object with metal pins that connects a piece of electrical equipment to the power supply.

examples.text: Вынь вилку из розетки.
examples.translation: Take the plug out of the socket.

faults.quote: Note the stress: the final syllable is accented, so it sounds like
faults.why: Restates what the IPA and audio already show; misses the construction 'кататься/ездить на велосипеде'.

notes: To say 'ride a bike', use 'кататься на велосипеде' (for fun or as a skill) or 'ездить на велосипеде' (regularly or as transport).
In informal everyday speech, it is very often shortened to 'велик' (/ˈvʲelʲɪk/).

senses.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle that you sit on and move by turning the two pedals with your feet.

examples.text: Я купил новый велосипед.
examples.translation: I bought a new bicycle.

examples.text: В парке много людей катается на велосипедах.
examples.translation: Many people are riding bikes in the park.

faults.quote: /svʲiˈnʲja/
faults.why: Unstressed 'и' reduces to /ɪ/: /svʲɪˈnʲja/.

faults.quote: Used both for the farm animal and as an insult for a
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses irregular plural stem stress and meat distinction.

faults.quote: A big pink pig lives at my grandmother's village.
faults.why: Unnatural English ('lives at my grandmother's village').

notes: In the plural, the stress shifts to the first syllable: 'свиньи' (nominative), 'свиней' (genitive/accusative).
'Свинья' is only the animal; the meat (pork) is 'свинина'.

senses.definition: A pink or black farm animal with short legs and a curved tail, kept for its meat.

examples.text: В деревне у бабушки живёт большая розовая свинья.
examples.translation: My grandmother has a big pink pig at her place in the country.

senses.definition: An unpleasant, greedy, or very messy person.

examples.text: Кто оставил здесь столько мусора? Настоящая свинья.
examples.translation: Who left so much trash here? A real pig.

faults.quote: /kʰɑːn.siː/
faults.why: Chandrabindu indicates a nasalized vowel /ɑ̃ː/, not a nasal consonant /n/.

notes: The related verb 'to cough' is 'खाँसना' (khā̃snā). To say 'I have a cough', use 'मुझे खाँसी है' (literally 'to me there is a cough').

senses.definition: An illness or reflex action that makes you push air out of your throat with a sudden sound.

examples.text: मुझे बहुत तेज़ खाँसी है।
examples.translation: I have a very bad cough.

faults.quote: िमलनसार
faults.why: Devanagari vowel sign 'ि' is placed before the consonant instead of after 'म' (मिलनसार).

faults.quote: Used to refer to someone you work with in an office
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Compound of 'सह-' (together) and 'कर्मी' (worker). Plural oblique form is 'सहकर्मियों' (sahkarmiyõ).

senses.definition: A person you work with in the same organization or profession.

examples.text: मेरे सभी सहकर्मी बहुत मिलनसार हैं।
examples.translation: All my colleagues are very friendly.

faults.quote: मैंने काँटा और चम्मच से खाना खाया।
faults.why: Ungrammatical: masculine '-आ' noun 'काँटा' must take the oblique form 'काँटे' before postposition 'से'.

faults.quote: While it means 'fork' in a dining context, it also refers
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already listed in the entry.

notes: Changes to 'काँटे' (kā̃ṭe) in the plural and in the singular before a postposition.

senses.definition: A sharp, pointed part on the stem of a plant, or a sharp splinter or fishbone.

examples.text: गुलाब के पौधे में काँटे होते हैं।
examples.translation: There are thorns on a rose plant.

senses.definition: A small tool with three or four sharp points used for picking up and eating food.

examples.text: मैंने काँटे और चम्मच से खाना खाया।
examples.translation: I ate the food with a fork and spoon.

faults.quote: Patjhad specifically refers to the season of shedding leaves.
faults.why: Wordy and repetitive across both notes; restates the definition.

notes: In much of India, trees shed their leaves in late winter or early spring (February–March) rather than after summer.

senses.definition: The season of the year when leaves fall from the trees.

examples.text: पतझड़ में पेड़ों के पत्ते झड़ जाते हैं।
examples.translation: In autumn, the leaves fall off the trees.

faults.quote: (hearing) The sense or act of hearing.
faults.why: Not a separate lexical sense of 'कान'; the example is just an idiom ('कान लगाना').

faults.quote: ear; hearing
faults.why: 'कान' means 'ear', not 'hearing'.

faults.quote: It is masculine; remember to use 'mere' or 'mere'
faults.why: Restates gender and gives a nonsensical duplicate 'mere or mere' instead of 'merā / mere'.

notes: The plural has the same form as the singular in the direct case: 'एक कान' (one ear), 'दो कान' (two ears).
Used in common expressions such as 'कान लगाकर सुनना' (to listen carefully).

senses.definition: One of the two organs on the sides of the head with which people and animals hear.

examples.text: मेरे कान में दर्द है।
examples.translation: I have pain in my ear.

faults.quote: /ku.ziˈɲɐj.ɾu/
faults.why: European Portuguese IPA; Brazilian Portuguese is /ko.ziˈɲe(j).ɾu/.

faults.quote: as 'cozinheiro' implies a job.
faults.why: 'Cozinheiro' is also commonly used for home cooks (e.g. 'um bom cozinheiro').

faults.quote: Use 'o cozinheiro' for someone who cooks as a profession
faults.why: Restates the definition; fails to mention the feminine form 'a cozinheira'.

notes: The feminine form is 'a cozinheira'.

senses.definition: A person who prepares and cooks food, especially as a job.

examples.text: O cozinheiro preparou um prato especial.
examples.translation: The cook prepared a special dish.

faults.quote: Escovei o dente depois de comer.
faults.why: Brushing teeth uses the plural 'os dentes' in natural Portuguese, and in English.

faults.quote: Used for the hard white structures in the mouth, but also
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions in the entry.

notes: In sense 2, it is almost always used in the phrase 'dente de alho' (clove of garlic).

senses.definition: One of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.

examples.text: Escovei os dentes depois de comer.
examples.translation: I brushed my teeth after eating.

senses.definition: A single small section of a garlic bulb.

examples.text: Adicionei um dente de alho ao molho.
examples.translation: I added a clove of garlic to the sauce.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'o desconhecido' most commonly refers to a stranger
faults.why: Restates sense 0 without adding useful grammar or usage info.

faults.quote: It can also mean the unknown, referring to unfamiliar situations
faults.why: Restates sense 1.

notes: When referring to a female stranger, use the feminine form 'a desconhecida'.
Also commonly used as an adjective meaning 'unknown' or 'unfamiliar'.

senses.definition: A person you do not know.

examples.text: Não fale com estranhos ou desconhecidos na rua.
examples.translation: Do not speak with strangers in the street.

senses.definition: A situation, place, or thing that is not known or experienced.

examples.text: Eles viajaram para o desconhecido.
examples.translation: They traveled into the unknown.

faults.quote: She is my good friend since childhood.
faults.why: Unnatural English tense with 'since'; should be 'She has been my good friend since childhood.'

notes: 'Teman' is the general word for friend; for a close or best friend, use 'sahabat'.

senses.definition: A person you know well and like.

examples.text: Dia adalah teman baik saya sejak kecil.
examples.translation: She has been my good friend since childhood.

senses.definition: Someone who goes somewhere with you or shares an activity with you.

examples.text: Saya mencari teman untuk pergi ke pasar.
examples.translation: I am looking for someone to go to the market with.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with just 'tidur', which is the verb 'to sleep'.
faults.why: Redundant with note 0, which already gives the meaning of 'tidur'.

notes: Literally 'place' (tempat) + 'to sleep' (tidur). Distinguish from 'kamar tidur' (bedroom) and 'kasur' (mattress).

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for sleeping or resting on.

examples.text: Dia duduk di atas tempat tidur sambil membaca buku.
examples.translation: She sat on the bed reading a book.

faults.quote: Tenang describes both an inner emotional state (calm, unbothered) and a physical
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses and their glosses.

notes: Do not confuse with 'diam', which means 'silent' (not speaking) or 'still' (not moving).
'Tenang saja!' is a common spoken expression meaning 'Don't worry!' or 'Take it easy!'.

senses.definition: Of a person or feeling: free from worry, fear, or excitement.

examples.text: Dia tetap tenang meskipun ada masalah besar.
examples.translation: He stayed calm even though there was a big problem.

senses.definition: Of a place, water, or atmosphere: peaceful, still, and with little noise.

examples.text: Suasana di desa itu sangat tenang pada malam hari.
examples.translation: The atmosphere in that village is very quiet at night.

faults.quote: To depart or travel to a destination rapidly, usually by plane.
faults.why: Traveling by plane is part of 'to fly' and already covered in sense 0's definition.

faults.quote: Used for birds, planes, and anything moving through the air.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions of the senses.

notes: Combined with 'pesawat' as 'pesawat terbang' (airplane).

senses.definition: To move through the air using wings, or to travel in an aircraft.

examples.text: Burung itu terbang tinggi di atas pohon.
examples.translation: That bird is flying high above the tree.

examples.text: Besok saya akan terbang ke Jakarta.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will fly to Jakarta.

faults.quote: This is the standard, universal way to express gratitude in Indonesian.
faults.why: Restates the definition and neutral register without adding practical usage info like responses or prepositions.

notes: Often shortened to 'makasih' in casual conversation. The standard reply is 'sama-sama' (you're welcome).
Say 'terima kasih banyak' for 'thank you very much', and use 'atas' for 'for' (e.g. terima kasih atas...).

senses.definition: An expression used to tell someone that you are grateful to them.

examples.text: Terima kasih atas bantuan Anda.
examples.translation: Thank you for your help.

faults.quote: In many Arabic dialects, 'جزر' is used collectively

faults.why: Collective الجزر with the definite article means 'carrots' in general, not 'a carrot'.

notes: Collective noun referring to carrots in general; the singulative form for a single carrot is جَزَرَة (jazara).

senses.definition: A long, tapering orange root eaten as a vegetable.

examples.text: آكُلُ الجَزَرَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
examples.translation: I eat carrots every day.

faults.quote: Events that happen to a person by chance
faults.why: حظ means luck/fortune, not 'chance/happenstance' (which is صدفة); example even translates it as 'luck'.

faults.quote: لَقَد الْتَقَيْنَا صُدْفَةً بِحَظٍّ كَبِير.
faults.why: Awkward phrasing; uses صدفة for 'by chance' and tacks on بحظ كبير unnaturally.

notes: Commonly used in حَظّ سَعِيد (ḥaẓẓ saʿīd, 'good luck') and حَظّ سَيِّئ (ḥaẓẓ sayyiʾ, 'bad luck'). Plural: حُظُوظ (ḥuẓūẓ).
Unlike نَصِيب (naṣīb, 'fate, lot'), which refers to what is destined, حَظّ refers to good or bad fortune.

senses.definition: Success or failure apparently brought by chance rather than through one's own actions.

examples.text: حَظِّي جَيِّدٌ اليَوْمَ.
examples.translation: My luck is good today.

examples.text: أَتَمَنَّى لَكَ حَظًّا سَعِيدًا.
examples.translation: I wish you good luck.

faults.why: Should note the irregular (broken) plural هَدَايَا (hadāyā), which A2 learners need.

notes: Irregular plural: هَدَايَا (hadāyā).

senses.definition: Something given willingly to someone without payment, especially on a special occasion.

examples.text: اشْتَرَيْتُ هَدِيَّةً جَمِيلَةً لِصَدِيقِي فِي عِيدِ مِيلَادِهِ.
examples.translation: I bought a nice gift for my friend on his birthday.

faults.quote: /ˈmab.naj/
faults.why: Final ى (alif maqṣūra) is pronounced /aː/, not /aj/.

notes: Ends in alif maqṣūra (ى), pronounced /aː/; when indefinite, it takes -an (مَبْنًى, mabnan). Irregular plural: مَبَانٍ (mabānin, definite المَبَانِي al-mabānī).

senses.definition: A structure with walls and a roof, such as a house, school, or office block.

examples.text: هَذَا المَبْنَى جَدِيدٌ وَكَبِيرٌ.
examples.translation: This building is new and big.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a female parent.
faults.why: Restates the definition; omits the irregular plural أُمَّهَات (ʾummahāt).

notes: Irregular plural: أُمَّهَات (ʾummahāt). Also used in kunyas (teknonyms) meaning 'mother of' (e.g. أُمّ عَلِيّ, Umm ʿAlī) and in compound expressions.

senses.definition: A female parent.

examples.text: هَذِهِ أُمِّي الطَّيِّبَةُ.
examples.translation: This is my kind mother.

senses.definition: The main source, origin, or foundation of something.

examples.text: الحَاجَةُ أُمُّ الاِخْتِرَاعِ.
examples.translation: Necessity is the mother of invention.

faults.why: Missing the everyday restaurant meaning 'menu' (short for Speisekarte).

faults.quote: It covers payment cards, tickets for public transport or events
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already listed.

notes: Often stands for a compound whose meaning is clear from context: 'Bankkarte' (bank card), 'Fahrkarte' or 'Eintrittskarte' (ticket), 'Speisekarte' (menu), 'Landkarte' (map), or 'Postkarte' (postcard).

senses.definition: A small piece of plastic or stiff paper, such as a bank card, ID card, postcard, or playing card.

examples.text: Kann ich mit Karte bezahlen?
examples.translation: Can I pay by card?

senses.definition: A pass for travel on public transport or for entry to an event.

examples.text: Hast du schon die Karten für das Konzert?
examples.translation: Do you already have the tickets for the concert?

senses.definition: A list of food and drinks available in a restaurant or café.

examples.text: Können wir bitte die Karte haben?
examples.translation: Can we have the menu, please?

senses.definition: A plan of a city, region, or country, on paper or on a screen.

examples.text: Wir brauchen eine Karte von der Stadt.
examples.translation: We need a map of the city.

faults.quote: Unlike in some other languages, the word is never used
faults.why: Pointless negative note; also misleading as 'Kartoffel' is used as slang for Germans.

notes: Plural: 'die Kartoffeln'. In southern Germany and Austria you will also hear 'Erdapfel'.

senses.definition: A round vegetable that grows underground and is a common food.

examples.text: Ich koche heute Kartoffeln mit Gemüse.
examples.translation: I am cooking potatoes with vegetables today.

faults.quote: Used as a general term for any feline, but most commonly
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning instead of giving useful grammar or vocabulary.

notes: 'Die Katze' is the general word for any cat; a male cat specifically is 'der Kater', and a kitten is 'das Kätzchen'.

senses.definition: A small furry animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet.

examples.text: Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
examples.translation: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

faults.quote: If you want to talk about individual items of clothing, use
faults.why: Misleading: 'Kleider' usually means dresses; an individual item is 'das Kleidungsstück', and colloquial 'clothes' is 'Klamotten'.

notes: Uncountable and always singular in German, even when translated as plural 'clothes' in English.
A single item of clothing is 'das Kleidungsstück'. In everyday speech, people very often say 'die Klamotten' (plural) for 'clothes'.

senses.definition: The things that people wear on their body, such as shirts, trousers, and jackets.

examples.text: Sie kauft sich neue Kleidung für den Winter.
examples.translation: She is buying new clothes for the winter.

examples.text: Diese Kleidung ist sehr bequem.
examples.translation: These clothes are very comfortable.

faults.quote: Use the feminine article 'la' before 'birra'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already shown in the headword.

notes: Both uncountable ('bevo birra', I drink beer) and countable for a glass, bottle, or can ('una birra', a beer).

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from grain and hops, or a glass, bottle, or can of it.

examples.text: Prendiamo una birra fresca al bar.
examples.translation: Let's grab a cold beer at the bar.

faults.quote: /ˈbɔk.ka/
faults.why: Standard Italian has a close-mid vowel /o/ in 'bocca': /ˈbok.ka/.

faults.quote: Used both for the anatomical mouth on the face and for opening
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses defined in the entry.

notes: Plural 'le bocche' (spelled with 'ch' to keep the hard /k/ sound). Very common in the expression 'In bocca al lupo!' ('Good luck!', literally 'into the wolf's mouth').

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Ha aperto la bocca per parlare.
examples.translation: He opened his mouth to speak.

senses.definition: An opening or entrance to a space, cave, or container.

examples.text: La grotta ha una bocca stretta.
examples.translation: The cave has a narrow entrance.

faults.quote: "Borsa" has several distinct meanings depending on context: a handbag, a plastic
faults.why: Merely lists the senses already shown in the entry.

notes: The scholarship sense is almost always used in the full phrase 'borsa di studio'.
Do not confuse with 'borsellino' (a small coin purse) or 'portafoglio' (wallet).

senses.definition: A container of cloth, leather, or plastic used to carry personal items, books, or shopping.

examples.text: Ho lasciato le chiavi nella borsa.
examples.translation: I left my keys in my bag.

senses.definition: Money given to a student to help pay for their studies, usually in the phrase 'borsa di studio'.

examples.text: Ha vinto una borsa di studio per l'università.
examples.translation: She won a scholarship for university.

senses.definition: The market where company shares and financial securities are bought and sold.

examples.text: Oggi la borsa ha chiuso in positivo.
examples.translation: Today the stock market closed up.

faults.quote: Use 'bottiglia' for glass or plastic containers meant for liquids like water,
faults.why: Restates the definition.

senses.definition: A container for liquid with a narrow neck, typically made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: Ho comprato una bottiglia di vino rosso per la cena.
examples.translation: I bought a bottle of red wine for dinner.

faults.quote: Metto una calza pulita prima di indossare le scarpe.

senses.definition: A piece of soft clothing worn on the foot inside a shoe.

examples.text: Devo comprare due paia di calze di lana.
examples.translation: I need to buy two pairs of wool socks.

senses.definition: A long, thin garment that fits closely over the foot and leg, often made of nylon.

examples.text: Ha indossato un abito elegante con le calze nere.
examples.translation: She wore an elegant dress with black stockings.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a Japanese word containing kanji.

faults.quote: (composition) To author or compose a book, article, or piece of music.
faults.why: Writing words on a surface and writing a book/report are shades of one meaning.
