examples.translation: The bag is too heavy.

senses.definition: Of a mood, atmosphere, or topic: serious, tense, or grave.

examples.text: 분위기가 무겁네요.
examples.translation: The atmosphere is heavy.

faults.quote: To feel unwell or sick; to be ill.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a verb infinitive rather than a quality or state.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with '슬프다', which means 'to be sad'
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; a note on the 'ㅡ' drop conjugation (아파요) is needed instead.

notes: When a specific body part hurts, use '[body part] + -이/가 아프다' (e.g., 머리가 아파요, 'My head hurts').
The vowel 'ㅡ' drops before '-아/어' (아파요, 아팠어요).

senses.definition: Unwell or in poor health.

examples.text: 몸이 아파서 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.translation: I could not go to school because I was sick.

senses.definition: Feeling or causing physical pain in a part of the body.

examples.text: 배가 너무 아파요.
examples.translation: My stomach hurts so much.

faults.why: Missing a note on the irregular 'ㄹ' drop before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (단, 답니다).

notes: Irregular 'ㄹ' adjective: 'ㄹ' drops before endings starting with 'ㄴ', 'ㅂ', or 'ㅅ' (e.g., 단 음식 'sweet food', 답니다 'is sweet').
Do not confuse with the homonymous verb '달다' ('to hang, attach' or 'to ask for').

senses.definition: Having the pleasant taste of sugar or honey.

examples.text: 이 사과는 정말 달아요.
examples.translation: This apple is really sweet.

faults.quote: Note that 'rodzice' is always plural.
faults.why: Self-contradictory: says it is always plural, then notes singular 'rodzic' exists.

notes: The singular form 'rodzic' (a parent) is mainly used in formal or official contexts (e.g., at school).
Do not confuse this with 'rodzeństwo', which means 'siblings'.

senses.definition: A person's mother and father.

examples.text: Moi rodzice przyjadą w odwiedziny w weekend.
examples.translation: My parents are coming for a visit this weekend.

faults.quote: róg has multiple distinct meanings: a street corner, an animal's horn
faults.why: Restates the glosses and mentions a musical horn sense not in the entry.

faults.quote: The place where two streets meet.
faults.why: Too narrow: 'róg' also means the corner of a room, table, or building.

notes: For the corner of a street or exterior object, use 'na rogu' (on the corner); for the inside corner of a room, use 'w rogu' (in the corner).

senses.definition: The place or point where two streets, walls, or edges meet.

examples.text: Spotkamy się na rogu ulicy.
examples.translation: We will meet at the street corner.

senses.definition: A hard, pointed growth on the head of some animals.

examples.text: Byk ma dwa duże rogi.
examples.translation: The bull has two large horns.

notes: 'Rok' has a suppletive plural: 'lata' (nominative) and 'lat' (genitive). With numbers, use '1 rok', '2–4 lata', and '5+ lat' (e.g., 'Mam dwadzieścia lat' – I am twenty years old).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months.

examples.text: Ten rok był bardzo udany.
examples.translation: This year was very successful.

faults.quote: Note that 'rolnik' specifically refers to someone who works with land
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition of 'farmer' with vague remarks.

senses.definition: A person who owns or works on a farm, growing crops or keeping animals.

examples.text: Rolnik wstaje wcześnie rano, aby pracować na polu.
examples.translation: The farmer gets up early in the morning to work in the field.

faults.quote: When you use this to mean meeting a romantic partner, it is
faults.why: Restates sense 1 without adding grammar or usage information.
Should note the particles taken: 을/를 or 와/과/하고.

corrected.shortGloss: to meet; to see; to date
notes: Used both for meeting someone for the first time and for meeting up with someone you already know.
Takes the object particle 을/를 (친구를 만나다) or the ‘with’ particles 와/과, 하고, 랑/이랑 (친구와 만나다).

senses.definition: To come together with someone by arrangement or by chance.

examples.text: 오늘 저녁에 친구를 만나요.
examples.translation: I am meeting a friend this evening.

senses.definition: To be in a romantic relationship with someone.

examples.text: 요즘 그 사람을 만나고 있어요.
examples.translation: I am seeing that person these days.

faults.quote: It is a descriptive verb in Korean, meaning you use it to
faults.why: False: 젖다 is an action verb (동사, 젖는다), needing past 젖었다 for present state.

corrected.shortGloss: to get wet; to be soaked
notes: An action verb (동사) meaning ‘to become wet’. To say something ‘is wet’ right now, use the past tense 젖었어요 or the state form 젖어 있어요.
Regular ㅈ verb: the ㅈ stays before vowels (젖어요, 젖어서).

senses.definition: To become soaked with water or another liquid.

examples.text: 비가 와서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.translation: My clothes got all wet because it rained.

senses.definition: To become deeply absorbed in a feeling, mood, or memory (with 에).

examples.text: 그는 추억에 젖어 있었다.
examples.translation: He was lost in memories.

notes: Formed from 수영 (swimming) + 하다 (to do). Often split with the object particle as 수영을 하다.

senses.definition: To move through water using the arms and legs.

examples.text: 나는 매일 아침 수영장에서 수영해요.
examples.translation: I swim at the pool every morning.

faults.quote: Used when propelling something through the air using your hand or arm.
faults.why: Repeats sense 0's definition almost word for word.

notes: Takes 을/를 for the thing thrown and 에게/한테 (to a person) or 에 (at a place) for the target.

senses.definition: To send something through the air with a movement of the hand and arm.

examples.text: 공을 멀리 던지세요.
examples.translation: Throw the ball far.

senses.definition: To direct a look, question, or remark toward someone.

examples.text: 그에게 질문을 던졌다.
examples.translation: I threw a question at him.

faults.quote: /ut̚.da/
faults.why: After obstruent /t̚/, /t/ undergoes post-obstruent tensing to [t͈]: /ut̚.t͈a/.
Should note that 웃다 is a regular ㅅ verb (웃어요), unlike 짓다/잇다.

notes: Covers both laughing out loud and smiling silently; context or adverbs like 크게 (loudly) or 활짝 (brightly) make the meaning clear.
Regular ㅅ verb: the ㅅ is kept before vowels (웃어요, 웃어서). Do not confuse with 울다 (to cry).

senses.definition: To make sounds and movements of the face because something is funny.

examples.text: 친구의 재미있는 이야기 때문에 크게 웃었다.
examples.translation: I laughed out loud at my friend's funny story.

senses.definition: To curve the corners of the mouth upward to show happiness or friendliness, without making a sound.

examples.text: 그는 사진을 찍을 때 밝게 웃었다.
examples.translation: He smiled brightly when having his picture taken.

faults.why: Missing crucial grammar note: adjectival noun ('ein Fremder' without definite article).

faults.quote: Note the difference between 'der Fremde' (a stranger or foreigner) and 'fremd'
faults.why: Explains basic noun vs. adjective difference instead of adjectival noun declension.

faults.quote: A person who comes from another country.
faults.why: Means someone unfamiliar/not from here ('outsider'); 'Ausländer' is used for foreign nationality.

notes: Declines like an adjective: 'der Fremde', but 'ein Fremder' (masculine) and 'eine Fremde' (feminine).
For someone from another country (a foreigner), use 'der Ausländer'.

senses.definition: A person you do not know, or who is not from the place where they are.

examples.text: Ich spreche nie mit Fremden auf der Straße.
examples.translation: I never talk to strangers on the street.

examples.text: Er fühlt sich hier noch wie ein Fremder.
examples.translation: He still feels like an outsider here.

faults.why: Should explain how 'ein Freund von mir' vs. 'mein Freund' distinguishes the two senses.

notes: 'Mein Freund' usually means 'my boyfriend'. To say 'a friend of mine' without romantic meaning, say 'ein Freund von mir' or 'ein guter Freund'.
The feminine form is 'die Freundin' (female friend or girlfriend), and the plural is 'die Freunde'.

senses.definition: A male person you know well and like, who is not a romantic partner.

examples.text: Er ist ein sehr guter Freund von mir.
examples.translation: He is a very good friend of mine.

senses.definition: A man or boy with whom someone is in a romantic relationship.

examples.text: Sie geht heute Abend mit ihrem Freund ins Kino.
examples.translation: She is going to the cinema with her boyfriend this evening.

faults.quote: /ˈfʁʏlɪŋ/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and quality; 'ü' before 'h' is long /yː/, not short /ʏ/.

faults.quote: In Southern Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, you will often hear the term 'der Lenz'
faults.why: 'Lenz' is archaic/poetic everywhere, not an everyday Southern/Austrian/Swiss regionalism ('Frühjahr' is the common synonym).

notes: Use 'im Frühling' to say 'in (the) spring'. Another common word for spring is 'das Frühjahr'.

senses.definition: The season between winter and summer, when the weather gets warmer and plants begin to grow.

examples.text: Im Frühling blühen die Blumen im Garten.
examples.translation: In spring the flowers bloom in the garden.

faults.quote: Often used in compounds like Fußgänger (pedestrian) or Fußball (football).
faults.why: Should mention the essential A1/A2 phrase 'zu Fuß' (on foot) instead of random compounds.

notes: The plural is 'die Füße'.
Note the common phrase 'zu Fuß gehen' (to walk, to go on foot).

senses.definition: The lower part of the leg that you stand and walk on.

examples.text: Mein Fuß tut weh.
examples.translation: My foot hurts.

senses.definition: The lowest part of a mountain, hill, or tall object.

examples.text: Wir warteten am Fuß des Berges.
examples.translation: We waited at the foot of the mountain.

faults.quote: Note that nouns in German always begin with a capital letter
faults.why: Generic rule applying to all German nouns, not specific to 'Garten'.

notes: The plural is 'die Gärten' (with an umlaut).

senses.definition: A piece of land next to a house where grass, flowers, or vegetables are grown.

examples.text: Wir trinken Kaffee im Garten.
examples.translation: We are drinking coffee in the garden.

faults.quote: スマホの信号が弱いです。
faults.why: Cell phone reception is 電波 (denpa), not 信号; 信号 here is an English calque.

faults.quote: like a phone signal or a gesture
faults.why: Phone reception is 電波 and a gesture is 合図; neither is called 信号 in everyday Japanese.

notes: In everyday speech, 信号 almost always means a traffic light. Note that 'green light' is 青信号 (ao-shingō, literally 'blue signal') and 'red light' is 赤信号 (aka-shingō).
For a hand gesture or cue between people, use 合図 (aizu); for cell phone or Wi-Fi reception, use 電波 (denpa).

senses.definition: A set of coloured lights at a road junction or crossing that controls traffic.

examples.text: 次の信号を左に曲がってください。
examples.translation: Please turn left at the next traffic light.

senses.definition: A physical or electronic sign used to convey a warning or instruction, such as a railway signal or SOS.

examples.text: 船がSOSの信号を送った。
examples.translation: The ship sent an SOS signal.

faults.quote: it can also describe any face-to-face meeting or consultation.
faults.why: 面接 specifically means an interview for selection/admission; a general meeting or consultation is 面談.
Both senses mean an assessment/selection interview (for a job or school); they are one sense.

notes: Used with する (面接する, 'to interview').
Refers to an interview to judge an applicant (for a job, school, or visa). A journalist's or celebrity interview is インタビュー, and a one-on-one consultation or talk (e.g. parent-teacher) is 面談 (mendan).

senses.definition: A formal meeting in which an applicant is asked questions to see if they are suitable for a job, school, or programme.

examples.text: 明日は大切な面接があります。
examples.translation: I have an important interview tomorrow.

examples.text: バイトの面接を受けた。
examples.translation: I had a part-time job interview.

faults.quote: 恐怖心を感じる。
faults.why: Uses the compound noun 恐怖心 rather than the headword 恐怖 itself, duplicating note [1].

notes: A somewhat formal noun for strong fear or terror; in everyday conversation, the adjective 怖い (kowai, 'scary; afraid') is much more common.
Often seen in compounds such as 恐怖心 (kyōfushin, 'feeling of fear') and 恐怖症 (kyōfushō, 'phobia', e.g. 高所恐怖症 'fear of heights').

senses.definition: A strong feeling of being afraid or terrified of danger, pain, or something frightening.

examples.text: 彼は恐怖で動けなくなった。
examples.translation: He was paralysed with fear.

examples.text: 戦争の恐怖を忘れてはいけない。
examples.translation: We must not forget the horrors of war.

notes: Usually written in hiragana (ぶどう) or katakana (ブドウ); the kanji is 葡萄.

senses.definition: A small, round purple or green fruit that grows in bunches on vines and is eaten raw or used to make wine.

examples.text: ぶどうはワインの原料です。
examples.translation: Grapes are the main ingredient in wine.

faults.why: Kanji headword 豚 is missing its required hiragana reading ぶた.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'buta-goya' (pigsty) or other compound words
faults.why: Note [0] restates the senses; note [1] warns against confusing 'pig' with 'pigsty'.

notes: Pork is more specifically called 豚肉 (butaniku), though 豚 alone is often used on menus and in dish names (such as 豚バラ, 'pork belly').
In some compounds, 豚 is read とん (ton), as in とんかつ (tonkatsu, 'pork cutlet') and 豚汁 (tonjiru, 'pork miso soup', also read butajiru).

senses.definition: A pink or spotted farm animal with short legs, raised for its meat.

examples.text: 農場に豚がたくさんいる。
examples.translation: There are many pigs on the farm.

senses.definition: The meat of a pig eaten as food.

examples.text: カレーには牛より豚を入れるのが好きだ。
examples.translation: I prefer putting pork rather than beef in my curry.

faults.quote: Glück is used for both 'luck' (good fortune by chance) and 'happiness'
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses and glosses; does not mention that 'Glück' is uncountable.

faults.quote: We had a lot of luck with the weather.
faults.why: Calque of 'Glück haben'; natural English is 'We were very lucky with the weather'.

notes: Uncountable (no plural). 'To be lucky' is expressed with 'Glück haben' (literally 'to have luck').
To wish someone good luck, say 'Viel Glück!' (not 'Gutes Glück!').

senses.definition: Good things that happen by chance; favorable circumstances.

examples.text: Wir hatten viel Glück mit dem Wetter.
examples.translation: We were very lucky with the weather.

senses.definition: A feeling of joy, satisfaction, and well-being.

examples.text: Echtes Glück kann man nicht kaufen.
examples.translation: You cannot buy true happiness.

faults.quote: In everyday spoken German, 'Gras' is also commonly used as a slang
faults.why: Restates sense 1 instead of giving useful grammar such as the irregular plural 'die Gräser'.

notes: Usually singular; the plural 'die Gräser' refers to different types or blades of grass.

senses.definition: The small green plants that cover the ground in gardens, fields, and parks.

examples.text: Die Kinder spielen draußen im hohen Gras.
examples.translation: The children are playing outside in the tall grass.

senses.definition: (informal) Dried cannabis flowers smoked as a drug.

examples.text: Er hat gestern Abend etwas Gras geraucht.
examples.translation: He smoked some weed last night.

faults.quote: If you are talking about individual strands, you use the plural 'die Haare'.
faults.why: False: in everyday German, plural 'die Haare' is the most common way to mean head hair.
Countable vs. collective use of hair is one meaning explained in the note, not two senses.

notes: Unlike English 'hair', German usually uses the plural 'die Haare' for the hair on someone's head (e.g. 'Ich wasche mir die Haare'). The singular 'das Haar' is used for a single strand, or in a more formal style for all the hair on one's head.

senses.definition: The fine thread-like strands that grow on a person's head or body, or on an animal.

examples.text: Sie hat lange, braune Haare.
examples.translation: She has long, brown hair.

examples.text: Ich habe ein Haar in meiner Suppe gefunden.
examples.translation: I found a hair in my soup.

faults.quote: (animal) A young, small male chicken.
faults.why: In modern everyday German, 'Hähnchen' almost exclusively means chicken as food.

notes: Plural: 'die Hähnchen'.
Used for chicken as food. For the living bird, use 'das Huhn' (plural: 'die Hühner').

senses.definition: Chicken meat or a whole chicken prepared as food, especially roasted.

examples.text: Ich bestelle ein halbes Hähnchen mit Pommes.
examples.translation: I am ordering half a roast chicken with fries.

faults.quote: (food) The part of an animal, such as a chicken or pig
faults.why: Animal leg/meat is the same core meaning; furniture leg (桌子腿) is a better extension.
Should mention the common classifier 条 (tiáo) instead of stating leg vs. foot.

notes: Takes the classifier 条 (tiáo), e.g., 两条腿 (two legs).
Also used for the legs of furniture, such as 桌子腿 (table leg).

senses.definition: The limb of a person or animal used for standing and walking; also the leg of an animal eaten as food, or a support on a piece of furniture.

examples.text: 我的腿很酸。
examples.translation: My legs are very sore.

examples.text: 我想吃鸡腿。
examples.translation: I want to eat a chicken leg.

faults.quote: 纸 is a measure word (量词) for flat, thin items
faults.why: False: 纸 is an uncountable noun taking the classifier 张 (zhāng), not a common classifier.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 支 (zhī), which is the measure word
faults.why: Unhelpful comparison caused by falsely treating 纸 as a classifier in note 0.

notes: Counted in sheets using the classifier 张 (zhāng), e.g., 一张纸 (a sheet of paper).

senses.definition: A thin material used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

examples.text: 请给我一张纸。
examples.translation: Please give me a piece of paper.

faults.quote: (sunday) Sunday, the seventh day of the week.
faults.why: 星期 alone rarely means Sunday; the example actually uses the compound 星期天.

faults.quote: week; Sunday
faults.why: Sunday is not a standard everyday meaning of 星期 by itself.

notes: Takes the classifier 个 (gè), e.g., 一个星期 (one week).
Followed by numbers 1 to 6 to name Monday through Saturday (星期一 to 星期六), and by 天 or 日 for Sunday (星期天, 星期日).

senses.definition: A period of seven days.

examples.text: 我上个星期去了北京。
examples.translation: I went to Beijing last week.

faults.quote: 飞机 is a compound word formed by 'fly' (飞) and 'machine' (机).
faults.why: Filler note; should instead give the standard classifier 架 (jià) and verb 坐 (zuò).

notes: Takes the classifier 架 (jià), e.g., 一架飞机 (an airplane). To travel by plane is 坐飞机 (zuò fēijī).

senses.definition: A powered flying vehicle with wings.

examples.text: 我坐飞机去北京。
examples.translation: I am taking a plane to Beijing.

faults.quote: 汽车 is the general term for a car or automobile.
faults.why: Restates the gloss instead of giving the classifier 辆 (liàng) and everyday usage vs. 车.

notes: Takes the classifier 辆 (liàng), e.g., 一辆汽车 (a car).
In everyday speech, people often just say 车 (chē) for 'car', while 公共汽车 (gōnggòng qìchē) means 'bus'.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels, especially a car.

examples.text: 他买了一辆新汽车。
examples.translation: He bought a new car.

faults.quote: 맵다 describes food that contains hot spices like chili.
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the essential irregular ㅂ-conjugation (매워요, 매운).

notes: Irregular ㅂ-adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (매워요, 매운 음식).
Do not confuse with 뜨겁다, which means hot in temperature (to the touch).

senses.definition: Having a strong, burning taste caused by chili peppers or other spices.

examples.text: 김치가 너무 매워요.
examples.translation: The kimchi is too spicy.

faults.quote: Used to describe people or actions that show no fear
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

notes: Related to the noun 용기 (courage); before a noun, it takes the form 용감한.

senses.definition: Not afraid of danger or difficult situations; showing courage.

examples.text: 그 소방관은 화재 현장에서 매우 용감했다.
examples.translation: That firefighter was very brave at the fire scene.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 시끄러워요 (the polite form)
faults.why: Confusingly warns against its own polite form while omitting the irregular ㅂ-conjugation.

faults.quote: (annoyance) Bothersome or annoying because people keep talking too much
faults.why: Oversplit and mistranslated; its own example ('chat noisily') shows sense 0.

notes: Irregular ㅂ-adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (시끄러워요, 시끄러운 곳).
As an exclamation, 시끄러워! or 시끄러! is used to tell someone 'Be quiet!' or 'Shut up!'.

senses.definition: Full of or making a lot of loud, unpleasant noise.

examples.text: 밖이 너무 시끄러워서 잘 수 없어요.
examples.translation: It is too noisy outside, so I cannot sleep.

faults.quote: 부끄럽다 often captures both the feeling of being shy or bashful
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses while omitting the irregular ㅂ-conjugation.

faults.quote: To feel nervous, timid, or shy in front of other people.
faults.why: Adjectives should be defined as qualities or states, not with 'to' infinitives.

notes: Irregular ㅂ-adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (부끄러워요, 부끄러운 기억).
Compare 수줍다, which specifically describes being shy or bashful in manner rather than feeling ashamed of a mistake.

senses.definition: Feeling shame or embarrassment because of something wrong, foolish, or humiliating.

examples.text: 거짓말을 한 것이 정말 부끄럽다.
examples.translation: I feel truly ashamed for telling a lie.

senses.definition: Feeling nervous, timid, or bashful in front of other people.

examples.text: 나는 낯선 사람 앞에서 부끄러워서 말을 잘 못한다.
examples.translation: I am shy in front of strangers, so I cannot speak well.

faults.quote: Use this for someone who stays steady during a crisis
faults.why: Restates the definitions already given in the senses.

faults.quote: To feel peaceful and composed, not worried, anxious, or overly excited.
faults.why: Adjectives should be defined as qualities, not as 'to' infinitives.

notes: Do not confuse with 조용하다 (quiet/silent), which describes the absence of noise; 차분하다 describes a composed state of mind or a restful, understated atmosphere.

senses.definition: Of a person or mind: peaceful and composed, not anxious or easily excited.

examples.text: 그녀는 위기 상황에서도 차분하게 행동했다.
examples.translation: She acted calmly even in a crisis.

senses.definition: Of a color, tone, or atmosphere: soft, quiet, and not flashy or overwhelming.

examples.text: 방을 차분한 색으로 꾸미고 싶어요.
examples.translation: I want to decorate the room in muted colors.

faults.quote: /tɔˈa.lɛ.ta/
faults.why: Wrong stress placement; Polish stresses the penultimate syllable /tɔ.aˈlɛ.ta/.

faults.quote: Toaleta is the standard word for both the room and the fixture
faults.why: In Polish, 'toaleta' primarily means the room; the fixture is usually 'sedes' or 'muszla klozetowa'.
For a learner, the restroom and toilet are a single everyday sense, with room primary.

notes: The standard, polite word used in public places. In a home, people often ask for 'łazienka' (bathroom), whereas 'toaleta' or colloquial 'ubikacja' refers more specifically to the toilet room.

senses.definition: A room with a toilet, especially in a public building, or the toilet itself.

examples.text: Przepraszam, gdzie jest toaleta?
examples.translation: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

faults.quote: bag, sack
faults.why: 'Sack' in Polish is 'worek', not 'torba'.

faults.quote: bag; sack
faults.why: 'Sack' is inaccurate for 'torba'; it translates 'worek'.

faults.quote: Use 'torba' for grocery bags, duffel bags, or heavy-duty sacks
faults.why: Heavy-duty sacks are 'worki' (singular 'worek'), not 'torby'.

notes: While 'torba' is used for shopping bags, travel bags, or shoulder bags, the diminutive 'torebka' is used for a woman's handbag or a small paper/plastic bag.

senses.definition: A container made of cloth, paper, leather, or plastic, used for carrying things.

examples.text: Włożyłam zakupy do torby.
examples.translation: I put the groceries in the bag.

faults.why: Both senses mean the plant 'grass'; 'skosić trawę' is literally 'mow the grass', not a separate 'lawn' sense.

faults.quote: Used as both a mass noun for the plant itself
faults.why: Restates the definitions instead of adding useful usage info.

notes: Usually uncountable in everyday use. Do not confuse with 'trawnik', which refers specifically to a lawn (an area of mown grass).

senses.definition: A common wild or garden plant with thin green leaves that covers the ground.

examples.text: Siedzieliśmy na zielonej trawie.
examples.translation: We were sitting on the green grass.

examples.text: Muszę skosić trawę w ogrodzie.
examples.translation: I have to mow the grass in the garden.

faults.quote: Trudny means 'difficult' or 'hard' in the sense of something
faults.why: Merely restates the gloss and definition.

notes: Compare with 'ciężki', which primarily means physically 'heavy', though in spoken Polish it is also often used to mean 'hard/grueling' (e.g., 'ciężki dzień' – a hard day) and 'twardy', which means physically 'hard/solid'.

senses.definition: Not easy; requiring effort, skill, or time to do or understand.

examples.text: To było bardzo trudne zadanie.
examples.translation: That was a very difficult task.

senses.definition: Of a person, character, or situation: demanding and not easy to deal with.

examples.text: On ma trudny charakter.
examples.translation: He has a difficult personality.

faults.quote: Note that the Polish word for strawberry is a feminine noun.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender field and adds trivial cultural filler.

notes: Distinguished from 'poziomka', which is the much smaller, aromatic wild strawberry found in forests.

senses.definition: A small, juicy red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: Uwielbiam jeść świeże truskawki z cukrem.
examples.translation: I love eating fresh strawberries with sugar.

faults.why: Missing required hiragana reading 'きっぷ' for a kanji headword.

notes: 切符 (kippu) is mainly used for paper transport tickets (trains, buses). For events, movies, concerts, or flights, チケット (chiketto) is much more common.

senses.definition: A printed piece of paper that allows you to travel on public transport or enter a place.

examples.text: 切符を忘れないでください。
examples.translation: Please do not forget your ticket.

faults.quote: 一月はとても寒いです。
faults.why: Uses compound '一月' (ichigatsu, January) rather than standalone '月' (tsuki, month).

notes: Standalone 月 is read 'tsuki'. In month names it is read '-gatsu' (e.g., 一月 ichigatsu, January), and when counting months it uses '-kagetsu' (e.g., 二ヶ月 nikagetsu, two months).
The moon in the sky is often politely or affectionately called お月様 (otsuki-sama), especially with children.

senses.definition: The large object that shines in the night sky and changes its shape.

examples.text: 今夜は月がとてもきれいです。
examples.translation: The moon is very beautiful tonight.

senses.definition: A period of about thirty days, or one of the twelve parts of a year.

examples.text: 新しい月が始まりました。
examples.translation: A new month has started.

faults.quote: A series of carriages coupled together and traveling on a track.
faults.why: Splits one everyday meaning ('train') into two indistinguishable senses.

notes: Although 電車 literally means 'electric train', it is the standard everyday word for any passenger train in Japan.
列車 (ressha) is a more formal or general term used in station announcements and for long-distance or non-electric trains.

senses.definition: A public transport vehicle that runs on railway tracks, especially one powered by electricity.

examples.text: 毎日電車で学校へ行きます。
examples.translation: I go to school by train every day.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical device and for the act
faults.why: merely restates the two senses; misses vital collocation note (電話をかける / 電話をする).

notes: To say 'make a phone call', use 電話をかける (denwa o kakeru) or combine it with する as 電話する (denwa suru). To 'answer the phone' is 電話に出る (denwa ni deru).

senses.definition: A device used to talk to someone who is far away.

examples.text: 電話が鳴っています。
examples.translation: The phone is ringing.

senses.definition: The act of speaking with someone by telephone.

examples.text: あとで母に電話をかけます。
examples.translation: I will make a phone call to my mother later.

faults.quote: it is pronounced [마싣따] (ma-sit-tta).
faults.why: Standard pronunciation is [마딛따] (though [마싣따] is also permitted and common in speech).

faults.quote: younger speakers might use '존맛' (jon-mat), though that is vulgar
faults.why: Vulgar slang is unneeded for A2; conjugation note (-있는/-있어) is much more useful.

notes: Pronounced [마딛따] (standard) or [마싣따] (also accepted and very common in speech).
Although an adjective in meaning, it takes the verb modifier ending -는 (맛있는 음식, 'delicious food'). Opposite: 맛없다.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a pleasant or satisfying flavor.

examples.text: 이 김치는 정말 맛있어요.
examples.translation: This kimchi is really delicious.

faults.why: Missing note on irregular ㅡ conjugation (기뻐요) and third-person grammar (기뻐하다).

notes: Describes a feeling of joy about an event or news, unlike 행복하다, which describes a deeper, lasting state of happiness.

senses.definition: Feeling pleasure and satisfaction about something.

examples.text: 만나서 기뻐요.
examples.translation: I am happy to meet you.

examples.text: 좋은 소식을 들어서 정말 기뻐요.
examples.translation: I am really pleased to hear the good news.

faults.why: Hot weather and feeling hot from the weather are shades of one sense.
Missing essential A2 note on ㅂ-irregular conjugation (더워요, 더운).

notes: Used for weather, room temperature, or feeling hot in the heat. For objects or food hot to the touch, use 뜨겁다; for spicy food, use 맵다.
ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (더워요, 더운).

senses.definition: Of weather or air: having a high temperature; of a person: feeling uncomfortably warm.

examples.text: 오늘 날씨가 정말 덥네요.
examples.translation: The weather is really hot today.

examples.text: 너무 더워서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.translation: I felt so hot that I opened the window.

faults.why: Being kind to customers and treating neighbors kindly are the exact same sense.

faults.quote: 친절하다 describes someone who is helpful, polite, and considerate in their actions.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

notes: Often takes the particle -에게/-한테 for the person one is kind to. Unlike 다정하다 (warm and affectionate), 친절하다 focuses on polite, helpful behavior, including toward strangers.

senses.definition: Polite, helpful, and considerate toward others.

examples.text: 그 직원은 손님에게 아주 친절해요.
examples.translation: That employee is very kind to customers.

faults.quote: 요즘 경제 상황이 어려워요.
faults.why: Definition says 'in a poor financial situation or needing help', which describes people/households, not 'economic situation'.
Missing essential A2 note on ㅂ-irregular conjugation (어려워요, 어려운).

notes: ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (어려워요, 어려운). Opposite: 쉽다 (easy).
Compare with 힘들다, which focuses on physical or mental exhaustion rather than complexity.

senses.definition: Not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

examples.text: 이 수학 문제는 너무 어려워요.
examples.translation: This math problem is too difficult.

senses.definition: Of a financial situation or a person's circumstances: poor or full of hardship.

examples.text: 그 시절에는 살기가 정말 어려웠어요.
examples.translation: Life was really hard back then.

faults.quote: Use जागना (to wake up) for the moment you stop sleeping.
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1; जागना itself is commonly used for staying/being awake.
Should mention the transitive counterpart जगाना (to wake someone up) and intransitivity.

corrected.shortGloss: to wake up; to be awake
notes: Intransitive (does not take ने in the past tense). Its transitive counterpart is जगाना (to wake someone up).
In everyday speech, उठना (to get up) is also very commonly used to mean 'to wake up'.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping.

examples.text: मैं रोज़ सुबह छह बजे जागता हूँ।
examples.translation: I wake up at six every morning.

senses.definition: To remain awake and not sleeping.

examples.text: वह पूरी रात जाग रहा था।
examples.translation: He was awake all night.

faults.quote: (slip) To lose footing and drop to the floor or ground.
faults.why: A person falling and an object falling are the same sense; 'slip' comes from फिसलना.

faults.quote: to fall down, to slip
faults.why: गिरना does not mean 'to slip' (which is फिसलना in the example).
Missing the common everyday sense 'to decrease / drop' (prices, temperature).

notes: Intransitive (does not take ने in the past tense). Do not confuse it with its transitive counterpart गिराना (to drop or knock something down).
Often used in the compound verb गिर जाना to emphasize the completion of falling.

senses.definition: To move downward and hit the ground by accident or gravity, of an object or person.

examples.text: पेड़ से सेब नीचे गिर गया।
examples.translation: The apple fell down from the tree.

examples.text: वह बारिश में फिसल कर गिर गया।
examples.translation: He slipped and fell in the rain.

senses.definition: To become lower in amount, level, or value.

examples.text: रात में तापमान बहुत गिर गया।
examples.translation: The temperature dropped a lot at night.

faults.quote: This is a general verb for kissing. In very informal or slang
faults.why: Restates the gloss with vague filler and a broken romanization ('chūm nā').

faults.why: False claim; हाथ चूमना (to kiss a hand) is completely standard in Hindi.

notes: Transitive verb: takes the postposition ने with the subject in past (perfective) tenses, and को with a specific person as the object.

senses.definition: To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or respect.

examples.text: माँ ने अपने बच्चे को चूमा।
examples.translation: The mother kissed her child.

faults.quote: to think; to consider; to wonder
faults.why: Includes 'to wonder', which is not in the senses, while omitting 'to plan/intend'.

corrected.shortGloss: to think; to consider; to plan
notes: Used with the postposition के बारे में (about) for the topic of thought: उसके बारे में सोचो (think about him/her).
To express thinking of doing something, use the infinitive in -ने + का or की before सोचना.

senses.definition: To use your mind to consider something or form an opinion.

examples.text: मुझे इसके बारे में सोचना होगा।
examples.translation: I will have to think about this.

senses.definition: To have a plan or intention to do something.

examples.text: हम कल बाहर जाने की सोच रहे हैं।
examples.translation: We are thinking of going out tomorrow.

faults.quote: (smile) To show amusement or friendliness with a small expression of the
faults.why: Directly contradicts note[0]; हँसना means to laugh, whereas 'to smile' is मुस्कुराना.

notes: Intransitive (does not take ने in the past tense). Do not confuse with मुस्कुराना (to smile quietly).
Takes the postposition पर (at) for the person or thing being laughed at: किसी पर हँसना (to laugh at someone).

senses.definition: To make sounds and smile because something is funny or you are happy.

examples.text: वे बहुत ज़ोर से हँस रहे थे।
examples.translation: They were laughing very loudly.

examples.text: मेरी बात पर मत हँसो।
examples.translation: Don't laugh at what I said.

faults.quote: the names of the months are masculine and are not capitalized
faults.why: Month names are nouns in German and are always capitalized.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'Monat' (month) with 'Moment' (moment)
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; note should mention plural 'die Monate' and dative 'Monaten' instead.

notes: The plural is 'die Monate' (dative plural: 'den Monaten', as in 'vor zwei Monaten' — two months ago).

senses.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided, or a period of about thirty days.

examples.text: Der Februar ist der kürzeste Monat des Jahres.
examples.translation: February is the shortest month of the year.

examples.text: Ich fahre in einem Monat in den Urlaub.
examples.translation: I am going on vacation in a month.

faults.quote: Like in English, 'der Mond' refers to our specific moon.
faults.why: Pure filler telling an English speaker that German works just like English.

senses.definition: The natural satellite that orbits the earth and shines in the night sky.

examples.text: Der Mond scheint heute Nacht sehr hell.
examples.translation: The moon is shining very brightly tonight.

faults.quote: (future) The day following today. | glosses en: tomorrow
faults.why: 'Tomorrow' is the lowercase adverb 'morgen', not the masculine noun 'der Morgen'.

faults.quote: morning; tomorrow
faults.why: Includes 'tomorrow', which belongs to the lowercase adverb 'morgen', not this noun.

notes: Do not confuse the capitalized noun 'der Morgen' (morning) with the lowercase adverb 'morgen' (tomorrow).
To say 'in the morning', use 'am Morgen' for a specific morning, or the adverb 'morgens' for habitual actions.

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: Mein Morgen beginnt immer mit einer Tasse Kaffee.
examples.translation: My morning always begins with a cup of coffee.

examples.text: Wir treffen uns morgen früh am Morgen.
examples.translation: We are meeting early in the morning tomorrow.

faults.why: Should mention the irregular umlaut plural 'die Münder', which A2 learners cannot guess.

notes: The plural is irregular with an umlaut: 'die Münder'.
Used for people. For animals, 'das Maul' is normally used (which is rude when used for a person).

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Mach bitte deinen Mund auf.
examples.translation: Please open your mouth.

examples.text: Sie hat einen kleinen Mund.
examples.translation: She has a small mouth.

faults.quote: /lâː/
faults.why: Wrong tone mark; huyền tone in Hanoi IPA is /laː˨˩/, not circumflex.

faults.quote: Used to link a subject to its definition, identity, or classification
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of explaining that 'là' is not used before adjectives.

notes: Connects a subject to a noun ('Tôi là giáo viên'), not directly to an adjective ('Tôi mệt' = I am tired, without 'là').

senses.definition: To link a subject with a noun or noun phrase stating what or who it is.

examples.text: Tôi là học sinh.
examples.translation: I am a student.

senses.definition: To press clothes with a heated iron to make them smooth.

examples.text: Tôi cần là chiếc áo này trước khi đi làm.
examples.translation: I need to iron this shirt before going to work.

faults.quote: A person whose job is to drive a vehicle
faults.why: Defines a noun inside a verb entry; the example uses 'lái xe' as a verb.

faults.quote: Anh ấy là tài xế lái xe buýt.
faults.why: 'Tài xế' means driver; 'lái xe buýt' here is a verb phrase modifying it.

faults.quote: Can function both as a verb meaning 'to drive'
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without adding usage information.

notes: Literally 'to steer a vehicle'; used for driving cars, buses, or trucks, and often for riding motorbikes.

senses.definition: To operate and control the movement of a car or other road vehicle.

examples.text: Tôi học lái xe vào năm ngoái.
examples.translation: I learned to drive last year.

examples.text: Anh ấy lái xe buýt ở Hà Nội.
examples.translation: He drives a bus in Hanoi.

faults.quote: Cảm ơn bạn đã làm ơn giúp tôi hôm nay.
faults.why: Awkward phrasing; 'làm ơn' in the verbal sense means showing charity or pity.

faults.quote: It can also function as a verb phrase meaning 'to do a favor'
faults.why: Restates sense 1 without adding useful context.

notes: Placed before the verb in a polite request, often when asking a stranger for help.

senses.definition: Used before a verb to politely ask someone for help or a favor.

examples.text: Làm ơn chỉ đường cho tôi ra bến xe.
examples.translation: Please show me the way to the bus station.

faults.quote: /lɑːm˨˩ viək̚˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong tone on 'việc': nặng tone with final stop is low (/viək̚˧˨ʔ/), not rising.

faults.quote: Máy tính này không làm việc nữa.

senses.definition: To do a job or perform duties and tasks.

examples.text: Tôi làm việc ở văn phòng từ thứ Hai đến thứ Sáu.
examples.translation: I work at the office from Monday to Friday.

faults.quote: Use 'làm vỡ' when you cause a hard object
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to explain the causative 'làm' + resultative 'vỡ' pattern.

senses.definition: To cause a hard, brittle object to break into pieces, usually by dropping or hitting it.

examples.text: Tôi vô tình làm vỡ cái bát.
examples.translation: I accidentally broke the bowl.

faults.quote: To let go of something so it falls to the ground.
faults.why: Cadere is intransitive; transitive 'to drop' requires 'far cadere' (as in the example).

senses.definition: To move downward and hit the ground accidentally, or of an object, to come down from a higher position.

examples.text: Attento a non cadere sul ghiaccio.
examples.translation: Careful not to fall on the ice.

examples.text: Le foglie cominciano a cadere dagli alberi.
examples.translation: The leaves are starting to fall from the trees.

faults.why: All three senses describe the same basic physical quality of warmth/heat.

faults.quote: Oggi fa molto caldo in città.
faults.why: In 'fare caldo', 'caldo' functions as a noun, not an adjective.

notes: Covers both English 'hot' and 'warm'. Also used as a masculine noun meaning 'heat' or 'warm weather', especially in 'fa caldo' (it's hot) and 'avere caldo' (to feel hot).

senses.definition: Having or producing a high or comfortably high temperature; keeping the body warm.

examples.text: Il caffè è ancora troppo caldo per berlo.
examples.translation: The coffee is still too hot to drink.

examples.text: Mi piace indossare un maglione caldo in inverno.
examples.translation: I like to wear a warm sweater in winter.

faults.quote: Use 'calmo' when someone is peaceful, quiet, or not worried.
faults.why: Restates the definition and glosses without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Commonly used with 'stare' or 'restare' in the imperative: 'Stai calmo!' (Calm down! / Stay calm!).

senses.definition: Of a person, free from agitation or worry; of a place, weather, or water, still and peaceful.

examples.text: Il mare oggi è molto calmo.
examples.translation: The sea is very calm today.

examples.text: Cerca di restare calmo durante l'esame.
examples.translation: Try to stay calm during the exam.

faults.quote: Use camminare when focusing on the physical action of walking
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the crucial grammar point that it takes 'avere'.

notes: Although it is an intransitive verb of motion, it takes 'avere' in compound tenses ('ho camminato').

senses.definition: To move on foot at a regular pace.

examples.text: Mi piace camminare nel parco la mattina.
examples.translation: I like to walk in the park in the morning.

faults.quote: Also used for birds and roosters making their natural sounds.
faults.why: Simply repeats Sense 1.

notes: Takes 'avere' in compound tenses ('ho cantato').

senses.definition: To make musical sounds with the voice.

examples.text: Mi piace cantare sotto la doccia.
examples.translation: I like to sing in the shower.

senses.definition: Of a bird, rooster, or insect, to make its characteristic call.

examples.text: Il gallo comincia a cantare all'alba.
examples.translation: The rooster starts to crow at dawn.

faults.quote: Refers to human skin, animal fur, or leather material depending on context.
faults.why: Merely restates the senses and glosses.

faults.quote: El perro tiene la piel muy gruesa.
faults.why: On a live dog, 'piel' means skin; 'pelo' or 'pelaje' is fur.

faults.quote: Compré una chaqueta de piel.
faults.why: In Mexican Spanish, 'chamarra' is much more natural than 'chaqueta'.

notes: For the peel or skin of most fruits, use 'la cáscara' instead.

senses.definition: The outer layer covering the body of a person or animal.

examples.text: Ella tiene la piel muy suave.
examples.translation: She has very soft skin.

senses.definition: Tanned animal hide or pelt used as a material for clothing, shoes, or bags.

examples.text: Compré una chamarra de piel.
examples.translation: I bought a leather jacket.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'el pie', which only refers to
faults.why: Repeats what is already stated in note 0, and is missing a needed note.

notes: Usually refers to a person's leg (or animal meat); for the leg of a live four-legged animal or a piece of furniture, use 'la pata'.

senses.definition: The lower limb of the human body, from the hip to the ankle.

examples.text: Me duele la pierna después de caminar tanto.
examples.translation: My leg hurts after walking so much.

senses.definition: The leg of an animal, such as chicken or pork, prepared as food.

examples.text: Voy a cocinar una pierna de pollo al horno.
examples.translation: I am going to cook a chicken leg in the oven.

faults.quote: Note the difference between the three common meanings: a botanical plant,

notes: For building levels, 'planta' is mainly used in 'planta baja' (ground floor) and 'planta alta' (upper floor); numbered floors use 'el piso'.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in soil and has leaves, stems, and roots.

examples.text: Tengo que regar las plantas del jardín.
examples.translation: I have to water the plants in the garden.

senses.definition: A level or story of a building.

examples.text: La recepción está en la planta baja.
examples.translation: The reception is on the ground floor.

senses.definition: The bottom surface of the foot.

examples.text: Me duele la planta del pie.
examples.translation: The sole of my foot hurts.

senses.definition: A large factory or industrial facility.

examples.text: Su hermano trabaja en una planta automotriz.
examples.translation: His brother works at an automotive plant.

faults.quote: Use 'ir a la playa' when you are going to the beach.
faults.why: Trivial literal translation that adds no grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Do not confuse with 'la costa', which refers to the entire coastline or coastal region rather than the sandy shore itself.

senses.definition: A sandy or stony shore by the sea or a lake where people go to swim or relax.

examples.text: Nos gusta caminar por la playa al atardecer.
examples.translation: We like to walk along the beach at sunset.

faults.quote: It also refers to a small piece of bread or pastry
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1 without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: In everyday French, 'canapé' is the standard word for a sofa or couch, much more common than 'sofa'.

senses.definition: A long upholstered seat with a back and arms for two or more people.

examples.text: Il s'est endormi sur le canapé.
examples.translation: He fell asleep on the sofa.

senses.definition: A small decorative piece of bread or pastry topped with savory food.

examples.text: Nous avons préparé des canapés pour la fête.
examples.translation: We prepared canapés for the party.

faults.quote: With a low temperature, especially referring to the weather.
faults.why: Low temperature of weather and objects is a single sense, not two.

notes: To say a person feels cold, use the dative ('Mir ist kalt'), never 'Ich bin kalt' (which means being emotionally cold).
Takes umlaut in comparative and superlative: kälter, am kältesten.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm.

examples.text: Es ist heute sehr kalt draußen.
examples.translation: It is very cold outside today.

examples.text: Das Wasser ist mir zu kalt.
examples.translation: The water is too cold for me.

senses.definition: Of a person or behaviour: unfriendly and showing no emotion.

examples.text: Er begrüßte uns mit einem kalten Lächeln.
examples.translation: He greeted us with a cold smile.

faults.quote: Kaufen is the standard verb for buying.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding grammatical or usage information.

notes: Takes a dative pronoun for the recipient: 'Ich kaufe mir/dir ein Buch' (I'm buying myself/you a book).
Contrast with 'einkaufen' (to do the shopping / go grocery shopping, used without a direct object).

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.

examples.text: Ich möchte einen neuen Mantel kaufen.
examples.translation: I would like to buy a new coat.

examples.text: Wir haben frisches Brot beim Bäcker gekauft.
examples.translation: We bought fresh bread at the bakery.

faults.why: Missing note on irregular stem-changing forms (kannte, gekannt).

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to be familiar with
notes: Do not confuse with 'wissen': use 'kennen' with a noun for people, places, or things you are familiar with; use 'wissen' for facts (often with a clause like 'Ich weiß, dass...').
Irregular past forms with vowel change: kannte, hat gekannt.

senses.definition: To be familiar with a person, place, or thing through experience.

examples.text: Ich kenne diese Stadt sehr gut.
examples.translation: I know this city very well.

examples.text: Kennst du meine Schwester schon?
examples.translation: Do you already know my sister?

faults.why: Missing common everyday sense 'young / little' for children ('als ich klein war').

notes: For a person's height, German uses 'klein' (not 'kurz', which is only for objects and time).

senses.definition: Not large in size, amount, or extent.

examples.text: Das ist ein sehr kleines Auto.
examples.translation: That is a very small car.

examples.text: Wir machen eine kleine Pause.
examples.translation: We are taking a short break.

senses.definition: Of a person: not tall.

examples.text: Mein Bruder ist ziemlich klein.
examples.translation: My brother is quite short.

senses.definition: Of a child or sibling: young; not yet grown up.

examples.text: Als ich klein war, wohnten wir auf dem Land.
examples.translation: When I was little, we lived in the countryside.

faults.quote: for stairs, use 'treppensteigen'
faults.why: 'treppensteigen' is not a standard verb and is wrongly capitalized (it is 'die Treppe hinaufsteigen/nehmen').

faults.quote: Klettern is specifically used for climbing with hands and feet
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim; fails to mention that 'klettern' takes 'sein' in the perfect.

notes: Forms the perfect tense with 'sein' (ist geklettert).
Used for climbing with hands and feet. For stairs or mountains walked on foot, use 'steigen' (e.g. 'auf einen Berg steigen', 'die Treppe hinaufsteigen').

senses.definition: To go up or over something using hands and feet.

examples.text: Die Kinder klettern gerne auf die Bäume im Park.
examples.translation: The children like to climb the trees in the park.

examples.text: Er klettert am Wochenende in einer Kletterhalle.
examples.translation: He climbs in a climbing gym on the weekend.

faults.quote: 'ลุง' is used for an older brother of either your mother
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two sense definitions without adding usage information.

notes: For a parent's younger sibling, use น้า (mother's side) or อา (father's side). An older sister of either parent is ป้า (aunt).
Often used before a man's name or nickname as a title (e.g., ลุงสมชาย — Uncle Somchai), and as a first-person pronoun ('I') by an older man speaking to someone younger.

senses.definition: The older brother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: ลุงของฉันใจดีมาก
examples.translation: My uncle is very kind.

senses.definition: A friendly, respectful term of address for an older man, even a stranger.

examples.text: สวัสดีครับลุง
examples.translation: Hello, uncle.

faults.quote: The male reproductive organ of humans and animals.
faults.why: Colloquial slang sense is unnecessary and distracting for an A1-A2 learner's entry.

faults.quote: As a noun, ไข่ most commonly refers to bird eggs used
faults.why: Merely restates the senses; misses the essential classifier (ฟอง / ใบ).

notes: The classifier for eggs is ฟอง (or colloquially ใบ): ไข่สองฟอง (two eggs). Chicken egg is ไข่ไก่.

senses.definition: An oval object laid by a bird, especially a chicken, or by a fish or reptile, often eaten as food.

examples.text: ฉันชอบกินไข่ต้มทุกเช้า
examples.translation: I like to eat a boiled egg every morning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'ห้อง' (room).
faults.why: Unhelpful and arbitrary comparison; misses grammar of placing numbers after ชั้น and classifier use.

notes: To name a specific floor or school grade, put the number directly after ชั้น (e.g., ชั้นสาม — 3rd floor). Also used as a classifier for floors, layers, and shelves.

senses.definition: One level or story of a building.

examples.text: ห้องของฉันอยู่ชั้นสาม
examples.translation: My room is on the third floor.

senses.definition: A flat board attached to a wall or inside a cabinet for holding things, or one tier of a rack.

examples.text: หนังสืออยู่บนชั้น
examples.translation: The books are on the shelf.

senses.definition: A year level in school, or a level of rank or quality.

examples.text: น้องสาวเรียนอยู่ชั้นประถม
examples.translation: My younger sister is in primary school.

faults.quote: The system of rails, engines, and cars used for transportation.
faults.why: Oversplit induced by English 'railway station' for สถานีรถไฟ (train station); रेलवे track is ทางรถไฟ.

faults.quote: The word 'รถไฟ' is used both for the vehicle itself and
faults.why: Restates the oversplit sense instead of giving the classifier (ขบวน).

notes: Do not confuse รถไฟ (intercity train) with รถไฟฟ้า (electric urban transit, such as the BTS Skytrain or MRT subway).
The classifier for a whole train is ขบวน, and for an individual carriage is ตู้.

senses.definition: A series of connected carriages that travel on railway tracks to carry passengers or goods.

examples.text: ฉันนั่งรถไฟไปเชียงใหม่
examples.translation: I took the train to Chiang Mai.

examples.text: สถานีรถไฟอยู่ไม่ไกลจากที่นี่
examples.translation: The train station is not far from here.

faults.quote: /ʔa.pʰaːt.men/
faults.why: Missing tone marks in Thai IPA transcription (/ʔà.pʰáːt.mén/).

faults.quote: This is a loanword from English, commonly used in Thai cities
faults.why: Misses the important everyday Thai distinction between อพาร์ตเมนต์ (rental building) and คอนโด (condo).

corrected.headword: อพาร์ตเมนต์
notes: In Thailand, อพาร์ตเมนต์ usually refers to a rental building owned by a single landlord (or a room in one), whereas privately owned units with shared facilities are called คอนโด (condo).

senses.definition: A rented room or set of rooms for living in, or the multi-story building containing them.

examples.text: ฉันอาศัยอยู่ในอพาร์ตเมนต์เล็ก ๆ ในเมือง
examples.translation: I live in a small apartment in the city.
examples.matchedForm: อพาร์ตเมนต์

faults.quote: To praise or celebrate someone or something in a song or poem.
faults.why: Poetic sense ('sing of/celebrate') is not needed at A2; keep only the basic sense.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages that use different verbs for singing professionally versus singing
faults.why: Pure filler; also falsely equates humming with τραγουδώ (humming is μουρμουρίζω).
Missing the aorist stem (τραγούδησα), which is essential for Greek verbs.

notes: Also commonly used in the uncontracted form τραγουδάω (-άω/-ώ conjugation); aorist: τραγούδησα.

senses.definition: To make musical sounds with the voice.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει να τραγουδώ στο μπάνιο.
examples.translation: I like to sing in the shower.

faults.quote: To dislike something very much or find it extremely unpleasant.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning ('hate' vs 'dislike intensely'); both examples show casual use.

faults.quote: Μισώ is a strong verb used to express deep hatred or intense
faults.why: Restates the definition and duplicates note[1].

notes: Follows the -ώ (-άς, -άει) or -ώ (-είς, -εί) pattern; aorist: μίσησα.
For casual everyday dislikes, Greek speakers also commonly use σιχαίνομαι ('can't stand') or δεν μου αρέσει καθόλου ('I don't like at all').

senses.definition: To feel intense dislike or hatred for someone or something.

examples.text: Μισώ να ξυπνάω νωρίς το πρωί.
examples.translation: I hate waking up early in the morning.

faults.why: Should mention the irregular aorist έπλυνα and the idiomatic use for brushing teeth.

notes: Aorist: έπλυνα. Used for washing hands, dishes, clothes, and also idiomatically for brushing teeth (πλένω τα δόντια μου).
For cleaning a room or house, use καθαρίζω instead; for washing oneself, use the passive πλένομαι.

senses.definition: To clean something with water and usually soap.

examples.text: Πλένω τα πιάτα μετά το φαγητό.
examples.translation: I wash the dishes after eating.

examples.text: Πρέπει να πλένεις τα χέρια σου συχνά.
examples.translation: You must wash your hands often.

faults.quote: /ˈfεύ.ɣω/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA containing Greek letters 'εύ' and 'ω' instead of /ˈfev.ɣo/.

faults.quote: To escape or run away from danger or a situation.
faults.why: In the example, έφυγε simply means 'left/went away'; 'escape' is δραπετεύω or ξεφεύγω.
Missing the highly irregular and essential aorist stem (έφυγα, subjunctive να φύγω).

notes: Irregular aorist: έφυγα (subjunctive: να φύγω). Note that the combination ευ is pronounced /ev/ in the present tense, but /f/ in the aorist.
Takes από before the place you are leaving (e.g., φεύγω από το σπίτι, 'I leave the house').

senses.definition: To go away from a place or person.

examples.text: Πρέπει να φύγω τώρα γιατί έχω δουλειά.
examples.translation: I have to leave now because I have work.

faults.quote: This is the standard verb for dancing. It can be used both
faults.why: Explaining transitivity that works identically to English is filler; mention pronunciation of ευ and aorist instead.

notes: The letter combination ευ is pronounced /ev/ in the present tense (χορεύω), but becomes /ps/ in the aorist: χόρεψα.

senses.definition: To move one's body rhythmically to music.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει να χορεύω στα πάρτι.
examples.translation: I like to dance at parties.

faults.quote: Any male or female person who shares the same parents
faults.why: The inclusive masculine plural 'hermanos' is a standard grammar rule already explained in the notes.

notes: The feminine form is 'la hermana' (sister).
The plural 'los hermanos' can refer to brothers or to siblings of both sexes.

senses.definition: A male person who has the same parents as another person; in the plural, brothers or siblings.

examples.text: Mi hermano vive en Madrid.
examples.translation: My brother lives in Madrid.

examples.text: Tengo tres hermanos: dos chicas y un chico.
examples.translation: I have three siblings: two girls and one boy.

faults.quote: A thin layer of frozen water that forms on surfaces
faults.why: Ice on a windshield is still 'ice' ('frost' is 'escarcha'); oversplit of one meaning.

faults.quote: Used both for frozen water in cubes or blocks
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: Spelled with a silent 'h' and pronounced like the 'y' in 'yes'. In plural ('hielos'), it often means 'ice cubes'.

senses.definition: Water that has frozen and become solid.

examples.text: Ponle más hielo a mi refresco, por favor.
examples.translation: Put more ice in my soft drink, please.

examples.text: El parabrisas del coche está cubierto de hielo esta mañana.
examples.translation: The car windscreen is covered in ice this morning.

notes: Use 'hijo' for a son and 'hija' for a daughter. The plural 'hijos' refers to sons or to children of both sexes.

senses.definition: A male child in relation to his parents; in the plural, sons or children.

examples.text: Mi hijo mayor estudia en la universidad.
examples.translation: My oldest son studies at the university.

examples.text: ¿Tienes hijos?
examples.translation: Do you have children?

faults.quote: Es un gran paso para el hombre.
faults.why: In Armstrong's quote, 'para el hombre' translates 'for a man', whereas 'mankind' is 'la humanidad'.

faults.quote: Note that 'hombre' is also used to mean 'mankind'
faults.why: Simply repeats sense 1 without adding extra grammatical or usage information.

notes: Do not confuse 'el hombre' (man) with 'el hambre' (hunger).
Often used in Spain as an informal exclamation ('¡Hombre!') to show surprise, agreement, or greeting.

senses.definition: An adult male human being.

examples.text: Aquel hombre camina muy rápido por la calle.
examples.translation: That man is walking very fast down the street.

senses.definition: Human beings in general, or a person regardless of sex or age.

examples.text: El perro es el mejor amigo del hombre.
examples.translation: A dog is man's best friend.

faults.quote: Use rencontrer for both planned meetings (like meeting a friend for coffee)
faults.why: False: 'rencontrer' is not used in standard French for casual planned meetups with known friends.

faults.quote: To come to the same place as another person
faults.why: 'Rencontrer' means to meet for the first time or by chance, not casual meetups ('retrouver').

faults.quote: Je vais rencontrer mes amis au café ce soir.
faults.why: Anglicism; in France one says 'retrouver' or 'voir' one's friends at a cafe.

notes: Used for meeting someone for the first time or by chance. For planned meetups with people you already know, use 'retrouver' or 'voir'.
Takes a direct object with no preposition: rencontrer quelqu'un (to meet someone).

senses.definition: To make the acquaintance of someone for the first time, or to have a formal meeting with someone.

examples.text: J'ai rencontré ma femme à l'université.
examples.translation: I met my wife at university.

senses.definition: To come across someone by chance, or to face a problem or difficulty.

examples.text: J'ai rencontré mon ancien professeur au supermarché.
examples.translation: I ran into my old teacher at the supermarket.

corrected.shortGloss: to repair; to fix; to make up for

senses.definition: To make something broken or damaged work again.

examples.text: Il faut réparer la machine à laver.
examples.translation: We need to repair the washing machine.

senses.definition: To put right or make amends for a mistake or a wrong.

examples.text: Il essaie de réparer son erreur.
examples.translation: He is trying to make up for his mistake.

faults.quote: (message) To follow up on a phone call or message.
faults.why: Answering a question and replying to a message are the same basic sense.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'correspondre', which means to correspond or match.
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'répondre' with 'correspondre'; mentioning the irregular participle 'répondu' is more useful.

notes: Takes the preposition 'à' before the person or thing being answered (répondre à une question, répondre à Paul), unlike English which takes a direct object.
Past participle: répondu.

senses.definition: To say or write something back to someone, or in reaction to a question, call, or message.

examples.text: Il faut répondre à la question du professeur.
examples.translation: You must answer the teacher's question.

examples.text: Elle n'a pas encore répondu à mon message.
examples.translation: She hasn't replied to my message yet.

faults.quote: Il habite dans une maison très riche.
faults.why: 'Une maison riche' is unnatural in French; 'riche' applies to people, families, or countries.

notes: Has the same form in the masculine and feminine (un homme riche, une femme riche).

senses.definition: Of a person, family, or country: having a large amount of money or valuable possessions.

examples.text: Elle vient d'une famille très riche.
examples.translation: She comes from a very wealthy family.

senses.definition: Of food, soil, or an experience: containing a large amount of fat, nutrients, or interesting elements (often with 'en').

examples.text: Ce gâteau au chocolat est un peu trop riche.
examples.translation: This chocolate cake is a little too rich.

examples.text: Les oranges sont riches en vitamines.
examples.translation: Oranges are rich in vitamins.

faults.quote: Ne t'inquiète pas, je rigole, je fais juste rire.
faults.why: 'Je fais juste rire' means 'I just make people laugh', not 'I'm just kidding' ('je dis ça pour rire').

faults.quote: Notice that the final 'e' in the infinitive is silent.
faults.why: Final 'e' is always silent in French; present forms or 'rire de' construction are more helpful.

notes: Irregular verb: je ris, tu ris, il rit, nous rions, vous riez, ils rient; past participle: ri. Takes 'de' before what you laugh at (rire d'une blague).
Do not confuse with 'sourire' (to smile).

senses.definition: To make the sounds and facial movements that show amusement or happiness.

examples.text: Tout le monde a ri en écoutant sa blague.
examples.translation: Everyone laughed when listening to his joke.

senses.definition: To speak or act in a joking way, without being serious (especially in 'pour rire').

examples.text: Ne t'inquiète pas, je disais ça pour rire.
examples.translation: Don't worry, I was saying that as a joke.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sympathetic sense ('poor thing', 'arme ik') while keeping a less common sense.

notes: Also exists as a homonymous de-noun 'de arm' meaning the body part 'arm' (plural: 'armen').

senses.definition: Having little money or few possessions.

examples.text: De man was erg arm en had geen huis.
examples.translation: The man was very poor and had no home.

senses.definition: Deserving pity or sympathy; unfortunate.

examples.text: Het arme kind was zijn moeder kwijt.
examples.translation: The poor child had lost his mother.

senses.definition: Lacking in a certain quality or substance (often with 'aan').

examples.text: Deze grond is arm aan voedingsstoffen.
examples.translation: This soil is poor in nutrients.

faults.quote: Lacking courage; timid or cowardly.
faults.why: 'Wees niet zo bang' simply means 'don't be so afraid', not 'cowardly' ('laf').

faults.quote: Use 'bang' when someone is experiencing fear or anxiety
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving the essential prepositions 'voor' (of) and 'om' (to).

notes: Takes the preposition 'voor' for 'afraid of' (e.g., 'bang voor spinnen') and 'om te' before a verb (e.g., 'bang om te vallen').
'Ik ben bang van wel / niet' is a common expression meaning 'I'm afraid so / not'.

senses.definition: Feeling fear or worry.

examples.text: Ik ben bang in het donker.
examples.translation: I am afraid of the dark.

examples.text: Mijn broertje is bang voor honden.
examples.translation: My little brother is scared of dogs.

faults.quote: De film begint over five minuten.
faults.why: Contains the English word 'five' instead of Dutch 'vijf'.

faults.quote: but 'hebben' can sometimes be used when focusing purely on the action.
faults.why: 'Beginnen' always takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense in standard Dutch, never 'hebben'.

faults.quote: To come into existence or have its starting point somewhere.
faults.why: Does not match the example ('the movie starts in five minutes', an event starting).

notes: Irregular verb: past tense 'begon / begonnen', past participle 'begonnen'. Always takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense ('ik ben begonnen').
Often used with 'met' ('beginnen met werken') or 'aan' when starting a task or item ('aan een boek beginnen').

senses.definition: To start doing something or taking part in an activity.

examples.text: We beginnen om acht uur met de les.
examples.translation: We start the lesson at eight o'clock.

senses.definition: Of an event, period, or thing: to have its starting point in time or space.

examples.text: De film begint over vijf minuten.
examples.translation: The movie starts in five minutes.

faults.quote: To grasp someone's feelings, motives, or situation.
faults.why: Shades of the same everyday meaning 'to understand'; no need to split for A2.

faults.quote: Do not confuse begrijpen with horen.
faults.why: Learners confuse 'begrijpen' (grasp meaning) with 'verstaan' (hear/make out speech), not 'horen'.

notes: Irregular verb: past tense 'begreep / begrepen', past participle 'begrepen'.
Compare with 'verstaan': 'begrijpen' means to grasp the meaning of something, while 'verstaan' means to hear speech clearly or understand a language.

senses.definition: To know the meaning of something, or why something happens or someone acts a certain way.

examples.text: Ik begrijp niet wat je bedoelt.
examples.translation: I don't understand what you mean.

examples.text: Ik begrijp waarom je zo moe bent.
examples.translation: I understand why you are so tired.

faults.quote: De bediende was erg beleefd tegen alle gasten.
faults.why: 'Bediende' means servant; for a waiter in a restaurant, Dutch uses 'ober'.

faults.quote: Use beleefd to describe someone who has good manners
faults.why: Purely repeats the definition.

notes: Takes the preposition 'tegen' for the person you are polite to ('beleefd tegen iemand'). The opposite is 'onbeleefd' (impolite/rude).

senses.definition: Having good manners and showing respect for others.

examples.text: De ober was erg beleefd tegen alle gasten.
examples.translation: The waiter was very polite to all the guests.

faults.quote: fire; flames
faults.why: Does not cover sense 1 (a light).

faults.quote: In German, 'Feuer' is used for both a small flame
faults.why: Restates what the senses already show; lacks article usage note for sense 1.

faults.quote: The act or process of lighting something
faults.why: Refers to the means (a lighter or match) to light a cigarette, not the process.

notes: When asking for or offering a light for a cigarette, 'Feuer' is used without an article (e.g., 'Haben Sie Feuer?').
Do not confuse it with 'der Brand', which refers to a destructive fire or a fire fought by emergency services.

senses.definition: Burning flames that give off heat and light.

examples.text: Das Feuer brennt sehr hell im Kamin.
examples.translation: The fire is burning very brightly in the fireplace.

senses.definition: A match or lighter used to light something, especially a cigarette.

examples.text: Haben Sie Feuer?
examples.translation: Do you have a light?

faults.quote: Used with the verb 'haben' (to have fever).
faults.why: Misses the key grammar point: used without an indefinite article ('Fieber haben').

faults.quote: Das ganze Land ist im Fußballfieber.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'Fußballfieber' rather than the standalone lemma 'Fieber'.

notes: Uncountable; used without an indefinite article after 'haben' (e.g., 'Fieber haben' — to have a fever).
Unlike English 'temperature', 'die Temperatur' in German usually refers to weather or general measurements, though 'erhöhte Temperatur' means a slight fever.

senses.definition: A body temperature that is higher than normal because of an illness.

examples.text: Ich habe heute hohes Fieber.
examples.translation: I have a high fever today.

senses.definition: A state of intense nervous excitement or agitation, often in compounds.

examples.text: Vor dem Finale hat die ganze Stadt das Fieber gepackt.
examples.translation: Before the final, the fever gripped the whole city.

faults.quote: Note the difference between 'Fleisch' (meat/flesh) and 'Haut' (skin).
faults.why: Both notes are filler; learners do not confuse meat with skin or longer compounds.

notes: Uncountable and used without a plural. Types of meat are formed as compounds: 'das Rindfleisch' (beef), 'das Schweinefleisch' (pork), 'das Hähnchenfleisch' (chicken).

senses.definition: The flesh of animals when used as food.

examples.text: Ich esse am liebsten rotes Fleisch.
examples.translation: I prefer eating red meat.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of a human or animal body between the skin and bones.

examples.text: Die Wunde ging tief bis ins Fleisch.
examples.translation: The wound went deep into the flesh.

notes: Compound of 'der Flug' (flight) and 'das Zeug' (thing/gear). Plural: 'die Flugzeuge'.
To say 'by plane', use 'mit dem Flugzeug'.

senses.definition: A vehicle with wings and engines that flies through the air.

examples.text: Das Flugzeug fliegt nach Berlin.
examples.translation: The airplane is flying to Berlin.

notes: Plural: 'die Fotos'.
To say 'take a photo of', use 'ein Foto von (+ dative) machen'.

senses.definition: A picture made using a camera.

examples.text: Kannst du ein Foto von uns machen?
examples.translation: Can you take a photo of us?

faults.quote: the base form 묻다 changes to 물어봐요 (polite)
faults.why: 묻다 conjugates to 물어요 (ㄷ-irregular). 물어봐요 is a different verb, 물어보다.

faults.quote: 선생님께 모르는 것을 물어봤어요.
faults.why: Uses 물어봤어요 (from 물어보다) instead of a conjugated form of 묻다.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to get on / stain (clothing)' (옷에 김치가 묻다).

faults.quote: This verb is a homonym. You must use context to know
faults.why: Filler note; should instead explain the ㄷ-irregular vs regular conjugation difference.

corrected.shortGloss: to ask; to bury; to get on (stain)
notes: When meaning 'to ask', it is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel (물어요, 물었어요). In everyday speech, 물어보다 is often used instead.
When meaning 'to bury' or 'to stick/stain', it conjugates regularly (묻어요, 묻었어요).

senses.definition: To ask a question to get information from someone.

examples.text: 모르는 것이 있으면 저에게 물으세요.
examples.translation: If there is something you do not know, please ask me.

senses.definition: To put something into the ground and cover it with earth.

examples.text: 강아지가 뼈를 땅에 묻었어요.
examples.translation: The puppy buried the bone in the ground.

senses.definition: For a liquid, powder, or stain to stick to or get onto a surface.

examples.text: 흰 셔츠에 커피가 묻었어요.
examples.translation: Coffee got on my white shirt.

faults.quote: 그는 내 문자에 대답하지 않았다.
faults.why: For text messages, 답장하다 is natural; 대답하다 is mainly for spoken replies and contradicts note 0.

notes: Takes the particle 에 for the question or person being answered (질문에 대답하다). Mainly used for spoken replies; for letters or text messages, use 답장하다.
Do not confuse with 응답하다, which is more formal and used for official responses, surveys, or signals.

senses.definition: To say something in response to a question or a call.

examples.text: 선생님의 질문에 대답하세요.
examples.translation: Please answer the teacher's question.

examples.text: 불러도 대답이 없어요.
examples.translation: Even when I call out, there is no answer.

faults.quote: Used when someone is startled by a sudden sound, sight, or
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving usage information like the common collocation 깜짝 놀라다.

corrected.shortGloss: to be surprised; to be startled
notes: Often used with the adverb 깜짝 (깜짝 놀라다, to be startled) and takes the particle 에 for the cause of surprise (소리에 놀라다).
Do not confuse with 놀리다 (to tease) or 놀다 (to play/hang out).

senses.definition: To feel sudden shock or surprise because something unexpected happened.

examples.text: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.translation: I was startled because of a sudden loud noise.

examples.text: 그 소식을 듣고 정말 놀랐습니다.
examples.translation: I was really surprised to hear that news.

faults.quote: (fade) To lose color or become faint from exposure to light.
faults.why: 'To fade' is a different verb, 바래다 (past 바랬다), not 바라다.

faults.quote: 햇빛을 오래 받아서 커튼 색이 바랐다.
faults.why: Ungrammatical for 'faded'; the verb for fading is 바래다 (커튼 색이 바랬다).

faults.quote: or the shorter '-길 바래' in casual speech.
faults.why: 바래 is a common misspelling; the standard casual form of 바라다 is 바라.

corrected.shortGloss: to hope; to wish; to want
notes: Often used in the pattern -기를 바라다 ('to hope that...').
Conjugates with -아 as 바라요 / 바라 (not 바래요 / 바래, which is a common colloquial misspelling, or from the verb 바래다 'to fade').

senses.definition: To hope or wish for something to happen.

examples.text: 시험에 합격하기를 바랍니다.
examples.translation: I hope you pass the exam.

examples.text: 좋은 결과가 있기를 바라요.
examples.translation: I hope for a good result.

faults.why: Should note that 짓다 is ㅅ-irregular (짓다 -> 지어요, 지었다) and takes object particle 미소를 짓다.

notes: Formed from 미소 (a smile) + 짓다 (to make), and often used with the object particle as 미소를 짓다. 짓다 is a ㅅ-irregular verb: ㅅ drops before a vowel (미소 지어요, 미소 지었다).
Unlike 웃다 (to laugh or smile), 미소 짓다 specifically refers to a quiet, gentle smile without sound.

senses.definition: To make a gentle, quiet happy expression by curving the corners of your mouth.

examples.text: 그녀는 나를 보고 살짝 미소 지었다.
examples.translation: She looked at me and gave a slight smile.

corrected.headword: นาฬิกาข้อมือ
notes: Combines นาฬิกา (clock or watch) and ข้อมือ (wrist). For a wall or desk clock, use นาฬิกา alone. Its classifier is เรือน.

senses.definition: A small clock worn on a strap around the wrist.

examples.text: ฉันซื้อนาฬิกาข้อมือเรือนใหม่เมื่อวานนี้
examples.translation: I bought a new wristwatch yesterday.
examples.matchedForm: นาฬิกาข้อมือ

faults.quote: ตำรวจกำลังช่วยโบก The car traffic.
faults.why: The Thai example sentence switches into English in the middle.

notes: Used for both the police force as a whole and an individual police officer (classifier: คน, or นาย in formal contexts).

senses.definition: A member of the police force, or the police force as a whole.

examples.text: ตำรวจกำลังช่วยโบกรถอยู่บนถนน
examples.translation: The police officer is helping direct traffic on the road.

faults.quote: แถว (thɛ̌w) is very commonly used in Thai to mean 'around'
faults.why: Merely restates sense 2 instead of adding useful grammatical or usage information.

notes: Commonly used in the phrase เข้าแถว or ต่อแถว (to line up, to queue). Also used as a classifier for rows and lines.

senses.definition: A line of people standing and waiting for their turn.

examples.text: กรุณาต่อแถวเพื่อซื้อตั๋วครับ
examples.translation: Please get in line to buy a ticket.

senses.definition: A straight line of people, seats, or things arranged next to each other.

examples.text: นั่งลงที่แถวแรกได้เลยครับ
examples.translation: You can sit right in the first row.

senses.definition: The area or neighborhood around a particular place.

examples.text: แถวบ้านฉันมีร้านอาหารอร่อยเยอะมาก
examples.translation: There are many delicious restaurants around my house.

corrected.headword: ฤดูใบไม้ร่วง
notes: Literally 'season of falling leaves'. Because Thailand has a tropical climate (hot, rainy, and cool seasons), this word is used for the temperate season in other countries.

senses.definition: The season between summer and winter, when temperatures cool and leaves fall from trees.

examples.text: ฤดูใบไม้ร่วงเป็นช่วงเวลาที่อากาศเริ่มเย็นลง
examples.translation: Autumn is the time when the weather starts to get cooler.
examples.matchedForm: ฤดูใบไม้ร่วง

faults.quote: Used to describe anyone from infancy until adolescence.
faults.why: Restates the definition of 'child' without adding usage value.

faults.quote: เขาเป็นเด็กของหัวหน้าแผนก — He is the department manager's subordinate.
faults.why: Calling someone 'เด็กของ...' means protégé or mistress (slang); standard for subordinate is ลูกน้อง.

notes: Do not confuse with ลูก (lûuk), which means someone's own son or daughter (offspring).

senses.definition: A young human being who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: เด็กคนนี้ฉลาดมาก
examples.translation: This child is very smart.

faults.quote: In some regions of Latin America, 'pájaro' can have slang meanings
faults.why: Vague and misleading warning for Mexican Spanish, where 'pájaro' is completely normal in everyday speech.
