senses.definition: A small animal with feathers and wings that can usually fly.

examples.text: El pájaro canta muy temprano en la mañana.
examples.translation: The bird sings very early in the morning.

faults.quote: The supreme leader of the Catholic Church.

faults.quote: dad; pope

senses.definition: A male parent.

examples.text: Mi papá cocina muy rico los domingos.
examples.translation: My dad cooks very well on Sundays.

senses.definition: In the plural (los papás): a person's mother and father.

examples.text: Mis papás viven en Guadalajara.
examples.translation: My parents live in Guadalajara.

faults.quote: When talking about your job or a task in a group
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and belongs in sense 1's definition rather than a separate note.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'cartón', which refers to cardboard
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'papel' with 'cartón'.

notes: For a single sheet of paper, use 'una hoja (de papel)'; 'el papel' as a material is uncountable.

senses.definition: A thin material used for writing, printing, or wrapping things.

examples.text: Necesito una hoja de papel para escribir una nota.
examples.translation: I need a sheet of paper to write a note.

senses.definition: The part played by an actor in a performance, or a person's function in a situation.

examples.text: Ella interpretó el papel principal en la obra.
examples.translation: She played the lead role in the play.

senses.definition: An official document, especially in the plural ('papeles') for identification or paperwork.

examples.text: Tengo que organizar todos los papeles de la oficina.
examples.translation: I have to organize all the office paperwork.

faults.quote: Note the spelling: the 'd' at the end of 'bloed'
faults.why: Standard Dutch final devoicing, already shown in the IPA.

faults.quote: Refers to a person's descent, lineage, or family background.

notes: Uncountable noun (mass noun); it has no plural form.

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows through the bodies of humans and animals.

examples.text: Hij verloor veel bloed bij het ongeluk.
examples.translation: He lost a lot of blood in the accident.

senses.definition: A person's descent, lineage, or family background.

examples.text: Muziek maken zit bij die familie in het bloed.
examples.translation: Making music is in the blood in that family.

faults.quote: Used for both physical items with bound pages and digital
faults.why: Obvious filler; same as English 'book'.

notes: Plural: 'boeken'. The diminutive 'het boekje' is very common for a small book, booklet, or magazine.

senses.definition: A written work or set of printed pages fastened together inside a cover.

examples.text: Ik lees een spannend boek in de tuin.
examples.translation: I am reading an exciting book in the garden.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'sign' (traffic sign, noticeboard), which is in shortGloss.

faults.quote: Use 'bord' when talking about a dinner plate or a
faults.why: Merely restates the senses and glosses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'table', which is 'tafel'.

notes: Plural: 'borden'.

senses.definition: A flat, usually round dish that you put food on to eat from.

examples.text: Zet het bord maar op de tafel.
examples.translation: Just put the plate on the table.

senses.definition: A large flat surface in a classroom for writing on, or a flat board for playing games.

examples.text: De docent schrijft de som op het bord.
examples.translation: The teacher writes the sum on the board.

senses.definition: A flat piece of metal, wood, or plastic in a public place that gives information, directions, or a warning.

examples.text: Heb je dat bord langs de weg gezien?
examples.translation: Did you see that sign by the road?

senses.definition: A large area of land covered with trees and undergrowth.

examples.text: We maken een lange wandeling door het bos.
examples.translation: We are taking a long walk through the forest.

senses.definition: A collection of things held or tied together, such as flowers or keys.

examples.text: Ik kreeg een mooie bos bloemen voor mijn verjaardag.
examples.translation: I got a nice bouquet of flowers for my birthday.

senses.definition: A baked food made from flour, water, and usually yeast; or a single whole loaf of it.

examples.text: Ik koop elke ochtend vers brood bij de bakker.
examples.translation: I buy fresh bread at the bakery every morning.

examples.translation: That friend is still immature in his thinking.

examples.translation: The weather is bad, so I am not going to the mountain today.

senses.definition: Morally wrong or unpleasant in character or behavior.

examples.text: 그 사람은 성격이 나빠서 친구가 없어요.
examples.translation: That person has a bad personality, so they have no friends.

examples.text: 이 의자는 아주 단단해요.

senses.definition: Of a person's resolve or preparation: firm and unwavering.

examples.text: 그녀는 단단한 결심을 하고 공부를 시작했다.
examples.translation: She made a firm resolution and started studying.

faults.quote: In a restaurant, use 'die Rechnung' when asking to pay.

senses.definition: A document showing the amount of money you need to pay for a meal, goods, or a service.

examples.text: Die Rechnung, bitte.
examples.translation: The bill, please.

senses.definition: The process or result of calculating numbers.

examples.text: Diese Rechnung ist sehr einfach.
examples.translation: This calculation is very simple.

faults.quote: (travel) The general experience or process of traveling.

examples.text: Im Zoo habe ich eine giftige Schlange gesehen.
examples.translation: At the zoo, I saw a venomous snake.

senses.definition: A line of people or vehicles waiting their turn.

examples.text: Vor dem Kino gab es eine lange Schlange.
examples.translation: There was a long line in front of the cinema.

faults.why: Missing the everyday café sense 'hot chocolate' ('eine heiße Schokolade').

senses.definition: A sweet food made from cocoa beans, eaten as candy or used in cooking.

senses.definition: A sweet drink made with chocolate or cocoa and milk.

examples.text: Ich trinke gern eine heiße Schokolade.

faults.quote: often used without an article when referring to the institution itself (e.g., 'Ich gehe zur Schule')

examples.translation: She is the head of the department.

examples.text: Hoe laat ga je vanavond naar huis?
examples.translation: What time are you going home tonight?

faults.why: Missing required hiragana reading (いえ / うち) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: While 'ie' is the standard word for a physical house or building
faults.why: Restates the two senses; further, 家 itself can be read both いえ and うち.

notes: Read いえ for a physical house or a family lineage, and often うち when talking about one's own home or household (帰るうち, うちの猫).

senses.definition: A building where people live, or the place where one lives.

examples.text: 駅の近くに新しい家を買いました。
examples.translation: I bought a new house near the station.

senses.definition: A family or household, especially across generations.

examples.text: 彼は古い家の出身です。
examples.translation: He comes from an old family.

faults.quote: While 'arashi' specifically refers to a violent storm with heavy wind
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: storm; tempest
faults.why: Does not cover the figurative sense of uproar or commotion.

senses.definition: Violent weather with very strong wind and heavy rain.

examples.text: 嵐が近づいている。
examples.translation: A storm is approaching.

senses.definition: A sudden outburst of intense activity, emotion, or criticism.

examples.text: 会場は拍手の嵐に包まれた。
examples.translation: The hall erupted in a storm of applause.

faults.quote: Often used with particles like に (ni) for 'in the morning'
faults.why: As a relative time noun, 朝 is normally used adverbially without に.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the early part of the day
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

faults.quote: 今朝は寒いです。
faults.why: Uses the separate lexicalized word 今朝 (けさ) rather than 朝 (あさ).

notes: Like other time words (昼 'daytime', 夜 'night'), 朝 is usually used directly without the particle に to mean 'in the morning' (朝起きる 'wake up in the morning').

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until around noon.

examples.text: 朝はコーヒーを飲みます。
examples.translation: I drink coffee in the morning.

notes: Covers both email and phone text messages (SMS). Takes する to mean 'to email' or 'to text'.

senses.definition: A message sent electronically by computer or mobile phone.

examples.text: 重要なメールを送りました。
examples.translation: I sent an important email.

examples.text: 後でメールを返します。
examples.translation: I will reply to the message later.

faults.quote: While '病気' (byōki) generally refers to an illness or disease
faults.why: Restates the glosses and example[1] instead of giving useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Use '病気になる' (byōki ni naru) to mean 'to get sick' and '病気だ' (byōki da) to mean 'to be sick'.
Usually refers to serious or ongoing conditions; for minor issues like a cold (風邪) or headache, Japanese speakers name the specific symptom.

senses.definition: A condition of the body or mind that causes poor health.

examples.text: 病気で学校を休んだ。
examples.translation: I stayed home from school due to illness.

examples.text: 母は病気だ。
examples.translation: My mother is ill.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (じてんしゃ) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: While 'bike' is very common in casual English, in Japanese 'jitensha'
faults.why: Filler note; misses the critical false friend 'バイク' (baiku = motorcycle) and verb usage.

notes: Use with the verb '乗る' (noru): '自転車に乗る' (to ride a bicycle). Beware that the loanword 'バイク' (baiku) usually means 'motorcycle', not bicycle.
In casual spoken slang, people often call it 'チャリ' (chari).

senses.definition: A vehicle with two wheels, pedals, and handlebars, moved by the rider's legs.

examples.text: 自転車で学校へ行きます。
examples.translation: I go to school by bicycle.

faults.quote: A unit or item in a sequence or a space in a grid.
faults.why: Conflates ordinal suffix '-me' with marginal noun 'mesh'; misses common sense 'eyesight/vision'.

faults.quote: The word 'me' is primarily the anatomical organ. It is also used
faults.why: Merely restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage guidance.

notes: Appears in many common expressions, such as '目がいい／悪い' (to have good/bad eyesight) and 'ひどい目に遭う' (to have a terrible experience).
Added directly after a counter or number as a suffix (-目), it forms ordinal numbers: '二人目' (the second person), '三日目' (the third day).

senses.definition: The organ of sight in humans and animals, or the ability to see.

examples.text: 目が疲れた。
examples.translation: My eyes are tired.

examples.text: 私は目が悪いです。
examples.translation: I have bad eyesight.

senses.definition: Something that one undergoes, especially something unpleasant.

examples.text: 昨日はひどい目に遭った。
examples.translation: I had a terrible experience yesterday.

faults.quote: line of people; procession; matrix
faults.why: Includes 'matrix', which is absent from the senses and unnecessary at A2.

faults.quote: While '行列' can refer to a formal procession or a mathematical matrix
faults.why: Restates the senses and mentions a technical mathematical meaning irrelevant to beginners.

notes: Commonly used in '行列ができる' (a line forms) and '行列に並ぶ' (to stand in a line). Unlike '列' (retsu), which can be any row or line of things, '行列' specifically refers to a long line of people.

senses.definition: A line of people waiting to buy something or enter a place.

examples.text: 人気のラーメン屋には長い行列ができていた。
examples.translation: There was a long line at the popular ramen shop.

senses.definition: A group of people moving in a line for a ceremony, parade, or funeral.

examples.text: 祭りの行列が通りをゆっくりと進んでいく。
examples.translation: The festival procession moves slowly down the street.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (かいぎ) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: Used for formal discussions where people gather to deliberate or decide
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim instead of providing useful collocations or grammar.

notes: Can be used with 'する' (会議する, to hold a meeting). Other common collocations include '会議を開く' (to hold a meeting) and '会議に出る' (to attend a meeting).
Unlike '打ち合わせ' (uchiawase), which is a smaller, informal check-in or planning session, '会議' refers to a more official or structured gathering.

senses.definition: A formal gathering where people discuss work, exchange ideas, or make decisions.

examples.text: 明日の午後、会議があります。
examples.translation: There is a meeting tomorrow afternoon.

examples.text: 会議が長引いています。
examples.translation: The meeting is dragging on.

faults.quote: While '游客' specifically refers to someone traveling for pleasure or sightseeing, '来访者'
faults.why: Contrasts with formal '来访者' instead of everyday '客人' (guest/visitor); notes[1] also restates definition.

notes: Refers to tourists or visitors at sightseeing spots and public attractions; for someone visiting a home or person, use 客人 (kèrén).

senses.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure or sightseeing, especially on holiday.

examples.text: 故宫里有很多游客。
examples.translation: There are many tourists in the Forbidden City.

examples.text: 我们需要给游客提供更好的服务。
examples.translation: We need to provide better service to the tourists.

faults.quote: It is a round, deep dish used primarily for serving liquids
faults.why: Restates the definition word-for-word instead of giving useful grammar (like its classifier).

notes: Takes the measure word 个 (gè) or 只 (zhī) for the object itself, and is also used directly as a measure word for a bowlful of food (e.g., 两碗米饭, 'two bowls of rice').

senses.definition: A round, deep dish used for holding food, especially soup or rice.

examples.text: 桌子上有一个碗。
examples.translation: There is a bowl on the table.

faults.quote: 我在看电视。
faults.why: 'Watching television' illustrates the broadcast medium (sense 1), not the physical appliance (sense 0).

faults.quote: While 电视 can refer to the television set itself, it is also
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: When referring to the physical appliance, use the measure word 台 (tái): 一台电视 (yī tái diànshì); 电视机 (diànshìjī) also specifically means 'TV set'.

senses.definition: An electronic device with a screen used for watching broadcast programs.

examples.text: 我们买了一台新电视。
examples.translation: We bought a new TV set.

senses.definition: Broadcast content or programs viewed on a television screen.

examples.text: 我在看电视。
examples.translation: I am watching television.

faults.quote: '表兄弟姐妹' refers to cousins who are the children of your father's sisters
faults.why: Restates the definition word-for-word; notes[2] also wrongly says it includes siblings.

notes: Used as a collective term; for an individual cousin, use specific terms by gender and relative age: 表哥 (older male), 表弟 (younger male), 表姐 (older female), or 表妹 (younger female).
Cousins who are the children of your father's brothers are called 堂兄弟姐妹 (tángxiōngdìjiěmèi) instead.

senses.definition: Cousins who are the children of one's mother's siblings or father's sisters.

examples.text: 春节的时候，我和表兄弟姐妹一起玩。
examples.translation: During the Spring Festival, I hang out with my cousins.

faults.quote: As a noun, 鱼 refers to both the living animal in water
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses instead of giving the needed measure word 条 (tiáo).

faults.quote: fish, seafood
faults.why: '鱼' specifically means fish meat, not 'seafood' in general (which is 海鲜).

notes: Takes the measure word 条 (tiáo) for whole fish: 一条鱼 (yī tiáo yú).

senses.definition: An animal that lives and swims in water, breathes with gills, and has fins.

examples.text: 水里有一条红色的鱼。
examples.translation: There is a red fish in the water.

senses.definition: The flesh of fish used as food.

examples.text: 晚饭我们吃清蒸鱼。
examples.translation: We are having steamed fish for dinner.

faults.quote: Note the liaison after the article: 'les éléphants' is pronounced
faults.why: Standard liaison rule applying to all vowel-initial nouns, not specific to this word.

notes: The 'ph' is pronounced like an English 'f', and the final 't' is silent.

senses.definition: A very large grey mammal with a long trunk and large ears, native to Africa and Asia.

examples.text: L'éléphant mange des feuilles avec sa trompe.
examples.translation: The elephant eats leaves with its trunk.

faults.quote: /l‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃/
faults.why: IPA must be a transcription of the lemma without the article.

faults.quote: L'enfant is grammatically masculine (un enfant) even when referring to a girl
faults.why: False: 'enfant' can be both masculine ('un enfant') and feminine ('une enfant').

faults.quote: Do not confuse with le bébé, which specifically means an infant
faults.why: Unnecessary distinction; 'bébé' is an obvious cognate.

notes: Can be masculine ('un enfant') or feminine ('une enfant') depending on the child's sex, though the masculine is used generically and in the plural.

senses.definition: A young person, not yet grown up.

examples.text: L'enfant joue dans le parc avec son ballon.
examples.translation: The child is playing in the park with his ball.

senses.definition: A son or daughter of any age in relation to their parents.

examples.text: Ils ont trois enfants qui habitent à Paris.
examples.translation: They have three children who live in Paris.

faults.quote: While 'entreprise' most commonly refers to a commercial company or business
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: For a small shop or local business, 'le commerce' is used instead; 'société' is a common synonym for a registered company.

senses.definition: A business organization that sells goods or services.

examples.text: Il travaille pour une grande entreprise de technologie.
examples.translation: He works for a large technology company.

senses.definition: An ambitious project or undertaking.

examples.text: Cette rénovation est une entreprise difficile.
examples.translation: This renovation is a difficult undertaking.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'attente', which means waiting.
faults.why: 'Entretien' and 'attente' do not look or sound similar enough to confuse.

notes: Often used as short for 'entretien d'embauche' (job interview). Do not confuse with 'interview', which is used for media and journalism.

senses.definition: A formal meeting where someone is asked questions to see if they are suitable for a job.

examples.text: J'ai un entretien pour un nouveau poste demain matin.
examples.translation: I have an interview for a new position tomorrow morning.

senses.definition: The action of keeping something in good condition by checking or repairing it regularly.

examples.text: La voiture nécessite un entretien régulier.
examples.translation: The car requires regular maintenance.

faults.quote: Use 'erreur' for mistakes in work, calculations, or judgment.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or contrast information.

notes: Often used in the phrase 'par erreur' (by mistake).
Do not confuse with 'faute', which is used for spelling or grammar mistakes ('une faute d'orthographe') and moral or rule-breaking faults.

senses.definition: Something done wrong; an incorrect action, belief, or calculation.

examples.text: Il y a une erreur dans ce rapport.
examples.translation: There is a mistake in this report.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'kız kardeş' (sister)
faults.why: Etymological trivia in note 0 created an artificial confusion no beginner has.

notes: Used for both male and female nurses.

senses.definition: A person trained to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital or clinic.

examples.text: Hemşire hastanın tansiyonunu ölçüyor.
examples.translation: The nurse is taking the patient's blood pressure.

notes: Literally 'every time' ('her' + 'zaman'). A very common, slightly shorter synonym is 'hep'.
Do not confuse it with 'her gün' (every day).

senses.definition: At all times or on every occasion.

examples.text: O, her zaman kahvaltıda çay içer.
examples.translation: She always drinks tea at breakfast.

faults.quote: Hesap is used both for the restaurant bill and for bank or
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses the crucial consonant voicing rule (hesap -> hesabı).

faults.quote: An arrangement with a bank to keep your money safe.
faults.why: Too narrow; 'hesap' is equally used for user accounts on websites and social media.

notes: The final 'p' changes to 'b' when a vowel suffix is added: 'hesabı' (the bill), 'hesabım' (my account).
To ask for the bill at a restaurant, you can say 'Hesap, lütfen!'.

senses.definition: A statement of how much you must pay for food and drinks at a restaurant or cafe.

examples.text: Garson, hesabı getirir misiniz?
examples.translation: Waiter, could you bring the bill?

senses.definition: An arrangement with a bank to hold your money, or a personal profile on a website or app.

examples.text: Bankada yeni bir hesap açtım.
examples.translation: I opened a new account at the bank.

senses.definition: The act or result of working out an amount using numbers.

examples.text: Bu işte bir yanlış hesap var.
examples.translation: There is a miscalculation in this matter.

faults.quote: Feeling very happy, eager, and impatient about something good that is about
faults.why: In Turkish, 'heyecanlı' also commonly means nervous or anxious before an exam or speech.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with mutlu, which simply means happy
faults.why: Unnecessary comparison; should instead note that 'heyecanlı' also covers stage fright or nervousness.

notes: Covers both English 'excited' (about how you feel) and 'exciting' (about a movie, match, or event).
When describing a person, it also commonly means 'nervous' or 'anxious' (for example, before an exam or interview).

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling strong anticipation, eagerness, or nervousness about something that is happening or about to happen.

examples.text: Yarın tatile gideceğimiz için çok heyecanlıyım.
examples.translation: I am very excited because we are going on vacation tomorrow.

senses.definition: Of an event or thing: causing strong feelings of interest, enthusiasm, or suspense.

examples.text: Maçın son dakikaları çok heyecanlıydı.
examples.translation: The last minutes of the match were very exciting.

notes: Always requires a negative verb in Turkish (e.g. 'Hiçbir zaman gitmedim' — literally 'I never didn't go').
More emphatic than 'hiç' alone; 'asla' is a strong synonym.

senses.definition: At no time in the past or future; on no occasion.

examples.text: Hiçbir zaman bu kadar lezzetli bir yemek yemedim.
examples.translation: I have never eaten such a delicious meal.

faults.quote: Used for travel, events, and admission to places.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

faults.quote: Can also be spelled 'karcis'
faults.why: 'karcis' is a synonym (from Dutch), not an alternate spelling of 'tiket'.

notes: A common synonym is 'karcis', which is especially used for short-distance transport, parking, or small admission booths.

senses.definition: A printed or digital pass that gives you the right to travel on a vehicle or enter an event or place.

examples.text: Saya membeli tiket kereta api ke Bandung.
examples.translation: I bought a train ticket to Bandung.

faults.quote: (turn) The act or point of turning toward a different direction.
faults.why: 'Tikungan' means a bend in the road, not the act of turning or turning point.

notes: Formed from 'tikung' + '-an'. It refers to the physical bend in a road, whereas a junction or turn-off is 'belokan'.

senses.definition: A bend or curve in a road, path, or river.

examples.text: Kurangi kecepatan saat melewati tikungan tajam.
examples.translation: Reduce speed when passing a sharp curve.

examples.text: Rumahnya terletak tepat setelah tikungan pertama.
examples.translation: His house is located right after the first bend.

faults.quote: you can say tikus gotong for a large rat
faults.why: A sewer rat is 'tikus got' (from 'got' = gutter), not 'tikus gotong'.

faults.quote: Baterai tikus komputer ini sudah habis.
faults.why: In everyday Indonesian, speakers use the English word 'mouse' or formal 'tetikus', rarely 'tikus'.

notes: 'Tikus' covers both rats and mice. To be specific, people say 'tikus got' (sewer rat) for a large rat, or 'tikus kecil' (or the scientific term 'mencit') for a small mouse.

senses.definition: A small grey or brown rodent with a long tail.

examples.text: Seekor tikus berlari melintasi lantai dapur.
examples.translation: A rat ran across the kitchen floor.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'all that is needed / just have to' (e.g. tinggal makan).

corrected.shortGloss: to live; to stay; to be left; only have to
notes: When meaning 'to live' or 'to stay', it is followed by the preposition 'di' (e.g., 'tinggal di Jakarta').

senses.definition: To have your home in a place, or to stay somewhere temporarily.

examples.text: Saya tinggal di Bandung.
examples.translation: I live in Bandung.

senses.definition: To continue to be in a place or condition after others have gone or been used.

examples.text: Uang saya tinggal sedikit.
examples.translation: I have very little money left.

senses.definition: Used before a verb to mean that only one simple action remains to be done.

examples.text: Makanannya sudah siap, kamu tinggal makan.
examples.translation: The food is ready, you just have to eat.

faults.quote: (height) (of a person) of more than average height
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are both physical height; splitting 'tall' and 'high' is an English distinction.

faults.quote: whereas for objects or places it usually means high.
faults.why: For buildings, trees, and towers, 'tinggi' translates to 'tall' just as naturally as 'high'.

notes: Covers both English 'tall' (for people, trees, buildings) and 'high' (for mountains, walls, prices, temperatures). For long horizontal things, use 'panjang'.

senses.definition: Of great vertical extent from bottom to top, or of more than average height.

examples.text: Adik saya sangat tinggi sekarang.
examples.translation: My younger sibling is very tall now.

examples.text: Gedung itu sangat tinggi.
examples.translation: That building is very tall.

senses.definition: Greater than normal in degree, amount, level, or cost.

examples.text: Harga makanan di sini cukup tinggi.
examples.translation: The price of food here is quite high.

faults.quote: (town) A large town.
faults.why: In Turkish, 'şehir' does not have a separate sense for 'town'; merge into one sense.

notes: The 'i' drops before a vowel suffix: 'şehre' (to the city), 'şehrim' (my city).
'Kent' is a common synonym. For a smaller town, 'kasaba' or 'ilçe' is used.

senses.definition: A large and permanent human settlement; a city or large town.

examples.text: İstanbul büyük ve kalabalık bir şehirdir.
examples.translation: Istanbul is a big and crowded city.

examples.text: Yaz aylarında bu sakin şehre çok turist geliyor.
examples.translation: Many tourists come to this quiet city during the summer months.

faults.quote: Ne kadar şeker bir bebek!
faults.why: Uses 'şeker' as an adjective ('sweet/cute'), whereas the entry and sense are for a noun.

faults.quote: Besides meaning actual sugar and candy, 'şeker' is a very common term
faults.why: merely restates the three senses already listed in the entry.

notes: Most often heard in the possessive form 'şekerim' (my sweet, darling) as a friendly form of address.
Can also be used as an adjective meaning 'sweet' or 'cute' (e.g., 'çok şeker bir bebek').

senses.definition: A sweet white or brown substance used to sweeten food and drinks.

examples.text: Çaya iki şeker attım.
examples.translation: I put two lumps of sugar in the tea.

senses.definition: A small sweet food made mainly of sugar.

examples.text: Çocuklar bayramda şeker toplar.
examples.translation: Children collect candy during the holiday.

senses.definition: An affectionate word used to address someone you like or love.

examples.text: Nasılsın şekerim, her şey yolunda mı?
examples.translation: How are you, darling, is everything alright?

faults.quote: Yağmur başladığı için şemsiye mi açtı.
faults.why: Ungrammatical: 'şemsiye mi' is a question particle; 'his umbrella' in accusative is 'şemsiyesini'.

faults.quote: While it is carried like an accessory, şemsiye belongs to weather protection
faults.why: Trivial semantic categorization of no practical use to a language learner.

faults.quote: /ʃæm.siˈje/
faults.why: Standard Turkish IPA uses /e/ here: /ʃemsiˈje/.

notes: Takes the buffer consonant 'y' or 'n' when suffixes beginning with a vowel are added (e.g., 'şemsiyeyi' - the umbrella, 'şemsiyesini' - his/her umbrella).

senses.definition: A folding object that you hold over your head to protect yourself from rain or sun.

examples.text: Yağmur başladığı için şemsiyesini açtı.
examples.translation: He opened his umbrella because it started to rain.

faults.quote: Used both for physical objects that resist pressure and for abstract concepts
faults.why: Merely summarizes the senses already present in the entry.

notes: The opposite is 'yumuşak' (soft, gentle). For strong drinks like coffee or tea, 'sert' means strong in flavor or effect, though for tea 'koyu' (dark/strong) is also common.

senses.definition: Of an object or surface: firm and solid; not easy to press, bend, or cut.

examples.text: Bu yatak çok sert, uyuyamadım.
examples.translation: This bed is very hard, I couldn't sleep.

senses.definition: Of a person, rule, or behavior: demanding obedience; not gentle or forgiving.

examples.text: Müdürümüz bugün çok sertti.
examples.translation: Our manager was very strict today.

senses.definition: Of weather, wind, or a drink: intense or strong in force or flavor.

examples.text: Dışarıda çok sert bir rüzgâr var.
examples.translation: There is a very strong wind outside.

faults.quote: /seˈsiz/
faults.why: Missing the geminate /s/ across the morpheme boundary; pronounced /sesˈsiz/.

faults.quote: Kütüphanede herkes çok sessiz çalışıyor.
faults.why: Uses 'sessiz' adverbially ('quietly') instead of as an adjective.

notes: Formed from 'ses' (sound, voice) + '-siz' (without). Both 's' sounds are pronounced clearly (/sesˈsiz/).

senses.definition: Of a person or thing: making little or no sound; not talking much.

examples.text: Bugün neden bu kadar sessizsin?
examples.translation: Why are you so quiet today?

senses.definition: Of a place or time: free from noise or disturbance; peaceful.

examples.text: Bu mahalle geceleri çok sessiz.
examples.translation: This neighborhood is very quiet at night.

faults.quote: 강물이 아주 맑아요.
faults.why: Uses the compound noun 강물 (river water) instead of the headword 강 (river).

notes: 강 is used for large rivers, while 천 or 내 is used for smaller streams or creeks.

senses.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing to the sea or a lake.

examples.text: 이 강은 아주 깊고 넓어요.
examples.translation: This river is very deep and wide.

faults.quote: 정원 has two completely different meanings depending on the context
faults.why: merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: Do not confuse 정원 (a landscaped garden with plants and flowers) with 마당 (the open yard or courtyard of a house).

senses.definition: A piece of ground next to a house, used for growing flowers, grass, or trees.

examples.text: 할아버지께서 예쁜 꽃을 정원에 심으셨어요.
examples.translation: Grandfather planted pretty flowers in the garden.

senses.definition: The maximum number of people officially allowed in a group, vehicle, or building.

examples.text: 이 버스의 정원은 쉰 명입니다.
examples.translation: The capacity of this bus is fifty people.

faults.quote: (describing) Being unusual, special, or different from the normal.
faults.why: Sense 1 is the determiner/prefix 별 (別), a different part of speech from the noun 별.

faults.quote: 오늘은 별일 없어요.
faults.why: Uses the lexicalized compound noun 별일 instead of the headword.

senses.definition: A bright point of light that you see in the night sky, or a shape with five or more points representing it.

examples.text: 밤하늘에 별이 많이 보여요.
examples.translation: I see many stars in the night sky.

faults.quote: /bakaˈsjones/
faults.why: Gives Latin American seseo /s/ instead of Castilian Spanish /θ/ (/bakaˈθjones/).

notes: Always used in the plural in Spanish when referring to time off work or school (e.g. 'estar de vacaciones', 'irse de vacaciones').

senses.definition: To become higher in price, temperature, or level.

examples.text: El precio de la gasolina va a subir mañana.
examples.translation: The price of gasoline is going to go up tomorrow.

senses.definition: To transfer files or photos to the internet.

examples.text: Voy a subir las fotos de las vacaciones a internet.
examples.translation: I am going to upload the vacation photos to the internet.

faults.quote: /ˈsuθjo/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican Spanish /s/ (/ˈsusjo/).

faults.quote: Use 'sucio' for anything that is not clean, from clothes to rooms.
faults.why: Filler note that merely restates the definition; misses the 'ser' vs. 'estar' distinction.

faults.quote: In Mexico, the verb 'ensuciar' is used
faults.why: Implies 'ensuciar' is specific to Mexico when it is standard across all Spanish.

notes: Used with 'estar' for things that need cleaning (El plato está sucio) and with 'ser' for someone with messy habits or for something dishonest (Es un negocio sucio).

senses.definition: Not clean; covered in dirt or needing to be washed.

examples.text: Mis zapatos están muy sucios después de caminar por el campo.
examples.translation: My shoes are very dirty after walking through the countryside.

senses.definition: Unfair or dishonest in behavior or competition.

examples.text: Jugaron sucio para ganar el partido.
examples.translation: They played dirty to win the game.

faults.why: Should mention verb mood after 'tal vez' (subjunctive vs. indicative), which is reflected in the example.

notes: Interchangeable with 'quizá' or 'quizás'. Always written as two words.
When placed before the verb, it is often followed by the subjunctive (Tal vez venga mañana), or by the indicative when the speaker feels more certain.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible but not certain.

examples.text: Tal vez llueva más tarde.
examples.translation: Maybe it will rain later.

faults.quote: (time) During the part of the day between noon and evening.
faults.why: 'Tarde' meaning 'afternoon' is a feminine noun ('la tarde'), not an adverb.

faults.quote: As an adverb, 'tarde' can describe both a time of day
faults.why: False grammar claim; 'tarde' only refers to the afternoon as a noun, contradicting note 1.

notes: Used with 'ser' to say it is late in the day (Ya es muy tarde — It's very late). Do not confuse with the feminine noun 'la tarde' (the afternoon).

senses.definition: After the expected, usual, or proper time, or near the end of the day.

examples.text: Llegué tarde a la reunión porque había mucho tráfico.
examples.translation: I arrived late to the meeting because there was a lot of traffic.

examples.text: Ayer me dormí muy tarde.
examples.translation: I went to sleep very late yesterday.

faults.quote: rude; crude; gross
faults.why: Includes 'gross', a false friend the note explicitly warns against using.

notes: False friend: 'grosero' does not mean 'gross' in the sense of disgusting (like spoiled food or a messy room); for that, use 'asqueroso'.

senses.definition: Lacking manners or acting without respect toward others.

examples.text: Fue muy grosero no saludar al entrar a la sala.
examples.translation: It was very rude not to greet anyone when entering the room.

senses.definition: Using or involving language or actions that are vulgar or offensive.

examples.text: Él siempre cuenta chistes groseros en las fiestas.
examples.translation: He always tells crude jokes at parties.

faults.quote: To find something pleasant or enjoyable.
faults.why: Defines the verb with the experiencer as subject, contradicting its grammatical structure.

notes: In Spanish, the grammar of 'gustar' is reversed compared to English: the thing liked is the subject, and the person who likes it is the indirect object (me, te, le, nos, les).
Say 'Me gusta el café' (literally 'Coffee is pleasing to me'), never 'Yo gusto el café'. For plural things, use 'gustan' (e.g., 'Me gustan los libros').

senses.definition: To be pleasing or enjoyable to someone (translated as 'to like').

examples.text: Me gusta mucho leer por la noche.
examples.translation: I really like to read at night.

examples.text: A mi hermano le gustan los deportes.
examples.translation: My brother likes sports.

faults.quote: Hablar is the most general verb for both speaking and talking.
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and senses without adding usage information.

notes: Do not confuse with 'decir' (to say/tell). Use 'hablar' for speaking a language or conversing (often with 'con' for the person and 'de' or 'sobre' for the topic), and 'decir' for the specific words or information said.

senses.definition: To know and be able to use a language, or to utter words aloud.

examples.text: Ella habla español muy bien.
examples.translation: She speaks Spanish very well.

senses.definition: To have a conversation with someone.

examples.text: Tengo que hablar con mi jefe mañana.
examples.translation: I have to talk with my boss tomorrow.

faults.quote: This is the most common way to say hello in all
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss.

notes: The 'h' is always silent in Spanish; pronounce it just like 'ola'.

senses.definition: Used as a greeting when meeting someone or answering the phone.

examples.text: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás?
examples.translation: Hello! How are you?

faults.quote: 石头 (shítou) is the most common, everyday word for a stone
faults.why: Restates the gloss; should mention the classifier 块 (kuài) instead.

notes: Counted with the measure word 块 (kuài): 一块石头 (a stone).
石头 is the everyday word; 石 (shí) alone appears mostly in compound words or formal writing, and 岩石 (yánshí) refers to geological rock formations.

senses.definition: A hard piece of rock found on the ground.

examples.text: 路边有很多石头。
examples.translation: There are many stones by the side of the road.

senses.definition: The hard mineral substance that rocks are made of, used as a building material.

examples.text: 这个房子是用石头盖的。
examples.translation: This house is built of stone.

faults.why: Missing the essential measure words that distinguish the two senses (节/堂 vs. 门).

notes: Commonly used in the verb-object phrases 上课 (shàngkè, to attend or teach class) and 下课 (xiàkè, to finish class).
Use the measure word 节 (jié) or 堂 (táng) for an individual class period (一节课), and 门 (mén) for a course or subject (一门课).

senses.definition: A period of time in which students are taught, or a unit of instruction in a textbook.

examples.text: 我要去上课。
examples.translation: I am going to class.

examples.text: 今天我们学习第一课。
examples.translation: Today we are studying Lesson One.

senses.definition: A specific subject or course studied at school.

examples.text: 我最喜欢的课是数学。
examples.translation: My favorite subject is math.

faults.why: A2 learners need the specific measure word for horses: 匹 (pǐ).

notes: The measure word for horses is 匹 (pǐ): 一匹马 (a horse).

senses.definition: A large four-legged animal that people ride or use for carrying and pulling things.

examples.text: 他在草原上骑马。
examples.translation: He is riding a horse on the grassland.

faults.quote: Used to refer to any living organism that is not a plant
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler defining English concepts; should state the measure word 只 (zhī).

notes: Individual animals are usually counted with 只 (zhī): 一只小动物 (a small animal); types of animals use 种 (zhǒng).

senses.definition: A living creature such as a dog, bird, or fish, that is not a plant or a human.

examples.text: 大熊猫是一种很有名的动物。
examples.translation: The giant panda is a very famous animal.

examples.text: 我们应该爱护小动物。
examples.translation: We should care for small animals.

faults.quote: If you are talking about a bag, use 包 (bāo);
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'box' with 'bag' or 'basket'; should contrast with 箱子 (xiāngzi) instead.

faults.quote: box; container
faults.why: 'Container' is too broad and is not in the sense glosses.

notes: 盒子 is for small boxes or cases; for large boxes, crates, or chests (such as moving boxes or suitcases), use 箱子 (xiāngzi).

senses.definition: A small container with flat sides and usually a lid, made of cardboard, plastic, wood, or metal.

examples.text: 把礼物放进这个盒子里。
examples.translation: Put the gift into this box.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with briefkaart, which specifically means postcard.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; 'kaartje' is also commonly used for postcards.

notes: Diminutive of 'kaart' (map, card), lexicalized with the everyday meaning of 'ticket' or 'greeting card'.

senses.definition: A printed or digital pass that lets you travel on public transport or enter an event.

examples.text: Ik koop een kaartje voor de trein naar Amsterdam.
examples.translation: I am buying a ticket for the train to Amsterdam.

senses.definition: A small piece of thick paper for writing a greeting or short message, or a small label.

examples.text: We sturen een leuk kaartje voor zijn verjaardag.
examples.translation: We are sending a nice card for his birthday.

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'kantoor' refers both to the physical space
faults.why: Restates the two senses; better to note the idiomatic 'op kantoor' without article.

faults.quote: Zij werkt bij een advocatenkantoor.
faults.why: Uses compound 'advocatenkantoor' instead of the headword 'kantoor'.

notes: Note the fixed phrase 'op kantoor' (at the office), used without an article. Plural: 'kantoren'.

senses.definition: A room or building where people work at desks.

examples.text: Ik werk vandaag op kantoor.
examples.translation: I am working at the office today.

examples.text: Zijn kantoor is op de derde verdieping.
examples.translation: His office is on the third floor.

senses.definition: A business or agency that provides professional or administrative services.

examples.text: Zij werkt bij een groot juridisch kantoor.
examples.translation: She works at a large legal firm.

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'kind' refers to any young person before they reach adulthood
faults.why: Restates sense 0 and actually contradicts sense 1.

notes: The plural is irregular: 'kinderen' (pronounced /ˈkɪndərə(n)/).

senses.definition: A young person who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: Dat kleine kind speelt in de tuin.
examples.translation: That small child is playing in the garden.

senses.definition: A son or daughter of any age in relation to their parents.

examples.text: Zij heeft drie volwassen kinderen.
examples.translation: She has three adult children.

faults.quote: Takes the neuter article 'het'.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

senses.definition: A small mammal with long ears, soft fur, and a short tail that hops.

examples.text: Het konijn hopt door het groene gras.
examples.translation: The rabbit hops through the green grass.

faults.quote: De baby heeft een klein kopje.
faults.why: The anatomical diminutive of 'kop' is usually 'koppie'; for a baby, 'hoofdje' is normal.

notes: Diminutive of 'kop' (cup, mug, animal head). In everyday speech, 'kopje' is the default word for a standard teacup or coffee cup.

senses.definition: A small container with a handle, used for hot drinks, or the amount it holds.

examples.text: Wil je een kopje koffie?
examples.translation: Do you want a cup of coffee?

faults.quote: When you want to specifically refer to the sandy strip... 바닷가
faults.why: Reverses the distinction: 바닷가 is the general native word for seaside; 해변 means beach/seashore.

notes: A Sino-Korean word for the beach or seashore; in everyday conversation, the native word 바닷가 (seaside) is also very common.

senses.definition: The land along the edge of the sea, especially a sandy or pebbly area.

examples.text: 해변을 따라 산책하는 것은 정말 즐거워요.
examples.translation: Walking along the beach is really enjoyable.

faults.quote: A demonstrative pronoun used to refer to something close to the speaker.
faults.why: '이' meaning 'this' is primarily a determiner (관형사) before a noun, not this noun entry.

faults.quote: '이' is a perfect example of a homonym in Korean.
faults.why: Filler restating the senses.

notes: For 'tooth', 이 (or native spoken 이빨) is everyday; 치아 is the formal or medical term. In compounds it often becomes -니, as in 앞니 (front tooth) and 어금니 (molar).
Do not confuse with the determiner 이 ('this', placed before a noun, as in 이 책 'this book') or the subject particle 이.

senses.definition: One of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting and chewing.

examples.text: 음식을 먹은 후에는 이를 잘 닦아야 합니다.
examples.translation: You must brush your teeth well after eating.

senses.definition: The Sino-Korean word for the number two.

examples.text: 일 더하기 이는 삼이에요.
examples.translation: One plus two is three.

notes: Often used in compounds for specific types of rooms or shops, such as 공부방 (study room), 노래방 (karaoke room), and PC방 (internet cafe).

senses.definition: A space within a building enclosed by walls and a door.

examples.text: 제 방은 작지만 아주 따뜻해요.
examples.translation: My room is small, but very warm.

faults.quote: (baby) A very young child or infant. | glosses en: baby, infant
faults.why: '아이' means child; 'baby/infant' is '아기'. Oversplit and misleading gloss.

faults.quote: Use '애' only with friends or people younger than you.
faults.why: '애' is informal/spoken, not restricted to speaking with friends or younger people.

notes: In casual conversation, it is very often contracted to 애 (plural 애들). Do not confuse with 아기 (baby).

senses.definition: A young person who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: 공원에서 아이들이 뛰어놀고 있어요.
examples.translation: The children are running and playing in the park.

faults.quote: /pʌsɯ/
faults.why: Standard Korean pronunciation of 버스 has a tense initial consonant: [p͈ʌsɯ] (뻐쓰).

faults.quote: As a loanword, it is pronounced similarly to the English word.
faults.why: Trivial filler, and misses that initial ㅂ is pronounced tense [p͈] and '버스를 타다' is used.

notes: Often pronounced with a tense initial sound, like [뻐쓰]. Use 버스를 타다 for 'to take/ride a bus' and 버스에서 내리다 for 'to get off a bus'.

senses.definition: A large motor vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route.

examples.text: 버스를 기다려요.
examples.translation: I am waiting for the bus.

faults.quote: It is the most common adjective for general positive assessment.
faults.why: Filler note that repeats the gloss; should instead give useful grammar like the adverbial جَيِّدًا.

faults.quote: (behavior) Morally right or behaving in a correct, kind manner.
faults.why: Shades of 'good'; for a kind/decent person Arabic normally uses طَيِّب, while جَيِّد is general.

notes: The accusative form جَيِّدًا (jayyidan) is used as the adverb 'well' (e.g., أَعْرِفُهُ جَيِّدًا — I know him well).
For a kind or good-hearted person, طَيِّب (ṭayyib) is more natural than جَيِّد.

senses.definition: Of a high standard, quality, or level; satisfactory or favourable.

examples.text: هَذَا الطَّعَامُ جَيِّدٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This food is very good.

faults.quote: Use 'ḍaʿīf' to describe anything that lacks power
faults.why: Restates the senses in Latin transliteration instead of giving the irregular plural ضِعَاف / ضُعَفَاء.

notes: Takes the broken plural ضِعَاف (ḍiʿāf) or ضُعَفَاء (ḍuʿafāʾ). Opposite: قَوِيّ (qawī, 'strong').

senses.definition: Not physically strong; lacking bodily power or health.

examples.text: الرَّجُلُ ضَعِيفٌ بَعْدَ المَرَضِ.
examples.translation: The man is weak after the illness.

senses.definition: Low in intensity, force, or quality.

examples.text: إِشَارَةُ الإِنْتَرْنِت ضَعِيفَةٌ.
examples.translation: The internet signal is weak.

faults.quote: While 'thāqīl' literally means heavy
faults.why: Wrong transliteration 'thāqīl' (has a short 'a': thaqīl) and misses the idiom ثَقِيلُ الظِّلِّ.

notes: Takes the broken plural ثِقَال (thiqāl). Opposite: خَفِيف (khafīf, 'light').
To call a person dull or unpleasant, Arabic uses the set phrase ثَقِيلُ الظِّلِّ (thaqīlu ẓ-ẓill, literally 'heavy of shadow') or ثَقِيلُ الدَّمِ ('heavy of blood').

senses.definition: Of great physical weight; hard to lift or move.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ ثَقِيلَةٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This suitcase is very heavy.

senses.definition: Hard to bear or endure; oppressive, intense, or tiresome.

examples.text: هُوَ شَخْصٌ ثَقِيلُ الظِّلِّ.
examples.translation: He is a tiresome person.

faults.quote: embarrassed; awkward
faults.why: 'Awkward' (said of a situation, 'embarrassing') is مُحْرِج (muḥrij), not مُحْرَج (muḥraj).

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who feels uneasy or self-conscious
faults.why: Repeats the definition; should warn about the lookalike مُحْرِج (muḥrij, 'embarrassing') which is unvocalized identically.

notes: Do not confuse with مُحْرِج (muḥrij, with 'i'), which is spelled identically without vowels (محرج) but means 'embarrassing' or 'awkward' (e.g., مَوْقِف مُحْرِج — an awkward situation).

senses.definition: Feeling shy, uncomfortable, or self-conscious in a social situation.

examples.text: شَعَرْتُ أَنَّنِي مُحْرَجٌ عِنْدَمَا سَقَطْتُ أَمَامَ الْجَمِيعِ.
examples.translation: I felt embarrassed when I fell in front of everyone.

faults.why: Misses that أَبَدًا is predominantly used with future negation (لَنْ) or as a standalone 'Never!'.

notes: Used mainly in negative sentences (especially with لَنْ for the future, or لَا / مَا) to mean 'never' or 'not at all'. For past 'never' ('I have never...'), قَطُّ (qaṭṭu) or لم ... مِنْ قَبْلُ is often preferred in formal Arabic.
Can also stand alone as a strong negative reply: 'Never!' or 'Not at all!'.

senses.definition: With negation: at no time in the future or in general; on no occasion.

examples.text: لَنْ أَنْسَى هَذَا الْيَوْمَ أَبَدًا.
examples.translation: I will never forget this day.

senses.definition: With negation or as a standalone reply: in no way; to no extent.

examples.text: هَذَا لَيْسَ صَحِيحًا أَبَدًا.
examples.translation: This is not true at all.

faults.quote: Note that 'nariz' is a feminine noun, so use 'la' or 'una'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and the definition, which are already given.

notes: The plural is 'las narices'. In Spanish, you say 'la nariz' (with the definite article) where English uses 'my/his/her nose'.

senses.definition: The part of the face that you use for breathing and smelling.

examples.text: Se limpió la nariz con un pañuelo.
examples.translation: He wiped his nose with a tissue.

faults.quote: snow
faults.why: Omits the common Mexican sense 'ice cream; sorbet' present in sense 1.

faults.quote: While 'nieve' means snow, it is also commonly used in Mexico
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a contrast with 'helado' is more useful.

notes: In Mexico, 'nieve' usually means a water-based fruit sorbet (nieve de agua), though in many areas it is used for any scoop of ice cream (as opposed to 'helado', which is milk-based).

senses.definition: Frozen water that falls from the sky in soft white flakes.

examples.text: La nieve cubre todo el campo durante el invierno.
examples.translation: The snow covers the entire field during the winter.

senses.definition: (Mexico) A frozen dessert, especially a water-based fruit sorbet, or a scoop of ice cream.

examples.text: Vamos a comprar una nieve de limón al parque.
examples.translation: Let's go buy a lemon sorbet at the park.

faults.quote: A female person who is a few years of age.
faults.why: Too narrow; 'niña' covers any female child up to adolescence, not just toddlers.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a female child from birth up to adolescence.
faults.why: Restates what the definition itself should say.

notes: The masculine form is 'el niño' (boy); the plural 'los niños' can mean 'boys' or 'children' in general.
For a teenage girl or young woman, use 'la muchacha' or (in Mexico) 'la chava'.

senses.definition: A female child, from infancy up to adolescence.

examples.text: La niña juega en el parque con sus amigos.
examples.translation: The girl plays in the park with her friends.

faults.quote: (evening) The early part of the night
faults.why: Spanish 'noche' is one concept covering dark hours; English 'night' vs 'evening' is one sense.

faults.quote: While 'noche' is the general word for night, it is also
faults.why: Repeats the glosses instead of adding new usage information.

notes: Spanish has no separate word for 'evening' after dark: 'noche' covers both 'evening' and 'night' from sunset onward.
Common expressions: 'buenas noches' (good evening / good night), 'en la noche' or 'por la noche' (at night / in the evening), 'de la noche' (p.m., for times after dark, e.g. 'las ocho de la noche').

senses.definition: The dark part of the day between sunset and sunrise, including the evening hours after dark.

examples.text: La noche es muy tranquila en el pueblo.
examples.translation: The night is very quiet in the town.

examples.text: Salimos a cenar en la noche.
examples.translation: We are going out to dinner in the evening.

faults.quote: Guarde mis fotos en la nube para tener espacio en mi teléfono.
faults.why: Missing accent mark: 'Guarde' is subjunctive/imperative; past 'I saved' must be 'Guardé'.

faults.quote: In the context of technology, 'la nube' refers to cloud computing
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1.

notes: Do not confuse 'nube' (a cloud in the sky) with 'niebla' or 'neblina' (fog or mist near the ground).

senses.definition: A white or grey mass in the sky made of tiny water droplets.

examples.text: Hoy el cielo está cubierto de nubes blancas.
examples.translation: Today the sky is covered with white clouds.

senses.definition: Online storage and services accessed over the internet.

examples.text: Guardé mis fotos en la nube para tener espacio en mi teléfono.
examples.translation: I saved my photos in the cloud to have space on my phone.

faults.quote: One of two equal parts of something, or fifty percent.
faults.why: As a noun, 'a meia' is not 'half'; example uses determiner 'meio'.

faults.quote: Preciso comprar uma meia nova para usar com o tênis.
faults.why: Socks are bought in pairs (meias or um par de meias), not singly.

faults.quote: Meia is used for both socks and stockings.
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding usage information.

notes: In Brazil, 'meia' is also used as a spoken word for the number 6 (short for 'meia dúzia', half a dozen) when giving phone numbers or addresses.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the foot and lower leg inside a shoe.

examples.text: Preciso comprar meias novas para usar com o tênis.
examples.translation: I need to buy new socks to wear with my sneakers.

senses.definition: A ticket sold at half the standard price, typically for students or seniors (short for 'meia-entrada').

examples.text: Com a carteira de estudante, você paga meia no cinema.
examples.translation: With a student ID, you pay half-price at the movies.

faults.quote: girl; young woman; daughter
faults.why: 'daughter' is not in any sense's glosses.

faults.quote: A young woman or a teenager.
faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, calling a teenager or young woman 'menina' is one continuous sense.

notes: In Brazil, 'menina' is commonly used not only for female children, but also informally for teenagers and young women (alongside 'garota' and 'moça').

senses.definition: A female child, teenager, or young woman.

examples.text: A menina correu para o parque com os amigos.
examples.translation: The girl ran to the park with her friends.

examples.text: Aquela menina estuda na mesma universidade que eu.
examples.translation: That girl studies at the same university as me.

faults.quote: Used for eating, working, or gathering around.
faults.why: Purely repeats the definition of what a table is.

notes: For an office desk or study desk, 'mesa' (or 'mesa de trabalho') is the most common everyday word, though 'escrivaninha' specifically means a writing desk.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs used for eating, working, or placing things on.

examples.text: O prato já está na mesa.
examples.translation: The plate is already on the table.

examples.text: Deixei os documentos em cima da sua mesa.
examples.translation: I left the documents on your desk.

faults.quote: Used for physical metal coins (a moeda) as well as the abstract
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses in the entry.

notes: Do not confuse with 'dinheiro' (money in general) or 'nota' / 'cédula' (banknote, paper bill).

senses.definition: A small, flat, round piece of metal used as money.

examples.text: Ela tirou uma moeda da bolsa para pagar o ônibus.
examples.translation: She took a coin out of her bag to pay for the bus.

senses.definition: The system or type of money officially used in a country.

examples.text: O real é a moeda oficial do Brasil.
examples.translation: The real is the official currency of Brazil.

faults.quote: A very high hill that dominates the local landscape.
