examples.text: Eles vão enviar o pacote por transportadora amanhã.
examples.translation: They are going to ship the package by carrier tomorrow.

faults.quote: Used to describe something that is not correct, inaccurate, or morally wrong.
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding usage information.

notes: Typically used with the verb 'estar' rather than 'ser' when talking about mistakes or being mistaken (e.g., 'Você está errado' — You are wrong).
Often used as an adverb in informal speech to mean 'incorrectly' (e.g., 'escrever errado').

senses.definition: Not correct; containing a mistake or being inaccurate.

examples.text: A resposta dele estava errada.
examples.translation: His answer was wrong.

senses.definition: Not fair, honest, or morally acceptable.

examples.text: Mentir para os amigos é errado.
examples.translation: Lying to friends is wrong.

faults.why: Missing note on the irregular sound of 'lh' and open/closed 'o' in conjugation.

notes: In the present tense, 'eu escolho' has a closed 'o' sound (/o/), while 'você/ele escolhe' has an open 'o' sound (/ɔ/).
Do not confuse with 'eleger', which specifically means to elect someone by voting.

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want from a group of options.

examples.text: Preciso escolher um presente para ela.
examples.translation: I need to choose a gift for her.

examples.text: Você pode escolher o que quiser comer hoje.
examples.translation: You can choose whatever you want to eat today.

faults.quote: Unlike English 'write', 'escrever' is very commonly used for both physical writing
faults.why: English 'write' is also normally used for typing emails and messages; the contrast is false.
Lacks the irregular past participle 'escrito', which A2 learners must know.

faults.quote: To be the author of a book, article, or other creative work.
faults.why: Writing a text and writing a book are shades of the same everyday meaning.

notes: Has an irregular past participle: 'escrito' (written).

senses.definition: To form letters or words on paper or a screen, or to produce a text such as a message, letter, or book.

examples.text: Eu preciso escrever um e-mail urgente.
examples.translation: I need to write an urgent email.

examples.text: Ele vai escrever um livro sobre história.
examples.translation: He is going to write a book about history.

faults.quote: A color that is deep or intense rather than light or bright.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('A color that is...') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: Used to describe rooms, hallways, or times of day when there is
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the two sense definitions without adding grammar or usage help.

faults.quote: dark; dim; gloomy
faults.why: 'Gloomy' is not in any sense's glosses.

notes: As a masculine noun, 'o escuro' means 'the dark' (e.g., 'ter medo do escuro' — to be afraid of the dark).
The opposite is 'claro' (light/bright).

senses.definition: With little or no light.

examples.text: O quarto estava muito escuro à noite.
examples.translation: The room was very dark at night.

senses.definition: Of a color or shade: deep and closer to black than to white; not light.

examples.text: Ela prefere usar roupas de tom azul-escuro.
examples.translation: She prefers to wear dark blue clothes.

faults.quote: Note the liaison with the definite article: 'l'hôpital' is pronounced
faults.why: Confuses elision with liaison; poorly written and misses the irregular plural 'hôpitaux'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'la pharmacie'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'hôpital' and 'pharmacie'.

notes: Irregular plural: 'les hôpitaux' (/o.pi.to/).
The initial 'h' is mute, allowing elision ('l'hôpital') and liaison ('les hôpitaux' /le.z‿o.pi.to/).

senses.definition: A building where sick or injured people are given medical treatment.

examples.text: Il doit aller à l'hôpital pour sa jambe cassée.
examples.translation: He has to go to the hospital for his broken leg.

notes: Used for a large clock on a wall, tower, or public building. Compare 'la montre' (wristwatch) and 'le réveil' (alarm clock).

senses.definition: A large device, usually on a wall or building, that shows the time.

examples.text: L'horloge du salon indique midi.
examples.translation: The living room clock shows noon.

faults.quote: A large, old, and often luxurious private house.
faults.why: Historical/architectural sense ('hôtel particulier'), not an everyday standalone A2 meaning; 'hôtel de ville' is more useful in a note.

faults.quote: Note that the initial 'h' is silent and aspirate in spelling origin
faults.why: Confusing and contradictory explanation about 'aspirate in spelling origin'.

notes: The initial 'h' is mute, taking elision ('l'hôtel') and liaison ('des hôtels' /de.z‿o.tɛl/).
Also found in 'l'hôtel de ville' (town hall / city hall).

senses.definition: A building where people pay to stay when they are traveling.

examples.text: Nous avons réservé une belle chambre dans cet hôtel près de la gare.
examples.translation: We booked a nice room in this hotel near the station.

faults.quote: /l‿ɥil/
faults.why: IPA includes the definite article; it must be of the lemma 'huile' (/ɥil/).

faults.quote: L'huile is feminine, so use de l'huile or la/l'
faults.why: 'de l'huile' and 'l'huile' are used before any vowel sound regardless of gender, not because it is feminine.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with the verb rouiller (to rust) or un oeil
faults.why: Bizarre filler note warning against words that neither look nor sound similar.

notes: Usually an uncountable noun used with the partitive article 'de l'' ('acheter de l'huile', to buy oil).

senses.definition: A smooth, thick liquid obtained from plants or animals, used in cooking.

examples.text: Ajoutez un filet d'huile dans la poêle chaude.
examples.translation: Add a drizzle of oil to the hot pan.

senses.definition: A thick liquid from petroleum used to lubricate engines or burn as fuel.

examples.text: Il faut vérifier le niveau d'huile avant de partir en voyage.
examples.translation: You need to check the oil level before going on a trip.

faults.quote: /lœj/
faults.why: IPA includes the definite article; it must be of the lemma 'œil' (/œj/).

faults.quote: Be careful with the gender: 'œil' is masculine, so you say 'mon œil'
faults.why: Restates gender and gives a misleading example ('mon' is also used with feminine vowel-initial nouns).

notes: Irregular plural: 'les yeux' (/le.z‿jø/).

senses.definition: The organ in the face that you use to see.

examples.text: Elle a un grain de beauté près de l'œil.
examples.translation: She has a beauty spot near her eye.

senses.definition: A way of looking at something, or close attention given to it.

examples.text: Garde un œil sur le gâteau dans le four.
examples.translation: Keep an eye on the cake in the oven.

faults.quote: post office, agency, service
faults.why: 'Ufficio' alone does not mean 'post office'; that is 'ufficio postale'.

faults.quote: A responsibility, duty, or function assigned to someone.
faults.why: Literary or bureaucratic sense, not everyday A2 usage.
Missing the plural form 'gli uffici' (single -i).

notes: The plural has a single '-i': 'gli uffici'.
Do not confuse with 'azienda', which means a company or business as a whole.

senses.definition: A room or building where people work at desks.

examples.text: Lavoro in un ufficio nel centro della città.
examples.translation: I work in an office in the city center.

senses.definition: A department or public service branch that handles specific tasks, such as 'ufficio postale' (post office) or 'ufficio informazioni' (information desk).

examples.text: Dove si trova l'ufficio informazioni?
examples.translation: Where is the information office?

faults.quote: Ufficio postale is made of ufficio (office) and postale (postal).
faults.why: Explains transparent literal components instead of giving useful grammar such as the plural.

notes: In everyday speech, people often just say 'la posta' ('Vado in posta').
The plural is 'gli uffici postali'.

senses.definition: A place where you go to send letters and parcels, pay bills, and buy stamps.

examples.text: Vado all'ufficio postale per spedire questo pacco.
examples.translation: I am going to the post office to send this parcel.

faults.quote: The academic community or staff of such an institution.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning (building/institution/staff); should be one sense.
Nouns ending in an accented vowel are invariable in the plural ('le università').

notes: Like all nouns ending in an accented vowel, it does not change in the plural: 'le università'.
To say you attend university, use 'fare l'università' or 'andare all'università'.

senses.definition: An institution of higher education where students study for a degree.

examples.text: Studio legge all'Università di Bologna.
examples.translation: I study law at the University of Bologna.

faults.quote: Notice the elision with the definite article: 'lo uomo' becomes 'l'uomo'.
faults.why: The plural is 'gli uomini', which is highly irregular and missing; meanwhile note[0] repeats the senses.

notes: The plural is irregular: 'gli uomini' (the men).

senses.definition: An adult male person.

examples.text: L'uomo cammina veloce sotto la pioggia.
examples.translation: The man is walking fast in the rain.

senses.definition: A human being of any gender, or humankind in general.

examples.text: Ogni uomo ha il diritto di esprimere le proprie opinioni.
examples.translation: Every human being has the right to express their opinions.

faults.quote: Notice the irregular plural: un uovo, ma due uova (feminine plural).
faults.why: Uses Italian 'ma' instead of English 'but' in an English note.

notes: The plural is irregular and becomes feminine: 'un uovo' / 'l'uovo' (masculine), but 'due uova' / 'le uova' (feminine).

senses.definition: The oval food with a shell laid by a hen or other bird.

examples.text: Ho mangiato un uovo a colazione.
examples.translation: I ate an egg for breakfast.

faults.quote: A place or environment where there is a lack of noise.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('a place or environment').
Quiet thing and quiet place are shades of one meaning.

notes: While 'silencioso' refers to something or someone that makes little or no noise, 'callado' is used specifically for a person who is not speaking or tends not to talk much.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise, or having no noise.

examples.text: El motor de este coche eléctrico es muy silencioso.
examples.translation: The engine of this electric car is very quiet.

examples.text: Buscamos un lugar silencioso para estudiar.
examples.translation: We are looking for a quiet place to study.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'sin' is a preposition, not an expression.

faults.quote: Used to indicate the absence or lack of something.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.
Preposition 'sin' has one core meaning; noun vs. infinitive belongs in notes.

notes: Followed by a noun, pronoun, or infinitive verb (unlike English 'without' + -ing: 'sin decir' = 'without saying').
Do not confuse with 'sino' ('but rather'), which introduces an alternative after a negative statement.

senses.definition: Not having, using, or doing something; in the absence of.

examples.text: Me gusta el café sin azúcar.
examples.translation: I like coffee without sugar.

examples.text: Se fue sin decir adiós.
examples.translation: He left without saying goodbye.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'single / only / sole' (before a noun).
Should note that 'estar solo' means 'to be alone' or 'to feel lonely'.

notes: Usually used with 'estar' ('estar solo' = to be alone) or 'sentirse' ('sentirse solo' = to feel lonely).
Placed before a noun, it means 'single' or 'only' ('un solo día' = a single day); after a noun, it means 'alone' or 'by itself' ('café solo' = black coffee).
Also used as an invariable adverb meaning 'only' (like 'solamente').

senses.definition: Without any other people present; on one's own.

examples.text: Prefiero vivir solo en este piso.
examples.translation: I prefer to live alone in this flat.

senses.definition: Unhappy because of having no friends or company.

examples.text: Me siento un poco solo los domingos por la tarde.
examples.translation: I feel a bit lonely on Sunday afternoons.

senses.definition: Used before a noun to emphasize that there is only one.

examples.text: No dijo una sola palabra en toda la reunión.
examples.translation: He didn't say a single word in the whole meeting.

faults.quote: /son.ɾeˈiɾ/
faults.why: Standard Spanish 'r' after 'n' is a trill /r/, not a tap /ɾ/.

notes: Conjugated like 'reír': the stem vowel 'e' changes to 'i' in most forms, and many forms carry a written accent (sonrío, sonríes, sonríe).

senses.definition: To make a happy expression by curving the corners of your mouth upwards.

examples.text: Ella empezó a sonreír cuando vio a su perro.
examples.translation: She started to smile when she saw her dog.

notes: بَيْضَة is a unit noun ('one egg'); the collective noun is بَيْض (bayḍ, 'eggs') and the counted plural is بَيْضَات (bayḍāt).

senses.definition: An oval object with a shell laid by a bird, especially a chicken, eaten as food.

examples.text: آكُلُ بَيْضَةً مَعَ الخُبْزِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
examples.translation: I eat an egg with bread every morning.

faults.quote: /ˈɣurfata maˈʕiː.ʃa/
faults.why: First word has accusative case ending -ta instead of pause form /ˈɣur.fat/.

faults.quote: نجلس في غُرْفَة مَعِيشَة كل مساء.
faults.why: Uses indefinite 'a living room' where Arabic requires definite 'غرفة المعيشة'.

notes: Made definite by adding الـ to the second word: غُرْفَة المَعِيشَة (the living room); plural غُرَف مَعِيشَة.
Often called صَالَة (ṣāla) in everyday speech.

senses.definition: The main room in a home where people sit and relax together.

examples.text: نَجْلِسُ فِي غُرْفَةِ المَعِيشَةِ كُلَّ مَسَاءٍ.
examples.translation: We sit in the living room every evening.

faults.quote: lesson; class; study
faults.why: Includes 'study', which is not covered by the senses.

faults.quote: In an academic context, 'dars' is the standard word for a lesson
faults.why: Restates the gloss; broken plural دُرُوس (durūs) is needed instead.

notes: Broken plural: دُرُوس (durūs).
Do not confuse with دِرَاسَة (dirāsa), which means 'study' or 'studies' in general.

senses.definition: A period of time in which students are taught, or a unit of teaching in a course or book.

examples.text: سَأَحْضُرُ دَرْسَ اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ غَدًا.
examples.translation: I will attend the Arabic language lesson tomorrow.

senses.definition: Something learned from an experience, especially a difficult one.

examples.text: تَعَلَّمْتُ دَرْسًا قَاسِيًا مِن هَذِهِ التَّجْرِبَةِ.
examples.translation: I learned a hard lesson from this experience.

faults.why: Missing the common broken plural مَدَارِس (madāris).

notes: Broken plural: مَدَارِس (madāris).
Refers to primary or secondary school; for university or college, use جَامِعَة (jāmiʕa) or كُلِّيَّة (kulliyya).

senses.definition: A place where children go to be educated.

examples.text: ذَهَبَ الطِّفْلُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
examples.translation: The child went to school in the morning.

faults.quote: The word لوحة covers several flat surfaces, most commonly a painting
faults.why: merely repeats the senses and glosses.

faults.quote: تعليق لوحة جميلة على الجدار.
faults.why: Noun phrase fragment rather than a natural sentence.

notes: Plural: لَوْحَات (lawḥāt).
Used in common compounds like لَوْحَة مَفَاتِيح (keyboard) and لَوْحَة إِعْلَانَات (notice board).

senses.definition: A picture made with paint on canvas, wood, or another surface.

examples.text: عَلَّقْتُ لَوْحَةً جَمِيلَةً عَلَى الجِدَارِ.
examples.translation: I hung a beautiful painting on the wall.

senses.definition: A flat board or sign used for writing or displaying notices and information.

examples.text: تُوجَدُ لَوْحَةُ الإِعْلَانَاتِ فِي المَدْخَلِ.
examples.translation: The notice board is in the entrance.

faults.quote: Used as a formal or standard term for a meal
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding grammar or usage guidance.

faults.quote: In some regions of Germany, particularly in the south, 'Mahlzeit!' is
faults.why: Used across Germany at work, not particularly southern.

notes: Plural: 'die Mahlzeiten'.
Around lunchtime, 'Mahlzeit!' is commonly used at work as a casual greeting among colleagues, even when not eating.

senses.definition: Food eaten at a regular time of day, or the occasion of eating it.

examples.text: Das Frühstück ist die erste Mahlzeit des Tages.
examples.translation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

examples.text: Sie bereiten eine warme Mahlzeit zu.
examples.translation: They are preparing a warm meal.

faults.quote: When you use this word for a computer peripheral, it stays feminine
faults.why: Obvious filler restating the noun's gender.

notes: The plural form takes an umlaut: 'die Mäuse'.

senses.definition: A small grey or brown rodent with a long tail.

examples.text: Die kleine Maus läuft schnell unter das Sofa.
examples.translation: The little mouse runs quickly under the sofa.

senses.definition: A small hand-held device used to move the cursor on a computer screen.

examples.text: Ich brauche eine neue Maus für meinen Laptop.
examples.translation: I need a new mouse for my laptop.

faults.quote: Note that 'Medizin' can refer both to the academic field and
faults.why: Restates the two senses; moreover, English 'medicine' also covers both.

notes: Usually uncountable. For an individual pharmaceutical product or drug, 'das Medikament' is also very common.
Do not confuse with 'die Droge', which in German almost exclusively means an illegal or addictive recreational drug.

senses.definition: A substance, such as a pill or liquid, taken to treat an illness.

examples.text: Hast du deine Medizin schon genommen?
examples.translation: Have you taken your medicine yet?

senses.definition: The science and practice of preventing, diagnosing, and treating disease.

examples.text: Sie studiert Medizin in Berlin.
examples.translation: She is studying medicine in Berlin.

faults.quote: In German, the word 'Milch' is almost always feminine ('die Milch').
faults.why: Restates the gender and misleadingly implies it is not always feminine.

notes: Uncountable (no plural in everyday use); to count portions, use 'zwei Gläser Milch' (two glasses of milk) or 'eine Packung Milch' (a carton of milk).

senses.definition: The white liquid produced by cows and other female mammals, used as a drink or in cooking.

faults.quote: Minute is a feminine noun. When you say how many minutes
faults.why: Restates the gender and states an obvious rule that applies to English too.

notes: Plural: 'die Minuten' (e.g., 'in fünf Minuten' — in five minutes).

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.

examples.text: Ich brauche nur noch eine Minute.
examples.translation: I only need one more minute.

faults.quote: Unlike simply saying 'iyi' (good) or 'sevimli' (cute), 'arkadaş canlısı'
faults.why: Filler note comparing unrelated words and merely restating the definition.

notes: Formed from 'arkadaş' (friend) + 'canlısı' (fond of). Used for both people and animals (especially pets) to mean sociable and affectionate.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: kind, pleasant, and eager to interact with others.

examples.text: O çok arkadaş canlısı bir insan.
examples.translation: He is a very friendly person.

faults.why: Missing note on common compounds ('iş arkadaşı', 'ev arkadaşı') and plural vocative 'arkadaşlar' (guys/everyone).

notes: The general word for 'friend'; for a closer, deeper bond, 'dost' is used.

Often used in compounds like 'iş arkadaşı' (colleague), 'sınıf arkadaşı' (classmate), and 'ev arkadaşı' (flatmate). In the plural, 'arkadaşlar!' is a very common way to address a group ('guys!', 'everyone!').

senses.definition: A person you know well and like, with whom you have a bond of mutual affection.

examples.text: Yarın arkadaşımla buluşacağım.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I'm going to meet up with my friend.

senses.definition: A person with whom one works or shares an activity.

examples.text: Ofisteki diğer arkadaşlarla kahve içtik.
examples.translation: We had coffee with the other colleagues in the office.

faults.quote: Aferin sana, aslan gibi başardın.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation; in Turkish one says 'aslanlar gibi' or vocative 'aslanım'.

notes: Often used affectionately or in praise (especially as 'aslanım', literally 'my lion') to encourage someone or call a boy or man brave and strong.

senses.definition: A large wild cat of Africa and India, with a yellowish-brown coat and a mane in the male.

examples.text: Aslan ormanda kükredi.
examples.translation: The lion roared in the forest.

senses.definition: A brave, strong, or admirable person.

examples.text: Aferin benim aslan oğluma!
examples.translation: Well done to my brave boy!

faults.quote: It is used exclusively for the animal, not for the pieces in
faults.why: Self-contradictory and false: claims 'at' is not used for chess, then says it is, and falsely claims 'ad' ends in a /d/ sound in citation form (it devoices to /at/, only becoming /d/ before a vowel).

notes: Do not confuse with 'ad' (name) or the verb 'atmak' (to throw). In isolation, 'at' and 'ad' sound identical (/at/), [t] vs. [d] only appears when a vowel suffix is added: 'atı' (his horse) vs. 'adı' (his name).

senses.definition: A large four-legged animal with a mane and tail, used for riding and carrying loads.

examples.text: At çiftlikte koşuyor.
examples.translation: The horse is running on the farm.

examples.text: Hafta sonu ata binmeyi seviyorum.
examples.translation: I like riding a horse at the weekend.

senses.definition: The chess piece shaped like a horse's head.

examples.text: At ile şahı tehdit etti.
examples.translation: He threatened the king with the knight.

faults.quote: Do not confuse sec with vide (empty); sec means free from moisture
faults.why: Bizarre filler note; nobody confuses 'sec' (dry) with 'vide' (empty).

notes: The feminine form is sèche (/sɛʃ/), changing both spelling and pronunciation.
For wines or pastries, sec means dry or plain (not sweet), as in du vin blanc sec.

senses.definition: Free from moisture or liquid; not wet.

examples.text: Le linge est sec maintenant, on peut le ranger.
examples.translation: The laundry is dry now, we can put it away.

senses.definition: Of a voice, tone, or manner: cold, abrupt, or unfriendly.

examples.text: Il a répondu d'un ton très sec.
examples.translation: He answered in a very sharp tone.

faults.why: Missing the essential intransitive sense 'to emit an odor' (e.g., ça sent bon).

faults.quote: Sentir can mean both to smell (perceive an odor) and to feel
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and definitions without adding usage information.

notes: Irregular verb (je sens, tu sens, il sent, nous sentons). Followed directly by an adjective, it means to smell a certain way: ça sent bon (it smells good).
Used reflexively (se sentir), it describes how someone feels physically or emotionally: je me sens fatigué (I feel tired).

senses.definition: To perceive a scent or odor using your nose.

examples.text: J'aime sentir les fleurs dans le jardin.
examples.translation: I like to smell the flowers in the garden.

senses.definition: To give off a particular odor or scent.

examples.text: Ça sent très bon dans la cuisine !
examples.translation: It smells very good in the kitchen!

senses.definition: To experience a physical sensation or an emotion.

examples.text: Je sens le vent froid sur mon visage.
examples.translation: I feel the cold wind on my face.

faults.why: Needs a note explaining that possessive 'ses' changes to match the subject.

notes: Literally 'to squeeze in one's arms', this is the standard way to say 'to hug'. The possessive (ses) changes to match the subject: je te serre dans mes bras.

senses.definition: To hold someone close in your arms to show affection or comfort.

examples.text: Elle l'a serré dans ses bras pour le consoler.
examples.translation: She hugged him to comfort him.

notes: Before a noun, seul means 'only' or 'single' (la seule personne). After a noun or a verb like être, it means 'alone' (un homme seul, elle est seule).

senses.definition: Without other people; on one's own.

examples.text: Il aime voyager seul.
examples.translation: He likes to travel alone.

senses.definition: Being the only one of its kind; no more than one.

examples.text: C'est le seul choix que nous avons.
examples.translation: This is the only choice we have.

faults.quote: It can also describe a mood or atmosphere that feels gloomy and sad.
faults.why: Purely repeats sense 1 without adding useful contrast or usage guidance.

notes: For colors, foncé is the standard word for a dark shade (bleu foncé = dark blue), while sombre describes a color that looks dull, heavy, or gloomy.

senses.definition: With little or no light; deep in shade or color.

examples.text: La pièce est sombre sans les lampes.
examples.translation: The room is dark without the lamps.

senses.definition: Of a mood, expression, or situation: sad and without hope or joy.

examples.text: Il a un regard sombre aujourd'hui.
examples.translation: He has a gloomy look today.

faults.why: Missing the common preposition 'met' (blij zijn met = to be happy with/about).

notes: Unlike 'gelukkig' (deep, long-term happiness or contentment with life), 'blij' is a temporary feeling of pleasure about something specific.
Often used with the preposition 'met': 'blij zijn met iets' (to be happy with/about something).

senses.definition: Feeling pleased or glad about something.

examples.text: Ik ben zo blij met mijn nieuwe fiets.
examples.translation: I am so happy with my new bike.

examples.text: Hij was erg blij om het goede nieuws te horen.
examples.translation: He was very glad to hear the good news.

faults.quote: Boos is the standard everyday word for feeling angry or cross
faults.why: Restates the gloss; should instead mention the preposition 'op' (boos op iemand).

notes: Takes the preposition 'op' for a person ('boos op iemand' = angry with someone) and 'over' for a thing ('boos over iets' = angry about something).
More common and slightly milder in everyday speech than 'kwaad'.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing strong displeasure or anger.

examples.text: Waarom ben je zo boos op mij?
examples.translation: Why are you so angry with me?

examples.text: De docent werd boos omdat niemand zijn huiswerk had gemaakt.
examples.translation: The teacher got angry because nobody had done their homework.

faults.quote: Use 'bouwen' for physical construction like houses, blocks, or larger structures.
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1, which shows abstract use ('aan onze toekomst bouwen').

notes: For physical structures, 'bouwen' is more specific than 'maken' (to make). For abstract things, it is often used with the preposition 'aan' ('bouwen aan' = to work on / build up).

senses.definition: To make a structure by putting parts together, such as a house, bridge, or tower.

examples.text: De kinderen bouwen een hoge toren met blokken.
examples.translation: The children are building a high tower with blocks.

senses.definition: To establish or develop something abstract over time, such as a future or a relationship.

examples.text: We willen samen aan onze toekomst bouwen.
examples.translation: We want to build our future together.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with branden (to burn).
faults.why: 'Branden' is not a common confusable for 'breken'; auxiliary 'hebben'/'zijn' usage is much more useful.

faults.quote: To make something fall into pieces.
faults.why: Omits intransitive use (to break/snap on its own) and lists 'fracture' in sense 0 glosses.

notes: Irregular (strong) verb: brak, gebroken.
Takes 'hebben' when someone breaks something (Ik heb het glas gebroken) and 'zijn' when something breaks by itself (Het glas is gebroken).

senses.definition: To separate into pieces, or to make something separate into pieces, from a blow or strain.

examples.text: Pas op dat je de vaas niet breekt.
examples.translation: Be careful not to break the vase.

senses.definition: To crack or fracture a bone in the body.

examples.text: Hij viel van de trap en brak zijn arm.
examples.translation: He fell down the stairs and broke his arm.

faults.quote: To spend a period of time somewhere or doing something.
faults.why: 'Brengen' does not mean 'to spend time'; that is the separable verb 'doorbrengen'.

faults.quote: We gaan onze vakantie in Spanje brengen.
faults.why: Ungrammatical in Dutch; must be 'doorbrengen'.
Senses 0 and 1 are the same Dutch meaning split by English 'bring' vs 'take'.

faults.quote: Kun je die doos even naar hier brengen?
faults.why: In Netherlandic Dutch, 'hierheen brengen' is natural, not 'naar hier brengen'.

notes: Irregular verb: bracht, gebracht.
Covers both English 'bring' (towards the speaker) and 'take' (to another place or person). Contrast with 'halen' (to go and get/fetch).

senses.definition: To take or carry someone or something to a place or person.

examples.text: Ik zal je naar het station brengen.
examples.translation: I will take you to the station.

examples.text: Kun je die doos even hierheen brengen?
examples.translation: Can you bring that box over here?

faults.quote: The word ends in '-hane'
faults.why: Modern spelling is 'hastane', not 'hastahane'; saying it ends in '-hane' is misleading.
Should mention the long 'a' in the second syllable, which spelling does not show.

notes: The second 'a' is pronounced long (/hastaːne/), because the word comes from 'hasta' (sick) + '-hane' (house). The older spelling 'hastahane' is now obsolete.

senses.definition: A building where sick or injured people are given medical treatment.

examples.text: Yaralıyı hemen hastaneye kaldırdılar.
examples.translation: They rushed the injured person to the hospital immediately.

faults.quote: /haˈta/
faults.why: The final 'a' is long in standard Turkish (/haˈtaː/).

faults.quote: (technical) A technical malfunction, flaw, or system failure.
faults.why: A computer or technical error is the same basic sense of 'error/mistake' for A2.

faults.quote: Hata is a very common word for a mistake
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss; should instead note the common verb collocation 'hata yapmak'.

notes: Commonly used with the verb 'yapmak' ('hata yapmak' = to make a mistake). With machines or software, 'hata vermek' means 'to give an error'.
As a near-synonym, 'yanlış' is both an adjective ('wrong') and a noun ('mistake/wrong answer'), while 'hata' is only a noun.

senses.definition: An action, decision, or result that is wrong or not intended, including a fault in a system.

examples.text: Raporu hazırlarken küçük bir hata yaptım.
examples.translation: I made a small mistake while preparing the report.

examples.text: Program çalışırken beklenmeyen bir hata verdi.
examples.translation: The program gave an unexpected error while running.

faults.quote: (mind) To keep something in your mind and not forget it.
faults.why: Oversplit; 'keep in mind' in Turkish is usually 'aklında tutmak' or 'unutmamak', not a distinct sense.

faults.quote: Bu önemli kuralı her zaman hatırlamak gerek.
faults.why: Reads like an English calque of 'always remember this rule'; natives say 'unutmamak gerek' or 'akılda tutmak gerek'.

faults.quote: Use hatırlamak when something comes back to your mind
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case when specific (e.g., 'Onu hatırlıyorum' — I remember him/her/it).
For 'Remember to do X!' in English, Turkish normally uses the negative of 'unutmak' (to forget): 'Unutma!' (Don't forget!), rather than 'hatırlamak'.

senses.definition: To have or bring a fact, event, or person back into your mind.

examples.text: Yarın doğum günün olduğunu yeni hatırladım.
examples.translation: I just remembered that tomorrow is your birthday.

examples.text: Adını hatırlıyorum ama yüzünü unuttum.
examples.translation: I remember his name, but I forgot his face.

faults.quote: Derin bir hava al.
faults.why: Unidiomatic Turkish; 'take a deep breath' is 'derin bir nefes al', while 'hava almak' means to get fresh air.

faults.quote: Bu şarkının havası çok hoş.
faults.why: 'Şarkının havası' means the vibe/feel of the song, not its melody.

faults.quote: The word hava has several common meanings.
faults.why: Merely repeats all the senses already listed in the entry.

faults.quote: A tune or melody of a song.
faults.why: Folk 'tune/air' sense is marginal for A2 compared to weather, air, and atmosphere/vibe.

notes: Common expressions: 'hava almak' (to get some fresh air), 'hava durumu' (weather forecast), and informal 'hava atmak' (to show off).

senses.definition: The state of the sky and temperature at a particular time and place, such as rain, sun, heat, or wind.

examples.text: Bugün hava çok güzel.
examples.translation: Today the weather is very nice.

senses.definition: The invisible gas surrounding the earth that we breathe, or open outdoor space.

examples.text: Oda çok sıcak oldu, biraz temiz hava alalım.
examples.translation: The room has gotten very hot; let's get some fresh air.

senses.definition: The general mood, feeling, or atmosphere of a place, thing, or person.

examples.text: Bu kafenin havası çok hoş.
examples.translation: The atmosphere of this café is very pleasant.

faults.quote: /ha.va.li.ma.nɯ/
faults.why: Missing stress mark in IPA (/ha.va.li.maˈnɯ/).

notes: Often used interchangeably with 'havaalanı'. While 'havalimanı' officially refers to a larger international airport, they mean the same thing in everyday speech.
This is a compound noun ('hava' + 'liman' + '-ı'), so case suffixes attach with a buffer 'n': 'havalimanına' (to the airport), 'havalimanında' (at the airport).

senses.definition: A large place where aircraft regularly take off and land, with buildings for passengers.

examples.text: Uçağımıza yetişmek için havalimanına erken gitmeliyiz.
examples.translation: We must go to the airport early to catch our plane.

faults.quote: It can also function as a verb, meaning 'to snow'.
faults.why: 雪 alone is not a verb in modern Mandarin; 'to snow' is 下雪.

faults.quote: Unlike some other languages that have separate words for 'snow on the
faults.why: English also uses one word; learners need the verb 下雪 and measure word 场.

notes: To say 'it is snowing', combine it with the verb 下 (xià, to fall): 下雪 (xià xuě). A snowfall is counted with the measure word 场 (cháng), e.g. 一场大雪 (a heavy snowfall).

senses.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky and cover the ground.

examples.text: 今天下了很大的雪。
examples.translation: It snowed very heavily today.

faults.why: Sense 0 mixes physical roads with 'on the way', while sense 1 also includes 'route'.

notes: Counted with the measure word 条 (tiáo). Also used after a number to name a bus route: 1路车 (bus line 1).
For a small path or trail, use 小路 (xiǎolù); for a city street with shops and buildings, 街 (jiē) or 街道 (jiēdào) is also common.

senses.definition: A built track or street for people and vehicles to travel along.

examples.text: 这条路很宽。
examples.translation: This road is very wide.

senses.definition: The route, direction, or journey taken to get somewhere; figuratively, a way of doing something.

examples.text: 他在回家的路上。
examples.translation: He is on the way home.

examples.text: 我们需要找一条新路。
examples.translation: We need to find a new way forward.

faults.quote: a common pattern in Chinese for animal names that imply grandeur.
faults.why: Vague filler; learners need the measure word 头 (tóu) or 只 (zhī).

notes: Counted with the measure word 头 (tóu) or 只 (zhī): 一头大象 (an elephant). Literally 'big elephant'; 象 (xiàng) is used in compounds like 象牙 (xiàngyá, ivory).

senses.definition: A very large grey mammal with a long trunk, large ears, and tusks.

examples.text: 大象有很长的鼻子。
examples.translation: Elephants have very long trunks.

faults.quote: 经理正在开会，请稍等。
faults.why: Uses 开会 rather than the headword 会议.

faults.quote: For a quick casual chat or get-together, use 会 (huì) or 聚会
faults.why: 会 (huì) is the everyday spoken word for a work meeting (开会), not a casual chat.

notes: Counted with 个 (gè) or 场 (chǎng). 会议 is the full, slightly formal noun for a meeting or conference; in everyday speech, 'to have a meeting' is usually 开会 (kāi huì). For a social get-together with friends, use 聚会 (jùhuì).

senses.definition: An organized gathering of people to discuss work or official matters.

examples.text: 我们明天有一个重要的会议。
examples.translation: We have an important meeting tomorrow.

faults.quote: A person who is perceived as clumsy, awkward, or socially inept.
faults.why: Regional slang not standard in Mexico and unnecessary for an A2 beginner.

faults.quote: While it literally means the animal, 'pato' can be used as
faults.why: Merely restates the senses.

notes: The female is 'la pata', which also means an animal's leg or a piece of furniture's leg.
In some parts of Latin America (especially the Caribbean and South America), 'pato' is a derogatory slang term for a gay man.

senses.definition: A common water bird with a flat beak, short neck, and webbed feet.

examples.text: Hay un pato nadando en el estanque del parque.
examples.translation: There is a duck swimming in the park pond.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'pelo' with 'pila', which means battery or sink.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion between two phonetically and semantically unrelated words.

notes: In Mexico, both 'pelo' and 'cabello' are very common for human head hair, with 'cabello' sounding slightly more polite or formal.
When talking about the hair on someone's head as a whole, Spanish uses the singular with the definite article: 'Tengo el pelo corto' (I have short hair).

senses.definition: The mass of fine threads growing on a person's head or body, or a single one of these threads.

examples.text: Ella tiene el pelo largo y negro.
examples.translation: She has long black hair.

senses.definition: The thick coat of soft hair covering the body of an animal.

examples.text: El perro tiene el pelo muy suave.
examples.translation: The dog has very soft fur.

notes: Do not confuse 'perro' (dog), pronounced with a rolled 'rr' sound, with 'pero' (but), which has a single 'r'.
In Mexico, 'perro' is also used colloquially as an adjective meaning 'tough', 'intense', or 'awesome' (e.g., 'hace un calor perro').

senses.definition: A common four-legged animal that barks and is often kept as a pet or working animal.

examples.text: Mi perro corre por todo el parque.
examples.translation: My dog runs all over the park.

faults.quote: /peθ/
faults.why: Mexican Spanish uses seseo (/pes/), not the Peninsular interdental fricative /θ/.

faults.quote: fish (living); fish (as food)
faults.why: 'Pez' only means a living fish; fish as food is 'pescado'.

notes: Use 'el pez' for a live fish in the water, and 'el pescado' for fish caught to be eaten as food.
The plural is 'los peces' (the 'z' changes to 'c' before 'e').

senses.definition: A cold-blooded animal with fins and gills that lives and swims in water.

examples.text: Hay un pez muy colorido en la pecera.
examples.translation: There is a very colorful fish in the tank.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the current day.
faults.why: First sentence merely restates the gloss.

faults.quote: Unlike in English where 'today' can act as a noun
faults.why: False grammar claim: วันนี้ easily functions as a noun subject (e.g., วันนี้สนุกมาก).

notes: Usually placed at the beginning or end of a sentence.
Also used as a noun meaning 'today' (e.g., วันนี้เป็นวันหยุด 'Today is a holiday').

senses.definition: On or during this present day.

examples.text: วันนี้อากาศดีมาก
examples.translation: Today the weather is very good.

examples.text: ฉันจะไปตลาดวันนี้
examples.translation: I will go to the market today.

faults.quote: Used to confirm that something is true or correct.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition and glosses.

faults.quote: ใช่, ฉันเข้าใจแล้ว
faults.why: Thai does not use English-style commas after interjections; use a space instead.

notes: Confirms that a fact is true ('that's right'), unlike ครับ (khráp) and ค่ะ (khâ), which are polite particles that can also serve as a general 'yes'.
Often used at the end of a sentence in ใช่ไหม (châi mái, 'right?') to form a yes/no question, and negated as ไม่ใช่ (mâi châi, 'no / that's not right').

senses.definition: Used to confirm that a statement is true or correct.

examples.text: ใช่ ฉันเข้าใจแล้ว
examples.translation: Yes, I understand now.

faults.quote: To favor, appreciate, or be fond of; often used in very formal
faults.why: Royal/high-register verb 'to favor' is not A2; everyday adjective 'favorite' (คนโปรด/ของโปรด) is.

notes: As 'please', used mainly on signs and in formal announcements. In everyday speech, people add ครับ/ค่ะ or use ช่วย...หน่อย (chûai ... nòi) instead.
Placed after a noun, it means 'favorite' in everyday speech (e.g., อาหารโปรด 'favorite food', คนโปรด 'favorite person').

senses.definition: Used in formal notices, signs, and announcements to politely ask someone to do something.

examples.text: โปรดรักษาระยะห่าง
examples.translation: Please maintain a safe distance.

senses.definition: Placed after a noun: liked more than others of the same kind.

examples.text: นี่คืออาหารจานโปรดของฉัน
examples.translation: This is my favorite dish.

faults.quote: Use this for both apologizing for a mistake and for getting someone's
faults.why: Restates the two senses directly without adding new usage information.

faults.quote: If you want to be very formal, you can add 'khrap'
faults.why: Adding ครับ/ค่ะ is standard everyday politeness, not 'very formal'.

faults.quote: ขอโทษครับ จะผ่านไปทางนี้ได้ไหม
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing for asking to pass; ขอทางหน่อยครับ is what native speakers say.

notes: In spoken Thai, normally followed by the polite particle ครับ (khráp, male speaker) or ค่ะ (khâ, female speaker): ขอโทษครับ / ขอโทษค่ะ.

senses.definition: Used to apologize for a mistake or inconvenience.

examples.text: ขอโทษที่มาสาย
examples.translation: Sorry for being late.

senses.definition: Used to politely get someone's attention or ask to get past.

examples.text: ขอโทษครับ ห้องน้ำอยู่ที่ไหนครับ
examples.translation: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

faults.quote: Used both to express non-possession (not having something) and non-existence
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses without explaining how they are structured.
Both senses lack examples, though learners need to see possession vs. existence word order.

corrected.shortGloss: to not have; there is no
notes: Literal negation of มี (mii, 'to have / there is'). Placed directly before the noun that is lacking or absent.

senses.definition: To not own, hold, or possess something.

examples.text: วันนี้ฉันไม่มีเวลา
examples.translation: I don't have time today.

senses.definition: Used to say that something or someone is not present or does not exist.

examples.text: ในตู้เย็นไม่มีน้ำ
examples.translation: There is no water in the fridge.

faults.why: Missing irregular present tense stem жив- (живу, живёшь), essential for A2 learners.

notes: Irregular present tense stem жив-: я живу́, ты живёшь, они живу́т. In the past tense, stress moves to the prefix in the negative: не́ жил, не́ жила.
When talking about living in a place, follow жить with в or на and the prepositional case (e.g., жить в Москве).

senses.definition: To have your home in a particular place.

examples.text: Я живу в большом городе.
examples.translation: I live in a big city.

senses.definition: To be alive or spend one's life in a particular way.

examples.text: Мы должны жить и радоваться каждому дню.
examples.translation: We must live and enjoy every day.

faults.quote: Он взял книгу со стола.
faults.why: Uses the perfective partner взять instead of the headword брать.

faults.quote: Мы решили взять машину напрокат на выходные.
faults.why: Uses the perfective partner взять instead of the headword брать.

faults.quote: to take; to catch; to rent
faults.why: Includes 'to catch', which is not covered in the senses.
Does not mention the irregular present tense stem бер- (беру, берёшь).

corrected.shortGloss: to take; to borrow; to rent
notes: Imperfective; pairs with the perfective взять. It has an irregular present tense stem бер-: я беру́, ты берёшь, они беру́т (past: брал, брала́, бра́ли).

senses.definition: To get hold of something with your hands, or to take something with you.

examples.text: Я всегда беру с собой зонт.
examples.translation: I always take an umbrella with me.

senses.definition: To borrow, hire, or rent something for temporary use.

examples.text: В отпуске мы обычно берём машину напрокат.
examples.translation: On vacation we usually rent a car.

faults.quote: to jump; to skip
faults.why: Lists 'to skip' instead of 'to bounce', mismatching the senses.

notes: Use прыгать for general or repeated jumping (imperfective). For a single, completed jump, use the perfective verb прыгнуть.

senses.definition: To push yourself off the ground into the air using your legs.

examples.text: Дети любят прыгать на батуте.
examples.translation: Children love to jump on the trampoline.

senses.definition: To move up and down repeatedly, like a ball.

examples.text: Мяч весело прыгал по дороге.
examples.translation: The ball was bouncing merrily along the road.

faults.why: Does not name the unidirectional partner идти or the stem change (хожу, ходишь).

corrected.shortGloss: to walk; to go; to attend
notes: Multidirectional verb of motion (going on foot repeatedly, habitually, or back and forth); compare unidirectional идти (going one way right now).
Note the consonant change and shifting stress in the present tense: я хожу́, ты хо́дишь, они хо́дят.

senses.definition: To move on foot, or to walk around without a single direction.

examples.text: Я люблю ходить по парку по вечерам.
examples.translation: I like to walk in the park in the evenings.

senses.definition: To go to or attend a place regularly, or to make a round trip.

examples.text: Дети должны ходить в школу каждый день.
examples.translation: Children must go to school every day.

faults.quote: To actively promote an idea, project, or interest.
faults.why: Slang/colloquial usage ('pushing a law'); usually expressed with проталкивать or продвигать.

notes: Imperfective, used for continuous or repeated pushing. For a single, sudden push, use the perfective verb толкнуть.

senses.definition: To press against someone or something with force in order to move them away.

examples.text: Он начал толкать тяжёлую дверь.
examples.translation: He began to push the heavy door.

faults.quote: crop, cultivation
faults.why: 'cultivation' is the act of growing (pertanian/penanaman), not the plant itself.

notes: 'Tanaman' usually refers to cultivated or potted plants (from 'tanam', to plant), whereas 'tumbuhan' refers to any plant, especially in nature or biology.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in soil or a pot, with roots, stems, and leaves.

examples.text: Dia menyiram tanaman di halaman setiap pagi.
examples.translation: She waters the plants in the yard every morning.

senses.definition: Plants grown in large quantities for food or sale.

examples.text: Musim kemarau ini merusak banyak tanaman padi di desa.
examples.translation: This dry season damaged many rice crops in the village.

faults.quote: hand; arm; sleeve; worker
faults.why: 'sleeve' is not in the senses (and means 'lengan baju').

faults.quote: A person who performs manual labor or assists with work.
faults.why: Figurative sense ('tangan kanan' / 'buah tangan' idioms aside) is unnatural as presented in the example.

notes: In everyday Indonesian, 'tangan' covers both the hand and the arm. 'Lengan' specifically refers to the arm (or a shirt sleeve).

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers and palm.

examples.text: Dia melambaikan tangan saat melihat saya.
examples.translation: She waved her hand when she saw me.

senses.definition: The whole upper limb from the shoulder to the hand.

examples.text: Tangan saya pegal setelah mengangkat barang berat.
examples.translation: My arm aches after lifting heavy things.

faults.quote: Use 'tangga' for both the permanent architectural stairs in a house
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown.

notes: To specify a portable ladder, you can say 'tangga lipat' (folding ladder); a single step is 'anak tangga'.

senses.definition: A set of steps for going from one level of a building to another.

examples.text: Dia naik tangga ke lantai dua.
examples.translation: He went up the stairs to the second floor.

senses.definition: A piece of equipment with rungs used for climbing up or down.

examples.text: Tolong ambilkan tangga untuk memperbaiki lampu.
examples.translation: Please get the ladder to fix the light.

faults.quote: It is always followed by a noun, never a verb.
faults.why: False: 'tanpa' is very commonly followed by verbs (e.g. 'tanpa berkata apa-apa', without saying anything).

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'tanpa' is a single-word preposition, not a multi-word expression.

notes: Can be followed by a noun ('tanpa gula', without sugar) or a verb ('tanpa menunggu', without waiting).

senses.definition: Not having, using, or doing something.

examples.text: Dia pergi tanpa payung.
examples.translation: He left without an umbrella.

examples.text: Saya minum kopi tanpa gula.
examples.translation: I drink coffee without sugar.

notes: Do not confuse 'dâu tây' (strawberry) with 'dâu tằm' (mulberry); in casual speech, 'dâu' alone often refers to strawberry.
Takes the classifier 'quả' (Northern) or 'trái' (Southern) for an individual fruit.

senses.definition: A small, sweet red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: Tôi thích ăn dâu tây chấm với sữa đặc.
examples.translation: I like eating strawberries dipped in condensed milk.

faults.quote: /zajŋ͡m˨˩/
faults.why: Wrong IPA; that represents 'dạnh'. Northern IPA for 'dạy' is /zaj˧˨ʔ/.

faults.quote: Can also mean to scold or discipline someone, especially children, to
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding usage info.

faults.quote: The teacher teaches us to learn Vietnamese.
faults.why: Calqued translation; 'dạy học' or 'dạy ... tiếng Việt' means 'teaches us Vietnamese'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'dậy' (to wake up / get up), which is pronounced identically in Northern Vietnamese.
Commonly forms compounds like 'dạy học' (to teach) and 'dạy bảo' (to upbringing/discipline).

senses.definition: To give lessons or show someone how to do something.

examples.text: Cô giáo dạy chúng tôi tiếng Việt.
examples.translation: The teacher teaches us Vietnamese.

senses.definition: To discipline or correct someone's behavior, especially a child's.

examples.text: Mẹ phải dạy lại nó vì dạo này nó hư quá.
examples.translation: Mother has to discipline him because he has been so naughty lately.

faults.quote: /zəˀ/

notes: Antonym: 'khó' (difficult, hard).

senses.definition: Not difficult; requiring little effort to do or understand.

examples.text: Bài tập này rất dễ.
examples.translation: This exercise is very easy.

senses.definition: Used before a verb or adjective: likely or prone to happen.

examples.text: Trời mưa thì đường rất dễ trơn.
examples.translation: When it rains, the road easily gets slippery.

faults.quote: /ɗǐa/

faults.quote: Regardless of the region, the word 'dĩa' is used to refer

Takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc'.

senses.definition: (chiefly Northern) A small tool with long thin points used for picking up food.

examples.text: Cho tôi xin thêm một cái dĩa để ăn bít tết.
examples.translation: Please give me another fork to eat the steak.

senses.definition: (chiefly Southern) A flat, usually round dish from which food is eaten or served.

examples.text: Làm ơn đặt dĩa cơm lên bàn.
examples.translation: Please put the plate of rice on the table.

faults.quote: (tourism) To journey across different regions or countries as a tourist.
faults.why: Both senses mean to travel for pleasure as a tourist; should be merged.

corrected.shortGloss: to travel; to go on a trip
notes: Often preceded by 'đi' ('đi du lịch' = to go traveling / to go on holiday).
Also used as a noun meaning 'tourism' (e.g., 'ngành du lịch' = the tourism industry).

senses.definition: To travel to different places for pleasure and sightseeing.

examples.text: Năm ngoái chúng tôi đi du lịch ở miền Nam.
examples.translation: Last year we traveled in the South.

faults.quote: To spend time studying and mastering new knowledge.
faults.why: Transitive and intransitive uses of 'study' are the same core meaning; 'spending time' is from 花.

senses.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill by studying or practicing.

examples.text: 我在图书馆学习中文。
examples.translation: I am studying Chinese in the library.

examples.text: 他每天晚上都花两个小时学习。
examples.translation: He spends two hours studying every evening.

faults.quote: To reach a desired result or attain a state through searching
faults.why: Finding keys and finding a job are the same sense of 'find' after looking.

faults.quote: Use 找到 when the object was lost or hidden and has
faults.why: Too narrow (misses finding a job/place) and fails to explain 找 (look for) vs. 找到 (find).

notes: Formed from 找 (zhǎo, to look for) + 到 (dào, result complement showing success): 找 is the search, 找到 is the result of finding.
Do not confuse with 发现 (fāxiàn, to discover or notice), which is used for noticing something new or realizing a fact rather than finding what you were looking for.

senses.definition: To successfully locate or get someone or something that was lost or being looked for.

examples.text: 我终于找到了我的钥匙。
examples.translation: I finally found my keys.

examples.text: 他找到了一份好工作。
examples.translation: He found a good job.

faults.quote: To be unfaithful to someone or betray a secret for personal

faults.why: Example uses the compound verb 出卖 (chūmài) instead of the headword 卖.

notes: Opposite of 买 (mǎi, to buy). Be careful with the tones: 卖 (mài, falling tone) means 'to sell', while 买 (mǎi, dipping tone) means 'to buy'.

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: 这家店卖新鲜的水果。
examples.translation: This shop sells fresh fruit.

faults.quote: 跳 (tiào) is used both for physical jumping and for the
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a note on the everyday compound 跳舞 (to dance) is much more useful.

corrected.shortGloss: to jump; to beat (of the heart)
notes: Also appears in the common separable verb 跳舞 (tiàowǔ, to dance).

senses.definition: To push yourself suddenly off the ground using your legs.

examples.text: 他高兴得跳了起来。
examples.translation: He jumped up with joy.

senses.definition: Of a heart, pulse, or eyelid: to move or throb repeatedly.

examples.text: 紧张的时候，我的心跳得很快。
examples.translation: When I am nervous, my heart beats very fast.

faults.quote: 丢 is commonly used when you cannot find an object or
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of explaining how 丢 is used grammatically (both 'to lose' and 'to be lost').

senses.definition: To no longer have something because you do not know where it is, or to go missing.

examples.text: 我的手机丢了。
examples.translation: I lost my phone.

senses.definition: To toss something or get rid of it as unwanted.

examples.text: 把这个垃圾丢进垃圾桶。
examples.translation: Throw this trash into the trash can.

faults.quote: /ˈbard.zɔ/
faults.why: 'dz' in 'bardzo' is an affricate /d͡z/, not a stop-fricative cluster /d.z/.

faults.quote: Lubię cię bardzo.
faults.why: 'Bardzo' naturally precedes the verb in neutral Polish word order ('Bardzo cię lubię').

senses.definition: To a high degree; used with adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: Ten film jest bardzo ciekawy.
examples.translation: This movie is very interesting.

senses.definition: To a great extent or with much feeling; used with verbs.

examples.text: Bardzo cię lubię.
examples.translation: I like you a lot.

faults.quote: (direction) Led astray, wandering, or taking a wrong direction.

faults.why: 'Błędny trop' means 'false/wrong lead' (sense 0), not 'misled' or 'wandering'.

examples.translation: Your calculations are incorrect.

examples.text: To była błędna decyzja.
examples.translation: That was a wrong decision.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'Bez' is a standard preposition (prep), not a multi-word expression.

notes: Requires the genitive case. Before some consonant clusters, it takes the form beze (e.g., beze mnie — without me).

senses.definition: Not having, lacking, or not accompanied by.

examples.text: Piję kawę bez cukru.
examples.translation: I drink coffee without sugar.

examples.text: Wyszedłem z domu bez kluczy.
examples.translation: I left the house without my keys.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'unpaid' (as in 'bezpłatny urlop' - unpaid leave, 'bezpłatny staż').

senses.definition: Costing no money; provided without charge.

examples.text: Wstęp do muzeum jest bezpłatny w każdą środę.
examples.translation: Admission to the museum is free every Wednesday.

senses.definition: Of work or time off: done or taken without receiving pay.

examples.text: Wzięła miesiąc bezpłatnego urlopu.
examples.translation: She took a month of unpaid leave.

faults.quote: /bɛpˈsɛt͡ʂ.nɨ/
faults.why: Corrupted IPA: transposed /s/ and /p/ and dropped /j/. Correct is /bɛsˈpjɛt͡ʂ.nɨ/.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk.

senses.definition: Having the color of snow or milk.

examples.text: Ho comprato una camicia bianca.
examples.translation: I bought a white shirt.

senses.definition: Having no writing, marks, or printing on it.

senses.definition: Having the color of the deep sea or the night sky.

examples.text: Ho comprato una giacca blu per il lavoro.
examples.translation: I bought a blue jacket for work.

faults.why: 'Un brutto sogno' (a bad dream) belongs to sense 1, not physical appearance.

faults.why: With 'tempo' (weather), 'brutto' precedes the noun: 'c'è brutto tempo' or 'il tempo è brutto'.

faults.quote: Used for both physical appearance and general unpleasantness
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; not attractive.

examples.translation: That gray building is really ugly.

senses.definition: Unpleasant, undesirable, or nasty.

examples.text: Ho fatto un brutto sogno stanotte.
examples.translation: I had a bad dream last night.

examples.translation: She is a very kind person to everyone.

examples.text: वह अभी बहुत जवान है।
examples.translation: He is still very young.

faults.quote: Severe, harsh, or stern in nature or behavior.

Do not confuse with कठोर (kaṭhor), which means physically hard, harsh, or strict.

senses.definition: Not easy; requiring great effort, skill, or thought to do, understand, or endure.

senses.definition: Having a high temperature; producing or feeling heat.

examples.text: 趁热喝吧。
examples.translation: Drink it while it's hot.

faults.quote: /krà.paẁ dɛ̂ːn.thaːŋ/
