senses.definition: A small furry domestic animal with four legs, a tail, and whiskers, often kept as a pet.

examples.text: De kat slaapt op de bank.
examples.translation: The cat is sleeping on the couch.

faults.quote: Note that 'keuken' refers both to the physical room where you cook
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses in the entry.

faults.quote: It is a feminine noun, so use 'de' in the singular
faults.why: Restates the article already shown in the headword.

senses.definition: The room in a house or restaurant where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.text: Ik sta in de keuken om het avondeten klaar te maken.
examples.translation: I am in the kitchen preparing dinner.

senses.definition: A style of cooking associated with a particular country or region.

examples.text: Ik hou erg van de Japanse keuken.
examples.translation: I really like Japanese cuisine.

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'kip' is used for both the live bird and the meat
faults.why: Restates the two senses; lacks countability note.

notes: Countable (plural 'kippen') when referring to the bird; uncountable (no article) when referring to the meat.

senses.definition: A common farm bird kept for its eggs and meat.

examples.text: De boer voert elke ochtend de kippen.
examples.translation: The farmer feeds the chickens every morning.

senses.definition: The meat of this bird eaten as food.

examples.text: We eten vanavond kip met rijst en groenten.
examples.translation: We are eating chicken with rice and vegetables tonight.

faults.quote: Used for a person's female child, matching the masculine noun 'hijo'.
faults.why: Restates the definition; fails to mention that plural 'hijos' means 'children'.

notes: The masculine form is 'el hijo' (son). In the plural, 'los hijos' refers to sons or to sons and daughters together ('children').

senses.definition: A female child in relation to her parents.

examples.text: Mi hija mayor estudia en la universidad.
examples.translation: My oldest daughter studies at the university.

faults.quote: The most common confusion is with 'la hoja' (the sheet of paper)
faults.why: Pure filler restating that the word has two senses already listed.

notes: Remember that the 'h' is silent and the 'j' has a strong 'h' sound (/ˈoxa/). Do not confuse it with 'la hija' (daughter).

senses.definition: The flat, typically green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch.

examples.text: En otoño las hojas caen de los árboles.
examples.translation: In autumn the leaves fall from the trees.

senses.definition: A single thin, flat piece of paper used for writing or printing.

examples.text: Necesito una hoja de papel para escribir una carta.
examples.translation: I need a sheet of paper to write a letter.

notes: Use 'la hora' for clock time (¿Qué hora es? — What time is it?), and 'el tiempo' for uncountable time or weather (No tengo tiempo — I don't have time).

senses.definition: The specific point in time shown on a clock or watch.

examples.text: Disculpe, ¿qué hora es?
examples.translation: Excuse me, what time is it?

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: La clase dura una hora.
examples.translation: The class lasts one hour.

faults.quote: Remember that 'isla' is feminine, so it takes 'la isla' and 'una
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the header.

notes: Unlike in English 'island', the 's' in 'isla' is always pronounced.

senses.definition: A piece of land completely surrounded by water.

examples.text: Pasamos las vacaciones en una isla tropical.
examples.translation: We spent our vacation on a tropical island.

faults.quote: (joint) The point or piece where two or more things are joined
faults.why: Technical construction/plumbing sense not needed for an A2 beginner.

notes: In Mexico, 'junta' is the everyday word for a work or school meeting (on par with 'reunión').

senses.definition: A meeting where people gather to discuss work, school, or official matters.

examples.text: Tenemos una junta importante con los directores mañana.
examples.translation: We have an important meeting with the directors tomorrow.

senses.definition: A committee or group of people who manage an organization or govern a country.

examples.text: La junta directiva aprobó el nuevo presupuesto.
examples.translation: The board of directors approved the new budget.

faults.quote: Having characteristics associated with youth, such as energy or freshness.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning ('young/youthful'); should be one sense.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine (um homem jovem, uma mulher jovem); the plural is 'jovens'.
Also used as a noun meaning 'young person' (os jovens = young people).

senses.definition: In the early stage of life, or having the energy and freshness of youth; not old.

examples.text: Ela é muito jovem para entender isso.
examples.translation: She is too young to understand that.

examples.text: Ele tem um espírito jovem.
examples.translation: He has a youthful spirit.

faults.quote: Use 'lavar' for cleaning surfaces or objects with water
faults.why: False restriction: 'lavar' is also standard for body parts (lavar as mãos/o rosto/o cabelo).

faults.quote: /laˈvaɾ/
faults.why: Final /ɾ/ is European/regional; broad Brazilian Portuguese transcription uses /ʁ/ or /h/.

notes: Used for objects (clothes, dishes, a car) and specific body parts (lavar as mãos, lavar o cabelo). For washing your whole body, use 'tomar banho'.

senses.definition: To clean something, or a part of the body, using water and usually soap.

examples.text: Preciso lavar a louça depois do jantar.
examples.translation: I need to wash the dishes after dinner.

examples.text: Lave bem as mãos antes de comer.
examples.translation: Wash your hands well before eating.

notes: When meaning 'to remember', it commonly takes 'de' in Brazil even without 'se': 'Eu lembro da festa' or formally 'Eu me lembro da festa' (I remember the party).
It can also mean 'to remind someone of' by resemblance: 'Ela lembra a mãe' (She looks like / reminds me of her mother).

senses.definition: To keep something in your mind or bring it back into your thoughts.

examples.text: Eu lembro daquele dia na praia.
examples.translation: I remember that day at the beach.

senses.definition: To make someone think of something they might have forgotten, or of someone similar.

examples.text: Você pode me lembrar de comprar leite?
examples.translation: Can you remind me to buy milk?

faults.quote: Used to describe something that moves, happens, or acts at a low
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Do not confuse with 'devagar', which is mainly an adverb ('Ele anda devagar' = He walks slowly). 'Lento' is an adjective and agrees with the noun ('O trânsito está lento', 'A internet está lenta').

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or working at a low speed; not fast.

examples.text: O computador está muito lento hoje.
examples.translation: The computer is very slow today.

faults.quote: Sông is a natural stream of water flowing in a channel
faults.why: Restates the definition; classifier 'con' note is needed instead.

notes: Takes the classifier 'con' (e.g., con sông), except before a river's proper name (e.g., sông Hồng).

senses.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing to the sea, a lake, or another river.

examples.text: Con sông này rất dài và đẹp.
examples.translation: This river is very long and beautiful.

faults.quote: Sống is a versatile verb. Use it to talk about being alive
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses given below.

corrected.shortGloss: to live; to be alive; to reside
notes: For where someone lives, 'sống ở' and simply 'ở' are both common (Tôi sống ở Hà Nội / Tôi ở Hà Nội); 'ở' is shorter and also used for where you are staying or currently are.
As an adjective, 'sống' also means 'raw' or 'undercooked' (cá sống, raw fish).

senses.definition: To have life; to be alive.

examples.text: Mọi sinh vật đều muốn sống.
examples.translation: Every living thing wants to live.

senses.definition: To have your home in a place.

examples.text: Tôi sống ở thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
examples.translation: I live in Ho Chi Minh City.

senses.definition: To spend your life in a particular way.

examples.text: Họ sống rất hạnh phúc.
examples.translation: They live very happily.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'sốt' primarily means a high body temperature or fever.
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving usage such as 'bị sốt' or 'cơn sốt'.

notes: For having a fever, 'sốt' is commonly used with 'bị' (bị sốt, to have a fever) or as a verb/adjective on its own (Em bé đang sốt); the classifier for a bout of fever is 'cơn' (cơn sốt).
In the culinary sense ('sauce', from French 'sauce'), it is also spelled 'xốt'.

senses.definition: An illness or condition in which body temperature is higher than normal.

examples.text: Em bé bị sốt và khóc suốt đêm.
examples.translation: The baby had a fever and cried all night.

senses.definition: A thick liquid served with food to add flavor.

examples.text: Món cá này ăn kèm với sốt cà chua rất ngon.
examples.translation: This fish dish is delicious with tomato sauce.

faults.quote: /sɯ˧ tɨ˦/
faults.why: Wrong vowel and tone for 'tử' (hỏi tone on /ɯ/, not /ɨ˦/).

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with domestic cats (mèo)
faults.why: Absurd warning; nobody confuses the words 'sư tử' and 'mèo'.

notes: Takes the animal classifier 'con' (con sư tử).

senses.definition: A large wild cat of Africa and India, the male of which has a thick mane.

examples.text: Con sư tử đang gầm lên trong rừng.
examples.translation: The lion is roaring in the forest.

corrected.shortGloss: to repair; to fix; to correct
notes: In everyday speech, 'sửa' alone is usually preferred for small items (sửa xe, sửa bài), while 'sửa chữa' sounds more formal or refers to larger maintenance and repair work.
Do not confuse with 'sửa đổi', which means to amend or modify something (such as a law or plan) rather than fix damage.

senses.definition: To put something that is damaged or broken back into good working order.

examples.text: Họ đang sửa chữa con đường này.
examples.translation: They are repairing this road.

senses.definition: To set right a mistake, fault, or shortcoming.

examples.text: Anh ấy nhận ra sai lầm và cố gắng sửa chữa.
examples.translation: He realized his mistake and tried to correct it.

faults.quote: It is neutral and appropriate in almost every situation, whether you are
faults.why: Filler restating the register field; better to note who says it and the standard reply.

notes: Literally 'with safety'. Typically said to the person who is leaving, though also used by both speakers; a common reply is اللّٰه يُسَلِّمُكَ (allāh yusallimuka, 'may God keep you safe').

senses.definition: Said when leaving someone or ending a conversation.

examples.text: سَأَذْهَبُ الآنَ، مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.
examples.translation: I am leaving now, goodbye.

faults.quote: If you are speaking to a woman, use the feminine form 'آسفة'
faults.why: False grammar: 'آسفة' agrees with the speaker's gender (a woman speaking), not the addressee's.

notes: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says آسِف (āsif) and a woman says آسِفَة (āsifa), regardless of who is being spoken to.
Takes the preposition عَلَى (ʿalā) before the thing you are apologizing for.

senses.definition: Feeling or expressing regret for something you have done wrong.

examples.text: أَنَا آسِفٌ عَلَى التَّأْخِيرِ.
examples.translation: I am sorry for the delay.

senses.definition: Feeling or expressing sympathy for someone else's misfortune or bad news.

examples.text: أَنَا آسِفٌ لِسَمَاعِ هٰذَا الْخَبَرِ الْمُحْزِنِ.
examples.translation: I am sorry to hear this sad news.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: Single-word preposition (ظرف/حرف جر), not a multi-word expression.
Missing the common everyday temporal sense ('at, upon, when', e.g., عند الوصول).

notes: Followed by a noun in the genitive case (مَجْرُور) or a pronoun suffix.

With pronoun suffixes it is the standard way to say 'to have': عِنْدِي (ʿindī, 'I have'), عِنْدَكَ (ʿindaka, 'you have'). Unlike مَعَ (maʿa), which means having something on your person right now, عِنْدَ expresses general ownership.

senses.definition: At a place, near something, or at someone's home or workplace.

examples.text: سَأَلْتَقِيكَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
examples.translation: I will meet you at the school gate.

senses.definition: Used with a noun or pronoun to express ownership or possession.

examples.text: عِنْدِي كِتَابٌ جَدِيدٌ.
examples.translation: I have a new book.

senses.definition: At the time of an event or occasion.

examples.text: اتَّصِلْ بِي عِنْدَ الوُصُولِ.
examples.translation: Call me upon arrival.

faults.quote: /laˈkin/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and stress: pronounced /ˈlaːkin/ with a long 'ā' (dagger alif).

faults.quote: الطقس بارد، لَكِنْ الجو جميل.
faults.why: Ungrammatical in MSA: لَكِنْ (with sukūn) cannot precede a nominal clause; requires لَكِنَّ or a verb.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: It is a conjunction, as the sense definition itself says.

faults.quote: Use this to connect two ideas that contrast or contradict each other.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition; missing notes on unvoweled long 'ā' and لَكِنْ vs لَكِنَّ.

notes: Pronounced with a long 'ā' (lākin) even though the alif is not written in standard spelling.
In formal Arabic, لَكِنْ (lākin) is followed by a verb, whereas لَكِنَّ (lākinna) is followed by a noun or pronoun suffix (e.g., لَكِنَّهُ lākinnahu, 'but he').

senses.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what was just said.

examples.text: أَرَدْتُ الذَّهَابَ، لَكِنْ لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ.
examples.translation: I wanted to go, but I could not.

faults.quote: Không is one of the most versatile words in Vietnamese, serving as
faults.why: Restates the three senses instead of adding usage information.

notes: Placed directly before verbs and adjectives to negate them; before nouns, use 'không phải (là)' instead.
At the end of a clause, it often pairs with 'có' before the verb ('có ... không?') to form a yes/no question.

senses.definition: Used before a verb or adjective to make it negative.

examples.text: Tôi không hiểu.
examples.translation: I do not understand.

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer or express refusal.

examples.text: Không, cảm ơn bạn.
examples.translation: No, thank you.

senses.definition: Placed at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.

examples.text: Bạn có mệt không?
examples.translation: Are you tired?

faults.quote: A hard, transparent material used for windows, bottles, or mirrors.
faults.why: 'Kính' is sheet or optical glass (windows, lenses); bottle glass is 'thủy tinh'.

faults.quote: While 'kính' refers to spectacles, it also means the material 'glass'.
faults.why: Restates the two senses and misses the needed contrast with 'thủy tinh'.

notes: For eyeglasses, takes the classifier 'cái' or 'đôi', or is specified as 'kính mắt' (glasses) or 'kính râm' (sunglasses).
As a material, 'kính' refers only to flat panes or lenses (windows, tabletops); glass used for bottles or cups is 'thủy tinh'.

senses.definition: A pair of lenses set in a frame and worn over the eyes to aid vision or protect from the sun.

examples.text: Tôi cần mua một cái kính mới.
examples.translation: I need to buy a new pair of glasses.

senses.definition: Hard, transparent glass made in flat sheets or panes, such as for windows or doors.

examples.text: Cửa sổ này được làm bằng kính.
examples.translation: This window is made of glass.

faults.quote: Use kỳ nghỉ when talking about a planned vacation, holiday, or period
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition without adding usage or contrast.

notes: Refers to a period of time off (such as 'kỳ nghỉ hè', summer vacation), whereas a public or festive holiday is 'ngày lễ'.

senses.definition: A period of time spent away from work or school for rest or travel.

examples.text: Chúng tôi đã có một kỳ nghỉ dài ở biển.
examples.translation: We had a long vacation at the beach.

faults.quote: /kɪ̀ tʰi/
faults.why: Uses English-like '/ɪ/' and grave accent instead of Vietnamese '/i/' and tone marks.

notes: Refers to a formal examination or exam session (such as an entrance or final exam), whereas a smaller classroom test or quiz is 'bài kiểm tra'.

senses.definition: An important official examination or series of tests to assess knowledge or ability.

examples.text: Cô ấy đang chuẩn bị cho kỳ thi cuối năm.
examples.translation: She is preparing for the end-of-year exam.

faults.quote: While 'lá' on its own can mean a leaf, a page, or
faults.why: 'Lá' does not mean a book page ('trang'); it is a classifier for letters/cards.

notes: Literally 'plant leaf'; adding 'cây' distinguishes it from other uses of 'lá' (such as in 'lá thư', letter, or 'lá bài', playing card).
Often takes the classifier 'chiếc' when counting individual fallen leaves.

senses.definition: A flat, usually green part of a plant or tree that grows from a stem or branch.

examples.text: Những chiếc lá cây chuyển sang màu vàng vào mùa thu.
examples.translation: The leaves turn yellow in autumn.

faults.quote: 駅の出口はあちらです。
faults.why: Uses the compound word 出口 (deguchi) instead of the standalone word 口 (kuchi).

faults.quote: While 'kuchi' primarily refers to the mouth on a face, it is
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the two senses.

notes: In compounds, it is often voiced as -guchi and means 'entrance' or 'exit' (e.g., 入口 iriguchi, 出口 deguchi).
Used in many common idioms relating to speech (口が堅い, tight-lipped) and taste (口に合う, to suit one's taste).

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: 口を大きく開けてください。
examples.translation: Please open your mouth wide.

senses.definition: An opening or hole in a container or space.

examples.text: 袋の口をしっかり閉じてください。
examples.translation: Please close the opening of the bag tightly.

senses.definition: One's words, way of speaking, or gossip.

examples.text: 彼は口がうまいから気をつけて。
examples.translation: Be careful, because he has a smooth tongue.

faults.quote: While 橋 is pronounced 'hashi' (with a high-to-low pitch accent), be careful
faults.why: Pitch accents are reversed: in standard Tokyo Japanese, 橋 is low-high and 箸 is high-low.

faults.quote: In Japan, you will often see bridges decorated with traditional motifs, making
faults.why: Cultural trivia unrelated to language usage.

notes: Do not confuse with 箸 (chopsticks) or 端 (edge), which are also spelled 'hashi' in hiragana. In Tokyo Japanese, 橋 rises in pitch (ha-SHI, dropping on a following particle), whereas 箸 starts high and drops (HA-shi).

senses.definition: A structure built over a river, road, or railway to allow people or vehicles to cross.

examples.text: あの橋を渡ってください。
examples.translation: Please cross that bridge.

examples.text: 川に新しい橋がかかりました。
examples.translation: A new bridge was built over the river.

faults.quote: It is distinct from 'kōppu' (コップ), which typically refers to a glass
faults.why: コップ is pronounced 'koppu' with a short 'o' and geminate 'pp', not a long 'kōppu'.

faults.quote: A disposable container or a measurement unit in cooking.
faults.why: Conflates two distinct meanings (disposable cup and cooking measurement) in one sense.

notes: Typically refers to cups with handles (for coffee or tea) or paper/plastic cups. Contrast with コップ (koppu), which usually refers to a drinking glass or tumbler without a handle.
As a cooking measurement in Japan, 1 cup (１カップ) is 200 ml.

senses.definition: A small container, usually with a handle for hot drinks, or made of paper or plastic.

examples.text: コーヒーをカップに注いだ。
examples.translation: I poured the coffee into the cup.

senses.definition: A unit of volume used in cooking, equal to 200 milliliters in Japan.

examples.text: 小麦粉を1カップ加えます。
examples.translation: Add one cup of flour.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (さとう) for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: 砂糖 is the standard term for sugar used in cooking, baking, or
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition and gloss without adding useful learner info.

notes: Often takes the polite prefix お (お砂糖, o-satō) in everyday conversation.
Pronounced the same as the common surname 佐藤 (Satō).

senses.definition: A sweet crystalline substance obtained from plants, used to flavor food and drinks.

examples.text: コーヒーに砂糖を入れますか？
examples.translation: Do you take sugar in your coffee?

faults.why: The name of a person and the name of a thing are the same sense.

faults.quote: あなたの名前は何ですか？
faults.why: Using あなた to ask someone's name is unnatural in Japanese; お名前は？ is natural.

notes: Can refer to a person's full name or just their given name (in contrast to 名字 myōji, surname).
When asking someone for their name, add the polite prefix お: お名前は何ですか (O-namae wa nan desu ka?).

senses.definition: A word or set of words by which a person, place, or thing is known and addressed.

examples.text: お名前を教えていただけますか。
examples.translation: Could you tell me your name?

examples.text: この花の名前を知っていますか。
examples.translation: Do you know the name of this flower?

faults.quote: Use 'estudiar' for the active process of learning...
faults.why: Restates the definition without contrasting it with 'aprender' (to learn).

notes: Refers to the effort of studying; use 'aprender' for the result of actually learning something.

senses.definition: To spend time learning about a subject or preparing for an exam.

examples.text: Tengo que estudiar mucho para el examen de mañana.
examples.translation: I have to study a lot for tomorrow's exam.

senses.definition: To look at or consider something carefully in order to understand it.

examples.text: Vamos a estudiar las opciones antes de decidir.
examples.translation: We are going to examine the options before deciding.

faults.quote: it is usually used reflexively: 'Me extraña que no haya venido'
faults.why: 'Me extraña' is a 'gustar'-type indirect object construction, not a reflexive one.

notes: In Mexico and Latin America, 'extrañar' is the standard verb for missing someone or something (in Spain, 'echar de menos' is more common).

In the sense 'to find strange', it is usually used like 'gustar', with the thing causing surprise as the subject: 'Me extraña su actitud' (His attitude surprises me) or 'Me extraña que no esté aquí' (+ subjunctive).

senses.definition: To feel sad because someone or something is no longer with you.

examples.text: Extraño mucho a mi familia cuando viajo.
examples.translation: I miss my family a lot when I travel.

senses.definition: To seem unusual or unexpected to someone.

examples.text: Me extraña que las tiendas estén cerradas hoy.
examples.translation: I find it strange that the shops are closed today.

faults.quote: /ˈfaθil/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican /s/ (seseo).

faults.quote: Used for tasks or situations that require very little effort.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('un examen fácil', 'una pregunta fácil'); the plural is 'fáciles'.
In colloquial Mexican Spanish, the diminutive 'facilito' is very common and means 'super easy'.

senses.definition: Not difficult; requiring little effort.

examples.text: Es un examen muy fácil.
examples.translation: It is a very easy exam.

examples.text: La tarea fue fácil de terminar.
examples.translation: The homework was easy to finish.

faults.quote: Unlike many Spanish adjectives ending in -z, the plural form is 'felices'
faults.why: All Spanish words ending in -z change z to c in the plural; 'feliz' is regular.

notes: Can be used with both 'ser' (to be a happy person, or to describe a happy time) and 'estar' (to feel happy right now).
Like all Spanish words ending in '-z', the 'z' changes to 'c' in the plural: 'felices'.

senses.definition: Feeling, showing, or causing joy and satisfaction.

examples.text: Ella está muy feliz con su nuevo trabajo.
examples.translation: She is very happy with her new job.

examples.text: Fue un día muy feliz para toda la familia.
examples.translation: It was a very happy day for the whole family.

faults.quote: Used for people, animals, and things that lack visual appeal.
faults.why: Both notes just repeat the two sense definitions without adding grammar or usage info.

notes: In Mexico, 'feo' is also commonly used as an adverb with verbs like 'doler' (to hurt) or 'oler' (to smell) to mean 'badly' or 'terribly': 'Me duele bien feo' (It hurts really bad).

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; lacking beauty or attractiveness.

examples.text: Ese edificio es muy feo.
examples.translation: That building is very ugly.

senses.definition: Of a situation, remark, or weather: unpleasant, unkind, or bad.

examples.text: Me hizo un comentario muy feo.
examples.translation: He made a very nasty comment to me.

faults.quote: Salgo tarde de trabajar porque tengo mucho trabajo hoy.
faults.why: 'Tener mucho trabajo' means workload/tasks, not a paid job or employment.

faults.quote: Use 'el trabajo' when talking about your job or employment
faults.why: Restates the senses already given in the entry.

notes: Also commonly used for the workplace itself ('ir al trabajo', 'estar en el trabajo').
Do not confuse with 'la obra', which refers to a construction site, a play, or a work of art.

senses.definition: A regular activity that you do to earn money, or the place where you do it.

examples.text: Conseguí un buen trabajo en el centro.
examples.translation: I got a good job downtown.

senses.definition: Physical or mental effort used to do something, or tasks to be done.

examples.text: Hoy tengo mucho trabajo en la oficina.
examples.translation: I have a lot of work at the office today.

senses.definition: A task, paper, or project done as schoolwork.

examples.text: Tengo que entregar un trabajo de historia mañana.
examples.translation: I have to hand in a history paper tomorrow.

faults.quote: The set of wheels and other mechanisms used by an aircraft
faults.why: Technical aviation sense ('tren de aterrizaje') is not needed at A2.

faults.quote: Used for both passenger trains and freight trains.
faults.why: Repeats the definition and is just like English 'train'.

notes: To say 'by train', use 'en tren' without an article ('viajar en tren').

senses.definition: A long vehicle made up of connected cars that moves on railway tracks.

examples.text: El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.
examples.translation: The train leaves at eight in the morning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'viajero', which describes someone
faults.why: Unnecessary distinction; 'turista' and 'viajero' parallel English 'tourist' and 'traveler'.

notes: Takes the same form for men and women: 'el turista' (male) and 'la turista' (female).

senses.definition: A person who travels to and visits places for pleasure.

examples.text: El turista toma fotos de la catedral.
examples.translation: The tourist takes photos of the cathedral.

faults.quote: A tube through which blood circulates in the body.
faults.why: Anatomical sense ('vaso sanguíneo') is too technical for A2.

notes: Refers to a drinking glass or a plastic/paper cup without a handle. For the material 'glass', use 'el vidrio'; for a wineglass or stemmed glass, use 'la copa'.

senses.definition: A tall, handleless container made of glass, plastic, or paper, used for drinking or for the amount it holds.

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.translation: I want a glass of cold water.

faults.quote: A person who lives in a town, city, or community.
faults.why: As the note says, neighborhood resident and next-door neighbor are one everyday concept.
Should mention the feminine form 'la vecina' for A2 learners.

notes: The feminine form is 'la vecina'.
Used both for someone living right next door and for fellow residents of the same building or neighborhood ('los vecinos del barrio').

senses.definition: A person who lives next door to you or in the same building or neighborhood.

examples.text: Mi vecino nuevo toca la guitarra por las tardes.
examples.translation: My new neighbor plays the guitar in the afternoons.

faults.quote: In France, 'pantalon' refers to trousers or pants
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful learner information.

notes: Singular in French for a single garment (un pantalon), unlike English 'trousers' or 'pants'.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing that covers the lower body and each leg separately.

examples.text: Il porte un pantalon bleu.
examples.translation: He is wearing blue trousers.

faults.quote: Used both for the material you write on and for
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to note countability and plural usage.

notes: Uncountable for the material (du papier); for a single sheet, use 'une feuille de papier'. In the plural (les papiers), it refers to identity documents.

senses.definition: Thin material in sheets used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'une feuille de papier pour écrire une note.
examples.translation: I need a sheet of paper to write a note.

senses.definition: An official document, or (in the plural) documents proving a person's identity.

examples.text: Il faut garder vos papiers d'identité sur vous.
examples.translation: You must keep your identity papers with you.

faults.quote: A parking fine left on a car's windshield.
faults.why: Dated colloquialism, especially with electronic ticketing; not essential for A2.

faults.quote: A type of tied neckwear shaped like a butterfly.
faults.why: The compound 'nœud papillon' means bow tie, not 'papillon' alone.

notes: Also used in the common compound 'un nœud papillon' (a bow tie) and 'le papillon' for the butterfly stroke in swimming.

senses.definition: An insect with large, often colourful wings that develops from a caterpillar.

examples.text: Un beau papillon jaune s'est posé sur la fleur.
examples.translation: A beautiful yellow butterfly landed on the flower.

faults.quote: park; parking lot; fleet
faults.why: 'fleet' is not in the senses, and 'parking lot' is wrong for standalone 'parc'.

faults.quote: A designated area for parking vehicles.
faults.why: In France, a parking lot is 'un parking' or formally 'parc de stationnement', not 'parc' alone.

faults.quote: Il faut laisser la voiture dans le parc.
faults.why: In French of France, speakers say 'sur le parking', not 'dans le parc'.

notes: Often used in compounds like 'un parc d'attractions' (amusement park) or 'un parc national' (national park). For a car park, everyday French uses 'un parking' (though 'parc de stationnement' is used on formal signs).

senses.definition: A large public area with grass and trees in a town, used for walking and relaxing.

examples.text: Nous aimons nous promener dans le parc le dimanche.
examples.translation: We like to walk in the park on Sundays.

senses.definition: A small enclosed area where a baby or young child can play safely, or an enclosure for animals.

examples.text: Le bébé joue tranquillement dans son parc.
examples.translation: The baby is playing quietly in his playpen.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (さる) for a word written in kanji.

faults.quote: A derogatory term used to describe someone who is foolish
faults.why: Slang/derogatory insult sense is not an everyday A2 meaning; example uses literal simile.

faults.quote: monkey; ape
faults.why: Includes 'ape', which is absent from the sense glosses.

notes: Can also be written in katakana as サル, especially in biological contexts.
Covers both monkeys and tail-less apes, though specific names like ゴリラ (gorilla) are usually preferred for apes.

senses.definition: A furry animal that climbs trees and is closely related to humans.

examples.text: 動物園で猿を見ました。
examples.translation: I saw monkeys at the zoo.

faults.quote: Used for any reflective surface, from small hand mirrors to large
faults.why: Restates the obvious meaning of 'mirror' without adding useful learner information.

notes: Commonly used in the phrase 鏡を見る (kagami o miru, 'to look in the mirror').

senses.definition: A piece of glass that reflects images of people or objects.

examples.text: 鏡で自分の顔を見た。
examples.translation: I looked at my face in the mirror.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (しゅくだい) for a word written in kanji.

faults.quote: In a school context, this refers specifically to assignments given
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Common collocations: 宿題をする (to do homework), 宿題が出る (to be given homework), 宿題を出す (to assign or hand in homework).

senses.definition: School assignments that a student is expected to complete at home.

examples.text: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
examples.translation: I forgot my homework.

senses.definition: An issue or question left to be addressed or decided at a later time.

examples.text: それは次の会議の宿題にしましょう。
examples.translation: Let's leave that as a task for the next meeting.

faults.quote: In Japanese, 'menyuu' is used for both the physical list
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses defined below.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'ryouori' (料理)
faults.why: Misspells the romaji for 料理 as 'ryouori' instead of 'ryouri', and the contrast is unnecessary.

notes: Also used for a list of services and prices at places like hair salons, or a menu on a computer screen.

senses.definition: A list of food and drink options available in a restaurant or cafe.

examples.text: メニューをください。
examples.translation: Please give me the menu.

senses.definition: A set of planned exercises, practices, or tasks.

examples.text: 今日のトレーニングメニューは厳しいです。
examples.translation: Today's training routine is tough.

faults.quote: /kʰaː/
faults.why: Missing rising tone mark on /kʰǎː/.

faults.quote: Besides meaning human and animal legs, 'ขา' is also used
faults.why: merely restates the definitions of the senses without adding grammatical or usage info

faults.quote: It can also be used colloquially to refer to a person
faults.why: merely restates sense 2

notes: Uses the classifier ข้าง (khâang) for a single leg, and คู่ (khûu) for a pair of legs.
Also used in the common expressions ขาไป (khǎa bpai, 'the outbound trip') and ขากลับ (khǎa glàp, 'the return trip').

senses.definition: The limb of a human or animal used for standing and walking.

examples.text: ฉันเจ็บขามากหลังจากไปวิ่ง
examples.translation: My leg hurts a lot after going for a run.

senses.definition: A vertical support of a piece of furniture or part of a garment that covers the leg.

examples.text: โต๊ะตัวนี้ขาหักไปหนึ่งข้าง
examples.translation: This table has one broken leg.

senses.definition: (informal) A regular participant, player, or fan of a particular activity.

examples.text: คืนนี้เราขาดขาช้อปไปหนึ่งคน
examples.translation: Tonight we are missing one shopping buddy.

faults.quote: This is the general term for any kind of bird.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss; misses the required classifier ตัว.

notes: Takes the classifier ตัว (dtua) for individual birds and ฝูง (fǔung) for a flock.

senses.definition: A feathered animal with two wings and a beak that lays eggs and can usually fly.

examples.text: มีนกเกาะอยู่บนกิ่งไม้
examples.translation: There is a bird perched on the tree branch.

faults.quote: /kʰwaːm.faːn/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and missing rising tone on ฝัน; should be /kʰwaːm.fǎn/.

faults.quote: It can refer both to the mental activity during sleep and
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given below.

notes: Formed with the prefix ความ- (khwaam-), which turns the verb ฝัน (fǎn, 'to dream') into an abstract noun. In everyday speech, ฝัน alone is often used as a noun too.

senses.definition: Images, thoughts, or feelings experienced while sleeping.

examples.text: ฉันจำความฝันเมื่อคืนไม่ได้เลย
examples.translation: I cannot remember last night's dream at all.

senses.definition: An ambition, hope, or goal for the future.

examples.text: การเป็นนักดนตรีคือความฝันของเขา
examples.translation: Being a musician is his dream.

faults.quote: Used as the standard term for a male parent.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful learner information.

notes: Often preceded by คุณ (khun) as คุณพ่อ (khun phâaw) to sound more polite, especially when speaking about someone else's father.
Also used before a mother's or child's name, or by older men as a warm first-person pronoun ('I') when speaking to younger people.

senses.definition: A male parent.

examples.text: พ่อของฉันทำอาหารเก่งมาก
examples.translation: My dad is very good at cooking.

faults.quote: /châw.mɔːŋ/
faults.why: Wrong consonant symbol /ch/, wrong vowel /âw/, and wrong vowel /ɔː/; should be /tɕʰûa.moːŋ/.

faults.quote: hour
faults.why: Does not include the second sense (class period/lesson).

faults.quote: Used both for a clock hour of sixty minutes and for
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the useful abbreviation ชม. and classifier note.

notes: As a time unit, it is placed directly after a number without a separate classifier (e.g., สองชั่วโมง, 'two hours'). Commonly abbreviated in writing as ชม.

senses.definition: A period of time lasting sixty minutes.

examples.text: ฉันรอเขามาหนึ่งชั่วโมงแล้ว
examples.translation: I have been waiting for him for an hour.

senses.definition: A scheduled class period or lesson at school.

examples.text: เรามีชั่วโมงภาษาไทยตอนบ่าย
examples.translation: We have a Thai class in the afternoon.

faults.quote: Used for both physical markets (like a farmer's market) and the
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses already listed in the entry.

faults.quote: Κάνω την αγορά των δώρων μέσω διαδικτύου.
faults.why: Stilted nominalization; in plural 'αγορές' is natural for shopping, singular is a single purchase.

notes: Do not confuse with 'το μαγαζί' (shop), which is a single store; 'η αγορά' is an open-air market or shopping area.
In the plural ('οι αγορές'), it often means 'shopping' or 'purchases' (e.g., 'κάνω αγορές' — to go shopping).

senses.definition: An area or street with many stalls or shops where people go to buy food and other goods.

examples.text: Πήγαμε νωρίς το πρωί στην αγορά για φρέσκα φρούτα.
examples.translation: We went to the market early in the morning for fresh fruit.

senses.definition: The act of buying something, or the thing bought.

examples.text: Η αγορά του αυτοκινήτου ήταν μια καλή απόφαση.
examples.translation: The purchase of the car was a good decision.

senses.definition: The business and trade of buying and selling goods in a country or area.

examples.text: Η αγορά είναι ασταθής αυτή την περίοδο.
examples.translation: The market is unstable during this period.

faults.quote: Used both for a personal name and for one's reputation
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.
Missing note on irregular neuter declension in -μα (genitive 'του ονόματος', plural 'τα ονόματα').

notes: To ask 'What is your name?', Greek usually uses 'Πώς σε λένε;' (literally 'How do they call you?') rather than 'το όνομα'.
Declines with an extra syllable in the genitive ('του ονόματος') and plural ('τα ονόματα').

senses.definition: The word or words that a person, animal, or thing is known by.

examples.text: Το όνομά του είναι Γιώργος.
examples.translation: His name is George.

senses.definition: The opinion that people have about someone or something.

examples.text: Έχει καλό όνομα στην αγορά.
examples.translation: He has a good reputation in the market.

faults.quote: As a neuter noun, it takes the article 'το' in the
faults.why: Restates the gender and the article already shown in the headword.

notes: In the plural ('τα νερά') or with 'ένα' ('ένα νερό'), it often means a bottle or glass of water when ordering.

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain and that people, animals, and plants need to live.

examples.text: Θέλω ένα ποτήρι νερό, παρακαλώ.
examples.translation: I want a glass of water, please.

faults.quote: Used to address or refer to the brother of one's mother
faults.why: Repeats the definition word for word.

notes: The feminine form is 'η θεία' (aunt); in the plural, 'οι θείοι' can mean 'uncle and aunt' together.
Also used affectionately by children to address an older family friend.

senses.definition: The brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt.

examples.text: Ο θείος μου μένει στην Αθήνα.
examples.translation: My uncle lives in Athens.

faults.quote: Used both literally for tasting food and figuratively for experiencing feelings
faults.why: Restates the two senses; missing the irregular stem change (tat- -> tad-) and accusative case.

faults.quote: İlk defa zaferin tadını tatmak harika bir duyguydu.
faults.why: Pleonastic ('tasting the taste of victory'); natural Turkish uses 'zaferi tatmak'.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case (-ı/-i/-u/-ü).
The final 't' softens to 'd' before a vowel suffix (e.g., tadıyor, tadacak).

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to test its flavour.

examples.text: Çorbayı tatmak için bir kaşık aldı.
examples.translation: He took a spoonful to taste the soup.

senses.definition: To experience or feel something, often for the first time.

examples.text: İlk defa zaferi tatmak harika bir duyguydu.
examples.translation: Tasting victory for the first time was a great feeling.

faults.why: Turkish 'tavşan' covers both rabbit and hare as a single everyday concept.

notes: Covers both 'rabbit' and 'hare'; when a distinction is needed, 'ada tavşanı' means rabbit and 'yaban tavşanı' means hare.

senses.definition: A small mammal with long ears, soft fur, and strong back legs for hopping.

examples.text: Bahçede küçük bir tavşan zıplıyor.
examples.translation: A small rabbit is hopping in the garden.

faults.quote: Tavuk is used both for the live farm bird and for the
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a contrast with 'horoz' (rooster) and 'piliç' is more useful.

faults.quote: Akşam yemekte tavuk yedik.
faults.why: 'Akşam yemeğinde' is the natural phrasing for 'for dinner', and 'in the evening' is redundant.

notes: Specifically refers to the female bird (hen) as well as the species in general; a rooster is 'horoz'.

senses.definition: A common farm bird kept for its eggs and meat, especially the female.

examples.text: Bahçede birkaç tavuk geziniyor.
examples.translation: A few chickens are wandering around in the garden.

senses.definition: The meat of this bird used as food.

examples.text: Akşam yemeğinde tavuk yedik.
examples.translation: We ate chicken for dinner.

faults.why: Both senses and examples describe the same core meaning ('dangerous/unsafe'); the split is artificial.

notes: Formed from 'tehlike' (danger) + '-li' (having).
Compare 'riskli' (risky), which often implies a chance of failure or loss rather than direct harm.

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or serious trouble; not safe.

examples.text: Bu köpek çok tehlikeli, yaklaşma.
examples.translation: This dog is very dangerous, do not get close.

examples.text: Gece yalnız yürümek bu mahallede tehlikeli.
examples.translation: Walking alone at night in this neighborhood is dangerous.

faults.quote: Yaz aylarında teknelerle den açılıyorlar.
faults.why: Corrupt word 'den' instead of 'denize' (to sea), making the sentence ungrammatical.

faults.quote: A large, shallow container used for mixing or kneading dough.
faults.why: Traditional kneading trough is a rare/rural sense not needed by an A2 learner.

faults.quote: While tekne most commonly means a boat or vessel, it can also
faults.why: Simply repeats the definitions in the senses.

notes: Usually refers to a small or medium-sized boat (such as a fishing boat or yacht), whereas 'gemi' refers to a large ship and 'kayık' to a small rowboat.

senses.definition: A small or medium-sized watercraft for travelling on water.

examples.text: Yaz aylarında teknelerle denize açılıyorlar.
examples.translation: In the summer months, they go out to sea in boats.

faults.quote: /bylˈmak/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: Turkish 'u' is /u/, not front rounded /y/.

faults.quote: Bulmak is the standard verb for locating something lost or hidden
faults.why: merely restates the two senses and examples already given in the entry.

notes: Forms the aorist with -ur: bulur (he/she finds).

senses.definition: To discover where something or someone is, or to get something needed.

examples.text: Anahtarlarımı sonunda buldum.
examples.translation: I finally found my keys.

senses.definition: To have a certain opinion or judgment about something.

examples.text: Bu şehri çok pahalı buluyorum.
examples.translation: I find this city very expensive.

faults.quote: /bylyʃˈmak/
faults.why: Wrong vowels: Turkish 'u' is /u/, not front rounded /y/.

faults.quote: Takes the dative case (-e/-a) for the person or place
faults.why: False grammar: takes comitative (-le/-la) for the person and locative (-de/-da) for the place.

notes: Takes -(y)le (with) for the person you meet and -de/-da (at/in) for the place: arkadaşımla kafede buluşmak (to meet my friend at the café).
Refers to meeting by arrangement; for meeting someone for the first time, use 'tanışmak'.

senses.definition: To come together with someone at an agreed time and place.

examples.text: Yarın akşam saat sekizde kafede buluşalım.
examples.translation: Let's meet at the café tomorrow evening at eight o'clock.

senses.definition: Of roads, rivers, or lines: to join at a common point.

examples.text: Bu iki nehir vadinin sonunda buluşuyor.
examples.translation: These two rivers meet at the end of the valley.

faults.quote: Do not confuse bulut with buz (ice).
faults.why: Pure filler: 'bulut' and 'buz' are not easily confused.

senses.definition: A white or grey mass in the sky made of small drops of water.

examples.text: Gökyüzünde tek bir bulut bile yok.
examples.translation: There is not a single cloud in the sky.

faults.quote: /buɾaˈda/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'burada' is stressed on the first syllable (/ˈbuɾada/).

notes: Stressed on the first syllable; in everyday speech the middle vowel is often dropped, sounding like 'burda'.
Contrasts with 'şurada' (right over there, nearby) and 'orada' (there, further away).

senses.definition: In or at this place.

examples.text: Ben burada bekliyorum.
examples.translation: I am waiting here.

examples.text: Anahtar burada.
examples.translation: The key is here.

faults.quote: Beyond the face, 'burun' is also used for geographical capes
faults.why: Restates the senses already listed in the entry.

notes: When a suffix starting with a vowel is added, the second 'u' drops: burun → burnu (its nose), burnum (my nose).

senses.definition: The part of the face used for breathing and smelling.

examples.text: Soğuk havada burnum hep kızarır.
examples.translation: My nose always gets red in cold weather.

senses.definition: A narrow piece of land that sticks out into the sea.

examples.text: Gemi kayalık burundan güvenle döndü.
examples.translation: The ship safely rounded the rocky cape.

senses.definition: The front end of a ship, boat, aircraft, or shoe.

examples.text: Uçağın burnu bulutların arasından göründü.
examples.translation: The nose of the plane appeared from among the clouds.

faults.quote: (page) A single page or sheet showing a specific month
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the same noun; 'page' comes from the classifier 页.
Missing the standard classifiers 本 (book/pad) and 张 (sheet).

notes: Takes the classifier 本 (běn) for a calendar pad or book, or 张 (zhāng) and 页 (yè) for a single sheet.
Also used for the calendar app on a phone or computer.

senses.definition: A chart, set of pages, or app showing the days, weeks, and months of a year.

examples.text: 我在日历上记下了看医生的日子。
examples.translation: I marked the day of the doctor's visit on the calendar.

faults.quote: 礼物 (lǐwù) is the standard word for a present or gift
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definition instead of giving useful grammar such as classifiers.

notes: Takes the classifiers 件 (jiàn) or 份 (fèn); 买一份礼物 (to buy a gift), 送礼物 (to give a gift).

senses.definition: Something that you give to someone on a special occasion or to thank them.

examples.text: 我在商店买了一份生日礼物。
examples.translation: I bought a birthday gift at the shop.

faults.quote: It is often used as a treat or gift. Since it is
faults.why: Wordy filler; classifier info should be concise and include 盒 (box) and 颗 (piece).

notes: Loanword from English 'chocolate'.
Common classifiers: 块 (kuài, piece or bar), 颗 (kē, small piece), and 盒 (hé, box).

senses.definition: A sweet brown food or candy made from cocoa beans.

examples.text: 我想吃一块巧克力。
examples.translation: I want to eat a piece of chocolate.

faults.quote: Paper money, specifically used in older or formal contexts; also refers to
faults.why: Conflates two unrelated meanings (banknote and ballot/vote) into one sense.

faults.quote: banknote
faults.why: Alone, 票 rarely means banknote in modern everyday speech (钞票 or 票子 is used).

faults.quote: In Chinese, '票' is a versatile word used for any small piece
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the essential classifier 张 (zhāng).

notes: Takes the classifier 张 (zhāng). Often combined with the vehicle or event: 火车票 (train ticket), 电影票 (movie ticket), 机票 (plane ticket).

senses.definition: A printed piece of paper or electronic record that gives you the right to travel or enter an event.

examples.text: 我要买一张去上海的票。
examples.translation: I want to buy a ticket to Shanghai.

senses.definition: A ballot or vote in an election or poll.

examples.text: 他得到了很多票。
examples.translation: He got a lot of votes.

faults.quote: Do not confuse the shower 'regadera' with a garden watering can
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: I like to sing when I am under the shower.
faults.why: Calque of 'bajo la regadera'; natural English is 'in the shower'.

notes: In Mexico, 'la regadera' is the everyday word for the shower (along with the phrase 'bañarse en la regadera', to take a shower), whereas in Spain and several other countries 'la ducha' is used.

senses.definition: A bathroom fixture that sprays water on you so you can wash.

examples.text: Me gusta cantar cuando estoy en la regadera.
examples.translation: I like to sing when I am in the shower.

senses.definition: A container with a spout used for watering plants.

examples.text: Llena la regadera con agua fresca para las flores del jardín.
examples.translation: Fill the watering can with fresh water for the garden flowers.

faults.quote: A collection of garments that are going to be washed
faults.why: Being washed is a context of 'ropa' (clothes), not a separate sense.

notes: 'La ropa' is an uncountable singular noun (e.g., 'mucha ropa sucia' — 'a lot of dirty clothes'). To count individual items, use 'una prenda (de ropa)'.

senses.definition: Things that you wear to cover your body, such as shirts, pants, and dresses.

examples.text: Guarda tu ropa en el clóset.
examples.translation: Put your clothes away in the closet.

examples.text: Tengo que lavar y tender la ropa hoy.
examples.translation: I have to wash and hang out the laundry today.

faults.quote: Used on almost every savory dish at the table
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia about salt rather than a language usage note.

notes: Although it ends in a consonant, 'la sal' is a feminine noun (e.g., 'la sal fina').

senses.definition: A white substance obtained from sea water or mines, used to season and preserve food.

examples.text: Le falta un poco de sal a la sopa.
examples.translation: The soup needs a little bit of salt.

faults.quote: In Mexico and many other Spanish-speaking countries, 'la sala' is the
faults.why: Note [0] restates sense 0; note [1] compares unrelated words.

notes: In Mexico, 'la sala' is the standard word for the living room at home (called 'el salón' in Spain or 'el living' in parts of South America). In public buildings, it often appears in compounds like 'sala de espera' (waiting room) or 'sala de cine' (movie theater auditorium).

senses.definition: The main room in a home used for sitting, relaxing, and entertaining guests.

examples.text: Toda la familia está reunida en la sala.
examples.translation: The whole family is gathered in the living room.

senses.definition: A room or hall in a public building used for a particular purpose, such as waiting, meetings, or showing movies.

examples.text: Esperamos una hora en la sala de espera del hospital.
examples.translation: We waited for an hour in the hospital waiting room.

faults.quote: Note that 'sangre' is a feminine noun, so you must use
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the gender field and the senses already shown.

notes: To say that a body part is bleeding, Spanish commonly uses the verb 'sangrar' or the phrase 'salir sangre' (e.g., 'Me sale sangre de la nariz' — 'My nose is bleeding').

senses.definition: The red liquid that flows through the body of humans and animals.

examples.text: Se cortó el dedo y le salió un poco de sangre.
examples.translation: He cut his finger and a little blood came out.

senses.definition: Family origins or heritage, especially as the source of someone's traits.

examples.text: La música es algo que llevan en la sangre.
examples.translation: Music is something that is in their blood.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'occhiali da sole', which specifically means sunglasses.
faults.why: 'Occhiali da sole' is a subtype/collocation, not a confusable false friend.

notes: Always masculine plural in Italian, even when referring to a single pair (un paio di occhiali).
Takes the article 'gli' (and plural 'degli', 'agli'). Common collocation: 'occhiali da sole' (sunglasses).

senses.definition: Lenses in a frame worn on the face to see better or to protect the eyes.

examples.text: Ho dimenticato gli occhiali sul tavolo della cucina.
examples.translation: I forgot my glasses on the kitchen table.

faults.quote: Of an advanced age, no longer a young person or child.
faults.why: Saying 'of an advanced age' is misleading; 'grande' means grown-up or older, not elderly.

faults.quote: grown-up, old, adult
faults.why: 'Old' (elderly) is 'vecchio' or 'anziano'; 'grande' means grown-up or older (than someone).

notes: When placed after a noun, 'grande' usually refers to physical size ('big', 'large'); before a noun, it often means 'great' or 'wonderful'.
Before singular nouns starting with a consonant (except s + consonant, z, x, gn, ps), it often shortens to 'gran' (e.g., 'un gran bel film', 'una gran donna').

senses.definition: Of large physical size or larger than average.

examples.text: Ho visto un cane grande nel parco.
examples.translation: I saw a big dog in the park.

senses.definition: Of a person: no longer a child, or older than another child or sibling.

examples.text: Quando sarò grande, voglio viaggiare.
examples.translation: When I grow up, I want to travel.

senses.definition: Of high importance, value, or quality.

examples.text: Quella è stata una grande festa.
examples.translation: That was a great party.

faults.quote: adj
faults.why: 'Gratis' is primarily an adverb ('for free') and also used as an invariable adjective.

notes: Used both as an invariable adjective (never changes form for gender or number) and as an adverb ('entrare gratis' = to get in for free).
Unlike 'libero' (free as in available or not busy), 'gratis' (or 'gratuito') is strictly about costing no money.

senses.definition: Costing no money; without charge.

examples.text: Il caffè è gratis oggi per tutti i clienti.
examples.translation: Coffee is free today for all customers.

faults.quote: (refusal) An expression used to politely decline something. | glosses en: no thank you
faults.why: 'Grazie' alone does not mean 'no thank you' in Italian (unlike French 'merci').

faults.quote: Used constantly in daily conversation to express gratitude.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful usage information; misses the preposition 'di'/'per' or 'grazie a'.

notes: Followed by 'di' or 'per' before a noun or infinitive ('grazie di tutto', 'grazie per l'aiuto'). 'Grazie a' means 'thanks to'.
Can be intensified as 'grazie mille' (thanks a lot).Note that 'grazie tante' is often used ironically.

senses.definition: An expression used to show that you are grateful to someone, or when politely accepting or declining an offer.

examples.text: Grazie per l'aiuto!
examples.translation: Thanks for the help!

examples.text: No, grazie, non ho fame.
examples.translation: No, thank you, I'm not hungry.

faults.quote: Guarda lavagna, per favore.
faults.why: Ungrammatical Italian: missing the definite article 'la' ('Guarda la lavagna').

faults.quote: Use 'guardare' when you direct your eyes at someone or something
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions instead of noting that 'guardare' takes a direct object without a preposition.

notes: Takes a direct object with no preposition in Italian: 'guardare qualcosa' = to look AT something.
Do not confuse with 'vedere' (to see), which refers to perceiving with the eyes rather than intentionally looking or watching.

senses.definition: To turn your eyes towards something or someone in order to see them.

examples.text: Guarda la lavagna, per favore.
examples.translation: Look at the board, please.

senses.definition: To look at something with attention for a period of time, such as a television show, a match, or a film.

examples.text: Stasera voglio guardare un bel film.
examples.translation: Tonight I want to watch a good movie.

faults.quote: يَومٌ سَعِيدٌ لَكَ. — Have a lucky/fortunate day.
faults.why: Means 'happy day', not 'lucky'; translation is forced to fit the sense.

faults.quote: This is the standard word for happy.
faults.why: Restates the gloss; missing the irregular plural (سُعَدَاء) and preposition (بِـ).

notes: Followed by the preposition بِـ (bi-) for the cause of happiness: سَعِيدٌ بِـ (happy with/about). The masculine plural is irregular: سُعَدَاء (suʿadāʾ).
Also very common as a male given name (Said).

senses.definition: Feeling or bringing pleasure and contentment.

examples.text: أَنَا سَعِيدٌ بِلِقَائِكَ.
examples.translation: I am happy to meet you.

senses.definition: Having or marked by good luck.

examples.text: أَتَمَنَّى لَكَ حَظًّا سَعِيدًا.
examples.translation: I wish you good luck.

faults.why: Note mentions objects and abstract things, which are everyday meanings missing from senses.

notes: The masculine plural is irregular: أَقْوِيَاء (ʾaqwiyāʾ).
Often used as a noun meaning 'a strong person' (الْقَوِيّ) or 'the strong' (الْأَقْوِيَاء).

senses.definition: Having great physical power, or able to withstand force without breaking.

examples.text: الرَّجُلُ قَوِيٌّ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: The man is very strong.

senses.definition: Having force of character, influence, or intensity.

examples.text: لَدَيْهَا شَخْصِيَّةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ.
examples.translation: She has a strong personality.

examples.text: هَبَّتْ رِيحٌ قَوِيَّةٌ.
examples.translation: A strong wind blew.

faults.quote: Something that costs little money or is available at a low price.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Something that...').

notes: Primarily describes a low price (the opposite of غَالٍ, expensive), though it can also describe goods as cheap or shoddy.

senses.definition: Costing little money; low in price.

examples.text: هَذَا الْقَمِيصُ رَخِيصٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This shirt is very cheap.

faults.why: 'Cold' for weather and 'cold' for objects/drinks are the same literal meaning.

faults.quote: Used for both weather and objects like water or food.
faults.why: Obvious from the English gloss 'cold'.

notes: Describes temperature (the opposite of حَارّ, hot). To say a person feels cold, use بَرْدَان (bardān), not بَارِد.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm or hot.

examples.text: الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ الْيَوْمَ.
examples.translation: The weather is cold today.

examples.text: أُرِيدُ مَاءً بَارِدًا.
examples.translation: I want cold water.

faults.quote: you can also use 'شَابّ' (shābb) specifically for a young person
faults.why: شَابّ means a youth/young adult, whereas صَغِير for age means a young child or younger.

notes: The masculine plural is irregular: صِغَار (ṣiḡār). Often specified as صَغِيرُ السِّنّ (young in age) when referring to age.

senses.definition: Not large in size, amount, or scale.

examples.text: هَذَا بَيْتٌ صَغِيرٌ.
examples.translation: This is a small house.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: in an early stage of life, or younger than another.

examples.text: لَدَيَّ أَخٌ صَغِيرٌ.
examples.translation: I have a little brother.

faults.why: Hiragana reading おす is missing for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: 圧す (also read osu), which is a more formal or kanji-specific way of saying to press or stamp/seal.
faults.why: Stamping a seal is 捺す, not 圧す; 押す itself is standard for stamping.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to stamp (a seal)' (ハンコを押す).

corrected.shortGloss: to push; to press; to stamp
notes: Godan verb (押さない, 押します, 押して). Its opposite on doors and signs is 引く (hiku, 'to pull').

senses.definition: To use physical force to move something away from yourself.

examples.text: 重いドアを一生懸命押した。
examples.translation: I pushed the heavy door with all my might.

senses.definition: To press a button, key, or switch to operate something.

examples.text: エレベーターのボタンを押してください。
examples.translation: Please press the elevator button.

senses.definition: To stamp a seal or mark onto paper.

examples.text: ここにハンコを押してください。
examples.translation: Please stamp your seal here.

faults.quote: If you are just making a simple mark or a line, use 書く (kaku) instead.
faults.why: In everyday speech 描く is normally read かく for drawing pictures; えがく is literary/figurative.

faults.quote: 鉛筆で猫を描く。
faults.why: Under reading えがく, sketching a cat with a pencil is unnatural (that uses かく).

corrected.shortGloss: to paint; to depict; to picture
notes: Godan verb. The kanji 描く has two readings: in everyday speech, drawing a picture is usually pronounced かく (kaku). The reading えがく (egaku) is more formal or literary, and is also used for portraying a theme in art or picturing something in one's mind.

senses.definition: To paint, draw, or portray a scene or subject in a work of art or writing.

examples.text: この小説は家族の愛を描いている。
examples.translation: This novel depicts family love.

senses.definition: To imagine or visualize a scene or future in one's mind.

examples.text: 未来の姿を心に描く。
examples.translation: I picture the future in my mind.

faults.quote: (facilitate) To perform an action that makes a task or situation easier for someone else.
faults.why: 手伝う means helping someone do a task, not an inanimate tool facilitating work.

faults.quote: このツールは仕事を早く終わらせることを手伝います。
faults.why: Unnatural English calque; inanimate tools do not take 手伝う with a こと-clause.

notes: Godan verb (手伝わない, 手伝います, 手伝って). Takes を for the task or person you help (母を手伝う, 料理を手伝う).
Used for pitching in with work or chores. For saving someone from danger or trouble, use 助ける (tasukeru).

senses.definition: To help someone by doing part of their work or chores with them.

examples.text: 母の料理を手伝います。
examples.translation: I help my mother with the cooking.

examples.text: 引っ越しを手伝ってくれませんか。
examples.translation: Could you help me with my move?

faults.why: Hiragana reading まつ is missing for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: (anticipation) To anticipate or look forward to something with expectation.
faults.why: 待つ simply means 'to wait for / await'; 'look forward to' is 楽しみにする.

faults.quote: Often confused with 'to hang on' (matte), but 'matsu' is the general verb
faults.why: 待って is just the te-form of 待つ; both notes are unhelpful filler.

notes: Godan verb (待たない, 待ちます, 待って). Takes を for the person or thing waited for (バスを待つ, 'to wait for the bus').
The te-form 待って is very common in requests: ちょっと待ってください ('Please wait a moment').

senses.definition: To stay in a place or delay acting until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: 駅で友達を待つ。
examples.translation: I wait for my friend at the station.

examples.text: 少し待ってください。
examples.translation: Please wait a moment.

faults.quote: Note that it is a weak noun in the plural
faults.why: Ohr is a mixed noun (genitive des Ohres, plural die Ohren), not a weak noun.

notes: Irregular plural: die Ohren (despite taking -es/-e in the singular genitive: des Ohres).

senses.definition: The organ of the body used for hearing.

examples.text: Sie hat sich beim Spielen das Ohr leicht verletzt.
examples.translation: She slightly hurt her ear while playing.

senses.definition: The ability to recognize and appreciate sounds, especially in music or language.

examples.text: Er hat ein gutes Ohr für Musik.
examples.translation: He has a good ear for music.

faults.quote: Note that 'Öl' is used both for cooking oil and for machine
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the two senses; English 'oil' works the exact same way.
Cooking oil and engine/fuel oil are one general concept ('oil'), or at minimum need no note.

notes: Usually uncountable in everyday use; the plural die Öle refers to different types of oil.

senses.definition: A smooth, thick liquid made from plants or animals, used in cooking.

examples.text: Ich brauche etwas Öl für den Salat.
examples.translation: I need some oil for the salad.

senses.definition: A thick liquid from the ground or made artificially, used as fuel or to make machines run smoothly.

examples.text: Das Auto braucht neues Öl.
examples.translation: The car needs new oil.

faults.quote: whereas 'ein Paar' can simply mean two random objects.
faults.why: 'Ein Paar' (capitalized) means a matching pair or couple, never two random objects.

notes: Do not confuse capitalized ein Paar ('a pair' or 'a couple') with lowercase ein paar ('a few', e.g. ein paar Minuten).

senses.definition: Two things of the same type that belong or are used together.

examples.text: Ich brauche ein neues Paar Schuhe.
examples.translation: I need a new pair of shoes.

senses.definition: Two people who are married, in a romantic relationship, or doing something together.

examples.text: Sie sind ein glückliches Paar.
examples.translation: They are a happy couple.

faults.quote: In a work or academic context, the plural 'Papiere' can also mean
faults.why: Restates sense 1, and ID papers are not specific to work or academic contexts.

notes: As a material, Papier is uncountable; for a single sheet, say ein Blatt Papier. In the plural (die Papiere), it usually means official identity documents.

senses.definition: A thin material made from wood, used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

examples.text: Ich brauche ein neues Blatt Papier für den Drucker.
examples.translation: I need a new sheet of paper for the printer.

senses.definition: Official documents, especially those proving a person's identity (usually in the plural).

examples.text: Haben Sie alle Ihre Papiere bei sich?
examples.translation: Do you have all your papers with you?

faults.quote: The liquid that falls from the sky as rain.
faults.why: 'Agua' for rain is mainly in fixed phrases; in Mexico 'agua' also commonly means 'agua fresca'.

notes: Feminine, but takes the masculine singular articles 'el' and 'un' when they come right before it (el agua fría, las aguas frías).
In Mexico, 'un agua' or 'agua de sabor' refers to 'agua fresca', a popular drink made from fruit, flowers, or grains blended with water and sugar.

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain and that people, animals, and plants need to live.

examples.text: Tengo sed, por favor dame un vaso de agua.
examples.translation: I am thirsty, please give me a glass of water.

senses.definition: In Mexico, a non-alcoholic drink made of water, sugar, and fruit, grains, or flowers.

examples.text: Me da un agua de jamaica, por favor.
examples.translation: Can I have a hibiscus water, please?

faults.quote: A person with whom you have a romantic relationship
faults.why: Unlike German/French, Spanish 'amigo' does not mean 'boyfriend'; that is 'novio' or 'pareja'.

notes: The feminine form is 'la amiga'; the plural 'los amigos' can refer to male friends or a mixed group.
In Mexico, calling someone 'amigo' or 'amiga' is common in polite casual interactions with strangers, such as shopkeepers or waiters.

senses.definition: A person you know well, like, and trust, who is not typically a family member.

examples.text: Mi mejor amigo vive cerca de mi casa.
examples.translation: My best friend lives near my house.

faults.quote: In Spanish, 'animal' includes everything from insects to humans
faults.why: Explains scientific biology rather than Spanish usage; adds nothing over English 'animal'.

faults.quote: When used to describe a person, 'ser un animal' can mean
faults.why: merely restates sense 1.

senses.definition: A living creature such as a dog, bird, or insect, that is not a plant or a human.

examples.text: El perro es mi animal favorito.
examples.translation: The dog is my favorite animal.

senses.definition: An insulting term for a person who behaves roughly, rudely, or without manners.

examples.text: No comas así, pareces un animal.
examples.translation: Don't eat like that, you're acting like an animal.

faults.quote: A duration of twelve consecutive months.
faults.why: Calendar year and a twelve-month period are shades of one meaning, both translated 'year'.

notes: Do not drop the tilde on 'ñ': 'ano' means 'anus'.
To say someone's age, Spanish uses 'tener' + number + 'años': 'Tengo veinte años' (I am twenty years old).

senses.definition: A period of twelve months, either from January 1 to December 31 or as a unit of time and age.

examples.text: Este año voy a viajar mucho.
examples.translation: This year I am going to travel a lot.

examples.text: Viví en México por un año entero.
examples.translation: I lived in Mexico for a whole year.

faults.quote: Use this adjective for anything covered in liquid, most commonly water.
faults.why: First sentence merely restates the definition.

notes: Passive participle of βρέχω (to wet, to rain), declined as a regular adjective (-ος, -η, -ο).

senses.definition: Covered or soaked in water or another liquid.

examples.text: Τα ρούχα μου είναι βρεγμένα από τη βροχή.
examples.translation: My clothes are wet from the rain.

examples.text: Μην πατάς στο χαλί με βρεγμένα παπούτσια.
examples.translation: Do not step on the carpet with wet shoes.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'possible' (e.g. είναι δυνατόν, όλο και πιο δυνατό).

faults.why: Merely restates the senses already listed in the entry.

senses.definition: Having great physical strength, force, or intensity.

examples.text: Είναι ένας πολύ δυνατός αθλητής.
examples.translation: He is a very strong athlete.

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: having a high volume.

examples.text: Η μουσική ήταν πολύ δυνατή.
examples.translation: The music was very loud.

senses.definition: Able to be done or to happen.

examples.text: Θα έρθω το συντομότερο δυνατό.
examples.translation: I will come as soon as possible.

faults.quote: While it most commonly describes something physically unattractive, it is also frequently

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; lacking beauty.

examples.text: Αυτός ο πίνακας είναι πολύ άσχημος.
examples.translation: This painting is very ugly.

senses.definition: Unpleasant, disagreeable, or bad (of weather, news, situations, or behaviour).

examples.text: Είχε πολύ άσχημη συμπεριφορά στο πάρτι.
examples.translation: His behaviour at the party was very bad.

faults.quote: red; bright and fiery

senses.definition: Having the colour of blood or a ripe tomato.

examples.text: Φόρεσε ένα κόκκινο παλτό για το κρύο.
examples.translation: She wore a red coat for the cold.

faults.quote: Extremely high temperature, like weather or a very intense sensation.

faults.quote: Extremely high temperature, like weather or a very intense sensation.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun phrase ('Extremely high temperature').

faults.why: Directly repeats note[0].

examples.translation: Don't touch the pot, it's boiling hot.

examples.text: Ο καυτός ήλιος του μεσημεριού μας ανάγκασε να μείνουμε στη σκιά.
examples.translation: The scorching midday sun forced us to stay in the shade.

faults.quote: La pianta can mean a growing green thing, a building floor plan,
faults.why: Restates the senses and glosses without adding usage information.

senses.definition: A living thing that grows in the ground and has leaves, roots, and a stem or trunk.

examples.text: Ho una spina nella pianta del piede.
examples.translation: I have a thorn in the sole of my foot.

faults.quote: (market) An open-air market or marketplace.

senses.definition: An open public space in a city or town, usually surrounded by buildings.

examples.text: La gente si incontra nella piazza principale del paese.
examples.translation: People meet in the main square of the town.

faults.why: Single stone and stone as a building material are countable/uncountable uses of one sense.

senses.definition: The hard, solid mineral material that rocks are made of, or a single piece of it.

examples.translation: I found a smooth stone near the river.

examples.text: La vecchia casa è fatta di pietra.
examples.translation: The old house is made of stone.

senses.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone used in jewelry.

examples.text: Quell'anello ha una pietra blu molto rara.
examples.translation: That ring has a very rare blue gemstone.

faults.quote: Use 'fare pioggia' or simply the verb 'piovere' when talking about
