faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'temporale', which specifically means a thunderstorm
faults.why: Unnecessary contrast between different words with no obvious confusion.

notes: The plural adds no 'i': 'le piogge' (not *le pioggie). To say 'it is raining', use the verb 'piovere' ('piove').

senses.definition: Water falling in drops from clouds in the sky.

examples.text: La pioggia cade lentamente sui tetti della città.
examples.translation: The rain falls slowly on the roofs of the city.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sports sense 'goal' (in football/soccer) and transport 'gate'.

notes: Used for rooms and buildings. A heavy main street entrance to an apartment building is often called 'il portone', while a car or train door is 'lo sportello'.

senses.definition: The movable barrier that you open or close to enter or leave a room or building.

examples.text: Chiudi la porta, per favore.
examples.translation: Close the door, please.

senses.definition: A large opening in a wall around a city, or the boarding area for passengers at an airport.

examples.text: La porta della città è molto antica.
examples.translation: The city gate is very old.

senses.definition: The frame with a net into which players try to kick or hit the ball in sports like football.

examples.text: Il calciatore ha tirato la palla direttamente in porta.
examples.translation: The football player kicked the ball straight into the goal.

faults.quote: foot; base; stem
faults.why: Includes 'stem', which is not covered in the senses or glosses.

notes: Used in common expressions like 'à pied' (on foot), e.g., 'aller à l'école à pied' (to walk to school).

senses.definition: The bottom part of the leg used for standing and walking.

examples.text: J'ai mal au pied après cette longue promenade.
examples.translation: My foot hurts after this long walk.

senses.definition: The lower part of an object, piece of furniture, or plant that supports it.

examples.text: Le pied de la lampe est en bois.
examples.translation: The base of the lamp is made of wood.

faults.quote: Animal vertebrado acuático que vive en el agua, respira por branquias
faults.why: Definition is written in Spanish instead of English.

faults.quote: Carne de este animal que se come como alimento.
faults.why: Definition is written in Spanish instead of English.

faults.quote: which is spelled with an 'i' after the 's'
faults.why: False claim: 'poison' is spelled with one 's', not an 'i' after the 's'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'le poison' (poison), which is spelled with a single 's' and pronounced with a /z/ sound (/pwa.zɔ̃/).
As an animal, it is countable ('un poisson', 'des poissons'); as food, it is usually used with the partitive article ('du poisson').

senses.definition: An animal that lives in water, breathes through gills, and uses fins to swim.

examples.text: Il y a des poissons colorés dans l'aquarium.
examples.translation: There are colorful fish in the aquarium.

senses.definition: The flesh of this animal eaten as food.

examples.text: Je mange du poisson tous les vendredis.
examples.translation: I eat fish every Friday.

faults.quote: Elle lit un roman policier dans le train.
faults.why: Uses 'policier' as an adjective modifying 'roman', not as a noun.

notes: To refer to a female police officer, use 'la policière'.
Do not confuse 'le policier' (the officer) with 'la police' (the police force).

senses.definition: A person whose job is to enforce the law, maintain order, and catch criminals.

examples.text: Le policier demande les papiers de la voiture.
examples.translation: The police officer is asking for the car papers.

senses.definition: A film, television show, or novel about a crime and its investigation.

examples.text: Ce soir, on regarde un bon vieux policier à la télé.
examples.translation: Tonight, we're watching a good old crime film on TV.

faults.quote: It is a masculine noun: un portefeuille.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the entry fields.

faults.quote: A flat case or folder for carrying loose papers
faults.why: Dated sense; modern French uses 'chemise', 'dossier', or 'porte-documents' for folders.

notes: Do not confuse 'un portefeuille' (for banknotes and cards) with 'un porte-monnaie' (a small purse mainly for coins) or 'un sac à main' (a handbag).

senses.definition: A small folding case that fits in a pocket, used to carry banknotes, bank cards, and identity documents.

examples.text: J'ai oublié mon portefeuille dans la voiture.
examples.translation: I forgot my wallet in the car.

faults.quote: (weather) Having little or no rain; arid.
faults.why: Dry weather and dry objects are one basic meaning for beginners.

faults.quote: (person) Lean and thin in build.
faults.why: Literary/dated sense; 'сухощавый' or 'худой' is standard at A2.

faults.quote: После дождя асфальт быстро стал сухой.
faults.why: After 'стал', the instrumental 'сухим' (or the verb 'высох') is standard, not nominative.

faults.quote: Used to describe things that have no water or moisture
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to note the short form 'сух/суха/сухо' or 'сухое вино'.

notes: Also used of wine that is not sweet: сухое вино (dry wine).
To say 'it is dry' about the weather or a place, use the impersonal form сухо: На улице сухо (It is dry outside).

senses.definition: Free from moisture, liquid, or rain; not wet.

examples.text: Возьми сухое полотенце.
examples.translation: Take a dry towel.

examples.text: Этим летом была очень сухая погода.
examples.translation: This summer the weather was very dry.

faults.quote: Use 'бедный' when someone has very little money or when
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Stronger is нищий (destitute, begging). Can also be used as a noun: бедные (the poor).

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions.

examples.text: Он родился в бедной семье.
examples.translation: He was born into a poor family.

senses.definition: Deserving sympathy or pity because of a sad or difficult situation.

examples.text: Бедный кот, он промок под дождём.
examples.translation: Poor cat, he got wet in the rain.

faults.quote: Use 'сильный' for physical strength, like a person or an
faults.why: Restates the senses; better to note the collocation 'сильный дождь' (heavy rain) concisely.

notes: Used where English says 'heavy' or 'bad' for weather, pain, or feelings: сильный дождь (heavy rain), сильная боль (severe pain).

senses.definition: Having great physical power or strength.

examples.text: Он очень сильный человек.
examples.translation: He is a very strong person.

senses.definition: Great in degree, force, or intensity.

examples.text: Сегодня дует сильный ветер.
examples.translation: A strong wind is blowing today.

faults.quote: (weather) Having a low temperature... / (temperature) Having a low temperature
faults.why: Cold weather and cold objects are the exact same meaning.

faults.quote: This is the standard word for 'cold.' Use it for
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss and senses.

notes: Compare прохладный (cool, pleasantly chilly). To say 'it is cold' (weather) or 'I am cold', use the adverb/predicative холодно: Мне холодно (I am cold).

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm.

examples.text: Сегодня очень холодный день.
examples.translation: Today is a very cold day.

examples.text: Я хочу выпить холодный чай.
examples.translation: I want to drink cold tea.

faults.quote: angry; evil; vicious
faults.why: 'Vicious' is not in any sense's glosses, though fierce/biting (e.g. dog) fits sense 2.

notes: Takes на + accusative for the person you are angry at: Он злой (or зол) на меня. In the predicate, the short form зол / зла / злы is very common.
Of a dog, злая собака means 'fierce/biting dog' (Осторожно, злая собака! — 'Beware of the dog!').

senses.definition: Feeling strong displeasure or hostility towards someone.

examples.text: Он очень злой на своего друга.
examples.translation: He is very angry at his friend.

senses.definition: Cruel, mean, or wishing harm to others; fierce.

examples.text: В сказках всегда есть злой волшебник.
examples.translation: In fairy tales, there is always an evil wizard.

faults.quote: (necessity) To have to have something, or to be obliged
faults.why: Artificial split; both senses mean 'to need'.
Missing essential grammar note on the pronoun replacement with 'en' ('J'en ai besoin').

notes: Followed by a noun (without an article for uncountable/plural nouns, e.g., 'avoir besoin d'aide') or an infinitive verb ('avoir besoin de dormir').
To say 'to need it/them', replace 'de + noun' with the pronoun 'en' before the verb (e.g., 'J'en ai besoin').

senses.definition: To require something or someone, or to find it necessary to do something.

examples.text: J'ai besoin de vacances pour me reposer.
examples.translation: I need a vacation to rest.

examples.text: Nous avons besoin de ce livre pour le cours.
examples.translation: We need this book for the class.

faults.quote: add 'grand' before 'faim' (avoir grand-faim) or 'très' before 'faim' in casual
faults.why: 'Avoir grand-faim' is literary/archaic for A2, and 'très faim' is standard, not merely casual.

notes: Unlike English, which uses 'to be' with an adjective, French uses the verb 'avoir' (to have) with the noun 'faim' (never say 'je suis faim').
To say 'very hungry', place 'très' before 'faim' (e.g., 'J'ai très faim').

senses.definition: To feel the need to eat something.

examples.text: Après une longue promenade, j'ai toujours faim.
examples.translation: After a long walk, I am always hungry.

faults.quote: Do not use 'être' with 'peur'. Saying 'je suis peur' is incorrect
faults.why: Repeats note 0; misses how to introduce the object of fear with 'de'.

corrected.shortGloss: to be afraid; to be scared
notes: Unlike English ('to be afraid'), French uses the verb 'avoir' (to have) with the noun 'peur' (never say 'je suis peur').
Use the preposition 'de' before a noun or an infinitive to say what you are afraid of (e.g., 'avoir peur du noir', 'avoir peur de tomber').

senses.definition: To feel fear or anxiety about something or someone.

examples.text: J'ai peur des araignées.
examples.translation: I am afraid of spiders.

examples.text: Il a peur de rentrer tout seul dans le noir.
examples.translation: He is scared to go home all alone in the dark.

faults.why: Missing the essential auxiliary verb sense ('J'ai mangé') needed at A1/A2.
Note is filler restating senses instead of giving irregular present-tense forms and 'il y a'.

notes: Highly irregular verb. Present tense: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont. Past participle: eu (/y/).
Also appears in the very common impersonal expression 'il y a' (there is / there are).

senses.definition: To own, possess, or hold something, or to have a relationship or characteristic.

examples.text: J'ai un chat noir et deux chiens.
examples.translation: I have a black cat and two dogs.

senses.definition: Used as an auxiliary verb with a past participle to form compound past tenses of most verbs.

examples.text: Nous avons fini notre travail.
examples.translation: We have finished our work.

senses.definition: Used with a number and 'ans' to state someone's age.

examples.text: Elle a vingt ans.
examples.translation: She is twenty years old.

senses.definition: Used with certain nouns (such as 'faim', 'soif', 'froid', 'chaud', 'peur') to express a physical sensation or state.

examples.text: Tu as froid sans manteau ?
examples.translation: Are you cold without a coat?

faults.quote: A densely populated urban area that is smaller than a city.
faults.why: Greek 'πόλη' does not distinguish 'city' from 'town'; this splits by English translation.

notes: Covers both 'city' and 'town' (small towns are sometimes called 'η κωμόπολη'); contrasts with 'το χωριό' (village).
Do not confuse with 'πολύ' (/poˈli/, 'very/much'), which is stressed on the second syllable.

senses.definition: A large urban settlement where many people live and work, covering both a city and a town.

examples.text: Η Αθήνα είναι μια μεγάλη πόλη.
examples.translation: Athens is a big city.

examples.text: Πήγαμε σε μια παραθαλάσσια πόλη για το σαββατοκύριακο.
examples.translation: We went to a seaside town for the weekend.

faults.quote: Dark lenses worn to protect the eyes from bright sunlight.
faults.why: Eyeglasses and sunglasses are one sense of 'γυαλιά' ('γυαλιά ηλίου' is a compound).

notes: Always plural ('τα γυαλιά') for a pair of glasses; the singular 'το γυαλί' means 'glass' (the material). Specify 'γυαλιά ηλίου' for sunglasses or 'γυαλιά μυωπίας / πρεσβυωπίας' for prescription glasses.

senses.definition: A pair of lenses in a frame worn in front of the eyes to improve vision or protect them from the sun.

examples.text: Φοράω τα γυαλιά μου για να διαβάσω το βιβλίο.
examples.translation: I wear my glasses to read the book.

examples.text: Έχω τα γυαλιά ηλίου μου στην τσάντα.
examples.translation: I have my sunglasses in my bag.

faults.quote: The result or consequence of an action or effort.
faults.why: Metaphorical 'fruit/result' in Greek is 'ο καρπός', not 'το φρούτο'.

faults.quote: Αυτή η επιτυχία είναι ο καρπός των κόπων του.
faults.why: Example uses 'καρπός' instead of the headword 'φρούτο'.

faults.quote: and metaphorically for an outcome or result.
faults.why: 'Φρούτο' is not used metaphorically for an outcome (that is 'καρπός').

faults.quote: Τρώω ένα φρούτο κάθε μέρα για υγεία.
faults.why: 'Για υγεία' and 'eat a fruit' are unnatural; 'piece of fruit' in English.

notes: Countable in Greek: 'ένα φρούτο' means 'a piece of fruit'. For botanical fruit or metaphorical 'fruit of one's labor', Greek uses 'ο καρπός'.

senses.definition: The sweet, edible part of a tree or plant that contains seeds, such as an apple or orange.

examples.text: Τρώω ένα φρούτο κάθε μέρα.
examples.translation: I eat a piece of fruit every day.

faults.quote: In Greek, the word 'σαλόνι' is primarily used to describe
faults.why: Restates the definition and glosses without adding usage information.

notes: Often overlaps with 'το καθιστικό', which refers more specifically to a smaller, informal sitting room or family room.

senses.definition: The main room in a home where people sit, relax, and receive guests.

examples.text: Το σαλόνι είναι πολύ μεγάλο και φωτεινό.
examples.translation: The living room is very big and bright.

examples.text: Καθίσαμε στο σαλόνι για να πιούμε καφέ.
examples.translation: We sat in the living room to have coffee.

faults.quote: A person who receives medical treatment in a hospital or clinic.
faults.why: Entry POS is adjective, but sense 1 is defined as a noun.
Needs a note contrasting 'estar enfermo' (temporary illness) with 'ser enfermo'.

notes: Usually used with 'estar' (estar enfermo = to be sick/ill). Also used as a noun (el enfermo / la enferma) meaning 'patient' or 'sick person'.

senses.definition: Not feeling well; suffering from an illness or disease.

examples.text: Me siento enfermo y no quiero salir de la cama.
examples.translation: I feel sick and I don't want to get out of bed.

faults.quote: Enseñar covers both 'to teach' (helping someone learn) and 'to show'
faults.why: Restates the senses and glosses without adding usage information.
Missing essential grammar note: takes 'a' + infinitive ('enseñar a nadar').

notes: Followed by 'a' + infinitive when teaching how to do something (e.g., enseñar a leer = to teach how to read).
Do not confuse with 'aprender' (to learn).

senses.definition: To help someone learn a skill, subject, or language.

examples.text: Quiero enseñar español a los niños.
examples.translation: I want to teach Spanish to the children.

senses.definition: To let someone see something.

examples.text: Te voy a enseñar mi nueva casa.
examples.translation: I am going to show you my new house.

faults.quote: To know the meaning of words, symbols, or a specific language.
faults.why: Understanding what someone says and understanding a word are the same sense.
Missing critical stem-changing verb note (e -> ie: entiendo, entiendes).

notes: Stem-changing verb (e → ie) in the present tense: entiendo, entiendes, entiende...
Often interchangeable with 'comprender', though 'comprender' can imply deeper understanding or empathy.

senses.definition: To grasp the meaning of words, a language, or what someone says.

examples.text: No entiendo lo que dices.
examples.translation: I don't understand what you are saying.

examples.text: No entiendo esta palabra en el texto.
examples.translation: I don't understand this word in the text.

faults.quote: To be the author of a book, article, or song.
faults.why: Writing a letter and writing a novel are one everyday sense for beginners.
Missing irregular past participle 'escrito', essential for A2 learners.

notes: Has an irregular past participle: 'escrito' (written).
Takes the preposition 'a' before a recipient: 'Escribo a mi madre'.

senses.definition: To produce words or text on paper or a screen, or to compose a text or book.

examples.text: Voy a escribir una carta.
examples.translation: I am going to write a letter.

examples.text: Escribe novelas de misterio.
examples.translation: He writes mystery novels.

faults.quote: You will often hear 'babcia' used affectionately for any elderly woman
faults.why: Restates sense 1 instead of giving extra grammar or usage guidance.

faults.quote: Use 'babcia' in formal or neutral contexts
faults.why: 'Babcia' corresponds to 'grandma'; the formal term is 'babka'.

faults.quote: An affectionate way to address or refer to an older woman.
faults.why: Meta-linguistic definition; define as the person ('an older woman'), not 'a way to refer'.

notes: When addressing her directly, use the vocative form 'babciu'. The formal word 'babka' is rarely used for family today.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Moja babcia piecze najlepsze ciasto.
examples.translation: My grandmother bakes the best cake.

senses.definition: (informal) An older woman.

examples.text: Ta miła babcia zawsze karmi ptaki w parku.
examples.translation: That nice old lady always feeds the birds in the park.

faults.quote: Use 'błąd' for general mistakes, wrong calculations, or computer bugs.
faults.why: Merely repeats the senses and examples without adding grammar or usage help.

notes: The vowel 'ą' changes to 'ę' in all other forms (e.g. genitive 'błędu', plural 'błędy'). Common collocation: 'popełnić/zrobić błąd' (to make a mistake).
Do not confuse with 'wina', which means blame or fault ('to moja wina' = 'it's my fault').

senses.definition: Something done or written wrongly.

examples.text: Zrobiłem poważny błąd w obliczeniach.
examples.translation: I made a serious mistake in the calculations.

senses.definition: A flaw or malfunction in a computer program or system.

examples.text: Program przestał działać z powodu błędu w kodzie.
examples.translation: The program stopped working due to a bug in the code.

faults.quote: Like in English, 'banan' can also be used colloquially to describe
faults.why: Slang idiom note is unhelpful at A2 while key grammar (accusative -a) is missing.

notes: Like most fruits and vegetables in Polish, 'banan' takes the '-a' ending in the accusative singular ('zjeść banana'), just like animate masculine nouns.

senses.definition: A long curved fruit with yellow skin and soft sweet flesh.

examples.text: Zjadłem banana na śniadanie.
examples.translation: I ate a banana for breakfast.

faults.quote: In Polish, 'bank' is used for both the institution and the building
faults.why: Repeats the definition and is identical to English.

notes: Do not confuse with 'brzeg', which is used for the bank of a river or lake.

senses.definition: An institution or building where people keep, borrow, or manage money.

examples.text: Muszę dzisiaj pójść do banku, żeby wypłacić pieniądze.
examples.translation: I have to go to the bank today to withdraw money.

faults.why: Missing distinction from 뽀뽀하다 (light peck) and particle usage (-에게/한테).

faults.quote: or greeting
faults.why: 키스하다 implies a romantic or deep kiss, not a casual greeting.

notes: Takes the particle -에게/-한테 for the person kissed, or -와/-과 (with). Usually implies a romantic kiss on the lips; for a light peck or kissing a child, use 뽀뽀하다.

senses.definition: To touch someone's lips with yours as a sign of romantic love.

examples.text: 두 사람이 작별하며 키스했다.
examples.translation: The two people kissed as they said goodbye.

faults.quote: both for the moment you open your eyes (waking up)
faults.why: Contradicts note 1; 일어나다 means getting up, whereas 깨다 means opening one's eyes.

corrected.shortGloss: to get up; to stand up; to happen
notes: Intransitive verb. Do not confuse with 깨다, which means to regain consciousness or stop sleeping; 일어나다 refers to getting out of bed or rising.

senses.definition: To wake up and get out of bed after sleeping.

examples.text: 매일 아침 7시에 일어납니다.
examples.translation: I get up at 7 o'clock every morning.

senses.definition: To stand up from a sitting or lying position.

examples.text: 의자에서 천천히 일어났다.
examples.translation: He stood up slowly from the chair.

senses.definition: To happen or take place, especially of an event or incident.

examples.text: 어젯밤에 큰 사고가 일어났다.
examples.translation: A big accident happened last night.

faults.quote: Use 도착하다 when focusing on the end point of a journey.
faults.why: Restates the definition while omitting the required particle -에 (not -을/를).

notes: Takes the location particle -에 for the destination (e.g., 역에 도착하다), never the object particle -을/-를.

senses.definition: To reach a place at the end of a journey.

examples.text: 기차가 역에 도착했습니다.
examples.translation: The train arrived at the station.

faults.quote: To happen, arrive, or occur, such as a season, a feeling, or
faults.why: Conflates precipitation falling (비가 오다) with time/events arriving (봄이 오다); glosses lack 'fall'.

faults.quote: when the destination is where the speaker currently is or will be
faults.why: Unlike English, Korean 오다 is strictly deictic to the speaker's location, not the listener's.

corrected.shortGloss: to come; to fall (of rain or snow)
notes: Unlike English 'come', 오다 is only used for movement toward the speaker's own current or future location. When moving toward the listener ('I'm coming to your place'), Korean uses 가다 (to go).

senses.definition: To move toward the place where the speaker is or will be.

examples.text: 친구들이 집에 와요.
examples.translation: My friends are coming to my house.

senses.definition: Of rain or snow: to fall from the sky.

examples.text: 밖에 비가 와요.
examples.translation: It is raining outside.

senses.definition: Of a season, time, or communication: to arrive or come about.

examples.text: 드디어 봄이 왔어요.
examples.translation: Spring has finally come.

faults.quote: 아이가 실수로 컵을 깨다.
faults.why: Unconjugated dictionary form '-다' is unnatural for a full sentence example.

faults.quote: 아침에 일찍 잠에서 깨다.
faults.why: Unconjugated dictionary form used as a sentence fragment.

notes: In the 'break' sense, 깨다 is transitive (to break something); its passive/intransitive pair is 깨지다 (to get broken). In the 'wake up' sense, it is used with 잠에서 or 잠을.

senses.definition: To make something hard or fragile break into pieces by hitting or dropping it.

examples.text: 아이가 실수로 컵을 깼다.
examples.translation: The child accidentally broke the cup.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping and become conscious.

examples.text: 오늘 아침에 일찍 잠에서 깼어요.
examples.translation: I woke up early this morning.

faults.quote: Use 'mirar' when you want to say 'look at' someone or something.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without explaining grammar (personal 'a' or lack of preposition).

notes: While 'ver' is about perceiving with the eyes (and is often preferred in Mexico for watching TV or movies), 'mirar' implies intentionally directing your eyes at something.
Unlike English 'look at', 'mirar' takes a direct object without a preposition, except the personal 'a' before a person (e.g., 'Miro la foto', 'Miro a Juan').

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward something or someone to see or observe it.

examples.text: Tienes que mirar el mapa para encontrar el camino.
examples.translation: You have to look at the map to find the way.

examples.text: Me gusta mirar las estrellas por la noche.
examples.translation: I like to watch the stars at night.

faults.quote: Used for things or people covered in liquid.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of explaining the required verb 'estar'.

notes: Used with the verb 'estar' because being wet is a resulting state (e.g., 'Mi ropa está mojada').

senses.definition: Covered or soaked with water or another liquid.

examples.text: Cuidado, el piso está mojado.
examples.translation: Careful, the floor is wet.

examples.text: Llegué a casa con los zapatos mojados.
examples.translation: I got home with wet shoes.

faults.quote: Used for moving through water by using one's body.
faults.why: Restates the definition directly; no special usage note is needed here.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body.

examples.text: Me gusta nadar en el mar durante el verano.
examples.translation: I like to swim in the sea during the summer.

examples.text: Ellos aprendieron a nadar en la alberca.
examples.translation: They learned to swim in the pool.

faults.quote: /neseθiˈtaɾ/
faults.why: Mexican Spanish has seseo (/s/), not /θ/, and cannot mix both in 'necesitar'.

faults.quote: 'necesitar' is used when you are lacking something necessary, such as an object
faults.why: False restriction: 'necesitar' is also very commonly followed by an infinitive verb.

faults.quote: To have to have something; to be unable to function
faults.why: Sense 1 is the exact same meaning as sense 0, just used hyperbolically.

notes: Can be followed directly by a noun ('Necesito ayuda') or by an infinitive verb ('Necesito descansar').

senses.definition: To require something or have to do something because it is essential or very important.

examples.text: Necesito un paraguas porque va a llover.
examples.translation: I need an umbrella because it is going to rain.

examples.text: Necesito descansar un poco antes de seguir.
examples.translation: I need to rest a little before continuing.

faults.quote: to think; to consider; to intend
faults.why: 'to consider' is not in the senses' glosses.

notes: Use 'pensar em' when thinking about someone or something, or intending to do something (e.g., 'Estou pensando em você').

senses.definition: To use your mind to form thoughts, have an opinion, or reflect on something.

examples.text: Eu penso muito antes de tomar uma decisão.
examples.translation: I think a lot before making a decision.

senses.definition: To intend or plan to do something (with 'em').

examples.text: Nós pensamos em viajar nas férias.
examples.translation: We plan to travel during the holidays.

faults.quote: Use pequeno when describing physical size or scope. For people, especially children,
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses without adding usage or grammar information.

notes: Comparative and superlative forms are usually 'menor' (smaller/smallest), though 'mais pequeno' is heard in some regions.

senses.definition: Not large in size, amount, or scale.

examples.text: Comprei um carro pequeno para andar na cidade.
examples.translation: I bought a small car to drive around the city.

senses.definition: Of a person: young and not yet grown up.

examples.text: Eu era muito pequeno quando morava lá.
examples.translation: I was very young when I lived there.

faults.why: Missing the very common A1/A2 sense 'to miss' (a bus, train, opportunity) and 'waste' (time).

corrected.shortGloss: to lose; to miss; to waste
notes: Irregular in the first-person singular present: 'eu perco' (and subjunctive 'perca').
'Perder' translates both 'to lose' and 'to miss' (for transport, events, or opportunities; e.g., 'perder o ônibus' — to miss the bus).

senses.definition: To no longer have something, or to be unable to find it.

examples.text: Eu perdi as chaves de casa.
examples.translation: I lost my house keys.

senses.definition: To fail to win a game, match, or competition.

examples.text: Nosso time perdeu o jogo ontem.
examples.translation: Our team lost the game yesterday.

senses.definition: To arrive too late for a bus, train, or event, or fail to take an opportunity.

examples.text: Se você não correr, vai perder o ônibus.
examples.translation: If you don't run, you will miss the bus.

senses.definition: To fail to make good use of time or effort.

examples.text: Não quero perder tempo com isso.
examples.translation: I don't want to waste time with this.

faults.quote: (threat) Able to hurt... / (risk) Involving risk or uncertainty
faults.why: Shades of one meaning ('dangerous / risky') split into two senses.

faults.quote: Used to describe things, people, or situations that can cause harm
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

notes: The middle 'o' is pronounced closed (/o/) in the masculine singular ('perigoso'), but opens to /ɔ/ in the feminine ('perigosa') and plurals ('perigosos', 'perigosas').

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or serious problems.

examples.text: É perigoso nadar neste rio por causa das correntes.
examples.translation: It is dangerous to swim in this river because of the currents.

faults.quote: /ʔaj˩/
faults.why: Wrong tone; ไอ has a mid tone (/ʔaj˧/), not a low tone.

faults.quote: (symptom) The act of pushing air out of the throat
faults.why: As a noun, ไอ means 'vapor/steam'. 'Cough' is a verb (or อาการไอ as noun).

notes: Often combined with other nouns, as in ไอน้ำ (water vapor, steam) or ไอแดด (heat haze from the sun).

senses.definition: Vapor, steam, or fumes rising from a liquid or surface.

examples.text: มีไอขึ้นมาจากถ้วยกาแฟ
examples.translation: There is steam rising from the coffee cup.

faults.quote: ฉันรู้สึกมีลม in ท้อง
faults.why: Contains the English word 'in' instead of Thai 'ใน'.

faults.quote: In Thai, 'ลม' is used not only for weather like wind
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses important expressions like เป็นลม (to faint).

notes: Also appears in the very common expression เป็นลม, which literally means 'to become wind' but idiomatic for 'to faint' or 'to feel dizzy'.

senses.definition: Moving air outside, such as a wind or breeze.

examples.text: วันนี้ลมพัดแรงมาก
examples.translation: The wind is blowing very hard today.

senses.definition: Gas in the stomach or intestines.

examples.text: ฉันรู้สึกว่ามีลมในท้อง
examples.translation: I feel like I have gas in my stomach.

notes: Placed before a country's name, e.g., ประเทศไทย (Thailand) or ประเทศญี่ปุ่น (Japan). In casual speech, ประเทศ is often dropped and only the name is used.
Takes itself as a classifier: สามประเทศ (three countries).

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and territory.

examples.text: คุณมาจากประเทศอะไร
examples.translation: What country do you come from?

examples.text: ฉันอยากไปเที่ยวต่างประเทศ
examples.translation: I want to travel abroad.

faults.quote: ฉันเห็นแกะหลายตัว in the meadow.
faults.why: Contains English words 'in the meadow.' inside the Thai example.

faults.quote: (carve) To carve, chisel, or engrave wood or ice.
faults.why: Entry POS is noun, but senses 1 and 2 are verbs.

faults.quote: (unpack) To unwrap, peel, or open something packaging.
faults.why: Entry POS is noun, not verb; also 'something packaging' is ungrammatical English.

faults.quote: sheep; to carve; to unpack
faults.why: Includes verb glosses in a noun entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse the animal meaning with the action meanings
faults.why: Repetitive filler notes; misses the noun classifier (ตัว).

notes: The classifier for sheep is ตัว (tua), e.g., แกะสามตัว (three sheep). For mutton or lamb meat, use เนื้อแกะ.
Homophonous with the common verb แกะ, which means 'to unwrap', 'to peel', or 'to carve'.

senses.definition: A farm animal with thick wool, kept for its wool and meat.

examples.text: ฉันเห็นแกะหลายตัวในทุ่งหญ้า
examples.translation: I see many sheep in the meadow.

faults.quote: (livestock) General term for cattle, including oxen or bulls.
faults.why: Thai วัว is a single concept covering cow, bull, ox, and cattle.

notes: General term for cattle of either sex (cow, bull, or ox). The classifier is ตัว (tua). For beef, use เนื้อวัว (or simply เนื้อ).

senses.definition: A large farm animal kept for its milk, meat, or labor; a cow, bull, or ox.

examples.text: วัวกินหญ้าอยู่ในทุ่งนา
examples.translation: The cows are eating grass in the field.

faults.why: Missing irregular stem change to 'wsi' in oblique cases and 'na' preposition rule.

notes: Has the irregular form 'wsi' in the genitive, dative, and locative singular.
Takes the preposition 'na' rather than 'w': 'na wsi' (in a village / in the countryside), 'jechać na wieś' (to go to the countryside).

senses.definition: A small settlement in a rural area, smaller than a town.

examples.text: Moi dziadkowie mieszkają na małej wsi.
examples.translation: My grandparents live in a small village.

senses.definition: Land outside towns and cities, with fields, farms, and nature.

examples.text: W weekend chcę uciec z miasta na wieś.
examples.translation: This weekend I want to escape from the city to the countryside.

faults.quote: Wino is a neuter noun, so its ending stays the same
faults.why: Restates the noun's gender and general Polish grammar rules.

notes: Do not confuse the genitive form 'wina' with the feminine noun 'wina' (guilt, fault).

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

examples.text: Pijemy czerwone wino do obiadu.
examples.translation: We are drinking red wine with dinner.

faults.quote: To winogrono jest bardzo słodkie.
faults.why: Polish speakers almost always use the plural 'winogrona' when talking about eating grapes.

notes: Usually used in the plural ('winogrona') to refer to a bunch of grapes or the fruit in general.

senses.definition: A small, round, juicy fruit that grows in clusters on vines and is used to make wine.

examples.text: Te zielone winogrona są bardzo słodkie.
examples.translation: These green grapes are very sweet.

faults.quote: the names of the seasons are feminine.
faults.why: False grammar claim: 'lato' (summer) is neuter and 'przedwiośnie' is neuter.

faults.quote: Don't confuse this with 'wczesna wiosna' (early spring)
faults.why: Warning not to confuse a noun with its own transparent adjective+noun collocation is filler.

notes: To say 'in spring', use the instrumental case 'wiosną' or the phrase 'na wiosnę'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between winter and summer, when the weather becomes warmer and plants grow.

examples.text: Wiosna to moja ulubiona pora roku.
examples.translation: Spring is my favorite season.

examples.text: Wiosną wszystko zaczyna kwitnąć.
examples.translation: In spring everything starts to bloom.

faults.why: Water in a glass and water in a lake are the same basic meaning.

faults.quote: water; mineral water
faults.why: 'Mineral water' is not a separate gloss in the senses.

faults.quote: Woda is the fundamental word for water.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding useful information.

notes: When ordering water in a restaurant, you will usually be asked whether you want it 'gazowana' (sparkling) or 'niegazowana' (still).

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain, fills rivers and lakes, and is used for drinking and washing.

examples.text: Poproszę szklankę wody.
examples.translation: I would like a glass of water.

examples.text: Woda w jeziorze jest dzisiaj bardzo zimna.
examples.translation: The water in the lake is very cold today.

faults.quote: [0] (food) A small loaf ... [1] (bakery) A small, individual loaf

senses.definition: A small, individual roll of bread, eaten either plain or sliced open with a filling such as cheese or meat.

examples.text: Ik haal even een broodje kaas bij de bakker.
examples.translation: I'm just going to get a cheese roll at the bakery.

examples.text: De warme broodjes liggen vers in de mand.
examples.translation: The warm bread rolls are fresh in the basket.

faults.quote: Ik moet even bellen naar het reisbureau.
faults.why: Uses the compound 'reisbureau' instead of the standalone word 'bureau'.

faults.why: Contradicts the note: 'bureau' in NL Dutch means an agency/station, not a room ('kantoor').

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat surface used for working, writing, or studying.

examples.text: Hij zit achter zijn bureau te werken aan de computer.
examples.translation: He is sitting at his desk working on the computer.

senses.definition: An organization, agency, or public department (especially a police station) that provides a specific service.

examples.text: De dief werd door de agenten meegenomen naar het bureau.
examples.translation: The thief was taken to the station by the police officers.

faults.why: The standard Dutch plural is 'cadeaus'; 'cadeaux' is outdated and non-standard.

notes: Borrowed from French, so 'eau' is pronounced /oː/. The plural is 'cadeaus' and the very common diminutive is 'het cadeautje'.

senses.definition: Something that you give to someone, usually for a special occasion like a birthday.

examples.text: Ik kocht een mooi cadeau voor haar verjaardag.
examples.translation: I bought a nice gift for her birthday.

faults.quote: [0] (coffee) A small establishment ... [1] (drinks) A local drinking establishment
faults.why: A Dutch 'café' serves coffee by day and alcohol by night; it is one concept.

senses.definition: A casual establishment where people go to socialize and drink coffee during the day or alcoholic drinks such as beer and wine in the evening.

examples.text: We drinken een kopje koffie in het gezellige café om de hoek.
examples.translation: We are drinking a cup of coffee in the cozy café around the corner.

examples.text: Zullen we na het werk nog even een biertje drinken in het café?
examples.translation: Shall we grab a quick beer at the pub after work?

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'geld', which is the general word for

notes: Often shortened to 'contant' or the English loanword 'cash' in everyday speech, especially with the verb 'betalen' (contant betalen = to pay in cash).

senses.definition: Money in the form of physical coins and banknotes, rather than a bank card or digital payment.

examples.text: Heb je genoeg contant geld bij je voor de markt?
examples.translation: Do you have enough cash with you for the market?

faults.quote: The verb tekenen is a classic 'false friend' for English speakers.
faults.why: Invented false friend ('to token'/'to take'); misses useful distinction with 'ondertekenen'.

notes: For signing a document, 'ondertekenen' is also very common and more specific than 'tekenen'.

senses.definition: To create a picture or shape using a pencil, pen, or other tool.

examples.text: Ik vind het leuk om bomen te tekenen in het park.
examples.translation: I like to draw trees in the park.

senses.definition: To write your name on a document to show agreement.

examples.text: Je moet dit contract tekenen om het huis te huren.
examples.translation: You must sign this contract to rent the house.

faults.quote: to pull; to draw; to move
faults.why: 'to draw' is not in any sense's glosses.

senses.definition: To move something towards yourself using force.

examples.text: Hij moet aan de hendel trekken om de deur te openen.
examples.translation: He has to pull the handle to open the door.

senses.definition: To travel or move in a particular direction, especially in groups or across a distance.

examples.text: De vogels trekken in de herfst naar het zuiden.
examples.translation: The birds migrate south in the autumn.

faults.quote: Used when you feel happy and satisfied about your own achievements
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition.

notes: Takes the preposition 'op': 'trots zijn op iemand/iets' (to be proud of someone/something).

senses.definition: Feeling pleased and satisfied about something you or someone else has achieved.

examples.text: Zij is erg trots op haar dochter.
examples.translation: She is very proud of her daughter.

examples.text: Ik ben trots op wat we hebben bereikt.
examples.translation: I am proud of what we have achieved.

faults.quote: (sleepy) Feeling the need for sleep. | glosses en: sleepy, drowsy

senses.definition: On many occasions or at short intervals.

examples.translation: I often see him in the supermarket.

faults.quote: (appearance) Pleasant, attractive, or cute in a charming way.

senses.definition: Causing laughter or amusement.

examples.text: Ele contou uma piada muito engraçada.
examples.translation: He told a very funny joke.

senses.definition: Unusual or slightly suspicious in a way that is hard to explain.

examples.text: É engraçado, eu tinha certeza de que deixei a chave aqui.
examples.translation: That's funny, I was sure I left the key here.

senses.definition: To help someone learn a subject or skill, or show them how to do something.

examples.translation: She likes to teach math to the children.

examples.translation: Can you teach me how to drive?

faults.quote: Used when you are bored by a specific activity or by
faults.why: Restates the definition; a note on taking 'estar'/'ficar' and preposition 'com' is much more useful.

notes: Used with 'estar' or 'ficar' and usually followed by 'com': 'estar entediado com algo' (to be bored with something).

senses.definition: Feeling weary and impatient because one has nothing interesting to do.

examples.text: Fico entediado quando não tenho nada para fazer.
examples.translation: I get bored when I have nothing to do.

notes: Takes the preposition 'de' when it means knowing a lot about a subject: 'entender de música' (to know about music).

senses.definition: To know the meaning of something or grasp what someone is saying.

senses.definition: To have knowledge or skill in a particular subject (with 'de').

examples.text: Meu pai entende muito de carros.
examples.translation: My father knows a lot about cars.

faults.quote: [0] (hope) ... [1] (desire) To ardently desire

senses.definition: To want something to happen or be true, and think that it is possible.

examples.text: Spero che domani faccia bel tempo.
examples.translation: I hope the weather is nice tomorrow.

examples.text: Spero di vincere questo premio.
examples.translation: I hope to win this prize.

faults.quote: (thickness) Having a large distance between opposite sides.

senses.definition: Many times; on many occasions.

examples.translation: I often go to the market to buy fruit.

faults.quote: Use 'spingere' when you are pushing an object away from you
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of sense 0 while missing irregular past forms.

senses.definition: To apply force to something to move it away from oneself.

examples.text: Devi spingere la porta per aprirla.
examples.translation: You have to push the door to open it.

senses.definition: To encourage or motivate someone to do something.

examples.text: Il mio allenatore mi spinge a dare il massimo.
examples.translation: My coach pushes me to give my best.

faults.quote: Sporco is the standard word for dirty. Use it for anything

senses.definition: Not clean; covered in dirt or stains.

examples.text: Ha fatto un gioco sporco per vincere la gara.
examples.translation: He played a dirty game to win the race.

faults.quote: Stanco is the standard word for feeling tired or fatigued.

examples.translation: I will buy meat at the supermarket.

examples.text: 最近お腹に肉がついてきた。
examples.translation: I have been putting on weight around my stomach lately.

faults.why: こども (kodomo) and こうどう (kōdō) do not sound alike; 'kodo' is also a wrong transcription.
Lacks the polite suffix お子さん (okosan) needed when referring to someone else's child.

notes: Also commonly written as 子ども.
When talking politely about someone else's child, use お子さん (okosan) instead.

senses.definition: A young person who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: 公園で子供たちが遊んでいます。
examples.translation: Children are playing in the park.

senses.definition: A person's son or daughter of any age.

examples.text: 彼には子供が二人います。
examples.translation: He has two children.

faults.quote: 'ovelha' is used for both the singular and plural forms
faults.why: False and self-contradictory: the plural is 'ovelhas', marked with '-s' on the noun itself.

faults.quote: Portuguese clearly marks the number with the article or the verb
faults.why: Misleading: the noun itself takes a regular plural in '-s' ('ovelhas').

notes: Strictly a female sheep (a ewe), though used generally for sheep of any sex. A male sheep (a ram) is 'o carneiro'.

senses.definition: A farm animal with thick wool that is raised for its wool, meat, or milk.

examples.text: A ovelha branca come grama no campo.
examples.translation: The white sheep eats grass in the field.

faults.quote: Use 'parede' for the vertical surfaces of a room or building
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage advice.

notes: Used for the walls of a room or building. For a freestanding outside wall around a yard or property, use 'o muro'.

senses.definition: A vertical structure that divides a room or forms the side of a building.

examples.text: O quadro está pendurado na parede da sala.
examples.translation: The picture is hanging on the living room wall.

faults.why: Lacks the everyday uncountable sense 'stone' as a building material, while sense 1 mixes it with 'gem'.

faults.quote: A hard, solid mineral mass or precious gem.
faults.why: Conflates stone as a material with a precious gem, while the glosses only give 'gem, jewel'.

notes: The everyday word for any stone or rock, small or large. 'A rocha' is used mainly in geology or for massive rock formations.

senses.definition: A hard, solid piece of mineral matter found on the ground.

examples.text: Ela tropeçou em uma pedra no caminho.
examples.translation: She tripped over a stone on the path.

senses.definition: The hard mineral substance that rocks are made of, often used for building.

examples.text: Eles construíram uma casa de pedra.
examples.translation: They built a stone house.

senses.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone used in jewelry.

examples.text: O anel tem uma pedra preciosa muito brilhante.
examples.translation: The ring has a very shiny gemstone.

faults.quote: O gato tem a pele macia.
faults.why: A living cat's soft coat is 'pelo', not 'pele' ('pele' as fur refers to detached pelts or fur clothing).

faults.quote: The natural covering or fur of an animal.
faults.why: Living human and animal skin are one sense; 'pele' as fur only refers to a pelt or fur garment.

notes: Do not confuse with 'o pelo', which is the hair or fur on a living animal's body (e.g., 'o pelo do gato'). 'Pele' means 'fur' only as a pelt or garment (such as 'casaco de pele', fur coat).

senses.definition: The natural outer layer that covers the body of a person or animal.

examples.text: O sol forte queimou a minha pele.
examples.translation: The strong sun burned my skin.

senses.definition: The skin of an animal, with or without the fur, removed to make clothing or leather.

examples.text: Ela estava usando um casaco de pele.
examples.translation: She was wearing a fur coat.

faults.quote: replaced by the more formal term 'Bedienung'
faults.why: 'Bedienung' is everyday, not formal, and 'Kellner' is still standard.
Missing the unchanged plural form ('die Kellner').

notes: Plural: die Kellner. The feminine form is 'die Kellnerin' (plural: 'die Kellnerinnen').
In restaurants, you can also hear 'die Bedienung' (server/waitstaff), which is used regardless of gender.

senses.definition: A man whose job is to serve food and drinks to customers in a restaurant or café.

examples.text: Der Kellner bringt uns die Speisekarte.
examples.translation: The waiter is bringing us the menu.

faults.why: Professional chef and someone who cooks are shades of one meaning.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'der Kuchen' (the cake)
faults.why: 'Koch' and 'Kuchen' are not easily confused; plural with umlaut ('Köche') is needed instead.

notes: Plural: die Köche. The feminine form is 'die Köchin' (plural: 'die Köchinnen').
'Koch' usually refers to a professional chef, though it is also used in expressions like 'ein guter Koch sein' (to be a good cook).

senses.definition: A person who prepares and cooks food, especially as a job in a restaurant.

examples.text: Mein Bruder arbeitet als Koch in einem Hotel.
examples.translation: My brother works as a chef in a hotel.

examples.text: Er ist ein sehr guter Koch.
examples.translation: He is a very good cook.

faults.quote: suitcase; trunk
faults.why: 'trunk' is not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: A 'Koffer' is a hard or soft case for travel.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

faults.quote: You can remember it with the phrase: 'Ich packe meinen Koffer'
faults.why: 'meinen Koffer' is accusative singular, so it does not show the plural form.

notes: The plural form is the same as the singular: 'die Koffer'.

senses.definition: A case with a handle and often wheels, used for carrying clothes and belongings when traveling.

examples.text: Ich muss noch meinen Koffer packen.
examples.translation: I still need to pack my suitcase.

faults.quote: If you mean a friend you just happen to know, do not
faults.why: Colloquially, 'Kollege' is actually often used among men to mean 'buddy' or 'mate'.
Missing that 'Kollege' is a weak masculine noun (n-declension: 'den/dem Kollegen').

notes: Plural: die Kollegen. 'Kollege' is a weak masculine noun (n-declension), taking '-n' in all cases except the nominative singular (e.g. 'mit meinem Kollegen').
The feminine form is 'die Kollegin' (plural: 'die Kolleginnen').

senses.definition: A person you work with in the same company or profession.

examples.text: Mein Kollege hilft mir bei diesem Projekt.
examples.translation: My colleague is helping me with this project.

faults.quote: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen im Kopf.
faults.why: Redundant and unnatural in both German and English, and lacks the standalone word 'Kopf'.

faults.quote: If you are talking about the 'head' of an organization
faults.why: The head of an organization is usually 'Leiter' or 'Chef' in German, not 'Kopf'.

faults.quote: The top or upper part of something, such as a mountain
faults.why: Mountain top is 'Gipfel', not 'Kopf'; marginal/inaccurate sense for A2.

notes: Plural: die Köpfe.
To say your head hurts, say 'Mir tut der Kopf weh' or 'Ich habe Kopfschmerzen' (I have a headache).

senses.definition: The upper part of the human or animal body, containing the brain, eyes, nose, mouth, and ears.

examples.text: Mir tut heute der Kopf weh.
examples.translation: My head hurts today.

senses.definition: A person's thoughts, memory, or imagination.

examples.text: Das Lied geht mir nicht mehr aus dem Kopf.
examples.translation: I can't get that song out of my head.

faults.quote: The colour of human or animal blood.
faults.why: Artificial split; 'red' is a single colour sense.

faults.quote: In Thai culture, red is traditionally associated with good luck
faults.why: Cultural trivia is not useful usage guidance for a beginner.

notes: Thai colour words usually begin with สี (sǐi, 'colour'). In casual speech or fixed compounds, สี is sometimes dropped (e.g., รถแดง 'red car').

senses.definition: Of the colour of blood or a ripe strawberry.

examples.text: รถคันนั้นสีแดง
examples.translation: That car is red.

faults.quote: /sa.ʔaːt/
faults.why: Missing tone marks; standard Thai pronunciation is /sà.ʔàːt/.

faults.quote: Use 'สะอาด' for anything that is not dirty.
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions without adding grammatical or usage insight.

senses.definition: Free from dirt, marks, or stains; not dirty.

examples.text: ห้องนอนนี้สะอาดมาก
examples.translation: This bedroom is very clean.

senses.definition: Free from corruption or illegal activity.

examples.text: เขาเป็นนักการเมืองที่สะอาด
examples.translation: He is a clean politician.

faults.quote: เงียบ describes a place or person that is quiet, silent
faults.why: Restates the glosses without providing extra usage information.

faults.quote: deserted, calm, lonesome
faults.why: 'Lonesome' is a wrong translation; 'quiet' should be the first gloss.

notes: Do not confuse with นิ่ง (nîng), which means still or motionless without necessarily implying silence.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise; silent.

examples.text: ห้องนี้เงียบมากตอนกลางคืน
examples.translation: This room is very quiet at night.

senses.definition: Of a place or business: having little activity, traffic, or people.

examples.text: ถนนสายนี้เงียบในวันหยุด
examples.translation: This street is quiet on holidays.

faults.quote: เหนื่อย (nèuai) is the standard word for feeling physically or mentally tired.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful contrast.

faults.quote: If you feel 'exhausted' or 'worn out,' you can add the word มาก
faults.why: Adding 'very' to an adjective is generic grammar, not word-specific.
Should contrast with ง่วง (sleepy), which beginners frequently confuse with เหนื่อย.

notes: Describes physical or mental fatigue. Do not confuse with ง่วง (ngûang), which means 'sleepy' (needing sleep).

senses.definition: Needing rest because of physical or mental effort.

examples.text: ฉันเหนื่อยมากหลังจากทำงานทั้งวัน
examples.translation: I am very tired after working all day.

faults.quote: Used to describe physical size, but also to mean 'major' or 'important'
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Important or high-ranking in position.
faults.why: Too narrow; ใหญ่ also applies to major events or serious problems.

notes: Like other Thai adjectives, ใหญ่ follows the noun (and classifier) it modifies: บ้านหลังใหญ่ (a big house).

senses.definition: Of great physical size or extent.

examples.text: บ้านหลังนี้ใหญ่มาก
examples.translation: This house is very big.

senses.definition: Important, serious, or high-ranking.

examples.text: นี่เป็นปัญหาใหญ่สำหรับเรา
examples.translation: This is a major problem for us.

faults.quote: Berjalan usually refers to moving on foot, but it is also used
faults.why: Restates the senses; should instead note the informal spoken form 'jalan'.

corrected.shortGloss: to walk; to proceed, to function
notes: In casual conversation, the prefix 'ber-' is often dropped, and people simply say 'jalan'.
Do not confuse this with 'pergi' (to go somewhere). 'Berjalan' describes moving on foot, whereas 'pergi' focuses on leaving or going to a destination.

senses.definition: To move forward on foot by taking steps.

examples.text: Dia berjalan ke sekolah setiap pagi.
examples.translation: He walks to school every morning.

senses.definition: To proceed, take place, or function as intended.

examples.text: Rencana itu berjalan dengan lancar.
examples.translation: The plan is going smoothly.

faults.quote: (escape) To run away or escape from a place or danger.
faults.why: 'Berlari' only means to run; 'to flee' is 'melarikan diri' or 'kabur'.

faults.quote: Berlari is the active verb meaning 'to run', formed with the prefix
faults.why: Restates the gloss; better to note the common informal form 'lari'.

notes: Formed from the root 'lari' with the prefix 'ber-'. In everyday speech, the root 'lari' is very often used on its own with the same meaning.
To say 'to run away' or 'to flee', use the reflexive phrase 'melarikan diri' or the informal word 'kabur'.

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: Anak-anak berlari di taman setiap sore.
examples.translation: The children run in the park every afternoon.

faults.quote: Indonesian does not use different verbs for these as English does.
faults.why: False claim: English also uses the same verb ('play') for both games and instruments.

faults.quote: /bərˈmaɪn/
faults.why: In Indonesian, 'main' is two syllables (/ma.in/), not a diphthong (/maɪn/).

corrected.shortGloss: to play (a game, sport, or instrument)
notes: Can be followed directly by a noun for the game, sport, or musical instrument (e.g., 'bermain bola', 'bermain gitar').
In casual conversation, the prefix 'ber-' is usually dropped, and people simply say 'main' (which also means 'to hang out' or 'to visit').

senses.definition: To take part in a game, a sport, or a fun activity.

examples.text: Anak-anak suka bermain bola di lapangan.
examples.translation: The children like to play ball on the field.

senses.definition: To perform music on a musical instrument.

examples.text: Dia sedang belajar bermain gitar.
examples.translation: He is learning to play the guitar.

faults.quote: Saya berpikir bahwa film itu sangat menarik.
faults.why: A calque of English 'I think that...'; Indonesian normally uses 'menurut saya' or 'saya rasa'.

faults.quote: (opinion) To have a certain opinion or belief about a matter.
faults.why: Shades of the same core meaning 'to think', which is one sense in Indonesian.

notes: 'Berpikir' is intransitive (it does not take a direct object). To say 'think about something', use 'berpikir tentang...' or the transitive verb 'memikirkan'.
To express an opinion like 'I think this is good', Indonesians usually say 'menurut saya...' or 'saya rasa...' rather than 'saya berpikir...'.

senses.definition: To use your mind to consider something, reason, or form a thought.

examples.text: Dia sedang berpikir sebelum menjawab pertanyaan itu.
examples.translation: He is thinking before answering that question.

examples.text: Saya berpikir untuk pindah ke kota lain.
examples.translation: I am thinking of moving to another city.

faults.quote: (energy) Acting with high energy, intensity, or a strong fighting spirit.
faults.why: Both senses describe the same quality of being full of 'semangat' (enthusiasm/energy).

faults.quote: Use this word when you want to describe someone who is full
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition without adding grammar or usage help.

faults.quote: He is very enthusiastic to go on vacation tomorrow.
faults.why: 'Enthusiastic to go' is unidiomatic in English; 'excited to go' is natural.

notes: Formed from the noun 'semangat' (spirit, enthusiasm) with the prefix 'ber-'.
In casual speech, the root 'semangat' is often used as an adjective on its own, or as an exclamation ('Semangat!') to cheer someone on ('Keep it up!').

senses.definition: Full of energy, interest, and eagerness to do something.

examples.text: Dia sangat bersemangat untuk pergi berlibur besok.
examples.translation: He is very excited to go on vacation tomorrow.

examples.text: Mereka bersemangat mendukung tim sepak bola di stadion.
examples.translation: They were enthusiastic in supporting the soccer team at the stadium.

faults.quote: Me compré un zapato nuevo para la fiesta.
faults.why: People buy a pair of shoes (unos zapatos), not a single shoe.

notes: Usually used in the plural (los zapatos) to refer to a pair of shoes.
Use zapato for dress or everyday shoes. For athletic shoes, Mexican Spanish uses los tenis, and for sandals, las sandalias or las chanclas.

senses.definition: An item of footwear with a firm sole that covers the foot.

examples.text: Me compré unos zapatos nuevos para la fiesta.
examples.translation: I bought some new shoes for the party.

faults.quote: (eliges, elgió)
faults.why: Misspells 'eligió' as 'elgió' and omits the g -> j spelling change (elijo).

notes: Stem-changing verb (e → i) in the present and preterite (eliges, eligió), with a spelling change g → j before o and a (elijo, elija).
Very similar to escoger, which is slightly more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want from a group of options.

examples.text: Tienes que elegir un regalo para tu hermana.
examples.translation: You have to choose a gift for your sister.

senses.definition: To choose someone for an official position by voting.

examples.text: Los ciudadanos van a elegir al nuevo presidente mañana.
examples.translation: The citizens are going to elect the new president tomorrow.

faults.quote: /emoθjoˈnaðo/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican Spanish /s/ (seseo).

faults.quote: While 'emocionado' often means 'excited' (eager and happy), it can also mean
faults.why: Note [0] merely restates the two senses; Note [1] warns of an unlikely confusion.
Missing note on using 'estar' and avoiding the false friend 'excitado' (sexually aroused).

notes: Used with estar: Estoy muy emocionado.
This is the standard translation for English 'excited'. Avoid excitado, which in Spanish usually means 'sexually aroused'.

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling very happy and eager about something that is happening or going to happen.

examples.text: Estoy muy emocionado por el viaje a la playa.
examples.translation: I am very excited about the trip to the beach.

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling a strong, tender emotion because of something touching or meaningful.

examples.text: Ella estaba muy emocionada al ver el regalo.
examples.translation: She was very moved when she saw the gift.

faults.quote: (begin) To start doing something... / (start) To take place
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 split 'start' and 'begin'; example 0.1 already shows sense 1.
Missing the stem change (e -> ie) and spelling change (z -> c).

notes: Stem-changing verb (e → ie) in the present tense (empiezo, empiezas), with a spelling change z → c before e (empecé).
Takes the preposition a before an infinitive: empezar a trabajar (to start working).
Synonym of comenzar, though empezar is more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: To begin doing something, or for an event or activity to begin happening.

examples.text: Voy a empezar a estudiar español mañana.
examples.translation: I am going to start studying Spanish tomorrow.

examples.text: La película va a empezar en cinco minutos.
examples.translation: The movie is going to start in five minutes.

faults.quote: /emˈpu.xaɾ/
faults.why: Wrong stress placement; stress is on the last syllable /empuˈxaɾ/.

notes: The opposite of empujar (to push) in Mexico is jalar (to pull).
When meaning 'to push someone to do something', it takes the preposition a before an infinitive: empujar a alguien a hacer algo.

senses.definition: To press against something with force in order to move it away from you.

examples.text: Tienes que empujar la puerta para abrirla.
examples.translation: You have to push the door to open it.

senses.definition: To strongly encourage or pressure someone to do something.

examples.text: Ella siempre me empuja a alcanzar mis metas.
examples.translation: She always pushes me to reach my goals.

faults.quote: Used as an adverb to indicate happening before the usual time,
faults.why: Restates the definition and POS; 'vroeg' is also the past tense of 'vragen'.

notes: Compare with 'vroeger' (earlier / formerly), which refers to the past.
The form 'vroeg' is also the singular past tense of 'vragen' (to ask).

senses.definition: Before the usual or expected time, or near the beginning of a period.

examples.text: Ik moet morgen heel vroeg opstaan.
examples.translation: I have to get up very early tomorrow.

faults.quote: (expect) To anticipate something that is going to happen.
faults.why: 'Wachten' does not mean 'to expect' (which is 'verwachten', as note 1 rightly says).

faults.quote: to wait; to expect
faults.why: Includes false gloss 'to expect'.

notes: Use 'wachten op' when waiting for someone or something.
Do not confuse 'wachten' (to wait) with 'verwachten' (to expect).

senses.definition: To stay in a place or delay acting until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: Ik moet op de bus wachten.
examples.translation: I have to wait for the bus.

notes: Separable verb phrase: in a main clause 'worden' is conjugated and 'wakker' stays later in the sentence ('Ik word wakker').
Do not confuse with 'opstaan' (to get up out of bed). You wake up first, and then you get up.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping.

examples.text: Ik word elke ochtend om zeven uur wakker.
examples.translation: I wake up every morning at seven o'clock.

faults.quote: (temperature) Having or giving out a moderate degree of heat
faults.why: Physical warmth of weather, objects, food and drinks is one sense in Dutch.

notes: Used more broadly than English 'warm', including for cooked meals and hot drinks ('een warme maaltijd', 'warme chocolademelk'). Use 'heet' when something is uncomfortably or dangerously hot.

senses.definition: Having a moderately high or pleasantly heated temperature, of weather, rooms, food, or drinks.

examples.text: Het is vandaag erg warm buiten.
examples.translation: It is very warm outside today.

examples.text: Drink deze thee op als hij nog warm is.
examples.translation: Drink this tea while it is still warm.

senses.definition: Showing enthusiasm, affection, or kindness.

examples.text: Ze kreeg een warm onthaal van haar familie.
examples.translation: She received a warm welcome from her family.

faults.quote: (growth) To increase in size or quantity; to grow.
faults.why: Archaic/literary homonym ('to wax/rise'), not an everyday A2 sense.

faults.quote: This verb has two very different meanings.
faults.why: Notes explain the archaic sense and an unlikely confusion; misses reflexive 'zich wassen'.

notes: Used with a reflexive pronoun when washing yourself: 'Ik was me elke ochtend' (I wash every morning).

senses.definition: To clean something or oneself with water and usually soap.

examples.text: Ik moet mijn handen wassen voor het eten.
examples.translation: I have to wash my hands before eating.

examples.text: Zij is de auto aan het wassen.
examples.translation: She is washing the car.

faults.quote: Добрый is the standard word for 'kind' or 'good-natured'
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage info.

faults.quote: У неё очень добрый характер. — She has a very kind character.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English one says 'kind nature' or 'she is very kind-hearted'.

notes: Do not confuse with хороший ('good' in quality or general assessment): добрый describes warmth of heart and readiness to help, except in fixed greetings like доброе утро ('good morning').

senses.definition: Having or showing a warm, friendly, and caring nature.

examples.text: Моя бабушка — очень добрый и отзывчивый человек.
examples.translation: My grandmother is a very kind and responsive person.

senses.definition: Used in standard greetings and wishes to express goodwill.

examples.text: Доброе утро! Желаю вам доброго дня!
examples.translation: Good morning! I wish you a good day!

faults.quote: /zɐˈvʲistlʲɪvɨj/
faults.why: The 'т' in 'стл' is silent in Russian; IPA must be /zɐˈvʲislʲɪvɨj/.

faults.quote: This word is often used as a negative personality trait
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition; misses the silent 'т' pronunciation note.

notes: The letter т is silent in this word: pronounce it as if written зависливый.
Do not confuse with ревнивый ('jealous'), which is used for romantic relationships or fear of losing someone's affection, whereas завистливый means wanting what someone else has.

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy because someone else has something you want.

examples.text: Он очень завистливый человек и всегда сравнивает себя с другими.
examples.translation: He is a very envious person and always compares himself to others.

faults.quote: Мать была обеспокоенная долгим отсутствием сына.
faults.why: Ungrammatical/unnatural: with an instrumental complement, the short form 'обеспокоена' or instrumental 'обеспокоенной' is required.

faults.quote: Derived from the passive past participle of беспокоить
faults.why: It is from the perfective verb 'обеспокоить', not imperfective 'беспокоить'.

notes: Takes the instrumental case for the cause of worry (обеспокоенный чем-либо) or the preposition за + accusative for the person worried about.
