senses.definition: Feeling or showing worry, anxiety, or unease about something.

examples.text: Родители были очень обеспокоены долгим отсутствием сына.
examples.translation: The parents were very worried by their son's long absence.

examples.text: У врача был обеспокоенный голос.
examples.translation: The doctor had a concerned voice.

faults.quote: bad; poor; unpleasant
faults.why: 'Unpleasant' is in shortGloss but not in the sense glosses.
Notes are trivial filler and miss the crucial irregular comparative 'хуже' (worse).

notes: Has an irregular comparative form: хуже ('worse'), and superlative: худший ('worst').
The corresponding adverb is плохо ('badly'), which is also used impersonally to mean 'to feel unwell' (Мне плохо — 'I feel sick/unwell').

senses.definition: Not good; of low quality, unpleasant, or unfavourable.

examples.text: Вчера была плохая погода.
examples.translation: The weather was bad yesterday.

examples.text: У меня сегодня плохое настроение.
examples.translation: I am in a bad mood today.

faults.quote: Стакан полный воды.
faults.why: Ungrammatical as a predicate with a genitive complement; Russian says 'Стакан полон воды' or 'полный стакан воды'.

faults.quote: Полный can mean holding as much as possible, entirely complete, or describing
faults.why: Merely repeats the definitions of the three senses.

notes: When saying what something is full of, полный takes the genitive case (полный воды — 'full of water') and often uses the short forms полон, полна, полно, полны.
Do not confuse with целый ('whole', 'entire'), which stresses that something is intact or undivided (целый день — 'the whole day').

senses.definition: Containing as much or as many as possible; having no empty space.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.translation: A full glass of water stood on the table.

senses.definition: Having all its parts; not lacking anything; total or absolute.

examples.text: Это полный список всех участников.
examples.translation: This is the complete list of all participants.

senses.definition: Of a person or body: slightly overweight; having a rounded build.

examples.text: Это был невысокий, немного полный мужчина.
examples.translation: He was a short, slightly plump man.

faults.quote: 我吃得太满了。
faults.why: Ungrammatical for eating; Mandarin uses 吃得太饱了 for being stuffed with food.

faults.quote: 杯子里的水满了。
faults.why: Awkward phrasing and calqued translation ('the water is full'); the cup is full.

faults.quote: 满 can mean physically full (a cup or a room) or figuratively full
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the senses.

faults.quote: (feeling) To be completely satisfied or to have reached a limit.
faults.why: Alone, 满 rarely means 'satisfied' (that is 满意); reaching a limit (age/time) is distinct.

notes: Often used as a resultative complement after a verb (e.g., 装满 zhuāngmǎn 'to pack full', 坐满 zuòmǎn 'to fill all the seats').
Do not use 满 for being full from eating; use 饱 (bǎo) instead (我吃饱了 'I am full').

senses.definition: Holding or containing as much as possible.

examples.text: 杯子里的水倒满了。
examples.translation: The cup has been filled with water.

examples.text: 房间里坐满了人。
examples.translation: The room is packed with people.

senses.definition: Covering an entire place or surface.

examples.text: 他忙得满头大汗。
examples.translation: He was so busy his whole head was covered in sweat.

faults.quote: He is still young in age.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of 年纪还轻; in English we simply say 'He is still young'.

notes: The opposite of 轻 is 重 (zhòng, 'heavy' or 'serious').
For 'young', the two-character word 年轻 (niánqīng) is much more common than 轻 alone.

senses.definition: Having little weight; not heavy.

examples.text: 这个箱子很轻。
examples.translation: This box is very light.

senses.definition: Small in degree, force, or seriousness.

examples.text: 她受了轻伤。
examples.translation: She suffered a slight injury.

senses.definition: Not far advanced in years (usually used with 年纪 'age').

examples.text: 他年纪还轻。
examples.translation: He is still young.

faults.quote: pián yí
faults.why: Standard Mandarin pronunciation has a neutral tone on the second syllable (piányi), as note[0] states.

faults.quote: /pʰi̯ɛn˧˥ i˧˥/
faults.why: Second syllable has a neutral tone, not a second tone (/˧˥/).

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'biàn yí' which is a different term meaning 'to give an advantage to'.
faults.why: False: 'to give an advantage to' is also pronounced piányi; biànyí is literary for 'convenient'.

notes: Pronounced piányi (with a neutral tone on 宜), even though 便 is most often read biàn (as in 方便 fāngbiàn 'convenient').
Its opposite is 贵 (guì, 'expensive'). It simply means low-priced and does not imply poor quality.

senses.definition: Costing little money; low in price.

examples.text: 这本书很便宜。
examples.translation: This book is very cheap.

examples.text: 有没有更便宜一点儿的？
examples.translation: Do you have anything a bit cheaper?

faults.quote: white; blank; clear
faults.why: Includes 'clear', which is not covered by any of the senses.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk.
faults.why: Noun definition ('the colour...') for an adjective; should be 'of the colour of...'.

faults.quote: 白 is the standard word for white, as well as things that are blank or unfilled.
faults.why: Merely repeats the glosses of the two senses.

notes: When modifying a noun directly, a single-syllable adjective like 白 is often used without 的 for common items (e.g., 白衬衫 'white shirt', 白纸 'blank paper'), or as 白色 (báisè) with 的 (白色的衬衫).

senses.definition: Having the colour of snow or milk.

examples.text: 她穿着一件白衬衫。
examples.translation: She is wearing a white shirt.

senses.definition: With nothing written, printed, or added.

examples.text: 请在白纸上写下你的名字。
examples.translation: Please write your name on the blank paper.

faults.quote: Used when something does not require money.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful usage information.

notes: Can modify a noun (免费饮料 'free drinks'), be used with 是…的 (是免费的 'is free'), or come directly before a verb as an adverb ('free of charge', e.g., 免费参观 'visit for free').
Only means 'costing no money'. For 'free time', use 有空 (yǒukòng); for 'freedom / unrestricted', use 自由 (zìyóu).

senses.definition: Costing no money.

examples.text: 这个公园是免费的。
examples.translation: This park is free.

examples.text: 我们提供免费的饮料。
examples.translation: We provide free drinks.

faults.quote: This vegetable tastes very good.
faults.why: 'Dieses Gemüse' refers to a vegetable dish or type, not a single piece.

notes: Usually uncountable and used in the singular without an article (e.g., 'Ich esse gern Gemüse' = I like eating vegetables).

senses.definition: Plants or parts of plants that are eaten as savoury food.

examples.text: Ich esse jeden Tag frisches Gemüse.
examples.translation: I eat fresh vegetables every day.

examples.text: Kochen wir heute Abend noch etwas Gemüse dazu?
examples.translation: Shall we cook some vegetables to go with it tonight?

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'Büro' (office)
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'Geschäft' with 'Büro'; plural form is more useful.

notes: Plural: 'die Geschäfte'.
In everyday speech, 'der Laden' is very common for a small shop.

senses.definition: A place where goods or services are sold to the public.

examples.text: Das Geschäft ist heute wegen des Feiertags geschlossen.
examples.translation: The shop is closed today because of the holiday.

senses.definition: Commercial activity, a company, or a business transaction.

examples.text: Er macht gute Geschäfte in der Stadt.
examples.translation: He is doing good business in the city.

faults.quote: Used for anything given voluntarily to someone else, usually on a special
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: Plural: 'die Geschenke'.
Only used for a present you give someone; for a natural ability ('a gift for music'), German uses 'das Talent' or 'die Begabung'.

senses.definition: Something that you give to someone, especially on a special occasion or to thank them.

examples.text: Ich habe ein schönes Geschenk für meine Mutter gekauft.
examples.translation: I bought a nice gift for my mother.

examples.text: Vielen Dank für das tolle Geschenk!
examples.translation: Many thanks for the great present!

faults.quote: It is a neuter noun, so always use 'das' with it.
faults.why: Restates the gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

faults.quote: While 'Gesicht' refers to the physical face, it is also frequently used
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: (expression) The way someone looks or feels, often shown by their eyes
faults.why: 'Ein trauriges Gesicht machen' ('make a sad face') is the same basic sense.

notes: Plural: 'die Gesichter'.
Commonly used in expressions like 'ein freundliches/trauriges Gesicht machen' (to put on a friendly/sad face).

senses.definition: The front part of a person's head, where the eyes, nose, and mouth are, or the expression shown on it.

examples.text: Sie wäscht sich das Gesicht mit kaltem Wasser.
examples.translation: She washes her face with cold water.

examples.text: Er machte ein trauriges Gesicht, als er die Nachricht hörte.
examples.translation: He made a sad face when he heard the news.

faults.quote: In German, 'Glas' refers both to the solid material and the drinking
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses irregular plural 'Gläser' and invariable quantity use.

notes: The plural for drinking glasses is 'die Gläser' (with umlaut). When used as a unit of measure after a number, it stays singular: 'zwei Glas Wasser' (two glasses of water).
As a material, 'Glas' is uncountable and has no plural.

senses.definition: A container made of glass used for drinking, or the amount of liquid it holds.

examples.text: Ich trinke ein Glas Wasser.
examples.translation: I am drinking a glass of water.

senses.definition: A hard, transparent substance used for making windows, bottles, and other objects.

examples.text: Das Fenster besteht aus Glas.
examples.translation: The window is made of glass.

senses.definition: A glass container with a wide opening and a lid, used for storing food such as jam or honey.

examples.text: Ich habe ein Glas Marmelade gekauft.
examples.translation: I bought a jar of jam.

faults.why: Needs a note on the non-obvious stem change in conjugation (целую, целуешь).

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is поцеловать.
Present tense drops -ова- and adds -у-: я целую, ты целуешь, они целуют.

senses.definition: To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or greeting.

examples.text: Мать любит целовать своего ребёнка в щёку.
examples.translation: A mother loves to kiss her child on the cheek.

faults.quote: Осторожно на льду, можно легко падать.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: 'можно легко' with a single unintended fall requires perfective 'упасть', not 'падать'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is упасть.
Do not confuse with капать, which means 'to drip' (like water or rain).

senses.definition: To move downwards from a higher level or lose balance and drop to the ground.

examples.text: Осенью листья падают с деревьев.
examples.translation: In autumn, leaves fall from the trees.

examples.text: Ребёнок учится ходить и часто падает.
examples.translation: The child is learning to walk and falls often.

senses.definition: To decrease in amount, value, or intensity.

examples.text: Цены на овощи начинают падать летом.
examples.translation: Prices for vegetables begin to drop in the summer.

faults.quote: Он всегда любит давать советы.
faults.why: Definition says 'hand something to someone' (physical), but the example is 'give advice' (abstract).
Missing irregular present tense stem (даю, даёшь) and everyday imperative forms (давай/давайте for 'let's').

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is дать.
Present tense drops -ва-: я даю, ты даёшь, они дают. The imperative давай / давайте is very commonly used to mean 'let's'.

senses.definition: To hand, provide, or offer something to someone.

examples.text: Бабушка всегда даёт детям конфеты.
examples.translation: Grandma always gives candy to the children.

examples.text: Он любит давать советы.
examples.translation: He likes to give advice.

senses.definition: To allow or permit someone to do something (with dative + infinitive).

examples.text: Мама не даёт мне смотреть телевизор поздно.
examples.translation: Mom does not let me watch TV late.

faults.quote: Он не мог продать своих друзей.
faults.why: Uses the perfective verb 'продать' instead of the headword 'продавать'.

faults.quote: To be unfaithful to someone's trust for personal gain.
faults.why: 'Betray' is colloquial/marginal for A2 and mostly used in the perfective 'продать'; drop it.
Lacks the perfective pair (продать) and irregular present tense conjugation (продаю, продаёшь).

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is продать.
Present tense drops -ва-: я продаю, ты продаёшь, они продают. Opposite of покупать ('to buy').

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: Они продают свежие овощи на рынке.
examples.translation: They sell fresh vegetables at the market.

faults.quote: Use 'отправлять' when you send physical objects (mail, parcels) or digital items
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1, where 'отправлять' is used for sending people (employees on a trip).
Missing the essential perfective aspect partner 'отправить'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is отправить.
Takes the dative case for the recipient (отправлять другу) or в/на + accusative for a destination (отправлять в Москву). Close in meaning to посылать.

senses.definition: To cause mail, a parcel, or a message to go to a destination.

examples.text: Я отправляю письмо другу.
examples.translation: I am sending a letter to a friend.

examples.text: Он отправляет посылку за границу.
examples.translation: He is sending a parcel abroad.

senses.definition: To direct or arrange for a person to go somewhere for a purpose.

examples.text: Начальник отправляет сотрудников в командировку.
examples.translation: The boss is sending employees on a business trip.

faults.why: Missing the common temporal sense (short time, event, or story).
Should mention the common broken plural قِصَار (qiṣār).

notes: Used for physical length, height, and duration. Feminine: قَصِيرَة (qaṣīra); masculine plural: قِصَار (qiṣār).

senses.definition: Measuring a small distance from end to end.

examples.text: هَذَا الْخَيْطُ قَصِيرٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This string is very short.

senses.definition: Of a person: of small height.

examples.text: أَخِي قَصِيرٌ وَلَكِنَّهُ سَرِيعٌ.
examples.translation: My brother is short, but he is fast.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a small amount of time.

examples.text: قَرَأْتُ قِصَّةً قَصِيرَةً.
examples.translation: I read a short story.

faults.quote: Describes someone who is not afraid of danger or difficult situations.
faults.why: Meta-language ('Describes someone who...') instead of a direct adjective definition.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who faces danger without fear.
faults.why: Notes repeat the definition and add filler instead of giving the irregular plural.

notes: Feminine: شُجَاعَة (šujāʿa); masculine plural: شُجْعَان (šujʿān). Note that شَجَاعَة (šajāʿa, with a fatḥa on the first letter) is the noun 'bravery'.

senses.definition: Ready to face danger or difficulty without showing fear.

examples.text: الطِّفْلُ الشُّجَاعُ لَمْ يَبْكِ عِنْدَ الطَّبِيبِ.
examples.translation: The brave child did not cry at the doctor's.

faults.why: Note [0] mentions the everyday 'tasty/delicious' sense for food, which is missing from senses.

notes: Often used in conversation as an interjection meaning 'okay', 'fine', or 'well then'.

senses.definition: Of a person: having a gentle, caring, and good-hearted nature.

examples.text: هُوَ رَجُلٌ طَيِّبٌ يُسَاعِدُ الْجَمِيعَ.
examples.translation: He is a kind man who helps everyone.

senses.definition: Pleasant, agreeable, or of good quality.

examples.text: كَانَ يَوْمًا طَيِّبًا.
examples.translation: It was a pleasant day.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a pleasant taste.

examples.text: هَذَا الطَّعَامُ طَيِّبٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This food is very tasty.

faults.quote: /qaˈliq/
faults.why: Wrong stress in IPA; in a CVCV word like qaliq, stress is on the first syllable.

faults.quote: Use qaliq to describe someone who is feeling nervous or uneasy
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical information such as the prepositions it takes.

notes: Takes عَلَى (ʿalā) for worrying about someone's safety, and مِنْ (min) or بِشَأْنِ (bi-šaʾni) for worrying about a thing or situation.
Do not confuse with the noun قَلَق (qalaq, 'worry, anxiety').

senses.definition: Feeling uneasy or nervous about something that is happening or might happen.

examples.text: أَنَا قَلِقٌ بِشَأْنِ الِامْتِحَانِ غَدًا.
examples.translation: I am worried about the exam tomorrow.

faults.why: Missing the common temporal sense ('long' in duration, e.g., a long time).

faults.quote: The feminine form is 'طَوِيلَة' (ṭawīlah).
faults.why: Gives the predictable feminine form but omits the essential irregular plural طِوَال (ṭiwāl).

notes: Covers both English 'tall' and 'long'. Feminine: طَوِيلَة (ṭawīla); masculine plural: طِوَال (ṭiwāl).

senses.definition: Of a person or vertical object: of great or more than average height.

examples.text: هَذَا الرَّجُلُ طَوِيلٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This man is very tall.

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from one end to the other.

examples.text: الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلٌ.
examples.translation: The road is long.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a great amount of time.

examples.text: اِنْتَظَرْنَا وَقْتًا طَوِيلًا.
examples.translation: We waited a long time.

faults.why: Northern Vietnamese 'óc' closes with double labiovelar /awk͡p̚˧˥/, not plain /ɔk̚/.

faults.quote: To have tears from your eyes as a natural reaction

faults.quote: Use khóc when expressing sadness, grief, or physical pain through tears
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition of crying.

notes: Refers to crying from emotion or pain; for eyes watering (e.g., from onions or wind), use 'chảy nước mắt'.

senses.definition: To shed tears, typically while making sounds of pain, grief, or emotion.

examples.text: Em bé đang khóc vì đói.
examples.translation: The baby is crying because it's hungry.

faults.why: Missing the medial labial glide /w/ represented by 'o' in 'khỏe' (/xwɛ˧˩˧/).

faults.quote: Khỏe is very flexible. It describes both a state of being healthy
faults.why: Restates the two senses without adding usage information.

notes: The standard word used in greetings to ask how someone is ('Bạn có khỏe không?').
Also spelled 'khoẻ' under the newer tone-placement convention.

senses.definition: In a good physical state; not ill.

examples.text: Dạo này bạn có khỏe không?
examples.translation: How have you been lately?

senses.definition: Having great physical power and muscle strength.

examples.text: Anh ấy rất khỏe, có thể nhấc bổng cái thùng nặng này.
examples.translation: He is very strong and can lift this heavy crate right up.

senses.definition: Having good physical health; free from illness and physically strong.

examples.text: Ông ấy đã bảy mươi tuổi nhưng vẫn rất khỏe mạnh.
examples.translation: He is seventy years old, but he is still very healthy.

faults.quote: Used to express that an action or state does not happen
faults.why: Both notes merely define 'never' and 'not', missing placement before the verb.

senses.definition: At no time in the past, present, or future; not ever.

examples.text: Anh ấy không bao giờ đến đúng giờ.
examples.translation: He never arrives on time.

faults.quote: In spoken Vietnamese, this is often shortened to just 'không'
faults.why: In yes/no questions ('Có... không?'), 'không' is the question particle or negative reply, not shortened 'không có'.

faults.quote: Used to express both personal possession (I don't have) and existence
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to not have; there is no
notes: Placed before a noun to negate possession or existence. In southern spoken Vietnamese, it is also commonly used before verbs to emphasize negation (e.g., 'Tôi không có biết' = 'I don't know').

senses.definition: To not possess or own something.

examples.text: Tôi không có tiền.
examples.translation: I don't have any money.

senses.definition: Used to say that something or someone does not exist or is not present.

examples.text: Ở đây không có ai.
examples.translation: There is no one here.

faults.quote: While 'walad' commonly means 'boy', it can also be used
faults.why: Restates the glosses and senses while omitting the crucial irregular plural (أَوْلَاد).
Missing examples for both senses of this core A1/A2 word.

notes: The broken plural is أَوْلَاد (ʾawlād), which often refers to 'children' in general regardless of gender.

senses.definition: A male child or youth.

examples.text: يَلْعَبُ الوَلَدُ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ.
examples.translation: The boy is playing in the park.

senses.definition: A person's male child, or a child of either sex (especially in the plural).

examples.text: لَدَيْهِمْ ثَلَاثَةُ أَوْلَادٍ.
examples.translation: They have three children.

faults.quote: احْتَرَمْتُ وَالِدَانِ الصَّدِيق.
faults.why: Severely ungrammatical: dual noun in idafa must drop ن and be accusative here (وَالِدَيِ الصَّدِيقِ).

senses.definition: A person's mother and father together.

examples.text: أَحْتَرِمُ وَالِدَيَّ كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: I respect my parents a lot.

faults.quote: Used commonly as a sweetener in Arabic coffee, tea, and desserts.
faults.why: World-knowledge filler that teaches nothing about the Arabic word (and traditional Arabic coffee is unsweetened).

notes: Uncountable mass noun.

senses.definition: A sweet white or brown substance used to sweeten food and drinks.

examples.text: أُحِبُّ الشَّايَ مَعَ السُّكَّرِ.
examples.translation: I like tea with sugar.

faults.quote: قَدَمِي تَؤْلِمُنِي بَعْدَ المَشْيِ كَثِيرًا.

senses.definition: The lower part of the leg upon which a person stands and walks.

examples.text: قَدَمِي تُؤْلِمُنِي بَعْدَ المَشْيِ الطَّوِيلِ.
examples.translation: My foot hurts after the long walk.

faults.quote: this must be used as a predicate phrase in Korean.
faults.why: False: 돈이 많은 is very commonly used attributively before nouns (e.g., 돈이 많은 사람).

senses.definition: Having a lot of money; rich or wealthy.

terms: to have a lot of money

examples.text: 그는 돈이 많아서 좋은 차를 샀어요.
examples.translation: He is rich, so he bought a nice car.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 split a single meaning; 부럽다 is generally benign envy.

faults.quote: Use this when you feel a pang of desire
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition while missing the irregular ㅂ conjugation and argument structure.

senses.definition: Causing someone to wish they had the same good fortune, quality, or possession; feeling such a wish.

examples.translation: I'm so envious that you live in such a pretty house.

faults.quote: Used for physical textures that are soft to the touch
faults.why: Merely repeats the senses instead of noting the irregular ㅂ conjugation (부드러워요).
Missing irregular ㅂ conjugation (부드러워요, 부드러운).

notes: Irregular ㅂ adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (부드러워요, 부드러운).

senses.definition: Of food, fabric, skin, or a surface: soft, tender, or smooth to the touch.

examples.text: 이 빵은 아주 부드러워요.
examples.translation: This bread is very soft.

examples.text: 아기 피부는 정말 부드러워요.
examples.translation: A baby's skin is really smooth.

senses.definition: Of a person, voice, or manner: kind, calm, and not harsh.

examples.text: 그 선생님은 목소리가 부드러워요.
examples.translation: That teacher has a gentle voice.

faults.quote: Lacking knowledge or information about a certain subject.
faults.why: 'Uninformed' (~에 어둡다) is an advanced idiom, while common A2 'gloomy/dark (color/mood)' is missing.

faults.quote: 어둡다 describes a place or time that is dark
faults.why: Restates sense 0 instead of giving the irregular ㅂ conjugation (어두워요, 어두운).
Missing irregular ㅂ conjugation (어두워요, 어두운).

notes: Irregular ㅂ adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (어두워요, 어두운). Its opposite is 밝다 ('bright').

senses.definition: Having little or no light; not bright in color.

examples.text: 방 안이 어두워서 불을 켰어요.
examples.translation: It was dark inside the room, so I turned on the light.

senses.definition: Of a mood, expression, or atmosphere: sad, heavy, or not cheerful.

examples.text: 오늘따라 표정이 왜 그렇게 어두워요?
examples.translation: Why do you look so gloomy today?

faults.why: Missing irregular ㄹ conjugation note (ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ: 긴, 깁니다).

notes: Irregular ㄹ adjective: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, and ㅅ (긴, 깁니다), though it stays before 어/아 (길어요). Its opposite is 짧다 ('short').
Use 길다 for length (머리가 길다, 'to have long hair') and 크다 for overall size or a person's height (키가 크다, 'to be tall').

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from one end to the other.

examples.text: 이 길은 너무 길어요.
examples.translation: This road is too long.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a large amount of time.

examples.text: 긴 시간 동안 기다렸어요.
examples.translation: I waited for a long time.

faults.quote: adv
faults.why: Time words (时间名词) in Chinese are nouns, even when used adverbially; defined as a noun.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with '现在' (xiàn zài), which means 'now'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'today' with 'now'; replace with standard word-order note.

notes: Time words like 今天 are placed either at the start of the sentence or directly after the subject (e.g., 我今天很忙 or 今天我很忙), never at the end as in English.

senses.definition: On or during this present day; the day happening now.

examples.text: 今天天气很好。
examples.translation: The weather is very good today.

faults.quote: 经常 indicates that an action happens repeatedly over a period of time
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage information.

faults.quote: (routine) Occurring regularly as a matter of routine.
faults.why: Adjectival sense in a 'pos: adv' entry; example actually uses the derived word 经常性.

notes: Placed after the subject and before the verb. Very close in meaning to 常常 (chángcháng); both mean 'often' and are interchangeable in most everyday contexts.

senses.definition: Many times at short intervals; on many occasions.

examples.text: 他经常去图书馆看书。
examples.translation: He often goes to the library to read.

faults.quote: A thing that is able to happen or exist.
faults.why: Noun definition and glosses inside an adverb entry; adjectival/modal uses are also common.

notes: As an adverb ('maybe', 'might'), it goes before the verb (他可能不来). It is also used as an adjective meaning 'possible' (这完全可能) and a noun meaning 'possibility' (有这个可能).

senses.definition: Perhaps; used to say that something may or may not happen or be true.

examples.text: 他明天可能不来。
examples.translation: He might not come tomorrow.

senses.definition: Able to happen or be done; or the chance that something may happen.

examples.text: 这种事情完全可能发生。
examples.translation: This kind of thing could very well happen.

examples.text: 这件事情很有可能成功。
examples.translation: There is a good possibility that this will succeed.

notes: In simple 'subject + adjective' sentences (e.g., 他很高 'He is tall'), 很 is normally required before the adjective and carries little emphasis unless stressed. Without 很, the sentence implies a comparison.
Do not use 很 before the adjective in 比 (bǐ) comparisons (say 他比我高, not 他比我很高).

senses.definition: To a high degree; also used as a default link before predicate adjectives.

examples.text: 今天的天气很好。
examples.translation: The weather today is very nice.

examples.text: 他很高兴。
examples.translation: He is very happy.

faults.quote: 总是 (zǒngshì) indicates that something happens on every occasion without exception
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the glosses 'always' and 'often' without useful grammar guidance.

notes: Placed after the subject and before the verb or adjective. In spoken Chinese it can often be shortened to 总 (zǒng).

senses.definition: At all times; on every occasion.

examples.text: 他总是笑得很开心。
examples.translation: He always smiles happily.

examples.text: 他上班总是迟到。
examples.translation: He is always late for work.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (ほし) for kanji headword.

faults.quote: star; heavenly body
faults.why: 'heavenly body' is not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: Can also be used metaphorically in Japanese to describe someone who
faults.why: Describes a marginal metaphorical use instead of everyday usage.

notes: In everyday speech, 星 (ほし) refers to any point of light in the night sky, including visible planets, as well as the five-pointed star shape (☆).

senses.definition: A bright point of light seen in the night sky, or a large ball of burning gas in space.

examples.text: 夜空に星がたくさん見える。
examples.translation: I can see many stars in the night sky.

faults.quote: 少し休みましょう。
faults.why: Uses the verb 休む (休みましょう), not the noun 休み.

notes: Often used with the polite prefix お as お休み (おやすみ), which is also the standard greeting for 'good night' (おやすみなさい).

senses.definition: A day or period of time away from work or school, or a day when a shop is closed.

examples.text: 来週は休みをとります。
examples.translation: I will take time off next week.

examples.text: 明日は学校が休みです。
examples.translation: There is no school tomorrow.

senses.definition: A short pause for rest during work, study, or another activity.

examples.text: 昼休みに散歩をしました。
examples.translation: I took a walk during my lunch break.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (もうふ) for kanji headword.

notes: Counted with the counter 枚 (まい) for flat objects.
Do not confuse with 掛け布団 (かけぶとん), which is a thick quilt or duvet.

senses.definition: A thick, soft cover used on a bed to keep warm.

examples.text: 寒い夜なので、毛布をもう一枚使います。
examples.translation: It is a cold night, so I will use one more blanket.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (おかね) for kanji headword.

faults.quote: (wealth) Wealth or personal fortune.
faults.why: 'Money' as currency and 'having a lot of money' are a single sense.

notes: The prefix お is standard in everyday speech; 金 (かね) without お sounds rough or blunt.
For physical cash as opposed to card or digital payment, use 現金 (げんきん).

senses.definition: Coins, banknotes, or funds used to buy things and pay for services.

examples.text: お金が足りません。
examples.translation: I do not have enough money.

examples.text: 彼はお金をたくさん持っています。
examples.translation: He has a lot of money.

notes: Commonly used in expressions like 熱がある (to have a fever), 熱が出る (to develop a fever), and 熱が下がる (for a fever to go down).
Do not use 熱 for hot weather; use 暑さ (あつさ) instead.

senses.definition: A body temperature that is higher than normal because of illness.

examples.text: 熱があるから、今日は休みます。
examples.translation: I have a fever, so I will take the day off today.

senses.definition: The quality of being hot, or high temperature produced by fire, a machine, or the sun.

examples.text: この機械は熱を持ちやすいです。
examples.translation: This machine tends to build up heat.

faults.quote: To know what a word or expression signifies.
faults.why: Understanding a word and understanding in general are the same sense.

notes: Capire is an -isc- verb, adding -isc- in singular and third-person plural present forms (capisco, capisci, capisce, capiscono).

senses.definition: To grasp the meaning of words, a language, or a situation.

examples.text: Non capisco questa parola.
examples.translation: I don't understand this word.

faults.quote: Used to describe both poor quality and bad behavior.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a note on position or irregular comparative 'peggiore' is needed.

faults.quote: Oggi c'è un cattivo tempo.
faults.why: Unnatural with the indefinite article; 'Oggi fa cattivo tempo' is natural Italian.

notes: Has the irregular comparative 'peggiore' (worse), alongside regular 'più cattivo' (often used for behavior).
Usually placed after the noun for behavior or quality, but before it in set phrases like 'cattivo tempo' (bad weather).

senses.definition: Of poor quality, unpleasant, or unfavorable.

examples.text: Oggi fa cattivo tempo.
examples.translation: Today the weather is bad.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: behaving badly, unkind, or disobedient.

examples.text: Il cane è stato cattivo oggi.
examples.translation: The dog was naughty today.

faults.quote: Use chiedere when you want to ask a question or request information.
faults.why: Merely restates the senses; notes on prepositions (chiedere a) and irregular past participle (chiesto) are missing.

notes: Takes 'a' before the person being asked: chiedere qualcosa a qualcuno (to ask someone for something).
Has an irregular past participle (chiesto) and past historic (chiesi).

senses.definition: To put a question to someone in order to get information.

examples.text: Posso chiederti una cosa?
examples.translation: Can I ask you something?

senses.definition: To speak or write to someone in order to get something from them.

examples.text: Voglio chiedere un favore al mio amico.
examples.translation: I want to ask my friend for a favor.

faults.quote: Used for physical objects like doors and windows, but also for locking
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses; should instead give the irregular past participle 'chiuso'.

corrected.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to turn off
notes: Has an irregular past participle (chiuso) and past historic (chiusi).
For electrical appliances and lights, 'spegnere' is normally used rather than 'chiudere'.

senses.definition: To move a door, window, lid, or similar object so that it is no longer open.

examples.text: Ricordati di chiudere la finestra prima di uscire.
examples.translation: Remember to close the window before going out.

senses.definition: To stop operating a shop, business, or public building for the day or permanently.

examples.text: Il supermercato chiude alle nove di sera.
examples.translation: The supermarket closes at nine in the evening.

senses.definition: To stop the flow of water or gas by turning a tap or valve.

examples.text: Non dimenticare di chiudere il rubinetto dell'acqua.
examples.translation: Don't forget to turn off the water tap.

faults.quote: Used both when meeting someone and when leaving them.
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses directly below it.

notes: Informal: used with friends, family, children, and peers. Use 'buongiorno', 'buonasera', or 'arrivederci' with strangers or in formal situations.

senses.definition: Used as an informal greeting when meeting someone.

examples.text: Ciao, come stai?
examples.translation: Hello, how are you?

senses.definition: Used as an informal farewell when leaving someone.

examples.text: Ci vediamo domani, ciao!
examples.translation: See you tomorrow, bye!

faults.quote: Miedo is a noun, so it usually appears with a verb like
faults.why: Redundant with notes[1]; can be merged and improved with preposition usage.

faults.quote: Tengo miedo a las arañas.
faults.why: Normally 'Tengo miedo de las arañas' or 'Les tengo miedo a las arañas'.

notes: Spanish uses 'tener miedo (de)' where English uses 'to be afraid (of)', or 'dar miedo' for 'to be scary'.

senses.definition: The unpleasant feeling you have when you think you are in danger or something bad might happen.

examples.text: Le tengo miedo a las arañas.
examples.translation: I am afraid of spiders.

faults.quote: Espero un minuto, por favor.
faults.why: Confuses 1st person 'espero' with imperative 'espera'/'espere'; unidiomatic with 'por favor'.

faults.quote: Used identically to the English 'minute' when talking about time.
faults.why: Filler note stating the obvious.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds, or a very short period of time.

examples.text: Espera un minuto, por favor.
examples.translation: Wait a minute, please.

faults.quote: Used as an adjective to describe someone or something that is attractive,
faults.why: Adjective sense does not belong in a noun entry ('el mono').

faults.quote: A single piece of clothing that covers the body, including the legs
faults.why: Peninsular Spanish usage; in Mexico a jumpsuit/overalls is 'overol', not 'mono'.

faults.quote: monkey; jumpsuit; cute
faults.why: Includes non-Mexican sense ('jumpsuit') and adjective sense ('cute').

faults.quote: In Mexico, 'tener mono' is not commonly used for the animal; stick
faults.why: Bizarre and unhelpful note about a Peninsular slang idiom ('tener mono').

notes: In everyday Mexican Spanish, 'chango' is also very commonly used to mean 'monkey'.

senses.definition: An animal with a long tail that lives in warm countries and climbs trees.

examples.text: El mono salta de rama en rama en la selva.
examples.translation: The monkey jumps from branch to branch in the jungle.

faults.quote: Used similarly to English 'the world', often to emphasize size or universality.
faults.why: Filler note; misses key everyday phrase 'todo el mundo' (everyone).

notes: The phrase 'todo el mundo' very often means 'everyone' or 'everybody', not just 'the whole world'.

senses.definition: The earth and all the people, places, and things on it.

examples.text: Quiero viajar por todo el mundo.
examples.translation: I want to travel around the whole world.

senses.definition: A particular area of activity or group of people and their way of life.

examples.text: El mundo de la moda es muy competitivo.
examples.translation: The fashion world is very competitive.

faults.quote: Use the masculine article 'el' with 'museo'.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

senses.definition: A building where objects of historical, scientific, or artistic interest are kept and shown to the public.

examples.text: Fuimos al museo de historia ayer por la tarde.
examples.translation: We went to the history museum yesterday afternoon.

faults.quote: (remember) To think of someone with care and remember them
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning ('to miss/think fondly of someone or something absent').

faults.quote: 老师一直在想念着他毕业的学生们。
faults.why: 想念 is rarely used with 着, and 学生们 after a modifier is unnatural.

notes: More emotional and formal than 想 (xiǎng). While 想 can also mean 'to want to' or 'to think', 想念 specifically means missing someone or something absent.

senses.definition: To feel longing for someone or something that is far away or in the past.

examples.text: 我在国外的时候，常常想念我的家人。
examples.translation: When I was abroad, I often missed my family.

faults.why: Should explain that 游泳 is a separable verb (离合词), e.g., 游了一次泳.

notes: A separable verb (离合词, verb-object compound): aspect particles, duration, and measure words go between 游 and 泳 (e.g., 游了泳, 游一个小时泳).

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your arms and legs.

examples.text: 我夏天喜欢去游泳。
examples.translation: I like to go swimming in the summer.

faults.quote: 虽然多年没见，但我一眼就认识了她。
faults.why: Ungrammatical for 'recognized at a glance'; Chinese requires the resultative 认出(来), not 认识了.

faults.quote: (identification) To identify someone or something by sight, hearing, or prior experience.
faults.why: Recognizing characters/things by familiarity belongs with sense 0; instant identification is 认出.

faults.quote: understand, realize, cognition
faults.why: 'cognition' is a noun, but the entry and sense are for a verb.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to recognize; to get to know
notes: Use 认识 for being acquainted with a person, knowing a place, or recognizing written characters. Use 知道 (zhīdào) for knowing a fact or piece of information.

senses.definition: To know or be familiar with a person, place, or written character; or to meet and get to know someone.

examples.text: 我认识这个人，他是我的老朋友。
examples.translation: I know this person; he is my old friend.

examples.text: 这个汉字你认识吗？
examples.translation: Do you recognize this Chinese character?

senses.definition: To understand the nature or significance of a situation or issue.

examples.text: 我们应该正确认识这个问题。
examples.translation: We should properly understand this issue.

faults.quote: (possession) To have to have something; to be in a situation
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the exact same meaning ('to need something').

faults.quote: to have to have something, must have
faults.why: 'to have to have something' is a definition phrase, not a natural translation gloss.

notes: Can be followed by a noun (需要水, 'need water') or a verb phrase (需要休息, 'need to rest'). Also used as a noun meaning 'need' or 'requirement'.
Unlike 要 (yào), which often means 'to want' or 'to be going to', 需要 specifically emphasizes necessity.

senses.definition: To need something or have to do something because it is necessary.

examples.text: 我需要一杯热水。
examples.translation: I need a cup of hot water.

examples.text: 学习一门新语言需要很多时间。
examples.translation: Learning a new language requires a lot of time.

faults.quote: Use 问 when you want to ask someone a question or inquire
faults.why: Purely restates the definition without adding usage or contrast information.

notes: Takes two objects directly (问 + person + question/thing): 问老师一个问题 (ask the teacher a question).
Do not confuse with 请 (qǐng) or 让 (ràng), which are used for 'asking' someone to do something (making a request). 问 is only for asking for information.

senses.definition: To speak or write to someone in order to get an answer or information.

examples.text: 我想问你一个问题。
examples.translation: I want to ask you a question.

faults.quote: Used for the general act of preparing food with heat.
faults.why: Restates the definition and adds unhelpful comparison with 'mencuci' (to wash).

notes: Formed from the root 'masak' with the active prefix 'meN-'. In casual speech, the root 'masak' is often used on its own as a verb.

senses.definition: To prepare food for eating by heating it.

examples.text: Dia sedang memasak nasi di dapur.
examples.translation: He is cooking rice in the kitchen.

faults.quote: To utter or recite written text out loud.
faults.why: Reading silently and reading aloud are shades of one meaning.

notes: Formed from the root 'baca' with the active prefix 'meN-'. In imperatives (commands), drop the prefix and use 'baca'.

senses.definition: To look at written words and understand what they mean, either silently or aloud.

examples.text: Saya suka membaca buku di perpustakaan.
examples.translation: I like to read books in the library.

examples.text: Dia membaca puisi di depan kelas.
examples.translation: He is reading a poem in front of the class.

faults.quote: To cause someone to stop sleeping.
faults.why: Waking someone up is 'membangunkan', not 'membangun', as the entry's own note admits.

faults.quote: Tolong bangunkan adik sebelum jam tujuh.
faults.why: Uses 'bangunkan' (from 'membangunkan'), not the headword 'membangun'.

faults.quote: to build; to construct; to wake someone up
faults.why: Includes false meaning 'to wake someone up' (which is 'membangunkan').

notes: Formed from the root 'bangun' (to wake up / get up), but with the prefix 'meN-' it means 'to build'. To say 'wake someone up', use 'membangunkan' (with the suffix '-kan').

senses.definition: To make a building or other structure by putting parts together.

examples.text: Mereka sedang membangun rumah baru di dekat sungai.
examples.translation: They are building a new house near the river.

senses.definition: To create and develop something over time, such as a business, career, or relationship.

examples.text: Mereka bekerja keras untuk membangun bisnis keluarga.
examples.translation: They worked hard to build the family business.

faults.quote: To make something easier or more possible for someone.
faults.why: Helping a person and a thing helping someone are the same basic meaning.

notes: Formed from the root 'bantu' with the active prefix 'meN-'. Related words include 'bantuan' (help/assistance) and 'pembantu' (helper/domestic worker).

senses.definition: To make it easier for someone to do something, or to do part of the work for them.

examples.text: Dia membantu ibunya memasak di dapur.
examples.translation: She helps her mother cook in the kitchen.

examples.text: Aplikasi ini membantu saya belajar bahasa Indonesia.
examples.translation: This application helps me learn Indonesian.

faults.quote: Tolong membawa buku itu ke sini.
faults.why: Direct imperatives in Indonesian drop the 'meN-' prefix; it should be 'Tolong bawa'.

faults.quote: To hold or support something while moving from one place to another.
faults.why: Indonesian 'membawa' covers both English 'bring/take' and 'carry' as a single concept.

corrected.shortGloss: to bring; to take; to carry
notes: Formed from the root 'bawa' with the active prefix 'meN-'. In commands (e.g. after 'tolong' or 'jangan'), drop the prefix and use 'bawa'.
Unlike English, 'membawa' does not depend on direction: it translates as 'bring', 'take', or 'carry' depending on context.

senses.definition: To hold or have something with you when you go somewhere.

examples.text: Jangan lupa membawa payung karena hari ini akan hujan.
examples.translation: Don't forget to bring an umbrella because it is going to rain today.

examples.text: Dia membawa tas berat ke sekolah.
examples.translation: She is carrying a heavy bag to school.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'κουρασμένος', which means tired or exhausted.
faults.why: Unrelated word; learners have no reason to confuse 'άρρωστος' with 'κουρασμένος'.

faults.quote: Unhealthy or morbid in a figurative or mental sense.
faults.why: For 'morbid jealousy' Greek normally uses 'αρρωστημένος'; marginal sense for A2.

notes: Used both for a short-term illness like a cold and for a serious condition.

senses.definition: Suffering from an illness; not feeling well.

examples.text: Είμαι άρρωστος και δεν μπορώ να πάω στη δουλειά.
examples.translation: I am sick and I cannot go to work.

faults.quote: Το ολισθηρό δρόμος είναι επικίνδυνος για τους οδηγούς.
faults.why: Ungrammatical gender agreement: 'δρόμος' is masculine ('Ο ολισθηρός δρόμος'), not neuter.

faults.quote: /e.piˈci.ði.nos/
faults.why: Missing nasal/stop for 'νδ'; standard pronunciation is /epiˈcinðinos/ or /epiˈciðinos/, best shown with nasal.

faults.quote: (risk) Involving a high level of risk or uncertainty
faults.why: Shades of one meaning ('dangerous / risky'); Note 0 even contradicts Sense 1.

notes: Used both for physical danger and for risky actions or decisions.

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or serious problems.

examples.text: Ο παγωμένος δρόμος είναι επικίνδυνος για τους οδηγούς.
examples.translation: The icy road is dangerous for drivers.

examples.text: Είναι επικίνδυνο να οδηγείς τόσο γρήγορα.
examples.translation: It is dangerous to drive so fast.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('The colour...') instead of a quality ('Having the colour...').

senses.definition: Having the colour of snow or milk.

examples.text: Το χιόνι είναι άσπρο.
examples.translation: Snow is white.

senses.definition: Of a person or face: lacking colour because of fear, shock, or illness.

examples.text: Έγινε άσπρος από τον φόβο του.
examples.translation: He went pale from fear.

faults.quote: He shared a piquant detail about their story.
faults.why: 'A piquant detail' is unnatural in everyday English; 'a juicy/spicy detail' is natural.

notes: 'Πικάντικος' describes food with a strong, rich, or mildly hot flavour (like aged cheese or spiced sausage), whereas 'καυτερός' specifically means burning hot from chilli.

senses.definition: Of food: having a strong, savoury, or pleasantly hot flavour from spices.

examples.text: Αυτή η σάλτσα είναι αρκετά πικάντικη.
examples.translation: This sauce is quite spicy.

senses.definition: Of a story, joke, or gossip: excitingly indiscreet or slightly risqué.

examples.text: Μας είπε μια πικάντικη λεπτομέρεια για τη σχέση τους.
examples.translation: He told us a juicy detail about their relationship.

faults.quote: (fortunate) Having good luck or enjoying favorable life circumstances.

faults.quote: Note the masculine gender: der Kaffee.

examples.translation: I like to drink a coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: A single sheet or page displaying the days, weeks and months

examples.text: Ich esse gerne Käse auf meinem Brot.

faults.quote: A piece of furniture with shelves or drawers

examples.text: Wir müssen noch einen Kasten Wasser für die Party kaufen.

senses.definition: Having little money or lacking basic material needs.

examples.text: Mucha gente pobre necesita ayuda en esta ciudad.
examples.translation: Many poor people need help in this city.

examples.text: Έκανα μεγάλη πατάτα χθες στη δουλειά.
examples.translation: I made a huge blunder yesterday at work.

faults.quote: Used for both a backyard garden with flowers and a small patch
faults.why: Restates the definition and adds an obvious contrast with 'πάρκο'.

notes: Also used for a large public garden (e.g., ο Εθνικός Κήπος, the National Garden).

senses.definition: A piece of land next to a house where people grow flowers, grass, or vegetables.

examples.text: Ο κήπος μας έχει πολλά λουλούδια.
examples.translation: Our garden has many flowers.

faults.quote: /ˈaz ˈvɛzis/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in 'vezes': it has a closed /e/ (/ˈvezis/), not open /ɛ/.

faults.quote: Never use 'à vez'.
faults.why: 'Um de cada vez' / 'à vez' exists in some contexts; overstates the rule.

notes: Always plural ('às vezes') and written with a grave accent (`à`), from the contraction of the preposition 'a' + article 'as'.

senses.definition: On some occasions, but not always.

examples.text: Às vezes, eu gosto de caminhar sozinho na praia.
examples.translation: Sometimes, I like to walk alone on the beach.

examples.text: O trânsito fica muito ruim às vezes.
examples.translation: Traffic gets really bad sometimes.

faults.quote: to watch; to attend to; to assist
faults.why: Lists 'to assist', contradicting the note and lacking a corresponding sense.

faults.quote: it does not mean 'to assist' or 'to help'.
faults.why: It actually can mean 'to assist/help' in formal or medical contexts, though 'ajudar' is everyday.

notes: When meaning 'to watch' or 'to attend', formal grammar requires the preposition 'a' ('assistir a um filme'), though in everyday Brazilian speech the 'a' is very often dropped ('assistir um filme').
Watch out for the false friend: in everyday speech, it means 'to watch', not 'to help'. For 'to help', use 'ajudar' ('assistir' means 'to assist' only in formal or medical contexts).

senses.definition: To look at something for a period of time, such as a film, a show, or a sports match.

examples.text: Eu gosto de assistir a filmes de terror no fim de semana.
examples.translation: I like to watch horror movies on the weekend.

senses.definition: To be present at an event, class, or performance.

examples.text: Nós assistimos à palestra sobre tecnologia ontem.
examples.translation: We attended the lecture about technology yesterday.

faults.quote: (color) The colour of a clear sky... / (appearance) A common color...
faults.why: Both senses mean the exact same color 'blue'; should be one sense.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the ocean.
faults.why: Defined as a noun ('The colour...') instead of an adjective ('Having the color...').

notes: Does not change form for masculine and feminine ('o carro azul', 'a camisa azul'). The plural is 'azuis'.

senses.definition: Of the color of a clear sky or the deep sea.

examples.text: O céu está muito azul hoje.
examples.translation: The sky is very blue today.

examples.text: Ele comprou uma camisa azul.
examples.translation: He bought a blue shirt.

faults.quote: Refers to something that is at a small distance from the ground
faults.why: Doesn't cover low prices, levels, or volume, which the example itself uses.

faults.quote: Refers to a person who is not tall.
faults.why: Meta-language ('Refers to...'); should be an adjectival phrase ('Of a person: not tall').

notes: For a person's height, use 'baixo' ('short'), not 'pequeno' ('small' in size or young in age).
Can also be used as an adverb meaning 'quietly' or 'in a low voice', as in 'falar baixo' (to speak quietly).

senses.definition: Of a person: not tall; below average height.

examples.text: O meu irmão é baixo.
examples.translation: My brother is short.

senses.definition: Close to the ground, or small in amount, level, price, or intensity.

examples.text: O preço da gasolina está baixo hoje.
examples.translation: The price of gasoline is low today.

examples.text: A mesa da sala é bem baixa.
examples.translation: The living room table is quite low.

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: not loud; quiet.

examples.text: A música está muito baixa, não consigo ouvir.
examples.translation: The music is very low; I can't hear it.

faults.quote: Barato is used to describe items that do not cost much money.
faults.why: Purely restates the definition and gloss.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with 'barata', which means 'cockroach'
faults.why: Misleading: 'barata' is also the regular feminine form of the adjective 'barato'.

notes: The feminine form is 'barata' ('uma roupa barata'). As a feminine noun ('a barata'), the same word also means 'cockroach'.
The opposite is 'caro' (expensive).

senses.definition: Costing little money; low in price.

examples.text: Comprei um sapato muito barato na liquidação.
examples.translation: I bought a very cheap pair of shoes at the sale.

faults.quote: Durmak covers three main ideas: stopping movement, staying in a place
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses and glosses.

corrected.shortGloss: to stop; to stay, remain; to stand
notes: Takes the locative case (-da/-de) for the place where someone or something stops, stays, or stands.
Used as an auxiliary after -ıp/-ip or -a/-e to show continuous action (e.g. bakıp durmak 'to keep looking').

senses.definition: To cease moving or doing something.

examples.text: Araba kırmızı ışıkta durdu.
examples.translation: The car stopped at the red light.

senses.definition: To remain in a particular place or state.

examples.text: Bugün evde duracağım.
examples.translation: I will stay at home today.

senses.definition: To be in an upright position on one's feet (often with ayakta).

examples.text: Otobüste bütün yol ayakta durdum.
examples.translation: I stood the whole way on the bus.

faults.quote: Borrowed from French 'douche', 'duş' is used both for the bathroom fixture
faults.why: Etymology and obvious usage are filler; misses essential collocations 'duş almak' and 'duş yapmak'.

faults.quote: Water sprayed on you to wash.
faults.why: Defines the water rather than the act of washing or the bathroom fixture.

notes: To say 'to take a shower', Turkish uses duş almak or duş yapmak.

senses.definition: An act of washing oneself under sprayed water, or the bathroom fixture used for this.

examples.text: Sabahları soğuk bir duş alıyorum.
examples.translation: I take a cold shower in the mornings.

faults.quote: Düşmek is an intransitive verb meaning to fall or drop.
faults.why: Restates the glosses; fails to mention the dative case (-a/-e) for the destination.

notes: Takes the ablative case (-dan/-den) for where something falls from, and the dative (-a/-e) for where it lands.

senses.definition: To move downwards quickly from a higher position, usually by accident.

examples.text: Elma ağaçtan yere düştü.
examples.translation: The apple fell from the tree to the ground.

senses.definition: To go down in price, temperature, value, or amount.

examples.text: Bugün hava sıcaklığı çok düştü.
examples.translation: The air temperature dropped a lot today.

faults.quote: and the locative case (-de) when you dwell or ponder on a topic.
faults.why: Düşünmek does not take a bare locative for the topic; 'bu konuda' is an adverbial phrase.

faults.quote: to think; to consider; to wonder
faults.why: 'To wonder' is not in the senses, while sense 1 ('to plan, intend') is missing.

corrected.shortGloss: to think, consider; to plan, intend
notes: Takes the accusative case (-ı/-i/-u/-ü) for the person, thing, or action (-mayı/-meyi) being thought about or planned.
Do not confuse with sanmak, which means 'to suppose' or 'to think (mistakenly)' without being sure.

senses.definition: To use one's mind to reflect on something or form an opinion.

examples.text: Bu konuyu biraz düşünmek istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to think about this subject a little.

senses.definition: To have an intention or plan to do something.

examples.text: Yarın İstanbul'a gitmeyi düşünüyorum.
examples.translation: I am thinking of going to Istanbul tomorrow.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'bahçe çiti' which specifically means a garden fence.
faults.why: Both notes are trivial filler; no learner confuses 'duvar' with 'bahçe çiti'.

senses.definition: A vertical structure that divides or encloses an area, such as the side of a room or building.

examples.text: Odanın duvarı maviye boyandı.
examples.translation: The wall of the room was painted blue.

faults.quote: to fall; to drop; to decrease
faults.why: 'to decrease' is not covered by the senses (and in Dutch 'dalen'/'zakken' is used).

faults.quote: Use 'vallen' for physical objects or people dropping to the ground.
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses irregular forms ('viel', 'is gevallen') and auxiliary 'zijn'.
Lacks the common everyday sense 'to occur on a certain day/date' (e.g., holidays).

notes: Strong verb: 'viel, vielen, is gevallen' (always takes the auxiliary 'zijn' in the perfect tense).
Intransitive ('to fall'); to say 'to drop something', use 'laten vallen' (literally 'to let fall').

senses.definition: To move downwards from a higher position, or to lose one's balance and hit the ground.

examples.text: De bladeren vallen in de herfst van de bomen.
examples.translation: The leaves fall from the trees in autumn.

examples.text: Pas op dat je niet valt op het ijs.
examples.translation: Watch out that you don't fall on the ice.

senses.definition: Of an event or date: to take place on a particular day.

examples.text: Mijn verjaardag valt dit jaar op een zondag.
examples.translation: My birthday falls on a Sunday this year.

faults.quote: Use 'vandaag' to refer specifically to the current day.
faults.why: Restates the gloss; learners instead need the common expression 'vandaag de dag' (nowadays).

faults.quote: Vandaag ben ik erg druk.
faults.why: In standard Dutch, 'het druk hebben' is preferred over 'druk zijn' for having much to do.

notes: Commonly used in the fixed expression 'vandaag de dag', meaning 'nowadays' or 'these days'.

senses.definition: On or during this present day.

examples.text: Vandaag heb ik het erg druk.
examples.translation: Today I am very busy.

faults.why: Lacks the irregular strong verb forms ('ving, vingen, heeft gevangen').

notes: Strong verb: 'ving, vingen, heeft gevangen'.
Used for catching moving objects or capturing animals/people. To 'catch' a bus or train, use 'halen' or 'nemen' instead.

senses.definition: To take hold of something moving through the air with your hands.

examples.text: De keeper kan de bal makkelijk vangen.
examples.translation: The goalkeeper can easily catch the ball.

senses.definition: To capture an animal or a person so that they cannot escape.

examples.text: Ze probeerden de ontsnapte kat te vangen.
examples.translation: They tried to catch the escaped cat.

faults.quote: and an adverb ('je bent hier veilig').
faults.why: In 'je bent hier veilig', 'veilig' is a predicative adjective, not an adverb.

faults.quote: Free from danger or the threat of damage; reliable
faults.why: Both senses mean protected from danger or risk; they are shades of one meaning.

notes: Can also be used as an adverb meaning 'safely' (e.g., 'veilig thuiskomen' — to get home safely).
Do not confuse with 'zeker', which means 'certain' or 'sure', whereas 'veilig' means free from danger or risk.

senses.definition: Protected from harm or danger, or not involving risk.

examples.text: Je bent hier helemaal veilig.
examples.translation: You are completely safe here.

examples.text: Dit wachtwoord is niet erg veilig.
examples.translation: This password is not very secure.

faults.quote: Feeling regret or sympathy for a situation; sorry.
faults.why: 'verdrietig' means sad/sorrowful, not apologetic or regretful ('sorry').

faults.quote: Ik ben verdrietig dat ik je feestje heb moeten missen.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of English 'I am sad/sorry that...'; Dutch uses 'Het spijt me' or 'Ik vind het jammer'.

faults.quote: sad; unhappy; sorry
faults.why: 'sorry' is not a valid translation of 'verdrietig'.

notes: Derived from 'het verdriet' (grief, sorrow). Do not confuse with 'zielig' (pitiful, pathetic) or 'jammer' (a pity, unfortunate).

senses.definition: Feeling or showing sorrow or unhappiness.

examples.text: Ze werd erg verdrietig toen ze het slechte nieuws hoorde.
examples.translation: She became very sad when she heard the bad news.

faults.quote: to look at; to watch; to see
faults.why: 'to see' is 'ver', not 'mirar', and is not in the senses.

faults.quote: Vamos a mirar una película esta noche.
faults.why: In Spain, one says 'ver una película', not 'mirar' (as note[0] even states).

faults.quote: You have to look into the eyes when you speak.
faults.why: Calqued translation; natural English is 'look people in the eye'.
Should mention that 'mirar' is transitive (takes a direct object without 'a' for things).

notes: Unlike English 'look at', 'mirar' takes a direct object without a preposition for things (e.g., 'Miro la foto', not *'Miro a la foto'*); use 'a' only before a person.
While 'mirar' means 'to look at' (focusing your attention), 'ver' means 'to see' and is also the verb used in Spain for watching TV or a movie ('ver la tele', 'ver una película').

senses.definition: To direct your eyes towards something or someone and pay attention to it.

examples.text: Mira esa foto en la pared.
examples.translation: Look at that photo on the wall.

examples.text: Tienes que mirar a la gente a los ojos cuando hablas.
examples.translation: You have to look people in the eye when you speak.

senses.definition: To face or overlook a particular direction or place.

examples.text: Mi habitación mira al mar.
examples.translation: My room looks out on the sea.

faults.quote: Used to describe people, objects, or clothes that are covered or soaked
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage information.
Should note that it takes 'estar' (not 'ser') to mean being wet.

notes: Used with the verb 'estar' (never 'ser') because being wet is a resulting state: 'El suelo está mojado'.
Do not confuse with 'húmedo', which means damp or humid rather than thoroughly wet.

senses.definition: Covered or soaked in water or another liquid.

examples.text: Tengo el abrigo mojado por la lluvia.
examples.translation: My coat is wet from the rain.

faults.quote: To float or be covered in a large amount of liquid
faults.why: Figurative sense 'be swimming in' is not needed for an A2 entry; 'float' is inaccurate.

faults.quote: Use 'nadar' when talking about the physical action of swimming
faults.why: Restates the definition without useful grammar or contrast.

notes: To say 'to go swimming', Spanish uses 'ir a nadar'.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body.

examples.text: Me gusta nadar en la piscina durante el verano.
examples.translation: I like to swim in the pool during the summer.

faults.quote: /nese.siˈtaɾ/
faults.why: Gives seseo pronunciation; Castilian Spanish (es-ES) uses /θ/ for 'c' before 'e': /neθesiˈtaɾ/.
Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning ('to need something').

faults.quote: to have to have something
faults.why: Clumsy, unnatural phrase used as a gloss instead of 'to need'.

notes: Followed directly by a noun ('Necesito ayuda') or an infinitive verb without a preposition ('Necesito descansar').
For obligations ('have to' / 'must'), 'tener que' + infinitive is much more common than 'necesitar'.

senses.definition: To require something or someone because it is essential or very important.

examples.text: Necesito un paraguas porque está lloviendo.
examples.translation: I need an umbrella because it is raining.

examples.text: Hoy necesito acostarme temprano.
examples.translation: Today I need to go to bed early.

faults.quote: Làng refers specifically to a rural village, typically smaller and more
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage information.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with thành phố (city) or thị trấn (town).
faults.why: No learner confuses the words for 'village' and 'city'; filler note.

notes: Often used directly without a classifier, or with 'ngôi' (ngôi làng) in more descriptive contexts.

senses.definition: A small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a town.

examples.text: Tôi lớn lên ở một ngôi làng nhỏ gần sông.
examples.translation: I grew up in a small village near the river.

faults.why: Cold weather and cold objects are the same literal sense of low temperature.

faults.quote: Used for both weather and physical objects. It is the general
faults.why: Merely restates the gloss and definitions.

faults.quote: /laːjŋ˧˨/
faults.why: Short vowel /a/ in 'anh' rime and glottalized low tone (˧˨ʔ or ˨˩ʔ), not long /aː/.

notes: Compare 'mát' (cool, pleasantly fresh) and 'rét' (freezing or biting cold, used mainly for weather in northern Vietnam).

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm or hot.

examples.text: Thời tiết hôm nay rất lạnh.
examples.translation: The weather is very cold today.

examples.text: Tôi thích uống nước lạnh vào mùa hè.
examples.translation: I like drinking cold water in the summer.

faults.why: Compound verb 'lau dọn' (wipe and tidy) is a single general sense of cleaning up.

notes: Combines 'lau' (to wipe, to mop) and 'dọn' (to tidy, to clear). Compared to 'dọn dẹp' (tidying and organizing), 'lau dọn' includes wiping surfaces clean.

senses.definition: To clean surfaces and put a room or house in order.

examples.text: Tôi cần lau dọn nhà cửa vào cuối tuần này.
examples.translation: I need to clean up the house this weekend.

faults.quote: /laj35/
faults.why: Vowel is schwa /əj/, not /aj/, and tone should use standard IPA tone letters.

faults.quote: Lấy is one of the most versatile verbs in Vietnamese.
faults.why: Vague filler mentioning 'prepositional particle' jargon without explaining how a beginner uses it.

corrected.shortGloss: to take; to get; to marry
notes: Do not confuse with 'cầm': 'lấy' means to take or get something, whereas 'cầm' means to hold something in your hand.
In 'lấy vợ' (to take a wife) and 'lấy chồng' (to take a husband), it is the everyday way to say 'to get married'.

senses.definition: To reach for and take hold of something, or to obtain or fetch it.

examples.text: Lấy giúp tôi cốc nước với.
examples.translation: Please get me a glass of water.

senses.definition: To take someone as one's husband or wife.

examples.text: Anh ấy quyết định lấy cô ấy sau ba năm hẹn hò.
examples.translation: He decided to marry her after three years of dating.

faults.quote: To make a ringing sound, like a bell or a telephone.
faults.why: People 'bellen' (ring a bell); a phone 'gaat' or 'rinkelt', it does not 'bel'.

faults.quote: De telefoon zit de hele dag te bellen.
faults.why: Unidiomatic Dutch; a telephone does not 'bellen' (people do), it 'gaat' or 'rinkelt'.

faults.quote: Used both for making a phone call and for a doorbell
faults.why: Restates the senses and falsely claims it is used for a telephone ringing.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'bellen' meaning blowing soap bubbles
faults.why: Soap bubbles are 'bellen blazen' (noun plural); unlikely confusion and 'bel' is the same noun.

notes: When calling a person on the phone, 'bellen' can be used with a direct object ('Ik bel mijn moeder') or with 'met' ('Ik bel met mijn moeder').
For the sound a phone makes when it rings, Dutch uses 'gaan' or 'rinkelen' ('De telefoon gaat'), not 'bellen'.

senses.definition: To contact or speak to someone by telephone.

examples.text: Ik ga mijn moeder even bellen.
examples.translation: I am going to call my mother quickly.

senses.definition: To press or ring a bell, such as a doorbell or bicycle bell.

examples.text: Er wordt bij de voordeur gebeld.
examples.translation: Someone is ringing the front doorbell.

faults.quote: Use betalen when you give money for goods or services.
faults.why: First sentence restates the definition; fails to mention 'betalen' also takes a direct object.

notes: For the thing being paid for, you can use a direct object ('de rekening betalen') or the preposition 'voor' ('betalen voor de jas').

senses.definition: To give money in exchange for goods or services.

examples.text: Ik wil graag met pin betalen.
examples.translation: I would like to pay by card.

examples.text: Hoeveel moet ik betalen voor deze jas?
examples.translation: How much do I have to pay for this jacket?

faults.quote: /bəˈzuxə(n)/
faults.why: Wrong consonant: 'k' is pronounced /k/, not /x/ (/bəˈzukə(n)/).
Should note that 'bezoeken' is irregular (bezocht, heeft bezocht) and less informal than 'op bezoek gaan'.

notes: Irregular verb: 'bezocht', 'heeft bezocht'. It always takes a direct object without a preposition.
For visiting friends or family in everyday speech, 'op bezoek gaan bij' or 'langsgaan bij' is often more natural than 'bezoeken'.

senses.definition: To go to see a person or a place such as a city or museum.

examples.text: Ik ga morgen mijn oma bezoeken.
examples.translation: I am going to visit my grandma tomorrow.

senses.definition: To regularly go to an institution, such as a school, or to attend an event.

examples.text: Welke school bezoeken jouw kinderen?
examples.translation: Which school do your children attend?

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the exact same meaning ('worried/concerned'), shown by identical examples.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with erg (bad or very)
faults.why: 'bezorgd' and 'erg' do not look or sound alike; unhelpful filler note.
Needs the prepositions it takes: 'bezorgd over' or 'bezorgd om'.

notes: Followed by the preposition 'over' or 'om' ('bezorgd over/om iemand').
Also the past participle of 'bezorgen' (to deliver): 'Het pakketje is bezorgd' (The parcel has been delivered).

senses.definition: Feeling anxious or troubled that something bad might happen to someone or something.

examples.text: Ze is bezorgd over haar examen van morgen.
examples.translation: She is worried about her exam tomorrow.

examples.text: Mijn ouders zijn erg bezorgd als ik te laat thuis ben.
examples.translation: My parents are very worried when I get home late.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the deep ocean.
faults.why: Defined as a noun ('The colour...') instead of an adjective ('Having the colour...').

faults.quote: Being intoxicated by alcohol.
faults.why: Dated/marginal slang for A2, whereas 'bruised' ('een blauwe plek') is very common.

faults.quote: Dutch speakers often use 'blauw' to describe the colour of the sky
faults.why: Pointless filler note.

notes: Also used for bruises on the skin: 'een blauwe plek' (a bruise) and 'een blauw oog' (a black eye).

senses.definition: Having the colour of a clear sky or the sea.

examples.text: De lucht is vandaag erg blauw.
examples.translation: The sky is very blue today.

faults.quote: to win; to earn; to gain
faults.why: shortGloss includes 'to gain', which is not covered by the senses.
Missing common everyday senses: 'to beat/defeat (someone)' and 'to gain (time, weight, experience)'.

faults.quote: While 'ganar' is used for winning games or competitions, it also means
faults.why: Merely restates the senses; should instead explain how 'ganar a alguien' means 'to beat someone'.

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to beat; to earn; to gain
notes: To say you beat an opponent, use 'ganar a': 'Le gané a Juan' (I beat Juan).
Do not confuse with 'conseguir' (to get/obtain), which focuses on achieving a goal rather than winning or earning.

senses.definition: To come first in a game, match, or competition, or to get a prize.

examples.text: Es difícil ganar el partido contra ellos.
examples.translation: It is difficult to win the match against them.

senses.definition: To do better than another person or team in a game or competition.

examples.text: Siempre me ganas al ajedrez.
examples.translation: You always beat me at chess.

senses.definition: To receive money in exchange for work done.

examples.text: Quiero ganar más dinero para viajar.
examples.translation: I want to earn more money to travel.

senses.definition: To get or increase something useful or wanted, such as time, weight, or experience.

examples.text: Tomamos un atajo para ganar tiempo.
examples.translation: We took a shortcut to gain time.

faults.quote: Words said to show you are grateful.
faults.why: Defines an expression as a noun ('Words said...') instead of how it is used.

faults.quote: In Spanish, the word is plural, but it is used exactly like
faults.why: Trivial observation; better to mention 'gracias por' + noun/infinitive and common replies like 'de nada'.

notes: Followed by 'por' + noun or infinitive: 'gracias por venir' (thanks for coming). The most common reply is 'de nada' (you're welcome).
For emphasis, say 'muchas gracias' (thanks a lot) or 'muchísimas gracias' (thank you very much).

senses.definition: Used to tell someone that you are grateful for something they have given or done.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por tu ayuda.
examples.translation: Thanks a lot for your help.

examples.text: Gracias por el regalo.
examples.translation: Thank you for the gift.

faults.quote: or with the verb 'ser', it strictly refers to physical size
faults.why: False: with 'ser' it can also refer to age or importance ('El problema es grande').

faults.quote: Cuando sea grande, quiero viajar por el mundo.
faults.why: In Peninsular Spanish (es-ES), 'cuando sea mayor' is standard; 'cuando sea grande' is mainly Latin American.

notes: Before any singular noun (masculine or feminine), 'grande' shortens to 'gran' and usually means 'great': 'un gran día', 'una gran mujer'.
After a noun, it remains 'grande' and refers to size: 'una casa grande' (a big house).

senses.definition: Of a physical size or amount greater than normal or average.

examples.text: Ese perro es muy grande y necesita mucho espacio.
examples.translation: That dog is very big and needs a lot of space.

senses.definition: Of high importance, relevance, or quality.

examples.text: Tengo una gran noticia para ti.
examples.translation: I have great news for you.

senses.definition: Of a child: grown up or older.

examples.text: Los niños ya están muy grandes.
examples.translation: The children are already very big.

faults.quote: Not smooth or made without care.
faults.why: Literary/marginal sense ('acabado grosero'); in everyday Spanish 'basto' or 'tosco' is used for rough textures.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with crudo, which refers to food
