Missing everyday sense 'email / inbox' (sprawdzić pocztę).

notes: For the building, use the preposition 'na', not 'w': 'na poczcie' (at the post office), 'iść na pocztę' (to go to the post office).

senses.definition: A place where you send letters, buy stamps, and pick up parcels.

examples.text: Muszę pójść na pocztę, żeby wysłać paczkę.
examples.translation: I need to go to the post office to send a parcel.

senses.definition: Letters and parcels that are sent or delivered, or the system that delivers them.

examples.text: Dzisiaj nie było żadnej poczty w skrzynce.
examples.translation: There was no mail in the mailbox today.

senses.definition: Electronic mail or an email inbox.

examples.text: Codziennie rano sprawdzam pocztę.
examples.translation: I check my email every morning.

faults.quote: /pɔdɛkst͡ʂɨˈtɔvanɨ/
faults.why: Wrong transcription and stress: 'sc' is /st͡s/, not /st͡ʂ/, and stress is penultimate (/pɔ.dɛks.t͡sɨ.tɔˈva.nɨ/).

faults.quote: This word is often used to describe someone who is looking forward
faults.why: Restates the definition and misses the grammatical construction (+ instrumental case).

notes: Followed by a noun in the instrumental case to say what someone is excited about (e.g., 'podekscytowany wyjazdem' — excited about the trip).

senses.definition: Feeling very happy and eager about something that is happening or going to happen.

examples.text: Jestem podekscytowany wyjazdem na wakacje.
examples.translation: I am excited about going on vacation.

faults.why: Should contrast 'podłoga' (surface walked on) with 'piętro' (storey/level), as both translate to 'floor'.

notes: Refers only to the surface you walk on (usually with 'na': 'na podłodze' — on the floor). For a level or storey of a building, use 'piętro'.

senses.definition: The lower surface of a room that you walk on.

examples.text: Muszę umyć podłogę w kuchni.
examples.translation: I need to wash the floor in the kitchen.

faults.quote: /pɔˈdru.ʐɔ.vat͡ɕ/
faults.why: Wrong stress: Polish has penultimate stress, so it is /pɔ.druˈʐɔ.vat͡ɕ/.

notes: Imperfective verb used for the general activity of traveling. To express means of transport, use the instrumental case (e.g., 'podróżować pociągiem' — to travel by train).

senses.definition: To go from one place to another, especially over a long distance.

examples.text: Uwielbiam podróżować po całym świecie.
examples.translation: I love to travel all over the world.

examples.text: On musi dużo podróżować w swojej pracy.
examples.translation: He has to travel a lot for his work.

faults.why: In Polish, 'poduszka' is one concept covering both English 'pillow' and 'cushion'.

faults.quote: Use 'poduszka' for both the object you sleep on and the decorative
faults.why: Merely restates the English glosses.

senses.definition: A soft cloth bag filled with feathers, foam, or other soft material, used to rest your head on in bed or placed on a sofa or chair.

examples.text: Położyłem głowę na miękkiej poduszce.
examples.translation: I rested my head on the soft pillow.

examples.text: Na kanapie leży kolorowa poduszka.
examples.translation: A colorful cushion is lying on the sofa.

faults.quote: The final part of the day, just before nightfall.
faults.why: 'Tarde' covers both English 'afternoon' and early 'evening' as one continuous period, not distinct senses.

faults.quote: usually starts when people have finished their work or daily activities, regardless
faults.why: False claim: 'la noche' starts when it gets dark, not regardless of clock time.

notes: 'La tarde' covers both English 'afternoon' and early 'evening', from noon until it gets dark (when 'la noche' begins).
In Mexico, 'en la tarde' is more common than 'por la tarde' for 'in the afternoon'; 'buenas tardes' means 'good afternoon/evening'.

senses.definition: The part of the day between noon and nightfall.

examples.text: Tengo una reunión en la tarde.
examples.translation: I have a meeting in the afternoon.

examples.text: Nos vemos a las siete de la tarde.
examples.translation: See you at seven in the evening.

faults.quote: While 'tarea' can refer to a general task or assignment, in everyday
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses the common collocation 'hacer la tarea' (to do one's homework).

notes: For schoolwork, it is usually used in the singular in Mexico: 'hacer la tarea' (to do one's homework).

senses.definition: School work that a student is given to do outside of the classroom.

examples.text: Tengo mucha tarea para mañana.
examples.translation: I have a lot of homework for tomorrow.

senses.definition: A specific piece of work to be done, at work or at home.

examples.text: Limpiar la cocina es mi tarea de hoy.
examples.translation: Cleaning the kitchen is my task for today.

faults.why: Sense [0] restricts 'tarjeta' to payment cards, omitting everyday ID, transit, and business cards.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'carta', which is a letter you write
faults.why: Incomplete contrast: 'carta' is also used for playing cards ('jugar a las cartas').

notes: When paying, 'con tarjeta' alone means 'by credit or debit card' ('tarjeta de crédito' / 'tarjeta de débito').
Do not confuse with 'carta', which is used for playing cards ('jugar a las cartas'), letters, and restaurant menus.

senses.definition: A small plastic or paper card used for paying, identification, or access.

examples.text: Voy a pagar con tarjeta.
examples.translation: I am going to pay by card.

senses.definition: A piece of stiff paper with a picture or message, sent for an occasion or from a trip.

examples.text: Le compré una tarjeta de cumpleaños.
examples.translation: I bought her a birthday card.

faults.quote: The amount that a spoon can hold.
faults.why: Standard Spanish uses 'cucharada' for 'spoonful'; 'cuchara' for this is informal/secondary.

faults.quote: It also refers to the measurement 'a spoonful'
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and overlooks the standard word 'cucharada'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'el cuchillo' (knife). For the measurement 'spoonful', the standard word is 'la cucharada' (and 'la cucharadita' for 'teaspoonful').

senses.definition: A utensil with a shallow bowl at one end, used for eating, stirring, or serving food.

examples.text: Usa la cuchara para comer la sopa.
examples.translation: Use the spoon to eat the soup.

faults.quote: A small, perforated object used to make necklaces or bracelets.
faults.why: 'Bead' is too specific for A2 while common 'calculation/count' is missing.
Missing the everyday sense of 'count' or 'calculation' (e.g. 'hacer cuentas', 'perder la cuenta').

notes: Do not confuse 'la cuenta' with 'el cuento' (story, tale).
Very common in the phrase 'darse cuenta (de algo)', meaning 'to realize (something)'.

senses.definition: A statement of the money owed for food, drink, or a service.

examples.text: Por favor, ¿nos trae la cuenta?
examples.translation: Could you bring us the bill, please?

senses.definition: An arrangement to keep money in a bank, or a personal profile on a website or app.

examples.text: Necesito abrir una cuenta en este banco.
examples.translation: I need to open an account at this bank.

senses.definition: The act or result of counting or calculating.

examples.text: He perdido la cuenta de cuántas veces he ido.
examples.translation: I have lost count of how many times I have gone.

faults.quote: In Spain, 'ducha' is used for both the act of showering
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to note the collocation 'darse una ducha'.

notes: To say 'to take a shower', Spanish uses 'darse una ducha' or the reflexive verb 'ducharse' (rather than 'tomar'). For a bathtub, use 'la bañera'.

senses.definition: An act of washing the body under sprayed water.

examples.text: Me voy a dar una ducha rápida antes de salir.
examples.translation: I'm going to take a quick shower before going out.

senses.definition: The device or enclosure in a bathroom that sprays water for washing the body.

examples.text: La ducha del hotel es bastante grande.
examples.translation: The hotel shower is quite big.

faults.quote: A difficult or important task that someone decides to do.
faults.why: Literary/formal sense ('undertaking'), not an everyday A2 meaning.

faults.quote: Used most often to mean a company or business corporation
faults.why: Simply repeats the definitions of the two senses.

senses.definition: An organization that sells goods or services in order to make money.

examples.text: Trabajo en una empresa de tecnología en el centro de la ciudad.
examples.translation: I work at a technology company in the city center.

faults.quote: Often served with olive oil and vinegar or salt.
faults.why: Repeats the definition and gives culinary trivia instead of linguistic guidance.

senses.definition: A cold dish of raw or cooked vegetables, usually dressed with oil, vinegar, and salt.

examples.text: Voy a preparar una ensalada fresca para la cena.
examples.translation: I am going to make a fresh salad for dinner.

faults.quote: Used to describe a person's state of mind or an event
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage info.
Should mention the common broken plural forms حَزَانَى and حِزَان.

notes: Describes both a person feeling sorrow and something that causes sorrow (such as news or a story). The masculine plural is irregular: حَزَانَى (ḥazānā) or حِزَان (ḥizān).
Differs from كَئِيب (depressed, gloomy), which describes a deeper or more lasting low mood.

senses.definition: Feeling, showing, or causing sorrow; unhappy.

examples.text: هَذَا خَبَرٌ حَزِينٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This is very sad news.

examples.text: يَبْدُو الرَّجُلُ حَزِينًا بَعْدَ فَقْدِ صَدِيقِهِ.
examples.translation: The man looks unhappy after losing his friend.

faults.quote: This word is used for things that do not cost money.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition instead of giving useful grammar or usage notes.

notes: Do not confuse with حُرّ (ḥurr), which means 'free' in the sense of having liberty or not being busy.
The adverbial form مَجَّانًا (majjānan, 'for free') is very commonly used with verbs (e.g., حَصَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ مَجَّانًا — I got it for free).

senses.definition: Costing no money.

examples.text: هَذَا التَّطْبِيقُ مَجَّانِيٌّ.
examples.translation: This application is free.

examples.text: هَلْ هَذِهِ الْخِدْمَةُ مَجَّانِيَّةٌ؟
examples.translation: Is this service free of charge?

faults.quote: Use this word to describe something that is factually incorrect or
faults.why: Simply restates the two sense definitions.

faults.quote: while 'خَاطِئ' carries a heavier, more serious tone.
faults.why: خاطئ is standard and completely normal for test answers; the real contrast is prescriptivist.

notes: In everyday Modern Standard Arabic, خَاطِئ is the standard adjective for 'wrong' or 'incorrect' (and is slightly more formal than غَيْر صَحِيح, 'not correct'). Note that strict grammar purists prefer مُخْطِئ for someone who makes an unintentional mistake, reserving خَاطِئ for deliberate wrongdoing.

senses.definition: Not correct; containing a mistake.

examples.text: هَذَا الْجَوَابُ خَاطِئٌ.
examples.translation: This answer is wrong.

senses.definition: Having committed a sin or moral wrong.

examples.text: الْإِنْسَانُ خَاطِئٌ بِطَبْعِهِ.
examples.translation: Humanity is sinful by nature.

faults.quote: it often appears as 'ghāli' (غالي) with a suffix, such as 'ghāliya'
faults.why: Confuses the definite form الغالي with the feminine suffix ـة (غالية).

notes: A defective adjective (اسم منقوص): when masculine, indefinite, and in the nominative or genitive case, the final ي drops into tanwīn (غَالٍ, ghālin). The ي returns with the definite article (الْغَالِي, al-ghālī) and in the feminine form (غَالِيَة, ghāliya).

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

examples.text: هَذَا الْهَاتِفُ غَالٍ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This phone is very expensive.

senses.definition: Highly valued or deeply loved by someone.

examples.text: أَنْتَ صَدِيقٌ غَالٍ عِنْدِي.
examples.translation: You are a dear friend to me.

faults.quote: In Italian, "erba" covers both the grass on a lawn and
faults.why: Restates the two senses; better to note plural usage 'erbe aromatiche' for culinary herbs.

faults.quote: Aggiungi un po' di erba fresca alla zuppa.
faults.why: Unnatural in the singular; Italians say 'erbe fresche' or 'erbe aromatiche' for cooking.

notes: For cooking herbs, the plural 'erbe' or 'erbe aromatiche' is normally used.

senses.definition: The thin green plants covering the ground in a garden, park, or field.

examples.text: I bambini giocano sull'erba.
examples.translation: The children are playing on the grass.

senses.definition: A plant used in cooking or medicine for its scent or flavor.

examples.text: Aggiungi delle erbe fresche alla zuppa.
examples.translation: Add some fresh herbs to the soup.

faults.quote: (morality) A moral fault or wrongdoing.
faults.why: Marginal/literary extension of sense 0; example just means 'recognizing one's mistake'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'orrore', which means horror.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion for learners since 'orrore' is a transparent cognate.

notes: Commonly used in 'fare un errore' or 'commettere un errore' (to make a mistake), and 'per errore' (by mistake).

senses.definition: Something done or said that is wrong or inaccurate.

examples.text: Ho fatto un errore nel calcolo.
examples.translation: I made a mistake in the calculation.

examples.text: Riconoscere i propri errori è il primo passo per migliorare.
examples.translation: Recognizing one's mistakes is the first step to improving.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'esame' (test or exam) with 'processo'
faults.why: English speakers do not confuse 'exam' with a legal trial.

notes: Use 'fare un esame' or 'dare un esame' for taking a test, and 'superare' or 'passare un esame' for passing it.

senses.definition: A formal test of a student's knowledge or skill in a subject.

examples.text: Domani ho un esame importante di matematica.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I have an important math exam.

senses.definition: A medical check or analysis of part of the body.

examples.text: Il medico mi ha prescritto un esame del sangue.
examples.translation: The doctor prescribed a blood test for me.

senses.definition: A careful study or inspection of a situation or problem.

examples.text: La situazione richiede un esame approfondito.
examples.translation: The situation requires a thorough review.

faults.quote: /leˈstaːte/
faults.why: IPA must transcribe the lemma 'estate' without the article 'l''.

faults.quote: Note that 'estate' takes a feminine article: 'l'estate'
faults.why: Restates the gender field and basic A1 article elision rules.

notes: Use 'd'estate' or 'in estate' to say 'in (the) summer'.

senses.definition: The warmest season of the year, between spring and autumn.

examples.text: Quest'estate andiamo al mare in Sicilia.
examples.translation: This summer we are going to the seaside in Sicily.

faults.quote: Used as a noun to refer to a person you do not
faults.why: Merely repeats the POS and the two sense definitions.

faults.quote: Questo è un discorso di famiglia e nessun estraneo deve sapere.
faults.why: 'Sapere' without an object ('saperlo') sounds incomplete and unnatural in Italian.

notes: The feminine form is 'l'estranea'. Also used as an adjective meaning 'unrelated' or 'foreign' (with 'a': 'estraneo ai fatti').

senses.definition: A person whom you do not know.

examples.text: Non bisogna mai aprire la porta a un estraneo.
examples.translation: You must never open the door to a stranger.

senses.definition: A person who does not belong to a particular group, family, or place.

examples.text: È una questione di famiglia e nessun estraneo deve intromettersi.
examples.translation: It is a family matter and no outsider should get involved.

faults.quote: snob, preppy, stuck-up
faults.why: 'Stuck-up' is an adjective, not a noun gloss.

faults.quote: Ella es muy fresa y solo compra ropa de marca.
faults.why: 'Muy fresa' uses the word as an adjective in a noun entry.

notes: In sense 2 (Mexican slang), 'el/la fresa' refers to a person of either gender, and 'fresa' is also very commonly used as an invariable adjective (e.g., 'es muy fresa').

senses.definition: A small, red, sweet fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.

examples.text: Compré un kilo de fresas frescas en el mercado.
examples.translation: I bought a kilo of fresh strawberries at the market.

senses.definition: (Mexico, informal) A wealthy or pretentious person who acts snobby or preppy.

examples.text: Es una fresa que solo compra ropa de marca.
examples.translation: She's a snob who only buys designer clothes.

faults.quote: (abstract) The result, product, or outcome of an effort or action.
faults.why: Confuses 'la fruta' with the masculine noun 'el fruto' ('frutos' in the example).

faults.quote: whereas in English we often use the plural 'fruit'
faults.why: 'Fruit' is singular uncountable in English too, not plural.

faults.quote: fruit; produce
faults.why: 'Produce' is not in the senses and includes vegetables.

notes: Like English 'fruit', singular 'la fruta' is often used collectively for fruit in general ('comer mucha fruta'), while 'una fruta' or 'las frutas' refers to individual pieces or types of fruit.
For the figurative 'fruit' or result of an effort (or botanical fruit in general), Spanish uses the masculine noun 'el fruto' ('dar fruto').

senses.definition: The sweet, fleshy, edible part of a plant that contains seeds.

examples.text: Es importante comer mucha fruta y verdura para mantenerse sano.
examples.translation: It is important to eat a lot of fruit and vegetables to stay healthy.

notes: Use 'gallina' for the live female bird; the male is 'el gallo' (rooster), and chicken meat or a young bird is 'el pollo'.

senses.definition: An adult female farm bird raised for its eggs and meat.

examples.text: La gallina puso un huevo fresco esta mañana.
examples.translation: The hen laid a fresh egg this morning.

senses.definition: (informal) A person who is easily frightened or lacks courage.

examples.text: No seas gallina y sube a la montaña rusa.
examples.translation: Don't be a chicken and get on the roller coaster.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a female sibling. In Spanish, family terms
faults.why: Restates the definition and makes a vague, unhelpful claim about articles.

notes: The masculine plural 'los hermanos' means both 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters' (siblings).

senses.definition: A girl or woman who has the same parents as another person.

examples.text: Ella es mi hermana mayor.
examples.translation: She is my older sister.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: If you want to say something is 'morally right'
faults.why: False claim: 正しい is regularly used for 'morally right' (e.g., 正しい行い).

notes: An i-adjective (correctly inflected as 正しくない, 正しかった). It covers both factual accuracy ('correct answer') and moral or procedural rightness ('the right thing to do').

senses.definition: In accordance with fact, truth, rules, or morality; free from error.

examples.text: 彼の答えは正しいです。
examples.translation: His answer is correct.

examples.text: それは正しいやり方ではありません。
examples.translation: That is not the right way to do it.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: dirty; messy; unfair
faults.why: shortGloss includes 'messy', which is missing from the senses.

notes: Also commonly used for messy handwriting (字が汚い) or rude language (言葉が汚い).
Do not confuse with the verb 汚れる (yogoreru, 'to get dirty') or the na-adjective 清潔 (seiketsu, 'clean/sanitary').

senses.definition: Not clean; covered in dirt, or untidy and messy.

examples.text: この部屋はとても汚い。
examples.translation: This room is very dirty.

senses.definition: Not fair or honest; sneaky or underhanded.

examples.text: それは汚いやり方だ。
examples.translation: That is an unfair way of doing things.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

faults.quote: その国は天然資源が貧しい。
faults.why: 天然資源に乏しい is standard for natural resources; 貧しい sounds unnatural here.

notes: More formal and literary than 貧乏 (binbō, a noun/na-adjective used in everyday speech for having no money).

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions; living in poverty.

examples.text: 彼は貧しい家庭で育った。
examples.translation: He grew up in a poor family.

senses.definition: Lacking in quality, quantity, or richness.

examples.text: 当時はまだ貧しい食事だった。
examples.translation: Back then, the meals were still meager.

faults.quote: Full of activity; crowded or hectic.
faults.why: English interference: 忙しい does not mean 'crowded/bustling' for a street (use にぎやか).

faults.quote: この通りはいつも忙しいですね。
faults.why: Direct calque of English 'busy street'; unnatural in Japanese.

faults.quote: like a busy street
faults.why: Teaches an English calque; a lively/crowded street is にぎやか, not 忙しい.

notes: Describes people having a lot to do, or time periods/workplaces full of work. Do not use it for a crowded street or lively place (use にぎやか instead).

senses.definition: Having a lot to do; occupied with many tasks, or full of work.

examples.text: 最近、仕事がとても忙しいです。
examples.translation: I have been very busy with work lately.

examples.text: 明日は忙しい一日になりそうだ。
examples.translation: Tomorrow looks like it will be a busy day.

faults.quote: Use 弱い (yowai) to describe anything that lacks strength
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding grammatical or usage guidance.

notes: Takes the particle に (ni) to mark what someone is bad at, vulnerable to, or has low tolerance for (e.g., お酒に弱い, 寒さに弱い).
Opposite: 強い (tsuyoi, 'strong').

senses.definition: Lacking physical strength, power, or intensity; delicate or frail.

examples.text: 今日は風が弱いです。
examples.translation: The wind is weak today.

examples.text: 私は昔から体が弱い。
examples.translation: I have had a frail body for a long time.

senses.definition: Having little skill, resistance, or tolerance for something.

examples.text: 私はお酒に弱いです。
examples.translation: I cannot hold my liquor well.

examples.text: 彼はプレッシャーに弱い。
examples.translation: He does not handle pressure well.

faults.quote: To be bitten by an insect or animal.
faults.why: Defines an active transitive verb in the passive ('to be bitten' instead of 'to bite').

faults.quote: This verb is highly versatile. Use it for physical cutting
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses already listed in the entry.
Lacks the very common everyday sense 'to disconnect / hang up (a phone call)'.

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to bite; to pass (time); to hang up
notes: Transitive verb: takes 'ने' (ne) in the perfective tenses. Its intransitive counterpart is 'कटना' (kaṭnā, to be cut).
Do not confuse with 'तोड़ना' (toṛnā, to break or pluck), used for snapping things or picking fruit and flowers.

senses.definition: To divide or separate something using a sharp tool such as a knife or scissors.

examples.text: मैं सब्ज़ी काट रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am cutting the vegetables.

senses.definition: Of an animal, insect, or snake: to wound or sting with the teeth or mouthparts.

examples.text: मच्छर ने मुझे काट लिया।
examples.translation: The mosquito bit me.

senses.definition: To pass or spend a period of time, especially when waiting or enduring boredom.

examples.text: स्टेशन पर समय काटना मुश्किल है।
examples.translation: It is difficult to pass time at the station.

senses.definition: To disconnect a phone call or deduct an amount of money.

examples.text: उसने गुस्से में फ़ोन काट दिया।
examples.translation: He hung up the phone in anger.

faults.quote: चलना is one of the most common verbs in Hindi
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler restating the senses instead of giving grammar or usage help.
Should contrast with 'जाना' (to go) and note that as an intransitive verb it never takes 'ने'.

corrected.shortGloss: to walk; to move; to work; to come along
notes: Intransitive verb: it never takes 'ने' (ne) in the past tense (e.g., वह चला — he walked/left).
Unlike 'जाना' (jānā, to go to a place), 'चलना' focuses on the movement itself or means 'to come along with the speaker' (मेरे साथ चलो — come with me).

senses.definition: To move on foot, or of a vehicle or wind, to move along.

examples.text: हम पार्क में धीरे-धीरे चल रहे हैं।
examples.translation: We are walking slowly in the park.

senses.definition: To set off, leave, or come along with someone.

examples.text: चलो, अब घर चलते हैं।
examples.translation: Come on, let's go home now.

senses.definition: Of a machine, device, business, or event: to function, operate, or be in progress.

examples.text: मेरा फ़ोन अब ठीक से नहीं चल रहा है।
examples.translation: My phone is not working properly now.

faults.quote: /ˈsiːx.nɑː/
faults.why: Wrong consonant: 'ख' in सीखना is aspirated velar /kʰ/, not uvular/velar fricative /x/.

faults.quote: सीखना (sīkhnā) is an intransitive or transitive verb used when you acquire
faults.why: Restates the definition and vaguely says 'intransitive or transitive' without explaining 'ने' usage.

notes: Transitive verb: takes 'ने' (ne) in perfective tenses (e.g., मैंने हिंदी सीखी — I learned Hindi).
The person you learn from is marked with 'से' (se). Do not confuse with its causative 'सिखाना' (sikhānā, to teach a skill).

senses.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill by studying, practicing, or being taught.

examples.text: मैं हिंदी सीखना चाहता हूँ।
examples.translation: I want to learn Hindi.

faults.quote: Used to express physical movement to rhythm, or metaphorically when someone
faults.why: Restates the definition and adds an unillustrated metaphorical sense instead of useful grammar.

notes: Intransitive verb: it does not take 'ने' (ne) in the past tense (e.g., वह नाचा — he danced).

senses.definition: To move your body to the rhythm of music.

examples.text: शादी में सब लोग नाच रहे थे।
examples.translation: Everyone was dancing at the wedding.

faults.quote: though specifically using a pencil implies 'pencil se chitra banana'.
faults.why: Unhelpful filler written in Roman Hindi instead of Devanagari, restating the example.

corrected.shortGloss: to draw a picture; to paint
notes: A compound expression formed from 'चित्र' (picture, masculine noun) and 'बनाना' (to make). In everyday speech, 'तसवीर बनाना' (tasvīr banānā) or 'ड्राइंग बनाना' (ḍrāiṅg banānā) are also very common.

senses.definition: To create a picture of something using a pencil, pen, or brush.

examples.text: मैं पेंसिल से चित्र बना रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am drawing a picture with a pencil.

faults.quote: 是 links a subject to a noun that identifies it, functioning much
faults.why: Restates the first sense's definition without adding new grammatical information.

notes: Unlike English 'to be', 是 normally links nouns and cannot link a subject directly to an adjective; adjectives take adverbs like 很 (hěn) instead (e.g. 她很高 'she is tall').
Negated with 不 (bù) as 不是 (bú shì), never with 没 (méi).

senses.definition: Used to state what someone or something is, linking a subject to a noun.

examples.text: 我是学生。
examples.translation: I am a student.

senses.definition: Used to express agreement or confirmation.

examples.text: 是，我明白了。
examples.translation: Yes, I understand.

faults.quote: Use 打破 when you physically smash something into pieces or when you
faults.why: Merely restates the two sense definitions without adding new usage facts.

notes: Do not confuse with 坏 (huài), which describes being broken or out of order (e.g. 手机坏了 'the phone is broken'), whereas 打破 is the action of smashing something or breaking a limit.

senses.definition: To break or smash an object so that it falls into pieces.

examples.text: 他不小心把花瓶打破了。
examples.translation: He accidentally broke the vase.

senses.definition: To exceed or end an existing record, limit, or state such as silence.

examples.text: 她打破了世界纪录。
examples.translation: She broke the world record.

faults.quote: Use 穿 for clothes, shoes, hats, and glasses.
faults.why: False: hats and glasses take 戴 (dài) in Mandarin, never 穿.

faults.quote: 穿 can also mean 'to pierce' or 'to pass through', like threading
faults.why: Merely repeats the second sense instead of adding new usage guidance.

faults.quote: To have clothes, shoes, or accessories on one's body.
faults.why: Misleading: accessories take 戴 (dài), whereas 穿 is only for garments and footwear.

corrected.shortGloss: to wear; to put on; to pass through
notes: Use 穿 for clothing, shoes, and socks. For hats, glasses, scarves, gloves, and jewelry, use 戴 (dài) instead.

senses.definition: To put or have clothing or footwear on one's body.

examples.text: 他今天穿了一件红色的毛衣。
examples.translation: He is wearing a red sweater today.

senses.definition: To pass through an opening or space, or to pierce through something.

examples.text: 这根线太粗，穿不过针眼。
examples.translation: This thread is too thick to pass through the eye of the needle.

faults.quote: Achieved or solved with too much haste, appearing shallow.
faults.why: 'Una soluzione troppo facile' is just a shade of 'easy', not a distinct A2 sense.
Missing essential grammar note: invariable for gender (-e singular, -i plural) and 'facile da' + infinitive.

notes: The form is the same for masculine and feminine singular, and becomes 'facili' in the plural.
Followed by 'da' before an infinitive: 'facile da capire' (easy to understand).

senses.definition: Not requiring much effort or difficulty to do or understand.

examples.text: Questo esercizio è molto facile.
examples.translation: This exercise is very easy.

faults.why: Missing the crucial grammar rule: 'fare' agrees in number with the body part that hurts.

corrected.shortGloss: to hurt; to be bad for
notes: For body aches, use an indirect object pronoun (mi, ti, gli/le...) and make 'fare' agree with the body part: 'mi fa male la testa' (my head hurts), 'mi fanno male i piedi' (my feet hurt).
With a reflexive pronoun ('farsi male'), it means to hurt or injure oneself.

senses.definition: To cause physical or emotional pain, or to ache.

examples.text: Ho corso troppo ieri e adesso mi fanno male le gambe.
examples.translation: I ran too much yesterday and now my legs hurt.

examples.text: Le sue parole mi hanno fatto male.
examples.translation: His words hurt me.

senses.definition: To be harmful or bad for someone's health or well-being.

examples.text: Fumare fa male alla salute.
examples.translation: Smoking is bad for your health.

faults.quote: Use felice for both general happiness ('essere felice') and fortunate circumstances
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses in the entry.

faults.quote: Being favorable or lucky.
faults.why: Attributive 'un felice incontro' is literary/formal and marginal for A2; 'happy' covers greetings.

notes: The singular form 'felice' is used for both masculine and feminine (plural 'felici').
Usually expresses a deeper joy than 'contento', which is more common for everyday satisfaction or being pleased with something.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing joy and contentment.

examples.text: Sono molto felice di vederti qui oggi.
examples.translation: I am very happy to see you here today.

faults.quote: It is commonly used both for physical movement (stopping walking or driving)
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already defined in the entry.
Doesn't contrast intransitive 'fermarsi' (to stop oneself/come to a halt) with transitive 'fermare' (to stop something).

notes: Use reflexive 'fermarsi' when someone or something comes to a stop ('il treno si ferma'), and non-reflexive 'fermare' when stopping something else ('fermare la macchina').
Like all reflexive verbs, it forms compound tenses with 'essere': 'mi sono fermato/a'.

senses.definition: To cease moving or come to a halt.

examples.text: La macchina deve fermarsi al semaforo rosso.
examples.translation: The car must stop at the red light.

senses.definition: To remain somewhere for a short time, such as for a meal or the night.

examples.text: Posso fermarmi a dormire da te stasera?
examples.translation: Can I stay the night at your place tonight?

faults.why: Missing the irregular '-isc-' conjugation (finisco) and the 'avere' vs. 'essere' auxiliary split.

corrected.shortGloss: to finish; to end; to run out
notes: Takes '-isc-' in most present-tense forms: 'finisco, finisci, finisce, finiamo, finite, finiscono'.
In compound tenses, it takes 'avere' when transitive ('ho finito il libro', I finished the book) and 'essere' when intransitive ('il film è finito', the movie has ended).
Followed by 'di' before an infinitive: 'ho finito di mangiare' (I finished eating).

senses.definition: To complete an activity or use up the whole of something.

examples.text: Ho deciso di finire il libro stasera.
examples.translation: I decided to finish the book tonight.

senses.definition: To come to an end, or to have nothing left of a supply.

examples.text: Il film finisce alle dieci.
examples.translation: The movie ends at ten.

examples.text: È finito il latte, dobbiamo comprarlo.
examples.translation: The milk has run out, we need to buy some.

faults.quote: Thắng has multiple distinct meanings depending on context: winning a competition...
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses the crucial regional note that 'brake' is Southern (Northern uses 'phanh').

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to defeat; to brake
notes: In the sense 'to brake', 'thắng' is mainly used in Southern Vietnamese; Northern speakers usually say 'phanh'.

senses.definition: To be successful in a competition, game, or conflict, or to defeat an opponent.

examples.text: Đội của chúng tôi đã thắng trận đấu hôm nay.
examples.translation: Our team won the match today.

senses.definition: To slow down or stop a vehicle by using the brake.

examples.text: Bạn phải thắng gấp khi thấy đèn đỏ.
examples.translation: You must brake suddenly when you see a red light.

faults.quote: Thành phố refers specifically to a large town or city...
faults.why: Restates the definition and gives unneeded etymology.

notes: Often placed directly before a city's name in formal contexts (e.g., Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh).

senses.definition: A large and important town where many people live and work.

examples.text: Hà Nội là một thành phố lớn ở Việt Nam.
examples.translation: Hanoi is a large city in Vietnam.

faults.quote: A person between thirteen and nineteen years old.
faults.why: False equivalence with English 'teenager'; combines 'thanh niên' (young adults) and 'thiếu niên' (adolescents).

faults.quote: specifically referring to teenagers between thirteen and nineteen years old.
faults.why: False claim; it is a collective term for adolescents and young adults roughly aged 10–30.

notes: A collective term combining 'thiếu niên' (adolescents, roughly ages 10–15) and 'thanh niên' (young adults, roughly ages 16–30).

senses.definition: Young people collectively, including both adolescents and young adults.

examples.text: Nhiều thanh thiếu niên thích sử dụng mạng xã hội mỗi ngày.
examples.translation: Many young people like to use social media every day.

faults.quote: Use 'thấp' for people who are short in height...
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Do not confuse with 'ngắn', which means short in length or duration rather than height.

senses.definition: Of a person: of small height; not tall.

examples.text: Anh ấy hơi thấp so với bạn bè.
examples.translation: He is a bit short compared to his friends.

senses.definition: Of a thing, level, or amount: not high; close to the ground or bottom.

examples.text: Cái bàn này quá thấp đối với tôi.
examples.translation: This table is too low for me.

faults.quote: /tʰəjŋ͡m˧˥/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA with a final labial-velar nasal /ŋ͡m/ that does not exist in 'thấy'.

faults.quote: Thấy is one of the most common verbs in Vietnamese...
faults.why: Filler that only restates the senses; misses the common resultative usage after perception verbs.

corrected.shortGloss: to see; to feel; to find
notes: Often placed after verbs of looking, listening, or searching to show successful perception (e.g., 'nhìn thấy' to see, 'nghe thấy' to hear, 'tìm thấy' to find).

senses.definition: To perceive someone or something with the eyes or other senses.

examples.text: Tôi thấy một con chim trên cây.
examples.translation: I see a bird in the tree.

senses.definition: To experience an emotion or physical sensation (often short for 'cảm thấy').

examples.text: Hôm nay tôi thấy rất vui.
examples.translation: Today I feel very happy.

senses.definition: To have a particular impression or opinion about something.

examples.text: Bạn thấy phim này thế nào?
examples.translation: How do you find this movie?

faults.quote: Used figuratively, 'çorba' can mean a messy, tangled situation
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense; misses the useful collocation 'çorba içmek'.

faults.quote: We drank a hot lentil soup before dinner in the evening.
faults.why: Calqued 'drank soup' and redundant 'before dinner in the evening'.

notes: In Turkish, you 'drink' soup (çorba içmek) rather than 'eat' it.

senses.definition: A liquid dish, typically served hot, made by boiling meat, vegetables, or grains in stock or water.

examples.text: Akşam yemekten önce sıcak bir mercimek çorbası içtik.
examples.translation: We had a hot lentil soup before dinner.

senses.definition: An informal word for a disordered, confused state or a messy mixture of things.

examples.text: Projeyi o kadar kötü yönetti ki ortalık tamamen çorba oldu.
examples.translation: He managed the project so poorly that everything became a complete mess.

faults.quote: /tʃyn.cy/
faults.why: Missing primary stress mark on the first syllable (/ˈtʃyn.cy/).

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'çünkü' is a single-word conjunction, not a multi-word expression.

faults.quote: çünkü connects a statement to the reason or explanation that follows it.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of the word.

notes: Unlike 'diye' or 'için', which go at the end of a clause, 'çünkü' comes at the beginning of the clause giving the reason.

senses.definition: For the reason that; used to introduce an explanation or cause for something just stated.

examples.text: Bugün dışarı çıkmıyorum, çünkü hava çok soğuk.
examples.translation: I am not going out today, because the weather is very cold.

faults.quote: (hill) A very high hill that rises steeply above the surrounding land.
faults.why: Artificial split of 'mountain'; 'hill' in Turkish is 'tepe', not 'dağ'.

faults.quote: When adding suffixes, the soft 'ğ' remains silent and lengthens the preceding
faults.why: Between vowels (e.g. dağa), 'ğ' does not simply lengthen the preceding vowel.

notes: The letter 'ğ' (yumuşak g) is not pronounced as a consonant; in 'dağ', it simply lengthens the 'a' sound (/daː/).
A smaller hill is called 'tepe'.

senses.definition: A very high natural elevation of the earth's surface rising steeply above the surrounding land, larger than a hill.

examples.text: Kışın bu dağlar hep karla kaplanır.
examples.translation: In winter these mountains are always covered with snow.

faults.quote: /daiˈɾe/
faults.why: Missing long vowel /aː/ in the first syllable (/daː.i.ˈɾe/).

faults.quote: The word also has a geometric sense, so context is key
faults.why: Merely repeats that the word has a second sense.

notes: Beware of the false friend 'apartman': in Turkish, 'apartman' refers to the whole apartment building, while 'daire' is an individual flat inside it.

senses.definition: A self-contained home located on one floor of a larger residential building.

examples.text: Yeni dairemiz çok geniş ve aydınlık.
examples.translation: Our new apartment is very spacious and bright.

senses.definition: A flat, round shape whose edge is at the same distance from the center at every point.

examples.text: Kağıdın üzerine büyük bir daire çizdim.
examples.translation: I drew a big circle on the paper.

senses.definition: An office, department, or bureau, especially in government or public administration.

examples.text: Babam bir devlet dairesinde çalışıyor.
examples.translation: My father works in a government office.

faults.quote: /ˈpɛi̯n ˌdu.n/
faults.why: 'doen' is a monosyllable /dun/, not disyllabic /du.n/.

faults.quote: Pijn doen can mean both to feel pain (like an ache)
faults.why: 'Pijn doen' means to be painful; 'to feel pain' is 'pijn hebben'.

faults.quote: Pay attention to the context to know whether it is active
faults.why: Restates the senses and gives unhelpful advice instead of irregular forms and contrast.

notes: Irregular verb ('doen'): hij doet pijn, deed pijn, heeft pijn gedaan.
Do not confuse with 'pijn hebben' (to be in pain): 'Mijn voet doet pijn' (My foot hurts) vs. 'Ik heb pijn' (I am in pain).

senses.definition: Of a body part: to be sore or painful.

examples.text: Mijn hoofd doet pijn na een lange dag.
examples.translation: My head hurts after a long day.

senses.definition: To cause physical or emotional pain to someone.

examples.text: Die woorden deden me echt pijn.
examples.translation: Those words really hurt me.

faults.quote: While 'pittig' primarily describes hot or spicy food, it is also
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses already listed in the entry.

notes: For food, 'pittig' and 'scherp' both mean spicy/hot (from chilli or pepper), whereas 'gekruid' means seasoned with herbs or spices without necessarily being hot.

senses.definition: Of food: having a hot, burning taste from chilli or pepper.

examples.text: Deze curry is erg pittig.
examples.translation: This curry is very spicy.

senses.definition: Requiring a lot of effort, strength, or endurance.

examples.text: Dat was een pittige training.
examples.translation: That was a tough workout.

senses.definition: Of a person or character: lively, assertive, and full of spirit.

examples.text: Ze heeft een pittig karakter.
examples.translation: She has a spirited personality.

faults.quote: /ˈproːvə(n)/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'oe' in Dutch is pronounced /u/, so /ˈpruvə(n)/.

faults.quote: Use 'proeven' when you test food by eating a small bit
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Do not confuse with 'proberen' (to try or attempt something) or 'smaken' (to have a particular flavour, e.g. 'De soep smaakt goed' — The soup tastes good).

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to test its flavour, or to detect a flavour.

examples.text: Wil je even proeven of de soep goed is?
examples.translation: Do you want to taste whether the soup is good?

senses.definition: To sense or experience a quality, feeling, or atmosphere.

examples.text: Je kunt de spanning in de lucht proeven.
examples.translation: You can taste the tension in the air.

faults.quote: Ik wil graag de wereld rondreizen en nieuwe culturen ontdekken.
faults.why: Uses the different compound verb 'rondreizen' instead of the headword 'reizen'.

faults.quote: Use 'reizen' when talking about traveling in general or making a
faults.why: Wordy filler; a learner needs the auxiliary verb ('hebben'/'zijn') instead.

notes: In the perfect tense, use 'zijn' when a destination or route is mentioned ('Ik ben naar Parijs gereisd') and 'hebben' for travelling as an activity ('Ik heb veel gereisd').

senses.definition: To go from one place to another, especially over a long distance or by public transport.

examples.text: Ik reis meestal met de trein naar mijn werk.
examples.translation: I usually travel to work by train.

faults.quote: its past tense is irregular: ik rente, wij renten
faults.why: Completely false: 'rennen' is regular and takes '-de(n)' (ik rende, wij renden).
Running on foot and rushing around are shades of one meaning.

notes: Regular verb: ik rende, wij renden, gerend. Takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense when a direction or destination is given ('Ik ben naar huis gerend') and 'hebben' otherwise ('Ik heb de hele dag gerend').

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking, or to rush about in a hurry.

examples.text: Ik moet rennen om de trein te halen.
examples.translation: I need to run to catch the train.

faults.quote: Often used in clothing to store small items like keys, phones,
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving useful lexical or grammatical help.

faults.quote: Il a sorti un bonbon de sa poche.
faults.why: In French, 'sa poche' means his clothing pocket, not a separate pouch.

notes: The diminutive 'la pochette' means a small pouch, folder, or wallet; 'le livre de poche' is a paperback book.

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into or onto clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: J'ai mis mes clés dans ma poche.
examples.translation: I put my keys in my pocket.

senses.definition: A small bag or sealed sack, such as for liquids, ice, or a marsupial's young.

examples.text: Elle a mis une poche de glace sur son genou.
examples.translation: She put an ice pack on her knee.

faults.why: Missing the plural form ('pommes de terre') and the everyday spoken synonym 'la patate'.

notes: Literally 'apple of earth' (compare 'la pomme', apple). In the plural, only 'pomme' takes an '-s': 'des pommes de terre'.
In everyday spoken French, 'la patate' is very commonly used instead.

senses.definition: A round, starchy vegetable that grows underground and is widely used in cooking.

examples.text: J'ai acheté un sac de pommes de terre pour faire de la purée.
examples.translation: I bought a bag of potatoes to make mashed potatoes.

faults.quote: Use the feminine article 'la' or 'une' with this noun.
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

notes: Do not confuse with 'la pomme de terre' (potato), which is sometimes shortened to 'pomme' in dish names like 'pommes sautées'.

senses.definition: A round, crunchy fruit with red, yellow, or green skin that grows on trees.

examples.text: Je mange une pomme rouge.
examples.translation: I am eating a red apple.

faults.quote: door; gateway
faults.why: 'shortGloss' includes 'gateway', which is not covered by the single sense; airport/boarding gate sense is missing.

notes: Used for room, building, and car doors; a garden or fence gate is usually 'le portail' or 'la grille'.

senses.definition: A movable panel that you open and close to enter or leave a room, building, or vehicle.

examples.text: Ouvre la porte, s'il te plaît.
examples.translation: Open the door, please.

senses.definition: An exit for boarding at an airport, or an entrance gate in a city wall.

examples.text: L'embarquement commence à la porte 12.
examples.translation: Boarding begins at gate 12.

faults.quote: Use 'la poste' when referring to the post office building or
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Est-ce que la poste est déjà arrivée aujourd'hui ?
faults.why: In France, delivered letters are 'le courrier'; 'la poste' is the postal service (e.g. 'par la poste').

notes: Do not confuse with the masculine noun 'le poste' (a job position, a police station, or a radio/TV set).
For the letters and parcels delivered to your home, use 'le courrier' rather than 'la poste'.

senses.definition: The building or public office where you go to buy stamps and send letters or parcels.

examples.text: Je vais à la poste pour envoyer ce colis.
examples.translation: I am going to the post office to send this parcel.

senses.definition: The public service and system that collects and delivers letters and packages.

examples.text: J'ai envoyé les documents par la poste.
examples.translation: I sent the documents by mail.

faults.quote: /ˈʂklaŋka/
faults.why: Standard Polish uses dental /n/ before /k/ within native roots, not velar /ŋ/.

notes: Unlike 'kieliszek' (a stemmed glass for wine or spirits), 'szklanka' is a flat-bottomed glass used for water, juice, or tea.

senses.definition: A flat-bottomed drinking container made of glass, or the amount of liquid it holds.

examples.text: Nalej mi proszę szklankę wody.
examples.translation: Please pour me a glass of water.

faults.quote: A specific method, style, or approach to a craft or activity.
faults.why: Metaphorical 'school of thought/style' is unnecessary clutter for an A2 beginner.

faults.quote: While 'szkoła' primarily refers to the physical place of learning...
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions in the entry instead of giving usage guidance.

notes: Use 'do szkoły' for going to school and 'w szkole' for being at school (note the vowel shift 'o' → 'o' and 'ł' → 'l').

senses.definition: A place where children and young people go to be educated, or the time spent learning there.

examples.text: Moje dziecko chodzi do szkoły.
examples.translation: My child goes to school.

faults.quote: Even though the English word 'hospital' can be used as an adjective...
faults.why: Explains general Polish vs. English grammar rather than anything specific to 'szpital'.

notes: Takes the ending '-a' in the genitive singular ('do szpitala' — to the hospital) and '-u' in the locative ('w szpitalu' — in the hospital).

senses.definition: A large building where doctors and nurses treat people who are injured or ill.

examples.text: Muszę dzisiaj jechać do szpitala.
examples.translation: I have to go to the hospital today.

examples.text: W tym szpitalu pracują bardzo dobrzy lekarze.
examples.translation: Very good doctors work in this hospital.

faults.quote: Musimy zrobić szybki zakup w sklepie.
faults.why: Singular 'zrobić zakup' is unnatural in Polish; the plural 'zrobić szybkie zakupy' is standard.

faults.quote: Szybki is the standard adjective for 'fast' or 'quick'...
faults.why: Pure filler restating the glosses and definitions.

notes: The comparative form is irregular: 'szybszy' (faster). The corresponding adverb is 'szybko' (quickly, fast).

senses.definition: Moving or able to move at high speed.

examples.text: To jest bardzo szybki samochód.
examples.translation: This is a very fast car.

senses.definition: Lasting a short time or done without delay.

examples.text: Musimy zrobić szybkie zakupy.
examples.translation: We need to do some quick shopping.

faults.quote: Tak, lubiękawę.
faults.why: Missing space between 'lubię' and 'kawę'.
Missing the everyday degree adverb sense ('so', as in 'tak bardzo' / 'tak dobry').

senses.definition: Used to give an affirmative answer or show agreement.

examples.text: Tak, lubię kawę.
examples.translation: Yes, I like coffee.

senses.definition: In this way or manner.

examples.text: Zrób to tak.
examples.translation: Do it like this.

senses.definition: To such a high degree or extent, used before adjectives and adverbs for emphasis.

examples.text: Dlaczego to jest tak drogie?
examples.translation: Why is this so expensive?

notes: Literally 'male sibling', from 'erkek' (male) and 'kardeş' (sibling).
In everyday speech, people often say 'abi' (written 'ağabey') for an older brother and 'kardeş' for a younger sibling.

senses.definition: A male sibling.

examples.text: Erkek kardeşim üniversitede okuyor.
examples.translation: My brother is studying at university.

faults.quote: Bugün işe erken gittim.

notes: Used mostly as an adverb ('erken gelmek' — to come early), and also as an adjective ('erken saat' — early hour) without changing form. Opposite: 'geç' (late).

senses.definition: Happening or done before the usual or expected time.

examples.text: Sabah erken bir saatte yola çıktık.
examples.translation: We set off at an early hour in the morning.

examples.text: Bugün işe erken gittim.
examples.translation: I went to work early today.

faults.quote: spouse; partner; mate (of an animal); peer
faults.why: 'peer' is not covered by the senses, and 'mate (of an animal)' is too narrow.

corrected.shortGloss: spouse, partner; matching one of a pair
notes: 'Eş' is the standard polite, gender-neutral word for husband or wife. You will also hear 'koca' (husband) and 'karı' (wife), though 'karı' can sound rude outside fixed phrases.

senses.definition: A person's husband or wife.

examples.text: Eşim yarın akşam yemeğe gelecek.
examples.translation: My spouse is coming for dinner tomorrow evening.

senses.definition: Either of two things that belong together as a pair, or a partner in a game or activity.

examples.text: Bu çorabın eşini bulamıyorum.
examples.translation: I cannot find the match to this sock.

faults.quote: (condition) Worn, faded, or damaged from much use.
faults.why: For things and clothes, 'old' and 'worn from use' are one sense in Turkish.

faults.quote: 'Eski' can also mean 'former' when placed directly before a noun
faults.why: Restates sense 1 without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: Used for things, places, and times (opposite: 'yeni' — new), never for a person's age. For an old person, use 'yaşlı'; 'eski arkadaş' means an old (long-time or former) friend, not an elderly one.

senses.definition: Having existed or been used for a long time; not new.

examples.text: Bu eski arabayı tamir etmek çok zaman alır.
examples.translation: It takes a lot of time to fix this old car.

senses.definition: Having held a role or relationship in the past, or known for a long time.

examples.text: Eski okul arkadaşım dün beni sokakta gördü.
examples.translation: My old school friend saw me on the street yesterday.

faults.quote: Et is the general word for meat used as food, as well
faults.why: Merely restates the two definitions.

notes: In everyday food contexts, 'et' on its own often refers to red meat (beef or lamb), contrasted with 'tavuk' (chicken) and 'balık' (fish).
Do not confuse with 'ot' (grass, herb).

senses.definition: The flesh of an animal eaten as food.

examples.text: Akşam yemeği için kırmızı et pişirdim.
examples.translation: I cooked red meat for dinner.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of a human or animal body.

examples.text: Diken elime battı ama sadece ete geldi.
examples.translation: The thorn pricked my hand, but it only went into the flesh.

faults.quote: Use repareren when something mechanical, electronic, or physical is broken
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: The everyday informal equivalent is 'maken' (e.g., 'mijn fiets laten maken'). Do not confuse with 'opknappen', which means to renovate or refurbish.

senses.definition: To make something broken or damaged work again.

examples.text: De monteur kon mijn fiets gelukkig snel repareren.
examples.translation: Fortunately, the mechanic was able to repair my bicycle quickly.

faults.quote: Use 'rijden' for operating a car or travelling in a vehicle.
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses irregular forms and 'hebben' vs 'zijn' auxiliary usage.
Needs a note on its strong conjugation (reed, gereden) and auxiliary verbs.

notes: Strong verb: 'reed', 'heeft/is gereden'. Takes 'zijn' when a destination or direction is mentioned ('Ik ben naar huis gereden') and 'hebben' for the activity itself ('Ik heb de hele dag gereden').
'Rijden' is also used when a vehicle itself moves or operates on a route (e.g., 'De treinen rijden vandaag niet' — The trains aren't running today).

senses.definition: To operate and control a motor vehicle, or to travel in one.

examples.text: Ik moet voorzichtig rijden in de regen.
examples.translation: I have to drive carefully in the rain.

senses.definition: To travel on a bicycle, motorbike, or horse.

examples.text: Zij rijdt elke dag op haar fiets naar school.
examples.translation: She rides her bike to school every day.

faults.quote: Rijk is primarily used to describe people with lots of money
faults.why: Restates the senses and contrasts with an unrelated word ('duur'); misses 'rijk aan'.

notes: For the 'abundant in' sense, use the preposition 'aan' (e.g., 'rijk aan vitamines' — rich in vitamins).

senses.definition: Of a person or country: having a lot of money, property, or valuable possessions.

examples.text: Hij is erg rijk geworden door zijn nieuwe bedrijf.
examples.translation: He has become very rich through his new company.

senses.definition: Containing a large amount or variety of something desirable.

examples.text: Deze soep is erg rijk aan vitamines.
examples.translation: This soup is very rich in vitamins.

faults.quote: The colour of blood or a ripe strawberry.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('The colour...') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: Having a complexion that has become flushed or pink
faults.why: A red face is just a normal application of the colour red, not a separate sense.

notes: Inflected form before a noun: 'rode' (with a single 'o' and 'd' instead of 't', e.g., 'de rode auto', 'het rode huis').
For red hair, Dutch often uses 'rood' or 'ros', and 'roodharig' (red-haired) as an adjective.

senses.definition: Having the colour of blood or a ripe strawberry.

examples.text: Zij draagt vandaag een mooie rode jurk.
examples.translation: She is wearing a nice red dress today.

examples.text: Zijn gezicht werd helemaal rood toen hij moest spreken.
examples.translation: His face went completely red when he had to speak.

faults.why: Missing irregular verb forms (rook, geroken) and the preposition 'naar' (smell of/like).

notes: Strong verb: 'rook', 'heeft geroken'.
To say something smells 'like' or 'of' something, use 'ruiken naar' (e.g., 'Het ruikt hier naar verse koffie'). To smell something deliberately (take a sniff at), use 'ruiken aan'.

senses.definition: To perceive or notice a scent using your nose.

examples.text: Ik kan de koffie al ruiken vanaf de gang.
examples.translation: I can already smell the coffee from the hallway.

senses.definition: To give off a particular scent or odour.

examples.text: Deze rozen ruiken heel lekker.
examples.translation: These roses smell very nice.

faults.quote: In German, 'Bank' is a classic example of a homonym. It means
faults.why: Restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: The plural depends on the meaning: 'die Banken' (financial institutions) vs. 'die Bänke' (benches).

senses.definition: An institution where people keep their money or get financial services, or its building.

examples.text: Ich muss heute zur Bank gehen, um Geld abzuheben.
examples.translation: I have to go to the bank today to withdraw money.

senses.definition: A long seat for two or more people, often found in parks or public places.

examples.text: Wir setzen uns kurz auf die Bank im Park.
examples.translation: We sit down for a moment on the bench in the park.

faults.quote: Note that 'Biene' is feminine (die Biene).
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the entry header.

faults.quote: Bees are often associated with spring and summer.
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia that offers no useful linguistic help to an A2 learner.

senses.definition: A small yellow-and-black flying insect that collects nectar and makes honey.

examples.text: Im Sommer fliegen viele Bienen von Blume zu Blume.
examples.translation: In summer, many bees fly from flower to flower.

faults.why: Learners need the contrast with 'Blüte' (blossom on a tree), as 'blossom' is glossed.

notes: For the blossoms on trees or bushes, use 'die Blüte' rather than 'die Blume'.

senses.definition: The coloured part of a plant, or a small plant grown for its colourful blooms.

examples.text: Sie hat eine rote Blume im Garten gepflückt.
examples.translation: She picked a red flower in the garden.

notes: Singular in German for a single pair of glasses, unlike English 'glasses': 'Die Brille ist neu' (The glasses are new).

senses.definition: A pair of lenses in a frame worn on the face to help a person see better.

examples.text: Ich brauche meine Brille zum Lesen.
examples.translation: I need my glasses for reading.

faults.quote: Use 'รู้' when you know a fact, information, or how to do something (a skill).
faults.why: รู้ is not used for knowing how to do a skill; เป็น is used instead.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to be familiar with
notes: Use รู้จัก for being acquainted or familiar with a person, place, or thing. Use รู้ for knowing a fact or piece of information (and เป็น after a verb for knowing how to do a skill).

senses.definition: To be acquainted or familiar with a person, place, or thing.

examples.text: คุณรู้จักเขาไหม
examples.translation: Do you know him?

examples.text: ผมไม่ค่อยรู้จักแถวนี้เท่าไร
examples.translation: I am not very familiar with this area.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to be aware of
notes: Use รู้ for knowing a fact or piece of information (e.g., knowing the answer). Use รู้จัก for being acquainted or familiar with a person, place, or thing (e.g., knowing a friend or a city).

senses.definition: To have information or facts in one's mind, or to be aware of something.

examples.text: ฉันรู้ว่าเขามาแล้ว
examples.translation: I know that he has arrived already.

examples.text: เขาไม่รู้เรื่องนี้เลย
examples.translation: He does not know about this at all.

faults.quote: เขาตื่นเต้นกับข่าวนี้มาก
faults.why: Uses the compound word ตื่นเต้น (excited), not ตื่น meaning startled or panicked.

corrected.shortGloss: to wake up; to be startled
notes: Often combined with นอน (to sleep) as ตื่นนอน (to wake up from sleep). Also appears in common compounds like ตื่นเต้น (excited/nervous) and ตื่นตัว (alert).

senses.definition: To stop sleeping.

examples.text: ฉันตื่นเช้าทุกวัน
examples.translation: I wake up early every day.

senses.definition: To become suddenly frightened, panicked, or startled.

examples.text: ม้าตื่นเมื่อได้ยินเสียงดัง
examples.translation: The horse was startled when it heard the loud noise.

faults.quote: เดิน is the standard verb for walking on foot, but it is

examples.text: ฉันชอบเดินไปทำงานทุกเช้า

examples.text: นาฬิกาเรือนนี้ยังเดินอยู่ไหม

faults.quote: ยืน refers to the act of standing upright on one's feet.

senses.definition: To be in an upright position on one's feet.

examples.text: เขายืนรอรถเมล์

faults.quote: tomorrow; the next day

notes: Do not confuse with the noun 'der Morgen' (morning), which is capitalized. Combine them as 'morgen früh' (tomorrow morning).

examples.text: Ich habe morgen einen Termin.
examples.translation: I have an appointment tomorrow.

faults.quote: Use müde when you need rest or sleep, or when you

examples.translation: After the long workday, I am very tired.

senses.definition: Having no more patience or enthusiasm for something.

examples.text: Ich bin es müde, immer dasselbe zu erklären.
examples.translation: I am tired of always explaining the same thing.

faults.quote: Mutig is used for people who act despite fear. Do not

examples.text: Sie war sehr mutig, als sie dem Hund geholfen hat.
examples.translation: She was very brave when she helped the dog.

faults.quote: wet; damp

faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun phrase ('Weather...').

faults.quote: glass; drinking glass; vessel

examples.translation: She bought a red dress for the party.

faults.quote: A trip from one place to another and back again.

faults.quote: To be on the point of or about to happen.
faults.why: Colloquial/southern usage for weather or bodily states; northern A2 uses 'sắp'.

senses.definition: To feel a desire to do or have something.

examples.text: Tôi muốn ăn phở.
examples.translation: I want to eat pho.

faults.quote: /nam/
