senses.definition: Old in age; grown-up; eldest among siblings.

examples.text: 你今年多大了？
examples.translation: How old are you this year?

examples.text: 他比我大两岁。
examples.translation: He is two years older than me.

faults.why: Misses the essential A1/A2 usage of 错 as a result complement after a verb (e.g. 写错, 说错).

faults.quote: Used as an adjective to describe something that is not right
faults.why: Restates the part of speech and definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with '不对' (bú duì), which is often used
faults.why: Misleading; 不对 is the standard everyday way to say 'wrong/incorrect', often interchangeable with 错.

notes: Very often placed directly after a verb to show an action was done wrongly: 写错 (xiěcuò, write wrongly), 走错 (zǒucuò, go the wrong way), 买错 (mǎicuò, buy the wrong thing).
Also used as a noun meaning 'mistake' or 'fault', as in 犯错 (fàncuò, make a mistake) or 是我的错 (shì wǒ de cuò, it's my fault).

senses.definition: Not correct or true; mistaken.

examples.text: 这个答案是错的。
examples.translation: This answer is wrong.

examples.text: 对不起，我打错电话了。
examples.translation: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.

faults.quote: السَّمَاءُ صَافِيَةٌ وَأَزْرَقُ.
faults.why: Ungrammatical gender agreement: السماء (sky) is feminine, so it requires زرقاء, not أزرق.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the deep sea.
faults.why: Defined as a noun ('The colour of...') rather than an adjective ('Of the colour...').

notes: The feminine form is زَرْقَاء (zarqāʾ) and the plural for people is زُرْق (zurq). Non-human plurals take the feminine singular زَرْقَاء.
Like other primary colour adjectives on the pattern أَفْعَل (afʿal), it does not take nunation (tanwīn).

senses.definition: Of the colour of a clear sky or the deep sea.

examples.text: يَرْتَدِي قَمِيصًا أَزْرَقَ.
examples.translation: He is wearing a blue shirt.

examples.text: السَّمَاءُ صَافِيَةٌ وَزَرْقَاءُ.
examples.translation: The sky is clear and blue.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who lacks money or basic necessities.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of the first sense.

faults.quote: It is often used with a sense of empathy or mild sadness.
faults.why: Vague filler note with no grammatical or lexical utility.

notes: The masculine plural is فُقَرَاء (fuqarāʾ), which does not take nunation. It is also commonly used as a noun meaning 'a poor person'.
When meaning 'lacking in', it takes the preposition بِـ (bi-) or إِلَى (ʾilā).

senses.definition: Having very little money and few possessions.

examples.text: هَذَا الرَّجُلُ فَقِيرٌ وَيَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مُسَاعَدَةٍ.
examples.translation: This man is poor and needs help.

senses.definition: Lacking in a particular substance or quality (not used for low-grade workmanship).

examples.text: تُرْبَةُ هَذِهِ المَنْطِقَةِ فَقِيرَةٌ بِالمَوَادِّ الغِذَائِيَّةِ.
examples.translation: The soil in this area is poor in nutrients.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'jiddin' (serious/solemn)
faults.why: Wrong Arabic word and transliteration: 'jiddan' means 'very'; 'serious/solemn' is جَادّ (jādd) or جِدِّيّ (jiddī).

faults.quote: Use 'khatir' when something poses a real risk of harm or damage.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of the first sense.

notes: For 'serious' in the sense of 'not joking' or 'earnest', use جَادّ (jādd) or جِدِّيّ (jiddī), not خَطِير.

senses.definition: Able to hurt people or cause serious damage.

examples.text: هَذَا الطَّرِيقُ خَطِيرٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This road is very dangerous.

senses.definition: Of a situation, illness, or problem: very bad and requiring urgent attention.

examples.text: الوَضْعُ خَطِيرٌ فِي المَدِينَةِ.
examples.translation: The situation in the city is critical.

faults.quote: Use سَرِيع for things that move fast like cars or people.
faults.why: Merely restates the two sense definitions without adding grammatical or usage info.

notes: The accusative form سَرِيعًا (sarīʿan) or the phrase بِسُرْعَةٍ (bi-surʿatin) is used as the adverb 'quickly'.

senses.definition: Moving or capable of moving at high speed.

examples.text: هَذِهِ السَّيَّارَةُ سَرِيعَةٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: This car is very fast.

senses.definition: Happening or done in a short time.

examples.text: تَنَاوَلْتُ غَدَاءً سَرِيعًا قَبْلَ العَمَلِ.
examples.translation: I had a quick lunch before work.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who is physically or mentally tense.
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions and example contexts.

notes: Active participle of the verb تَوَتَّرَ (tawattara, 'to become tense or strained').

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling nervous, worried, or unable to relax.

examples.text: كَانَ الطَّالِبُ مُتَوَتِّرًا قَبْلَ الامْتِحَانِ.
examples.translation: The student was nervous before the exam.

senses.definition: Of a situation or relationship: not calm or friendly, and likely to cause conflict.

examples.text: العَلَاقَةُ بَيْنَهُمَا مُتَوَتِّرَةٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: The relationship between them is very tense.

faults.quote: yapraklar sarariyor ve dökülüyor.
faults.why: Spelling error: 'sarariyor' should be 'sararıyor' (dotless ı).

faults.quote: /sonbaˈhaɾ/
faults.why: Compounds with 'son' carry primary stress on the first syllable: /ˈsonbahaɾ/.
Should mention 'sonbaharda' (in autumn) as a very common usage for A2 learners.

notes: Compound of 'son' (last, end) and 'bahar' (spring). Another common, slightly more literary word for autumn is 'güz'.
To say 'in autumn', add the locative suffix '-da': 'sonbaharda'.

senses.definition: The season of the year between summer and winter, when leaves fall from the trees.

examples.text: Sonbahar gelince yapraklar sararıyor ve dökülüyor.
examples.translation: When autumn arrives, the leaves turn yellow and fall.

faults.quote: to ask; to inquire; to consult
faults.why: 'to consult' is not covered in the senses.

faults.quote: (örneğin: ona sormak)
faults.why: Notes must be in English ('for example', not 'örneğin').
Missing distinction from 'istemek' (to ask for / request), a classic A1/A2 trap.

faults.quote: I want to ask a question to the teacher.
faults.why: Unnatural English calque; should be 'ask the teacher a question'.

notes: Takes the dative case (-e/-a) for the person being asked (e.g. 'ona sormak' — to ask him/her) and the accusative case (-i/-ı) for the thing asked about.
Used only for asking a question for information. To ask for something (to request), use 'istemek' or 'rica etmek'.

senses.definition: To put a question to someone in order to get information.

examples.text: Öğretmene bir soru sormak istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to ask the teacher a question.

senses.definition: To ask about someone's well-being or whereabouts.

examples.text: Annem seni sordu.
examples.translation: My mother asked about you.

faults.why: Must mention consonant gemination before vowel suffixes ('sırrı', 'sırrım'), which violates standard patterns.

faults.quote: Sır is used for information kept hidden from others, like a personal secret.
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0.

notes: The final 'r' doubles when a suffix starting with a vowel is added: 'sırrı' (the secret), 'sırrım' (my secret).
Often used with verbs like 'saklamak' or 'tutmak' (to keep a secret) and 'vermek' (to give away a secret).
Do not confuse with 'sıra' (row, line, turn).

senses.definition: Something that is kept hidden from other people.

examples.text: Bu seninle benim aramızdaki bir sır.
examples.translation: This is a secret between you and me.

senses.definition: Something that is not understood or explained.

examples.text: Evrenin sırları hâlâ çözülmeyi bekliyor.
examples.translation: The mysteries of the universe are still waiting to be solved.

faults.why: Missing the everyday A1/A2 school/classroom meaning 'school desk' or 'bench'.

faults.quote: queue; order; row
faults.why: Should include 'turn' and 'desk' to match the core senses.

notes: Commonly used in expressions like 'sıra beklemek' (to wait in line) and 'sıraya girmek' (to get in line).
Do not confuse with 'sır' (secret).

senses.definition: A line of people or vehicles waiting for something.

examples.text: Sırada çok insan var.
examples.translation: There are many people in the queue.

senses.definition: The position or turn of someone in a sequence or series.

examples.text: Şimdi sıra sende.
examples.translation: Now it is your turn.

senses.definition: A horizontal arrangement of objects or seats side by side.

examples.text: Ön sırada oturduk.
examples.translation: We sat in the front row.

senses.definition: A desk for students in a classroom, or a long bench for sitting.

examples.text: Öğrenciler sıralarına oturdu.
examples.translation: The students sat at their desks.

faults.quote: extending from the neck to the hips.
faults.why: Contradicts note 0; 'sırt' is only the upper/mid back, from neck to waist.

notes: Refers specifically to the upper and middle part of the back, from the neck down to the waist. For the lower back, Turkish uses 'bel'.

senses.definition: The rear part of the human body, extending from the neck and shoulders to the waist.

examples.text: Sırtım çok ağrıyor.
examples.translation: My back hurts a lot.

senses.definition: The long, narrow top part of a hill or mountain range.

examples.text: Dağın sırtından şehri görebiliyorduk.
examples.translation: We could see the city from the ridge of the mountain.

faults.quote: While 'hassen' is a very strong word in German, it is sometimes
faults.why: Notes 0 and 1 repeat the exact same point and partially contradict each other.

notes: 'hassen' is a strong word in German, though it is also used casually for everyday annoyances. For milder dislikes, prefer 'nicht mögen' (to not like).

senses.definition: To feel intense dislike or hostility toward someone or something.

examples.text: Ich hasse es, wenn der Wecker so früh klingelt.
examples.translation: I hate it when the alarm clock rings so early.

examples.text: Sie hasst Lügen mehr als alles andere.
examples.translation: She hates lies more than anything else.

faults.quote: For things that are not visually appealing but in a more subtle
faults.why: 'unhübsch' is rare and elevated, not a useful recommendation for an A2 learner.

notes: 'hässlich' is a very strong and direct word. To be more polite, say 'nicht schön' (not nice/pretty) instead.

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; not attractive.

examples.text: Er trägt einen sehr hässlichen Pullover.
examples.translation: He is wearing a very ugly sweater.

senses.definition: Of behavior or a situation: unpleasant, mean, or morally wrong.

examples.text: Das war eine hässliche Bemerkung von ihm.
examples.translation: That was a nasty remark from him.

faults.why: Hot objects and hot weather are the same literal temperature meaning.
Lacks the crucial A1/A2 grammar warning: 'Mir ist heiß' (not 'Ich bin heiß').

faults.quote: Use 'heiß' for high temperatures. For things that are only 'warm'
faults.why: Both notes are filler; learners already know hot vs. warm and won't confuse 'hitzig'.

notes: To say that a person feels hot, use the dative: 'Mir ist heiß' (I am hot). Never say 'Ich bin heiß', which means 'I am sexually aroused' or 'attractive'.
For spicy food ('hot' in English), German uses 'scharf', not 'heiß'.

senses.definition: Having a high temperature.

examples.text: Vorsicht, die Suppe ist noch sehr heiß!
examples.translation: Careful, the soup is still very hot!

examples.text: Heute ist es wirklich heiß draußen.
examples.translation: It is really hot outside today.

faults.why: Helping a person and helping someone do something are shades of one meaning.
Should mention the irregular stem vowel change (du hilfst, er hilft; geholfen).

notes: Irregular verb with a vowel change in the present tense: 'du hilfst', 'er/sie/es hilft' (past: 'half', 'hat geholfen').
Always takes the dative case for the person being helped: 'Ich helfe dir' (not 'dich'). Use 'bei' + dative for the task: 'Er hilft mir bei den Hausaufgaben'.

senses.definition: To make it easier or possible for someone to do something by offering aid.

examples.text: Kannst du mir bitte beim Kochen helfen?
examples.translation: Can you please help me with the cooking?

examples.text: Diese Software hilft mir, meine Arbeit schneller zu erledigen.
examples.translation: This software helps me get my work done faster.

faults.quote: today
faults.why: Sense 1 ('nowadays') is missing from shortGloss.

faults.quote: While 'heute' means 'on this day', it can also be used
faults.why: Note 0 restates the senses; Note 1 states a general V2 grammar rule.

notes: Combine directly with parts of the day: 'heute Morgen' (this morning), 'heute Nachmittag' (this afternoon), 'heute Abend' (this evening / tonight).

senses.definition: On this present day.

examples.text: Heute ist ein sonniger Tag.
examples.translation: Today is a sunny day.

senses.definition: At the present period of time, compared with the past.

examples.text: Heute reisen die Menschen viel mehr als früher.
examples.translation: Nowadays, people travel much more than in the past.

faults.quote: /los ˈpaðɾes/
faults.why: IPA should transcribe the word without the article.

faults.quote: Hoy en el colegio celebran el día de los padres.
faults.why: Father's Day in Spain is 'el Día del Padre'; this example is unnatural.

notes: The masculine plural 'los padres' refers to 'parents' (mother and father together) as well as to more than one father.

senses.definition: A person's mother and father considered together.

examples.text: Mis padres viven en el campo.
examples.translation: My parents live in the countryside.

senses.definition: More than one father.

examples.text: Los dos padres esperaban a sus hijos a la salida del colegio.
examples.translation: The two fathers were waiting for their children outside the school.

faults.quote: Aprendí a comer con los palillos en mi viaje a Japón.
faults.why: In Spanish, 'comer con palillos' takes no definite article.

notes: In Spain, 'un palillo' alone usually means a toothpick; chopsticks are often called 'palillos chinos' unless the context makes it clear.

senses.definition: Small thin wooden sticks used to remove food from between the teeth.

examples.text: ¿Me traes unos palillos, por favor?
examples.translation: Could you bring me some toothpicks, please?

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks used as eating utensils, especially in East Asian cuisine.

examples.text: Aprendí a comer con palillos en mi viaje a Japón.
examples.translation: I learned to eat with chopsticks on my trip to Japan.

faults.quote: /los pantaˈlones/
faults.why: IPA should not include the article.

faults.quote: Unlike in some regions of Latin America where 'pantalón' can occasionally refer to underwear
faults.why: False claim (confuses 'pantalón' with 'pantaletas'/'calzones'); replace with note on singular 'el pantalón'.

notes: Can be used in the singular ('el pantalón') or the plural ('los pantalones') to refer to a single pair of trousers.
'Pantalones cortos' means 'shorts'.

senses.definition: An outer garment covering the body from the waist to the ankles, with a separate part for each leg.

examples.text: Me he comprado unos pantalones nuevos para el trabajo.
examples.translation: I bought some new trousers for work.

faults.why: Must explain the essential 'ser malo' (bad/evil) vs 'estar malo' (sick/spoiled) distinction.

faults.quote: Me siento un poco malo hoy.
faults.why: In Spain, 'estar malo' or 'encontrarse mal' is used, not 'sentirse malo'.

notes: Shortens to 'mal' before a masculine singular noun (e.g., 'un mal día').
Used with 'ser' for poor quality or bad character ('es malo'), and with 'estar' for being ill or spoiled food ('está malo').
Its irregular comparative is 'peor' (worse).

senses.definition: Of poor quality, unpleasant, or not satisfactory.

examples.text: Ayer vimos una película muy mala.
examples.translation: Yesterday we saw a very bad film.

senses.definition: Of a person (with 'estar'): physically unwell; of food: spoiled.

examples.text: Hoy no voy a trabajar porque estoy malo.
examples.translation: I'm not going to work today because I'm ill.

senses.definition: Of a person or character (with 'ser'): cruel, wicked, or poorly behaved.

examples.text: El villano de la historia es muy malo.
examples.translation: The villain of the story is very evil.

faults.quote: The early part of the day, between sunrise and noon.
faults.why: This entry's POS is adverb; 'la mañana' (morning) is a feminine noun.

notes: Do not confuse the adverb 'mañana' (tomorrow) with the feminine noun 'la mañana' (the morning): 'mañana por la mañana' means 'tomorrow morning'.

senses.definition: On the day after today.

examples.text: Mañana voy a estudiar español.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to study Spanish.

faults.quote: Use this when you have too much work or are currently
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; omits that it takes the preposition بِـ (bi-).

notes: Followed by the preposition بِـ (bi-) to say what someone is busy with (مَشْغُول بِـ 'busy with').

senses.definition: Of a person: having a lot to do or currently occupied with an activity.

examples.text: أَنَا مَشْغُولٌ جِدًّا الْيَوْمَ بِالْعَمَلِ.
examples.translation: I am very busy with work today.

examples.text: هَلْ أَنْتَ مَشْغُولٌ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّحْظَةِ؟
examples.translation: Are you busy right now?

senses.definition: Of a phone line, seat, or room: currently in use and not available.

examples.text: خَطُّ الْهَاتِفِ مَشْغُولٌ.
examples.translation: The phone line is busy.

faults.quote: A person who is not willing to work or put in effort.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('A person who...').

faults.quote: Unlike the English word 'lazy', which can be very judgmental, 'kasul'
faults.why: False pragmatics claim; كَسُول is just as judgmental as 'lazy', and omits irregular feminine/plural forms.

notes: As an adjective on the فَعُول (faʿūl) pattern, it often stays unchanged for the feminine singular (بِنْت كَسُول), though كَسُولَة is also common in modern Arabic. The plural is كُسَالَى (kusālā).

senses.definition: Unwilling to work, study, or make an effort.

examples.text: هُوَ وَلَدٌ كَسُولٌ لَا يُحِبُّ الدِّرَاسَةَ.
examples.translation: He is a lazy boy who does not like studying.

faults.quote: Flat, level ground, often referring to a plain or valley.
faults.why: Defines the noun 'plain' in an adjective entry, and falsely includes 'valley'.

faults.quote: easy; simple; uncomplicated
faults.why: Includes 'uncomplicated', which is absent from the sense glosses.

faults.quote: Use 'sahl' to describe a task or test that required little effort.
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning without adding useful grammatical or usage information.

notes: Do not confuse with بَسِيط (basīṭ, 'simple'), which means 'plain' or 'uncomplicated' rather than 'not difficult'.

senses.definition: Not difficult to do, understand, or achieve.

examples.text: الِامْتِحَانُ كَانَ سَهْلًا.
examples.translation: The exam was easy.

senses.definition: Of land or terrain: flat, level, and easy to cross.

examples.text: مَشَيْنَا فِي أَرْضٍ سَهْلَةٍ.
examples.translation: We walked on flat ground.

faults.quote: Use 'مبتل' to describe something that has absorbed liquid or is
faults.why: Pure filler restating the definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'مطر' (rain), which is the noun
faults.why: No learner would confuse مُبْتَلّ (mubtall) with the unrelated noun مَطَر (maṭar).

notes: The final لّ (ll) is doubled; the feminine form is مُبْتَلَّة (mubtalla).
Followed by بِـ (bi-) to indicate the liquid (مُبْتَلّ بِالْمَاء 'wet with water').

senses.definition: Covered or soaked with water or another liquid.

examples.text: ثِيَابِي مُبْتَلَّةٌ بِسَبَبِ الْمَطَرِ.
examples.translation: My clothes are wet because of the rain.

faults.quote: الْجِسْمُ السَّلِيمُ فِي الْعَقْلِ الصَّحِيحِ.
faults.why: Inverts the famous proverb الْعَقْلُ السَّلِيمُ فِي الْجِسْمِ السَّلِيمِ and swaps in الصَّحِيحِ.

faults.quote: correct; true; real; healthy
faults.why: Contains 'real', which is not covered by the senses or sense glosses.

faults.quote: Use 'sahih' for both factual correctness ('that is correct') and moral integrity
faults.why: Mentions 'moral integrity', which is not a sense in the entry.

notes: Often used on its own in conversation to mean 'That's right!' or, with rising intonation, 'Really?' / 'Is that true?'.

senses.definition: In accordance with fact or truth; without mistakes.

examples.text: هَذَا الْجَوَابُ صَحِيحٌ.
examples.translation: This answer is correct.

senses.definition: Free from illness or injury; in good physical condition.

examples.text: وُلِدَ الطِّفْلُ صَحِيحَ الْجِسْمِ.
examples.translation: The child was born with a healthy body.

faults.quote: Aman describes a state of being free from harm or danger.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.
Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning; both examples mean 'safe'.

notes: In casual conversation, 'aman' is often used on its own to mean 'all good', 'under control', or 'no worries'.
Do not confuse with 'tenang', which means calm or quiet.

senses.definition: Protected from danger, harm, or trouble; secure.

examples.text: Rumah ini terasa sangat aman.
examples.translation: This house feels very safe.

examples.text: Jalanan di sini aman untuk pejalan kaki.
examples.translation: The streets here are safe for pedestrians.

senses.definition: (informal) Under control; without any problem.

examples.text: Tenang saja, semuanya sudah aman.
examples.translation: Just relax, everything is all good now.

faults.why: Missing IPA transcription.

notes: Literally 'male child' ('anak' = child, 'laki-laki' = male). Used for both 'son' and 'boy' depending on context.
A more formal single word for 'son' is 'putra'.

senses.definition: A person's male child.

examples.text: Anak laki-laki saya suka bermain sepak bola.
examples.translation: My son likes to play football.

senses.definition: A male child.

examples.text: Ada banyak anak laki-laki di taman.

faults.quote: child; offspring; native; part

senses.definition: A young human who is not yet an adult.

examples.text: Anak itu sedang bermain bola di lapangan.
examples.translation: The child is playing ball in the field.

senses.definition: A person's son or daughter of any age.

examples.text: Mereka mempunyai tiga orang anak.
examples.translation: They have three children.

senses.definition: The young of an animal, placed before the animal's name.

examples.text: Kucing itu melahirkan empat ekor anak kucing.
examples.translation: The cat gave birth to four kittens.

faults.quote: /ˈanak pəˈruman/
faults.why: Wrong IPA for 'perempuan'; it is /pərəmˈpuan/, not /pəˈruman/.

faults.quote: In the context of family, it specifically means 'daughter', whereas in general
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

notes: Literally 'female child' ('anak' = child, 'perempuan' = female). Used for both 'daughter' and 'girl'.

senses.definition: A person's female child.

examples.text: Dia sangat bangga pada anak perempuan sulungnya.
examples.translation: He is very proud of his eldest daughter.

senses.definition: A female child.

examples.text: Ada seorang anak perempuan yang sedang bermain di taman.
examples.translation: There is a girl playing in the park.

senses.definition: To set up or create an organization, group, or digital space.

examples.text: 我建了一个微信群。
examples.translation: I set up a WeChat group.

faults.why: Should mention that in Chinese, eating soup is expressed with 喝 (喝汤).

notes: In Chinese, 喝 is also used for soup: 喝汤 (hē tāng, to eat/have soup).
Do not confuse 喝 (hē, with 口 'mouth' on the left) with the similar-looking 渴 (kě, with 氵 'water' on the left), which means 'thirsty'.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.text: 我口渴了，想喝点水。
examples.translation: I'm thirsty and want to drink some water.

examples.text: 每天喝八杯水对身体好。
examples.translation: Drinking eight glasses of water a day is good for your health.

faults.quote: 打扫 is the general word for cleaning rooms or spaces by sweeping
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

notes: Used for rooms, houses, or open spaces (e.g., 打扫房间, 打扫卫生), not for washing small objects or clothes.

senses.definition: To make a room or area clean by sweeping, dusting, or tidying up.

examples.text: 周末我需要打扫房间。
examples.translation: I need to clean my room this weekend.

examples.text: 我们一起把客厅打扫干净吧。
examples.translation: Let's clean up the living room together.

faults.quote: If you are just paying a brief visit to a place or
faults.why: False: 访问 means an official or formal visit (or to interview), not a brief visit.

faults.quote: Use 参观 when you are visiting a place for interest or observation
faults.why: Merely repeats the sense definition.

notes: Used only for places you look around (like museums, schools, or factories), never for people. To visit a person, use 看 (kàn), 看望 (kànwàng), or 拜访 (bàifǎng).

senses.definition: To go and look around a place such as a museum, school, or factory for sightseeing or learning.

examples.text: 下周我们打算去博物馆参观。
examples.translation: We plan to visit the museum next week.

examples.text: 很多学生来工厂参观。
examples.translation: Many students come to tour the factory.

faults.quote: Often shortened to '대' in casual speech, as in '대 student' (대학생) or 'going to dae' (대에 가다).
faults.why: Completely false: 대학교 shortens to 대학, and '대에 가다' is not Korean.

notes: Often shortened to '대학' (as in '대학에 가다', to go to university). A university student is '대학생'.

senses.definition: An institution of higher education where students study for a degree after high school.

examples.text: 누나와 형은 모두 대학교에 다닙니다.
examples.translation: Both my older sister and older brother attend university.

notes: Used for counting the levels of a building with Sino-Korean numerals (1층, 2층, 3층).
Do not confuse with '바닥' (floor/ground surface); '층' refers to the story or level of a building, while '바닥' is the physical surface you walk on.

senses.definition: One of the horizontal levels of a building.

examples.text: 우리 집은 3층에 있어요.
examples.translation: My home is on the third floor.

senses.definition: A sheet or thickness of a substance lying on or between others.

examples.text: 케이크에 크림을 여러 층으로 발랐어요.
examples.translation: I spread several layers of cream on the cake.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'weather' (e.g. 날이 좋다 / 날이 춥다).

faults.quote: While '날' often refers to a generic 'day', it can also mean
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: 칼날이 매우 날카롭다.
faults.why: Uses the compound noun 칼날 instead of the standalone word 날.

notes: Used as a native Korean noun (좋은 날, 마지막 날). For numbered dates of the month or counting days with Sino-Korean numbers, '일' is used instead (1일, 3일).

senses.definition: A twenty-four-hour period, or a particular day for an event or occasion.

examples.text: 우리 만날 날을 정하자.
examples.translation: Let's set a day to meet.

senses.definition: The state of the weather on a given day, especially in expressions about how nice, cold, or warm it is.

examples.text: 오늘은 날이 정말 좋네요.
examples.translation: The weather is really nice today.

senses.definition: The sharp cutting edge of a tool or weapon such as a knife.

examples.text: 칼의 날이 매우 날카롭다.
examples.translation: The blade of the knife is very sharp.

faults.quote: While 식당 most commonly means a commercial restaurant, it can also refer
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses without adding usage information.

faults.quote: restaurant; dining room
faults.why: Uses 'dining room', which does not appear in the sense glosses ('cafeteria, dining hall, canteen').

notes: '식당' is used for everyday restaurants and cafeterias; '레스토랑' is used specifically for Western-style or upscale restaurants.

senses.definition: A place where meals are prepared and served to paying customers.

examples.text: 이 근처에 맛있는 식당이 있어요?
examples.translation: Is there a good restaurant around here?

senses.definition: A room or hall in a school, workplace, or other building where people eat meals.

examples.text: 점심 시간에 학생 식당으로 갔어요.
examples.translation: I went to the student cafeteria at lunchtime.

faults.quote: adj
faults.why: 有空 is a verb-object compound (verb), not an adjective.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 有空间 (yǒu kōng jiān)...
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; note should instead mention the spoken儿化 form 有空儿 and 4th tone 空.

corrected.shortGloss: to be free; to have free time
notes: A separable verb-object phrase; its negative form is 没空 (méikòng, to be busy).
Here 空 is pronounced in the fourth tone (kòng, free time), not the first tone (kōng, empty). Often pronounced 有空儿 (yǒukòngr) in northern speech.

senses.definition: To have spare time; to be free or available.

examples.text: 你周末有空吗？
examples.translation: Are you free this weekend?

faults.quote: Use 强壮 to describe physical strength, a muscular build...
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

faults.quote: He goes to the gym often, and now his body is very strong.
faults.why: Calqued translation of 身体很强壮 ('his body is very strong').

notes: Describes physical power and a sturdy build in people or animals, unlike 健康 (jiànkāng, healthy), which simply means free from illness.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: physically strong and solidly built.

examples.text: 他经常去健身房，现在身体很强壮。
examples.translation: He goes to the gym often and is very strong and fit now.

faults.why: Missing essential A1/A2 senses: 'well/recovered', 'done/ready', and 'OK/agreed'.

faults.quote: 好 is one of the most versatile adjectives in Mandarin...
faults.why: Vague filler note; should explain 好 + verb ('easy/good to...') and fourth-tone 爱好.

corrected.shortGloss: good; well; ready; easy to; OK
notes: Placed before a verb (好 + verb), it means 'easy to' or 'pleasant to', forming common words like 好吃 (delicious) and 好看 (good-looking).
Also read fourth tone (hào) when meaning 'to like', as in 爱好 (àihào, hobby).

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or satisfactory.

examples.text: 今天天气很好。
examples.translation: The weather is very nice today.

senses.definition: In good health, or recovered from an illness.

examples.text: 你的感冒好了吗？
examples.translation: Are you over your cold?

senses.definition: Finished, ready, or completed (often after a verb).

examples.text: 晚饭做好了。
examples.translation: Dinner is ready.

senses.definition: Before a verb: easy or pleasant to do.

examples.text: 这个字很好写。
examples.translation: This character is easy to write.

senses.definition: Used to express agreement or acceptance.

examples.text: 好，我们明天见。
examples.translation: OK, see you tomorrow.

faults.quote: Used to describe people who are warm, gentle, and well-meaning.
faults.why: Both notes are filler restating the definition and part of speech.

notes: Describes someone's moral character or inner nature (e.g. 心底善良), rather than a single polite action.

senses.definition: Of a person or their nature: kind, gentle, and caring toward others.

examples.text: 她是一个非常善良的人，经常帮助别人。
examples.translation: She is a very kind person and often helps others.

faults.quote: fast; happy; sharp
faults.why: Includes 'happy', which is not in the senses (and only occurs in compounds), while omitting 'soon'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 高兴 (gāoxìng), which simply means happy...
faults.why: Learners do not confuse standalone 快 with 高兴; a note on 快…了 ('about to') is needed instead.

notes: In the pattern 快（要）…了, it works as an adverb meaning 'about to' or 'almost': 快到了 (almost there).

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or acting at high speed.

examples.text: 这辆车开得真快。
examples.translation: This car is going really fast.

senses.definition: Happening in a very short time from now; about to.

examples.text: 快要下雨了，我们赶紧回家吧。
examples.translation: It is about to rain; let's hurry home.

senses.definition: Of a blade or tool: having a keen edge that cuts easily.

examples.text: 这把刀很快，切菜很容易。
examples.translation: This knife is very sharp, so cutting vegetables is easy.

faults.quote: The day after today. | glosses en: tomorrow
faults.why: Includes adverbial sense 'tomorrow' in a feminine noun entry ('la mañana').

notes: Takes 'por' to mean 'in the morning' ('por la mañana') and 'de' after a clock time ('las ocho de la mañana').
Without an article, 'mañana' is an adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; 'mañana por la mañana' means 'tomorrow morning'.

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: Me gusta tomar café por la mañana.
examples.translation: I like to have coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: Aunque termina en -o, 'mano' es un sustantivo femenino
faults.why: Note is written in Spanish instead of English.

notes: Feminine despite ending in '-o' ('la mano', 'las manos', 'una mano fría').

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the palm and fingers.

examples.text: Levanta la mano si tienes una pregunta.
examples.translation: Raise your hand if you have a question.

senses.definition: Help or assistance, especially in expressions such as 'echar una mano'.

examples.text: ¿Me puedes echar una mano con estas cajas?
examples.translation: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

senses.definition: A single layer of paint or varnish applied to a surface.

examples.text: La pared necesita otra mano de pintura.
examples.translation: The wall needs another coat of paint.

faults.quote: Use 'manta' for any thick fabric covering meant to keep you warm
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Distinguish from 'la sábana' (thin bed sheet) and 'el edredón' (duvet or comforter).

senses.definition: A thick cover made of wool or other warm fabric, used on a bed or sofa.

examples.text: Hace mucho frío, necesito otra manta para dormir.
examples.translation: It's very cold; I need another blanket to sleep.

faults.quote: Used commonly as a spread for bread or toast and in cooking.
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler explaining obvious real-world concepts and non-existent slang confusions.

senses.definition: A solid yellow dairy fat made from cream, used for spreading on bread and in cooking.

examples.text: Prefiero el pan tostado con mantequilla.
examples.translation: I prefer toast with butter.

faults.quote: In Spain and across Latin America, 'manzana' means both the fruit
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

senses.definition: The round fruit of the apple tree, with crisp flesh and red, green, or yellow skin.

examples.text: Me gusta comer una manzana verde por la mañana.
examples.translation: I like to eat a green apple in the morning.

senses.definition: An area of buildings surrounded by four streets in a town or city.

examples.text: La panadería está a solo una manzana de aquí.
examples.translation: The bakery is just one block away from here.

faults.quote: or when speaking to someone informally (singular 'sen').
faults.why: Worded as 'or' (either/or) instead of 'and'; also missing the plural/formal form 'hoşça kalın'.

notes: Said by the person leaving when speaking to one person informally ('sen'). For multiple people or to be polite ('siz'), say 'hoşça kalın'.
The person staying behind replies with 'güle güle'.

senses.definition: Used to say goodbye to someone when you are the one leaving.

examples.text: Hoşça kal, yarın görüşürüz.
examples.translation: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of one meaning; example 1 is a calque ('quick coffee').

faults.quote: Used both for physical speed (people, cars) and abstract speed
faults.why: States the obvious that works the same way in English.

notes: Can also be used as an adverb meaning 'quickly' or 'fast' without changing form (e.g. 'hızlı koşmak' — to run fast).

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or done at high speed or in a short time.

examples.text: Bu hızlı trenle iki saatte şehre varabiliriz.
examples.translation: We can reach the city in two hours on this high-speed train.

examples.text: İnternet bağlantımız bugün çok hızlı.
examples.translation: Our internet connection is very fast today.

faults.quote: In Turkish, içmek is used for both drinking liquids and smoking
faults.why: Both notes state the obvious or repeat the senses; missing mention of 'çorba içmek' (soup).

notes: In Turkish, soup and medicine are also 'drunk' with 'içmek': 'çorba içmek' (to have soup), 'ilaç içmek' (to take medicine).

senses.definition: To take a liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.text: Yemekten sonra soğuk bir limonata içmek istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to drink a cold lemonade after dinner.

senses.definition: To inhale smoke from a cigarette, pipe, or similar.

examples.text: Babam kahveden sonra dışarıda sigara içiyor.
examples.translation: My father is smoking a cigarette outside after coffee.

faults.quote: The person who is in need takes the dative case (-e/-a) while
faults.why: Completely backwards: the thing needed takes the dative (-e/-a), and the person takes possessive/genitive.

faults.quote: Yeni bir arabaya ihtiyacım var.
faults.why: Uses 'ihtiyacı var' instead of the headword verb 'ihtiyacı olmak' in both examples.
Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning; sense 1 is artificial filler.

faults.quote: /içtiyɑʤɯ olmɑk/
faults.why: Uses non-IPA symbol 'y' instead of /j/.

notes: 'İhtiyaç' takes a possessive suffix for the person who needs, and the thing needed takes the dative case (-e/-a). In the present tense, 'olmak' is usually replaced by 'var' (or 'yok' in the negative): 'Suya ihtiyacım var' (I need water).

senses.definition: To require something or someone.

examples.text: Yardıma ihtiyacın olursa bana haber ver.
examples.translation: Let me know if you need help.

examples.text: Bu işi bitirmek için zamana ihtiyacımız olacak.
examples.translation: We will need time to finish this job.

faults.quote: İlaç is a general word for both medicine and medication, whether
faults.why: Repeats the definition and gloss; misses the useful collocation 'ilaç içmek/almak' and consonant voicing.

faults.quote: A chemical substance used to treat plants against pests or diseases.
faults.why: Agricultural sense ('pesticide') is not priority for an A2 beginner, and mismatches 'shortGloss' ('remedy').

notes: Before a suffix starting with a vowel, the final 'ç' changes to 'c': 'ilacı' (the medicine).
In Turkish, you normally say 'ilaç içmek' (literally 'to drink medicine') or 'ilaç almak' for taking medicine, even for pills.

senses.definition: A substance, such as a pill, liquid, or cream, used to treat an illness or injury.

examples.text: Yemekten sonra bu ilacı içmen gerekiyor.
examples.translation: You need to take this medicine after the meal.

faults.quote: Asciutto is the general word for something not wet.
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding grammar, usage, or contrast information.

faults.quote: lean, skinny
faults.why: 'Skinny' has a negative connotation that 'asciutto' (fit/lean) lacks.

notes: For dry wine or very dry weather and climates, use secco instead of asciutto.

senses.definition: Not wet; free from moisture or liquid.

examples.text: Dopo la pioggia, il sentiero è finalmente asciutto.
examples.translation: After the rain, the path is finally dry.

senses.definition: Of a person or body: thin and fit, with little body fat.

examples.text: È un corridore molto asciutto e veloce.
examples.translation: He is a very lean and fast runner.

faults.quote: To pay attention to a specific noise or sound in one's environment.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are identical in meaning; listening to a sound is already in sense 0.
Should note that 'ascoltare' takes a direct object without a preposition (unlike English 'listen to').

notes: Do not confuse with sentire, which simply means to hear a sound without actively paying attention.
Takes a direct object without a preposition: ascoltare la musica (to listen to music).

senses.definition: To pay attention to someone speaking or to a sound.

examples.text: Mi piace ascoltare la musica la sera.
examples.translation: I like to listen to music in the evening.

examples.text: Ascolta quel rumore strano nel giardino.
examples.translation: Listen to that strange noise in the garden.

senses.definition: To take someone's advice or heed what they say.

examples.text: Perché non ascolti mai i miei consigli?
examples.translation: Why do you never listen to my advice?

faults.quote: To remain somewhere until an event occurs.
faults.why: Waiting for someone/something and waiting until something happens are the same sense.
Sense 2 ('expect') requires the reflexive form 'aspettarsi', which is not explained.

notes: Takes a direct object without a preposition: aspettare il treno (to wait for the train), not aspettare per.
In the sense 'to expect', it is usually reflexive (aspettarsi): non me lo aspettavo (I didn't expect it). Do not confuse with sperare (to hope).

senses.definition: To stay in one place or delay action until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: Ti aspetto davanti alla stazione.
examples.translation: I'll wait for you in front of the station.

examples.text: Aspettiamo che finisca la pioggia prima di uscire.
examples.translation: Let's wait until the rain stops before going out.

senses.definition: (usually reflexive, aspettarsi) To believe or anticipate that something will happen.

examples.text: Non mi aspettavo una risposta così gentile.
examples.translation: I wasn't expecting such a kind reply.

faults.quote: Use assaggiare when you want to try the flavour of food
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of sense 0.

faults.quote: To experience something for the first time in a small way.
faults.why: Figurative sense is transparent and not essential as a separate sense for an A2 learner.

notes: Use assaggiare only for food and drink. Do not confuse it with provare, which is used for trying on clothes or trying out activities, or sapere di (to taste of).

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to try its flavour.

examples.text: Vuoi assaggiare questa pasta?
examples.translation: Do you want to try this pasta?

notes: Weak noun (N-declension): takes '-n' in all singular and plural forms except the nominative singular ('den/dem/des Löwen', plural 'die Löwen').

senses.definition: A large wild cat that lives mainly in Africa, with a mane on the male.

examples.text: Der Löwe ist der König der Tiere.
examples.translation: The lion is the king of the beasts.

faults.quote: (belly) The region of the body often referred to as the belly
faults.why: 'Magen' means the stomach (organ), not the belly region ('Bauch').

notes: Refers specifically to the internal organ where food goes. For the belly or abdomen in general, use 'der Bauch' ('Mir tut der Bauch weh').
Plural: 'die Mägen'.

senses.definition: The organ inside the body where food goes and is digested after being eaten.

examples.text: Mein Magen knurrt, weil ich Hunger habe.
examples.translation: My stomach is growling because I am hungry.

faults.why: Missing irregular plural 'die Männer', which is essential for an A2 learner.

notes: Irregular plural: 'die Männer'.
With a possessive ('mein Mann', 'ihr Mann'), it means 'husband'. For an unmarried partner, use 'der Freund' (boyfriend).

senses.definition: An adult male person.

examples.text: Der Mann wartet an der Haltestelle.
examples.translation: The man is waiting at the bus stop.

senses.definition: The man that someone is married to.

examples.text: Sie geht mit ihrem Mann ins Kino.
examples.translation: She is going to the cinema with her husband.

faults.quote: (technical) The outer surface, shell, or protective covering of an object
faults.why: Technical sense 'casing/sheath' is not everyday vocabulary for an A2 learner.

faults.quote: coat; cloak; casing
faults.why: 'cloak' is not in the senses, and 'casing' is a marginal technical sense.

notes: Plural: 'die Mäntel'.
'Mantel' is a long coat reaching below the hips. A shorter coat or jacket is 'die Jacke'.

senses.definition: A long warm piece of clothing worn outdoors over other clothes to protect against cold or rain.

examples.text: Im Winter trage ich immer meinen warmen Mantel.
examples.translation: In winter I always wear my warm coat.

faults.quote: While 'Markt' is used for the physical location, it also refers
faults.why: Notes restate the senses and explain a different word ('Marktplatz') while omitting plural and prepositions.

notes: Plural: 'die Märkte'.
Often used with 'auf': 'auf den Markt gehen' (to go to the market), 'auf dem Markt kaufen' (to buy at the market).

senses.definition: An outdoor place or event with stalls where people buy and sell food and other goods.

examples.text: Wir kaufen unser frisches Gemüse auf dem Markt.
examples.translation: We buy our fresh vegetables at the market.

senses.definition: The business or system of buying and selling goods, or the demand for them.

examples.text: Dieses neue Produkt hat den Markt verändert.
examples.translation: This new product has changed the market.

faults.quote: /aˈma/
faults.why: Conjunction 'ama' has initial stress: /ˈa.ma/.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'ama' is a conjunction, not an expression.

faults.quote: Use "ama" to connect two contrasting thoughts, just like "but" in English.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition and gloss without adding usage or grammar info.

notes: The stress is on the first syllable (/ˈa.ma/).
More common in everyday speech than its synonyms 'fakat' and 'lakin'.

senses.definition: Used to introduce a contrasting statement or exception.

examples.text: Hava güzel ama biraz soğuk.
examples.translation: The weather is nice, but a little cold.

faults.quote: İhtiyar amca karşıdan karşıya geçmek için yardım istedi.
faults.why: Sense 1 defines a term of address, so the example should show direct address.

notes: Used specifically for your father's brother; your mother's brother is 'dayı'.
Placed after a first name as a respectful title for an older man (e.g., Ahmet Amca), or used alone to address an older male stranger.

senses.definition: The brother of one's father.

examples.text: Yarın amcam bizi ziyarete gelecek.
examples.translation: Tomorrow my uncle is coming to visit us.

senses.definition: A respectful or affectionate term used to refer to or address an older man who is not a relative.

examples.text: Ahmet Amca, sana yardım edeyim mi?
examples.translation: Uncle Ahmet, shall I help you?

faults.quote: /a.naːhˈtaɾ/
faults.why: The second 'a' in 'anahtar' is short: /a.nahˈtaɾ/.

faults.quote: A small device for turning an electrical circuit on or off.
faults.why: 'anahtar' for light switch is technical; everyday speech uses 'düğme', making the example unnatural.

faults.quote: Used for door keys, mechanical wrenches, and electrical switches alike.
faults.why: merely repeats the senses.

notes: Also used figuratively for a solution or answer Key (e.g., 'cevap anahtarı' — answer key).

senses.definition: A small metal object that opens or closes a lock.

examples.text: Evimin anahtarını masanın üzerinde unuttum.
examples.translation: I forgot my house key on the table.

senses.definition: A metal tool used for gripping and turning nuts and bolts.

examples.text: Musluğu tamir etmek için bir İngiliz anahtarı gerekiyor.
examples.translation: A monkey wrench is needed to fix the faucet.

faults.quote: To know what a particular word, sign, or symbol means.
faults.why: Understanding what a word means is the exact same sense as understanding speech or writing.

faults.quote: Use 'anlamak' for both understanding a person's words and grasping a concept.
faults.why: Both notes are filler; they miss key grammar like the irregular stem narrowing (anlıyor).

notes: The final vowel of the stem 'anla-' narrows to 'ı' before '-yor': 'anlıyorum' (I understand).
With the ablative case (-den/-dan), it means to know a lot about or have a knack for something (e.g., 'müzikten anlamak').

senses.definition: To grasp the meaning of words, a language, a person, or a concept.

examples.text: Seni çok iyi anlıyorum.
examples.translation: I understand you very well.

senses.definition: To become aware of a fact or situation.

examples.text: Geç kaldığımı yeni anladım.
examples.translation: I just realized I am late.

faults.quote: Anlatmak is used both when telling a story and when explaining how
faults.why: Restates the two senses without adding helpful usage information.

notes: Do not confuse with 'söylemek', which is used for saying a short piece of information (e.g., telling the time or one's name); 'anlatmak' is for stories, events, or explanations.

senses.definition: To give an account of a story, event, or experience in words.

examples.text: Bana bu hikâyeyi baştan anlat.
examples.translation: Tell me this story from the beginning.

senses.definition: To make a subject or idea clear and easy to understand.

senses.definition: A written or printed message sent to someone in an envelope by post.

examples.text: Dostałem dzisiaj list od mojej babci.
examples.translation: I received a letter from my grandmother today.

faults.quote: Don't confuse this with 'lod', which is not a Polish word.
faults.why: Useless filler warning against a non-existent word.

notes: In the singular ('lód') it means frozen water; in the plural ('lody') it means 'ice cream'.
The 'ó' changes to 'o' in declined forms: lodu (of ice), lody (ice cream).

senses.definition: Water that has frozen solid.

examples.text: Na jeziorze jest cienki lód.
examples.translation: There is thin ice on the lake.

senses.definition: (usually plural: lody) A sweet frozen dessert made from cream or milk.

examples.text: Latem często jemy lody.
examples.translation: We often eat ice cream in the summer.

faults.quote: This is the standard, everyday word for a refrigerator in Poland.
faults.why: Pure filler that adds nothing to the gloss and register field.

notes: Related to 'lód' (ice). A freezer is 'zamrażarka'.

senses.definition: A kitchen appliance that keeps food and drinks cold.

examples.text: Włóż mleko do lodówki.
examples.translation: Put the milk in the fridge.

faults.quote: stone; rock
faults.why: Missing 'brick' (sense 1), whereas 'rock' is not in the glosses.

faults.quote: Hard solid non-metallic mineral matter of which rock is made, used for building.
faults.why: Overly technical definition; in Dutch 'steen' in construction also means a baked clay brick.

faults.quote: Used for both small pebbles and larger rocks, as well as the building material.
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage information.

notes: Plural: 'stenen'. As an uncountable material ('van steen'), it refers to either natural stone or brick.

senses.definition: A hard piece of rock found on the ground.

examples.text: Hij schopte tegen een steen op de weg.
examples.translation: He kicked a stone on the road.

senses.definition: A hard block of baked clay or natural rock, or this material in general, used for building.

examples.text: Het huis is gebouwd van rode steen.
examples.translation: The house is built of red brick.

faults.quote: In Dutch, just like in English, this word refers to both the
faults.why: Pure filler that merely repeats the two senses given below.
Missing the everyday sense of a star shape or rating symbol (e.g. a four-star hotel).

notes: Plural: 'sterren', diminutive: 'sterretje' (also used for an asterisk '*' or a sparkler).

senses.definition: A bright point of light in the night sky that is a large ball of burning gas.

examples.text: De sterren schijnen fel vannacht.
examples.translation: The stars are shining brightly tonight.

senses.definition: A shape or symbol with five or more points, often used to rate the quality of hotels, restaurants, or films.

examples.text: We slapen in een hotel met vier sterren.
examples.translation: We are sleeping in a four-star hotel.

senses.definition: A very famous or talented person in entertainment or sports.

examples.text: Zij is een grote ster in de muziekwereld.
examples.translation: She is a big star in the music world.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'kruk', which is a stool without a
faults.why: Wait: 'stoel' is a false friend with English 'stool', which is the real reason learners confuse them.

notes: False friend: despite looking like English 'stool', 'stoel' means a chair with a back. A stool without a back is 'de kruk'.

senses.definition: A seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.

examples.text: Ik zit op een comfortabele stoel.
examples.translation: I am sitting on a comfortable chair.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'onwear', which specifically refers to a thunderstorm
faults.why: The Dutch word for thunderstorm is 'onweer', misspelled here as 'onwear'.

faults.quote: Use 'storm' when there is strong, disruptive weather with heavy winds and
faults.why: Restates sense 0's definition without adding anything new.

notes: In Dutch, 'storm' focuses on very strong wind; for a thunderstorm with lightning and thunder, use 'het onweer'.

senses.definition: A period of very bad weather with strong winds and often rain.

examples.text: De storm veroorzaakte veel schade aan de daken.
examples.translation: The storm caused a lot of damage to the roofs.

senses.definition: A sudden, strong reaction or outburst from a large number of people.

examples.text: Er ontstond een storm van kritiek op het nieuwe plan.
examples.translation: A storm of criticism arose over the new plan.

faults.quote: The surface of the road or the outdoor area outside.
faults.why: 'Op straat' (in/on the street, outdoors) is a prepositional usage of the same sense, not a distinct meaning.

faults.quote: street; road
faults.why: 'road' is not in the glosses, and the note explicitly contrasts 'straat' with 'weg' (road).

notes: Refers to a paved road in a town or city with buildings; use 'de weg' for a general road or highway between places.
Notice the prepositions: 'in een straat' (living in a street), 'op straat' (out in the street, outdoors).

senses.definition: A public road in a city, town, or village, usually with houses or other buildings on one or both sides.

examples.text: Zij woont in een rustige straat.
examples.translation: She lives on a quiet street.

examples.text: De kinderen spelen buiten op straat.
examples.translation: The children are playing outside in the street.

faults.quote: 있다 is one of the most common verbs in Korean.
faults.why: Filler restating the senses; misses the opposite 없다 and honorific 계시다/있으시다.
Splits 'to stay, remain' (a verb taking 눈/고 and 에) into sense 0 instead of giving its own sense.

corrected.shortGloss: to be; to exist; to have; to stay
notes: The opposite of 있다 is 없다 (to not exist; to not have). Its honorific form is 계시다 for a person's location or existence, and 있으시다 for possession.
To say someone has something, mark the item with 이/가 (not 을/를): 시간이 있다 (to have time).
In the meaning 'to stay', 있다 behaves as an action verb (e.g. 집에 있는다); in other meanings it behaves like an adjective in the plain present tense (있다).

senses.definition: To exist or be present in a place.

examples.text: 교실에 학생이 있어요.
examples.translation: There are students in the classroom.

senses.definition: To have or possess something.

examples.text: 질문이 있습니다.
examples.translation: I have a question.

senses.definition: To remain or stay in a place for a period of time.

examples.text: 주말에는 집에 있을 거예요.
examples.translation: I will stay at home on the weekend.

faults.quote: to take away; to bring
faults.why: 'To bring' is 가져오다, the opposite of 가져가다; including it misleads the learner.

faults.quote: 가방을 가져가다.
faults.why: Bare infinitive phrase rather than a natural sentence, and redundant with example 0.

corrected.shortGloss: to take (with one); to take away
notes: Use 가져가다 (take) when moving something away from the current location, and 가져오다 (bring) when moving it toward the current location.
Do not confuse with 가지다 (to have, to hold), which does not express movement to another place.

senses.definition: To take or carry something with oneself away from the current place to another.

examples.text: 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요.
examples.translation: It is raining, so please take an umbrella with you.

notes: Compound verb from 전화 (telephone, phone call) + 하다 (to do); also used in the separated form 전화를 하다.
Mark the person being called with -에게, -한테 (colloquial), or -께 (honorific): 친구한테 전화해요 (I'm calling my friend).

senses.definition: To call someone on the telephone.

examples.text: 어머니께 전화해요.
examples.translation: I am calling my mother.

faults.quote: Do not use 짓다 for abstract 'making' like 'making a mistake'
faults.why: False: 짓다 IS used for abstract things like 죄를 짓다 (commit a sin/crime), 이름을 짓다 (name), 표정을 짓다.
Missing the crucial ㅅ-irregular conjugation note (짓다 → 지어요, 지었다).

faults.quote: He made a smile / He smiled.
faults.why: Includes an unnatural calque ('He made a smile') and a slash alternative.

corrected.shortGloss: to build; to cook (rice); to make
notes: ㅅ-irregular verb: the final ㅅ drops before a vowel (짓다 → 지어요, 지었습니다, 지은).
Unlike 만들다 (to make in general), 짓다 is used with specific nouns: 집을 짓다 (build a house), 밥을 짓다 (cook rice), 이름을 짓다 (give a name), 미소를 짓다 (smile), 죄를 짓다 (commit a sin).

senses.definition: To build a house, building, or nest.

examples.text: 그들은 새로운 집을 짓고 있어요.
examples.translation: They are building a new house.

senses.definition: To cook rice or prepare herbal medicine.

examples.text: 어머니께서 밥을 짓고 계십니다.
examples.translation: My mother is cooking rice.

senses.definition: To form a facial expression, come up with a name, or compose poetry.

examples.text: 그는 밝은 미소를 지었다.
examples.translation: He gave a bright smile.

faults.quote: 열다 is used both for physical objects like doors and windows, and
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the ㄹ-irregular conjugation (열다 → 엽니다, 여세요).

notes: ㄹ-irregular verb: the final ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, and ㅅ (열다 → 엽니다, 여세요, 여는).
Do not confuse with 켜다, which means 'to turn on' a light, appliance, or electronic device.

senses.definition: To move a door, window, lid, or container so that it is no longer closed.

examples.text: 더워서 창문을 열었습니다.
examples.translation: It was hot, so I opened the window.

senses.definition: To hold or host an event, meeting, or festival, or to start a business or account.

examples.text: 다음 주에 회의를 엽니다.
examples.translation: We are holding a meeting next week.

faults.quote: In Dutch, nouns like 'bed' are neuter, so use the article 'het'.
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already shown in the headword.

notes: The plural is 'bedden'. In phrases like 'naar bed gaan' (to go to bed) and 'in bed liggen' (to lie in bed), no article is used.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture that you sleep on.

examples.text: Ik lig lekker in mijn bed.
examples.translation: I am lying comfortably in my bed.

faults.quote: In Dutch, 'het been' can refer both to the limb used
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the two distinct plurals ('benen' vs 'beenderen').

faults.quote: with 'de been', which does not exist in standard Dutch
faults.why: Filler gender note, and false in idioms like 'op de been zijn'.

notes: The plural is 'benen' for legs, and 'beenderen' for bones of the skeleton.
For a single bone (especially in food or for a dog), 'het bot' is much more common in everyday speech than 'het been'.
Used for human legs (and horses); for most other animals, use 'de poot'.

senses.definition: One of the limbs of the body that a person uses for standing and walking.

examples.text: Ik heb pijn in mijn been na het hardlopen.
examples.translation: My leg hurts after running.

senses.definition: One of the hard parts that make up the skeleton inside the body, or the material they are made of.

examples.text: De arts zag een breuk in het been.
examples.translation: The doctor saw a fracture in the bone.

faults.quote: Takes the neuter article 'het': het bier.
faults.why: Restates the gender and article already in the headword.

faults.quote: Hij bestelde een koud bier op het terras.
faults.why: To order a glass of beer, Dutch speakers normally use the diminutive 'een biertje'.

notes: 'Bier' is usually uncountable for the drink in general. To order or talk about a glass or bottle of beer, use the diminutive 'het biertje' (plural 'biertjes').

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from grain, water, hops, and yeast.

examples.text: Drink je liever wijn of bier bij het eten?
examples.translation: Do you prefer to drink wine or beer with your meal?

faults.quote: In de herfst vallen alle gele en rode bladeren van de bomen.
faults.why: The plural of 'blad' has a long vowel: 'bladeren' /ˈblaːdərə(n)/ and 'bladen' /ˈblaːdə(n)/.

notes: The plural is 'bladeren' (or 'blâren') for plant leaves, and 'bladen' for sheets of paper or magazines. In both plurals the 'a' is pronounced long (/aː/).

senses.definition: A flat green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch.

examples.text: In de herfst vallen alle gele en rode bladeren van de bomen.
examples.translation: In autumn, all the yellow and red leaves fall from the trees.

senses.definition: A flat, thin piece of paper.

examples.text: Pak een schoon blad papier om op te schrijven.
examples.translation: Take a clean sheet of paper to write on.

senses.definition: A thin book with a paper cover, published every week or month, with articles and pictures.

examples.text: Ze leest elke week een interessant blad in de trein.
examples.translation: She reads an interesting magazine on the train every week.

faults.quote: from the shoulder down to the fingertips. It is also used as
faults.why: แขน ends at the wrist (not fingertips) and is not a classifier for sleeves.

notes: The classifier for arms and sleeves is ข้าง (for one) or คู่ (for a pair).

senses.definition: The upper limb of the human body from the shoulder to the wrist.

examples.text: เขายกแขนขึ้น
examples.translation: He raised his arm.

senses.definition: The part of a garment that covers the arm.

examples.text: เสื้อตัวนี้แขนยาว
examples.translation: This shirt has long sleeves.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'turn' (e.g. my turn,ตาฉัน).

faults.quote: The word 'ตา' is a prime example of a homonym in Thai.
faults.why: Filler note stating the obvious fact that the word has multiple meanings.

notes: For 'grandfather', ตา specifically means the mother's father; the father's father is ปู่. It is also used as a polite pronoun or title for any older man of that age.
The classifier for eyes is ข้าง (one eye) or คู่ (a pair of eyes); in formal contexts ดวง is also used.

senses.definition: The organ of the body used for seeing.

examples.text: เธอมีตาสีน้ำตาล
examples.translation: She has brown eyes.

senses.definition: The father of one's mother, or a polite term of address for an elderly man.

examples.text: วันหยุดนี้ฉันจะไปเยี่ยมตากับยาย
examples.translation: This holiday I will go visit my maternal grandparents.

senses.definition: An opportunity or time to do something in a sequence, such as in a game.

examples.text: ต่อไปเป็นตาคุณ
examples.translation: Next is your turn.

faults.quote: Let's go eat a meal.
faults.why: Unnatural English calque; 'Let's go eat' or 'Let's go have a meal' is natural.

notes: กินข้าวหรือยัง ('Have you eaten rice yet?') is a very common everyday greeting, similar to 'How are you?' or 'Have you eaten?'.

senses.definition: The white or brown grains of a grass plant, cooked and eaten as a staple food.

examples.text: ฉันชอบกินข้าวหอมมะลิ
examples.translation: I like eating jasmine rice.

senses.definition: Food in general, or a meal.

examples.text: ไปกินข้าวกันเถอะ
examples.translation: Let's go have a meal.

faults.quote: Use 'งาน' broadly for any kind of task or duty, including professional
faults.why: Notes [0] and [1] merely restate the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Commonly used with ทำ in ทำงาน ('to work'). Do not confuse with อาชีพ, which specifically means a career or profession.

senses.definition: A task or activity that you do, or regular paid employment.

examples.text: วันนี้ฉันมีงานต้องทำเยอะ
examples.translation: Today I have a lot of work to do.

senses.definition: An organized social occasion, ceremony, or celebration.

examples.text: ไปงานเลี้ยงวันเกิดกันเถอะ
examples.translation: Let's go to the birthday party.

corrected.headword: ฤดูใบไม้ผลิ
notes: Literally means 'season of budding leaves'. Because Thailand has a tropical climate (with hot, rainy, and cool seasons), this word is used when talking about countries with temperate climates.

senses.definition: The season after winter and before summer, when temperatures rise and plants begin to grow.

examples.text: ฤดูใบไม้ผลิเป็นช่วงเวลาที่อากาศอบอุ่นขึ้นและดอกไม้เริ่มบาน
examples.translation: Spring is the time when the weather gets warmer and flowers start to bloom.
examples.matchedForm: ฤดูใบไม้ผลิ

faults.why: Missing irregular stem-changing conjugation (e > ie: me despierto).

faults.quote: (awareness) To begin to feel interest or awareness about something.
faults.why: Figurative sense of a feeling awakening is not needed at A2; keep entry focused.

notes: Stem-changing verb (e > ie) in stressed syllables: me despierto, te despiertas.
Use reflexive 'despertarse' when waking up on your own, and 'despertar' (without 'se') for waking someone else up.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping and become awake.

examples.text: Siempre me despierto muy temprano los lunes.
examples.translation: I always wake up very early on Mondays.

faults.quote: (shape) To trace or outline a shape, figure, or path
faults.why: Drawing a circle on a board is the same everyday meaning as drawing a picture.

notes: Do not confuse with 'pintar' (to paint or color with paints).

senses.definition: To make a picture, shape, or design with a pencil, pen, or chalk.

examples.text: Me gusta dibujar animales en mi cuaderno.
examples.translation: I like to draw animals in my notebook.

examples.text: El profesor dibujó un círculo en la pizarra.
examples.translation: The teacher drew a circle on the board.

faults.quote: /diˈfi.sil/
faults.why: Castilian Spanish (es-ES) uses /θ/ for 'c' before 'i', not /s/: /diˈfi.θil/.

faults.quote: Used for tasks, situations, and problems that require effort or skill.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving grammar information like invariant gender form.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine singular (un examen difícil, una pregunta difícil); plural is 'difíciles'.
Do not confuse with 'duro', which refers to physical hardness (una piedra dura) or toughness.

senses.definition: Needing much effort, skill, or understanding to do, deal with, or understand.

examples.text: Este ejercicio de gramática es muy difícil para mí.
examples.translation: This grammar exercise is very difficult for me.

examples.text: El jefe nuevo es una persona difícil.
examples.translation: The new boss is a difficult person.

senses.definition: Not likely to happen.

examples.text: Es difícil que llueva hoy.
examples.translation: It's unlikely to rain today.

notes: Usually means 'fun' or 'enjoyable'. For something or someone that makes you laugh ('funny'), 'gracioso' is more specific, though 'divertido' is also used.

senses.definition: Providing enjoyment or entertainment.

examples.text: La fiesta de anoche fue muy divertida.
examples.translation: Last night's party was really fun.

senses.definition: Causing laughter or amusement.

examples.text: Tu hermano es muy divertido, siempre cuenta chistes.
examples.translation: Your brother is very funny; he always tells jokes.

faults.quote: to hurt; to ache; to care about
faults.why: 'To care about' is not covered in the senses and is misleading.

faults.quote: hurt, pain, regret
faults.why: With 'doler', the thing causes pain ('to hurt'); the subject does not 'regret'.
Should explicitly note the o > ue stem change and plural form 'duelen'.

notes: Stem-changing verb (o > ue). Used like 'gustar' with indirect object pronouns: 'me duele la cabeza' (singular) vs. 'me duelen los pies' (plural).

senses.definition: To cause physical pain in a part of the body.

examples.text: Me duele la cabeza después de trabajar todo el día.
examples.translation: My head hurts after working all day.

senses.definition: To cause emotional pain or sadness.

examples.text: Me duele ver a mis amigos sufrir.
examples.translation: It hurts me to see my friends suffer.

faults.quote: To narrate a fictional story, book, or film to an audience.
faults.why: Telling a story is already covered by sense 0 and its example.

faults.quote: or simply the direct object.
faults.why: The person being told is the indirect object, not the direct object.

notes: Takes the person being told as an indirect object or with 'aan' (e.g., 'vertel het mij' or 'vertel het aan mij'), and often takes 'over' for the topic.
Do not confuse with 'zeggen' (to say), which focuses on the words spoken rather than sharing information or a story.

senses.definition: To give information to someone in words, or to relate a story.

examples.text: Kun je mij dat verhaal nog eens vertellen?
examples.translation: Can you tell me that story again?

faults.quote: /vərˈtɛkə(n)/
faults.why: Missing the second /r/ in /vərˈtrɛkə(n)/.

faults.quote: To twist or distort one's face, usually because of pain
faults.why: Distorting one's face is too marginal and idiomatic for an A2 entry.
Should mention irregular forms (vertrok, is vertrokken) and that it is intransitive vs. 'verlaten'.

notes: Irregular verb: vertrok, vertrokken. Takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense ('Ik ben vroeg vertrokken').
'Vertrekken' is used without a direct object ('Ik vertrek om acht uur'). To say you are leaving a specific place or person, use 'verlaten' ('Ik verlaat het gebouw') or 'weggaan bij/uit'.

senses.definition: To leave a place in order to go somewhere else.

examples.text: De trein naar Amsterdam vertrekt over vijf minuten.
examples.translation: The train to Amsterdam leaves in five minutes.

faults.quote: De kinderen zijn verveeld op een regenachtige middag.
faults.why: For 'are bored', Dutch naturally uses 'zich vervelen'; 'verveeld' is mainly used attributively or adverbially.

notes: Most often describes someone's expression, tone, or manner ('een verveelde blik'). To say 'I am bored', Dutch usually uses the reflexive verb 'zich vervelen' ('Ik verveel me').
Do not confuse with 'vervelend', which means 'boring' or 'annoying'.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing impatience and lack of interest because you have nothing to do or something is dull.

examples.text: Hij keek verveeld uit het raam tijdens de lange les.
examples.translation: He looked out the window, bored, during the long lesson.

faults.quote: Vies has two main meanings: physically dirty, and tasting or feeling unpleasant
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses without adding usage information.

notes: Inflected form is 'vieze' (with 'z'): 'een vieze tafel'.
Often stronger and more conversational than 'vuil' (dirty, soiled), carrying a sense of disgust.

senses.definition: Not clean; covered in dirt or stains.

examples.text: Door de regen zijn mijn schoenen erg vies geworden.
examples.translation: Because of the rain, my shoes have become very dirty.

senses.definition: Unpleasant in taste, smell, or feel; causing disgust.

examples.text: Dit drankje smaakt echt heel vies.
examples.translation: This drink tastes really disgusting.

faults.quote: Vinden has two major meanings: physically discovering where something is, and expressing
faults.why: Restates the two senses while omitting irregular forms (vond, gevonden).

notes: Irregular verb: vond, heeft gevonden.

For personal opinions, use 'vinden' rather than 'denken' (which is for facts or suppositions): 'Ik vind deze film leuk' (I think this movie is nice) and 'Wat vind je ervan?' (What do you think of it?).

senses.definition: To discover where someone or something is, either by searching or by chance.

examples.text: Kun jij mijn sleutels vinden?
examples.translation: Can you find my keys?

senses.definition: To have a particular opinion or feeling about someone or something.

examples.text: Wat vind je van dit boek?
examples.translation: What do you think of this book?

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'reich' as a suffix
faults.why: Suffix '-reich' has the exact same meaning as sense 1; misses the preposition 'an'.

notes: In the sense of 'rich in something', it takes 'an' + dative ('reich an Ideen'). Do not confuse with the noun 'das Reich' (empire, realm).

senses.definition: Having a lot of money or property.

examples.text: Er ist sehr reich geworden.
examples.translation: He has become very rich.

senses.definition: Containing a large amount of something.

examples.text: Dieses Land ist reich an Bodenschätzen.
examples.translation: This country is rich in natural resources.

faults.quote: Use 'reisen' when talking about your travels in general
faults.why: Repeats note 0 while omitting the essential auxiliary verb 'sein'.

faults.quote: to travel; to go
faults.why: 'To go' is too broad for 'reisen' and not in the sense glosses.

corrected.shortGloss: to travel; to go on a trip
notes: Forms its perfect tense with 'sein' ('Ich bin nach Italien gereist').
Unlike 'fahren' (going by vehicle), 'reisen' is used for longer journeys or traveling in general ('Ich reise gern').

senses.definition: To go from one place to another, especially over a long distance or on a trip.

examples.text: Wir reisen nächsten Sommer nach Italien.
examples.translation: We are traveling to Italy next summer.

examples.text: Sie reist beruflich viel durch das ganze Land.
examples.translation: She travels a lot for work throughout the whole country.

faults.quote: (competition) To participate in a race or competition of speed.
faults.why: 'Um die Wette rennen' is an idiom; 'rennen' alone just means to run fast.
Must mention irregular stem change (rannte, ist gerannt) and 'sein' auxiliary for A2 learners.

corrected.shortGloss: to run; to sprint; to race
notes: Irregular verb with vowel change, taking 'sein' in the perfect tense: 'rannte', 'ist gerannt'.
In everyday German, 'laufen' is used for both walking and running; use 'rennen' to emphasize running fast or sprinting.

senses.definition: To move very quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: Ich muss zum Bahnhof rennen, sonst verpasse ich den Zug.
examples.translation: I have to run to the station, otherwise I will miss the train.

examples.text: Die Kinder rennen um die Wette.
examples.translation: The children are racing each other.

faults.quote: you will often hear people use 'heile machen'
faults.why: Two long notes about baby talk 'heile machen'; misses unstressed '-ieren' verb grammar.

notes: Like all verbs ending in '-ieren', it forms its past participle without 'ge-': 'repariert'.
