examples.text: Ξέρω να κολυμπάω.
examples.translation: I know how to swim.

faults.quote: πετώ has two very common meanings: moving through the air
faults.why: Restates the two sense definitions without adding usage or grammar information.

faults.quote: To move through the air using wings.
faults.why: Too narrow; also used for airplanes and people traveling by plane.

faults.quote: To send something through the air quickly using your hand.
faults.why: Misses the very common meaning 'to throw away' (rubbish).

corrected.shortGloss: to fly; to throw, to throw away
notes: Also very commonly used in the form πετάω in everyday speech. Simple past (aorist): πέταξα.
Do not confuse with πηδώ / πηδάω ('to jump').

senses.definition: To move or travel through the air (of a bird, aircraft, or passenger).

examples.text: Τα πουλιά πετούν ψηλά στον ουρανό.
examples.translation: The birds fly high in the sky.

senses.definition: To send something through the air with your hand, or to get rid of something as rubbish.

examples.text: Πέταξε την μπάλα στον φίλο του.
examples.translation: He threw the ball to his friend.

examples.text: Μην πετάς τα σκουπίδια κάτω.
examples.translation: Don't throw rubbish on the ground.

faults.quote: To function properly or work, often said of a plan or a machine.
faults.why: Colloquial figurative sense, not for A2; false to say it is used for machines.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical action of walking and metaphorically for machines
faults.why: Restates senses and falsely claims it is used for machines.

notes: Equally common in the uncontracted form περπατάω in everyday speech. Simple past (aorist): περπάτησα.

senses.definition: To move forward on foot at a normal speed.

examples.text: Μ' αρέσει να περπατώ στο πάρκο το πρωί.
examples.translation: I like to walk in the park in the morning.

faults.why: Greek does not distinguish drawing from artistic painting in this verb; splitting is an English projection.

faults.quote: The female artist is painting the landscape in nature.
faults.why: Unnatural English calque ('the female artist', 'in nature').

notes: Covers both drawing (with a pencil or pen) and artistic painting (on a canvas). For painting a wall, house, or object a single colour, use βάφω instead.

senses.definition: To make a picture using pencils, pens, or paint.

examples.text: Το παιδί ζωγραφίζει ένα σπίτι με το μολύβι του.
examples.translation: The child is drawing a house with his pencil.

examples.text: Της αρέσει να ζωγραφίζει τοπία.
examples.translation: She likes painting landscapes.

faults.quote: To spend the night at a place other than your own home.
faults.why: Not a distinct sense of the verb; just 'to sleep' used with a location.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'μένω' (to stay/live)
faults.why: Learners have no reason to confuse 'κοιμάμαι' with 'μένω'.

notes: Passive in form, but active in meaning. Imperfect: κοιμόμουν; simple past (aorist): κοιμήθηκα (which can mean either 'I slept' or 'I fell asleep').

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed in a natural state of unconsciousness, or to fall into this state.

examples.text: Κοιμάμαι πάντα νωρίς τα βράδια.
examples.translation: I always go to sleep early at night.

examples.text: Θα κοιμηθώ στο σπίτι του φίλου μου απόψε.
examples.translation: I will sleep at my friend's house tonight.

faults.quote: To rest one's body on the floor or ground.
faults.why: Sitting on furniture and sitting on the floor are the same sense.

faults.quote: Unlike English where 'sit' often implies a chair
faults.why: False claim about English; 'sit' does not imply a chair.

faults.quote: to sit
faults.why: Misses the common transport sense ('to take/ride').

notes: Followed directly by a vehicle (without a preposition) to mean taking that form of transport, as in นั่งรถเมล์ (to take the bus) or นั่งแท็กซี่ (to take a taxi).

senses.definition: To rest with your weight supported on your bottom, or to move into this position.

examples.text: เขานั่งบนเก้าอี้ตัวนั้น
examples.translation: He sat on that chair.

examples.text: พวกเขานั่งบนพื้นเพื่อกินข้าว
examples.translation: They sat on the floor to eat.

senses.definition: To travel as a passenger in or on a vehicle.

examples.text: ฉันนั่งรถเมล์ไปทำงานทุกวัน
examples.translation: I take the bus to work every day.

faults.quote: Use 'เจ็บ' for physical pain (like a headache or a cut).
faults.why: A headache in Thai is ปวดหัว, not เจ็บหัว (which means a sore scalp/head injury).

faults.quote: ฉันเจ็บหัว — I have a headache.
faults.why: Unnatural Thai for a headache; speakers say ปวดหัว.

faults.quote: When talking about emotional pain, 'เจ็บ' is often used to describe hurt
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1.

corrected.shortGloss: to hurt; to feel pain; to be hurt
notes: เจ็บ is used for sharp, surface, or localized pain (such as a cut, wound, or sore throat: เจ็บคอ). Do not confuse it with ปวด, which is used for dull, deep, or aching pain inside the body (such as a headache: ปวดหัว, or stomachache: ปวดท้อง).

senses.definition: To feel or cause physical pain or soreness.

examples.text: วันนี้ฉันเจ็บคอมาก
examples.translation: My throat hurts a lot today.

examples.text: แผลนี้เจ็บมาก
examples.translation: This wound is very painful.

senses.definition: To experience emotional hurt or distress.

examples.text: ฉันเจ็บที่เขาไม่พูดความจริง
examples.translation: I am hurt that he did not tell the truth.

faults.quote: To be obliged or compelled to do something due to circumstances.
faults.why: Literary/formal alone; everyday usage is in compounds like จำใจ or จำเป็น, and example uses จำใจ.

notes: To say you can or cannot remember something, pair it with ได้ or ไม่ได้: จำได้ (can remember) and จำไม่ได้ (cannot remember).
Do not confuse with เตือน, which means to remind someone else.

senses.definition: To keep something in your mind and be able to bring it back into your thoughts.

examples.text: ฉันจำชื่อเขาไม่ได้
examples.translation: I cannot remember his name.

senses.definition: To learn information so that you can repeat or use it from memory.

examples.text: นักเรียนต้องจำคำศัพท์เหล่านี้
examples.translation: The students need to memorize these vocabulary words.

faults.quote: Most specifically refers to an architectural structure spanning a physical obstacle
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammar information.

notes: False friend: do not confuse with English 'most' (in Polish, 'najwięcej' or 'większość').
Takes the ending -u in the genitive singular (mostu) and -em in the locative (na moście).

senses.definition: A structure built over a river, road, or railway so that people or vehicles can cross.

examples.text: Ten most jest bardzo stary.
examples.translation: This bridge is very old.

examples.text: Musimy przejść przez most, żeby dostać się na drugą stronę rzeki.
examples.translation: We have to cross the bridge to get to the other side of the river.

faults.why: Missing the essential A1/A2 sense 'to speak (a foreign language)'.

corrected.shortGloss: to speak; to say; to tell
notes: Imperfective verb. Its main perfective partner is 'powiedzieć' (to say/tell once).
With languages, use 'po' + the -u form (mówić po polsku / po angielsku) or the instrumental case (mówić płynną polszczyzną).
Do not confuse with 'rozmawiać' (to converse, to have a two-way conversation).

senses.definition: To communicate information or thoughts to someone in words.

examples.text: Mów mi wszystko, co wiesz.
examples.translation: Tell me everything you know.

senses.definition: To produce words aloud using one's voice; to talk.

examples.text: Dziecko uczy się mówić.
examples.translation: The child is learning to speak.

senses.definition: To be able to communicate in a particular language.

examples.text: Czy mówisz po angielsku?
examples.translation: Do you speak English?

faults.quote: A form of the verb móc (to be able to)
faults.why: Mixes a conjugated form of the verb 'móc' into the entry for the adverb/particle 'może'.

faults.quote: maybe; perhaps; can
faults.why: 'can' belongs to the verb 'móc', not the adverb 'może'.

notes: Often used in questions or with the future tense to make a polite suggestion (e.g., Może napijesz się kawy? — Would you maybe like some coffee?).
Has the same spelling and pronunciation as the 3rd-person singular form of the verb 'móc' (on/ona może — he/she can).

senses.definition: Used to express uncertainty, possibility, or a polite suggestion.

examples.text: Może jutro pójdziemy do kina.
examples.translation: Maybe we will go to the cinema tomorrow.

examples.text: Może chcesz herbaty?
examples.translation: Would you maybe like some tea?

faults.quote: /ˈmu.zɛ.um/
faults.why: Wrong stress: Polish words ending in -um are stressed on the penultimate syllable (/muˈzɛ.um/).
Fails to mention that 'muzeum' does not decline (stays 'muzeum') in all singular cases.

notes: Like other neuter nouns ending in -um, it does not change its form in the singular (e.g., idę do muzeum, jestem w muzeum), but declines normally in the plural (nominative plural: muzea).

senses.definition: A building where objects of historical, scientific, or artistic interest are kept and shown to the public.

examples.text: W niedzielę idziemy do muzeum sztuki współczesnej.
examples.translation: On Sunday we are going to the museum of contemporary art.

faults.quote: /ˈço.ɾa/
faults.why: Wrong initial consonant: before back vowel /o/, χ is velar /x/, not palatal /ç/.

faults.quote: βορά
faults.why: Misspelled: 'north' in Greek is 'βορρά' (from βορράς), not 'βορά' (which means prey).

faults.quote: (land) A specific area, region, or stretch of land.
faults.why: Poetic/literary shade of 'country'; also misses the everyday island sense 'main town (Chora)'.

faults.quote: While it can mean 'land' in a poetic or literary sense
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Do not confuse with 'το κράτος', which refers specifically to the state as a political and administrative entity.
On Greek islands (usually capitalized as 'η Χώρα'), it refers to the island's capital or main town.

senses.definition: A nation with its own government and borders, or a distant land.

examples.text: Η Ελλάδα είναι μια πανέμορφη χώρα.
examples.translation: Greece is a very beautiful country.

senses.definition: The main town or capital of a Greek island.

examples.text: Το βράδυ θα πάμε βόλτα στη Χώρα του νησιού.
examples.translation: In the evening we will go for a walk in the island's main town.

faults.quote: While ουρά primarily means an animal's tail, it is very commonly used
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a note giving common collocations with 'queue' is more helpful.

notes: In the 'queue' sense, common expressions include 'κάνω ουρά' (to queue up) and 'περιμένω στην ουρά' (to wait in line).

senses.definition: A line of people waiting their turn for something.

examples.text: Είχε μεγάλη ουρά στο ταμείο του σουπερμάρκετ.
examples.translation: There was a long queue at the supermarket checkout.

senses.definition: The movable part at the back of an animal's body.

examples.text: Ο σκύλος κουνάει την ουρά του όταν σε βλέπει.
examples.translation: The dog wags its tail when it sees you.

faults.quote: While 'δώρο' usually means a gift or present, in a work context
faults.why: Restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Do not confuse with 'το χάρισμα', which refers to a natural talent or gift, not a physical object.
In Greece, private-sector employees traditionally receive extra holiday payments known as 'το δώρο Χριστουγέννων' (Christmas bonus) and 'το δώρο Πάσχα' (Easter bonus).

senses.definition: Something given to someone as a sign of affection or to celebrate an occasion.

examples.text: Αγόρασα ένα δώρο για τα γενέθλια της φίλης μου.
examples.translation: I bought a gift for my friend's birthday.

senses.definition: An extra payment given to employees for major holidays.

examples.text: Πήρα το δώρο των Χριστουγέννων από τη δουλειά.
examples.translation: I received the Christmas bonus from work.

faults.quote: head; leader; mind
faults.why: Includes 'mind', which is not covered by any of the senses.

faults.quote: Refers to the top part of the human body containing the brain
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Often used figuratively for one's mind or stubbornness, as in 'κάνω του κεφαλιού μου' (to do things one's own way).

senses.definition: The upper part of the body of a person or animal that contains the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.

examples.text: Με πονάει το κεφάλι μου.
examples.translation: My head hurts.

senses.definition: The person in charge of a group or organization.

examples.text: Αυτός είναι το κεφάλι της εταιρείας.
examples.translation: He is the head of the company.

faults.quote: The word 'عَيْن' has multiple common meanings in Arabic, most notably
faults.why: Restates the senses; misses the feminine gender exception and distinct broken plurals.

notes: Feminine despite lacking the '-a' (ة) ending. The plural is عُيُون ('uyūn) or أَعْيُن (a'yun).

senses.definition: The organ of sight in humans and animals.

examples.text: فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
examples.translation: He opened his eyes in the morning.

senses.definition: A natural source of water coming up from the ground.

examples.text: تَجْرِي مِيَاهُ الْعَيْنِ بَيْنَ الصُّخُورِ.
examples.translation: The water of the spring flows between the rocks.

faults.quote: small cups with handles, often used for Arabic coffee
faults.why: Arabic coffee cups (فناجين) characteristically do not have handles.

faults.quote: cup; small container with a handle for hot drinks
faults.why: Includes a full definition in the shortGloss instead of concise translations.

notes: Differs from كُوب (kūb), which is larger and used for water, juice, or mugs. Plural: فَنَاجِين (fanājīn).

senses.definition: A small cup used for serving hot drinks such as coffee or tea.

examples.text: شَرِبْتُ فِنْجَانَ قَهْوَةٍ صَبَاحًا.
examples.translation: I drank a cup of coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: ملأ وِعَاء الشوربة حتي الأافة.
faults.why: Corrupted Arabic spelling: 'حتي الأافة' instead of 'حَتَّى الحَافَّةِ'.
'Container' and 'bowl' are translations of one general concept of a vessel/receptacle in Arabic.

notes: Plural: أَوْعِيَة (aw'iya).

senses.definition: A hollow object, such as a bowl or pot, used for holding food or liquids.

examples.text: وَضَعَ الطَّعَامَ فِي وِعَاءٍ نَظِيفٍ.
examples.translation: He put the food in a clean container.

examples.text: مَلَأَ وِعَاءَ الشُّورْبَةِ حَتَّى الحَافَّةِ.
examples.translation: He filled the soup bowl to the brim.

faults.quote: Used to refer generally to monkeys, especially those with tails
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the common broken plural forms.

notes: Plural: قُرُود (qurūd) or قِرَدَة (qirada).

senses.definition: An intelligent animal that lives in trees and has a long tail, or a large tailless primate.

examples.text: رَأَيْتُ قِرْدًا يَتَسَلَّقُ الشَّجَرَةَ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ.
examples.translation: I saw a monkey climbing the tree in the park.

faults.quote: While 高い (takai) means both 'high' in height and 'expensive' in price
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding usage information.
Needs a note distinguishing the two antonyms: 安い (cheap) and 低い (low).

notes: An i-adjective. Its opposite depends on the meaning: 低い (hikui, low/short) for height, and 安い (yasui, cheap) for price.

senses.definition: Having a large distance from the bottom to the top, or being far above the ground.

examples.text: 富士山はとても高い山です。
examples.translation: Mount Fuji is a very high mountain.

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: この時計は高いです。
examples.translation: This watch is expensive.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (しつれい) for a word written in kanji.

faults.quote: When used as a noun or adjective, it means rude or impolite
faults.why: Restates the gloss without explaining how the na-adjective or noun is used.

notes: Takes な (na) before a noun when used as an adjective (e.g., 失礼な人, a rude person). Also functions as a noun and a する (suru) verb.
In set phrases like 失礼します (shitsurei shimasu), it serves as a polite 'excuse me' when entering or leaving a room, hanging up the phone, or interrupting someone.

senses.definition: Not polite; showing a lack of respect or good manners.

examples.text: 失礼な態度をとらないでください。
examples.translation: Please do not act in a rude manner.

senses.definition: Used as a polite formula when entering or leaving a place, ending a call, or interrupting someone.

examples.text: それでは、失礼します。
examples.translation: Well then, excuse me (I'll be leaving now).

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (はやい) for a word written in kanji.

faults.quote: あの車はとても速い。
faults.why: Uses the kanji 速い instead of the headword 早い.

faults.quote: Use 早い when you arrive at a meeting ahead of schedule
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning 'early' instead of giving grammatical or usage help.

notes: 早い mainly refers to an early point in time or something taking little time. For physical speed, the homophone 速い (hayai) is standard, though 早い is often used for both in everyday writing.

senses.definition: Happening or done before the usual or expected time.

examples.text: 明日は朝が早いです。
examples.translation: I have an early morning tomorrow.

senses.definition: Taking very little time, or done at a rapid pace.

examples.text: 母は仕事が早いです。
examples.translation: My mother is quick at her work.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (はずかしい) for a word written in kanji.

faults.quote: Feeling shame because of an action or situation that is socially unacceptable
faults.why: Defines feeling ashamed, whereas the glosses are 'shameful, embarrassing' (causing shame).
No examples provided for a multi-sense word with both subjective and objective uses.

notes: An i-adjective. It can describe both the person feeling embarrassed or shy (私は恥ずかしい, I am embarrassed) and the thing that causes embarrassment or shame (恥ずかしい話, an embarrassing story).

senses.definition: Feeling uncomfortable, self-conscious, or timid in front of others.

examples.text: 人前で歌うのは恥ずかしいです。
examples.translation: I feel embarrassed singing in front of people.

senses.definition: Causing a feeling of shame or embarrassment; disgraceful.

examples.text: そんな恥ずかしいことはしないでください。
examples.translation: Please don't do such a shameful thing.

faults.quote: It is a calm night at the sea, isn't it?
faults.why: 海が静かな modifies 夜: 'a night when the sea is calm', not 'a calm night'.

notes: A na-adjective: use な (na) before a noun (静かな部屋, a quiet room) and に (ni) as an adverb (静かに話す, to speak quietly).
静か describes a lack of noise or commotion. For a person who does not talk much, おとなしい (otonashii) or 無口 (mukuchi) is often used.

senses.definition: Having or making very little sound or noise.

examples.text: 図書館はとても静かです。
examples.translation: The library is very quiet.

senses.definition: Free from rough movement or disturbance; peaceful.

examples.text: 今日の海はとても静かですね。
examples.translation: The sea is very calm today, isn't it?

faults.why: Missing note on irregular conjugation (er läuft, lief, ist gelaufen) and auxiliary 'sein'.

faults.quote: In some regions of Germany, 'laufen' is the standard word for walking,
faults.why: Repeats note [0] and overstates regionality; 'gehen' does not sound formal.

corrected.shortGloss: to run; to walk; to go
notes: Strong verb with vowel change: er läuft, lief, ist gelaufen (takes 'sein' in the perfect tense).
In everyday spoken German, 'laufen' very often means 'to walk' (on foot) as well as 'to run' or 'to jog'.

senses.definition: To move on foot, either at a walking pace or by running.

examples.text: Wir laufen jeden Morgen durch den Park.
examples.translation: We run through the park every morning.

examples.text: Nimmst du den Bus oder läufst du?
examples.translation: Are you taking the bus or walking?

senses.definition: Of a machine, event, or plan: to work, operate, or proceed.

examples.text: Das Projekt läuft sehr gut.
examples.translation: The project is going very well.

senses.definition: Of a film, show, or music: to be playing or showing.

examples.text: Was läuft heute Abend im Kino?
examples.translation: What is on at the cinema tonight?

faults.quote: Use 'laut' when the volume is high, whether it is music,
faults.why: First sentence merely restates the definition.

notes: Opposite of 'leise' (quiet, soft). Can also be used as an adverb ('Sprich bitte lauter' — Speak louder, please).

senses.definition: Making a lot of noise; having a high volume.

examples.text: Die Musik ist zu laut.
examples.translation: The music is too loud.

examples.text: Er ist ein sehr lauter Mensch.
examples.translation: He is a very noisy person.

faults.quote: live, dwell
faults.why: 'Dwell' is archaic/literary in English for a neutral everyday German verb; also in shortGloss.

notes: Use 'leben' for living in a country, city, or general environment ('in Deutschland leben'), and 'wohnen' for a specific residence, street, or address ('in einer Wohnung wohnen').

senses.definition: To be alive; not to be dead.

examples.text: Seine Großeltern leben noch.
examples.translation: His grandparents are still alive.

senses.definition: To have one's home in a particular place or live in a particular way.

examples.text: Ich lebe seit zwei Jahren in Berlin.
examples.translation: I have been living in Berlin for two years.

faults.quote: Use 'lecker' to describe food or drink that tastes good.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful learner information.

notes: Very common in everyday speech; 'köstlich' is a stronger, more formal word for 'delicious'.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a pleasant taste.

examples.text: Das Abendessen war wirklich sehr lecker.
examples.translation: The dinner was really very tasty.

faults.why: Empty container and empty room/street are the same core meaning for A2.

faults.quote: (expression) Without expression or thought.

faults.quote: Used for physical objects that have nothing inside them (a box, a glass)
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the sense definitions.

senses.definition: Having nothing or nobody inside; not filled or occupied.

examples.text: Das Glas ist schon wieder leer.
examples.translation: The glass is already empty again.

examples.text: Die Straßen waren spät am Abend vollkommen leer.
examples.translation: The streets were completely empty late in the evening.

senses.definition: Of a battery: out of power; of a page or screen: with nothing written on it.

examples.text: Mein Handyakku ist fast leer.
examples.translation: My phone battery is almost dead.

faults.quote: The current mood or spirits of a person.

faults.quote: dzisiaj ma złą pogodę ducha.

faults.quote: Pogoda is most commonly used to talk about the state
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage notes.

faults.quote: weather; mood
faults.why: 'Mood' is inaccurate for pogoda.

notes: Usually singular and uncountable. Also appears in the set phrase 'pogoda ducha' (cheerfulness, serenity).

senses.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place, such as sun, rain, or wind.

examples.text: Dzisiaj jest ładna pogoda.
examples.translation: The weather is nice today.

faults.quote: /ˈpu.kuj/

faults.quote: The word 'pokój' is a classic example of a Polish word

senses.definition: A part of a house or building enclosed by walls, floor, and ceiling.

examples.text: Mój pokój jest bardzo jasny.
examples.translation: My room is very bright.

senses.definition: A state in which there is no war or conflict.

examples.text: Wszyscy pragniemy pokoju na świecie.
examples.translation: We all desire peace in the world.

faults.quote: /pɔˈli.t͡ɕant/
faults.why: The sequence 'cj' is pronounced /t͡sj/, not alveolo-palatal /t͡ɕ/.

faults.quote: It is a standard term used in both formal and informal
faults.why: Filler that merely restates the neutral register field.

notes: For a female police officer, use 'policjantka'. The nominative plural for male or mixed groups is 'policjanci'.

senses.definition: A member of the police force whose job is to enforce the law and maintain public order.

examples.text: Policjant zatrzymał samochód do kontroli drogowej.
examples.translation: The police officer stopped the car for a traffic check.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same everyday meaning 'to help'.
Should also mention how to express what one helps with ('w' + locative) or for ('na' + accusative).

notes: Imperfective verb; its perfective pair is 'pomóc'.
Takes the dative case (komu?) for the person helped, and 'w' + locative (w czym?) for the task. For medicine or remedies, use 'na' + accusative (e.g., 'pomagać na ból głowy').

senses.definition: To make it easier for someone to do something, or to improve a situation.

examples.text: Muszę pomagać rodzicom w domu.
examples.translation: I have to help my parents at home.

examples.text: Ta aplikacja pomaga nam lepiej organizować czas.
examples.translation: This app helps us organize our time better.

faults.quote: Unlike English 'take', it often implies grabbing or physically moving something
faults.why: Contradicts itself; 'pakken' is preferred for physical grabbing, while 'nemen' is more abstract.

faults.quote: Ik neem de sleutels van de tafel.
faults.why: In Netherlands Dutch, 'pakken' is normally used for picking up keys from a table.

faults.quote: To accept something that is offered or provided to you.
faults.why: Should cover having food, drink, or medicine, which is how the example uses it.
Needs the irregular principal parts (nam, heeft genomen).

notes: Strong verb: nemen – nam – heeft genomen.
For physically picking up or grabbing an object, Dutch usually prefers 'pakken'. For taking someone or something to a place, use 'brengen' or 'meenemen', not 'nemen'.

senses.definition: To take hold of something or bring it with you.

examples.text: Vergeet niet een paraplu te nemen.
examples.translation: Don't forget to take an umbrella.

senses.definition: To choose, or to use a route or form of transport.

examples.text: Ik neem de trein naar Amsterdam.
examples.translation: I am taking the train to Amsterdam.

senses.definition: To have or accept food, drink, or medicine.

examples.text: Neem jij nog een koekje bij de koffie?
examples.translation: Will you have another cookie with your coffee?

faults.quote: Dit is een heel nieuw idee voor onsteam.
faults.why: Typo: missing space in 'onsteam' ('ons team').

faults.quote: new; fresh; recent
faults.why: 'Fresh' is not in the senses and is normally 'vers' in Dutch.

faults.quote: Use 'nieuw' for things that have just been made, bought, or
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition and basic antonym.

notes: Takes the '-e' ending ('nieuwe') before most nouns, except singular indefinite 'het'-words (een nieuw huis, het nieuwe huis).

senses.definition: Recently made, built, bought, or started, and not used before.

examples.text: Ik heb een nieuwe jas gekocht voor de winter.
examples.translation: I bought a new coat for the winter.

senses.definition: Not known, seen, or experienced before.

examples.text: Dit is een heel nieuw idee voor ons team.
examples.translation: This is a completely new idea for our team.

faults.quote: This is a separable verb, but in many clauses the parts split
faults.why: 'Nodig hebben' is an adjective + verb collocation, not a separable verb, and word order description is backwards.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with just 'hebben' (to have)
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding useful grammatical information.

notes: Conjugate 'hebben' and place 'nodig' near the end of the clause, after the object (Ik heb hulp nodig). Only used with a noun or pronoun, never with 'te' + verb (use 'moeten' or 'hoeven' to say you need to do something).

senses.definition: To require something or someone.

examples.text: Ik heb een nieuwe jas nodig voor de winter.
examples.translation: I need a new coat for the winter.

examples.text: Heb je deze boeken morgen echt nodig?
examples.translation: Do you really need these books tomorrow?

faults.quote: In Dutch, it is very common to use 'nooit' with 'niet'
faults.why: Combining 'nooit' and 'niet' is non-standard in Netherlands Dutch and confuses beginners.

faults.quote: Nooit is the absolute opposite of 'altijd' (always).
faults.why: Obvious filler note.

notes: Often combined with 'nog' as 'nog nooit' (never before / not ever yet) when talking about life experience up to now.

senses.definition: At no time in the past, present, or future.

examples.text: Ik ben nog nooit in Nederland geweest.
examples.translation: I have never been to the Netherlands.

examples.text: Dat zal ik nooit vergeten.
examples.translation: I will never forget that.

faults.quote: Nu weet ik wat ik moet doen.
faults.why: Example shows the temporal sense ('now, at this point'), not the discourse marker 'well then'.

faults.quote: Nu is almost always used to indicate the current moment.
faults.why: Restates the definition without useful usage advice.

notes: In informal spoken Dutch, 'nou' is often used instead of 'nu', especially as a filler word ('Nou, ik weet het niet' – Well, I don't know).
Can also be used as a conjunction meaning 'now that', which sends the verb to the end of the clause (Nu het regent, blijven we binnen).

senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: Ik ben nu bezig met mijn werk.
examples.translation: I am busy with my work right now.

examples.text: Nu weet ik wat ik moet doen.
examples.translation: Now I know what I have to do.

faults.why: Missing the spelling-preserving plural 'gli alberghi' (-go to -ghi).

notes: The plural is 'gli alberghi', adding an 'h' to keep the hard 'g' sound.
Both 'albergo' and 'hotel' are common in Italy; do not confuse with 'ostello' (hostel).

senses.definition: A building where you pay to stay in a room during your travels.

examples.text: L'albergo si trova vicino alla stazione.
examples.translation: The hotel is near the station.

faults.quote: (sailing) A long vertical pole on a sailing ship that supports
faults.why: Nautical 'mast' is too technical and infrequent for an A2 beginner.

faults.quote: (mechanics) A mechanical rod or bar that transmits power in a
faults.why: Mechanical 'shaft/axle' is too technical for an A2 beginner.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'albero' with 'ombra' (shadow/shade), though you will often
faults.why: No learner confuses 'albero' with 'ombra'; pure filler.

notes: Do not confuse with 'albergo' (hotel).

senses.definition: A tall plant with a wooden trunk, branches, and leaves.

examples.text: C'è un grande albero nel giardino.
examples.translation: There is a big tree in the garden.

faults.quote: (romance) A romantic partner or boyfriend.
faults.why: Euphemistic/dated sense; teaching A2 learners 'amico' means 'boyfriend' causes confusion with 'ragazzo'/'fidanzato'.
Missing irregular plural 'gli amici' (and feminine 'le amiche').

notes: The masculine plural is 'gli amici' (with a soft 'c' sound). For a female friend, use 'l'amica' (plural 'le amiche', keeping the hard 'k' sound).
To say 'a friend of mine', put the possessive without an article: 'un mio amico'.

senses.definition: A person you know well and like, who is not a relative.

examples.text: Lui è un mio caro amico.
examples.translation: He is a dear friend of mine.

faults.quote: The plural is 'anatre'.
faults.why: States a completely regular plural (-a to -e) and basic article elision.

senses.definition: A common water bird with webbed feet, a short neck, and a flat beak.

examples.text: Ci sono molte anatre nel laghetto del parco.
examples.translation: There are many ducks in the park pond.

senses.definition: The meat of this bird, eaten as food.

examples.text: Stasera cuciniamo l'anatra all'arancia.
examples.translation: Tonight we are cooking duck a l'orange.

faults.quote: While 'anello' is a ring for your finger, it is also used
faults.why: Note 0 restates the senses; Note 1 contrasts an unrelated word ('orecchini').

notes: The plural is 'gli anelli'. (In poetic or set phrases referring to fingers or hair, the feminine plural 'le anella' also exists.)

senses.definition: A small circle of metal or other material worn on a finger as jewelry.

examples.text: Ha comprato un bellissimo anello d'oro.
examples.translation: She bought a beautiful gold ring.

senses.definition: A circular object or part, such as a keyring or a link in a chain.

examples.text: Ho messo le chiavi su un nuovo anello.
examples.translation: I put the keys on a new ring.

faults.quote: This verb is very versatile. Use it when leaving a house
faults.why: Restates the definitions and glosses without adding grammatical or usage insight.

corrected.shortGloss: to come out; to leave; to turn out
notes: Intransitive; takes the postposition से (se) for the place exited or source.
Differs from जाना (to go) by emphasizing exiting from inside a place or starting a journey.

senses.definition: To come out, emerge, or appear from inside something.

examples.text: बादलों के पीछे से सूरज निकल आया।
examples.translation: The sun came out from behind the clouds.

senses.definition: To leave a place or set out on a journey.

examples.text: मैं अभी घर से निकल रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am leaving the house right now.

senses.definition: To turn out or prove to be a certain way.

examples.text: वह बहुत चालाक निकला।
examples.translation: He turned out to be very clever.

faults.quote: it is often paired with the past participle 'khada'
faults.why: 'खड़ा' (khaṛā) is an adjective, not a past participle, and is already part of the headword.
Should mention that खड़ा inflects for gender and number (खड़ा/खड़ी/खड़े).

corrected.shortGloss: to stand; to stand up; to stop
notes: The adjective खड़ा changes to match the gender and number of the subject: खड़ा (m. sg.), खड़ी (f.), खड़े (m. pl. or formal).
Used both for the action of standing up and the state of being upright.

senses.definition: To be in or rise to an upright position on one's feet.

examples.text: वह बस स्टॉप पर खड़ा है।
examples.translation: He is standing at the bus stop.

senses.definition: Of a vehicle: to come to a stop or be parked.

examples.text: गाड़ी यहाँ आकर खड़ी हो गई।
examples.translation: The car came and stopped here.

faults.quote: to sit; to rest; to settle
faults.why: 'to rest' and 'to settle' are not covered by the senses.

faults.quote: Used for the physical act of sitting down on a chair
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful learner information.
Needs to explain that the stative 'is sitting' uses the perfective participle (बैठा है), not रहा है.

corrected.shortGloss: to sit; to sit down; to board
notes: To say someone 'is sitting' (a state), Hindi uses the perfective form बैठा है / बैठी है, whereas बैठ रहा है means 'is in the act of sitting down'.

senses.definition: To be in or lower oneself into a sitting position.

examples.text: कृपया कुर्सी पर बैठिए।
examples.translation: Please sit on the chair.

senses.definition: To get into or ride in a vehicle.

examples.text: हम सब बस में बैठ गए।
examples.translation: We all got on the bus.

faults.quote: To move quickly over an obstacle or down from a height.
faults.why: Jumping up, over, or down are the same core meaning of कूदना.

faults.quote: to jump; to leap; to bounce
faults.why: 'to bounce' is उछलना, not covered by the senses here.

faults.quote: Used for any action where the body leaves the ground
faults.why: Restates the basic definition of jumping.

notes: Intransitive; in the perfective (past) tenses, the subject does not take ने (ne).

senses.definition: To push oneself off the ground or from a surface into the air using the legs.

examples.text: वह खुशी से कूदने लगा।
examples.translation: He started jumping with joy.

examples.text: बिल्ली दीवार से कूद गई।
examples.translation: The cat jumped off the wall.

faults.quote: To function or operate, often used for machines or systems.
faults.why: Confuses जाना (to go) with चलना (to run/work for machines).

faults.quote: यह गाड़ी अच्छी चलती है।
faults.why: Example uses चलना (चलती), not the headword जाना.
Must mention the irregular perfective stem गय- (गया, गई, गए).

notes: Has an irregular perfective (past) form: गया (m. sg.), गई (f. sg.), गए (m. pl.), गईं (f. pl.).
Also widely used as a helping verb after another verb's stem to show completion or change of state (e.g., सो जाना 'to fall asleep') and to form the passive voice.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another; to leave.

examples.text: मैं बाज़ार जा रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am going to the market.

examples.text: वह कल दिल्ली गया।
examples.translation: He went to Delhi yesterday.

faults.why: Missing everyday sense 'to seem / to feel (to someone)' (e.g., bana zor geldi).

faults.quote: to become, to reach
faults.why: 'Gelmek' does not mean 'to become' on its own; example means 'to reach/get to'.
Should mention the irregular aorist stem 'gelir' (not *geler).

corrected.shortGloss: to come; to arrive; to seem
notes: Takes the dative case (-e/-a) for the destination (eve gelmek = to come home) and ablative (-den/-dan) for the origin.
The present/aorist tense takes the irregular vowel -i-: gelir (he/she comes).

senses.definition: To move towards the speaker or arrive at a place.

examples.text: Yarın bize gelecekler.
examples.translation: They are coming to our place tomorrow.

senses.definition: To reach a particular point, time, or topic.

examples.text: Sonunda bu konuya geldik.
examples.translation: We finally got to this topic.

senses.definition: To seem or feel a certain way to someone (with the dative case).

examples.text: Bu soru bana çok kolay geldi.
examples.translation: This question seemed very easy to me.

faults.quote: Used for both people and things that are recently made
faults.why: 'Genç' is not used for recently made objects; that contradicts note[1] and is false.
Should note consonant softening (genç -> genci) and common noun usage ('a youth').

notes: Used for living beings; for objects that are not old, use 'yeni' (new).
Also frequently used as a noun meaning 'young person' or 'youth' (gençler = young people); final 'ç' softens to 'c' before a vowel (genci).

senses.definition: Having lived for only a short time; not old.

examples.text: Genç adam parkta kitap okuyor.
examples.translation: The young man is reading a book in the park.

faults.quote: While 'gergin' literally means stretched or tight like a rubber band
faults.why: merely restates the senses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'yorulmuş' (tired)
faults.why: Learners have no reason to confuse 'gergin' with 'yorulmuş'.

notes: Derived from the verb 'germek' (to stretch, to tighten).

senses.definition: Feeling anxious, nervous, or irritable due to stress.

examples.text: Sınavdan önce kendimi çok gergin hissediyorum.
examples.translation: I feel very tense before the exam.

senses.definition: Of a situation or relationship: strained and uneasy.

examples.text: Odada çok gergin bir hava vardı.
examples.translation: There was a very tense atmosphere in the room.

senses.definition: Of a rope, wire, or muscle: stretched tight; not slack.

examples.text: Çadırın ipleri çok gergin olmalı.
examples.translation: The tent ropes must be very taut.

faults.quote: To introduce something new or put into practice.
faults.why: Sense 2 ('introduce a rule') is just a shade of sense 1 ('bring about/introduce').

corrected.shortGloss: to bring; to cause; to introduce
notes: Used for bringing something toward the speaker or current topic location; use 'götürmek' for taking something away to another place.

senses.definition: To carry or take someone or something to the speaker or a specified place.

examples.text: Lütfen bana bir bardak su getir.
examples.translation: Please bring me a glass of water.

senses.definition: To cause a result, or to introduce something new such as a rule.

examples.text: Şirket yeni bir kural getirdi.
examples.translation: The company introduced a new rule.

faults.quote: Gezi refers generally to a trip, excursion, or tour
faults.why: Simply repeats the definition and glosses.

faults.quote: Yarın okul için müzeye bir gezi düzenleyeceğiz.
faults.why: 'Okul için' (for the school) is unnatural for 'school trip'; 'okul gezisi' is natural.

notes: Refers to a shorter outing, sightseeing tour, or excursion; for longer journeys or travel in general, use 'seyahat' or 'yolculuk'.

senses.definition: A short journey or outing for pleasure, sightseeing, or education.

examples.text: Yarın müzeye bir okul gezisi düzenleyeceğiz.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we will organize a school trip to the museum.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'mas' is a single-word coordinating conjunction, not a multi-word expression.

faults.quote: A conjunction used to join two contrasting ideas or statements.
faults.why: Metalanguage ('A conjunction used to...'); should define the function directly.

notes: Do not confuse 'mas' (but) with 'mais' (more). In many regions of Brazil, both are pronounced /ˈmajs/, and native speakers sometimes mix them up in informal writing.

senses.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what was just said.

examples.text: Eu queria sair, mas está chovendo.
examples.translation: I wanted to go out, but it is raining.

examples.text: Ele estudou muito, mas não passou na prova.
examples.translation: He studied a lot, but he did not pass the test.

faults.quote: wet; damp; soaked
faults.why: Includes 'damp', which the sense glosses lack and Note 1 explicitly contrasts with 'molhado'.

faults.quote: Molhado is the standard word for 'wet'. Use it for anything
faults.why: Restates the gloss and definition without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: Usually used with the verb 'estar' (estou molhado = I am wet) or 'ficar' (fiquei molhado = I got wet).
Do not confuse with 'úmido', which means 'damp' or 'humid'.

senses.definition: Covered or soaked with water or another liquid.

examples.text: O chão está molhado por causa da chuva.
examples.translation: The floor is wet because of the rain.

examples.text: Minhas roupas ficaram molhadas depois da tempestade.
examples.translation: My clothes got soaked after the storm.

faults.quote: a temperature that is neither refreshing nor soothing.
faults.why: False claim; 'morno' can describe a pleasant, soothing temperature (as in Example 0: 'banho morno').

faults.quote: While it can be used metaphorically to describe a lack of enthusiasm
faults.why: Merely restates Sense 1.

faults.quote: I took a lukewarm shower to relax before sleeping.
faults.why: In English, a relaxing shower is 'warm', not 'lukewarm' (which sounds unpleasant).

notes: Note the vowel change in the stressed syllable: the masculine singular 'morno' has a closed 'o' (/o/), while the feminine 'morna' and plurals 'mornos/mornas' have an open 'o' (/ɔ/).

senses.definition: Moderately warm; neither hot nor cold.

examples.text: Tomei um banho morno para relaxar antes de dormir.
examples.translation: I took a warm shower to relax before going to sleep.

examples.text: O café ficou morno depois de alguns minutos.
examples.translation: The coffee got lukewarm after a few minutes.

senses.definition: Lacking enthusiasm, energy, or intensity.

examples.text: A recepção ao novo projeto foi morna.
examples.translation: The reception to the new project was lukewarm.

faults.quote: /ˈmuj.tu/
faults.why: Wrong transcription; in Portuguese 'muito' has a nasal diphthong (/ˈmũj.tu/), despite the spelling.

notes: When 'muito' is an adverb modifying a verb, adjective, or other adverb, it never changes form. When it quantifies a noun ('many', 'much'), it agrees in gender and number (muito/muita/muitos/muitas).
Despite having no 'n', 'm', or tilde after the 'i', the first syllable is pronounced with a nasal vowel (/ˈmũj.tu/).

senses.definition: To a high degree or in a large amount.

examples.text: Eu estou muito cansado hoje.
examples.translation: I am very tired today.

examples.text: Ele trabalha muito.
examples.translation: He works a lot.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'aber' is a conjunction (and modal particle), not a multi-word expression.

faults.quote: Used to link two contrasting ideas or statements.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of explaining that 'aber' does not change word order.

notes: As a coordinating conjunction, 'aber' does not change the word order of the clause it introduces; It can also stand after the subject or verb ('Ich möchte, ich habe aber keine Zeit').
Do not confuse with 'sondern', which is used after a negative statement to replace it with the correct alternative (e.g., 'Nicht rot, sondern blau').

senses.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what was said before.

examples.text: Ich bin müde, aber ich muss arbeiten.
examples.translation: I am tired, but I have to work.

examples.text: Das Wetter ist schön, aber kalt.
examples.translation: The weather is nice, but cold.

faults.why: Missing the essential A1/A2 sense 'of a particular age' ('Wie alt bist du?').
Should mention the umlaut in comparative ('älter') and superlative ('am ältesten').

notes: Takes an umlaut in the comparative ('älter') and superlative ('am ältesten').
Before a noun, 'alt' can also mean 'former' or 'long-standing' (e.g., 'meine alte Schule' = my former school; 'ein alter Freund' = an old friend).

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time; not young or new.

examples.text: Mein Großvater ist schon sehr alt.
examples.translation: My grandfather is already very old.

examples.text: Ich brauche ein neues Auto, denn mein altes ist kaputt.
examples.translation: I need a new car because my old one is broken.

senses.definition: Of a specified age.

examples.text: Wie alt bist du? — Ich bin zwanzig Jahre alt.
examples.translation: How old are you? — I am twenty years old.

faults.why: Lacks the irregular conjugation ('fängt an', 'fing an', 'hat angefangen') and preposition 'mit'.

notes: Separable and irregular verb: 'du fängst an', 'er fängt an'; past 'fing an'; perfect 'hat angefangen'.
Use 'mit' + dative to say what someone starts doing or working on ('mit der Arbeit anfangen').
More common in everyday speech than its synonym 'beginnen'.

senses.definition: To begin doing something, or for an event to begin.

examples.text: Der Film fängt um acht Uhr an.
examples.translation: The movie starts at eight o'clock.

examples.text: Wann fängst du mit der Arbeit an?
examples.translation: When do you start work?

faults.quote: Use 'ängstlich' to describe someone who is generally timid or fearful
faults.why: Restates the definition and contrasts with rare 'angstvoll' instead of warning about 'Ich habe Angst'.

notes: Usually describes a nervous manner or a timid personality. To say 'I am afraid (of...)', German uses the noun 'Angst': 'Ich habe Angst (vor...)', not 'Ich bin ängstlich'.

senses.definition: Feeling or showing fear or worry; easily frightened.

examples.text: Er ist ein ängstlicher Hund, der vor lauten Geräuschen zittert.
examples.translation: He is a timid dog that trembles at loud noises.

examples.text: Sie blickte ängstlich in den dunklen Keller.
examples.translation: She looked anxiously into the dark cellar.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'ankommen' with 'anrufen' (to call on the phone).
faults.why: Unlikely confusion; note should instead explain the auxiliary 'sein' and 'es kommt auf (+ acc.) an'.

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive; to depend on; to be received
notes: Separable verb ('er kommt an'); forms the perfect tense with 'sein' ('ist angekommen').
In the sense 'to depend on / to matter', it is used impersonally with 'auf' + accusative: 'Es kommt auf das Wetter an' or 'Es kommt darauf an' (It depends).

senses.definition: To reach a place at the end of a journey.

examples.text: Wann kommt der Zug in Berlin an?
examples.translation: When does the train arrive in Berlin?

senses.definition: Used with 'auf' (+ accusative) to say that something is decided by or depends on something else.

examples.text: Es kommt auf das Wetter an.
examples.translation: It depends on the weather.

senses.definition: To be received or reacted to by people in a particular way.

examples.text: Das Geschenk ist bei ihr gut angekommen.
examples.translation: The gift went over well with her.

faults.quote: To have a strong aversion to doing something.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning (both examples take verb complements).

notes: Stronger than 'không thích' (to not like), but often used casually in everyday speech, or even playfully (e.g., 'ghét thế!' — 'how annoying / cute!').

senses.definition: To feel a strong dislike for someone, something, or doing something.

examples.text: Tôi ghét phải dậy sớm vào mùa đông.
examples.translation: I hate having to wake up early in the winter.

examples.text: Cô ấy ghét ăn hành trong phở.
examples.translation: She hates eating green onions in pho.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'già' (old) with 'trẻ' (young).
faults.why: Restates the senses and warns against an antonym instead of the real confusable 'cũ'.
Needs a note contrasting 'già' (old in age) with 'cũ' (old/used for inanimate objects).

faults.quote: old; mature; overripe
faults.why: 'mature' is not covered by the senses.

notes: Used for living things (people, animals, plants). For inanimate objects that are old or not new, use 'cũ' instead.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: having lived for a long time.

examples.text: Bà tôi đã già nhưng vẫn rất khỏe mạnh.
examples.translation: My grandmother is old but still very healthy.

senses.definition: Of vegetables or fruit: past the best stage for eating; tough or fibrous from age.

examples.text: Quả mướp này già rồi, ăn sẽ bị xơ.
examples.translation: This luffa gourd is too old; it will be stringy to eat.

faults.quote: /zaː ʔiŋ˨˩/
faults.why: Corrupted IPA missing the /ɗ/ in 'đình' and the level tone on 'gia'.

faults.quote: Used broadly to mean parents, children, and all extended relatives
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

senses.definition: A group of parents and children, or broader relatives, connected by blood or marriage.

examples.text: Gia đình tôi luôn quây quần bên nhau vào dịp Tết.
examples.translation: My family always gathers together during Tet.

faults.quote: /ziəː˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: 'giá' has /aː/, not the diphthong /iə/ ('gía').

faults.quote: giá is a versatile word in Vietnamese. Its most common meaning
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses in the entry.

notes: In the sense of 'bean sprouts', it is also commonly called 'giá đỗ' (Northern) or 'giá đậu'.

senses.definition: The amount of money you must pay to buy something.

examples.text: Giá của chiếc áo này là bao nhiêu?
examples.translation: What is the price of this shirt?

senses.definition: A shelf, rack, or stand used to hold or support objects.

examples.text: Hãy đặt cuốn sách lên giá sách.
examples.translation: Please put the book on the bookshelf.

senses.definition: Sprouted mung beans used as a vegetable in cooking.

examples.text: Phở thường được ăn kèm với giá và rau thơm.
examples.translation: Pho is usually eaten with bean sprouts and fresh herbs.

faults.quote: /zaːk˧˦ məː˧˧/
faults.why: Wrong vowel in 'giấc': 'ấ' is /ə̆/ (/zə̆k̚˧˥/), not /aː/ ('giác').

faults.quote: Use 'giấc mơ' when talking about mental images during sleep
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses.

notes: For an ambition or life goal, 'ước mơ' is even more common than 'giấc mơ'.

senses.definition: A series of thoughts, images, or emotions occurring during sleep.

examples.text: Đêm qua tôi có một giấc mơ đẹp.
examples.translation: I had a beautiful dream last night.

senses.definition: A cherished hope or ambition for the future.

examples.text: Anh ấy đang cố gắng thực hiện giấc mơ của mình.
examples.translation: He is trying to realize his dream.

faults.quote: /ˈmɔl.to/
faults.why: Standard Italian has a close-mid vowel /o/ in 'molto': /ˈmol.to/.

notes: As an adverb (modifying a verb, adjective, or other adverb), 'molto' is invariable and never changes its ending.
Before a noun (meaning 'much' or 'many'), it acts as an adjective and agrees in gender and number: molto, molta, molti, molte.

senses.definition: To a high degree; used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: Questo libro è molto interessante.
examples.translation: This book is very interesting.

senses.definition: To a great extent or in a large amount; used with verbs.

examples.text: Ho lavorato molto oggi.
examples.translation: I worked a lot today.

faults.quote: 'soffice', which specifically describes things that are fluffy or airy
faults.why: Overstated distinction; 'morbido' and 'soffice' overlap heavily (e.g., pillows, sweaters), and 'morbido' vs 'dolce'/'leggero' for English 'soft' is what learners need.

notes: Used for physical textures (like a pillow, fabric, or tender meat) and gentle sensations, not for quiet sounds ('basso') or mild weather ('mite', 'dolce').

senses.definition: Easy to press or yield to touch; not hard or stiff.

examples.text: Il cuscino è molto morbido.
examples.translation: The pillow is very soft.

senses.definition: Gentle, smooth, or pleasing; not harsh or sharp.

examples.text: La luce della stanza era morbida e accogliente.
examples.translation: The light in the room was soft and welcoming.

faults.quote: The darkest color, the opposite of white.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('The darkest color').

notes: Like most colour adjectives in Italian, 'nero' usually comes after the noun it describes and agrees with it in gender and number.

senses.definition: Of the darkest colour, like coal or the night sky.

examples.text: Ho comprato una giacca nera.
examples.translation: I bought a black jacket.

senses.definition: Very dark, gloomy, or without light; also used for a bad mood or bleak situation.

examples.text: Il cielo è pieno di nuvole nere.
examples.translation: The sky is full of dark clouds.

faults.quote: /nerˈvɔ.zo/
faults.why: In standard Italian, the stressed 'o' in '-oso' is close-mid /o/: /nerˈvo.zo/ (or /nerˈvo.so/).

faults.quote: its most common use is for feeling anxious or tense
faults.why: In everyday Italian, 'nervoso' very commonly means annoyed, irritated, or on edge, making it a partial false friend of English 'nervous'.

notes: Watch out: in everyday Italian, 'nervoso' very often means annoyed, irritated, or on edge, not just anxious before an event (for which 'agitato' or 'in ansia' are common).

senses.definition: Easily annoyed, tense, or in an irritable mood.

examples.text: Oggi sei particolarmente nervoso, è successo qualcosa?
examples.translation: You are particularly on edge today, did something happen?

senses.definition: Feeling anxious, agitated, or worried about something.

examples.text: Sono molto nervoso per l'esame di domani.
examples.translation: I am very nervous about tomorrow's exam.

faults.quote: Used before a verb to make a sentence negative.
faults.why: Confuses 'no' with 'non'. 'Non' goes before a verb; 'no' does not.

faults.quote: Io non mangio carne.
faults.why: Uses 'non', which is a different word from 'no' in Italian.

faults.quote: Used both to negate a verb ('Non lo so' - I don't know)
faults.why: Falsely states that 'no' is used to negate a verb, giving an example with 'non'.

notes: Do not confuse 'no' with 'non'. Use 'no' on its own to answer a question or after a word for contrast ('Oggi no'), but use 'non' before a verb ('Non lo so').

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer, refuse, or disagree, or placed after a word to negate it.

examples.text: No, non posso venire stasera.
examples.translation: No, I cannot come tonight.

senses.definition: Used at the end of a statement to ask for confirmation.

examples.text: Vieni anche tu alla festa, no?
examples.translation: You're coming to the party too, right?

faults.quote: Use 'werken' when talking about having a job, doing tasks, or functioning
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions and glosses instead of giving grammatical or usage help.

notes: Take 'bij' for an employer ('Ik werk bij een bank') and 'als' without an article for a profession ('Ik werk als leraar').

senses.definition: To do a job or perform tasks, especially for pay.

examples.text: Ik werk vandaag tot vijf uur.
examples.translation: I'm working until five o'clock today.

senses.definition: To function or operate properly, of a machine, device, or plan.

examples.text: Mijn telefoon werkt niet goed.
examples.translation: My phone isn't working properly.

faults.quote: To find out or become aware of something.
faults.why: 'Weten' means 'to know'; 'find out' is only an English translation of 'willen weten'.
Missing the irregular principal parts and present-tense forms (weet, wist, geweten).

notes: Irregular verb: weten – wist – geweten. In the present singular, all forms are 'weet' (ik/jij/hij weet).
Use 'weten' for facts, information, or clauses ('Ik weet waar hij woont'). Use 'kennen' for being familiar with a person, place, or thing ('Ik ken hem').

senses.definition: To have information or a fact in your mind; to be aware of something.

examples.text: Ik weet het antwoord op deze vraag.
examples.translation: I know the answer to this question.

examples.text: Ik wil graag weten hoe laat de trein vertrekt.
examples.translation: I would like to know what time the train leaves.

faults.quote: Wat wil je tonight doen?
faults.why: Contains the English word 'tonight' instead of Dutch 'vanavond'.

faults.quote: To be willing or ready to do something.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning; 'niet willen' is just 'to refuse / not want to'.

notes: Irregular modal verb: ik wil, jij/u wilt (or wil), hij/zij wil; past: wilde or wou; past participle: gewild.

senses.definition: To wish to have or do something, or to be willing to do it.

examples.text: Ik wil graag een kopje koffie.
examples.translation: I would like a cup of coffee.

examples.text: Wat wil je vanavond doen?
examples.translation: What do you want to do tonight?

faults.quote: except for de-words in the singular with an indefinite article
faults.why: Backwards grammar rule: singular indefinite 'het'-words (neuter), not 'de'-words, take uninflected 'wit'.

notes: When inflected before a noun, the 't' is doubled to keep the vowel short: 'witte' (e.g. 'witte wijn', 'het witte huis', but 'een wit huis').

senses.definition: Having the colour of snow or milk.

examples.text: De sneeuw is wit.
examples.translation: The snow is white.

faults.quote: (mess) A complete mess or a hopeless tangle of things.
faults.why: Unnatural as a standalone sense; the idiom 'la stessa zuppa' means 'the same old story'.

faults.quote: Questa situazione è una vera zuppa.
faults.why: Unidiomatic; 'zuppa' alone is not used this way to mean a mess.

notes: Use 'zuppa' for a thick, hearty soup (often with bread, beans, or vegetables, but without pasta or rice). For a broth-based soup with pasta or rice, Italians use 'minestra'.

senses.definition: A thick hot dish made of vegetables, pulses, meat, or fish cooked in liquid, often served with bread.

examples.text: La zuppa di verdure è calda e saporita.
examples.translation: The vegetable soup is hot and flavorful.

faults.quote: Lanciare la palla al cane.
faults.why: A sentence fragment, not a natural full sentence.
Missing note on spelling/pronunciation change in conjugations (e.g., tu lanci, noi lanciamo).

notes: Drops the 'i' before 'i' or 'e' in conjugated forms (e.g., 'tu lanci', 'lancerò').
Often contrasted with 'buttare' or 'gettare', which usually imply throwing something away rather than aiming or throwing with force.

senses.definition: To send something through the air by moving your hand or arm quickly.

examples.text: Il bambino lancia la palla al cane.
examples.translation: The boy throws the ball to the dog.

senses.definition: To start or introduce something new, such as a product, a project, or a campaign.

examples.text: L'azienda vuole lanciare un nuovo prodotto sul mercato.
examples.translation: The company wants to launch a new product on the market.

faults.quote: (clothes) Wash clothes by hand or with a machine.
faults.why: 'Lavare i vestiti' is just the regular meaning of 'lavare' applied to clothes.

notes: For washing oneself or a part of one's body, use the reflexive form 'lavarsi' (e.g., 'lavarsi le mani' — to wash one's hands).

senses.definition: To clean something using water and usually soap.

examples.text: Devo lavare i piatti dopo cena.
examples.translation: I need to wash the dishes after dinner.

examples.text: Oggi devo lavare i vestiti scuri.
examples.translation: Today I need to wash the dark clothes.

faults.quote: Questo computer non lavora bene oggi.
faults.why: False friend with English 'work'; for machines functioning, Italian uses 'funzionare', not 'lavorare'.
Must warn the learner not to use 'lavorare' for machines/devices working (use 'funzionare').

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'lavorare' with 'fabbricare'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'lavorare' with 'fabbricare'.

notes: Takes the auxiliary verb 'avere' in compound tenses ('ho lavorato').
Do not use 'lavorare' to say that a machine, device, or plan works; use 'funzionare' instead (e.g., 'il telefono non funziona').

senses.definition: To do a job or perform tasks and activities, especially to earn a living.

examples.text: Mio fratello lavora in un grande ufficio in centro.
examples.translation: My brother works in a large office downtown.

faults.quote: /baˈket.te/
faults.why: Double 'c' before 'h' is geminated (/bakˈket.te/), and lemma is 'bacchetta' (/bakˈket.ta/).

faults.quote: chopsticks; drumsticks; wand
faults.why: 'wand' is singular ('la bacchetta magica') and is not covered in the senses.

notes: Plural of 'la bacchetta' (stick, rod, wand, or conductor's baton); used in the plural for items that come in pairs, like chopsticks or drumsticks.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used for eating East Asian food.

examples.text: Uso sempre le bacchette quando mangio il sushi.
examples.translation: I always use chopsticks when I eat sushi.

senses.definition: A pair of wooden sticks used for playing the drums.

examples.text: Il batterista ha rotto le bacchette durante il concerto.
examples.translation: The drummer broke his drumsticks during the concert.

faults.why: Senses 0, 1, and 2 are contextual shades of 'to speak/talk', not distinct meanings.
Missing note on dropping 'ber-' ('bicara') in informal speech and common prepositions.

notes: In everyday conversation, the prefix 'ber-' is often dropped ('bicara').
Commonly followed by 'dengan' or 'sama' (with/to) and 'tentang' (about).

senses.definition: To utter words, converse with someone, or address an audience.

examples.text: Saya ingin berbicara dengan kepala sekolah tentang nilai anak saya.
examples.translation: I want to talk with the principal about my child's grades.

examples.text: Bayi itu sudah mulai belajar berbicara.
examples.translation: That baby has started learning to speak.

faults.quote: While 'berdiri' refers to the physical act of standing, it is also
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: Intransitive. Compare 'mendirikan' (to build, to establish something) and 'tegak' (upright, vertical).

senses.definition: To be in or rise to an upright position on one's feet.

examples.text: Dia berdiri di depan pintu.
examples.translation: He is standing in front of the door.

senses.definition: To be founded or established, as an organization, building, or state.

examples.text: Sekolah ini berdiri sejak tahun 1990.
examples.translation: This school was established in 1990.

faults.quote: This is the standard term for the act of swimming.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the gloss and saying it is a regular verb.
Should explain the morphology (ber- + renang -> berenang, dropping one 'r').

notes: Formed from 'ber-' + 'renang', where one 'r' is dropped.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving the body, arms, and legs.

examples.text: Dia suka berenang di pagi hari.
examples.translation: He likes to swim in the morning.

faults.quote: to hope; to expect
faults.why: 'to expect' is in shortGloss, while sense 1 is 'to rely, to depend'.

faults.quote: To rely or depend on someone or something for help.
faults.why: 'Berharap pada' is 'to place one's hopes in / expect from', a shade of hoping.

faults.quote: Derived from the root 'harap' (hope).
faults.why: Restates the lemma and gloss without adding usage help.

notes: Takes 'agar' or 'supaya' when hoping someone else will do something, and 'pada' or 'kepada' when placing hopes in someone.

senses.definition: To want something to happen or to place one's hopes in someone or something.

examples.text: Saya berharap cuaca akan cerah besok.
examples.translation: I hope the weather will be clear tomorrow.

examples.text: Jangan terlalu berharap pada orang lain.
examples.translation: Do not count too much on other people.

faults.quote: Berhenti comes from the root 'henti', with the prefix 'ber-' forming
faults.why: Restates the gloss; can be combined concisely with note 1.

notes: Intransitive (e.g., 'berhenti bekerja' = to stop working). To stop something else, use the transitive 'menghentikan'.

senses.definition: To no longer move, happen, or do something.

examples.text: Mobil itu berhenti di depan rumah.
examples.translation: The car stopped in front of the house.

senses.definition: To leave a job or school, or to give up a habit.

examples.text: Dia memutuskan untuk berhenti dari pekerjaannya.
examples.translation: He decided to quit his job.

faults.quote: /ˈmʲjɛʂkat͡ɕ/
faults.why: Standard Polish IPA for 'mieszkać' is /ˈmʲɛʂ.kat͡ɕ/, without /j/.

notes: Distinguish 'mieszkać' from 'żyć'. Use 'mieszkać' for the place where you have your home (often followed by 'w' + locative), and 'żyć' for being alive or how you lead your life.

senses.definition: To have your home in a particular place.

examples.text: Mieszkam w Warszawie.
examples.translation: I live in Warsaw.

examples.text: Gdzie mieszkasz?
examples.translation: Where do you live?

faults.quote: apartment; flat; housing

faults.why: Starting with 'To' makes 'mieszkanie' sound like 'This apartment' rather than the verbal noun 'living'.

senses.definition: A set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a larger building.

examples.translation: I am looking for a new apartment in the city center.

senses.definition: The act of living or residing in a place.

examples.text: Mieszkanie w dużym mieście jest bardzo drogie.

faults.quote: In Polish, remember that nouns change their ending (case)

examples.text: Zajmie mi to tylko minutę.

faults.quote: Used for holding food, liquids, or mixing ingredients.

examples.text: Wlała zupę do miski.
examples.translation: She poured the soup into a bowl.

faults.quote: Used for both people and things. When describing a person...

examples.text: On jest bardzo miłym człowiekiem.

senses.definition: Of a thing or experience: giving a good or enjoyable feeling.

examples.text: To był miły wieczór.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'प्याला' (pyala), which is typically a cup

examples.text: मेरा भाई कल आएगा।
examples.translation: My brother will come tomorrow.

senses.definition: A friendly form of address for a man or boy.

examples.text: कैसे हो भाई?
examples.translation: How are you, mate?

faults.quote: moon; lunar month

faults.quote: A term of endearment, often used for a loved one

senses.definition: The natural satellite of the Earth that shines in the night sky.

examples.text: आज रात चाँद बहुत सुंदर दिख रहा है।

faults.quote: /ɡəɳʈɑː/

senses.definition: A period of sixty minutes.

examples.text: मैं एक घंटे में वापस आऊँगा।

senses.definition: A large metal bell or gong, especially in a temple.

examples.text: मंदिर में एक बड़ा घंटा लगा है।
examples.translation: A large bell hangs in the temple.

faults.quote: /sɛnḍəʋic/

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.translation: Do you sell bread here?

faults.quote: شَاهَدَ النَّاسُ العَرْضَ فِي الشَّارِعِ.

examples.text: شَاهَدْتُ فِيلْمًا جَمِيلًا مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي.
examples.translation: I watched a beautiful film with my friends.

senses.definition: The solid part of the earth's surface not covered by water, or an area of ground used for farming.

examples.translation: I have to take this medicine twice a day.

senses.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

examples.translation: We swam in the lake on a warm summer day.
