notes: Comparative: częściej (more often). Opposite: rzadko (rarely).

senses.definition: Many times or on many occasions; at short intervals.

examples.text: Ona często czyta książki wieczorem.
examples.translation: She often reads books in the evening.

faults.why: 'To brush' is just a translation of 'czyścić' with 'zęby' or 'buty', not a separate sense.

faults.quote: Muszę czyścić buty przed wyjściem.
faults.why: Wrong aspect for a single action before going out; would be perfective 'wyczyścić'.

faults.quote: like cleaning a room or wiping a surface.
faults.why: Misleading: cleaning a room in Polish is 'sprzątać pokój', not 'czyścić pokój'.

notes: Imperfective verb; the perfective pair is 'wyczyścić'.
Used for removing dirt from objects and surfaces (e.g. buty — shoes, dywan — carpet). For tidying a room or house, use 'sprzątać'; for washing with water and soap, use 'myć'.

senses.definition: To remove dirt, stains, or mess from an object or surface, often by brushing or rubbing.

examples.text: On zawsze czyści buty przed wyjściem.
examples.translation: He always cleans his shoes before going out.

faults.quote: clean; pure; sheer
faults.why: Includes 'sheer', which is not covered by any of the senses.

faults.quote: Mam czysty pokój po całym sprzątaniu.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing ('po całym sprzątaniu' sounds like a calque of 'after all the cleaning').

faults.quote: czysty primarily means clean or free from dirt, but it is
faults.why: Just repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Opposite: brudny (dirty).

senses.definition: Free from dirt, marks, or stains.

examples.text: Po sprzątaniu cały pokój jest czysty.
examples.translation: After cleaning, the whole room is clean.

senses.definition: Not mixed with anything else; free from harmful or unwanted substances.

examples.text: W górach jest czyste powietrze.
examples.translation: There is clean, pure air in the mountains.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'vagón' or 'tren', which refer to parts
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1; also 'tren' is the whole train, not a part of one.

faults.quote: A carriage or a section of a train used to transport passengers.
faults.why: In everyday Spain Spanish, a train carriage is usually 'vagón'; 'coche' is railway jargon.

notes: In Spain, 'coche' is the standard word for a car. In most of Latin America, people say 'el carro' or 'el auto' instead.
Note the preposition in 'en coche' (by car), without an article: 'Voy al trabajo en coche'.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: Mi padre va al trabajo en coche todos los días.
examples.translation: My father goes to work by car every day.

faults.why: Should give the feminine form 'la cocinera' for this animate role noun.

notes: The feminine form is 'la cocinera'.
'Cocinero' is the general word for a professional cook; 'el/la chef' is used specifically for a head chef.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to prepare and cook food.

examples.text: El cocinero prepara la cena para todos los clientes.
examples.translation: The cook prepares dinner for all the customers.

faults.quote: A secondary school or high school.
faults.why: False in Spain (and contradicts note 0): public high school is 'instituto', not 'colegio'.
Missing the crucial false-friend warning that 'colegio' does not mean 'college' (university).

notes: False friend: 'colegio' means 'school' (for children), not 'college' or 'university' ('la universidad').
In Spain, 'el colegio' (informally 'el cole') usually refers to primary school or a private school; a public secondary school is 'el instituto'.

senses.definition: A place where children go to be educated, especially at primary level.

examples.text: Los niños van al colegio por la mañana.
examples.translation: The children go to school in the morning.

faults.why: Missing two everyday senses: 'classmate' (central for A1/A2 learners) and 'romantic partner'.

faults.quote: A person with whom one works.
faults.why: 'Coworker', 'classmate', and 'teammate' are all uses of one core sense (fellow member/sharer).

notes: The feminine form is 'la compañera'.
Often followed by 'de' to specify what is shared: 'compañero de clase' (classmate), 'compañero de trabajo' (colleague), 'compañero de piso' (flatmate). For a personal friend, use 'amigo'.

senses.definition: A person who shares an activity, place, or group with another, such as at school, at work, or on a trip.

examples.text: Mi compañero de trabajo me ayudó con el proyecto.
examples.translation: My colleague helped me with the project.

examples.text: Hablé con mis compañeros de clase después del examen.
examples.translation: I spoke with my classmates after the exam.

senses.definition: A person with whom one has a romantic relationship, especially when living together.

examples.text: Vino a la cena con su compañero.
examples.translation: He came to the dinner with his partner.

faults.quote: rabbit; coney
faults.why: 'Coney' is archaic in English and not in the senses' glosses.

senses.definition: A small animal with long ears, soft fur, and a short tail that lives in burrows and hops.

examples.text: El conejo corre por el campo buscando hierba fresca.
examples.translation: The rabbit runs through the field looking for fresh grass.

senses.definition: Meat from this animal, eaten as food.

examples.text: Hoy comemos conejo al ajillo con patatas.
examples.translation: Today we are eating garlic rabbit with potatoes.

faults.why: Missing the common Mexican Spanish sense 'flashlight' (lámpara de mano / lámpara).

notes: In Mexico, 'lámpara' is commonly used for a handheld flashlight as well as a table or floor lamp.
Do not confuse with 'foco', which refers to the lightbulb itself.

senses.definition: A device that produces artificial light for a room or desk.

examples.text: Voy a encender la lámpara porque está oscureciendo.
examples.translation: I am going to turn on the lamp because it is getting dark.

senses.definition: A small portable electric light carried in the hand.

examples.text: Se fue la luz, pásame la lámpara.
examples.translation: The power went out, pass me the flashlight.

faults.quote: In Mexico and many other Spanish-speaking countries, 'la leche' is widely used
faults.why: Slang '¡la leche!' / 'estar de la leche' is Peninsular Spanish, not Mexican.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'la piel' or other food items
faults.why: Nonsensical warning; nobody confuses 'leche' with 'piel' (skin).

faults.quote: A colloquial expression used to indicate anger, bad luck, or intensity.
faults.why: Peninsular slang sense is inappropriate for an A2 Mexican Spanish entry, and poorly defined.

faults.quote: milk; wow / hell; cream
faults.why: Includes 'cream' which is not in the senses, and Peninsular slang.

notes: In everyday Mexican Spanish, 'mala leche' is sometimes used colloquially to mean ill will or bad luck.

senses.definition: The white liquid produced by cows and other female mammals, drunk by people and used in cooking.

examples.text: Bebo un vaso de leche todas las mañanas.
examples.translation: I drink a glass of milk every morning.

faults.quote: While 'llave' is the word for a door key, it is also
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses and glosses already given in the entry.

faults.quote: Necesito una llave para ajustar este tornillo.
faults.why: Wrenches ('llaves') are used on nuts ('tuercas') or bolts, whereas 'tornillo' usually takes a screwdriver.

notes: Do not confuse with 'clave', which means a secret code or password.

senses.definition: A small metal object used to open or lock a door, car, or padlock.

examples.text: Busqué la llave en mi bolso para entrar a la casa.
examples.translation: I looked for the key in my bag to get into the house.

senses.definition: A device that controls the flow of water from a pipe.

examples.text: Cierra bien la llave del agua para no desperdiciarla.
examples.translation: Turn off the water faucet tightly so as not to waste it.

senses.definition: A metal tool used for holding and turning nuts and bolts.

examples.text: Necesito una llave para apretar esta tuerca.
examples.translation: I need a wrench to tighten this nut.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, where you might say 'the rain is falling,'
faults.why: Overly wordy and misleading; English also normally says 'it is raining'.

notes: To say 'it is raining', Spanish normally uses the verb 'llover' ('está lloviendo' or 'llueve').

senses.definition: Water that falls from the clouds in drops.

examples.text: Me gusta mucho caminar bajo la lluvia.
examples.translation: I really like walking in the rain.

faults.quote: Even though it ends in -a, luna is a feminine noun.
faults.why: Illogical filler note: nouns ending in -a are regularly feminine, and it restates gender.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, you almost always include the article 'la'
faults.why: False contrast: English also says 'the moon' and 'the sun' with the definite article.

faults.quote: moon; satellite
faults.why: 'satellite' is not in the sense glosses.

senses.definition: The round object that moves around the Earth and shines in the sky at night.

examples.text: La luna está muy brillante esta noche.
examples.translation: The moon is very bright tonight.

faults.quote: For a formal context or a more upscale restaurant, some people may
faults.why: Vague filler note; missing the feminine form 'la camarera' and barman usage.

notes: The feminine form is 'la camarera' (waitress). In Spain, it is also used for a bartender.
Standard in Spain; in Latin America, 'el mesero' or 'el mozo' is much more common.

senses.definition: A person who serves food and drinks to customers in a restaurant, cafe, or bar.

examples.text: El camarero nos trajo la cuenta después de comer.
examples.translation: The waiter brought us the bill after eating.

faults.quote: Used to mean both the natural countryside ('ir al campo') and a
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already given in the entry.
Missing the basic sense of an agricultural field (piece of farmland).

notes: In the singular ('el campo'), it often refers to the countryside in general ('vivir en el campo' = to live in the country).
Not to be confused with 'el pueblo', which refers specifically to a village or small town.

senses.definition: Land outside towns and cities, with nature and farms.

examples.text: Este fin de semana vamos a descansar al campo.
examples.translation: This weekend we are going to rest in the countryside.

senses.definition: An area of land on a farm used for growing crops or keeping animals.

examples.text: Los agricultores trabajan en los campos de trigo.
examples.translation: The farmers work in the wheat fields.

senses.definition: An area of ground marked out for playing a sport.

examples.text: Los jugadores ya están saltando al campo de fútbol.
examples.translation: The players are already stepping onto the football pitch.

senses.definition: An area of study, work, or professional activity.

examples.text: Ella trabaja en el campo de la medicina.
examples.translation: She works in the field of medicine.

faults.quote: Carne comestible de este animal.
faults.why: Definition is written in Spanish instead of English.

notes: Unlike English, which distinguishes between 'pig' and 'pork', Spanish uses 'cerdo' (or 'carne de cerdo') for both the live animal and its meat.

senses.definition: A farm animal with pink or dark skin and a short snout, kept for its meat.

examples.text: Los cerdos están en el barro de la granja.
examples.translation: The pigs are in the mud on the farm.

senses.definition: The meat from a pig eaten as food.

examples.text: Compramos carne de cerdo para la cena.
examples.translation: We bought pork for dinner.

faults.quote: /tʃoˈkolate/
faults.why: Wrong stress in IPA: 'chocolate' is stressed on the third syllable (/tʃokoˈlate/).

notes: As a countable noun ('un chocolate'), it usually refers to a cup of thick hot chocolate, often eaten in Spain with churros. For a chocolate bar, use 'una tableta de chocolate' or 'una chocolatina'.

senses.definition: A sweet food made from cocoa beans, eaten as a bar or used in desserts.

examples.text: A ella le encanta el chocolate negro.
examples.translation: She loves dark chocolate.

senses.definition: A thick, warm drink made by mixing melted chocolate or cocoa with milk or water.

examples.text: Vamos a tomar un chocolate con churros.
examples.translation: Let's go have a hot chocolate with churros.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical sky above and for heaven in a
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses in the entry without adding useful information.

notes: Also commonly used in Spain as an affectionate term for a person ('mi cielo' = my darling / sweetheart).

senses.definition: The space above the earth where the sun, moon, clouds, and stars appear.

examples.text: El cielo está completamente despejado hoy.
examples.translation: The sky is completely clear today.

senses.definition: In some religions, the place where God lives and where good people go after death.

examples.text: Creemos que las almas buenas van al cielo.
examples.translation: We believe good souls go to heaven.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'estudante' (student) or 'aluno' (pupil).
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'professor' with 'estudante' or 'aluno'.

notes: Used for both school teachers and university lecturers. The feminine form is 'a professora'.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to teach, especially in a school or university.

examples.text: O professor explicou a lição com calma.
examples.translation: The teacher explained the lesson calmly.

faults.quote: While 'quadro' can refer to any framed picture, it is most commonly
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already shown in the entry.

notes: For the classroom board, 'a lousa' is also very common in Brazil.

senses.definition: A picture, especially one made with paint, that hangs on a wall in a frame.

examples.text: Ela comprou um quadro lindo para a sala de estar.
examples.translation: She bought a beautiful painting for the living room.

senses.definition: A large board on a classroom wall used for writing on with chalk or markers.

examples.text: O professor escreveu a resposta no quadro.
examples.translation: The teacher wrote the answer on the board.

senses.definition: A chart or table used to organize information.

examples.text: Os dados estão organizados no quadro da página seguinte.
examples.translation: The data is organized in the chart on the next page.

faults.quote: (number) The ordinal number that comes after third.
faults.why: 'Quarto' in 'no quarto andar' is an ordinal determiner/adjective, not the noun 'o quarto'.

faults.quote: As a noun, 'quarto' most commonly means bedroom in daily speech.
faults.why: Restates the primary sense and mixes in a different part of speech.

notes: As an adjective or numeral, 'quarto' (feminine 'quarta') means 'fourth', as in 'o quarto andar' (the fourth floor).

senses.definition: A room for sleeping in a house, apartment, or hotel.

examples.text: O meu quarto é grande e tem uma cama confortável.
examples.translation: My bedroom is big and has a comfortable bed.

senses.definition: One of four equal parts of something.

examples.text: Adicione um quarto de xícara de óleo à massa.
examples.translation: Add a quarter of a cup of oil to the batter.

faults.quote: In Brazil, 'queijo' is almost always used to refer to dairy cheese.
faults.why: Tautological filler that restates the meaning of cheese.

notes: Do not confuse 'queijo' (/ʒ/, cheese) with 'queixo' (/ʃ/, chin).

senses.definition: A solid or soft food made from milk.

examples.text: Gosto de comer pão com queijo no café da manhã.
examples.translation: I like to eat bread with cheese for breakfast.

faults.quote: This word is also used for the computer peripheral 'mouse' in Brazil.
faults.why: False for Brazil: Brazilians say 'o mouse', while 'o rato' is European Portuguese.

faults.quote: (technology) The hand-operated electronic device used to move a cursor
faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, a computer mouse is called 'mouse', not 'rato'.

notes: Used for both mice and rats. To refer specifically to a small mouse, 'o camundongo' is also used in Brazil, and 'a ratazana' for a large rat.
For a computer mouse, Brazilian Portuguese uses the English word 'o mouse' (unlike European Portuguese, which uses 'o rato').

senses.definition: A small rodent with a long, thin tail, often found in houses, streets, or fields.

examples.text: O rato correu para trás do armário.
examples.translation: The mouse ran behind the cupboard.

faults.quote: /ˈka.fə/
faults.why: Standard Indonesian pronounces final 'e' in 'kafe' as /e/, not schwa /ə/.

faults.quote: Kafe refers to a small, casual establishment serving coffee, tea, and light
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Do not confuse with 'warung', which is a traditional, much simpler local food or coffee stall ('warung kopi').

senses.definition: A small place where people go to drink coffee and eat light snacks.

examples.text: Mereka duduk di kafe sambil minum kopi sore.
examples.translation: They sat at a café while drinking afternoon coffee.

faults.quote: Used to refer to your mother's or father's father.
faults.why: Restates sense 0 definition.

faults.quote: Can also be used respectfully as a polite term of address
faults.why: Restates sense 1 definition without adding usage detail (like short form 'Kek').

notes: In direct address, it is often shortened to 'Kek' (e.g., 'Terima kasih, Kek').Like other Indonesian kinship terms, it is also used as a pronoun ('I' or 'you') when speaking to or as a grandfather.

senses.definition: The father of your mother or father.

examples.text: Kakek saya tinggal di desa.
examples.translation: My grandfather lives in the village.

senses.definition: A polite term of address or reference for an elderly man.

examples.text: Permisi, Kakek, mau dibantu menyeberang jalan?
examples.translation: Excuse me, sir, would you like help crossing the street?

faults.why: Indonesian does not distinguish 'leg' and 'foot' as separate senses; it is one anatomical concept.

faults.quote: Dia mencopot sepatunya dari kaki.
faults.why: 'Mencopot sepatu dari kaki' is redundant and unnatural; 'melepas sepatu' is normal.

notes: In Indonesian, 'kaki' covers both 'leg' and 'foot'. Context usually makes it clear, but you can specify 'paha' (thigh), 'betis' (calf), or 'telapak kaki' (sole of the foot) to be precise.
Commonly used in 'jalan kaki' (to walk / go on foot).

senses.definition: The lower limb of a person or animal, including both the leg and the foot.

examples.text: Kakinya sakit setelah berlari jauh.
examples.translation: His leg hurts after running far.

examples.text: Ukuran sepatu kaki saya 40.
examples.translation: My foot's shoe size is 40.

senses.definition: The lower supporting part or base of an object, furniture, or mountain.

examples.text: Kaki meja itu patah satu.
examples.translation: One of the table legs is broken.

faults.quote: Use 'kalah' when you do not win a game, a competition, or
faults.why: Mostly restates sense 0 definition.

corrected.shortGloss: to lose; to be defeated; to be inferior to
notes: For losing a game or competition, use 'kalah' (opposite of 'menang', to win). Do not confuse with 'hilang', which means to lose an object (to go missing).
Placed before an adjective ('kalah' + adjective), it means to be less [adjective] than something else, e.g., 'kalah cepat' (slower) or 'kalah bagus' (not as good).

senses.definition: To fail to win a game, competition, fight, or election.

examples.text: Tim kami kalah dalam pertandingan itu.
examples.translation: Our team lost the match.

senses.definition: To be surpassed by or not as good as something else in a particular quality.

examples.text: Mobil ini kalah cepat dibanding mobil itu.
examples.translation: This car is slower than that car.

faults.why: Splitting calendar into abstract system and physical chart is unnecessary for A2; chart is primary.

faults.quote: calendar page
faults.why: 'Kalender' means the whole calendar, not specifically a 'calendar page'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'jadwal' (schedule/timetable). A 'kalender' shows the dates of the year; a 'jadwal' shows planned events or times.

senses.definition: A chart, app, or system that shows the days, weeks, and months of a year.

examples.text: Dia menandai tanggal penting di kalender.
examples.translation: She marked an important date on the calendar.

faults.quote: Used both for the astronomical object in the sky and for
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Also used for the star shape or rating symbol (e.g., beş yıldızlı otel, 'five-star hotel') and the asterisk (*).

senses.definition: A bright point of light in the night sky.

examples.text: Gökyüzünde çok fazla yıldız var.
examples.translation: There are a lot of stars in the sky.

senses.definition: A famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

examples.text: O oyuncu sinemanın en büyük yıldızı oldu.
examples.translation: That actor became the biggest star of cinema.

faults.quote: Yol is a versatile word in Turkish. Beyond its literal meaning
faults.why: Restates the senses already listed in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse yol with yün (wool) or yıl (year)
faults.why: Unhelpful filler; these words are not notably confused beyond sharing a first letter.

notes: Common travel expressions include yola çıkmak (to set off on a journey), yolda (on the way), and İyi yolculuklar! (Have a good trip!).

senses.definition: A surface or route built for vehicles and people to travel along.

examples.text: Bu yol şehir merkezine gider.
examples.translation: This road goes to the city center.

senses.definition: A method or course of action for achieving something.

examples.text: Bu sorunu çözmenin başka bir yolu olmalı.
examples.translation: There must be another way to solve this problem.

senses.definition: An act of traveling from one place to another, or the distance traveled.

examples.text: Uzun bir yol bizi bekliyor.
examples.translation: A long journey awaits us.

faults.quote: Bugün çok yorgun hissediyorum.
faults.why: Calque of English 'feel tired'; natural Turkish is 'Bugün çok yorgunum' or 'kendimi yorgun hissediyorum'.

faults.quote: Showing signs of wear or depletion through long use or age.
faults.why: Calling furniture 'yorgun' is a poetic metaphor, not an everyday A2 sense; 'eski' means old/worn.

faults.quote: tired; exhausted
faults.why: 'Exhausted' contradicts the note and isn't in the sense glosses.

notes: Often used in the phrase yorgun düşmek (to fall tired / become worn out). Stronger exhaustion is expressed with bitkin or yorgunluktan ölmek (to be dead tired).

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep because of physical or mental effort.

examples.text: Bugün çok yorgunum, erken yatacağım.
examples.translation: I am very tired today; I will go to bed early.

faults.quote: The biological reproductive body produced by animals, containing the embryo.
faults.why: A bird's egg laid in nature and an egg eaten as food are one everyday concept.

faults.quote: Used both for the food item and for the biological cell
faults.why: Restates the oversplit definitions without adding useful learner information.

notes: Common breakfast terms include haşlanmış yumurta (boiled egg), sahanda yumurta (fried egg), and çırpılmış yumurta (scrambled eggs).

senses.definition: An oval object with a thin shell laid by a female bird, especially a chicken, often eaten as food.

examples.text: Kahvaltıda bir yumurta yedim.
examples.translation: I ate an egg for breakfast.

faults.quote: /jumusak/
faults.why: Wrong consonant: 'ş' represents /ʃ/, not /s/, and primary stress is missing (/jumuˈʃak/).

faults.quote: Used for physical textures that yield to pressure, as well as
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses in the entry; misses the stem mutation to 'yumuşa-'.

notes: The opposite is sert (hard, harsh). Also used in the alphabet name yumuşak g for the letter ğ.

senses.definition: Of an object or material: not hard or firm; easy to press or bend.

examples.text: Bu yatak çok yumuşak ve rahat.
examples.translation: This bed is very soft and comfortable.

senses.definition: Of a voice, person, or weather: gentle, mild, and not harsh.

examples.text: Öğretmenimiz çok yumuşak bir sesle konuştu.
examples.translation: Our teacher spoke in a very gentle voice.

faults.why: Missing everyday A1 sense 'to go (well/badly)' as in 'Hoe gaat het?'.

faults.quote: to go; to leave; to become; to fit
faults.why: 'to become' and 'to fit' are not covered by any of the senses.
Missing irregular forms (ging/gingen, is gegaan) for a core irregular verb.

corrected.shortGloss: to go; to leave; to be going to
notes: Irregular verb: past 'ging' / 'gingen', past participle 'gegaan' (takes 'zijn': 'ik ben gegaan').
Do not confuse with 'lopen' (to walk); 'gaan' means moving to a place by any means.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.

examples.text: Ik ga morgen naar Amsterdam.
examples.translation: I am going to Amsterdam tomorrow.

senses.definition: Used before an infinitive to talk about a future action or beginning.

examples.text: Het gaat regenen.
examples.translation: It is going to rain.

senses.definition: To proceed or go in a certain way; used when asking how someone is.

examples.text: Hoe gaat het met je?
examples.translation: How are you doing?

senses.definition: To leave a place.

examples.text: Het is laat, wij moeten nu gaan.
examples.translation: It is late, we have to go now.

faults.quote: It does not change for gender, only for the definiteness and number
faults.why: False grammar: Dutch adjectives drop -e before indefinite singular neuter ('het') nouns ('een geel huis').

faults.quote: The color of a lemon or a ripe banana.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality ('Having the color...').

notes: Spelled 'gele' with a single 'e' when an '-e' ending is added (e.g., 'een gele banaan', 'het gele huis', but 'een geel huis').

senses.definition: Having the color of a lemon or a ripe banana.

examples.text: De citroen is geel.
examples.translation: The lemon is yellow.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same basic meaning ('dangerous / risky').

faults.quote: Used to describe something that can cause harm or injury.
faults.why: Note 0 restates the definition and Note 1 makes an artificial contrast with 'erg'.

senses.definition: Able to cause harm, injury, or damage; not safe.

examples.text: Het is gevaarlijk om op het ijs te lopen.
examples.translation: It is dangerous to walk on the ice.

faults.quote: to give; to hand over; to produce
faults.why: 'to produce' is not covered by the senses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse geven with 'gaan' (to go) or 'geven'
faults.why: Unhelpful filler warning; learners do not confuse 'geven' with 'gaan' or 'vinden'.

corrected.shortGloss: to give; to hand over; to provide
notes: Irregular verb: past 'gaf' / 'gaven', past participle 'gegeven' (with 'hebben').

senses.definition: To hand something to someone, or let them have it.

examples.text: Kun je mij dat boek even geven?
examples.translation: Can you hand me that book for a moment?

senses.definition: To provide, host, or hold something such as a lesson, party, or answer.

examples.text: Ze geeft elke dinsdag les aan kinderen.
examples.translation: She gives lessons to children every Tuesday.

faults.quote: Use gezond both for people who are in good physical shape

faults.why: Highlights a marginal idiom in the short gloss.

faults.quote: Use 'verkaufen' when you give an item to someone in exchange
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of 'to sell'.

notes: Inseparable verb (past participle 'verkauft', without 'ge-'). The opposite is 'kaufen' (to buy).
The person buying is in the dative case (or with 'an' + accusative), and the item sold is in the accusative: 'Sie verkauft mir ihr Auto.'

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: Sie möchte ihr altes Auto verkaufen.
examples.translation: She wants to sell her old car.

faults.quote: It is also used in a professional context to mean 'to design'
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding new usage information.

notes: Unlike 'pintar' (to paint), which uses paint or color, 'desenhar' refers to making lines and shapes with a pencil, pen, or similar tool.

senses.definition: To make a picture or diagram by drawing lines with a pencil, pen, or similar tool.

examples.text: Eu gosto de desenhar retratos no meu tempo livre.
examples.translation: I like to draw portraits in my free time.

senses.definition: To plan and draw the shape or structure of something before it is made.

examples.text: O arquiteto vai desenhar a nova casa da família.
examples.translation: The architect is going to design the family's new house.

faults.quote: Difícil is used for tasks or situations that are not easy
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses irregular plural 'difíceis' and invariability for gender.

notes: Do not confuse with 'duro', which means physically hard or solid to the touch.
Has the same form for masculine and feminine, and an irregular plural: 'difíceis'.

senses.definition: Not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

examples.text: Este exercício é muito difícil.
examples.translation: This exercise is very difficult.

examples.text: É difícil entender o que ele disse.
examples.translation: It is hard to understand what he said.

faults.quote: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'dirigir' is the standard verb for operating a vehicle.
faults.why: Note [0] restates sense 0; misses the spelling change 'g' to 'j' (eu dirijo).

corrected.shortGloss: to drive; to manage; to direct
notes: Spelling changes 'g' to 'j' before 'o' or 'a' to keep the /ʒ/ sound (e.g., 'eu dirijo').
In European Portuguese, 'conduzir' is normally used for driving a vehicle instead of 'dirigir'.

senses.definition: To operate and control a motor vehicle.

examples.text: Eu aprendi a dirigir aos dezoito anos.
examples.translation: I learned to drive when I was eighteen.

senses.definition: To be in charge of an organization, project, or artistic production.

examples.text: Ela dirige a empresa com muita eficiência.
examples.translation: She manages the company very efficiently.

faults.quote: O que você quer dizer? — What do you want to say?
faults.why: 'Querer dizer' is an idiom meaning 'to mean', not 'to want to say'.

faults.quote: It is an irregular verb, which you will need to practice
faults.why: Vague filler instead of showing the actual key irregular forms.

corrected.shortGloss: to say; to tell; to mean
notes: Highly irregular: present 'eu digo', past 'eu disse', future 'eu direi', participle 'dito'.

senses.definition: To speak or state something in words to someone.

examples.text: Sempre digo a verdade para os meus amigos.
examples.translation: I always tell my friends the truth.

examples.text: Ela disse que vem amanhã.
examples.translation: She said that she is coming tomorrow.

senses.definition: To convey a particular meaning, or to state information in writing.

examples.text: O que você quer dizer com isso?
examples.translation: What do you mean by that?

examples.text: O que esta placa diz?
examples.translation: What does this sign say?

faults.quote: When used as an adjective, 'doce' means sweet as a flavor
faults.why: Merely repeats the senses; misses the useful 'água doce' (fresh water) collocation.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('o bolo doce', 'a fruta doce').
In 'água doce', it means 'fresh water' (as opposed to 'água salgada', salt water).
Also used as a masculine noun ('um doce') meaning a sweet, candy, or dessert.

senses.definition: Having the pleasant taste of sugar or honey.

examples.text: Este suco de laranja está muito doce.
examples.translation: This orange juice is very sweet.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: gentle, pleasant, and kind.

examples.text: Ela tem um sorriso doce e acolhedor.
examples.translation: She has a sweet and welcoming smile.

faults.quote: /tɕʰi.ɡwa.ɰi.s͈a/
faults.why: Wrong tensification in IPA: 의사 does not tensify to [s͈a]; 과 tensifies to [k͈wa].

faults.quote: use the shorter version '치과 선생님'
faults.why: '치과 선생님' is actually longer than '치과의사', and is a title of address.

notes: Compound of 치과 (dentistry/dental clinic) and 의사 (doctor); usually written with a space as 치과 의사.
When addressing a dentist directly, use 의사 선생님 or 치과 선생님 rather than 치과의사.

senses.definition: A doctor who treats teeth and gums.

examples.text: 치과의사는 정기적인 검진이 중요하다고 말했습니다.
examples.translation: The dentist said that regular checkups are important.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'mind / intelligence' (e.g., 머리가 좋다).

faults.quote: (position) The top, upper end, or initial part
faults.why: Less common spatial sense taking the place of the essential 'mind/brains' sense.

faults.quote: This word can also metaphorically mean the 'top' or 'beginning'
faults.why: Merely restates sense 2 instead of giving useful usage advice.

notes: While 머리 is commonly used for both 'head' and 'hair' (especially hairstyle), use 머리카락 to refer specifically to strands of hair.

senses.definition: The top part of the body that contains the eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and brain.

examples.text: 머리가 아파요.
examples.translation: I have a headache.

senses.definition: The hair that grows on a person's head.

examples.text: 오늘 머리를 잘랐어요.
examples.translation: I got my hair cut today.

senses.definition: A person's ability to think, learn, and understand.

examples.text: 그 친구는 머리가 정말 좋아요.
examples.translation: That friend is really smart.

faults.why: Fails to mention that '분' as a counter for people takes native Korean numbers.

notes: With 'minute', use Sino-Korean numbers (일 분, 십 분). With 'person', use native Korean numbers (한 분, 두 분).
As a counter for people, 분 is the honorific equivalent of 명.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.

examples.text: 10분 후에 만나요.
examples.translation: Let's meet in 10 minutes.

senses.definition: A polite noun or counter used to refer to people respectfully.

examples.text: 어떤 분을 찾으세요?
examples.translation: Who are you looking for?

faults.quote: Even though these two meanings are written the same in Korean
faults.why: Stating that homonyms are written the same is unnecessary filler.

notes: Like English 'leg', Sense 1 is also used for the legs of furniture (such as a table or chair).

senses.definition: The lower limb of a person or animal used for standing and walking, or a support for furniture.

examples.text: 다리를 다쳐서 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.translation: I hurt my leg, so I need to go to the hospital.

senses.definition: A structure built to cross over a river, road, or valley.

examples.text: 한강에 아주 큰 다리가 있어요.
examples.translation: There is a very large bridge over the Han River.

faults.quote: Cansado functions as an adjective meaning tired, but it can also describe
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the essential ser/estar distinction for learners.

notes: Use with 'estar' to mean 'tired' (Estoy cansado) and with 'ser' to mean 'tiring' or 'tiresome' (Es un viaje muy cansado).
To say you are tired of something, use 'cansado de' (Estoy cansado de esperar).

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep, usually after physical or mental effort.

examples.text: Llego a casa muy cansado después de trabajar.
examples.translation: I get home very tired after working.

senses.definition: Causing fatigue, boredom, or annoyance because of being long, hard, or repetitive.

examples.text: El viaje en autobús fue muy cansado.
examples.translation: The bus trip was very tiring.

faults.quote: (nature) To make a short, high sound, usually said of birds.
faults.why: A bird singing is the same basic sense as singing, not a separate everyday meaning.

faults.quote: Cantar is used for people singing, but also for birds chirping
faults.why: Restates the senses; 'cantar la tetera' is not a standard Mexican expression.

notes: Also used for the sounds made by birds (los pájaros cantan), roosters (el gallo canta), and crickets.

senses.definition: To make musical sounds with the voice.

examples.text: Me gusta cantar en la regadera.
examples.translation: I like to sing in the shower.

examples.text: Los pájaros empiezan a cantar al amanecer.
examples.translation: The birds start singing at dawn.

faults.quote: That which costs a lot of money.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('that which') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: 'caro' can also mean 'dear' in an emotional sense (e.g., 'el precio más caro'
faults.why: 'El precio más caro' refers to high cost, not emotional affection.

notes: The opposite of 'caro' is 'barato' (cheap).
Often used as an adverb with 'costar' or 'salir': 'Me salió muy caro' (It cost me a lot).

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: Este coche es muy caro.
examples.translation: This car is very expensive.

examples.text: Los boletos de avión son caros en diciembre.
examples.translation: Plane tickets are expensive in December.

faults.quote: (envy) Wanting something that another person has.
faults.why: Directly contradicts note[0]; in Spanish, wanting another's possessions is 'envidioso', not 'celoso'.

notes: Use 'celoso' for romantic or personal jealousy (fear of losing someone's affection). To mean wanting what someone else has, use 'envidioso' or 'tener envidia'.

senses.definition: Unhappy or worried because you think someone you love might prefer someone else.

examples.text: Se puso celoso cuando ella habló con su compañero.
examples.translation: He got jealous when she talked to her classmate.

faults.quote: or to switch off a device.
faults.why: Switching off a device in Mexican Spanish is 'apagar', not 'cerrar'.

corrected.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to lock
notes: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie) in the present tense: cierro, cierras, cierra, cerramos, cierran.
Also used for turning off a water faucet or gas valve (cerrar la llave).

senses.definition: To move something, such as a door or lid, so that an opening is covered or blocked.

examples.text: Cierra la puerta cuando salgas de la casa.
examples.translation: Close the door when you leave the house.

senses.definition: To fasten a door, lock, or container, especially with a key.

examples.text: No olvides cerrar el coche con llave.
examples.translation: Don't forget to lock the car.

senses.definition: Of a business, store, or public place: to stop operating for the day or permanently.

examples.text: El banco cierra a las cuatro de la tarde.
examples.translation: The bank closes at four in the afternoon.

faults.quote: /tɯʎʎida/
faults.why: Wrong initial consonant: ㅌ is aspirated /tʰ/, not plain /t/.

faults.quote: To be not the same as another; to differ.
faults.why: Colloquial misuse for 다르다; teaches a non-standard sense that contradicts note[0].

corrected.shortGloss: to be wrong, to be incorrect
notes: Usually used in the past tense (틀렸다) to mean something is wrong or incorrect: 답이 틀렸어요 (The answer is wrong).
Do not confuse with 다르다 (to be different). Although native speakers casually say 틀리다 to mean 'different', this is considered non-standard.

senses.definition: To be incorrect, mistaken, or not right.

examples.text: 제 답이 틀렸어요.
examples.translation: My answer is wrong.

examples.text: 전화번호가 틀린 것 같아요.
examples.translation: I think the phone number is wrong.

faults.quote: to be; to equal
faults.why: 'to equal' is not in the senses and is unnatural for A2.

notes: Unlike regular verbs, 이다 is a copula (predicative particle) that attaches directly to a noun with no space.
In polite speech, it becomes 이에요 after a consonant (학생이에요) and 예요 after a vowel (사과예요). The formal polite form is 입니다.

senses.definition: To be a specified person or thing.

examples.text: 저는 학생입니다.
examples.translation: I am a student.

examples.text: 이것은 사과예요.
examples.translation: This is an apple.

faults.why: Loving people and loving things like music are shades of one meaning.

notes: Carries a much stronger and deeper emotional weight than 좋아하다 (to like).

senses.definition: To feel deep affection or passion for a person or thing.

examples.text: 나는 내 가족을 진심으로 사랑합니다.
examples.translation: I truly love my family.

examples.text: 그는 음악을 정말 사랑해요.
examples.translation: He really loves music.

faults.quote: /ɡuɾiwohada/
faults.why: Wrong vowels: ㅡ is /ɯ/ (not /u/) and 워 is /wʌ/ (not /wo/).

faults.quote: 고향에 계신 부모님을 그리워하다.
faults.why: Dictionary infinitive phrase instead of a natural conjugated sentence.
Should contrast with the adjective 그립다, which A2 learners confuse with 그리워하다.

notes: Takes the object marker -을/를. Unlike the adjective 그립다 (which mainly expresses first-person longing with -이/가), 그리워하다 is an active verb and can also describe a third person missing someone or something.

senses.definition: To feel sad because someone or something is absent; to long for.

examples.text: 그는 고향에 계신 부모님을 그리워해요.
examples.translation: He misses his parents back in his hometown.

faults.quote: Being accurate and without any errors.
faults.why: Participle phrase instead of an infinitive verb definition (affects all senses).

faults.quote: 맞다 has several common meanings depending on context
faults.why: Merely restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage guidance.

corrected.shortGloss: to be correct; to fit; to be hit
notes: Frequently used as 맞아요 ('That's right') in everyday conversation to agree with someone.
In the sense 'to fit or suit', it takes the particle -에 or -한테/에게.

senses.definition: To be accurate, true, or without error.

examples.text: 그 사람이 한 말은 다 맞아요.
examples.translation: Everything that person said is right.

senses.definition: To be the right size, shape, or style for someone or something.

examples.text: 이 옷은 저한테 아주 잘 맞아요.
examples.translation: These clothes fit me very well.

senses.definition: To receive a physical blow, or to get caught in rain or snow.

examples.text: 아이가 장난을 치다가 혼나서 맞았어요.
examples.translation: The child got scolded and spanked for messing around.

faults.quote: to throw; to drop; to cast
faults.why: 'to cast' is not covered in the senses; 'to drop' is a misleading translation.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'werfen' meaning to cast or drop
faults.why: Tells learner not to confuse the word with itself; misses stem vowel change e -> i.

faults.quote: To let something fall or drop carelessly, or to discard something.
faults.why: 'werfen' does not mean 'to let fall' (fallen lassen); throwing into a bin is sense 0.

notes: Strong verb with vowel change in the present tense: du wirfst, er wirft; past: warf, hat geworfen.

senses.definition: To send something through the air with a quick movement of the hand and arm, or to put something somewhere quickly.

examples.text: Er wirft den Ball über den Zaun.
examples.translation: He throws the ball over the fence.

examples.text: Sie wirft das Papier in den Mülleimer.
examples.translation: She throws the paper into the trash can.

senses.definition: To direct a look at someone or something, or to project light or a shadow.

examples.text: Kannst du bitte kurz einen Blick darauf werfen?
examples.translation: Can you please take a quick look at this?

faults.why: Missing essential A1/A2 note on the highly irregular present-tense conjugation (ich/er weiß).

notes: Irregular verb: ich weiß, du weißt, er weiß, wir wissen; past: wusste, hat gewusst.
Use 'wissen' for knowing facts or information (often followed by a clause like 'wo', 'wann', 'ob', 'dass'). Use 'kennen' for being familiar with people, places, or things.

senses.definition: To have information or a fact in your mind; to be aware of something.

examples.text: Ich weiß nicht, wie spät es ist.
examples.translation: I don't know what time it is.

examples.text: Weißt du, wo mein Schlüssel ist?
examples.translation: Do you know where my key is?

faults.quote: To claim or assert something, often used when doubting the speaker.
faults.why: Subjective modal use with perfect infinitive is B2/C1 grammar, far too advanced for A2.
Should mention the irregular singular forms (ich/er will) and that 'möchten' is more polite.

notes: Modal verb with irregular singular forms: ich will, du willst, er will; past: wollte, hat gewollt.
For polite requests (like ordering food), use 'ich möchte' (I would like) instead of 'ich will', which sounds demanding.
Do not confuse with the English false friend 'will': the German future tense uses 'werden', not 'wollen'.
When the direction or place is clear, the main motion verb can be omitted: 'Ich will nach Hause' (I want [to go] home).

senses.definition: To have a strong wish, intention, or plan to do or have something.

examples.text: Ich will ein neues Fahrrad kaufen.
examples.translation: I want to buy a new bicycle.

examples.text: Sie will heute nicht zur Arbeit gehen.
examples.translation: She does not want to go to work today.

faults.quote: To write one's name on a document to show agreement or ownership.
faults.why: In everyday German, 'to sign' is 'unterschreiben'; 'zeichnen' for signing is formal bureaucratic jargon.

faults.quote: Sie muss das Dokument mit ihrem Namen zeichnen.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing; a native speaker would say 'das Dokument unterschreiben'.

notes: Use 'zeichnen' for drawing lines with a pencil, pen, or chalk. Use 'malen' when painting with a brush and colors, or when children draw/color a picture.
Because the stem ends in -chn, an extra -e- is added before -st and -t: du zeichnest, er zeichnet, gezeichnet.

senses.definition: To make a picture of something using a pencil, pen, or similar tool.

examples.text: In meiner Freizeit zeichne ich gerne Porträts.
examples.translation: I like to draw portraits in my free time.

faults.quote: To have a particular name.
faults.why: Defines the reflexive 's'appeler' without noting it, and misses the transitive meaning 'to name'.

corrected.shortGloss: to call; to phone; to name
notes: Doubles the 'l' before a silent 'e' (j'appelle, ils appellent), pronounced /ɛl/, vs. nous appelons.
Reflexive s'appeler means 'to be called': Comment tu t'appelles ? (What is your name?).

senses.definition: To contact someone by telephone, or to summon a service.

examples.text: Je vais appeler un taxi pour rentrer.
examples.translation: I am going to call a taxi to go home.

senses.definition: To call out to someone loudly so that they come or pay attention.

examples.text: J'appelle mon chat pour qu'il rentre.
examples.translation: I'm calling my cat so he comes inside.

senses.definition: To give a name to someone or something; (reflexive s'appeler) to have a particular name.

examples.text: Comment tu t'appelles ?
examples.translation: What is your name?

faults.why: Learners need the contrast with 'amener' (used for people and animals, vs. 'apporter' for things).

notes: Used for things you can carry (apporter un gâteau); for people or animals, use amener instead.
Opposes emporter, which means to take something away from a place.

senses.definition: To carry an object to a place or to someone.

examples.text: Tu peux apporter un gâteau pour la fête ?
examples.translation: Can you bring a cake for the party?

senses.definition: To provide or produce something useful, such as help, proof, or a change.

examples.text: Cette solution va apporter un vrai changement.
examples.translation: This solution will bring a real change.

faults.quote: /a.pʁɑ̃d/
faults.why: Wrong standard IPA: missing final /ʁ/; standard citation form is /a.pʁɑ̃dʁ/.

notes: Conjugates like prendre (j'apprends, nous apprenons, ils apprennent; past participle: appris).
Followed by à + infinitive: apprendre à nager (to learn/teach how to swim). With an indirect object (apprendre quelque chose à quelqu'un), it means 'to teach'.

senses.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill by studying or practicing, or to hear news.

examples.text: Je veux apprendre à parler français.
examples.translation: I want to learn to speak French.

senses.definition: To help someone else gain knowledge or a skill.

examples.text: Il m'a appris à jouer de la guitare.
examples.translation: He taught me how to play the guitar.

faults.quote: To be taken into custody by the police.
faults.why: Defines the passive ('to be arrested') instead of the active transitive meaning ('to arrest').

notes: Takes de + infinitive to mean 'to stop doing something' (arrêter de fumer).
Use the reflexive s'arrêter when a person or vehicle comes to a stop (Le bus s'arrête ici).

senses.definition: To stop doing something, or to cause someone or something to stop moving or working.

examples.text: Il faut arrêter de parler pendant le cours.
examples.translation: You must stop talking during class.

senses.definition: (of the police) To take someone into custody.

examples.text: La police a décidé d'arrêter le voleur.
examples.translation: The police decided to arrest the thief.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'arriver à + infinitive' (to manage to do something).

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive; to happen; to manage (to)
notes: Uses être as its auxiliary verb in compound tenses (Je suis arrivé(e) hier).

senses.definition: To reach a place at the end of a journey, or to come.

examples.text: Nous allons arriver à la gare dans dix minutes.
examples.translation: We are going to arrive at the station in ten minutes.

senses.definition: To take place, especially without being planned.

examples.text: Qu'est-ce qui va arriver maintenant ?
examples.translation: What is going to happen now?

senses.definition: (with à + infinitive or y) To succeed in doing something, especially after trying.

examples.text: Je n'arrive pas à ouvrir cette porte.
examples.translation: I can't manage to open this door.

faults.quote: /pov/
faults.why: Missing the final /ʁ/ in standard French pronunciation (/povʁ/).

notes: Before a noun (e.g., 'un pauvre homme'), 'pauvre' means unfortunate or pitiful; after a noun (e.g., 'un homme pauvre'), it means lacking money.

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions.

examples.text: Cette famille est pauvre et a besoin d'aide.
examples.translation: This family is poor and needs help.

senses.definition: Deserving pity or sympathy.

examples.text: Le pauvre chat a perdu son chemin sous la pluie.
examples.translation: The poor cat lost its way in the rain.

faults.quote: payer le garcon
faults.why: Missing cedilla in 'garçon' and missing note on stem-changing conjugation (je paie / je paye).

notes: Used without a preposition before the item bought ('payer l'addition' = to pay for the bill).
In the present tense, the 'y' can change to 'i' before a silent 'e' (je paie or je paye).

senses.definition: To give money in exchange for goods or services.

examples.text: Je vais payer par carte bancaire.
examples.translation: I am going to pay by bank card.

senses.definition: To pay for food, a drink, or a gift for someone else.

examples.text: Laisse-moi te payer un café.
examples.translation: Let me buy you a coffee.

faults.quote: To use your mind; to have an opinion.
faults.why: Lumps together two distinct basic meanings (believing an opinion vs. thinking about something).

corrected.shortGloss: to think; to believe; to intend
notes: Use 'penser à' for having someone or something in mind ('Je pense à toi'), and 'penser de' when asking for an opinion ('Que penses-tu de ce film ?').

senses.definition: To have a particular opinion or belief.

examples.text: Je pense qu'il a raison.
examples.translation: I think he is right.

senses.definition: To use the mind to consider or remember someone or something.

examples.text: Je pense souvent à mes vacances.
examples.translation: I often think about my holidays.

senses.definition: To have the intention to do something (followed by an infinitive).

examples.text: Je pense partir demain matin.
examples.translation: I plan to leave tomorrow morning.

faults.quote: Perdre is used both when you misplace an object and when
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses defined right below.
Missing the common A2 meaning 'to waste' (perdre son temps).

notes: The reflexive form 'se perdre' means 'to get lost'.

senses.definition: To no longer have something, or to be unable to find it.

examples.text: J'ai peur de perdre mes clés.
examples.translation: I am afraid of losing my keys.

senses.definition: To fail to win a game, match, or competition.

examples.text: Notre équipe risque de perdre le match.
examples.translation: Our team might lose the match.

senses.definition: To fail to make good use of time or an opportunity.

examples.text: Dépêche-toi, on perd du temps !
examples.translation: Hurry up, we're wasting time!

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense 'young / little' for children or siblings (e.g. petit frère).
Should give the feminine form 'petite' where the final 't' is pronounced.

notes: Placed before the noun it modifies (e.g., 'un petit chien').
The final 't' is silent in the masculine ('petit' /pə.ti/) but pronounced in the feminine ('petite' /pə.tit/).

senses.definition: Of a size that is less than normal or usual.

examples.text: J'ai un petit chat noir.
examples.translation: I have a small black cat.

senses.definition: Of a person: not tall.

examples.text: Il est plus petit que son frère.
examples.translation: He is shorter than his brother.

senses.definition: Of a child or sibling: young or younger.

examples.text: Mon petit frère a cinq ans.
