faults.quote: it can also mean 'still' (e.g., 'Você sempre mora lá?'
faults.why: False claim; 'sempre' means 'always' in that sentence, not 'still'.

faults.quote: always; still; after all
faults.why: Includes false meaning 'still' and European/advanced sense 'after all' missing from senses.

notes: Usually placed before the main verb (e.g., 'Eu sempre acordo cedo'), or at the end of the sentence for emphasis.
Combine with 'que' ('sempre que') to mean 'whenever' or 'every time that'.

senses.definition: At all times, or on every occasion.

examples.text: Eu sempre acordo cedo.
examples.translation: I always wake up early.

examples.text: Ela está sempre sorrindo.
examples.translation: She is always smiling.

faults.quote: I will sit in the chair.
faults.why: Unnatural English preposition and tense; 'I'm going to sit on the chair' is natural.

notes: Can also be used reflexively ('sentar-se'), though in everyday Brazilian Portuguese the pronoun is usually dropped.
Do not confuse with 'sentir' (to feel).

senses.definition: To rest the body in an upright position on a chair or other surface.

examples.text: Eu vou sentar na cadeira.
examples.translation: I'm going to sit on the chair.

senses.definition: To place someone in a sitting position.

examples.text: Ela sentou a criança no banco.
examples.translation: She sat the child down on the bench.

faults.quote: you always use the verb 'sentir' (to feel) followed by the noun 'saudades' (plural).
faults.why: False: singular 'saudade' is equally common, and 'ter saudades' or 'estar com saudades' are too.

notes: Followed by the preposition 'de' when naming who or what you miss (e.g., 'sentir saudades de casa').
Can be used with singular 'saudade' or plural 'saudades', and often with 'ter' or 'estar com' instead of 'sentir'.

senses.definition: To feel longing or nostalgia for someone who is absent or something in the past.

examples.text: Eu sinto muitas saudades da minha família.
examples.translation: I miss my family very much.

examples.text: Nós sentimos saudades dos tempos de escola.
examples.translation: We miss our school days.

faults.why: Missing essential A1/A2 uses of 'ser': telling time/dates and permanent locations.

faults.quote: Use 'estar' instead for temporary states, locations, or conditions
faults.why: Misleading: fixed locations (buildings, cities) and event locations take 'ser', not 'estar'.

faults.quote: to be from
faults.why: 'From' translates the preposition 'de', not the verb 'ser' itself.

notes: Highly irregular verb (present: 'sou, é, somos, são'; past: 'fui, foi, fomos, foram').
Used for permanent traits, identity, origin, time, and fixed or event locations; use 'estar' for temporary states and movable locations.

senses.definition: To have a given identity, profession, or permanent quality.

examples.text: Eu sou brasileiro.
examples.translation: I am Brazilian.

examples.text: Este carro é azul.
examples.translation: This car is blue.

senses.definition: Used with 'de' to indicate origin, possession, or material.

examples.text: Ela é de São Paulo.
examples.translation: She is from São Paulo.

senses.definition: To indicate the time, day, or date.

examples.text: Hoje é segunda-feira.
examples.translation: Today is Monday.

examples.text: São duas horas.
examples.translation: It is two o'clock.

senses.definition: To be permanently located in a place, or to take place somewhere.

examples.text: A festa vai ser na minha casa.
examples.translation: The party is going to be at my house.

faults.quote: That which makes little or no noise.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun phrase ('That which...') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: The electric car is very silent.
faults.why: Unnatural English collocation; in English a car is 'very quiet', not 'very silent'.

faults.quote: Used for things or people that do not produce sound.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or pronunciation help (such as metaphony in plural/feminine).

notes: The stressed 'o' is pronounced closed (/o/) in the masculine singular ('silencioso'), but open (/ɔ/) in the feminine ('silenciosa') and plurals.

senses.definition: Making little or no noise; having no sound.

examples.text: O carro elétrico é muito silencioso.
examples.translation: The electric car is very quiet.

faults.quote: /ˈniɡ.dɨ/
faults.why: In Polish, 'n' before 'i' is palatalized to /ɲ/: /ˈɲiɡ.dɨ/.

faults.quote: At any time (used in questions or after certain conjunctions
faults.why: False sense: 'nigdy' means 'never', not 'ever' (which is 'kiedykolwiek').

faults.quote: Czy byłeś kiedykolwiek w Warszawie?
faults.why: Example uses 'kiedykolwiek' instead of the headword 'nigdy'.

notes: Requires a negated verb with 'nie' in Polish (double negation), e.g., 'nigdy nie wiem' (I never know).

senses.definition: At no time in the past or future; on no occasion.

examples.text: Nigdy nie zapomnę tego dnia.
examples.translation: I will never forget this day.

faults.why: Missing common everyday senses: low in value/amount (prices, temperature) and low in pitch (voice).

notes: Used both for people who are short in height and for things that are low. Its opposite is 'wysoki' (tall, high).

senses.definition: Of a person: having little height.

examples.text: Mój brat jest bardzo niski.
examples.translation: My brother is very short.

senses.definition: Of an object or place: having little height, or close to the ground.

examples.text: To krzesło jest bardzo niskie.
examples.translation: This chair is very low.

senses.definition: Below average in amount, level, value, or intensity.

examples.text: Zimą temperatury są tu bardzo niskie.
examples.translation: In winter, temperatures are very low here.

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: deep in pitch.

examples.text: Ten aktor ma niski głos.
examples.translation: This actor has a low voice.

faults.quote: Note that 'noc' is feminine. You will see its ending change
faults.why: Restates gender and basic Polish case inflection; 'dobranoc' is a separate compound, not a case form.

notes: Feminine noun ending in a consonant. Common time expressions include 'w nocy' (at night) and 'nocą' (by night).

senses.definition: The period of darkness between sunset and sunrise.

examples.text: Noc jest bardzo ciemna.
examples.translation: The night is very dark.

examples.text: Pracuję w nocy.
examples.translation: I work at night.

faults.quote: leg
faults.why: The note and shortGloss say 'noga' also means 'foot' (human), but sense 0 omits 'foot'.

notes: In everyday Polish, 'noga' often refers to the foot as well as the whole leg (e.g. when talking about shoes), whereas 'stopa' is specifically the anatomical foot.

senses.definition: The lower limb of a human or animal, including the foot, used for standing and walking.

examples.text: Boli mnie noga.
examples.translation: My leg hurts.

senses.definition: A vertical support of a piece of furniture, such as a table or chair.

examples.text: Stół ma złamaną nogę.
examples.translation: The table has a broken leg.

faults.quote: To press an object closely against yourself.
faults.why: Hugging a person and hugging an object are the same sense.
Should mention the common reflexive form 'przytulać się' (to cuddle/hug each other).

corrected.shortGloss: to hug; to cuddle; to embrace
notes: Imperfective verb; the perfective partner is 'przytulić'.
Often used reflexively as 'przytulać się' (to hug each other, or to cuddle up to someone: 'przytulać się do kogoś').

senses.definition: To hold someone or something close in your arms, especially to show affection.

examples.text: Dziecko lubi przytulać swoją mamę przed snem.
examples.translation: The child likes to hug their mother before bed.

faults.quote: To go bad or become unfit for eating or drinking.
faults.why: Intransitive 'go bad' requires the reflexive 'psuć się'; non-reflexive 'psuć' is transitive.

faults.quote: Stare zabawki często się psują.
faults.why: Uses reflexive intransitive 'psuć się' under a transitive definition ('to damage something').

faults.quote: Deszcz może psuć nam cały dzień.
faults.why: Unnatural aspect; a single event ('whole day') takes perfective 'zepsuć', not imperfective 'psuć'.

faults.quote: ruin, spoill, mess up
faults.why: Typo 'spoill' in glosses.

corrected.shortGloss: to break; to spoil; to ruin
notes: Imperfective verb; the perfective partner is 'zepsuć'.
Used with 'się' ('psuć się'), it is intransitive and means 'to break down' (for machines) or 'to go bad / spoil' (for food or weather).

senses.definition: To damage something so that it stops working properly, or (with 'się') to stop working.

examples.text: Nie baw się tym telefonem, bo go psujesz.
examples.translation: Don't play with that phone, because you're breaking it.

examples.text: Stare samochody często się psują.
examples.translation: Old cars often break down.

senses.definition: To make a mood, plan, health, or relationship worse.

examples.text: Zła pogoda zawsze psuje mi humor.
examples.translation: Bad weather always ruins my mood.

senses.definition: (with 'się', of food) To go bad and become unfit to eat.

examples.text: Mleko szybko psuje się w upale.
examples.translation: Milk spoils quickly in the heat.

faults.quote: /ˈpsʂt͡ʂɔ.wa/
faults.why: Extra 's' in onset; 'pszczoła' is pronounced /ˈpʂt͡ʂɔ.wa/.

faults.quote: Pszczoła refers specifically to the honeybee or similar stinging flying insects
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to note pronunciation or contrast with 'osa' (wasp).

notes: Do not confuse with 'osa' (wasp) or 'trzmiel' (bumblebee).

senses.definition: A yellow-and-black flying insect that makes honey and can sting.

examples.text: Pszczoła zbiera nektar z kwiatów w ogrodzie.
examples.translation: A bee is gathering nectar from flowers in the garden.

faults.quote: Ptak is the general term for any creature with feathers and wings
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: The common diminutive is 'ptaszek' (little bird).

senses.definition: An animal with feathers, wings, and a beak that lays eggs and can usually fly.

examples.text: Ptak śpiewa w ogrodzie.
examples.translation: A bird is singing in the garden.

faults.quote: It is a diminutive of 'pudeło'
faults.why: Non-existent Polish word; the base noun is 'pudło' (a large box), not 'pudeło'.

notes: Originally a diminutive of 'pudło' (a large box), 'pudełko' is the standard everyday word for most boxes.
For a cardboard shipping or moving box, 'karton' is also very common.

senses.definition: A small or medium-sized container with flat sides, usually made of cardboard, plastic, or wood, used for storing things.

examples.text: Włożyłem buty do pudełka.
examples.translation: I put the shoes into the box.

faults.quote: Use it to describe a person who is feeling down or a
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a note on ser vs. estar is needed instead.

notes: Invariable for gender: takes the same form for masculine and feminine nouns (plural 'tristes').
Often used with 'estar' for a temporary feeling ('Ela está triste') and 'ser' for a sad thing or nature ('É uma história triste').

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling sorrow or unhappiness.

examples.text: Ela está muito triste hoje.
examples.translation: She is very sad today.

senses.definition: Causing a feeling of sorrow or gloom.

examples.text: O filme tem um final muito triste.
examples.translation: The movie has a very sad ending.

notes: In Portuguese, 'usar' is the standard verb for having clothes, shoes, glasses, or accessories on your body ('to wear'), whereas 'vestir' usually means 'to put on' or 'to dress'.

senses.definition: To employ an object, tool, or method for a purpose.

examples.text: Preciso usar o computador para trabalhar.
examples.translation: I need to use the computer to work.

senses.definition: To have clothing, glasses, or an accessory on your body.

examples.text: Ela gosta de usar roupas confortáveis em casa.
examples.translation: She likes to wear comfortable clothes at home.

faults.quote: Can be used for physical spaces, objects, or even abstract feelings like
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage information.

faults.quote: empty, vacant, hollow
faults.why: 'Hollow' for a physical object is 'oco', not 'vazio'.

faults.quote: The parking lot was vacant.
faults.why: Unnatural English; 'empty' is normal for a parking lot.

notes: The feminine form is 'vazia'.

senses.definition: Containing nothing; not occupied by anyone or anything.

examples.text: A geladeira está vazia.
examples.translation: The fridge is empty.

examples.text: O estacionamento estava vazio.
examples.translation: The parking lot was empty.

senses.definition: Lacking substance, meaning, or sincerity.

examples.text: Ele me deu uma promessa vazia.
examples.translation: He gave me an empty promise.

faults.quote: Something that has been owned or used for a long time, often
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('Something that...').

faults.quote: old; ancient
faults.why: Includes 'ancient', which is absent from the senses and misleading (see note 1).

notes: When referring to people, 'velho' can sound blunt or disrespectful; 'idoso' (elderly) is more polite.
Do not confuse with 'antigo', which means 'ancient', 'old-fashioned', or 'former' (as in 'meu antigo trabalho', my former job).

senses.definition: Having lived or existed for a long time.

examples.text: O meu avô é um homem muito velho.
examples.translation: My grandfather is a very old man.

senses.definition: Of an object: having been owned or used for a long time, often worn out.

examples.text: Eu comprei um carro velho.
examples.translation: I bought an old car.

faults.quote: Unlike 'comprar' (to buy), 'vender' focuses on the action of passing an
faults.why: Merely defines the word again by contrasting it with 'buy'.

faults.quote: In Brazil, you will often hear 'vender' used in retail contexts just
faults.why: Pure filler stating that 'sell' is used in retail like in English.

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: Eles querem vender o carro antigo.
examples.translation: They want to sell the old car.

examples.text: Aquela loja vende roupas muito bonitas.
examples.translation: That shop sells very beautiful clothes.

faults.quote: In the present tense, it is often omitted in casual speech
faults.why: Polish drops subject pronouns, not the verb 'być' (except when replaced by 'to').
Missing the essential A1/A2 use as the future auxiliary (będę, będziesz, etc.).
Combining state/feeling with physical location while splitting from identity is unnatural.

notes: Irregular verb. Present tense: jestem, jesteś, jest, jesteśmy, jesteście, są.
Noun predicates (like professions or nationalities) after 'być' take the instrumental case (e.g., 'Jestem lekarzem'), while adjectives take the nominative ('Jestem zmęczony').

senses.definition: To have a particular identity, quality, or state.

examples.text: On jest lekarzem.
examples.translation: He is a doctor.

examples.text: Dzisiaj jestem zmęczony.
examples.translation: I am tired today.

senses.definition: To be in a particular place, or to exist.

examples.text: Jestem w domu.
examples.translation: I am at home.

senses.definition: Used in the future tense (będę, będziesz, etc.) with an imperfective verb to talk about the future.

examples.text: Jutro będę pracować.
examples.translation: I will be working tomorrow.

faults.why: Polish learners need the aspect pair (imperfective całować / perfective pocałować).

notes: Imperfective verb (present: całuję, całujesz). The perfective pair is 'pocałować'.
Often used with the reflexive pronoun 'się' (całować się) to mean 'to kiss each other'.

senses.definition: To touch someone with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or greeting.

examples.text: Ona lubi całować swojego chłopaka w policzek.
examples.translation: She likes to kiss her boyfriend on the cheek.

faults.quote: Cebula is a staple vegetable in Polish cooking
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia and a far-fetched 'bułka' comparison provide no useful linguistic guidance.

senses.definition: A round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste.

examples.text: Kroję cebulę do zupy.
examples.translation: I am cutting an onion for the soup.

faults.quote: Use the genitive case after 'chcieć' when you want to express wanting an object
faults.why: Misleading: concrete countable nouns regularly take the accusative (e.g. 'chcę nową książkę').

notes: Present tense: chcę, chcesz, chce, chcemy, chcecie, chcą. Imperfective verb (perfective: zechcieć).
Followed by an infinitive ('chcę odpocząć'), the genitive for uncountable or abstract things ('chcę spokoju'), or the accusative for specific countable items ('chcę tę książkę').
The impersonal reflexive phrase 'chce mi się' (+ infinitive or genitive) is very common and means 'I feel like' (e.g., 'Chce mi się spać' — I feel like sleeping).

senses.definition: To have a desire for something or a wish to do something.

examples.text: Chcę dzisiaj odpocząć.
examples.translation: I want to rest today.

examples.text: Czy chcesz napić się herbaty?
examples.translation: Do you want to have some tea?

faults.quote: While 'lopen' translates to 'walk' in the sense of moving on foot,
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.
Missing irregular principal parts (liep, gelopen) and false-friend warning with German/Flemish 'run'.

corrected.shortGloss: to walk; to run (of a machine); to go
notes: Irregular verb: liep, heeft/is gelopen. Takes 'zijn' when a destination or route is given (Ik ben naar huis gelopen) and 'hebben' for the activity itself.
In the Netherlands, 'lopen' means to walk; for running, use 'rennen' or 'hardlopen'. (In Belgium, 'lopen' often means to run, like German 'laufen'.)

senses.definition: To move on foot at a normal pace.

examples.text: Ik loop elke dag naar mijn werk.
examples.translation: I walk to work every day.

senses.definition: To function, be in operation, or progress, such as a machine, a clock, or an event.

examples.text: De klok loopt precies op tijd.
examples.translation: The clock runs right on time.

senses.definition: To extend or lead from one place to another, such as a road, river, or line.

examples.text: Er loopt een smal pad door het bos.
examples.translation: A narrow path runs through the woods.

faults.why: Being lazy by nature and feeling lazy/sluggish in the heat are one sense.

faults.quote: Lui can describe both a person who dislikes work and a physical
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions without adding grammatical or usage help.

notes: Inflected form: 'luie' (een luie kat, de luie mensen).

senses.definition: Unwilling to work, make an effort, or be active.

examples.text: Hij is te lui om de trap te nemen.
examples.translation: He is too lazy to take the stairs.

examples.text: Door de warmte voel ik me vandaag erg lui.
examples.translation: Because of the heat, I feel very lazy today.

faults.quote: Clearly audible or spoken with force.
faults.why: 'Luid' means loud, not clear; 'clear' comes from 'duidelijk' in the idiom 'luid en duidelijk'.

faults.quote: clear, audible, loud
faults.why: 'Luid' does not mean 'clear'.

faults.quote: Hij sprak in een luid en duidelijk stemgeluid.
faults.why: 'In een ... stemgeluid' is unnatural Dutch; 'luid en duidelijk' is used adverbially.

notes: In everyday spoken Dutch, 'hard' is much more common than 'luid' for loud sounds or voices (De muziek staat te hard; Praat niet zo hard). 'Luid' is somewhat more formal or used in fixed phrases like 'luid en duidelijk' (loud and clear).

senses.definition: Producing a lot of sound; not quiet.

examples.text: We hoorden een luide knal op straat.
examples.translation: We heard a loud bang in the street.

examples.text: Hij was luid aan het telefoneren in de trein.
examples.translation: He was talking loudly on the phone on the train.

faults.why: Lacks the everyday modal particle sense softening imperatives ('Ga maar zitten', 'Kijk maar').

faults.quote: As a conjunction, 'maar' is used to connect two clauses
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions of the two senses.

notes: As a conjunction ('but'), 'maar' does not change the word order of the clause that follows it.
With imperatives, 'maar' is a very common particle that makes a command sound friendly, reassuring, or permissive: 'Kom maar binnen!' (Come on in!), 'Laat maar' (Never mind / leave it).

senses.definition: Used to connect two statements or ideas when the second contrasts with the first.

examples.text: Het weer is mooi, maar ik moet vandaag werken.
examples.translation: The weather is nice, but I have to work today.

senses.definition: No more than a certain amount, number, or degree.

examples.text: Ik heb maar vijf euro bij me.
examples.translation: I only have five euros with me.

senses.definition: Used with imperatives to soften a command, give permission, or encourage someone.

examples.text: Ga maar lekker zitten.
examples.translation: Go ahead and have a seat.

faults.quote: Used when you have multiple options and need to pick the best
faults.why: Restates the definition; replace with verb group/conjugation and particle usage (を).

corrected.shortGloss: to choose; to select; to pick
notes: A godan (Group 1) transitive verb (選ぶ → 選びます, 選んで) taking the particle を.
More common in everyday speech than the formal 選択する (せんたくする).

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want from a group of options.

examples.text: どのプレゼントを選びますか。
examples.translation: Which present will you choose?

examples.text: たくさんの中から一つを選ぶのは難しい。
examples.translation: It is difficult to choose one from many.

faults.quote: Used when someone encounters something unexpected that causes a reaction of surprise
faults.why: Restates the definition; replace with the particle it takes (に) and verb group.

corrected.shortGloss: to be surprised; to be startled
notes: An intransitive godan (Group 1) verb. The cause of surprise is marked with the particle に.
Slightly more formal than びっくりする, which is very common in casual conversation.

senses.definition: To feel sudden shock or surprise because of something unexpected.

examples.text: 突然のニュースに驚いた。
examples.translation: I was surprised by the sudden news.

faults.why: Missing everyday A1/A2 senses: to decide on (〜にする) and to wear accessories.

corrected.shortGloss: to do; to play; to wear; to decide on
notes: An irregular verb (する → します, して, した). Added directly to many nouns to form verbs, e.g., 勉強する (to study).
Used with を for accessories and items tied or put on the body (ネクタイをする), whereas 着る is for clothes worn on the upper/whole body.

senses.definition: To perform an action, task, or activity.

examples.text: 毎日宿題をする。
examples.translation: I do my homework every day.

senses.definition: To take part in a sport or game.

examples.text: 友達とテニスをする。
examples.translation: I play tennis with my friends.

senses.definition: To choose or decide on something (used with the particle に).

examples.text: 飲み物はコーヒーにします。
examples.translation: I'll have coffee to drink.

senses.definition: To put on or wear small items such as accessories, ties, or watches.

examples.text: 父は青いネクタイをしている。
examples.translation: My father is wearing a blue tie.

faults.why: Should mention its irregular imperative (くれ) or the polite equivalent くださる.

corrected.shortGloss: to give (to me); to do for me
notes: Used only when someone gives to you or your in-group (the giver takes が/は, the recipient takes に). When you give to others, use あげる; for superiors giving to you, use くださる.
Follows the -te form of a verb (〜てくれる) to show someone does an action as a favor for you. It is an ichidan (Group 2) verb, except its plain command form is くれ.

senses.definition: To give something to the speaker or someone close to the speaker.

examples.text: 友達がプレゼントをくれた。
examples.translation: My friend gave me a present.

senses.definition: Used after a verb in the -te form to show that someone does something as a favor for the speaker.

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれた。
examples.translation: My mother cooked for me.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (おぼえる) for a headword containing kanji.
Needs to explain that 覚えている (oboete iru) is used for the state 'to remember'.

corrected.shortGloss: to memorize; to remember; to learn
notes: To say you currently 'remember' something, use the -te iru form: 覚えている (おぼえている).
Do not confuse with 思い出す (おもいだす), which means to recall or bring back to mind something you had temporarily forgotten.

senses.definition: To commit information to memory, or (as 覚えている) to keep it in your memory.

examples.text: 新しい単語を覚えるのは難しい。
examples.translation: Memorizing new words is difficult.

examples.text: 彼の名前を覚えていますか。
examples.translation: Do you remember his name?

senses.definition: To acquire a new skill or habit through practice or experience.

examples.text: 仕事のやり方を早く覚えたい。
examples.translation: I want to learn how to do the job quickly.

faults.quote: Use cocinar for preparing and making food, whether on the stove...
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammar help; also inaccurate regarding uncooked food.

senses.definition: To prepare food by heating it so it is ready to eat.

examples.text: Me gusta cocinar sopa caliente los días de lluvia.
examples.translation: I like to cook hot soup on rainy days.

faults.quote: Used for any main meal, as well as the general act
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a contrast with 'almorzar' in Mexico is more helpful.

faults.quote: to have lunch, to dine
faults.why: 'To dine' usually implies evening dinner (cenar) in modern English, whereas 'comer' is midday.

notes: In Mexico, 'comer' refers to the main midday meal (lunch), whereas 'almorzar' usually refers to a hearty late-morning meal or brunch.

senses.definition: To put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.

examples.text: Voy a comer una manzana.
examples.translation: I am going to eat an apple.

senses.definition: To have lunch, the main afternoon meal of the day.

examples.text: Siempre comemos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.translation: We always have lunch at two in the afternoon.

faults.quote: To believe or accept something as true, especially a lie
faults.why: Figurative calque of English 'to buy (an excuse)', marginal for an A2 beginner.

faults.quote: Use comprar for any transaction where you exchange money for goods
faults.why: Restates the basic definition of 'to buy' without adding useful learner information.

notes: When saying who you are buying something for or from, use an indirect object pronoun (like 'le') and the preposition 'a': 'Le compré flores a mi mamá' (I bought flowers for my mom).

senses.definition: To obtain something by paying money for it.

examples.text: Voy al mercado a comprar fruta fresca para la semana.
examples.translation: I am going to the market to buy fresh fruit for the week.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'con' is a basic single-word preposition, not a multi-word expression.

faults.quote: Con is the primary way to say 'with' in Spanish.
faults.why: Restates the glosses and senses without adding new information.

notes: When 'con' is followed by 'mí' (me) or 'ti' (you), they combine into the single words 'conmigo' (with me) and 'contigo' (with you).
Used with nouns to form common expressions of manner, such as 'con cuidado' (carefully) or 'con ganas' (enthusiastically).

senses.definition: Used to show that people or things are together, or that something includes another thing.

examples.text: Voy al cine con mis amigos.
examples.translation: I am going to the movie theater with my friends.

senses.definition: Used to indicate the tool, object, or means used to do something.

examples.text: Escribo con un lápiz nuevo.
examples.translation: I write with a new pencil.

senses.definition: Used to indicate that someone or something has a particular feature, quality, or possession.

examples.text: Es una chica con mucho talento.
examples.translation: She is a girl with a lot of talent.

faults.why: Missing note on irregular first-person singular present form 'conozco' (used in the example).

notes: Irregular in the 'yo' form of the present tense: 'conozco'.
Use 'conocer' for being familiar with people or places, and 'saber' for knowing facts, information, or how to do something.
When the direct object is a person, always place the preposition 'a' before them (e.g., 'Conozco a Juan').

senses.definition: To have experience with or be familiar with a person, place, or thing.

examples.text: Conozco muy bien este barrio de la ciudad.
examples.translation: I know this neighborhood of the city very well.

senses.definition: To see and speak to someone for the first time, or to visit a place for the first time.

terms: to visit for the first time

examples.text: Hoy voy a conocer a los padres de mi novia.
examples.translation: Today I am going to meet my girlfriend's parents.

faults.quote: The primary verb for transfer of possession, equivalent to 'to give'
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding grammar or usage information.

faults.quote: Be careful to distinguish it from verbs of receiving (παίρνω).
faults.why: Generic filler; instead, the irregular aorist 'έδωσα' should be noted.

faults.quote: to give; to offer; to yield
faults.why: Includes 'to yield', which is not covered by the senses.
Missing common A2 meaning 'to take/sit an exam' (δίνω εξετάσεις) or hold an event.

corrected.shortGloss: to give; to offer; to take (an exam)
notes: Has an irregular simple past (aorist) stem: έδωσα (I gave), να δώσω.

senses.definition: To hand something over to someone else or transfer possession.

examples.text: Μου δίνεις το βιβλίο, σε παρακαλώ;
examples.translation: Will you give me the book, please?

senses.definition: To provide or offer something such as a result, opportunity, or payment.

examples.text: Αυτή η δουλειά δίνει καλό μισθό.
examples.translation: This job offers a good salary.

senses.definition: To sit or take an examination, or to give a performance.

examples.text: Αύριο δίνω εξετάσεις στα ελληνικά.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am taking an exam in Greek.

faults.quote: this verb is used both literally for physical embraces and metaphorically
faults.why: Mostly restates the two senses; need only mention the related noun αγκαλιά.

notes: Related to the noun η αγκαλιά (hug, embrace, one's arms).

senses.definition: To hold someone close in your arms to show love or affection.

examples.text: Της αρέσει να αγκαλιάζει τους φίλους της όταν τους συναντά.
examples.translation: She likes to hug her friends when she meets them.

senses.definition: To accept or support an idea, cause, or group enthusiastically.

examples.text: Η τοπική κοινωνία αγκάλιασε τη νέα πρωτοβουλία.
examples.translation: The local community embraced the new initiative.

faults.why: Missing note on irregular present conjugation (κλαίω, κλαις, κλαίει) and aorist (έκλαψα).

faults.quote: To feel deep sadness or regret about a situation.
faults.why: Mourning/lamenting is marginal or poetic for A2; primary everyday sense is sufficient.

notes: Conjugated with contracted endings in the present: κλαίω, κλαις, κλαίει, κλαίμε, κλαίτε, κλαίνε. The simple past (aorist) is έκλαψα.
Colloquially used to mean 'to laugh hard' (to cry with laughter).

senses.definition: To shed tears because of strong emotion, such as sadness, pain, or joy.

examples.text: Το παιδί κλαίει γιατί έχασε το παιχνίδι του.
examples.translation: The child is crying because he lost his toy.

faults.quote: /teˈlʲcno/
faults.why: Corrupt IPA containing /c/ instead of /o/; should be /te.liˈo.no/ or /teˈʎo.no/.

faults.quote: Τελειώσαμε το γάλα.
faults.why: For 'we ran out of milk', Greek naturally uses intransitive 'Μας τελείωσε το γάλα'.

corrected.shortGloss: to finish; to end; to run out
notes: Used both transitively ('to finish something') and intransitively ('to come to an end').
To say 'we ran out of X', use the intransitive 3rd person with an indirect object: μας τελείωσε το γάλα (literally 'the milk finished on us').

senses.definition: To complete an activity, or (of an event or period) to come to an end.

examples.text: Τελειώνω τη δουλειά μου στις πέντε.
examples.translation: I finish my work at five.

senses.definition: Of a supply or item: to be completely used up so that none is left.

examples.text: Μας τελείωσε το γάλα.
examples.translation: We have run out of milk.

faults.quote: /θiˈmamai/
faults.why: In Modern Greek 'αι' is pronounced /e/, so the IPA must be /θiˈmame/.
Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same everyday meaning 'to remember'.

notes: Takes passive endings (-μαι, -σαι, -ται, -όμαστε, -όσαστε, -ούνται) even though its meaning is active. The simple past (aorist) is θυμήθηκα.

senses.definition: To keep a person, fact, or event in your mind, or to bring it back into your thoughts.

examples.text: Θυμάμαι τα παιδικά μου χρόνια.
examples.translation: I remember my childhood years.

examples.text: Δεν θυμάμαι πού έβαλα τα κλειδιά μου.
examples.translation: I don't remember where I put my keys.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'to act / to play a role' (in movies, theater).

faults.quote: This verb is imperfective, meaning it describes an ongoing or habitual action.
faults.why: Explains what 'imperfective' means without giving the perfective counterparts (сыграть, поиграть).

corrected.shortGloss: to play (game, sport, instrument); to act (role)
notes: Use 'играть в' + accusative case for games or sports (e.g., играть в футбол — to play soccer).
Use 'играть на' + prepositional case for musical instruments (e.g., играть на гитаре — to play the guitar).
Imperfective; the perfective is сыграть (for a single game, piece, or role) or поиграть (to play for a while).

senses.definition: To take part in a game or sport, or to amuse oneself with toys.

examples.text: Мы любим играть в футбол по выходным.
examples.translation: We love to play soccer on weekends.

senses.definition: To make music on a musical instrument.

examples.text: Она умеет играть на пианино.
examples.translation: She knows how to play the piano.

senses.definition: To perform a role in a play or film.

examples.text: В этом фильме он играет главную роль.
examples.translation: He plays the main role in this movie.

faults.quote: To come to the end of something naturally, or for an event
faults.why: Intransitive 'to come to an end' is the reflexive verb заканчиваться, not заканчивать.

faults.quote: Фильм уже заканчивается.
faults.why: Uses the reflexive verb заканчиваться instead of the headword заканчивать.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective is закончить.

Takes a direct object in the accusative case, or an infinitive verb (e.g., заканчивать работать — to finish working). For an event ending by itself ('The movie is ending'), use the reflexive заканчиваться.

senses.definition: To bring an activity or task to an end.

examples.text: Я обычно заканчиваю работу в шесть часов.
examples.translation: I usually finish work at six o'clock.

senses.definition: To complete one's studies at a school or university.

examples.text: Она заканчивает университет в этом году.
examples.translation: She is graduating from university this year.

faults.quote: To be aware of a smell or to notice something.
faults.why: Using слышать for smells is colloquial/regional; A2 learners should learn чувствовать запах.
Missing the perfective counterpart услышать and the irregular II-conjugation pattern after ш.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective is услышать.
Belongs to the second conjugation despite ending in -ать (я слышу, ты слышишь, они слышат).
Слышать means to perceive sound with your ears ('to hear'), whereas слушать means to pay attention to sound ('to listen').

senses.definition: To perceive sound with your ears.

examples.text: Я слышу странный шум за стеной.
examples.translation: I hear a strange noise behind the wall.

senses.definition: To receive news or information about someone or something.

examples.text: Ты слышал последнюю новость?
examples.translation: Did you hear the latest news?

faults.quote: though you can also use живописать for painting in a more artistic
faults.why: Misleading: живописать is archaic/bookish; artists actually use писать (писа́ть маслом) for serious painting.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with писать, which means to write text rather
faults.why: False: писать IS used by artists to mean 'to paint' (писать картину маслом).

faults.quote: Художник любит рисовать пейзажи маслом.
faults.why: Professional oil painting by an artist is normally 'писать маслом', not 'рисовать маслом'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective is нарисовать.
Conjugates with the suffix -уй- in the present tense (я рисую, ты рисуешь, они рисуют).
In everyday speech, рисовать covers both drawing (with pencils or pens) and painting (with brushes and paints). Professional artists often use писать for painting in oils or watercolors.

senses.definition: To make a picture using a pencil, pen, crayons, or paints.

examples.text: Дети любят рисовать цветными карандашами.
examples.translation: Children love to draw with colored pencils.

examples.text: На уроке мы рисовали красками.
examples.translation: In class we painted with paints.

faults.quote: /ɐbʲnʲɪˈmatʲ/
faults.why: The /b/ is not palatalized before /nʲ/ in standard Russian; it is /ɐbnʲɪˈmatʲ/.

faults.quote: To include or contain something; to surround something.
faults.why: Archaic/poetic sense; modern Russian uses охватывать, not обнимать, for 'encompass'.

faults.quote: Его работа обнимает многие темы.
faults.why: Unnatural Russian; 'encompasses many topics' is 'охватывает многие темы', never 'обнимает'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective is обнять (which has an irregular future tense: я обниму, ты обнимешь).
For hugging each other mutually, use the reflexive verb обниматься.

senses.definition: To put your arms around someone and hold them close, especially to show affection.

examples.text: Мама крепко обнимает своих детей.
examples.translation: Mom hugs her children tightly.

faults.quote: /beˈdava/
faults.why: Wrong stress and vowel length; Turkish 'bedava' is /bedaːˈva/.

faults.quote: Used for things that cost no money. Don't confuse it with 'bedavaya'
faults.why: First sentence restates the gloss; 'bedavaya' is just the dative of Sense 2.

faults.quote: Evi resmen bedava fiyata sattı.
faults.why: 'Bedava fiyata' is unnatural; Turkish uses 'bedavaya' or 'yok pahasına' here.

notes: Unlike 'ücretsiz', which is more formal and common on signs, 'bedava' is the everyday spoken word. It is also used as an adverb ('bedava almak' — to get for free).

senses.definition: Not costing any money; provided without payment.

examples.text: Bu ürün bugün bedava.
examples.translation: This product is free today.

senses.definition: Sold or obtained at a very low price (especially in the dative, 'bedavaya').

examples.text: Bu arabayı neredeyse bedavaya aldık.
examples.translation: We bought this car for next to nothing.

faults.quote: /be.en.mek/
faults.why: Missing stress and wrong final consonant; should be /be.enˈmec/ or /beːnˈmec/.
Missing the crucial grammar note that 'beğenmek' takes the accusative case (-i).

faults.quote: [1] (approve) To approve of something; to consider something satisfactory.
faults.why: 'Kararımı beğendin mi?' is just liking a decision; oversplit from Sense 0.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case (-i): 'Filmi beğendim' (I liked the film).
Unlike 'sevmek' (to love, to be fond of), 'beğenmek' is about judging something to be good, attractive, or to your taste—such as clothes, food, a movie, or someone's work.

senses.definition: To find someone or something good, attractive, or to one's taste.

examples.text: Bu elbiseyi çok beğendim.
examples.translation: I liked this dress a lot.

examples.text: Yeni evinizi beğendiniz mi?
examples.translation: Do you like your new house?

faults.quote: /beклеˈmek/
faults.why: Contains Cyrillic characters 'кле' instead of IPA symbols.

faults.quote: and the dative case (-e / -a) when waiting at a place or waiting for an event
faults.why: False grammar rule: 'beklemek' takes the accusative (-i), and locative (-de) for places.

faults.quote: To stay until something happens or until a condition is met.
faults.why: Waiting for the rain to stop is exactly Sense 0 ('to wait for').

corrected.shortGloss: to wait (for); to expect; to guard
notes: Unlike English 'wait for', 'beklemek' is transitive and takes the accusative case (-i / -ı / -u / -ü): 'Seni bekliyorum' (I am waiting for you).

senses.definition: To stay in a place until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: Durakta otobüsü bekliyorum.
examples.translation: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.

examples.text: Yağmurun durmasını bekledik.
examples.translation: We waited for the rain to stop.

senses.definition: To think or believe that something will happen or someone will do something.

examples.text: Senden daha iyi bir sonuç bekliyordum.
examples.translation: I was expecting a better result from you.

senses.definition: To watch over and protect a place.

examples.text: Köpek bütün gece evi bekledi.
examples.translation: The dog guarded the house all night.

faults.quote: /belˈci/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'belki' has initial stress /ˈbelci/ in Turkish.

faults.quote: paired with 'de' or 'da' at the end of the clause for emphasis (belki de)
faults.why: In 'belki de', 'de' (never 'da') comes immediately after 'belki', not at clause end.

faults.quote: Belki is the everyday word for 'maybe' or 'perhaps'.
faults.why: Purely restates the gloss without adding useful information.

notes: Often followed directly by 'de' ('belki de') to mean 'perhaps' or 'for all we know': 'Belki de haklısın' (Maybe you're right).

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible but not certain.

examples.text: Belki yarın gelir.
examples.translation: Maybe he will come tomorrow.

faults.quote: Saçları tamamen beyazlamış.
faults.why: Uses the derived verb 'beyazlamak' (to turn white), not the adjective 'beyaz'.

faults.quote: Turkish primarily uses beyaz for the general color.
faults.why: Turkish also has the common native synonym 'ak', used in many fixed expressions.

faults.quote: The color of snow or milk.
faults.why: Defines the adjective as a noun ('The color of...').

faults.quote: Beyaz is the standard word for the color white.
faults.why: Filler note that merely restates the gloss.

notes: 'Beyaz' is the everyday word for white. Its synonym 'ak' appears mostly in set phrases and names, such as 'Akdeniz' (the Mediterranean Sea) or 'saçı sakalı ak' (with white hair and beard).

senses.definition: Having the color of snow or milk.

examples.text: Üzerinde beyaz bir gömlek vardı.
examples.translation: He was wearing a white shirt.

faults.quote: To make a shop, office, or facility accessible to visitors.
faults.why: Defines it transitively, but the example is intransitive and common reflexive 'sich öffnen' is unmentioned.

notes: In everyday spoken German, 'aufmachen' is much more common for physical objects like doors, windows, and bottles. 'Öffnen' is preferred in formal contexts, for shops, or on computers.
When something opens by itself, use the reflexive form 'sich öffnen' (Die Tür öffnet sich).

senses.definition: To move something such as a door, window, or container so that it is no longer closed; also used for digital files or accounts.

examples.text: Kannst du bitte das Fenster öffnen?
examples.translation: Can you please open the window?

senses.definition: Of a shop, office, or facility: to start doing business for the day, or to make a business open to customers.

examples.text: Die Bäckerei öffnet jeden Tag um sechs Uhr.
examples.translation: The bakery opens every day at six o'clock.

faults.quote: In colloquial speech, Germans frequently use 'häufig'
faults.why: 'Häufig' is actually slightly more formal/written than 'oft', not colloquial.
Missing the crucial irregular comparative 'öfter' (learners often wrongly say 'ofter').

notes: The comparative form ('more often') has an umlaut: 'öfter'. In everyday speech, 'öfter' is also frequently used to mean 'fairly often'.
In standard main clauses, 'oft' usually comes after the conjugated verb (Ich gehe oft...), unlike in English where it precedes the verb.

senses.definition: Many times; on many occasions.

examples.text: Ich gehe oft im Park spazieren.
examples.translation: I often go for a walk in the park.

examples.text: Wir sehen uns leider nicht sehr oft.
examples.translation: Unfortunately, we do not see each other very often.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'Ohne' is a preposition, not an 'expression'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'ohne' with 'und'.
faults.why: Nobody confuses 'ohne' with 'und'; note about 'ohne ... zu' or article omission is needed.

notes: 'Ohne' always takes the accusative case (e.g., ohne meinen Bruder). However, it is very often used without an article directly before a noun (ohne Zucker, ohne Brille).
With verbs, use the structure 'ohne ... zu' + infinitive to mean 'without doing something' (Er ging, ohne etwas zu sagen).

senses.definition: In the absence of someone or something; not having or using something.

examples.text: Ich trinke den Kaffee ohne Zucker.
examples.translation: I drink the coffee without sugar.

examples.text: Ohne meine Brille sehe ich nichts.
examples.translation: Without my glasses I can't see anything.

faults.quote: embarrassing; awkward; painful
faults.why: 'Painful' is archaic and not in the senses; misleads A2 learners.

faults.quote: Requiring a high degree of precision or meticulous attention to detail.
faults.why: C1/formal collocation ('peinlich genau'); not an everyday A2 sense.

faults.quote: While 'peinlich' can mean painful in a literal, archaic, or formal
faults.why: Archaic legal history ('peinliche Befragung') is useless for an A2 learner; dative construction note needed.

notes: To say 'I am embarrassed', use the dative construction 'Es ist mir peinlich' (literally: 'It is embarrassing to me').
Although related to the word 'Pein' (pain), 'peinlich' in modern German only means 'embarrassing', never physically 'painful' (which is 'schmerzhaft').

senses.definition: Causing a feeling of shame or awkwardness in a social situation.

examples.text: Es war mir sehr peinlich, als ich meinen Text vergessen habe.
examples.translation: I was very embarrassed when I forgot my lines.

examples.text: Stell bitte keine peinlichen Fragen vor den anderen Leuten!
examples.translation: Please don't ask awkward questions in front of the other people!

faults.quote: Use putzen for cleaning rooms, windows, or shoes, and specifically for
faults.why: Restates the definitions and examples without adding grammatical or usage insight.

notes: In the phrase 'sich (mir/dir...) die Zähne putzen' (to brush one's teeth), German typically uses a dative reflexive pronoun rather than a possessive like 'meine'.
'Putzen' is the everyday word for wiping, scrubbing, or mopping. Do not confuse it with 'waschen' (used for laundry, dishes, hands, or hair) or 'reinigen' (formal or dry-cleaning).

senses.definition: To remove dirt from surfaces, rooms, or objects by wiping, scrubbing, or mopping.

examples.text: Ich muss heute noch das Bad und die Fenster putzen.
examples.translation: I still have to clean the bathroom and the windows today.

senses.definition: To clean one's teeth with a toothbrush (or to blow one's nose).

examples.text: Du solltest dir vor dem Schlafen die Zähne putzen.
examples.translation: You should brush your teeth before going to sleep.

faults.why: Missing common everyday sense 'blank' (e.g., blank page/form, pusta kartka).

faults.quote: Pusty is the most common way to say 'empty'
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and definitions without adding useful grammar or usage info.

notes: Do not confuse with 'wolny' (free, available), which is used when asking if a seat or room is unoccupied rather than physically empty.

senses.definition: Containing nothing inside; not holding any objects or liquid.

examples.text: Szklanka jest pusta.
examples.translation: The glass is empty.

senses.definition: Without people or activity.

examples.text: W niedzielę rano miasto jest puste.
examples.translation: On Sunday morning the city is empty.

senses.definition: Having nothing written, printed, or recorded on it.

examples.text: Weź pustą kartkę papieru.
examples.translation: Take a blank sheet of paper.

faults.quote: Use 'pustynia' when talking about large sandy or rocky barren regions
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

notes: To say 'in the desert', use the preposition 'na' with the locative case: 'na pustyni'.

senses.definition: A large, hot, dry area of land with very little rain and few plants.

examples.text: Na pustyni w dzień jest bardzo gorąco.
examples.translation: It is very hot in the desert during the day.

faults.quote: Showing excessive pride in oneself; arrogant.
faults.why: The sense 'arrogant/haughty' is literary and archaic in modern everyday Polish; A2 learners only need 'delicious'.

faults.quote: While 'pyszny' is the most common word for 'delicious', it has
faults.why: Explains a marginal literary sense that a beginner will not encounter in everyday speech.

notes: In informal speech, the noun 'pycha' is also used as an exclamation meaning 'yum!' or 'delicious!' (e.g., 'Ale pycha!').

senses.definition: Having a very pleasant taste.

examples.text: To ciasto jest naprawdę pyszne.
examples.translation: This cake is really delicious.

faults.quote: Często pytać o twoje zdrowie.
faults.why: Ungrammatical Polish: uses the infinitive 'pytać' instead of the conjugated form 'pytam' or 'pyta'.

faults.quote: Muszę pytać o drogę na dworzec.
faults.why: Unnatural aspect choice; a single action requires the perfective 'zapytać' ('Muszę zapytać').

faults.quote: To check on someone's health or status out of interest.
faults.why: Asking about someone ('pytać o kogoś/coś') is the exact same construction and meaning as sense 0.
Should mention the preposition 'o' + accusative case used for the topic of the question.

notes: Imperfective verb; its perfective pair is 'zapytać' (or 'spytać'). To introduce the topic of the question, use 'o' + accusative case (e.g., 'pytać o drogę' — to ask for directions).
Do not confuse with 'prosić', which means to ask for a favor or an object (to request). You 'pytasz' for information, but 'prosisz' for help.

senses.definition: To speak or write to someone in order to get an answer or information.

examples.text: Dzieci zawsze pytają o wszystko.
examples.translation: Children always ask about everything.

examples.text: Marek często pyta o twoje zdrowie.
examples.translation: Marek often asks about your health.

faults.quote: /ˈp.wɨ.vat͡ɕ/
faults.why: Invalid syllable break inside the initial consonant cluster; should be /ˈpwɨ.vat͡ɕ/.

faults.quote: Drewno może pływać na wodzie.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing; in Polish something floats 'po wodzie' or 'na powierzchni wody', without 'może'.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to sail / go by boat' (e.g., 'pływać łódką/statkiem').

corrected.shortGloss: to swim; to float; to sail
notes: 'Pływać' is an indeterminate motion verb used for general ability, habitual action, or moving in various directions. Use 'płynąć' for a single movement in one direction going on right now.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving the body.

examples.text: Latem lubię pływać w jeziorze.
examples.translation: In summer I like to swim in the lake.

senses.definition: To stay or move on the surface of a liquid without sinking.

examples.text: Drewno pływa na wodzie, a kamień tonie.
examples.translation: Wood floats on water, and stone sinks.

senses.definition: To travel on water in a boat or ship.

examples.text: W weekendy często pływamy łódką po rzece.
examples.translation: On weekends we often go boating on the river.

faults.quote: ฟัง is used for both intentional listening and the physical act
faults.why: False and contradicts note[1]; ฟัง is intentional listening, while ได้ยิน is physical hearing.

faults.quote: listen, hear
faults.why: 'Hear' translates ได้ยิน, not ฟัง.

faults.quote: To pay attention to a sound or what someone is saying.
faults.why: Repeats sense 0 instead of giving the distinct sense 'to obey / heed advice'.

notes: Do not confuse with ได้ยิน (dâi-yin, 'to hear'), which is perceiving sound rather than actively listening.

senses.definition: To give attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.

examples.translation: I like to listen to music while working.

senses.definition: To heed or follow someone's advice or orders.

examples.text: เด็กคนนี้ไม่ยอมฟังพ่อแม่เลย
examples.translation: This child refuses to listen to his parents at all.

faults.quote: while 'กิน' (kin) is used for eating food, 'ดื่ม' (dùm) is
faults.why: Wrong romanization 'dùm' (it is dʉ̀ʉm), and กิน is commonly used for liquids in speech.

faults.quote: To swallow a liquid intentionally.
faults.why: Same meaning as sense 0; 'swallow' and 'guzzle' are inaccurate glosses for ดื่ม.

notes: In everyday spoken Thai, กิน (gin, 'to eat/consume') is very often used for liquids too (e.g., กินน้ำ 'to drink water'), whereas ดื่ม is slightly more polite or formal.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.text: ฉันชอบดื่มน้ำเย็นในวันที่อากาศร้อน
examples.translation: I like to drink cold water on a hot day.

faults.quote: Used for physical openings like doors and windows, but also for
faults.why: Merely restates senses 0 and 1.

notes: The opposite is ปิด (pìt), which means both 'to close' and 'to turn off'.

senses.definition: To move something such as a door, window, or lid so that it is no longer shut.

examples.text: ช่วยเปิดประตูหน่อยครับ
examples.translation: Please open the door.

senses.definition: To cause a light, machine, or electrical device to start working.

examples.text: เปิดไฟให้หน่อยครับ
examples.translation: Please turn on the light.

senses.definition: To start operating or be open for business.

examples.text: ร้านนี้เปิดกี่โมงครับ
examples.translation: What time does this shop open?

faults.quote: Use ชิม when you want to check if a dish needs
faults.why: Restates the definition.

notes: Used only for tasting food or drink. Often paired with ลอง (lɔɔng, 'to try out') as ลองชิม ('to try tasting').

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to see how it tastes.

examples.text: แม่ให้ฉันชิมแกงก่อนตักใส่ชาม
examples.translation: Mom let me taste the curry before scooping it into a bowl.

faults.quote: You can also use it to say 'to operate' for machines.
faults.why: Second sentence merely restates sense 1.

notes: Compound of ทำ (tham, 'to do/make') + งาน (ngaan, 'work/job'). To say where you work, use ทำงานที่ (tham-ngaan thîi).

senses.definition: To do a job or perform duties.

examples.text: เขาไปทำงานทุกวัน
examples.translation: He goes to work every day.

senses.definition: Of a machine, system, or organ: to operate or function.

examples.text: เครื่องนี้ทำงานไม่ปกติ
examples.translation: This machine is not working normally.

faults.quote: Ziek is used for both physical illness and nausea.
faults.why: False: 'ziek' means ill, not nauseous ('misselijk').

notes: Unlike English 'sick', 'ziek' means ill in general, not nauseous; for nausea or needing to vomit, use 'misselijk'.

senses.definition: Suffering from an illness; not well.

examples.text: Ik ben ziek en kan vandaag niet naar het werk komen.
examples.translation: I am sick and cannot come to work today.

senses.definition: Fed up with someone or something (used with 'van').

examples.text: Ik ben echt ziek van al dat gezeur.
examples.translation: I am really sick of all that nagging.

faults.quote: Wij gaan vanavond een film zien.
faults.why: In Netherlandic Dutch, 'een film kijken' is normal; 'zien' is mainly used in the perfect.
Should mention irregular principal parts (zag, gezien).

notes: Strong verb: past 'zag' / 'zagen', past participle 'gezien'.
'Zien' is passive perception with the eyes (to see), whereas 'kijken' is intentional looking or watching.

senses.definition: To perceive or notice something with your eyes, or to have watched a film or show.

examples.text: Ik zie een mooie vogel in de boom.
examples.translation: I see a beautiful bird in the tree.

examples.text: Heb je die nieuwe film al gezien?
examples.translation: Have you seen that new movie yet?

senses.definition: To understand or realize a fact or situation.

examples.text: Nu zie ik wat je bedoelt.
examples.translation: Now I see what you mean.

faults.why: Identity, temporary state and location are all the copula 'to be'; conversely, auxiliary use is missing.

faults.quote: De sleutels zijn op tafel.
faults.why: Dutch uses positional verbs ('De sleutels liggen op tafel'), not 'zijn', for objects on surfaces.

notes: Highly irregular: present 'ben, bent, is, zijn'; past 'was, waren'; past participle 'geweest'.
For the location of objects, Dutch often prefers 'liggen', 'staan', or 'zitten' over 'zijn'.

senses.definition: To have a certain identity, quality, or state, or to be in a place.

examples.text: Ik ben student en ik ben vandaag erg moe.
examples.translation: I am a student and I am very tired today.

examples.text: Wij zijn al thuis.
examples.translation: We are already home.

senses.definition: Used with a past participle to form the perfect tense of verbs of movement or change of state, and to form the passive.

examples.text: Zij is gisteren naar Amsterdam gegaan.
examples.translation: She went to Amsterdam yesterday.

faults.quote: for the physical location of objects that are not standing upright
faults.why: Misleading: flat objects take 'liggen'; 'zitten' is specifically for things inside a container or attached.

notes: Strong verb: past 'zat' / 'zaten', past participle 'gezeten'.
Do not confuse with 'zetten' (to put/place): 'zitten' describes a state, while 'zetten' describes an action.

senses.definition: To rest with your body supported by a seat or the ground.

examples.text: Ik zit op de bank.
examples.translation: I am sitting on the sofa.

senses.definition: To be located inside a container, bag, or enclosed space.

examples.text: De sleutels zitten in mijn tas.
examples.translation: The keys are in my bag.

faults.quote: /ɡɐ̃ˈɲaɾ/
faults.why: European Portuguese IPA; Brazilian Portuguese uses /ɡɐ̃ˈɲaʁ/.

faults.quote: To receive something as a gift or to earn something
faults.why: Conflates 'earning' (for work) and 'receiving' (a gift) into one sense.

faults.quote: While 'ganhar' is commonly used for 'winning' a competition...
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses and senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to earn; to get
notes: When meaning 'to beat' an opponent, it takes the preposition 'de': 'Ganhamos do outro time' (We beat the other team).
Do not confuse with 'vencer', which means to win or overcome an opponent, but never to earn money or receive a gift.

senses.definition: To come first in a game, competition, or contest, or to defeat an opponent.

examples.text: Nós vamos ganhar o jogo hoje.
examples.translation: We are going to win the game today.

senses.definition: To obtain money in return for work.

examples.text: Ela ganha um salário alto no novo emprego.
examples.translation: She earns a high salary at her new job.

senses.definition: To be given something, such as a present or prize.

examples.text: Ganhei um livro de presente no meu aniversário.
examples.translation: I got a book as a present on my birthday.

faults.why: 'Kind' and 'polite' are shades of one meaning in Portuguese 'gentil'.

faults.quote: kind; polite; charming
faults.why: 'Charming' is not in the senses and is not a standard meaning of 'gentil'.
Missing note on irregular plural 'gentis' and uniform gender.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('um homem gentil', 'uma mulher gentil'). The plural is 'gentis'.
False friend: 'gentil' means kind or polite, whereas English 'gentle' (soft, mild) is usually 'suave', 'delicado', or 'meigo'.

senses.definition: Caring, considerate, and polite toward others.

examples.text: Ela foi muito gentil ao me ajudar com as malas.
examples.translation: She was very kind to help me with the suitcases.

faults.quote: I really like to travel during the vacations.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of 'nas férias'; in English, 'on vacation' or 'during the holidays'.

notes: Always takes the preposition 'de' before a noun or verb: 'Eu gosto de café' (I like coffee), 'Gosto de ler' (I like reading).
Before a definite article, 'de' contracts: 'de + o' → 'do', 'de + a' → 'da'.

senses.definition: To find something or someone pleasant or enjoyable.

examples.text: Eu gosto muito de viajar nas férias.
examples.translation: I really like traveling on vacation.

examples.text: Você gosta de música brasileira?
examples.translation: Do you like Brazilian music?

faults.why: Missing note on vowel metaphony (/o/ in masculine singular, /ɔ/ in feminine and plurals).

faults.quote: The chocolate cake turned out very delicious.
faults.why: 'Very delicious' is unnatural in English.

notes: The stressed 'o' is closed /o/ in the masculine singular ('gostoso'), but open /ɔ/ in the feminine and plural forms ('gostosa', 'gostosos', 'gostosas').
When describing a person, 'gostoso/gostosa' is informal and means sexually attractive ('hot'), not 'nice'. Be careful not to use it politely about people.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a very pleasant flavor.

examples.text: O bolo de chocolate ficou muito gostoso.
examples.translation: The chocolate cake turned out delicious.

senses.definition: Of an experience or thing: giving a feeling of pleasure or comfort.

examples.text: Que banho gostoso depois de um dia quente!
examples.translation: What a nice shower after a hot day!

senses.definition: Of a person (informal): physically and sexually attractive.

examples.text: Ele acha a vizinha muito gostosa.
examples.translation: He thinks his neighbor is very hot.

faults.quote: It means 'big' or 'large' in size.
faults.why: Restates the glosses instead of concisely explaining the position change.

notes: Position changes the meaning: after a noun it refers to physical size ('um homem grande' = a big man); before a noun it usually means 'great' ('um grande homem' = a great man).
Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('casa grande', 'carro grande').

senses.definition: Above average in physical size or extent.

examples.text: Ela comprou uma casa grande.
examples.translation: She bought a big house.

senses.definition: Important, admirable, or of high quality.

examples.text: Ele é um grande escritor.
examples.translation: He is a great writer.

faults.quote: Used for both wearing clothes already on your body and putting
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses the common alternative form φοράω used in example[0].

notes: Also very commonly used in the uncontracted form φοράω (as in the first example); aorist stem φόρεσ- (φόρεσα).
βάζω ('to put') is also common for putting on clothes, shoes, or accessories.

senses.definition: To have clothes, shoes, or accessories on your body.

examples.text: Σήμερα φοράω ένα μπλε μπλουζάκι.
examples.translation: Today I am wearing a blue T-shirt.

senses.definition: To put an item of clothing or an accessory on your body.

examples.text: Φόρεσε το παλτό σου γιατί κάνει κρύο.
examples.translation: Put on your coat because it is cold.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with περπατώ, which means to walk
faults.why: Notes restate senses and give a bogus confusion pair; irregular aorist έτρεξα is missing.

faults.quote: Η βρύση τρέχει ζεστό νερό.
faults.why: Unnatural transitive use and calqued English translation.

corrected.shortGloss: to run; to hurry; to flow
notes: Irregular aorist stem τρέξ- (έτρεξα).

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: Πρέπει να τρέξω για να προλάβω το λεωφορείο.
examples.translation: I have to run to catch the bus.

senses.definition: To move or act hurriedly; to rush around.

examples.text: Τρέχω όλη μέρα για τις δουλειές.
examples.translation: I've been rushing around all day running errands.

senses.definition: To flow, of water or another liquid, or of a tap.

examples.text: Τρέχει ζεστό νερό από τη βρύση.
examples.translation: Hot water is running from the tap.

faults.quote: It is often confused by learners with the noun 'μύτη'
faults.why: Note [0] restates the senses; note [1] invents an implausible confusion with μύτη.

corrected.shortGloss: to smell; to give off an odor
notes: Like English 'smell', used both transitively ('smell something') and intransitively ('smell good/bad'); alone without an adverb it often implies smelling bad.

senses.definition: To notice or perceive an odor with your nose.

examples.text: Μυρίζω τα φρέσκα λουλούδια στον κήπο.
examples.translation: I smell the fresh flowers in the garden.

senses.definition: To have or give off a smell.

examples.text: Το φαγητό μυρίζει υπέροχα σήμερα.
examples.translation: The food smells wonderful today.

corrected.shortGloss: to work; to be employed; to function
notes: The everyday word for working; εργάζομαι is a more formal synonym used for employment.
Colloquially with a person in the accusative, it also means 'to tease, pull someone's leg' (Με δουλεύεις; — Are you kidding me?).

senses.definition: To do work or have a job.

examples.text: Δουλεύω σε ένα γραφείο στο κέντρο.
examples.translation: I work in an office downtown.

senses.definition: To operate or function properly, like a machine or device.

examples.text: Το πλυντήριο δεν δουλεύει σήμερα.
examples.translation: The washing machine is not working today.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'πηγαίνω' (to go)
faults.why: Note [0] restates the senses; note [1] warns against an implausible confusion with πηγαίνω.

faults.quote: To show someone the way or lead them to a specific destination.
faults.why: Defines leading a person, while the example is about a road leading somewhere.

corrected.shortGloss: to drive; to lead; to guide
notes: In spoken Greek, the colloquial synonym οδηγάω is also heard; aorist οδήγησα.

senses.definition: To control the movement of a car or other vehicle.

examples.text: Οδηγώ προσεκτικά στην πόλη.
examples.translation: I drive carefully in the city.

senses.definition: To take someone to a place, or (of a road or path) to go to a place.

examples.text: Αυτός ο δρόμος οδηγεί στο κέντρο.
examples.translation: This road leads to the city center.

faults.quote: lonely; solitary
faults.why: Omits the second sense 'remote, isolated'

notes: While 'allein' simply means alone (physically by yourself), 'einsam' carries the emotional weight of feeling lonely and missing company.

senses.definition: feeling sad because you are alone and have no one to talk to

examples.text: Manchmal fühle ich mich an den Wochenenden einsam.
examples.translation: Sometimes I feel lonely on the weekends.

senses.definition: of a place: far away from other people or places

examples.text: Sie wohnt in einem sehr einsamen Haus in den Bergen.
examples.translation: She lives in a very remote house in the mountains.

faults.quote: pos: noun
faults.why: Senses and examples treat it as an expression/interjection, contradicting 'pos: noun' and primaryGloss 'apology'.

faults.quote: apology; excuse; pardon
faults.why: 'excuse' is not covered in the senses.

notes: Often used on its own as an interjection meaning 'Excuse me!' or 'I'm sorry!' (short for 'Ich bitte um Entschuldigung').
Plural: 'die Entschuldigungen'.

senses.definition: a statement saying that you are sorry for something you have done wrong

examples.text: Er hat meine Entschuldigung angenommen.
examples.translation: He accepted my apology.

senses.definition: said to apologize for a minor fault, or to politely get someone's attention or ask to pass

examples.text: Entschuldigung, wissen Sie, wie spät es ist?
examples.translation: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Entschuldigung, das war mein Fehler.
examples.translation: Sorry, that was my mistake.

senses.definition: a reason given to explain why you did something wrong or were absent

examples.text: Hast du eine gute Entschuldigung für deine Verspätung?
examples.translation: Do you have a good excuse for being late?

faults.why: Missing note on syntax (dative recipient, 'von'/'über' for topic) and inseparable prefix 'er-'.

notes: Use 'erzählen' for recounting a story or sharing experiences. To simply state a fact or pass on quick information, use 'sagen' (to say/tell).
The person being told takes the dative case ('jemandem etwas erzählen'). Use 'von' (+ dative) or 'über' (+ accusative) for 'to tell about'.
Inseparable verb: the past participle is 'erzählt' (without 'ge-').

senses.definition: to give someone an account of a story, experience, or sequence of events in words

examples.text: Er erzählt mir eine spannende Geschichte.
examples.translation: He is telling me an exciting story.

examples.text: Kannst du mir erzählen, was gestern passiert ist?
examples.translation: Can you tell me what happened yesterday?

faults.quote: [0] (consumption) ... [1] (dining) ...
faults.why: Eating food and having a meal are the same core verb sense in German.
Redundant notes on 'fressen', while the essential irregular forms (isst, aß, gegessen) are missing.

notes: Irregular strong verb: 'du isst', 'er/sie/es isst'; past tense 'aß'; past participle 'hat gegessen'.
'essen' is used for humans. For animals, use 'fressen' instead (using 'fressen' for people is rude).

senses.definition: to put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it, or to have a meal

examples.text: Ich esse jeden Tag einen Apfel.
examples.translation: I eat an apple every day.

examples.text: Wir essen heute zusammen zu Mittag.
examples.translation: We are having lunch together today.

faults.quote: When you are the one operating a car, 'fahren' means 'to drive'.
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 without adding grammatical or usage information.

faults.quote: Remember that 'fahren' is a strong verb: the past tense is 'fuhr'
faults.why: Mentions strong forms but omits the crucial present stem vowel change ('du fährst', 'er fährt') and auxiliary ('sein' vs. 'haben').

corrected.shortGloss: to go (by vehicle); to travel; to drive
notes: Use 'fahren' for any transport involving a vehicle (car, bus, train, bike), unlike 'gehen', which means to go on foot.
Strong verb with a stem vowel change: 'du fährst', 'er/sie/es fährt'; past tense 'fuhr'; past participle 'gefahren'.
Takes 'sein' in the perfect tense for movement from place to place ('Ich bin nach Berlin gefahren'), and 'haben' when driving an object ('Ich habe das Auto gefahren').

senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere in a vehicle, such as a car, train, bus, or bicycle

examples.text: Wir fahren am Wochenende mit dem Zug nach Berlin.
examples.translation: We are going to Berlin by train this weekend.

senses.definition: to control and operate a vehicle while it is moving

examples.text: Er fährt bei Regen immer sehr vorsichtig.
examples.translation: He always drives very carefully in the rain.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning (kind, polite, considerate).

faults.quote: Amable is a very common way to describe someone who is polite
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammar or usage information.

notes: It has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns (un hombre amable, una mujer amable).
Do not confuse with 'simpático' (nice/likeable in personality) or 'amigable' (friendly/sociable). 'Amable' focuses on being polite, helpful, and considerate.

senses.definition: Polite, pleasant, and considerate towards others.

examples.text: La recepcionista es muy amable con los clientes.
examples.translation: The receptionist is very kind to the customers.

examples.text: Fue muy amable de su parte ayudarme cuando estaba enfermo.
examples.translation: It was very kind of him to help me when I was sick.

faults.quote: to like very much, to be very fond of
faults.why: 'Amar' means to love deeply or adore, never merely 'to like very much'.

faults.quote: reserved for romantic partners or family members
faults.why: Directly contradicts sense 1 ('Amo a mi mejor amigo') and everyday hyperbole ('amo los tacos').

notes: For people, 'amar' expresses deep romantic or familial devotion. In Mexico, 'querer' is much more common for everyday 'to love' with friends, family, or new partners.

senses.definition: To feel deep romantic love or profound affection for someone.

examples.text: Ellos se aman profundamente.
examples.translation: They love each other deeply.

senses.definition: To like or enjoy something very much.

examples.text: ¡Amo los tacos de este lugar!
examples.translation: I love the tacos from this place!

faults.quote: The colour of a lemon, or the colour of the sun.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('The colour...') instead of a quality ('Of the colour...').

faults.quote: Describing someone who looks pale or sickly, often associated with illness.
faults.why: Marginal figurative use not needed as a separate sense for an A2 beginner.

notes: It changes its ending to match the gender and number of the noun (amarillo, amarilla, amarillos, amarillas).

senses.definition: Having the color of a ripe lemon or the sun.

examples.text: El limón es amarillo.
examples.translation: The lemon is yellow.

faults.quote: use 'amable' or 'simpático' when talking about a person's character.
faults.why: Contradicts sense 0; in Mexico 'amigable' is very commonly used for friendly people.

notes: It has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns (un perro amigable, una persona amigable).
