faults.why: 'Siempre suelo' is redundant and unnatural; say 'Suelo olvidar' or 'Siempre olvido'.

notes: Can be used directly ('olvidé la cita'), as 'olvidarse de' ('me olvidé de la cita'), or with 'se' + indirect object pronoun where the thing forgotten agrees with the verb: 'se me olvidó la llave' / 'se me olvidaron las llaves'.

senses.definition: To fail to remember something.

examples.text: Siempre olvido las fechas de los cumpleaños.
examples.translation: I always forget birthday dates.

senses.definition: To leave something behind somewhere by mistake.

examples.text: Voy a volver al restaurante porque creo que olvidé mi paraguas.
examples.translation: I am going to go back to the restaurant because I think I left my umbrella behind.

faults.quote: Use '약하다' to describe someone who is physically frail, an object
faults.why: First sentence merely restates the three sense definitions; missing the particle 에 for sense 1.
Physical weakness of people and objects are shades of one meaning; intensity/degree sense is better.

notes: The opposite is 강하다 (strong). In pronunciation, ㄱ + ㅎ combines to sound like ㅋ [야카다].
When meaning 'weak at' a subject or skill, mark the area with the particle 에 (e.g. 수학에 약하다).

senses.definition: Lacking physical strength, power, or sturdiness; easily broken or overcome.

examples.text: 그는 몸이 약하다.
examples.translation: He is physically weak.

examples.text: 이 의자는 다리가 약하다.
examples.translation: This chair has weak legs.

senses.definition: Of low intensity, force, or effectiveness, such as wind, heat, or a signal.

examples.text: 여기는 와이파이 신호가 약해요.
examples.translation: The Wi-Fi signal is weak here.

senses.definition: Not good at a particular subject, skill, or activity, or easily affected by something.

examples.text: 나는 수학에 약하다.
examples.translation: I am weak at math.

faults.quote: Feeling shy and uncomfortable due to being the center of attention.
faults.why: As the entry's own note states, 'shy' is 부끄럽다/수줍다; 창피하다 means embarrassed or ashamed.

faults.quote: embarrassed; ashamed; shy
faults.why: 'Shy' is inaccurate for 창피하다; it means embarrassed or ashamed.

notes: Unlike 부끄럽다 (which also covers being bashful or shy), 창피하다 specifically focuses on losing face or feeling humiliated in front of others.
Can describe both the person feeling embarrassed (내가 창피하다) and the situation or behavior causing embarrassment (행동이 창피하다).

senses.definition: Feeling or causing a loss of face, humiliation, or shame because of a mistake or awkward situation.

examples.text: 모두가 보는 앞에서 넘어져서 너무 창피했어요.
examples.translation: I was so embarrassed because I fell down in front of everyone.

faults.why: Missing two core A1/A2 uses: 'to be fond of / like' (with 이/가) and 'okay / fine' (expressing agreement).

faults.quote: 좋다 is an adjective meaning 'good', 'nice', or 'fine'.
faults.why: Restates POS and glosses without adding usage information.

notes: Because 좋다 is an adjective, the thing that is good or liked takes the subject particle 이/가 (e.g. 커피가 좋아요, 'I like coffee'). Contrast with the verb 좋아하다 (to like), which takes the object particle 을/를 (커피를 좋아해요).
In pronunciation, ㅎ + ㄷ combines to sound like ㅌ [조타], and before a vowel ㅎ is silent (좋아요 [조아요]).

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or satisfactory.

examples.text: 오늘 날씨가 참 좋다.
examples.translation: The weather is really nice today.

examples.text: 머리 스타일이 아주 좋네요.
examples.translation: Your hairstyle looks very good.

senses.definition: Pleasing or dear to someone; used with 이/가 to express liking or preferring something.

examples.text: 나는 겨울보다 여름이 더 좋다.
examples.translation: I like summer more than winter.

senses.definition: Suitable, favorable, or agreeable; often used to accept a suggestion.

examples.text: 내일 다섯 시에 만날까요? — 네, 좋아요!
examples.translation: Shall we meet at five tomorrow? — Yes, sounds good!

faults.quote: To be free and not busy with any work or tasks.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a verb infinitive ('To be...') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: Use this when you have spare time or when a place
faults.why: Merely restates the two sense definitions.

notes: The opposite is 바쁘다 (busy) for people or time, and 붐비다 or 복잡하다 (crowded) for places.
Unlike 심심하다 (bored), which means wanting something interesting to do, 한가하다 simply means having free time or few people around and often feels relaxing.

senses.definition: Having spare time and not occupied with work or tasks.

examples.text: 주말에는 보통 한가해요.
examples.translation: I am usually free on weekends.

senses.definition: Of a place: quiet and having very few people or little activity.

examples.text: 이 카페는 평일 오후에 아주 한가하다.
examples.translation: This cafe is very quiet on weekday afternoons.

faults.quote: Used when someone has nothing interesting to do and feels bored.
faults.why: Both notes merely repeat the definitions; missing the crucial distinction between 심심하다 (bored) and 지루하다 (boring).

faults.quote: To feel tired and restless because you have nothing interesting to
faults.why: Adjective defined as an infinitive ('To feel...') instead of a quality.

notes: Do not confuse with 지루하다 (boring/tedious). 심심하다 describes a person feeling bored from having nothing to do, while 지루하다 describes something (like a movie or class) that is dull and tiresome.
When describing food, it is similar to 싱겁다 (not salty enough, bland).

senses.definition: Feeling restless and weary from having nothing interesting to do.

examples.text: 할 일이 없어서 너무 심심해요.
examples.translation: I have nothing to do, so I am so bored.

senses.definition: Of food: lacking salt or seasoning; slightly bland.

examples.text: 국이 좀 심심하니까 소금을 더 넣으세요.
examples.translation: The soup is a bit bland, so add some more salt.

faults.quote: (check) To check or verify a situation or information.
faults.why: Looking into a calendar is just sense 0 (to look/see); not a separate meaning.
Should mention how to express 'look at' (auf + accusative or anschauen).

notes: Especially common in Southern Germany and Austria; in the north, 'gucken' (colloquial) or 'sehen' is more frequent.
To say 'look at something', use 'auf' + accusative (auf die Uhr schauen) or the separable verb 'anschauen'.

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward something, or to check and see.

examples.text: Schau mal, da ist ein Vogel.
examples.translation: Look, there is a bird.

examples.text: Ich schaue kurz in den Kalender.
examples.translation: I'll quickly look at the calendar.

senses.definition: To look at something for a period of time, especially a film or show.

examples.text: Wir schauen heute Abend einen Film.
examples.translation: We are watching a movie tonight.

faults.quote: Schicken is used for sending items, messages, or people to a destination.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; better to note the dative + accusative pattern.

notes: Takes a dative recipient and an accusative object (jemandem etwas schicken), or 'an' + accusative.
More everyday than 'senden', which is mostly used in formal contexts or for broadcasting (TV, radio).

senses.definition: To cause something or someone to go or be taken to a destination.

examples.text: Ich schicke dir morgen das Paket.
examples.translation: I will send you the package tomorrow.

examples.text: Er schickt seine Kinder zur Schule.
examples.translation: He sends his children to school.

faults.quote: (slide) To cause something to move smoothly across a surface.
faults.why: Pushing a table and sliding a book are the same core sense of 'schieben'.
Missing irregular principal parts (schob, hat geschoben) for a strong verb.

notes: Strong verb: schob, hat geschoben.
Describes a steady, continuous motion along a surface (like pushing a cart or sliding furniture), whereas 'stoßen' means a sudden shove or impact.

senses.definition: To move something continuously across a surface or into a position by applying steady force.

examples.text: Ich schiebe den Tisch zur Wand.
examples.translation: I am pushing the table to the wall.

examples.text: Er schiebt das Buch über den Tisch.
examples.translation: He slides the book across the table.

notes: Strong verb with vowel change in the present tense (du schläfst, er schläft); past: schlief, hat geschlafen.
Do not confuse with 'einschlafen', which means to fall asleep.

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed and your mind and body inactive, especially at night.

examples.text: Ich schlafe jeden Tag acht Stunden.
examples.translation: I sleep eight hours every day.

examples.text: Das Baby schläft jetzt friedlich.
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping peacefully now.

faults.quote: Use 'schlecht' as a general antonym for 'gut'.
faults.why: Restates the senses; should explain the dative construction 'mir ist schlecht' vs 'ich bin schlecht'.
Missing the everyday sense 'spoiled/off' (of food) or 'poorly/badly' as an adverb.

notes: In the health sense, always use the dative ('Mir ist schlecht' = I feel sick/nauseous). Saying 'Ich bin schlecht' means 'I am bad (at something) or evil'.

senses.definition: Unpleasant, of low quality, or not going well; the opposite of 'gut'.

examples.text: Das Wetter ist heute leider sehr schlecht.
examples.translation: The weather is unfortunately very bad today.

examples.text: Ich habe heute Nacht schlecht geschlafen.
examples.translation: I slept badly last night.

senses.definition: Used with a dative pronoun: feeling nauseous or physically unwell.

examples.text: Mir ist nach dem Essen schlecht.
examples.translation: I feel sick after eating.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: no longer fresh and unsafe to eat or drink.

examples.text: Die Milch ist schlecht geworden.
examples.translation: The milk has gone bad.

faults.quote: Feeling something unexpected happened.
faults.why: Awkward English phrasing; should define the quality of feeling surprise.

notes: Commonly used with the verb 'ficar' (to become/get) and the preposition 'com', as in 'fiquei surpreso com a notícia' (I was surprised by the news).

senses.definition: Feeling surprise because something unexpected happened.

examples.text: Ele ficou muito surpreso com o presente.
examples.translation: He was very surprised by the gift.

faults.quote: /tawˈvɛs/
faults.why: Has closed-mid vowel /e/, not open-mid /ɛ/: /tawˈves/.

faults.quote: Unlike in English, 'talvez' is rarely used as a standalone answer
faults.why: False claim; 'Talvez.' is very common and natural as a standalone answer in Brazil.

faults.quote: followed by a verb in the subjunctive mood when the uncertainty is higher
faults.why: Rule depends on word order (before vs. after the verb), not degree of uncertainty.

notes: When 'talvez' comes before the verb, the verb must be in the subjunctive mood (e.g., 'Talvez ele venha' — Maybe he will come). If it comes after the verb, the indicative is used.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible, but not certain.

examples.text: Talvez ele chegue mais tarde.
examples.translation: Perhaps he will arrive later.

examples.text: Não tenho certeza, talvez seja melhor esperar.
examples.translation: I am not sure, maybe it is better to wait.

faults.quote: (afternoon) During the part of the day between noon and evening.
faults.why: 'Tarde' meaning afternoon is a feminine noun (used in 'à tarde'), not an adverb.

faults.quote: late; in the afternoon
faults.why: Includes 'in the afternoon', which belongs to the noun 'tarde' inside a prepositional phrase.

notes: As an adverb, 'tarde' never changes form (e.g., 'acordei tarde' — I woke up late, 'é muito tarde' — it is very late).
Do not confuse with the feminine noun 'a tarde' (the afternoon), seen in 'boa tarde' (good afternoon) and 'à tarde' (in the afternoon).

senses.definition: After the usual, expected, or planned time, or near the end of the day or night.

examples.text: Desculpe, cheguei muito tarde hoje.
examples.translation: Sorry, I arrived very late today.

examples.text: Já está tarde, preciso ir embora.
examples.translation: It is already late, I need to leave.

faults.quote: or 'adeus' (goodbye) if you want to sound slightly more formal
faults.why: In Brazil, 'adeus' is dramatic or permanent (farewell forever), not a slightly formal goodbye.

notes: The standard everyday way to say goodbye in Brazil in almost any situation. Often combined with 'até logo' or 'até mais' (see you later); 'adeus' is rarely used and sounds dramatic (farewell forever).

senses.definition: Used when leaving someone or when someone is leaving.

faults.why: Missing the essential A1/A2 sense 'ter que / ter de' (to have to, must).

faults.quote: Unlike in some languages where you use 'to have' for age
faults.why: Self-contradictory; says 'unlike languages that use to have, Portuguese uses ter (to have)'.

faults.quote: Você tem frio?
faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, temporary sensations like cold/hunger normally take 'estar com' ('Está com frio?').

faults.quote: to have; to own; to possess
faults.why: Does not cover the existence ('there be') or obligation ('have to') senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to have; there is / there are; to have to
notes: Irregular in the present tense: eu tenho, você/ele/ela tem, nós temos, vocês/eles/elas têm (notice the circumflex accent in the plural 'têm', pronounced the same as 'tem').

Unlike English, which uses 'to be' for age, Portuguese uses 'ter': 'Eu tenho 20 anos' (I am 20 years old). For hunger, thirst, or cold, Brazilians usually say 'estar com' ('Estou com fome') rather than 'ter'.

senses.definition: To own, possess, or hold something, or to have a relationship with someone.

examples.text: Eu tenho um carro novo e dois irmãos.
examples.translation: I have a new car and two brothers.

senses.definition: Used in the singular form 'tem' (or past 'tinha') to say that something exists or is present in a place.

examples.text: Tem muita gente na festa hoje.
examples.translation: There are many people at the party today.

senses.definition: Used with 'que' or 'de' before an infinitive verb to say that someone must do something.

examples.text: Eu tenho que trabalhar amanhã.
examples.translation: I have to work tomorrow.

senses.definition: To be of a certain age, or to experience a state or feeling.

examples.text: Quantos anos você tem?
examples.translation: How old are you?

faults.quote: Hij renst heel hard naar de bus.
faults.why: 'renst' is not a Dutch word; the third-person singular of 'rennen' is 'rent'.
Missing the common sense 'harsh, severe, or intense' (harde wind, hard werken, harde woorden).

notes: Like most Dutch adjectives, 'hard' is also used unchanged as an adverb ('loudly', 'fast', 'hard', e.g. 'hard werken').
Unlike English 'hard', it usually does not mean 'difficult'—use 'moeilijk' or 'lastig' for that.

senses.definition: Firm and solid to the touch; not soft.

examples.text: Dit brood is erg hard geworden.
examples.translation: This bread has become very hard.

senses.definition: High in volume; loud.

examples.text: De muziek staat te hard.
examples.translation: The music is on too loud.

senses.definition: Moving or done at high speed.

examples.text: Hij rent heel hard naar de bus.
examples.translation: He is running very fast to the bus.

senses.definition: Strong in force, effort, or severity.

examples.text: Zij werkt elke dag heel hard.
examples.translation: She works very hard every day.

examples.text: Er staat vandaag een harde wind.
examples.translation: There is a strong wind today.

faults.quote: Ik haten broccoli.
faults.why: Ungrammatical conjugation: first-person singular of 'haten' is 'Ik haat', not 'Ik haten'.

faults.quote: Ik haten vandaar opstaan in de ochtend.
faults.why: Completely ungrammatical ('Ik haten') and 'vandaar' means 'hence/from there', not 'early' ('vroeg').
Senses 0 and 1 are the same meaning split artificially into two.

notes: 'Haten' is much stronger in Dutch than 'to hate' in English. For everyday things you dislike, use 'een hekel hebben aan' or 'niet leuk/lekker vinden'.

senses.definition: To feel intense dislike towards someone or something.

examples.text: Ik haat het om vroeg op te staan.
examples.translation: I hate getting up early.

faults.quote: /ˈɦɛb.bən/
faults.why: Dutch does not have geminate consonants inside a word; the IPA is /ˈɦɛ.bə(n)/.
Note states the obvious and omits irregular basic forms (heb, hebt/heeft, had, gehad) and 'honger/gelijk hebben'.

notes: Irregular verb: ik heb, jij hebt (heb je), hij/zij heeft, wij hebben; past: had/hadden; past participle: gehad.
Used with nouns for many states where English uses 'to be': 'honger/dorst hebben' (to be hungry/thirsty), 'gelijk hebben' (to be right), 'het koud/warm hebben' (to be cold/warm).

senses.definition: To own, hold, or be connected with something or someone.

examples.text: Ik heb een rode auto en twee fietsen.
examples.translation: I have a red car and two bikes.

senses.definition: To experience a physical feeling, need, or state.

examples.text: Ik heb honger.
examples.translation: I am hungry.

senses.definition: Used as an auxiliary verb with a past participle to form the perfect tense.

examples.text: Wij hebben gisteren gevoetbald.
examples.translation: We played football yesterday.

faults.quote: Entire; complete.
faults.why: Entry pos is 'adv', Note 1 warns not to confuse with adjective 'heel', yet Sense 1 is the adjective.

faults.quote: /heːl/
faults.why: Dutch initial 'h' is voiced glottal /ɦ/: /ɦeːl/.

notes: Used before adjectives and adverbs ('heel mooi'). To modify a verb, use 'erg' or 'heel erg' instead (e.g. 'Ik mis je heel erg').
As an adjective before a noun, 'heel' (inflected 'hele') means 'whole' or 'entire': 'een hele taart' (a whole cake), 'de hele dag' (all day).

senses.definition: To a high degree; used to strengthen an adjective or adverb.

examples.text: Het is vandaag heel koud buiten.
examples.translation: It is very cold outside today.

examples.text: Ik ben heel erg moe.
examples.translation: I am really very tired.

faults.quote: While 'heerlijk' can mean wonderful or lovely in general, it is most
faults.why: Note 0 restates the two senses; Note 1 compares with unrelated 'mooi' instead of close synonym 'lekker'.

notes: Stronger and more enthusiastic than 'lekker' (tasty, nice), used for both food and pleasant experiences.

senses.definition: Tasting or smelling very good.

examples.text: Deze soep is echt heerlijk.
examples.translation: This soup is truly delicious.

senses.definition: Giving great comfort, pleasure, or enjoyment.

examples.text: Wat een heerlijk weer vandaag!
examples.translation: What wonderful weather today!

faults.quote: Il fait un temps magnifique aujourd'hui.
faults.why: The example does not contain any form of the word 'beau'.
The example has no translation.

notes: It usually goes before the noun it describes (un beau jardin).
Before a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h, it changes to bel (un bel homme); its feminine form is belle, and the masculine plural is beaux.

senses.definition: Very pleasant to look at; attractive or pretty.

examples.text: Elle porte une belle robe rouge.
examples.translation: She is wearing a beautiful red dress.

senses.definition: Pleasant, nice, or sunny, especially regarding the weather.

examples.text: Il fait très beau aujourd'hui.
examples.translation: The weather is very nice today.

examples.text: C'est un beau jour pour une promenade.
examples.translation: It is a fine day for a walk.

faults.quote: The feminine form changes to 'blanche' before feminine nouns (e.g., une chemise blanche).
faults.why: Color adjectives in French normally follow the noun, as the note's own example shows.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk.
faults.why: An adjective must be defined as a quality, not as a noun.

notes: The feminine form is blanche (e.g., une chemise blanche); the c in blanc is silent.

senses.definition: Having the color of snow or milk.

examples.text: Les montagnes sont couvertes de neige blanche en hiver.
examples.translation: The mountains are covered with white snow in winter.

senses.definition: Having no writing, marks, or printing; empty.

examples.text: Veuillez signer sur la page blanche à la fin du document.
examples.translation: Please sign on the blank page at the end of the document.

faults.quote: (body) A dark mark on the skin caused by an injury.
faults.why: This sense ('un bleu', a bruise) is a noun, not an adjective.

faults.quote: blue; bruised; rare (meat)
faults.why: 'Bruised' is not covered by the adjective senses ('un bleu' is a noun).

faults.quote: Meat that is cooked very little and remains red inside.
faults.why: An adjective must be defined as a quality ('of meat: cooked...'), not as a noun.

faults.quote: In French, colors generally agree in gender and number with the noun
faults.why: Long explanation of regular adjective agreement is filler.

notes: When ordering steak in France, bleu means very rare—cooked for only a few seconds on each side.

senses.definition: Having the color of a clear sky or the sea.

examples.text: Le ciel est bleu aujourd'hui.
examples.translation: The sky is blue today.

senses.definition: Of meat: cooked very little so that it stays red and cool inside.

examples.text: Je voudrais mon steak bleu, s'il vous plaît.
examples.translation: I would like my steak rare, please.

faults.quote: (absorb) Make a liquid disappear by taking it in.
faults.why: Figurative sense ('absorb') with an archaic example ('papier buvard') is marginal for A2.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to drink alcohol'.

notes: Irregular verb: je bois, tu bois, il boit, nous buvons, vous buvez, ils boivent; past participle: bu (j'ai bu).

senses.definition: To take a liquid into the body through the mouth.

examples.text: Il fait chaud, je veux boire de l'eau.
examples.translation: It is hot, I want to drink some water.

senses.definition: To consume alcoholic drinks.

examples.text: Je ne bois pas d'alcool quand je conduis.
examples.translation: I don't drink alcohol when I drive.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'right, correct' (e.g. le bon train, la bonne réponse).

notes: The feminine form is bonne (/bɔn/). Bon usually goes before the noun it describes (un bon livre).
Do not confuse bon (good, an adjective) with bien (well, usually an adverb); the comparative of bon is meilleur (better).

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or satisfactory.

examples.text: C'est une bonne idée.
examples.translation: That's a good idea.

senses.definition: Pleasant to the taste; delicious.

examples.text: Ce croissant est très bon.
examples.translation: This croissant is very good.

senses.definition: Correct, accurate, or suitable for a purpose.

examples.text: Est-ce que nous sommes dans le bon train ?
examples.translation: Are we on the right train?

senses.definition: Kind, generous, or caring toward others.

examples.text: Il est très bon avec les enfants.
examples.translation: He is very kind with children.

faults.quote: to remember; to remind; to look like
faults.why: 'to look like' is not a separate sense in the entry.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'ricordare qualcuno', which means 'to resemble'
faults.why: Say 'do not confuse' about the same verb; lacks syntax for 'remind someone to do'.

notes: Often used reflexively as 'ricordarsi' (often with 'di': 'ricordarsi di qualcosa/qualcuno') with no change in meaning.
To say 'remind someone of/to do something', use 'ricordare qualcosa a qualcuno' or 'ricordare a qualcuno di fare qualcosa'.

senses.definition: To keep something in your mind, or bring it back into your thoughts.

examples.text: Non riesco a ricordare il suo nome.
examples.translation: I cannot remember his name.

senses.definition: To cause someone to remember something, or to make someone think of a person or thing.

examples.text: Questo posto mi ricorda la mia infanzia.
examples.translation: This place reminds me of my childhood.

examples.text: Ricordami di comprare il latte.
examples.translation: Remind me to buy milk.

faults.quote: (fortune) To be favorable or fortunate towards someone.
faults.why: Literary figurative sense, not needed for A2 learners; also misleads in shortGloss as 'to smile'.

faults.quote: to laugh; to smile
faults.why: Misleads learner into thinking 'ridere' means 'to smile' (which Note 0 explicitly warns against).

notes: Do not confuse 'ridere' (to laugh) with 'sorridere' (to smile).
Has an irregular past participle: 'riso' (takes the auxiliary 'avere': 'ho riso'). Followed by 'di' for 'to laugh at/about'.

senses.definition: To make sounds with your voice and smile because you find something funny.

examples.text: Tutti hanno iniziato a ridere quando lui è caduto.
examples.translation: Everyone started to laugh when he fell.

faults.quote: Can mean both fixing a physical object and taking shelter from the weather.
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without explaining that 'to take shelter' requires the reflexive 'ripararsi'.

faults.quote: to repair; to protect; to take shelter
faults.why: 'to take shelter' is not covered by the senses (and is normally reflexive 'ripararsi').

notes: In the sense of 'to take shelter', it is used reflexively: 'ripararsi' (e.g., 'ripararsi dalla pioggia').

senses.definition: To fix something that is broken or damaged so that it works again.

examples.text: Devo riparare la bicicletta prima di partire.
examples.translation: I need to repair the bicycle before leaving.

senses.definition: To protect someone or something from harm or bad weather.

examples.text: Questo cappotto ripara dal freddo.
examples.translation: This coat protects against the cold.

faults.quote: I don't know what to answer to this question.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English one says 'how to answer this question', not 'answer to'.
Missing irregular past participle 'risposto', which is essential for an A2 learner.

notes: Irregular past participle: 'risposto' (takes the auxiliary 'avere': 'ho risposto').
Always takes the preposition 'a' before the person or thing being answered (e.g., 'rispondere a una domanda', 'rispondere al telefono').

senses.definition: To say or write something in response to a question, message, or greeting.

examples.text: Non so cosa rispondere a questa domanda.
examples.translation: I don't know how to answer this question.

senses.definition: To pick up a ringing telephone or go to open the door when someone knocks or rings.

examples.text: Il telefono squilla, ma nessuno vuole rispondere.
examples.translation: The phone is ringing, but nobody wants to answer.

faults.quote: /ˈrɔm.pe.re/
faults.why: Wrong vowel quality: stressed 'o' in 'rompere' is closed /o/ (/ˈrom.pe.re/), not open /ɔ/.

corrected.shortGloss: to break; to tear; to annoy
notes: Irregular simple past ('ruppi', 'rompesti', etc.) and past participle ('rotto').
In the sense 'to annoy', it is informal and often used in idioms like 'rompere le scatole' (or simply 'Non rompere!').

senses.definition: To damage something so that it separates into pieces or stops working.

examples.text: Ho fatto cadere il bicchiere e si è rotto.
examples.translation: I dropped the glass and it broke.

senses.definition: To tear or make a hole in cloth, paper, or similar materials.

examples.text: Ho rotto i pantaloni giocando a calcio.
examples.translation: I tore my pants playing soccer.

senses.definition: To annoy or bother someone persistently (informal).

examples.text: Non mi rompere le scatole adesso.
examples.translation: Don't bother me right now.

faults.quote: yaşamak, which refers to living in a general biological or life-experience sense rather than having a fixed residence.
faults.why: Yaşamak is also very commonly used for residing in a city or country.

faults.quote: Oturmak primarily means to sit down or to reside in a place.
faults.why: Restates the glosses; fails to note that 'sit' takes both dative and locative.

corrected.shortGloss: to sit, to sit down; to live; to fit
notes: For sitting, use the dative (-e/-a) for the action of sitting down ('sandalyeye oturmak') and the locative (-de/-da) for the state of sitting ('sandalyede oturmak').
For living in a place, it always takes the locative (-de/-da) and refers to one's home, neighbourhood, or city; 'yaşamak' is also used for cities and countries, or for being alive.

senses.definition: To rest your weight on your bottom on a chair, the floor, or another surface, or to move into this position.

examples.text: Lütfen sandalyeye oturun.
examples.translation: Please sit on the chair.

senses.definition: To have your home in a particular place.

examples.text: Ankara'da oturuyorum.
examples.translation: I live in Ankara.

senses.definition: Of clothing or an object: to be the right size and shape, or to settle into the right position.

examples.text: Bu ceket üzerime tam oturdu.
examples.translation: This jacket fits me perfectly.

faults.quote: /o.jaˈmak/
faults.why: Wrong transcription (belongs to 'oyamak'); 'oynamak' is /oj.naˈmak/.

faults.quote: Oynamak is used for sports, games, and musical instruments, but note that for instruments it takes the ablative case
faults.why: Completely false: Turkish never uses 'oynamak' or the ablative case for playing musical instruments.

faults.quote: to play; to dance; to gamble
faults.why: Mentions 'to gamble', which is not in the senses, and omits 'to move/wiggle'.
Missing the common A2 sense of acting in a film/play or a film being shown.

corrected.shortGloss: to play; to dance; to act; to wiggle
notes: Do not use 'oynamak' for playing a musical instrument; Turkish uses 'çalmak' instead (e.g. 'piyano çalmak').

senses.definition: To take part in a game or sport, or to have fun with toys or friends.

examples.text: Çocuklar bahçede futbol oynuyor.
examples.translation: The children are playing football in the garden.

senses.definition: To move your body to folk or upbeat music.

examples.text: Düğünde herkes oynamaya başladı.
examples.translation: Everyone started to dance at the wedding.

senses.definition: To perform a role in a film or play, or for a film or play to be showing.

examples.text: Bu filmde çok ünlü bir aktör oynuyor.
examples.translation: A very famous actor plays in this film.

senses.definition: To move or shift slightly when it should be fixed in place.

examples.text: Bu diş biraz oynuyor.
examples.translation: This tooth is wiggling a little bit.

faults.quote: (desire) To desire or feel a need for something
faults.why: Missing a person and missing the old days are the exact same meaning of 'özlemek'.

faults.quote: It is common to confuse this with 'arzulamak', which means 'to desire'
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'özlemek' with 'arzulamak'; a note on English 'miss' (kaçırmak) is needed.

notes: Takes a direct object in the accusative case, and the past tense is very often used for a present feeling: 'Seni çok özledim' (I miss you so much).
Only used for missing a person, place, or thing you are fond of. For missing a bus, flight, or opportunity, use 'kaçırmak'.

senses.definition: To feel sad because you are away from someone or something you love or used to have.

examples.text: Annemi ve eski günleri çok özlüyorum.
examples.translation: I miss my mother and the old days very much.

faults.quote: It can also be used to politely get someone's attention
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1 without adding usage or grammar information.

notes: Literally means 'I wish for an excuse' (from 'özür dilemek', to apologize). To say what you are sorry for, use the ablative case (-den/-dan) or a clause with 'için', and use the dative (-e/-a) for the person you apologize to.

senses.definition: Said to apologize when you have made a mistake, caused trouble, or hurt someone.

examples.text: Geç kaldığım için özür dilerim.
examples.translation: I'm sorry for being late.

senses.definition: Said to politely get someone's attention, interrupt them, or ask them to repeat something.

examples.text: Özür dilerim, bu masa boş mu?
examples.translation: Excuse me, is this table free?

faults.quote: Pahalı is used for items that cost a lot of money.
faults.why: First sentence just repeats the definition.

notes: Its opposite is 'ucuz' (cheap).

senses.definition: Costing a lot of money.

examples.text: Bu telefon çok pahalı.
examples.translation: This phone is very expensive.

faults.quote: Used for the start of an activity, a process, or a duration.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

faults.quote: Use this for when something gets moving or begins to happen.
faults.why: Repeats the meaning of the verb.

notes: Followed directly by a verb to mean 'start doing something' (e.g., เริ่มเรียน, to start studying).
Often compounded as เริ่มต้น with the same meaning.

senses.definition: To start doing something, or to begin to happen.

examples.text: เราจะเริ่มเรียนภาษาไทยกันพรุ่งนี้
examples.translation: We will start learning Thai tomorrow.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the same core meaning (winning a contest or beating an opponent).

faults.quote: ทีมของเราเอาชนะคู่ต่อสู้ได้ในนาทีสุดท้าย
faults.why: Uses the compound เอาชนะ instead of the headword ชนะ alone.

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to beat; to overcome
notes: Can be used without an object ('to win') or followed directly by the opponent or competition ('to beat someone', 'to win a race').
For overcoming a difficulty or inner struggle, the compound เอาชนะ is usually preferred.

senses.definition: To come first in a competition, or to defeat an opponent.

examples.text: ทีมของเราชนะการแข่งขันเมื่อวานนี้
examples.translation: Our team won the match yesterday.

senses.definition: To succeed in dealing with a difficulty, fear, or obstacle (often as เอาชนะ).

examples.text: เราต้องเอาชนะความกลัวของตัวเอง
examples.translation: We must overcome our own fears.

faults.quote: ครูจ่ายเอกสารให้นักเรียน
faults.why: Handing out papers in class is แจก, not จ่าย; จ่าย is for disbursing money/supplies.

faults.quote: To distribute or hand out items to multiple people.
faults.why: Dispensing items (like medicine) is narrow; everyday shopping (จ่ายตลาด) is much more useful.

faults.quote: When you 'pay' a person or a company, 'จ่าย' is the standard
faults.why: Restates the basic gloss without new grammatical or usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to pay; to shop for groceries
notes: Used for paying money (e.g., จ่ายเงิน 'pay money', จ่ายค่าอาหาร 'pay for food'). For spending time, use ใช้.
Commonly used in จ่ายตลาด ('to do the grocery shopping at a market').

senses.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or bills.

examples.text: ฉันต้องจ่ายค่าอาหาร
examples.translation: I have to pay for the food.

senses.definition: To buy food and household goods, especially at a market.

examples.text: แม่ไปจ่ายตลาดทุกเช้า
examples.translation: Mom goes grocery shopping at the market every morning.

faults.quote: To spend a period of time learning or attending classes in a
faults.why: Not a separate sense; duration is expressed by มา...แล้ว, not by เรียน itself.

faults.quote: Use เรียน when talking about studying a subject at school or university,
faults.why: Restates the definition.

corrected.shortGloss: to study; to learn; to inform (formal)
notes: Covers both studying a subject (at school or university) and learning a practical skill.
Do not confuse with ศึกษา, which is a more formal word for academic study or research.

senses.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill by studying, taking lessons, or attending school.

examples.text: ฉันเรียนภาษาไทยทุกวัน
examples.translation: I study Thai every day.

senses.definition: To formally address or inform someone of higher status (often at the start of a letter or email).

examples.text: เรียน ผู้จัดการฝ่ายบุคคล
examples.translation: Dear Human Resources Manager,

faults.why: Forgetting a fact, an action, or an object are one sense in Thai.

faults.quote: to forget; to be oblivious to
faults.why: 'To be oblivious to' is not in the senses and not an A2 gloss.

faults.quote: Used for both forgetting a memory or fact (e.g., forgetting a name)
faults.why: Just repeats the two senses below.

notes: Can be followed by a noun (forget a thing or fact) or directly by a verb (forget to do something).
To say you left something behind somewhere, use ลืม...ไว้ (e.g., ลืมกุญแจไว้ที่บ้าน 'left my keys at home').
Also appears in the common expression ลืมตา ('to open one's eyes').

senses.definition: To fail to remember a fact or to do something, or to accidentally leave something behind.

examples.text: ฉันลืมชื่อของเขาไปแล้ว
examples.translation: I have forgotten his name.

examples.text: อย่าลืมปิดไฟก่อนออกจากบ้าน
examples.translation: Don't forget to turn off the lights before leaving the house.

faults.quote: to smell; to hear; news
faults.why: Includes noun 'news' and literary 'hear' which is not an everyday standalone verb sense.

faults.quote: To perceive sound with the ears; to hear about something.
faults.why: As a standalone verb in modern Mandarin, 闻 only means 'to smell'; 'hear' is literary/bound.

faults.quote: 此 闻 让 人 惊 讶 。
faults.why: Ungrammatical pseudo-classical sentence with spaces between characters, using 闻 as a noun.

notes: In modern spoken Chinese, 闻 as a standalone verb only means 'to smell' (unlike 听 tīng, 'to listen/hear').
Its older meaning 'to hear' survives in common compound words like 新闻 (xīnwén, news) and 听说 / 耳闻.

senses.definition: To perceive a scent or odor with the nose, or to sniff at something.

examples.text: 我闻到了饭菜的香味。
examples.translation: I smelled the aroma of the food.

examples.text: 你闻闻这朵花，真香！
examples.translation: Smell this flower, it smells so good!

faults.quote: to eat; to drink; to suffer
faults.why: 'To drink' is not a standard Mandarin sense of 吃.

faults.quote: Besides food, 吃 is used for drinks that involve a spoon
faults.why: Neither 吃药 (pills) nor 吃面 (noodles) are drinks; soup takes 喝汤 in standard Mandarin.

faults.quote: To consume a liquid or take medication.
faults.why: 吃 does not mean 'to consume a liquid' in standard Mandarin, and merges nicely with sense 0.

corrected.shortGloss: to eat; to take (medicine); to suffer
notes: Besides solid food, 吃 is used for taking medicine: 吃药 (chī yào).
For liquids (water, tea, soup), standard Mandarin uses 喝 (hē): 喝水 (drink water), 喝汤 (eat/drink soup).

senses.definition: To put food in your mouth and swallow it, or to have a meal; also used for taking medicine.

examples.text: 我们去吃晚饭吧。
examples.translation: Let's go eat dinner.

examples.text: 饭后记得吃药。
examples.translation: Remember to take your medicine after the meal.

senses.definition: To suffer from or endure something unpleasant (often in fixed expressions).

examples.text: 这次创业他吃了很多苦。
examples.translation: He suffered a lot of hardship starting this business.

faults.quote: To depart or leave a place.
faults.why: In Mandarin, 'to leave' is 走 (zǒu), not 走路 (zǒulù), which only means 'to walk'.

faults.quote: 时间不早了，我们该走路了。
faults.why: Unnatural Mandarin; a native speaker says 该走了 ('should leave'), not 该走路了.

corrected.shortGloss: to walk; to go on foot
notes: 走路 is a separable verb (走 + 路, 'walk + road'), so modifiers go in the middle: 走了很多路 (walked a long way).
Do not confuse 走路 ('to walk / go on foot') with 走 alone, which often means 'to leave' (我们该走了, 'we should leave').

senses.definition: To move or travel on foot.

examples.text: 我每天走路去上学。
examples.translation: I walk to school every day.

faults.why: 笑 is one undifferentiated concept in Chinese covering both smiling and laughing.
Missing the common transitive sense 'to laugh at / make fun of' (笑我).

faults.quote: 笑 can mean both to smile and to laugh, depending on the context.
faults.why: Merely restates the glosses without adding usage guidance.

corrected.shortGloss: to smile; to laugh; to laugh at
notes: To specify 'to smile', use 微笑 (wēixiào); to specify 'to laugh out loud', use 大笑 (dàxiào).
When followed directly by a person or thing (笑某人), it means 'to laugh at' or 'to make fun of'.

senses.definition: To smile or laugh when happy, amused, or being friendly.

examples.text: 听到这个笑话大家都笑了。
examples.translation: Everyone laughed when they heard the joke.

examples.text: 她看着我笑了。
examples.translation: She looked at me and smiled.

senses.definition: To laugh at or make fun of someone.

examples.text: 我的中文不好，请别笑我。
examples.translation: My Chinese isn't good, please don't laugh at me.

faults.why: Should note that 离开 is transitive and directly takes the place/person left without a preposition.

faults.quote: 离开 combines the concept of separating (离) and opening up or starting (开).
faults.why: Etymological breakdown is unhelpful filler compared to explaining its grammar.

notes: 离开 is directly followed by the place or person being left, with no preposition: 离开北京 (leave Beijing), never *离开从北京.
Unlike 走 (zǒu, 'to leave'), 离开 usually takes an object naming what or whom you are leaving.

senses.definition: To go away from a place or person.

examples.text: 他明天就要离开北京了。
examples.translation: He is going to leave Beijing tomorrow.

examples.text: 请不要离开这个房间。
examples.translation: Please do not leave this room.

senses.definition: To be separated from or do without something or someone.

examples.text: 现代人很难离开手机。
examples.translation: Modern people find it hard to do without their phones.

faults.why: Form I verbs in Arabic need the imperfect (present) stem vowel noted (يَسْبَحُ).

notes: Imperfect: يَسْبَحُ (yasbaḥu); verbal noun: سِبَاحَة (sibāḥa, swimming).

senses.definition: To move the body through water.

examples.text: سَبَحْتُ فِي البَحْرِ اليَوْمَ.
examples.translation: I swam in the sea today.

senses.definition: To float or drift on the surface of a liquid.

examples.text: سَبَحَتِ الأَوْراقُ عَلَى سَطْحِ المَاءِ.
examples.translation: The leaves floated on the surface of the water.

faults.quote: /ʔaʕtˤa/
faults.why: Final alif maqṣūra represents a long vowel /aː/.

faults.quote: Used for giving physical objects, but also for abstract concepts
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses that أَعْطَى takes two direct objects without a preposition.
Physical and abstract 'give' are one everyday sense.

notes: Imperfect: يُعْطِي (yuʕṭī). Takes two direct objects (the recipient and the thing given), or takes لِـ (li-) before the recipient.

senses.definition: To hand, provide, or offer something to someone.

examples.text: أَعْطِنِي الْكِتَابَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: Give me the book, please.

examples.text: هَذَا الْعَمَلُ يُعْطِي فُرْصَةً لِلتَّعَلُّمِ.
examples.translation: This job gives a chance to learn.

faults.quote: Note that 'حَمَلَ' is a versatile verb. It is used for carrying
faults.why: Filler restating the senses; misses the imperfect stem vowel (يَحْمِلُ) and the 'be pregnant' sense.

corrected.shortGloss: to carry; to bear; to be pregnant
notes: Imperfect: يَحْمِلُ (yaḥmilu).

senses.definition: To hold and take something or someone from one place to another.

examples.text: حَمَلَ الرَّجُلُ الصُّنْدُوقَ إِلَى السَّيَّارَةِ.
examples.translation: The man carried the box to the car.

senses.definition: To take on or have something abstract, such as a responsibility, meaning, or document.

examples.text: يَحْمِلُ الطَّالِبُ مَسْؤُولِيَّةً كَبِيرَةً.
examples.translation: The student bears a big responsibility.

senses.definition: Of a woman: to be pregnant, or to conceive a child.

examples.text: حَمَلَتْ بِطِفْلِهَا الأَوَّلِ.
examples.translation: She became pregnant with her first child.

faults.quote: Used for putting on or wearing clothing, shoes, or accessories.
faults.why: Restates the definitions; should give the imperfect form (يَلْبَسُ) instead.

faults.quote: He is wearing a blue shirt today.
faults.why: To express ongoing 'is wearing' in MSA, the imperfect يَلْبَسُ or active participle is normal, or translate past.

notes: Imperfect: يَلْبَسُ (yalbasu). Covers both the action of putting clothes on and the state of wearing them.

senses.definition: To put clothes, shoes, or accessories on the body, or to have them on.

examples.text: يَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا أَزْرَقَ الْيَوْمَ.
examples.translation: He is wearing a blue shirt today.

examples.text: لَبِسَ مِعْطَفَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ.
examples.translation: He put on his coat before going out.

faults.quote: The verb 'عاش' (to live) refers to the act of existing
faults.why: First sentence restates the gloss and contrasts a verb with a noun; hollow verb conjugation (يَعِيشُ) is missing.

notes: Hollow verb; imperfect: يَعِيشُ (yaʕīšu), 1st person past: عِشْتُ (ʕištu).
Broader than سَكَنَ (sakana, to reside/dwell), which refers more specifically to one's housing or address.

senses.definition: To be alive, or to spend one's life in a particular way or time.

examples.text: عَاشَ جَدِّي طَوِيلًا.
examples.translation: My grandfather lived for a long time.

senses.definition: To have one's home in a particular place.

examples.text: أَنَا أَعِيشُ فِي القَاهِرَةِ.
examples.translation: I live in Cairo.

faults.quote: /zaˈpɔ.mi.nat͡ɕ/
faults.why: Wrong stress: Polish stresses the penultimate syllable (/za.pɔˈmi.nat͡ɕ/).
Should mention that it takes the genitive case or 'o' + locative.

notes: Imperfective verb (used for habits or repeated actions); its perfective partner is 'zapomnieć'.
Followed by the genitive case (zapominać hasła), 'o' + locative (zapominać o spotkaniu), or an infinitive.

senses.definition: To fail to remember a fact, information, or an intention.

examples.text: Często zapominam wyłączyć światło.
examples.translation: I often forget to turn off the light.

senses.definition: To accidentally leave an item behind somewhere.

examples.text: Nie zapominaj swojego telefonu.
examples.translation: Don't forget your phone.

faults.quote: /zasˈkɔ.ʂɔ.nɨ/
faults.why: Wrong consonant (/t͡ʂ/, not /ʂ/) and wrong stress (penultimate: /za.skɔˈt͡ʂɔ.nɨ/).

faults.quote: This is a masculine adjective. Use 'zaskoczona' for feminine subjects
faults.why: Standard Polish adjective inflection is basic grammar, not lexical information for a specific entry.

notes: Usually followed by a noun in the instrumental case to show the cause (e.g., 'zaskoczony wynikiem' — surprised by the result).

senses.definition: Feeling wonder or shock because something unexpected has happened.

examples.text: Byłem bardzo zaskoczony, gdy zobaczyłem go w mieście.
examples.translation: I was very surprised when I saw him in the city.

faults.quote: /zaf.stɨˈdzo.nɨ/
faults.why: Uses non-IPAdigraph 'dz' instead of /d͡z/, and /o/ instead of Polish /ɔ/.
Senses 0 and 1 are the same meaning (embarrassed/abashed); sense 0's example matches sense 1.

notes: Do not confuse with 'nieśmiały' (shy), which is a personality trait; 'zawstydzony' is a temporary feeling in a specific situation.

senses.definition: Feeling embarrassed, ashamed, or self-conscious because of something you did or an awkward situation.

examples.text: Byłem bardzo zawstydzony, kiedy wszyscy zaczęli na mnie patrzeć.
examples.translation: I was very embarrassed when everyone started looking at me.

faults.quote: /ˈzav.ʂɛ/
faults.why: Voiced 'w' assimilates to voiceless /f/ before voiceless /ʂ/: /ˈzaf.ʂɛ/.

faults.quote: Use 'zawsze' to talk about things that happen at all times
faults.why: Notes only restate the definition and list random basic time adverbs nobody confuses phonetically.

senses.definition: At all times or on every occasion.

examples.text: Ona zawsze pije kawę rano.
examples.translation: She always drinks coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: /zaˈzdro.snɨ/
faults.why: Uses /o/ instead of standard Polish /ɔ/: /zaˈzdrɔ.snɨ/.

faults.quote: When someone is 'zazdrosny' because they want what you have
faults.why: Restates the two senses while omitting the required preposition and case ('o' + accusative).

notes: Takes the preposition 'o' followed by the accusative case to name the person or thing (e.g., 'zazdrosny o brata' — jealous of one's brother).

senses.definition: Unhappy because you want something that someone else has.

examples.text: Byłem zazdrosny o jego nowy samochód.
examples.translation: I was envious of his new car.

senses.definition: Feeling suspicious or fearful that a romantic partner might give their attention to someone else.

examples.text: On jest bardzo zazdrosny o swoją dziewczynę.
examples.translation: He is very jealous of his girlfriend.

faults.quote: To gain understanding or insight through observation or practice.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning (to learn/acquire knowledge).

faults.quote: It is a versatile term often used for both self-directed learning
faults.why: Restates note 0 and adds no practical usage guidance.

notes: While เรียน (riian) usually refers to studying a subject or attending school, เรียนรู้ (riian-rúu) emphasizes the process of gaining knowledge, skills, or insight through experience and practice.
Often takes จาก (jàak, 'from') to indicate the source of learning: เรียนรู้จาก... (to learn from...).

senses.definition: To gain knowledge, understanding, or a skill through study, practice, or experience.

examples.text: ฉันชอบเรียนรู้สิ่งใหม่ๆ ทุกวัน
examples.translation: I like to learn new things every day.

examples.text: เราต้องเรียนรู้จากความผิดพลาดของตัวเอง
examples.translation: We have to learn from our own mistakes.

faults.quote: to lose; to be allergic; to be inferior to
faults.why: Includes 'to be inferior to', which is not covered in the senses.

faults.quote: It differs from 'màai chánaa' (not winning), as 'pháe' is the direct verb
faults.why: Both notes are filler restating the glosses or making trivial comparisons with bad romanization.

corrected.shortGloss: to lose; to be allergic to
notes: In the allergy sense, it takes the allergen directly as an object without a preposition (e.g., แพ้อาหารทะเล — to be allergic to seafood). Also used in แพ้ท้อง (to have morning sickness).
Do not confuse with หาย (hǎai) or ทำหาย (tham hǎai), which mean 'to lose' an object.

senses.definition: To be defeated in a game, match, competition, or fight.

examples.text: เราไม่อยากแพ้ในเกมนี้
examples.translation: We don't want to lose in this game.

senses.definition: To have an allergic or adverse physical reaction to a substance.

examples.text: ฉันแพ้เกสรดอกไม้
examples.translation: I am allergic to pollen.

faults.quote: To hold something tightly against your body or to cling to something.
faults.why: Hugging a person and hugging a teddy bear are the same sense in Thai.

faults.quote: This verb is used for both a physical embrace with the arms
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage advice.

notes: Unlike อุ้ม (ûm), which means to lift and hold someone or something in your arms (such as carrying a baby or pet), กอด simply means to wrap your arms around them.
Also appears in the common expression กอดอก (kɔ̀ɔt òk, 'to fold/cross one's arms across the chest').

senses.definition: To hold someone or something closely in your arms, especially to show affection.

examples.text: ฉันชอบกอดแม่
examples.translation: I like to hug my mom.

examples.text: เด็กน้อยกอดตุ๊กตาหมีไว้แน่น
examples.translation: The little child hugged the teddy bear tightly.

faults.quote: to pull; to attract; to stretch
faults.why: Includes 'to stretch', which is not in the senses.

faults.quote: สีแดงช่วยดึงดูดสายตาได้ดี
faults.why: Uses the distinct compound verb ดึงดูด (to attract) instead of the lemma ดึง.

faults.quote: Use 'ดึง' when you physically pull an object towards yourself
faults.why: Notes 0 and 2 merely repeat the definitions of senses 0 and 1.

notes: Often seen on doors as the opposite of ผลัก (phlàk, 'to push away') or ดัน (dan, 'to push/press').
To mean 'to attract' attention or interest, the compound ดึงดูด (dɯng-dùut) is usually used rather than ดึง alone.

senses.definition: To apply force to move something towards yourself or in the direction of the force.

examples.text: เขาดึงประตูให้เปิดออก
examples.translation: He pulled the door open.

faults.quote: Used for everything from chopping food to cutting hair or fabric.
faults.why: Contradicts note 1: in Thai, chopping/slicing food usually uses หั่น or สับ, not ตัด.

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to trim; to disconnect
notes: Used for cutting hair, nails, paper, cloth, grass, or trees (often with scissors or clippers). For slicing or chopping food in cooking, Thai uses หั่น (hàn) or สับ (sàp) instead.

senses.definition: To divide, trim, or separate something using a sharp tool such as scissors or a knife.

examples.text: ฉันจะไปตัดผมพรุ่งนี้
examples.translation: I am going to get my hair cut tomorrow.

senses.definition: To stop a supply, connection, or relationship, such as electricity, water, or a phone call.

examples.text: เขาตัดสายโทรศัพท์ทิ้ง
examples.translation: He hung up the phone.

faults.why: Polish plurale tantum nouns have nonvirile (plural) gender; clarify if schema lacks it.

notes: 'Spodnie' is a plural-only noun (nonvirile gender). Even for one pair of trousers, use plural verbs and adjectives (e.g., 'nowe spodnie są...').
Do not confuse with the diminutive 'spodenki', which specifically means 'shorts'.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing that covers the body from the waist down, with a separate part for each leg.

examples.text: Muszę kupić nowe spodnie, bo te są za krótkie.
examples.translation: I need to buy new trousers because these are too short.

faults.quote: Use 'spokojny' to describe a person who does not panic...
faults.why: Merely restates the two sense definitions without adding usage information.

notes: The adverb 'spokojnie!' is commonly used as an exclamation meaning 'calm down!' or 'take it easy!'.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: not worried, nervous, or excited; feeling at ease.

examples.text: Mój brat jest bardzo spokojnym człowiekiem.
examples.translation: My brother is a very calm person.

senses.definition: Of a place or time: free from noise, disturbance, or busy activity.

examples.text: To bardzo spokojne miejsce na wakacje.
examples.translation: This is a very quiet place for a vacation.

faults.why: Work and social arranged meetings are shades of one Polish sense ('arranged meeting').

faults.quote: Spotkanie is a very versatile word. While it is the standard...
faults.why: Both notes are filler restating the senses or obvious part-of-speech differences.

notes: Takes the preposition 'z' + instrumental case for the person you are meeting (e.g., 'spotkanie z przyjacielem' — a meeting with a friend), and 'na' + accusative for going to a meeting ('iść na spotkanie').

senses.definition: An occasion when people come together by arrangement, either for work or socially.

examples.text: Muszę dzisiaj przygotować prezentację na spotkanie.
examples.translation: I have to prepare a presentation for the meeting today.

examples.text: To było bardzo miłe spotkanie przy kawie.
examples.translation: It was a very nice get-together over coffee.

senses.definition: An occasion of meeting someone, especially unexpectedly.

examples.text: Nasze przypadkowe spotkanie w sklepie było zaskoczeniem.
examples.translation: Our chance meeting at the store was a surprise.

faults.quote: This verb describes planned meetings (e.g., meeting a friend for coffee)
faults.why: Transitive 'spotykać kogoś' means meeting by chance; planned meetings require reflexive 'spotykać się z kimś'.

faults.quote: To come together with someone by appointment or by chance.
faults.why: Conflates transitive 'spotykać' (chance encounter) with reflexive 'spotykać się' (planned meeting / dating).

corrected.shortGloss: to meet; to run into; to meet up
notes: Imperfective verb; the perfective partner is 'spotkać'.
Without 'się' ('spotykać kogoś' + accusative), it usually means running into someone by chance. For planned meetings or dating, use the reflexive 'spotykać się z kimś' (+ instrumental).

senses.definition: To come across someone, especially by chance while going somewhere.

examples.text: Często spotykam moich sąsiadów w parku.
examples.translation: I often run into my neighbors in the park.

senses.definition: (reflexive: spotykać się) To come together with someone by arrangement, or to spend time together socially or romantically.

examples.text: W weekendy często spotykam się z przyjaciółmi.
examples.translation: On weekends I often meet up with friends.

faults.quote: Used for people, 'alto' means 'tall'. For objects or places,
faults.why: Restates the senses and glosses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'altezza', which is the noun 'height'.
faults.why: Unlikely confusion between basic adjective and noun; misses irregular comparative 'più alto' / 'superiore'.

faults.quote: Located at a great distance from the ground or base.
faults.why: Only covers position above ground, not vertical measurement of objects (a mountain) or levels.

notes: Placed before some nouns, it changes meaning: 'un uomo alto' (a tall man) vs. 'un alto funzionario' (a high-ranking official).

senses.definition: Of a person, building, tree, etc.: of greater than average height.

examples.text: Mio fratello è molto alto.
examples.translation: My brother is very tall.

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from base to top, or situated far above the ground; also great in amount, degree, or level.

examples.text: La montagna è molto alta.
examples.translation: The mountain is very high.

examples.text: I prezzi sono troppo alti qui.
examples.translation: Prices are too high here.

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: strong in volume.

examples.text: La musica è troppo alta.
examples.translation: The music is too loud.

faults.quote: To feel a strong sense of sympathy or attraction towards someone.
faults.why: Artificial split; 'amare' towards a person means to love, not 'to like a friend'.

faults.quote: Penso che lui ami molto la sua nuova amica.
faults.why: Saying someone 'ama molto la sua amica' means romantic love, not just liking a friend.
Should mention 'volere bene a', the everyday phrase for loving family and friends.

notes: For romantic love, Italians say 'ti amo', whereas for affection toward family and friends they usually say 'ti voglio bene'.
For liking or loving everyday things, food, or hobbies, 'piacere' or 'adorare' is more common in speech.

senses.definition: To feel deep romantic love or strong affection for someone.

examples.text: Amo molto la mia famiglia.
examples.translation: I love my family very much.

senses.definition: To like or enjoy something very much.

examples.text: Molti italiani amano bere il caffè la mattina.
examples.translation: Many Italians love to drink coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: /aˈmi.ke.vo.le/
faults.why: Wrong stress: primary stress in 'amichevole' is on 'che' (/amiˈkevole/).

faults.quote: Used to describe both people who are warm and approachable, and situations
faults.why: Purely repeats the definitions of the two senses.

notes: Has the same form 'amichevole' for both masculine and feminine singular (plural 'amichevoli').

senses.definition: Of a person or their behaviour: kind, warm, and pleasant to others.

examples.text: Il nuovo collega è molto amichevole con tutti.
examples.translation: The new colleague is very friendly with everyone.

senses.definition: Of an agreement, relationship, or sports match: without conflict or competition.

examples.text: Hanno trovato un accordo amichevole.
examples.translation: They reached an amicable agreement.

faults.quote: to go; to move; to fit
faults.why: Misses 'to work/function' (sense 1) and includes 'to move' which is not a gloss.
Lacks the very common A1/A2 uses 'Come va?' (how is it going?) and 'mi va' (to feel like).

corrected.shortGloss: to go; to work; to fit; to feel like
notes: Irregular in the present tense: vado, vai, va, andiamo, andate, vanno. Takes 'essere' in compound tenses (sono andato/a).
Takes 'a' before cities and infinitives (vado a Roma, vado a dormire) and 'in' before countries and means of transport (vado in Italia, vado in treno).

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.

examples.text: Domani vado a Roma.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to Rome.

senses.definition: To proceed or be in a particular state, especially in greetings.

examples.text: Ciao Marco, come va?
examples.translation: Hi Marco, how is it going?

senses.definition: Of a machine or device: to function or operate.

examples.text: La macchina non va più.
examples.translation: The car is not working anymore.

senses.definition: To be the right size, or to suit or please someone (especially in 'andare bene' or 'mi va').

examples.text: Questi pantaloni mi vanno bene.
examples.translation: These pants fit me well.

examples.text: Ti va un caffè?
examples.translation: Do you feel like a coffee?

faults.quote: bored; weary
faults.why: 'weary' is not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: Use 'annoiato' when someone feels dull and listless because nothing interesting is
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: Durante la lezione lunga, mi sono sentito molto annoiato.
faults.why: Unnatural phrasing; in Italian one would say 'mi sono annoiato molto' or 'ero molto annoiato'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'noioso', which means 'boring' (describing the thing or person causing the boredom).

senses.definition: Feeling tired and impatient because something is not interesting or there is nothing to do.

examples.text: I bambini erano molto annoiati durante il viaggio.
examples.translation: The children were very bored during the trip.

faults.why: Missing essential A2 grammar note: stem-changing verb (o > ue in present, o > u in preterite).

faults.quote: Siempre me suelo dormir leyendo un libro.
faults.why: 'Siempre' + 'soler' is redundant; also splits the pronominal 'dormirse' awkwardly for A2.

notes: Stem-changing verb: the 'o' changes to 'ue' in the present tense (duermo, duermes...) and to 'u' in the third-person preterite (durmió, durmieron) and gerund (durmiendo).
For the action of falling asleep, use the reflexive form 'dormirse'.

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed and your body inactive.

examples.text: Los niños necesitan dormir ocho horas.
examples.translation: Children need to sleep eight hours.

senses.definition: (reflexive, dormirse) To pass into the state of sleep.

examples.text: Siempre me duermo leyendo un libro.
examples.translation: I always fall asleep reading a book.

faults.quote: /ˈdul.se/
faults.why: In Castilian Spanish (es-ES), 'c' before 'e' is /θ/, so /ˈdulθe/, not seseo /ˈdulse/.

faults.quote: Used both for food tasting of sugar and figuratively for a gentle,
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to note invariable gender and 'agua dulce' (fresh water).

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine (el vino dulce, la fruta dulce).
In the phrase 'agua dulce', it means 'fresh water' (as opposed to 'agua salada', salt water).

senses.definition: Having a taste like that of sugar or honey.

examples.text: Esta fruta está muy dulce y madura.
examples.translation: This fruit is very sweet and ripe.

senses.definition: Pleasant, mild, and gentle in character, sound, or appearance.

examples.text: Tiene una voz muy dulce cuando habla.
examples.translation: She has a very sweet voice when she speaks.

faults.quote: Duro is a versatile word. It can describe a physical object
faults.why: Pure filler that just summarizes the three senses already listed below.

notes: Do not confuse with 'difícil' (complicated, not easy to solve or do). A 'trabajo duro' is exhausting or demanding, while a 'trabajo difícil' is complex.
Also commonly used as an adverb without changing form: 'trabajar duro' (to work hard).

senses.definition: Firm and solid; not easily bent, broken, or pressed.

examples.text: La cama es demasiado dura para mi espalda.
examples.translation: The bed is too hard for my back.

senses.definition: Of food: difficult to cut or chew.

examples.text: La carne estaba muy dura y no pude terminarla.
examples.translation: The meat was very tough and I couldn't finish it.

senses.definition: Requiring great physical or emotional effort; difficult to bear.

examples.text: Ha sido un año muy duro para nuestra familia.
examples.translation: It has been a very tough year for our family.

faults.quote: To notice that something is absent or not present in a place
faults.why: Using 'echar de menos' for noticing misplaced keys is literary/archaic; everyday Spanish uses 'faltar'.

notes: This is the standard way to say 'to miss' someone or something in Spain; in Latin America, 'extrañar' is more common.
Adverbs like 'mucho'usually go right after 'echar': 'Te echo mucho de menos' (I miss you a lot).

senses.definition: To feel sad because someone you love is not with you, or because you do not have something you used to have.

examples.text: Echo mucho de menos a mis padres cuando estoy en el extranjero.
examples.translation: I miss my parents a lot when I am abroad.

examples.text: ¿Echas de menos la comida de tu país?
examples.translation: Do you miss the food from your country?

faults.quote: Having received academic instruction or training.
faults.why: Contradicts the note! 'Educado' is a false friend and means polite; academically educated is 'culto'/'formado'.

faults.quote: polite; well-educated
faults.why: Includes the false friend 'well-educated', misleading English learners.

notes: False friend: 'educado' (and 'buena educación') refers to good manners and politeness, not academic schooling. To say someone is well-educated academically, use 'culto' or 'con estudios'.
Its opposite is 'maleducado' (rude, impolite).

senses.definition: Having good manners and showing respect for others.

examples.text: Los niños fueron muy educados durante la cena.
examples.translation: The children were very polite during dinner.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with rezar (to pray), which sounds similar.
faults.why: Besar and rezar do not sound similar in Castilian Spanish (/b...s/ vs /r...θ/).

notes: Takes the personal 'a' before a person (besar a alguien), and is used reflexively (besarse) when people kiss each other.

senses.definition: To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or greeting.

examples.text: Ella decidió besar a su novio en la mejilla antes de salir.
examples.translation: She decided to kiss her boyfriend on the cheek before leaving.

faults.quote: A target or objective in a shooting game or sport.
faults.why: Noun sense included in an adjective entry.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk; the lightest colour.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality.

faults.quote: white; blank; target
faults.why: Includes 'blank' (missing from senses) and 'target' (a noun, not an adjective).

notes: The phrase 'en blanco' means 'blank' (e.g., una página en blanco — a blank page).
Also used as a masculine noun (el blanco) meaning the colour white or a 'target'.

senses.definition: Having the colour of snow or milk; of the lightest colour.

examples.text: La nieve es muy blanca.
examples.translation: The snow is very white.

faults.quote: Lacking firmness in texture, often because it is overcooked or ripe.
faults.why: Softness of objects and softness of food are the same basic meaning.

faults.quote: Blando is used for anything that yields easily to pressure.
faults.why: Restates the definition while missing the false friend warning for English 'bland'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'suave', which means 'smooth' to the touch or 'gentle/mild' (a pillow is 'blando'; silk is 'suave').
False friend: does not mean 'bland' (tasteless), which is 'soso' or 'insípido'.

senses.definition: Not hard or firm; yielding easily when pressed or chewed.

examples.text: El colchón es muy blando.
examples.translation: The mattress is very soft.

examples.text: La fruta está demasiado blanda.
examples.translation: The fruit is too soft.

faults.quote: good; kind; tasty; okay
faults.why: 'okay' is listed in shortGloss (an interjection) but is not among the adjective senses.
Missing the crucial ser vs. estar distinction with 'bueno' (kind/good vs. tasty/healthy/attractive).

notes: Shortens to 'buen' before a masculine singular noun (e.g., un buen libro).
Used with 'ser' for general quality or moral character (es bueno = he is kind), and with 'estar' for taste, health, or physical attractiveness (está bueno = it is tasty).

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, beneficial, or satisfactory.

examples.text: Es un buen libro para aprender español.
examples.translation: It is a good book for learning Spanish.

senses.definition: Having a kind, helpful, or morally positive nature.

examples.text: Ella es una persona muy buena.
examples.translation: She is a very kind person.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: pleasant in flavour; delicious.

examples.text: La paella está muy buena.
examples.translation: The paella is very tasty.

faults.quote: Note that 'piwo' is a neuter noun.
faults.why: Restates the gender field and duplicates the example sentence.

notes: The diminutive 'piwko' is very common in casual conversation (e.g., 'Idziemy na piwko?' – 'Shall we go for a beer?').

senses.definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grain and flavoured with hops.

examples.text: Poproszę zimne piwo.
examples.translation: I would like a cold beer.

faults.quote: Kupili działkę i budują dom na nowym placu.
faults.why: Redundant and unnatural; Sense 1 is mainly used in compounds like 'plac zabaw' or 'plac budowy'.

notes: Do not confuse 'plac' (an urban square or designated outdoor area) with 'miejsce' (a general word for 'place' or 'space').
Takes the preposition 'na' for both location ('na placu' – in the square) and direction ('na plac' – to the square).

senses.definition: An open public area in a town or city, usually where several streets meet.

examples.text: Spotkamy się na głównym placu miasta.
examples.translation: We will meet at the main town square.

senses.definition: An outdoor area used for a specific purpose, such as a playground or construction site.

examples.text: Dzieci bawią się na placu zabaw.
examples.translation: The children are playing on the playground.

faults.quote: common
faults.why: Polish has no 'common' gender; pluralia tantum nouns have non-virile plural gender or no singular gender.

faults.quote: Boli mnie cały kręgosłup i plecy.
faults.why: Uses singular verb 'boli' by proximity, contradicting the note about plural verb agreement.

notes: 'Plecy' is a plural-only noun (non-virile plural) and always takes plural verbs and adjectives, even for one person's back (e.g., 'Bolą mnie plecy' – 'My back hurts').

senses.definition: The rear part of the human body, from the neck to the hips.

examples.text: Od siedzenia przy biurku bolą mnie plecy.
examples.translation: My back hurts from sitting at a desk.

examples.text: Położył się na plecach na trawie.
examples.translation: He lay down on his back on the grass.

faults.quote: A strong inclination, attraction, or affinity toward something or someone.
faults.why: Too marginal and literary for an A2 beginner entry; 'train' is the only needed sense.

faults.quote: Note that 'pociąg' can also mean an attraction
faults.why: Merely repeats Sense 1 and is unneeded at A2.

notes: To say 'by train', use the instrumental case without a preposition: 'jechać pociągiem' (to go by train).

senses.definition: A series of connected railway carriages pulled by an engine along a track.

examples.text: Pociąg odjeżdża z peronu trzeciego.
examples.translation: The train leaves from platform three.

faults.quote: (swallow) To move a liquid from the mouth to the stomach.
faults.why: Swallowing is part of drinking, not a distinct sense of 'beber'.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to drink alcohol'.

notes: In Mexico and most of Latin America, 'tomar' is much more common than 'beber' in everyday speech, though both are understood.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.text: Siempre debo beber agua después de correr.
examples.translation: I always need to drink water after running.

senses.definition: To consume alcoholic drinks.

examples.text: Si vas a manejar, es mejor no beber.
examples.translation: If you are going to drive, it is better not to drink.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'abrazar', which means to hug.
faults.why: Unrelated form and sound; learners do not confuse 'besar' with 'abrazar'.

notes: Takes the personal 'a' before a person (besar a alguien), and is used reflexively (besarse) when people kiss each other.

senses.definition: To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or greeting.

examples.text: Ella decidió besar a su novio en la mejilla.
examples.translation: She decided to kiss her boyfriend on the cheek.

faults.quote: white; blank; target
faults.why: 'Target' is a noun meaning and not in the senses of this adjective entry.

faults.quote: The colour of snow or milk.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality.

faults.quote: Something that has no writing, print, or marks on it.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Something that...').

faults.quote: El examen estaba en blanco porque no estudié.
faults.why: Uses the adverbial idiom 'en blanco' (where 'blanco' is a noun), not the adjective.

faults.quote: As an adjective, remember to match the gender: 'una camisa blanca'
faults.why: Standard regular gender agreement applies to almost all Spanish adjectives.

notes: To say a page or screen is 'blank' (empty of writing), Spanish uses the phrase 'en blanco': 'una hoja en blanco' (a blank sheet of paper).

senses.definition: Having the color of snow or milk; of the lightest color.

examples.text: Me compré una camisa blanca para la fiesta.
examples.translation: I bought a white shirt for the party.

senses.definition: Of a person or their skin: having a light complexion, or pale from fear or illness.

examples.text: Se puso blanco del susto.
examples.translation: He turned pale from the fright.

faults.quote: When referring to food, 'bueno' means 'tasty' or 'delicious'.
faults.why: Restates sense 2 without adding usage information (like taking 'estar' vs 'ser').

notes: Shortens to 'buen' directly before a masculine singular noun (e.g., 'un buen libro').
With 'ser', it means good in quality, healthy, or kind ('es bueno'). With 'estar', it means tasty for food ('está bueno').
Do not confuse 'bueno' (adjective, describes nouns) with 'bien' (adverb, describes verbs or how someone feels: 'estoy bien').

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or satisfactory.

examples.text: Esta es una buena película.
examples.translation: This is a good movie.

senses.definition: Having a kind, helpful, or moral character.

examples.text: Él es un hombre muy bueno.
examples.translation: He is a very kind man.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: tasting pleasant.

examples.text: ¡Qué bueno está este postre!
examples.translation: How delicious this dessert is!

faults.quote: (position) Facing or opposite to someone or something.
faults.why: As 'facing/opposite', 对 is a verb or bound morpheme (as in 面对面), not a standalone adjective.

faults.quote: 我们面对面坐着。
faults.why: Uses the set phrase 面对面, not 对 as an adjective.

notes: Its opposite is 错 (cuò, 'wrong'). Predicate adjectives like 对 are often used with 是……的: 这是对的 ('This is right').
对 is also very common as a preposition meaning 'to' or 'towards' (对我说, 'say to me') and as a measure word for a pair.

senses.definition: Free from error; conforming to fact or truth.

examples.text: 你的回答是对的。
examples.translation: Your answer is correct.

faults.quote: Used to describe size, age, or degree.
faults.why: Merely restates the senses without adding usage information.

notes: Often prefixed to a surname to address a younger friend or colleague affectionately, e.g. 小李 ('Little Li').

senses.definition: Little in size, volume, or scale; not big.

examples.text: 这件衣服太小了。
examples.translation: This piece of clothing is too small.

senses.definition: Young in years; younger than someone else.

examples.text: 他比我小三岁。
examples.translation: He is three years younger than me.

faults.quote: (condition) Not worn out or used before; in good condition.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the single everyday meaning 'new'; merge them.

faults.quote: 新 (xīn) is used for things that are recently made, bought, or
faults.why: Restates the definition without giving extra grammatical or usage help.

notes: For fresh food or air, use 新鲜 (xīnxiān) rather than 新 alone.

senses.definition: Recently made, bought, or started; not old or worn.

examples.text: 我买了一辆新车。
examples.translation: I bought a new car.

examples.text: 这件衣服看起来很新。
examples.translation: This piece of clothing looks very new.

faults.quote: 渴 (kě) is the state of being thirsty. It is often combined
faults.why: Restates the gloss; 渴 is most often used simply as 口渴 or 很渴.

notes: Often used in the compound 口渴 (kǒukě, literally 'mouth-thirsty') with the same meaning.
Do not confuse with 喝 (hē, 'to drink'): 渴 has the water radical (氵) on the left, while 喝 has the mouth radical (口).

senses.definition: Feeling a need to drink something.

examples.text: 我今天没喝水，所以我很渴。
examples.translation: I didn't drink water today, so I am very thirsty.

faults.quote: /kau̯˥ ɕiŋ˥˩/
faults.why: 兴 in 高兴 is pronounced in the neutral tone in standard Mainland Mandarin, though 4th tone is also heard; more importantly, pinyin has a space.

faults.quote: gāo xìng
faults.why: Pinyin for a single two-syllable word should not have a space between syllables.

notes: Describes being pleased or glad about something specific, often in polite expressions like 很高兴认识你 ('Nice to meet you'). The second syllable is often spoken in a neutral tone (gāoxing).

senses.definition: Feeling pleased and cheerful about something.

examples.text: 见到你我很高兴。
examples.translation: I am very happy to see you.

examples.text: 他听到这个消息很高兴。
examples.translation: He was very pleased when he heard the news.

faults.quote: Used as a color, it behaves like any other adjective.
faults.why: Generic grammar rule applicable to almost all Spanish adjectives.

notes: When describing people, 'negro' can be sensitive depending on tone and context, though 'mi negro/negra' is also used as an affectionate nickname. 'Moreno' or 'afrodescendiente' are common neutral alternatives.

senses.definition: Having the darkest color, like coal or the night sky.

examples.text: Lleva una camisa negra y un pantalón gris.
examples.translation: He is wearing a black shirt and gray pants.

senses.definition: Very dark or without light; also used for coffee without milk.

examples.text: El cielo está muy negro; va a llover.
examples.translation: The sky is very dark; it's going to rain.

faults.quote: /neɾˈβjos(o)/
faults.why: Final /o/ is not optional in standard Mexican Spanish.

faults.quote: It is a false friend to English 'nervous' if used incorrectly
faults.why: 'Nervioso' is a true cognate of English 'nervous', not a false friend.

notes: Use 'estar nervioso' for a temporary feeling (being anxious or on edge) and 'ser nervioso' for a personality trait (being naturally excitable or restless).

senses.definition: Anxious or uneasy, especially because of something that is going to happen.

examples.text: Estoy muy nervioso por el examen de mañana.
examples.translation: I am very nervous about tomorrow's exam.

senses.definition: Having a naturally high-strung, excitable, or restless personality.

examples.text: Mi hermano es muy nervioso; no puede quedarse quieto ni un segundo.
examples.translation: My brother is very restless; he can't sit still for even a second.

faults.quote: If you need to make a negative sentence even stronger
