faults.why: Repeats note 0 and falsely claims 'nadie'/'nunca' merely strengthen negation.

notes: Put 'no' directly before the verb to make a sentence negative. When negative words like 'nada' (nothing), 'nadie' (nobody), or 'nunca' (never) follow the verb, 'no' is still required before the verb: 'No veo nada' (I don't see anything).

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer or express disagreement or refusal.

examples.text: —¿Quieres ir al cine? —No, gracias.
examples.translation: —Do you want to go to the movies? —No, thanks.

senses.definition: Used before a verb, adjective, or adverb to make it negative.

examples.text: No quiero comer ahora.
examples.translation: I do not want to eat now.

senses.definition: Used at the end of a statement to ask for confirmation.

examples.text: Tú eres de Guadalajara, ¿no?
examples.translation: You're from Guadalajara, right?

faults.why: Conflates idioms (胸が躍る, 踊らされる) that are beyond A2.

faults.why: 踊らされる is the causative-passive of 踊る (or passive of 踊らす), not passive potential.

faults.quote: (travel) To stay at a place for a period of time, such

notes: Used for wall/desk calendars, digital calendar apps, and personal paper planners or appointment diaries (also more formally called 'terminarz').

senses.definition: A chart, book, app, or system that shows the days, weeks, and months of a year and is used to record plans and appointments.

examples.text: Muszę zapisać to spotkanie w kalendarzu.
examples.translation: I have to write this meeting down in my calendar.

examples.text: Na ścianie w kuchni wisi nowy kalendarz.
examples.translation: A new calendar is hanging on the wall in the kitchen.

faults.quote: The hard seed inside a stone fruit such as a peach or
faults.why: False friend with English 'stone': a fruit stone/pit in Polish is 'pestka', never 'kamień'.

faults.quote: W środku brzoskwini jest duży kamień.
faults.why: Completely unidiomatic calque from English; Polish speakers say 'pestka'.

faults.quote: as well as the hard seed inside certain fruits like cherries or
faults.why: Teaches a false meaning based on English 'stone'.

notes: Do not confuse with 'skała', which refers to a large rock formation or cliff.
Unlike English 'stone', 'kamień' is never used for the hard seed inside fruit (which is 'pestka').

senses.definition: A hard piece of solid mineral matter found on the ground.

examples.text: Dziecko rzuciło kamień do wody.
examples.translation: The child threw a stone into the water.

senses.definition: A hard crust that builds up inside kettles and pipes or on teeth.

examples.text: Muszę usunąć kamień z czajnika.
examples.translation: I need to remove the limescale from the kettle.

faults.why: Closed and open-faced sandwiches are a single lexical concept in Polish ('kanapka').

notes: In Poland, a typical homemade 'kanapka' is an open-faced slice of bread with butter and toppings (such as cheese, cold cuts, or tomato), though the word is also used for closed sandwiches.

senses.definition: One or two slices of bread with butter and toppings or a filling such as cheese, meat, or vegetables.

examples.text: Na kolację zrobiłam dwie kanapki z serem i pomidorem.
examples.translation: For supper I made two cheese and tomato sandwiches.

faults.quote: Used both for the live farm bird and for the meat
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

faults.quote: La gallina cuida a su pequeño pollo en el campo.
faults.why: A baby chick with its mother is normally called 'pollito', not 'pequeño pollo'.

notes: For the live adult bird on a farm, 'la gallina' (hen) and 'el gallo' (rooster) are more common; 'pollito' is usually used for a baby chick.
Do not confuse with 'la polla', which is vulgar slang for male anatomy in Spain and some other regions.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken eaten as food.

examples.text: Me gusta comer pollo asado con papas.
examples.translation: I like to eat roast chicken with potatoes.

senses.definition: A young domestic chicken.

examples.text: Compramos varios pollos para criar en la granja.
examples.translation: We bought several young chickens to raise on the farm.

faults.quote: /ˈpɾeθjo/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican /s/ (/ˈpɾesjo/).

faults.quote: Use 'precio' when talking about the objective amount of money
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful learner guidance.

notes: Often contrasted with 'el costo', which usually refers to the total expense of producing or doing something.

senses.definition: The amount of money required to buy something.

examples.text: El precio de este libro es muy alto.
examples.translation: The price of this book is very high.

faults.quote: In colloquial speech, 'caer en el primo' or 'verle la cara de primo'
faults.why: 'Caer en el primo' is invented; the Mexican idiom is 'verle la cara de tonto/menso'.

faults.quote: (slang) A naive person who is easy to trick.
faults.why: Primarily Peninsular slang, marginal for an A2 learner of Mexican Spanish.
Missing note on feminine form 'la prima' and plural 'los primos'.

notes: The feminine form is 'la prima' (female cousin). The plural 'los primos' can refer to male cousins or a mixed group.

senses.definition: A son of your aunt or uncle.

examples.text: Mi primo vive en la Ciudad de México.
examples.translation: My cousin lives in Mexico City.

faults.quote: (village) A very small town in the country, often quiet and rural.
faults.why: Spanish 'pueblo' does not split English 'town' and 'village' into two separate senses.

faults.quote: While 'pueblo' can mean a city or town in general
faults.why: Inaccurate ('pueblo' does not mean city) and merely repeats the definition.

notes: When referring to people, 'el pueblo' means a whole nation or community, whereas 'la gente' means people in general.

senses.definition: A small population center in the countryside, smaller than a city.

examples.text: Mis abuelos viven en un pueblo pequeño en las montañas.
examples.translation: My grandparents live in a small town in the mountains.

senses.definition: All the persons who belong to a nation, community, or ethnic group.

examples.text: Es un pueblo que lucha por sus derechos.
examples.translation: It is a people that fights for its rights.

faults.quote: El puente cruza el río muy rápido.
faults.why: A bridge is a static structure and cannot cross a river 'very quickly'.

notes: In Mexico, 'hacer puente' or 'tener puente' is very common for having a long weekend around a public holiday.

senses.definition: A structure built over a river, road, or railway so that people or vehicles can cross.

examples.text: Cruzamos el puente para llegar al otro lado del río.
examples.translation: We crossed the bridge to get to the other side of the river.

senses.definition: A long weekend when a holiday falls next to or near a weekend.

examples.text: Tenemos un puente en noviembre y vamos a ir a la playa.
examples.translation: We have a long weekend in November and we are going to the beach.

faults.quote: To let something drop down or become detached
faults.why: Standard 'caer' is intransitive; transitive 'drop' is a dialectal error ('laísmo'/'loísmo' area)

faults.quote: no vayas a caer el agua
faults.why: Ungrammatical in standard Spanish; should be 'tirar' or 'derramar el agua'
Missing irregular yo-form 'caigo' and 'caérsele algo a alguien' for accidental dropping

corrected.shortGloss: to fall; to make an impression; to fall on (a date)
notes: Irregular in the 'yo' present form: caigo (past participle: caído).
Use 'caerse' when someone trips or falls down, or with an indirect object for dropping something accidentally (Se me cayó el vaso — I dropped the glass).

senses.definition: To move downwards from a higher to a lower place.

examples.text: Las hojas secas empiezan a caer en otoño.
examples.translation: The dry leaves begin to fall in autumn.

senses.definition: Used with 'bien' or 'mal' and an indirect object to say how likeable someone is.

examples.text: Mi nuevo compañero de trabajo me cae muy bien.
examples.translation: I really like my new coworker.

senses.definition: Of a date or holiday: to take place on a particular day.

examples.text: Este año mi cumpleaños cae en sábado.
examples.translation: This year my birthday falls on a Saturday.

faults.quote: Use cálido when describing weather, a friendly personality, or a comfortable
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already shown in the entry

notes: Used for pleasant temperatures (climate, rooms) or warm feelings. For objects, food, or drinks that are warm or hot to the touch, use 'caliente' or 'calentito'.

senses.definition: Having a pleasant, comfortable degree of heat.

examples.text: El sol de la tarde es muy cálido.
examples.translation: The afternoon sun is very warm.

senses.definition: Showing kindness, enthusiasm, or affection in a welcoming way.

examples.text: Nos dieron una bienvenida muy cálida.
examples.translation: They gave us a very warm welcome.

faults.quote: Describes weather that makes you feel heat.
faults.why: In Spain, hot weather is 'caluroso' (un día caluroso), not 'un día caliente'

faults.quote: Hoy hace un día muy caliente.
faults.why: Unnatural in European Spanish; 'un día muy caluroso' or 'hace mucho calor' is used

faults.quote: Caliente refers to the temperature of an object or the weather.
faults.why: False for Castilian Spanish, where 'caliente' is not used for weather

notes: Used with 'estar' for things, food, or drinks that are hot to the touch. For hot weather in Spain, use 'caluroso' or 'hacer calor', not 'caliente'.

senses.definition: Having a high temperature; hot or warm to the touch.

examples.text: Ten cuidado con el plato, que está muy caliente.
examples.translation: Be careful with the plate, it is very hot.

faults.quote: tired; exhausted
faults.why: Misses the second sense ('tiring, tedious') and adds 'exhausted'

faults.quote: /kanˈsado/
faults.why: Should use /ð/ or broad /d/ consistently; here /d/ is fine, but example[1] is unnatural

faults.quote: Sus explicaciones largas son un poco cansadas.
faults.why: In Spain 'ser cansado' applies to chores, trips, or work ('tiring'), rarely explanations ('pesadas')

notes: Used with 'estar' to mean 'tired' (Estoy cansado), and with 'ser' to mean 'tiring' (Es un trabajo muy cansado).

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep after physical or mental effort.

examples.text: Estoy muy cansado después de trabajar todo el día.
examples.translation: I am very tired after working all day.

senses.definition: Of an activity or job: causing fatigue; requiring a lot of effort.

examples.text: Ha sido un viaje muy largo y cansado.
examples.translation: It has been a very long and tiring trip.

faults.why: Missing pronunciation note on the silent 't' in 'listen', a classic beginner pitfall.

notes: La 't' es muda. A diferencia de 'hear' (oír sin intentarlo), 'listen' implica prestar atención y lleva la preposición 'to' antes de lo que se escucha (ej. 'listen to music').

senses.definition: Prestar atención a un sonido o a lo que alguien dice.

examples.text: Please listen to the teacher.
examples.translation: Por favor, escucha al maestro.

examples.text: I like to listen to jazz in the evening.
examples.translation: Me gusta escuchar jazz por la noche.

senses.definition: Aceptar el consejo de alguien o seguir sus indicaciones.

examples.text: I told him not to go, but he didn't listen.
examples.translation: Le dije que no fuera, pero no me hizo caso.

faults.quote: Se usa para indicar el lugar donde una persona tiene su hogar.
faults.why: Restates sense 0 definition; misses the crucial homograph pronunciation contrast with adjective 'live' (/laɪv/).

faults.quote: All living things need water.
faults.why: Uses the lexicalized adjective/noun phrase 'living things' instead of the verb 'live'.

notes: Como verbo se pronuncia /lɪv/ (con 'i' corta); no lo confundas con el adjetivo o adverbio 'live' ('en vivo'), que se pronuncia /laɪv/.

senses.definition: Tener el hogar o la residencia en un lugar determinado.

examples.text: I live in a small apartment near the park.
examples.translation: Vivo en un apartamento pequeño cerca del parque.

senses.definition: Estar con vida o seguir existiendo.

examples.text: My great-grandmother lived until she was ninety-eight.
examples.translation: Mi bisabuela vivió hasta los noventa y ocho años.

faults.quote: en el Reino Unido es más común decir 'sitting room' o 'lounge'
faults.why: 'Living room' is also very common in the UK; the note overstates the difference.

senses.definition: Habitación principal de una casa destinada a descansar, ver la televisión o recibir visitas.

examples.text: The family gathered in the living room to watch a movie.
examples.translation: La familia se reunió en la sala de estar para ver una película.

faults.quote: Se sintió muy solitario en la nueva ciudad
faults.why: Unnatural calque in Spanish: 'sentirse solitario' is not used for feeling lonely; it is 'sentirse solo'.

faults.quote: Lugar apartado donde hay poca gente o es difícil llegar.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Lugar apartado...').

faults.quote: solitario, sentirse solo
faults.why: In Spanish, 'estar/sentirse solo' is the standard translation for feeling lonely; 'solitario' means solitary/lone.

notes: No confundas 'lonely' (triste por falta de compañía, 'sentirse solo') con 'alone' (físicamente sin nadie más, 'estar solo').

senses.definition: Triste porque se está sin compañía y se echa de menos a otras personas.

examples.text: He felt very lonely in the new city after moving away from his friends.
examples.translation: Se sintió muy solo en la nueva ciudad después de alejarse de sus amigos.

senses.definition: Dicho de un lugar: apartado y por donde pasa poca gente.

examples.text: They walked down a lonely road far away from the town.
examples.translation: Caminaron por un camino solitario muy lejos del pueblo.

faults.quote: Se usa para hablar de distancia o de tiempo.
faults.why: Pure filler restating the two senses; misses useful beginner grammar like 'How long...?'.

notes: La pregunta 'How long...?' se usa para preguntar tanto por la duración ('¿Cuánto tiempo...?') como por la longitud ('¿Qué tan largo...?').

senses.definition: Que tiene mucha longitud o distancia de un extremo a otro.

examples.text: She has very long hair.
examples.translation: Ella tiene el cabello muy largo.

senses.definition: Que dura mucho tiempo.

examples.text: It was a long day at work.
examples.translation: Fue un día largo en el trabajo.

faults.quote: To do something for someone or on their behalf.
faults.why: Defines the prepositional/coverb use as a full action verb, contradicting its glosses 'for, to'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this verb with its passive-marker use in some complex
faults.why: Vague and unhelpful without showing how the passive or causative use actually works.

corrected.shortGloss: to give; to, for; to let
notes: Placed before a verb phrase (给 + person + verb), it acts like 'to' or 'for' to mark the recipient or beneficiary (e.g. 给我打电话, call me).
In spoken Mandarin, it can also mark the agent in a passive sentence, like 被 (bèi).

senses.definition: To hand or pass something to someone.

examples.text: 请把那本书给我。
examples.translation: Please give me that book.

senses.definition: Used before a verb to introduce the person who receives or benefits from the action.

examples.text: 我给你买了一杯咖啡。
examples.translation: I bought a cup of coffee for you.

senses.definition: To allow or let someone do something.

examples.text: 请给我看看你的照片。
examples.translation: Please let me look at your photos.

faults.quote: to speak; to say; to explain
faults.why: 'To explain' is not in the glosses, while 'to scold' is missing from shortGloss.

faults.quote: To explain or scold someone for a mistake.
faults.why: Conflates 'explain' with 'scold', while the glosses and example only cover scolding.

faults.quote: 说 (shuō) is the most common verb for speaking, talking, or saying
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to speak, to say; to scold
notes: 说 takes the words spoken or the language (说中文) as its direct object; to simply 'talk' with no object, use 说话 (shuōhuà).
Do not confuse with 告诉 (gàosu, to tell someone); 说 cannot take the listener as a direct object (*说他).

senses.definition: To utter words, express something in words, or speak a language.

examples.text: 请慢一点说，我听不懂。
examples.translation: Please speak a little slower, I don't understand.

examples.text: 他会说一点儿汉语。
examples.translation: He can speak a little Chinese.

senses.definition: To scold or criticize someone for a fault.

examples.text: 因为我迟到了，老师说了我几句。
examples.translation: Because I was late, the teacher scolded me a bit.

faults.why: Fails to mention that single-character 忘 almost always requires 了 (忘了) or a resultative complement.

notes: Rarely used alone; it is usually followed by 了 (忘了) or another verb (忘带, forget to bring), or replaced by the two-syllable verb 忘记 (wàngjì).
Do not confuse the character 忘 with 忙 (máng, busy).

senses.definition: To fail to remember something, or fail to do something one intended to do.

examples.text: 我忘带手机了。
examples.translation: I forgot to bring my cell phone.

examples.text: 对不起，我忘了你的名字。
examples.translation: Sorry, I forgot your name.

faults.quote: To apply paint to a surface to create a picture.
faults.why: 'Draw' and 'paint' are an English distinction; in Chinese 画 is a single sense.

faults.quote: She painted a beautiful scenery on the paper.
faults.why: 'A beautiful scenery' is ungrammatical in English ('scenery' is uncountable).

notes: 画 is also a noun meaning 'picture' or 'painting' (一幅画); the verb-object phrase 画画 (huàhuà) is used when no specific object is named.
Unlike 写 (xiě, to write characters), 画 is used for creating pictures, shapes, or lines.

senses.definition: To make a picture, image, or line with a pen, pencil, or brush.

examples.text: 他喜欢用铅笔画猫。
examples.translation: He likes to draw cats with a pencil.

examples.text: 她在纸上画了一幅美丽的风景。
examples.translation: She painted a beautiful landscape on the paper.

faults.why: Missing the everyday A1/A2 sense used for ordering or requesting ('bring me / I'll have').

corrected.shortGloss: to come; to arrive; to bring (when ordering)
notes: 来 indicates movement toward the speaker, opposite to 去 (qù, to go away from the speaker).
Often used after another verb as a directional complement showing motion toward the speaker (e.g. 进来, come in; 回来, come back).

senses.definition: To move or travel toward the speaker or a specified place.

examples.text: 他明天来北京。
examples.translation: He is coming to Beijing tomorrow.

senses.definition: Of a time, season, or event: to arrive or happen.

examples.text: 春天来了。
examples.translation: Spring has come.

senses.definition: Used in everyday speech to order food or drink, or to offer to do something oneself.

examples.text: 服务员，来两杯咖啡。
examples.translation: Waiter, bring us two cups of coffee.

faults.quote: I don't understand what words you are saying.
faults.why: Unnatural literal translation; should be 'I don't know what you're talking about.'

faults.quote: The word '말' is a classic example of a homonym in Korean.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions and state the obvious about context.
Should mention the vowel length distinction ([말] horse vs. [말ː] speech) and honorific 말씀.

notes: The 'speech/word' sense has an honorific form, 말씀, and is traditionally pronounced with a long vowel [말ː], whereas 'horse' has a short vowel [말].
Common collocations: 말을 하다 (to speak/talk) and 말을 타다 (to ride a horse).

senses.definition: The words, speech, or language that people use to express thoughts and feelings.

examples.text: 무슨 말을 하는지 모르겠어요.
examples.translation: I don't know what you are talking about.

senses.definition: A large animal with four legs, hooves, and a mane that people ride.

examples.text: 말을 타는 것은 재미있습니다.
examples.translation: Riding a horse is fun.

faults.quote: A tool with a long handle and bristles used for sweeping
faults.why: Modern everyday Korean uses '빗자루' for broom; standalone '비' is rare for A2.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with '비(가) 오다' (to rain), where '비'
faults.why: Confusing note: telling learners not to confuse a noun with its main collocation.

faults.quote: 비를 들고 마당을 쓸어요.
faults.why: Unnatural; native speakers say '빗자루로 마당을 쓸어요' and the translation is a calque.

notes: In Korean, 'to rain' is expressed by pairing 비 with the verbs 오다 (to come) or 내리다 (to fall): 비가 오다 / 비가 내리다.

senses.definition: Water that falls in drops from the clouds in the sky.

examples.text: 밖에 비가 많이 와요.
examples.translation: It is raining a lot outside.

faults.quote: A number given to a particular edition of a magazine or newspaper.
faults.why: 호수 (號數) is primarily room/apartment number or clothing/shoe size, not magazine edition.

faults.quote: 잡지 이번 호수에 흥미로운 기사가 많이 실렸다.
faults.why: Ungrammatical word choice; 'this issue' is '이번 호', never '이번 호수'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 오수, which means wastewater or drainage.
faults.why: 오수 is an advanced word that A2 learners will not confuse with 호수.

notes: These two meanings come from different Sino-Korean words: 湖水 (lake) and 號數 (assigned number or size).

senses.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

examples.text: 주말에 공원 호수 근처에서 산책을 했다.
examples.translation: I took a walk near the park lake on the weekend.

senses.definition: An assigned number for a room or apartment, or a standard size for clothes, shoes, or rings.

examples.text: 정확한 아파트 동과 호수를 적어 주세요.
examples.translation: Please write down your exact apartment building and unit number.

faults.quote: While '숙제' primarily refers to school assignments, it is also frequently used
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given; should mention collocations like 숙제를 하다.

notes: Commonly used with 하다: 숙제를 하다 (to do homework), and 내주다: 숙제를 내주다 (to assign homework).

senses.definition: Schoolwork that a student is given to do at home.

examples.text: 오늘 숙제가 너무 많아요.
examples.translation: I have too much homework today.

senses.definition: A difficult problem or task that remains to be solved.

examples.text: 이 문제는 우리 팀이 풀어야 할 큰 숙제입니다.
examples.translation: This issue is a major challenge our team needs to solve.

faults.quote: When talking about eating specifically, Koreans often use the verb '먹다'
faults.why: Bizarre filler note claiming Koreans use 'to eat' rather than 'mouth' when talking about eating.

notes: Frequently used in everyday expressions about food and speech, such as 입에 맞다 (to suit one's taste), 입이 짧다 (to be a picky eater), and 입이 무겁다 (to be good at keeping secrets, literally 'to have a heavy mouth').

senses.definition: The opening in the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking, including the lips.

examples.text: 입을 크게 벌리세요.
examples.translation: Please open your mouth wide.

examples.text: 음식이 입에 맞아요?
examples.translation: Does the food suit your taste?

faults.quote: Used to describe an action occurring before the usual or expected time.
faults.why: Repeats the definition verbatim.

notes: Can also be used as an adjective meaning 'early', agreeing in gender and number (e.g., 'a una hora temprana').
Its opposite is 'tarde' (late).

senses.definition: Before the usual or expected time, or near the beginning of a period.

examples.text: Llegamos muy temprano al aeropuerto.
examples.translation: We arrived at the airport very early.

examples.text: Es temprano para cenar.
examples.translation: It is early to eat dinner.

faults.quote: /teˈneɾ ˈambe/
faults.why: Missing /ɾ/ in 'hambre'; should be /teˈneɾ ˈambɾe/.

notes: Spanish uses 'tener' + the noun 'hambre' ('to have hunger') instead of 'to be'. Never say 'estoy hambre'.
To say 'very hungry', use the adjective 'mucha' (agreeing with feminine 'hambre'), not 'muy': 'tengo mucha hambre'.

senses.definition: To feel the need to eat.

examples.text: Tengo mucha hambre, ¿podemos ir a comer ya?
examples.translation: I am very hungry, can we go eat now?

notes: Literally 'to have thirst', following the Spanish pattern of using 'tener' + noun for bodily states instead of 'to be'.
To say 'very thirsty', use 'mucha' (agreeing with the feminine noun 'sed'), not 'muy': 'tengo mucha sed'.

senses.definition: To feel the need to drink.

examples.text: Después de correr bajo el sol, tengo mucha sed.
examples.translation: After running in the sun, I am very thirsty.

faults.quote: To be obliged or forced to do something.
faults.why: Does not explain that the obligation sense requires the construction 'tener que + infinitive'.

corrected.shortGloss: to have; to hold; to be; to have to
notes: Irregular in the present tense (tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen) and preterite (tuve, tuviste, tuvo...).
Do not confuse with 'haber': 'tener' means to possess, while 'haber' is the auxiliary verb for compound tenses ('he comido') and expresses existence ('hay').
For obligation ('to have to'), always use 'tener que' + infinitive.

senses.definition: To own, possess, or hold something, or to have a relationship or characteristic.

examples.text: Tengo un coche nuevo en el estacionamiento.
examples.translation: I have a new car in the parking lot.

senses.definition: Used with a noun to express age or a physical or emotional state such as hunger, thirst, heat, cold, or fear.

examples.text: Tengo mucha sed después de correr.
examples.translation: I am very thirsty after running.

examples.text: Mi hermana tiene veinte años.
examples.translation: My sister is twenty years old.

senses.definition: (as 'tener que' + infinitive) To need or be obliged to do something.

examples.text: Tengo que estudiar español esta noche.
examples.translation: I have to study Spanish tonight.

faults.quote: In some contexts, 'acabar' is a synonym, but 'terminar' often emphasizes
faults.why: Vague filler distinction; fails to mention key prepositions like 'terminar de + infinitive'.

corrected.shortGloss: to finish; to end; to complete
notes: Use 'terminar de' + infinitive to mean 'to finish doing something' (e.g., 'Ya terminé de comer').
In Mexico, 'terminar (con alguien)' is also commonly used to mean to break up with a romantic partner.

senses.definition: To bring an activity or task to an end, or to come to an end.

examples.text: Voy a terminar mi trabajo pronto.
examples.translation: I am going to finish my work soon.

examples.text: La película termina de forma muy triste.
examples.translation: The movie ends in a very sad way.

faults.quote: The plural form is 'sąsiedzi' when referring to a group of neighbors, regardless of their gender.
faults.why: False: an all-female group of neighbors is 'sąsiadki', not 'sąsiedzi'.

faults.quote: (proximity) A person or thing that is located near or next to another.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning (person/country next door) should be one sense.

notes: For a female neighbor, use 'sąsiadka' (plural 'sąsiadki').
The plural 'sąsiedzi' is used for male or mixed-gender groups (note the vowel and consonant shift: -ąd → -edzi).

senses.definition: A person who lives next to or near you, or a person or country next to another.

examples.text: Mój sąsiad zawsze pomaga mi z zakupami.
examples.translation: My neighbor always helps me with the shopping.

examples.text: Niemcy są naszym zachodnim sąsiadem.
examples.translation: Germany is our western neighbor.

faults.quote: common
faults.why: Polish has no 'common' gender; plurale tantum nouns have no singular gender (non-virile plural).

faults.quote: (idiom) A difficult situation or unexpected obstacle in a process.
faults.why: Colloquial idiom 'zaczynają się schody' is not a core standalone sense for A2.

notes: Always plural (plurale tantum), even for a single staircase: 'schody są strome' (the stairs are steep).
Do not confuse with 'stopień' (a single step on a staircase).

senses.definition: A set of steps for going from one level of a building to another.

examples.text: Muszę wejść po schodach na trzecie piętro.
examples.translation: I have to walk up the stairs to the third floor.

faults.quote: (nature) A steep, nearly vertical face of a cliff, mountain, or glacier.
faults.why: Mountaineering sense ('rock face') is too specialized for an A2 beginner entry.

notes: Used for the walls of a room or building. For a freestanding outdoor wall around a property or city, use 'mur'.

senses.definition: A vertical side of a room or building that supports it or divides it into spaces.

examples.text: Obraz wisi na ścianie.
examples.translation: The picture is hanging on the wall.

faults.quote: (mystery) Something that is difficult to understand or explain.
faults.why: Not a distinct everyday sense of 'sekret'; 'mystery' is normally 'tajemnica' (as note[0] admits).

faults.quote: To jest wielki sekret natury.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation; Polish says 'tajemnica natury', not 'sekret natury'.

notes: 'Sekret' usually refers to personal information kept from others. 'Tajemnica' is broader and also means 'mystery'.

senses.definition: Information that is kept hidden from other people.

examples.text: Muszę ci powiedzieć sekret.
examples.translation: I have to tell you a secret.

faults.quote: The Polish word 'sen' is versatile and covers both the act of sleeping and the imagery of dreams.
faults.why: Purely restates the two senses and glosses while omitting the irregular stem 'sn-' and 'marzenie'.

notes: The vowel 'e' drops in all declined forms: 'snu' (genitive), 'we śnie' (in a dream / in one's sleep).
For a dream in the sense of a life goal or wish, use 'marzenie', not 'sen'.

senses.definition: The natural state of rest of the body and mind.

examples.text: Zdrowy sen jest ważny dla organizmu.
examples.translation: Healthy sleep is important for the body.

senses.definition: The images, thoughts, or feelings experienced while sleeping.

examples.text: Miałem dzisiaj dziwny sen.
examples.translation: I had a strange dream today.

faults.why: Should explicitly state that 'com vergonha' is used with 'estar' or 'ficar', not 'ser'.

notes: Used with 'estar' or 'ficar' (never 'ser') to describe a temporary feeling: 'estar com vergonha' (to feel shy/embarrassed), 'ficar com vergonha' (to get shy/embarrassed). For a permanent personality trait, use 'tímido' (shy).
Followed by 'de' + infinitive or noun to name the cause: 'com vergonha de falar' (too shy to speak).

senses.definition: Feeling ashamed or uncomfortable because of an action or situation.

examples.text: Fiquei com vergonha do que eu disse na reunião.
examples.translation: I felt embarrassed about what I said at the meeting.

senses.definition: Feeling timid or nervous in front of other people.

examples.text: A criança ficou com vergonha de falar com os visitantes.
examples.translation: The child felt too shy to talk to the visitors.

faults.quote: Começar is the most common verb for 'to start' or 'to begin'
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding usage information while missing the spelling change (ç → c).

notes: Followed by the preposition 'a' before an infinitive verb: 'começar a trabalhar' (to start working).
The 'ç' changes to 'c' before 'e' to keep the /s/ sound (e.g., 'comece').

senses.definition: To begin doing something, or to begin to happen.

examples.text: O filme vai começar agora.
examples.translation: The movie is going to start now.

examples.text: Ela começou a aprender português ontem.
examples.translation: She started learning Portuguese yesterday.

faults.quote: To wear away, corrode, or consume a surface or material gradually.
faults.why: The 'corrode' sense is marginal for an A2 learner and clutters a core vocabulary entry.

faults.quote: Used as a standard transitive or intransitive verb for taking food.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions of the senses.

notes: Warning: in casual Brazilian slang, 'comer alguém' has a vulgar sexual meaning, so avoid using 'comer' with a person as the direct object.

senses.definition: To put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.

examples.text: Gosto de comer pão fresco todas as manhãs.
examples.translation: I like to eat fresh bread every morning.

faults.quote: To believe or accept a story, an idea, or an excuse.
faults.why: Figurative idiom ('comprar uma ideia/desculpa') is not an essential A2 sense.

faults.quote: Used for almost all common transactions in Brazil.
faults.why: Filler note that adds no useful linguistic information.

notes: To say whom you are buying something from, use the preposition 'de': 'Comprei o carro de um amigo' (I bought the car from a friend).

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.

examples.text: Eu preciso comprar frutas frescas na feira.
examples.translation: I need to buy fresh fruit at the street market.

faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'conhecer' very commonly means to visit or experience a place for the first time.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to meet; to visit
notes: Do not confuse with 'saber'. Use 'conhecer' for being acquainted with people, places, or things; use 'saber' for knowing facts, information, or how to do something.
The 'c' changes to 'ç' before 'o' and 'a' to keep the /s/ sound (e.g., 'eu conheço').

senses.definition: To be familiar or acquainted with a person, place, or thing.

examples.text: Eu conheço muito bem este bairro.
examples.translation: I know this neighborhood very well.

senses.definition: To be introduced to someone for the first time.

examples.text: Foi um prazer conhecer você.
examples.translation: It was a pleasure to meet you.

senses.definition: To visit or see a place for the first time.

examples.text: Meu sonho é conhecer o Rio de Janeiro.
examples.translation: My dream is to visit Rio de Janeiro.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a word with kanji.

faults.quote: (perception) To notice or perceive something with one's eyes.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning as sense 0 (being visible / able to see).

corrected.shortGloss: to be visible; to be able to see; to look like
notes: An intransitive (ichidan) verb taking が for the thing seen. It describes what naturally enters your field of vision, whereas 見る (miru) is the active act of looking.
Do not confuse with 見られる (mirareru), the potential form of 見る, which means 'to be able to watch' (when conditions or rules allow, e.g., a movie).

senses.definition: To be within one's field of vision; to be able to see something.

examples.text: 山から海が見える。
examples.translation: You can see the sea from the mountain.

examples.text: 遠くに光が見えた。
examples.translation: A light came into view in the distance.

senses.definition: To appear or look a certain way to the observer.

examples.text: 彼はとても若く見える。
examples.translation: He looks very young.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a word with kanji.

faults.quote: 計画は順調に行く。
faults.why: Unnatural aspect; 順調にいっている or 順調にいくでしょう is natural, and this sense is usually written in kana.
Missing irregular te/ta-form (行って/行った) and secondary reading ゆく.

notes: Has an irregular te-form (行って, itte) and past form (行った, itta). Also read ゆく (yuku) in more formal or literary contexts.
Takes に or へ for the destination. Contrast with 来る (kuru), which means to come toward the speaker's location.

senses.definition: To move from one's current location to another place.

examples.text: 明日、学校へ行く。
examples.translation: I will go to school tomorrow.

senses.definition: To proceed or turn out in a particular way (often written in hiragana).

examples.text: すべてうまく行った。
examples.translation: Everything went well.

faults.quote: (ascend) To go up a path, stairs, or slope.
faults.why: Climbing a mountain and going up a slope are one sense in Japanese for 登る.
Missing note on the common particles に (toward the top) vs を (along the route).

notes: Takes に when focusing on reaching the top (山に登る) and を when focusing on the path or surface traversed (坂を登る). Also spelled 上る for stairs or slopes.
Contrast with 上がる (あがる), which refers to going up in a more general sense (such as going upstairs or entering a home) and focuses on the final point reached.

senses.definition: To go up a mountain, slope, stairs, or vertical surface by one's own effort.

examples.text: 週末に山に登った。
examples.translation: I climbed a mountain on the weekend.

examples.text: この坂を登ると駅がある。
examples.translation: If you go up this slope, there is a station.

faults.quote: To make food hot and ready to eat.
faults.why: Inaccurate: 料理する includes preparing cold dishes (e.g., sashimi, salad), not just heating food.

faults.quote: This verb acts like a suru-verb, meaning you can also use
faults.why: Wordy and uses romaji; misses that ご飯を作る is more common in daily speech.

notes: Can also be used as 料理をする. For specific ingredients or dishes it is transitive (魚を料理する, 'to cook fish').
In everyday conversation, ご飯を作る (gohan o tsukuru, 'to make a meal') is often more natural than 料理する.

senses.definition: To prepare food for eating by cutting, seasoning, or heating ingredients.

examples.text: 毎日自分で料理する。
examples.translation: I cook for myself every day.

examples.text: 週末は家族のために料理する。
examples.translation: I cook for my family on the weekends.

faults.quote: 彼は高いところから飛び降りた。
faults.why: Uses the compound verb 飛び降りる (to jump down) instead of the lemma 飛ぶ.

faults.quote: While 飛ぶ primarily means to move through the air
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses that the 'jump' sense is also written 跳ぶ.

notes: Takes を for the space moved through (空を飛ぶ, 'to fly in the sky').
In the sense 'to jump' or 'to leap', it is also commonly written 跳ぶ. Do not confuse with 跳ねる (はねる), which implies hopping or bouncing.

senses.definition: To move through the air, such as a bird or airplane.

examples.text: 鳥が空を飛んでいる。
examples.translation: A bird is flying in the sky.

senses.definition: To push oneself off the ground into the air or across a gap.

examples.text: 犬が高く飛んだ。
examples.translation: The dog jumped high.

faults.quote: A person who is receiving medical treatment.
faults.why: Entry POS is adjective, so a noun sense does not belong here.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine ('o menino doente', 'a menina doente'). usually used with 'estar' for temporary illness, and also used as a noun ('o/a doente') meaning 'patient'.

senses.definition: Having poor health or an illness.

examples.text: Ele está doente e não pode vir trabalhar hoje.
examples.translation: He is sick and cannot come to work today.

faults.quote: to sleep; to rest
faults.why: 'to rest' is not in the glosses; sense 1 is 'to stay the night'.

faults.quote: at friends' house
faults.why: Unnatural English phrasing; should be 'at a friend's house' or 'at some friends' house'.

corrected.shortGloss: to sleep; to stay the night
notes: In the present tense, the 'o' changes to 'u' in the first-person singular: 'eu durmo'.

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed and your body inactive, usually at night.

examples.text: Eu preciso dormir cedo hoje.
examples.translation: I need to go to sleep early today.

senses.definition: To spend the night somewhere away from home.

examples.text: Vamos dormir na casa de uns amigos neste fim de semana.
examples.translation: We are going to stay the night at some friends' house this weekend.

faults.quote: Duro is a very versatile word. Use it for anything that resists
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions and fail to mention common informal usage ('broke').
Missing the very common everyday informal Brazilian sense 'broke, without money'.

notes: In informal Brazilian Portuguese, 'estar duro' is a very common way to say you have no money ('broke').

senses.definition: Firm and solid to the touch; not soft or easy to chew.

examples.text: O colchão está muito duro.
examples.translation: The mattress is very hard.

examples.text: Este pão já está duro.
examples.translation: This bread is already stale and hard.

senses.definition: Difficult to deal with; demanding or harsh.

examples.text: Hoje foi um dia duro no trabalho.
examples.translation: Today was a tough day at work.

senses.definition: (informal) Having no money.

examples.text: Não posso sair hoje porque estou duro.
examples.translation: I can't go out today because I'm broke.

faults.quote: Ela é uma mulher muito instruída e educada.
faults.why: Uses 'educada' to mean 'polite' inside the example meant to illustrate 'educated'.

faults.quote: Possessing a good level of formal schooling or knowledge.
faults.why: As the note says, this is a false friend; listing it as a sense misleads beginners.

notes: False friend: 'educado' means 'polite' or 'well-mannered' (opposite: 'mal-educado'). To say someone has a good formal education, use 'instruído' or 'estudado'.

senses.definition: Having or showing good manners and respect towards others.

examples.text: O rapaz foi muito educado comigo no restaurante.
examples.translation: The young man was very polite to me at the restaurant.

faults.why: Pushing an object and pushing a person are the same basic meaning.
Note should explicitly warn that 'puxar' on doors is a false friend for English 'push'.

notes: Watch out for the false friend on door signs: 'empurre' means 'push', while 'puxe' (from 'puxar') means 'pull'.

senses.definition: To use physical force to move something or someone away from you.

examples.text: Você precisa empurrar a porta para abrir.
examples.translation: You need to push the door to open it.

examples.text: Não é educado empurrar as pessoas na fila.
examples.translation: It is not polite to push people in line.

faults.why: Missing the essential perfective aspect counterpart 'narysować' (and 'porysować' for scratching).

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'pisać' (to write), which is for
faults.why: Unnecessary warning; English speakers do not confuse 'rysować' with 'pisać'.

notes: Imperfective verb. The perfective counterpart is 'narysować' (for drawing) or 'porysować' / 'zarysować' (for scratching).
Use 'rysować' for drawing with a pencil, crayon, or pen, and 'malować' for painting with a brush.

senses.definition: To create a picture or design on a surface using a pencil, pen, or crayon.

examples.text: Lubię rysować krajobrazy ołówkiem.
examples.translation: I like to draw landscapes with a pencil.

senses.definition: To damage a surface by making thin marks or lines on it, often accidentally.

examples.text: Klucze mogą rysować ekran telefonu.
examples.translation: Keys can scratch the phone screen.

faults.quote: It is a feminine noun; pay attention to the case endings,
faults.why: Restates the grammatical gender already shown in the gender field.

notes: Refers to a large flowing body of water; for smaller streams, use 'strumień' or 'potok'.

senses.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

examples.text: Wisła to najdłuższa rzeka w Polsce.
examples.translation: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland.

faults.quote: Chłopiec lubi rzucać piłkę do psa.
faults.why: Throwing something to an animate recipient normally takes the dative ('rzucać piłkę psu').

faults.quote: On planuje rzucać palenie w przyszłym miesiącu.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: 'planować' with a specific future time requires the perfective 'rzucić', not imperfective 'rzucać'.

corrected.shortGloss: to throw; to drop; to quit
notes: Imperfective verb, used for ongoing, repeated, or habitual actions. The perfective counterpart is 'rzucić'.

senses.definition: To send something through the air from your hand with a quick movement of your arm.

examples.text: Chłopiec lubi rzucać piłkę psu.
examples.translation: The boy likes to throw the ball to the dog.

senses.definition: To throw something down or let it fall, often carelessly.

examples.text: Nie wolno rzucać śmieci na ziemię.
examples.translation: You must not throw garbage on the ground.

senses.definition: To stop doing a job, habit, or activity, or to end a romantic relationship with someone.

examples.text: On próbuje rzucać palenie już trzeci raz.
examples.translation: He is trying to quit smoking for the third time already.

faults.quote: Jem zdrową sałatka na obiad.
faults.why: Ungrammatical case: direct object of 'jeść' must be in the accusative ('zdrową sałatkę'), not nominative.

notes: 'Sałatka' refers to a prepared dish of mixed ingredients, whereas 'sałata' means lettuce.

senses.definition: A cold dish of mixed raw or cooked vegetables, often with meat, eggs, or cheese, served with a dressing.

examples.text: Jem zdrową sałatkę na obiad.
examples.translation: I am eating a healthy salad for lunch.

faults.quote: 'знать' is used for facts and general knowledge, while 'быть знакомым'
faults.why: False claim: 'знать' is freely used for knowing people and places, contradicting sense 1.

notes: Imperfective verb used for both knowing facts and knowing people or places.
Do not confuse with 'уметь', which means knowing how to do something (having a skill).

senses.definition: To have information or facts in your mind.

examples.text: Я знаю, где находится музей.
examples.translation: I know where the museum is located.

senses.definition: To be familiar with a person, place, or thing through experience.

examples.text: Мы давно знаем этого человека.
examples.translation: We have known this person for a long time.

faults.quote: /ɪtˈɕi/
faults.why: Wrong consonant in IPA: 'идти' is pronounced /ɪˈtʲːi/, not with /ɕ/.
Missing common everyday sense 'to suit, to look good on' (одежда идёт).

corrected.shortGloss: to go; to walk; to fall (of rain/snow); to suit
notes: Unidirectional verb of motion (moving in one direction right now). Contrasts with 'ходить' (habitual or round-trip movement) and 'ехать' (going by vehicle).
Irregular past tense: шёл, шла, шло, шли.

senses.definition: To move on foot, or (of a vehicle) to travel in a certain direction.

examples.text: Мы идём домой.
examples.translation: We are going home.

senses.definition: For time, an event, a movie, or a process to take place or pass.

examples.text: Время идёт быстро.
examples.translation: Time goes by quickly.

senses.definition: For rain, snow, or hail to fall from the sky.

examples.text: На улице идёт дождь.
examples.translation: It is raining outside.

senses.definition: To look good on someone (with the person in the dative case).

examples.text: Тебе очень идёт это платье.
examples.translation: This dress suits you very well.

faults.quote: Мы планируем останавливаться в небольшом отеле.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: a single planned stay requires perfective 'остановиться', not imperfective 'останавливаться'.

faults.quote: Use 'останавливаться' for both physical movement stopping and for staying
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; should instead give the perfective pair 'остановиться'.

corrected.shortGloss: to stop; to stay (at a hotel)
notes: Imperfective verb; its perfective partner is 'остановиться'.
Intransitive (coming to a stop on one's own). To stop someone or something else, use 'останавливать' / 'остановить'.

senses.definition: To cease moving or to pause during an activity.

examples.text: Автобус останавливается на каждой остановке.
examples.translation: The bus stops at every stop.

senses.definition: To live temporarily in a place as a guest or traveler, taking 'в' or 'у' with the prepositional or genitive case.

examples.text: В командировках мы обычно останавливаемся в небольшом отеле.
examples.translation: On business trips we usually stay in a small hotel.

faults.quote: /nɐˈɕitʲ/
faults.why: Wrong consonant in IPA: 'с' before 'и' is /sʲ/, not /ɕ/ (/nɐˈsʲitʲ/).

faults.quote: Use 'носить' for clothes, accessories, or glasses that you have on
faults.why: Restates sense 0; should explain multidirectional vs unidirectional 'нести'.

notes: Do not confuse 'носить' (to wear habitually) with 'надеть' (the single action of putting clothes on).
For carrying, 'носить' is a multidirectional verb (carrying repeatedly or in multiple trips). For carrying something in one direction right now, use 'нести'.

senses.definition: To have clothes, shoes, glasses, or accessories on one's body, or to keep a hairstyle or beard.

examples.text: Она всегда носит удобную обувь.
examples.translation: She always wears comfortable shoes.

senses.definition: To carry things on foot repeatedly, habitually, or in several trips.

examples.text: Он целое утро носит тяжёлые коробки в машину.
examples.translation: He has been carrying heavy boxes to the car all morning.

faults.quote: This is an 'imperfective' verb indicating a repeated or habitual action
faults.why: Misleading: both 'лазить' and 'лезть' are imperfective; they differ in directionality, not aspect.

faults.quote: Ему пришлось лазить под кровать за игрушкой.
faults.why: Unnatural verb choice: a single action of getting a toy requires 'лезть' or 'залезть', not multidirectional 'лазить'.

notes: Multidirectional imperfective verb used for repeated, habitual, or aimless climbing. Its unidirectional partner (climbing in one direction right now) is 'лезть' (also imperfective).
Takes 'по' + dative for climbing around on something (лазить по деревьям) and 'в' / 'под' + accusative for getting into or under a space.

senses.definition: To go up, down, or over something using one's hands and feet, repeatedly or in various directions.

examples.text: Дети любят лазить по деревьям.
examples.translation: Children love to climb trees.

senses.definition: To crawl or reach into a tight space or container repeatedly.

examples.text: Кот постоянно лазит под кровать.
examples.translation: The cat is constantly crawling under the bed.

faults.quote: Fácil is a very versatile adjective used for anything
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage or grammar help.
Should note that 'fácil' is invariable for gender and forms the plural 'fáceis'.

faults.quote: something that can be done with little effort.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('something that...').

faults.quote: Something or someone that is simple to deal with or influence.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('Something or someone...').

faults.quote: He is an easygoing person to deal with.
faults.why: Unnatural English ('easygoing to deal with' blends two idioms).

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine, and the irregular plural 'fáceis' (perguntas fáceis).
Followed by 'de' before an infinitive: fácil de fazer (easy to do).

senses.definition: Not difficult; able to be done or understood with little effort.

examples.text: A prova de matemática estava fácil.
examples.translation: The math test was easy.

senses.definition: Of a person: pleasant and not difficult to get along with.

examples.text: Ele é uma pessoa fácil de lidar.
examples.translation: He is an easy person to deal with.

faults.why: Missing key prepositions used with 'falar': 'com' (to/with) and 'sobre'/'de' (about).

corrected.shortGloss: to speak; to talk; to say
notes: Takes 'com' for the person spoken to (falar com alguém) and 'sobre' or 'de' for the topic (falar sobre/de algo).
In Brazilian Portuguese, 'falar' often replaces 'dizer' (to say/tell) in everyday speech: Ele falou que vem (He said he is coming).

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words, converse, or communicate in a language.

examples.text: Ela gosta de falar com os amigos durante o almoço.
examples.translation: She likes to talk to her friends during lunch.

examples.text: Você fala português?
examples.translation: Do you speak Portuguese?

senses.definition: To communicate information or state something to someone.

examples.text: Preciso falar a verdade para ele.
examples.translation: I need to tell him the truth.

faults.quote: to close; to shut; to lock
faults.why: 'to lock' is not in any sense's glosses (and is properly 'trancar').

faults.quote: close down, shut down
faults.why: 'Close down' implies permanent closure, but the sense and example cover daily closing.
Missing the common everyday sense 'to finalize/conclude' (a deal, bill, or agreement).

faults.quote: Use 'fechar' for almost anything that moves into a closed position
faults.why: Merely restates the basic definitions.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'abrir', which is the opposite
faults.why: Trivial antonym note; learners do not confuse 'fechar' and 'abrir'.

corrected.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to finalize
notes: To say 'to lock' with a key, use 'trancar'.

senses.definition: To move something so that an opening is covered, or to bring its parts together.

examples.text: Por favor, feche a porta ao sair.
examples.translation: Please close the door when leaving.

senses.definition: To stop operating for the day, or to go out of business permanently.

examples.text: A loja vai fechar às oito da noite hoje.
examples.translation: The store will close at eight tonight.

senses.definition: To finalize or settle an agreement, deal, or bill.

examples.text: Eles fecharam o negócio ontem.
examples.translation: They closed the deal yesterday.

faults.quote: While primarily used to describe physical appearance, 'feio' is also used
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses given in the entry.

faults.quote: Behaving in a way that is considered rude, inappropriate, or morally offensive.
faults.why: Applied to actions and situations ('É feio gritar'), not only to people behaving.

notes: Can also describe something serious or unpleasant, such as bad weather or an accident: A coisa está feia (Things look bad).

senses.definition: Unpleasant to look at; lacking beauty.

examples.text: Ele acha aquele prédio muito feio.
examples.translation: He thinks that building is very ugly.

senses.definition: Of an action or behavior: socially unacceptable, rude, or shameful.

examples.text: É feio gritar com os outros.
examples.translation: It is rude to yell at others.

faults.why: Should note that 'feliz' is invariable for gender (plural 'felizes') and differs with 'ser' vs. 'estar'.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine, with the plural 'felizes'.
Used with 'ser' for a lasting state (Sou uma pessoa feliz) and with 'estar' or 'ficar' for a reaction or current mood (Estou feliz por você).
Placed before a noun in greetings: Feliz Natal! (Merry Christmas!), Feliz aniversário! (Happy birthday!).

senses.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure, contentment, or joy.

examples.text: Ela está muito feliz com o novo emprego.
examples.translation: She is very happy with her new job.

examples.text: Fico feliz em te ver.
examples.translation: I am glad to see you.

faults.quote: Used for physical objects that resist pressure, or metaphorically for a tough
faults.why: merely restates the two senses; better to give the opposite 软 (ruǎn)

notes: Its opposite is 软 (ruǎn, soft).

senses.definition: Firm and solid; not easily pressed, bent, or cut.

examples.text: 这张床有点硬。
examples.translation: This bed is a bit hard.

senses.definition: Of a person or attitude: firm, unyielding, or stubborn.

examples.text: 他的态度很硬。
examples.translation: His attitude is very tough.

faults.quote: róng yì
faults.why: Multi-character words are written without spaces in pinyin (róngyì, often with neutral tone róngyi).

faults.quote: It is easy for it to snow here in the winter.
faults.why: Calqued and unnatural English for the 'likely to' sense.

notes: Its opposite is 难 (nán, difficult). Before a verb, 容易 can also mean 'likely to' or 'prone to' (e.g., 容易感冒, easily catches a cold).

senses.definition: Not difficult; needing little effort.

examples.text: 这个问题很容易回答。
examples.translation: This question is very easy to answer.

senses.definition: Likely or prone to happen.

examples.text: 冬天很容易感冒。
examples.translation: It is easy to catch a cold in winter.

faults.quote: kè qi
faults.why: Pinyin for a single word should not have spaces between syllables (kèqi).

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who is polite, courteous, and well-behaved in social
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0 without adding usage information.

notes: Often used in the negative to tell a guest or friend not to stand on ceremony, or in reply to 'thank you': 不用客气 / 别客气 (You're welcome / Make yourself at home).

senses.definition: Behaving in a polite and courteous way towards others.

examples.text: 他是一个非常客气的人。
examples.translation: He is a very polite person.

senses.definition: Standing on ceremony; overly formal or modest with someone.

examples.text: 我们是老朋友了，别这么客气。
examples.translation: We are old friends, don't be so formal.

faults.quote: tiresome, trixing, hard
faults.why: 'trixing' is a typo for 'tiring'.

faults.quote: tired; exhausted; to tire
faults.why: Entry is an adjective with no verb sense, so 'to tire' mismatches; misses 'tiring'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 生气 (shēngqì), which means angry; 累 is purely
faults.why: Note 0 restates the definition, and Note 1 warns against an unlikely confusion.

notes: Can describe both a person feeling tired (我很累, I'm very tired) and an activity that makes you tired (这工作很累, This job is very tiring).
Also read lěi ('to accumulate', as in 积累) and léi ('cumbersome').

senses.definition: Needing rest or sleep; feeling physical or mental fatigue.

examples.text: 今天工作很忙，我真的很累。
examples.translation: Work was very busy today, and I am really tired.

senses.definition: Causing fatigue; hard and demanding.

examples.text: 搬家是一件很累的事情。
examples.translation: Moving house is a very tiring thing.

faults.quote: wú liáo
faults.why: Pinyin for a single word should not have spaces between syllables (wúliáo).

faults.quote: Something that is dull, uninteresting, or a waste of time.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun ('Something that is...').

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 讨厌 (tǎoyàn), which means annoying or hateful.
faults.why: Unrelated word that learners have no special reason to confuse with 无聊.

notes: Describes both a person feeling bored (我很无聊, I'm bored) and a thing that is boring (电影很无聊, the movie is boring). Be careful: saying 你很无聊 means 'You are boring/silly', not 'You are bored'.

senses.definition: Feeling restless and uninterested because you have nothing to do.

examples.text: 今天下雨，我待在家里觉得很无聊。
examples.translation: It is raining today, and I feel very bored staying at home.

senses.definition: Dull and uninteresting.

examples.text: 这部电影太无聊了，我中途就睡着了。
examples.translation: This movie was so boring that I fell asleep halfway through.

faults.quote: the subject of the sentence in English is the object being missed
faults.why: Confuses grammatical roles; clarify the dative experiencer (को) and feminine possessive (की) vs direct object.

corrected.shortGloss: to miss; to remember, to come to mind
notes: The person who remembers or misses takes को (e.g., मुझे). For missing someone (sense 1), that person takes the feminine possessive की (मुझे तुम्हारी याद आती है); for recalling something (sense 2), it is the subject (मुझे उसका नाम याद आया).
Do not confuse with याद करना (to consciously remember, memorize, or think of someone).

senses.definition: To feel sad because you are separated from someone or something you care about.

examples.text: मुझे तुम्हारी बहुत याद आती है।
examples.translation: I miss you very much.

senses.definition: To suddenly remember something or have a thought enter your mind.

examples.text: अचानक मुझे उसका नाम याद आ गया।
examples.translation: Suddenly, I remembered his name.

faults.quote: To make a task or a process easier or less difficult
faults.why: Sense 1 is the same meaning ('to help'); the example itself just translates as 'helps'.

notes: Because मदद (help) is a feminine noun, the person or thing being helped takes the feminine postposition की (e.g., उसकी मदद करो — help him/her).

senses.definition: To give assistance or support to someone, or to make something easier to do.

examples.text: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
examples.translation: Can you help me?

examples.text: यह नई तकनीक काम को आसान करने में मदद करती है।
examples.translation: This new technology helps make the work easier.

faults.quote: Used when someone succeeds in a game, competition, or battle.
faults.why: Restates the definitions without adding grammatical or usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to conquer, to overcome
notes: Can be used both with and without ने in the perfective (e.g., हम मैच जीते or हमने मैच जीता). To defeat a person or team, हराना is more common than जीतना.

senses.definition: To come first in a game, race, or competition, or to gain a prize.

examples.text: हमारी टीम ने मैच जीत लिया।
examples.translation: Our team won the match.

senses.definition: To succeed in overcoming an opponent, a place, or a difficulty.

examples.text: उसने अपनी मेहनत से डर को जीत लिया।
examples.translation: He overcame his fear through hard work.

faults.quote: This phrase is used for both a person performing their job
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses directly below it.

notes: Do not confuse with मेहनत करना, which specifically means 'to work hard' or 'to put in effort'.

senses.definition: To do a job for pay, or to spend time and effort doing a task.

examples.text: मेरे पिता बैंक में काम करते हैं।
examples.translation: My father works at a bank.

senses.definition: Of a machine, device, or system: to function or operate properly.

examples.text: यह कंप्यूटर ठीक से काम नहीं कर रहा है।
examples.translation: This computer is not working properly.

faults.quote: to come; to arrive; to happen
faults.why: Includes 'to happen' which is not in the senses, while omitting 'to know' (sense 1).

corrected.shortGloss: to come, to arrive; to know (a skill)
notes: Irregular in the perfective (past): आया (m. sg.), आए (m. pl.), आई (f. sg.), आईं (f. pl.).
In sense 2 (knowing a language or skill), the person takes को and आना agrees with the skill or infinitive verb: मुझे तैरना आता है (I know how to swim).

senses.definition: To move towards or reach the place where the speaker is or is talking about.

examples.text: कल हमारे घर आना।
examples.translation: Come to our house tomorrow.

senses.definition: To be known or mastered by someone, especially a language or practical skill.

examples.text: मुझे हिंदी बोलना आता है।
examples.translation: I know how to speak Hindi.

faults.quote: Telefonu erken saatte çalmak beni uyandırdı.
faults.why: Ungrammatical Turkish; a ringing phone takes conjugated verb or verbal noun (Telefonun çalması).
Missing everyday A1/A2 sense 'to knock (on a door)' (kapıyı çalmak).

faults.quote: çalmak has several very common meanings that depend entirely on the context.
faults.why: Both notes are pure filler stating the obvious about context; missing usage note on cases.

corrected.shortGloss: to play (music); to steal; to ring; to knock
notes: For playing music, Contrast with 'oynamak', which is used for games, sports, and acting.
With 'kapı' (door), 'kapıyı çalmak' means to knock on the door or ring the doorbell.

senses.definition: To make music on an instrument, or for music to play from a device.

examples.text: Akşamları gitar çalmak beni rahatlatıyor.
examples.translation: Playing the guitar in the evenings relaxes me.

senses.definition: To secretly take something that belongs to someone else.

examples.text: Hırsız cüzdanımı çalmak istedi.
examples.translation: The thief wanted to steal my wallet.

senses.definition: To make a ringing sound, such as a phone, alarm, or bell.

examples.text: Sabah erkenden telefon çaldı.
examples.translation: The phone rang early in the morning.

senses.definition: To knock on a door or ring a doorbell.

examples.text: İçeri girmeden önce lütfen kapıyı çalın.
examples.translation: Please knock on the door before coming in.

faults.quote: /tʃaɫɯˈma maˈsasɯ/
faults.why: Missing /ʃ/ sound in 'çalışma' and wrong stress placement.

faults.quote: Bilgisayarımı çalışma masası üzerine koydum.
faults.why: Missing genitive suffix; natural Turkish requires 'çalışma masasının üzerine' or 'çalışma masasına'.

notes: A compound noun from 'çalışma' (working/studying) and 'masa' (table). When adding case suffixes, a buffer 'n' is inserted after the possessive ending '-sı': 'çalışma masasında' (on the desk).

senses.definition: A table used for working, writing, or studying.

examples.text: Bilgisayarımı çalışma masasının üzerine koydum.
examples.translation: I put my computer on the desk.

faults.quote: followed by the dative case (-e/-a) or the infinitive with -meye/-mayı.
faults.why: False grammar: '-mayı' is accusative, which 'çalışmak' never takes; it takes '-meye/-maya' (dative).

faults.quote: Sorunu çözmek için elimden geldiğince çalışıyorum.
faults.why: With 'için', 'çalışıyorum' means 'working', not 'trying'; 'trying to solve' requires dative 'çözmeye çalışıyorum'.
Missing everyday sense 'to function / operate / run' (of a machine, car, or shop).

faults.quote: çalışmak is extremely versatile. Depending on the context, it can mean
faults.why: Pure filler restating the glosses.

corrected.shortGloss: to work; to study; to try; to function
notes: When meaning 'to try to do something', it takes a verbal noun in the dative case (-meye/-maya): 'anlamaya çalışmak' (to try to understand).
When meaning 'to study (a subject)', the subject usually takes the dative case (-e/-a): 'sınava çalışmak' (to study for an exam).

senses.definition: To do a job or perform tasks, especially to earn money.

examples.text: Babam her gün sabah erkenden çalışmaya başlar.
examples.translation: My father starts working early in the morning every day.

senses.definition: To spend time learning about a subject or preparing for an exam.

examples.text: Yarınki sınav için sabaha kadar çalıştı.
examples.translation: He studied until morning for tomorrow's exam.

senses.definition: To make an effort to do something.

examples.text: Bu sorunu çözmeye çalışıyorum.
examples.translation: I am trying to solve this problem.

senses.definition: Of a machine, device, or system: to operate or function properly.

examples.text: Asansör bozuk, bugün çalışmıyor.
examples.translation: The elevator is broken; it isn't working today.

faults.quote: Çanta is used broadly for handbags, backpacks, and plastic carrier bags alike.
faults.why: False: 'çanta' is not used for plastic carrier bags, which are called 'poşet' or 'torba'.
'Çanta' is a single general concept in Turkish; handbag, backpack, and schoolbag are one sense.

notes: Used for structured bags like handbags, backpacks ('sırt çantası'), and schoolbags ('okul çantası'). A plastic carrier bag or grocery bag is called 'poşet', and a small wallet for money and cards is 'cüzdan'.

senses.definition: A container made of leather, cloth, or synthetic material with handles or straps, used for carrying personal belongings, books, or work items.

examples.text: Anahtarlarımı çantamda unuttum.
examples.translation: I left my keys in my bag.

examples.text: Öğrenci ağır okul çantasını sırtına taktı.
examples.translation: The student put his heavy school bag on his back.

faults.quote: /tʃɑːtɯ/

faults.quote: While 'çatı' is most commonly used for the roof of a building
faults.why: Filler note that merely repeats the two sense definitions.

notes: Often used in the phrase 'tek çatı altında' (under one roof) for people living together or organizations uniting.

senses.definition: The top structure that covers and protects a building.

examples.text: Yoğun kar yağışı nedeniyle evin çatısı çöktü.
examples.translation: The roof of the house collapsed due to the heavy snowfall.

senses.definition: The overarching structure or framework that brings an organization or group together.

examples.text: Bu şirketler tek bir çatı altında birleşti.
examples.translation: These companies united under one roof.

notes: In Brazil, 'consertar' is the everyday verb for fixing broken objects; 'reparar' is more formal (and usually means 'to notice' in speech).
Do not confuse with the homophone 'concertar' (with a 'c'), a formal verb meaning to arrange or harmonize.

senses.definition: To make something broken or damaged work properly again.

examples.text: Preciso consertar a bicicleta este fim de semana.
examples.translation: I need to fix the bicycle this weekend.

faults.quote: Construir is used for large-scale projects like buildings or bridges
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the irregular present-tense conjugation (construo, constrói).

senses.definition: To make something, especially a building or structure, by putting parts together.

examples.text: Eles vão construir uma casa nova perto da praia.
examples.translation: They are going to build a new house near the beach.

senses.definition: To form or develop something abstract over time, such as a relationship, career, or idea.

examples.text: Precisamos construir uma base sólida para o nosso projeto.
examples.translation: We need to build a solid foundation for our project.

faults.quote: Corajoso is used for someone who faces danger or difficulty without

senses.definition: Showing courage; not afraid of danger or difficult situations.

examples.text: Ele foi muito corajoso ao enfrentar aquele problema sozinho.
examples.translation: He was very brave to face that problem alone.

faults.quote: /koˈʁɛʁ/

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.

examples.text: Preciso correr para não perder o ônibus.
examples.translation: I need to hurry so I don't miss the bus.

faults.quote: While 'cortar' covers physical cutting, it is also used for abstract things

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to slice; to cut off

senses.definition: To divide, shorten, or open something using a sharp tool like a knife or scissors.

examples.text: Preciso cortar o pão para o café da manhã.
examples.translation: I need to cut the bread for breakfast.

senses.definition: To stop, interrupt, or disconnect a supply, service, or relationship.

examples.text: Eles vão cortar a energia se não pagarmos a conta.
examples.translation: They are going to cut off the power if we don't pay the bill.

senses.definition: To transfer possession of something to someone else.

examples.text: Tôi cho cô ấy một ít hoa quả.
examples.translation: I gave her some fruit.

senses.definition: To allow or permit someone to do something.

examples.text: Mẹ không cho tôi đi chơi tối nay.
examples.translation: My mother is not letting me go out tonight.

senses.definition: Used after a verb to indicate the recipient or beneficiary of an action.

examples.text: Anh ấy mua một món quà cho bạn gái.
examples.translation: He bought a gift for his girlfriend.

faults.quote: Use 'chờ' when you are staying in one place

faults.why: 'Chờ' is completely everyday and neutral, not more formal than 'đợi'.

senses.definition: To stay in a place or delay action until someone arrives or something happens.

examples.text: Tôi đang chờ xe buýt ở trạm.
examples.translation: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.

examples.text: Chờ tôi một chút nhé.
examples.translation: Please wait for me a moment.

faults.quote: Unlike simply listening to music, chơi đàn requires physical action

faults.quote: /cəː˧˧/
faults.why: Missing the final glide /j/ of 'chơi'.

corrected.shortGloss: to play; to hang out; to have fun
notes: Often used in 'đi chơi' (literally 'go play'), a very common phrase meaning to go out for fun, hang out, or take a trip.

senses.definition: To take part in a game or sport, or to perform on a musical instrument.

examples.text: Chúng tôi thích chơi bóng đá vào cuối tuần.

senses.definition: To spend time relaxing, having fun, or socializing with friends.

examples.text: Hôm nay bạn có muốn đi chơi không?
examples.translation: Do you want to go out and have fun today?

faults.quote: /tɕɔn˧˥/
faults.why: Wrong tone: 'chọn' has the nặng tone (˧˨ʔ), not the sắc tone (˧˥).

faults.quote: Use chọn when you are picking something from a group
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

senses.definition: To pick someone or something from a number of options.

examples.text: Tôi muốn chọn một cuốn sách hay.
examples.translation: I want to choose a good book.

examples.text: Bạn đã chọn được món ăn chưa?
examples.translation: Have you chosen a dish yet?

faults.quote: to sleep; to rest
faults.why: Does not mean 'to rest', as note[1] itself explains.

senses.definition: To rest with your eyes closed and your body in a natural state of inactivity.

examples.text: Voy a dormir ocho horas esta noche.
examples.translation: I am going to sleep for eight hours tonight.

senses.definition: To spend the night somewhere away from home.

examples.text: Mañana voy a dormir en casa de mi amigo.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to stay over at my friend's house.

faults.quote: /ˈdulθe/
faults.why: Uses Peninsular /θ/ instead of Mexican Spanish /s/.

faults.quote: It can also be used metaphorically to describe a pleasant, kind
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 without adding grammar or usage information.

senses.definition: Having a taste like sugar or honey.

examples.text: Esta fruta está muy dulce.
examples.translation: This fruit is very sweet.

senses.definition: Of a person, voice, or manner: pleasant, gentle, and kind.

examples.text: Ella tiene un carácter muy dulce.
examples.translation: She has a very sweet personality.

faults.quote: Duro is highly versatile. It describes physical hardness, like a rock
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage guidance.

senses.definition: Solid, firm, and not easy to bend, cut, or press.

examples.translation: The bed was very hard.

senses.definition: Difficult to endure or requiring great effort.

examples.text: Fue un año muy duro para todos.
examples.translation: It was a very tough year for everyone.

faults.quote: Having received a high level of schooling or academic knowledge.
faults.why: Teaches the English false friend that note[0] specifically warns against.

faults.quote: polite; well-mannered; educated
faults.why: Includes false-friend gloss 'educated'.
