faults.why: Restates the meaning and gives unhelpful morphology instead of prepositions used.

notes: Form IV verb (imperfect يُرْسِلُ, verbal noun إِرْسَال). Takes إِلَى (ilā) or لِـ (li-) to mark the recipient.

senses.definition: To cause a message, item, or person to go to a destination or recipient.

examples.text: أَرْسَلَ أَحْمَدُ رِسَالَةً إِلَى صَدِيقِهِ.
examples.translation: Ahmed sent a message to his friend.

faults.quote: This verb is almost always followed by the preposition 'في'
faults.why: Usually takes أَنْ + subjunctive or a direct object; 'في أن' is unnatural.

faults.quote: أَمَلْتُ في أن نلتقي قريباً.
faults.why: Unvocalized and uses awkward 'في أن' instead of 'آمل أن'; imperfect is much more natural.

faults.quote: to hope; to wish
faults.why: 'to wish' is not in the sense glosses.

notes: Imperfect يَأْمُلُ (yaʾmulu, 1st person آمُلُ). Usually followed by أَنْ (ʾan) + subjunctive verb, or by فِي (fī) + noun.
Also common in the form أَمِلَ (ʾamila).

senses.definition: To want something to happen and believe that it is possible.

examples.text: آمُلُ أَنْ نَلْتَقِيَ قَرِيبًا.
examples.translation: I hope that we meet soon.

faults.quote: /qaˈtˤa.ʕa/
faults.why: Arabic 3-consonant CVCVCV verbs stress the first syllable: /ˈqa.tˤa.ʕa/.

faults.quote: This verb is highly versatile. It can mean cutting a physical object
faults.why: Merely summarizes the three senses already listed in the entry.

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to cross; to cut off
notes: Imperfect يَقْطَعُ (yaqṭaʿu).
Do not confuse with قَصَّ (qaṣṣa), which specifically refers to cutting with scissors (such as hair, paper, or cloth).

senses.definition: To divide or separate something using a knife or sharp tool.

examples.text: قَطَعَ الطَّبَّاخُ اللَّحْمَ بِالسِّكِّينِ.
examples.translation: The chef cut the meat with the knife.

senses.definition: To go from one side of a street, area, or distance to the other.

examples.text: قَطَعَ الرَّجُلُ الشَّارِعَ بِسُرْعَةٍ.
examples.translation: The man crossed the street quickly.

senses.definition: To stop a supply, connection, or relationship.

examples.text: قَطَعَ الاتِّصَالَ بَعْدَ مُشْكِلَةٍ.
examples.translation: He cut off the connection after a problem.

faults.quote: /iʃˈtɑːqa ʔiˈlaj/
faults.why: إِلَى in isolation is /ʔi.laː/, not /ʔiˈlaj/ (which only occurs before pronoun suffixes).

faults.quote: To feel sad because a person is absent or far away.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the exact same meaning ('to miss someone').

faults.quote: This verb always requires the preposition 'إِلَى'
faults.why: It very commonly takes لِـ (li-) instead of إِلَى.

notes: Form VIII hollow verb (imperfect يَشْتَاقُ yaštāqu). Takes إِلَى (ʾilā) or لِـ (li-) before the person or thing missed.
Only means feeling longing for someone or something, never failing to hit or failing to catch transport.

senses.definition: To feel longing for someone or something that is absent or far away.

examples.text: أَشْتَاقُ إِلَى عَائِلَتِي كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: I miss my family very much.

faults.quote: 작게 말해서 안 들려요.
faults.why: Uses the passive lemma 들리다 instead of the headword 듣다.
Missing the common A1/A2 sense 'to take (a class/course)' (수업을 듣다).
Missing irregular conjugation note: 듣다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb (들어, 들어요).

corrected.shortGloss: to listen to; to hear; to take (a class)
notes: ㄷ-irregular verb: the final ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel (듣다 → 들어요, 들었어요).
Covers both intentional 'listening' and passive 'hearing'. For 'to be audible / can be heard', Korean often uses the passive verb 들리다.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.

examples.text: 저는 매일 아침 음악을 들어요.
examples.translation: I listen to music every morning.

senses.definition: To perceive a sound or learn news with your ears.

examples.text: 그 소식을 듣고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.translation: I was very surprised to hear that news.

senses.definition: To attend or take a class, course, or lecture.

examples.text: 이번 학기에 한국어 수업을 들어요.
examples.translation: I am taking a Korean class this semester.

faults.quote: to make laugh, to crack someone up
faults.why: Missing 'to be funny', even though example[0] translates it as 'funny'.

corrected.shortGloss: to be funny; to make someone laugh; to be ridiculous
notes: Causative of 웃다 (to laugh). Even when translated into English as an adjective ('is funny'), 웃기다 conjugates as an action verb in Korean (e.g., 웃기는 이야기 'a funny story').
As an exclamation, '웃기네!' (or '웃기고 있네!') sounds sarcastic and dismissive ('Don't make me laugh! / That's ridiculous!').

senses.definition: To be amusing, or to cause someone to laugh.

examples.text: 그 친구는 정말 웃겨요.
examples.translation: That friend is really funny.

examples.text: 친구를 웃기려고 농담을 했어요.
examples.translation: I told a joke to make my friend laugh.

senses.definition: To be absurd or ridiculous.

examples.text: 그 상황이 정말 웃기네요.
examples.translation: That situation is truly ridiculous.

faults.why: Missing very common A1/A2 senses: 'to read (books/menus)', 'to take (an exam)', and auxiliary '-아/어 보다' ('to try').
Senses 0, 1, and 2 oversplit basic visual perception ('look at/see/watch') at the expense of other core meanings.

corrected.shortGloss: to see; to look at; to watch; to read; to take (a test)
notes: Covers 'to see', 'to look at', and 'to watch'. Do not confuse with its passive form 보이다 (to be visible).
After another verb in the -아/어 form (-아/어 보다), it acts as an auxiliary verb meaning 'to try doing' (e.g., 먹어 보다 'to try eating').

senses.definition: To perceive with the eyes, or to turn your eyes toward something; to watch a movie or show.

examples.text: 어제 친구하고 영화를 봤어요.
examples.translation: I watched a movie with my friend yesterday.

examples.text: 잠깐 이 사진 좀 보세요.
examples.translation: Please look at this photo for a moment.

senses.definition: To read a book, newspaper, menu, etc.

examples.text: 아침마다 신문을 봐요.
examples.translation: I read the newspaper every morning.

senses.definition: To take an exam or go through an interview.

examples.text: 내일 한국어 시험을 봐요.
examples.translation: I am taking a Korean exam tomorrow.

faults.quote: to look for; to find
faults.why: Omits sense 2 ('to withdraw').
Both notes merely restate the glosses of the senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to look for; to find; to withdraw (money)
notes: Because 찾다 means both 'to look for' (process) and 'to find' (result), tense and aspect clarify the meaning: 찾고 있어요 means 'I am looking for it', while 찾았어요 usually means 'I found it'.

senses.definition: To try to discover where someone or something is.

examples.text: 열쇠를 찾고 있어요.
examples.translation: I am looking for my keys.

senses.definition: To discover or get back something that was lost or needed.

examples.text: 드디어 답을 찾았어요.
examples.translation: I finally found the answer.

senses.definition: To take money out of a bank account or ATM.

examples.text: 은행에서 돈을 찾았어요.
examples.translation: I withdrew money at the bank.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the exact same meaning ('to sell') with nearly identical examples.
Replaced needed grammar info (ㄹ-irregular conjugation) with a filler note.

notes: ㄹ-irregular verb: the final ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, and ㅅ (e.g., 팝니다, 파는, 파세요).
The opposite verb is 사다 (to buy).

senses.definition: To give or offer something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: 그 가게는 신선한 과일을 팔아요.
examples.translation: That shop sells fresh fruit.

faults.quote: Estoy muy hambriento después de la caminata larga.
faults.why: Calque: Spanish naturally says 'Tengo mucha hambre', as the entry's own note points out.

faults.quote: sediento de algo
faults.why: 'Sediento' literally means thirsty, which is confusing as a primary gloss for 'hungry'.

notes: En inglés se usa el verbo 'to be' ('I am hungry'), a diferencia del español que suele usar 'tener' ('tengo hambre').
En sentido figurado va seguido de la preposición 'for' ('hungry for success').

senses.definition: Que siente la necesidad o el deseo de comer.

examples.text: I am so hungry after the long walk.
examples.translation: Tengo mucha hambre después de la larga caminata.

senses.definition: Que tiene un deseo fuerte por conseguir algo.

examples.text: She is hungry for success in her new job.
examples.translation: Ella está ávida de éxito en su nuevo trabajo.

faults.quote: Sentir un dolor físico o causar daño a alguien.
faults.why: Merges two distinct syntactic/semantic senses (intransitive 'be painful' vs transitive 'injure') and defines 'hurt' falsely as 'sentir dolor'.

notes: Es un verbo irregular cuyas tres formas son iguales: 'hurt - hurt - hurt'.
También se usa como adjetivo ('Are you hurt?' — ¿Estás herido?).

senses.definition: Causar dolor una parte del cuerpo.

examples.text: My back hurts after sitting all day.
examples.translation: Me duele la espalda después de estar sentado todo el día.

senses.definition: Causar daño o dolor físico o emocional a alguien.

examples.text: Be careful, you might hurt yourself.
examples.translation: Ten cuidado, podrías lastimarte.

faults.quote: No confundas 'husband' con 'house', que es 'casa'.
faults.why: Unhelpful filler warning about an unlikely confusion.

notes: Su equivalente femenino es 'wife' (esposa) y el término neutro es 'spouse' (cónyuge).

senses.definition: Hombre con el que una persona está casada.

examples.text: My husband and I are going on a trip next week.
examples.translation: Mi esposo y yo vamos a ir de viaje la próxima semana.

faults.quote: no se usa con 'a' o 'an' a menos que especifiques
faults.why: Partially false: 'an ice cream' is very common in everyday English for a cone or individual serving.

faults.quote: No confundir con 'iced coffee' o 'iced tea'
faults.why: Unnecessary filler note; learners do not confuse 'ice cream' with 'iced tea'.

notes: Es incontable cuando se refiere al alimento en general ('some ice cream'), pero contable cuando se refiere a una porción o cono ('an ice cream').

senses.definition: Postre dulce y congelado que se prepara con leche o crema.

examples.text: I love eating chocolate ice cream on a hot day.
examples.translation: Me encanta comer helado de chocolate en un día caluroso.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para el hielo en cubitos en las bebidas
faults.why: Filler note explaining that 'ice' works just like Spanish 'hielo'; misses the needed countability note.

notes: Es un sustantivo incontable (no se dice 'an ice' ni 'ices'); para unidades individuales se usa 'ice cube' (cubito de hielo).

senses.definition: Agua que se ha congelado y se ha vuelto sólida por el frío.

examples.text: Put some ice in my drink, please.
examples.translation: Pon algo de hielo en mi bebida, por favor.

notes: Used for both fingers and toes. To be specific, say 'palec u ręki' (finger) or 'palec u nogi' (toe).
The stem loses its 'e' in all declined forms: 'palca' (genitive), 'palce' (plural).

senses.definition: One of the five movable parts at the end of a human hand.

examples.text: Wskazał na mapę palcem.
examples.translation: He pointed at the map with his finger.

senses.definition: One of the five movable parts at the end of a human foot.

examples.text: Uderzył się w palec u nogi o próg.
examples.translation: He stubbed his toe on the threshold.

faults.quote: /paˈmjɛ.tat͡ɕ/
faults.why: Wrong transcription of nasal vowel 'ę': should be /paˈmjɛn.tat͡ɕ/.
Missing the 'pamiętać o + locative' pattern used in sense 1's example.

faults.quote: You must keep the keys in mind.
faults.why: Unnatural translation; in English one says 'remember to take the keys'.

corrected.shortGloss: to remember; to keep in mind
notes: Imperfective verb. Takes the accusative for recalling past things ('pamiętam to'), or 'o' + locative for not forgetting something ('pamiętaj o kluczach').

senses.definition: To have a memory of someone or something from the past.

examples.text: Pamiętam nasz pierwszy spacer.
examples.translation: I remember our first walk.

senses.definition: To keep something in mind so you do not forget it.

examples.text: Musisz pamiętać o kluczach.
examples.translation: You must remember the keys.

faults.quote: Used both for the raw material and for documents or identity papers.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses.

notes: In the sense of official documents or ID, it is usually used in the plural ('papiery') and is informal.
Do not confuse with 'gazeta', which means newspaper ('a paper' in English).

senses.definition: Thin material used for writing, printing, or wrapping things.

examples.text: Muszę kupić papier do drukarki.
examples.translation: I need to buy paper for the printer.

senses.definition: Official documents showing identity, ownership, or permission, usually in the plural.

examples.text: Policjant sprawdził moje papiery.
examples.translation: The police officer checked my papers.

faults.quote: Polish uses 'para' for both objects and people, similar to English
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding grammar or usage help.

faults.quote: When referring to two people in a romantic relationship, use 'para'
faults.why: Pure filler restating the senses instead of explaining genitive plural usage.

notes: When meaning 'a pair of', it is followed by a noun in the genitive plural: 'para butów' (a pair of shoes).

senses.definition: Two things of the same type that are worn or used together.

examples.text: Muszę kupić nową parę butów.
examples.translation: I need to buy a new pair of shoes.

senses.definition: Two people who are together in a romantic relationship.

examples.text: To bardzo szczęśliwa para.
examples.translation: They are a very happy couple.

senses.definition: The hot gas produced when water boils.

examples.text: Z garnka unosi się gorąca para.
examples.translation: Hot steam is rising from the pot.

notes: A small folding rain umbrella is also often called 'parasolka' (feminine).

senses.definition: A folding object that you hold over your head to protect yourself from rain or sun.

examples.text: Muszę wziąć parasol, bo zaczyna padać.
examples.translation: I need to take an umbrella because it is starting to rain.

faults.quote: This is a very versatile verb. Use it for fixing broken
faults.why: merely restates the senses already listed

faults.quote: वे आपस में झगड़ा ठीक करना चाहते हैं।
faults.why: झगड़ा ठीक करना is unnatural; सुलझाना is used for disputes, ठीक करना for situatons/relations
missing common everyday sense 'to cure / make someone well'

corrected.shortGloss: to fix; to correct; to cure
notes: Transitive compound verb (takes ने in perfective tenses). Its intransitive counterpart is ठीक होना ('to get fixed, to recover').
For improving skills or habits, सुधारना is preferred over ठीक करना.

senses.definition: To repair a damaged machine or object, or put something back in order.

examples.text: उसने मेरी घड़ी ठीक की।
examples.translation: He fixed my watch.

senses.definition: To correct an error, mistake, or problem.

examples.text: अध्यापक ने छात्र की गलती ठीक की।
examples.translation: The teacher corrected the student's mistake.

senses.definition: To restore a person or illness to health.

examples.text: इस दवा ने मेरी खाँसी ठीक कर दी।
examples.translation: This medicine cured my cough.

faults.quote: देखना (dekhnā) covers the entire range of visual perception
faults.why: merely summarizes the three senses

faults.quote: मैंने कल बाजार में एक पुराना दोस्त देखा।
faults.why: animate direct object 'friend' naturally takes को (एक पुराने दोस्त को देखा)

corrected.shortGloss: to see; to look at; to watch
notes: Transitive verb (takes ने in perfective tenses). Do not confuse with दिखना ('to be visible / to seem') or दिखाना ('to show').
When meaning 'to look at' a specific person or thing, the object usually takes को (e.g. मेरी तरफ़ देखो / मुझे देखो 'look at me').

senses.definition: To perceive or notice someone or something with the eyes.

examples.text: मैंने कल बाज़ार में अपने एक पुराने दोस्त को देखा।
examples.translation: I saw an old friend of mine in the market yesterday.

senses.definition: To direct one's eyes toward something.

examples.text: उसने खिड़की से बाहर देखा।
examples.translation: He looked out of the window.

senses.definition: To look at something attentively over a period of time, such as a film or match.

examples.text: हम रात को एक अच्छी फ़िल्म देखेंगे।
examples.translation: We will watch a good film tonight.

faults.why: missing irregular perfective stems (लिया, लिए, ली, लीं) and polite imperative (लीजिए)
senses 0 (take) and 2 (accept/receive) are shades of the same basic meaning

corrected.shortGloss: to take; to receive; to buy
notes: Irregular in the perfective (लिया, लिए, ली, लीं) and polite imperative (लीजिए). Takes ने in perfective tenses.
Often used after another verb's stem (e.g. रख लेना, पढ़ लेना) to show completeness or that the action benefits the subject.

senses.definition: To get hold of something, or to accept something offered.

examples.text: उसने मेज़ से किताब ली।
examples.translation: She took the book from the table.

examples.text: उसने मेरा उपहार खुशी से ले लिया।
examples.translation: He happily accepted my gift.

senses.definition: To buy or get something, such as food, clothes, or tickets.

examples.text: मैं बाज़ार से फल लेने जा रहा हूँ।
examples.translation: I am going to the market to buy fruit.

faults.quote: to lose; to misplace
faults.why: omits sense 1 ('to get lost')

notes: Used both transitively ('to lose something', often compounded with देना as खो देना) and intransitively ('to get lost', often compounded with जाना as खो जाना).

senses.definition: To no longer have something, or to be unable to find it.

examples.text: मैंने अपनी चाबी खो दी है।
examples.translation: I have lost my key.

senses.definition: To go missing or be unable to find one's way.

examples.text: हम अनजान शहर में खो गए।
examples.translation: We got lost in the unfamiliar city.

faults.quote: you often use the verb with the postposition 'में' (in) when
faults.why: completely fabricated grammar claim; सोना does not take में to mean falling asleep
'to sleep' and 'to go to sleep' are one sense; example 1 shows 'sleep'

corrected.shortGloss: to sleep; to go to sleep
notes: Intransitive verb (never takes ने). When compounded with जाना (सो जाना), it specifically means 'to fall asleep'.
Do not confuse with the homonym सोना ('gold', masculine noun) or with लेटना ('to lie down').

senses.definition: To rest with the eyes closed in a natural state of sleep, or to go to sleep.

examples.text: बच्चा अभी सो रहा है।
examples.translation: The baby is sleeping right now.

examples.text: मैं रात को जल्दी सो जाता हूँ।
examples.translation: I go to sleep early at night.

faults.quote: Aunque 'beach' se refiere principalmente a la orilla del mar
faults.why: Wordy filler; 'playa' also includes sand or pebbles, and the vowel contrast with 'bitch' is more useful.

notes: Se usa a menudo con las preposiciones 'at' o 'on' ('at the beach', 'on the beach').
Pronuncia una 'i' larga (/biːtʃ/) para no confundirla con la palabra malsonante 'bitch' (/bɪtʃ/).

senses.definition: Franja de arena o piedras a la orilla del mar, de un río o de un lago.

examples.text: We spent the whole day at the beach.
examples.translation: Pasamos todo el día en la playa.

faults.quote: /bɛər/
faults.why: British IPA (/bɛər/) instead of US English (/bɛr/).

notes: Se pronuncia /bɛr/ (rima con 'air'), no como 'beer' (/bɪr/, cerveza).
No confundir con el verbo 'to bear', que significa soportar o llevar.

senses.definition: Mamífero grande de pelaje espeso, cola muy corta y garras fuertes.

examples.text: We saw a large bear walking near the river in the forest.
examples.translation: Vimos un oso grande caminando cerca del río en el bosque.

faults.quote: Se usa para describir algo o alguien que es muy agradable
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: Es más intenso que 'pretty' (lindo, bonito). En personas se usa sobre todo para mujeres o niños; para hombres suele preferirse 'handsome' (guapo).

senses.definition: Que es muy agradable a la vista o a los sentidos; que tiene gran belleza.

examples.text: She wore a beautiful dress to the party.
examples.translation: Se puso un vestido hermoso para la fiesta.

examples.text: The view from the mountain was absolutely beautiful.
examples.translation: La vista desde la montaña era absolutamente hermosa.

faults.quote: (respuesta) Se usa para responder a la pregunta '¿Por qué?'.
faults.why: Answering 'why?' is the exact same causal conjunction sense as sense 0.

faults.quote: porque; debido a
faults.why: 'Debido a' corresponds to 'because of' (which the note explicitly warns against) and is not in the sense glosses.

faults.quote: /bɪˈkɒz/
faults.why: Uses British vowel /ɒ/ instead of US /ɔː/ or /ʌ/.

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 'because' is a conjunction, not a multi-word expression.

notes: Se usa antes de una oración con sujeto y verbo ('because it was raining'). Antes de un sustantivo o pronombre se usa 'because of' ('because of the rain', por la lluvia).

senses.definition: Introduce la causa o razón de algo, o responde a la pregunta 'why?'.

examples.text: I was late because I missed the bus.
examples.translation: Llegué tarde porque perdí el autobús.

examples.text: Why are you sad? — Because I lost my keys.
examples.translation: ¿Por qué estás triste? — Porque perdí mis llaves.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para el mueble donde duermes como, en expresiones
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the crucial learner point about omitting 'the' in 'go to bed' / 'in bed'.

notes: En expresiones cotidianas como 'go to bed' (irse a dormir), 'be in bed' (estar acostado) o 'get out of bed' (levantarse), no se usa el artículo 'the'.

senses.definition: Mueble que se usa para acostarse a dormir o descansar.

examples.text: She went to bed early because she was tired.
examples.translation: Se fue a la cama temprano porque estaba cansada.

senses.definition: Porción de tierra en un jardín preparada para sembrar plantas o flores.

examples.text: He planted roses in the flower bed.
examples.translation: Plantó rosas en el cantero de flores.

faults.quote: Use posiłek to talk about a meal in a general way
faults.why: Restates the definition and obvious countability; fleeting vowel (-e- drops in inflected forms) is needed.

notes: The 'e' drops in all other forms: bez posiłku (genitive singular), posiłki (nominative plural).

senses.definition: Food eaten at a regular time of day, or the occasion of eating it.

examples.text: Regularne posiłki są bardzo ważne dla zdrowia.
examples.translation: Regular meals are very important for your health.

faults.quote: 'Potrzebować' is for needing an object or person.
faults.why: 'Potrzebować' can also take an infinitive (e.g., potrzebuję odpocząć); better to state the contrast accurately.

notes: Takes the genitive case for the thing needed (e.g., potrzebuję pomocy — I need help).
To express obligation ('need to / have to do something'), Polish normally uses 'musieć' + infinitive rather than 'potrzebować'.

senses.definition: To have a need for something or someone.

examples.text: Potrzebuję nowej kurtki na zimę.
examples.translation: I need a new jacket for the winter.

examples.text: Czy potrzebujesz pomocy z tym zadaniem?
examples.translation: Do you need help with this task?

notes: An adverb used with verbs and in impersonal time expressions (Jest późno — It is late). To say a person is late, use the verb 'spóźnić się' or adjective 'spóźniony'.
The comparative form is 'później' (later). Opposite: 'wcześnie' (early).

senses.definition: Near the end of the day, or far into the night.

examples.text: Jest już bardzo późno, muszę iść spać.
examples.translation: It is already very late; I have to go to sleep.

senses.definition: After the expected, arranged, or usual time.

examples.text: Przyszedłeś późno na spotkanie.
examples.translation: You arrived late for the meeting.

faults.why: Missing two very common A1/A2 senses: workplace ('iść do pracy') and written assignment/paper.

faults.quote: work, labor, task
faults.why: 'Task' contradicts note[1] and is not what uncountable 'praca' (effort) means.

notes: For a specific task or exercise, use 'zadanie' (though 'praca domowa' means 'homework').

senses.definition: Regular paid employment; a job.

examples.text: Szukam nowej pracy.
examples.translation: I am looking for a new job.

senses.definition: Physical or mental effort done to achieve or make something.

examples.text: To wymaga dużo ciężkiej pracy.
examples.translation: This requires a lot of hard work.

senses.definition: The place where someone works.

examples.text: O której godzinie wracasz z pracy?
examples.translation: What time do you get back from work?

senses.definition: A piece of writing or project done for school or university, or a work of art.

examples.text: Muszę napisać pracę na jutro.
examples.translation: I have to write a paper for tomorrow.

faults.quote: Ten komputer nie chce pracować.
faults.why: Calque from English; in Polish, broken devices do not 'działają' ('Ten komputer nie działa').

notes: Use 'w' + locative for a workplace (pracować w szkole/w firmie) and 'jako' + nominative for a profession (pracować jako nauczyciel).

senses.definition: To do a job for pay, or to put effort into a task.

examples.text: Muszę dzisiaj długo pracować.
examples.translation: I have to work late today.

senses.definition: Of an engine, machine, or organ: to be running or operating.

examples.text: Silnik pracuje bardzo cicho.
examples.translation: The engine runs very quietly.

faults.quote: /us ˈpajs/
faults.why: Broad IPA of the lemma should not include the definite article.

notes: In Portuguese, the masculine plural 'os pais' is used to refer to both a mother and a father together, or two fathers. The singular 'pai' means 'father'.
Do not confuse this with 'os países', which means 'the countries' (plural of 'o país').

senses.definition: The mother and father, or the two parents, of a person considered together.

examples.text: Os meus pais moram no interior.
examples.translation: My parents live in the countryside.

faults.quote: Use 'ouvir' for the physical act of hearing...
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1; in Brazilian Portuguese, 'ouvir' and 'escutar' are both used for listening.
Missing note on the irregular first-person singular form 'eu ouço' (/ˈowsu/).

notes: Irregular in the 1st person singular present indicative: 'eu ouço' (and present subjunctive 'que eu ouça').
In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, 'ouvir' and 'escutar' are largely interchangeable for both 'hear' and 'listen to' (e.g., 'ouvir música' or 'escutar música').

senses.definition: To perceive a sound with your ears.

examples.text: Eu consigo ouvir o barulho do mar.
examples.translation: I can hear the sound of the sea.

senses.definition: To pay attention to someone speaking or to a sound such as music or the radio.

examples.text: Gosto de ouvir música enquanto trabalho.
examples.translation: I like to listen to music while I work.

faults.quote: if you are paying a person, you must use the preposition 'a'
faults.why: False in Brazilian Portuguese; 'pagar alguém' (direct object, no preposition) is standard and more common.

faults.quote: O trabalho duro sempre paga bem.
faults.why: Anglicism calqued from 'pay off' / 'pay well'; not how 'pagar' is used in Portuguese.

notes: In Brazilian Portuguese, you can take either the thing bought or the person paid as a direct object ('pagar a conta', 'pagar o garçom'), or use 'por' for the item ('pagar pelo jantar').
Has two past participles: 'pagado' (used with 'ter'/'haver', though 'pago' is very common in speech) and the irregular short form 'pago' (used with 'ser'/'estar': 'a conta está paga').

senses.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or work, or to settle a bill or debt.

examples.text: Eu preciso pagar a conta do restaurante.
examples.translation: I need to pay the restaurant bill.

senses.definition: To suffer punishment or bad consequences as a result of an action or mistake.

examples.text: Ele vai pagar caro pelo que fez.
examples.translation: He is going to pay dearly for what he did.

faults.quote: Parar is the most common way to say stop.
faults.why: Restates the gloss instead of explaining the grammar ('parar de' + infinitive).

faults.quote: The bus will stop there in front.
faults.why: Calqued translation of 'ali na frente'; natural English is 'up ahead' or 'just ahead'.

faults.quote: To stay in a place for a period of time
faults.why: Staying at a hotel is marginal/regional for A2 compared to 'stop moving' vs 'stop doing'.

notes: To say 'stop doing something', use 'parar de' followed by the infinitive (e.g., 'parar de falar', 'parar de fumar').
The expression 'ir parar em' is very common and means 'to end up in' a place (e.g., 'Como você foi parar lá?').

senses.definition: To cease moving, or to cause a person or vehicle to cease moving.

examples.text: O ônibus vai parar ali na frente.
examples.translation: The bus is going to stop right up ahead.

senses.definition: To cease doing an activity or for an event or process to come to an end.

examples.text: Temos que parar de falar agora.
examples.translation: We have to stop talking now.

faults.quote: Preciso pegar esse papel na parede.

faults.quote: Pegar is one of the most common verbs in Brazilian Portuguese.

corrected.shortGloss: to take; to pick up; to catch; to grab
notes: 'Pegar' is the standard everyday verb in Brazil for picking things up, fetching something, or taking transport. In European Portuguese, 'apanhar' is used instead in most of these contexts.

senses.definition: To take hold of, pick up, or go and get an object.

examples.text: Vou pegar o livro que está na mesa.
examples.translation: I am going to get the book that is on the table.

senses.definition: To board and travel on a bus, train, plane, or taxi.

examples.text: Eu pego o ônibus todo dia às sete.
examples.translation: I take the bus every day at seven.

senses.definition: To intercept and hold something moving through the air, or to capture someone or something.

examples.text: Ele conseguiu pegar a bola no ar.
examples.translation: He managed to catch the ball in the air.

senses.definition: To contract an infectious illness such as a cold or the flu.

examples.text: Acho que peguei uma gripe forte.
examples.translation: I think I caught a bad flu.

faults.quote: /vɨˈswat͡ɕ/
faults.why: This is the IPA for perfective 'wysłać'; 'wysyłać' is /vɨˈsɨ.wat͡ɕ/.
Sending things and sending people are the same basic meaning in Polish and English.

notes: Imperfective verb (used for ongoing or repeated actions); its perfective counterpart is 'wysłać'.
The recipient takes the dative case, or follows the preposition 'do' + genitive.

senses.definition: To cause something to go or be taken to a place or person, by mail, electronically, or by telling someone to go.

examples.text: Muszę wysyłać te dokumenty pocztą co tydzień.
examples.translation: I have to send these documents by mail every week.

examples.text: Szef lubi wysyłać pracowników na szkolenia za granicę.
examples.translation: The boss likes to send employees to training abroad.

faults.quote: Used as both a utensil for eating and a unit of measurement
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

notes: Refers to a normal soup spoon or tablespoon; for a smaller teaspoon, use the diminutive 'łyżeczka'.

senses.definition: A utensil with a shallow bowl on a handle, used for eating soup, stirring, or serving food.

examples.text: Połóż łyżkę obok talerza.
examples.translation: Put the spoon next to the plate.

senses.definition: The amount of food or liquid that fits in a large spoon, used as a measure in cooking.

examples.text: Dodaj dwie łyżki cukru do ciasta.
examples.translation: Add two tablespoons of sugar to the dough.

faults.quote: Used to indicate the material, tool, or manner used to do something.

faults.why: Ungrammatical calque from English; in Polish it is 'Pisał list piórem' (no preposition).

faults.quote: When it means 'with' (accompaniment or instrument), it takes the instrumental case
faults.why: False grammar rule: 'z' + instrumental is not used for instruments/tools in Polish.

Spelled and pronounced 'ze' before certain consonant clusters, e.g., 'ze mną' (with me), 'ze szkoły' (from school).

senses.definition: In the company of someone, or having something included or attached.

examples.text: Idę do kina z przyjacielem.
examples.translation: I am going to the cinema with a friend.

examples.text: Poproszę kawę z mlekiem.
examples.translation: I'd like a coffee with milk, please.

senses.definition: Indicating the place someone or something comes from, leaves, or is taken out of.

examples.translation: I am coming back home from work.

senses.definition: Indicating the material or ingredients something is made of.

examples.text: To jest stół z drewna.
examples.translation: This is a table made of wood.

faults.quote: In or to a foreign country.

faults.quote: Across the national border of a country.

senses.definition: In a foreign country or countries.

examples.text: Pracuję za granicą od dwóch lat.
examples.translation: I have been working abroad for two years.

faults.quote: When talking about the 'teeth' of a saw or gear, Polish uses

The final 'b' is devoiced to a 'p' sound at the end of the word, but pronounced 'b' before endings ('zęby').

senses.definition: One of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.

examples.text: Boli mnie ząb.

senses.definition: One of a row of pointed parts on an object such as a comb, saw, zipper, or gear.

senses.definition: To be absent, not present, or not enough.

examples.text: Manca il sale nella pasta.
examples.translation: The pasta needs salt.

senses.definition: Of a person or thing: to have one's absence felt with sadness by someone.

examples.text: Mi manchi tanto.
examples.translation: I miss you so much.

senses.definition: To remain before a time, place, or goal is reached.

examples.text: Mancano solo cinque minuti alla fine.
examples.translation: There are only five minutes left until the end.

faults.quote: To slowly consume or damage something, like rust does to metal.
faults.why: Figurative sense ('corrode') is not needed at A2 level.

senses.definition: To put food into the mouth, chew it, and swallow it, or to have a meal.

faults.quote: Turn on an electronic device or appliance.

senses.definition: To move something to a particular place or position.

senses.definition: To not win; to be defeated in a game, match, or struggle, or to give in to something.

faults.why: Restates the definitions and glosses.

senses.definition: For one's heart to ache with grief, distress, or sympathy (often as 心が痛む or 胸が痛む).

notes: An intransitive godan verb (立たない, 立ちます); its transitive pair is 立てる. Because 立つ means to move into a standing position, 'to be standing' is expressed with 立っている.

senses.definition: To rise to one's feet, or (as 立っている) to be in an upright position.

senses.definition: To leave for a destination or start a journey.

examples.translation: I plan to depart for Japan tomorrow.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (おしえる) for a headword containing kanji.

senses.definition: To impart knowledge or skills to someone; to instruct.

senses.definition: To give someone information they do not know, such as an address, a name, or directions.

examples.translation: They showed me the way to the station.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading (きく) for a headword containing kanji.

faults.quote: To pay attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a sound, music, or speech, or to perceive a sound or piece of news.

senses.definition: To ask someone a question in order to get information.

senses.definition: Que siente vergüenza, timidez o incomodidad ante los demás por una situación torpe o por haber hecho el ridículo.

faults.quote: Se usa para objetos, espacios y también para situaciones abstractas

senses.definition: A sweet substance, usually in the form of white crystals, used to sweeten food and drinks or found in food.

examples.text: Pijesz kawę z cukrem czy bez?
examples.translation: Do you drink coffee with sugar or without?

examples.text: Ten jogurt ma dużo cukru.
examples.translation: This yogurt has a lot of sugar.

faults.quote: to know (a person, place, or fact)
faults.why: Senses do not include 'fact', and Note 0 says 'wiedzieć' is for facts.

corrected.shortGloss: to know (a person, place, or skill); to be familiar with
notes: Distinguish 'znać' from 'wiedzieć'. Use 'znać' for familiarity with a person, place, language, or noun ('znać odpowiedź' – to know the answer). Use 'wiedzieć' for facts and clauses ('wiedzieć, że...' – to know that...).
'Znać' takes a direct object in the accusative case (or genitive when negated). Its present tense forms are irregular: znam, znasz, zna, znamy, znacie, znają.

senses.definition: To have met and be familiar with a person, or to have visited and be familiar with a place.

examples.text: Znam tego człowieka bardzo dobrze.
examples.translation: I know this man very well.

examples.text: Znasz dobrze to miasto?
examples.translation: Do you know this city well?

senses.definition: To have knowledge or command of a skill, language, or piece of information.

examples.text: Znam język polski.
examples.translation: I know Polish.

faults.quote: Staram się znajdować moje klucze w pokoju.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: a single attempt to find keys requires perfective 'znaleźć', not imperfective 'znajdować'.

faults.quote: to find; to locate
faults.why: Omits the very common reflexive sense 'to be located' present in sense 1.

corrected.shortGloss: to find; (with się) to be located
notes: Imperfective verb (used for repeated actions or ongoing processes); its perfective counterpart is 'znaleźć' (for a single completed action).
With the reflexive pronoun 'się' ('znajdować się'), it means 'to be located' or 'to find oneself' somewhere.

senses.definition: To discover where something or someone is after searching or by chance.

examples.text: Często znajduję ciekawe książki w tym sklepie.
examples.translation: I often find interesting books in this shop.

senses.definition: (reflexive, znajdować się) To be located in a specific place or position.

examples.text: Szpital znajduje się blisko stacji.
examples.translation: The hospital is located near the station.

faults.quote: use the preposition 'z' followed by the instrumental case: 'Jestem znudzony z tego filmu'
faults.why: Completely false grammar: 'znudzony' takes bare instrumental ('znudzony tym filmem'), and 'tego filmu' is genitive.

faults.quote: /ˈznudzɔnɨ/
faults.why: Wrong stress: Polish words are stressed on the penultimate syllable (/znuˈd͡zɔ.nɨ/).

notes: Do not confuse 'znudzony' (bored, how a person feels) with 'nudny' (boring, causing boredom).
To say what you are bored with, follow 'znudzony' directly with a noun in the instrumental case without a preposition: 'Jestem znudzony tym filmem' (I am bored with this movie).

senses.definition: Feeling tired and impatient because something is not interesting or you have nothing to do.

examples.text: Byłem znudzony, bo cały dzień padał deszcz.
examples.translation: I was bored because it was raining all day.

faults.quote: /ʐɔˈwɔdɛk/
faults.why: Missing nasalization/consonant for 'ą' before 'd'; standard pronunciation is /ʐɔˈwɔn.dɛk/.

faults.quote: The genitive case of 'żołądek' is 'żołądka'. Be careful with the vowel change!
faults.why: False claim: the 'e' drops out (fleeting vowel), it does not change into another vowel.

notes: Distinguish between 'żołądek' (the internal digestive organ) and 'brzuch' (the belly or abdomen as a body part).
The 'e' in the final syllable is a fleeting vowel and drops in all declined forms (e.g., genitive singular 'żołądka').

senses.definition: The internal organ in the body where food is digested.

examples.text: Boli mnie żołądek po tym obiedzie.
examples.translation: My stomach hurts after that lunch.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a woman in a marriage.
faults.why: Restates the definition; note 1 also contains filler about register.

notes: The masculine counterpart is 'mąż' (husband).

senses.definition: The woman that someone is married to.

examples.text: Moja żona bardzo lubi kawę.
examples.translation: My wife likes coffee very much.

faults.quote: pero en el inglés británico formal a veces se usa 'have got'
faults.why: 'Have got' is informal, not formal, and is also used in American English.
Missing irregular forms (has, had) and how questions/negatives are formed for the main verb.

faults.quote: También es el verbo auxiliar principal para formar los tiempos compuestos
faults.why: Simply restates sense 1.

notes: Es un verbo irregular: la tercera persona del singular en presente es 'has' y el pasado y participio son 'had'.
Como verbo principal, forma preguntas y negaciones con el auxiliar 'do' (ej. 'Do you have time?', 'I don't have a car'). En el habla informal también se usa 'have got'.

senses.definition: Poseer algo, contar con ello o mantener una relación familiar o personal.

examples.text: I have a new car.
examples.translation: Tengo un coche nuevo.

senses.definition: Consumir alimentos o bebidas.

examples.text: Let's have a cup of coffee.
examples.translation: Tomemos una taza de café.

senses.definition: Realizar una acción, vivir una experiencia o padecer una dolencia.

examples.text: Did you have a good time at the party?
examples.translation: ¿Lo pasaste bien en la fiesta?

senses.definition: Usarse como verbo auxiliar con un participio pasado para formar los tiempos compuestos.

examples.text: They have finished their work.
examples.translation: Ellos han terminado su trabajo.

notes: Para decir que te duele la cabeza, lo más común es usar 'My head hurts' o 'I have a headache'.

senses.definition: Parte superior del cuerpo que contiene los ojos, la nariz, la boca y el cerebro.

examples.text: She nodded her head to say yes.
examples.translation: Ella asintió con la cabeza para decir que sí.

senses.definition: Persona que dirige o está al mando de una organización, grupo o institución.

examples.text: He is the head of the company.
examples.translation: Él es el jefe de la empresa.

faults.why: Learners need to know it is countable in English and requires 'a' ('have a headache').

notes: Es un sustantivo contable, por lo que en singular siempre lleva el artículo 'a', a diferencia del español: 'I have a headache' (Tengo dolor de cabeza).
También se usa en sentido figurado para algo que causa muchos problemas (ej. 'That project is a real headache').

senses.definition: Dolor continuo localizado en la cabeza.

examples.text: I have a terrible headache from staring at the computer screen.
examples.translation: Tengo un dolor de cabeza terrible por mirar la pantalla de la computadora.

faults.quote: Usa 'healthy' para hablar de una persona que está bien físicamente
faults.why: Merely repeats the definitions of the two senses without adding usage information.

notes: No lo confundas con el sustantivo 'health' (salud). Su comparativo es 'healthier' y su superlativo 'healthiest'.

senses.definition: De una persona, un animal o el cuerpo: que goza de buena salud y no está enfermo.

examples.text: Eating vegetables keeps you healthy.
examples.translation: Comer verduras te mantiene sano.

senses.definition: De un alimento, hábito o lugar: que es bueno o beneficioso para la salud.

examples.text: This is a very healthy snack.
examples.translation: Este es un refrigerio muy saludable.

faults.quote: /hɪər/
faults.why: Uses British IPA (/hɪər/) instead of US English (/hɪr/).

faults.quote: oír; escuchar
faults.why: Does not cover sense 1 (enterarse), and 'escuchar' contradicts the note comparing it with 'listen'.

faults.quote: oir hablar
faults.why: Missing accent mark on 'oír'.

notes: Es un verbo irregular: su pasado y participio pasado son 'heard' (/hɜrd/).
No lo confundas con 'listen' (escuchar). 'Hear' es percibir un sonido sin intentarlo; 'listen' es prestar atención voluntariamente.

senses.definition: Percibir un sonido a través de los oídos.

examples.text: I can hear someone knocking at the door.
examples.translation: Puedo oír a alguien llamando a la puerta.

senses.definition: Recibir información o noticias sobre algo o alguien.

examples.text: Did you hear the news?
examples.translation: ¿Te enteraste de las noticias?

faults.quote: Muszę płacić za zakupy kartą.
faults.why: A single payment takes perfective 'zapłacić'; imperfective 'płacić' needs a habitual or ongoing context.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is 'zapłacić' (used for a single completed payment).
Takes 'za' + accusative for what is paid for ('płacę za kawę'), the dative for the recipient ('płacę kelnerowi'), and the instrumental for the payment method ('płacę kartą').

senses.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or debts.

examples.text: Zazwyczaj płacę za zakupy kartą.
examples.translation: I usually pay for the shopping by card.

examples.text: Czy płacisz gotówką?
examples.translation: Are you paying in cash?

senses.definition: To suffer negative consequences for one's actions or mistakes.

examples.text: Będziesz za to płacić.
examples.translation: You will pay for this.

faults.quote: Liście zaczynają padać na ziemię.
faults.why: Falling leaves take 'opadać' or 'spadać' in Polish, not 'padać'.

faults.quote: This verb is imperfective, meaning it describes an ongoing action or a
faults.why: Defines what imperfective means in general instead of giving the specific aspect pairs.

corrected.shortGloss: to rain / snow; to fall; to collapse
notes: Imperfective. For weather, the perfective pair is 'spaść' ('spadł śnieg' – it snowed); for falling or collapsing, the perfective pair is 'paść' or 'upaść'.
Used alone ('Pada'), it always means 'It is raining'. For snow or hail, the noun is added: 'Pada śnieg' (It is snowing), 'Pada grad' (It is hailing).

senses.definition: Of rain, snow, or hail: to fall from the sky.

examples.text: W listopadzie często pada deszcz.
examples.translation: It often rains in November.

senses.definition: To drop to the ground, or (of light or a shadow) to fall onto a surface.

examples.text: Światło słoneczne pada na stół.
examples.translation: Sunlight falls on the table.

senses.definition: To lose strength from extreme tiredness, or (of a battery or device) to stop working.

examples.text: Po całym dniu pracy padam ze zmęczenia.
examples.translation: After a whole day of work, I am collapsing from exhaustion.

faults.quote: W tej restauracji jemy sushi pałeczki.
faults.why: Ungrammatical: means of eating requires the instrumental case 'pałeczkami', not accusative 'pałeczki'.

faults.quote: It has two very common meanings: eating utensils and drumsticks.
faults.why: Restates the senses and glosses without adding useful usage information.

notes: Plural of 'pałeczka' (a small stick or baton). In the senses 'chopsticks' and 'drumsticks', it is normally used in the plural.
To say 'with chopsticks', use the instrumental plural 'pałeczkami' without a preposition: 'jeść pałeczkami'.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks used for eating East Asian food.

examples.text: W tej restauracji jemy sushi pałeczkami.
examples.translation: In this restaurant we eat sushi with chopsticks.

senses.definition: A pair of sticks used to play drums.

examples.text: Perkusista zgubił pałeczki przed koncertem.
examples.translation: The drummer lost his drumsticks before the concert.

faults.quote: A large, decorative ceiling light fixture with many arms and bulbs.
faults.why: Dated/literary sense; everyday Polish for chandelier is 'żyrandol', not 'pająk'.

faults.quote: Note that the word is masculine and follows standard inflection patterns
faults.why: Restates the gender field without giving concrete grammar help.

notes: Masculine animate: the singular accusative matches the genitive ('Boję się tego pająka' – I'm afraid of this spider).
Do not confuse with 'pajęczyna', which is the spider's web.

senses.definition: A small eight-legged creature that spins webs to catch insects.

examples.text: W kącie pokoju siedzi duży pająk.
examples.translation: A large spider is sitting in the corner of the room.

faults.quote: Płakać is the most common way to say 'to cry' or 'to weep'.
faults.why: Restates the gloss without adding grammar or usage information.

faults.quote: It refers to the act of shedding tears due to sadness, pain,
faults.why: Repeats the definition of the first sense.
Lacks the irregular present-tense stem 'płacz-' ('płaczę', 'płaczesz') and the perfective pair.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective pair is 'zapłakać' (to burst into tears) or 'popłakać się' (to have a cry).
In the present tense, the '-k-' changes to '-cz-': 'ja płaczę' (I cry), 'ty płaczesz' (you cry), 'oni płaczą' (they cry).

senses.definition: To shed tears because of sadness, pain, or strong emotion.

examples.text: Dziecko zaczęło głośno płakać.
examples.translation: The child started to cry loudly.

senses.definition: To complain or express self-pity about a situation.

examples.text: Przestań już płakać i weź się do pracy.
examples.translation: Stop whining already and get to work.

faults.quote: It is often used with 'de', as in 'de graça'
faults.why: 'Grátis' is not used with 'de' (*de grátis is non-standard); 'de graça' uses 'graça'.

faults.quote: Something that costs no money.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('Something that...').

notes: 'Grátis' is invariable: it keeps the same form whether singular or plural, masculine or feminine. It can also be used as an adverb ('entrar grátis').
Do not say 'de grátis'; the common synonym is 'de graça' (for free).

senses.definition: Costing no money; provided without charge.

examples.text: A amostra do perfume é grátis.
examples.translation: The perfume sample is free.

examples.text: Temos entrada grátis para crianças hoje.
examples.translation: We have free admission for children today.

faults.quote: While 'hoje' usually refers to the current day, it can also
faults.why: Restates the two senses without adding usage information.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'ontem' (yesterday) or 'amanhã' (tomorrow).
faults.why: Pointless warning about unrelated words that do not look or sound alike.

notes: The initial 'h' is silent. For the sense 'nowadays', the phrase 'hoje em dia' is also very common.

senses.definition: On this present day.

examples.text: Eu vou trabalhar hoje.
examples.translation: I am going to work today.

senses.definition: In the present era; at the present time.

examples.text: Hoje, as pessoas usam mais o computador.
examples.translation: Nowadays, people use computers more.

faults.quote: by adding 'ir' + 'a' + infinitive (e.g., 'eu vou comer'
faults.why: Portuguese takes the bare infinitive ('ir' + infinitive), never 'ir a' + infinitive like Spanish.
Missing the everyday auxiliary sense 'to be going to' (near future) and greeting sense ('Como vai?').

faults.quote: To function correctly or fit well (usually referring to clothes
faults.why: Marginal sense for A2 while core senses of 'ir' are missing.

corrected.shortGloss: to go; to be going to; to do (fare)
notes: Unlike Spanish, the future construction 'ir' + infinitive never uses 'a' between the verbs: 'Eu vou comer' (I am going to eat).
Followed by 'a' (combining with articles as 'ao', 'à') or 'para' to indicate destination, and 'de' for means of transport ('ir de ônibus').
Highly irregular: present 'vou, vai, vamos, vão'; past (shared with 'ser') 'fui, foi, fomos, foram'.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.

examples.text: Eu vou ao mercado comprar pão.
examples.translation: I am going to the market to buy bread.

examples.text: Nós vamos para a praia amanhã.
examples.translation: We are going to the beach tomorrow.

senses.definition: Used before an infinitive verb to express a future action or intention.

examples.text: Vai chover hoje à tarde.
examples.translation: It is going to rain this afternoon.

senses.definition: To get along or fare in a particular way, especially in greetings.

examples.text: Oi, tudo bem? Como vai você?
examples.translation: Hi, all good? How are you doing?

faults.quote: It can mean 'already' (something completed), 'now' (at this exact moment)
faults.why: Merely repeats the glosses and definitions without adding useful grammar or usage tips.

notes: In questions, 'já' often translates to 'ever' ('Você já foi ao Brasil?' — Have you ever been to Brazil?).
With 'não' ('já não'), it means 'no longer' or 'not anymore'.

senses.definition: Before now, or earlier than expected.

examples.text: Eu já comi.
examples.translation: I have already eaten.

senses.definition: At this very moment, without delay.

examples.text: Vem aqui já!
examples.translation: Come here right now!

faults.quote: While 'jogar' is the go-to verb for sports and competitive games
faults.why: Restates the two senses instead of contrasting with 'brincar' and 'tocar' (classic learner confusion).

notes: English 'to play' splits into three verbs in Portuguese: use 'jogar' for sports and games with rules, 'brincar' for children's play or playing with toys, and 'tocar' for musical instruments.
Often used with 'fora' as 'jogar fora' (to throw away).

senses.definition: To take part in a sport, video game, or game with rules.

examples.text: Eles adoram jogar futebol no parque.
examples.translation: They love to play soccer in the park.

senses.definition: To send something through the air or drop it somewhere; to discard.

examples.text: Não jogue papel no chão.
examples.translation: Do not throw paper on the floor.

faults.quote: Se usa 'here' para indicar el lugar donde está la persona
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding usage information.

notes: Se usa sin preposición con verbos de movimiento ('come here', no 'to here').
Al ofrecer o entregar algo a alguien, se suele decir 'Here you go' o 'Here you are' (Aquí tienes).

senses.definition: En este lugar o hacia este lugar.

examples.text: Put your bag here.
examples.translation: Pon tu bolsa aquí.

examples.text: Come here, please.
examples.translation: Ven aquí, por favor.

faults.quote: Trabajo o preparación que se hace de antemano para entender mejor
faults.why: Figurative idiom 'do one's homework' is marginal for A2; school sense suffices.

faults.quote: Necesito terminar mi tarea escolar antes de poder ver la televisión.
faults.why: Calqued 'tarea escolar'; in natural Spanish one simply says 'mi tarea' or 'mis deberes'.

notes: Es un sustantivo incontable: no tiene plural (no se dice 'homeworks') ni se usa con 'a'.
Se usa con el verbo 'do' (hacer la tarea), no con 'make': 'do your homework'.

senses.definition: Trabajo que los profesores mandan a los estudiantes para hacer en casa.

examples.text: I need to finish my homework before I can watch television.
examples.translation: Necesito terminar mi tarea antes de poder ver la televisión.

faults.quote: Tenemos esperanza de que haga mejor tiempo mañana.
faults.why: Unnatural calque of the gloss; natural Spanish is 'Esperamos que haga mejor tiempo mañana'.

notes: No confundir con 'wait' (esperar físicamente a que pase el tiempo o llegue alguien): 'hope' expresa el deseo de que algo ocurra.
Para respuestas cortas, se usa 'I hope so' (Espero que sí) y 'I hope not' (Espero que no).

senses.definition: Querer que algo ocurra y creer que es posible.

examples.text: I hope you can come to my party.
examples.translation: Espero que puedas venir a mi fiesta.

examples.text: We hope for better weather tomorrow.
examples.translation: Esperamos que haga mejor tiempo mañana.

faults.quote: Estructura con patas que sirve para sostener algo, como madera
faults.why: Sawhorse sense is rare and technical for A2; usually called 'sawhorse' anyway.

faults.quote: Es un sustantivo común para el animal grande que se monta
faults.why: Pure filler that repeats the definition.

notes: Para decir 'montar a caballo', se usa 'ride a horse'.

senses.definition: Animal mamífero grande de cuatro patas que se usa para montar o tirar de carros.

examples.text: The horse runs fast in the green field.
examples.translation: El caballo corre rápido en el campo verde.

faults.quote: En inglés, el artículo 'the' se usa antes de hospital cuando
faults.why: Misleading: US English always uses 'the hospital' (unlike UK 'in hospital'), just like Spanish.

notes: La 'h' inicial sí se pronuncia, como una 'j' suave (/ˈhɑːspɪtl/).
En inglés estadounidense siempre lleva artículo ('in the hospital'), igual que en español, a diferencia del británico ('in hospital').

senses.definition: Lugar o edificio donde las personas enfermas o heridas reciben atención médica.

examples.text: The ambulance took the patient to the hospital.
examples.translation: La ambulancia llevó al paciente al hospital.

faults.quote: The color of a lemon or a sunflower.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun; should be 'Having the color of...'.

faults.quote: (health) Having a pale or unhealthy complexion.
faults.why: 'Sallow/pale' is marginal for A2; simple color sense is what learners need.

faults.quote: In addition to the color, 'amarelo' can describe someone who looks pale
faults.why: merely restates the second sense.

notes: Agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes (amarelo, amarela, amarelos, amarelas).

senses.definition: Having the color of a ripe lemon, gold, or a sunflower.

examples.text: A banana fica amarela quando está madura.
examples.translation: A banana turns yellow when it is ripe.

faults.quote: While 'amigável' describes a person or a situation, it can also describe
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already in the entry.

faults.quote: It is different from 'amigo' (friend), which is a noun.
faults.why: 'Amigo' is also very commonly used as an adjective meaning 'friendly' for people.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine singular; the plural is 'amigáveis'.

senses.definition: Kind, pleasant, and without hostility toward other people.

examples.text: Ela sempre tem uma atitude amigável com os novos colegas.
examples.translation: She always has a friendly attitude toward new colleagues.

senses.definition: Of technology or instructions: easy to use or understand.

examples.text: O novo aplicativo é bem amigável para iniciantes.
examples.translation: The new app is very user-friendly for beginners.

faults.quote: (operate) To function or operate, especially regarding machines or systems.
faults.why: 'Funcionar' is standard for machines operating; 'andar' is mostly just vehicles moving.

senses.definition: To move on foot at a normal speed.

examples.text: Eu gosto de andar pelo parque aos domingos.
examples.translation: I like to walk through the park on Sundays.

senses.definition: To travel using a vehicle, bicycle, or animal (used with 'de').

examples.text: Você sabe andar de bicicleta?
examples.translation: Do you know how to ride a bike?

senses.definition: To be in a certain state or doing something repeatedly lately.

examples.text: Ele anda muito cansado ultimamente.
examples.translation: He has been very tired lately.

faults.quote: While it often translates to 'excited', avoid confusing it with 'nervoso'
faults.why: Misses the actual A2 false friend: English 'excited' vs Portuguese 'excitado' (sexually aroused).

faults.quote: Use 'animado' to describe someone who is looking forward to something

senses.definition: Of a person: feeling happy, enthusiastic, and eager about something.

examples.text: Estou muito animado para a festa de sábado.
examples.translation: I am very excited for the party on Saturday.

senses.definition: Of a place or event: full of people, activity, and energy.

examples.text: O centro da cidade estava muito animado ontem à noite.
examples.translation: The city center was very lively last night.

faults.quote: Used for food containing chili or sharp spices, but also applied metaphorically

notes: Comes from 'pimenta' (pepper/chili). Unlike English 'hot', 'quente' in Portuguese only refers to temperature, so use 'apimentado' or 'picante' for spicy food.

senses.definition: Of food: having a strong, burning flavor from chili or pepper.

examples.text: Esta comida está muito apimentada.
examples.translation: This food is very spicy.

senses.definition: Of a joke, story, or comment: slightly suggestive or sensual.

examples.text: Ele contou uma piada meio apimentada no jantar.
examples.translation: He told a rather risqué joke at dinner.

faults.quote: /ˈkɒliːɡ/
