senses.definition: Persona con la que se trabaja, especialmente en una profesión o empresa.

examples.text: I am having lunch with a colleague.
examples.translation: Voy a almorzar con un colega.

examples.text: My colleague helped me finish the project.
examples.translation: Mi compañero de trabajo me ayudó a terminar el proyecto.

faults.why: Missing irregular past forms ('came', 'come'), essential for A2 learners.

faults.quote: venir; llegar; suceder
faults.why: 'Suceder' is not in the glosses; sense 2 actually illustrates origin ('provenir').

faults.quote: Suceder o tener su origen en algo.
faults.why: Conflates 'happen' and 'originate (come from)' in one sense.

notes: Verbo irregular: pasado 'came' (/keɪm/), participio 'come' (/kʌm/).
Indica movimiento hacia donde está el hablante o el oyente, a diferencia de 'go' (ir hacia otro lugar).

senses.definition: Moverse hacia el lugar donde está quien habla o con quien se habla.

examples.text: Come here and look at this.
examples.translation: Ven aquí y mira esto.

senses.definition: Llegar a un lugar o asistir a un evento.

examples.text: The train hasn't come yet.
examples.translation: El tren todavía no ha llegado.

examples.text: Can you come to the party tomorrow?
examples.translation: ¿Puedes venir a la fiesta mañana?

senses.definition: Tener su origen o procedencia en un lugar o cosa (con 'from').

examples.text: Where do you come from?
examples.translation: ¿De dónde eres?

faults.quote: compañía, competición
faults.why: 'Competición' means competition, completely false as a gloss for 'company'.

faults.quote: La palabra 'company' puede referirse tanto a un negocio como a la
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses without adding usage information.

faults.quote: empresa; compañía; compañía
faults.why: Duplicate word 'compañía' in shortGloss.

notes: Con el sentido de 'empresa' es contable (plural 'companies'). Con el sentido de 'estar acompañado' o 'invitados' es incontable y no lleva artículo 'a'.

senses.definition: Organización o negocio que vende productos o servicios.

examples.text: She works for a large technology company.
examples.translation: Ella trabaja para una gran empresa de tecnología.

senses.definition: Hecho de estar con otras personas, o personas invitadas en casa.

examples.text: I really enjoy your company.
examples.translation: Disfruto mucho de tu compañía.

examples.text: We're having company for dinner tonight.
examples.translation: Tenemos visitas a cenar esta noche.

faults.quote: En España se dice comúnmente 'ordenador', mientras que en gran parte de
faults.why: Explains Spanish regional vocabulary rather than how to use the English word.

senses.definition: Máquina electrónica que procesa datos y sirve para trabajar, usar internet, etc.

examples.text: I need to buy a new computer for work.
examples.translation: Necesito comprar una computadora nueva para el trabajo.

faults.quote: Cuando un alimento se vuelve comestible o cambia su estado por la
faults.why: Verb defined with 'Cuando...' instead of an infinitive verb phrase.

notes: 'Cook' es el término general para preparar comida con calor; 'bake' se usa específicamente para hornear pan, pasteles o galletas.
Como sustantivo, la persona que cocina es 'a cook' (cocinero/a), no 'cooker'.

senses.definition: Preparar alimentos aplicando calor para que estén listos para comer.

examples.text: I like to cook dinner for my family on Sundays.
examples.translation: Me gusta cocinar la cena para mi familia los domingos.

senses.definition: Dicho de un alimento: hacerse comestible por la acción del calor.

examples.text: The pasta needs ten minutes to cook properly.
examples.translation: La pasta necesita diez minutos para cocerse bien.

faults.quote: En Estados Unidos, 'yard' se usa comúnmente para referirse al terreno
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and glosses of sense 0 without contrasting it with 'garden'.

notes: En Estados Unidos, 'yard' es todo el terreno con césped que rodea una casa (como 'front yard' o 'backyard'), mientras que 'garden' se reserva para la zona donde se cultivan flores o verduras.

senses.definition: Terreno alrededor de una casa que suele tener césped, plantas o árboles.

examples.text: The children are playing in the yard.
examples.translation: Los niños están jugando en el jardín.

senses.definition: Medida de longitud que equivale a tres pies o unos noventa y un centímetros.

examples.text: The fabric is sold by the yard.
examples.translation: La tela se vende por yarda.

faults.quote: (tiempo) Período de tiempo que tarda la Tierra en dar una vuelta
faults.why: Twelve months and Earth's orbital period are one everyday meaning for an A2 learner.

notes: Para decir la edad se usa el verbo 'be' ('I am twenty years old'), nunca 'have'.
Los años del calendario suelen leerse en dos partes de dos cifras: 1995 se dice 'nineteen ninety-five'.

senses.definition: Período de doce meses, o de 365 días, que equivale al tiempo que tarda la Tierra en dar una vuelta alrededor del Sol.

examples.text: The year has twelve months.
examples.translation: El año tiene doce meses.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para colores como para describir el estado de ánimo
faults.why: Teaches an outdated slang sense ('cowardly') not in the entry and unhelpful at A2.

senses.definition: Del color del limón, la yema de huevo o el oro.

examples.text: The taxi is bright yellow.
examples.translation: El taxi es de un amarillo brillante.

faults.quote: sí; claro; ¡bien!
faults.why: Includes 'claro', which is not in any sense's glosses.

faults.quote: Se usa principalmente para responder afirmativamente a una pregunta o propuesta.
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of sense 0.

notes: En la lengua hablada informal se dice muy a menudo 'yeah' (/jæ/).

senses.definition: Expresión que se usa para dar una respuesta afirmativa o mostrar acuerdo o aceptación.

examples.text: Yes, I want a cup of coffee.
examples.translation: Sí, quiero una taza de café.

senses.definition: Expresión de entusiasmo o alegría por algo que ha salido bien.

examples.text: Yes! We won the game.
examples.translation: ¡Bien! Ganamos el partido.

faults.quote: El día que precede inmediatamente al día de hoy.
faults.why: Defines the adverb as a noun ('El día...') instead of an adverb ('En el día...').

faults.quote: Se usa para referirse al día inmediatamente anterior al de hoy.
faults.why: Restates the definition word for word.

notes: Para las partes del día se dice 'yesterday morning' (ayer por la mañana) y 'yesterday afternoon' (ayer por la tarde), pero para la noche anterior se usa 'last night' (anoche).

senses.definition: En el día inmediatamente anterior a hoy.

examples.text: I went to the store yesterday.
examples.translation: Ayer fui a la tienda.

faults.quote: Aunque 'river' siempre se refiere a un río natural, a veces
faults.why: Explains an obvious figurative use shared with Spanish; contrasts or articles are more useful.

notes: En nombres propios se suele usar con 'the': 'the Mississippi River' o 'the River Thames'. Para corrientes de agua pequeñas se usa 'stream' o 'creek' (arroyo).

senses.definition: Gran corriente natural de agua que fluye por un cauce hasta desembocar en el mar, en un lago o en otro río.

examples.text: The river flows through the valley.
examples.translation: El río fluye por el valle.

faults.quote: camino; carretera; calle
faults.why: Includes 'calle', which is absent from the sense glosses and contradicts the note.

notes: Se usa sobre todo para vías que conectan pueblos o ciudades. Para una vía urbana con edificios a los lados es más común decir 'street' (calle).

senses.definition: Vía pública hecha para que circulen vehículos entre dos lugares.

examples.text: The road to the city is very long.
examples.translation: La carretera a la ciudad es muy larga.

faults.quote: Open the sunroof of the car.
faults.why: Uses the compound word 'sunroof' instead of the headword 'roof'.
Roof of a building and roof of a car/cave are the same basic concept.

notes: En inglés se distingue entre 'roof' (la cubierta exterior de un edificio o vehículo) y 'ceiling' (el techo visto desde el interior de una habitación). Su plural es 'roofs'.

senses.definition: Cubierta exterior en la parte superior de un edificio o de un vehículo.

examples.text: The cat is sleeping on the roof.
examples.translation: El gato está durmiendo en el tejado.

examples.text: We tied the luggage to the roof of the car.
examples.translation: Atamos el equipaje al techo del coche.

faults.quote: La palabra 'room' sirve tanto para una habitación de la casa como
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the crucial countability distinction between them.

notes: Cuando significa 'habitación' es contable ('two rooms'), pero cuando significa 'espacio disponible' es incontable y se usa sin 'a' ni plural ('There is no room').

senses.definition: Parte interior de una casa o edificio separada por paredes.

examples.text: My room is on the second floor.
examples.translation: Mi habitación está en el segundo piso.

senses.definition: Espacio disponible para que quepa algo o alguien.

examples.text: There is no room in the car for more bags.
examples.translation: No hay espacio en el coche para más maletas.

faults.quote: Dicho de una cosa, hecha con poca maña, tosca o sin pulir.
faults.why: Sense 1 ('crudely made') is literary/archaic and unsuitable for an A2 learner.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para el comportamiento maleducado como para describir algo tosco
faults.why: Restates the senses (including the marginal one) instead of giving usage grammar.

notes: Para indicar a quién se dirige la falta de respeto, se usa con la preposición 'to': 'Don't be rude to your mother'.

senses.definition: Que muestra mala educación o falta de respeto hacia los demás.

examples.text: It was rude of him to leave without saying goodbye.
examples.translation: Fue grosero de su parte irse sin decir adiós.

faults.quote: (observe) To observe or watch something over a period of time.
faults.why: Looking at and watching with إِلَى are shades of one meaning; watching TV is شَاهَدَ.
Missing the common sense 'to look into, examine, consider' (used with فِي).

faults.quote: /naˈðˤa.ra/
faults.why: In MSA, 3-syllable words with three light syllables stress the first syllable: /ˈna.ðˤa.ra/.

notes: Takes the preposition إِلَى (ilā) to mean 'to look at', and فِي (fī) to mean 'to look into / consider'.
Imperfect form: يَنْظُرُ (yanẓuru). Do not confuse with رَأَى (raʾā, 'to see') or شَاهَدَ (šāhada, 'to watch').

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something.

examples.text: نَظَرَ الطَّالِبُ إِلَى السَّبُّورَةِ.
examples.translation: The student looked at the board.

senses.definition: To examine or think carefully about a matter or issue.

examples.text: سَنَنْظُرُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمُشْكِلَةِ غَدًا.
examples.translation: We will look into this problem tomorrow.

faults.quote: /it.tˤa.sˤa.la/
faults.why: The geminate /t/ in اتَّصَلَ (from و-ص-ل) is plain /t/, not emphatic /tˤ/.

faults.quote: To join two things together or to be physically linked.
faults.why: اتَّصَلَ is intransitive ('to be connected'); it does not mean 'to join two things together'.

faults.quote: This verb is also used for physical connections, like two wires
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 instead of noting that بِ (bi-) is required in all senses.

corrected.shortGloss: to call; to contact; to connect
notes: Always takes the preposition بِـ (bi-) before the person or thing contacted or connected to.

senses.definition: To contact someone, especially by telephone.

examples.text: اتَّصَلْتُ بِصَدِيقِي أَمْسِ.
examples.translation: I called my friend yesterday.

senses.definition: To be linked or joined to something else, such as a room or a network.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الْغُرْفَةُ تَتَّصِلُ بِالْمَطْبَخِ مُبَاشَرَةً.
examples.translation: This room connects directly to the kitchen.

faults.quote: (planning) To consider an action or to plan for something.
faults.why: Thinking about something and considering an action with فِي are the same sense.

faults.quote: To use your mind to process thoughts, form ideas, or have an opinion.
faults.why: فَكَّرَ does not mean 'to have an opinion' (that is رَأَى or اعْتَقَدَ).

faults.quote: /fakˈkara/
faults.why: Stress falls on the heavy first syllable /ˈfak.ka.ra/, not the second.

notes: Takes the preposition فِي (fī) or بِـ (bi-) to mean 'to think about' or 'to consider'.
Refers to the mental process of thinking or pondering. For 'to think that' (holding an opinion), use اعْتَقَدَ (iʿtaqada) or ظَنَّ (ẓanna).

senses.definition: To use your mind to reflect on something or consider a possibility.

examples.text: أُفَكِّرُ فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ.
examples.translation: I am thinking about the future.

examples.text: فَكَّرْتُ فِي السَّفَرِ إِلَى الْخَارِجِ.
examples.translation: I thought about traveling abroad.

faults.quote: This verb is used for picking one item or option
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition; a note on its hollow conjugation is needed instead.

notes: A Form VIII hollow verb (from the root خ-ي-ر): the long vowel shortens before consonant suffixes, e.g., اخْتَرْتُ (ixtartu, 'I chose'), while the imperfect keeps ā: يَخْتَارُ (yaxtāru).

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want out of several options.

examples.text: اخْتَارَ الطَّالِبُ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا.
examples.translation: The student chose a new book.

examples.text: يَجِبُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَخْتَارَ لَوْنًا لِلْغُرْفَةِ.
examples.translation: You must choose a color for the room.

faults.quote: Used specifically for creating visual art with tools like pencils or brushes.
faults.why: Restates the definition directly; imperfect vowel (يَرْسُمُ) is much more useful for a Form I verb.

faults.quote: to draw; to paint
faults.why: 'to paint' is in shortGloss and the definition ('brush'), but missing from the sense's glosses.

notes: Imperfect form: يَرْسُمُ (yarsumu).
Do not confuse with صَوَّرَ (ṣawwara), which means 'to photograph' or 'to film'.

senses.definition: To make a picture or design using a pencil, pen, or brush.

examples.text: رَسَمَ الطِّفْلُ قِطَّةً عَلَى الْوَرَقَةِ.
examples.translation: The child drew a cat on the paper.

faults.quote: Note the difference between 'chegar' and 'ir' (to go).
faults.why: Explains the obvious difference between 'arrive' and 'go'.

faults.quote: When using 'chegar', use the preposition 'a' to indicate where you arrived
faults.why: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, 'chegar em' is far more common than 'chegar a'.
Should mention the very common imperative 'Chega!' ('Enough! / Stop!').

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive; to reach; to be enough
notes: For arriving at a destination, 'chegar em' is standard in everyday Brazilian speech (chegar em casa), while 'chegar a' is preferred in formal writing.
In the 1st person singular preterite, 'g' becomes 'gu' before '-ei': eu cheguei.
The command 'Chega!' is very common for 'That's enough!' or 'Stop it!'.

senses.definition: To come to a place, time, or point.

examples.text: Eu vou chegar em casa às seis.
examples.translation: I will get home at six.

senses.definition: To be as much as is needed.

examples.text: Dois ovos chegam para a receita.
examples.translation: Two eggs are enough for the recipe.

faults.quote: Use 'cheio' when a container cannot hold anything more.
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the two senses.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'farto', which is specifically about being
faults.why: 'Farto' is not a common point of confusion in Brazilian Portuguese; 'cheio de' is needed.

notes: Followed by 'de' to say what something is full of (cheio de gente). In informal speech, 'estar cheio de' also means 'to be fed up with'.

senses.definition: Containing as much as is possible; having no empty space.

examples.text: O copo está cheio de água.
examples.translation: The glass is full of water.

senses.definition: Of a place or schedule: having many people or things in it.

examples.text: O restaurante está muito cheio hoje.
examples.translation: The restaurant is very crowded today.

faults.quote: Consegui cheirar o bolo assando no forno.
faults.why: 'Cheirar' as a transitive verb means to deliberately sniff; involuntary smelling is 'sentir o cheiro'.

notes: As a transitive verb, 'cheirar' means to actively sniff something. To say you smell something passively, use 'sentir o cheiro de' (Senti o cheiro do bolo).
To say what something smells like, use 'cheirar a' (Isto cheira a alho).

senses.definition: To breathe in through the nose to notice a scent.

examples.text: Ela cheirou a flor no jardim.
examples.translation: She smelled the flower in the garden.

senses.definition: To give off a particular scent or odor.

examples.text: Estas flores cheiram muito bem.
examples.translation: These flowers smell very good.

faults.quote: While 'chorar' is the direct translation of 'to cry', it is
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definitions and glosses.

faults.quote: to cry; to weep
faults.why: Does not cover the second sense ('to whine').

corrected.shortGloss: to cry; to weep; to whine
notes: Takes 'por' or 'de' for the cause of crying (chorar de alegria — to cry for joy). In informal Brazilian Portuguese, 'chorar' can also mean to haggle for a discount.

senses.definition: To shed tears because of sadness, pain, or strong emotion.

examples.text: O bebê começou a chorar de fome.
examples.translation: The baby started to cry from hunger.

senses.definition: To complain or plead in a needy or annoying way.

examples.text: Não adianta chorar, eu não vou mudar de ideia.
examples.translation: There is no use whining, I am not going to change my mind.

faults.quote: Colocar is slightly more formal than pôr.
faults.why: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'colocar' is extremely common in everyday speech and is completely neutral.

faults.quote: put on, wear
faults.why: 'Colocar' denotes the action of putting clothes on, not the state of wearing them.

faults.quote: Use colocar when you are physically placing an object in a specific
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0.

corrected.shortGloss: to put; to place; to put on
notes: In Brazil, 'colocar' and 'botar' (more informal) are often preferred in speech over 'pôr' because they have regular conjugations.
In the 1st person singular preterite, 'c' changes to 'qu' before '-ei': eu coloquei.

senses.definition: To move something into a particular place or position.

examples.text: Preciso colocar os livros na prateleira.
examples.translation: I need to put the books on the shelf.

senses.definition: To dress oneself in a piece of clothing or an accessory.

examples.text: Vou colocar meu casaco porque está frio.
examples.translation: I am going to put on my coat because it is cold.

faults.quote: (believe) To believe or trust that something will happen.
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the same meaning ('to hope') split by grammar (ότι vs να).

faults.quote: to hope; to expect
faults.why: Includes 'to expect', which is absent from the senses' glosses.

faults.quote: Used to express that you want something to be true
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving the aorist stem (έλπισα).

notes: Followed by 'να' + subjunctive (e.g., ελπίζω να έρθεις), 'ότι/πως' + indicative, or 'σε' + noun (to place hope in).
Simple past (aorist): έλπισα.

senses.definition: To want something to happen or be true, and think that it is possible.

examples.text: Ελπίζω ότι θα έρθεις αύριο.
examples.translation: I hope that you will come tomorrow.

examples.text: Ελπίζω να έχουμε καλό καιρό στις διακοπές.
examples.translation: I hope we have good weather on vacation.

faults.why: Missing the essential A1 sense 'to call / name' (Πώς σε λένε;).
Missing the highly irregular aorist 'είπα' and subjunctive 'να πω'.

faults.quote: Αυτή η λέξη τι λέει;
faults.why: Unnatural Greek for 'What does this word mean?'; 'λέω' for meaning is used as 'Τι θα πει...;' or 'Πώς το λες αυτό;'.

corrected.shortGloss: to say; to tell; to call
notes: Highly irregular in the simple past (aorist): είπα, and simple subjunctive: να πω (imperative: πες).
In the present tense, short forms without 'γ' are standard in speech: λέω, λες, λέει, λέμε, λέτε, λένε (also λέγω, λέγεις, etc.).
Do not confuse with 'μιλώ' (to speak/talk). Use 'λέω' when stating what is said or told, and 'μιλώ' for the act of talking or speaking a language.

senses.definition: To express something in words, or to give information to someone.

examples.text: Τι λες;
examples.translation: What are you saying?

examples.text: Μου είπε την αλήθεια.
examples.translation: He told me the truth.

senses.definition: To use a particular name for someone or something.

examples.text: Πώς σε λένε; — Με λένε Μαρία.
examples.translation: What do they call you? (What is your name?) — My name is Maria.

senses.definition: To suggest an idea or ask someone's opinion about a plan.

examples.text: Τι λες να πάμε για καφέ;
examples.translation: What do you say we go for a coffee?

senses.definition: To intend to convey a particular meaning (especially in 'τι θα πει' = what does it mean).

examples.text: Τι θα πει αυτή η λέξη;
examples.translation: What does this word mean?

faults.quote: (transport) To transport large quantities of things or people
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the same core meaning applied to people vs vehicles.

faults.quote: Use κουβαλώ when you are physically carrying something
faults.why: Repeats the definition while omitting the common form 'κουβαλάω' and aorist 'κουβάλησα'.

corrected.shortGloss: to carry; to lug; to transport
notes: Also very commonly used in the uncontracted form 'κουβαλάω' in everyday speech. Simple past (aorist): κουβάλησα.
Unlike 'φέρνω' (to bring), which focuses on delivering something somewhere, 'κουβαλώ' emphasizes the physical effort of carrying or hauling.

senses.definition: To carry or move something or someone from one place to another, especially when it is heavy or takes effort.

examples.text: Κουβαλάω τις τσάντες από το σούπερ μάρκετ.
examples.translation: I am carrying the bags from the supermarket.

examples.text: Τα φορτηγά κουβαλάνε υλικά για την οικοδομή.
examples.translation: The trucks are transporting materials for the construction site.

faults.quote: It is conjugated as a -ώ verb in the present tense.
faults.why: Vague and unhelpful (-ώ has two conjugation classes); should give 'ξυπνάω' and aorist 'ξύπνησα'.

corrected.shortGloss: to wake up; to wake someone up
notes: Used both intransitively (to wake up) and transitively (to wake someone else up).
Also very commonly 'ξυπνάω' in the present tense (ξυπνάω, ξυπνάς, ξυπνάει...). Simple past (aorist): ξύπνησα.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping and become awake.

examples.text: Ξυπνώ νωρίς κάθε πρωί.
examples.translation: I wake up early every morning.

senses.definition: To cause someone to stop sleeping.

examples.text: Μην τον ξυπνάς ακόμα, είναι κουρασμένος.
examples.translation: Do not wake him up yet, he is tired.

faults.quote: This verb is highly versatile. Use it for physical arrival
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses instead of giving the aorist 'έφτασα' and preposition 'σε'.

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive; to reach; to be enough
notes: Simple past (aorist): έφτασα. When meaning 'to arrive at', it is followed by 'σε' (στο, στη, στον...).
In the meaning 'to be enough', it is mostly used in the 3rd person: φτάνει (singular) or φτάνουν (plural). 'Φτάνει!' alone means 'Enough! / Stop it!'.

senses.definition: To get to a place, especially at the end of a journey.

examples.text: Θα φτάσουμε στο χωριό πριν νυχτώσει.
examples.translation: We will reach the village before it gets dark.

senses.definition: To be as much or as many as needed.

examples.text: Τα χρήματα που έχω δεν φτάνουν για το εισιτήριο.
examples.translation: The money I have is not enough for the ticket.

faults.why: Missing everyday sense 'to fail to do something unintentionally' (forget to do).

faults.quote: olvidar; dejar atrás
faults.why: 'dejar atrás' is not in the glosses; 'olvidar; dejarse' fits better.

notes: Es un verbo irregular: el pasado es 'forgot' y el participio es 'forgotten'.

senses.definition: Dejar de tener en la memoria información o un hecho.

examples.text: I always forget where I put my keys.
examples.translation: Siempre olvido dónde pongo mis llaves.

senses.definition: No hacer algo por descuido o falta de memoria.

examples.text: Don't forget to lock the door.
examples.translation: No te olvides de cerrar la puerta con llave.

senses.definition: Dejar algo en un lugar sin intención.

examples.text: Don't forget your umbrella before you leave.
examples.translation: No te dejes el paraguas antes de salir.

faults.quote: No confundir con 'spoon' (cuchara) o 'knife' (cuchillo).
faults.why: Filler note; learners do not confuse the word 'fork' with 'spoon' or 'knife'.

senses.definition: Utensilio de mesa con un mango y puntas que se usa para pinchar los alimentos.

examples.text: We need another knife and fork.
examples.translation: Necesitamos otro cuchillo y tenedor.

senses.definition: Lugar donde un camino o río se divide en dos partes.

examples.text: Take the left turn at the fork in the road.
examples.translation: Gira a la izquierda en la bifurcación del camino.

faults.why: Missing fundamental sense 'not a prisoner or under control; having liberty'.

faults.quote: La palabra «free» tiene varios significados muy comunes: puede indicar que algo
faults.why: Note merely restates the senses and glosses.
Senses 1 (person not busy) and 2 (seat not in use) both mean available/unoccupied.

notes: En español «free» corresponde tanto a «gratis» (sin costo) como a «libre» (con libertad o disponible).

senses.definition: Que no cuesta dinero.

examples.text: Museum entry is free on Tuesdays.
examples.translation: La entrada al museo es gratis los martes.

senses.definition: De una persona, tiempo o cosa: que no está ocupado ni en uso.

examples.text: Are you free this evening?
examples.translation: ¿Estás libre esta tarde?

examples.text: Is this seat free?
examples.translation: ¿Está libre este asiento?

senses.definition: Que no está prisionero, encerrado ni bajo el control de otros.

examples.text: They let the birds go free.
examples.translation: Dejaron libres a los pájaros.

faults.quote: neutral
faults.why: 'fridge' is informal/colloquial shortening of 'refrigerator'.

faults.quote: En el inglés británico también se usa a veces la abreviatura 'fridge'
faults.why: Misleading: 'fridge' is the main everyday word in UK, not just 'used sometimes'.

notes: Es la forma abreviada y cotidiana de «refrigerator». Nótese que se escribe con «d», a diferencia de la palabra completa.

senses.definition: Electrodoméstico que se usa para conservar fríos los alimentos y las bebidas.

examples.text: Put the milk back in the fridge, please.
examples.translation: Guarda la leche en el refrigerador, por favor.

faults.quote: Se usa para describir a alguien que actúa con valor
faults.why: Merely restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Se aplica tanto a personas ('a brave firefighter') como a sus acciones o decisiones ('a brave choice').

senses.definition: Que muestra valor ante el peligro, el dolor o las dificultades.

examples.text: It was a brave decision to speak the truth.
examples.translation: Fue una decisión valiente decir la verdad.

faults.quote: Let us take a break for lunch.
faults.why: Uses 'break' as a noun ('a break') in a verb entry; also stiff ('Let us').
Missing the essential everyday sense of a machine/device stopping working (averiarse).

faults.quote: El verbo 'break' es muy común y tiene muchos significados
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving the needed irregular forms (broke, broken).

notes: Es un verbo irregular: pasado 'broke' (/broʊk/), participio 'broken' (/ˈbroʊkən/).
No confundir con 'brake', que suena igual pero significa frenar o el freno.

senses.definition: Hacer que algo se divida en pedazos o que un hueso se fracture, o dividirse así.

examples.text: Be careful not to break the glass.
examples.translation: Ten cuidado de no romper el vaso.

senses.definition: Dicho de una máquina o aparato: dejar de funcionar por un daño.

examples.text: My phone broke yesterday, so I can't call you.
examples.translation: Mi teléfono se averió ayer, así que no puedo llamarte.

senses.definition: No cumplir una ley, una regla o una promesa.

examples.text: You should never break a promise.
examples.translation: Nunca debes romper una promesa.

senses.definition: Interrumpir una actividad para hacer una pausa breve.

examples.text: Let's break for lunch and continue at two.
examples.translation: Hagamos una pausa para almorzar y continuemos a las dos.

faults.quote: como verbo para indicar que se está tomando esa comida (to have breakfast).
faults.why: Claims 'to have breakfast' uses 'breakfast' as a verb; misses the needed article note.

notes: Generalmente se usa sin artículo: 'have breakfast' (desayunar), 'at breakfast' (en el desayuno), 'for breakfast' (de desayuno).

senses.definition: La primera comida del día, que se toma por la mañana.

examples.text: I like to eat eggs and toast for breakfast.
examples.translation: Me gusta comer huevos y tostadas en el desayuno.

faults.quote: Aunque 'bridge' se refiere principalmente a construcciones físicas, también se usa
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

senses.definition: Estructura construida sobre un río, un camino o un vacío para permitir el paso de un lado a otro.

examples.text: The bridge crosses the wide river.
examples.translation: El puente cruza el río ancho.

senses.definition: Algo que conecta o sirve como enlace entre dos situaciones, grupos o ideas distintas.

examples.text: This program acts as a bridge between the two communities.
examples.translation: Este programa actúa como un puente entre las dos comunidades.

faults.quote: to pull; to draw; to attract
faults.why: Lists 'to draw' and 'to attract', which are not in the senses, and omits 'take after'.

faults.quote: In Brazilian Portuguese, it is also used colloquially to mean 'to resemble'
faults.why: Repeats sense 1, which is already in the entry.
Should warn learners that 'Pull' on doors is a false friend for 'puxar' (which means pull).

notes: False friend on doors: 'puxar' means 'to pull' (its opposite is 'empurrar', 'to push').
In the sense 'to take after', it is used both directly ('puxou o pai') and with 'a' ('puxou ao pai').

senses.definition: To apply force to something to move it towards you.

examples.text: Preciso puxar a porta para abri-la.
examples.translation: I need to pull the door to open it.

senses.definition: To resemble a relative in appearance or character.

examples.text: Ele puxou o pai.
examples.translation: He takes after his father.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense of breaking a rule, promise, or record.

faults.quote: Use 'quebrar' for physical objects like plates, glass, or bones.
faults.why: Merely restates the definitions of the senses.

notes: Used both transitively ('Quebrei o copo' — I broke the glass) and intransitively ('O copo quebrou' — The glass broke).
Do not confuse with 'romper', which implies tearing, snapping, or severing (like a rope, a relationship, or a contract).

senses.definition: To separate into pieces, fracture, or stop working from damage.

examples.text: Não deixe o prato cair, ele vai quebrar.
examples.translation: Don't let the plate fall, it will break.

examples.text: O meu celular quebrou ontem.
examples.translation: My cell phone broke yesterday.

senses.definition: To fail to keep a rule, promise, or agreement, or to beat a record.

examples.text: Ele nunca quebra uma promessa.
examples.translation: He never breaks a promise.

senses.definition: To go out of business or lose all one's money.

examples.text: A loja quase quebrou durante a crise.
examples.translation: The shop almost went bankrupt during the crisis.

faults.why: Hot objects and hot weather are the same basic meaning of 'quente'.

faults.quote: Unlike English, where you might distinguish between 'hot' and 'warm' quite strictly
faults.why: Misleading: Portuguese uses 'morno' for warm/lukewarm liquids and objects.

faults.quote: Today is a quite hot day.
faults.why: Unnatural English word order ('a quite hot day' instead of 'quite a hot day').

notes: For weather and clothing, 'quente' covers both 'hot' and pleasantly 'warm'; for lukewarm food or water, use 'morno'.
Do not confuse with the noun 'calor' (heat): say 'O dia está quente' (The day is hot), but 'Estou com calor' (I am/feel hot).

senses.definition: Having a high temperature; hot or warm.

examples.text: O café está muito quente agora.
examples.translation: The coffee is very hot right now.

examples.text: Hoje está um dia bastante quente.
examples.translation: Today is quite a hot day.

faults.quote: When used to mean 'to love', it is often applied to friends and family
faults.why: Confuses Portuguese with Spanish 'querer'; in Portuguese it requires 'bem' ('querer bem') and is marginal at A2.

faults.quote: To have feelings of affection or love for someone.
faults.why: Literary/fixed expression ('querer bem'); not an everyday standalone A2 sense in Brazil.

faults.quote: to want; to love
faults.why: Includes 'to love', which misleads learners into using 'querer' like Spanish 'Te quiero'.

notes: Irregular in the present (eu quero, ele quer) and preterite (eu quis, ele quis).
To make a polite request ('I would like'), use the imperfect 'Eu queria...' or 'Eu gostaria de...'.
With 'dizer', 'querer dizer' means 'to mean' (e.g., 'O que isso quer dizer?' — What does this mean?).

senses.definition: To feel a desire for something or to wish to do something.

examples.text: Eu quero um café bem quente.
examples.translation: I want a very hot coffee.

examples.text: Ele quer aprender a falar português.
examples.translation: He wants to learn to speak Portuguese.

faults.quote: In Portuguese, 'rápido' is used as an adjective, while 'rapidamente' is the adverb.
faults.why: Contradicts itself in the next sentence; 'rápido' is the standard everyday adverb ('fast/quickly') too.

notes: Also used invariable as an adverb meaning 'fast' or 'quickly' (e.g., 'Ela fala muito rápido' — She speaks very fast), which is much more common in everyday speech than 'rapidamente'.

senses.definition: Moving or able to move at high speed.

examples.text: Ele é um atleta muito rápido.
examples.translation: He is a very fast athlete.

examples.text: O trem é muito rápido.
examples.translation: The train is very fast.

senses.definition: Done or happening in a short time.

examples.text: Preciso de uma resposta rápida.
examples.translation: I need a quick answer.

faults.quote: na górě - at the top / upstairs
faults.why: Uses Czech character 'ě' instead of Polish 'rz' ('na górze').

faults.quote: A very high hill, standing prominently above the surrounding land.
faults.why: Shades of the same landform meaning as sense 0; 'high hill' is unnatural.

faults.quote: We walked up to the green high hill
faults.why: Unnatural English ('green high hill').

notes: Notice how 'góra' means both a mountain and the top or upper part of something (e.g., 'na górze' – at the top / upstairs, 'do góry' – upwards). In the plural, 'góry' often refers to a mountain range (e.g., 'jechać w góry' – to go to the mountains).

senses.definition: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface; a mountain or large hill.

examples.text: Ta góra jest bardzo wysoka i trudna do zdobycia.
examples.translation: This mountain is very high and difficult to climb.

senses.definition: The highest part, surface, or upper floor of something.

examples.text: Książka leży na górze szafki.
examples.translation: The book is lying on top of the cabinet.

faults.quote: Characterized by high air temperature; describing the weather.
faults.why: Hot objects and hot weather are the same literal temperature sense.

faults.quote: When describing food or liquid, 'gorący' implies it could burn you
faults.why: Repeats note 0 and the example in sense 0.

notes: Distinguish 'gorący' (hot) from 'ciepły' (warm). For weather, 'upalny' (scorching/sweltering) is also common for very hot days.

senses.definition: Having a high temperature; very warm to the touch or of the weather.

examples.text: Uważaj, herbata jest bardzo gorąca.
examples.translation: Be careful, the tea is very hot.

examples.text: To był wyjątkowo gorący dzień.
examples.translation: It was an exceptionally hot day.

senses.definition: Of feelings, wishes, or a welcome: full of strong emotion, enthusiasm, or affection.

examples.text: Dziękujemy za gorące przyjęcie.
examples.translation: Thank you for the warm welcome.

faults.quote: Used both for a medical fever and figuratively for intense excitement
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses without adding usage information.

senses.definition: A body temperature higher than normal, usually caused by illness.

examples.text: Mam wysoką gorączkę i muszę zostać w łóżku.
examples.translation: I have a high fever and must stay in bed.

senses.definition: A state of intense excitement, nervous energy, or hurried activity.

examples.text: W sklepach panuje już przedświąteczna gorączka.
examples.translation: There is already a pre-holiday rush in the shops.

faults.quote: Kto to jest za gość?
faults.why: Ungrammatical blend of 'Kto to jest?' and 'Co to za gość?'.

notes: The plural form is irregular: 'goście' (nominative) and 'gości' (genitive/accusative). In Polish, the idiomatic phrase 'mamy gości' (we have guests) uses the accusative form 'gości'.

senses.definition: A person invited to visit someone's home or attend an event, or staying at a hotel.

examples.text: Mamy dzisiaj gości na kolacji.
examples.translation: We have guests for dinner today.

senses.definition: An informal way to refer to a man.

examples.text: Co to za gość?
examples.translation: Who is that guy?

faults.quote: No lo confundas con 'bad', que se refiere principalmente a una calidad moral
faults.why: False claim: 'bad' is constantly used for general low quality, not mainly moral quality.

notes: Cuando significa 'digno de lástima' (como en 'poor thing!'), siempre va delante del sustantivo, nunca después del verbo 'be'.
El grupo 'the poor' (con artículo y sin sustantivo) es plural y significa 'los pobres' en general.

senses.definition: Que tiene poco dinero o pocos recursos para vivir.

examples.text: Many people in the city are very poor.
examples.translation: Muchas personas en la ciudad son muy pobres.

senses.definition: De baja calidad, o que no alcanza el nivel necesario.

examples.text: The service at the restaurant was very poor.
examples.translation: El servicio en el restaurante fue muy malo.

senses.definition: Que despierta compasión o lástima por estar en una situación difícil.

examples.text: You poor thing, let me help you.
examples.translation: Pobrecito, déjame ayudarte.

faults.quote: en otros países de habla inglesa a veces se prefiere 'mail centre'
faults.why: False: 'post office' is standard across the English-speaking world; 'mail centre' is a sorting facility.

notes: No lo confundas con 'mailbox' (buzón), que es la caja donde se depositan o reciben las cartas.

senses.definition: Lugar público donde se compran sellos y se envían o recogen cartas y paquetes.

examples.text: I need to go to the post office to mail this package.
examples.translation: Necesito ir a la oficina de correos para enviar este paquete.

faults.quote: En España se dice 'patata', mientras que en la mayor parte
faults.why: Explains Spanish dialectology to a Spanish speaker instead of how the English word works.
Missing irregular plural spelling 'potatoes' with '-es'.

notes: Su plural es irregular en la escritura: se añade '-es' ('potatoes').

senses.definition: Tubérculo comestible redondeado que crece bajo tierra, de piel marrón o rojiza y pulpa blanca o amarilla.

examples.text: I like to eat a baked potato with butter.
examples.translation: Me gusta comer una papa asada con mantequilla.

faults.quote: Sentirse muy satisfecho por algo que tú o alguien cercano
faults.why: Adjective defined as an infinitive verb phrase ('Sentirse...') instead of a quality ('Que se siente...').

faults.quote: Tener un gran sentido de dignidad o amor propio.
faults.why: Adjective defined as an infinitive verb phrase ('Tener...') instead of a quality ('Que tiene...').

notes: Se usa con la preposición 'of' ('proud of someone/something') o seguido de 'to' + infinitivo ('proud to be here').
En inglés, 'proud' suele ser una cualidad positiva (sentirse satisfecho), a diferencia de 'arrogant' (arrogante).

senses.definition: Que se siente muy satisfecho por algo bueno que uno mismo o alguien cercano ha hecho o logrado.

examples.text: I am so proud of your hard work.
examples.translation: Estoy muy orgulloso de tu arduo trabajo.

senses.definition: Que tiene un gran sentido de la dignidad o del amor propio.

examples.text: She is a proud woman who never asks for help.
examples.translation: Es una mujer orgullosa que nunca pide ayuda.

faults.quote: In Polish, 'ostry' covers both the physical sharpness of an object
faults.why: Merely restates the senses already shown in the entry.

notes: To describe a person who is mentally 'sharp' or quick-witted, use 'bystry' rather than 'ostry'.

senses.definition: Having a thin edge or point that can cut or pierce something.

examples.text: Muszę naostrzyć ten nóż, bo nie jest wystarczająco ostry.
examples.translation: I have to sharpen this knife, because it is not sharp enough.

senses.definition: Having a strong, burning taste, like chilli or horseradish.

examples.text: Bardzo lubię ostry sos do pizzy.
examples.translation: I really like spicy pizza sauce.

senses.definition: Intense, sudden, or severe in degree or effect.

examples.text: Poczułem ostry ból w kolanie.
examples.translation: I felt a sharp pain in my knee.

faults.quote: to open; to turn on
faults.why: 'To turn on' is absent from the senses and is not a standard meaning.

faults.quote: Sklep otwiera o ósmej rano.
faults.why: Intransitive 'opens' requires the reflexive 'otwiera się' in Polish; 'otwiera' is transitive.

notes: Imperfective verb; its perfective pair is 'otworzyć'.
It is transitive (takes an object in the accusative case). When something opens by itself or a shop opens for the day, use the reflexive 'otwierać się'.

senses.definition: To move something so that it is no longer shut, or to unfasten a container.

examples.text: Zawsze otwieram okno rano, żeby wpuścić świeże powietrze.
examples.translation: I always open the window in the morning to let in fresh air.

senses.definition: To start a business, shop, bank account, or computer file.

examples.text: W przyszłym miesiącu otwierają tu nową restaurację.
examples.translation: Next month they are opening a new restaurant here.

faults.quote: Owca is a feminine noun.
faults.why: Restates the gender field; could more concisely note irregular genitive plural 'owiec' and 'baran'.

notes: Refers to sheep in general or specifically a female sheep; a male sheep (ram) is 'baran'. Note the irregular genitive plural 'owiec'.

senses.definition: A farm animal with thick wool, raised for its fleece, meat, and milk.

examples.text: Na łące pasła się owca.
examples.translation: A sheep was grazing in the meadow.

faults.quote: While 'owoc' is the direct equivalent of 'fruit', it is also used metaphorically
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Unlike English uncountable 'fruit', Polish 'owoc' is countable: use singular 'owoc' for one piece of fruit, and the plural 'owoce' when talking about fruit in general.

senses.definition: The sweet, fleshy part of a plant that contains seeds and is eaten as food.

examples.text: Muszę kupić świeże owoce na deser.
examples.translation: I need to buy fresh fruit for dessert.

senses.definition: A positive outcome or result of effort or work.

examples.text: To są owoce naszej ciężkiej pracy.
examples.translation: These are the fruits of our hard work.

faults.quote: In Polish, 'łóżko' is used for the physical piece of furniture; use the verb 'spać'
faults.why: Pointless filler note; no learner confuses the noun 'bed' with the verb 'to sleep'.

notes: The diminutive 'łóżeczko' is the standard word for a baby's crib or cot.
Note the vowel change in the genitive plural: 'łóżek'.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for sleeping on.

examples.text: Muszę kupić nowe łóżko do sypialni.
examples.translation: I need to buy a new bed for the bedroom.

faults.quote: sediento; con muchas ganas
faults.why: Names a figurative sense ('con muchas ganas') not present in the senses.

faults.quote: Se usa para indicar que necesitas beber algo.
faults.why: Restates the definition instead of giving useful grammar/usage contrast with Spanish.

notes: En inglés se usa con el verbo 'be' ('I am thirsty'), mientras que en español se usa 'tener sed' (no digas 'I have thirst').

senses.definition: Que siente la necesidad de beber.

examples.text: I am very thirsty after running outside.
examples.translation: Tengo mucha sed después de correr afuera.

faults.why: Missing the irregular past tense ('threw') and past participle ('thrown').

faults.quote: Hacer caer a alguien al suelo con violencia o fuerza.
faults.why: Throwing someone/something to the ground is just a sub-case of sense 0.

notes: Verbo irregular: pasado 'threw' (/θruː/), participio 'thrown' (/θroʊn/).
A diferencia de 'drop' (dejar caer algo), 'throw' implica impulsar el objeto con fuerza por el aire.

senses.definition: Impulsar algo con la mano o con fuerza para que se mueva por el aire o caiga.

examples.text: Throw the ball to me, please.
examples.translation: Lánzame la pelota, por favor.

senses.definition: Organizar o dar una fiesta o celebración.

examples.text: We want to throw a party for her birthday.
examples.translation: Queremos organizar una fiesta para su cumpleaños.

faults.quote: mientras que 'tíquet' o 'boleto' son más habituales para transporte.
faults.why: Confuses English and Spanish words, falsely claiming English uses 'tíquet' or 'boleto'.

notes: Abarca tanto billetes de transporte ('train ticket') como entradas a espectáculos ('concert ticket') y multas de tráfico ('speeding ticket'). No debe confundirse con el recibo de compra, que en inglés se llama 'receipt'.

senses.definition: Documento o comprobante que permite viajar en un transporte o entrar a un espectáculo.

examples.text: I bought a ticket for the train.
examples.translation: Compré un boleto para el tren.

senses.definition: Aviso oficial de que se ha cometido una infracción de tráfico y se debe pagar una sanción.

examples.text: The officer gave me a speeding ticket.
examples.translation: El oficial me puso una multa por exceso de velocidad.

faults.quote: Se usa para indicar falta de energía o sueño, pero también para
faults.why: Merely repeats the two definitions instead of explaining the preposition 'of' for sense 2.

notes: En el sentido de estar harto o aburrido de algo, va seguido de la preposición 'of' + sustantivo o verbo en '-ing' ('tired of waiting').

senses.definition: Que necesita descansar o dormir porque le falta energía.

examples.text: I was so tired after work that I went straight to bed.
examples.translation: Estaba tan cansado después del trabajo que me fui directo a la cama.

senses.definition: Que siente fastidio o aburrimiento por algo que se repite demasiado.

examples.text: I am tired of listening to the same complaints every day.
examples.translation: Estoy harto de escuchar las mismas quejas todos los días.

faults.quote: 'today' se refiere específicamente a las horas del día.
faults.why: False: 'today' refers to the whole current day; 'tonight' is used specifically for the evening/night.

notes: También puede funcionar como sustantivo ('Today is Monday'). Para referirse a la noche del día de hoy, se suele usar 'tonight' ('esta noche') en lugar de 'today at night'.

senses.definition: En el día presente.

examples.text: I am very busy today.
examples.translation: Estoy muy ocupado hoy.

senses.definition: En la época actual.

examples.text: Many people work from home today.
examples.translation: Mucha gente trabaja desde casa hoy en día.

faults.quote: (departure) To leave a place or depart.
faults.why: Shades of one meaning ('to go'); example 他已经去了 often means 'he passed away'.
Missing essential A1/A2 directional complement usage after verbs of motion (e.g., 出去, 回去).

notes: Indicates movement away from the speaker, contrasting with 来 (lái, to come).
Often placed before another verb to express going somewhere to do something (e.g., 去买东西, to go shopping).

senses.definition: To move or travel to a place away from the speaker.

examples.text: 明天我要去北京。
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to Beijing.

senses.definition: Used after a verb of motion to show movement away from the speaker.

examples.text: 请把这本书拿出去。
examples.translation: Please take this book out.

senses.definition: To remove or get rid of something.

examples.text: 这件衣服上的污渍去不掉。
examples.translation: The stain on this piece of clothing cannot be removed.

faults.quote: Used for both physical movement stopping (like a car or a person
faults.why: Merely restates the definition; fails to note common verb-object compounds like 停车.

corrected.shortGloss: to stop; to pause; to park
notes: Often used in the verb-object compound 停车 (tíngchē, to park a car or stop a vehicle) and the two-syllable verb 停止 (tíngzhǐ, to cease).

senses.definition: To stop moving, happening, or doing something.

examples.text: 雨停了，我们可以出去了。
examples.translation: The rain has stopped, so we can go out.

senses.definition: To park a vehicle.

examples.text: 请把车停在路边。
examples.translation: Please park the car by the side of the road.

faults.quote: Use 打开 when physically opening a door, a book, or a container,
faults.why: Restates the two senses; misses contrasting with its opposites 关/关上 and 合上.

notes: Compound verb formed from 打 (action prefix) + 开 (open). Its common opposites are 关上 (guānshàng, to close/turn off) for doors and devices, and 合上 (héshàng, to close) for books.

senses.definition: To move something so that it is no longer closed, folded, or sealed.

examples.text: 请把书打开到第三页。
examples.translation: Please open the book to page three.

senses.definition: To start the operation of an electrical appliance, device, or app.

examples.text: 天黑了，把灯打开吧。
examples.translation: It is getting dark; turn on the light.

faults.quote: To come to a stop or bring to a standstill.
faults.why: At A2, 住 means 'stop/hold fast' as a resultative complement after a verb, not standalone.

notes: Often followed by 在 (zài) before the place name (e.g., 住在北京, to live in Beijing).
Frequently placed directly after another verb as a complement to show that something stops or stays firmly in place, such as 记住 (jìzhù, to remember) or 拿住 (názhù, to hold tightly).

senses.definition: To have one's home in a particular place.

examples.text: 你住在哪里？
examples.translation: Where do you live?

senses.definition: To stay somewhere temporarily, such as at a hotel.

senses.definition: Used after a verb to indicate coming to a halt or holding firmly in place.

examples.translation: Please stop and do not walk any further.

senses.definition: To answer a telephone or video call.

examples.translation: The phone is ringing; I'll go answer it.

examples.text: Do głowy przychodzą mi różne pomysły.
examples.translation: Various ideas come to my mind.

The feminine form is 'przyjaciółka', and the irregular plural is 'przyjaciele'.

senses.definition: A person you know well, like, and trust deeply; a close friend.

examples.text: Mój przyjaciel zawsze mi pomaga w trudnych chwilach.
examples.translation: My friend always helps me in difficult moments.

faults.quote: /ˈpʂɨ.jaz.nɨ/

faults.why: Merely restates the two definitions without adding grammatical or usage information.

notes: Often followed by the dative case or 'dla' + genitive to show who or what something is friendly toward (e.g., 'przyjazny środowisku' or 'przyjazny dla środowiska' — environmentally friendly).

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: kind and pleasant to others.

examples.text: Nasz nowy sąsiad jest bardzo przyjazny.
examples.translation: Our new neighbor is very friendly.

senses.definition: Of a place or thing: welcoming, safe, or well suited for someone or something.

examples.text: To miasto jest bardzo przyjazne dla rowerzystów.
examples.translation: This city is very friendly to cyclists.

faults.quote: To reach a destination while traveling by vehicle.

notes: Used specifically for arriving by vehicle (car, train, bus, bike) or of the vehicle itself. For arriving on foot, use 'przychodzić'.
Imperfective verb, used for repeated actions or an ongoing arrival. For a single completed arrival, use 'przyjechać'.

senses.definition: To come to or reach a place by vehicle, or of a vehicle: to arrive at a destination.

examples.text: Codziennie przyjeżdżam do pracy autobusem.
examples.translation: I come to work by bus every day.

examples.text: Pociągi przyjeżdżają na stację zgodnie z rozkładem.
examples.translation: The trains arrive at the station on schedule.

faults.quote: przynosić is the imperfective counterpart of przenieść or przynieść.

faults.quote: /pʂɨˈnɔ.ɕić/

notes: Imperfective verb, used for ongoing or repeated actions. For a single completed action of bringing, use the perfective 'przynieść'.

senses.definition: To carry something to the place where someone is.

examples.text: Kelner przynosi nam menu.
examples.translation: The waiter is bringing us the menu.

senses.definition: To result in or produce a particular state, feeling, or outcome.

examples.text: Ta praca przynosi dobre rezultaty.
examples.translation: This work brings good results.

faults.quote: El color del cielo despejado.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun instead of a quality.

faults.quote: A diferencia del español, en inglés 'blue' es tanto un color como

senses.definition: Del color del cielo despejado o del mar.

examples.text: The sky is blue today.
examples.translation: El cielo está azul hoy.

senses.definition: Triste o desanimado.

examples.text: She felt a bit blue after the long week.
examples.translation: Se sintió un poco triste después de una semana larga.

faults.why: Needs a note contrasting 'boat' (smaller craft) with 'ship' (large vessel).

senses.definition: Vehículo diseñado para navegar por el agua, especialmente uno pequeño o mediano.

examples.text: We took a small boat to cross the lake.
examples.translation: Tomamos un bote pequeño para cruzar el lago.

faults.quote: Acción de registrar o asegurar un servicio con antelación.
faults.why: As a noun, 'book' does not mean a reservation ('booking' does); 'book' is the verb.

notes: Como verbo ('to book'), significa hacer una reserva (por ejemplo, 'to book a hotel room').

senses.definition: Conjunto de hojas de papel, impresas o en blanco, unidas por un lado y cubiertas con una tapa.

examples.text: I am reading a very interesting book.
examples.translation: Estoy leyendo un libro muy interesante.

faults.quote: No confundas 'border' (la línea o límite físico) con 'abroad'
faults.why: 'border' and 'abroad' are neither false friends nor commonly confused.

notes: Para referirse al límite físico de una superficie (como una mesa o un acantilado) se usa 'edge', mientras que 'border' es una línea divisoria o una franja alrededor de algo.

senses.definition: La línea que separa dos países, estados o regiones.

examples.text: We had to show our passports at the border.
examples.translation: Tuvimos que mostrar nuestros pasaportes en la frontera.

senses.definition: Franja que rodea el extremo de una superficie o tela, a menudo como adorno.

examples.text: The garden has a beautiful border of colorful flowers.
examples.translation: El jardín tiene un hermoso borde de flores coloridas.

notes: Usa 'bored' (con -ed) para describir cómo se siente alguien ('I am bored' = estoy aburrido), y 'boring' (con -ing) para lo que causa el aburrimiento ('The movie is boring' = la película es aburrida).

senses.definition: Que siente cansancio o desinterés por no tener nada que hacer o porque algo no es entretenido.

examples.text: I was so bored during the long meeting.
examples.translation: Estuve muy aburrido durante la larga reunión.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

senses.definition: To take hold of something with your hand, or pass it to someone.

examples.text: 机の上のペンを取ってください。
examples.translation: Please pass me the pen on the desk.

senses.definition: To get, reserve, or take something such as a ticket, seat, or time off.

examples.translation: I will get movie tickets.

senses.definition: To remove or take off something attached or worn, such as a lid, glasses, or dirt.

examples.translation: I remove the dirt from the hat.

senses.definition: To damage a physical object so that it no longer works or falls into pieces.

examples.text: 子供がテレビを壊した。
examples.translation: The child broke the television.

senses.definition: To harm or ruin one's health, stomach, or a plan.

examples.text: 無理をして体を壊さないでください。
examples.translation: Please do not ruin your health by pushing yourself too hard.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to hang up; to turn off

senses.definition: To divide, separate, or trim something using a knife, scissors, or another sharp tool.

examples.text: ナイフでパンを切る。
examples.translation: I cut the bread with a knife.

senses.definition: To end a phone call, turn off a switch, or break off a connection.

examples.text: 電話を切る。
examples.translation: I hang up the phone.

faults.why: Missing hiragana reading for a kanji headword.

corrected.shortGloss: to throw; to toss; to pitch

senses.definition: To propel an object through the air using your hand or arm.

examples.text: ボールを遠くに投げる。
examples.translation: I throw the ball far away.

faults.why: Should mention the particles used: から (from), に (onto / in an exam).

senses.definition: To move downwards from a higher place to a lower one, without being pushed.

examples.text: 木からリンゴが落ちる。

senses.definition: To fail to pass a test, examination, or selection.

examples.text: 試験に落ちた。
examples.translation: I failed the exam.

notes: No confundas 'stranger' con 'foreigner' (extranjero). 'Stranger' es alguien que no conoces, sin importar su nacionalidad; 'foreigner' es alguien de otro país.

senses.definition: Persona a la que no conoces.

examples.text: Never talk to a stranger.
examples.translation: Nunca hables con un desconocido.

examples.text: He is a total stranger to me.
examples.translation: Es un completo desconocido para mí.

faults.quote: /ˈstrɔːbəri/
faults.why: British IPA; standard US pronunciation has a secondary stress on -berry: /ˈstrɔˌbɛri/.

senses.definition: Fruta pequeña, roja y dulce con pequeñas semillas en la superficie.

notes: En inglés estadounidense se usa la preposición 'on' para decir en qué calle está algo (ej. 'on Main Street').

senses.definition: Vía pública en un pueblo o ciudad que tiene edificios a los lados.

examples.text: The library is on the next street.
examples.translation: La biblioteca está en la siguiente calle.

faults.quote: pero también para sabores o olores intensos
faults.why: Grammatical error in Spanish: 'o olores' must be 'u olores' before a word starting with 'o-'.

senses.definition: Que tiene mucha fuerza física o poder muscular.

examples.text: He is a strong man who can lift heavy boxes.
examples.translation: Él es un hombre fuerte que puede levantar cajas pesadas.

senses.definition: Que es resistente, firme o difícil de romper.

examples.text: We need a strong rope to climb the mountain.
examples.translation: Necesitamos una cuerda resistente para escalar la montaña.

senses.definition: Que tiene un sabor, olor o efecto muy intenso.

examples.text: This coffee is too strong for me.
examples.translation: Este café está demasiado fuerte para mí.

senses.definition: Acción, decisión o idea que no es correcta o acertada.

examples.text: I made a big mistake in the report.
examples.translation: Cometí un gran error en el informe.

faults.quote: La riqueza o fortuna total que posee una persona.

senses.definition: Medio de cambio, en forma de monedas, billetes o saldo bancario, que se usa para comprar cosas o pagar servicios.

examples.text: I don't have enough money to buy this shirt.

faults.quote: Un niño pequeño que es muy inquieto, travieso o juguetón.

examples.text: The monkey climbed to the top of the tree to find some fruit.

faults.quote: Período de tiempo de unas cuatro semanas o treinta días.

examples.translation: Febrero es el mes más corto del año.

examples.text: I will travel to Spain in a month.
examples.translation: Viajaré a España en un mes.

faults.quote: Cuerpo celeste que brilla en el cielo por la noche.

examples.text: The moon is very bright tonight.
examples.translation: La luna está muy brillante esta noche.

examples.text: W centrum miasta stoi wysoki budynek.
examples.translation: There is a tall building in the city center.

senses.definition: Greater than normal in amount, level, or degree (such as prices, temperature, or quality).

examples.text: Ceny w tym sklepie są bardzo wysokie.
examples.translation: The prices in this shop are very high.

faults.quote: (design) A detached area or structure separated from others, like a
faults.why: Kitchen island is a minor transparent extension, unnecessary as a separate sense at A2.

faults.quote: Used literally for geographical islands, but also metaphorically for a detached
faults.why: Filler note explaining transparent metaphorical uses identical to English.

notes: Takes the preposition 'na': 'na wyspie' (on an island), 'na wyspę' (to an island).

senses.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water.

examples.text: Wypoczywaliśmy na pięknej, tropikalnej wyspie.
examples.translation: We were relaxing on a beautiful, tropical island.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'wolny' meaning 'vacant' or 'unoccupied'.
faults.why: Tells learner not to confuse the word with itself and contradicts sense 2.
Missing the fundamental sense 'free' (not controlled/restricted, or single in relationship).

faults.quote: Polish uses 'wolny' for both 'slow' (not fast) and 'free'
faults.why: Merely restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage information (e.g. 'za darmo' vs 'wolny').

notes: Notice that 'wolny' does not mean 'free of charge' (use 'darmowy' or 'za darmo' for that).
In the sense of 'slow', the opposite is 'szybki' (fast); in the sense of 'free/available', the opposite is 'zajęty' (busy/occupied).

senses.definition: Moving or happening at a low speed.

examples.text: Ten samochód jest bardzo wolny.
examples.translation: This car is very slow.

senses.definition: Not busy; having no work, plans, or obligations.

examples.text: Czy masz jutro czas? Jestem wolny po południu.
examples.translation: Do you have time tomorrow? I am free in the afternoon.

senses.definition: Not currently being used or occupied by someone.

examples.text: Czy to krzesło jest wolne?
examples.translation: Is this chair available?

senses.definition: Able to act as one wants, not under control or in a relationship.

examples.text: Mamy wolny wybór.
examples.translation: We have a free choice.

faults.quote: Unlike some languages where hair is a collective singular noun
faults.why: Repeats note 0 in different words.

notes: In Polish, hair on the head is always plural ('włosy są...' = hair is...). The singular 'włos' refers to a single strand of hair.

senses.definition: The mass of thin threads that grows on a person's head.

examples.text: Ona ma długie, brązowe włosy.
examples.translation: She has long, brown hair.

examples.text: Muszę dzisiaj umyć włosy.
examples.translation: I have to wash my hair today.

faults.quote: Ceny paliwa ciągle wspinają się w górę.
faults.why: Unnatural English calque; in Polish, prices 'rosną' or 'idą w górę', not 'wspinają się'.

faults.quote: To gradually increase or make progress toward a higher level or position.
faults.why: Figurative sense is literary or rare; not needed for A2 and caused a bad calque.
Should state the preposition and case used for the destination: 'na' + accusative.

notes: Imperfective verb (perfective: 'wspiąć się'). Usually followed by the preposition 'na' + accusative (e.g., 'wspinać się na górę / na drzewo').
Contrast with 'wchodzić' (to walk up/go up), which is used for everyday things like stairs or hills.

senses.definition: To go up a steep surface, such as a mountain, rock, or tree, often using both hands and feet.

examples.text: Musimy wspinać się na tę górę przez kilka godzin.
examples.translation: We have to climb this mountain for several hours.

faults.quote: the word 'wujek' is specifically used for the brother of your mother
faults.why: In contemporary Polish, 'wujek' is the standard everyday word for any uncle; note 1 contradicts note 0.

faults.quote: The brother of one's parent.
faults.why: Incomplete: also covers the husband of one's aunt ('ciocia').

notes: Traditionally, 'stryj' or 'stryjek' was used for a father's brother, but in modern everyday Polish 'wujek' is used for any uncle.

senses.definition: The brother of one's mother or father, or the husband of one's aunt.

examples.text: Mój wujek przyjedzie do nas w niedzielę.
examples.translation: My uncle is coming to visit us on Sunday.

senses.definition: A friendly or polite form of address used by children for an adult male family friend.

examples.text: Powiedz cześć wujkowi.
examples.translation: Say hello to uncle.

faults.quote: to choose; to select
faults.why: Does not include 'to elect' from sense 1.

notes: Imperfective verb (perfective: 'wybrać'). Use 'wybierać' for the ongoing process or repeated actions, and 'wybrać' for a single completed choice.

senses.definition: To decide which person or thing you want out of the available options.

examples.text: Trudno jest wybierać prezent dla kogoś, kogo nie znasz dobrze.
examples.translation: It is hard to choose a gift for someone you do not know well.

senses.definition: To choose someone for an official position by voting.

examples.text: W przyszłym miesiącu ludzie będą wybierać nowego prezydenta.
examples.translation: Next month people will be electing a new president.

faults.quote: Used in many contexts, from physical cutting with a knife
faults.why: Merely restates the senses; should give the aorist stem (έκοψα / να κόψω).

faults.quote: To obtain a document or ticket.
faults.why: Too broad; used specifically for issuing/buying tickets, receipts, or invoices, not any document.

corrected.shortGloss: to cut; to stop; to buy (a ticket)
notes: The aorist (simple past) is έκοψα, and the perfective stem is κόψ- (να κόψω).

senses.definition: To divide, slice, or trim something using a sharp tool such as a knife or scissors.

examples.text: Κόβω το ψωμί σε φέτες.
examples.translation: I cut the bread into slices.

senses.definition: To give up a habit, or to cut off a supply or connection.

examples.text: Πρέπει να κόψω το κάπνισμα.
examples.translation: I must quit smoking.

senses.definition: To buy or issue a ticket, receipt, or fine.

examples.text: Κόβω εισιτήριο για το τρένο.
examples.translation: I am buying a train ticket.

faults.why: Missing the everyday A1/A2 sense 'to call on the phone' (παίρνω τηλέφωνο).

faults.quote: Παίρνω is one of the most versatile verbs in Greek.
faults.why: Restates the senses while omitting the crucial irregular aorist πήρα / να πάρω.

corrected.shortGloss: to take; to get; to buy; to call
notes: Irregular aorist (simple past): πήρα; perfective subjunctive/future: να/θα πάρω.
Spelled with αι, unlike περνάω ('to pass'), which is pronounced the same in the stem (/per-/).

senses.definition: To pick up, grasp, or take something or someone with you.

examples.text: Παίρνω το βιβλίο από το τραπέζι.
examples.translation: I take the book from the table.

senses.definition: To buy or receive something.

examples.text: Πρέπει να πάρω λίγο ψωμί από τον φούρνο.
examples.translation: I need to get some bread from the bakery.

senses.definition: To use a means of public transport.

examples.text: Θα πάρω το λεωφορείο για το κέντρο.
examples.translation: I will take the bus to the center.

senses.definition: To telephone someone (often with τηλέφωνο).

examples.text: Θα σε πάρω τηλέφωνο το βράδυ.
examples.translation: I will call you in the evening.

faults.quote: συναντώ is the standard verb for 'meeting' someone
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving the common variant συναντάω, aorist συνάντησα, and passive συναντιέμαι.

notes: Also very commonly used in the form συναντάω in everyday speech. Aorist: συνάντησα.
For a mutual meeting ('we meet up'), the passive form συναντιέμαι is often used: Θα συναντηθούμε αύριο ('We will meet tomorrow').

senses.definition: To come together with someone, either by arrangement or by chance.

examples.text: Συναντώ τον φίλο μου στην πλατεία.
examples.translation: I meet my friend in the square.

senses.definition: To come across or face something such as a difficulty or obstacle.

examples.text: Συναντώ συχνά προβλήματα σε αυτόν τον δρόμο.
examples.translation: I often encounter problems on this road.

faults.quote: Βρίσκω αυτή τη ιδέα πολύ ενδιαφέρουσα.
faults.why: Ungrammatical omission of final -ν before a vowel: must be 'την ιδέα', not 'τη ιδέα'.

faults.quote: βρίσκω is one of the most common verbs in Greek
faults.why: Pure filler note.

corrected.shortGloss: to find; to discover; to think
notes: Irregular aorist (simple past): βρήκα; perfective subjunctive/future: να/θα βρω.

senses.definition: To discover or locate something or someone, either after searching or by chance.

examples.text: Δεν βρίσκω τα κλειδιά μου πουθενά.
examples.translation: I cannot find my keys anywhere.

senses.definition: To have a particular opinion or impression of someone or something.

examples.text: Βρίσκω αυτή την ιδέα πολύ ενδιαφέρουσα.
examples.translation: I find this idea very interesting.

faults.quote: much more common than the formal vlepo in many active contexts.
faults.why: False claim: βλέπω is completely neutral, everyday, and is the normal verb for watching TV.

faults.quote: Το βράδυ κοιτάζω τηλεόραση με την οικογένειά μου.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation in Greek; watching TV is 'βλέπω τηλεόραση', not 'κοιτάζω τηλεόραση'.

faults.quote: Πρέπει να κοιτάζω την ώρα πριν φύγω.
faults.why: Wrong aspect: before a single future event ('πριν φύγω'), perfective 'να κοιτάξω' is required.

corrected.shortGloss: to look at; to check; to look after
notes: Also very common in the shorter form κοιτάω (or κοιτώ). Aorist: κοίταξα; imperative: κοίτα! ('look!').
Unlike English 'watch', watching TV or a film in Greek uses βλέπω (βλέπω τηλεόραση), while κοιτάζω means directing your eyes at something.

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something.

examples.text: Κοιτάζω τη θάλασσα από το παράθυρο.
examples.translation: I look at the sea from the window.

senses.definition: To examine or check something to get information or see its condition.

examples.text: Πρέπει να κοιτάξω την ώρα πριν φύγω.
examples.translation: I need to check the time before I leave.

senses.definition: To take care of someone or attend to a matter.

examples.text: Η γιαγιά κοιτάζει τα παιδιά το απόγευμα.
examples.translation: Grandma looks after the children in the afternoon.

faults.quote: lluvia; precipitación
faults.why: Includes 'precipitación', which is not in the sense glosses and is overly technical.

notes: Es incontable en inglés, por lo que no se dice 'a rain' ni 'rains' para hablar de un evento normal. Se dice 'the rain' o simplemente 'rain'.

senses.definition: Agua que cae de las nubes en forma de gotas.

examples.text: The rain fell all night long.
examples.translation: La lluvia cayó durante toda la noche.

faults.quote: No confundas 'read' (leer) con 'look at'
faults.why: Filler note; learners do not confuse 'read' with 'look at'.

notes: Es un verbo irregular: el pasado y el participio ('read') se escriben igual que el presente, pero se pronuncian /rɛd/ (como el color 'red').

senses.definition: Mirar palabras o signos escritos y entender su significado, en silencio o en voz alta.

examples.text: I like to read a book before I go to sleep.
examples.translation: Me gusta leer un libro antes de ir a dormir.

senses.definition: Interpretar o entender el significado de un gesto, una situación o un símbolo.

examples.text: It is hard to read her feelings sometimes.
examples.translation: A veces es difícil interpretar sus sentimientos.

faults.quote: Es uno de los colores básicos en inglés y se usa tanto
faults.why: Pure filler note stating the obvious.

senses.definition: Del color de la sangre o de un tomate maduro.

examples.text: She wore a bright red dress to the party.
examples.translation: Llevó un vestido rojo brillante a la fiesta.

faults.why: Should explain the difference between 'remember' and 'remind', and 'remember + -ing' vs 'to'.

notes: Se usa directamente con el objeto, sin preposición ('I remember that day' = Me acuerdo de ese día). Seguido de un verbo, usa '-ing' para un recuerdo del pasado ('I remember meeting her') y 'to' para algo que no debes olvidar hacer ('Remember to call her').
No confundir con 'remind' (recordarle algo a alguien).

senses.definition: Tener o traer a la memoria algo del pasado o un dato.

examples.text: I always remember his birthday.
examples.translation: Siempre recuerdo su cumpleaños.

senses.definition: No olvidar hacer algo necesario.

examples.text: Remember to lock the door before you leave.
examples.translation: Acuérdate de cerrar la puerta con llave antes de irte.

faults.quote: fix
faults.why: Domain is in English instead of Spanish.

notes: En la conversación diaria es más común usar 'fix' (arreglar); 'repair' suena un poco más formal o se usa para averías más complejas.

senses.definition: Hacer que algo que está roto o dañado vuelva a funcionar o a estar en buen estado.

examples.text: He needs to repair his car before the trip.
examples.translation: Necesita reparar su carro antes del viaje.

faults.quote: en contextos más científicos o formales también se usa 'avian'.
faults.why: Unhelpful for A2 and implies 'avian' is a common noun substitute.

notes: En inglés, 'bird' se usa tanto para pájaros pequeños como para aves grandes (águilas, pingüinos, etc.).

senses.definition: Animal vertebrado con plumas, alas y pico, generalmente capaz de volar.

examples.text: A little bird is singing in the tree.
examples.translation: Un pajarito está cantando en el árbol.

faults.quote: y 'at' para la época de fiestas ('at my birthday').
faults.why: 'At my birthday' is unidiomatic in US English without 'party'.

notes: Para referirse al día del cumpleaños se usa la preposición 'on': 'on my birthday' (en mi cumpleaños).

senses.definition: Día en que se cumple un año más desde el nacimiento de una persona.

examples.text: My birthday is in July.
examples.translation: Mi cumpleaños es en julio.

faults.why: Missing common everyday senses: coffee/tea without milk, and Black (race/ethnicity).

faults.quote: El color más oscuro de todos, como el de la noche
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('El color...').

faults.quote: Aunque 'black' es el color negro, también se usa para describir
faults.why: Merely restates the senses.

notes: Cuando se refiere a personas o cultura afrodescendiente, en inglés estadounidense suele escribirse con mayúscula ('Black').

senses.definition: Del color más oscuro, como el carbón o la noche sin luz.

examples.text: The cat has soft black fur.
examples.translation: El gato tiene un pelaje negro y suave.

senses.definition: Perteneciente o relativo a las personas de origen africano o afroamericano.

examples.text: She is a famous Black writer.
examples.translation: Ella es una famosa escritora negra.

senses.definition: Dicho del café o del té: que se sirve sin leche ni crema.

examples.text: I always drink my coffee black.
examples.translation: Siempre tomo el café solo.

faults.quote: El corte en su dedo sacó un poco de sangre.
faults.why: Calqued translation ('su dedo' instead of 'el dedo', 'sacó sangre').

notes: Es un sustantivo incontable. No se dice 'a blood', sino 'some blood' o simplemente 'blood'.
Se pronuncia con un sonido de vocal corta, similar a 'but', no como 'food'.

senses.definition: Líquido rojo que circula por el cuerpo de las personas y los animales.

examples.text: He lost a lot of blood in the accident.
examples.translation: Perdió mucha sangre en el accidente.

faults.quote: /waˈsˤala/
faults.why: Stress in Arabic 3-light-syllable words falls on the first syllable: /ˈwasˤala/.

faults.quote: Used when someone finishes a journey to a location.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage value.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'يصل' which is the present tense form.
faults.why: Weirdly warns not to confuse a verb with its own irregular present form.
Missing the common transitive sense 'to connect, join, link'.

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive, to reach; to connect
notes: The initial و (wāw) drops in the present tense: يَصِلُ (yaṣilu).Takes إِلَى (ʾilā) or a direct object for the destination.
When meaning 'to connect', the present tense is also يَصِلُ (yaṣilu), and it takes بـِ (bi-) for the thing connected to.

senses.definition: To reach a place at the end of a journey.

examples.text: وَصَلَ الْقِطَارُ إِلَى الْمَحَطَّةِ.
examples.translation: The train arrived at the station.

senses.definition: To join or link two things together.

examples.text: وَصَلَ الجِسْرُ بَيْنَ المَدِينَتَيْنِ.
examples.translation: The bridge connected the two cities.

faults.quote: To turn away from something or lose interest in it.
faults.why: Higher-register C1/C2 meaning; A2 learners only need the musical sense.

notes: Used only for playing musical instruments (often with the preposition عَلَى ʿalā before the instrument). For playing sports or games, use لَعِبَ (laʿiba).

senses.definition: To make music on a musical instrument.

examples.text: عَزَفَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى القِيثَارَةِ.
examples.translation: The man played the guitar.

faults.why: Identity and state are the same copular 'to be' sense.

faults.quote: to be; to exist
faults.why: Names 'to exist', which is absent from the senses.

faults.quote: كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا فِي الْأَمْسِ.
faults.why: أَمْسِ is used directly without فِي الْـ (أَمْسِ or بِالأَمْسِ).

notes: Arabic omits 'to be' in simple present-tense sentences. كَانَ is used to put a sentence into the past tense (and its present form يَكُونُ yakūnu is used for the future or after modal words).
The noun or adjective that follows كَانَ as its predicate takes the accusative case (-an): كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا (The weather was nice).

senses.definition: Used as the past tense of 'to be' to state what someone or something was, or where or how they were.

examples.text: كَانَ أَبِي مُعَلِّمًا.
examples.translation: My father was a teacher.

examples.text: كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا أَمْسِ.
examples.translation: The weather was beautiful yesterday.

faults.quote: /saˈmi.ʕa/
faults.why: Stress in Arabic 3-light-syllable words falls on the first syllable: /ˈsamiʕa/.

notes: Present tense: يَسْمَعُ (yasmaʿu).
