senses.definition: At all times; on every occasion.

examples.text: Я всегда рад тебе помочь.
examples.translation: I am always glad to help you.

examples.text: Она всегда встаёт рано утром.
examples.translation: She always gets up early in the morning.

faults.quote: /fsʲɪˈra/
faults.why: Wrong transcription: 'вчера' has /t͡ɕ/, not /sʲ/ (/ft͡ɕɪˈra/).

faults.quote: This word is invariable; it does not change based on
faults.why: Generic statement true of all Russian adverbs; adds no specific value.

notes: The initial в- is pronounced /f/ before ч.
Combine directly with morning, afternoon, or evening without a preposition: вчера утром (yesterday morning), вчера вечером (last night / yesterday evening).
To modify a noun, use the adjective вчерашний (yesterday's).

senses.definition: On the day before today.

examples.text: Вчера я был в кино.
examples.translation: I was at the cinema yesterday.

faults.quote: While 'Brief' refers to a physical letter sent by post
faults.why: English 'letter' also means alphabet character ('der Buchstabe'); note misses this crucial false friend.

notes: Plural: 'die Briefe'.
Refers only to a message sent by post. A letter of the alphabet is 'der Buchstabe'.

senses.definition: A written or printed message sent in an envelope by post.

examples.text: Ich habe heute einen Brief im Briefkasten gefunden.
examples.translation: I found a letter in the mailbox today.

faults.quote: In Germany, you usually board the bus at the front door
faults.why: Cultural trivia instead of useful grammar (missing plural 'die Busse' and 'mit dem Bus').

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'die Bahn', which refers to the train system.
faults.why: No English speaker will confuse 'Bus' with 'Bahn'.

notes: Plural: 'die Busse' (spelled with a double 's').
To say 'by bus', use 'mit dem Bus'.

senses.definition: A large motor vehicle that carries passengers along a regular route.

examples.text: Der Bus kommt erst in zehn Minuten.
examples.translation: The bus won't arrive for another ten minutes.

examples.text: Ich fahre jeden Morgen mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
examples.translation: I take the bus to work every morning.

faults.quote: A person who has the main authority or is the owner
faults.why: Both senses mean the same thing (boss/head of a workplace or company).
Misses the important English false friend ('chef' in a kitchen is 'der Koch' or 'der Küchenchef').

notes: Plural: 'die Chefs'. A female boss is 'die Chefin' (plural: 'die Chefinnen').
False friend: does not mean a restaurant cook ('der Koch'), though 'der Küchenchef' is the head chef.

senses.definition: The person who is in charge of a workplace, department, or company.

examples.text: Mein Chef ist heute leider nicht im Büro.
examples.translation: My boss is unfortunately not in the office today.

faults.quote: and the plural form remains der Computer (with a slight vowel length
faults.why: Plural article is 'die' ('die Computer'), not 'der', and there is no vowel length difference.

faults.quote: such as Computerbildsschirm (computer screen)
faults.why: Misspelled German word ('Computerbildsschirm' with double 's' instead of 'Computerbildschirm') in a filler note.

notes: The plural form is identical to the singular: 'die Computer'.
In everyday speech, 'der Rechner' is also very commonly used for a computer.

senses.definition: An electronic machine used for storing and processing data, working, and using the internet.

examples.text: Ich arbeite den ganzen Tag am Computer.
examples.translation: I work at the computer all day.

faults.quote: Use 'schiena' when talking about the anatomical back of a person
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and shortGloss without adding useful usage details.

notes: Refers only to the anatomical back. For the back part of an object or place, use 'il retro' or 'il fondo'; for the adverb or preposition 'behind', use 'dietro'.

senses.definition: The rear part of the human body, from the neck to the hips.

examples.text: Mi fa male la schiena dopo aver lavorato al computer.
examples.translation: My back hurts after working at the computer.

examples.text: Si è sdraiato sulla schiena per guardare le stelle.
examples.translation: He lay on his back to look at the stars.

faults.quote: (slang) A physical feeling of illness the day after drinking too much
faults.why: 'Avere la scimmia' means a strong craving or obsession, not a hangover ('postumi della sbornia').

faults.quote: 'avere la scimmia' is a common idiom meaning to have a hangover
faults.why: False meaning; 'avere la scimmia' means to have an addiction, craving, or obsession.

notes: Used in everyday Italian for both monkeys and tailless apes.
The plural is 'le scimmie' (keeping the '-i-').

senses.definition: A primate that climbs trees, typically having a long tail; also used generally for apes.

examples.text: La scimmia mangia una banana sull'albero.
examples.translation: The monkey is eating a banana in the tree.

notes: The stress falls on the '-ni-' syllable: scri-va-NÌ-a.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat surface used for working, writing, or studying.

examples.text: Ho messo il computer portatile sulla scrivania.
examples.translation: I put the laptop on the desk.

faults.quote: (period) The time in a person's life when they attend an educational
faults.why: Shades of the same basic meaning of 'school' that do not need separation at A2.

faults.quote: Used both for the physical building and the institution itself, just like

notes: No article is used in common expressions like 'andare a scuola' (to go to school), 'essere a scuola' (to be at school), and 'finire la scuola' (to finish school).

senses.definition: A place or institution where children and young people go to learn, or the time spent there.

examples.text: I bambini vanno a scuola ogni mattina.
examples.translation: The children go to school every morning.

examples.text: Ho conosciuto il mio migliore amico a scuola.
examples.translation: I met my best friend at school.

faults.quote: Use 'sedia' for an ordinary single-person chair with a back.
faults.why: Simply repeats the definition in the notes.

notes: Refers to an ordinary chair; an upholstered armchair is 'la poltrona', and a stool without a back is 'lo sgabello'.

senses.definition: A movable seat for one person, with a back and usually four legs.

examples.text: Ho messo la borsa sulla sedia vicino alla finestra.
examples.translation: I put the bag on the chair near the window.

faults.quote: /ˈro.ti laˈpis/
faults.why: Stress in 'lapis' is on the first syllable, not the final one.

notes: While 'roti lapis' is the standard Indonesian term, many speakers simply use the English loanword 'sandwich' in everyday speech.

senses.definition: Food made of two or more slices of bread with a filling between them.

examples.text: Dia membuat roti lapis isi keju untuk sarapan.
examples.translation: She made a cheese sandwich for breakfast.

faults.quote: cover both western-style bread and various sweet or savory pastries, cakes, and buns.
faults.why: False claim: cakes and pastries are 'kue', not 'roti' (which covers bread and buns/rolls).

notes: Covers both loaves of sliced bread ('roti tawar') and individual sweet or savory bread buns and rolls. Cakes, cookies, and pastries are called 'kue', not 'roti'.

senses.definition: A baked food made from flour and water, including both loaves of bread and individual sweet or savory buns.

examples.text: Dia makan sepotong roti untuk sarapan.
examples.translation: He ate a piece of bread for breakfast.

examples.text: Ibu membeli roti isi cokelat di toko.
examples.translation: Mother bought a chocolate-filled bun at the shop.

faults.quote: Used specifically for the main room where visitors are received and seated.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition without contrasting it with 'ruang keluarga' (family room).

notes: Literally 'guest room' ('ruang' + 'tamu'), used for the front sitting room where visitors are received. A bedroom for guests is 'kamar tamu', and the private living room for the family is 'ruang keluarga'.

senses.definition: The room in a house used for sitting and entertaining guests.

examples.text: Mereka duduk di ruang tamu sambil minum teh.
examples.translation: They sat in the living room while drinking tea.

faults.quote: (space) A designated area or zone for a specific purpose.
faults.why: Not a distinct sense from sense 0; 'ruangan' is an enclosed room or hall.

faults.quote: Ruangan tamu itu cukup besar.
faults.why: Unnatural collocation: 'living room' is 'ruang tamu', not 'ruangan tamu'.

notes: Refers to an enclosed room or large interior space in a building. By contrast, 'ruang' is used for abstract space or in fixed compound names of rooms (like 'ruang tamu', living room, or 'ruang makan', dining room), and 'kamar' is used for a bedroom or bathroom.

senses.definition: An enclosed room or interior space within a building.

examples.text: Dia sedang membersihkan ruangan itu.
examples.translation: She is cleaning that room.

faults.quote: Use 'abrigo' when referring to an overcoat or winter coat
faults.why: Merely restates the definition and gloss of sense 0.

notes: Do not confuse with 'chaqueta', which refers to a lighter, shorter jacket.

senses.definition: An outer garment worn over other clothes to provide warmth in cold weather.

examples.text: Hace mucho frío hoy, así que ponte el abrigo.
examples.translation: It is very cold today, so put on your coat.

senses.definition: Protection or a place that provides protection from bad weather or danger.

examples.text: Los excursionistas buscaron abrigo bajo las rocas durante la tormenta.
examples.translation: The hikers looked for shelter under the rocks during the storm.

faults.why: In Spain, 'abuelo/a' is very commonly used colloquially for any elderly person.

notes: The feminine form is 'la abuela' (grandmother). In the plural, 'los abuelos' commonly means 'grandparents'.

senses.definition: The father of your father or mother.

examples.text: Mi abuelo cuenta historias muy divertidas.
examples.translation: My grandfather tells very funny stories.

senses.definition: (informal) An elderly man.

examples.text: Había varios abuelos tomando el sol en el banco del parque.
examples.translation: There were several old men sunbathing on the park bench.

faults.quote: /aˈsej.te/
faults.why: Castilian Spanish (es-ES) uses /θ/ ('distinción'), not /s/, for 'ce': /aˈθejte/.

notes: In Spain, 'aceite' on its own almost always refers to olive oil ('aceite de oliva').

senses.definition: A smooth, thick liquid made from plants, used in cooking and on salads.

examples.text: Echa un poco de aceite en la sartén.
examples.translation: Pour a little oil into the pan.

senses.definition: A thick liquid used to lubricate engines or machines.

examples.text: Tengo que cambiarle el aceite al coche.
examples.translation: I have to change the oil in the car.

faults.quote: /aðolesˈtente/
faults.why: Wrong consonant /t/ instead of /θ/ for 'ce' in es-ES (/aðolesˈθente/).

notes: The form does not change for gender; only the article changes: 'el adolescente' (male), 'la adolescente' (female).
Do not confuse with 'joven', which is broader and includes people in their twenties.

senses.definition: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult.

examples.text: Los adolescentes suelen pasar mucho tiempo con sus amigos.
examples.translation: Teenagers usually spend a lot of time with their friends.

faults.quote: /alˈdu.to/
faults.why: Corrupted IPA: transposed /l/ to the first syllable instead of /aˈðulto/.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who has reached full physical and legal maturity.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition of an adult.

notes: The feminine form is 'la adulta'.

senses.definition: A person who is fully grown and no longer a child or teenager.

examples.text: La entrada cuesta diez euros para los adultos.
examples.translation: The ticket costs ten euros for adults.

faults.quote: In modern Mandarin, the second syllable '朵' is typically pronounced
faults.why: Neutral tone is shown in reading; unlikely confusion with 耳环; measure word missing.

notes: The common measure words are 只 (zhī) for one ear and 双 (shuāng) or 对 (duì) for a pair of ears.

senses.definition: The organ of hearing on each side of the head.

examples.text: 他的耳朵很大。
examples.translation: His ears are very big.

notes: 婚礼 refers to the wedding ceremony and celebration itself, whereas 婚姻 (hūnyīn) refers to the state of marriage. The common measure word is 场 (chǎng).

senses.definition: The ceremony and celebration of getting married.

examples.text: 他们的婚礼办得很隆重。
examples.translation: Their wedding was very grand.

faults.quote: 瓶子 is a general word for any bottle, regardless of the material.
faults.why: Restates the gloss; misses that 瓶 alone is used as a measure word and in compounds.

notes: The measure word for a bottle as an object is 个 (gè). To count bottles of liquid or name a type of bottle, drop 子 and use 瓶 alone: 一瓶水 (a bottle of water), 塑料瓶 (plastic bottle).

senses.definition: A container for liquids with a narrow neck, usually made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: 桌子上有一个空瓶子。
examples.translation: There is an empty bottle on the table.

notes: Unlike English 'chicken', 鸡 (jī) alone usually refers to the live bird or a whole cooked bird; use 鸡肉 for the meat as an ingredient or dish.

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.text: 这里的鸡肉很好吃。
examples.translation: The chicken here is delicious.

faults.why: Should note that 肉 by itself often defaults to pork (猪肉) in everyday cooking.

faults.quote: 他身上有很多肉。 — He has a lot of flesh on his body.
faults.why: Calqued translation; 身上有肉 idioms mean being plump/meaty, or use a clearer example for flesh/pulp.

notes: To specify the animal, place its name before 肉: 牛肉 (beef), 鸡肉 (chicken), 猪肉 (pork). In everyday cooking, 肉 by itself often defaults to pork.

senses.definition: The flesh of animals eaten as food.

examples.text: 我今天不想吃肉。
examples.translation: I don't want to eat meat today.

senses.definition: The soft part of the body of a person or animal, or the edible pulp of a fruit.

examples.text: 这个西瓜的肉很甜。
examples.translation: The flesh of this watermelon is very sweet.

faults.quote: Use 끝내다 when you are actively bringing a task or event
faults.why: Restates the definition and duplicates the transitive contrast in note[1].

corrected.shortGloss: to finish; to complete; to end
notes: 끝내다 is transitive (taking 를/을). Do not confuse it with the intransitive 끝나다 (to end/finish by itself): 일을 끝내다 (to finish the work) vs. 일이 끝나다 (the work ends).

senses.definition: To bring a task, event, or activity to its conclusion.

examples.text: 오늘까지 숙제를 끝내야 해요.
examples.translation: I have to finish my homework by today.

examples.text: 드디어 그 프로젝트를 끝냈어요.
examples.translation: I finally finished that project.

faults.quote: to fly; to soar
faults.why: Includes 'to soar', which is absent from the sense glosses.

notes: 날다 is a ㄹ-irregular verb: the final ㄹ drops before endings starting with ㄴ, ㅂ, or ㅅ (e.g., 나니, 납니다, 나세요).

senses.definition: To move through the air using wings or in an aircraft.

examples.text: 새가 하늘을 높이 날아요.
examples.translation: The bird is flying high in the sky.

examples.text: 비행기가 구름 위로 날고 있습니다.
examples.translation: The airplane is flying above the clouds.

senses.definition: To lower the body into a seated position on a chair, the floor, or a perch.

examples.text: 의자에 앉아요.
examples.translation: I sit on the chair.

examples.text: 새가 나뭇가지에 앉았어요.
examples.translation: The bird perched on the tree branch.

faults.quote: whereas 부지런히 하다 emphasizes working diligently.
faults.why: Pointless comparison to an arbitrary adverbial phrase instead of explaining usage.

senses.definition: To do a job or perform labor.

examples.text: 아버지는 회사에서 열심히 일합니다.
examples.translation: My father works hard at the company.

faults.quote: This is the most common, everyday word for buying things.
faults.why: Pure filler that restates the gloss without adding grammatical or usage info.

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.

examples.text: 시장에서 사과를 사요.
examples.translation: I buy apples at the market.

faults.quote: /alˈmo.a.ða/
faults.why: Wrong stress: 'almohada' is stressed on the 'a' (/almoˈaða/), not the 'o'.

senses.definition: A soft cushion used to support the head while sleeping in bed.

examples.text: Siempre pongo dos almohadas en la cama para dormir mejor.
examples.translation: I always put two pillows on the bed to sleep better.

faults.quote: In Spain and many parts of Latin America, 'la araña' also refers

examples.translation: I saw a big spider in the garden.

senses.definition: A large, decorative light fixture with several arms that hangs from the ceiling.

examples.text: La araña del salón es muy antigua.
examples.translation: The chandelier in the living room is very old.

notes: Often shortened to 'la bici' in everyday conversation. Use 'ir en bicicleta' or 'montar en bicicleta' for riding a bike.

senses.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle with pedals that you ride by pushing with your feet.

examples.text: Voy al trabajo en bicicleta todos los días.
examples.translation: I go to work by bike every day.

faults.quote: Used for both human and animal mouths, as well as openings of
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses without adding useful usage information.

senses.definition: The part of the face used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Abre la boca para tomar la medicina.
examples.translation: Open your mouth to take the medicine.

senses.definition: The entrance or opening of a tunnel, cave, subway station, or bottle.

examples.text: Te espero en la boca del metro.
examples.translation: I'll wait for you at the subway entrance.

faults.quote: This word is a direct phonetic loan from English. It is a
faults.why: Wordy etymology note; a learner needs the measure word instead.

examples.text: 我想买一个火腿三明治当午餐。
examples.translation: I want to buy a ham sandwich for lunch.

notes: Refers to rural farming areas and villages. Use 郊区 (jiāoqū) for the suburbs or outskirts of a city.

senses.definition: Land outside towns and cities, with fields and villages.

examples.text: 他老家在农村。
examples.translation: His family home is in the countryside.

faults.quote: 我们去海边看日出。
faults.why: Uses compound word 海边 (seaside) instead of 海 as an independent word.

faults.quote: 金黄色的麦浪像一片海洋。
faults.why: Uses a different word, 海洋 (ocean), rather than the headword 海.

faults.quote: A large lake or a great expanse of something.
faults.why: Mixes a literal地理 sense ('large lake' in place names) with the metaphorical 'vast expanse' sense.

faults.quote: Used both literally for the ocean and metaphorically for anything vast and
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; better to explain usage with 大海 / 海洋.

notes: In everyday speech, often used in two-syllable words like 大海 (dàhǎi, the sea) or 海边 (hǎibiān, the seaside/beach).

senses.definition: The large body of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface.

examples.text: 这是我第一次看海。
examples.translation: This is my first time seeing the sea.

senses.definition: A vast expanse or huge gathering of something, such as people, flowers, or clouds.

examples.text: 广场上到处都是人，像一片人海。
examples.translation: There were people everywhere in the square, like a sea of people.

faults.quote: 下午 refers specifically to the time from noon until evening.

notes: Placed before the clock time (e.g., 下午三点, 3 p.m.) and before the verb in a sentence.

examples.translation: I am free this afternoon.

notes: Counted with 把 (bǎ). In southern China, a small soup spoon is also commonly called 调羹 (tiáogēng).

examples.text: 请给我一把勺子喝汤。
examples.translation: Please give me a spoon to eat the soup.

faults.quote: The word often appears in compound words related to construction or nature
faults.why: Vague filler note; almost all common kanji appear in compounds.

faults.why: Cultural trivia, not linguistic usage advice needed by a learner.

examples.text: 皿を洗う。
examples.translation: I wash the plates.

faults.quote: Use '天気' when asking or talking about today's conditions
faults.why: Restates the basic definition without adding useful linguistic information.

senses.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place, such as sunshine, rain, or wind.

examples.text: 今日の天気はとてもいいです。
examples.translation: Today's weather is very good.

faults.quote: /kse.no.doˈçi.o/

faults.quote: Used specifically for a commercial establishment where people pay to stay overnight.

senses.definition: A building where travelers pay to stay for one or more nights.

examples.translation: The hotel is near the port.

faults.quote: /ta maˈʎa/
faults.why: IPA must be a transcription of the word without the article.

notes: For hair on the head, Greek uses the plural 'τα μαλλιά'; the singular 'το μαλλί' usually means 'wool'.
Do not confuse with 'η τρίχα', which refers to a single strand of hair or to body hair.

senses.definition: The mass of fine threads growing on a person's head.

examples.text: Έχει μακριά και ξανθά μαλλιά.
examples.translation: She has long, blonde hair.

faults.quote: eye; lookout; burner
faults.why: Includes 'lookout', which is not covered by any sense in the entry.

faults.quote: Also refers to the burners on a stove, which look like eyes.
faults.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding grammatical or usage guidance.

notes: Also means the 'evil eye' (e.g., 'έχει μάτι' = he/she has been jinxed).

senses.definition: One of the two organs in the face that you see with.

examples.text: Το παιδί άνοιξε το ένα του μάτι.
examples.translation: The child opened one of his eyes.

senses.definition: A heating element on the top of a stove.

examples.text: Άναψε το μάτι της κουζίνας για να βράσει το νερό.
examples.translation: He turned on the stove burner to boil the water.

faults.quote: Μου αρέσει να τρώω ένα γλυκό σταφύλι το απόγευμα.
faults.why: Unnatural; in Greek 'ένα σταφύλι' sounds like eating a single berry or unspecified bunch.

faults.quote: To σταφύλι generally refers to the fruit
faults.why: Uses Latin characters 'To' instead of Greek 'Το'.

notes: Often used as an uncountable singular in Greek ('τρώω σταφύλι' = I eat grapes), as well as in the plural ('σταφύλια'). A single grape berry is 'μια ρώγα σταφύλι'.

senses.definition: A small round green or dark purple fruit that grows in bunches on a vine and is eaten or used to make wine.

examples.text: Το φθινόπωρο τρώμε γλυκά σταφύλια.
examples.translation: In autumn we eat sweet grapes.

faults.quote: Used both to refer to one's own grandmother and as a respectful
faults.why: Restates the two senses; meanwhile a note on its irregular plural 'γιαγιάδες' is missing.

notes: Takes the irregular plural 'οι γιαγιάδες'.

senses.definition: The mother of one's father or mother.

examples.text: Η γιαγιά μου φτιάχνει την καλύτερη πίτα.
examples.translation: My grandmother makes the best pie.

senses.definition: A familiar and affectionate way to refer to or address an elderly woman.

examples.text: Καλημέρα, γιαγιά, πώς είστε σήμερα;
examples.translation: Good morning, grandma, how are you today?

faults.quote: /asˈte.os/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: the digraph ει is pronounced /i/, so it is /aˈsti.os/.

faults.quote: Use αστείος when something makes you laugh or smile, like a funny
faults.why: merely restates the definition and gloss.

notes: Declines in gender, number, and case (αστείος, αστεία, αστείο). The neuter singular το αστείο is also used as a noun meaning 'joke'.

senses.definition: Causing laughter or amusement.

examples.text: Είναι πολύ αστείος άνθρωπος και μας κάνει να γελάμε.
examples.translation: He is a very funny person and makes us laugh.

senses.definition: Odd, trivial, or ridiculous in a way that is not taken seriously.

examples.text: Φοράει ένα αστείο καπέλο στο πάρτι.
examples.translation: He is wearing a silly hat at the party.

faults.quote: The colour of a clear sky or the deep sea.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('the colour of') instead of a quality ('having the colour').

notes: Unlike most Greek adjectives, μπλε is indeclinable: it does not change form for gender, number, or case.

senses.definition: Having the colour of a clear sky or the deep sea.

examples.text: Ο ουρανός είναι μπλε σήμερα.
examples.translation: The sky is blue today.

faults.quote: The color of a lemon or a ripe banana.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('the color of') instead of a quality ('having the color').

faults.quote: Note that this is the primary word for the color yellow.
faults.why: Pure filler note that merely restates the gloss.

notes: Unlike borrowed colour words such as μπλε or ροζ, κίτρινος declines normally for gender, number, and case (κίτρινος, κίτρινη, κίτρινο).

senses.definition: Having the color of a lemon or a ripe banana.

examples.text: Το λεμόνι είναι κίτρινο.
examples.translation: The lemon is yellow.

notes: To mean 'never' in a full clause, ποτέ requires a negative particle such as δεν or μην before the verb (e.g., δεν πάω ποτέ — I never go). On its own as a short answer, Ποτέ! also means 'Never!'
In questions and conditional sentences without negation, it means 'ever' or 'at any time'.

senses.definition: At no time in the past or future.

examples.text: Δεν πάω ποτέ εκεί.
examples.translation: I never go there.

senses.definition: At any time, especially in questions or conditionals.

examples.text: Πήγες ποτέ στην Ελλάδα;
examples.translation: Have you ever been to Greece?

faults.quote: regardless of the gender or number of the noun it describes.
faults.why: Adverbs modify adjectives, verbs, or other adverbs, not nouns.

notes: As an adverb modifying an adjective, verb, or another adverb, πολύ is invariable (e.g., πολύ καλή — very good).
Do not confuse it with the adjective πολύς, πολλή, πολύ ('much, many, a lot of'), which declines to agree with the noun it modifies (e.g., πολλή δουλειά — a lot of work).

senses.definition: To a high degree.

examples.text: Είναι πολύ όμορφο.
examples.translation: It is very beautiful.

senses.definition: To a great extent or in a large amount.

examples.text: Δουλεύει πολύ σήμερα.
examples.translation: He is working a lot today.

faults.quote: Selalu is used for actions or states that happen without stopping
faults.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful grammar or usage notes.

notes: Usually placed directly before the verb or adjective it modifies (e.g., 'Dia selalu sibuk' — He is always busy).

senses.definition: At all times; on every occasion.

examples.text: Dia selalu datang tepat waktu setiap pagi.
examples.translation: He always comes on time every morning.

faults.quote: Use selamat tinggal only when you won't see the person for a
faults.why: Misses the crucial rule: only the person leaving says 'selamat tinggal' to those staying.

faults.quote: /səˈlamat tiŋˈɡal/
faults.why: In Indonesian, stress on 'tinggal' falls on the penultimate syllable: /ˈtiŋɡal/.

notes: Said by the person leaving to the person staying behind (literally 'safe staying'). The person staying replies 'selamat jalan' ('safe travels').
Quite formal or final; for casual everyday goodbyes, use 'sampai jumpa' ('see you') instead.

senses.definition: Said by someone who is leaving to those who are staying behind, especially when parting for a long time.

examples.text: Dia melambaikan tangan dan mengucapkan selamat tinggal sebelum naik kereta.
examples.translation: He waved his hand and said goodbye before boarding the train.

faults.quote: Selesai describes the state of something being finished, whether it is
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Do not confuse with 'habis', which means 'used up' or 'run out' (for food, money, time). Use 'selesai' for tasks, events, or activities reaching their end.
To say someone 'finishes' something (transitive), use the affixed form 'menyelesaikan'.

senses.definition: To come to an end, or to be completed.

examples.text: Pekerjaan rumah saya sudah selesai.
examples.translation: My homework is already finished.

examples.text: Film itu baru saja selesai.
examples.translation: That movie just finished.

faults.quote: Something that covers or obscures a surface or area completely.
faults.why: Poetic metaphor; in everyday Indonesian, 'menyelimuti' (verb) is used for this, not the noun.

faults.quote: Used primarily for bedding that provides warmth. Can also be used figuratively
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses in the entry.

notes: Adding the prefix 'ber-' gives 'berselimut' (to wear or be covered by a blanket), and 'me-...-i' gives 'menyelimuti' (to cover or blanket something).

senses.definition: A large piece of cloth used on a bed to keep warm while sleeping.

examples.text: Dia menarik selimut agar tidak kedinginan.
examples.translation: He pulled up the blanket so he wouldn't get cold.

faults.quote: Feeling comfortable, at ease, and free from worry or physical discomfort.
faults.why: 'Senang' does not mean physically comfortable or cozy in standard Indonesian (that is 'nyaman').

faults.quote: Duduk di taman ini sangat senang dan tenang.
faults.why: Ungrammatical; 'senang' describes a person's feeling, not an activity like sitting ('nyaman' or 'menyenangkan').
Missing the very common everyday sense 'to like; to enjoy doing something'.

faults.quote: Senang is the most common word for feeling happy, pleased, or glad
faults.why: Restates the glosses without adding useful information.

notes: Describes a person's feeling ('Saya senang' — I am happy). To say a thing or activity is pleasant or fun, use 'menyenangkan' ('Film itu menyenangkan' — That movie was fun).

senses.definition: Feeling pleased, glad, or satisfied about something.

examples.text: Saya senang bisa bertemu denganmu hari ini.
examples.translation: I am glad to be able to meet you today.

senses.definition: Finding pleasure in an activity or thing; fond of.

examples.text: Adik saya senang membaca buku cerita.
examples.translation: My younger sibling likes reading storybooks.

faults.quote: /duanɔːtʰit/
faults.why: Wrong vowel, final consonant, and missing tones for ดวงอาทิตย์ (/duaŋ˧.ʔaː˧.tʰit̚˦˥/).

corrected.headword: ดวงอาทิตย์
notes: The prefix and classifier ดวง is used for celestial bodies (like the sun, moon, and stars) and round or shining things.
In everyday speech, พระอาทิตย์ is more common than ดวงอาทิตย์; final ย์ is silent.

senses.definition: The star that gives the earth light and heat by day.

examples.text: ดวงอาทิตย์ขึ้นทางทิศตะวันออก
examples.translation: The sun rises in the east.
examples.matchedForm: ดวงอาทิตย์

corrected.headword: ข้อผิดพลาด
notes: Counted with the classifier ข้อ (e.g. ข้อผิดพลาดสามข้อ, 'three mistakes').
Unlike ผิด ('to be wrong'), which is a verb, ข้อผิดพลาด is a noun used especially in careful or work contexts; ความผิดพลาด is a close synonym.

senses.definition: Something done incorrectly, or an inaccurate judgment.

examples.text: เราต้องตรวจสอบรายงานนี้เพื่อหาข้อผิดพลาด
examples.translation: We must check this report to find any mistakes.
examples.matchedForm: ข้อผิดพลาด

examples.text: เขายอมรับว่านี่เป็นข้อผิดพลาดของเขาเอง
examples.translation: He admits that this was his own mistake.
examples.matchedForm: ข้อผิดพลาด

faults.quote: [1] (lifestyle) A young person who is fashionable
faults.why: Shades of one meaning ('teenager / young person'); example[1] just means teenagers.

notes: Literally 'young age' (วัย 'age/stage of life' + รุ่น 'generation/budding'); used both as a noun ('a teenager', classifier คน) and as a modifier (เช่น เพลงวัยรุ่น 'teen music').

senses.definition: A young person in their teens or early twenties, or young people as a group.

examples.text: วัยรุ่นไทยชอบไปเดินห้างสรรพสินค้าในวันหยุด
examples.translation: Thai teenagers like to go to the shopping mall on weekends.

examples.text: ร้านนี้เป็นที่นิยมของกลุ่มวัยรุ่น
examples.translation: This shop is popular among young people.

faults.quote: /ʔaː˨˩.kaːt̚˥˩/
faults.why: Wrong tones for อากาศ: อา is mid tone /˧/ and กาศ is low tone /˨˩/.

faults.quote: เปิดหน้าต่างเพื่อให้มีอากาศ fresh เข้ามา
faults.why: Untranslated English word 'fresh' mixed into the Thai example sentence.

faults.quote: [0] อากาศ covers both 'the air we breathe'
faults.why: Note [0] restates the senses; note [1] compares unrelated words for seasons.

notes: Final ศ is pronounced like a final /t/ stop; often paired with สภาพ in สภาพอากาศ ('weather conditions').

senses.definition: The conditions outside at a particular time, such as heat, coolness, rain, or sunshine.

examples.text: วันนี้อากาศดีมาก เหมาะกับการไปเดินเล่น
examples.translation: The weather is very nice today, great for going for a walk.

senses.definition: The invisible gas around the earth that people and animals breathe.

examples.text: เปิดหน้าต่างเพื่อให้มีอากาศบริสุทธิ์เข้ามา
examples.translation: Open the window to let fresh air in.

notes: Use ผนัง for the wall of a room or building (counted with ด้าน or ฝั่ง); use กำแพง for a freestanding outer wall, boundary wall, or city wall.

senses.definition: An upright side of a room or building that encloses or divides space.

examples.text: เขาทาสีผนังห้องนอนใหม่เป็นสีขาว
examples.translation: He repainted the bedroom wall white.

faults.quote: Used for both human and animal mouths, as well as the openings
faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses without adding usage information.

notes: Notice the common expressions 'boca arriba' (face up) and 'boca abajo' (face down).

senses.definition: The opening in the face of a person or animal used for eating, drinking, and speaking.

examples.text: Abre la boca para tomar la medicina.
examples.translation: Open your mouth to take the medicine.

senses.definition: The open end or entrance of something such as a cave, bottle, or subway station.

examples.text: La cueva tiene una boca muy oscura.
examples.translation: The cave has a very dark opening.

faults.quote: (status) The legal union between two people.
faults.why: 'Boda' means the wedding event, not the legal state of marriage ('matrimonio').

faults.quote: Ellos celebran el quinto aniversario de su matrimonio.
faults.why: The example does not contain the headword 'boda'.

notes: 'Boda' refers to the wedding ceremony and reception (also often used in the plural, 'las bodas', or in phrases like 'aniversario de bodas'). For the legal institution or state of being married, use 'el matrimonio'.

senses.definition: The ceremony and celebration when two people get married.

examples.text: La boda de mi hermana será en la playa.
examples.translation: My sister's wedding will be on the beach.

faults.why: Note mentions 'handbag/purse', a very common sense in Mexico, but senses omit it.

notes: In Mexico, 'bolsa' is the everyday word for a shopping bag, a handbag/purse (often called 'un bolso' in Spain), and a clothes pocket (alongside 'el bolsillo').

senses.definition: A flexible container made of plastic, paper, or cloth used for carrying or holding things.

examples.text: Llevo las manzanas en una bolsa de plástico.
examples.translation: I am carrying the apples in a plastic bag.

senses.definition: A small bag carried by a person (especially a woman) to hold personal items.

examples.text: Dejé mi celular en la bolsa.
examples.translation: I left my cell phone in my purse.

senses.definition: A small pouch sewn into or onto clothing for carrying small items.

examples.text: Metí las llaves en la bolsa del pantalón.
examples.translation: I put the keys in my pants pocket.

faults.quote: Used for drinks like water, wine, and beer.
faults.why: Obvious real-world fact that adds no linguistic or usage value.

notes: Followed by 'de' + noun without an article to say both what a bottle contains ('una botella de agua', a bottle of water) and what type of bottle it is ('una botella de vidrio', a glass bottle).

senses.definition: A container for liquids with a narrow neck, usually made of glass or plastic.

examples.text: Pusieron una botella de vino en la mesa.
examples.translation: They put a bottle of wine on the table.

faults.quote: सर्दी (sardī) can refer to both the weather season (winter) and
faults.why: Merely restates the three senses already listed in the entry.
Missing key dative construction: को सर्दी लगना (to feel cold / catch a cold).

notes: Do not confuse with ठंडा (ṭhaṇḍā), which is an adjective ('cold'), whereas सर्दी is a noun. Note that ठंड (ṭhaṇḍ) is a common synonym for cold weather.
To say someone feels cold or has caught a cold, use the dative construction: मुझे सर्दी लग रही है (I am feeling cold) or मुझे सर्दी लग गई है (I caught a cold).

senses.definition: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.

examples.text: सर्दी के मौसम में लोग गरम चाय पीते हैं।
examples.translation: People drink hot tea in the winter season.

senses.definition: Low temperature or the physical feeling of being cold.

examples.text: आज बाहर बहुत सर्दी है।
examples.translation: It is very cold outside today.

senses.definition: A common illness affecting the nose and throat, causing sneezing and a runny nose.

examples.text: मुझे सर्दी हो गई है।
examples.translation: I have caught a cold.

faults.quote: This term is a direct transliteration of the English 'traffic light'
faults.why: Obvious from the headword and gloss.

notes: In everyday speech, लाल बत्ती (lāl battī, literally 'red light') or सिग्नल (signal) is also very commonly used to refer to a traffic light.

senses.definition: A set of coloured lights at a road junction that control traffic.

examples.text: ट्रैफ़िक लाइट लाल होने पर रुकना चाहिए।
examples.translation: You should stop when the traffic light turns red.

faults.quote: A formal meeting where someone is asked questions to see if
faults.why: Too narrow; excludes media or journalistic interviews, which note[1] admits the word covers.

faults.quote: This is a common loanword from English used widely in professional
faults.why: Obvious loanword; misses useful collocations like इंटरव्यू देना (to be interviewed).

notes: Notice the verb direction in Hindi: a candidate or guest 'gives' an interview — इंटरव्यू देना (to be interviewed) — while the interviewer 'takes' it — इंटरव्यू लेना (to interview someone).
The formal Sanskrit-derived word साक्षात्कार (sākṣātkār) is used mainly in news broadcasts and official notices.

senses.definition: A formal meeting in which someone is asked questions to assess them for a job or admission, or to gather their views for the media.

examples.text: कल मेरा एक महत्वपूर्ण इंटरव्यू है।
examples.translation: I have an important interview tomorrow.

faults.why: Physical corner and street corner are shades of one meaning; 'geometry' domain is misleading.

faults.quote: corner, angle
faults.why: Geometric 'angle' in Hindi is कोण (koṇ), not कोना (konā).

faults.quote: Use 'कोना' for the interior angle of a room or a box.
faults.why: False restriction: कोना is used equally for exterior corners (as in example[0] 'table corner').

notes: As a regular masculine noun ending in -आ (-ā), it changes to कोने (kone) in the oblique singular (e.g., कमरे के कोने में — in the corner of the room) and in the direct plural.

senses.definition: The place, point, or area where two edges, walls, or streets meet.

examples.text: मेज़ का कोना नुकीला है।
examples.translation: The corner of the table is sharp.

examples.text: वह सड़क के कोने पर खड़ा है।
examples.translation: He is standing on the street corner.

faults.quote: feminine
faults.why: चम्मच is primarily masculine in standard Hindi dictionaries (some speakers use it as feminine).

faults.quote: It is a general term; if you specifically need a smaller
faults.why: Trivial filler using unscripted Romanized Hindi ('chota chammach').

notes: Usually masculine in standard Hindi (एक बड़ा चम्मच — a tablespoon, एक छोटा चम्मच — a teaspoon), though many speakers also treat it as feminine.

senses.definition: A small utensil with a shallow bowl at the end of a handle, used for eating, stirring, or serving food.

examples.text: उसने सूप पीने के लिए चम्मच का इस्तेमाल किया।
examples.translation: He used a spoon to eat the soup.

faults.quote: The domestic bird raised for its meat and eggs.
faults.why: 'thịt gà' means only chicken meat; the live bird is 'gà' or 'con gà'.

faults.quote: It refers to both the live animal as food source
faults.why: False: 'thịt gà' never refers to the live animal.

faults.quote: Người nông dân nuôi nhiều thịt gà trong trang trại.
faults.why: Absurd in Vietnamese ('raises much chicken meat'); one raises 'gà', not 'thịt gà'.

faults.quote: Chúng tôi ăn thịt gà cho bữa tối.
faults.why: 'cho bữa tối' is a calque of 'for dinner'; natural Vietnamese is 'vào bữa tối'.

notes: Combines 'thịt' (meat) and 'gà' (chicken). Refers only to the meat as food; the live bird is 'gà' (or 'con gà').

senses.definition: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.text: Tối nay nhà mình ăn thịt gà nhé.
examples.translation: Let's eat chicken for dinner tonight.

faults.quote: flesh, skin
faults.why: 'thịt' means flesh, not skin ('da'), which the definition itself excludes.

faults.quote: meat; flesh; body
faults.why: 'body' is not a gloss of either sense.

faults.quote: When used generally, thịt refers to animal meat used as food.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses without adding usage information.

notes: Placed before the name of an animal to name its meat: 'thịt bò' (beef), 'thịt lợn' (pork), 'thịt gà' (chicken). Does not usually include fish ('cá') or seafood ('hải sản').

senses.definition: The flesh of an animal eaten as food, especially of mammals and birds.

examples.text: Chúng tôi ăn thịt bò vào bữa tối.
examples.translation: We eat beef for dinner.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of a human or animal body between the skin and the bones.

examples.text: Vết thương sâu làm rách cả da lẫn thịt.
examples.translation: The deep wound tore both skin and flesh.

faults.why: Wrong initial consonant: 'th' in Vietnamese is aspirated /tʰ/, not unaspirated /t/.

notes: Takes the classifier 'con' ('một con thỏ'). Covers both rabbits and hares; a wild hare can be specified as 'thỏ rừng'.

senses.definition: A small animal with long ears, soft fur, and a short tail, kept as a pet or living in the wild.

examples.text: Con thỏ đang ăn cỏ ngoài vườn.
examples.translation: The rabbit is eating grass in the garden.

faults.quote: /tʰəːj21 tʰiat̚35/
faults.why: 'tiết' has unaspirated /t/ and diphthong /iə/, not aspirated /tʰ/ or /ia/.

faults.quote: Use thời tiết when talking about atmospheric conditions like rain
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage value.

notes: Do not confuse with 'khí hậu' (climate), which refers to the long-term weather pattern of a region.

senses.definition: The conditions of the air and sky at a particular time and place, such as sun, rain, wind, or cold.

examples.text: Thời tiết hôm nay rất đẹp.
examples.translation: The weather today is very nice.

examples.text: Thời tiết thay đổi thất thường khiến tôi dễ bị cảm.
examples.translation: The unpredictable weather makes me catch a cold easily.

faults.quote: Nhà tôi nuôi một con thú cưng rất đáng yêu.
faults.why: 'một con thú cưng' is awkward; 'thú cưng' is used generically without 'một con'.

notes: From 'thú' (animal) and 'cưng' (beloved, pampered). Usually used as a general term (e.g. 'nuôi thú cưng', to keep pets); for a specific animal at home, speakers normally name it directly ('con chó', 'con mèo').

senses.definition: An animal kept at home for companionship and pleasure.

examples.text: Chung cư này không cho phép nuôi thú cưng.
examples.translation: This apartment building does not allow keeping pets.

faults.quote: 那个女人是我的老师。
faults.why: Pointing out someone as '那个女人' is rude, contradicting the usage note.

notes: Referring to a specific person as 女人 (e.g., 那个女人) can sound blunt or disrespectful. In polite contexts, prefer 女士 (nǚ shì, lady/Ms.) or 女生 (nǚ shēng, girl/young woman).

senses.definition: An adult female person.

examples.text: 照片里的那个女人是谁？
examples.translation: Who is that woman in the photo?

faults.quote: evening, dusk, nightfall
faults.why: 'Evening' is too broad and overlaps with 晚上; 'dusk' or 'late afternoon' is primary.

notes: Refers specifically to the time around sunset as day turns to night, whereas 晚上 (wǎn shang) covers the whole evening and night.

senses.definition: The time at the end of the day just before night falls, around sunset.

examples.text: 傍晚的时候，公园里有很多人在散步。
examples.translation: Around dusk, there are many people taking a walk in the park.

faults.quote: The period of human development between childhood and adulthood.
faults.why: 青少年 means young people; the time period requires adding 时期 (as in the example).

notes: Combines 青年 (young adults) and 少年 (early teens/pre-teens). It is mostly used collectively in formal contexts, news, or public policy; in everyday conversation, people usually say 年轻人 (young people) or 中学生 (middle/high schoolers).

senses.definition: A young person in the transition from childhood to adulthood; teenagers and young adults collectively.

examples.text: 这个活动很受当地青少年的欢迎。
examples.translation: This activity is very popular among local youth.

faults.quote: In Mandarin, the 'zi' at the end is often pronounced
faults.why: Pronunciation note repeats reading; misses the common classifier 把 (bǎ) and mistranslates 凳子 as 'bench'.

notes: Takes the measure word 把 (bǎ), e.g., 一把椅子 (a chair). Refers to a seat with a backrest, unlike 凳子 (dèng zi, stool), which has no back.

senses.definition: A piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a backrest.

examples.text: 请坐在椅子上。
examples.translation: Please sit on the chair.

faults.quote: A projecting part on a wheel, comb, or saw
faults.why: Mechanical sense is not essential for an A2 beginner; keep only the anatomical tooth.
Missing useful note on 'pasta al dente', a very common expression for A2 learners.

notes: The phrase 'al dente' (literally 'to the tooth') describes pasta or rice cooked so it is still firm when bitten.

senses.definition: One of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.

examples.text: Ho un dolore forte a un dente.
examples.translation: I have a sharp pain in a tooth.

faults.quote: masculine
faults.why: Nouns in -ista are common gender (masculine or feminine depending on the person).

notes: Takes 'il' for a male dentist and 'la' for a female dentist; the plural is 'i dentisti' (masculine) or 'le dentiste' (feminine).

senses.definition: A doctor who takes care of people's teeth.

examples.text: Domani devo andare dal dentista per un controllo.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I have to go to the dentist for a check-up.

faults.quote: Used both for hot sandy regions like the Sahara
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia about polar deserts is unhelpful for a language learner.

faults.quote: A place that is completely empty of people.
faults.why: Figurative use is transparent from English and not a separate core sense for A2.

notes: Do not confuse with English 'dessert', which is 'il dolce' or 'il dessert' in Italian.

senses.definition: A large, dry area of land with very little rain and few plants.

examples.text: Il vento soffia forte nel deserto.
examples.translation: The wind blows hard in the desert.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'dito' (finger) with 'mano' (hand)
faults.why: No learner confuses 'dito' and 'mano'; instead, note 'il dito del piede' for toe.

notes: The plural is irregular and becomes feminine: 'le dita' (both for fingers as a set and for toes).
To be clear that you mean a toe rather than a finger, say 'il dito del piede' (literally 'finger of the foot').

senses.definition: One of the five long parts at the end of the hand.

examples.text: Mi sono chiuso un dito nella porta.
examples.translation: I caught my finger in the door.

senses.definition: One of the five parts at the end of the foot.

examples.text: Ho sbattuto il dito del piede contro il tavolo.
examples.translation: I stubbed my toe against the table.

faults.quote: Use 'divano' for any standard soft seat for multiple people
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding useful linguistic information.

faults.quote: While 'sofà' and 'canapè' exist, 'divano' is by far
faults.why: Unnecessary discussion of rare synonyms an A2 learner does not need.

senses.definition: A long, soft seat with a back and arms, for two or more people.

examples.text: Mi piace leggere sul divano.
examples.translation: I like to read on the sofa.

faults.quote: /kuanː kaː fɛ/
faults.why: Wrong vowel, missing tones, and bogus length marks; Hanoi IPA is /kwaːn˧˦ kaː˨˩ fe˧˧/.

faults.quote: Often shortened simply to 'quán cà' or 'cà phê'
faults.why: Never shortened to 'quán cà' in Vietnamese.

notes: In casual speech, people often just say đi cà phê ('to go for coffee') instead of naming the shop.
Traditional Vietnamese quán cà phê often have low stools on the pavement rather than indoor tables.

senses.definition: A small establishment where coffee, tea, and other drinks are served.

examples.text: Chúng tôi thường gặp nhau ở quán cà phê vào buổi sáng.
examples.translation: We usually meet at the café in the morning.

faults.quote: /kwən˨/
faults.why: Incomplete tone mark for huyền tone; Hanoi IPA is /kwən˨˩/.

faults.quote: In Vietnamese, 'quần' refers generally to trousers or pants
faults.why: Restates the definition; better to give the classifier (cái/chiếc) and common compounds.

notes: Takes the classifier cái or chiếc (e.g., một chiếc quần, 'a pair of trousers').
Used as the base for other legwear: quần đùi or quần soóc (shorts), quần bò (jeans), quần lót (underwear).

senses.definition: An outer garment covering the body from the waist down, with a separate part for each leg.

examples.text: Tôi đang tìm mua một chiếc quần mới.
examples.translation: I am looking to buy a new pair of trousers.

faults.quote: /kuaŋ˧˩ tɕuəŋ˨˩/
faults.why: Wrong vowel /uə/ instead of /ɨə/ in 'trường'; Hanoi IPA is /kwaːŋ˧˩˧ tɕɨəŋ˨˩/.

faults.quote: Often found at the center of major cities, serving as a
faults.why: Encyclopedic filler restating what a public square is.

senses.definition: An open public area in a town or city, usually surrounded by buildings.

examples.text: Nhiều người đang đi dạo ở quảng trường lớn.
examples.translation: Many people are walking in the large square.

faults.quote: quen can mean knowing a person, being familiar with a place
faults.why: Merely repeats the two sense definitions.

corrected.shortGloss: to know; to be familiar with; to be used to
notes: Do not confuse with biết, which means knowing facts, information, or how to do something rather than personal familiarity.

senses.definition: To know a person personally or be familiar with a place or thing.

examples.text: Tôi quen anh ấy từ lâu rồi.
examples.translation: I have known him for a long time.

senses.definition: To be accustomed or used to something through habit or experience.

examples.text: Tôi chưa quen thời tiết ở đây.
examples.translation: I am not used to the weather here yet.

faults.quote: Use quên when something slips your mind or you fail to
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0.

notes: Often followed by mất ('lost') as a particle to emphasize that something has slipped your mind: quên mất ('completely forgot').
Do not confuse with quen (no tone mark, 'to be familiar with'); the opposite of quên is nhớ ('to remember').

senses.definition: To be unable to remember a fact, information, or something one planned to do.

examples.text: Tôi quên tên của anh ấy mất rồi.
examples.translation: I forgot his name.

senses.definition: To leave something behind by mistake.

examples.text: Tôi quên ô ở nhà rồi.
examples.translation: I left my umbrella at home.

faults.quote: (time) The early part of the day.
faults.why: In everyday speech 'το πρωί' means morning; 'το πρωινό' as 'morning' is literary/poetic.

faults.quote: Το πρωινό είναι η αγαπημένη μου ώρα.
faults.why: Unnatural; a native speaker would say 'Το πρωί είναι η αγαπημένη μου ώρα της μέρας.'

notes: The noun 'το πρωινό' means 'breakfast', whereas 'το πρωί' is the normal word for 'morning'.
Comes from the adjective 'πρωινός, -ή, -ό' (morning, early), as in 'πρωινή βόλτα' (morning walk).

senses.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.

examples.text: Τρώω το πρωινό μου κάθε μέρα στις οκτώ.
examples.translation: I eat my breakfast every day at eight.

faults.quote: In Greek, the word 'ουρανός' refers to both the physical sky
faults.why: merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.

senses.definition: The space above the earth where you see the sun, moon, stars, and clouds.

examples.text: Ο ουρανός σήμερα είναι καθαρός και μπλε.
examples.translation: The sky is clear and blue today.

senses.definition: In some religions, the place where God lives and where good people go after they die.

examples.text: Λένε ότι οι καλοί άνθρωποι πάνε στον ουρανό.
examples.translation: They say that good people go to heaven.

faults.quote: /etaˈɾi.a/
faults.why: Wrong vowel: the first 'ε' is /e/ but 'αι' is also /e/, pronounced /eteˈɾi.a/.

notes: Often spelled 'εταιρία' in everyday writing, though 'εταιρεία' is the standard spelling.

senses.definition: A business organization that sells goods or services.

examples.text: Η εταιρεία μας προσφέρει νέες υπηρεσίες.
examples.translation: Our company offers new services.

notes: The feminine 'η γάτα' is the default word for any cat; the masculine 'ο γάτος' is used only to specify a male cat.
The diminutive 'το γατάκι' means 'kitten', or affectionately any cat.

senses.definition: A small furry animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet.

faults.why: As a loanword, 'το κέικ' is indeclinable (does not change in plural or genitive).

notes: Indeclinable loanword: its form stays 'κέικ' in all cases, singular and plural (e.g. 'τα κέικ').
Used for sponge, loaf, or bundt cakes; for a frosted layer cake or birthday cake, Greek uses 'η τούρτα'.

senses.definition: A sweet baked food made from flour, sugar, eggs, and butter, without cream layers or frosting.

examples.text: Έφτιαξα ένα σπιτικό κέικ σοκολάτας για τον απογευματινό καφέ.
examples.translation: I made a homemade chocolate cake for the afternoon coffee.

faults.quote: Used to express uncertainty or possibility. Unlike English, it is often
faults.why: Restates definition, and teaches literary inversion instead of everyday 'peut-être que' at A2.

notes: Usually placed after the conjugated verb (Il viendra peut-être). At the start of an everyday sentence, it is followed by 'que': Peut-être qu'il viendra.

senses.definition: Used to say that something is possible or may be true.

examples.text: Il viendra peut-être demain.
examples.translation: Maybe he will come tomorrow.

faults.quote: Complete or occupied with many things or people.
faults.why: Being full of people is the same meaning as being full of something.
Missing the very common everyday construction 'plein de' meaning 'lots of'.

faults.quote: Do not confuse 'plein' (full) with 'vide' (empty).
faults.why: Unhelpful filler note; feminine form and 'plein de' usage are needed instead.

notes: Feminine form: pleine (/plɛn/, nasal vowel is lost). Takes 'de' before a noun: plein d'eau (full of water).
In everyday speech, 'plein de' (invariable) is very common for 'lots of': J'ai plein d'amis.

senses.definition: Holding or containing as much as possible, with no empty space left.

examples.text: Le verre est plein d'eau.
examples.translation: The glass is full of water.

examples.text: Le restaurant est plein ce soir.
examples.translation: The restaurant is full tonight.

senses.definition: (plein de, informal) A large number or amount of.

examples.text: Il y a plein de monde dans la rue.
examples.translation: There are lots of people in the street.

faults.quote: To have tears in the eyes, for example when peeling onions.
faults.why: Shedding tears from onions is the same basic sense; English gloss is also unnatural.

faults.quote: Use 'pleurer' for both emotional crying and simply shedding tears
faults.why: Restates the two senses instead of giving useful grammar or usage.

senses.definition: To produce tears because of sadness, pain, strong emotion, or irritation to the eyes.

examples.text: Elle commence à pleurer en regardant ce film triste.
examples.translation: She starts to cry while watching this sad movie.

examples.text: Couper des oignons me fait pleurer.
examples.translation: Cutting onions makes me cry.

faults.quote: Cette table a un bois bien poli.
faults.why: Unnatural French phrasing and awkward English translation ('has a very smooth wood').

faults.quote: Poli comes from the verb polir (to polish), which is why
faults.why: Etymology filler; preposition usage ('poli avec') and antonym ('impoli') are more useful.

notes: Feminine: polie (pronounced the same). Opposite: impoli (impolite, rude). Takes 'avec' or 'envers' before a person.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: having good manners and showing respect for others.

examples.text: Il est toujours très poli avec ses voisins.
examples.translation: He is always very polite to his neighbors.

senses.definition: Of a surface: made smooth and shiny by rubbing.

examples.text: La table est en bois poli.
examples.translation: The table is made of polished wood.

faults.quote: Use "porter" both for wearing clothes and accessories (like a scarf
faults.why: merely repeats the two senses given right below.

notes: Also used for hair, beards, and perfume: porter la barbe (to have a beard), porter du parfum (to wear perfume).

senses.definition: To have clothes, shoes, jewelry, or glasses on your body.

examples.text: Il aime porter un costume bleu au bureau.
examples.translation: He likes to wear a blue suit to the office.

senses.definition: To hold something or someone and take them from one place to another.

examples.text: Elle m'aide à porter les sacs de courses.
examples.translation: She helps me carry the shopping bags.

faults.quote: Used in the phrase 'ser un queso' in some regions
faults.why: Obscure regional slang not used in Mexico and unhelpful for A2 learners.

notes: Usually an uncountable noun when speaking in general ('Compré queso'), though it can be countable when referring to whole wheels or types of cheese.
In Mexico, 'quesillo' (or 'queso Oaxaca') is a very popular stringy white cheese, whereas 'queso' is the general term.

senses.definition: A food made from the pressed curds of milk.

examples.text: Me gusta ponerle mucho queso a mis tacos.
examples.translation: I like to put a lot of cheese on my tacos.

faults.quote: Like in English, 'ratón' refers to both the small rodent
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already shown in the entry.
In Mexico, the English loanword 'mouse' is commonly preferred for the computer device.

notes: In Mexico, people very often use the English loanword 'el mouse' for a computer mouse alongside 'ratón'.
The plural is 'los ratones' (adding '-es' and dropping the written accent).
Do not confuse 'ratón' (mouse) with 'la rata' (rat), which is a larger rodent.

senses.definition: A small rodent with pointed snout and a long tail.

examples.text: El gato atrapó un ratón en el jardín.
examples.translation: The cat caught a mouse in the yard.

senses.definition: A small hand-held device moved on a flat surface to control the cursor on a computer screen.

examples.text: Haz clic con el botón derecho del ratón.
examples.translation: Click with the right mouse button.

notes: In Mexico, you will very often hear the short form 'el refri' in everyday conversation.
In Spain and the Caribbean, 'la nevera' is the standard word for a refrigerator; in Mexico, 'hielera' is used for a cooler box.

senses.definition: An appliance used to keep food and drinks cold.

examples.text: Voy a guardar la leche en el refrigerador.
examples.translation: I am going to put the milk in the refrigerator.

faults.quote: A thing that is obtained for free or at no cost.
faults.why: A promotional gift is just a shade of the main meaning 'gift'.

notes: The phrase 'de regalo' means 'as a gift' or 'for free' (e.g., 'Me dieron una bolsa de regalo').
Do not confuse the noun 'el regalo' with 'regalo' ('I give as a gift'), the 'yo' form of the verb 'regalar'.

senses.definition: Something given to someone without payment, especially to celebrate an occasion or show affection.

examples.text: Le compré un regalo a mi hermano por su cumpleaños.
examples.translation: I bought a gift for my brother for his birthday.

faults.quote: While English uses two different words for 'clock' and 'watch'
faults.why: Restates the glosses without giving useful information on how to distinguish them.

notes: The plural is 'los relojes'.
To specify when needed, use 'reloj de pared' (wall clock), 'reloj despertador' (alarm clock), or 'reloj de pulsera' (wristwatch).

senses.definition: A device hung on a wall or placed on furniture to show the time.

examples.text: El reloj de la pared marca las tres.
examples.translation: The wall clock shows three o'clock.

senses.definition: A small timepiece worn on the wrist to tell the time.

examples.text: Me compré un reloj nuevo para correr.
examples.translation: I bought a new watch for running.

faults.quote: Use 아름답다 for something that is pleasing to the eyes
faults.why: Restates sense 0 instead of giving grammar (such as ㅂ-irregular conjugation).

faults.quote: Refers to something that is wonderful or touching
faults.why: Defines an adjective as 'Refers to something' instead of a quality.

notes: Irregular ㅂ adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (아름다워요, 아름다운).
Compared with 예쁘다 (pretty, cute), which is used for everyday things, people, or small items, 아름답다 feels grander or more poetic, and also describes inner qualities or deeds.

senses.definition: Very pleasing to look at or listen to.

examples.text: 꽃이 정말 아름답다.
examples.translation: The flower is truly beautiful.

senses.definition: Of a person's heart or actions: admirable and moving.

examples.text: 그녀의 마음씨는 참 아름답다.
examples.translation: She has a truly beautiful heart.

faults.quote: Used when a situation, place, or action carries a real chance
faults.why: Restates the definition.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 어렵다 (to be difficult); while both sound similar
faults.why: 위험하다 and 어렵다 do not sound similar; artificial warning.
Physical danger and risk of a bad outcome are one sense of 위험하다.

notes: Formed from the noun 위험 (danger, risk) + 하다; conjugates as 위험해요 (polite) and 위험한 before a noun.

senses.definition: Likely to cause harm, injury, or a bad outcome.

examples.text: 혼자서 밤에 그 골목길을 걸어가는 것은 위험합니다.
examples.translation: Walking down that alley alone at night is dangerous.

examples.text: 지금 그 사업에 투자하는 것은 너무 위험해요.
examples.translation: Investing in that business right now is too risky.

faults.quote: Use 가볍다 when something weighs very little. It is also used figuratively
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the ㅂ-irregular conjugation.

notes: Irregular ㅂ adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (가벼워요, 가벼운).
Opposite of 무겁다 (heavy; serious).

senses.definition: Weighing very little; easy to lift.

examples.text: 이 가방은 정말 가벼워요.
examples.translation: This bag is really light.

senses.definition: Not serious, intense, or heavy in degree.

examples.text: 가벼운 운동을 시작했어요.
examples.translation: I started some light exercise.

faults.quote: use the polite form '배고파요' or the honorific '배고프세요'
faults.why: For elders or in formal settings, the honorific lexical form 시장하시다 (시장하세요) is normally used.

faults.quote: You cannot say 'I hunger' as an action.
faults.why: Unhelpful remark about English; misses ㅡ-irregular conjugation and optional subject particle 가.

notes: From 배 (stomach) + 고프다 (empty, hungry); also often written with a particle as 배가 고프다.
Drops ㅡ before -아/-어: 배고파요.
When speaking to or about someone older or of higher status, the honorific word 시장하시다 (시장하세요) is preferred over 배고프시다.

senses.definition: Feeling the need to eat food.

examples.text: 점심을 안 먹어서 너무 배고파요.
examples.translation: I didn't eat lunch, so I am very hungry.

faults.why: Both senses describe something feeling new or fresh; no examples are provided.

faults.quote: When you see something you've never encountered before, it feels '새롭다'
faults.why: Restates the definition and misses the ㅂ-irregular conjugation.

notes: Irregular ㅂ adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel (새로워요, 새로운).
Unlike the determiner 새 (brand-new, as in 새 옷 'new clothes'), 새롭다 is a full adjective and often describes things, ideas, or experiences that feel fresh or novel.

senses.definition: Not existing or experienced before; feeling fresh or different from before.

examples.text: 새로운 환경에 적응하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.translation: Adjusting to a new environment is not easy.

examples.text: 고향에 오랜만에 오니 기분이 새로워요.
examples.translation: Coming back to my hometown after a long time feels fresh.

faults.why: Missing crucial usage note: 'écouter' is directly transitive (no 'à' unlike English 'listen to').

notes: Takes a direct object with no preposition: 'écouter la musique' (to listen to music).
Unlike 'entendre' (to hear, which happens without trying), 'écouter' means actively paying attention to a sound.

senses.definition: To pay attention to a sound or to someone speaking.

examples.text: J'aime écouter les oiseaux chanter le matin.
examples.translation: I like to listen to the birds singing in the morning.

senses.definition: To follow someone's advice or act on what they say.

examples.text: Tu devrais écouter tes parents.
examples.translation: You should listen to your parents.

faults.quote: Takes the auxiliary verb avoir in compound tenses.
faults.why: Almost all French verbs take 'avoir'; an irregular verb needs its key forms noted instead.
Writing words, writing to someone, and writing a book are shades of one meaning.

notes: Irregular verb: past participle 'écrit', plural present 'nous écrivons, vous écrivez, ils écrivent'.
Takes 'à' before the person receiving a message: 'écrire à un ami' (to write to a friend).

senses.definition: To form letters or words on a surface or screen, or to compose a text or message.

examples.text: Écris-moi quand tu arrives.
examples.translation: Write to me when you arrive.

examples.text: Victor Hugo a écrit Les Misérables.
examples.translation: Victor Hugo wrote Les Misérables.

faults.quote: (hug) To take someone into your arms.
faults.why: In modern everyday French, 'embrasser' means 'to kiss'; 'to hug' is literary/dated and already in the note.

notes: False friend: in modern everyday French, 'embrasser' means 'to kiss' (on the lips or on the cheeks in greeting). To say 'to hug', use 'serrer dans ses bras' or 'faire un câlin'.

senses.definition: To touch someone with your lips to greet them or show affection.

examples.text: Elle aime embrasser ses parents avant de partir.
examples.translation: She likes to kiss her parents goodbye before leaving.

faults.quote: Used to describe someone who is physically well and strong.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding grammatical or usage information.

notes: Invariable phrase used of people and animals. Do not confuse with 'sain', which usually describes healthy food, air, or habits.

senses.definition: Of a person or animal: physically well and free from illness.

examples.text: Grâce au sport, il est en bonne santé.
examples.translation: Thanks to sports, he is in good health.

faults.quote: /baŋ.ca/
faults.why: Wrong transcription: 'k' before back vowel 'a' is velar /k/, not palatal /c/.

faults.quote: Used in the same way as the English word 'bank'.
faults.why: Both notes are filler; instead note the irregular stress on the first syllable and 'bank'.

notes: Stress is on the first syllable ('ban-ka), unlike most Turkish words.
Do not confuse with 'bank', which means a park bench.

senses.definition: A financial institution or building where people keep, borrow, or exchange money.

examples.text: Yarın sabah bankaya gideceğim.
examples.translation: I will go to the bank tomorrow morning.

faults.quote: /ˈbaɲo/
faults.why: Turkish does not have the palatal nasal /ɲ/; it is pronounced /ˈban.jo/.

faults.quote: Used both for the room with a shower or tub and for
faults.why: Restates the senses; better to note the collocation 'banyo yapmak' and difference from 'tuvalet'.

notes: For the act of bathing or showering, use the verb 'banyo yapmak' (to take a bath/shower).
A 'banyo' has a shower or bathtub; a room with only a toilet and sink is called 'tuvalet'.

senses.definition: A room in a home containing a bath or shower, and usually a sink and toilet.

examples.text: Banyo koridorun sonunda.
examples.translation: The bathroom is at the end of the hall.

senses.definition: An act of washing one's body in a bathtub or shower.

examples.text: Çocuklar akşamları banyo yapmayı sever.
examples.translation: Children like taking a bath in the evenings.

faults.quote: A specific curved glass used traditionally in Turkey for drinking black tea.
faults.why: Oversplit: 'bardak' alone does not mean a tulip tea glass; the example uses 'çay bardağı'.

faults.quote: glass; cup; mug
faults.why: Includes 'mug', which is omitted from the senses and contrasted in the notes.

notes: The final 'k' softens to 'ğ' before a vowel suffix: 'bardağı' (the glass), 'bardağa' (into the glass).
Covers drinking glasses as well as paper or plastic cups. A small cup with a handle (for coffee or tea) is 'fincan', and a large mug is 'kupa'.

senses.definition: A container without a handle, made of glass, plastic, or paper, used for drinking liquids.

examples.text: Bardağa biraz su doldurdum.
examples.translation: I poured some water into the glass.

examples.text: Bir bardak çay içelim mi?
examples.translation: Shall we drink a glass of tea?
