faults.why: 'Duduk' and 'tidur' do not look or sound alike.

faults.quote: to sit; to reside
faults.why: Includes the obsolete 'reside' sense.

notes: Covers both the action 'to sit down' and the state 'to be sitting'. Notice the related verbs 'menduduki' (to occupy/sit on) and 'mendudukkan' (to seat someone).

senses.definition: To rest the body on a chair or the floor with the weight supported by the buttocks, or to move into this position.

examples.text: Silakan duduk di kursi itu.
examples.translation: Please sit in that chair.

faults.quote: Dunia comes from Arabic via loan, and it is used both
faults.why: Etymology and restating the two senses do not help an A2 learner.

notes: Often used in the polite expression 'meninggal dunia' (to pass away, literally 'to leave the world').

senses.definition: The earth and all its countries and peoples.

examples.text: Dia ingin keliling dunia.
examples.translation: He wants to travel around the world.

senses.definition: A sphere of activity, interest, or a specific domain of life.

examples.text: Dia bekerja di dunia pendidikan.
examples.translation: She works in the world of education.

faults.quote: /iːmeɪl/
faults.why: Uses English vowel length and diphthong phonemes rather than Indonesian phonology.

notes: While 'surel' (surat elektronik) is the official Indonesian term, 'email' is much more common in both everyday and professional use.

senses.definition: A message sent and received electronically over the internet, or the system for sending such messages.

examples.text: Saya mengirim email kepada klien saya pagi ini.
examples.translation: I sent an email to my client this morning.

faults.quote: Enak is extremely versatile. While it most commonly describes delicious food
faults.why: merely summarizes the three senses already shown below.

faults.quote: My body doesn't feel very well today.
faults.why: Literal calque of the idiom 'tidak/kurang enak badan' ('to feel unwell').

notes: In the health sense, it is most commonly used in the phrase 'tidak enak badan' or 'kurang enak badan' (feeling unwell / under the weather).

senses.definition: Of food or drink: having a very pleasing taste.

examples.text: Makanan ini sangat enak dan gurih.
examples.translation: This food is very delicious and savory.

senses.definition: Providing physical comfort or a pleasant feeling.

examples.text: Tempat tidur ini empuk dan enak untuk tidur.
examples.translation: This bed is soft and comfortable for sleeping.

senses.definition: Of the body or one's mood: feeling healthy, well, or at ease.

examples.text: Badan saya kurang enak hari ini.
examples.translation: I'm not feeling very well today.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'scrivere' (to write)
faults.why: Learners do not confuse 'disegnare' and 'scrivere'; note is missing first-person spelling/stress rule.

notes: While 'disegnare' covers both drawing and designing (especially fashion or objects), use 'progettare' for the technical planning of buildings, machines, or systems.
In the 'noi' form (disegniamo), the 'i' is kept in spelling after 'gn'. Takes 'avere' in compound tenses.

senses.definition: To create a picture, image, or shape using a pencil, pen, or other tool.

examples.text: Mi piace disegnare ritratti a matita nel mio tempo libero.
examples.translation: I like to draw pencil portraits in my free time.

senses.definition: To plan and create the form or appearance of clothes, furniture, or other objects.

examples.text: La mia amica vuole disegnare abiti da sposa.
examples.translation: My friend wants to design wedding dresses.

faults.quote: funny; amusing
faults.why: Omits 'fun / entertaining', the core translation of the second sense.
Missing essential grammar note that -e adjectives only change for number (-e / -i), not gender.

notes: Like all adjectives ending in -e, it has the same form for masculine and feminine singular, changing only in the plural (divertenti).
Covers both things that make you laugh ('funny') and things that are enjoyable to do ('fun').

senses.definition: Making people laugh.

examples.text: Quel film comico è molto divertente.
examples.translation: That comedy film is very funny.

senses.definition: Enjoyable and pleasant to do or experience.

examples.text: La festa di ieri sera è stata davvero divertente.
examples.translation: Last night's party was really fun.

faults.quote: Questo caffè è troppo dolce senza abbastanza amaro.
faults.why: 'Senza abbastanza amaro' is unnatural and unidiomatic in Italian.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'caro', which means dear
faults.why: Notes restate senses and warn against an unlikely confusion instead of explaining -e adjective agreement.

notes: Has the same form for masculine and feminine singular (dolce), changing to 'dolci' in the plural.
As a masculine noun (il dolce, i dolci), it means 'dessert', 'cake', or 'sweets'.

senses.definition: Having a taste like sugar or honey.

examples.text: Questo caffè è troppo dolce per i miei gusti.
examples.translation: This coffee is too sweet for my taste.

senses.definition: Pleasant, soft, and not harsh or severe.

examples.text: La nonna ha una voce molto dolce.
examples.translation: Grandma has a very gentle voice.

faults.quote: The day after today.
faults.why: Noun definition for an adverb; should be 'On the day after today'.

faults.quote: Chi sa cosa ci riserva il domani.
faults.why: 'Il domani' is a masculine noun meaning 'the future', not an A2 adverb sense.

notes: Used without a preposition to say 'on': 'domani lavoro' (I work tomorrow). Combine directly with parts of the day: 'domani mattina' (tomorrow morning), 'domani sera' (tomorrow evening).
'A domani!' means 'See you tomorrow!'

senses.definition: On or for the day after today.

examples.text: Domani ho un esame importante.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I have an important exam.

faults.quote: Used for both the unit of time (60 seconds) and
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; misses the common colloquial pronunciation 'dakka'.

notes: In everyday speech, it is very often pronounced 'dakka', especially in the phrase 'bir dakika' (wait a minute).
Do not confuse with 'an' (moment), which refers to an instant or a specific point in time.

senses.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.

examples.text: Bir saat altmış dakikadır.
examples.translation: One hour is sixty minutes.

senses.definition: A very short period of time; a moment.

examples.text: Bir dakika bekleyin, hemen geliyorum.
examples.translation: Wait a moment, I am coming right away.

notes: A compound verb formed from 'dans' (dance) and 'etmek' (to do). Before suffixes starting with a vowel, the 't' softens to 'd' (e.g., 'dans ediyor', 'dans edeceğim').

senses.definition: To move one's body rhythmically to music.

examples.text: Müzik başladığında herkes dans etmeye başladı.
examples.translation: When the music started, everyone began to dance.

faults.quote: /daːˈjɯ/
faults.why: The first vowel is short in standard Turkish: /daˈjɯ/.

faults.quote: Yaşlı dayı bankta oturup gazetemsi okuyordu.
faults.why: 'gazetemsi' (newspaper-ish) is a corrupt typo for 'gazetesini' (his newspaper).

faults.quote: maternal uncle; tough guy
faults.why: 'tough guy' is not covered by the senses.

notes: Turkish distinguishes uncles by side of the family: 'dayı' is your mother's brother, while 'amca' is your father's brother.
Also used colloquially to address or refer to an older man, though 'amca' is generally more polite with strangers.

senses.definition: The brother of one's mother.

examples.text: Yarın dayım bizi ziyarete gelecek.
examples.translation: Tomorrow my uncle is coming to visit us.

senses.definition: An informal form of address or reference for an older man.

examples.text: Yaşlı dayı bankta oturup gazetesini okuyordu.
examples.translation: The old fellow was sitting on the bench reading his newspaper.

faults.quote: A large, overwhelming quantity or expanse of something.
faults.why: Poetic metaphor ('sea of X'), not a distinct everyday sense for an A2 learner.

faults.quote: Deniz primarily refers to the sea or ocean, but in
faults.why: Restates the definitions without giving useful usage information.

notes: Notice the common phrase 'denize girmek' (literally 'to enter the sea'), which is the standard way to say 'to go swimming in the sea'.

senses.definition: The large body of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface, or a specific part of it.

examples.text: Yaz aylarında denize girmeyi çok seviyorum.
examples.translation: I love swimming in the sea during the summer months.

faults.quote: study, do homework
faults.why: 'do homework' is 'ödev yapmak'; 'ders çalışmak' means to study.

notes: A compound verb made from 'ders' (lesson) and 'çalışmak' (to work/study). Do not confuse it with 'ödev yapmak' (to do homework).
Used when studying in general; to specify the subject studied, use 'çalışmak' directly with the subject name (e.g., 'matematik çalışmak' — to study math).

senses.definition: To spend time learning about a subject or preparing for school and exams.

examples.text: Sınav için bütün gece ders çalışmak zorundayım.
examples.translation: I have to study all night for the exam.

faults.quote: [1] (hill) A very high hill.
faults.why: 山 does not distinguish mountain and hill; both belong in one sense.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'hill' (sometimes expressed specifically as 小山)
faults.why: Redundant with note 0 and weirdly formulated; missing the measure word 座.

notes: Counted with the measure word 座 (zuò): 一座山 (a mountain).
Covers both mountains and hills; a small hill can be called 小山 (xiǎoshān).

senses.definition: A mountain or hill.

examples.text: 周末我们去爬山吧。
examples.translation: Let's go hike in the mountains this weekend.

examples.text: 那座山很高。
examples.translation: That mountain is very high.

notes: Literally 'glass cup': 玻璃 (glass, the material) + 杯 (cup). Unlike 杯子 (bēizi), which can be any cup or mug, 玻璃杯 is only for one made of glass.

senses.definition: A container made of glass used for drinking.

examples.text: 请帮我拿一个玻璃杯。
examples.translation: Please get me a glass.

faults.quote: 书桌 specifically refers to a desk used for reading, writing, or working
faults.why: Restates the definition; should give the measure word 张 instead.

notes: Counted with the measure word 张 (zhāng): 一张书桌 (a desk).
Literally 'book table'. Do not confuse with 桌子 (zhuōzi), the general word for any table.

senses.definition: A table for reading, writing, or working at.

examples.text: 他的书桌上放着一台电脑和几本书。
examples.translation: There is a computer and a few books on his desk.

faults.quote: 暴风雨 refers specifically to a storm with strong winds and heavy rain.
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the definition; should give the measure word 场.

notes: Counted with the measure word 场 (chǎng): 一场暴风雨 (a rainstorm).

senses.definition: A storm with strong winds and heavy rain.

examples.text: 一场暴风雨马上就要来了。
examples.translation: A rainstorm is on its way.

faults.quote: Something that is very popular or trending right now.
faults.why: Sense 1 is an adjective ('popular'), not a noun ('something popular'), or belongs underanger.

notes: Commonly used in expressions about anger, such as 发火 (fāhuǒ, to lose one's temper).
Also very common as an adjective meaning 'popular, trending': 这部电影最近很火 (This movie is very popular lately).

senses.definition: Flames, heat, and light produced when something burns.

examples.text: 大家围坐在火旁边取暖。
examples.translation: Everyone sat around the fire to keep warm.

senses.definition: Strong anger or temper.

examples.text: 别惹他发火。
examples.translation: Don't make him lose his temper.

faults.quote: το γράμμα means both a handwritten or printed letter sent
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

notes: Irregular neuter noun in -μα: genitive του γράμματος, plural τα γράμματα.

senses.definition: A written or printed message sent to someone by post.

examples.text: Έλαβα ένα γράμμα από τη φίλη μου χθες.
examples.translation: I received a letter from my friend yesterday.

senses.definition: A symbol of the alphabet used in writing.

examples.text: Κάθε λέξη αρχίζει με ένα γράμμα.
examples.translation: Every word begins with a letter.

faults.quote: Ο συνάδελφος μου με βοήθησε με την αναφορά.
faults.why: Missing second-syllable enclitic accent on proparoxytone noun; must be 'Ο συνάδελφός μου'.

faults.quote: Unlike some English terms, 'συνάδελφος' can imply a professional bond
faults.why: English 'colleague' has the exact same breadth of meaning; note is redundant with definition.

notes: Used for both genders with the appropriate article: ο συνάδελφος (male), η συνάδελφος (female).

senses.definition: A person you work with or who shares the same profession.

examples.text: Ο συνάδελφός μου με βοήθησε με την αναφορά.
examples.translation: My colleague helped me with the report.

faults.quote: or simply τηλεόραση when referring to the physical set.
faults.why: Saying a word is shortened to itself makes no sense.

faults.quote: television, TV set, screen
faults.why: 'Screen' is οθόνη in Greek, not τηλεόραση.

notes: To say 'on television', Greek uses the preposition σε: στην τηλεόραση.

senses.definition: An electronic device with a screen used for watching broadcast programmes.

examples.text: Άνοιξα την τηλεόραση για να δω τις ειδήσεις.
examples.translation: I turned on the television to watch the news.

senses.definition: The system or medium of broadcasting programmes for public viewing.

examples.text: Δεν βλέπω συχνά τηλεόραση.
examples.translation: I don't watch television often.

faults.quote: (device) A device that performs mathematical calculations.
faults.why: Alone, υπολογιστής always means 'computer' in modern everyday Greek; 'calculator' is κομπιουτεράκι or αριθμομηχανή.

faults.quote: I am opening the computer to check my emails.
faults.why: Calque of 'ανοίγω'; in English you 'turn on' a computer, not 'open' it.

notes: In formal contexts, often called ηλεκτρονικός υπολογιστής (abbreviated Η/Υ).
Do not confuse with το κομπιουτεράκι or η αριθμομηχανή ('pocket calculator').

senses.definition: An electronic machine used for work, storing data, and browsing the internet.

examples.text: Ανοίγω τον υπολογιστή για να δω τα email μου.
examples.translation: I am turning on the computer to check my emails.

faults.quote: While it means 'goodbye', it is often used as a casual 'see
faults.why: Contradicts note[1]; in Mexico 'adiós' is not a casual 'see you later' with friends.

faults.quote: goodbye; see you later
faults.why: 'See you later' is misleading for 'adiós', which literally and typically means 'goodbye'.

notes: In Mexico, 'adiós' can sound quite final with friends or family; for everyday partings, 'hasta luego' or 'nos vemos' are more common.
Also used in Mexico as a polite greeting when walking past someone in the street without stopping.

senses.definition: Said when leaving someone or when someone is leaving.

faults.quote: Used to talk about the current moment.
faults.why: First sentence restates the definition; the 'ahorita' point should be clear and direct.

notes: In Mexico, the diminutive 'ahorita' is extremely common in everyday speech and can mean 'right now', 'in a little while', or 'just a moment ago' depending on context.

senses.definition: At the present time or moment.

examples.text: Ahora tengo mucho trabajo.
examples.translation: I have a lot of work now.

senses.definition: Very soon, or just a moment ago.

examples.text: Vamos a comer ahora.
examples.translation: We are going to eat right now.

faults.quote: /eks.tɾaŋˈxe.ɾo/
faults.why: IPA omits 'al' from the headword 'al extranjero'.

senses.definition: To or toward a country other than one's own.

examples.text: Muchos jóvenes viajan al extranjero después de graduarse.
examples.translation: Many young people travel abroad after graduating.

faults.why: For Mexican Spanish, fails to mention that 'allá' and 'ahí' are much more common.

notes: Refers to a specific place away from the speaker. In Mexico, 'ahí' (nearby or general 'there') and 'allá' (further away or less specific) are much more common in everyday speech.

senses.definition: In or at that place, away from the speaker.

examples.text: Dejé las llaves allí, sobre la mesa.
examples.translation: I left the keys there, on the table.

faults.quote: Viven en un edificio muy alto.
faults.why: 'Edificio alto' (tall building) belongs to sense 0 (vertical stature), not sense 1 (elevated position/high).

faults.quote: Refers to a sound that is very loud or powerful.
faults.why: Defines an adjective with 'Refers to a sound that is...' instead of as a quality.

faults.quote: Used for both physical height in people and elevated position in things.
faults.why: Merely restates senses 0 and 1 without adding usage information.

notes: With 'ser', 'alto' describes permanent height (Es muy alto). Notice that as a noun, 'el alto' means 'stop' on traffic signs in Mexico (hacer alto).

senses.definition: Of a person, building, or tree: of more than average height from bottom to top.

examples.text: Su hermano mayor es muy alto.
examples.translation: His older brother is very tall.

examples.text: Viven en un edificio muy alto.
examples.translation: They live in a very tall building.

senses.definition: Far above the ground, or great in amount, level, or degree.

examples.text: Los precios están muy altos este año.
examples.translation: Prices are very high this year.

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: strong and easy to hear.

examples.text: La música está demasiado alta.
examples.translation: The music is too loud.

faults.why: Missing common classifiers (cái, chiếc, ngọn, bóng) needed by A2 learners.

notes: Takes the classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc' for a lamp or fixture, 'bóng' for a bulb, and 'ngọn' for a flame or candle.
Covers both household lamps and other light sources such as flashlights ('đèn pin') and traffic lights ('đèn giao thông').

senses.definition: A device that produces light, such as a lamp, bulb, or lantern.

examples.text: Hãy bật đèn lên vì trời đã tối.
examples.translation: Turn on the light because it is already dark.

faults.quote: To move towards here.

faults.quote: To reach a certain time or place.

faults.quote: Often used together with 'với' (đến với)
faults.why: 'Đến với' is poetic/abstract; note should explain direct object usage ('đến Hà Nội').

corrected.shortGloss: to arrive; to come; to, until

senses.definition: To reach or come to a place or time.

examples.text: Tàu đã đến ga Hà Nội.
examples.translation: The train has arrived at Hanoi station.

examples.text: Xin hãy đến đây.
examples.translation: Please come here.

senses.definition: Used to mark the end point of a journey, range, or period of time.

examples.text: Anh ấy làm việc từ sáng đến tối.
examples.translation: He works from morning until night.

faults.quote: /dɛw/

faults.quote: To have an accessory, piece of jewellery, glasses, or a bag

senses.definition: To wear or carry something attached to or hanging on the body, such as jewelry, glasses, or a bag.

examples.text: Tôi luôn đeo kính râm khi đi ra ngoài trời nắng.
examples.translation: I always wear sunglasses when going out in the sun.

examples.text: Học sinh đeo ba lô trên vai đến trường.
examples.translation: Students carry backpacks on their shoulders to school.

faults.quote: /ɗɛp˨˩/
faults.why: Nặng tone on checked syllables is low glottalized (/ɗɛp˨˩ˀ/ or /ɗɛp˧˨ʔ/), not plain falling /˨˩/.

faults.quote: Use 'đẹp' for both people and things. Unlike some languages

senses.definition: Pleasing to look at or experience; attractive or fine.

examples.text: Bức tranh này rất đẹp.
examples.translation: This painting is very beautiful.

examples.text: Bạn ấy có một nụ cười đẹp.
examples.translation: She has a beautiful smile.

faults.quote: A colloquial and sometimes pejorative term for a woman
faults.why: Invented English calque ('gossip hens'); 'gà mái' is not used this way in Vietnamese.

faults.quote: hen; motherly woman

notes: Takes the classifier 'con' ('con gà mái'). The male counterpart is 'gà trống' (rooster), where 'mái' and 'trống' mark female and male birds.

senses.definition: An adult female chicken.

examples.text: Con gà mái đang ấp trứng trong chuồng.
examples.translation: The hen is incubating eggs in the coop.

faults.quote: This expression is used to indicate the absence or lack of something.
faults.why: Restates the definition without adding usage information.

faults.quote: interchangeable with the prefix 'bi-' (without) in some contexts
faults.why: The prefix 'bi-' means 'with/by', not 'without' (which is 'bilā').

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: Should be classified as a preposition.

notes: Followed by a noun in the genitive case, or by أنْ (an) before a verb.
Interchangeable with بِلَا (bilā).

senses.definition: Not having or not using something; in the absence of.

examples.text: لا أستطيع الخروج بدون مفاتيحي.
examples.translation: I cannot go out without my keys.

examples.text: أحب القهوة بدون سكر.
examples.translation: I like coffee without sugar.

faults.why: Missing two vital A1/A2 senses: negative commands ('do not') and 'there is no'.

faults.quote: This is the most common way to say 'no'.
faults.why: Restates the glosses and senses.

notes: Used before a present-tense verb for 'not' (لا أعرف, I do not know) or with a second-person jussive verb for 'do not' (لا تذهب, do not go).

senses.definition: Used to give a negative answer, refuse, or disagree.

examples.text: هَل تُريد القَهوة؟ لَا، شُكْرًا.
examples.translation: Do you want coffee? No, thank you.

senses.definition: Used before a present-tense verb to say that an action does not happen.

examples.text: أَنَا لَا أَعرِف.
examples.translation: I do not know.

senses.definition: Used before a second-person verb to tell someone not to do something.

examples.text: لَا تَقْلَقْ.
examples.translation: Do not worry.

senses.definition: Used before an indefinite noun to say that something does not exist.

examples.text: لَا مُشْكِلَة.
examples.translation: No problem.

faults.why: Should mention the preposition على (ʿalā, 'for') and the standard reply عَفْوًا (ʿafwan).

senses.definition: A polite expression used to show gratitude.

examples.text: شُكْرًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَةِ.
examples.translation: Thanks for the help.

faults.why: Missing the very common everyday sense 'to have (on oneself)' when used with pronoun suffixes.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with the noun 'مَعِيَّة' (accompaniment).

faults.why: Slightly stiff sentence and calqued translation ('together with the bread').

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: Should be classified as a preposition.

notes: Followed by a noun in the genitive case (-i) or an attached pronoun suffix: مَعِي (maʿī, with me), مَعَكَ (maʿaka, with you).

senses.definition: In the company of or together with someone or something.

examples.text: أَنَا أَذْهَبُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي.
examples.translation: I go with my friend.

examples.text: أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ مَعَ الحَلِيبِ.
examples.translation: I drink tea with milk.

senses.definition: Used with a pronoun suffix to show that someone has something with them at the moment.

examples.text: هَلْ مَعَكَ قَلَمٌ؟
examples.translation: Do you have a pen with you?

faults.quote: /min faḍlik/

faults.why: Omits the final fatha (-ka) on the masculine form, failing to show the vowel contrast.

notes: The ending changes according to who you are addressing: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (min faḍlika) to a man, مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (min faḍliki) to a woman; in everyday speech both often become min faḍlak / min faḍlik.

senses.definition: A polite phrase used when asking for something or asking someone to do something.

examples.text: الْقَهْوَةَ مِنْ فَضْلِك.
examples.translation: Coffee, please.

faults.quote: Use bản đồ when you need to find your way
faults.why: Filler restating the meaning of 'map'; classifier 'tấm' would be useful instead.

senses.definition: A drawing of an area that shows where places, roads, and rivers are.

examples.text: Chúng ta cần xem bản đồ để tìm đường đến khách sạn.
examples.translation: We need to look at the map to find the way to the hotel.

faults.quote: Being one of two equal parts into which something is divided.

faults.why: Unnatural; 'half a portion' in everyday Vietnamese is 'nửa phần', not 'bán phần'.

faults.why: Ungrammatical English ('to half') and includes the non-verb bound morpheme sense.

faults.quote: bán means to sell goods or services in exchange for money.
faults.why: Restates the definition.

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.

examples.text: Cô ấy bán hoa quả ở chợ.
examples.translation: She sells fruit at the market.

faults.quote: The noun 'băng' has multiple unrelated meanings depending on context
faults.why: Pure filler restating that the entry has three senses; misses 'nước đá' (drink ice) distinction.

faults.quote: Cuộn băng này ghi lại âm nhạc từ những năm cũ.
faults.why: 'Từ những năm cũ' is unnatural phrasing in Vietnamese.

notes: For sense 1, 'băng' refers to natural ice in the environment (like icebergs or frost). Ice put in drinks is called 'đá' or 'nước đá'.

senses.definition: Water that has frozen solid in nature.

examples.text: Trời rất lạnh nên mặt hồ đã đóng băng.
examples.translation: It is very cold, so the lake surface has frozen into ice.

senses.definition: A strip of cloth or sticky material used to cover and protect a wound.

examples.text: Hãy dùng băng để quấn vết thương lại.

senses.definition: A long, narrow strip of material used for sticking things together or recording sound and video.

examples.text: Bố tôi vẫn giữ nhiều cuộn băng nhạc cũ.
examples.translation: My father still keeps many old music tapes.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with just 'bánh mì'
faults.why: Two long notes repeat the same point that 'bánh mì' alone also means a filled baguette.

notes: In everyday speech, a filled Vietnamese baguette is usually called simply 'bánh mì' (or 'bánh mì thịt'); 'bánh mì kẹp' emphasizes that it has fillings or refers to Western-style sliced-bread sandwiches.

senses.definition: Food consisting of fillings such as meat, cheese, or vegetables placed between slices of bread or inside a split roll.

examples.text: Tôi ăn một cái bánh mì kẹp vào buổi trưa.
examples.translation: I ate a sandwich at noon.

faults.quote: In Vietnamese, 'bánh mì' can refer to plain bread or to
faults.why: Restates the two senses directly below.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with other types of 'bánh'
faults.why: Filler warning; misses the useful classifiers ('ổ' or 'cái').

notes: Loaves or baguettes are counted with the classifiers 'ổ' (especially in the South) or 'cái' (common in the North).

senses.definition: A baked food made from flour and water, especially a crisp, individual-sized Vietnamese baguette.

examples.text: Tôi mua một ổ bánh mì ở tiệm.
examples.translation: I bought a loaf of bread at the bakery.

senses.definition: A Vietnamese sandwich made with a split baguette filled with meat, pâté, herbs, and pickled vegetables.

examples.text: Cô ấy thích ăn bánh mì thịt vào buổi sáng.
examples.translation: She likes to eat a meat sandwich in the morning.

faults.quote: /luθ/

examples.text: Tengo que hacer la maleta antes de ir al aeropuerto.
examples.translation: I have to pack my suitcase before going to the airport.

faults.quote: morning; tomorrow

senses.definition: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

examples.text: Me gusta tomar café por la mañana.
examples.translation: I like to drink coffee in the morning.

faults.quote: Aunque termina en -o, 'mano' es un sustantivo femenino

senses.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm that includes the fingers.

examples.translation: He raised his hand to ask a question.

senses.definition: A layer of paint or varnish applied to a surface.

examples.text: La pared necesita otra mano de pintura.
examples.translation: The wall needs another coat of paint.

faults.quote: Used for food and drinks that taste of sugar, like fruit
faults.why: Merely restates the first definition without adding grammar or usage guidance.

senses.definition: Having the taste of sugar or honey.

examples.text: 这个西瓜很甜。
examples.translation: This watermelon is very sweet.

senses.definition: Pleasant and endearing, such as a smile, voice, or sleep.

examples.text: 她笑得很甜。
examples.translation: She has a very sweet smile.

faults.quote: Use this for both physical health (feeling well) and general well-being

senses.definition: Not fast; taking a long time to move, happen, or do something.

examples.text: 这台电脑太慢了。

faults.quote: (starve) To suffer from a lack of food.
faults.why: Defines a verb inside an adjective entry; example just shows adjective with complement.

faults.why: True of almost every Chinese adjective; not specific to this word.

senses.definition: Feeling a need or desire for food.

examples.text: 我很饿，想吃饭。

examples.text: 我快饿死了！

faults.quote: red; popular; revolutionary

faults.why: Merely repeats Sense 1 instead of explaining usage like 红 vs 红色.

senses.definition: Having the color of blood or a ripe tomato.

examples.text: 她的脸变得很红。
examples.translation: Her face turned very red.

senses.definition: Popular, successful, or well-liked by the public.

examples.text: 这家新开的餐厅现在非常红。

notes: "Xin chào" is the standard polite greeting taught to learners, used in formal contexts or when addressing a group. In everyday conversation, native speakers usually greet one another with "chào" plus a pronoun showing age and relationship, such as "chào anh" or "chào chị".

senses.definition: Said as a polite greeting when meeting someone.

examples.text: Xin chào, rất vui được gặp bạn.
examples.translation: Hello, nice to meet you.

faults.quote: /sin lɔjˀ/

faults.why: Restates the definitions of the two senses without adding usage information.

senses.definition: Said to apologize when you have done something wrong.

examples.translation: Sorry, I'm late.

senses.definition: Said politely to get someone's attention or to interrupt.

examples.text: Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi đường.
examples.translation: Excuse me, may I ask for directions?

faults.quote: Used to refer to a nurse who cares for sick people in
faults.why: Merely repeats the definition of the word.

senses.definition: A person whose job is to care for sick or injured people, especially in a hospital.

examples.text: Cô y tá đang đo huyết áp cho bệnh nhân.
examples.translation: The nurse is taking the patient's blood pressure.

faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are shades of the same meaning (quiet/silent) and overlap.

senses.definition: With little or no noise; quiet and peaceful.

examples.text: Cả phòng đều yên lặng khi giáo viên bước vào.
examples.translation: The whole room was silent when the teacher entered.

examples.text: Đêm nay thật yên lặng và mát mẻ.
examples.translation: Tonight is really quiet and cool.

examples.translation: After being sick, he still feels very weak.

examples.text: Cái bàn này quá yếu, không để được nhiều đồ.
examples.translation: This table is too weak; it cannot hold many things.

examples.text: Tôi rất yếu môn toán.
examples.translation: I am very weak at math.

faults.quote: While 'granica' is the standard word for both physical borders
faults.why: Restates the senses without adding useful grammatical or usage information.

senses.definition: The official dividing line or area between two countries or regions.

examples.text: Staliśmy w długiej kolejce na granicy.
examples.translation: We stood in a long line at the border.

senses.definition: A point beyond which something cannot or should not go.

examples.text: To przekracza wszelkie granice cierpliwości.
examples.translation: This exceeds all limits of patience.

senses.definition: To become unable to find something, or to drop and leave something behind.

examples.text: Ciągle gubię klucze.

senses.definition: A bright point of light in the night sky.

examples.text: Jasna gwiazda świeci wysoko na ciemnym niebie.
examples.translation: A bright star is shining high in the dark sky.

senses.definition: A very famous and successful person, especially in entertainment or sports.

examples.text: Ta piosenkarka to wielka gwiazda muzyki.
examples.translation: That singer is a huge music star.

faults.quote: Herbata is the standard Polish word for tea.

notes: Also used for herbal and fruit infusions (e.g., 'herbata miętowa' for mint tea, 'herbata owocowa' for fruit tea).

senses.definition: A hot drink made by pouring boiling water over dried leaves, or the leaves themselves.

examples.text: Piję gorącą herbatę.
examples.translation: I am drinking hot tea.

faults.quote: /xɔˈtɛl/

faults.quote: Note the masculine gender.

examples.translation: I booked a room in this hotel.

faults.quote: Very large in size or extent; huge.

senses.definition: A married man in relation to his wife.

examples.text: Kocam bu akşam geç geleceğini söyledi.
examples.translation: My husband said he would come home late tonight.

senses.definition: A part of an object or machine that you hold or pull to move or open it.

examples.text: Kapının kolu kırılmış.
examples.translation: The door handle is broken.

senses.definition: A subdivision or offshoot of an organization, river, or field of study.

examples.translation: He used a ladder to paint the wall.

notes: Literally 'see again'; unlike English 'goodbye', it is used for both formal and casual everyday partings.

senses.definition: A polite and common expression used when parting ways with someone.

examples.text: 明天见，再见！
examples.translation: See you tomorrow, goodbye!

faults.quote: It is also used when offering to pay for someone's meal
faults.why: Restates sense 1 and its example instead of adding grammar or usage notes.

faults.quote: 我今天请客吃饭。
faults.why: Uses the compound word 请客 instead of showing 请 alone as a transitive verb.

notes: Placed directly before a verb to make a request polite (e.g., 请进 'please come in').
In 请问 (qǐngwèn, 'may I ask / excuse me'), it is used to politely get someone's attention before asking a question.

senses.definition: Used before a verb to politely ask someone to do something.

examples.text: 请坐。
examples.translation: Please sit down.

senses.definition: To ask someone to come to an event, or to pay for someone's meal.

examples.text: 今天我请你吃饭。
examples.translation: I am treating you to a meal today.

faults.why: Missing obligatory third-tone sandhi; first syllable is pronounced with a rising tone (/ni˧˥/).
Should mention the polite form 您好 (nínhǎo) and that friends rarely use 你好.

notes: Used with strangers, acquaintances, or in service settings; close friends usually greet each other by name or with 早 (zǎo, 'morning') or 嗨 (hāi, 'hi').
To show respect to elders, superiors, or customers, use 您好 (nín hǎo) instead.
Because two third tones are spoken together, 你 (nǐ) is pronounced with a rising second tone (ní hǎo).

senses.definition: A standard greeting said when meeting someone.

examples.text: 你好，很高兴认识你。
examples.translation: Hello, nice to meet you.

faults.why: Must warn beginners not to use 是 before adjectives (where 很 is used instead).

faults.quote: expression
faults.why: 是 is primarily a copular verb, not an expression.

notes: Links two nouns (我是学生 'I am a student') and does not change form for person or tense; negate with 不 (不是 bú shì).
Not used to link a subject to an adjective in simple descriptions: say 他很高 ('He is tall'), not 他是高.

senses.definition: To be; links a subject with a noun or pronoun that identifies or classifies it.

examples.text: 我是学生。
examples.translation: I am a student.

senses.definition: Used to confirm that a statement is true or to answer a question in the affirmative.

examples.text: 甲：你是老师吗？乙：是。
examples.translation: A: Are you a teacher? B: Yes.

faults.quote: no; not be; fault
faults.why: Includes 'fault', which is not covered in the senses (and is marginal for A2).

faults.quote: Used to express disagreement, refusal, or to say 'no'.
faults.why: 不是 means 'no, that's not true', not refusal (which is 不要 or 不行).

faults.quote: Used as a standalone expression to disagree or say 'no', as the
faults.why: Restates the senses and mentions an unincluded noun sense ('fault') without explaining pronunciation.

notes: Because 是 (shì) is in the fourth tone, 不 (bù) changes to the rising second tone: bú shì (often with a neutral tone on shi in fast speech).
As a standalone 'no', 不是 corrects an assumption ('that's not true'); it is not used to refuse an offer or request.

senses.definition: The negative form of 是 (shì, 'to be'), linking a subject to what it is not.

examples.text: 这本书不是我的。
examples.translation: This book is not mine.

senses.definition: Used alone to correct a mistaken assumption or statement.

examples.text: 不是，我没有去过那里。
examples.translation: No, I have never been there.

faults.quote: The darkest color, like coal or night.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun rather than a quality.

faults.quote: 那是黑色的汽车。
faults.why: Uses the compound 黑色 instead of the adjective 黑 alone, and lacks a classifier.

faults.quote: In Chinese, '黑' is used to describe both the darkest colour
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses; a grammar note on 黑 vs. 黑色 is needed.

notes: Before a noun, use 黑色 (hēisè) rather than 黑 alone for most objects (黑色的车 'a black car'), though 黑 attaches directly to a few common nouns like 黑头发 (black hair).

senses.definition: Of the darkest color, like coal or the night sky.

examples.text: 她的头发又黑又亮。
examples.translation: Her hair is black and shiny.

senses.definition: Having little or no light.

examples.text: 天黑了，我们回家吧。
examples.translation: It's getting dark, let's go home.

faults.why: Feeling awkward and an awkward situation are one adjective sense; example 0 even describes a situation.

faults.quote: A situation that is difficult to deal with or resolve.
faults.why: Adjective defined as a noun ('A situation...').

faults.quote: awkward, tricky, dilemma
faults.why: 'Dilemma' is a noun, not an adjective.

notes: Can describe either a person feeling embarrassed (我很尴尬) or an awkward situation (场面很尴尬).

senses.definition: Feeling embarrassed and uncomfortable, or causing people to feel this way.

examples.text: 他突然叫错我的名字，场面十分尴尬。
examples.translation: He suddenly called me by the wrong name, and the situation became very awkward.

examples.text: 那时候我感到很尴尬。
examples.translation: I felt very embarrassed at that time.

faults.quote: 难过 primarily describes a feeling of sadness or emotional pain
faults.why: Both notes simply restate the two senses already given.

notes: In everyday speech, 难过 most often means 'sad' (similar to 伤心); for physical discomfort, 难受 (nánshòu) is much more common.

senses.definition: Feeling sad or upset because of bad news or a disappointment.

examples.text: 听到这个消息，他感到很难过。
examples.translation: Hearing this news, he felt very sad.

senses.definition: Of life or times: difficult to get through or endure.

examples.text: 最近经济压力大，日子有点难过。
examples.translation: Financial pressure has been high lately, and life is a bit hard to get through.

faults.why: Senses 1 and 2 over-split and over-extend the word; Sense 2 uses adverb glosses for an adjective.

faults.quote: 这项工作他做得干干净净。
faults.why: Uses the reduplicated form 干干净净 instead of the lemma 干净.

faults.quote: 干净 is used both for physical cleanliness, like a clean room
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of explaining how 干净 is used after verbs as a result complement.

notes: Often placed directly after a verb of washing or tidying to show the result: 洗干净 (wash clean), 擦干净 (wipe clean), 收拾干净 (tidy up completely).

senses.definition: Free from dirt, dust, or stains; not dirty.

examples.text: 这件衣服洗得很干净。
examples.translation: This piece of clothing has been washed very clean.

examples.text: 请把房间收拾干净。
examples.translation: Please tidy up the room so it is clean.

senses.definition: Orderly, neat, and free of clutter or mess.

examples.text: 他的字写得很干净。
examples.translation: His handwriting is very neat.

faults.quote: Do not use this for height (use 矮 instead) or for a duration of time that is 'brief'
faults.why: False claim: 短 is very commonly used for a short duration of time (even the note's own 时间短 uses it).
Missing the everyday sense 'short in time; brief' (e.g. 时间很短).

notes: Used for length, distance, and duration of time. Do not use 短 for a person's height or the height of standing objects; use 矮 (ǎi) instead.

senses.definition: Measuring a small distance from one end to the other; not long.

examples.text: 这条绳子太短了。
examples.translation: This rope is too short.

senses.definition: Lasting or taking a small amount of time.

examples.text: 假期太短了，我还没休息够。
examples.translation: The holiday was too short; I haven't rested enough yet.

faults.quote: Use 'cara' primarily for the front part of the head, but it
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses and glosses.

notes: On a coin, 'cara' is heads and 'cruz' is tails. Colloquially, 'tener mucha cara' means to have a lot of nerve.

senses.definition: The front part of the head from the forehead to the chin, or the expression on it.

examples.text: Tiene una sonrisa amable en la cara.
examples.translation: She has a kind smile on her face.

senses.definition: One of the flat sides or surfaces of an object such as a sheet of paper or a coin.

examples.text: Escribe tu nombre en esta cara del papel.
examples.translation: Write your name on this side of the paper.

faults.quote: The soft part of the body of humans or animals located beneath
faults.why: Defines anatomical flesh while the primary meaning and example are about meat as food.

faults.quote: Used most often to mean meat eaten as food, but also refers
faults.why: Restates the glosses instead of giving a grammar or usage tip.

notes: In Spain, 'carne' on a menu usually means red meat or pork, listed separately from 'aves' (poultry) and 'pescado' (fish).

senses.definition: The flesh of an animal eaten as food.

examples.text: Compramos carne para la cena de esta noche.
examples.translation: We bought meat for dinner tonight.

senses.definition: The soft tissue of a human or animal body between the skin and the bones.

examples.text: El tigre clavó los dientes en la carne de su presa.
examples.translation: The tiger sank its teeth into the flesh of its prey.

faults.quote: highway, road, freeway
faults.why: 'Road' should be first; 'freeway' is 'autopista' or 'autovía' in Spain, not a general 'carretera'.

notes: Use 'carretera' for paved roads between towns; use 'calle' for streets inside a town and 'autopista' or 'autovía' for multi-lane motorways.

senses.definition: A paved road built for motor traffic between towns and cities.

examples.text: Vamos por la carretera de la costa.
examples.translation: We are taking the coast road.

faults.quote: like a playing card or a postcard.
faults.why: 'Carta' means a playing card, not a postcard ('tarjeta postal') or general information card ('tarjeta').

notes: In a restaurant in Spain, ask for 'la carta' for the main menu; 'el menú (del día)' refers to a fixed-price set meal.
For a credit card, ID card, or postcard, use 'la tarjeta', not 'la carta'.

senses.definition: A written or printed message sent to someone, usually in an envelope by post.

examples.text: Hoy he recibido una carta de mi abuela.
examples.translation: I received a letter from my grandmother today.

senses.definition: The list of dishes and drinks available to order in a restaurant.

examples.text: El camarero nos trajo la carta enseguida.
examples.translation: The waiter brought us the menu right away.

senses.definition: One of a set of small stiff cards marked with figures or numbers and used for playing games.

examples.text: ¿Jugamos una partida de cartas?
examples.translation: Shall we play a game of cards?

faults.quote: wallet; briefcase; handbag
faults.why: Includes 'handbag', which is absent from the senses and is mainly Latin American usage.

notes: In Spain, a woman's handbag is called 'el bolso'; in much of Latin America, 'la cartera' is used for a handbag and 'la billetera' for a wallet.

senses.definition: A small flat folding case kept in a pocket or bag for holding money, bank cards, and ID.

examples.text: Me he dejado la cartera en la mesa del restaurante.
examples.translation: I left my wallet on the restaurant table.

senses.definition: A flat rectangular bag with a handle, used for carrying documents, books, or a laptop.

examples.text: Lleva los documentos importantes en su cartera de cuero.
examples.translation: He carries the important documents in his leather briefcase.

faults.quote: /t͡ɕəːn/
faults.why: Wrong vowel length and missing tone mark; Hanoi IPA is /t͡ɕən˧˧/.

faults.quote: It is also used metaphorically for the base or bottom of objects
faults.why: Merely restates sense 1 without adding usage or grammar help.

notes: In Vietnamese, 'chân' covers both the leg and the foot; use 'bàn chân' to specify the foot and 'cẳng chân' for the lower leg.

senses.definition: The lower limb of a person or animal, including both the leg and the foot.

examples.text: Tôi bị đau chân sau khi chạy bộ.
examples.translation: My leg hurts after jogging.

senses.definition: The lowest supporting part or bottom of an object, piece of furniture, or mountain.

examples.text: Ngôi đền nằm ở chân núi.
examples.translation: The temple is located at the foot of the mountain.

faults.quote: To herd or tend livestock in a field.
faults.why: Verb sense included in a noun entry, contradicting both `pos` and `shortGloss`.

faults.quote: Used to refer to a warm bed cover.
faults.why: Restates the definition; a regional note ('chăn' in the North vs. 'mền' in the South) is more useful.

notes: Standard in northern Vietnam (usually with classifier 'cái' or 'chiếc'); in the South, 'mền' is commonly used instead.
Do not confuse with the homonym verb 'chăn' (to herd or graze livestock).

senses.definition: A warm cover used on a bed.

examples.text: Trời lạnh quá, hãy đắp thêm chăn.
examples.translation: It's so cold, put on another blanket.

faults.quote: The tree that produces limes.
faults.why: Fruit names in Vietnamese need 'cây' ('cây chanh') to mean the tree; 'chanh' alone is the fruit.

notes: In Vietnam, 'chanh' by default refers to the green lime (classifier 'quả' or 'trái'). To specify a yellow lemon, speakers say 'chanh vàng' or 'chanh tây'.

senses.definition: A small, round, green citrus fruit with sour juice, or a yellow lemon.

examples.text: Cho tôi thêm một lát chanh vào cốc nước đá.
examples.translation: Give me another slice of lime in the glass of ice water.

faults.quote: /t͡ɕajŋ˧ˀ˥/
faults.why: Wrong coda (/ŋ/ is for 'chanh') and wrong tone (sắc instead of nặng); 'chạy' is /t͡ɕaj˧˨ˀ/.

faults.quote: Besides physical running, 'chạy' is very commonly used for machines running
faults.why: Merely repeats sense 1 without adding extra usage information.

corrected.shortGloss: to run; to operate; to flee
notes: Also used for driving or riding vehicles (e.g., 'chạy xe máy' — to ride a motorbike) and in colloquial expressions meaning to scramble for something ('chạy tiền' — to scramble for money).

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, or (of a vehicle) to travel.

examples.text: Cô ấy chạy quanh công viên mỗi sáng.
examples.translation: She runs around the park every morning.

senses.definition: Of a machine, engine, or device: to function or operate.

examples.text: Chiếc máy này chạy bằng điện.
examples.translation: This machine runs on electricity.

senses.definition: To move away quickly to escape danger or a difficult situation.

examples.text: Thấy cảnh sát, kẻ trộm liền chạy mất.
examples.translation: Seeing the police, the thief immediately ran away.

faults.why: Missing the everyday sense of a shop or business closing for the day.

faults.quote: เปิด (pèet)
faults.why: Wrong vowel in romanization: เปิด is pronounced /pɤ̀ːt/ (pòet), not pèet.

faults.quote: Use this for physical objects like doors or windows.
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

corrected.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to turn off
notes: The opposite of เปิด (/pɤ̀ːt/), which means 'to open' or 'to turn on'.

senses.definition: To move something such as a door or lid so that an opening is covered.

examples.text: กรุณาปิดประตูด้วย
examples.translation: Please close the door.

senses.definition: To stop the operation of a machine, light, or electronic device.

examples.text: ช่วยปิดไฟก่อนออกจากห้อง
examples.translation: Please turn off the light before leaving the room.

senses.definition: Of a shop, restaurant, or business: to stop operating for the day or permanently.

examples.text: ร้านนี้ปิดกี่โมง
examples.translation: What time does this shop close?

faults.quote: For a loud vocalization of pain or surprise, a different verb is used.
faults.why: Unhelpful without naming the verb: ร้อง (/rɔ́ːŋ/) is used for shouting or crying out.

notes: Refers specifically to shedding tears; to cry out or shout in pain or surprise, use ร้อง (/rɔ́ːŋ/) alone.

senses.definition: To shed tears because of sadness, pain, or strong emotion.

examples.text: เด็กน้อยร้องไห้เพราะทำของเล่นหาย
examples.translation: The little child is crying because they lost their toy.

faults.quote: Used to express preference for things, activities, or people.
faults.why: Restates the basic meaning of the verb without adding usage insight.

faults.quote: ฉันชอบกินผลไม้
faults.why: Both examples show ชอบ + verb; one should show ชอบ + noun.

notes: Followed directly by a noun or another verb without a linking word: ชอบกาแฟ ('like coffee'), ชอบอ่าน ('like to read').
To say 'really like', place มาก (/mâːk/) at the end of the phrase: ชอบ...มาก.

senses.definition: To find someone or something pleasant, enjoyable, or appealing.

examples.text: ฉันชอบอาหารไทยมาก
examples.translation: I really like Thai food.

examples.text: เขาชอบอ่านหนังสือ
examples.translation: He likes reading books.

faults.why: Missing the common A2 sense 'to seem / to look' (+ adjective), e.g. ดูดี.

faults.quote: Use ดู when you are watching something for an extended period
faults.why: Duplicates the definition of sense 0.

corrected.shortGloss: to watch; to look at; to seem
notes: More active than มอง (/mɔːŋ/, 'to look towards / gaze at') and เห็น (/hěn/, 'to see').
Placed after another verb, it means 'to try doing something to see what happens', e.g., ลองชิมดู ('try tasting it').

senses.definition: To look at something attentively over a period of time, such as a show or game.

examples.text: ฉันชอบดูหนังตอนเย็น
examples.translation: I like to watch movies in the evening.

senses.definition: To direct your eyes at something or examine it.

examples.text: ช่วยดูเอกสารนี้หน่อย
examples.translation: Please take a look at this document.

senses.definition: To give a particular impression; to appear to be.

examples.text: วันนี้คุณดูเหนื่อยนะ
examples.translation: You look tired today.

notes: Literally 'to drive a vehicle' (ขับ + รถ). Used for cars, trucks, and buses; for bicycles and motorcycles, ขี่ (/kʰìː/, 'to ride') is normally used.

senses.definition: To operate and control a car or other four-wheeled motor vehicle.

examples.text: ฉันกำลังหัดขับรถ
examples.translation: I am learning to drive.

faults.quote: /ˈʕiːdaːn taʕaːm/
faults.why: טَعَام begins with emphatic /tˤ/, not plain /t/.

faults.quote: Used in East Asian dining.
faults.why: Repeats cultural trivia already stated in the definition.

notes: Literally 'food sticks' (plural of عُود 'stick' + طَعَام 'food'). With the definite article, only the second word takes الـ: عِيدَانُ الطَّعَامِ.

senses.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand and used for eating.

examples.text: آكُلُ السُّوشِي بِعِيدَانِ الطَّعَامِ.
examples.translation: I eat sushi with chopsticks.

faults.quote: When you use this word to mean money, it specifically refers to
faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0 instead of giving grammatical or usage info.

faults.quote: Be aware that this same word is also used in a literary
faults.why: Just restates that sense 1 exists.

notes: The accusative form نَقْدًا (naqdan) is very common as an adverb meaning 'in cash'.
The plural is نُقُود (nuqūd), which is the standard everyday word for 'money' in general.

senses.definition: Money in the form of notes and coins, rather than cards or bank transfers.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي الدَّفْعُ نَقْدًا؟
examples.translation: Can I pay in cash?

senses.definition: The act of judging the good and bad qualities of something, or expressing disapproval.

examples.text: تَعَرَّضَ الْكِتَابُ لِنَقْدٍ شَدِيدٍ.
examples.translation: The book faced harsh criticism.

faults.quote: While 'waiter' is the most common meaning, it can also refer to
faults.why: Vague filler note; mentioning the plural would be much more useful.

notes: Feminine: نَادِلَة (nādila). Plural: نُدُل (nudul) or نَادِلُونَ (nādilūna).

senses.definition: A person who serves food and drinks at tables in a restaurant or café.

examples.text: طَلَبْتُ مِنَ النَّادِلِ قَائِمَةَ الطَّعَامِ.
examples.translation: I asked the waiter for the menu.

faults.quote: The travel suitcase is very heavy.
faults.why: Calqued translation; in English حَقِيبَةُ السَّفَرِ is simply 'suitcase'.

notes: Plural: حَقَائِب (ḥaqāʾib). Often specified by a following noun, such as حَقِيبَة يَد ('handbag'), حَقِيبَة ظَهْر ('backpack'), or حَقِيبَة سَفَر ('suitcase').

senses.definition: A soft container used for carrying personal items, books, or shopping.

examples.text: وَضَعْتُ هَاتِفِي فِي الْحَقِيبَةِ.
examples.translation: I put my phone in the bag.

senses.definition: A large case with a handle used for carrying clothes when traveling.

examples.text: حَقِيبَةُ السَّفَرِ ثَقِيلَةٌ جِدًّا.
examples.translation: The suitcase is very heavy.

faults.quote: (lamp) A lamp or light source.
faults.why: Shades of the same meaning ('light'); merge into one sense.

notes: Plural: أَنْوَار (ʾanwār). Synonym with ضَوْء (ḍawʾ), which is equally common for physical or electric light.

senses.definition: The brightness that lets you see, from the sun, a lamp, or another source.

examples.text: النُّورُ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ قَوِيٌّ.
examples.translation: The light in the room is bright.

examples.text: أَطْفِئِ النُّورَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: Turn off the light, please.

faults.quote: Komik can describe both situations that make you laugh and
faults.why: Both notes are trivial filler; a note on the idiom 'komik duruma düşmek' helps more.

faults.quote: funny; amusing; comical
faults.why: Lacks the 'ridiculous' sense present in sense 1.

notes: Often used in the phrase 'komik duruma düşmek' (to make a fool of oneself).

senses.definition: Causing laughter or amusement.

examples.text: Çocuk çok komik bir hikâye anlattı.
examples.translation: The child told a very funny story.

senses.definition: Strange or unreasonable in a way that seems absurd.

examples.text: Bu kadar pahalı olması çok komik.
examples.translation: It is ridiculous for it to be this expensive.

faults.quote: Situated next to or near something; adjacent.
faults.why: The POS is noun, so an adjectival sense should be framed as attributive noun use or dropped.

notes: Can also be placed directly before another noun to mean 'neighboring', as in 'komşu köy' (neighboring village) or 'komşu ülke' (neighboring country).

senses.definition: A person who lives next to or very near you.

examples.text: Üst kat komşum bugün bize geldi.
examples.translation: My upstairs neighbor came to visit us today.

examples.text: Komşu köyde pazar kuruluyor.
examples.translation: A market is being held in the neighboring village.

faults.quote: Yarın bu konuyu tekrar konuşmak istiyorum.
faults.why: Shows 'to discuss a topic' (takes direct object), not 'to converse with someone'.

faults.quote: To speak English is very important in the world now.
faults.why: Unnatural calqued English ('Speaking English is very important...').

corrected.shortGloss: to speak; to talk; to discuss
notes: When talking WITH someone, use 'ile' (or the suffix -(y)la/-(y)le): 'arkadaşımla konuşmak' (to talk with my friend). When discussing a topic, it can take a direct object in the accusative case ('bu konuyu konuşmak').
Do not confuse with 'demek' (to say) or 'söylemek' (to tell), which focus on delivering a specific message.

senses.definition: To produce words using the voice, or to be able to use a language.

examples.text: Bebek henüz konuşmak için çok küçük.
examples.translation: The baby is still too young to speak.

examples.text: İngilizce konuşmak artık çok önemli.
examples.translation: Speaking English is very important now.

senses.definition: To have a conversation with someone or discuss a topic.

examples.text: Seninle biraz konuşmak istiyorum.
examples.translation: I want to talk with you for a bit.

examples.text: Yarın bu konuyu tekrar konuşalım.
examples.translation: Let's discuss this subject again tomorrow.

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'kedi' (cat).
faults.why: Useless filler; learners do not confuse unrelated spellings 'köpek' and 'kedi'.
Missing note on final consonant voicing (köpek -> köpeği) before vowel suffixes.

notes: Before a suffix starting with a vowel, the final 'k' softens to 'ğ': 'köpeği' (his/her dog, or the dog [acc.]), 'köpeğe' (to the dog).

faults.quote: /los pan.taˈlones/

faults.quote: /los paˈpas/

senses.definition: A person's mother and father together.

examples.text: Los papás de Juan van a venir a la cena.
examples.translation: Juan's parents are coming to dinner.

senses.definition: More than one father.

examples.text: En esta escuela, los papás también ayudan con los eventos.
examples.translation: At this school, the dads also help with the events.

senses.definition: Of poor quality, unpleasant, or unfavourable.

examples.text: Tuve un mal día en el trabajo.

senses.definition: Morally wrong, mean, or wicked; harmful to health.

senses.definition: Of a person: in poor health or feeling unwell (used with 'estar').

examples.text: Hoy no fui a trabajar porque estoy malo del estómago.
examples.translation: I didn't go to work today because I'm sick to my stomach.

senses.definition: Of food or drink: spoiled or tasting bad (used with 'estar').

examples.text: No tomes esa leche, creo que ya está mala.
examples.translation: Don't drink that milk, I think it has gone bad.

faults.quote: /maˈʝana/

senses.definition: On the day after today, or in the near future.

examples.text: Mañana voy a estudiar español.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I am going to study Spanish.

senses.definition: To operate and control the movement of a vehicle.

examples.text: Aprendí a manejar cuando tenía dieciséis años.
examples.translation: I learned to drive when I was sixteen years old.

senses.definition: To control, operate, or deal with a tool, business, or situation.

examples.text: Ella sabe manejar situaciones difíciles con mucha calma.
examples.translation: She knows how to handle difficult situations very calmly.

faults.why: Missing crucial grammar note: takes auxiliary 'zijn' in the perfect tense.

notes: Separable verb (past: kwam aan, aangekomen) that takes 'zijn' in the perfect tense.

senses.definition: To reach a destination or a place after a journey.

examples.text: We komen om acht uur aan in Amsterdam.
examples.translation: We arrive in Amsterdam at eight o'clock.

senses.definition: To become heavier in weight.

senses.definition: To touch something with your hand or fingers.

examples.text: Niet aankomen, dat is breekbaar!
examples.translation: Do not touch, that is fragile!

faults.quote: Al regen ik het, we gaan toch.

faults.why: merely restates the definition and gloss of sense 0.

senses.definition: Before now, or earlier than expected.

examples.text: Ben je al klaar?
examples.translation: Are you ready already?

senses.definition: Used with a time period to show how long a situation has lasted up to now.

examples.text: Ik woon al drie jaar in Utrecht.
examples.translation: I have been living in Utrecht for three years.

faults.quote: Said in reply when someone thanks you.

Often shortened to 'a.u.b.' in writing (from the formal 'alstublieft').

senses.definition: Used to be polite when asking for something or accepting an offer.

examples.text: Mag ik een kopje koffie, alsjeblieft?
examples.translation: Can I have a cup of coffee, please?

senses.definition: Said when handing something to someone.

examples.text: Alsjeblieft, je jas.
examples.translation: Here you go, your coat.

faults.quote: Anyway; in any case, used to offer a positive alternative

faults.why: 'kunnen we altijd nog...' is the natural Dutch phrasing for this usage.

notes: In a main clause, 'altijd' comes after the conjugated verb (e.g., 'Hij is altijd te laat' — He is always late).

senses.definition: At all times; on every occasion.

examples.text: De zon schijnt hier niet altijd.
examples.translation: The sun does not always shine here.

examples.text: Je bent altijd welkom bij ons.
examples.translation: You are always welcome at our place.

faults.why: Missing the essential perfective partner 'прийти' and the irregular 1sg consonant mutation.

faults.quote: Do not confuse it with 'приехать'
faults.why: Compares imperfective 'приходить' with perfective 'приехать' instead of imperfective 'приезжать'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective partner is прийти. Note the consonant change in the first person singular: я прихожу.

senses.definition: To reach a place or the speaker, especially on foot.

examples.text: Я всегда прихожу в школу рано.
examples.translation: I always arrive at school early.

examples.text: Друзья часто приходят ко мне в гости.
examples.translation: Friends often come to visit me.

faults.why: Missing the irregular present tense conjugation (режу, режешь).

faults.why: Stiff, calqued translation of 'нужно'.

senses.definition: To divide or slice something with a sharp tool such as a knife or scissors.

examples.text: Нужно резать хлеб острым ножом.
examples.translation: You should cut bread with a sharp knife.

examples.text: Яркий свет режет глаза.
examples.translation: The bright light hurts my eyes.

faults.quote: Use строить when talking about putting physical structures together
faults.why: Both notes merely restate the two senses and omit the perfective partner 'построить'.

corrected.shortGloss: to build; to construct; to make (plans)
notes: Imperfective; the perfective partner is построить.

senses.definition: To make a structure such as a house, road, or bridge by putting parts together.

examples.text: Рабочие будут строить новый дом.
examples.translation: The workers are going to build a new house.

senses.definition: To form or develop something non-physical, such as plans, a career, or relationships.

examples.text: Мы любим строить планы на выходные.
examples.translation: We love making plans for the weekend.

faults.quote: Мы часто встречать трудности в работе.
faults.why: Ungrammatical Russian: uses infinitive 'встречать' instead of conjugated 'встречаем' after 'мы'.

notes: Imperfective; the perfective partner is встретить.

examples.text: Я буду встречать друга на вокзале.
examples.translation: I will meet my friend at the station.

senses.definition: To welcome or receive someone who has just arrived.

examples.text: Гостей нужно встречать с улыбкой.
examples.translation: You should greet guests with a smile.

senses.definition: To come across or experience something.

examples.text: Мы часто встречаем трудности в работе.
examples.translation: We often encounter difficulties in our work.

senses.definition: To celebrate the arrival of a holiday or the New Year.

examples.text: Где ты будешь встречать Новый год?
examples.translation: Where will you celebrate the New Year?

faults.why: Example uses the predicative adverb 'скучно' instead of the verb 'скучать'.

senses.definition: To feel sad because someone or something is away from you.

examples.text: Я скучаю по тебе каждый день.

examples.text: Дети скучают дома в дождливый день.

examples.translation: You have to push the door to open it.

senses.definition: Feeling displeasure or anger because of something that happened.

examples.text: Mamá está muy enfadada porque rompí el jarrón.
examples.translation: Mom is very angry because I broke the vase.

faults.quote: It is a versatile food item used in both traditional Vietnamese

senses.definition: Persona que vive al lado o cerca de la casa de otra, o país situado junto a otro.
