senses.definition: Establecimiento pequeño e informal donde se sirve café, otras bebidas y comidas ligeras.

examples.text: Let's meet at the corner cafe for coffee.
examples.translation: Nos vemos en la cafetería de la esquina para tomar un café.

faults.quote: (substance) Masa compacta o bloque de una sustancia sólida.
faults.why: 'Cake of soap' is dated/marginal for A2; learners use 'bar of soap'.
Missing essential A2 countability note (countable for whole cakes, uncountable for portions).

faults.quote: Para pasteles salados o de pescado, se suele usar 'patty'.
faults.why: Misleading: 'fish cake' and 'crab cake' are standard in US English.

notes: Es contable cuando se refiere al pastel entero ('a cake'), pero incontable cuando se habla de una porción o de comer pastel en general ('some cake', 'a piece of cake').

senses.definition: Alimento dulce horneado que se suele comer como postre o en celebraciones.

examples.text: She baked a chocolate cake for the party.
examples.translation: Ella horneó un pastel de chocolate para la fiesta.

examples.text: Would you like a piece of cake?
examples.translation: ¿Quieres un trozo de pastel?

faults.why: System vs physical/digital chart of dates are shades of one everyday meaning; sense 0's example actually shows sense 1.

faults.quote: Mark the date on your calendar.
faults.why: Marking a date on your calendar refers to the physical/digital chart or schedule, not the abstract calendar system.

faults.quote: mientras que una 'diary' es un libro donde escribes tus citas personales
faults.why: In US English, 'diary' is a personal journal of feelings/events, not an appointment book ('planner').

notes: En inglés de EE. UU., 'calendar' también se usa para la agenda o aplicación donde se anotan citas y eventos.

senses.definition: Tabla, impresa o digital, que muestra los días, semanas y meses de un año, o el sistema con que se organizan.

examples.text: I tore the old page off the wall calendar.
examples.translation: Arranqué la hoja vieja del calendario de pared.

senses.definition: Agenda o registro donde se anotan las citas y eventos planeados.

examples.text: Mark the date on your calendar.
examples.translation: Marca la fecha en tu calendario.

faults.quote: Por favor llama su nombre para que nos escuche.
faults.why: 'Llama su nombre' is an ungrammatical calque in Spanish; should be 'grita su nombre' or 'llámala por su nombre'.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para el contacto telefónico como para gritar el nombre
faults.why: Restates senses 0 and 1 without adding grammar or usage info (e.g., direct object without preposition, 'call back').

notes: No lleva preposición antes de la persona a la que se llama ('call me', no 'call to me'). Con 'back' ('call someone back') significa devolver una llamada telefónica.

senses.definition: Comunicarse con alguien por teléfono.

examples.text: I will call you later today.
examples.translation: Te llamaré más tarde hoy.

senses.definition: Hablar en voz alta o gritar para atraer la atención de alguien o pedir que venga.

examples.text: She called my name from across the street.
examples.translation: Ella me llamó por mi nombre desde el otro lado de la calle.

senses.definition: Dar o usar un nombre o apodo para una persona o cosa.

examples.text: My friends call me Mike.
examples.translation: Mis amigos me llaman Mike.

faults.quote: Se usa para describir a una persona que no está nerviosa ni alterada
faults.why: Merely repeats the definitions; fails to mention the silent 'l' in pronunciation.

notes: La letra 'l' es muda al pronunciar esta palabra.
A diferencia de 'quiet' (silencioso, callado), 'calm' indica ausencia de nerviosismo, viento o agitación.

senses.definition: De una persona o su actitud: que no siente ni muestra nerviosismo, miedo o enojo.

examples.text: Try to stay calm during the test.
examples.translation: Intenta mantenerte tranquilo durante el examen.

senses.definition: Del clima, el mar o un lugar: sin viento, olas ni agitación.

examples.text: The sea was very calm this morning.
examples.translation: El mar estaba muy tranquilo esta mañana.

faults.quote: Aunque en otros países de habla inglesa se puede decir 'tee'
faults.why: 'Tee' is actually an informal US shortening; better to note the capitalized spelling 'T-shirt'.

faults.quote: Se distingue de una 'shirt' (camisa) en que la camiseta suele ser
faults.why: Repeats the definition right below it.

notes: Se escribe a menudo con mayúscula inicial ('T-shirt'). No se debe confundir con 'shirt' (camisa, generalmente con botones y cuello).

senses.definition: Prenda de ropa ligera, generalmente de algodón, de manga corta y sin botones ni cuello, que cubre el torso.

examples.text: I bought a plain white t-shirt at the store.
examples.translation: Compré una camiseta blanca sencilla en la tienda.

faults.why: Missing core A1/A2 senses: using transport ('take the bus') and taking medicine/courses/tests.

faults.quote: take se usa mucho con el significado de coger o agarrar algo
faults.why: Merely restates the senses without adding grammatical or usage information.
Must give the irregular past ('took') and past participle ('taken') for an A2 learner.

notes: Es un verbo irregular: pasado 'took' (/tʊk/), participio 'taken' (/ˈteɪkən/).
No se debe confundir con 'bring' (traer hacia donde está el hablante); 'take' indica llevar algo hacia otro lugar.

senses.definition: Agarrar o sujetar algo con las manos, o recibirlo.

examples.text: Please take this book from the table.
examples.translation: Por favor, toma este libro de la mesa.

senses.definition: Llevar o acompañar a alguien o algo de un lugar a otro.

examples.text: I will take you home after work.
examples.translation: Te llevaré a casa después del trabajo.

senses.definition: Usar un medio de transporte o seguir una ruta o camino.

examples.text: I usually take the bus to work.
examples.translation: Normalmente tomo el autobús para ir al trabajo.

senses.definition: Ingerir un medicamento, o realizar una actividad como un curso, un examen o una foto.

examples.text: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Toma esta medicina dos veces al día.

senses.definition: Requerir o necesitar una determinada cantidad de tiempo.

examples.text: It takes twenty minutes to get there.
examples.translation: Se tarda veinte minutos en llegar allí.

faults.why: Physical height of people and narrow upright objects (trees, buildings) is a single everyday sense.

faults.quote: Usa 'tall' para describir personas o cosas que tienen mucha altura vertical.
faults.why: Merely restates the definition.

notes: Se usa para personas y cosas estrechas o verticales (árboles, edificios). No lo confundas con 'high', que se usa para cosas anchas (montañas, muros) o que están a gran distancia del suelo.

senses.definition: De una persona, un edificio, un árbol, etc.: que tiene una estatura o altura mayor de lo normal, o que mide una altura determinada.

examples.text: My brother is very tall.
examples.translation: Mi hermano es muy alto.

examples.text: That is a very tall building.
examples.translation: Ese es un edificio muy alto.

faults.quote: Se usa tanto para la acción voluntaria de probar algo como para
faults.why: Repeats the two senses without explaining the grammar ('taste good' vs 'taste like').

faults.quote: saber a, tener un sabor de
faults.why: 'Tener un sabor de' is unidiomatic in Spanish; 'saber (bien/mal, etc.)' and 'saber a' are needed.

notes: Para describir cómo sabe algo se usa seguido de un adjetivo ('it tastes good' = sabe bien) o de 'like' más un sustantivo ('it tastes like chicken' = sabe a pollo).
No se debe confundir con 'try', que es más general (intentar algo o probar algo por primera vez); 'taste' se refiere solo a percibir el sabor.

senses.definition: Tomar un poco de comida o bebida para comprobar su sabor.

examples.text: Taste this soup to see if it needs more salt.
examples.translation: Prueba esta sopa para ver si necesita más sal.

senses.definition: De un alimento o una bebida: tener un sabor determinado.

examples.text: The cake tastes like lemon.
examples.translation: El pastel sabe a limón.

faults.quote: To put food in your mouth and swallow it.
faults.why: In Thai, กิน is equally used for drinking liquids and taking medicine, not just solid food.

faults.quote: This is the most common and standard way to say 'to eat'.
faults.why: Pure filler that adds nothing beyond the register and gloss.
Should mention the everyday polite alternative ทาน (thaan), which A2 learners hear constantly.

notes: In Thai, 'กิน' is used not only for solid food, but also for drinking liquids (e.g., กินน้ำ 'drink water') and taking medicine (กินยา).
In polite everyday conversation, 'ทาน' (thaan) is very commonly used instead; in formal settings, use 'รับประทาน' (ráp-prà-thaan).
In very informal or vulgar slang, you may hear 'แดก' (dɛ̀ɛk), which is rude outside of close friends.

senses.definition: To eat food, drink liquids, or take medicine.

examples.text: ฉันกินข้าวเย็นตอนหกโมง
examples.translation: I eat dinner at six o'clock.

senses.definition: To consume or use up a resource, time, or space.

examples.text: แอปนี้กินแบตเตอรี่มาก
examples.translation: This app uses up a lot of battery.

faults.quote: While 'ใส่' (sài) is used for wearing clothes, it is also a general verb
faults.why: Restates the two senses and glosses already shown in the entry.

notes: Covers both putting clothing on and wearing it, as well as accessories like glasses, shoes, hats, and rings.
'สวม' (sǔam) also means 'to wear' or 'to put on', but is more formal.

senses.definition: To put on or have clothes, shoes, or accessories on one's body.

examples.text: วันนี้เขาใส่เสื้อสีแดง
examples.translation: Today he is wearing a red shirt.

senses.definition: To put or add something into a container, dish, or place.

examples.text: แม่ใส่เกลือลงในแกง
examples.translation: Mother put salt into the curry.

faults.quote: up to, until
faults.why: Entry POS is verb, but sense 1 is glossed with prepositions ('up to, until').

faults.quote: Used to mark the successful completion of a journey or process.
faults.why: Vague filler that just restates the meaning of 'to reach'.

notes: Often follows movement verbs like 'ไป' (go) or 'มา' (come) to mean 'arrive': ไปถึง (get there), มาถึง (get here).
Also very commonly used as a preposition meaning 'to', 'until', or 'about' (e.g., รอถึงพรุ่งนี้ 'wait until tomorrow', คิดถึง 'think of / miss').

senses.definition: To arrive at a place or destination.

examples.text: ฉันเพิ่งถึงที่ทำงาน
examples.translation: I just got to work.

senses.definition: To reach or attain a certain point, time, or amount.

examples.text: ราคาขึ้นไปถึงพันบาท
examples.translation: The price went up to reach a thousand baht.

faults.quote: To take a break or pause for a period of time.
faults.why: Misses the core everyday meaning 'to be off work/school' or 'to be closed (of a shop)'.

faults.quote: เรามาหยุดพักกันก่อน
faults.why: 'Rest/break' here comes from พัก; หยุด alone means 'stop' (sense 0) or 'take a day off'.

faults.quote: Used for physical movement, time, or ongoing actions.
faults.why: Generic filler restating what 'to stop' means.

corrected.shortGloss: to stop; to take a day off
notes: Do not confuse with 'เลิก' (lɤ̂ɤk), which is used for quitting a habit, ending a relationship, or finishing work/school for the day.

senses.definition: To cease moving or doing something.

examples.text: รถหยุดแล้ว
examples.translation: The car has stopped.

examples.text: หยุดพูดเดี๋ยวนี้
examples.translation: Stop talking right now.

senses.definition: To take time off from work or school, or (of a business) to be closed for the day.

examples.text: พรุ่งนี้ร้านหยุด
examples.translation: Tomorrow the shop is closed.

examples.text: วันนี้ฉันหยุดงาน
examples.translation: Today I am off work.

faults.quote: (advice) To give advice or point out a lesson
faults.why: Figurative shade of 'to teach'; oversplit for an A2 entry.

faults.quote: Unlike the English word 'learn' (เรียน), this word strictly refers
faults.why: English 'learn' does not mean 'teach' either; pointless comparison.

notes: Can be followed directly by the person and the subject (e.g., สอนภาษาไทยเด็ก 'teach children Thai') or use ให้ (hâi) before the person.

senses.definition: To give lessons, show someone how to do something, or impart knowledge.

examples.text: คุณช่วยสอนภาษาไทยให้ผมหน่อยได้ไหม
examples.translation: Could you please teach me some Thai?

notes: Invariable adjective: it does not change form for gender or number. Also spelled ग़रीब (ġarīb), and often used as a noun meaning 'a poor person'.

senses.definition: Having very little money or few possessions.

examples.text: वह बहुत गरीब परिवार से है।
examples.translation: He comes from a very poor family.

faults.why: 'Polite' and 'humble' are shades of one meaning in विनम्र and should be one sense.

faults.quote: विनम्र (vinamra) describes a person's character.
faults.why: Restates the obvious; should note instead that it is somewhat formal and invariable.

notes: Invariable adjective (does not change for gender or number). It combines politeness with genuine humility, and is slightly more formal than everyday words like तमीज़दार (well-mannered).

senses.definition: Behaving respectfully towards others without arrogance or boastfulness.

examples.text: सफलता मिलने पर भी वह विनम्र बना रहा।
examples.translation: He remained humble even after achieving success.

faults.quote: clean; clear; pure
faults.why: Includes 'pure', which is not covered in the senses.

faults.quote: Saaf is widely used to describe things that are physically clean
faults.why: Merely repeats the two senses instead of giving grammar or usage help.

notes: Invariable adjective. Very common in the compound verb साफ़ करना (sāf karnā, to clean). Often written without the dot as साफ.

senses.definition: Free from dirt, marks, or impurities.

examples.text: मेरे कपड़े साफ़ हैं।
examples.translation: My clothes are clean.

senses.definition: Easy to see through, hear, or understand; not cloudy or confused.

examples.text: आज आसमान बिल्कुल साफ़ है।
examples.translation: Today the sky is completely clear.

faults.quote: While primarily used for taste, it can also describe a person's voice
faults.why: Restates the senses; the inflection note buried in the example belongs here.

notes: Inflecting adjective: changes to मीठे (mīṭhe) for masculine plural/oblique and मीठी (mīṭhī) for feminine. For water (मीठा पानी), it means 'fresh' (not salty).

senses.definition: Having the taste of sugar or honey.

examples.text: यह आम बहुत मीठा है।
examples.translation: This mango is very sweet.

senses.definition: Of a voice, words, or manner: pleasant and gentle.

examples.text: उसकी आवाज़ बहुत मीठी है।
examples.translation: Her voice is very sweet.

faults.why: Splits one meaning ('hot/warm' in temperature) into three artificial senses (weather, touch, comfort).

faults.quote: Very warm weather or high temperatures outdoors.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun phrase ('weather or temperatures').

faults.quote: A pleasant or comfortable level of heat.
faults.why: Defines an adjective as a noun phrase ('a level of heat').

notes: Invariable adjective. Equally common in the spelling गरम (garam, pronounced /ɡəɾəm/). Covers both 'hot' and 'warm'.

senses.definition: Having a high or pleasantly warm temperature.

examples.text: यह खाना बहुत गर्म है।
examples.translation: This food is very hot.

examples.text: आज बहुत गर्म दिन है।
examples.translation: Today is a very hot day.

faults.quote: A place that is far away from other people or empty.
faults.why: Adjective is defined as a noun ('A place that...') instead of a quality.

faults.quote: You can be 'alleen' without feeling 'eenzaam', but feeling 'eenzaam' usually implies
faults.why: Repeats the exact same contrast already explained in note 0.

notes: While 'alleen' simply means being physically by yourself (alone), 'eenzaam' describes the negative feeling of being isolated or missing company.
Inflected form: 'eenzame' (with a single 'a').

senses.definition: Feeling sad because you are alone or feel isolated from others.

examples.text: Hij voelt zich erg eenzaam sinds hij verhuisd is.
examples.translation: He has been feeling very lonely since he moved.

senses.definition: Of a place: far away from people and rarely visited.

examples.text: Ze maakten een lange wandeling door het eenzame bos.
examples.translation: They took a long walk through the lonely woods.

faults.quote: De film eindigt met een verrassend einde.
faults.why: Tautological phrasing ('eindigt met een ... einde'); unnatural Dutch.

notes: In the perfect tense, 'eindigen' takes the auxiliary verb 'zijn' (is geëindigd).
Unlike 'stoppen' (to stop doing something), 'eindigen' means that an event, period, or story comes to its end.

senses.definition: To come to an end or reach a conclusion.

examples.text: De film eindigt met een grote verrassing.
examples.translation: The film ends with a big surprise.

examples.text: De werkdag eindigt om vijf uur.
examples.translation: The workday ends at five o'clock.

faults.quote: /ˌɛntu.ziˈɑst/
faults.why: Wrong IPA for Dutch of the Netherlands; normally pronounced /ˌɛntuˈʃɑst/ or /ˌɛntuˈsjɑst/.

faults.quote: Use 'enthousiast' when someone is very happy and eager about an idea
faults.why: Notes restate the definition and give a random contrast; missing spelling/pronunciation and preposition notes.

notes: Borrowed from French: 'ou' is pronounced /u/ (like 'oe') and 'si' like /ʃ/ ('sj').
Often followed by the preposition 'over': 'enthousiast over iets zijn' (to be enthusiastic about something).

senses.definition: Showing intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.

examples.text: Ze was erg enthousiast over het nieuwe plan.
examples.translation: She was very enthusiastic about the new plan.

faults.quote: Do not confuse with 'eten' as the plural verb form
faults.why: Nonsensical note warning not to confuse a verb with its own plural form; irregular past forms are missing.

corrected.shortGloss: to eat; to have a meal
notes: Strong (irregular) verb: 'at, aten' (past), 'heeft gegeten' (perfect).
As a neuter noun, 'het eten' means food or a meal (especially dinner).

senses.definition: To put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it, or to have a meal.

examples.text: Hoe laat gaan we vanavond eten?
examples.translation: What time are we going to eat tonight?

examples.text: We gaan buiten eten omdat het mooi weer is.
examples.translation: We are going to eat outside because the weather is nice.

faults.quote: Used to describe something that contains a mistake
faults.why: Restates the definition; misses the common collocation 'fout gaan' and the noun 'de fout'.

notes: Often used with 'gaan': 'fout gaan' (to go wrong). As a noun, 'de fout' means a mistake.
Compare 'verkeerd': 'fout' is used for objective errors or breaking rules, while 'verkeerd' is much more common before a noun ('de verkeerde trein' = the wrong train).

senses.definition: Not correct or containing a mistake.

examples.text: Dat antwoord is fout.
examples.translation: That answer is wrong.

examples.text: Er is iets fout gegaan met mijn bestelling.
examples.translation: Something went wrong with my order.

faults.quote: Hace mucho frío hoy en la ciudad.
faults.why: 'Hace frío' uses the noun 'frío', not the adjective.
Low temperature of weather and of objects are the same adjective sense.
Missing the common figurative sense 'unfriendly or unemotional'.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with 'refriado'
faults.why: Misspelled Spanish word: 'resfriado', not 'refriado'.

notes: For weather and bodily sensations, Spanish usually uses the noun 'frío' with 'hacer' or 'tener': 'hace frío' (it is cold), 'tengo frío' (I am cold).
Do not confuse with 'resfriado', which means 'having a cold' (the illness): 'estoy resfriado'.

senses.definition: Having a low temperature; not warm or hot.

examples.text: Prefiero tomar el refresco bien frío.
examples.translation: I prefer to drink soda very cold.

examples.text: Hoy es un día muy frío.
examples.translation: Today is a very cold day.

senses.definition: Of a person or their behavior: unfriendly or showing no emotion.

examples.text: Se mostró muy frío conmigo en la reunión.
examples.translation: He was very cold toward me at the meeting.

faults.quote: strong; loud; tough
faults.why: 'Tough' is in shortGloss, but no sense or gloss covers it.

notes: Does not change form for masculine and feminine ('un hombre fuerte', 'una mujer fuerte'); plural 'fuertes'.
Often used as an adverb meaning 'loudly' or 'hard': 'habla más fuerte' (speak louder), 'llueve fuerte' (it's raining hard).
Distinct from 'duro', which means 'hard' to the touch or 'difficult'.

senses.definition: Having great physical power, resistance, or solidity.

examples.text: Él es muy fuerte y puede levantar esas cajas pesadas.
examples.translation: He is very strong and can lift those heavy boxes.

senses.definition: Of a sound, flavor, smell, or feeling: having high volume or great intensity.

examples.text: La música está muy fuerte y no puedo dormir.
examples.translation: The music is too loud and I cannot sleep.

faults.quote: Use 'ganar' for winning a competition or game, but also for 'earning'
faults.why: Note 0 restates the senses; Note 1 just gives the antonym 'perder'.

faults.quote: to win; to earn; to gain
faults.why: 'To gain' is in shortGloss, but no sense covers gaining weight, time, etc.

corrected.shortGloss: to win; to earn; to gain
notes: When talking about beating an opponent, use 'ganarle a alguien': 'Le gané a Juan' (I beat Juan).

senses.definition: To come first in a game, competition, or contest, or to defeat an opponent.

examples.text: Espero ganar el partido de tenis mañana.
examples.translation: I hope to win the tennis match tomorrow.

senses.definition: To receive money in exchange for work.

examples.text: Ella quiere ganar más dinero en su nuevo trabajo.
examples.translation: She wants to earn more money at her new job.

senses.definition: To acquire or increase something desirable, or to put on weight.

examples.text: Tomamos un atajo para ganar tiempo.
examples.translation: We took a shortcut to gain time.

faults.quote: /ˈɡɾaθjas/
faults.why: Castilian IPA with /θ/ for a Mexican Spanish (es-MX) entry; should be /ˈɡɾasjas/.

notes: Followed by 'por' before a noun or infinitive: 'gracias por venir' (thank you for coming). Strengthened with 'muchas' or 'mil': 'muchas gracias' (thank you very much).

senses.definition: A polite expression used to show gratitude or to decline an offer.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por tu ayuda.
examples.translation: Thank you very much for your help.

faults.quote: No longer a child; an adult or someone of older age.
faults.why: Defines an adjective partly as a noun ('an adult or someone...').

notes: Before a singular masculine or feminine noun, 'grande' shortens to 'gran' and means 'great': 'un gran libro' (a great book), vs. 'un libro grande' (a big book).
False friend: 'largo' means 'long', not 'large'.

senses.definition: Of more than average physical size or extent.

examples.text: Compramos una casa grande con un jardín hermoso.
examples.translation: We bought a big house with a beautiful garden.

senses.definition: Of a high level of importance, value, or excellence.

examples.text: Ella es una gran artista en su país.
examples.translation: She is a great artist in her country.

senses.definition: Of a person: grown up, or advanced in years (especially in Mexican Spanish).

examples.text: Cuando sea grande, quiero viajar por todo el mundo.
examples.translation: When I grow up, I want to travel all over the world.

faults.quote: good; kind; right
faults.why: Includes 'right', which is not covered by the senses.
Missing everyday senses 'skilled/good at' (mentioned in note 0) and 'suitable/right'.

faults.quote: It is very versatile. Use it for quality, taste, morality...
faults.why: Restates the senses instead of giving useful grammar or usage information (e.g. irregular comparative).

notes: The comparative form is irregular: 'lepszy' (better), and the superlative is 'najlepszy' (best).
To say someone is good at something, use 'dobry w' + locative (e.g. 'dobry w sporcie') or 'dobry z' + genitive for school subjects (e.g. 'dobry z matematyki').

senses.definition: Of high quality, pleasant, or tasty.

examples.text: To był bardzo dobry film.
examples.translation: That was a very good movie.

senses.definition: Of a person: kind, helpful, or morally upright.

examples.text: On jest dobrym człowiekiem.
examples.translation: He is a good person.

senses.definition: Skilled or competent at doing something.

examples.text: Ona jest dobra z matematyki.
examples.translation: She is good at math.

senses.definition: Suitable, convenient, or right for a particular purpose.

examples.text: To jest dobry moment na przerwę.
examples.translation: This is a good time for a break.

faults.quote: While 'dom' often refers to the physical building (house), it is also...
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.
Senses lack examples, though 'dom' has important prepositional idioms ('w domu' vs 'do domu').

notes: Do not confuse with 'mieszkanie', which specifically refers to an apartment or flat.
Notice the common expressions 'w domu' (at home, irregular locative '-u') and 'do domu' (home / homeward, genitive '-u').

examples.translation: I am home already.

senses.definition: A route, direction, or path taken to get from one place to another.

examples.text: Jesteśmy już w drodze do domu.
examples.translation: We are already on our way home.

examples.translation: I need to schedule an appointment with the doctor.

examples.translation: I am afraid of heights.

examples.translation: He feels a lot of fear when he hears thunder.

faults.quote: Be careful: do not confuse this with 'homem'

examples.translation: The boy is playing in the park.

examples.text: 제 동료를 소개합니다.
examples.translation: I would like to introduce my colleague.

examples.text: 카드로 계산할 수 있나요?

examples.text: 친구들과 카드 게임을 했어요.
examples.translation: I played a card game with my friends.

faults.quote: Used to refer to the entire planet, including its people and cultures.

senses.definition: The earth and all its countries, peoples, and cultures.

examples.text: 나는 언젠가 세계 여행을 하고 싶다.
examples.translation: I want to travel around the world someday.

senses.definition: A particular area of activity, interest, or experience.

examples.text: 그는 음악의 세계에 빠져 있다.
examples.translation: He is absorbed in the world of music.

faults.quote: A home on one floor of a bigger building.

senses.definition: A large high-rise residential building, or a home on one floor of such a building.

examples.text: 저는 아파트 15층에 살아요.
examples.translation: I live on the 15th floor of an apartment building.

faults.quote: Used as a basic seasoning in almost all Chinese dishes.
faults.why: Encyclopedic trivia that restates the definition; fails to give useful usage or classifier info.

faults.quote: Be careful not to confuse this with the character for 'rock' (岩

senses.definition: A white crystal substance used to season and preserve food.

examples.text: 菜里加一点盐会更好吃。
examples.translation: Adding a little salt to the dish will make it taste better.

faults.quote: While 楼 commonly refers to a building, it also refers to a
faults.why: Merely restates the two senses already given in the entry.

faults.why: Too broad; 楼 specifically refers to a multi-story building.

examples.text: 那座楼很高。
examples.translation: That building is very tall.

senses.definition: A level or story of a building.

examples.text: 我在二楼。
examples.translation: I am on the second floor.

faults.quote: 我在镜子里看我自己。

examples.text: 她出门前总是要照一下镜子。
examples.translation: She always looks in the mirror before going out.

faults.quote: 药店 is the everyday term for a regular pharmacy or drugstore.
faults.why: Restates the glosses and register without adding useful information.

faults.why: Explains the English difference between pharmacy and hospital, which learners already know.

notes: Takes the classifier 家 (jiā). Also called 药房 (yàofáng), which can also refer to the dispensary inside a hospital.

senses.definition: A shop that sells medicine and other health products.

examples.text: 我在药店买了一盒感冒药。
examples.translation: I bought a box of cold medicine at the pharmacy.

faults.why: 裙子 is one general concept in Chinese covering both skirts and dresses; splitting is English-driven.

senses.definition: A piece of clothing for women or girls that hangs from the waist, or a one-piece garment with a skirt.

examples.text: 这条红色的裙子很漂亮。
examples.translation: This red skirt is very pretty.

faults.why: Missing the common everyday sense 'low, small' (of an amount, price, or rate).

faults.why: merely restates the senses; should note that the form is identical in masculine and feminine.

examples.translation: After the flu, I felt very weak.

senses.definition: Of light, sound, or a signal: having low intensity, volume, or brightness.

examples.text: La lumière de cette lampe est trop faible pour lire.
examples.translation: The light from this lamp is too dim for reading.

senses.definition: Of an amount, price, or level: small in quantity or degree.

examples.text: Les prix sont très faibles en ce moment.
examples.translation: Prices are very low right now.

faults.quote: tired; exhausted

faults.why: Restates the definition of sense 0 without adding grammar or usage info.

faults.why: 'fatigué' and 'ennuyeux' look and sound nothing alike; not a real confusion pair.

examples.translation: I am very tired after this long day of work.

faults.why: Restates the senses without adding helpful usage or grammar information.

faults.quote: Use 'κακός' as a general term for 'bad'.

examples.translation: I had a bad day.

examples.text: Δεν είναι κακός άνθρωπος.
examples.translation: He is not a bad person.

faults.quote: Used identically to the English word 'menu' in a restaurant context.

examples.translation: I drink tea after the meal.

faults.why: Missing grammatical gender; मांस is masculine in Hindi.

senses.definition: Items that people wear to cover their bodies.

examples.text: मैंने नए कपड़े खरीदे।
